The tumor microenvironment in breast cancer consists of a complex interplay of tumor cells, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and immune cells, which can either promote or hinder tumor growth and progression. The objectives of this retrospective study were to determine the density of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in breast cancer tissues and to investigate its correlation with various clinicopathological factors.
Paraffin-embedded tissue samples and clinical data, including up to 5 years of follow-up information, were obtained from 172 breast cancer patients. The presence of TAMs was evaluated using immunohistochemical staining for the CD68 marker, which highlights macrophages. Our findings revealed that TAMs are more prevalent in breast cancer samples with high histopathological grade. Specifically, patients with a high density of TAMs had lower rates of disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival compared to those with low density of TAMs. Interestingly, a high-infiltration of TAMs was also associated with worse survival rates in node-negative breast cancer patients.
In conclusion, this study suggests that the number of TAMs in the tumor stroma is an independent predictor of survival time for breast cancer patients. Notably, high-infiltration of TAMs is a significant unfavorable prognostic factor for patients with invasive breast cancer, making it a useful prognostic marker for breast cancer.

title: Murine Dishevelled 3 Functions in Redundant Pathways with Dishevelled 1 and 2 in Normal Cardiac Outflow Tract, Cochlea, and Neural Tube Development
text:
Dishevelled (Dvl) proteins are key components of both the canonical beta-catenin/Wnt pathway and the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway, which regulate cell proliferation and patterning, as well as cell polarity within a sheet of cells and convergent extension movements that shape tissue. In mammals, three Dvl genes have been identified, and the roles of Dvl1 and Dvl2 in development have been previously determined. This study focuses on the functions of Dvl3 and identifies functional redundancy among the three murine Dvls.
Mutant mice lacking Dvl3 died perinatally with cardiac outflow tract abnormalities, including double outlet right ventricle and persistent truncus arteriosis. These mutants also displayed misoriented stereocilia in the organ of Corti, which was enhanced in combination with the loss of a single allele of the PCP component Vangl2/Ltap (LtapLp/+). Despite appearing normal during neurulation, Dvl3-deficient mutants displayed incomplete neural tube closure when combined with the deficiency of another Dvl. Intriguingly, increasing Dvl dosage genetically with Dvl transgenes demonstrated the ability of Dvls to compensate for one another and enable normal development. Interestingly, global canonical Wnt signaling appeared largely unaffected in double Dvl mutants, suggesting that low Dvl levels are sufficient for functional canonical Wnt signals.
In summary, this study shows that Dvl3 is essential for cardiac outflow tract development and its role in the PCP pathway during neurulation and cochlea development. Additionally, it highlights the functional redundancy of the three Dvls in multiple developmental processes.

title: Dynamics of adherens junctions in epithelial establishment, maintenance, and remodeling
text: The epithelial cadherin (E-cadherin)-catenin complex forms a mature adherens junction (AJ) by interacting with various cytoskeletal components and signaling molecules. This dynamic structure not only physically connects neighboring epithelial cells but also integrates intercellular adhesive contacts with the cytoskeleton, thereby defining each cell's apical-basal axis. Through these activities, the E-cadherin-catenin complex plays a crucial role in coordinating the formation, polarity, and function of all cells in an epithelium. Recent live-cell imaging studies have shed light on the mechanisms of E-cadherin turnover at junctions, which contributes to junction formation and the maintenance of epithelial integrity during tissue homeostasis and remodeling.

title: Long-term outcome of patients with asystole induced by head-up tilt test.
text:
AIMS: To evaluate the long-term outcome of the largest reported cohort of patients who experienced asystole during head-up tilt testing.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Since 1990, 1322 patients with syncope of unknown origin underwent tilt-table testing. Of these, 330 patients (24%) presented an abnormal response (syncope or pre-syncope). Specifically, 58 patients (17%) suffered a period of asystole (> or = 3000 ms) during the test, and the duration of asystole ranged from 3-90 seconds (median = 10 seconds). Two different tilting protocols (Westminster, 60 degrees, and isoproterenol, 80 degrees) were used, and the time to the syncopal episode and the duration of asystole differed significantly between the two protocols. However, neither the timing of asystole nor the type of therapy (pacemakers, drug therapy, or no specific treatment) influenced the outcome. In a cohort study of 120 age- and gender-matched patients without asystole, 12 patients (20%) developed recurrent syncopes during a 7-month follow-up period. In contrast, 34 patients (28%) without asystole presented syncopal episodes during a 6-month follow-up period (P = ns). The Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that patients without asystole had a mean time of 82 months until recurrence, while patients with asystole had a mean time of 92 months (P = ns). The number of previous syncopes was the only factor that significantly correlated with recurrence. There were no cardiac-related deaths.
CONCLUSIONS:
(1) Asystole during head-up tilt test does not necessarily imply a malignant outcome, and syncopal recurrences are rare.
(2) Pacemaker or drug therapy do not significantly influence the outcome, and the previous number of syncopal episodes is the only factor that correlates with recurrence.
(3) The tilting protocol (angle) may influence the time to and incidence of asystole during head-up tilt testing.

title: ZINC 15 – Ligand Discovery for Everyone
text: Investigators who could greatly benefit from insight into the biological activities of small molecules often face challenges in accessing this information. To address this gap between chemoinformatics and biology, we have developed a suite of tools that integrate with ZINC, a freely available web server. These tools enable investigators who are not computer specialists to annotate, purchase, and associate compounds with biological targets, providing a more streamlined process for accessing the information they need. The updated version of ZINC contains over 120 million "drug-like" compounds, with a quarter of them available for immediate delivery. These compounds are linked to high-value compounds such as metabolites, drugs, natural products, and annotated compounds from the literature, allowing users to access compounds based on their genetic associations and target classifications. New analysis tools have been implemented to make the platform user-friendly for both nonspecialists and experts, while ensuring that the original 3D formats of the molecules remain available for docking and other applications. ZINC is freely accessible at <http://zinc15.docking.org>.

title: Condensin-mediated remodeling of the mitotic chromatin landscape in fission yeast
text: The eukaryotic genome consists of DNA molecules significantly longer than the cells they reside within. During chromosome condensation in mitosis, these DNA molecules reach their maximum compactness. This process is facilitated by the action of condensin, a member of the structural maintenance of chromosomes (SMC) family. Despite significant progress in understanding the spatial organization of mitotic chromosomes, the mechanisms by which condensin shapes chromatin architecture remain incomplete. To address this knowledge gap, we utilized chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) to investigate mitotic chromosome condensation in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. This study revealed that the interphase landscape, characterized by small chromatin domains, is replaced by fewer but larger domains during mitosis. Condensin accomplishes this by establishing longer-range, intrachromosomal DNA interactions, which compact and individualize chromosomes. Simultaneously, local chromatin contacts are restricted by condensin, with profound implications for local chromatin function during mitosis. Our findings underscore the importance of condensin in transforming the chromatin landscape as cells prepare for cell division.

title: Efficacy of the 6-month thrice-weekly regimen in the treatment of new sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis under clinical trial conditions.
text:
BACKGROUND: The Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme of India recommends a thrice-weekly regimen of antitubercular drugs (2H(3)R(3)Z(3)E(3)/4H(3)R(3)) for patients with new smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. In this retrospective analysis, we evaluated the efficacy and tolerability of this regimen in HIV-negative patients with newly diagnosed smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis under clinical trial conditions.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from 268 patients who received the control regimen (2H(3)R(3)Z(3)E(3)/4H(3)R(3)) in two clinical trials conducted at the National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis, Chennai, India, between 2001 and 2006.
RESULTS: Of the 249 patients with available data, 238 (96%) had a favourable outcome at the end of treatment. Treatment failure occurred in 11 patients, of whom 7 had initial drug resistance and 4 had initial drug susceptibility. Of the 238 patients with a favourable outcome, 14 (6%) had recurrence of tuberculosis during the following 24 months. In the intention-to-treat analysis, 245 (94%) of 262 patients had a favourable status at the end of treatment. Of the 28 patients with initial drug resistance, 24 (86%) had a favourable outcome, with only 4 developing recurrence of tuberculosis in the following 2 years. Among the 221 patients initially infected with drug-susceptible organisms, drug resistance did not develop in any of the 7 patients in whom treatment failed or the 10 who had recurrence of tuberculosis. Moreover, 5 of the 7 patients in whom treatment failed continued to excrete drug-susceptible bacilli at 6 months. Adverse drug reactions were observed in 38 (14%) of the 262 patients, with only 3 (1.1%) requiring modification in treatment.
CONCLUSION: This thrice-weekly 6-month regimen of antitubercular drugs, when administered under full supervision, is associated with a high rate of favourable treatment outcomes in HIV-negative patients with newly diagnosed smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. The regimen shows few adverse drug reactions, with minimal modification required in most cases.

title: Curcumin attenuates inflammatory response in IL-1beta-induced human synovial fibroblasts and collagen-induced arthritis in mouse model.
text: Curcumin, a primary component of turmeric, has been found to exhibit anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant properties. Our study aimed to investigate if curcumin is effective against collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) in mice and IL-1beta-induced activation in fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs). DBA/1 mice were immunized with bovine type II collagen (CII) and treated with curcumin every other day for 2 weeks after immunization. The incidence of arthritis was evaluated based on paw thickness, and the proliferation of CII- or concanavalin A-induced splenic T cells were examined using IFN-gamma production. The levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-alpha and IL-1beta were evaluated in both the mouse ankle joint and serum, and the expression levels of prostaglandin E(2) (PGE(2)), cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) were determined in human FLSs. Our results showed that curcumin treatment downregulated the clinical arthritis score, splenic T cell proliferation, expression levels of TNF-alpha and IL-1beta in the ankle joint, and expression levels of IgG2a in serum. Additionally, curcumin inhibited PGE(2) production, COX-2 expression, and MMP secretion in FLSs by altering nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB transcription activity. These findings suggest that curcumin can effectively suppress the inflammatory response by inhibiting pro-inflammatory mediators and regulating humoral and cellular immune responses.

title: Loss of IGF-IEa or IGF-IEb impairs myogenic differentiation.
text: Recent years have seen growing interest in the actions of protein products resulting from alternative splicing of the Igf1 gene. However, the significance of these observations remains unclear. To investigate the functions of IGF-I splice variants, we examined the impact of reducing IGF-IEa and IGF-IEb on the proliferation and differentiation of cultured mouse myoblasts. Reducing total IGF-I or either IGF-IEa or IGF-IEb had no effect on cell viability in growth medium, but cells lacking either IGF-IEa or IGF-IEb proliferated significantly slower than control cells or cells lacking IGF-IEb in serum-free media. Specifically, simultaneous loss of both or specific loss of either splice variant significantly inhibited myosin heavy chain (MyHC) immunoreactivity by 70-80% (P < 0.01) under differentiation conditions (48 h in 2% horse serum) as determined by Western immunoblotting. Moreover, loss of IGF-IEb also reduced MyHC isoform mRNAs, with the exception of Myh7, to a lesser degree (∼20-40%, P < 0.05). Interestingly, provision of mature IGF-I, but not synthetic E peptides, restored Myh3 expression to control levels in cells lacking IGF-IEa or IGF-IEb. These findings suggest that IGF-I splice variants may regulate myoblast differentiation through the actions of mature IGF-I and not the E peptides.

title: Antimicrobial peptide pleurocidin synergizes with antibiotics through hydroxyl radical formation and membrane damage, and exerts antibiofilm activity.
text:
Background:
Pleurocidin, a 25-mer antimicrobial peptide (AMP), has been shown to exhibit bactericidal activity. However, the mechanisms of its synergistic activity when combined with conventional antibiotics and its antibiofilm effect are poorly understood.
Methods:
To investigate the interaction between pleurocidin and antibiotics, we performed a checkerboard assay. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, we measured hydroxyl radical formation using 3'-(p-hydroxyphenyl) fluorescein, detected the NAD(+)/NADH ratio with a NAD(+) cycling assay, and examined cytoplasmic membrane damage with propidium iodide. Additionally, we evaluated the antibiofilm effect of pleurocidin using a tissue culture plate method.
Results:
Our results showed that pleurocidin exhibited synergistic activity with all bacterial strains (fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) ≤ 0.5), except for Enterococcus faecium treated with a combination of pleurocidin and ampicillin (FICI = 0.75). We found that pleurocidin and antibiotics induced hydroxyl radical formation, which was caused by a transient NADH depletion. The addition of thiourea, a hydroxyl radical scavenger, prevented bacterial death, especially in the case of the combined treatment of pleurocidin and ampicillin, which showed synergisms. The combination of pleurocidin and erythromycin increased the permeability of bacterial cytoplasmic membrane. Furthermore, pleurocidin exhibited a potent inhibitory effect on preformed biofilm of bacterial organisms.
Conclusion:
Our findings suggest that the synergistic effect between pleurocidin and antibiotics is due to hydroxyl radical formation and membrane-active mechanisms. Pleurocidin exhibited antibiofilm activity, making it a potential therapeutic agent and adjuvant for antimicrobial chemotherapy.

title: Outcome of pregnancy in women with moderate or severe renal insufficiency.
text:
Women with mild pre-existing renal disease during pregnancy tend to have relatively few complications, but the risk of adverse outcomes in those with moderate or severe renal insufficiency is still unclear. To investigate, we evaluated the frequency and types of maternal and obstetrical complications as well as outcomes of pregnancy in 67 women with primary renal disease (82 pregnancies). All participants had initial serum creatinine concentrations of at least 1.4 mg/dL (124 mumol/L) and pregnancies that continued beyond the first trimester.
Our results showed that the average (±SD) serum creatinine level increased from 1.9 (±0.8) mg/dL (168 (±71) mumol/L) in early pregnancy to 2.5 (±1.3) mg/dL (221 (±115) mumol/L) in the third trimester. The incidence of hypertension rose from 28% at baseline to 48% in the third trimester, and that of high-grade proteinuria (urinary protein excretion >3000 mg/L) from 23% to 41% during the same period. Among the 70 pregnancies (57 women) for whom data were available during pregnancy and immediately postpartum, 43% experienced pregnancy-related decline in maternal renal function. Eight of these pregnancies (10% of the total) were associated with rapid acceleration of maternal renal insufficiency. Obstetrical complications included a high rate of preterm delivery (59%) and growth restriction (37%). Interestingly, the infant survival rate was 93%.
Our findings suggest that while pregnant women with moderate or severe renal insufficiency are at increased risk for complications due to worsening renal function, hypertension, and obstetrical complications, the fetal survival rate remains high.

title: High-mobility group box-1 protein induces osteogenic phenotype changes in aortic valve interstitial cells.
text:
The study aimed to investigate the role of the HMGB1-TLR4 axis in the development of calcific aortic valve (AV) disease, a condition characterized by inflammation and calcification of the valve. The study used immunohistochemical staining and immunoblotting to evaluate the expression of HMGB1 and TLR4 in human calcific AVs, as well as in-vitro experiments using cultured valvular interstitial cells (VICs).
The results showed that HMGB1 and TLR4 were abundantly expressed in calcific AVs, and HMGB1 significantly induced the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and promoted the osteoblastic differentiation and calcification of VICs. Further, HMGB1 activated the JNK MAPK and NF-κB signaling pathways, which are known to play a role in osteoblastic differentiation and calcification. However, the effects of HMGB1 were significantly suppressed when TLR4 was silenced using siRNA. Additionally, blockade of JNK MAPK and NF-κB phosphorylation prohibited HMGB1-induced production of pro-osteogenic factors and mineralization of VICs.

In conclusion, the study suggests that the HMGB1-TLR4 axis may play a significant role in the development of calcific AV disease by promoting osteoblastic differentiation and calcification of VICs, which are hallmarks of the disease. These findings may have implications for the development of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of calcific AV disease.

title: RiboSys, a high-resolution, quantitative approach to measure the in vivo kinetics of pre-mRNA splicing and 3'-end processing in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: We have developed methods for obtaining a quantitative description of RNA processing at the molecular level in budding yeast. Utilizing the yeast strains tetON (for induction studies) and tetOFF (for repression, derepression, and RNA degradation studies), we integrated reporter genes into the genome under the control of a tetO7 promoter. By adapting reverse transcription and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) techniques, we were able to determine the average number of mRNA copies per cell in a population. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) measurements of transcript numbers in individual cells validated the RT-qPCR approach for determining the average copy number, despite the diverse distribution of transcript levels within a population of cells. Additionally, RT-qPCR was used to identify the products of the successive steps in splicing of the reporter transcripts, and methods were developed to map and quantify 3'-end cleavage and polyadenylation. This system allows for the unprecedented quantitative monitoring of pre-mRNA production, splicing, 3'-end maturation, and degradation, which can be used for mathematical modeling. By employing this approach, we demonstrated that reporter transcripts are spliced prior to their 3'-end cleavage and polyadenylation, occurring cotranscriptionally.

title: Generation of mice with a conditional allele for the p75(NTR) neurotrophin receptor gene.
text: The p75(NTR) neurotrophin receptor has been linked to a variety of biological and pathological processes, although significant progress has recently been made in understanding its physiological function. However, many details and aspects remain unknown due to limitations in existing knockout mouse models. To address this, we have generated mice with a conditional p75(NTR) allele (p75(NTR-FX)) created by flanking Exons 4-6, which encode the transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains, with loxP sites. To validate this novel conditional allele, we generated both neural crest-specific p75(NTR) /Wnt1-Cre mutants and conventional p75(NTR) null mutants. Surprisingly, both mutants displayed abnormal hind limb reflexes, indicating that loss of p75(NTR) in neural crest-derived cells leads to a peripheral neuropathy similar to that seen in conventional p75(NTR) mutants. The novel conditional p75(NTR) allele provides new opportunities to explore the role of p75(NTR) in specific tissues and cells.

title: A Triple-Stain Flow Cytometric Method to Assess Plasma- and Acrosome-Membrane Integrity of Cryopreserved Bovine Sperm Immediately after Thawing in Presence of Egg-Yolk Particles1
text: Using flow cytometry to evaluate the viability and acrosome integrity of spermatozoa simultaneously would be a valuable tool in both research and routine work. In a recent study, a new triple-stain combination was developed for this purpose, enabling the simultaneous discrimination of sperm cells from egg yolk and debris particles. The combination of SYBR-14, propidium iodide (PI), and phycoerythrin-conjugated peanut agglutinin (PE-PNA) allowed for the flow cytometric analysis of frozen-thawed bovine sperm without the need for washing steps to remove egg yolk. Acrosome-damaged/reacted sperm cells were distinguished from acrosome-intact cells using PE-PNA. To assess the repeatability of the method, 10 bulls' processed ejaculates were analyzed in duplicate measurements, with three straws per batch. The method agreement analysis between the SYBR-14/PE-PNA/PI and fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-conjugated PNA staining showed FITC-PNA/PI staining to overestimate the live and acrosome-intact sperm cell subpopulation by an average of 6.3%. The new triple-stain combination was found to be highly repeatable and easy to use in routine applications, providing a more precise estimate of the rate of sperm cells with intact head membranes and acrosomes compared to the commonly used and validated FITC-PNA/PI staining.

title: Universal voluntary HIV testing with immediate antiretroviral therapy as a strategy for elimination of HIV transmission: a mathematical model.
text:
Approximately 3 million people globally were receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) at the end of 2007, yet an estimated 6.7 million people remained in need of treatment, and an additional 2.7 million individuals became infected with HIV during the same year. While prevention efforts can help reduce HIV incidence, they are unlikely to completely eliminate the disease. To explore the potential of universal voluntary HIV testing and immediate treatment with ART in driving the HIV epidemic towards elimination, we developed a theoretical strategy and examined its effectiveness using mathematical models.
We analyzed the impact of testing all individuals aged 15 and older for HIV annually and starting those diagnosed HIV positive on treatment immediately on the case reproduction number (using a stochastic model) and long-term dynamics of the HIV epidemic (employing a deterministic transmission model). We employed data from South Africa as our test case, assuming all HIV transmission occurred through heterosexual means.
Our findings reveal that the proposed strategy could significantly accelerate the transition from the current endemic phase, in which most adults living with HIV are not on ART, to an elimination phase, in which most are on treatment, within five years. It could reduce HIV incidence and mortality to less than one case per 1000 people per year by 2016, or within ten years of full implementation of the strategy, and lower the prevalence of HIV to less than 1% within 50 years. We estimate that in 2032, the yearly cost of the present strategy and the theoretical strategy would both be US$1.7 billion; however, after this time, the cost of the present strategy would continue to increase, while that of the theoretical strategy would decrease.
Our findings suggest that universal voluntary HIV testing and immediate ART, combined with current prevention efforts, have the potential to significantly impact severe generalised HIV/AIDS epidemics. This approach merits further mathematical modeling, research, and broad consultation.

title: Common variants in DGKK are strongly associated with risk of hypospadias
text: Hypospadias is a common congenital abnormality affecting the male external genitalia. To investigate the genetic underlying of this condition, we conducted a genome-wide association study using pooled DNA from 436 individuals with hypospadias (cases) and 494 controls of European descent. We identified the top-ranked SNPs and selected them for individual genotyping in a discovery sample of 133 cases and their parents, as well as an additional Dutch sample of 266 cases and 402 controls. Our individual genotyping results for two SNPs (rs1934179 and rs7063116) in the gene encoding diacylglycerol kinase κ (DGKK) demonstrated strong associations with hypospadias in all three samples (odds ratio (OR) = 2.5-3.8, P < 10^-5 in each sample). Moreover, we found that the expression of DGKK was lower in preputial tissue from cases than from controls, and this difference was more pronounced in individuals carrying the risk allele of rs1934179 (P = 0.047). Based on these findings, we propose DGKK as the major risk gene for hypospadias.

title: Neutrophils Suppress Intraluminal NK Cell-Mediated Tumor Cell Clearance and Enhance Extravasation of Disseminated Carcinoma Cells.
text:
Unlabeled Immune cells promote the initial metastatic dissemination of carcinoma cells from primary tumors. In contrast to their well-studied functions in the initial stages of metastasis, the specific roles of immune cells in facilitating progression through the critical later steps of the invasion-metastasis cascade remain poorly understood. Here, we define novel functions of neutrophils in promoting intraluminal survival and extravasation at sites of metastatic dissemination. We show that CD11b(+)/Ly6G(+) neutrophils enhance metastasis formation via two distinct mechanisms. First, neutrophils inhibit natural killer cell function, leading to a significant increase in the intraluminal survival time of tumor cells. Thereafter, neutrophils operate to facilitate extravasation of tumor cells through the secretion of IL1β and matrix metalloproteinases. These results identify neutrophils as key regulators of intraluminal survival and extravasation through their cross-talk with host cells and disseminating carcinoma cells.
Significance: This study provides important insights into the systemic contributions of neutrophils to cancer metastasis by identifying how neutrophils facilitate intermediate steps of the invasion-metastasis cascade. We demonstrate that neutrophils suppress natural killer cell activity and increase extravasation of tumor cells. Cancer Discov; 6(6); 630-49. ©2016 AACR.This article is highlighted in the In This Issue feature, p. 561.

title: High Km soluble 5'-nucleotidase from human placenta. Properties and allosteric regulation by IMP and ATP.
text: Human placental soluble "high Km" 5'-nucleotidase was separated from "low Km" 5'-nucleotidase and nonspecific phosphatase using AMP-Sepharose affinity chromatography. Following purification, the enzyme was obtained at a specific activity of 25.6 micromoles per minute per milligram, with a subunit molecular mass of 53 kilodaltons and a native molecular mass of 210 kilodaltons, indicating a tetrameric structure. The enzyme exhibited the highest activity towards IMP and GMP, with IMP being hydrolyzed 15 times faster than AMP. The enzyme showed a virtually absolute requirement for magnesium ions and was regulated by them. Purine nucleoside 5'-triphosphates, particularly dATP, ATP, and GTP, strongly activated the enzyme, with the potency order being dATP > ATP > GTP. The enzyme's activity was also influenced by the concentration of inorganic phosphate, which shifted the substrate velocity relationship from sigmoidal to hyperbolic. At physiological concentrations of cofactors (3 millimoles ATP, 1-4 millimoles inorganic phosphate, and 150 millimoles potassium chloride at pH 7.4), the enzyme was 25-35 times more active towards 100 micromoles IMP than towards 100 micromoles AMP. These findings indicate that: (a) soluble human placental high Km 5'-nucleotidase coexists in the human placenta with the low Km enzyme; (b) under physiological conditions, the enzyme favors the hydrolysis of IMP and is critically regulated by IMP, ATP, and inorganic phosphate levels; and (c) the kinetic properties of ATP and IMP are modulated by each other, suggesting a complex interplay between the associated binding sites.

title: Histones are incorporated in trans during reassembly of the yeast PHO5 promoter.
text: In yeast, the reprogramming of PHO5 promoter chromatin upon activation involves transient hyperacetylation and subsequent removal of histones from the promoter region in trans. During the process of repression, nucleosomes need to be reassembled on the inactive promoter. By utilizing a strain with dual-labeled and regulated versions of histone H3, we were able to determine the source of histones for the reassembly of inactive promoter chromatin. Our findings show that the incorporated histones derive from a source outside the chromatin fraction. Rapid promoter closure occurs through the actions of histone chaperones Asf1 and Hir1, as well as the SWI/SNF nucleosome remodeling complex.

title: National study of physician awareness and adherence to cardiovascular disease prevention guidelines.
text: Little is known about how physician specialty and patient characteristics influence adherence to cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention guidelines. In an online study of 500 physicians (300 primary care physicians, 100 obstetricians/gynecologists, and 100 cardiologists), we evaluated awareness of and adoption of national CVD prevention guidelines by specialty and the gender of patients. We also tested physician accuracy in assigning CVD risk levels and adherence to guidelines among high-, intermediate-, or low-risk patients. Using an experimental case study design, we found that intermediate-risk women were more likely to be assigned to a lower-risk category by primary care physicians than men with identical risk profiles (P < 0.0001). This trend was observed among obstetricians/gynecologists and cardiologists as well. We also found that assignment of risk level significantly predicted recommendations for lifestyle and preventive pharmacotherapy. After adjusting for risk assignment, the impact of patient gender on preventive care was not significant, except for less aspirin (P < 0.01) and more weight management recommended (P < 0.04) for intermediate-risk women. Although physicians did not rate themselves as very effective in their ability to help patients prevent CVD, they were unaware that more women than men die each year from CVD. Our findings suggest that perception of risk is the primary factor associated with CVD preventive recommendations. Gender disparities in recommendations for preventive therapy were primarily explained by lower perceived risk despite similar calculated risk for women versus men. Educational interventions for physicians are needed to improve the quality of CVD preventive care and lower morbidity and mortality from CVD for men and women.

title: TECHNICAL ADVANCE Floral dip: a simplified method for Agrobacterium-mediated
text: The Agrobacterium vacuum infiltration method has made it possible to transform Arabidopsis thaliana without the need for plant tissue culture or regeneration. In the current study, this method was evaluated and a significantly modified transformation protocol was developed. The labor-intensive vacuum infiltration process was replaced by a simple dipping method involving the insertion of developing floral tissues into a solution containing Agrobacterium tumefaciens, 5% sucrose, and 500 microliters per liter of surfactant Silwet L-77. Sucrose and surfactant play a critical role in the success of the floral dip method. Plants inoculated when they have numerous immature floral buds and few siliques produce transformed progeny at the highest rate. The use of plant tissue culture media, hormones, and pH adjustment is unnecessary, and Agrobacterium can be applied to plants at a range of cell densities. Repeated application of Agrobacterium improves transformation rates and overall yield of transformants by approximately twofold, and covering plants for 1 day to retain humidity after inoculation also increases transformation rates by twofold. Multiple ecotypes can be transformed using this method, making it an efficient tool for high-throughput transformation of Arabidopsis for various applications such as T-DNA gene tagging, positional cloning, or attempts at targeted gene replacement.

title: Pathway connectivity and signaling coordination in the yeast stress-activated signaling network
text: Stressed cells coordinate a multi-faceted response encompassing various levels of physiology. Despite extensive knowledge of the stress-activated regulatory network and underlying design principles for signal integration, many gaps remain. To bridge these knowledge gaps, we developed a computational and experimental approach integrating available protein interaction data, gene fitness contributions, mutant transcriptome profiles, and phosphoproteome changes in salt-stressed yeast cells. By inference, we constructed a salt-responsive signaling network in yeast, uncovering novel predictions, such as the identification of new regulators, unappreciated crosstalk between established pathways, and previously unsuspected 'hubs' of signal integration. We validated these predictions by demonstrating that Cdc14 phosphatase serves as a central hub in the network and that modification of RNA polymerase II correlates with the induction of stress-defense genes and the reduction of growth-related transcripts. Our findings underscore the importance of the inferred network in understanding stress biology, particularly in the context of human cancer, where the corresponding network is enriched with cancer-causing genes.

title: Premigratory and migratory neural crest cells are multipotent in vivo.
text: The neural crest (NC) is an embryonic stem cell population that gives rise to a wide range of cell types, including peripheral neurons, myelinating Schwann cells, and melanocytes. However, there has been a longstanding debate about whether individual NC cells are truly multipotent or if they are composed of a heterogeneous mixture of lineage-restricted progenitors. To address this question, we used in vivo fate mapping of single trunk NC cells in the R26R-Confetti mouse model, both during premigratory and migratory stages. By combining quantitative clonal analyses with definitive markers of differentiation, we found that the vast majority of individual NC cells are multipotent, with only a small number of clones contributing to a single derivative. Interestingly, this multipotency is maintained in migratory NC cells. Our findings provide conclusive evidence for the in vivo multipotency of both premigratory and migrating NC cells in the mouse.

title: Implementing the ESHRE 'poor responder' criteria in research studies: methodological implications.
text: The Bologna criteria for identifying poor ovarian response (POR) during in vitro fertilization (IVF) serve as a useful template for new research in this field of assisted conception. However, designing studies based on the European Society for Human Reproduction and Embryology (ESHRE) POR criteria can be methodologically complex due to the new definition's inclusion of various POR subpopulations with distinct baseline characteristics and unknown clinical outcomes. When conducting randomized controlled trials (RCTs), potential bias may arise if women from each subpopulation are not evenly distributed between intervention groups. In smaller or moderate-sized RCTs, a single-sequence randomization method may not ensure balanced allocation between groups. Stratified randomization methods offer an alternative methodological approach. Depending on the chosen methodology, patient outcomes within each intervention group may be better reported according to relevant subpopulations.

title: Generation of gene-edited rats by delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 protein and donor DNA into intact zygotes using electroporation
text: The CRISPR/Cas9 system's ability to generate gene-edited animals relies on microinjection into zygotes, which is time-consuming, inefficient, and requires high technical skills. To overcome these challenges, we optimized an electroporation method for intact rat zygotes using sgRNAs and Cas9 protein in combination or without ssODNs (~100 nt). This resulted in a high frequency of knockouts, ranging from 15% to 50% of analyzed animals. Notably, using ssODNs as a donor template led to precise knock-in mutations in 25-100% of analyzed animals, comparable to microinjection. Surprisingly, electroporation of long ssDNA or dsDNA donors, which were previously successful in microinjection, failed to generate genome-edited animals despite visualization of dsDNA within zygotes. Therefore, simultaneous electroporation of a large number of intact rat zygotes represents a rapid, simple, and efficient approach for generating a variety of genome-edited rats.

title: Uridylation of miRNAs by HEN1 SUPPRESSOR1 in Arabidopsis
text: HEN1-mediated 2'-O-methylation has been shown to protect plant microRNAs (miRNAs) and small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) as well as animal piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) from degradation and 3' terminal uridylation. However, the enzymes responsible for uridylating unmethylated miRNAs, siRNAs, or piRNAs in hen1 are unknown. In this study, a genetic screen identified a second-site mutation, hen1 suppressor1-2 (heso1-2), that partially suppresses the morphological phenotypes of the hypomorphic hen1-2 allele and the null hen1-1 allele in Arabidopsis. HESO1 encodes a terminal nucleotidyl transferase that preferentially adds untemplated uridine to the 3' end of RNA, which is completely abolished by 2'-O-methylation. The heso1-2 mutation affects the profile of u-tailed miRNAs and siRNAs and increases the abundance of truncated and/or normal-sized ones in hen1, leading to increased accumulation of miRNAs and siRNAs in hen1. In contrast, overexpressing HESO1 in hen1-2 causes more severe morphological defects and less accumulation of miRNAs. These findings demonstrate that HESO1 is an enzyme responsible for uridylating unmethylated miRNAs and siRNAs in hen1. These observations also suggest that uridylation may destabilize unmethylated miRNAs through an unknown mechanism and compete with 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease activities in hen1. These results have implications for the regulation of piRNA uridylation in hen1 in animals.

title: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis to Prevent HIV Infection: Current Status, Future Opportunities and Challenges
text:
As the global incidence of HIV surpasses 2 million new infections annually, effective interventions are urgently needed to reduce HIV transmission. Randomized, placebo-controlled studies have demonstrated that daily oral antiretroviral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) with a fixed-dose combination tablet containing tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine can significantly lower HIV incidence among diverse at-risk populations. These studies have shown that the efficacy of PrEP is directly linked to adherence levels. The official guidelines recommend providing PrEP to individuals at the highest risk of HIV acquisition, and implementation projects suggest that high levels of uptake and adherence are achievable outside of clinical trials. Nonetheless, several challenges hinder the implementation of PrEP, including:
1. Limited awareness and use among at-risk individuals
2. Uncertainty about adherence in real-world settings
3. Lack of training among healthcare providers in PrEP provision
4. Limited data on potential long-term adverse effects of tenofovir–emtricitabine
5. High costs of PrEP medications
6. Stigma associated with PrEP use and the behaviors that would warrant its use.
Innovative pharmacological approaches could help overcome these challenges. These include:
1. Less-than-daily oral dosing regimens and long-acting injectable medications to reduce pill burdens and facilitate adherence.
2. Local delivery of PrEP medications to the genital compartments via gels, rings, and films to minimize systemic drug exposure and potential toxicities.
As the portfolio of chemoprophylactic agents and delivery systems expands to cater to the diverse sexual health needs and product preferences of individuals who may benefit from PrEP, there is hope that antiretroviral chemoprophylaxis will become an accepted, feasible, and highly effective addition to existing HIV prevention strategies. By providing a safe and effective means of preventing HIV transmission, we can significantly reduce the global incidence of the disease and improve the health and wellbeing of individuals at risk.

title: Prepregnancy BMI and the risk of gestational diabetes: a systematic review of the literature with meta-analysis.
text:
This study aims to assess and quantify the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) based on prepregnancy maternal body mass index (BMI).
Design:
A systematic review of observational studies published over the last 30 years was conducted, searching four electronic databases (1977-2007). BMI was chosen as the sole measure of obesity, and all diagnostic criteria for GDM were adopted. Studies with selective screening for GDM were excluded, and there were no language restrictions. The quality of the primary studies was assessed, and a total of 1745 citations were screened, resulting in the inclusion of 70 studies (2 unpublished) involving 671,945 women (59 cohorts and 11 case-controls). The majority of the studies were of high or medium quality.
Results:
Compared to women with a normal BMI, underweight women had a significantly lower odds ratio (OR) of developing GDM (OR=0.75; 95% CI=0.69-0.82). Overweight, moderately obese, and morbidly obese women had higher ORs: 1.97 (95% CI=1.77-2.19), 3.01 (95% CI=2.34-3.87), and 5.55 (95% CI=4.27-7.21), respectively. For every 1 kg/m^2 increase in BMI, the prevalence of GDM increased by 0.92% (95% CI=0.73-1.10). The risk of GDM is positively associated with prepregnancy BMI.
Implications:
This information is crucial for counselling women planning a pregnancy.

title: Multiple risk behaviour: increasing socio-economic gap over time?
text:
BACKGROUND: Unhealthy behaviors often coincide with one another. In this study, we analyzed the relationship between education and lifestyle, defined as a cluster of risky behaviors, to assess changes in socioeconomic inequalities in multiple risk behavior over time.
METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Belgian Health Interview Surveys in 1997, 2001, and 2004, restricting our analysis to individuals aged ≥15 with information on health behaviors and education (n = 7431, n = 8142, and n = 7459, respectively). A lifestyle index was created based on the sum of four unhealthy behaviors: smoking, risky alcohol use, sedentary behavior, and poor diet. The lifestyle index was dichotomized as low (0-2) vs. high (3-4). We calculated summary measures, including Odds Ratios (OR) and Relative Index of Inequality (RII), using logistic regression, stratified by sex, to assess socioeconomic inequalities in multiple risk behavior.
RESULTS: Among adults, 7.5% combined three to four unhealthy behaviors. Lower educated men were at the greatest risk, with a significant increase in the odds ratio (OR) from 1.6 in 2001 to 3.4 in 2004 (P = 0.029) for men. While the increase in the OR among women was less pronounced, we found no gradient in the RII for either men or women.
CONCLUSION: Lower socioeconomic classes are more likely to engage in multiple risk behaviors. Our findings indicate an increasing polarization in socioeconomic inequalities among men, suggesting a need for targeted health promotion programs focusing on low socioeconomic classes and simultaneously addressing multiple risk behaviors.

title: Variations and Trends in Health Burden of Visual Impairment Due to Cataract: A Global Analysis.
text:
Purpose: To evaluate the global trends in the burden of visual impairment due to cataract in terms of disability-adjusted life years (DALY) and its correlations with the level of socioeconomic development in countries.
Methods: The study used data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2015, which provided global, regional, and national DALY numbers, crude rate, and age-standardized rate of cataract vision loss by age and sex. The study also obtained data on human development index (HDI), per capita gross domestic product (GDP), and other country-level data from international open databases. The study used regression analysis to assess the correlations between age-standardized DALY rate and socioeconomic variables.
Results: The study found that the global DALY numbers of cataract vision loss increased by 89.42% between 1990 and 2015, from 2048.18 thousands to 3879.74 thousands (p < 0.001). Females had higher DALY numbers and crude rate than males after adjusting for age and country (all p < 0.001). The age-standardized DALY rate was higher in countries with low HDI, with 91.03 for low HDI, 81.67 for medium HDI, 55.89 for high HDI, and 17.10 for very high HDI countries (p < 0.01), respectively. The national age-standardized DALY rates in 2015 were negatively associated with both HDI (R2 = 0.489, p < 0.001) and per capita GDP (R2 = 0.331, p < 0.001). Stepwise multiple regression showed that HDI was significantly correlated with national age-standardized DALY rates in 2015 after adjusting for other confounding factors (p < 0.001).
Conclusions: The study found that despite efforts to address visual impairment due to cataract, the global health burden of vision loss increased between 1990 and 2015. The study also found that the burden of visual impairment was significantly associated with socioeconomic development in countries, as measured by HDI and per capita GDP. The findings suggest that addressing visual impairment due to cataract requires a multi-faceted approach that includes improving socioeconomic development in countries, especially those with low and medium levels of development.

title: Multiplex genome engineering using CRISPR/Cas systems.
text: Elucidating the functional consequences of genetic variants and elements requires state-of-the-art genome editing tools. Type II prokaryotic CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats)/Cas systems have been established as precision tools for RNA-guided site-specific DNA cleavage. We have engineered two distinct type II CRISPR/Cas systems and demonstrated that Cas9 nucleases can be directed by short RNAs to effect precise cleavage at endogenous genomic locations in human and mouse cells. Additionally, Cas9 can be converted into a nicking enzyme, allowing for homology-directed repair with minimal mutagenic potential. Furthermore, multiple guide sequences can be encoded within a single CRISPR array, enabling simultaneous editing of multiple sites within the mammalian genome with ease and wide applicability.

title: Transformation of intact yeast cells treated with alkali cations.
text: Intact yeast cells treated with alkaline cations took up plasmid DNA. Li+, Cs+, Rb+, K+, and Na+ were found to be effective in inducing competence. The transformation of Saccharomyces cerevisiae D13-1A with plasmid YRp7 was studied in detail with CsCl. The optimum incubation time was 1 hour, and the optimum cell concentration was 5 x 10^7 cells per ml. The optimum concentration of Cs+ was 1.0 M. Transformation efficiency increased with increasing concentrations of plasmid DNA. The presence of polyethylene glycol was necessary for efficient plasmid uptake. Heat pulse and various polyamines or basic proteins enhanced the uptake of plasmid DNA. Additionally, circular DNA was taken up by Cs+-treated yeast cells, although the uptake efficiency was significantly lower compared to linear plasmid DNA. The transformation efficiency with Cs+ or Li+ was comparable to conventional protoplast methods for plasmids containing the ars1 gene, although it was not as efficient for plasmids containing a 2 microns origin replication.

title: Health-Related Quality of Life as Measured with EQ-5D among Populations with and without Specific Chronic Conditions: A Population-Based Survey in Shaanxi Province, China
text:
Study Objectives:
This study aimed to investigate the relationship between chronic conditions and other risk factors and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) measured by EQ-5D in a distributed sample located in Shaanxi Province, China.
Methods:
A multi-stage stratified cluster sampling method was used to select subjects. EQ-5D was employed to measure HRQoL. The likelihood of individuals with chronic diseases reporting problems in each EQ-5D dimension was calculated and tested relative to the reference groups. Multivariable linear regression models were used to investigate factors associated with EQ VAS.
Results:
The most frequently reported problems involved pain/discomfort (8.8%) and anxiety/depression (7.6%). Nearly half of the respondents who reported problems in any of the five dimensions were chronic patients. Higher EQ VAS scores were associated with the male gender, higher level of education, employment, younger age, living in an urban area, and access to free medical service. except for anemia, all chronic diseases were indicative of a negative EQ VAS score. The three leading risk factors were cerebrovascular disease, cancer, and mental disease. Increases in age, number of chronic conditions, and frequency of physical activity were found to have a gradient effect.
Conclusion:
The present work enhances the existing knowledge on population health status using mortality and morbidity data. Medical, policy, social, and individual attention are necessary for chronic disease management and improvement of HRQoL. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate the outcomes of chronic disease intervention programs.

title: Memory and Modularity in Cell-Fate Decision Making
text: Genetically identical cells exposed to the same environment can exhibit varying phenotypes, with some cells displaying marked differences. However, it is unclear how much of this variation is due to chance, external cues, or the individual cells' attempt to exhibit unique phenotypes through autonomous programs. To investigate this phenomenon, we studied thousands of Bacillus subtilis cells over hundreds of generations under constant conditions and observed their behavior. Our findings reveal that the decision between a solitary, motile state and a chained, sessile state is largely stochastic, with no autonomous control over the time spent in each state. In contrast, the time spent in connected chains of cells is tightly regulated, ensuring coordination among related cells in the multicellular state. We discovered that the regulatory circuit governing this decision is modular, with initiation and maintenance of chaining being genetically separable functions. Interestingly, stimulation of the same pathway that initiates chaining also promotes biofilm formation, suggesting that cells have an autonomous timing mechanism that allows for a trial commitment to multicellularity, which external cues can extend.

title: Lpd depletion reveals that SRF specifies radial versus tangential migration of pyramidal neurons
text: During corticogenesis, pyramidal neurons (approximately 80% of cortical neurons) originate from the ventricular zone, progress through a multipolar stage to become bipolar, and adhere to radial glial cells. Afterwards, they migrate to their appointed position within the cortex. As the bipolar neurons move radially, they remain connected to their glial foundation while passing through the subventricular and intermediate zones, regions rich in tangentially migrating interneurons and axon fiber tracts. We investigated the role of lamellipodin (Lpd), a homologue of a key regulator of neuronal migration and polarization in Caenorhabditis elegans, in corticogenesis. Lpd depletion caused bipolar pyramidal neurons to adopt a tangential, rather than radial-glial, migration path without affecting their cell fate. Mechanistically, Lpd depletion decreases the activity of SRF, a transcription factor regulated by changes in the ratio of polymerized to unpolymerized actin. As a result, Lpd depletion reveals a role for SRF in directing pyramidal neurons to select a radial migration pathway along glial cells rather than a tangential migration mode.

title: Identification of p18 INK4c as a tumor suppressor gene in glioblastoma multiforme.
text: Genomic alterations leading to abnormal activation of cyclin/cyclin-dependent kinase (cdk) complexes are the root cause of many common human tumor types, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). Heterozygous deletion of p16(INK4a) and, less frequently, genomic amplifications of genes encoding cyclins or cdks are the most common genomic alterations observed in GBM. We have uncovered a novel genetic alteration in GBM, specifically the deletion of the p18(INK4c) cdk inhibitor. This deletion frequently occurs in tandem with homozygous deletions of p16(INK4a). Immunohistochemical analysis of primary GBM tumors revealed that p18(INK4c) expression was absent in 43% of cases. To study the functional implications of p18(INK4c) deficiency in GBM, we employed lentiviral reconstitution of p18(INK4c) expression in p18(INK4c)-deficient but not p18(INK4c)-proficient GBM cells. Our findings designate p18(INK4c) as a GBM tumor suppressor gene and unveil an additional mechanism underlying aberrant cyclin/cdk activation in this aggressive malignancy.

title: Two-stage control of an oxidative stress regulon: the Escherichia coli SoxR protein triggers redox-inducible expression of the soxS regulatory gene.
text:
Escherichia coli responds to the redox stress imposed by generators of superoxide, such as paraquat, by inducing the synthesis of up to 80 proteins. The expression of a key subset of these proteins is regulated at the transcriptional level by the soxRS locus, which forms a two-stage control system. In the first stage, an intracellular redox signal triggers the SoxR protein as a transcriptional activator of the soxS gene, leading to increased levels of SoxS protein. In the second stage, the increased levels of SoxS protein activate the transcription of various genes in the soxRS regulon.
To investigate the regulation of soxS transcription, we constructed operon fusions of the E. coli lac genes to the soxS promoter. Expression from the soxS promoter was found to be strongly inducible by paraquat in a manner dependent on the functional soxR gene. Additionally, phenazine methosulfate, another superoxide-generating agent, also triggered soxR-dependent soxS expression, and the inductions were dependent on the presence of oxygen. However, other oxidative stress agents, such as H2O2, gamma rays, and heat shock, failed to induce soxS expression.
Further experiments revealed a specific redox signal for soxS induction, and direct evidence was obtained for a role of SoxR protein in the activation of the soxS gene. The binding of SoxR protein to the soxS promoter was found to be similar to that of its homolog MerR, with a footprint spanning the -10 to -35 region of the promoter. These findings provide insight into the complex regulatory mechanisms that govern E. coli's response to redox stress.

title: Air pollution and cardiovascular disease: a statement for healthcare professionals from the Expert Panel on Population and Prevention Science of the American Heart Association.
text:
Air pollution is a diverse mixture of gases, liquids, and tiny particles that can have a harmful impact on cardiovascular health. Epidemiological studies have consistently shown that short-term and long-term exposure to current levels of particulate matter in the air increases the risk of cardiovascular events, such as heart attacks and strokes. Researchers have proposed several possible mechanisms for how air pollution can cause these problems, including:
* Increased coagulation and thrombosis (the formation of blood clots)
* A tendency to irregular heart rhythms (arrhythmias)
* Acute vasoconstriction (narrowing of blood vessels)
* Systemic inflammation (swelling and redness in the body)
* Acceleration of atherosclerosis (the buildup of plaque in the arteries)
The purpose of this statement is to provide healthcare professionals and regulatory agencies with a comprehensive review of the available research on air pollution and cardiovascular disease. Additionally, the implications of these findings for public health and regulatory policies are addressed, as well as practical recommendations for healthcare providers and their patients. Finally, suggestions for future research are provided to help answer remaining scientific questions.

title: Non-invasive ventilation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients: helmet versus facial mask
text: The new helmet interface has the potential to increase the success rate of non-invasive ventilation by improving tolerance. In this study, we compared the helmet with the conventional facial mask in delivering non-invasive ventilation to patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. We used a prospective, controlled, and randomized study design with a cross-over component. In 10 patients, we measured gas exchange, inspiratory effort, patient-ventilator synchrony, and patient tolerance after 30 minutes of non-invasive ventilation delivered via either the helmet or facial mask. Before each trial, the patients breathed unassisted for a period of time. Our findings show that both interfaces improved gas exchange and inspiratory effort after non-invasive ventilation (p<0.05). However, the helmet was less efficient than the mask in reducing inspiratory effort (p<0.05) and worsened patient-ventilator synchrony, as indicated by longer delays to trigger on and cycle off the mechanical assistance and more ineffective efforts (p<0.005). Patient comfort was similar with both interfaces. The helmet and facial mask were equally tolerated, and both improved gas exchange and decreased inspiratory effort. However, the helmet was less effective in reducing inspiratory effort and worst in patient-ventilator interaction.

title: Case Management and Client Access to Health and Social Services in Outpatient Substance Abuse Treatment
text: A key objective of case management is to integrate and coordinate services across various treatment settings, including substance abuse services, housing, mental health, medical, and social services. However, case management is a multi-faceted concept that encompasses several essential dimensions, such as the extent of coverage, management of the referral process, and the location of case management activities (on-site, off-site, or both). This study aims to investigate the relationship between specific dimensions of case management and the utilization of health and social services in outpatient substance abuse treatment. Our findings indicate that more comprehensive case management during the referral process and provision of case management services both on-site and off-site are most consistent with predictions of higher use of health and social services among substance abuse clients. However, these effects are specific to general healthcare and mental health services, and case management appears to have limited impact on use of social services or aftercare plans.

title: Evidence that the Ipl1-Sli15 (Aurora Kinase-INCENP) Complex Promotes Chromosome Bi-orientation by Altering Kinetochore-Spindle Pole Connections
text: The attachment of sister kinetochores to microtubules from opposite spindle poles during mitosis (bi-orientation) remains poorly understood. In yeast, the ortholog of the Aurora B-INCENP protein kinase complex (Ipl1-Sli15) may play a role in this process, as it is necessary to prevent sister kinetochores from attaching to microtubules from the same spindle pole. We investigated the function of IPL1 in cells that cannot replicate their chromosomes but still duplicate their spindle pole bodies (SPBs). Unexpectedly, kinetochores detach from old SPBs and reattach to old and new SPBs with equal frequency in IPL1-expressing cells, while remaining attached to old SPBs in ipl1 mutants. This observation suggests that Ipl1-Sli15 may facilitate bi-orientation by promoting the turnover of kinetochore-SPB connections until the invading sister kinetochores create tension in the surrounding chromatin.

title: CRITICAL REVIEW Cutaneous Vasculitis Update: Diagnostic Criteria,
text: Vasculitis, or inflammation of the vessel wall, can lead to tissue damage and various clinical manifestations, including hemorrhage, aneurysm formation, infarction, and stenosis. The skin, due to its extensive blood vessels and susceptibility to exposure to cold temperatures, is affected by a wide range of vasculitic syndromes, some of which can be localized and self-limited, while others can be severe and life-threatening with multi-organ involvement. To distinguish vasculitis from other conditions, a biopsy is often necessary, as the characteristic signs of fibrinoid necrosis, endarteritis obliterans, and acellular scar of healed arteritis can be identified. In addition, extravascular findings such as patterned fibrosis or collagenolytic granulomas may be present. While vasculitis can be classified based on its etiology, many cases lack a clear cause, and a single etiologic agent can trigger different clinicopathologic expressions of vasculitis. Therefore, a morphological approach to classification is favored, which involves determining vessel size and the principal inflammatory response. These histologic patterns correspond with pathogenic mechanisms that, when combined with direct immunofluorescent examination, anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) status, and findings from the work-up for systemic disease, can lead to a specific diagnosis and more effective treatment. In this review, we focus on the diagnostic criteria, classification, epidemiology, etiology, pathogenesis, and evaluation of cutaneous vasculitis, with the aim of providing a comprehensive understanding of this complex and multifaceted condition.

title: E2F-dependent histone acetylation and recruitment of the Tip60 acetyltransferase complex to chromatin in late G1.
text: E2F proteins can either activate or repress gene expression by binding to specific DNA sequences. Upon mitogenic stimulation, repressive E2F4-p130-histone deacetylase complexes dissociate, while activating E2F1, -2, and -3 species come together to bind target promoters. As they bind, histones H3 and H4 become hyperacetylated, but it is unclear whether this is a prerequisite or a result of E2F's presence. Our research shows that activating E2F species are essential for hyperacetylation of target chromatin in human cells. Overexpression of a dominant-negative (DN) E2F1 mutant in serum-stimulated T98G cells blocked all E2F binding, H4 acetylation, and, to some extent, H3 acetylation. Target gene activation and S-phase entry were also hindered by DN E2F1. Conversely, ectopic activation of E2F1 led to rapid H3 and H4 acetylation, demonstrating a direct role for E2F in these processes. Previous research had shown that E2F1 binds histone acetyltransferases (HATs) p300/CBP and PCAF/GCN5. Our findings also revealed that ectopically expressed E2F1 bound an unrelated HAT called Tip60 and induced the recruitment of five subunits of the Tip60 complex (Tip60, TRRAP, p400, Tip48, and Tip49) to target promoters in vivo. Additionally, we found that E2F-dependent recruitment of Tip60 to chromatin took place in late G(1) phase following serum stimulation. Interestingly, we propose that the activities of multiple HAT complexes contribute to E2F-dependent acetylation, transcription, and S-phase entry.

title: Chemical approaches to stem cell biology and therapeutics.
text: Small molecules can help stem cells work better and do things they couldn't do before, which is great for using stem cells to treat diseases. Scientists have figured out how to design and test small molecules to see if they can change how stem cells work. This has led to the development of new ways to treat diseases using stem cells and drugs that target stem cells. In this discussion, we will cover recent progress in stem cell research and the development of new therapies, as well as new ideas and challenges for using small molecules to improve stem cell function and regenerative medicine.

title: Genome-wide maps of chromatin state in pluripotent and lineage-committed cells
text: We leveraged single-molecule-based sequencing technology to perform high-throughput profiling of histone modifications in mammalian cells. By analyzing over four billion base pairs of sequenced DNA from chromatin immunoprecipitated samples, we generated genome-wide maps of histone modifications in mouse embryonic stem cells, neural progenitor cells, and embryonic fibroblasts. Our results demonstrate that lysine 4 and lysine 27 trimethylation can effectively distinguish genes that are actively expressed, poised for expression, or stably repressed, providing insight into cell state and lineage potential. In addition, we observed trimethylation of lysine 36 on coding and non-coding transcripts, facilitating gene annotation. Lysine 9 and lysine 20 trimethylation was detected at satellite, telomeric, and active long-terminal repeat regions, and can spread into nearby unique sequences. Furthermore, we found that lysine 4 and lysine 9 trimethylation mark imprinting control regions. Our study demonstrates the power of comprehensive chromatin profiling in characterizing diverse mammalian cell populations, particularly when utilizing allele-specific readout of chromatin state using single nucleotide polymorphisms.

title: Oncofetal long noncoding RNA PVT1 promotes proliferation and stem cell-like property of hepatocellular carcinoma cells by stabilizing NOP2.
text:
Background: Many protein-coding oncofetal genes are highly expressed in murine and human fetal liver but are silenced in adult liver. These genes have been used as clinical markers for the recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and as therapeutic targets for HCC. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), on the other hand, have been implicated in fetal and adult liver development, but their expression profiles in fetal and adult liver have not been well-characterized.
Aims: To investigate the expression profiles of lncRNAs in fetal and adult liver in mice and to identify potential diagnostic markers for HCC.
Methods: We profiled the expression of lncRNAs in fetal and adult liver tissues using RNA sequencing. We then validated the expression of identified lncRNAs in HCC tissues and examined their potential functions in HCC cells.
Results: We identified many lncRNAs that were specifically expressed in fetal liver tissues, including lncRNA-mPVT1, which was found to promote cell proliferation, cell cycling, and the expression of stem cell-like properties in murine cells. In contrast, human lncRNA-hPVT1 was up-regulated in HCC tissues, and patients with higher expression of this lncRNA had a poor clinical prognosis. We also identified NOP2 as an RNA-binding protein that binds to lncRNA-hPVT1 and stabilizes its protein levels, thereby promoting the protumorigenic effects of lncRNA-hPVT1 on HCC cells.
Discussion: Our study demonstrates that the expression of many lncRNAs is up-regulated in early liver development and that the fetal liver can be used to identify new diagnostic markers for HCC. Furthermore, we suggest that the lncRNA-hPVT1/NOP2 pathway may have potential as a therapeutic target for the treatment of HCC.
Conclusion: Our findings provide new insights into the role of lncRNAs in liver development and cancer and highlight the potential of the fetal liver as a resource for the identification of new diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for HCC.

title: Candida albicans, a distinctive fungal model for cellular aging study
text: Unicellular eukaryotic organisms, such as Candida albicans, serve as popular models for understanding aging in eukaryotes. In addition to the well-studied yeast species Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Schizosaccharomyces pombe, Candida albicans provides another unique unicellular aging model. Both types of Candida cells, yeast (blastospore) and hyphal (filamentous), display similar replicative lifespans. By leveraging morphological changes, we can obtain cells of different ages. Old Candida cells tend to accumulate glycogen and oxidatively damaged proteins, providing insight into aging mechanisms. Notably, deleting the SIR2 gene shortens lifespan, while inserting an extra copy of SIR2 prolongs lifespan, suggesting that Sir2 regulates cellular aging in Candida albicans, identical to its function in S. cerevisiae. However, Sir2 deletion does not lead to the accumulation of extra-chromosomal rDNA molecules, but rather influences the retention of oxidized proteins in mother cells, implying that extra-chromosomal rDNA molecules may not be directly linked to cellular aging in Candida albicans. This novel aging model, which enables large-scale isolation of old cells, may facilitate biochemical characterizations and genomics/proteomics studies of cellular aging and help verify aging pathways observed in other organisms, including S. cerevisiae.

title: ANKTM1, a TRP-like Channel Expressed in Nociceptive Neurons, Is Activated by Cold Temperatures
text: Mammals utilize specialized neurons within the peripheral nervous system to detect temperature. Four TRPV-class channels have been identified as being involved in temperature sensing, specifically heat detection. In contrast, one TRPM-class channel is responsible for detecting cold temperatures. The Tempaway range of temperatures that activate these channels covers a significant portion of the physiological temperature range experienced by most mammals, with a notable exception in the realm of noxious cold temperatures. Here, we present the characterization of ANKTM1, a cold-activated channel with a lower activation temperature compared to the cold and menthol receptor, TRPM8. ANKTM1 is a distant relative of TRP channels; however, it shares very little amino acid similarity to TRPM8. This protein is expressed in a subset of nociceptive sensory neurons where it coexists with TRPV1/VR1 (the capsaicin/heat receptor) but not TRPM8. Notably, we identified noxious cold-sensitive sensory neurons that also respond to capsaicin but do not react to menthol.

title: Plasma vitamin D metabolites and risk of colorectal cancer in women.
text:
Objective: The experimental evidence suggests that 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D and its precursor, 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], may play a preventive role in the development of colorectal cancer. We therefore investigated the potential association between plasma concentrations of these vitamin D metabolites and the risk of colorectal cancer among a nested case-control sample of women from the Nurses' Health Study.
Methods: We identified 193 colorectal cancer cases, aged 46-78 years, diagnosed up to 11 years after blood collection, and paired them with two controls per case based on year of birth and month of blood draw. We calculated the odds ratios (OR) for the risk of colorectal cancer using conditional logistic regression, adjusting for potential confounders such as body mass index, physical activity, smoking, family history, use of hormone replacement therapy, aspirin use, and dietary intakes.
Results: We found a statistically significant inverse linear association between plasma 25(OH)D levels and the risk of colorectal cancer (P = 0.02), with women in the highest quintile exhibiting a half of the risk compared to those in the lowest quintile (OR, 0.53; 95% confidence interval, 0.27-1.04). This inverse association remained significant after limiting the analysis to women aged > or =60 years at blood collection (P = 0.006), but not among the younger women (P = 0.70). Moreover, the benefit of higher 25(OH)D concentrations was observed specifically for cancers at the distal colon and rectum (P = 0.02), although no association was found for cancers at the proximal colon (P = 0.81). In contrast, no significant association was observed between 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D and colorectal cancer risk, although risk was elevated among women in the highest quintile who were also in the lower half of the 25(OH)D distribution (OR, 2.52; 95% confidence interval, 1.04-6.11).
Conclusion: Our findings support the hypothesis that higher plasma levels of 25(OH)D are associated with a lower risk of colorectal cancer in older women, particularly for cancers at the distal colon and rectum. These results provide further evidence for the potential preventive role of vitamin D in colorectal cancer, suggesting that supplementation with 25(OH)D may be a promising strategy for colorectal cancer prevention in older women.

title: DNA Deamination Mediates Innate Immunity to Retroviral Infection
text: CEM15/APOBEC3G is a crucial cellular protein that enables resistance to infection by Vif-deficient human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Using an MLV-based system, we have discovered that CEM15/APOBEC3G functions as a DNA deaminase within virions during viral production, leading to widespread deamination of deoxycytidine to deoxyuridine within the retroviral minus (first)-strand cDNA. This deamination likely triggers viral destruction. Furthermore, HIV Vif can protect MLV from this CEM15/APOBEC3G-dependent restriction. Our findings suggest that targeted DNA deamination is a fundamental immune mechanism against retroviruses, and it likely contributes to the evolutionary changes observed in many viruses (including HIV).

title: Global, regional, and national disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) for 315 diseases and injuries and healthy life expectancy (HALE), 1990–2015: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2015
text:
Healthy life expectancy (HALE) and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) provide comprehensive measures of health across regions and time, allowing for evaluations of epidemiological patterns and health system performance. In a recent study, researchers aimed to update HALE and DALYs for geographies worldwide and assess how disease burden varies with development.
The study used data from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2015 (GBD 2015) to derive HALE and DALYs by sex for 195 countries and territories from 1990 to 2015. The study found that total global DALYs remained largely unchanged from 1990 to 2015, with declines in communicable, neonatal, maternal, and nutritional (Group 1) disease DALYs offset by increases in DALYs due to non-communicable diseases (NCDs). The study also found that much of this epidemiological transition was driven by changes in population growth and ageing, but it was accelerated by widespread improvements in socio-demographic index (SDI), a composite indicator constructed from measures of income per capita, average years of schooling, and total fertility rate.
The study found that total burden climbed for the majority of NCDs, while age-standardised DALY rates due to NCDs declined. However, age-standardised DALY rates due to several high-burden NCDs (including osteoarthritis, drug use disorders, depression, diabetes, congenital birth defects, and skin, oral, and sense organ diseases) either increased or remained unchanged, leading to increases in their relative ranking in many geographies. The study also found that from 2005 to 2015, HALE at birth increased by an average of 2·9 years (95% uncertainty interval 2·9-3·0) for men and 3·5 years (3·4-3·7) for women, while HALE at age 65 years improved by 0·85 years (0·78-0·92) and 1·2 years (1·1-1·3), respectively.
The study's findings suggest that while health is improving globally, this means more populations are spending more time with functional health loss, an absolute expansion of morbidity. The proportion of life spent in ill health decreases somewhat with increasing SDI, a relative compression of morbidity, which supports continued efforts to elevate personal income, improve education, and limit fertility. The study's analysis of DALYs and HALE and their relationship to SDI represents a robust framework on which to benchmark geography-specific health performance and SDG progress. The findings also highlight the importance of country-specific drivers of disease burden, particularly for causes with higher-than-expected DALYs, in informing financial and research investments, prevention efforts, health policies, and health system improvement initiatives for all countries along the development continuum.
The study was funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

title: Adverse drug events: database construction and in silico prediction.
text: Adverse drug events (ADEs) are harmful outcomes resulting from normal dosages of approved medications. These events are critical for drugs to remain on the market, yet many go unidentified until after approval, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. ADEs have affected millions of people worldwide. Preventing or reducing these events is a crucial aspect of drug discovery and development. To address this issue, we have developed a comprehensive database of ADEs, called MetaADEDB, which includes over 520,000 drug-ADE associations among 3059 unique compounds (1330 drugs) and 13,200 ADE items. The database is integrated through data mining and annotation with Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) concepts. Additionally, we have created a computational model, the phenotypic network inference model (PNIM), which can predict potential ADEs based on the database. PNIM demonstrated high accuracy in predicting ADEs through 10-fold cross-validation, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9. The prediction capability was also tested on an external validation set obtained from the US-FDA Adverse Events Reporting System, resulting in an AUC value of 0.912.
