Conversely, H2A.Z deposition is dispensable for nucleosome positioning. By regulating H2A.Z deposition using a steroid-inducible protein splicing strategy, we demonstrate that NFR establishment is necessary for H2A.Z deposition. These findings suggest an ordered pathway for the formation of promoter chromatin structure.

title: HIV seropositivity and tuberculosis in a large general hospital in Malawi.
text: The prevalence of Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS) in Malawi is significantly higher in Central Africa. Given that Tuberculosis (TB) is an initial manifestation of the disease, patients admitted to the TB wards of Zomba General Hospital were requested to provide permission for an HIV-antibodies test. Two additional studies were conducted: all medical in-patients suspected of immune deficiency from September 1986 and all blood donors from April 1988 were also tested for HIV seropositivity. Of the TB patients who volunteered, 26% were found to be seropositive. This percentage increased to 32% in the high-risk age group of 20-40 years. Similarly, the seropositivity among medical in-patients suspected of immune deficiency rose markedly from April 1987 to October 1988. Lastly, among the blood donors tested, 20% were found to be seropositive.

title: Determinants of neonatal mortality in Indonesia
text:
Background:
Neonatal mortality accounts for approximately 40% of under-five child mortality globally. Understanding the factors associated with neonatal mortality is essential to inform evidence-based interventions to prevent deaths. This study aimed to identify the determinants of neonatal mortality in Indonesia using a nationally representative sample of births from 1997 to 2002.
Methods:
The analysis was based on the 2002-2003 Indonesia Demographic and Health Survey, which provided survival information on 15,952 singleton live-born infants born between 1997 and 2002. Multilevel logistic regression using a hierarchical approach was employed to identify the community, socio-economic status, and proximate determinants associated with neonatal deaths.
Results:
The findings revealed significant differences in neonatal mortality rates across communities in Indonesia. Compared to the lowest mortality regions, infants born in East Java had significantly higher odds of neonatal death (OR = 5.01, p < 0.001), while infants born in North, Central, and Southeast Sulawesi and Gorontalo had higher odds (OR = 3.17, p = 0.03). As the percentage of deliveries assisted by trained attendants in the cluster increased, there was a progressive reduction in the odds of neonatal death. Additionally, the odds of neonatal death were higher for infants born to mothers and fathers who were employed (OR = 1.84, p < 0.001 and OR = 2.99, p = 0.02, respectively) and for infants born to unemployed fathers (OR = 2.99, p = 0.02). Other factors associated with higher odds of neonatal death included being a male infant (OR = 1.49, p = 0.01), having a short birth interval (OR = 2.82, p < 0.001), and being smaller than average-sized (OR = 2.80, p < 0.001). Infants receiving any postnatal care were significantly protected from neonatal death (OR = 0.63, p = 0.03).

title: High density mapping of the MHC identifies a shared role for HLA-DRB1*01:03 in inflammatory bowel diseases and heterozygous advantage in ulcerative colitis
text: Genome-wide studies of related chronic inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, have implicated strong associations with the major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Specifically, this region houses numerous immunological candidates, including classic HLA molecules. While earlier studies in IBD have identified associations at both HLA and non-HLA genes, they lacked the statistical power to fully comprehend the underlying genetic architecture and causative alleles. To overcome this limitation, we performed high-density single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) typing of the MHC in >32,000 IBD individuals, revealing multiple HLA alleles with a primary role for HLA-DRB1*01:03 in both Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. Noteworthy differences were observed between these diseases, including a predominant role for class II HLA variants and a hint towards an adaptive immune response-mediated pathogenesis in the colonic environment, as observed in ulcerative colitis.

title: High-Threshold Mechanosensitive Ion Channels Blocked by a Novel Conopeptide Mediate Pressure-Evoked Pain
text: Little is known about the molecular basis of somatosensory mechanotransduction in mammals, and so we screened a library of peptide toxins for effects on mechanically activated currents in cultured dorsal root ganglion neurons. One conopeptide analogue, termed NMB-1 for noxious mechanosensation blocker 1, selectively inhibits (IC50 1 µM) sustained mechanically activated currents in a subset of sensory neurons. Biotinylated NMB-1 retains activity and binds selectively to peripherin-positive nociceptive sensory neurons. The selectivity of NMB-1 was confirmed by the fact that it has no inhibitory effects on voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels, or ligand-gated channels such as acid-sensing ion channels or TRPA1 channels. In contrast, the tarantula toxin, GsMTx-4, which inhibits stretch-activated ion channels, had no effects on mechanically activated currents in sensory neurons. In behavioral assays, NMB-1 inhibits responses only to high intensity, painful mechanical stimulation and has no effects on low intensity mechanical stimulation or thermosensation. Unexpectedly, NMB-1 was found to also be an inhibitor of rapid FM1-43 loading (a measure of mechanotransduction) in cochlear hair cells. These data demonstrate that pharmacologically distinct channels respond to distinct types of mechanical stimuli and suggest that mechanically activated sustained currents underlie noxious mechanosensation. NMB-1 thus provides a novel diagnostic tool for the molecular definition of channels involved in hearing and pressure-evoked pain.

title: Hyperactive Neuroendocrine Secretion Causes Size, Feeding, and Metabolic Defects of C. elegans Bardet-Biedl Syndrome Mutants
text: Bardet-Biedl Syndrome (BBS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects multiple organs and systems, including the eyes, digestive system, and nervous system. Key symptoms include polydactyly (extra fingers or toes), retinopathy, hyperphagia (excessive hunger), obesity, short stature, cognitive impairment, and developmental delays. Research has shown that disruptions in BBS proteins in various organisms can lead to impaired cilia formation and function, which in turn can cause the multi-organ defects characteristic of BBS. In the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans, BBS genes are expressed specifically in the sixty ciliated sensory neurons of these animals, and bbs mutants exhibit sensory defects as well as abnormalities in body size, feeding, and metabolism. Surprisingly, we have found that in contrast to other cilia-defective mutants, C. elegans bbs mutants actually exhibit increased release of dense-core vesicles and organism-wide phenotypes associated with enhanced activities of insulin, neuropeptide, and biogenic amine signaling pathways. Our findings suggest that the altered body size, feeding, and metabolic abnormalities of bbs mutants may be caused by excessive secretion of dense-core vesicles, rather than solely by ciliary dysfunction. These results expand the role of BBS proteins to the regulation of dense-core-vesicle exocytosis and imply that some features of Bardet-Biedl Syndrome may be associated with an overactive neuroendocrine secretion.

title: Fiji: an open-source platform for biological-image analysis
text: Fiji is an open-source software distribution built on ImageJ, a popular platform for biological image analysis. By leveraging modern software engineering practices, Fiji combines cutting-edge libraries and multiple scripting languages to enable seamless prototyping of image processing algorithms. With Fiji, developers can quickly transform innovative algorithms into ImageJ plugins that can be easily shared with users through an integrated update system. We envision Fiji as a platform for fostering collaborative partnerships between computer science and biology researchers.

title: Pharmacologic characterization of a potent inhibitor of class I phosphatidylinositide 3-kinases.
text:
Ample evidence suggests that activation of the lipid phosphatidylinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway plays a central role in the development and progression of various types of cancer in humans. As a result, PI3K inhibitors hold significant promise as molecular cancer therapeutics. In this study, we examine the pharmacological properties of a prototype compound from a new series of class I PI3K inhibitors, known as PI103.
PI103 is a potent and selective inhibitor, demonstrating low IC50 values against recombinant PI3K isoforms p110α (2 nmol/L), p110β (3 nmol/L), p110δ (3 nmol/L), and p110γ (15 nmol/L). In addition, it inhibits TORC1 by 83.9% at 0.5 micromol/L and shows an IC50 of 14 nmol/L against DNA-PK. Importantly, PI103 demonstrates a high degree of selectivity within the PI3K family, with no activity against a panel of 70 other protein kinases.
PI103 exhibits potent antiproliferative and anti-invasive activity against a wide range of human cancer cell lines in vitro, and shows evidence of biomarker modulation consistent with inhibition of PI3K signaling. Notably, PI103 is rapidly metabolized in vivo, but displays rapid distribution to tumors and leads to tumor growth delay in xenograft models with various PI3K pathway abnormalities. Decreased phosphorylation of AKT is observed in U87MG gliomas, consistent with drug levels achieved. Additionally, we demonstrate inhibition of invasion in orthotopic breast and ovarian cancer xenograft models, and observe anti-angiogenic effects. Despite its rapid in vivo metabolism, PI103 is a valuable tool compound for exploring the biological function of class I PI3K and represents an important lead for further optimization of this novel class of targeted molecular cancer therapeutics.

title: Optimized CRISPR/Cas tools for efficient germline and somatic genome engineering in Drosophila.
text: The recently developed type II CRISPR/Cas system has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating genomes across various organisms. In this study, we present a versatile toolbox for high-efficiency genome engineering of Drosophila melanogaster, consisting of transgenic Cas9 lines and customizable guide RNA (gRNA) expression plasmids. By systematically evaluating these CRISPR/Cas components, we uncovered Cas9 lines with either ubiquitous or germline-restricted activity patterns. Additionally, we discovered that the U6:3 promoter offers the most potent activity among different gRNA expression sources. Using the appropriate combination of Cas9 and gRNA, we were able to target both essential and nonessential genes with transmission rates ranging from 25% to 100%. Furthermore, our optimized CRISPR/Cas tools can be used for offset nicking-based mutagenesis, as well as for precise genome editing through homology-directed repair with rates that render selection markers unnecessary. We also demonstrate a novel application of CRISPR/Cas-mediated technology in revealing loss-of-function phenotypes in somatic cells by efficiently targeting them with Cas9 expressed ubiquitously or in a tissue-restricted manner. Our CRISPR/Cas tools will greatly facilitate the fast evaluation of mutant phenotypes of specific genes and the precise modification of the genome with single-nucleotide precision. Our findings also pave the way for high-throughput genetic screening with CRISPR/Cas.

title: Cost-effectiveness of 10-Year Risk Thresholds for Initiation of Statin Therapy for Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease.
text:
In a new study, researchers used a microsimulation model to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of different 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk thresholds for statin use in adults without a history of ASCVD. The study, published in the American Heart Journal, found that the current 10-year risk threshold of 7.5% or higher used in the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) cholesterol treatment guidelines has an acceptable cost-effectiveness profile, but more lenient thresholds would be optimal.
The researchers analyzed data from a representative US population aged 40 to 75 years and used hypothetical individuals to estimate the number of ASCVD events prevented and the incremental costs per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained by different thresholds. They found that shifting from a 7.5% or higher risk threshold to a 3.0% or higher threshold would avert an additional 161,560 cardiovascular disease events and be more cost-effective. The study also showed that the optimal ASCVD threshold was sensitive to changes in patient preferences, statin price, and the risk of statin-induced diabetes.
According to the researchers, the findings of this study have important implications for the ACC/AHA cholesterol treatment guidelines and suggest that a more lenient risk threshold could be adopted in the future. This would result in more people benefiting from statin therapy and a greater reduction in ASCVD events. However, the study also highlighted the need for further research to understand how patient preferences and other factors affect the optimal risk threshold.
Overall, the study provides valuable insights into the cost-effectiveness of different ASCVD risk thresholds for statin use and underscores the importance of considering various factors when making treatment decisions. The findings of this study could help improve cholesterol treatment guidelines and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

title: Biochemical Properties of Highly Neuroinvasive Prion Strains
text: Prions transmit from peripheral entry points into the central nervous system (CNS), leading to progressive neurodegeneration and ultimately death. However, the underlying mechanisms of prion disease can vary greatly depending on the specific strain, or conformational variant, of the misfolded and aggregated protein PrP(Sc). While most prion strains enter the CNS, some strains fail to do so and do not cause any observable symptoms of disease. The reason for this variation in pathogenesis remains unclear. Using mouse-adapted prion strains, we discovered that highly neuroinvasive strains mainly form disperse aggregates in the brain and are non-fibrillar, conformationally unstable, and lead to rapidly lethal disease. These strains efficiently produce PrP(Sc) over short incubation periods. In contrast, weakly neuroinvasive prion strains form large fibrillary plaques and are stable, congophilic, and inefficiently produce PrP(Sc) over long incubation periods. Overall, our findings indicate that the most neuroinvasive prion strains are also the least stable, supporting the idea that the efficient replication and unstable nature of the most rapidly converting prions may be linked to their ability to efficiently invade the CNS.

title: The twin-arginine translocation (Tat) protein export pathway
text: The twin-arginine translocation (Tat) protein transport system is widespread in cytoplasmic membranes of both bacteria and archaea, with a unique capability to transport fully formed proteins across the membrane. To achieve this, the system must create a transmembrane pathway that can accommodate varying-sized structured molecules while maintaining the membrane's ionic impermeability. In the Gram-negative bacterium Escherichia coli, this challenging task is accomplished using just three small membrane proteins: TatA, TatB, and TatC. This Review summarizes recent advances in our comprehension of how this remarkable machine functions.

title: New developments in the ATSAS program package for small-angle scattering data analysis
text:
The latest development in the program package ATSAS (version 2.4) for the processing and analysis of isotropic small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering data has been revealed. These new features include:
(i) Multipath data manipulation and display tools for various platforms
(ii) Automated data processing and calculation of key parameters
(iii) Enhanced usage of high- and low-resolution models from other structural methods
(iv) Innovative algorithms for constructing three-dimensional models from weakly interacting oligomeric systems and complexes
(v) Improved tools for analyzing data from mixtures and flexible systems
The latest ATSAS release includes installers for major platforms such as Windows, Linux, and Mac OSX, along with enhanced user documentation. Additionally, web-related developments, including a user discussion forum and expanded online access to run ATSAS programs, are also presented.

title: The First Myriapod Genome Sequence Reveals Conservative Arthropod Gene Content and Genome Organisation in the Centipede Strigamia maritima
text:
Myriapods, such as centipedes and millipedes, exhibit a simplistic homogeneous body plan in comparison to other arthropods, despite being terrestrial. This peculiarity is remarkable, considering they achieved terrestrialism independently of insects. Notably, Myriapoda is the only arthropod class without a sequenced genome, underscoring the potential of this organism for shedding light on the ancestral arthropod genome. To investigate this, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the Strigamia maritima genome, revealing a compact genome with less gene loss and shuffling than seen in other arthropods. Our study uncovered numerous genes in conserved macro-synteny contexts, as well as minute examples of gene clustering. Intriguingly, S. maritima displays alternative solutions to similar problems encountered by insects, such as the absence of the olfactory receptor gene family and an expansion of other receptor gene families for olfaction in air. Additionally, this organism has evolved paralogues to generate coding sequence diversity, where insects use alternate splicing, with a notable example being the Dscam gene, which in Drosophila generates over 100,000 alternate splice forms but in S. maritima is encoded by over 100 paralogues.
Notably, our findings suggest an intriguing linkage between the absence of known photosensory proteins in a blind organism and the additional absence of canonical circadian clock genes. The phylogenetic position of myriapods allows us to elucidate where molecular mechanisms and traits emerged in arthropod evolution. For instance, we infer that juvenile hormone signaling evolved concurrently with the emergence of the exoskeleton in arthropods, and that RR-1 containing cuticle proteins evolved in the lineage leading to Mandibulata. Moreover, our study identifies specific times when gene expansions and losses occurred, offering a unique opportunity to explore the ancestral arthropod genome and gain insights into the evolution of specific life histories.

title: Genetic and Functional Diversification of Small RNA Pathways in Plants
text:
Multicellular eukaryotes produce small RNA molecules (approximately 21-24 nucleotides) of two main types: microRNA (miRNA) and short interfering RNA (siRNA). These small RNAs function as sequence-specific guides to regulate genes, transposons, and viruses, as well as modify chromatin and genome structure. To form or function, small RNAs require factors from gene families that encode DICER (or DICER-LIKE [DCL]) and ARGONAUTE proteins, and in some cases, RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RDR) proteins. Unlike most animals, plants have multiple DCL and RDR proteins.
Using Arabidopsis thaliana insertion mutants, unique functions for three DCL proteins in miRNA (DCL1), endogenous siRNA (DCL3), and viral siRNA (DCL2) biogenesis were identified. One RDR protein (RDR2) was essential for all endogenous siRNAs examined. The loss of endogenous siRNAs in dcl3 and rdr2 mutants was associated with a loss of heterochromatic marks and increased transcript accumulation at some loci. In dcl2 mutant plants, defects in siRNA-generation activity in response to turnip crinkle virus were linked to increased virus susceptibility.
Our findings suggest that the proliferation and diversification of DCL and RDR genes during plant evolution enabled specialized small RNA-directed pathways for development, chromatin structure, and defense.

title: Immunosuppressant FTY720 inhibits thymocyte emigration.
text: The thymus plays a crucial role in providing mature T cells to the peripheral immune system, but the mechanisms underlying cellular export from the thymus are not fully understood. In this study, we investigated the ability of a novel immunosuppressive agent, FTY720, to inhibit T cell export from the thymus. We found that daily administration of FTY720 at a dose of 1 mg/kg resulted in a significant decrease in the number of peripheral T lymphocytes. In contrast, long-term daily administration of FTY720 in the thymus led to a three to fourfold increase in the proportion of mature medullary thymocytes (CD4+CD8- and CD4-CD8+) and a slight decrease in the double-positive cell (CD4+CD8+) ratio. Phenotypic analysis revealed that these increased subsets represent possible recent thymic emigrants, and high levels of L-selectin expression on these subsets suggest that they were prevented from leaving the thymus. Using intrathymic labeling with fluorescein isothiocyanate, we found that only one-fourth of labeled cells could be detected in the lymph nodes and spleen of FTY720-treated mice compared to control mice. These results suggest that the immunosuppressive action of FTY720, at least in part, may be due to its inhibitory effect on T cell emigration from the thymus to the periphery.

title: Validating a conceptual model for an inter-professional approach to shared decision making: a mixed methods study
text:
BACKGROUND In recent years, there has been growing interest in incorporating inter-professional (IP) shared decision making (SDM) in primary care. To address this, we developed a conceptual model for IP SDM in primary care and evaluated its validity with stakeholders in Canada.
METHODS We conducted 15 individual interviews and 7 group interviews with 79 stakeholders, including healthcare professionals, patients, and family members. During these interviews, we asked stakeholders to:
1. Propose changes to the IP-SDM model.
2. Identify barriers and facilitators to implementing the model in clinical practice.
3. Assess the model's validity using a theory appraisal questionnaire.
RESULTS Stakeholders emphasized the importance of placing the patient at the center of the model and expanding the concept of family to include significant others. They also highlighted the need for clarity around outcomes, the importance of considering the dynamic nature of the model, and the need for resources and training to support successful implementation.
ztakers identified several barriers to implementing the model, including time constraints, insufficient resources, and an imbalance of power among health professionals. However, they also identified several facilitators, including education and training in inter-professionalism and SDM, motivation to achieve an IP approach to SDM, and mutual knowledge and understanding of disciplinary roles.
CONCLUSIONS Stakeholders validate the new IP-SDM model for primary care settings and proposed few modifications. Future research should assess the model's effectiveness in implementing SDM in IP clinical practice.

Please note that I have made some minor changes to the original text to improve readability, such as adding transitions and clarifying some of the sentences. However, I have tried to maintain the same meaning and tone as the original text.

title: Glutaminolysis activates Rag-mTORC1 signaling.
text: Amino acids, specifically glutamine, play a crucial role in regulating cell growth by activating the highly conserved kinase TORC1. However, the specific mechanism by which glutamine influences TORC1 activity has been poorly understood. Our findings reveal that glutamine, when combined with leucine, activates mammalian TORC1 (mTORC1) by enhancing glutaminolysis and the production of α-ketoglutarate. This process is essential for the activation of mTORC1, as inhibition of glutaminolysis prevents GTP loading of RagB and lysosomal translocation, resulting in the suppression of mTORC1 activity. Contrary to previous findings, we found that constitutively active Rag heterodimers can also activate mTORC1 independently of glutaminolysis. Interestingly, enhanced glutaminolysis or exposure to a cell-permeable α-ketoglutarate analog can stimulate lysosomal translocation and activation of mTORC1. Finally, our results demonstrate that glutaminolysis regulates both cell growth and autophagy, two processes that are controlled by mTORC1. Taken together, these findings suggest that mTORC1 senses and is activated by glutamine and leucine via glutaminolysis and α-ketoglutarate production upstream of Rag, which may provide an explanation for the addiction of cancer cells to glutamine.

title: microRNA-31/factor-inhibiting hypoxia-inducible factor 1 nexus regulates keratinocyte differentiation.
text:
Notch plays a crucial role in the transition from cell proliferation to differentiation in the epidermis and corneal epithelium. Furthermore, dysregulation of Notch signaling is associated with various skin disorders, including psoriasis, eczema, non-melanoma skin cancer, and melanoma, where differentiation and proliferation are impaired. While much is known about the downstream effects of Notch signaling, the factors that regulate Notch receptor signaling after ligand activation are not fully understood. Notch can undergo hydroxylation by factor-inhibiting hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (FIH-1), but the biological significance of this process is unclear.
Our study reveals that FIH-1 expression is increased in diseased epidermis and corneal epithelium. Elevating FIH-1 levels in primary human epidermal keratinocytes (HEKs) and human corneal epithelial keratinocytes (HCEKs) impairs differentiation in submerged cultures and in a three-dimensional organotypic raft model of human epidermis, partially through a decrease in Notch signaling. Conversely, knockdown of FIH-1 enhances keratinocyte differentiation. In vivo, loss of FIH-1 leads to increased Notch activity in the limbal epithelium, resulting in a more differentiated phenotype. MicroRNA-31 (miR-31) is an endogenous negative regulator of FIH-1 expression that mediates keratinocyte differentiation through Notch activation. Interestingly, ectopic expression of miR-31 in an undifferentiated corneal epithelial cell line promotes differentiation and recapitulates a corneal epithelium in a three-dimensional raft culture model.
Our results uncover a novel mechanism for keratinocyte fate decisions, where Notch signaling potential is, in part, controlled through the miR-31/FIH-1 axis. This study provides new insights into the regulation of Notch signaling and its implications for skin development and disease.

title: Advantages of larval control for African malaria vectors: Low mobility and behavioural responsiveness of immature mosquito stages allow high effective coverage
text: According to a sensitivity analysis of the MacDonald-Ross model, it has been suggested that targeting adult female mosquitoes with insecticides is the most effective way to reduce malaria transmission. However, these analyses have overlooked a crucial biological difference between mosquito adults and their immature stages: adult mosquitoes are highly mobile and can easily avoid control measures, while mosquito eggs, larvae, and pupae are confined to small aquatic habitats and cannot escape intervention. We propose that the inability to control adult mosquitoes is due to their mobility, allowing them to evade interventions such as excito-repellent insecticides. We develop a simple model that demonstrates how mosquitoes can avoid interventions and reduce the effectiveness of control measures. Historical evidence suggests that larval control of African malaria vectors can be effective, and we conclude that the only limitations to its effectiveness are practical rather than fundamental. We argue that larval control strategies against malaria vectors in sub-Saharan Africa have the potential to be highly effective when combined with adult control interventions, and should be prioritized for further development, evaluation, and implementation as an integral part of the Rolling Back Malaria initiative.

title: The Arabidopsis Chromatin-Modifying Nuclear siRNA Pathway Involves a Nucleolar RNA Processing Center
text: In Arabidopsis thaliana, small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) direct cytosine methylation at endogenous DNA repeats through a pathway involving two forms of nuclear RNA polymerase IV (Pol IVa and Pol IVb), RNA-DEPENDENT RNA POLYMERASE 2 (RDR2), DICER-LIKE 3 (DCL3), ARGONAUTE4 (AGO4), the chromatin remodeler DRD1, and the de novo cytosine methyltransferase DRM2. We demonstrate that RDR2, DCL3, AGO4, and NRPD1b (the largest subunit of Pol IVb) colocalize with siRNAs within the nucleolus, while Pol IVa and DRD1 are located external to the nucleolus and colocalize with endogenous repeat loci. Mutation-induced loss of pathway proteins leads to mislocalization of downstream proteins, revealing their order of action. Our findings suggest that Pol IVa acts first, and its localization is RNA-dependent, indicating an RNA template. We propose that the maintenance of heterochromatin involves locus-specific Pol IVa transcription followed by siRNA production and assembly of AGO4- and NRPD1b-containing silencing complexes within nucleolar processing centers.

title: Peripheral arterial disease in the elderly: The Rotterdam Study.
text: To investigate the age- and sex-specific prevalence of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and intermittent claudication (IC) in an elderly population, we conducted a population-based study among 7715 individuals aged 55 and older (40% men, 60% women). We determined the presence of PAD and IC by measuring the ankle-arm systolic blood pressure index (AAI) and using the World Health Organization/Rose questionnaire, respectively. PAD was defined as an AAI of <0.90 in either leg. The prevalence of PAD was 19.1% (95% confidence interval: 18.1%-20.0%): 16.9% in men and 20.5% in women. Approximately 1.6% (95% confidence interval: 1.3%-1.9%) of the study population reported symptoms of IC (2.2% in men, 1.2% in women). Among those with PAD, 6.3% reported symptoms of IC (8.7% in men, 4.9% in women), while in 68.9% of those with IC, an AAI below 0.90 was found. Individuals with an AAI <0.90 were more likely to be smokers, have hypertension, and have symptomatic or asymptomatic cardiovascular disease compared to those with an AAI of 0.90 or higher. The authors concluded that the prevalence of PAD in the elderly is high, while the prevalence of IC is relatively low, although both prevalences increase with advancing age. The vast majority of PAD patients do not experience symptoms of IC.

title: Antioxidants attenuate the plasma cytokine response to exercise in humans.
text: Exercise leads to a significant increase in plasma levels of TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, and IL-6, despite the unknown sources and stimuli of these cytokines. In order to investigate the role of oxidative stress and the potential contribution of monocytes in this cytokine response, we tested previously untrained individuals. Six healthy non-athletes underwent two 45-min cycling exercises at 70% of their maximum oxygen uptake (Vo(2 max)) before and after 60 days of antioxidant supplementation (vitamins E, A, and C), as well as 15 days of allopurinol and 3 days of N-acetylcysteine. Blood samples were collected at baseline, end-exercise, and 30 and 120 minutes post-exercise. Plasma cytokine levels were measured using ELISA, while monocyte intracellular cytokine levels were determined using flow cytometry. Before antioxidant supplementation, exercise significantly increased TNF-alpha levels by 60%, IL-1beta levels by threefold, and IL-6 levels by sixfold (P < 0.05). Following antioxidant supplementation, plasma IL-1beta levels became undetectable, the TNF-alpha response to exercise was abolished, and the IL-6 response was significantly blunted (P < 0.05). Exercise did not increase the percentage of monocytes producing these cytokines or their intensity. Our findings suggest that in untrained humans, oxidative stress is a major stimulus for exercise-induced cytokine production, and that monocytes play no role in this process.

title: Relation between colonic proglucagon expression and metabolic response to oligofructose in high fat diet-fed mice.
text: According to several studies, fermentable dietary fiber may play a role in controlling obesity and associated metabolic disorders. The present study aimed to investigate the potential role of short chain fructo-oligosaccharide (OFS), a non-digestible oligosaccharide, in mice fed a standard diet and in mice fed two different high-fat diets that induce metabolic disorders associated with obesity. We found several effects in mice that were consistent with previous studies in rats fed a standard diet enriched with OFS, including an increase in total and empty caecum weight, a significant decrease in epididymal fat mass, and an increase in colonic and portal plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels. However, interestingly, four-week treatment with OFS had different effects when added to the two different high-fat diets. OFS decreased energy intake, body weight gain, glycemia, and epididymal fat mass only when added to the high-fat-carbohydrate-free diet, where OFS promoted colonic proglucagon expression and insulin secretion. Our results suggest an association between the increase in proglucagon expression in the proximal colon and the effects of OFS on glycemia, fat mass development, and/or body weight gain. In conclusion, dietary oligosaccharides may constitute an interesting class of dietary fibers that promote endogenous GLP-1 production, with beneficial physiological consequences, although further studies are needed to confirm these findings in humans.

title: Aurora B phosphorylates spatially distinct targets to differentially regulate the kinetochore-microtubule interface.
text: Accurate chromosome segregation relies on meticulously regulated interactions between kinetochores and microtubules, yet the means by which plasticity is achieved to remedy diverse attachment flaws remains elusive. In this study, we demonstrate that Aurora B kinase phosphorylates three distinct targets within the conserved outer kinetochore KNL1/Mis12 complex/Ndc80 complex (KMN) network, the central player in kinetochore-microtubule attachments. The combinatorial phosphorylation of the KMN network generates graduated levels of microtubule binding activity, with complete phosphorylation significantly impairing microtubule binding. By altering the phosphorylation state of each protein, we find that chromosome segregation defects occur correspondingly. Notably, the spatial distribution of these targets along the kinetochore axis leads to their differential phosphorylation in response to changes in tension and attachment state. Our results suggest a mechanism whereby tension-dependent fine-tuning of kinetochore-microtubule interactions can occur, rather than generating exclusively binary changes in microtubule binding.

title: Prognostic importance of 6-mercaptopurine dose intensity in acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
text: The text describes the outcome of childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) patients treated with 6-mercaptopurine (6MP) and methotrexate. The study found that higher dose intensity of oral 6MP was associated with improved event-free survival (EFS), with a significant predictive value in multivariate analysis. Additionally, the occurrence of neutropenia was found to be detrimental to outcome. The analysis included 182 children who achieved remission and received weekly methotrexate 40 mg/m2 parenterally and daily oral 6MP, interrupted every 6 weeks during the first year by pulse chemotherapy. A total of 709 thioguanine nucleotides (TGNs), 418 methotrexate polyglutamates (MTXPGs), and 267 thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT) measurements, along with complete dose intensity information for 19,046 weeks of 6MP and methotrexate, were analyzed. The findings suggest that increased dose intensity of oral 6MP is an important determinant of EFS in ALL, particularly among children with a homozygous wild-type TPMT phenotype. However, achieving higher dose intensity at the expense of neutropenia may be counterproductive.

title: Orai1 and STIM1 are critical for breast tumor cell migration and metastasis.
text: Tumor metastasis is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths, and deciphering the molecular mechanisms underlying this process offers promising opportunities for developing novel cancer therapies. We investigated the role of Orai1 and STIM1, two proteins involved in store-operated calcium entry, in breast tumor cell migration and metastasis. Our findings reveal that these proteins are essential for breast tumor cell migration in vitro and tumor metastasis in mouse models. By suppressing Orai1 or STIM1 in highly metastatic human breast cancer cells or treating them with a pharmacological inhibitor of store-operated calcium channels, we observed a decrease in tumor metastasis in animal models. Our results demonstrate a critical role for Orai1 and STIM1 in tumor metastasis and suggest that targeting store-operated calcium entry channels may provide a new avenue for cancer therapy.

title: Mouse Spermatogenic Stem Cells Continually Interconvert between Equipotent Singly Isolated and Syncytial States
text:
The identity and behavior of mouse spermatogenic stem cells have long been a topic of interest. In the prevailing understanding, stem cell function is believed to be restricted to isolated (As) spermatogonia. However, our study challenges this notion by examining the dynamics of GFRα1+ stem cells in vivo and evaluating an alternative hypothesis that fragmented syncytial spermatogonia also contribute to stem cell function in homeostasis.
Using live imaging and pulse labeling, we quantitatively determined the fates of individual GFRα1+ cells and found that during steady-state spermatogenesis, the entire GFRα1+ population consists of a single stem cell pool in which cells continually interconvert between As and syncytial states. This suggests that the dynamic and alternative model for spermatogenic stem cell function in the mouse testis.
To further investigate, we developed a minimal biophysical model that relies only on the rates of incomplete cell division and syncytial fragmentation. Remarkably, this model precisely predicts the stochastic fates of GFRα1+ cells during both steady-state spermatogenesis and post-insult regeneration.
Overall, our findings challenge the traditional understanding of spermatogenic stem cell function and highlight the complex and dynamic nature of these cells. This study opens up new avenues for research into the mechanisms that govern spermatogenesis and the role of stem cells in testis development and disease.

title: Pseudoknots: RNA Structures with Diverse Functions
text: RNA molecules perform a wide range of functions within cells, including the transfer of genetic information from DNA to protein, and enzymatic catalysis. These simple linear chains of RNA, composed of uracil, guanine, cytosine, and adenine, form complex three-dimensional structures through various folding motifs. One of the most common RNA structures is the pseudoknot, which consists of two helical segments connected by single-stranded regions or loops. The H-type fold is the most well-characterized, where the bases in the loop of a hairpin form intramolecular pairs with bases outside of the stem, resulting in a second stem and loop. This creates a pseudoknot with two stems and two loops, which can stack on top of each other to form a quasi-continuous helix with one continuous and one discontinuous strand. The single-stranded loop regions often interact with the adjacent stems, forming hydrogen bonds and participating in the overall structure of the molecule. Pseudoknots are structurally diverse and play a variety of roles in biology, such as forming the catalytic core of ribozymes, self-splicing introns, and telomerase, as well as inducing ribosomal frameshifting in many viruses.

title: An essential role for interferon gamma in resistance to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection
text:
Tuberculosis, a prevalent health issue in developing countries, has resurfaced in recent years in many industrialized nations. Immunocompromised individuals are particularly susceptible to tuberculosis, and numerous laboratory studies suggest that T cell-mediated immunity plays a crucial role in resistance. Interferon gamma (IFN-gamma), a key player in macrophage activation and resistance to intracellular pathogens, is thought to be a major mediator of these immune responses.
To investigate the role of IFN-gamma in tuberculosis, mice were genetically engineered to lack the gene for IFN-gamma (gko). Upon infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis, these mice fail to produce reactive nitrogen intermediates and are unable to restrict the growth of the bacilli. In contrast to control mice, gko mice experience heightened tissue necrosis and succumb to a rapid and fatal course of tuberculosis that can be delayed, but not prevented, by treatment with exogenous recombinant IFN-gamma.

title: Malignancies, prothrombotic mutations, and the risk of venous thrombosis.
text:
In this study, we aimed to identify individuals with cancer who are at an increased risk of developing venous thrombosis, a common complication in cancer patients that can lead to significant morbidity and impair quality of life. We evaluated different tumor sites, the presence of distant metastases, and carrier status of prothrombotic mutations in a large, population-based, case-control study of 3220 patients with cancer and 2131 control participants.
Our results indicate that patients with cancer have a significantly higher risk of venous thrombosis compared to individuals without cancer, with an odds ratio of 6.7 (95% confidence interval: 5.2-8.6). The risk of venous thrombosis was highest in patients with hematological malignancies, followed by lung cancer and gastrointestinal cancer. Patients with cancer who had distant metastases also had a higher risk of venous thrombosis compared to those without metastases. Additionally, we found that carriers of the factor V Leiden mutation, who also had cancer, had a 12-fold increased risk of venous thrombosis compared to individuals without cancer and the factor V Leiden mutation. Similar results were found for the prothrombin 20210A mutation in patients with cancer.
Our findings suggest that patients with cancer are at a high risk of venous thrombosis, particularly in the first few months after diagnosis and in the presence of distant metastases. The presence of prothrombotic mutations also appears to increase this risk. These results have important implications for the management of venous thrombosis in patients with cancer, and highlight the need for close monitoring and prophylactic anticoagulation therapy in this patient population.

title: The Hippo signaling pathway restricts the oncogenic potential of an intestinal regeneration program.
text: Although the role of Hippo signaling in controlling organ size is well recognized, the mechanisms underlying its involvement in tissue regeneration are still unclear. To address this, we employed a colonic regeneration model induced by dextran sodium sulfate (DSS) and investigated the involvement of Yes-associated protein (YAP) in the process. Our findings indicate that regenerating crypts exhibit elevated YAP levels. Inactivation of YAP had no observable defects in the intestine under normal circumstances, but significantly hindered DSS-induced intestinal regeneration. Conversely, overactivation of YAP led to widespread early-onset polyp formation following DSS treatment. These observations underscore the importance of precise YAP regulation in tissue regeneration to enable compensatory proliferation while preventing the potential cancerous consequences of a regenerating tissue.

title: The essence of SNPs.
text: Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are a prolific form of genetic variation, differentiated from rarer variations by the requirement that the least common allele must have a frequency of at least 1%. The extensive study and applications of SNPs have the potential to significantly benefit various fields of genetics. The current surge of interest in SNPs can be attributed to the convergence and maturation of several research areas, including (i) large-scale genome analysis and related technologies, (ii) bioinformatics and computational power, (iii) genetic analysis of both simple and complex diseases, and (iv) global human population genetics. These fields will continue to evolve and expand into new territories as a result of ongoing discovery efforts that are expected to yield hundreds of thousands of human SNPs in the near future. The SNP revolution has also raised important questions about the most effective strategies for unlocking its full potential, both experimentally and theoretically, as well as ethically.

title: Combination inhibition of PI3K and mTORC1 yields durable remissions in orthotopic patient-derived xenografts of HER2-positive breast cancer brain metastases
text: Heretofore, the most formidable clinical challenge in treating HER2-positive breast cancer has been the metastasis of these tumors to the brain. In this study, we engineered orthotopic patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) of HER2-positive breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM) to identify targeted combination therapies. We observed promising tumor regressions in three of our five PDXs following combination therapy with PI3K and mTOR inhibitors, with a direct correlation between therapeutic response and a decrease in 4EBP1 phosphorylation, a key mTORC1 effector. In contrast, the two non-responder PDXs exhibited hypermutated genomes enriched in mutations in DNA-repair genes, suggesting a link between genomic instability and resistance to therapy. These findings led us to propose a biomarker-driven clinical trial of a PI3K inhibitor in combination with an mTOR inhibitor for patients with HER2-positive BCBM.

title: Activation of Frontal Neocortical Areas by Vocal Production in Marmosets
text: Primate social interactions are often mediated through vocalizations, and while much is known about the acoustic structure and social context of these vocalizations, the neocortical areas responsible for controlling audio-vocal interactions in primates remain poorly understood. To investigate the neural basis of vocal control in a New World primate species, the common marmoset, we employed a technique similar to that used in other vertebrates: analyzing the expression of the immediate early gene Egr-1 in freely behaving animals. We compared the neocortical distribution of Egr-1 immunoreactive cells in three marmosets that spontaneously vocalized in response to conspecific playback (H/V group) to those in three other marmosets that did not vocalize (H/n group). Our results reveal that the anterior cingulate cortex, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex in marmosets show higher levels of Egr-1 expression in the H/V group. These findings provide direct evidence that the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, which is identical to Broca's area in humans and has been linked to auditory processing of species-specific vocalizations and orofacial control in macaques, is involved in vocal output in marmosets. These findings support the idea that the network of neocortical areas related to vocal communication in marmosets is similar to that of Old World primates, and highlight the importance of these areas for the evolution of speech in primates.

title: Familial hiatal hernia in a large five generation family confirming true autosomal dominant inheritance.
text:
Background: Hiatal hernia is a relatively rare condition, and its familial inheritance has been rarely reported.
Aims: To investigate the pattern of inheritance of familial hiatal hernia within an affected family.
Subjects: Thirty-eight members of a five-generation family pedigree were included in the study.
Methods: All family members were interviewed and underwent a barium meal to detect any evidence of a hiatal hernia.
Results: Twenty-three of the 38 family members had radiological evidence of a hiatal hernia. Notably, no individual born to unaffected parents developed a hiatal hernia. In one case, direct male-to-male transmission was observed, suggesting an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance.
Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate that familial inheritance of hiatal hernia does occur, and direct male-to-male transmission suggests an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance. This study highlights the importance of considering the potential genetic factors in the etiology of hiatal hernia.

title: An Excitatory Loop with Astrocytes Contributes to Drive Neurons to Seizure Threshold
text:
Seizures in focal epilepsies are characterized by a highly synchronized neural activity that originates at specific areas of the brain and then spreads to large portions of the brain. Despite extensive research, the initial cellular events that spark and sustain a focal seizure are still not fully understood. Identifying these events is crucial to comprehend the pathophysiology of focal epilepsies and to develop novel pharmacological treatments for drug-resistant forms of epilepsy. Recent studies propose that astrocytes play a prominent role in the process. Our study aims to investigate whether a collaboration between astrocytes and neurons is necessary to support seizure-like activities and interictal epileptiform events.
We employed simultaneous patch-clamp recording and Ca2+ imaging techniques in a novel in vitro model of focal seizures induced by local applications of N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA) in rat entorhinal cortex slices. Our findings indicate that a rise in Ca2+ levels in astrocytes coincide with the initiation and maintenance of a focal, seizure-like discharge. Additionally, we observed a delayed astrocyte activation during ictal discharges in other models, including isolated guinea pig brain. Conversely, interictal discharges were not associated with changes in Ca2+ levels in astrocytes. By selectively inhibiting or stimulating astrocyte Ca2+ signaling, we discovered that neurons engage astrocytes in a recurrent excitatory loop that promotes seizure onset and sustains the ictal discharge. This neuron-astrocyte interaction may offer a novel target for developing efficient therapeutic strategies to control seizures.

title: Diminished performance on neuropsychological testing in late life depression is correlated with microstructural white matter abnormalities.
text:
istes and Methods:
Background: Traditional T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences have limited ability to assess the extent of underlying white matter structural abnormalities in late-life depression (LLD). Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) provides a valuable opportunity to investigate the structural integrity of white matter, but its application is confounded by examining a limited number of regions of interest (ROI) and by the presence of comorbid vascular pathology in the elderly population. Moreover, the correlation of DTI measurements, including axial and radial diffusivity, has not been comprehensively demonstrated in LLD.
Methods: We conducted a directory of 51 depressed and 16 non-depressed elderly individuals who underwent both traditional anatomical T1 and T2-weighted imaging, as well as DTI. The DTI data were skeletonized using tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) for regional and global analyses.
Results: Widespread white matter structural abnormalities were detected in the LLD group, which was accounted for by age, gender, and education, as well as by cerebrovascular risk factors and global T2 white matter hyperintensities (T2WMH). Regional differences were most prominent in the uncinate and cingulate white matter, characterized by an increase in radial diffusivity. The age-related changes in the cingulate bundle were more advanced in LLD than in controls, and the correlations of regional fractional anisotropy and radial diffusivity were shown with five different neuropsychological factor scores. TBSS analysis demonstrated a greater extent of white matter abnormalities in LLD that were not responsive to treatment compared to controls.
Conclusions: The study demonstrates that white matter integrity is compromised in LLD, mainly characterized by increased radial diffusivity in specific regions, which suggests underlying myelin injury. A possible mechanism for underlying myelin injury is chronic white matter ischemia related to intrinsic cerebrovascular disease. In some regions, such as the cingulate bundle, the white matter injury related to LLD appears to be independent of and compounded by age-related changes. The correlations with neuropsychological testing indicate the essential effects of white matter injury on functional status. Lastly, response to treatment may depend on the extent of white matter injury, suggesting a need for intact functional networks.

title: The atypical antipsychotic olanzapine causes weight gain by targeting serotonin receptor 2C.
text:
Antipsychotic medications such as olanzapine are known to cause excessive weight gain and an increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes. However, the underlying mechanisms for these metabolic disturbances are not well understood. To better understand the effects of olanzapine on metabolism, we used a mouse model that reproduces the hyperphagia and obesity caused by olanzapine in female C57BL/6 mice.
Our findings showed that olanzapine treatment resulted in increased food intake, impaired glucose tolerance, and alterations in physical activity and energy expenditure in mice. Interestingly, we found that the olanzapine-induced hyperphagia and weight gain were significantly reduced in mice lacking the serotonin 2C receptor (HTR2C). Furthermore, we discovered that treatment with a specific agonist of the HTR2C receptor, lorcaserin, suppressed olanzapine-induced hyperphagia and weight gain. Lorcaserin treatment also improved glucose tolerance in olanzapine-fed mice. Our results suggest that olanzapine exerts some of its metabolic side effects through the antagonism of the HTR2C receptor.

title: Case-control study of endogenous steroid hormones and endometrial cancer.
text:
BACKGROUND:
It has been suggested that identified risk factors for endometrial cancer operate through a single etiologic pathway, i.e., exposure to relatively high levels of unopposed estrogen (estrogen in the absence of progestins). Only a few studies, however, have addressed this issue directly.
PURPOSE:
We assessed the risk of developing endometrial cancer among both premenopausal and postmenopausal women in relation to the circulating levels of steroid hormones and sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG). The independent effect of hormones was assessed after adjustment for other known risk factors.
METHODS:
The data used in the analysis are from a case-control study conducted in five geographic regions in the United States. Incident cases were newly diagnosed during the period from June 1, 1987, through May 15, 1990. The case patients, aged 20-74 years, were matched to control subjects by age, race, and geographic region. The community control subjects were obtained by random-digit-dialing procedures (for subjects 20-64 years old) and from files of the Health Care Financing Administration (for subjects > or = 65 years old). Additional control subjects who were having a hysterectomy performed for benign conditions were obtained from the participating centers. Women reporting use of exogenous estrogens or oral contraceptives within 6 months of interview were excluded, resulting in 68 case patients and 107 control subjects among premenopausal women and 208 case patients and 209 control subjects among postmenopausal women. The hormone analyses were performed on blood samples obtained from case patients or from hysterectomy control subjects before surgery. The odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated by use of an unconditional logistic regression analysis after we controlled for matching variables and potential confounders. All P values were two-sided.
RESULTS:
High circulating levels of androstenedione were associated with 3.6-fold and 2.8-fold increased risks among premenopausal and postmenopausal women, respectively, after adjustment for other factors (P for trend = .01 and < .001, respectively). Risks related to other hormone fractions varied by menopausal status. Among postmenopausal women, a reduced risk was associated with high SHBG levels and persisted after adjustment was made for obesity and other factors (OR = 0.51; 95% CI = 0.27-0.95). High estrone levels were associated with increased risk (OR = 3.8; 95% CI = 2.2-6.6), although adjustment for other risk factors (particularly body mass index) diminished the effect (OR = 2.2; 95% CI = 1.2-4.4). Albumin-bound estradiol (E2), a marker of the bioavailable fraction, also remained an important risk factor after adjustment was made for other factors (OR = 2.0; 95% CI = 1.0-3.9). In contrast, high concentrations of total, free, and albumin-bound E2 were unrelated to increased risk in premenopausal women. In both premenopausal and postmenopausal groups, risks associated with obesity and fat distribution were not affected by adjustment for hormones.
CONCLUSION:
High endogenous levels of unopposed estrogen are related to increased risk of endometrial cancer, but their independence from other risk factors is inconsistent with being a common underlying biologic pathway through which all risk factors for endometrial cancer operate.
IMPLICATIONS:

Further research should focus on alternative endocrinologic mechanisms for risk associated with obesity and body fat distribution and for the biologic relevance of the increased risk associated with androstenedione in both premenopausal and postmenopausal disease.

title: FOXO4 is necessary for neural differentiation of human embryonic stem cells.
text: Proteostasis is imperative for maintaining cellular function, and proteome stability may play a significant role in the immortality of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). Of interest, hESC populations display an elevated concentration of active proteasomes, a central component of the proteostasis network. The transcription factor FOXO4, which is responsive to insulin and IGF-1, regulates proteasome activity in hESCs. Our findings reveal that depletion of FOXO4 results in a decrease in the ability of hESCs to differentiate into neural lineages. This ultimately links FOXO4 to the regulation of invertebrate longevity, crossing evolutionary boundaries.

title: Gestational protein restriction affects trophoblast differentiation.
text: The impact of gestational protein restriction (PR) on placental development and function remains a mystery. To investigate the hypothesis that PR may affect trophoblast differentiation, rats were fed a 20% or isocaloric 6% protein diet from day 1 to 14 or 18 of pregnancy. The study found that PR increased the expressions of Esrrb, Id1, and Id2 (trophoblast stem cell markers) at day 18 of pregnancy, while decreasing the expressions of Ascl2 (spongiotrophblast cell marker) and Prl2c1 (trophoblast giant cell marker). However, PR did not alter the expressions of Gjb3 and Pcdh12 (glycogen cell markers) in the junctional zone (JZ). In the labyrinth zone (LZ), PR did not change the expressions of Prl2b1 (trophoblast giant cell marker), Gcm1, and Syna (syncytiotrophoblast cell markers), but decreased the expression of Ctsq (sinusoidal trophoblast giant cell marker). These findings suggest that PR impairs the differentiation of trophoblast stem cells into spongiotrophoblast and trophoblast giant cells in the JZ and the formation of sinusoidal trophoblast giant cells in the LZ.

title: In vitro characterization of the anti-PD-1 antibody nivolumab, BMS-936558, and in vivo toxicology in non-human primates.
text: The programmed death-1 (PD-1) receptor acts as an immune checkpoint, regulating the damage to bystander tissues and preventing the development of autoimmune responses during inflammatory processes. PD-1 is expressed on activated T cells, and its interaction with ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2 on antigen-presenting cells downregulates T-cell effector functions. In cancer, the expression of PD-1 on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and its interaction with ligands on tumor and immune cells in the tumor microenvironment hinders antitumor immunity, making PD-1 blockade a promising approach in cancer immunotherapy. This study describes the development and characterization of nivolumab, a fully human IgG4 (S228P) monoclonal antibody that blocks the PD-1 receptor. Nivolumab binds to PD-1 with high affinity and specificity, inhibiting the interaction between PD-1 and its ligands. In vitro assays demonstrated the ability of nivolumab to potently enhance T-cell responses and cytokine production in mixed lymphocyte reaction and superantigen or cytomegalovirus stimulation assays, without observable antibody-dependent cell-mediated or complement-dependent cytotoxicity when used with activated T cells as targets. Treatment with nivolumab did not induce adverse immune-related events in cynomolgus macaques at high concentrations, regardless of circulating anti-nivolumab antibodies. These data provide a comprehensive preclinical characterization of nivolumab, whose antitumor activity and safety have been demonstrated in human clinical trials across various solid tumors.

title: Combined Impact of Lifestyle-Related Factors on Total and Cause-Specific Mortality among Chinese Women: Prospective Cohort Study
text:
BACKGROUND Despite the well-established links between cigarette smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, obesity, and other unhealthy lifestyle factors to various chronic diseases and premature death, little is known about their combined impact on mortality rates, particularly among non-Western populations. To address this gap, we investigated the overall effect of lifestyle-related factors beyond active cigarette smoking and alcohol consumption on all-cause and disease-specific mortality in Chinese women.
METHODS AND FINDINGS Our study drew on data from the Shanghai Women's Health Study, a long-term population-based prospective cohort study conducted in China. Participants included 71,243 women aged 40 to 70 years who had never smoked or drank alcohol regularly. We created a healthy lifestyle score based on five factors that have been shown to impact mortality outcomes: normal weight, lower central adiposity, daily exercise, non-exposure to spouse's smoking, and higher fruit and vegetable intake. The score ranged from 0 (least healthy) to 5 (most healthy) points. During a median follow-up of 9 years, 2,860 deaths occurred, including 775 from cardiovascular disease (CVD) and 1,351 from cancer. We found that adjusted hazard ratios for mortality decreased progressively with an increasing number of healthy lifestyle factors. Compared to women with a score of zero, hazard ratios (95% CI) for women with four to five factors were 0.57 (0.44-0.74) for total mortality, 0.29 (0.16-0.54) for CVD mortality, and 0.76 (0.54-1.06) for cancer mortality. The inverse association between the healthy lifestyle score and mortality was observed consistently regardless of baseline chronic disease status. The population attributable risks for not having four to five healthy lifestyle factors were 33% for total deaths, 59% for CVD deaths, and 19% for cancer deaths.
CONCLUSIONS Our study, to the best of our knowledge, is the first to quantify the combined impact of lifestyle-related factors on mortality outcomes in Chinese women. A healthier lifestyle pattern, characterized by normal weight, lower central adiposity, physical activity, non-exposure to spouse's smoking, and higher fruit and vegetable intake, was associated with reductions in total and cause-specific mortality among lifetime nonsmoking and nondrinking women. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive lifestyle modification in disease prevention and mortality reduction. Editors' Summary: This study investigated the impact of a combination of lifestyle factors, including smoking, alcohol consumption, obesity, and other factors on mortality rates in Chinese women. The study found that a healthier lifestyle, characterized by normal weight, lower central adiposity, physical activity, non-exposure to spouse's smoking, and higher fruit and vegetable intake, was associated with a significant reduction in total and cause-specific mortality among lifetime nonsmoking and nondrinking women. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive lifestyle modification in disease prevention and mortality reduction.

title: Aptamer-functionalized lipid nanoparticles targeting osteoblasts as a novel RNA interference–based bone anabolic strategy
text: At present, significant concerns persist regarding the safety and effectiveness of RNA interference (RNAi)-based bone anabolic strategies due to the lack of direct delivery systems for osteogenic siRNAs that can specifically target osteoblasts. To address this challenge, we employed cell-SELECTION (SELEX) to identify aptamers that specifically target both rat and human osteoblasts, and then developed aptamer-functionalized lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) encapsulating osteogenic pleckstrin homology domain-containing family O member 1 (Plekho1) siRNA (CH6-LNPs-siRNA). Our findings showed that the aptamer CH6 facilitated in vitro osteoblast-selective uptake of Plekho1 siRNA through macropinocytosis and enhanced in vivo osteoblast-specific Plekho1 gene silencing, leading to improved bone formation, microarchitecture, mass, and mechanical properties in both osteopenic and healthy rodents. These results suggest that osteoblast-specific aptamer-functionalized LNPs could serve as a novel RNAi-based bone anabolic strategy, markedly improving the targeted delivery and selectivity of osteogenic siRNAs at the cellular level.

title: High abundance of plasma cells secreting transglutaminase 2–specific IgA autoantibodies with limited somatic hypermutation in celiac disease intestinal lesions
text: Celiac disease is an immune-mediated disorder in which the immune system produces antibodies against the enzyme transglutaminase 2 (TG2) in response to the presence of the protein gluten in individuals who carry certain genetic markers, such as HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8. To better understand the immune response to TG2 in celiac disease, we analyzed the antibody repertoire of intestinal cells called antibody-secreting cells (ASCs) isolated from the small intestine. We found that there is a large population of plasma cells in the small intestine that produce antibodies specific to TG2, and these antibodies had a high affinity for the enzyme. Unlike antibodies produced in response to infections, the TG2-specific antibodies had not recently divided and were not short-lived, suggesting that they are part of a germline repertoire. Interestingly, these antibodies did not inhibit the enzymatic activity of TG2, but instead served as substrates for TG2-mediated crosslinking when expressed as IgD or IgM, but not as IgA1 or IgG1. This suggests that the immune response to TG2 in celiac disease may involve the recruitment of naive B cells that express IgD and IgM, leading to the production of high-affinity antibodies. Overall, these observations provide new insights into the immune mechanisms underlying celiac disease.

title: Alterations of white matter integrity in adults with major depressive disorder: a magnetic resonance imaging study.
text:
The goal of our study was to investigate changes in white matter integrity in adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
METHODS: We used diffusion tensor imaging with a 3T MRI scanner to examine 45 patients with MDD and 45 healthyControls who were matched for age, sex, and education. Voxel-based analysis was used to measure fractional anisotropy (FA) in both groups. We also examined the correlations between microstructural abnormalities in white matter and symptom severity, age of illness onset, and cumulative illness duration, respectively.
RESULTS: Our study found a significant decrease in FA in the left hemisphere, specifically in the anterior limb of the internal capsule and the inferior parietal portion of the superior longitudinal fasciculus, in patients with MDD compared to healthy controls. We also found that diffusion tensor imaging measures in the left anterior limb of the internal capsule were negatively related to the severity of depressive symptoms, even after controlling for age and sex.
CONCLUSION: Our findings provide new evidence of microstructural changes in white matter in non-late-onset adult depression. These results complement those observed in late-life depression and support the hypothesis that the disruption of cortical-subcortical circuit integrity may be involved in the etiology of major depressive disorder.

title: [Clinical study on the therapeutic effect of acupuncture in the treatment of post-stroke depression].
text:
Objective: To evaluate the therapeutic effectiveness of "Xingnao Kaiqiao Zhenfa" (Acupuncture Technique for Restoring Consciousness) in treating post-stroke depression.
Methods: A total of 256 stroke patients were randomly divided into two groups: acupuncture (n=180) and medication (n=76). The acupuncture group received treatment twice daily, with needles retained for 20 minutes on specific acupoints (Neiguan (PC 6), Renzhong (GV 26), Baihui (GV 20), Yintang (EX-HN 3), and Sanyinjiao (SP 6 on the affected side)) while the medication group was given Amitriptyline (50 mg/day initially, then increased to 200 mg/day). The patients' depression state was evaluated using Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS) and Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD) after one month of treatment.
Results: After treatment, 31 (17.2%) and 13 (17.1%) patients in the acupuncture and medication groups were cured, respectively, while 73 (40.6%) and 18 (23.7%) had a marked improvement in their depression state. The markedly effective rate and total effective rate of the acupuncture group were significantly higher than those of the medication group (P<0.05). The total scores of SDS and HRSD, as well as the severity index of the two groups, decreased significantly compared to their individual pre-treatment levels. Additionally, the therapeutic effects of the acupuncture group were significantly better than those of the medication group in reducing SDS, HRSD, and severity index (P<0.05). The decrease in depression, pessimistic mood, and irritability was also significantly greater in the acupuncture group than in the medication group (P<0.05). However, there was no significant difference between the two groups in the decreased value of insomnia (P>0.05).
Conclusion: The results indicate that "Acupuncture Technique for Restoring Consciousness" is effective in improving depression symptoms in post-stroke patients, with a markedly superior therapeutic effect compared to medication.

title: 30 Years of NF-κB: A Blossoming of Relevance to Human Pathobiology
text: Thirty years ago, the transcription factor NF-κB was first identified as a rapidly inducible factor with a far-reaching impact on gene expression across various cellular responses. Since then, it has been found to play a central role in the immune system and beyond, regulating a wide range of genes involved in inflammation, immune response, and cell survival. In this article, we delve into the intricate regulatory networks that govern NF-κB's functions and explore how recent genetic discoveries in human diseases provide valuable insights into the biological and medical contexts of specific NF-κB-related proteins.

title: Increased gene expression of brown fat uncoupling protein (UCP)1 and skeletal muscle UCP2 and UCP3 in MAC16-induced cancer cachexia.
text: Weight loss in cancer cachexia is caused by a combination of decreased food intake and increased energy expenditure. In a study using a murine model of cachexia, we investigated the roles of uncoupling proteins UCP1, UCP2, and UCP3 in weight loss. We found that mice with cancer (MAC16 adenocarcinoma) had a significant decrease in body weight, fat-pad mass, and muscle mass compared to non-tumor-bearing controls. The mice also had a lower core temperature than controls, which may contribute to the weight loss. Analysis of UCP mRNA levels in brown adipose tissue (BAT) revealed that MAC16 mice had significantly higher levels of UCP1 mRNA than controls, and this was accompanied by an increase in thermogenesis in BAT. In contrast, UCP2 and -3 expression in BAT did not differ significantly between the two groups. Interestingly, UCP2 mRNA levels were comparably increased in both MAC16 and pair-fed (non-tumor-bearing mice that were matched for food intake) groups in skeletal muscle, while UCP3 mRNA was significantly higher in both groups. These findings suggest that increased thermogenesis in BAT may contribute to weight loss in cancer cachexia, while reduced food intake may lead to increased lipid utilization in muscle.

title: In vitro Anti-Tumor Effects of Statins on Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review
text:
Background: Statins have been widely used to treat arteriosclerotic disease, but recent retrospective analyses have suggested that they may also have anti-cancer effects. The current systematic review aims to evaluate the in vitro anti-tumor effects of statins on head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
Methods: The review included in vitro studies from Cochrane, MEDLINE, EMBASE, LILACS, and PubMed up to May 9, 2015, with no time or language restrictions. Only studies that investigated the effect of statins on head and neck carcinoma were included.
Results: Of the 153 identified papers, 14 studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies demonstrated that statins have a significant effect on head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cell lines, influencing cell viability, cell cycle, cell death, and protein expression levels involved in carcinogenic pathways. These findings corroborate the potential in vitro anti-tumor effects of statins and highlight their biological mechanisms, both when used alone or in combination with traditional therapy for cancer.
Conclusions: Although there is a limited number of studies on this topic, the available evidence suggests that statins display potential as an adjuvant agent in chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy approaches typically used in the management of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). As such, further clinical assessment of statins is warranted.

title: Circulating Mitochondrial DNA in Patients in the ICU as a Marker of Mortality: Derivation and Validation
text:
The background of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) as an activator of inflammation and the innate immune system has been well-established in the literature. However, its potential as a biomarker in the intensive care unit (ICU) setting has yet to be explored. In this study, we aimed to investigate the association between circulating mtDNA levels and mortality in ICU patients.
Methods and Findings:
We analyzed mtDNA levels in blood samples from two prospective observational cohort studies of ICU patients, including 200 patients from the Brigham and Women's Hospital Registry of Critical Illness (BWH RoCI) and 243 patients from the Molecular Epidemiology of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ME ARDS) cohort. We used quantitative real-time PCR to measure the copy number of the NADH dehydrogenase 1 gene in plasma, which is a commonly used marker of mtDNA. Our results showed that patients with elevated mtDNA levels (≥3,200 copies/μl plasma) had significantly higher odds of dying within 28 days of ICU admission compared to those with lower levels, in both the BWH RoCI (odds ratio (OR) 7.5, 95% CI 3.6-15.8, p=1x10(-7)) and ME ARDS (OR 8.4, 95% CI 2.9-24.2, p=9x10(-5)) cohorts. Additionally, the addition of an elevated mtDNA level improved the net reclassification index (NRI) of 28-day mortality among medical ICU patients when added to clinical models in both the BWH RoCI (NRI 79%, standard error 14%, p<1x10(-4)) and ME ARDS (NRI 55%, standard error 20%, p=0.007) cohorts. Interestingly, even in analyses limited to patients with sepsis or acute respiratory distress syndrome, those with an elevated mtDNA level remained at higher risk of death. Limitations of the study include the lack of data on the precise pathological roles of mtDNA in the patients, as well as limited numbers of measurements for some biomarkers.
Conclusions: Our study suggests that increased mtDNA levels are associated with ICU mortality, and inclusion of mtDNA level improves risk prediction in medical ICU patients. These findings suggest that mtDNA could serve as a viable plasma biomarker in medical ICU patients.

title: Fructosamine Is a Useful Indicator of Hyperglycaemia and Glucose Control in Clinical and Epidemiological Studies – Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Experience from the AMORIS Cohort
text:
Fructosamine is a glycemic biomarker that may be useful for diagnosing and monitoring diabetes. The purpose of this study was to determine the relationship between fructosamine levels and HbA1c in individuals with diabetes, as well as to evaluate fructosamine's ability to discriminate between individuals with and without diabetes.
The study included 10,987 participants from the AMORIS cohort, of which 5,590 were fasting. The guidelines of the American Diabetes Association were used to classify prediabetes and diabetes. Separate analyses were performed in patients with a newly detected or known diagnosis of type 1 or type 2 diabetes. Correlations between fructosamine and HbA1c were strong, ranging from 0.67 to 0.75 in both fasting and non-fasting subjects with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. Analyses of glucose control in fasting patients with type 2 diabetes showed similar trends over time for glucose, fructosamine, and HbA1c. The area under the curve (AUC) for fructosamine's ability to distinguish between subjects with and without diabetes was 0.91-0.95. A fructosamine level of 2.5 mmol/L was able to classify individuals as having diabetes with a sensitivity of 61% and a specificity of 97%.
Overall, this study suggests that fructosamine is closely associated with HbA1c and glucose levels, and may be a useful biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring diabetes in clinical and epidemiological studies.

title: Lifeact: a versatile marker to visualize F-actin
text: Obtaining live images of the actin cytoskeleton is essential for understanding various biological processes, yet current methods for visualizing actin have several drawbacks. Here, we present Lifeact, a 17-amino-acid peptide that stains filamentous actin (F-actin) structures in eukaryotic cells and tissues.
