PI3K(p110alpha) signaling inhibited G protein-coupled receptor-stimulated extracellular signal-regulated kinase and Akt (via PI3K, p110gamma) activation in isolated cardiomyocytes. Because of these findings, we may conclude that exercise and enhanced PI3K(p110alpha) activity hinder the progression of heart disease and that supraphysiologic activity can be advantageous. Identification of genes crucial for hypertrophy in the athlete's heart may provide previously unrealized strategies for managing heart failure.

title: The effect of cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption and fruit and vegetable consumption on IVF outcomes: a review and presentation of original data
text:
Background: Lifestyle factors, including smoking, alcohol consumption, and nutritional habits, significantly impact health, wellness, and the risk of chronic diseases. In the realm of in-vitro fertilization (IVF) and pregnancy, lifestyle factors also influence oocyte production, fertilization rates, pregnancy, and pregnancy loss, while chronic, low-grade oxidative stress may underlie poor outcomes for some IVF cases.
Methods: We conducted a review of the current literature and collected original, previously unpublished data from couples attending the PIVET Medical Centre in Western Australia. Partners completed a one-week diary detailing their smoking, alcohol, and fruit and vegetable intake, which were then analyzed using multiple regression analysis to investigate their relationship with IVF clinical outcomes, including oocyte quantity, fertilization rates, pregnancy, and pregnancy loss.
Results: Of significant importance, male smoking was found to increase the risk of pregnancy loss (p = 0.029), while female smoking had an adverse effect on ovarian reserve. Additionally, both alcohol consumption (β = 0.074, p < 0.001) and fruit and vegetable consumption (β = 0.034, p < 0.001) showed positive effects on fertilization.
Conclusion: Our findings, along with those of the existing literature, indicate that lifestyle factors have a considerable impact on IVF clinical outcomes. While conflicting results persist regarding other lifestyle factors, such as nutritional habits, it is evident that chronic oxidative stress induced by lifestyle factors and poor nutritional habits are associated with a lower rate of IVF success.

title: Efficient Mitochondrial Genome Editing by CRISPR/Cas9
text: The CRISPR/Cas9 system has been extensively applied to edit nuclear DNA, but its potential for editing mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) remained un explored. We demonstrate here that the FLAG-Cas9 protein can localize to mitochondria and edit mtDNA with specific guide RNAs (gRNAs) targeting specific loci of the mitochondrial genome. The introduction of FLAG-Cas9 along with gRNA targeting the Cox1 and Cox3 genes leads to cleavage of the specific mtDNA loci. In addition, we observed disruptions in the protein homeostasis of mitochondria following mtDNA cleavage by CRISPR/Cas9. To enhance the specificity of CRISPR/Cas9, we developed a mitochondria-targeted Cas9 protein (mitoCas9) that localizes exclusively to mitochondria. This new version of Cas9, when combined with gRNA targeting mtDNA, results in specific cleavage of mtDNA, leading to disruptions in mitochondrial membrane potential and cell growth inhibition. Most notably, mitoCas9 can be used to edit mtDNA without affecting the genomic DNA. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of mtDNA editing using CRISPR/Cas9 and pave the way for its application in mitochondrial genome editing.

title: Histone Variant H2A.Z Marks the 5′ Ends of Both Active and Inactive Genes in Euchromatin
text: In the yeast species Saccharomyces cerevisiae, histone variant H2A.Z is deposited in euchromatin at the edges of silent heterochromatin to prevent its uncontrolled spread. We discovered that H2A.Z nucleosomes are present at the promoter regions of nearly all genes in euchromatin. They typically consist of two positioned nucleosomes flanking a nucleosome-free region (NFR) containing the transcription start site. Our findings are particularly striking given that H2A.Z enrichment occurs not only at actively transcribed genes but also at inactive loci. By mutating a typical promoter, we identified a 22-base-pair segment of DNA that is sufficient to program H2A.Z nucleosome formation, with the segment containing a Reb1 binding site and an adjacent dT:dA tract. Efficient H2A.Z deposition is further enhanced by a specific pattern of histone H3 and H4 tail acetylation and the bromodomain protein Bdf1, a component of the Swr1 remodeling complex that deposits H2A.Z.

title: Exercise and respiratory training improve exercise capacity and quality of life in patients with severe chronic pulmonary hypertension.
text:
Background: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is associated with reduced physical capacity, decreased quality of life, and a poor prognosis due to right heart failure. This study is the first prospective randomized trial to investigate the effects of exercise and respiratory training on patients with severe symptomatic PH.
Methods: Thirty patients with PH (21 women; average age 50±13 years; average pulmonary artery pressure 50±15 mm Hg; average World Health Organization [WHO] class 2.9±0.5; pulmonary arterial hypertension in 23 patients and chronic thromboembolic PH in 7 patients) on stable disease-targeted medication were randomly assigned to a control group (n=15) or a primary training group (n=15). Medication remains unchanged during the study period. Primary end points included changes in the distance walked in 6 minutes and quality of life scores measured by the Short Form Health Survey questionnaire from baseline to week 15. Additionally, changes in WHO functional class, Borg scale, and parameters of echocardiography and gas exchange were assessed.
Results: Patients in the primary and secondary training groups demonstrated an improved 6-minute walking distance, with a mean difference of 111 m (95% confidence interval 65-139 m; P<0.001) between the control and primary training groups. Exercise training was well tolerated and improved quality of life scores, WHO functional class, peak oxygen consumption, oxygen consumption at the anaerobic threshold, and achieved workload. There were no significant changes in systolic pulmonary artery pressure values at rest after 15 weeks of exercise and respiratory training within the training group (from 61±18 to 54±18 mm Hg).
Conclusions: These findings suggest that respiratory and physical training may be a promising adjunct to medical treatment in severe PH. These results complement the beneficial effects of modern medical treatment.

title: HIV-1 regulation of latency in the monocyte-macrophage lineage and in CD4+ T lymphocytes.
text: In 1996, the introduction of HAART (Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy) raised expectations for the eradication of HIV-1. However, the discovery of latent HIV-1 reservoirs in CD4+ T cells and the monocyte-macrophage lineage disappointed these hopes. These long-lived reservoirs pose a significant obstacle to HIV-1 eradication. This review focuses on the establishment and maintenance of HIV-1 latency in these two major targets for HIV-1 infection: CD4+ T cells and the monocyte-macrophage lineage. Understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the establishment, maintenance, and reactivation of HIV-1 latency in these reservoirs is crucial for effective therapeutic interventions. Achieving complete viral eradication, the ultimate goal for clinicians, may be attainable through targeted interventions aimed at latently and productively infected cells. We propose that innovative approaches, such as combining different types of proviral activators, may help significantly reduce the size of latent HIV-1 reservoirs in HAART-treated patients.

title: Effects of Electro-Acupuncture Therapy on Post-Stroke Depression in Patients with Different Degrees of Motor Function Impairments: a Pilot Study
text:
The current investigation assessed the impact of electro-acupuncture therapy on post-stroke depression (PSD) and examined whether motor function deficits interact with the therapeutic effects. Twenty-eight PSD patients were categorized based on their motor function grade into either a good or poor motor function group.
The study employed the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS), and Manual Muscle Test (MMT) to evaluate the subjects at the initial stages of the study and at 4, 8, 12, and 16 weeks following daily electro-acupuncture treatment.
The findings indicate that electro-acupuncture therapy significantly reduced PSD in the subjects, with the good motor function group exhibiting more notable improvement compared to the poor motor function group. Contrary to expectations, the degree of motor function impairment remained unchanged throughout the study in both groups.
The results of this investigation demonstrate that electro-acupuncture therapy can effectively alleviate PSD, and the treatment's effectiveness varies depending on the severity of motor function impairment.

title: T cell receptor ligation induces the formation of dynamically regulated signaling assemblies
text: T cell antigen receptor (TCR) activation leads to tyrosine kinase activation, signaling complex assembly, and immune synapse formation. In this study, we investigated the kinetics and mechanics of signaling complex formation in live Jurkat leukemic T cells using signaling proteins fluorescently labeled with variants of enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP). Within seconds of contacting coverslips coated with stimulatory antibodies, T cells forming small, dynamically regulated clusters that were enriched in TCR, phosphotyrosine, ZAP-70, LAT, Grb2, Gads, and SLP-76 proteins. These clusters excluded the lipid raft marker enhanced yellow fluorescent protein-GPI and were capable of inducing calcium elevations. LAT, Grb2, and Gads were transiently associated with the TCR, while ZAP-70-containing clusters persisted for more than 20 minutes. Photobleaching studies revealed that ZAP-70 continuously dissociated from and returned to these complexes. Notably, SLP-76 translocated to a perinuclear structure after clustering with the TCR. Our results highlight the dynamically changing composition of signaling complexes and demonstrate that these complexes can form rapidly, within seconds of TCR engagement, in the absence of either lipid raft aggregation or the formation of a central TCR-rich cluster.

title: Developmental heterogeneity of cardiac fibroblasts does not predict pathological proliferation and activation.
text:
The mediator of fibrosis in the heart is partly the result of the actions of extracellular matrix-depositing fibroblasts. Although these mesenchymal cells are thought to have multiple embryonic origins, the functional implications of this diversity are unclear. To investigate, we aimed to identify and characterize distinct surface markers on cardiac fibroblasts.
We discovered that Thy1(+)CD45(-)CD31(-)CD11b(-)Ter119(-) cells comprise the main population of cardiac fibroblasts. We investigated these cells' identities using flow cytometry, epifluorescence, confocal microscopy, and transcriptional profiling (RT-PCR and RNA-seq). In addition, we employed lineage tracing, transplantation analyses, and parabiosis to determine the origin of adult cardiac fibroblasts. Our findings indicate that the majority of cardiac fibroblasts derives from the epicardium, with smaller contributions from endothelial cells and a negligible contribution from Pax3-expressing cells. We also found that bone marrow and circulating cells do not give rise to cardiac fibroblasts. Interestingly, we found that proliferation rates of fibroblast subsets were identical after pressure overload injury, and the relative abundance of each lineage remained unchanged. Additionally, RNA-seq analysis revealed that Tie2-derived and Tbx18-derived fibroblasts within each operation group exhibited similar gene expression profiles.
Our findings indicate that the cardiac fibroblasts' proliferative response to pressure overload injury is not restricted to a single developmental subset. The parallel proliferation and activation of a diverse population of fibroblasts may suggest that common signaling mechanisms are responsible for their pathological response.

title: Pre-eclampsia: connecting angiogenic and metabolic pathways.
text:
Pre-eclampsia is a high blood pressure disorder that affects pregnant women worldwide, with an incidence of 5-8%. This review focuses on recent advancements in pre-eclampsia research, particularly in the areas of angiogenesis and metabolism.
First, we examine the 'angiogenic imbalance' theory, which suggests that pre-eclampsia results from an imbalance between factors that promote or inhibit angiogenesis, such as soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase (sFlt1), 2-methoxyestradiol (2-ME), and catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT).
Next, we explore the link between pre-eclampsia and dysfunctional metabolism of both homocysteine and placental glycogen. We hope that shedding light on the intricate connections between angiogenesis and metabolism in pre-eclampsia will enable the development or revision of outdated models of pathogenesis.
In summary, this review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of recent findings in pre-eclampsia research, highlighting the complex interplay between angiogenesis and metabolism in the disease's pathogenesis. By updating or reconsidering old models of pathogenesis, we hope to enhance our understanding of pre-eclampsia and ultimately improve treatment options for affected women.

title: Protein Lysine Acetylated/Deacetylated Enzymes and the Metabolism-Related Diseases
text: Lysine acetylation is a reversible post-translational modification, an epigenetic phenomenon, in which an acetyl group is transferred from acetyl CoA to the e-amino group of a targeted protein. This process is mediated by enzymes called acetyltransferases (HATs/KATs) and deacetylases (HDACs/KDACs). Lysine acetylation regulates various metabolic processes, including fatty acid oxidation, Krebs cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, angiogenesis, and others. Disturbances in lysine acetylation have been implicated in metabolic disorders such as obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease, which are referred to as metabolic complications. As research on proteomic acetylation continues to accumulate, lysine acetylation has been found to play a role in cellular immune function and degenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease and Huntington's disease. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge on lysine acetylation in modulating metabolism and its relationship to metabolism-related diseases, such as cardiovascular disease and metabolic disorders.

title: Differential Specificity of Endocrine FGF19 and FGF21 to FGFR1 and FGFR4 in Complex with KLB
text:
Recent studies suggest that beta-klotho (KLB) and endocrine fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19) and 21 (FGF21) regulate metabolic homeostasis and suppression of obesity and diabetes by redirecting fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signaling. However, the identity of the primary metabolic tissue in which FGFR-KLB mediates the differential actions and metabolic effects of FGF19 and FGF21 remains unclear.
We investigated the receptor and tissue specificity of FGF21 compared to FGF19 using direct and quantitative binding kinetics, as well as downstream signal transduction and expression of early response genes after administration of FGF19 and FGF21 in mice. Our findings revealed that FGF21 binds FGFR1 with significantly higher affinity than FGFR4 in the presence of KLB, while FGF19 binds both FGFR1 and FGFR4 in the presence of KLB with comparable affinity. The interaction of FGF21 with FGFR4-KLB is very weak, even at high concentrations, and could be insignificant at physiological concentrations. Both FGF19 and FGF21, but not FGF1, showed binding affinity to KLB. However, FGF1 cannot displace the binding of FGF19 and FGF21, and vice versa. These results suggest that KLB is essential for the binding of FGF19 and FGF21 to FGFRs, but not required for FGF1 binding.
Our findings indicate that FGF19 can primarily activate responses in the liver and to a lesser extent in adipose tissue, while FGF21 can activate responses significantly in adipose tissue and adipocytes. Among various metabolic and endocrine tissues, the response of adipose tissue to FGF21 is most prominent, and may be blunted by ablation of KLB or FGFR1.
In conclusion, our results indicate that FGF21 is unable to bind FGFR4-KLB complex with affinity comparable to FGFR1-KLB at physiological concentrations, and therefore is less likely to directly and significantly target the liver where FGFR4-KLB predominantly resides. However, both FGF21 and FGF19 have the potential to activate responses primarily in adipose tissue where FGFR1-KLB resides.

title: Therapeutic efficacy of a multi-epitope vaccine against Helicobacter pylori infection in BALB/c mice model.
text: Epitope vaccine offers promise for therapeutic vaccination against Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection. In this study, we created a multi-epitope vaccine, HUepi-LTB, comprised of five epitopes and the mucosal adjuvant E. coli heat-labile enterotoxin B subunit (LTB). We evaluated the therapeutic effect of HUepi-LTB against H. pylori infection in BALB/c mice. Construction of HUepi-LTB involved expressing three Th epitopes from UreB and two B cell epitopes from UreB and HpaA in E. coli. Our results indicate that oral therapeutic immunization with HUepi-LTB significantly reduces H. pylori colonization compared to oral immunization with PBS. The protection was found to be associated with antigen-specific CD4+ T cells, IgG, and mucosal IgA antibody responses. This multi-epitope vaccine may emerge as a promising candidate for controlling H. pylori infection.

title: DNA fragments in the blood plasma of cancer patients: quantitations and evidence for their origin from apoptotic and necrotic cells.
text: In cancer patients, elevated levels of DNA fragments have frequently been detected in their blood plasma. According to published data, only a small fraction of the DNA in plasma comes from cancer cells, but it is unclear how much of the circulating DNA is from cancer or noncancer cells. To quantify the fraction of plasma DNA derived from tumor cells, we used quantitative methylation-specific PCR to analyze the promoter region of the CDKN2A tumor suppressor gene in plasma samples from 30 unselected cancer patients. We found that the amount of tumor DNA in their plasma ranged from 3% to 93% of the total circulating DNA. We also investigated the origin of non-tumor DNA in plasma and found that T-cell DNA made up only a small contribution in most cases. To determine whether plasma DNA originates from apoptotic or necrotic cells, we treated cells with apoptotic inducers (staurosporine) or necrotic inducers (staurosporine plus oligomycin) in vitro and mice with liver injury induced by anti-CD95 or acetaminophen. We found that increasing amounts of DNA were released into the supernatants of treated cells and plasma samples from treated animals, and we were able to distinguish between apoptotic and necrotic plasma DNA using gel electrophoresis. The same characteristic patterns of DNA fragments were identified in plasma samples from different cancer patients, suggesting that apoptotic and necrotic cells are a significant source of plasma DNA in cancer patients.

title: Pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of eptifibatide in patients with acute coronary syndromes: prospective analysis from PURSUIT.
text: The article investigates the effects of the platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa antagonist eptifibatide on platelet aggregation in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The study included 48 patients who were randomly assigned to receive either an intravenous bolus and 72-hour infusion of eptifibatide or placebo. The researchers analyzed the correlation between plasma eptifibatide levels and receptor occupancy, as well as the inhibition of ex vivo platelet aggregation at different time points during treatment and after treatment termination. The results showed that eptifibatide produced prolonged and profound inhibition of platelet aggregation during therapy, but the aggregation response appeared to recover partially by 4 hours after the bolus. The study also found that the inhibition of platelet aggregation was greater with thrombin receptor agonist peptide compared to ADP stimulation, and that plasma eptifibatide levels correlated significantly with receptor occupancy but not with inhibition of platelet aggregation. These findings enhance the understanding of the relationship between the pharmacodynamic and clinical effects of eptifibatide in patients with ACS and may have important implications for its use in percutaneous interventions.

title: Proinflammatory cytokines underlying the inflammation of Crohn's disease.
text:
Objective: To synthesize the current understanding of the pro-inflammatory cytokines responsible for the inflammation associated with Crohn's disease and to explore the potential of utilizing this knowledge to develop therapies that target these cytokines.
Recent Advances: Emerging research is providing fresh insights into the role of both T helper cell (Th)1 and Th17 responses in the pathogenesis of Crohn's disease. Earlier studies conducted a decade ago highlighted the notion that Crohn's disease inflammation is primarily driven by an interleukin-12-mediated Th1 response, resulting in the production of interferon-gamma. However, more recent studies conducted mainly in murine models have revealed that a Th17 response is the primary culprit behind Crohn's disease inflammation through the production of interleukin-17. A more balanced perspective is now emerging, suggesting that interferon-gamma may still play a significant role in the inflammation associated with Crohn's disease, although it may arise from both the Th1 and Th17-mediated responses at different stages of the inflammatory process.
Conclusion: The latest findings continue to lend support to the idea that anti-interleukin-12p40, an antibody that inhibits both the Th1 and Th17 response, is the most potent anti-cytokine for the treatment of Crohn's disease.

title: STATISTICAL METHODS FOR ASSESSING AGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO METHODS OF CLINICAL MEASUREMENT
text: To evaluate the adequacy of a new measurement technique in comparison to an established one, it is crucial to assess whether they provide similar results. Unfortunately, many studies analyze these comparisons inappropriately, relying on correlation coefficients. However, this approach can be misleading. A more accurate method, based on graphical techniques and simple calculations, is available, and it provides valuable insights into the comparability of the two techniques. Moreover, this analysis is closely related to the assessment of repeatability, which is an essential consideration in measurement accuracy.

title: The multidrug ABC transporter BmrC/BmrD of Bacillus subtilis is regulated via a ribosome-mediated transcriptional attenuation mechanism
text: The expression of specific drug transporters in response to antibiotic pressure is a critical aspect of bacterial multidrug resistance, posing a significant threat to human health. To gain a deeper understanding of the underlying regulatory mechanisms, we investigated the transcriptional activation of the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter BmrC/BmrD in the Gram-positive bacterium Bacillus subtilis. By employing promoter-GFP fusions and live cell array technology, we demonstrate a temporally regulated transcriptional activation of the bmrCD genes in response to antibiotics targeting protein synthesis. Surprisingly, bmrCD expression only occurs during the late-exponential and stationary growth phases, regardless of the timing of the antibiotic challenge. We found that this is due to tight transcriptional control by the transition state regulator AbrB. Furthermore, our results reveal that the bmrCD genes are co-transcribed with bmrB (yheJ), a small open reading frame located upstream of bmrC. These stem-loops are essential for antibiotic-induced bmrCD transcription. Importantly, the antibiotic-induced bmrCD expression requires translation of bmrB, which acts as a regulatory leader peptide. Our findings demonstrate for the first time that a ribosome-mediated transcriptional attenuation mechanism controls the expression of a multidrug ABC transporter.

title: The neural crest is a source of mesenchymal stem cells with specialized hematopoietic stem cell niche function
text:
Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and osteolineage cells play a crucial role in the hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) niche in the bone marrow of long bones, but their developmental relationships are not well understood. In this study, we investigate the distinct functions of different MSC populations in the developing marrow of long bones.
Proliferative mesoderm-derived nestin(-) MSCs contribute to fetal skeletogenesis, but lose their MSC activity shortly after birth. In contrast, quiescent neural crest-derived nestin(+) cells maintain their MSC activity and differentiate into HSC niche-forming MSCs, which help establish the HSC niche by secreting Cxcl12. This process requires the ErbB3 receptor.
Interestingly, the neonatal Nestin-GFP(+) Pdgfrα(-) cell population also contains Schwann cell precursors, but does not comprise mature Schwann cells. This suggests that in the developing bone marrow HSC niche-forming MSCs share a common origin with sympathetic peripheral neurons and glial cells. Moreover, ontogenically distinct MSCs have non-overlapping functions in endochondrogenesis and HSC niche formation.
In summary, our findings reveal that different MSC populations in the developing marrow of long bones have distinct functions, and provide new insights into the developmental relationships between these cells and the HSC niche.

title: Hotspots of aberrant epigenomic reprogramming in human induced pluripotent stem cells
text: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) hold great promise for regenerative medicine and research on developmental biology, and their potential is further enhanced by their ability to acquire characteristics similar to embryonic stem (ES) cells through somatic cell reprogramming. However, the extent to which these cells fully restore their methylation patterns, which are characteristic of ES cells, remains unclear. To address this question, we have generated whole-genome profiles of DNA methylation at single-base resolution in five human iPSC lines, along with methylomes of ES cells, somatic cells, and differentiated iPSCs and ES cells. Our findings reveal a degree of variability in reprogramming processes among iPSCs, including the presence of somatic memory and aberrant methylation reprogramming. Furthermore, we identify megabase-scale regions of differentially methylated DNA proximal to centromeres and telomeres that show incomplete reprogramming of non-CpG methylation and differences in CG methylation and histone modifications. Lastly, our study demonstrates that errors in reprogramming CG methylation are transmitted to daughter cells at a high frequency, providing an iPSC reprogramming signature that persists after differentiation.

title: Inheritance of coronary artery disease in men: an analysis of the role of the Y chromosome
text: The incidence and prevalence of coronary artery disease (CAD) differ between men and women, with men being more commonly affected. To investigate the role of the Y chromosome in this sexual inequity, we genotyped 11 markers in 3233 unrelated British men from three cohorts. We tracked the Y chromosomes back to one of 13 ancient lineages, or haplogroups, and examined associations between these haplogroups and CAD risk. We found that two haplogroups (R1b1b2 and I) accounted for 90% of Y chromosome variants in British men, and that carriers of haplogroup I had a 50% higher risk of CAD than men with other Y chromosome lineages. This association was independent of traditional cardiovascular and socioeconomic risk factors and was observed in both cross-sectional and prospective studies. Analyzing the macrophage transcriptome in the Cardiogenics Study revealed that 19 molecular pathways showing differential expression between men with haplogroup I and other Y chromosome lineages were interconnected by common genes related to inflammation and immunity, many of which have a strong relevance to atherosclerosis. Our findings suggest that the human Y chromosome may play a role in the increased risk of CAD in men of European ancestry, possibly through interactions of immunity and inflammation. This study was funded by the British Heart Foundation, the UK National Institute for Health Research, the LEW Carty Charitable Fund, the National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia, the European Union 6th Framework Programme, and the Wellcome Trust.

title: Cytoscape 2.8: new features for data integration and network visualization
text:
Cytoscape is a widely used bioinformatics tool for visualizing and integrating biological networks. Its latest version, 2.8, boasts two significant new features: Custom Node Graphics and Attribute Equations.
Custom Node Graphics allow users to project images onto nodes, including dynamic or remote-located images. This feature enables the representation of complex data and the visualization of relationships between different entities in biological networks.
Attribute Equations, on the other hand, provide Cytoscape with spreadsheet-like functionality. These equations enable the dynamic computation of an attribute's value based on other attributes and network properties. This feature enables users to perform intricate data analysis and validation, streamlining the process of visualizing and integrating complex biological data.
Cytoscape is a desktop Java application released under the Library Gnu Public License (LGPL). Binary install bundles and source code for Cytoscape 2.8 are available for download from the official Cytoscape website.

title: Detection of Histone Modifications at Specific Gene Loci in Single Cells in Histological Sections
text: Chromatin immunoprecipitation assays have greatly advanced our understanding of the role of histone modifications in gene regulation. However, they lack the resolution to analyze individual cells. Here, we introduce a novel method that enables visualization of histone modifications at specific genomic loci with single-cell resolution in formaldehyde-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue sections through the integration of in situ hybridization and proximity ligation assays. We demonstrate that dimethylation of lysine 4 of histone H3 (H3K4me2) at the MYH11 locus is exclusive to smooth muscle cells (SMCs) in both human and mouse tissue sections and that the mark persists even in partially differentiated SMCs in atherosclerotic lesions that lack detectable expression of SMC marker genes. This innovative approach holds great promise for comprehensive investigations of epigenetic mechanisms in complex multicellular tissues during development and disease.

title: Mechanistic characterization of the sulfur-relay system for eukaryotic 2-thiouridine biogenesis at tRNA wobble positions
text: The wobble modification in transfer RNAs (tRNAs), 5-methoxycarbonylmethyl-2-thiouridine (mcm(5)s(2)U), is essential for the proper decoding of NNR codons in eukaryotes. The 2-thio group of mcm(5)s(2)U confers conformational rigidity by maintaining the C3'-endo ribose puckering, ensuring stable and accurate codon-anticodon pairing. We have identified five genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, YIL008w (URM1), YHR111w (UBA4), YOR251c (TUM1), YNL119w (NCS2), and YGL211w (NCS6), that are involved in the 2-thiolation of mcm(5)s(2)U. An in vitro sulfur transfer experiment revealed that Tum1p stimulated the cysteine desulfurase of Nfs1p and accepted persulfide sulfurs from Nfs1p. URM1 is a ubiquitin-related modifier, and UBA4 is an E1-like enzyme involved in protein urmylation. The carboxy-terminus of Urm1p was activated as an acyl-adenylate (-COAMP), then thiocarboxylated (-COSH) by Uba4p. The activated thiocarboxylate can be utilized in the subsequent reactions for 2-thiouridine formation, mediated by Ncs2p/Ncs6p. We were able to successfully reconstitute the 2-thiouridine formation in vitro using recombinant proteins, revealing that this process shares a common pathway and chemical reactions with protein urmylation. The sulfur flow of eukaryotic 2-thiouridine formation is distinct from the bacterial sulfur-relay system, which is based on persulfide chemistry.

title: High prevalence of asthma in cross country skiers.
text:
Objective:
To investigate the prevalence of asthma symptoms and bronchial hyperresponsiveness among Swedish cross-country skiers compared to non-skiers and to monitor changes in these parameters throughout the year.
Design: Cross-sectional study conducted during the winter ski season and summer.
Setting: Six ski clubs for elite skiers (comprising 47 participants) in two different areas of Sweden.
Participants: 42 élite cross-country skiers and 29 non-skiing referents.
Main Outcome Measures: Bronchial responsiveness, asthma symptoms, and lung function.
Results: Bronchial responsiveness was significantly higher and asthma symptoms more prevalent among skiers compared to referents. There was no difference in bronchial responsiveness within either group between winter and summer. Twelve of the 42 skiers used anti-asthmatic drugs regularly, and 23 had a combination of asthma symptoms and hyperresponsive airways or physician-diagnosed asthma, or both. In all, 33 skiers had symptoms of asthma or bronchial hyperresponsiveness. Only one of the referrals had symptoms of asthma and bronchial hyperresponsiveness, and they did not use anti-asthmatic drugs regularly.
Conclusions: Asthma, asthma-like symptoms, and bronchial hyperresponsiveness are significantly more common among cross-country skiers compared to the general population and non-skiers. Engaging in strenuous exercise at low temperatures, which involves breathing large volumes of cold air, is likely the primary explanation for the persistent asthma in skiers.

title: Characterization of biochemical properties of Bacillus subtilis RecQ helicase.
text:
The RecQ family of helicases plays a crucial role in safeguarding the genome. Unlike Escherichia coli, the Gram-positive bacterium Bacillus subtilis contains two RecQ-like homologues, RecQ[Bs] and RecS, which are essential for repairing DNA double-strand breaks. RecQ[Bs] also helps guide the cell cycle by binding to forked DNA. In this study, we conducted the first biochemical analysis of recombinant RecQ[Bs].
RecQ[Bs] weakly binds to single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) and blunt-ended double-stranded DNA (dsDNA), but strongly to forked dsDNA. The protein exhibits DNA-stimulated ATPase activity and ATP- and Mg(2+)-dependent DNA helicase activity with a 3' → 5' polarity. Molecular modeling reveals that RecQ[Bs] shares high sequence and structure similarity with E. coli RecQ. Surprisingly, RecQ[Bs] resembles truncated Saccharomyces cerevisiae Sgs1 and human RecQ helicases more than RecQ[Ec] in its enzymatic activities. RecQ[Bs] unwinds forked dsDNA and DNA duplexes with a 3'-overhang, but is inactive on blunt-ended dsDNA and 5'-overhung duplexes. Notably, RecQ[Bs] unwinds blunt-ended DNA with various structural features, including nicks, gaps, 5'-flaps, Kappa joints, synthetic replication forks, and Holliday junctions. These findings suggest RecQ[Bs] plays a crucial role in preserving genomic stability.

title: SOD1 Integrates Signals from Oxygen and Glucose to Repress Respiration
text:
Copper/zinc superoxide dismutase (SOD1) is an abundant enzyme that has been extensively studied as a regulator of antioxidant defense. In a groundbreaking study, we have uncovered a novel role for SOD1 in transmitting signals from oxygen and glucose to repress respiration in yeast.
Using the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a model organism, we found that SOD1 regulates respiration by interacting with two casein kinase 1-gamma (CK1γ) homologs, Yck1p and Yck2p. We identified a unique C-terminal degron in Yck1p/Yck2p that binds SOD1, promoting kinase stability by catalyzing superoxide conversion to peroxide. Interestingly, the same mechanism is observed in mammalian SOD1 and CK1γ, as well as in a human cell line, suggesting a general mechanism by which cells can repress respiration in favor of aerobic glycolysis.
Our findings may provide important insights into how rapidly proliferating cells and cancers accomplish glucose-mediated repression of respiration. By understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying this process, we may be able to develop novel strategies for targeting cancer cell metabolism and promoting more effective cancer treatments.

title: The prognostic impact of the platelet distribution width-to-platelet count ratio in patients with breast cancer
text:
Here is a possible revision of the text:
Activated platelets foster tumor cell growth, angiogenesis, and invasion. Platelet activity can be evaluated using platelet volume indices (PVIs), including platelet distribution width (PDW), mean platelet volume (MPV), and platelet distribution width-to-platelet count ratio (PDW/P). In patients with breast cancer, platelet-related markers, such as the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, have been found to be significant predictors of poor prognosis. However, the role of PVIs in predicting survival in breast cancer remains unexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a retrospective analysis of 275 patients with breast cancer, comparing PVIs with clinicopathological variables and assessing their association with disease-free survival (DFS) using the Cox proportional hazards model. We found that an elevated PDW/P was significantly correlated with age and HER2 status. Univariate analysis revealed that elevated PDW, MPV, and PDW/P, as well as tumor size, nuclear grade, and lymph node involvement, were associated with inferior DFS rates (p<0.05). On multivariate analysis, large tumor size and elevated PDW/P emerged as significant prognostic factors for DFS, with hazard ratios of 3.24 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.24-8.47) and 2.99 (95% CI: 1.18-7.57), respectively (p<0.05). Our study is the first to demonstrate that elevated PDW/P significantly reduces DFS in patients with breast carcinoma. The simplicity and affordability of measuring PDW/P make it a promising biomarker for improving risk assessment.

title: Persistent LCMV infection is controlled by blockade of type I interferon signaling.
text: During persistent viral infections, there is a chronic activation of the immune system, which is characterized by the expression of negative immune regulatory molecules, an elevated interferon signature, and damage to lymphoid tissues. We have shown in mice persistently infected with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus that blocking type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling using an IFN-I receptor neutralizing antibody reduces immune system activation, decreases the expression of negative immune regulatory molecules, and restores lymphoid architecture. IFN-I blockade, both before and after the establishment of persistent virus infection, resulted in enhanced virus clearance and was dependent on CD4 T cells. Our findings demonstrate a direct causal link between IFN-I signaling, immune activation, negative immune regulator expression, lymphoid tissue disorganization, and virus persistence, suggesting that therapies targeting IFN-I may be effective in controlling persistent virus infections.

title: Lam6 Regulates the Extent of Contacts between Organelles
text: In eukaryotic cells, communication between organelles is vital for proper cellular function. One important means of communication is through close proximity, known as contact sites, where organelles can exchange lipid and small solute molecules. These contact sites are dynamic in size and can adapt in response to environmental or cellular stimuli, but their regulation has been poorly understood. Our study shows that Lam6, a protein found in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's yeast), plays a critical role in the expansion and coordination of contact sites in the ER/mitochondria encounter structure (ERMES), vacuole and mitochondria patch (vCLAMP), and nuclear vacuolar junction (NVJ). Interestingly, Lam6 is not only found in these central contact sites but is also part of a large protein family that is conserved in vertebrates, suggesting that our work may hold potential for investigating the underlying principles of organelle communication.

title: Endocrine regulation of human fetal growth: the role of the mother, placenta, and fetus.
text: The fetal environment plays a crucial role in determining the baby's growth and long-term health. The normal growth and development of the fetus relies on intricate interactions between the mother, placenta, and the developing fetus itself. The mother supplies nutrients and oxygen to the fetus through the placenta, while the fetus regulates the mother's metabolism and nutrient supply through the production of hormones. The placenta acts as a conduit between mother and fetus, facilitating the exchange of nutrients, hormones, and other factors that influence fetal growth. Proper trophoblast invasion in early pregnancy and increased uteroplacental blood flow help ensure adequate growth and development of the uterus, placenta, and fetus. The placenta can also respond to fetal endocrine signals by increasing transport of maternal nutrients, activating transport systems, and producing placental hormones that modulate maternal physiology and behavior. Poor fetal growth can have significant short-term and long-term consequences, including increased mortality and morbidity. The endocrine regulation of fetal growth involves complex interactions among the mother, placenta, and fetus, which can have lasting impacts on the baby's physiology.

title: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition contributes to cardiac fibrosis
text: Cardiac fibrosis, characterized by an excessive buildup of extracellular matrix and a decrease in the number of microvascular structures, is a common consequence of various cardiovascular diseases. This process is mediated by the recruitment of fibroblasts, but the source of these fibroblasts remains unclear. Currently, there are no specific anti-fibrotic therapies available. Our study shows that cardiac fibrosis is actually the result of the transformation of endothelial cells into fibroblasts, a process known as endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT). We found that transforming growth factor-beta1 (TGF-β1) induces EndMT, while bone morphogenic protein 7 (BMP-7) preserves the endothelial phenotype. Interestingly, we found that the systemic administration of recombinant human BMP-7 (rhBMP-7) significantly inhibited EndMT and the progression of cardiac fibrosis in mouse models of pressure overload and chronic allograft rejection. Our findings suggest that EndMT plays a critical role in the progression of cardiac fibrosis, and that rhBMP-7 may be a promising therapeutic approach for intervening in the progression of chronic heart disease associated with fibrosis.

title: Coupled local translation and degradation regulate growth cone collapse
text: Locally synthesized proteins in growing axons play a crucial role in mediating responses to Semaphorin3A (Sema3A) and other guidance cues. However, only a select subset of the axonal proteome is locally produced, while the majority is transported from the soma. The reason for this selective localization is still unclear. We investigate the relationship between local protein synthesis and degradation in growth cones and find that they are intimately linked. Specifically, we identify ubiquitination and degradation of RhoA, a key mediator of Sema3A-induced growth cone collapse, as a critical process linked to local protein synthesis. Inhibiting RhoA degradation is sufficient to eliminate the protein-synthesis requirement for Sema3A-induced growth cone collapse. Additionally, we find that locally synthesized proteins are the primary substrates of the ubiquitin-proteasome system in growth cones, highlighting the importance of local protein degradation in maintaining growth cone function. Overall, our findings reveal a tightly regulated interplay between local protein synthesis and degradation in growth cones, underscoring the critical role of local translation in maintaining growth cone responses.

title: Cdk11 is a RanGTP-dependent microtubule stabilization factor that regulates spindle assembly rate
text: The production of Ran-guanosine triphosphate (GTP) around chromosomes leads to the local nucleation and stabilization of microtubules (MTs). The nuclear protein TPX2 is essential for RanGTP-dependent MT nucleation. To identify the MT stabilizer, we isolated nuclear localization signal (NLS)-containing proteins from Xenopus laevis egg extracts and found that this fraction contains the MT stabilization activity. Following purification, we used mass spectrometry to identify proteins present in active fractions, including cyclin-dependent kinase 11 (Cdk11). Cdk11 localizes at spindle poles and MTs in Xenopus culture cells and egg extracts, and recombinant Cdk11 demonstrates RanGTP-dependent MT stabilization activity, whereas a kinase-dead mutant does not. Depletion of Cdk11 in egg extracts abolishes RanGTP-dependent MT stabilization and significantly reduces the spindle assembly rate. In addition, simultaneous depletion of TPX2 completely inhibits centrosome-dependent spindle assembly. Our findings indicate that Cdk11 is responsible for RanGTP-dependent MT stabilization near chromosomes, which is essential for maintaining normal rates of spindle assembly and spindle function.

title: Population dynamics of a pathogen: the conundrum of vivax malaria
text:
draft:
Modeling population dynamics of pathogens within their hosts requires consideration of factors similar to those in ecology, as pathogens prey on host cells. However, in the context of multicellular hosts, infected cells are integrated with other cellular systems, which can intervene in the infection process. For instance, immune responses aim to detect and eliminate or contain pathogens, while homeostatic mechanisms attempt to compensate for cell loss. This review focuses on mathematical modeling applied to malaria, a disease caused by single-celled eukaryote parasites that infect red blood cells, with a particular emphasis on vivax malaria, which is often thought to be benign but can be disastrous to the host if not adequately contained by host immune responses. Models can help elucidate new field observations that suggest vivax malaria is more dangerous than previously thought.
SUPPLEMENTARY MATERIAL
Supplementary material is available online for authorized users in the electronic version of this article (doi:10.1007/s12551-010-0034-3).

title: Identification and analysis of ribonuclease P and MRP RNA in a broad range of eukaryotes
text: RNases P and MRP are ribonucleoprotein complexes involved in the processing of tRNAs and rRNAs, respectively. The RNA subunits of these enzymes are structurally similar and play a crucial role in the enzymatic reaction. Both RNAs have a highly conserved helical region, P4, which is essential for catalysis. By using a bioinformatics approach based on conserved elements, we analyzed available genomic sequences of eukaryotic organisms and identified a large number of novel nuclear RNase P and MRP RNA genes. For instance, this investigation more than tripled the number of known MRP RNA sequences. We present secondary structure models of many of the predicted RNAs, which show that all sequences are capable of folding into the consensus secondary structure of P and MRP RNAs. However, there is a great deal of variability in size, with some RNAs, such as the MRP RNA from Nosema locustae, being only 160 nucleotides in length, while others, such as the P RNA from Plasmodium knowlesi, are significantly larger, at 696 nucleotides. The P and MRP RNA genes are also found in tandem in some protists, further highlighting the close evolutionary relationship between these RNAs.

title: Calcium absorption varies within the reference range for serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D.
text:
Human calcium absorption is generally thought to be impaired when vitamin D levels are low, but the ideal serum vitamin D concentration that fully restores calcium absorption remains unknown. To investigate this, researchers conducted two experiments in spring, one year apart, in which participants received a 500 mg oral calcium load as part of a standard low-calcium breakfast and low-calcium lunch. Blood samples were taken before and at frequent intervals after the load to measure serum total calcium levels.
The study found that relative calcium absorption was significantly higher at serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25OHD) levels averaging 86.5 nmol/L than at levels averaging 50.2 nmol/L (current reference range). Specifically, calcium absorption was 65% higher at the higher 25OHD levels. These findings suggest that individuals with serum 25OHD levels at the lower end of the current reference range may not be optimizing their calcium intake and may benefit from higher vitamin D levels. The study concludes that the current reference range for 25OHD may be set too low and that optimal calcium absorption may require higher vitamin D levels than currently recommended.

title: Evolution of virulence in opportunistic pathogens: generalism, plasticity, and control
text: The standard theory of virulence evolution posits that virulence factors are maintained because they enhance the ability of parasitic organisms to exploit their hosts, leading to increased growth and transmission. However, recent studies have challenged this assumption, demonstrating that many opportunistic pathogens (OPs) do not conform to these expectations. Instead, virulence factors are often maintained for reasons unrelated to parasitism, such as advantages in non-parasitic contexts. In this review, we examine the current state of virulence evolution theory in the context of OPs and explore the importance of considering environments outside of the focal virulence site. We highlight the role of environmental correlations in shaping virulence selection and examine the mechanisms that drive these correlations, with a focus on generalist strategies and phenotypic plasticity. Finally, we discuss the key challenges that remain to be addressed in order to fully understand the evolution of OPs.

title: Genome-Wide Profiling of H3K56 Acetylation and Transcription Factor Binding Sites in Human Adipocytes
text:
The growing prevalence of obesity and metabolic disorders highlights the need for a deeper understanding of adipocyte biology. Specifically, the regulation of transcription in adipocytes is a crucial area of study, as it is a target for various therapeutic interventions. Both histone modifications and transcription factor binding play a significant role in shaping transcriptional outcomes. While several studies have profiled the epigenetic states and binding sites of transcription factors in the mouse 3T3-L1 cell line, such data are lacking in human adipocytes.
In this investigation, we aimed to identify H3K56 acetylation sites in human adipocytes derived from mesenchymal stem cells. H3K56 is acetylated by enzymes such as CBP and p300, and deacetylated by SIRT1, all of which have important functions in diabetes and insulin signaling. We found that nearly half of the genome exhibits H3K56 acetylation, with the highest levels of acetylation observed in genes involved in adipokine signaling and Type II Diabetes pathways.
To identify the transcription factors that recruit acetyltransferases and deacetylases to H3K56 acetylated regions, we analyzed the nearby DNA sequences and found an enrichment of the E2F recognition sequence. Using chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by high-throughput sequencing (ChIP-Seq), we confirmed that genes bound by E2F4, as well as those by HSF-1 and C/EBPα, have higher than expected levels of H3K56 acetylation. Moreover, we observed that the transcription factor binding sites and acetylation sites often neighbor each other, but rarely overlap.
Interestingly, we discovered a significant difference in the bound targets of C/EBPα between 3T3-L1 and human adipocytes, underscoring the need to create species-specific epigenetic and transcription factor binding site maps. Overall, this study provides the first comprehensive profile of H3K56 acetylation, E2F4, C/EBPα, and HSF-1 binding in human adipocytes, and will constitute an indispensable resource for elucidating the complex transcriptional regulation of adipocytes.

title: Detecting and characterizing circular RNAs
text: Circular RNA (circRNA) transcripts were first identified in the early 1990s, but due to the limited methods available for their analysis, study on these species has progressed slowly. However, recent advances in bioinformatic approaches and biochemical enrichment strategies, combined with deep sequencing, have enabled comprehensive studies of circRNAs. Recent studies have uncovered thousands of endogenous circRNAs in mammalian cells, with some showing high abundance and conservation across species. Research suggests that certain circRNAs may modulate microRNA (miRNA) function, and evidence implicating their roles in transcriptional control is emerging. These findings have significant implications for both therapeutic and research applications. However, the next challenge for the field will be to elucidate the regulatory mechanisms and functions of these unusual non-coding RNAs.

title: A classification of unstable angina revisited.
text: Unstable angina is a critical phase of coronary heart disease with diverse symptoms and an uncertain prognosis. A decade ago, a classification system for unstable angina was introduced based on clinical symptoms, which was later validated through prospective clinical studies to evaluate its correlation with the patients' prognosis. It has since been used in many large clinical trials to categorize patients. Recently, research has elucidated the pathophysiological roles of platelet activation and inflammation in unstable angina, leading to the identification of improved markers of myocardial injury, acute-phase proteins, and hemostatic markers that may predict clinical outcomes. Specifically, cardiac-specific troponin T and troponin I have been shown to be the most effective predictors of early risk in patients with angina at rest. Accordingly, it is suggested that the original classification be extended by subclassifying one group of unstable angina patients, those who experienced angina in the past 48 hours (class IIIB), into troponin-positive (T(pos)) and troponin-negative (T(neg)) subgroups. The 30-day risk of death and myocardial infarction is estimated to be up to 20% in class IIIB-T(pos) patients but less than 2% in class IIIB-T(neg) patients. Early results suggest that troponins may serve as surrogate markers for thrombus formation and can guide therapy with glycoprotein IIb/IIIa antagonists or low-molecular-weight heparins. These findings offer further support for incorporating troponin measurement into the clinical classification and represent a novel approach to treating high-risk patients.

title: Alcohol Intake and Blood Pressure: A Systematic Review Implementing a Mendelian Randomization Approach
text:
Background: Alcohol consumption has been identified as a modifiable risk factor for hypertension. However, observational studies are susceptible to confounding variables, and clinical trials are challenging to implement and have limited follow-up time. Mendelian randomization offers a robust approach to investigating the association between alcohol consumption and hypertension by utilizing a common genetic polymorphism in aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2). ALDH2 encodes the primary enzyme involved in alcohol metabolism. Individuals homozygous for the null variant (ALDH2*2*2) experience adverse symptoms upon drinking alcohol and consequently consume less alcohol compared to wild-type homozygotes (ALDH2*1*1) or heterozygotes (surrogate for moderate drinkers). We hypothesize that this polymorphism may influence the risk of hypertension by affecting alcohol consumption behavior.
Methods and Findings: We conducted fixed-effect meta-analyses of the ALDH2 genotype with blood pressure (n = 7,658) and hypertension (n = 4,219) from five and three studies, respectively, identified through a systematic review. Among males, we found an overall odds ratio of 2.42 (95% CI: 1.66-3.55, p = 4.8 x 10(-6)) for hypertension comparing ALDH2*1*1 with ALDH2*2*2 homozygotes and an odds ratio of 1.72 (95% CI: 1.17-2.52, p = 0.006) comparing heterozygotes (surrogate for moderate drinkers) with ALDH2*2*2 homozygotes. Moreover, systolic blood pressure was 7.44 mmHg (95% CI: 5.39-9.49, p = 1.1 x 10(-12)) higher among ALDH2*1*1 than ALDH2*2*2 homozygotes, and 4.24 mmHg (95% CI: 2.18-6.31, p = 0.00005) higher among heterozygotes than ALDH2*2*2 homozygotes.
Conclusions: These findings support the hypothesis that alcohol intake has a significant effect on blood pressure and the risk of hypertension.

title: Rapid and Sensitive RT-QuIC Detection of Human Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease Using Cerebrospinal Fluid
text:
Fast and accurate diagnosis of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) is crucial for patient care and transmission risk assessment. Prior RT-QuIC assays took 2.5-5 days to diagnose CJD, but a new improved assay can identify positive CSF samples within 4-14 hours with higher analytical sensitivity. In an analysis of 11 CJD patients, 10 were positive using the new assay, while 7 were positive using the previous method. Moreover, 46 of 48 CSF samples from sporadic CJD patients were positive, while all 39 non-CJD patients were negative, resulting in a diagnostic sensitivity of 95.8% and specificity of 100%. This enhanced speed and sensitivity in detecting prion seeds in CSF specimens should improve prospects for rapid and accurate ante mortem CJD diagnosis.
The challenge of early and accurate diagnosis of neurodegenerative protein misfolding diseases, including CJD, is longstanding and particularly important due to the deadly and transmissible nature of prions. The recently developed RT-QuIC test has emerged as a sensitive and specific diagnostic tool for CJD, with broad implementation underway. However, the current RT-QuIC method takes 2.5-5 days and misses 11-23% of CJD cases. Our improved RT-QuIC analysis of human CSF now enables CJD and non-CJD patients to be differentiated in a matter of hours rather than days, with enhanced sensitivity. These advances hold significant implications for tests diagnosing other misfolded protein aggregates associated with amyloid diseases, such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and tauopathies.

title: Wortmannin, a phosphoinositide 3-kinase inhibitor, selectively enhances cytotoxicity of receptor-directed-toxin chimeras in vitro and in vivo.
text: In this study, we investigated the potential of the Pl 3-kinase inhibitor wortmannin to enhance the cytotoxicity of ligand-toxin chimeras in human neoplastic cell lines. We found that at concentrations greater than the reported Ki for Pl 3-kinase inhibition, wortmannin combined with saporin or gelonin chimeras showed enhanced cytotoxicity, but produced subadditive cytotoxicity when combined with Pseudomonas exotoxin chimeras. Additionally, we found that low nanomolar concentrations of wortmannin selectively inhibiting Pl 3-kinase activity dramatically enhanced the cytotoxicity of the bFGF-SAP chimera in three of the four cell lines tested. However, a different Pl 3-kinase inhibitor, LY294002, failed to potentiate bFGF-SAP cytotoxicity. When administered to mice, the combination of wortmannin and bFGF-SAP resulted in a significant decrease in tumor volumes compared to vehicle-treated controls, suggesting that this combination may be a promising therapeutic approach for treating certain types of cancer. Overall, our results suggest that wortmannin may increase the cytotoxic efficacy of some ligand-toxin chimeras through an alternative pathway not involving Pl 3-kinase inhibition.

title: Chronic stress, glucocorticoid receptor resistance, inflammation, and disease risk.
text: We propose a model where chronic stress leads to glucocorticoid receptor resistance (GCR), which in turn compromises the ability to regulate inflammation. We test this model in two studies examining viral challenges. In study 1, we assessed stressful life events, GCR, and relevant control variables, including baseline antibody to the challenge virus, age, body mass index (BMI), season, race, sex, education, and virus type, among 276 healthy adult volunteers. After quarantine and exposure to one of two rhinoviruses, the volunteers were followed for 5 days to detect viral isolation and symptoms of a common cold. In study 2, we examined the same control variables and GCR in 79 subjects who were subsequently exposed to a rhinovirus and monitored at baseline and after viral challenge for the production of local (nasal secretions) proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6). Our findings suggest that individuals who have experienced recent long-term stressful experiences demonstrate GCR, and those with GCR are at higher risk of developing a cold. Similarly, in study 2, we found that subjects with greater GCR produced more local proinflammatory cytokines following viral infection. These results provide support for a model proposing that prolonged stressors lead to GCR, which in turn interferes with the proper regulation of inflammation. This model may have far-reaching implications for understanding the role of stress in various diseases, given the critical role of inflammation in these conditions.

title: Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase-Activating Polypeptide (PACAP), a Neuron-Derived Peptide Regulating Glial Glutamate Transport and Metabolism
text:
In the brain, glutamatergic neurotransmission is primarily terminated by the rapid uptake of synaptically released glutamate into astrocytes through the Na+-dependent glutamate transporters GLT-1 and GLAST, followed by its conversion into glutamine by the enzyme glutamine synthetase (GS). Recent studies have revealed that various factors can rapidly alter glial glutamate uptake through post-translational modifications of glutamate transporters. However, the only condition known to affect the expression of glial glutamate transporters and GS is the co-culturing of glia with neurons.
We demonstrate here that neurons regulate glial glutamate turnover via pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP). In the cerebral cortex, PACAP is synthesized by neurons and specifically acts on a subpopulation of astroglia involved in glutamate turnover. Exposure of astroglia to PACAP increases the maximal velocity of [(3)H]glutamate uptake by upregulating the expression of GLT-1, GLAST, and GS. Furthermore, the stimulatory effects of neuron-conditioned medium on glial glutamate transporter expression are significantly attenuated in the presence of PACAP-inactivating antibodies or the PACAP receptor antagonist PACAP 6-38. In contrast, vasoactive intestinal peptide promotes glutamate transporter expression at higher concentrations, suggesting that PACAP exerts its effects on glial glutamate turnover through PAC1 receptors. While activation of PKA is sufficient to promote GLAST expression, both PKA and PKC activation are required to optimize GLT-1 expression. The existence of multiple PAC1 receptor isoforms that activate PKA and PKC to different levels suggests a complex mechanism by which PACAP regulates glial glutamate transport and metabolism. Disruptions in these regulatory mechanisms may contribute to glutamate-associated neurological and psychiatric disorders.

title: Factors influencing B lymphopoiesis after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.
text: In 93 allograft recipients, the correlation between marrow B-cell precursors on days 80 and 365 and circulating B cells suggested that the post-transplantation B-cell deficiency is partially due to insufficient B lymphopoiesis. Variables affecting B lymphopoiesis were evaluated, and it was found that the number of marrow B-cell precursors on days 30, 80, and 365 was significantly lower in patients with severe acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) compared to those with mild GVHD. Additionally, the number of B-cell precursors on day 365 was 18 times lower in patients with extensive chronic GVHD than in those with no or limited chronic GVHD. The study found that the number of B-cell precursors was unrelated to factors such as CD34 cell dose, type of transplant (marrow versus blood stem cells), donor age, or patient age. It was concluded that post-transplantation B-cell deficiency may result from the inhibition of B lymphopoiesis by GVHD and/or its treatment.

title: Genetic variants rs1994016 and rs3825807 in ADAMTS7 affect its mRNA expression in atherosclerotic occlusive peripheral arterial disease
text:
Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD) is a vascular condition that affects the peripheral circulation. Recently, genetic studies have shown a connection between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in ADAMTS7 (a disintegrin and metalloprotease with thrombospondin motif 7) and the development of atherosclerosis. We aimed to investigate the expression of ADAMTS7 in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the frequency of ADAMTS7 SNPs in a sample of Turkish patients with PAD, as well as to assess the association between matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) levels and PAD development.
Methods:
In this case-control study, we used reverse transcription quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blot to determine ADAMTS7 mRNA and protein expression, respectively, and real-time PCR to determine the frequencies of ADAMTS7 SNPs in 115 PAD patients and 116 healthy controls. Plasma levels of nine MMPs were measured using a multiplex immunoassay system.
Results:
We found that ADAMTS7 mRNA levels were significantly higher in PAD patients than in controls (t=-2.75, P=.007). There was no significant difference in the frequencies of ADAMTS7 SNPs between PAD patients and controls (P>.05). In PAD patients, ADAMTS7 mRNA levels were significantly increased for the CC genotype of rs1994016 (t=-2.31, P=.026) and TT genotype of rs3825807 (t=-2.23, P=.032). Furthermore, plasma levels of MMP-1, MMP-3, MMP-7, MMP-10, MMP-12, and MMP-13 were significantly higher in PAD patients than in controls (P<.05).
Conclusion:
Our findings suggest that ADAMTS7 may be associated with the development of PAD. This is the first study to investigate the relationship between PAD and ADAMTS7 expression, as well as the effects of ADAMTS7 SNPs on PAD development. These results may have implications for the development of new diagnostic markers and therapeutic strategies for PAD.

title: Distinct Parietal and Temporal Pathways to the Homologues of Broca's Area in the Monkey
text: Recently, the homologues of Broca's region in the macaque monkey have been identified, which are located in the ventrolateral frontal lobe. While it is known that the inferior parietal lobule and lateral temporal cortical region project to the ventrolateral frontal cortex, the specific cortical areas that project to the homologues of Broca's region in the macaque monkey and the white matter pathways involved are still unknown. To investigate these connections, the autoradiographic method was used, which allows for the identification of the cortical area of axon origin, the exact course of axons in white matter, and their termination within specific cortical areas. The results demonstrated a ventral temporo-frontal stream of fibers originating from various auditory, multisensory, and visual association cortical areas in the intermediate superolateral temporal region, which primarily targets area 45 with a smaller termination in area 44. In contrast, a dorsal stream of axons originating from cortical areas in the inferior parietal lobule and adjacent caudal superior temporal sulcus was found to target both areas 44 and 45. These axons course through the superior longitudinal fasciculus, with some axons originating from the ventral inferior parietal lobule and forming a simple arcuate fasciculus. The cortex of the most rostral part of the inferior parietal lobule is preferentially linked with the ventral premotor cortex (ventral area 6), which controls orofacial musculature. The cortex of the intermediate part of the inferior parietal lobule is linked with both areas 44 and 45. These findings demonstrate the posterior parietal and temporal connections of the ventrolateral frontal areas in the macaque monkey, which were adapted for various aspects of language production. These precursor circuits, which exist in both the nonlinguistic, nonhuman primate brain and the human brain, provide insight into the functional interactions between Broca's ventrolateral frontal region and posterior parietal and temporal association areas. The results shed new light on the prelinguistic precursor circuitry of Broca's region and offer clues as to why these areas were adapted for language use in the human brain.

title: MIRA-seq for DNA methylation analysis of CpG islands
text:
Objective:
Develop a robust method for whole genome analysis of DNA methylation.
Materials and Methods:
Whole genome analysis of DNA methylation involves the use of affinity-based approaches, such as enrichment using methyl-CpG-binding proteins. One of these methods, the methylated-CpG island recovery assay (MIRA), is based on the high affinity of the MBD2b-MBD3L1 complex for CpG-methylated DNA. Here, we provide a detailed description of MIRA and its combination with next-generation sequencing platforms (MIRA-seq).
Results:
We assessed the performance of MIRA-seq and compared the data with whole genome bisulfite sequencing.
Conclusion:
MIRA-seq is a reliable, genome-scale DNA methylation analysis platform for scoring DNA methylation differences at CpG-rich genomic regions. The method does not have any limitations imposed by primer or probe design and is cost-effective.

title: How many images are in an auditory scene?
text:
If an auditory scene contains numerous spatially discrete sound sources, how many sound sources can the auditory system process? Experiment I investigate how many speech sources can be localized simultaneously on the azimuth plane. Different words were played from multiple loudspeakers, and listeners reported the total number of sound sources and their individual locations.
In experiment II, we assessed the accuracy of locating a single speech source in a mix of multiple speech sources. An additional sound source was added to an existing set of sound sources, and the task was to localize that extra source. In experiment III, we replicated the setup and task of experiment I, but with tones instead of speech sources. The results showed that the maximum number of sound sources that listeners can perceive is roughly four spatially separated speech signals and three for tonal signals. As the total number of sound sources increases, localization errors grow. When four or more speech sources already exist, the accuracy in localizing an added source is nearly chance.

title: Mobilization of intracellular copper stores by the ctr2 vacuolar copper transporter.
text: Copper plays a vital role in various cellular processes such as signaling, transcription, protein trafficking, iron mobilization, neuropeptide maturation, and normal development. While there is extensive knowledge on the mobilization of ions like calcium, there is a lack of information on how eukaryotic cells release copper from intracellular stores. We have discovered a mechanism by which the Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ctr2 protein provides bioavailable copper through the mobilization of intracellular copper reserves. Unlike Ctr1, which has structural similarity to the plasma membrane copper importer, Ctr2 is localized to the vacuole membrane through microscopic and biochemical fractionation studies. Our findings demonstrate that Ctr2 mobilizes vacuolar copper stores in a manner reliant on conserved amino acid residues within the Ctr1 and Ctr2 copper transport family, with ctr2 mutants accumulating excessive vacuolar copper. Moreover, a Ctr2 mutant that is mislocalized to the plasma membrane promotes extracellular copper uptake, supporting a direct role for Ctr2 in copper transport across membranes. These studies reveal a novel mechanism for copper mobilization and suggest that organisms cope with copper deprivation by utilizing intracellular vesicular stores.

title: Peroxisomes Are Signaling Platforms for Antiviral Innate Immunity
text: Over time, peroxisomes have been identified as playing a crucial role in regulating various metabolic processes within mammalian cells. These organelles work in conjunction with mitochondria to modulate the metabolism of lipids and reactive oxygen species. However, while mitochondria have gained recognition as a key site for antiviral signal transduction, the role of peroxisomes in immune defense remained unexplored. Here, our findings reveal that the RIG-I-like receptor (RLR) adaptor protein MAVS is localized to both peroxisomes and mitochondria. We discovered that peroxisomal and mitochondrial MAVS act in a sequential manner to establish an antiviral cellular state. Upon viral infection, peroxisomal MAVS prompts the rapid, interferon-independent expression of defense factors that provide short-term protection. In contrast, mitochondrial MAVS activates an interferon-dependent signaling pathway with delayed kinetics, which amplifies and stabilizes the antiviral response. The interferon regulatory factor IRF1 plays a pivotal role in regulating MAVS-dependent signaling from peroxisomes. These findings validate the importance of peroxisomes as a site of antiviral signal transduction.

title: Two-sided confidence intervals for the single proportion: comparison of seven methods. Stat. Med
text:
Methods for estimating proportions with simple interval estimates often exhibit poor coverage and can result in inappropriate intervals. When evaluating these methods, consider the following criteria:
1. How close do the achieved coverage probabilities come to their nominated values?
2. Are the intervals located either too close to or too far from the center of the scale?
3. What is the expected width of the intervals?
4. Are there any inconsistencies, such as intervals that fall outside [0,1] or zero-width intervals?
5. How user-friendly are the methods, whether through tables, software, or formulae?

In this study, seven methods for estimating single proportions were evaluated on a sample of 96,000 parameter space points. Of these methods, intervals based on tail areas and simpler score methods are recommended for use. Additionally, methods are available to align either the minimum or mean coverage probability with the nominated 1 -alpha.

title: Nuclear accumulation of HDAC4 in ATM deficiency promotes neurodegeneration in ataxia-telangiectasia
text:
Ataxia telangiectasia is a genetic disease that affects the brain and causes progressive damage to neurons. We found that a protein called ATM, which is mutated in ataxia telangiectasia, leads to a buildup of another protein called HDAC4 in the nucleus of neurons. This buildup causes the neurons to deteriorate and die.
We discovered that HDAC4 works by controlling the expression of other proteins that are important for neuron function. When HDAC4 accumulates in the nucleus of neurons, it changes the way these other proteins are expressed, leading to problems with neuron function.
We also found that the activity of a protein called PP2A, which helps regulate HDAC4, is affected in ataxia telangiectasia. In these cases, PP2A is less active, leading to more HDAC4 buildup in the nucleus.
Our results suggest that the location of HDAC4 in the cell, both inside and outside the nucleus, is crucial for the development of ataxia telangiectasia. When HDAC4 is in the nucleus, it can lead to problems with neuron function and death. But when it is in the cytoplasm, it can help protect neurons from damage.
Overall, our study shows that the regulation of HDAC4 is a key factor in the development of ataxia telangiectasia, and that the location of this protein in the cell is important for its function.

title: Regulation and function of the E-cadherin/catenin complex in cells of the monocyte-macrophage lineage and DCs.
text: E-cadherin is chiefly recognized as an adherens junction protein that helps maintain the epithelial barrier function. In epithelial cells, the cytoplasmic tail of E-cadherin forms a dynamic complex with catenins, regulating several intracellular signal transduction pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, Rho GTPase, and NF-κB signaling. Recent research has unveiled a novel and crucial role for this adhesion molecule in the functions of mononuclear phagocytes. E-cadherin regulates the maturation and migration of Langerhans cells, and its ligation prevents the induction of a tolerogenic state in bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (DCs). This regulatory functionality of β-catenin may determine the balance between immunogenicity and tolerogenicity of DCs in vitro and in vivo. Additionally, E-cadherin-mediated fusion of alternatively activated macrophages and osteoclasts is also highlighted. Moreover, the E-cadherin ligands CD103 and KLRG1 are expressed on DC-, T-, and NK-cell subsets and contribute to their interaction with E-cadherin-expressing DCs and macrophages. This review covers the regulation, function, and significance of E-cadherin expression in these key players of the immune system.

title: Polymorphism and ligand dependent changes in human glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) function: allosteric rescue of loss of function mutation.
text: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a critical role in regulating insulin secretion and is a key therapeutic target for the treatment of type II diabetes. However, the regulation of GLP-1R function is complex, involving multiple endogenous peptides and exogenous agonists. We investigated the effects of 10 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the GLP-1R on its ligand binding, cell surface receptor expression, and signaling pathways. Our findings showed both ligand- and pathway-specific effects for multiple SNPs, with the most significant effect observed at the Metº99 variant, where there was selective loss of peptide-induced responses across all pathways examined, but preservation of response to the small molecule compound 2. In contrast, at the Cysº333 variant, peptide responses were preserved but there was attenuated response to compound 2. Interestingly, we found that the loss of peptide function at the Metº99 receptor variant could be allosterically rescued by compound 2, providing proof-of-principle evidence that allosteric drugs could be used to treat patients with this loss of function variant.

title: Neuronal circuitry mechanism regulating adult quiescent neural stem cell fate decision
text: Adult neurogenesis, derived from neural stem cells within specialized niches, is regulated by neuronal activity and experience.
