These cues, acting on the local microenvironment, control multiple stages of adult neurogenesis, including neural progenitor proliferation, new neuron maturation, synaptic integration, and survival. While the direct impact of local neuronal circuitry on adult neural stem cells remains unexplored, our study demonstrates that certain radial glia-like quiescent neural stem cells (RGLs) in the adult mouse hippocampus are responsive to the neurotransmitter γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) through γ2-subunit-containing GABAA receptors. Clonal analysis of individual RGLs revealed that conditional deletion of γ2 results in a rapid exit from quiescence and enhanced symmetrical self-renewal. RGLs are situated near terminals expressing 67-kDa glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD67) of parvalbumin-expressing (PV+) interneurons, which release GABA and regulate RGL activity. Optogenetic control of the activity of dentate PV+ interneurons, but not that of somatostatin-expressing or vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP)-expressing interneurons, can influence the RGL choice between quiescence and activation. Furthermore, PV+ interneuron activation restores RGL quiescence after social isolation, an experience that triggers RGL activation and symmetrical division. Our investigation uncovers a niche cell–signal–receptor triad and a local circuitry mechanism that govern the activation and self-renewal mode of quiescent adult neural stem cells in response to neuronal activity and experience.

title: Global vitamin D levels in relation to age, gender, skin pigmentation and latitude: an ecologic meta-regression analysis
text:
We conducted a meta-analysis of cross-sectional studies on the global status of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D). Our analysis included 394 studies, and we found that the mean 25(OH)D level was 54 nmol/l (95% CI: 52-57 nmol/l). We observed that women had marginally higher 25(OH)D levels than men, and Caucasians had higher levels than non-Caucasians. Moreover, 25(OH)D levels were higher in subjects aged >15 years than in younger subjects. Unadjusted analysis showed no significant decrease in 25(OH)D levels with latitude (slope of curve -0.03 ± 0.12 nmol/l per degree latitude north or south of the equator, p = 0.8). However, after adjusting for age, gender, and ethnicity, we found a significant decline in 25(OH)D levels with latitude for Caucasians (−0.69 ± 0.30 nmol/l per degree, p = 0.02), but not for non-Caucasians (0.03 ± 0.39 nmol/l per degree, p = 0.14). Our findings revealed a widespread global vitamin D insufficiency compared to proposed threshold levels.
Some of the changes I made include:
* Changing "We performed a meta-analysis of cross-sectional studies on serum 25(OH)D status globally" to "We conducted a meta-analysis of cross-sectional studies on the global status of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D)"
* Changing "Serum 25(OH)D levels on average were 54 nmol/l, were higher in women than men, and higher in Caucasians than in non-Caucasians" to "Our analysis included 394 studies, and we found that the mean 25(OH)D level was 54 nmol/l (95% CI: 52-57 nmol/l). We observed that women had marginally higher 25(OH)D levels than men, and Caucasians had higher levels than non-Caucasians."
* Changing "There was no trend in serum 25(OH)D level with latitude" to "Unadjusted analysis showed no significant decrease in 25(OH)D levels with latitude (slope of curve −0.03 ± 0.12 nmol/l per degree latitude north or south of the equator, p = 0.8)."
* Changing "We studied vitamin D status (expressed as serum 25-hydroxy-vitamin D [25(OH)D]) in native subjects worldwide" to "Our findings revealed a widespread global vitamin D insufficiency compared to proposed threshold levels."
* Changing "A total of 394 studies were included" to "Our analysis included 394 studies"

title: Identification and characterization of a novel monocyte/macrophage differentiation-dependent gene that is responsive to lipopolysaccharide, ceramide, and lysophosphatidylcholine.
text: Researchers have isolated a novel differentiation-dependent cDNA (DIF-2) from human mononuclear phagocytes using differential display. The full-length cDNA was cloned and sequenced, revealing a protein composed of 156 amino acids with an isoelectric point of 8.84. Study findings show that DIF-2 mRNA is expressed in freshly isolated monocytes, but its levels are significantly downregulated upon differentiation. A similar downregulation was also observed in normal hepatocytes compared to undifferentiated HepG2 cells. Interestingly, exposure to lipopolysaccharide, ceramide, and lysophosphatidylcholine all result in increased DIF-2 transcription, while only lysophosphatidylcholine exhibited a weaker upregulation of DIF-2 expression. Previous research has already identified a homologous DIF-2 gene in mouse fibroblasts, which was found to be a serum growth factor-inducible immediate early gene. The current study suggests that DIF-2 is a gene that is closely linked to differentiation processes and responds strongly to lipopolysaccharide, ceramide, and lysophosphatidylcholine.

title: A Novel 3-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase That Regulates Reproductive Development and Longevity
text: Emerging endogenous small molecule metabolites, such as bile acid-like steroids, are being explored as a novel means to influence animal health and life span. In the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans, the dafachronic acids (DAs) regulate developmental timing and longevity through the conserved nuclear hormone receptor DAF-12, which is homologous to mammalian sterol-regulated receptors LXR and FXR. By employing metabolic genetics, mass spectrometry, and biochemical techniques, we have identified new activities in DAs biosynthesis and characterized an evolutionarily conserved short chain dehydrogenase, DHS-16, as a novel 3-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase. DHS-16 regulates DAF-12 activity governing longevity in response to signals from the gonad, providing insight into the possible manipulation of longevity in other animals. Our elucidation of the C. elegans bile acid biosynthetic pathways has also revealed the potential for novel ligands as well as striking biochemical conservation to other animals, which could open up new avenues for exploring longevity in metazoans.

title: An Argonaute transports siRNAs from the cytoplasm to the nucleus.
text: Ribonucleoprotein complexes comprising Argonaute-like proteins and small regulatory RNAs are involved in a wide range of cellular processes. Some of these small RNAs are believed to function within the nucleus, and we used a genetic screen in Caenorhabditis elegans to identify factors essential for RNA interference (RNAi) in nuclei. Through this screen, we found the Argonaute protein NRDE-3 to be essential for nuclear RNAi. In the absence of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), NRDE-3 resides in the cytoplasm. However, when siRNAs are present, NRDE-3 binds them and redistributes to the nucleus, where it interacts with nuclear-localized nascent transcripts. This process highlights the ability of specific Argonaute proteins to transport specific classes of small regulatory RNAs to distinct cellular compartments, thereby regulating gene expression.

title: Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-Bisphosphate Functions as a Second Messenger that Regulates Cytoskeleton–Plasma Membrane Adhesion
text: The interactions between the plasma membrane and the cytoskeleton play a crucial role in determining various cellular functions such as cell shape, the formation of cell processes, cell movement, and endocytosis. In this study, we employ optical tweezers to measure the tethering forces between the plasma membrane and the cytoskeleton and demonstrate that plasma membrane phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) acts as a second messenger that regulates the adhesion energy between the cytoskeleton and the plasma membrane. By manipulating PIP2 levels, we find that receptor stimulation that degrades PIP2 reduces the adhesion energy, a process that can be mimicked by expressing PH domains that sequester PIP2 or by targeting a 5'-PIP2-phosphatase to the plasma membrane to selectively lower plasma membrane PIP2 concentrations. Our results suggest that changes in plasma membrane PIP2 levels control dynamic membrane functions and cell shape by modulating the adhesion between the actin-based cortical cytoskeleton and the plasma membrane.

title: Tissue-resident memory T cells: local specialists in immune defence
text: T cells play a vital role in protecting against infection and cancer. The ability of memory T cells to migrate throughout the body is crucial to their ability to provide immune protection, however, recent studies have shown that specializing certain memory T cells into distinct tissue-resident subsets can give the host enhanced local immunity. In recent years, there has been significant progress in our understanding of the development and function of tissue-resident T cells, revealing mechanisms that can potentially influence vaccine design. This review summarizes the major advances and emerging concepts in this field, outlines what is known about the differentiation and protective functions of tissue-resident memory T cells in different parts of the body, and highlights key areas that remain unknown.

title: Defective replication stress response inhibits lymphomagenesis and impairs lymphocyte reconstitution
text:
DNA replication stress has been shown to promote genome instability in cancer, although the exact role of the replication stress response in cancer development is still unclear. One key protein involved in this response is SMARCAL1, which stabilizes DNA replication forks and prevents replication fork collapse, thereby preventing DNA breaks and apoptosis. While the fork regression/remodeling functions of SMARCAL1 have been investigated, its in vivo functions in replication stress and cancer are still not well understood.
To fill this knowledge gap, we used a gamma radiation (IR)-induced replication stressT-cell lymphoma mouse model and observed a significant inhibition of lymphomagenesis in mice lacking one or both alleles of Smarcal1. Remarkably, approximately one-quarter of the Smarcal1-deficient mice did not develop tumors. Furthermore, we found that hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs) and developing thymocytes in Smarcal1-deficient mice exhibited increased DNA damage and apoptosis during the proliferation burst following IR, and an impaired ability to repopulate the thymus after IR. Additionally, mice lacking Smarcal1 showed significant HSPC defects when challenged to respond to other replication stress stimuli.
Our findings reveal the critical function of the DNA replication stress response, and specifically, Smarcal1, in hematopoietic cell survival and tumor development. Furthermore, our results provide important insights into the immunodeficiency observed in individuals with mutations in SMARCAL1, suggesting that it is an HSPC defect.

title: Human DNA methylomes at base resolution show widespread epigenomic differences
text:
DNA cytosine methylation is a central epigenetic modification that plays a crucial role in various cellular processes, including genome regulation, development, and disease. In this study, we present the first genome-wide, single-base-resolution maps of methylated cytosines in a mammalian genome, derived from both human embryonic stem cells and fetal fibroblasts. By comparing these maps with those of messenger RNA and small RNA components of the transcriptome, several histone modifications, and sites of DNA-protein interaction for key regulatory factors, we identified widespread differences in the composition and patterning of cytosine methylation between the two genomes.
Interestingly, nearly one-quarter of all methylation identified in embryonic stem cells was found in a non-CG context, suggesting that these cells may employ distinct methylation mechanisms to regulate gene expression. Analyzing methylation in non-CG contexts revealed enrichment in gene bodies and depletion in protein binding sites and enhancers. Notably, non-CG methylation disappeared upon differentiation of embryonic stem cells and was restored in induced pluripotent stem cells.
Our study identified hundreds of differentially methylated regions proximal to genes involved in pluripotency and differentiation, and found significant reductions in methylation levels in fibroblasts, which corresponded to lower transcriptional activity. These reference epigenomes provide a solid foundation for future studies exploring the role of DNA cytosine methylation in human disease and development.

title: Laparoscopic adhesiolysis in patients with chronic abdominal pain: a blinded randomised controlled multi-centre trial.
text:
BACKGROUND: Laparoscopic adhesiolysis for chronic abdominal pain is a controversial and evidence-free treatment. Our study aimed to investigate whether laparoscopic adhesiolysis produces significant pain relief and improvement in quality of life in patients with adhesions and chronic abdominal pain.
METHODS: We enrolled 116 patients with chronic abdominal pain attributed to adhesions, and excluded other potential causes. Those who had adhesions confirmed during diagnostic laparoscopy were randomly assigned to either laparoscopic adhesiolysis or no treatment. Patient, assessor, and outcome evaluator ignorance of treatment allocation was ensured. Pain was assessed using visual analogue score (VAS), pain change score, analgesic use, and quality of life score at 12-month follow-up. Analysis was by intention to treat.
FINDINGS: Of the 100 patients randomly allocated to either laparoscopic adhesiolysis (52) or no treatment (48), both groups demonstrated substantial pain relief and improved quality of life. However, there was no significant difference between the groups in terms of pain relief (mean change from baseline VAS score at 12 months: difference 3 points, p=0.53; 95% CI -7 to 13).
INTERPRETATION: Although laparoscopic adhesiolysis provides relief from chronic abdominal pain, it is not more effective than diagnostic laparoscopy alone. Therefore, laparoscopic adhesiolysis cannot be recommended as a treatment for adhesions in patients with chronic abdominal pain.

title: Insulin Signaling and Dietary Restriction Differentially Influence the Decline of Learning and Memory with Age
text:
One of the most significant age-related cognitive declines is memory loss, which can have a profound impact on an individual's quality of life. While research has identified factors that promote longevity, the effects of these factors on learning and memory in older adulthood are not well understood. Here, we explore the effects of the C. elegans Insulin/IGF-1 receptor mutant daf-2 and a dietary restriction (DR) model, the eat-2 mutants, on memory performance in young and old adulthood.
Our findings reveal that daf-2 mutants exhibit improved memory performance in early adulthood but maintain learning ability better than other worms with age, unexpectedly showing no extension in long-term memory with age. In contrast, eat-2 mutants, which are a model of DR, demonstrate impaired long-term memory in young adulthood but maintain this level of memory longer than other worms with age.
Interestingly, we discovered that crh-1, the C. elegans homolog of the CREB transcription factor, is required for long-term associative memory, but not for learning or short-term memory. Our results also indicate that the expression of crh-1 declines with age and varies in the longevity mutants, and CREB expression and activity are correlated with memory performance.
Our research suggests that specific longevity treatments have acute and long-term effects on cognitive functions that decline with age by regulating rate-limiting genes necessary for learning and memory. These findings have important implications for the development of interventions aimed at mitigating age-related cognitive decline.

title: Unique response pathways are established by allosteric interactions among nuclear hormone receptors
text: Heterodimerization is a widespread mechanism among eukaryotic transcription factors, with the 9-cis retinoic acid receptor (RXR) serving as a common partner for various nuclear receptors, including the thyroid hormone receptor (T3R) and retinoic acid receptor (RAR). This raises the question of whether these complexes exhibit dual hormonal sensitivity. To investigate, we devised a strategy to compare the transcriptional properties of each receptor alone or in a heterodimer with RXR. Our findings reveal that the intrinsic binding properties of RXR are masked in T3R-RXR and RAR-RXR heterodimers, contrastingly, RXR functions as an inactive cofactor for the non-DNA-binding orphan receptors NGFI-B/Nurr1 when heterodimerized. Heterodimerization of RXR with constitutively active NGFI-B/Nurr1 creates a novel, hormone-dependent complex. Our results suggest that allosteric interactions within heterodimers give rise to complexes with distinct properties. We propose that allostery is a crucial feature underlying the generation of diversity in hormone response networks.

title: Midlife and Late‐Life Vascular Risk Factors and White Matter Microstructural Integrity: The Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Neurocognitive Study
text:
BACKGROUND: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) is a non-invasive method of assessing white matter (WM) microstructural integrity, which appears to detect injury earlier than conventional MRI techniques. However, the factors that contribute to poor WM microstructural integrity in older adults have yet to be determined. This study aimed to investigate the association between vascular risk factors in midlife and late life and measures of late-life WM microstructural integrity.
METHODS: Data from 1851 participants in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC) were used, who underwent 3-T magnetic resonance imaging, including DTI, as part of the ARIC Neurocognitive Study (ARIC-NCS). The association between lipids, glucose, and blood pressure from the baseline ARIC visit (1987-1989, ages 44-65, midlife) and visit 5 of ARIC (2011-2013, ages 67-90, late life, concurrent with ARIC-NCS) with regional and overall WM mean diffusivity and fractional anisotropy obtained at ARIC visit 5 was examined for ARIC participants. Additionally, the influence of WM hyperintensity volumes on these associations was considered.
RESULTS: Elevated blood pressure in both midlife and late life, as well as elevated glucose in midlife but not late life, were found to be associated with poorer late-life WM microstructural integrity. These associations were independent of the degree of WM hyperintensity and appeared stronger for individuals with the least amount of WM hyperintensity. There was limited support for an adverse association between lipids and WM microstructural integrity.
CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that hypertension in both midlife and late life, as well as elevated glucose in midlife, are associated with poorer WM microstructural integrity in late life. These findings highlight the importance of addressing vascular risk factors in midlife to promote better WM health in late life.

title: KRAS gene amplification and overexpression but not mutation associates with aggressive and metastatic endometrial cancer
text:
BACKGROUND About three-quarters of endometrial carcinomas are diagnosed at an early stage, yet 15-20% of these patients experience recurrence despite systemic therapies. While KRAS mutations have been linked to tumorigenesis in various human cancers, there is limited understanding of their clinical significance in endometrial carcinomas.
METHODS We conducted a comprehensive and integrated analysis of genome-wide expression related to KRAS mutations and copy-number alterations in primary and metastatic endometrial carcinoma lesions, using a primary investigation set and clinical validation set consisting of 414 primary tumors and 61 metastatic lesions.
RESULTS Approximately 3% of primary lesions and 18% of metastatic lesions showed amplification and gain of KRAS, which significantly correlated with poor outcome, high International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage, non-endometrioid subtype, high grade, aneuploidy, receptor loss, and high KRAS mRNA levels. In contrast, KRAS mutations were present in 14.7% of primary lesions without an increase in metastatic lesions, and were not associated with outcome but were significantly linked to endometrioid subtype, low grade, and obesity.
CONCLUSION These findings suggest that KRAS amplification and KRAS mRNA expression, which increase from primary to metastatic lesions, play a role in endometrial carcinoma disease progression.

title: Hyperhomocysteinemia and atherosclerotic vascular disease: pathophysiology, screening, and treatment. off.
text: Recent research has highlighted hyperhomocysteinemia as a significant risk factor for atherosclerotic vascular disease. This review focuses on the metabolism of homocysteine, the underlying causes of hyperhomocysteinemia, the pathophysiological effects of this condition, and epidemiological studies linking homocysteine levels to vascular disease. Screening for hyperhomocysteinemia should be considered for patients at high risk for vascular disease or those with abnormalities in homocysteine metabolism. Patients with homocysteine levels of 14 micromol/L or higher should be treated for primary prevention of vascular disease, while those with levels of 11 micromol/L or higher should be treated for secondary prevention. Treatment is most easily administrated through folic acid supplements (400-1000 microg) and high-potency multivitamins containing at least 400 microg of folate. In some cases, higher doses of folic acid and cyanocobalamin supplements may be necessary. Until more definitive clinical trial data becomes available, these conservative recommendations offer a safe, effective, and evidence-based approach to diagnosing, evaluating, and managing patients with hyperhomocysteinemia.

title: Best--worst scaling: What it can do for health care research and how to do it.
text: Statements asserting that "quality of care is more highly valued than waiting time" cannot be validated or refuted through traditional discrete choice experiments (DCEs) using utility parameters. While best-worst scaling allows respondents to perform a different choice task, there are several nuances to consider when designing and analyzing a best-worst choice experiment. This paper provides guidance on how to aggregate and analyze such data, and illustrates the richer insights that can be gained by incorporating best-worst tasks using a quality of life pilot study.

title: Genetic variants and non-genetic factors predict circulating vitamin D levels in Hispanic and non-Hispanic White women: the Breast Cancer Health Disparities Study.
text: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified common genetic variations in or near the GC, CYP2R1, CYP24A1, and NADSYN1/DHCR7 genes as being associated with circulating levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] in European populations. To confirm these findings, we analyzed six selected variants from these regions and their relationship with circulating 25(OH)D levels in 1,605 Hispanic women (629 U.S. Hispanics and 976 Mexicans) and 354 non-Hispanic White (NHW) women. We also assessed potential interactions between these variants and known non-genetic predictors of 25(OH)D levels, including body mass index (BMI), sunlight exposure, and vitamin D intake from diet and supplements. The minor alleles of the two GC polymorphisms (rs7041 and rs2282679) were significantly associated with lower 25(OH)D levels in both Hispanic and NHW women. The CYP2R1 polymorphism, rs2060793, was also significantly associated with 25(OH)D levels in both groups. However, no significant associations were found for the polymorphisms in the CYP24A1 gene. In Hispanic controls, 25(OH)D levels were significantly associated with the rs12785878T and rs1790349G haplotype in the NADSYN1/DHCR7 region. Interactions between the GC rs2282679 and BMI and between rs12785878 and time spent in outdoor activities were observed. These findings provide further support for the role of common genetic variants in influencing individual variations in circulating 25(OH)D levels. The observed interactions between SNPs and non-genetic factors warrant further confirmation.

title: Generation and characterization of methyl-lysine histone antibodies.
text:
Chapter Summary:
This chapter details the development and characterization of rabbit polyclonal antibodies targeting methylated histone H3-K9. The following protocols are provided: peptide design, rabbit immunizations, and quality controls for methyl-lysine histone antibodies. The in vivo characterization of these antibodies is then conducted using indirect immunofluorescence on wild-type and Suv39h-deficient mouse cells.
Histones are the primary components of nucleosomes, and their amino-terminal tails undergo various post-translational modifications, including acetylation, phosphorylation, methylation, ubiquitination, and ADP-ribosylation. Histones also play a crucial role in regulating gene expression by controlling access to the underlying nucleosomal template.
The development of high-quality, position-specific methyl-lysine histone antibodies is essential for further decoding of epigenetic information, which is indexed by specific methylation states of selected lysine residues in histone amino-termini. A comparative analysis reveals significant variations in the specificity and avidity of available methyl-lysine histone antibodies, emphasizing the need for comprehensive quality controls to ensure accurate experimental interpretation despite the intricate nature of histone lysine methylation.

title: The Hallmarks of Aging
text:
Aging is characterized by a progressive decline in physical function and increased susceptibility to death, primarily due to the accumulation of cellular damage over time. This deterioration predisposes individuals to a wide range of age-related diseases, including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular conditions, and neurodegenerative disorders. Recent advances in aging research have shed light on the complex genetic and biochemical mechanisms that control the aging process, revealing that the rate of aging can be influenced by genetic pathways and conserved processes across different organisms. Based on these findings, this Review identifies nine hallmarks of aging that are common across various species, with a particular focus on mammalian aging. These hallmarks include:
1. Genomic instability
2. Telomere attrition
3. Epigenetic alterations
4. Loss of proteostasis
5. Deregulated nutrient sensing
6. Mitochondrial dysfunction
7. Cellular senescence
8. Stem cell exhaustion
9. Altered intercellular communication.
Disentangling the interconnected relationships between these hallmarks and their relative contributions to aging is a major challenge, with the ultimate goal of identifying viable pharmaceutical targets to improve human health during aging, with minimal side effects.

title: A sensitive mass spectrometry platform identifies metabolic changes of life history traits in C. elegans
text: Abnormal nutrient metabolism is a hallmark of aging, and researchers are rapidly uncovering the underlying genetic and nutritional framework, particularly using the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans as a model organism. However, the direct metabolic consequences of perturbations in the life history of C. elegans remain to be fully understood. Recent advances in metabolomics have led to the optimization and validation of a sensitive mass spectrometry platform for identifying major metabolite classes in worms. This platform allowed for the detection of over 600 metabolites in a sample of 2500 worms, revealing marked changes in fatty acids, amino acids, and phospholipids during various stages of worm life history. These changes were independent of the germ line and were found to be controlled by the metabolic regulator AAK-2/AMPK in lipid metabolism. The study also showed that dietary intervention significantly influenced worm metabolite profiles, with specific regulation depending on the metabolite class. These MS-based methods are powerful tools for performing worm metabolomics studies on aging and metabolism.

title: Characterisation of antibiotic prescriptions for acute respiratory tract infections in Danish general practice: a retrospective registry based cohort study
text:
Inappropriate use of antibiotics is contributing to the growing problem of antimicrobial resistance. Despite guidelines issued in Denmark to promote rational antibiotic prescribing for acute respiratory tract infections in general practice, it is unclear if these recommendations are being followed. To better understand antibiotic prescription patterns for these infections, researchers analyzed electronic prescriptions labeled with clinical indications from Danish general practice.
They found that between July 2012 and June 2013, there were 456,532 antibiotic prescriptions issued for acute respiratory tract infections, with pneumonia being the most common indication (39%). Penicillin V was the most commonly prescribed antibiotic agent (58%), followed by macrolides (18%) and amoxicillin (15%). Interestingly, the use of second-line agents increased with age for all indications, and comprised more than 40% of prescriptions in patients aged >75 years. Women were also more often prescribed antibiotics, regardless of clinical indication.
These findings highlight the need for quality improvement strategies to address overuse of second-line antibiotics, particularly for pneumonia, acute otitis media, and acute rhinosinusitis. The study demonstrates the importance of monitoring antibiotic prescription patterns to ensure appropriate use and prevent resistance. The over-use of antibiotics, particularly so-called 'second-line' agents such as amoxicillin, increases resistance and may lead to a potentially catastrophic scenario where antibiotics are no longer effective. Further analysis of prescriptions given by out-of-hours clinics is also warranted.

title: Lack of Skeletal Muscle IL-6 Affects Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Activity at Rest and during Prolonged Exercise
text: Researchers studied how a protein called pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) is affected by a gene called interleukin-6 (IL-6) in skeletal muscle during exercise. Skeletal muscle-specific IL-6 knockout (IL-6 MKO) mice and normal mice (controls) exercised on a treadmill for different lengths of time, and the researchers measured the activity of PDH at rest and during exercise. They found that the activity of PDH was higher in IL-6 MKO mice than in controls at rest and during exercise, especially at longer exercise durations. The researchers also found that the activity of PDH was higher in IL-6 MKO mice than in controls at rest, but this difference was not seen during exercise. The researchers concluded that skeletal muscle IL-6 contributes to the regulation of PDH at rest and during prolonged exercise, and that this may help explain why muscle IL-6 normally dampens carbohydrate utilization during prolonged exercise.

title: Clinical and pathologic characteristics of patients with BRCA-positive and BRCA-negative breast cancer.
text: Mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes elevate an individual's likelihood of developing breast cancer. In this study, we examined the differences in tumor pathological features and clinical characteristics between patients with and without BRCA mutations in 491 women with breast cancer. Through a retrospective analysis of medical records, we discovered that BRCA-positive patients were younger at diagnosis compared to BRCA-negative patients. Additionally, triple-negative breast cancer was diagnosed more frequently in BRCA1-positive patients compared to BRCA2-positive patients. Furthermore, BRCA1 mutation carriers had higher nuclear grades than the other two groups (P < .001). These findings suggest that tumors associated with BRCA1 mutations can be grouped into two categories: triple-negative and non-triple-negative groups. Future studies should aim to determine whether BRCA1 mutation carriers with triple-negative breast cancer respond better to treatment than BRCA-negative patients with similar tumor pathology.

title: Interferons: Success in anti-viral immunotherapy.
text: The interferons (IFNs) are glycoproteins with potent antiviral activities that serve as one of the initial lines of defense against invading pathogens. These proteins are categorized into three groups, Type I, II, and III IFNs, based on the structure of their receptors on the cell surface. Due to their capacity to modulate immune responses, they have become a promising therapeutic option for managing chronic virus infections. In combination with other drugs, Type I IFNs are considered the "standard of care" for suppressing Hepatitis C (HCV) and Hepatitis B (HBV) infections, while Type III IFN has shown encouraging results as a treatment for HCV infection in phase III clinical trials. However, despite their effectiveness, using IFNs as a treatment is not without caution. As powerful cytokines, IFNs can affect a wide range of cell types, leading to unpleasant symptoms in patients. As a result, constant monitoring is necessary for patients receiving IFN treatment to achieve the treatment goals of suppressing virus infection and maintaining quality of life.

title: Genetic analysis of human obesity in an Italian sample.
text: An examination of the genetic factors contributing to obesity was conducted on a sample of nuclear families from Aosta, located in northern Italy. The sample consisted of the parents and siblings of obese elementary school children identified during a preliminary screening, as well as a similar number of non-obese children and their nuclear families. The total number of families included in the analysis was 67 from the obese group and 112 from the non-obese group. Various statistical tests were applied to determine the genetic influence on obesity and to investigate the presence of a dominant major gene with a weak effect. Our findings indicate that genetic factors are indeed present in the development of obesity. By using different statistical techniques, we found evidence of a dominant major gene with a modest effect on obesity.

title: The non-coding RNA landscape of human hematopoiesis and leukemia
text: Non-coding RNAs have emerged as pivotal regulators of gene expression and cell fate decisions in the human hematopoietic system, but their expression patterns and regulatory functions during both normal and malignant hematopoiesis remain inadequately understood. To address this gap in knowledge, we have generated a comprehensive resource that delineates the non-coding RNA landscape of the human hematopoietic system. Using highly specific non-coding RNA expression profiles for each blood cell population, we identified unique fingerprint non-coding RNAs, such as LINC00173 in granulocytes, and assigned these to critical regulatory circuits involved in blood homeostasis. By incorporating acute myeloid leukemia samples into the landscape, we further uncovered prognostically relevant non-coding RNA stem cell signatures shared between acute myeloid leukemia blasts and healthy hematopoietic stem cells. Our findings underscore the essential role of the non-coding transcriptome in the formation and maintenance of the human blood hierarchy, while highlighting the relatively unexamined function of long non-coding RNAs in haematopoiesis and leukemogenesis.

title: Incidence and risk of central nervous system metastases as site of first recurrence in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer treated with adjuvant trastuzumab.
text: BACKGROUND: The central nervous system (CNS) is a common site of recurrence in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer, even after exposure to adjuvant trastuzumab therapy. To determine the risk of CNS metastases as the first site of recurrence in these patients, we conducted a comprehensive meta-analysis of randomized trials. METHODS: We included randomized trials of adjuvant trastuzumab administered for 1 year to patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who reported CNS metastases as the first site of disease recurrence. Using fixed-effects inverse variance and random-effects models, we calculated the incidence, relative risk (RR), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of CNS metastases in trastuzumab-treated and control groups. RESULTS: A total of 9020 patients were included in our analysis. The incidence of CNS metastases as the first site of disease recurrence was 2.56% (95% CI 2.07% to 3.01%) in trastuzumab-treated patients compared to 1.94% (95% CI 1.54% to 2.38%) in control patients. The RR of the CNS as the first site of relapse in trastuzumab-treated patients was 1.35 (95% CI 1.02-1.78, P = 0.038). The ratio of CNS metastases to total number of recurrence events was 16.94% (95% CI 10.85% to 24.07%) and 8.33% (95% CI 6.49% to 10.86%) for the trastuzumab-treated and control groups, respectively. No significant differences were observed based on trastuzumab schedule or median follow-up time. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that adjuvant trastuzumab therapy is associated with an increased risk of CNS metastases as the site of first recurrence in HER2-positive breast cancer patients.

title: Neutrophils in the activation and regulation of innate and adaptive immunity
text: Neutrophils were once perceived as the last line of defense in an acute inflammatory response, primarily responsible for eliminating extracellular pathogens. However, recent research has expanded their repertoire of functions. The newfound array of effector molecules in a neutrophil's arsenal includes a variety of cytokines, extracellular traps, and humoral arm immune system molecules. Additionally, neutrophils play a key role in activating, regulating, and mediating the functions of both innate and adaptive immune cells. As such, they have a significant part to play in the development and progression of various diseases, such as infections caused by intracellular pathogens, autoimmune disorders, chronic inflammation, and cancer.

title: Functions of DNA methylation: islands, start sites, gene bodies and beyond
text: DNA methylation is often characterized as an epigenetic "silencing" mark, a function that was initially proposed in the 1970s. However, with the advancement of genome-scale mapping techniques, we can now investigate DNA methylation in various genomic contexts, including transcriptional start sites without CpG islands, gene bodies, regulatory elements, and repeat sequences. As we delve deeper into the complexities of DNA methylation, it appears that its function can vary depending on the context, and the relationship between DNA methylation and transcription is more intricate than initially thought. A deeper understanding of the roles of DNA methylation is crucial for interpreting changes in this mark that are observed in diseases such as cancer.

title: Metaplasia and transdifferentiation: from pure biology to the clinic
text: The process of transforming one tissue type into another is a well-established phenomenon in developmental biology, where the principles of cellular differentiation and lineage determination are understood. Although these transformations are rare in nature, we can now conceive of intentionally reprogramming cells from one tissue type to another through the manipulation of transcription factors. This novel approach has the potential to yield novel therapeutic strategies for a wide range of human diseases.

title: Pioglitazone Use and Risk of Bladder Cancer and Other Common Cancers in Persons With Diabetes.
text:
The study examines the association between pioglitazone use and the risk of various cancers in individuals with diabetes. The study population consists of 193,099 patients aged 40 years or older, of whom 34,181 received pioglitazone (median duration of use was 2.8 years). The primary outcomes of interest are the incidences of 10 different types of cancer, including bladder, prostate, female breast, lung/bronchus, endometrial, colon, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, pancreas, kidney/renal pelvis, rectum, and melanoma.
The study found that:
1. Pioglitazone use was not associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer, although the study could not exclude a small increased risk.
2. The use of pioglitazone was associated with an increased risk of prostate cancer (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) = 1.13; 95% CI = 1.02-1.26) and pancreatic cancer (adjusted HR = 1.41; 95% CI = 1.16-1.71).
3. The crude incidence of prostate and pancreatic cancer in pioglitazone users was higher than in non-users (453.3 vs 449.3 and 81.1 vs 48.4 per 100,000 person-years, respectively).
4. No clear patterns of risk were observed for any cancer according to time since initiation, duration, or dose of pioglitazone use.

The study suggests that pioglitazone may not be associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer, although a small increase could not be ruled out. However, pioglitazone use is associated with an increased risk of prostate and pancreatic cancer, which merits further investigation to determine whether these findings are causal or due to chance, residual confounding, or reverse causality.

title: Embryonic stem cell lines from human blastocysts: somatic differentiation in vitro
text: We describe the process of deriving pluripotent embryonic stem (ES) cells from human blastocysts. Two diploid ES cell lines have been cultured in vitro for extended periods, maintaining expression of markers typical of pluripotent primate cells. Human ES cells express the transcription factor Oct-4, which is essential for the development of pluripotent cells in mice. When transplanted into SCID mice, both lines have generated teratomas containing cells from all three embryonic germ layers. Similarly, in vitro differentiation of these cells leads to the formation of extraembryonic and somatic cell lineages. Furthermore, neural progenitor cells can be isolated from differentiating ES cell cultures and induced to differentiate into mature neurons. Notably, ES cells provide a valuable tool for studying early human embryology, serving as an investigative platform for discovering novel growth factors and therapeutic agents, and potentially serving as a source of cells for transplantation therapy.

title: Multipoint Kras oncogene mutations potentially indicate mucinous carcinoma on the entire spectrum of mucinous ovarian neoplasms
text: Kras mutations are a common occurrence in many human neoplasms, including those affecting the ovary. In this study, we aimed to investigate the Kras mutational status along the histological continuum from normal ovaries to the development of benign, borderline, and malignant ovarian mucinous neoplasms. We examined 7 cases of normal ovarian tissue, as well as 41 cases of malignant, 10 cases of borderline, and 7 cases of benign mucinous ovarian tumors. The prevalence of Kras mutations in normal ovarian tissue was 0% (n=0/7), while the prevalence in benign, borderline, and malignant mucinous neoplasms was 57.14% (n=4/7), 90% (n=9/10), and 75.61% (n=31/41), respectively. We identified six cases with novel Kras mutations not previously described in the COSMIC database, including A11V (n=3), V14I (n=2), and A11T (n=1) in mucinous carcinomas, and A11V (n=1) in a mucinous borderline tumor. Our findings suggest that Kras mutation is an essential event in the ovarian mucinous adenoma-borderline tumor-carcinoma sequence, as increasing numbers of Kras mutations have been shown to be the strongest predictor of definitive malignancy in ovarian mucinous neoplasms.

title: Identification and distinct regulation of yeast TATA box-containing genes.
text: Although one of the earliest identified eukaryotic transcriptional regulatory elements, the native TATA box sequence remains elusive. Using criteria associated with TATA boxes, we analyzed several Saccharomyces genomes and arrived at the consensus TATA(A/T)A(A/T)(A/G). Approximately 20% of yeast genes contain a TATA box. Interestingly, TATA box-containing genes are more likely to respond to stress, be highly regulated, and preferentially utilize the SAGA complex rather than TFIID compared to TATA-less promoters. The transcriptional regulation of yeast appears to be mechanistically bipolar, possibly reflecting a need to balance inducible stress-related responses with constitutive housekeeping functions.

title: IL6 derived from cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes chemoresistance via CXCR7 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
text: Various elements within the tumor microenvironment play a crucial role in the development of drug resistance in many cancer types. To investigate the factors involved in chemoresistance in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), we examined the molecular mechanisms at play. Our findings revealed that interleukin 6 (IL6), predominantly originating from cancer-associated fibroblasts, is the most significant driver of chemoresistance in ESCC. IL6 upregulates C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 7 (CXCR7) expression through the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3/nuclear factor-κB pathway. Notably, CXCR7 knockdown resulted in the inhibition of IL6-induced proliferation and chemoresistance. Moreover, silencing CXCR7 significantly decreased gene expression associated with stemness, chemoresistance, and epithelial–mesenchymal transition, as well as suppressed the proliferation ability of ESCC cells in three-dimensional culture systems and angiogenesis assays. Furthermore, in clinical samples, ESCC patients with high expression of CXCR7 and IL6 exhibited poorer overall survival and progression-free survival following cisplatin treatment after surgery. These results suggest that targeting the IL6–CXCR7 axis may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for ESCC treatment.

title: Myelodysplastic syndromes: revisiting the role of the bone marrow microenvironment in disease pathogenesis
text: Myelodysplastic syndromes are a diverse group of diseases marked by inefficient blood cell production and a predisposition to leukemic transformation. Understanding their development requires an examination of the intricate interplay between abnormal hematopoietic cells and their surrounding microenvironment. While the role of niche cells in disease progression is still unclear, recent advances in animal models and the study of the hematopoietic stem cell niche have provided valuable insights into this complex relationship. The data suggest that the microenvironment can significantly contribute to myelodysplasia and myeloproliferative disorders, bolstering the case for targeting mesenchymal-hematopoietic interactions as a potential therapeutic strategy.

title: SMC complexes differentially compact mitotic chromosomes according to genomic context
text: The structural maintenance of chromosomes (SMC) protein complexes play a crucial role in determining the conformation of chromosomes. Using a combination of Hi-C data and polymer modeling, we investigated the functions of cohesin and condensin, two highly conserved SMC complexes, in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. While cohesin is typically known for co-aligning sister chromatids, our findings reveal a more nuanced role for the complex in mitotic chromosome organization. In budding yeast, cohesin is primarily responsible for compacting the mitotic chromosome arms, an activity that can be fully explained by cis-looping of chromatin through polymer simulations. In contrast, condensin is dispensable for chromosome compaction along the arm regions, but instead, plays a targeted role in compacting the rDNA proximal regions and promoting resolution of peri-centromeric regions. Our results suggest that the conserved function of SMC complexes is to form chromatin loops, and that different SMC-dependent looping activities are selectively utilized to appropriately compact chromosomes.

title: Patterns of chlamydia testing in different settings and implications for wider STI diagnosis and care: a probability sample survey of the British population
text:
Background: The widespread implementation of chlamydia testing in non-specialist and community settings in the UK has resulted in many individuals receiving a chlamydia test without being offered comprehensive testing for other sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and HIV. To better understand the need for additional STI diagnostic services, we investigated sexual behavior among individuals who received a chlamydia test in different settings.
Methods: We conducted a probability sample survey of the British population between 2010 and 2012 (the third National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles). We analyzed weighted data on chlamydia testing (past year), including the location of the most recent test and diagnoses (past 5 years) from women and men aged 16-44 who reported having at least one sexual partner in the past year (4992 women and 3406 men).
Results: Of the 26.8% of women and 16.7% of men who reported receiving a chlamydia test in the past year, 28.4% of women and 41.2% of men tested in genitourinary medicine (GUM), 41.1% and 20.7% of women and men, respectively, tested in general practice (GP), and the remainder tested in other non-GUM settings. Women who tested outside of GUM were more likely to be older, in a relationship, and to live in rural areas. Individuals who tested outside of GUM reported fewer risk behaviors, but 11.0% of women and 6.8% of men tested in GP and 13.2% of women and 9.6% of men tested in other non-GUM settings reported "unsafe sex," defined as two or more sexual partners without using a condom with any partner in the past year. Individuals who received treatment for chlamydia outside of GUM in the past 5 years were less likely to report an HIV test in that time frame (women: 54.5% vs 74.1% in GUM; men: 23.9% vs 65.8% in GUM).
Conclusion: Most chlamydia testing occurred in non-GUM settings, among populations reporting fewer risk behaviors. However, there is a need to provide comprehensive STI care to the significant minority at higher risk.

title: Treatment of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: role of AMPK.
text: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) has emerged as a global health crisis and a significant risk factor for the development of insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), and hepatic cellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite the prevalence of NAFLD, current treatments are limited to lifestyle interventions such as exercise and weight loss. However, over the past decade, numerous experimental compounds have shown promise in improving NAFLD in animal models, with many of these therapeutics increasing the activity of the cellular energy sensor AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). AMPK activity is reduced by inflammation, obesity, and diabetes, making AMPK activation a viable therapeutic strategy for NAFLD. This review proposes three primary mechanisms by which AMPK activation may improve NAFLD and examines the mechanisms by which AMPK is activated. Additionally, the review identifies 27 studies that have used AMPK activators to reduce NAFLD and highlights future considerations for studies examining the relationship between AMPK and NAFLD.

title: Microenvironment-dependent growth of pre-neoplastic and malignant plasma cells in humanized mice
text: The majority of human cancers, including multiple myeloma, originate from a precursor state. Unfortunately, there is a lack of in vivo models that allow for the study of human precursor cells within the bone marrow microenvironment, interacting with non-malignant cells. To address this gap, we generated genetically humanized mice that enabled the growth of primary human precursor and malignant plasma cells together with non-malignant cells in vivo. Notably, growth was mostly confined to the bone marrow, mirroring the tumor distribution observed in patients with myeloma. Xenografts derived from these cells also captured the genomic complexity of the parental tumors and revealed additional somatic mutations. Moreover, xenografts derived from patients with preneoplastic gammopathy exhibited progressive growth, suggesting that the clinical stability of these lesions may partly be due to extrinsic growth controls. These findings demonstrate a novel approach to investigate the entire range of human plasma cell neoplasia and highlight the power of humanized models for comprehending the functional diversity of human tumors.

title: Effect of activated charcoal hemoperfusion on renal function in patients with paraquat poisoning.
text: The current investigation examined 19 patients diagnosed with paraquat (PQ) poisoning retrospectively, with the goal of evaluating the impact of activated charcoal hemoperfusion on renal function and PQ elimination. Our findings revealed that 7 patients succumbed to poisoning, while 12 survived. Non-oliguric renal failure occurred in all of the deceased patients. Among the surviving patients, 10 exhibited normal renal function, while 2 developed non-oliguric renal failure. There existed a linear correlation between the concentration of paraquat in the plasma and urine prior to and during activated charcoal hemoperfusion, as evidenced by the following equation: Y = 0.5820 + 1.7348X (R2 = 0.678; F = 35.768; P < 0.0001) before hemoperfusion, and Y = 0.6827 + 1.2649X (R2 = 0.626; F = 50.308; P < 0.0001) during hemoperfusion. These results suggest that in patients with normal renal function, the elimination kinetics of PQ by the kidneys are solely related to the plasma PQ concentration. Activated charcoal hemoperfusion had a limited impact on preventing acute kidney injury in patients with severe PQ poisoning.

title: Diabetes-induced effects on cardiomyocytes in chick embryonic heart micromass and mouse embryonic D3 differentiated stem cells.
text: Pregnancy-related diabetes, also known as gestational diabetes, poses a significant medical challenge due to the potential risks to both the developing fetus and the pregnant woman. Studies have shown that the underlying mechanisms of diabetic embryopathy are complex and involve various teratogenic factors. To investigate the cardiotoxic effects of hyperglycemia and hyperketonemia, two in vitro models were used in this study: primary chick embryonic cardiomyocytes and stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. The results showed adverse effects in both systems, including changes in beating activity, cell viability, protein content, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, DNA damage, and stem cell migration. The diabetic formulae used caused an increase in DNA damage and a decline in cell migration in mouse embryonic stem cells. These findings suggest that expecting mothers and maternity staff should closely monitor glycemic levels prior to conception to prevent potential adverse effects. Additionally, this study supports the recommendation of using antioxidants during pregnancy to prevent DNA damage caused by ROS production, which may contribute to heart defects and other developmental abnormalities.

title: Motion magnification
text:
We unveil a groundbreaking technique called motion magnification, which acts as a high-powered microscope for visualizing minute movements in video sequences. This innovative method amplifies subtle deformations that would otherwise go unnoticed, offering unparalleled insights into the behavior of load-bearing structures, the intricate movements of people, and the flexible adjustments of "rigid" structures under momentary pressure.
To achieve motion magnification, we employ a multistep process that begins with meticulous motion measurement. By analyzing the trajectories of feature points across a series of frames, we identify areas of notable motion and group pixels according to their position, color, and motion patterns. This allows us to isolate individual pixels that exhibit similar motion characteristics, which we refer to as "motion similarity."
The next step is to calculate a novel motion similarity measure that correlates the movements of these pixels over time. This novel measure is instrumental in grouping even the smallest motions according to their temporal relationship, which often reveals the underlying physical causes. By identifying outliers and isolating them from the rest of the pixels, we can discern the residual motion that cannot be explained by our layered motion model.
The principle of motion magnification lies in the ability to amplify the selected layer of motion by a specified amount. This allows us to emphasize or reveal subtle motions that were previously undetectable. To achieve this, we employ texture synthesis techniques that fill in any visible "holes" created by the amplified motions. The end result is a series of motion-magnified images that highlight or accentuate the subtlest movements within the original sequence.
Our demonstrations showcase the power of motion magnification in various domains. For example, we reveal the minute deformations in load-bearing structures that are crucial for understanding their stability and durability. We also illustrate how motion magnification can be used to analyze the intricate balance adjustments made by people during various activities, such as walking or running. Furthermore, we demonstrate the ability of motion magnification to reveal the subtle flexibility of "rigid" structures under hand pressure, shedding light on the complex mechanics of manipulation and dexterity.
In summary, motion magnification is a revolutionary technique that enhances our understanding of minute movements within video sequences. By analyzing the motion of individual pixels and amplifying the most significant patterns, this technique offers unparalleled insights into the behavior of complex systems, from load-bearing structures to the intricate motions of people and the flexible adjustments of "rigid" structures. With its ability to reveal subtle motions that are otherwise imperceptible, motion magnification has the potential to revolutionize a wide range of fields, from biomechanics to engineering and beyond.

title: Human TRPML1 channel structures in open and closed conformations
text: Transient receptor potential Mucolipin-1 (TRPML1) is a Ca2+-releasing cation channel that plays a crucial role in regulating calcium signaling and homeostasis within lysosomes. Mutations in TRPML1 can lead to Mucolipidosis type IV, a severe lysosomal storage disorder. Our study presents two high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures of the full-length human TRPML1: an apo structure at pH 7.0 with a resolution of 3.72 Å, and an agonist-bound structure at pH 6.0 with a resolution of 3.49 Å. The structure reveals a hydrophobic cavity in pore helix 1, helices S5 and S6, and a neighboring subunit helix S6 that houses the agonist, indicating a unique binding site compared to TRPV1, a TRP channel from a different subfamily. The opening of TRPML1 is associated with distinct dilations of its lower gate and a slight movement of pore helix 1. Our findings provide a deeper understanding of the regulatory mechanism of TRPML channels and shed light on the molecular basis of mucolipidosis type IV pathogenesis.

title: Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV): high-performance genomics data visualization and exploration
text: Effective data visualization is crucial in genomic data analysis. However, the enormous sizes and diversity of data sets generated by contemporary sequencing and array-based profiling techniques pose significant challenges to visualization tools. The Integrative Genomics Viewer (IGV) is a sophisticated viewer capable of handling large, diverse data sets while providing a seamless and intuitive user experience at various levels of genome resolution. A distinctive feature of IGV is its focus on the integrative nature of genomic studies, supporting both array-based and next-generation sequencing data, as well as the integration of clinical and phenotypic data. Although IGV is primarily utilized for viewing genomic data from public sources, its primary objective is to facilitate researchers in visualizing and exploring their own data sets or those from colleagues. To achieve this, IGV supports flexible loading of local and remote data sets and is optimized for high-performance data visualization and exploration on standard desktop systems. IGV is freely available for download from <http://www.broadinstitute.org/igv> under a GNU LGPL open-source license.

title: Can genome engineering be used to target cancer-associated enhancers?
text: Transcriptional dysregulation is a key factor in various diseases, including cancer. Enhancers, located far away from the promoter, play a critical role in shaping cell-specific transcription patterns in both healthy and diseased tissues. These findings suggest that targeting enhancers through therapeutic interventions may provide a more focused and effective approach to restoring normal epigenetic patterns in diseased tissues, potentially with fewer side effects compared to drugs that affect multiple epigenetic marks. New technologies, such as genomic nucleases and site-specific epigenetic regulators, are being developed to precisely engineer the genome at enhancers using DNA-binding proteins or RNA-DNA interactions. While this field holds promise, further advances are needed to enhance specificity and efficiency.

title: Long‐Term Follow‐up of CD19 CAR Therapy in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
text:
In this study, we investigated the safety and efficacy of background CD19-specific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells in adults with relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). We conducted a phase 1 trial at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC) and assessed safety and long-term outcomes in relation to demographic, clinical, and disease characteristics.
Our results show that 83% of patients achieved complete remission after receiving 19-28z CAR T cells, which were manufactured at MSKCC. However, severe cytokine release syndrome occurred in 26% of patients, and one patient died as a result of this syndrome. The median event-free survival was 6.1 months (95% CI, 5.0-11.5), and the median overall survival was 12.9 months (95% CI, 8.7-23.4). Notably, patients with a low disease burden (<5% bone marrow blasts) before treatment had markedly enhanced remission duration and survival, with a median event-free survival of 10.6 months (95% CI, 5.9-not reached) and a median overall survival of 20.1 months (95% CI, 8.7-not reached). In contrast, patients with a higher burden of disease (≥5% bone marrow blasts or extramedullary disease) had a greater incidence of cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxic events and shorter long-term survival than those with a low disease burden.
Overall, the median overall survival was 12.9 months in the entire cohort. Among patients with a low disease burden, the median overall survival was 20.1 months, accompanied by a markedly lower incidence of cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxic events after 19-28z CAR T-cell infusion compared with patients with a higher disease burden. These findings suggest that background CD19-specific CAR T cells may be a promising approach for treating relapsed B-cell ALL, particularly in patients with a low disease burden. (Funded by the Commonwealth Foundation for Cancer Research and others; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT01044069.)

title: Periosteum contains skeletal stem cells with high bone regenerative potential controlled by Periostin
text: Bone regeneration relies on the activation of poorly characterized skeletal stem cells (SSCs), which are found in the periosteum. Here, we demonstrate that periosteal cells (PCs) have greater bone regenerative potential compared to bone marrow stromal cells/skeletal stem cells (BMSCs) in mice. Although PCs and BMSCs share a common embryonic mesenchymal lineage, postnatally PCs exhibit greater clonogenicity, growth, and differentiation capacity than BMSCs. During bone repair, PCs can efficiently contribute to cartilage and bone and integrate long-term after transplantation. Using molecular profiling, we uncover genes encoding Periostin and other extracellular matrix molecules associated with the enhanced response to injury of PCs. We find that Periostin gene deletion impairs PC functions and fracture consolidation, and that periosteum-derived SSCs require Periostin to maintain a pool of PCs. Our results highlight the importance of studying periosteum and PCs to understand bone phenotypes.

title: Metabolism strikes back: metabolic flux regulates cell signaling.
text: Mammalian cells rely on growth factor signaling to absorb nutrients; however, the mechanism by which these cells coordinate the uptake of glucose and glutamine has remained a mystery. In this issue of Genes & Development, Wellen and colleagues (pp. 2784-2799) provide insight into this process, demonstrating that the flux of glucose through the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway regulates the glycosylation of growth factor receptors, allowing cells to consume glutamine. This mechanism ensures that cells do not engage in anabolic metabolism when nutrients are scarce, and highlights the important role that substrate availability plays in modulating cell signaling.

title: Association of Pembrolizumab With Tumor Response and Survival Among Patients With Advanced Melanoma.
text:
Background: The programmed death 1 (PD-1) pathway regulates the immune system's response to cancer, including melanoma. Anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibodies, such as pembrolizumab, can block this pathway and enhance the immune response against melanoma. The objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of pembrolizumab in patients with advanced melanoma.
Methods: This open-label, multicohort, phase 1b clinical trial enrolled patients aged 18 years and older with advanced or metastatic melanoma across academic medical centers in Australia, Canada, France, and the United States. The study included 655 patients, of which 135 were from a non-randomized cohort and 520 were from randomized cohorts. Patients received pembrolizumab every 2 or 3 weeks until disease progression or intolerable toxicity. The primary end point was the objective response rate (best overall response of complete response or partial response) in patients with measurable disease at baseline, assessed by independent central review. Secondary end points included toxicity, duration of response, progression-free survival, and overall survival.
Results: Of the 581 patients with measurable disease at baseline, an objective response was observed in 194 (33%), and in 60 of 133 treatment-naive patients (45%), respectively. Of the 194 responders, 74% had ongoing responses at the time of data cutoff, and 44% had responses that lasted for at least 1 year and 79% lasted for at least 6 months. Twelve-month progression-free survival rates were 35% in the total population and 52% in treatment-naive patients. Median overall survival in the total population was 23 months (95% CI, 20-29) with 12-month and 24-month survival rates of 66% (95% CI, 62%-69%) and 49% (95% CI, 44%-53%), respectively. In treatment-naive patients, median overall survival was 31 months (95% CI, 24-not reached) with 12-month and 24-month survival rates of 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%) and 60% (95% CI, 51%-68%), respectively. Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 14% of patients, and 4% discontinued treatment due to a treatment-related adverse event. There were no drug-related deaths.
Conclusion: The findings of this study suggest that pembrolizumab is effective in enhancing the immune response against melanoma and improving outcomes in patients with advanced disease. The overall objective response rate was 33%, and median overall survival was 23 months. Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 14% of patients, and there were no drug-related deaths. These results provide valuable insights into the efficacy and safety of pembrolizumab in the treatment of melanoma, and further support its use in the clinical management of this disease.
Trial Registration: clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT01295827.

title: Inflammatory signaling in human Tuberculosis granulomas is spatially organized
text: Granulomas are the defining feature of tuberculosis (TB) and yet their function and formation mechanisms remain inadequately understood. To gain insight into the role of granulomas in TB, we employed an unbiased approach to analyze the proteomes of granulomas from TB-infected individuals. Using laser-capture microdissection, mass spectrometry, and confocal microscopy, we produced comprehensive molecular maps of human granulomas. Our findings reveal that the central regions of granulomas harbor a pro-inflammatory environment characterized by the presence of antimicrobial peptides, reactive oxygen species, and pro-inflammatory eicosanoids. In contrast, the surrounding tissue exhibits a more anti-inflammatory signature. These observations are consistent across six human subjects and in rabbits. Notably, the delicate balance between systemic pro- and anti-inflammatory signals is crucial to TB disease outcome, yet our study reveals that these signals are spatially segregated within each granuloma. From the protein and lipid profiles of human and rabbit lesions analyzed here, we propose that the pathological response to TB is shaped by the precise spatial localization of these inflammatory pathways during granuloma formation.

title: Suppression of interferon-mediated anti-HBV response by single CpG methylation in the 5′-UTR of TRIM22
text:
Objective: Interferons (IFNs) exert direct antiviral activity, playing a crucial role in the early immune response against viral infections. However, IFN therapy for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is less effective than for other viral infections. To investigate the cellular targets of HBV in response to IFNs, we employed proteome-wide screening.
Methods: We used liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to identify proteins downregulated or upregulated by IFN treatment in HBV X protein (HBx)-stable and control cells. We also investigated IFN-stimulated genes downregulated by HBx and showed that HBx suppresses the transcription of TRIM22, an antiretroviral protein, through a single methylation event in its 5' untranslated region (5'-UTR).
Results: Our findings were validated using a mouse model, primary human hepatocytes, and human liver tissues. We found that HBV evades the host innate immune system by suppressing the transcription of TRIM22.
Conclusion: Our study elucidates a mechanism by which HBV dodges the host's innate immune response through the suppression of TRIM22. This discovery could lead to the development of new strategies for improving IFN-based therapies against HBV infection.

title: Developmental Analysis of Bone Marrow Neutrophils Reveals Populations Specialized in Expansion, Trafficking, and Effector Functions
text:
Neutrophils are innate immune cells that have a short half-life due to constant turnover in the bone marrow (BM). Although it is well established that neutrophils originate from the granulocyte-macrophage progenitor (GMP), the precise pathways involved in their differentiation are not fully understood. By using mass cytometry (CyTOF) and cell-cycle-based analysis, we identified three distinct neutrophil subsets within the BM: a proliferating committed neutrophil precursor (preNeu), non-proliferating immature neutrophils, and mature neutrophils. Transcriptomic profiling and functional assays revealed that preNeu require the C/EBPε transcription factor for their development from the GMP, and their proliferative program is replaced by a gain of migratory and effector functions as they mature. We found that preNeus expand in response to microbial and tumoral stress, and immature neutrophils are recruited to the periphery of tumor-bearing mice. Our study demonstrates that specialized BM granulocytic populations play a crucial role in maintaining homeostasis and responding to stress conditions.
Graphical Abstract:
No Caption available.
Highlights:

* Proliferation activity identifies committed neutrophil precursor in mice and humans
* Neutrophil subsets exhibit distinct transcriptomic and functional signatures
* Defect in neutrophil development leads to impaired neutrophil-mediated responses
* Increased circulating immature neutrophils are associated with cancer progression.
The neutrophil differentiation pathway remains poorly defined, and our findings provide a framework for understanding the developmental trajectory and functional properties of neutrophils.

title: TAK1-mediated autophagy and fatty acid oxidation prevent hepatosteatosis and tumorigenesis.
text: The TAK1 protein, a MAP kinase kinase kinase that is activated by TLRs, IL-1, TNF, and TGFβ, regulates cellular processes such as survival, growth, tumorigenesis, and metabolism in the liver. In this study, we investigated the role of TAK1 in regulating autophagy, lipid metabolism, and tumorigenesis in the liver. We found that TAK1-deficient mice had severe hepatosteatosis and increased mTORC1 activity, which resulted in suppressed autophagy. Ectopic activation of AMPK restored autophagy in TAK1-deficient hepatocytes. Additionally, TAK1 deficiency led to suppression of PPARα target genes and β-oxidation, which regulate hepatic lipid degradation. A high-fat diet challenge exacerbated steatohepatitis in TAK1-deficient mice, and inhibition of mTORC1 restored autophagy and PPARα target gene expression in these mice. These findings suggest that TAK1 regulates hepatic lipid metabolism and tumorigenesis via the AMPK/mTORC1 axis, affecting both autophagy and PPARα activity.

title: Formins at the Junction.
text: At the cell-cell interface between epithelial cells, the actin cytoskeleton and adhesion junctions are intimately linked through complexes known as the actin cytoskeleton. The regulation of the actin cytoskeleton is carried out by an assembly of proteins called the actin regulatory complex Arp2/3, which has been proven to play a critical role in the disassembly of junctional actin. However, the role of formins, the largest group of actin regulators, in this process has remained largely unexplored. Formins are proteins that dynamically shape the actin cytoskeleton within cells and exhibit multiple functions. This review will provide an overview of recent discoveries regarding the role of formins in regulating actin dynamics at cell-cell contacts and highlight their essential functions during the process of epithelialization.

title: CRISPR adaptation biases explain preference for acquisition of foreign DNA
text:
CRISPR-Cas (clustered, regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats coupled with CRISPR-associated proteins) is a bacterial immune system that fights off invading phages or plasmids. During the CRISPR adaptation process, short sections of DNA ("spacers") are acquired from foreign DNA and integrated into the CRISPR array. This has remained a mystery, as it is unclear how spacers are selectively acquired from foreign DNA while avoiding the self-chromosome.
Our study shows that spacer acquisition is dependent on replication, with DNA breaks formed at stalled replication forks promoting spacer acquisition. Chromosomal hotspots of spacer acquisition were found to be confined by Chi sites, which are high-enriched sequence octamers on the bacterial chromosome. These sites limit spacer acquisition from self-DNA, and we demonstrate that the avoidance of self is mediated by the RecBCD double-stranded DNA break repair complex.
Our results suggest that, in Escherichia coli, the acquisition of new spacers relies on RecBCD-mediated processing of double-stranded DNA breaks occurring primarily at replication forks, with the preference for foreign DNA due to the higher density of Chi sites on the self-chromosome, combined with the higher number of forks on the foreign DNA. This model accounts for the strong preference to acquire spacers both from high-copy plasmids and phages.

title: High-resolution mapping of open chromatin in the rice genome.
text: The regulation of gene expression is a complex process involving the interaction of transcription factors with various regulatory DNA elements. One notable characteristic of regions associated with regulatory proteins is their sensitivity to DNase I digestion. To investigate the genomic distribution of regulatory elements in rice (Oryza sativa), we generated high-resolution maps of DNase I hypersensitive (DH) sites in both seedling and callus tissues. Surprisingly, only approximately 25% of the DH sites were found in putative promoters, indicating that the majority of regulatory elements in rice are not located in these regions. Interestingly, we observed 58% more DH sites in the callus than in the seedling. Within both tissues, 31% of the DH sites displayed different levels of DNase I sensitivity. Moreover, genes that were differentially expressed between the seedling and callus were often associated with DH sites in both tissues. The DNA sequences within the DH sites were hypomethylated, consistent with the known characteristics of active gene regulatory elements. Notably, tissue-specific DH sites located in promoters showed higher levels of DNA methylation compared to the average methylation level of all DH sites in promoters. Additionally, we observed an elevation of H3K27me3 associated with intergenic DH sites. These findings suggest that epigenetic modifications play a crucial role in the dynamic changes in the numbers and DNase I sensitivity of DH sites during development.

title: Prospective study of body fat distribution and the risk of endometrial cancer.
text:
BACKGROUND: Epidemiological studies have shown that overall obesity is positively associated with the risk of endometrial cancer (EC). However, there is limited research on the relationship between body fat distribution and EC risk.
METHODS: We studied 51,948 women who reported their waist circumference (WC) and hip circumference in 1986 as part of the Nurses' Health Study. We calculated the waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and followed these women for 24 years, during which time 449 incident invasive EC cases were diagnosed.
RESULTS: In our analysis, we found that in the absence of adjustment for body mass index (BMI), the risk of EC was significantly higher in women with larger waists and wider hips compared to those with smaller waists and narrower hips. Specifically, the relative risks (RRs) for EC were 2.44 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.72-3.45) for WC and 1.69 (95% CI=1.20-2.40) for WHR. However, after adjusting for BMI, these positive associations were significantly attenuated and became non-significant; RR=1.08 (95% CI=0.69-1.67) for WC and 1.15 (95% CI=0.81-1.64) for WHR, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that after controlling for body mass index, there is no independent association between body fat distribution and the risk of EC.

title: Breast cancer clusters in the northeast United States: a geographic analysis.
text: A recent study has revealed high breast cancer mortality rates in the northeastern United States, particularly in Long Island, New York. The researchers aimed to determine whether the high mortality is uniform throughout the region or if there are specific clusters of deaths that cannot be explained by chance.
