They obtained demographic data and age-specific breast cancer mortality rates for 244 counties in 11 states and the District of Columbia over the period of 1988-1992. Using a novel spatial scan statistic that examines clusters of cases without specifying their size or location, the study found a significant and widespread cluster of breast cancer deaths in the New York City-Philadelphia metropolitan area, with a 7.4% higher mortality rate than the rest of the northeast. The cluster remained significant after accounting for race, urbanicity, and parity as confounding variables. Four smaller subclusters within this area were also identified as statistically significant. The findings suggest that the elevated breast cancer mortality on Long Island may be part of a larger pattern affecting large areas of the New York City-Philadelphia metropolitan area. The study highlights the importance of considering multiple risk factors, including age at first birth, age at menarche, age at menopause, breastfeeding, genetic mutations, and environmental factors, that may contribute to the observed cluster.

title: CD200R/CD200 Inhibits Osteoclastogenesis: New Mechanism of Osteoclast Control by Mesenchymal Stem Cells in Human
text: Homeostasis of the bone is maintained by the equilibrium between bone-forming osteoblasts and bone-degrading osteoclasts. Osteoblasts originate from mesenchymal cells, while osteoclasts belong to the myeloid lineage. Communication between osteoclasts and osteoblasts occurs through the secretion of soluble factors, cell-bone interactions, and cell-cell contact, which modulate their activities. CD200, an immunoglobulin superfamily member, is expressed on various cell types, including mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). The CD200 receptor (CD200R) is expressed on myeloid cells such as monocytes/macrophages. We hypothesize that CD200 could be a new molecule involved in the control of osteoclastogenesis and play a role in MSC-osteoclast communication in humans. In this study, we demonstrated that soluble CD200 inhibited the differentiation and maturation of osteoclast precursors in bone resorbing cells in vitro. Soluble CD200 did not affect the monocyte phenotype but inhibited the RANKL signaling pathway and the expression of osteoclast markers such as osteoclast-associated receptor (OSCAR) and nuclear factor of activated T cells cytoplasmic 1 (NFATc1). Moreover, MSCs inhibited osteoclast formation through cell-cell contact and CD200 expression on the MSC surface. Our results clearly demonstrate that MSCs, through CD200 expression, play a crucial role in regulating bone resorption and bone physiology. The CD200-CD200R couple has the potential to be a new target for controlling bone diseases.

title: Tumor-specific Th17-polarized cells eradicate large established melanoma.
text: CD4+ T cells can differentiate into various effector subsets, but the full scope of their roles in anti-tumor immunity remains unexplored. To investigate the impact of CD4+ T cell polarization on tumor rejection in a model mimicking human cancer, we generated a novel MHC class II-restricted T-cell receptor (TCR) transgenic mouse model, where CD4+ T cells recognize a previously unexplored epitope in tyrosinase-related protein 1 (TRP-1), which is expressed by both normal melanocytes and B16 melanoma cells. We found that CD4+ T cells could be polarized into Th0, Th1, and Th17 subtypes in vitro, based on their cytokine, chemokine, and adhesion molecule profiles as well as surface markers. Unexpectedly, we found that Th17-polarized cells were more effective in destroying advanced B16 melanoma, and this effect was dependent on interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) production. In contrast, depleting interleukin (IL)-17A and IL-23 had little impact. These findings suggest that the in vitro polarization of effector CD4+ T cells is crucial for successful tumor eradication, and this principle could be applied in designing clinical trials involving adoptive transfer-based immunotherapy for human malignancies.

title: Defining community acquired pneumonia severity on presentation to hospital: an international derivation and validation study.
text:
The study aimed to develop a practical severity assessment model for stratifying adults hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) into different management groups. The model was derived from a multicentre study combining data from three prospective studies in the UK, New Zealand, and the Netherlands. Prognostic variables were identified using multiple logistic regression, and the final model was tested against a validation cohort.
The study found that age ≥65 years and low serum albumin levels were independently associated with mortality beyond the modified British Thoracic Society (mBTS) rule. A six-point score, based on confusion, urea, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and age, enabled patients to be categorized according to increasing risk of mortality: score 0, 0.7%; score 1, 3.2%; score 2, 3%; score 3, 17%; score 4, 41.5%; and score 5, 57%. The validation cohort confirmed a similar pattern.
In summary, the study developed a simple and practical six-point severity assessment model for CAP patients that can help clinicians identify those at high risk of mortality and determine appropriate management strategies. The model takes into account readily available clinical variables and has been validated in a separate cohort of patients, providing a useful tool for clinical decision-making.

title: Mitochondrial iron chelation ameliorates cigarette-smoke induced bronchitis and emphysema in mice
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is linked to both cigarette smoking and genetic factors. Previous research has identified iron-responsive element-binding protein 2 (IRP2) as a key gene associated with COPD susceptibility. Our study found that mice lacking IRP2 were resistant to cigarette smoke (CS)-induced experimental COPD. We used RIP-seq, RNA-seq, and gene expression and functional enrichment clustering analysis to investigate the role of IRP2 in the lungs of mice. We found that IRP2 regulates mitochondrial function in the lungs, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and COPD. Interestingly, mice lacking the protein frataxin, which is involved in mitochondrial function, showed impaired airway mucociliary clearance (MCC) and higher pulmonary inflammation at baseline. In contrast, mice lacking the synthesis of cytochrome c oxidase, which is involved in mitochondrial respiration, were protected from CS-induced pulmonary inflammation and impairment of MCC. Treating mice with a mitochondrial iron chelator or feeding them a low-iron diet also protected them from CS-induced COPD. These findings suggest that targeting the mitochondrial-iron axis may be a potential therapeutic intervention for COPD.

title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Neutralize the Anti-tumor Effect of CSF1 Receptor Blockade by Inducing PMN-MDSC Infiltration of Tumors.
text: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) play a crucial role in tumor progression, making targeting them with CSF1R inhibitors an attractive therapeutic approach. However, the anti-tumor effects of these inhibitors have been limited. We have discovered the mechanism responsible for this limited efficacy. Our findings show that carcinoma-associated fibroblasts (CAF) are the primary sources of chemokines that attract granulocytes to the tumor site. Tumor cells produce CSF1, which suppresses the expression of granulocyte-specific chemokines in CAF through the action of HDAC2. Treatment with CSF1R inhibitors disrupts this crosstalk, leading to a significant increase in granulocyte infiltration into the tumor. Combining CSF1R inhibitors with a CXCR2 antagonist further blocks granulocyte infiltration and exhibits strong anti-tumor effects.

title: Phenotypic deficits in the HIV-1 envelope are associated with the maturation of a V2-directed broadly neutralizing antibody lineage
text:
The evolution of Broadly Neutralizing Antibodies (bnAbs) against HIV-1 is a result of an ongoing process of virus escape and antibody adaptation, which vaccine design aims to mimic. To achieve this, it is crucial to identify the properties of HIV-1 Env proteins that can induce bnAb responses. We investigated the changes in the Env protein of HIV-1 subtype C in a superinfected donor, CAP256, over a period of time, starting from the early stages of bnAb induction.
Longitudinal analysis of viral populations revealed significant changes in Env properties, with a shift towards reduced sensitivity to bnAb VRC26. These changes were associated with reduced infectivity, altered entry kinetics, and lower sensitivity to neutralization after CD4 attachment. Interestingly, VRC26 maintained its neutralization activity against cell-associated CAP256 virus, indicating that escape through the cell-cell transmission route is not the dominant escape pathway. The early escape variants were found to have reduced fitness, and the sustained sensitivity of the virus to bnAbs in cell-cell transmission limited its replication, providing insight into the mechanism of bnAb-mediated immune control.
Our findings highlight the plasticity of the HIV-1 Env protein in evading bnAb pressure and the importance of considering phenotypic traits when selecting and designing Env immunogens for vaccine development. The combination of Env variants with differential phenotypic patterns and bnAb sensitivity, as described here for CAP256, may maximize the potential for inducing bnAb responses through vaccination.

title: High somatic mutation and neoantigen burden are correlated with decreased progression-free survival in multiple myeloma
text: Tumor-specific mutations can lead to the creation of immunogenic neoantigens, which have been linked to responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors in highly mutated cancers. However, initial results of single-agent checkpoint inhibitors in multiple myeloma (MM) have been underwhelming. To investigate the connection between mutation and neoantigen landscape in MM patients and response to therapies, we analyzed interim data from the MMRF CoMMpass study (NCT01454297) on 664 MM patients. Our findings revealed a positive linear relationship between mutation and neoantigen burdens (R2=0.862). The average predicted neoantigen load was 23.52 neoantigens, with an average of 9.40 expressed neoantigens per patient. Survival analysis showed that patients with higher somatic missense mutation loads (N=163) had significantly shorter progression-free survival (PFS) compared to those with lower loads (0.493 vs 0.726 2-year PFS, P=0.0023). Similar results were observed when the analysis was stratified by disease stage and cytogenetic abnormalities. Our findings suggest that high mutation and neoantigen load are clinically relevant risk factors that negatively impact survival of MM patients under current standards of care.

title: Postmarket Safety Events Among Novel Therapeutics Approved by the US Food and Drug Administration Between 2001 and 2010
text:
Introduction:
Postmarket safety events of novel pharmaceuticals and biologics occur after initial regulatory approval when new safety risks are identified. These events can impact how these therapeutics are used in clinical practice and shape patient and clinician decision-making. This study aimed to characterize the frequency of postmarket safety events among novel therapeutics approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and to investigate whether any therapeutic characteristics known at the time of FDA approval were associated with an increased risk of postmarket safety events.
Methods:
This cohort study analyzed all novel therapeutics approved by the FDA between January 1, 2001, and December 31, 2010, and followed them up through February 28, 2017. The study included 222 novel therapeutics (183 pharmaceuticals and 39 biologics). Postmarket safety events were defined as withdrawals due to safety concerns, FDA issuance of incremental boxed warnings added in the postmarket period, and FDA issuance of safety communications.
Results:
From 2001 to 2010, the FDA approved 222 novel therapeutics, and during a median follow-up period of 11.7 years (interquartile range [IQR], 8.7-13.8 years), there were 123 new postmarket safety events (3 withdrawals, 61 boxed warnings, and 59 safety communications) affecting 71 (32.0%) of the novel therapeutics. The median time from approval to first postmarket safety event was 4.2 years (IQR, 2.5-6.0 years), and the proportion of novel therapeutics affected by a postmarket safety event at 10 years was 30.8% (95% CI, 25.1%-37.5%). In multivariable analysis, postmarket safety events were statistically significantly more frequent among biologics (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.93; 95% CI, 1.06-3.52; P = .03), therapeutics indicated for the treatment of psychiatric disease (IRR = 3.78; 95% CI, 1.77-8.06; P < .001), those receiving accelerated approval (IRR = 2.20; 95% CI, 1.15-4.21; P = .02), and those with near–regulatory deadline approval (IRR = 1.90; 95% CI, 1.19-3.05; P = .008). Events were statistically significantly less frequent among those with regulatory review times less than 200 days (IRR = 0.46; 95% CI, 0.24-0.87; P = .02).
Discussion:
The study found that among 222 novel therapeutics approved by the FDA from 2001 to 2010, 32% were affected by a postmarket safety event. Biologics, psychiatric therapeutics, and accelerated and near–regulatory deadline approval were statistically significantly associated with higher rates of events, highlighting the need for continuous monitoring of the safety of novel therapeutics throughout their life cycle. These findings underscore the importance of ongoing safety surveillance and the need for FDA regulatory review processes to take postmarket safety events into account.
Implications:
The study's findings have important implications for the regulation of novel therapeutics. The study highlights the need for continuous monitoring of the safety of novel therapeutics throughout their life cycle, particularly for biologics, psychiatric therapeutics, and therapeutics approved through accelerated or near–regulatory deadline review processes. The findings suggest that ongoing safety surveillance and monitoring are crucial to identifying safety concerns and ensuring the continued safety of novel therapeutics after initial approval. The study's conclusions underscore the need for FDA regulatory review processes to take postmarket safety events into account and to prioritize ongoing safety surveillance and monitoring throughout the life cycle of novel therapeutics.

title: Who is where at risk for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease? A spatial epidemiological analysis of health insurance claims for COPD in Northeastern Germany
text:
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has a high prevalence rate in Germany, and it is expected to increase further in the coming years. Although individual risk factors are well understood, there is limited knowledge about the spatial heterogeneity and population-based risk factors of COPD. This study aims to analyze the variation in COPD prevalence across northeastern Germany at the smallest possible spatial scale and identify location-specific population-based risk factors using health insurance claims from the AOK Nordost.
To visualize the spatial distribution of COPD prevalence at the municipal and urban district level, we employed the conditional autoregressive Besag-York-Mollié (BYM) model. Geographically weighted regression modeling (GWR) was used to analyze the ecological risk factors for COPD on a population-based level.
Our findings indicate that the sex- and age-adjusted COPD prevalence was 6.5% in 2012 and varied significantly across northeastern Germany. Population-based risk factors include the proportion of insurants aged 65 and older, insurants with migration background, household size, and area deprivation. The GWR model revealed that the population at risk for COPD varies significantly across northeastern Germany.
Area deprivation has a direct and indirect impact on COPD prevalence. As people age in socially disadvantaged areas, they are more likely to develop COPD, even if they are not directly affected by deprivation on an individual level. This emphasizes the importance of considering the impact of area deprivation on health when planning healthcare. Additionally, our results show that in some parts of the study area, insurants with migration background and those living in multi-person households are at elevated risk of COPD.
In conclusion, our findings highlight the importance of considering the spatial distribution of COPD prevalence and population-based risk factors when planning healthcare. By analyzing the variation in COPD prevalence across northeastern Germany, we can identify areas with elevated risk factors and tailor healthcare provisions accordingly.

title: Large intergenic non-coding RNA-RoR modulates reprogramming of human induced pluripotent stem cells
text: The process of converting lineage-committed cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) involves a comprehensive overhaul of the epigenome, resulting in altered patterns of gene expression. In this study, we investigate the transcriptional reorganization of large intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) during the derivation of human iPSCs and identify lincRNAs that are specifically expressed in these cells. Among these, we identify ten lincRNAs that are upregulated in iPSCs compared to embryonic stem cells, suggesting that their activation may play a role in the emergence of iPSCs. Through further investigation, we determine that these lincRNAs are direct targets of key pluripotency transcription factors and that one of these lincRNAs, lincRNA-RoR, plays a critical role in the reprogramming process. Our findings provide the first evidence for the functional importance of lincRNAs in the derivation of pluripotent stem cells.

title: Extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization: toward clinical application.
text: Two main types of extracellular vesicles (EVs), exosomes and shed microvesicles (sMVs), have been identified. These EVs vary in size distribution and protein/RNA profiles. EVs play crucial roles in cell-cell communication, both locally and systemically, and have been implicated in various cellular processes. This review focuses on the differing features of EV subtypes, methods for isolating EVs from cell culture media and body fluids, and approaches for quantifying EVs. Additionally, we discuss proteins selectively enriched in exosomes and sMVs that could potentially serve as markers to distinguish between EV subtypes, as well as the diverse applications of EVs in clinical diagnosis.

title: Up-regulated NRIP2 in colorectal cancer initiating cells modulates the Wnt pathway by targeting RORβ
text:
Colorectal cancer is one of the most common types of cancer worldwide, and colorectal cancer initiating cells (CCICs) are a small subpopulation responsible for the malignant properties of this disease. Abnormal activation of the Wnt signaling pathway is crucial for the self-renewal of CCICs. However, the underlying mechanisms are not well understood.
To identify novel intermediaries in the Wnt signaling pathway, we used retroviral library screening and found Nuclear Receptor-Interacting Protein 2 (NRIP2) as a novel interactor of the Wnt pathway in enriched colorectal cancer colosphere cells. We investigated the expression levels of NRIP2 and its interaction with retinoic acid-related orphan receptor β (RORβ) using techniques such as fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), immunohistochemistry (IHC), and Western blot. We also examined the role of NRIP2 in CCICs using overexpression and knockdown colorectal cancer cell models and verified the binding between NRIP2 and RORβ.
Our results showed that NRIP2 is significantly upregulated in CCICs from both cell lines and primary colorectal cancer tissues. Increased expression of NRIP2 enhanced Wnt activity, while silencing of NRIP2 attenuated Wnt activity. The transcription factor RORβ was found to be a key target through which NRIP2 regulates Wnt pathway activity. RORβ was found to be a transcriptional enhancer of the inhibitor HBP1 of the Wnt pathway. NRIP2 prevented RORβ from binding with downstream HBP1 promoter regions and reduced the transcription of HBP1. This, in turn, attenuated the HBP1-dependent inhibition of TCF4-mediated transcription.
Our findings demonstrate that NRIP2 is a novel interactor of the Wnt pathway in colorectal cancer initiating cells and that interactions between NRIP2, RORβ, and HBP1 mediate a new mechanism for CCIC self-renewal via the Wnt activity. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying colorectal cancer development and progression.

title: Speed Limits for Nonvesicular Intracellular Sterol Transport.
text: Sterol transport between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and plasma membrane (PM) occurs through non-vesicular mechanisms that require sterol transport proteins (STPs). In this study, we investigate the hypothesis that transport is more efficient at membrane contact sites where the ER is closely apposed to the PM. Our findings suggest that sterol desorption from the membrane, rather than STP-mediated diffusion, is the primary limitations in the cellular context, thereby argueing against the idea that having STP-mediated sterol transfer occur at contact sites provides any kinetic benefits. Instead, contact sites may function to compartmentalize lipid synthesis or transport machinery, providing opportunities for regulatory control.

title: Misunderstandings in prescribing decisions in general practice: qualitative study.
text:
Objective:
To identify and describe misunderstandings between patients and doctors during the prescribing process in general practice settings.
Design: Qualitative study.
Setting: 20 general practices in the West Midlands and south east England.
Participants: 20 general practitioners and 35 consulting patients.
Main outcome measures: Misunderstandings between patients and doctors with potential or actual adverse consequences for medication use.
Results: 14 categories of misunderstandings were identified, including:
1. Patient information unknown to the doctor: Doctors were unaware of patient information, leading to inaccurate assumptions and decisions.
2. Doctor information unknown to the patient: Patients were unaware of crucial information about their treatment, leading to confusion and miscommunication.
3. Conflicting information: There were instances where both patients and doctors provided conflicting information, leading to frustration and mistrust.
4. Disagreement about attribution of side effects: Patients and doctors disagreed on the cause of medication side effects, leading to misunderstandings and non-adherence.
5. Failure of communication about doctor's decisions: Patients were not adequately informed about the doctors' decisions, leading to confusion and lack of trust.
6. Relationship factors: The doctor-patient relationship was found to have a significant impact on the quality of communication and understanding during the prescribing process.
Conclusion: Patients' participation in the consultation is crucial to avoid misunderstandings and adverse outcomes. The authors are developing an educational intervention to address these issues.

title: Phase-plate cryo-EM structure of a biased agonist-bound human GLP-1 receptor–Gs complex
text: The class B glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) G protein-coupled receptor is a prime target for treating type 2 diabetes and obesity. Endogenous and synthetic GLP-1 peptides exhibit unique characteristics—differences in functional selectivity—that may lead to enhanced therapeutic outcomes. We have obtained the three-dimensional structure of the human GLP-1 receptor complexed with the G protein-biased peptide exendin-P5 and a Gαs heterotrimer at a resolution of 3.3 Å. The extracellular surface of the receptor features distinct organization of loops 3 and transmembrane segments in the exendin-P5-bound structure compared to previous GLP-1 receptor structures. Moreover, the angle of Gαs–α5 helix engagement varies by six degrees between the two structures, resulting in differences in the rate and extent of Gαs conformational reorganization. This structure offers insights into the molecular basis of biased agonism.

title: Therapeutic equivalence of alendronate 70 mg once-weekly and alendronate 10 mg daily in the treatment of osteoporosis. Alendronate Once-Weekly Study Group.
text:
Dosing frequency is a crucial aspect of managing chronic diseases, and particularly vital in the long-term management of osteoporosis. Less frequent dosing may improve compliance, resulting in maximized medication efficacy. Animal studies demonstrate that weekly dosing with alendronate 70 mg (seven times the daily oral dose) may provide equal efficacy compared to daily dosing with alendronate 10 mg due to its extended duration of action in bone. Additionally, dog studies suggest that the potential for esophageal irritation associated with daily oral bisphosphonates may be significantly reduced with once-weekly dosing. This dosing regimen offers patients increased convenience and compliance.
In a one-year, double-blind, multicenter study, we compared the efficacy and safety of oral once-weekly alendronate 70 mg (n=519), twice-weekly alendronate 35 mg (n=369), and daily alendronate 10 mg (n=370) in postmenopausal women aged 42 to 95 with osteoporosis and low bone mineral density (BMD). The primary endpoint was the equivalence of increases in lumbar spine BMD using strict pre-defined criteria. Secondary endpoints included changes in BMD at the hip, total body, and bone turnover, as well as biochemical markers of bone resorption and formation. All three dosing regimens met the equivalence criteria relative to daily therapy. Mean increases in lumbar spine BMD at 12 months were 5.1% (95% CI 4.8, 5.4) in the 70 mg once-weekly group, 5.2% (4.9, 5.6) in the 35 mg twice-weekly group, and 5.4% (5.0, 5.8) in the 10 mg daily treatment group. Increases in BMD at the total hip, femoral neck, trochanter, and total body were similar for the three dosing regimens. All three treatment groups similarly reduced biochemical markers of bone resorption (urinary N-telopeptides of type I collagen) and bone formation (serum bone-specific alkaline phosphatase) into the middle of the premenopausal reference range. All treatment regimens were well tolerated, with a similar incidence of upper GI adverse experiences. There were fewer serious upper GI adverse experiences, and a trend toward a lower incidence of esophageal events in the once-weekly dosing group compared to the daily dosing group. These findings are consistent with preclinical animal models and suggest that once-weekly dosing may have improved upper GI tolerability. Clinical fractures captured as adverse experiences were similar among the groups. In conclusion, the alendronate 70 mg once-weekly dosing regimen offers patients a more convenient and therapeutically equivalent alternative to daily dosing, with potential improved compliance and long-term persistence with therapy.

title: Association of Toll-Like Receptor 4 on Human Monocyte Subsets and Vulnerability Characteristics of Coronary Plaque as Assessed by 64-Slice Multidetector Computed Tomography.
text:
BACKGROUND: To date, the relationship between the expression of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR-4) on circulating monocytes and coronary plaque vulnerability in patients with stable angina pectoris (SAP) has not been investigated. Our study aimed to evaluate this relationship using 64-slice multidetector computed tomography (MDCT).
METHODS AND RESULTS: We enrolled 65 patients with SAP who underwent MDCT. We measured the expression of TLR-4 on three monocyte subsets (CD14++CD16-, CD14++CD16+, and CD14+CD16+) using flow cytometry. Intracoronary plaques were assessed by 64-slice MDCT, and their vulnerability was defined based on the presence of positive remodeling (remodeling index >1.05) and/or low computed tomography (CT) attenuation (<35 HU). We found that the circulating CD14++CD16+monocytes expressed higher levels of TLR-4 compared to CD14++CD16- and CD14+CD16+monocytes (P<0.001). Furthermore, the relative proportion of TLR-4 expression on CD14++CD16+monocytes was significantly higher in patients with vulnerable plaques compared to those without (10.4 [4.1-14.5] % vs. 4.5 [2.8-7.8] %, P=0.012). Additionally, there was a positive correlation between the expression of TLR-4 on CD14++CD16+monocytes and the remodeling index (r=0.28, P=0.025), and a negative correlation with CT attenuation value (r=-0.31, P=0.013).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that upregulation of TLR-4 on CD14++CD16+monocytes may be associated with coronary plaque vulnerability in patients with SAP.

title: Expandable Cardiovascular Progenitor Cells Reprogrammed from Fibroblasts.
text: Stem cell-based strategies for treating heart failure are becoming increasingly viable, but generating sufficient and functional autologous cells for transplantation remains a significant challenge. Our studies isolated a cell population with extensive proliferation capacity and limited cardiovascular differentiation potential during cardiac transdifferentiation of mouse fibroblasts. These induced expandable cardiovascular progenitor cells (ieCPCs) proliferated extensively, producing 10^16 cells from 10^5 starting fibroblasts, in chemically defined conditions. ieCPCs expressed cardiac signature genes and readily differentiated into functional cardiomyocytes (CMs), endothelial cells (ECs), and smooth muscle cells (SMCs) in vitro, even after long-term expansion. When transplanted into mouse hearts following myocardial infarction, ieCPCs spontaneously differentiated into CMs, ECs, and SMCs and improved cardiac function for up to 12 weeks after transplantation. Therefore, ieCPCs represent a powerful system for studying cardiovascular specification and providing strategies for regenerative medicine in the heart.

title: Thyroid hormone inhibits lung fibrosis in mice by improving epithelial mitochondrial function
text: Thyroid hormone (TH) plays a crucial role in maintaining cellular homeostasis during stress responses, but its involvement in lung fibrosis remains unclear. Our study found that the enzyme responsible for activating TH, iodothyronine deiodinase 2 (DIO2), was significantly higher in the lungs of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis compared to healthy individuals, and this increase correlated with disease severity. In addition, mice lacking DIO2 exhibited enhanced bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis. Aerosolized TH delivery improved survival and resolved fibrosis in two mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis, intratracheal bleomycin and inducible TGF-β1. The TH mimetic, sobetirome, also attenuated bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis. Following bleomycin-induced injury, TH promoted mitochondrial biogenesis, enhanced mitochondrial bioenergetics, and inhibited mitochondria-regulated apoptosis in alveolar epithelial cells both in vivo and in vitro. TH's antifibrotic properties were found to be dependent on the paths Ppargc1a and Pink1, suggesting a potential therapy for pulmonary fibrosis. In conclusion, TH protects alveolar epithelial cells and restores mitochondrial function, making it a promising treatment for pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Tenomodulin promotes human adipocyte differentiation and beneficial visceral adipose tissue expansion.
text: The proper regulation of energy storage in adipose tissue is critical for maintaining insulin sensitivity, and while the underlying molecular mechanisms are not yet fully understood. In this study, we investigate the role of type II transmembrane protein tenomodulin (TNMD) in this process. We find that TNMD is upregulated in adipose tissue from insulin-resistant individuals compared to insulin-sensitive individuals, despite matching for body mass index (BMI). Interestingly, TNMD expression increases in human preadipocytes during differentiation, and silencing TNMD in these cells impedes adipogenesis. When mice overexpressing TNMD are fed a high-fat diet, they exhibit increased epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) mass, and preadipocytes from these mice show enhanced proliferation rates, indicating elevated adipogenesis. In addition, the overexpressing mice display increased lipogenic gene expression in eWAT, as well as increased Ucp1 expression in brown adipose tissue, while liver triglyceride accumulation is diminished. Despite the expanded eWAT, the transgenic animals demonstrate improved systemic insulin sensitivity, decreased collagen deposition and inflammation in eWAT, and enhanced insulin stimulation of Akt phosphorylation. These findings suggest that TNMD exerts a protective effect in visceral adipose tissue, alleviating insulin resistance in obesity.

title: Evidence for a limit to human lifespan
text: The advancement of technology has significantly enhanced human lifespan since the 19th century. Statistical evidence indicates a continuous decrease in mortality rates among the elderly and an increase in the maximum age at death, which may contribute to further extending human lifespan. Moreover, observations on various animal species demonstrate that lifespan is adaptive and can be improved through genetic or pharmacological interventions, leading to the hypothesis that longevity may not be subject to strict, species-specific genetic limitations. By analyzing global demographic data, we find that improvements in survival rates with age decrease after the age of 100, and that the age of death of the world's oldest person has remained unchanged since the 1990s. Our results strongly suggest that the maximum human lifespan is fixed and subject to natural constraints.

title: Effect of Oral Semaglutide Compared With Placebo and Subcutaneous Semaglutide on Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial
text: The study compared the effects of oral semaglutide with placebo and open-label subcutaneous semaglutide on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes. The study was a randomized, parallel-group, dosage-finding trial with 5 weeks of follow-up at 100 sites in 14 countries. A total of 1106 patients were assessed, and 632 with type 2 diabetes and insufficient glycemic control were randomized. The study found that oral semaglutide resulted in better glycemic control than placebo over 26 weeks, as measured by changes in hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels. The study also found that oral semaglutide resulted in greater weight reductions than placebo, with dosages of 10 mg or more showing significant results. Adverse events were common in all groups, with mild to moderate gastrointestinal events being the most common. The findings of the study support the use of oral semaglutide as a treatment for type 2 diabetes and warrant further evaluation in longer-term and clinical outcomes, as well as safety.

title: Fast and accurate short read alignment with Burrows–Wheeler transform
text:
New DNA sequencing technologies have generated a vast number of short reads, prompting the development of faster and more accurate read alignment programs. Initial hash table-based methods, including MAQ, offer accuracy and feature richness, but are limited by their inability to support gapped alignment for single-end reads and slower performance when scaling up to resequencing hundreds of individuals.
To address these limitations, we introduced Burrows-Wheeler Alignment tool (BWA), a novel read alignment package relying on backward search with the Burrows-Wheeler Transform (BWT). BWA efficiently aligns short sequencing reads against a large reference sequence, such as the human genome, allowing for mismatches and gaps. It supports both base space reads from Illumina sequencing machines and color space reads from AB SOLiD machines.
Evaluations on simulated and real data demonstrate that BWA is approximately 10-20 times faster than MAQ while maintaining similar accuracy. BWA also outputs alignments in the industry-standard SAM (Sequence Alignment/Map) format, making it easy to perform downstream analyses using the open-source SAMtools software package.
BWA is available at: <http://maq.sourceforge.net>.

title: The financial cost of doctors emigrating from sub-Saharan Africa: human capital analysis
text:
The objective of this study is to estimate the financial loss incurred by countries in sub-Saharan Africa due to the migration of doctors who were educated domestically and later migrated to Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The study uses a human capital cost analysis approach, utilizing publicly available data, to estimate the cost of educating doctors in these nine sub-Saharan African countries. The countries included in the study are Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. The study examines the financial cost of educating a doctor, assuming that migration occurs after graduation, using current country-specific interest rates converted to US dollars. Additionally, the study calculates the financial loss to the destination countries of receiving trained doctors, as well as the savings to the destination countries of recruiting trained doctors.
The results of the study indicate that the estimated government-subsidized cost of educating a doctor in these nine countries ranged from $21,000 in Uganda to $58,700 in South Africa. The overall estimated loss of returns from investment for all doctors currently working in the destination countries was $2.17 billion (95% confidence interval $2.13 billion to $2.21 billion), with costs ranging from $2.16 million in Malawi to $1.41 billion in South Africa. The ratio of the estimated compound lost investment to gross domestic product showed that Zimbabwe and South Africa had the largest losses. In contrast, the benefit to the destination countries of recruiting trained doctors was highest for the United Kingdom ($2.7 billion) and the United States ($846 million).
In conclusion, the study demonstrates that the loss of investment incurred by sub-Saharan African countries due to the emigration of domestically educated doctors is substantial. The findings suggest that destination countries should consider investing in training programs for source countries and strengthening their health systems to mitigate these losses.

title: Chromatin modifying enzymes as modulators of reprogramming
text: Reprogramming of somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) involves a global epigenetic remodeling process. While several proteins have been identified that regulate the epigenetic states of cells before and after reprogramming, the role of specific chromatin-modifying enzymes in the process remains unclear. To investigate the role of these enzymes, we used short hairpin RNAs (shRNAs) to target genes involved in DNA and histone methylation pathways and identified enzymes that positively or negatively affect iPSC generation. We found that inhibiting the core components of the polycomb repressive complex 1 and 2, including the histone 3 lysine 27 methyltransferase EZH2, decreased reprogramming efficiency. On the other hand, suppressing the activity of SUV39H1, YY1, and DOT1L enhanced reprogramming. Specifically, inhibiting DOT1L, a histone methyltransferase, with shRNAs or a small molecule accelerated reprogramming, increasing the yield of iPSC colonies, and substituted for KLF4 and c-Myc (also known as MYC). Additionally, we found that inhibiting DOT1L early in the reprogramming process led to a marked increase in the expression of NANOG and LIN28, two factors that play essential roles in the enhancement of reprogramming. Our results implicate specific chromatin-modifying enzymes as barriers or facilitators of reprogramming and suggest that modulating these enzymes can be used to more efficiently generate iPSCs with fewer exogenous transcription factors. Furthermore, our findings reveal that genes associated with the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition lose their histone H3 lysine 79 methylation mark in the early stages of reprogramming, and that DOT1L inhibition facilitates the loss of this mark from genes that are fated to be repressed in the pluripotent state.

title: Natural variation in the parameters of innate immune cells is preferentially driven by genetic factors
text: The analysis of circulating immune cells provides valuable insights into human health and disease. To uncover the relative impact of environmental and genetic factors on immune cell parameters in healthy individuals, we combined standardized flow cytometry of blood leukocytes with genome-wide DNA genotyping of 1,000 healthy, unrelated individuals of Western European ancestry. Our findings revealed that smoking, age, sex, and latent infection with cytomegalovirus were the primary non-genetic factors influencing immune cell variation. Genome-wide association studies of 166 immunophenotypes identified 15 loci with enriched disease-associated variants. Additionally, we found that innate immune cell parameters were more strongly influenced by genetic factors, while adaptive cell parameters were primarily driven by environmental exposures. Our data establish a valuable resource for generating new hypotheses in immunology and highlight the importance of innate immunity in susceptibility to common autoimmune diseases. Both environmental and genetic factors play a role in shaping human immunity, and this study leverages data from the Milieu Intérieur Consortium to comprehensively examine the effects of lifestyle, environment, and genetics on human innate and adaptive immunity.

title: The transcriptional program, functional heterogeneity, and clinical targeting of mast cells
text: Mast cells are distinct immune cells that possess an array of receptors reacting to several extracellular cues, including antigen-bound IgE complexes, bacteria, viruses, cytokines, hormones, peptides, and drugs. Mast cells represent a relatively small population in tissues, yet their remarkable ability to rapidly respond by releasing stored and newly produced mediators lies at the core of their significance in health and disease. In this review, we outline the biology of mast cells and introduce novel concepts and perspectives regarding their involvement in human diseases beyond IgE-mediated allergic responses and antiparasitic functions. We highlight recent advances in mast cell research, including the regulation of mast cell functions, differentiation, survival, and the development of novel mouse models. Finally, we explore current and potential future avenues for therapeutic intervention of mast cell functions in inflammatory diseases.

title: LIN28B enhanced tumorigenesis in an autochthonous KRASG12V-driven lung carcinoma mouse model
text:
LIN28B is an RNA-binding protein that primarily regulates let-7 microRNAs, which are essential for various cellular processes, including inflammation, wound healing, embryonic stem cell development, and cancer. Studies have shown that LIN28B expression is associated with tumor initiation, progression, resistance, and poor outcome in various types of cancer, including lung cancer. However, the specific role of LIN28B in non-small cell lung adenocarcinomas remains unclear.
To investigate the functional role of LIN28B in lung tumorigenesis, we used a transgenic mouse model overexpressing LIN28B and driving KRASG12V. Our findings revealed that LIN28B overexpression significantly increased the number of CD44+/CD326+ tumor cells, upregulated VEGF-A and miR-21, and promoted tumor angiogenesis and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) accompanied by enhanced AKT phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of c-MYC. Additionally, LIN28B accelerated tumor initiation and proliferation, leading to a shorter overall survival. In line with these findings, analysis of lung adenocarcinomas in the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) revealed that LIN28B expression was present in 24% of KRAS-mutated cases, highlighting the relevance of our model.

title: Cost-effectiveness comparison between topical silver sulfadiazine and enclosed silver dressing for partial-thickness burn treatment.
text: The current standard of care for treating partial-thickness burns involves topical silver products such as silver sulfadiazine cream and enclosed dressings containing silver-impregnated foam or silver-laden sheets. However, the healthcare landscape is constrained by limited resources, with an emphasis on delivering evidence-based treatments that are cost-effective. This study employs a decision analysis to compare the incremental cost-utility ratio of enclosed silver dressings versus silver sulfadiazine cream in partial-thickness burn patients with a total body surface area (TBSA) less than 20%. A comprehensive literature review was conducted to identify clinically relevant health states in partial-thickness burn patients, including successful healing, infection, and noninfected delayed healing requiring either surgical intervention or conservative management. The probabilities of these health states were combined with Medicare Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) reimbursement codes (cost) and patient-derived utilities to construct the decision model. Utilities were measured using a visual analog scale during patient interviews. Expected costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were calculated using the roll-back method. The incremental cost-utility ratio of enclosed silver dressing relative to SSD was $40,167.99/QALY. A one-way sensitivity analysis of complication rates confirmed the robustness of the model. Assuming a maximum willingness to pay $50,000/QALY, the complication rate for SSD must be 22% or higher for enclosed silver dressing to be cost-effective. Using two-way sensitivity analysis, the study found that enclosed silver dressings are a cost-effective treatment option for partial-thickness burns across a range of complication rates for both treatment modalities.

title: Randomized clinical study of Hydrofiber dressing with silver or silver sulfadiazine in the management of partial-thickness burns.
text:
In a prospective, randomized study, the efficacy and safety of AQUACEL Ag Hydrofiber dressings with silver (n = 42) versus silver sulfadiazine (n = 42) were compared in the management of partial-thickness burns covering 5% to 40% of the body surface area (BSA) for up to 21 days. The study found that:
* AQUACEL Ag dressings were associated with lower pain and anxiety levels during dressing changes, less burning and stinging sensations during wear, fewer dressing changes, and less nursing time required compared to silver sulfadiazine.
* Silver sulfadiazine, on the other hand, offered greater flexibility and ease of movement.
* There were no significant differences between treatment groups in terms of adverse events, including infection.
* The AQUACEL Ag dressing protocol had lower total treatment costs (approximately Dollars 1040 vs. Dollars 1180) and a higher rate of re-epithelialization (73.8% vs. 60.0%), resulting in cost-effectiveness per burn healed of approximately Dollars 1,409.06 for AQUACEL Ag dressing and Dollars 1,967.95 for silver sulfadiazine.

Overall, the study suggests that a protocol of care using AQUACEL Ag dressings provides both clinical and economic benefits compared to silver sulfadiazine in patients with partial-thickness burns.

title: Hepatitis C virus and blood transfusion: past and present risks.
text: Since the early 1980s, the risk of hepatitis C virus (HCV) transmission through blood and blood products has significantly decreased. Contributing factors include the selection of non-remunerated donors, stringent donor screening to prevent HIV transmission, regional surrogate testing, and the introduction of anti-HCV testing. As a result, ALT surrogate testing has become obsolete. The current residual risk of HCV transmission due to donations during the anti-HCV window period stands at approximately 1 in 100,000 transfusions of cellular products. Transmission of HCV through plasma products treated with modern inactivation methods, such as solvent-detergent treatment, has not been reported. Hemovigilance programs, which are currently being established, will provide more data on the safety of blood transfusion. In the near future, the introduction of hepatitis C nucleic acid amplification technology (NAT) as a quality control measure for plasma products or blood donor screening by mini-pools is anticipated in many European countries. In the next two years, NAT testing of individual blood donations may become available, further reducing the residual risk. The cost-effectiveness of NAT testing will become relatively low in comparison with other public health measures.

title: p62/SQSTM1 by Binding to Vitamin D Receptor Inhibits Hepatic Stellate Cell Activity, Fibrosis, and Liver Cancer.
text: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) play a crucial role in liver fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Activation of the vitamin D receptor (VDR) in HSCs inhibits liver inflammation and fibrosis. Our findings reveal that p62/SQSTM1, a protein upregulated in liver parenchymal cells and downregulated in HCC-associated HSCs, negatively regulates HSC activation. Total body or HSC-specific p62 ablation exacerbates HSC activation, inflammation, fibrosis, and HCC progression. p62 interacts directly with VDR and RXR, promoting their heterodimerization and recruitment to target genes. Loss of p62 in HSCs impairs the repression of fibrosis and inflammation by VDR agonists, highlighting p62's role as a negative regulator of liver inflammation and fibrosis through its VDR-mediated signaling in HSCs, which supports HCC progression.

title: Developing criteria for evaluation of geroprotectors as a key stage toward translation to the clinic
text: In the forthcoming decades, a significant demographic shift towards an aging population will have far-reaching social and economic implications globally. To mitigate this growth, the development of geroprotectors, substances that slow aging, repair age-related damage, and extend healthy lifespan, or healthspan, could be a viable solution. Currently, over 200 geroprotectors have been identified in model organisms, and some are already in use for specific disease indications. However, the path to determining their impact on aging in humans remains uncertain. Obstacles in translating these findings to the clinic include a lack of a standardized set of criteria to define, select, and classify these substances, due to the complexity of the aging process and its immense diversity in mechanism of action. To overcome these challenges, there is a need for a scientific consensus on the following: (1) a definition of 'geroprotector', (2) selection criteria for geroprotectors, (3) a comprehensive classification system, and (4) an analytical model. Here, we review current approaches to selection and propose our own set of suggested selection criteria to standardize the process of identifying and analyzing new geroprotectors, ultimately saving time and resources in their translation to the clinic.

title: β-Catenin Signaling and Roles in Liver Homeostasis, Injury, and Tumorigenesis.
text: β-catenin (encoded by CTNNB1) is a crucial component of the cell surface cadherin protein complex, which acts as an intracellular signal transducer in the WNT signaling pathway. Deregulations in its activity have been linked to the development of hepatocellular carcinoma and other liver disorders. In addition to WNT, other signaling pathways can also converge at β-catenin. β-catenin interacts with transcription factors such as T-cell factor, forkhead box protein O, and hypoxia inducible factor 1α to regulate the expression of target genes. We investigate its role in the metabolic zonation of the adult liver. β-catenin also regulates the expression of genes involved in glucose, nutrient, and xenobiotic metabolism; alterations in its activity may contribute to the pathogenesis of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis. Activation of hepatic stellate cells, which is dependent on β-catenin signaling, is necessary for fibrosis. Many hepatic tumors such as hepatocellular adenomas, hepatocellular carcinomas, and hepatoblastomas often have CTNNB1 mutations leading to constitutive β-catenin activation, making it a potential therapeutic target. We explore how alterations in β-catenin activity contribute to liver disease and how these might be exploited in diagnosis, prognosis, and the development of therapeutics.

title: The global burden of dengue: an analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2013.
text:
Background: Dengue is the most common arbovirus infection worldwide, yet its burden remains inade in quantity. In this study, we estimated dengue mortality, incidence, and burden for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2013 using causal modeling tools.
Methods: We used vital registry, verb*al autopsy, and surveillance data to estimate mortality rates. We also modeled incidence from officially reported cases, adjusting our estimates for underreporting based on published expansion factors. A total of 1780 country-years of mortality data from 130 countries, 1636 country-years of dengue case reports from 76 countries, and expansion factor estimates for 14 countries were used in the analysis.
Findings: An average of 9221 dengue deaths per year were estimated between 1990 and 2013, with a mortality rate increasing from 8277 (95% uncertainty estimate 5353-10 649) in 1992 to a peak of 11 302 (6790-13 722) in 2010. This resulted in a total of 576 900 (330 000-701 200) years of life lost to premature mortality attributable to dengue in 2013. The incidence of dengue increased rapidly between 1990 and 2013, with the number of cases more than doubling every decade, from 8·3 million (3·3 million-17·2 million) apparent cases in 1990, to 58·4 million (23·6 million-121·9 million) apparent cases in 2013. When accounting for disability from moderate and severe acute dengue, and post-dengue chronic fatigue, 566 000 (186 000-1 415 000) years lived with disability were attributable to dengue in 2013. Considering fatal and non-fatal outcomes together, dengue was responsible for 1·14 million (0·73 million-1·98 million) disability-adjusted life-years in 2013.
Interpretation: Our results offer more evidence that the true symptomatic incidence of dengue probably falls within the commonly cited range of 50 million to 100 million cases per year. While our mortality estimates were lower than those presented elsewhere, the totality of evidence suggests that dengue mortality might, in fact, be substantially higher.
Funding: This study was funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

title: Formin-mediated actin polymerization at cell–cell junctions stabilizes E-cadherin and maintains monolayer integrity during wound repair
text: Cell-cell adhesion mediated by cadherins is crucial for maintaining the integrity of epithelial tissues in both homeostasis and development. However, the mechanisms that regulate actin polymerization at cell-cell junctions, which in turn affect cadherin stability, are not well understood. In this study, we investigated the role of formin-mediated actin polymerization at epithelial junctions. We identified two major factors, mDia1 and Fmnl3, that enhance actin polymerization and stabilize E-cadherin at adherens junctions. Fmnl3 localizes to junctions downstream of Src and Cdc42 and its depletion leads to a decline in F-actin and E-cadherin at junctions, resulting in weakened cell-cell adhesion. Notably, Fmnl3 expression is upregulated and junctional localization increases during collective cell migration. Depletion of Fmnl3 or mDia1 in migrating monolayers leads to the detachment of leading cells and impaired wound repair. In summary, our findings demonstrate that formin activity at epithelial cell-cell junctions is essential for adhesion and the maintenance of epithelial cohesion during dynamic processes such as wound repair.

title: A mechanically active heterotypic E-cadherin/N-cadherin adhesion enables fibroblasts to drive cancer cell invasion
text: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) facilitate the tumor's invasion and metastasis by exerting a physical force on cancer cells, enabling their collective invasion. This force transmission is mediated by a heterophilic adhesion involving the N-cadherin protein on the CAF membrane and the E-cadherin protein on the cancer cell membrane. This adhesion is mechanically active, meaning that it can be activated by external forces, leading to the recruitment of β-catenin and reinforcement of adhesion through an α-catenin/vinculin interaction. Impairment of the E-cadherin/N-cadherin adhesion significantly hinders CAFs' ability to guide collective cell migration and invasion, as well as repolarization of the CAFs away from the cancer cells. Additionally, nectins and afadin are recruited to the cancer cell/CAF interface, with afadin playing a crucial role in CAF repolarization, and heterotypic junctions between CAFs and cancer cells are observed in patient-derived material. Overall, our findings reveal that a mechanically active heterophilic adhesion between CAFs and cancer cells enables cooperative tumor invasion.

title: Long non-coding RNA HOTTIP promotes BCL-2 expression and induces chemoresistance in small cell lung cancer by sponging miR-216a
text: Despite progress in treating small cell lung cancer (SCLC), its multidrug chemoresistance and poor prognosis persist. Recently, we conducted a global analysis of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to identify their contributions to SCLC chemoresistance using microarray data, in vitro and in vivo assays. Our findings revealed that HOTTIP, a lncRNA frequently amplified in SCLC, was associated with SCLC cell chemosensitivity, proliferation, and poor prognosis of SCLC patients. Mechanistic investigations showed that HOTTIP functions as an oncogene in SCLC progression by binding to miR-216a and abrogating its tumor-suppressive function in this context. Moreover, HOTTIP elevates the expression of anti-apoptotic factor BCL-2, another target gene of miR-216a, and enhances chemoresistance of SCLC by regulating BCL-2. Overall, our study establishes a role for HOTTIP in SCLC progression and chemoresistance, highlighting its potential as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for clinical management of SCLC.

title: GSDS 2.0: an upgraded gene feature visualization server
text:
Title: Enhanced Gene Structure Display Server (GSDS) for Intuitive Investigation of Genes' Function and Evolution
Abstract:
Visualizing the structure and annotated features of genes can provide valuable insights into their function and evolution. Since its initial release in 2007, the Gene Structure Display Server (GSDS) has been widely used by over 60,000 researchers. In this update, we present GSDS 2.0, featuring a new user-friendly interface, expanded support for various types of annotations, and an integrated visual editor for customizing figures. Additionally, users can now add a user-specified phylogenetic tree to facilitate evolutionary analysis. The full source code is available for download.
Availability and Implementation:
The GSDS web server and source code are freely accessible at <http://gsds.cbi.pku.edu.cn>. For inquiries or feedback, please contact gaog@mail.cbi.pku.edu.cn or gsds@mail.cbi.pku.edu.cn.
Supplementary Information:
Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

Keywords: gene structure display, visualization, annotation, evolutionary analysis, bioinformatics, genomics.

title: SLP-65 regulates immunoglobulin light chain gene recombination through the PI(3)K-PKB-Foxo pathway
text: Although the crucial function of the adaptor protein SLP-65 during pre-B cell differentiation has been established, the molecular mechanism underlying its action is still not well understood. In this study, we uncovered a connection between SLP-65-mediated signaling and the phosphoinositide-3-OH kinase (PI3K)-protein kinase B (PKB)-Foxo pathway. We found that the forkhead box transcription factor Foxo3a promotes light chain rearrangement in pre-B cells. Our results suggest that PKB inhibits light chain recombination by phosphorylating Foxo proteins, while restoring SLP-65 function counteracts PKB activation and enhances Foxo3a and Foxo1 activity in pre-B cells. These findings provide new insights into the molecular function of SLP-65 and highlight a key role for Foxo proteins in regulating light chain recombination, receptor editing, and B cell selection.

title: A case-mix classification system for explaining healthcare costs using administrative data in Italy.
text: BACKGROUND The Italian National Health Service (NHS) provides universal coverage to all citizens, offering primary and hospital care with a copayment system for outpatient and drug services. Financing of Local Health Trusts (LHTs) is based on a capitation system adjusted only for age, gender, and area of residence. To better understand the factors influencing healthcare costs, we incorporated a risk-adjustment system (Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups System, ACG® System) using routinely collected administrative data in the Veneto Region (North-eastern Italy). METHODS All residents in the Veneto Region were included in the study, and the ACG system was applied to categorize the regional population based on the following data sources for the year 2015: Hospital Discharges, Emergency Room visits, Chronic disease registry for copayment exemptions, ambulatory visits, medications, home care database, and drug prescriptions. Simple linear regressions were used to compare an age-gender model to more comprehensive models incorporating potential cost drivers. RESULTS A basic age-gender model could only explain 8% of the variance in total costs for 2015. Adding variables related to diagnoses and pharmacy use increased explained variance by 23% and 17%, respectively. The adjusted R-squared value of the comprehensive model was six times higher than that of the simple age-gender model. CONCLUSIONS The ACG System significantly improves predictions of healthcare costs compared to simple age-gender adjustments. While aging is not the primary determinant of increasing healthcare costs, the accumulation of chronic conditions and resulting multimorbidity provide a better explanation.

title: EpCAM-regulated intramembrane proteolysis induces a cancer stem cell-like gene signature in hepatitis B virus-infected hepatocytes.
text: The study investigated the role of a protein called EpCAM in the development of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV). HBV infection leads to the loss of a protein called PRC2, which normally represses the expression of specific genes in hepatic progenitors. The study found that EpCAM, a gene normally expressed in these progenitors, is re-expressed in HBV-infected hepatocytes and promotes the growth of cancer stem cells (hCSCs), which are a subtype of HCCs with a poor prognosis. The study also found that inhibition of a molecular pathway involved in EpCAM RIP and Wnt signaling can be a potential therapeutic strategy for this subtype of HBV-associated HCCs. In summary, the study uncovered a new molecular mechanism underlying HBV-induced HCC and identifies a potential therapeutic target for this subtype of liver cancer.

title: Parathyroid Hormone Directs Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Cell Fate.
text: Intermittent PTH administration has been shown to build bone mass and prevent fractures, but the exact mechanism of its action is still not fully understood. To investigate, we used genetic deletion of the PTH/PTHrP receptor (PTH1R) in mesenchymal stem cells using Prx1Cre and observed reduced bone formation, increased bone resorption, and high levels of bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT). Surprisingly, we found that bone marrow adipocytes expressed classic adipogenic markers and high levels of RANKL, a protein that plays a key role in bone metabolism. Interestingly, RANKL levels were elevated not only in bone marrow, but also in the serum and other adipose depots. We also found that Pref1+RANKL+ marrow progenitors were twice as abundant in mutant mice compared to controls. Curiously, intermittent PTH administration to control mice significantly reduced BMAT. This observation was also seen in male osteoporotic patients. These findings suggest that marrow adipocytes have both osteogenic and adipogenic capacities and are uniquely responsive to PTH, which may explain the therapeutic benefits of PTH treatment.

title: Metformin attenuates blood-brain barrier disruption in mice following middle cerebral artery occlusion
text:
STUDY BACKGROUND: Metformin, a common medication for lowering blood sugar, has been shown to reduce stroke risk and inflammation in clinical trials. However, its effect on ischemic stroke in mice is not fully understood.
STUDY QUESTION: We investigated the effect of metformin on ischemic stroke in mice and explored the possible reasons why it works.
METHODS: We used 98 male mice to study the effects of metformin on transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). We gave the mice metformin (200 mg/kg) for up to 14 days after the stroke. We measured neurological function, brain damage, inflammation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, and the AMPK signaling pathway. We also tested the effects of metformin on brain cells (bEND.3 cells) in the laboratory.
RESULTS: We found that metformin reduced brain damage and inflammation in mice after tMCAO. Metformin also improved neurological function in the mice. We found that metformin decreased the number of immune cells (MPO+ cells, Gr1+ cells) and inflammatory chemicals (MPO activity and BBB permeability) in the brain. Metformin also activated a protein called AMPK and blocked a protein called NF-κB, which are involved in inflammation. Furthermore, metformin reduced the expression of cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and ICAM-1 in the brain. In the laboratory, metformin activated AMPK signaling pathway and reduced ICAM-1 expression in bEND.3 cells.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study shows that metformin reduces brain damage after ischemic stroke by decreasing inflammation and activating a protein called AMPK. This suggests that metformin may be a promising treatment for stroke.

title: Epstein-Barr Virus nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) confers resistance to apoptosis in EBV-positive B-lymphoma cells through up-regulation of survivin.
text: Resistance to programmed cell death, or apoptosis, is a crucial component of the complex mechanism that drives the development of tumors. The ubiquitous human gamma-herpesvirus, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), preferentially infects and establishes a latent infection in B-lymphocytes. EBNA1, a key protein encoded by EBV, is expressed in most EBV-positive malignancies and plays a vital role in the replication of the latent episome in conjunction with the replication of the host cells. In this study, we investigate the effects of EBNA1 on survivin up-regulation in EBV-infected human B-lymphoma cells. We demonstrate that EBNA1 forms a complex with Sp1 or Sp1-like proteins bound to their cis-element at the survivin promoter, which enhances the activity of the complex and up-regulates survivin. Additionally, we show that knockdown of survivin and EBNA1 leads to enhanced apoptosis in infected cells, providing evidence for a role of EBNA1 in suppressing apoptosis in EBV-infected cells. Based on these findings, we suggest that the oncogenic potential of EBV is linked to the up-regulation of the anti-apoptotic protein, survivin, by the EBV-encoded EBNA1 in EBV-associated B-lymphoma cells.

title: Microfluidic platform to evaluate migration of cells from patients with DYT1 dystonia.
text: BACKGROUND: Microfluidic platforms offer a cost-effective and time-efficient means of evaluating cellular processes, enabling researchers to study various biological and pathological events, such as the real-time imaging of cell migration. Cell migration plays a crucial role in both healthy and disease states, including development, wound healing, and maintaining homeostasis. NEW METHOD: Utilizing microfluidic chambers, we have developed a novel method to investigate the impact of a specific gene mutation on cell migration. Specifically, we have examined fibroblasts harboring a mutation in the TOR1A gene, which is associated with the hereditary neurological disorder DYT1 dystonia, and compared their migration properties to those of control cells. RESULTS: Our findings revealed that fibroblasts from DYT1 patients exhibited abnormalities in basic cell migration features, including reduced velocity and altered movement patterns. COMPARISON TO EXISTING METHOD: In contrast to traditional methods, our microfluidic approach allowed for the visualization of individual cells and provided greater resolution in assessing cell polarity and movement. CONCLUSION: We have demonstrated the value of using a microfluidic platform in evaluating the impact of a specific gene mutation on cell migration, uncovering various parameters that contribute to cellular dysfunction in DYT1 patients. This novel assay provides a means to study cellular behavior in a three-dimensional environment with single-cell resolution, offering insights into the mechanisms underlying neurological disorders.

title: Sugar-sweetened beverages and weight gain in children and adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text: BACKGROUND: The association between sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs) and weight remains controversial. OBJECTIVE: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to summarize the evidence in children and adults. DESIGN: PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases were searched through March 2013 for prospective cohort studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the SSB-weight relationship. Separate meta-analyses were conducted in children and adults and for cohorts and RCTs using random- and fixed-effects models. RESULTS: Thirty-two original articles were included in the meta-analyses: 20 in children (15 cohort studies, n = 25,745; 5 trials, n = 2772) and 12 in adults (7 cohort studies, n = 174,252; 5 trials, n = 292). In cohort studies, one daily serving increment of SSBs was associated with a 0.06 (95% CI: 0.02, 0.10) and 0.05 (95% CI: 0.03, 0.07)-unit increase in BMI in children and 0.22 kg (95% CI: 0.09, 0.34 kg) and 0.12 kg (95% CI: 0.10, 0.14 kg) weight gain in adults over 1 year in random- and fixed-effects models, respectively. RCTs in children showed reductions in BMI gain when SSBs were reduced [random and fixed effects: -0.17 (95% CI: -0.39, 0.05) and -0.12 (95% CI: -0.22, -0.20)], whereas RCTs in adults showed increases in body weight when SSBs were added [random and fixed effects: 0.85 kg; 95% CI: 0.50, 1.20 kg]. Sensitivity analyses of RCTs in children showed more pronounced benefits in preventing weight gain in SSB substitution trials compared with school-based educational programs and among overweight children compared with normal-weight children. CONCLUSION: Our systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies and RCTs provide evidence that SSB consumption promotes weight gain in children and adults.

title: The tumorigenic potential of pluripotent stem cells: What can we do to minimize it?
text: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) possess immense potential to revolutionize the manner in which we treat and comprehend human disease. Nonetheless, these cells also inherently possess a capacity to form tumors in immunocompromised individuals when introduced in their pluripotent state. Current therapeutic strategies involve transplantation of only differentiated hPSC derivatives, despite the possibility that transplanted cell populations may contain a small percentage of undifferentiated cells. Moreover, these cells have been frequently reported to acquire genetic alterations that, in some instances, are associated with certain types of human cancers. In this article, we strive to separate fact from panic and rationally evaluate the true tumorigenic potential of hPSCs. We also discuss a recent study exploring the impact of culture conditions on the genetic integrity of hPSCs. Finally, we present a set of logical guidelines for minimizing the tumorigenic potential of hPSC-derived cells. © 2016 The Authors. Inside the Cell published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

title: Epidemiology of sepsis and septic shock in critical care units: comparison between sepsis-2 and sepsis-3 populations using a national critical care database
text: A new study compared the sepsis populations identified by the old and new definitions of sepsis using a high-quality, national ICU database in England. The study found that the new definition, Sepsis-3, identifies a different population than the old definition, Sepsis-2, with 92% overlap between the two definitions. Specifically, Sepsis-3 identifies a smaller population of septic shock with improved predictive validity compared to Sepsis-2. The study also found that both Sepsis-2 and Sepsis-3 had similar incidence and mortality rates, but Sepsis-3 septic shock had a higher APACHE II score, greater mortality, and no risk-adjusted trends in mortality improvement compared to Sepsis-2 septic shock. The study concluded that Sepsis-3 identifies a similar sepsis population as Sepsis-2, but with a smaller septic shock population that is more predictive of mortality.

title: Thymic expression of the golli-myelin basic protein gene in the SJL/J mouse
text: The T cell antigen-specific repertoire is believed to be influenced by the expression of self-molecules in the thymus. Previous research has shown that a myelin basic protein (MBP)-like gene (golli-MBP) is expressed by immune cells, prompting this study to investigate whether golli-MBP is expressed in the mouse thymus and, if so, to characterize the transcripts of this gene in this organ. Using exon-specific primers for MBP and golli-MBP, cDNA from thymus and other tissues was amplified and analyzed via Southern blotting with exon-specific oligonucleotide probes. The amplified products were then subcloned and sequenced to determine the thymic transcripts, which were found to contain exons 1, 2, 3, 5A, 5B, 5C, 6, 7, 8, and 11 of the golli-MBP gene.

title: Urine microRNAs as biomarkers for bladder cancer: a diagnostic meta-analysis
text:
BACKGROUND:
The value of microRNA (miRNA) detection in diagnosing bladder cancer (BCa) remains controversial. To evaluate the current evidence, we conducted a systematic meta-analysis of published studies.
METHODS:
We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for studies published before March 31, 2015, and included studies that reported on the diagnostic accuracy of miRNA assays for BCa. We extracted the pooled sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratios, diagnostic odds ratio, and area under the curve (AUC) for each study. We performed subgroup analyses to examine between-study heterogeneity and used Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test to check for publication bias. We used RevMan 5.2 and Stata 11.0 for the meta-analysis.
RESULTS:
Our meta-analysis included 23 studies with a total of 719 BCa patients and 494 controls. The pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.75 (95% CI, 0.68-0.80) and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.70-0.80), respectively. The pooled positive likelihood ratio was 3.03 (95% CI, 2.50-3.67), and negative likelihood ratio was 0.33 (95% CI, 0.27-0.42). The diagnostic odds ratio was 9.07 (95% CI, 6.35-12.95). The pooled AUC was 0.81 (95% CI, 0.78-0.85). Subgroup analyses revealed that multiple miRNAs assays and urine supernatant assays had high accuracies in diagnosing BCa.
CONCLUSION:
Our findings suggest that miRNA assays may have potential as a non-invasive diagnostic tool for BCa. However, further validation through large prospective studies is needed to confirm these results.

title: Elevated Plasma Transforming Growth Factor &bgr;1 Levels Predict the Development of Hypertension in Normotensives: The 14-Year Follow-Up Study
text:
Background: Transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-β1) is a multifunctional cytokine involved in various biological processes, including the pathogenesis of hypertension and development of target organ damage. Although several studies have shown TGF-β1's role in vascular hypertrophy and remodeling, there are limited epidemiological studies on its predictive value for hypertension in large populations. This study aimed to investigate whether elevated TGF-β1 levels can predict the development of hypertension in a community-dwelling population.
Methods: In 2002-2004, 528 individuals received a comprehensive health examination in Uku town, Japan. Plasma TGF-β1 levels were measured, and data on blood pressure (BP), body mass index, and other blood tests were collected. Of 149 normotensives (BP <140/90 mmHg without antihypertensive medication) at baseline, 59 developed hypertension over a 14-year follow-up period.
Results: The receiver operating characteristic curve was used to determine the optimal cutoff value for plasma TGF-β1, which was 8.9 ng/ml. Compared to normotensives with lower TGF-β1 levels, those with higher levels were significantly more likely to develop hypertension after adjusting for potential confounders (odds ratio: 3.582; 95% CI: 1.025-12.525). Logistic regression analysis revealed a significant association between high TGF-β1 levels and hypertension development.
Conclusions: This study demonstrates a causal relationship between TGF-β1 and hypertension development in a community-dwelling population. Higher plasma TGF-β1 levels predicted the development of hypertension in normotensives, suggesting that TGF-β1 may serve as a predictive marker for hypertension risk assessment.

title: MYC Disrupts the Circadian Clock and Metabolism in Cancer Cells.
text:
The MYC oncogene encodes the transcription factor MYC, which binds to specific regions of the genome, called E-boxes (5'-CACGTG-3'), along with its heterodimeric partner CLOCK-BMAL1. This binding regulates the expression of genes involved in the circadian network. As a result, we hypothesized that excessive MYC expression disrupts the molecular clock in cancer cells by altering the regulation of E-box-driven genes. Our findings confirm this hypothesis, showing that deregulated MYC or N-MYC expression leads to the direct suppression and oscillation of BMAL1, which can be rescued by decreasing REV-ERBα expression. Interestingly, high levels of REV-ERBα expression are associated with poor clinical outcomes in N-MYC-driven human neuroblastomas that display low levels of BMAL1 expression. Additionally, re-expression of ectopic BMAL1 in neuroblastoma cell lines attenuates their clonogenicity. Our results reveal an unanticipated link between oncogenic transformation and the dysregulation of the circadian and metabolic cycles, which we propose to be beneficial for cancer growth.
Key points of the rewrite include:
* The MYC oncogene encodes the transcription factor MYC, which binds to specific sites in the genome called E-boxes along with CLOCK-BMAL1.
* Deregulated MYC expression disrupts the molecular clock in cancer cells by altering the regulation of E-box-driven genes.
* High levels of REV-ERBα expression are associated with poor clinical outcomes in N-MYC-driven human neuroblastomas that display low levels of BMAL1 expression.
