* Re-expression of ectopic BMAL1 in neuroblastoma cell lines attenuates their clonogenicity.
* Our results reveal an unanticipated link between oncogenic transformation and the dysregulation of the circadian and metabolic cycles, which we propose to be beneficial for cancer growth.

title: Integrated maps in quail (Coturnix japonica) confirm the high degree of synteny conservation with chicken (Gallus gallus) despite 35 million years of divergence
text: By comparing the genomes of quail and chicken, researchers have discovered changes in chromosome arrangement that have occurred over 35 million years of evolution. This information can be used to enhance the utility of quail in biological studies by predicting the position of genes based on chicken sequence data. Previously published genetic maps of quail and chicken, as well as cytogenetic data, were integrated to create an integrated linkage map for quail. This map was generated through segregation analysis of both anonymous markers and functional gene loci in 1,050 quail from three independent F2 populations. Ninety-two loci were resolved into 14 autosomal linkage groups and a Z chromosome-specific linkage group, which aligned with the quail AFLP map. The map spans 904.3 cM with an average distance of 9.7 cM between loci, but some markers on macrochromosomes CJA08, the gonosome CJAW, and 23 microchromosomes remain unassigned. The alignment of quail linkage groups with the chicken genome sequence assembly revealed high similarities in marker order between the two species for the eight macrochromosomes and 14 microchromosomes studied. Integrating the two microsatellite and AFLP quail genetic maps significantly improves the quality of the resulting information, which will facilitate the identification of Quantitative Trait Loci (QTL). The high conservation of gene order between macrochromosomes in quail and chicken suggests that a wealth of information can be mined in chicken to be used for genome analyses in quail.

title: Cadherin activity is required for activity-induced spine remodeling
text: Neural activity triggers the remodeling of pre- and postsynaptic membranes, which maintain their close association through cell adhesion molecules. Among these molecules, N-cadherin is redistributed, undergoes activity-dependent conformational changes, and is essential for synaptic plasticity. We discovered that depolarization leads to an increase in the width of spine heads, and that cadherin activity is crucial for this synaptic rearrangement. Using green fluorescent protein to visualize dendritic spines in hippocampal neurons, we found that activation of AMPA receptors results in an expansion of the synaptic apposition zone. N-cadherin-Venus fusion protein spreads along the growing spine heads. Overexpression of dominant-negative forms of N-cadherin hinders the spine expansion, while inhibition of actin polymerization with cytochalasin D abolishes the spine expansion. Our findings suggest that the cadherin-based adhesion machinery, in collaboration with the actin cytoskeleton, is essential for the remodeling of the synaptic apposition zone.

title: Aliskiren combined with losartan in type 2 diabetes and nephropathy.
text:
Title: Renal Protective Effects of Dual Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System Blockade in Hypertensive Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Nephropathy
Background: Diabetic nephropathy is the leading cause of end-stage renal disease in developed countries. This study aimed to evaluate the renoprotective effects of dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) by adding treatment with aliskiren, an oral direct renin inhibitor, to treatment with the maximum recommended dose of losartan and optimal antihypertensive therapy in patients with hypertension and type 2 diabetes with nephropathy.
Methods: This multinational, randomized, double-blind study enrolled 599 patients. After a 3-month, open-label run-in period, patients were randomly assigned to receive 6 months of treatment with aliskiren (150 mg daily for 3 months, followed by an increase in dosage to 300 mg daily for another 3 months) or placebo, in addition to losartan. The primary outcome was the reduction in the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, measured in an early-morning urine sample, at 6 months.
Results: The baseline characteristics of the two groups were similar. Treatment with 300 mg of aliskiren daily reduced the mean urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio by 20% (95% CI: 9-30; P<0.001), with a reduction of 50% or more in 24.7% of the patients who received aliskiren compared to 12.5% of those who received placebo (P<0.001). A small difference in blood pressure was seen between the treatment groups by the end of the study period (systolic, -2 mm Hg; diastolic, -1 mm Hg). The total number of adverse and serious adverse events was similar in the groups.
Conclusions: Aliskiren may have renoprotective effects that are independent of its blood pressure-lowering effect in patients with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and nephropathy who are receiving the recommended renoprotective treatment. (ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT00097955 [ClinicalTrials.gov].)

title: Overweight in Celiac Disease: Prevalence, Clinical Characteristics, and Effect of a Gluten-Free Diet
text:
BACKGROUND: Research has shown that a small percentage of celiac patients experience classic symptoms due to malabsorption, but there is a lack of data on the distribution of body mass index (BMI) in celiac populations and its relationship to clinical characteristics, as well as the response to treatment.
METHODS: We examined BMI measurements and other clinical and pathological characteristics from a database of 371 celiac patients diagnosed over a 10-year period and seen by a single gastroenterologist. To assess the response to gluten exclusion, we compared BMI at diagnosis and after 2 years of treatment in patients with serological evidence of dietary compliance.
RESULTS: Our analysis found that the mean BMI was 24.6 kg/m2 (ranging from 16.3 to 43.5). A total of 5% of patients were underweight (BMI <18.5), while 57% were normal and 39% were overweight (including 13% who were obese, defined as BMI ≥30.0). We observed a significant association between low BMI and female gender, history of diarrhea, reduced hemoglobin concentration, reduced bone mineral density (BMD), osteoporosis, and higher grades (subtotal/total) of villous atrophy. Notably, 81% of patients who were compliant with a gluten-free diet gained weight after 2 years, including 82% of initially overweight patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that the majority of celiac patients are not underweight at diagnosis and that a significant proportion is overweight. The lack of awareness of this large subgroup may contribute to the delayed or failed diagnosis of celiac disease. Further, the increase in weight of already overweight patients after dietary gluten exclusion may lead to increased morbidity. Modifications to the conventional gluten-free diet may be necessary to address this issue.

title: Structural Studies of a Four-MBT Repeat Protein MBTD1
text:
THE BACKGROUND OF THE POLYBETAIN GROUP (PcG) PROTEINS:
The Polycomb group (PcG) of proteins is a critical family of developmental regulators that play essential roles in the establishment and maintenance of transcriptional repression of developmental control genes. One such PcG protein, MBTD1, contains four MBT repeats and has been the focus of recent research.
METHODOLOGY AND PRINCIPAL FINDINGS:
To gain insight into the structure and function of MBTD1, we determined its crystal structure at 2.5 Å resolution by X-ray crystallography. Our findings reveal that MBTD1 shares a similar architecture with another four-MBT-repeat protein, L3MBTL2, which binds lower methylated lysine histones. Fluorescence polarization experiments further confirmed that MBTD1 selectively binds mono- and dimethyllysine histone peptides, similar to L3MBTL1 and L3MBTL2. However, our mutagenesis data based on L3MBTL1 suggested that histone peptides cannot bind to MBT repeats in any orientation.
CONCLUSIONS:
Our study reveals that the four MBT repeats in MBTD1 adopt an asymmetric rhomboid architecture. In line with previous findings on other MBT repeat proteins, MBTD1 binds mono- or dimethylated lysine histones through one of its four MBT repeats using a semi-aromatic cage.
ENHANCED VERSION:
This article can also be accessed in an enhanced version, which integrates interactive 3D representations and animated transitions with the text of the article. To access this enhanced functionality, a web plugin is required. Instructions for installation and use are available in Text S1.

title: Glutamine supports pancreatic cancer growth through a Kras-regulated metabolic pathway
text: Cancer cells have unique metabolic characteristics that distinguish them from their normal counterparts. One of these dependencies is an increased reliance on the amino acid glutamine to fuel anabolic processes. Researchers are actively investigating the spectrum of glutamine-dependent tumors and the mechanisms by which glutamine supports cancer metabolism. In this study, we identify a non-canonical pathway of glutamine use in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells that is critical for tumor growth. Unlike most cells, which use glutamate dehydrogenase (GLUD1) to convert glutamine-derived glutamate into α-ketoglutarate in the mitochondria to fuel the tricarboxylic acid cycle, PDAC cells rely on a distinct pathway in which glutamine-derived aspartate is transported into the cytoplasm and converted into oxaloacetate by aspartate transaminase (GOT1). This oxaloacetate is then converted into malate and then pyruvate, increasing the NADPH/NADP(+) ratio, which can potentially maintain the cellular redox state. PDAC cells are highly dependent on this series of reactions, as glutamine deprivation or genetic inhibition of any enzyme in this pathway leads to an increase in reactive oxygen species and a decrease in reduced glutathione. Moreover, knockdown of any component enzyme in this series of reactions results in a pronounced suppression of PDAC growth in vitro and in vivo. Interestingly, we find that the reprogramming of glutamine metabolism in PDAC is mediated by oncogenic KRAS, the signature genetic alteration in PDAC, through the transcriptional upregulation and repression of key metabolic enzymes in this pathway. The essentiality of this pathway in PDAC and the fact that it is dispensable in normal cells may provide novel therapeutic approaches to treat these refractory tumors.

title: CD4+ T cell help guides formation of CD103+ lung-resident memory CD8+ T cells during influenza viral infection.
text: Tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells provide enhanced protection at mucosal sites by providing effective immunity at the site of infection. In the context of lung-resident CD8(+) T cells, we found that CD4(+) T cells play a vital role in forming functional CD8(+) T cells after influenza virus infection. With the absence of CD4(+) T cells, CD8(+) T cells display reduced expression of CD103 (Itgae), become mislocalized away from airway epithelia, and have an impaired ability to recruit CD8(+) T cells to the lung airways upon heterosubtypic challenge. CD4(+) T cell-derived interferon-γ is necessary for generating lung-resident CD103(+) CD8(+) Trm cells. Furthermore, an increase in the transcription factor T-bet in "unhelped" lung Trm cells can be rescued by a reduction in T-bet, which allows for the development of CD103(+) CD8(+) Trm cells in the lung airways following respiratory infection.

title: Inhibition of Apoptosis Overcomes Stage-Related Compatibility Barriers to Chimera Formation in Mouse Embryos.
text: Cell types more developed in development than embryonic stem cells, such as epiblast stem cells (EpiSCs), often fail to contribute to chimeras when injected into pre-implantation-stage blastocysts, perhaps owing to the irreversible fate of the injected cells undergoing programmed cellular suicide, or apoptosis. To overcome this limitation, we demonstrate that temporary enhancement of cell survival through the expression of the anti-apoptotic gene BCL2 can enable EpiSCs and Sox17+ endoderm progenitors to integrate into blastocysts and contribute to chimeric embryos. Upon injection into blastocysts, BCL2-expressing EpiSCs can contribute to all major tissue types in chimeric animals, while Sox17+ endoderm progenitors specifically contribute in a tissue-specific manner to endodermal tissues. Additionally, the use of BCL2 expression technology enables rat EpiSCs to contribute to mouse embryonic chimeras, resulting in the formation of interspecies chimeras that can survive to adulthood. This approach offers a means to surpass the typical cellular compatibility limitations that impede chimera formation, thus expanding the potential applications of embryonic chimeras, including region-specific chimeras, in fundamental developmental biology research and regenerative medicine.

title: Computational and Statistical Analyses of Amino Acid Usage and Physico-Chemical Properties of the Twelve Late Embryogenesis Abundant Protein Classes
text: Late Embryogenesis Abundant Proteins (LEAPs) are proteins expected to play significant roles in desiccation tolerance, but their structure-function relationships are poorly understood due to the scarcity of three-dimensional structures. To address this limitation, we built LEAPdb, a database of LEAPs from plants and other organisms, which enabled the classification of 710 LEAPs into 12 non-overlapping classes based on their distinct properties. Using this resource, we computed and statistically analyzed various physico-chemical properties of LEAPs and their amino acid usage, revealing unique features for each class. Our detailed analysis rigorously characterized the 12 LEAP classes, which exhibited distinct structural and physico-chemical features. While most LEAPs are predicted to be intrinsically disordered proteins, our study suggests that LEAP class 7 (PF03168) and possibly LEAP class 11 (PF04927) may be natively folded proteins. This study provides a comprehensive description of the structural properties of this protein family, paving the way for further LEAP structure-function analysis. Additionally, since each LEAP class can be distinctly characterized by a unique set of physico-chemical properties, we can develop software to predict proteins as LEAPs.

title: Direct Reprogramming of Hepatic Myofibroblasts into Hepatocytes In Vivo Attenuates Liver Fibrosis.
text: Induction of induced hepatocytes (iHeps) from fibroblasts holds promise as a regenerative medicine strategy, but until now has only been demonstrated in cultured settings. In this study, we investigate in vivo iHep formation using transcription factor induction and genetic fate tracing in mouse models of chronic liver disease. We show that forced expression of transcription factors FOXA3, GATA4, HNF1A, and HNF4A from a polycistronic lentiviral vector can convert mouse myofibroblasts into cells with a hepatocyte phenotype. Additionally, we demonstrate in vivo expression of the same set of transcription factors from a p75 neurotrophin receptor peptide (p75NTRp)-tagged adenovirus can generate hepatocyte-like cells from myofibroblasts in fibrotic mouse livers, reducing liver fibrosis. By directly reprogramming pro-fibrogenic myofibroblats in the liver into hepatocyte-like cells with positive functional benefits, this in vivo reprogramming approach may provide new avenues for treating chronic liver disease.

title: Epithelial to Mesenchymal Transition by TGFβ-1 Induction Increases Stemness Characteristics in Primary Non Small Cell Lung Cancer Cell Line
text:
Background: The Cancer Stem Cell (CSC) hypothesis proposes that a small subset of cells within a tumor is responsible for both tumor initiation and progression. The Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) is a developmental program that is often activated during cancer invasion and metastasis. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between EMT and CSCs using the LC31 lung cancer primary cell line.
Methods: LC31 and A549 cell lines were treated with 2 ng/ml TGFβ-1 for 30 and 80 days, respectively. The expression of epithelial and mesenchymal markers was evaluated through morphological changes, immunofluorescence, and cytometry. RT-PCR was performed to assess the expression of Slug, Twist, and β-catenin genes. Stemness tests, including pneumosphere growth and marker expression, were performed on TGFβ-1-treated and untreated LC31 cell lines. Western blot and tumorigenicity assays using NOD/SCID mice were also conducted.
Results: Treatment of LC31 cell line with TGFβ-1 resulted in loss of epithelial morphology and assumption of a fibroblast-like appearance. Both the LC31 and A549 cell lines showed up-regulation of vimentin and CD90 and down-regulation of cytokeratin, e-cadherin, and CD326 with TGFβ-1 treatment. Slug, Twist, and β-catenin m-RNA transcripts were up-regulated in TGFβ-1-treated LC31 cell line, confirming EMT. This cell line showed over-expression of Oct4, Nanog, Sox2, and CD133, all markers of stemness. In addition, TGFβ-1-treated LC31 cell line exhibited increased pneumosphere-forming capacity and tumor-forming ability in NOD/SCID mice.

Discussion: The results of this study suggest that exposure to TGFβ-1 induces EMT in primary lung cancer cells, leading to the acquisition of mesenchymal markers and the expression of stem cell markers. This suggests that the two processes are linked and that mesenchymal changes may play a role in the development and progression of cancer. These findings may have implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for cancer treatment.

title: Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b Associate with Enhancers to Regulate Human Epidermal Stem Cell Homeostasis.
text: The genomic distribution and functional implications of endogenous Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b proteins in adult stem cells are currently uncharted. This study aims to explore their binding preferences in human epidermal stem cells and their roles in enhancer regulation. Our findings show that both Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b bind to enhancer regions in a histone H3K36me3-dependent manner, with a specific preference for the most active enhancers. Analysis of gene expression profiling data revealed that these proteins are essential for the production of enhancer RNAs associated with these enhancers. Furthermore, we found that both proteins play distinct roles in enhancer regulation, with Dnmt3a associating with p63 to maintain high levels of DNA hydroxymethylation at the center of enhancers in a Tet2-dependent manner, while Dnmt3b promotes DNA methylation along the body of the enhancer. Remarkably, depletion of either protein leads to the inactivation of their target enhancers and significantly impacts epidermal stem cell function. Overall, this study uncovered novel functions of Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b at enhancers that could contribute to their implicated roles in disease and tumorigenesis.

title: CDK inhibitors in cancer therapy: what is next?
text: The quest for drugs that obstruct cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) has been a concentrated area of research for over 15 years. Early prototypes, such as Flavopiridol and CY-202, are currently in late-stage clinical trials, but have only demonstrated moderate effectiveness thus far. Several newer generations of inhibitors are now being tested in clinical trials. In order to determine the clinical benefit of these drugs in cancer treatment, future approaches must incorporate both the lessons learned from previous compounds and the recent genetic information obtained from preclinical model analysis. Here, we will discuss crucial concepts that need to be considered when validating the clinical utility of CDK inhibitors in cancer therapy.

title: Lipid Desaturation Is a Metabolic Marker and Therapeutic Target of Ovarian Cancer Stem Cells.
text: Scientists have had difficulty analyzing the metabolic activity of cancer stem cells (CSCs) because they lacked the right tools. So, they used a technique called hyperspectral-stimulated Raman scattering imaging to study single living cancer cells and analyze their lipids using mass spectrometry. They found that CSCs have much higher levels of unsaturated lipids compared to non-CSCs. These higher levels were also seen in CSC-enriched spheroids compared to monolayer cultures of ovarian cancer cells or primary cells. When they inhibited the enzymes that change the structure of lipids, they found that it eliminated CSCs, stopped sphere formation in vitro, and blocked tumor growth in vivo. They also found that a protein called nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) regulates the expression of these enzymes, and inhibiting them stopped NF-κB signaling. Overall, their findings show that increased lipid unsaturation is a useful marker for identifying ovarian CSCs and a promising target for CSC-specific therapy.

title: Mesenchymal Inflammation Drives Genotoxic Stress in Hematopoietic Stem Cells and Predicts Disease Evolution in Human Pre-leukemia.
text: Mesenchymal cells in the bone marrow microenvironment may play a crucial role in the development of blood cancers, but the molecular mechanisms involved are not well understood. To investigate, we studied mice with a pre-leukemic disorder called Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS) and found that perturbation of mesenchymal cells leads to problems with the mitochondria, oxidative stress, and the activation of DNA damage response pathways in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. By analyzing the RNA of highly purified mesenchymal cells in mouse models and human pre-leukemic syndromes, we identified p53-S100A8/9-TLR inflammatory signaling as a shared mechanism underlying genotoxic stress in these cells. Furthermore, we found that the activation of this signaling pathway in the mesenchymal niche can predict the evolution and progression of leukemia in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), the most common pre-leukemic disorder. In conclusion, our findings suggest that mesenchymal niche-induced genotoxic stress in heterotypic stem and progenitor cells through inflammatory signaling is a targetable determinant of disease outcome in human pre-leukemia.

title: Novel Functional Sets of Lipid-Derived Mediators with Antiinflammatory Actions Generated from Omega-3 Fatty Acids via Cyclooxygenase 2–Nonsteroidal Antiinflammatory Drugs and Transcellular Processing
text: Aspirin therapy stops prostaglandin production without directly affecting lipoxygenases, yet it leads to the creation of bioactive lipoxins (LXs) through the acetylation of cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2). We have found that inflammatory fluids from mice treated with omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids and aspirin produce a new range of bioactive lipid signals. Human endothelial cells with elevated COX-2 activity, which are treated with aspirin, generate 18R-hydroxyeicosapentaenoic acid (HEPE) and 15R-HEPE from the omega-3 fatty acid C20:5. Each of these compounds is taken up by polymorphonuclear leukocytes, which then generate distinct classes of novel trihydroxy-containing mediators, including 5-series 15R-LX5 and 5,12,18R-triHEPE. These new compounds were discovered to be highly effective at inhibiting the migration of human polymorphonuclear leukocytes into the bloodstream in vivo (ATL analogue > 5,12,18R-triHEPE > 18R-HEPE). Acetaminophen and indomethacin also permit the generation of 18R-HEPE and 15R-HEPE using recombinant COX-2, as well as the oxygenation of other fatty acids that affect hematologic cells. These findings establish novel transcellular pathways for creating arrays of bioactive lipid mediators through COX-2-dependent oxygenations and cell-cell interactions, which can have a significant impact on microinflammation. The creation of these and related compounds provides a previously unknown mechanism for the therapeutic benefits of omega-3 supplementation, which may be crucial in conditions such as inflammation, cancer, and vascular diseases.

title: Cholesteryl Ester Transfer Protein (CETP) Polymorphisms Affect mRNA Splicing, HDL Levels, and Sex-Dependent Cardiovascular Risk
text: Variations in the Cholesteryl Ester Transfer Protein (CETP) gene have been linked to HDL levels, risk of coronary artery disease (CAD), and response to treatment. However, the underlying mechanisms of these variations remain unclear. To investigate, we analyzed mRNA allelic expression and splice isoform measurements in human liver tissues to identify genetic variants that influence CETP levels. Our findings revealed that certain variants in the CETP gene, specifically those located 2.5-7 kilobases upstream of the transcription start site, were associated with changes in CETP expression. We also identified a common alternatively spliced CETP isoform lacking exon 9, which inhibits CETP secretion in a dominant-negative manner. This isoform was found to be more prevalent in individuals carrying a specific variant in intron 8. The effects of these polymorphisms were evaluated in two clinical studies, which showed that both the rs247616 and rs5883T/rs9930761C variants were independently associated with increased HDL-C levels in male subjects. Additionally, the rs5883T/rs9930761C variant was found to be significantly associated with an increased incidence of myocardial infarction, stroke, and all-cause mortality in male subjects. These findings suggest that genetic variations in the CETP gene can have sex-dependent effects on cardiovascular risk through a mechanism that is independent of circulating HDL-C levels.

title: 6-Sulphated Chondroitins Have a Positive Influence on Axonal Regeneration
text: Chondroitin sulphate proteoglycans (CSPGs) in the glial scar inhibit axon regeneration by sulphating glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). After injury, chondroitin 6-sulphotransferase-1 (C6ST-1) is upregulated, resulting in an increase in 6-sulphated GAGs. In this study, we investigate whether this increase in 6-sulphated GAGs is responsible for the enhanced inhibition within the glial scar or represents a partial return to a more permissive embryonic state dominated by 6-sulphated GAGs. We used C6ST-1 knockout (KO) mice to examine post-injury changes in chondroitin sulphotransferase (CSST) expression and the effect of 6-sulphated chondroitin on both central and peripheral axon regeneration. Our findings show that after central nervous system (CNS) injury, wild-type (WT) animals upregulate mRNA for C6ST-1, C6ST-2, and C4ST-1, but KO does not upregulate any CSSTs. In contrast, after peripheral nervous system (PNS) injury, WT upregulates C6ST-1, while KO shows an upregulation of C6ST-2. We observed that nigrostriatal axons in WT show mild spontaneous axon regeneration, while KO shows fewer regenerating axons and more axonal retraction. However, in the PNS, repair of the median and ulnar nerves led to similar and normal levels of axon regeneration in both WT and KO. Functional tests on plasticity after repair also showed no evidence of enhanced plasticity in KO. Our results suggest that the upregulation of 6-sulphated GAGs after injury makes the extracellular matrix more permissive for axon regeneration, and that the balance of different CSs in the microenvironment around the lesion site is a crucial factor in determining the outcome of nervous system injury.

title: Tissue Mechanics Orchestrate Wnt-Dependent Human Embryonic Stem Cell Differentiation.
text: Regenerative medicine is based on understanding the mechanisms that control development and applying these insights to direct the fate of stem cells. During embryonic development, cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions play a crucial role in guiding the formation of different tissues. However, it remains unclear how these physical cues influence stem cells in a laboratory setting. To address this question, we used human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) to investigate whether the mechanical properties of the extracellular microenvironment can influence tissue-specific differentiation. We found that when hESCs are cultured on a hydrogel-based, compliant matrix, they accumulate more β-catenin at cell-cell adhesions and exhibit enhanced Wnt-dependent mesoderm differentiation. We discovered that this effect is mediated by Src-driven ubiquitination of E-cadherin by a Cbl-like ubiquitin ligase, which releases P120-catenin to enhance the transcriptional activity of β-catenin and initiate mesoderm differentiation. In contrast, when hESCs are cultured on a stiff hydrogel matrix, they exhibit elevated integrin-dependent GSK3 and Src activity, which leads to reduced β-catenin levels and inhibition of differentiation. Our findings demonstrate that the mechanical properties of the microenvironmental matrix can significantly influence the differentiation of hESCs by modulating their response to morphogens.

title: Predictive performance of the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score as a screening tool for sepsis, mortality, and intensive care unit admission in patients with febrile neutropenia
text: In the Sepsis-3 study, the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) score was developed and used to predict poor outcomes in patients with fever and neutropenia (FN). To evaluate the qSOFA score's performance as a screening tool, we analyzed a prospective adult FN data registry. We compared the qSOFA score with the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) criteria and Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer (MASCC) score for FN. Our results showed that qSOFA was a significant predictor of sepsis and ICU admission in multivariate analysis, but its performance was inferior to that of the MASCC score. However, the qSOFA score showed high specificity in predicting sepsis, 28-day mortality, and ICU admission, with low sensitivity. Our findings suggest that the preexisting risk stratification tool is more useful for predicting outcomes in patients with FN.

title: LIN28 Regulates Stem Cell Metabolism and Conversion to Primed Pluripotency.
text: RNA-binding proteins LIN28A and LIN28B play crucial roles in embryonic development, tumorigenesis, and pluripotency, but their precise functions are still poorly understood. Our data reveals that, just like LIN28A, LIN28B can cooperate effectively with NANOG, OCT4, and SOX2 during reprogramming to pluripotency, and that the reactivation of both endogenous LIN28A and LIN28B loci is essential for maximizing reprogramming efficiency in human fibroblasts. In contrast, LIN28B is activated earlier during reprogramming in human fibroblasts, while LIN28A is activated later during the transition to bona fide induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). In murine cells, both LIN28A and LIN28B facilitate the conversion from naive to primed pluripotency. Through proteomic and metabolomic analysis, we discovered that LIN28 regulates the maintenance of low mitochondrial function linked to primed pluripotency and regulates transcriptional control of one-carbon metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, and histone methylation. Moreover, our findings showed that LIN28 binds to mRNAs of proteins important for oxidative phosphorylation and modulates protein abundance. Together, our data demonstrates that LIN28A and LIN28B play collaborative roles in controlling reprogramming, naive/primed pluripotency, and stem cell metabolism.

title: Genetic Drift Can Compromise Mitochondrial Replacement by Nuclear Transfer in Human Oocytes.
text: Recent advancements in technology have made it possible to transfer mitochondria between oocytes from two different women in order to prevent the inheritance of mtDNA diseases. Although initial experiments have shown promise, the potential consequences of small amounts of mtDNA carryover remain unknown. Through the use of human mitochondrial replacement stem cell lines, our research reveals that, although low levels of heteroplasmy may disappear, they can also lead to mtDNA genotypic drift and a return to the original genotype. Interestingly, we found that either mtDNA genotype can coexist with the nucleus and that drift is unrelated to mitochondrial function. Therefore, while functional replacement of the mitochondrial genome is achievable, even minimal levels of heteroplasmy can compromise the stability of the mtDNA genotype and reduce the effectiveness of mitochondrial replacement.

title: TAL effectors are remote controls for gene activation.
text: TAL (transcription activator-like) effectors are a recently discovered class of DNA-binding proteins that exhibit predictable specificity in their binding to target DNA sequences. These proteins are produced by Gram-negative plant-pathogenic bacteria of the genus Xanthomonas, which utilize a type III secretion system (T3SS) to translocate multiple effector proteins into plant cells. Once inside the plant cell nucleus, TALs recognize and bind to specific DNA sequences, leading to the activation of plant genes involved in the bacterial infection process. The specificity of TAL binding is determined by a central domain composed of tandem repeats, with each repeat recognizing a specific base pair in the DNA. By rearranging these repeat modules, researchers can design TALs with desired DNA-binding specificities, a development that has important implications for the field of plant pathogenesis. In this summary, we provide an overview of the encoding of TAL specificity, including the first structural data and site-specific TAL nucleases.

title: Vascular heterogeneity and specialization in development and disease
text: Blood and lymphatic vessels infiltrate almost every tissue in the body, playing vital roles in physiology and disease. The inner lining of these networks is composed of a single layer of endothelial cells, which are specifically adapted to meet the needs of the tissue they serve. While researchers are making significant progress in understanding the general mechanisms of blood and lymphatic vessel development, the study of endothelial cell specialization remains largely descriptive. Recent advances in genetic animal models have provided valuable insights into how endothelial cells communicate with one another and interact with their surrounding tissue environment, offering a framework for understanding vessel-specific and organ-specific endothelial differentiation. Elucidating these underlying principles is essential for understanding how tissues develop, maintain their function, and become dysfunctional in disease.

title: Association of Intracerebral Hemorrhage Among Patients Taking Non–Vitamin K Antagonist vs Vitamin K Antagonist Oral Anticoagulants With In-Hospital Mortality
text:
Non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs) are increasingly used to prevent thromboembolic events, but there is limited data on the association between NOACs and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). This study aimed to assess the relationship between prior oral anticoagulant use and in-hospital mortality among patients with ICH.
The study was a retrospective cohort of 141,311 patients with ICH admitted to 1,662Get With The Guidelines-Stroke hospitals between October 2013 and December 2016. The exposure was defined as any use of oral anticoagulants (OACs) within seven days prior to hospital admission. The main outcome measure was in-hospital mortality.
The study found that among 141,311 patients with ICH, 10.6% were taking warfarin and 3.5% were taking NOACs preceding ICH, and 28.0% and 4.1% were taking concomitant single and dual antiplatelet agents, respectively. Patients who took prior oral anticoagulants were older and had a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation and prior stroke compared to those without prior oral anticoagulant use. The median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was similar across the three groups. The unadjusted in-hospital mortality rates were 32.6% for warfarin, 26.5% for NOACs, and 22.5% for no OACs. Compared to patients without prior oral anticoagulant use, patients taking prior warfarin or NOACs had higher in-hospital mortality rates (adjusted risk difference [ARD], 9.0% or 7.9% to 10.1%, and adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.62 or 1.53 to 1.71, respectively). In contrast, patients taking NOACs had a lower risk of in-hospital mortality compared to those taking warfarin (ARD, 3.3%, or 1.7% to 4.8%, and AOR, 0.75, or 0.69 to 0.81). The difference in mortality between NOAC-treated patients and warfarin-treated patients was numerically greater among patients taking dual antiplatelet agents (32.7% vs 47.1%; ARD, −15.0%, or −6.8% to −3.8%, and AOR, 0.50, or 0.29 to 0.86). However, the interaction P value was not statistically significant (0.07).
In conclusion, this study found that prior use of NOACs or warfarin was associated with higher in-hospital mortality compared to no oral anticoagulants among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage. Prior use of NOACs compared to warfarin was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital mortality.

title: Elevated red blood cell distribution width contributes to poor prognosis in patients undergoing resection for nonmetastatic rectal cancer
text: Various studies have shown that elevated red blood cell distribution width (RDW) is associated with a poor prognosis in various types of cancer. The present study aimed to investigate the prognostic role of RDW in patients with nonmetastatic rectal cancer undergoing curative resection. A retrospective analysis of 625 consecutive patients treated at our institution from 2009 to 2014 revealed that patients with high RDW-cv had significantly lower overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) compared to those with lower RDW-cv. Moreover, elevated RDW-sd was associated with lower OS, but not significantly different DFS. In multivariate analysis, elevated RDW-cv and RDW-sd were identified as independent prognostic factors for poor DFS and OS, respectively. These findings suggest that elevated RDW can be a useful marker for predicting poor prognosis in patients with nonmetastatic rectal cancer, which may warrant more intensive intervention or surveillance in the future.

title: Health workers cohort study: methods and study design.
text: Objective: To investigate the association between specific lifestyle and genetic factors and various health outcomes. Methods: We conducted a study from March 2004 to April 2006, enrolling a sample of employees and their family members from three health and academic institutions after obtaining informed consent. At baseline and follow-up (2010-2013), participants completed a self-administered questionnaire, underwent a physical examination, and provided blood samples. Results: A total of 10,729 participants aged 6 to 94 years were recruited at baseline, of which 70% were female and 50% were from the Mexican Social Security Institute. Approximately 42% of the adults in the sample were overweight, while 20% were obese. Conclusion: Our study provides valuable insights into disease mechanisms and prevention by analyzing risk factor information in a large sample of Mexicans.

title: Aberrant pro-atrial natriuretic peptide/corin/natriuretic peptide receptor signaling is present in maternal vascular endothelium in preeclampsia.
text:
Objective:
To investigate the dysregulation of pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (pro-ANP)/corin/natriuretic peptide receptor (NPR) signaling in the maternal vascular system of preeclampsia.
Study Design:
This study analyzed the concentrations of pro-ANP and corin in maternal venous blood from 197 pregnant women (84 normotensive, 16 with chronic hypertension, 11 mild, and 86 severe preeclampsia) and examined the expression of ANP and its receptors (NPR-A, NPR-B, and NPR-C) in subcutaneous fat tissue from 12 pregnant women undergoing cesarean section (6 normotensive and 6 preeclamptic).
Results:
1. Corin concentrations were significantly higher in mild and severe preeclampsia compared to normotensive and CHT groups (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, respectively).
2. Pro-ANP concentrations were significantly higher in CHT and severe preeclampsia compared to normotensive and mild preeclampsia groups (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, respectively).
3. ANP and NPR-B expression were undetectable in maternal vessels from normotensive and preeclamptic pregnancies, while NPR-A expression was reduced and NPR-C expression was increased in maternal vessel endothelium in preeclampsia.

Conclusions:

1. Atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) is a vasodilator, and NPR-C is a clearance receptor for ANP.
2. The upregulation of NPR-C expression suggests that circulating ANP clearance or degradation is increased in preeclampsia.
3. The findings suggest that pro-ANP/corin/NPR signaling is dominant in the vascular system in preeclampsia.

title: Optimising Strategies for Plasmodium falciparum Malaria Elimination in Cambodia: Primaquine, Mass Drug Administration and Artemisinin Resistance
text:
A recent field study in a low-transmission area of South West Cambodia found significant reductions in malaria prevalence through a combination of mass drug administration (MDA) and high treatment coverage of symptomatic patients with artemisinin-piperaquine plus primaquine. However, it was unclear which approaches contributed most to the reductions. To address this question, the study employed a mathematical model fitted to the trial data, which was used to:
* Assess the effects of different components of the interventions
* Optimize elimination strategies
* Explore the interactions between interventions and artemisinin resistance, which has recently been discovered in Western Cambodia.

The modeling results indicated that the initial reduction of P. falciparum malaria was primarily due to MDA with artemisinin-piperaquine, while the subsequent continued decline and near elimination resulted mainly from high coverage with artemisinin-piperaquine treatment combined with primaquine. Both of these strategies were more effective with the addition of primaquine. In contrast, MDA with artemisinin combination therapy (ACT) increased the proportion of artemisinin-resistant infections, although less than treating symptomatic cases with ACT, and this increase was slowed by adding primaquine. Artemisinin resistance reduced the effectiveness of interventions using ACT when the prevalence of resistance was high. The main results were robust to assumptions about primaquine action, and immunity.


The key findings of these modelling results for policymakers were:

* High coverage with ACT treatment can produce a long-term reduction in malaria, while the impact of MDA is generally only short-term.
* Primaquine enhances the effect of ACT in eliminating malaria and reduces the increase in proportion of artemisinin-resistant infections.
* Parasite prevalence is a better surveillance measure for elimination programmes than numbers of symptomatic cases.
* Combinations of interventions are most effective, and sustained efforts are crucial for successful elimination.

In conclusion, the study found that a combination of MDA and high treatment coverage with ACT plus primaquine was effective in reducing malaria in an area of low transmission in Cambodia. However, the intervention's effectiveness was impacted by artemisinin resistance, and the study highlighted the importance of monitoring parasite prevalence to evaluate the success of elimination programs. The study concluded that sustained efforts and a combination of interventions are crucial for successful malaria elimination.

title: Role of the Parasite-Derived Prostaglandin D2 in the Inhibition of Epidermal Langerhans Cell Migration during Schistosomiasis Infection
text: Epidermal Langerhans cells (LCs) play a crucial role in the immune system, and their dysfunction can lead to various immunological disorders. In this study, we investigated the impact of percutaneous infection with the parasite Schistosoma mansoni on LCs in C57BL/6 mice. We found that infection leads to the activation of LCs, but unexpectedly, they remain in the epidermis rather than migrating to the draining lymph nodes. Using an experimental model of LC migration induced by tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, we discovered that parasites produce soluble lipophilic factors that inhibit the departure of LCs from the epidermis and their accumulation in the draining lymph nodes. Specifically, we found that the lipid prostaglandin (PG)D2, but not other eicosanoids produced by the parasites, impedes the TNF-α–triggered migration of LCs through the adenylate cyclase–coupled PGD2 receptor (DP receptor). Moreover, we showed that the potent DP receptor antagonist BW A868C restores LC migration in infected mice. In a separate model of contact allergen-induced LC migration, we found that activation of the DP receptor not only inhibits LC emigration but also dramatically reduces the contact hypersensitivity responses after challenge. Taken together, our findings suggest that the inhibition of LC migration may represent a strategic mechanism used by schistosomes to evade the host immune system, and that PGD2 may play a crucial role in regulating cutaneous immune responses.

title: Axicabtagene Ciloleucel CAR T‐Cell Therapy in Refractory Large B‐Cell Lymphoma
text:
In a phase 1 trial, axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel), an autologous anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, demonstrated efficacy in patients with refractory large B-cell lymphoma who had failed traditional therapy.



In this multicenter, phase 2 trial, we enrolled 111 patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma, or transformed follicular lymphoma who had refractory disease despite prior therapy. Patients received a target dose of 2 x 106 anti-CD19 CAR T cells per kilogram of body weight following a conditioning regimen of low-dose cyclophosphamide and fludarabine. The primary endpoint was the rate of objective response (quantified as the combination of complete response and partial response), and secondary endpoints included overall survival, safety, and biomarker assessments.

title: Beta adrenergic blockade decreases the immunomodulatory effects of social disruption stress
text:
The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) plays a key role in regulating the immune system during physiological or psychological stress. Previous studies have shown that the activation of β-adrenergic receptors (βARs) by catecholamines produced by the SNS leads to an increase in pro-inflammatory cytokine production in various cell types. However, the impact of SNS activation on immune modulation during social defeat stress (SDR) has not been examined.
The present study aimed to investigate the effects of SNS activation during SDR on anxiety-like behavior and immune function. CD-1 mice were subjected to one, three, or six cycles of SDR, and their plasma and spleen were analyzed for catecholamine levels. The results showed an increase in catecholamines in the plasma and spleen after SDR. Pretreatment with the β-adrenergic antagonist propranolol reversed the SDR-induced increase in anxiety-like behavior in the open field test. Propranolol also abrogated splenomegaly, increased plasma levels of IL-6, TNF-α, and MCP-1, and reduced the SDR-induced increase in the percentage of CD11b(+) splenic macrophages and the expression of TLR2, TLR4, and CD86 on these cells. Additionally, supernatants from ex vivo cultures of splenocytes from propranolol-treated SDR mice contained lower levels of IL-6 compared to splenocytes from SDR vehicle-treated mice. Furthermore, propranolol pre-treatment restored the glucocorticoid insensitivity of CD11b(+) cells ex vivo.
These findings suggest that SNS activation during SDR leads to immune activation and priming, which in turn contribute to the development of anxiety-like behavior and immune dysregulation. The study highlights the importance of the SNS in regulating the immune system during social stress and identifies new targets for the treatment of stress-related disorders.

title: Stereotactic radiosurgery plus whole-brain radiation therapy vs stereotactic radiosurgery alone for treatment of brain metastases: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
In patients with brain metastases, there is limited understanding of whether adding upfront whole-brain radiation therapy (WBRT) to stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) results in improved survival or neurological function outcomes compared to SRS alone. This study aimed to determine if WBRT plus SRS leads to improved survival, brain tumor control, functional preservation, or reduced risk of neurological death in patients with 1-4 brain metastases.
This randomized controlled trial enrolled 132 patients from 11 hospitals in Japan between 1999 and 2003. The patients were randomly assigned to receive either WBRT plus SRS (65 patients) or SRS alone (67 patients). The primary outcome measure was overall survival, and secondary outcomes included brain tumor recurrence, salvage brain treatment, functional preservation, radiation-related toxic effects, and cause of death.
The median survival time and 1-year actuarial survival rate were similar between the two groups (7.5 months and 38.5% in the WBRT + SRS group vs. 8.0 months and 28.4% in the SRS alone group). However, the 12-month brain tumor recurrence rate was significantly lower in the WBRT + SRS group (46.8% vs. 76.4%). Additionally, fewer patients in the WBRT + SRS group required salvage brain treatment (10 vs. 29). The proportion of patients who died due to neurological causes was similar between the two groups (22.8% in the WBRT + SRS group vs. 19.3% in the SRS alone group). There were no significant differences in systemic or neurological functional preservation or radiation-related toxic effects between the two groups.
The findings of this study suggest that adding WBRT to SRS does not improve survival for patients with 1-4 brain metastases, but it does reduce the risk of intracranial recurrence. Therefore, salvage treatment is frequently required when upfront WBRT is not used. This trial was registered at umin.ac.jp/ctr under the identifier C000000412.

title: RANK signals from CD4+3− inducer cells regulate development of Aire-expressing epithelial cells in the thymic medulla
text: Medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs) play a crucial role in preventing autoimmunity by expressing tissue-restricted antigens to purge the developing T cell receptor repertoire of self-reactive specificities. We have uncovered a novel function for a CD4+3− inducer cell population, which was previously linked to the development of organized secondary lymphoid structures and maintenance of T cell memory, in the regulation of Aire-mediated promiscuous gene expression in the thymus. CD4+3− cells are closely associated with mTECs in the adult thymus, and their appearance in the fetal thymus is temporally linked with the emergence of Aire+ mTECs. Our findings demonstrate that RANKL signals from these cells promote the maturation of RANK-expressing CD80−Aire− mTEC progenitors into CD80+Aire+ mTECs, and that the absence of RANKL leads to autoimmunity. Together, our results reveal the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the generation of Aire+ mTECs and highlight an unexpected role for CD4+3−RANKL+ inducer cells in maintaining intrathymic self-tolerance.

title: Proteomic approach to characterize biochemistry of meat quality defects.
text:
Proteomics can be utilized to identify and characterize quality defects in meat products, including pale, soft, and exudative (PSE) meat (pork and poultry), woody broiler breast meat, reddish catfish fillets, and tough meat. Protein analysis can help identify the underlying causes of these defects by detecting differences in protein abundance and expression between normal and affected meat samples.
Studies have shown that proteomics can reveal differences in protein abundance between PSE broiler meat and normal broiler breast meat, with 15 proteins found to be differentially expressed in PSE meat. Similarly, eight proteins were found to be differently expressed in woody breast meat compared to normal breast meat. However, while inducing low oxygen and/or heat stress conditions to catfish fillets can result in the production of red fillets, hemoglobin was the only protein found to be differentially expressed between red and normal catfish fillets.
Proteomic data can provide valuable insights into the protein differences that contribute to meat quality defects. However, to fully understand the causes of these defects, it is important to analyze this data in conjunction with information on genetics, nutrition, the live animal environment, muscle to meat conversion, and sensory attributes. By evaluating these various factors, researchers can identify protein biomarkers that can be used to predict and prevent quality defects in meat products.

title: Phosphorylation of Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) by AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) links energy sensing to anti-inflammatory signaling
text: Adenosine 5'-monophosphate–activated protein kinase (AMPK) serves as a crucial regulator of cellular metabolism at both cellular and organismal levels. In addition to its metabolic function, AMPK also exhibits anti-inflammatory properties. Our findings reveal that pharmacological activation of AMPK can inhibit the Janus kinase (JAK)-signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) pathway in various cell types. In vitro kinase assays showed that AMPK directly phosphorylates two sites (Ser515 and Ser518) within the Src homology 2 domain of JAK1. Activation of AMPK enhances the interaction between JAK1 and 14-3-3 proteins in cultured vascular endothelial cells and fibroblasts, an effect that requires the presence of Ser515 and Ser518 and is abolished in AMPK-deficient cells. Mutation of these sites abolishes AMPK-mediated inhibition of JAK-STAT signaling stimulated by either the soluble interleukin-6 receptor alpha/interleukin-6 complex or the expression of a constitutively active V658F-mutant JAK1 in human fibrosarcoma cells. Clinically used AMPK activators, such as metformin and salicylate, augment the inhibitory phosphorylation of endogenous JAK1 and inhibit STAT3 phosphorylation in primary vascular endothelial cells. These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for exploring the role of AMPK activators in various diseases characterized by enhanced activation of the JAK-STAT pathway.

title: IAP antagonists induce anti-tumor immunity in multiple myeloma
text:
Researchers have discovered two proteins called cellular inhibitors of apoptosis (cIAP) 1 and 2 in about 3% of cancers. These proteins stop cancer cells from dying when they should, which makes them harder to treat. As a result, scientists are testing small-molecule drugs called IAP antagonists, like LCL161, to see if they can cause cancer cells to die. However, the researchers found that cIAP1 and cIAP2 are often deleted in a type of cancer called multiple myeloma (MM). This means that the noncanonical nuclear factor (NF)-κB pathway is always turned on in MM, even when it shouldn't be.
In a surprising discovery, the researchers found that LCL161 was effective in treating MM in mice and people with the disease. LCL161 didn't directly kill cancer cells, but it increased the production of a protein called type I interferon (IFN). This caused the immune system to become stronger and better able to fight cancer. The researchers also found that LCL161 worked even better when combined with another drug called anti-PD1, which helps the immune system recognize and attack cancer cells. In tests with mice, this combination caused complete remission of the cancer in every mouse treated.

title: Psychobiological Protective Factors Modifying the Association Between Age and Sexual Health in Men: Findings From the Men’s Health 40+ Study
text: As men age, their sexual health significantly declines. Among males over the age of 40, erectile dysfunction (ED) is the most common sexual disorder. Despite the identification of physical and psychological risk factors for ED, protective factors have yet to be explored. To date, no study has examined the joint impact of endocrine and psychosocial factors on the age-related increase in ED. A sample of 271 healthy men between the ages of 40 and 75 provided self-reported data on sexual function and a range of potential psychosocial protective factors, along with saliva samples for hormone and cytokine analysis. Around 35% of the participants reported at least mild ED. The study found direct associations between ED and factors such as perceived general health, emotional support, relationship quality, and intimacy motivation, but not with hormone or cytokine levels. Moderation analysis revealed that testosterone (T), dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), perceived general health, emotional support, intimacy motivation, and interleukin-6 (IL-6) moderated the association between age and ED. Group differences between older men with and without ED were observed for T, DHEA, and psychometric measures such as perceived general health, emotional support, satisfaction with life, and intimacy motivation. Both endocrine and psychosocial parameters moderated the association between age and sexual health, with perceived general health, emotional support, intimacy motivation, and relationship quality emerging as psychosocial protective factors against ED. Additionally, higher T and DHEA and lower IL-6 levels served as protective factors against an age-related increase in ED.

title: Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells in cancer research and precision oncology
text:
In recent years, advancements in tissue processing and culture, bioengineering, xenotransplantation, and genome editing have significantly expanded the potential of Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) for cancer research. This technology offers several advantages and limitations, and its integration with other patient-derived models of cancer, such as organoids, organs-on-chips, and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs), provides a more comprehensive understanding of human cancer. We will discuss the benefits and limitations of iPSC modeling and how it compares to other cancer modeling systems, as well as the challenges that need to be addressed for wider adoption of this technology.
In the field of cancer research, iPSCs have the potential to provide a more accurate representation of human cancer than traditional in vitro and in vivo models. Unlike conventional models, iPSCs are derived from patient-derived cells, allowing for the development of personalized cancer models that can be used to study disease progression, drug resistance, and cancer heterogeneity. This approach offers several advantages, including:
1. Personalized models: iPSCs can be generated from patient-derived cells, including cancer cells, providing a personalized representation of the patient's cancer.
2. Increased complexity: iPSCs can differentiate into multiple cell types, allowing for a more complex and comprehensive understanding of cancer biology.
3. Reduced animal usage: The use of iPSCs can reduce the need for animal models in cancer research, which can help to reduce the number of animals used in experiments.
4. Cost-effective: iPSCs can be re-expanded and re-used multiple times, making them a cost-effective alternative to traditional models.

However, there are also some limitations to consider:

1. Limited representation: iPSCs may not completely recapitulate the in vivo tumor microenvironment, which can limit their representation of cancer heterogeneity.
2. Difficulties in modeling certain aspects of cancer: Some aspects of cancer, such as the complex interplay between cancer cells and the immune system, may be difficult to model using iPSCs.
3. Insufficiently characterized signaling pathways: Some signaling pathways involved in cancer progression are not yet well-characterized, which can limit the accuracy of iPSC-based cancer models.
4. Ethical considerations: The use of patient-derived cells for iPSC generation raises ethical concerns related to patient privacy and informed consent.
To address these challenges, further research is needed to improve the functional representation of cancer in iPSC models and to better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying cancer progression. In addition, the development of standardized protocols and adequate quality control measures is essential for the widespread adoption of iPSC-based cancer research.
In summary, iPSCs present a promising tool for cancer research, offering a personalized and complex representation of human cancer. While there are still challenges to be addressed, the potential benefits of iPSC models make them an exciting area of research for understanding and treating cancer.

title: Structural basis for sequence-specific recognition of DNA by TAL effectors.
text: TAL (transcription activator-like) effectors, produced by phytopathogenic bacteria, recognize host DNA sequences through a central domain consisting of repeating units of 33-35 amino acids. Each unit targets a specific base pair by making use of two highly variable residues (known as repeat variable diresidues, RVDs) at positions 12 and 13. In this study, we present the crystal structures of an 11.5-repeat TAL effector in both DNA-free and DNA-bound states. Each TAL repeat consists of two helices connected by a short RVD-containing loop. The 11.5 repeats form a right-handed, superhelical structure that follows the sense strand of DNA duplex, with RVDs making contact with the major groove. The 12th residue stabilizes the RVD loop, while the 13th residue makes a base-specific contact. A better understanding of how TAL effectors recognize DNA may lead to the development of DNA-binding proteins with biotechnological applications.

title: Caveolin-1 deletion exacerbates cardiac interstitial fibrosis by promoting M2 macrophage activation in mice after myocardial infarction.
text:
The remodeling of the heart following a myocardial infarction (MI) is driven by an imbalance in the resolution of inflammation, leading to heart failure. Macrophage cells play a crucial role in post-MI inflammation, with different subtypes secreting mediators that either exacerbate inflammation and damage (M1 phenotype) or suppress inflammation and promote scar formation (M2 phenotype). Previous studies have shown that the absence of caveolin-1 (Cav1), a membrane scaffolding protein, is associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in mice, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of Cav1 in the activation of macrophages and its impact on cardiac remodeling using wild type C57BL6/J (WT) and Cav1(tm1Mls/J) (Cav1(-/-)) mice.
Echocardiography revealed that cardiac function was comparable between WT and Cav1(-/-) mice at 3 days post-MI. However, unexpectedly, a higher percentage of M2 macrophages (arginase-1 positive) were detected in the infarcted zone in the absence of Cav1. Conversely, restoring Cav1 function in WT mice after MI by adding back the Cav1 scaffolding domain reduced the M2 activation profile. Adoptive transfer of Cav1 null macrophages into WT mice on day 3 post-MI exacerbated adverse cardiac remodeling at day 14 post-MI. In vitro studies revealed that Cav1 null macrophages had a more pronounced M2 profile activation in response to IL-4 stimulation.
In conclusion, the study finds that Cav1 deletion promotes an array of maladaptive repair processes after MI, including increased TGF-β signaling, increased M2 macrophage infiltration, and dysregulation of the M1/M2 balance. The data also suggest that improving cardiac remodeling by regulating Cav1 function during the inflammatory response phase may be a therapeutic strategy.

title: Lipid hydroperoxide measurement by oxidation of Fe2+ in the presence of xylenol orange. Comparison with the TBA assay and an iodometric method
text: The study of the role of hydroperoxides and lipid peroxidation in disease requires the use of simple and sensitive methods for direct hydroperoxide measurement. We have developed a technique for measuring hydroperoxide levels that exploits the rapid hydroperoxide-mediated oxidation of iron (Fe2+) under acidic conditions. Upon oxidation, Fe3+ forms a chromophore with xylenol orange, which absorbs strongly at 560 nm, resulting in an apparent E560 value of 4.3×104 M−1 cm−1. This assay was validated in a study of liposomal lipid peroxidation and showed excellent agreement with results obtained using an iodometric method or by measuring conjugated dienes. In contrast, the assay involving thiobarbituric acid underestimates lipid peroxidation and does not directly measure hydroperoxides.

title: Roles of exosomes in cardioprotection.
text: Exosomes, which originate from endosomal cells, have gained attention as crucial mediators of intercellular communication. Exosomes released by various cardiac cell types, including cardiomyocytes, endothelial cells, and fibroblasts, modulate cellular functions. Intriguingly, exosomes released from human cardiac progenitor cells (CPCs) have been found to be cardioprotective, improving cardiac function after myocardial infarction to a similar extent as their parent cells. These exosomes are enriched in cardioprotective microRNAs, such as miR-146a-3p. Moreover, circulating exosomes have been shown to mediate remote ischaemic preconditioning. In addition, they are being investigated as diagnostic markers. The recent discovery that cell-derived extracellular signaling organelles, such as exosomes, can transmit the paracrine effects of stem cells, suggests that cell-free strategies could potentially replace cell transplantation. This review focuses on the emerging roles of exosomes in cardiovascular physiology, with a particular emphasis on the cardioprotective activities of CPC-derived exosomes.

title: The rate of change in declining steroid hormones: a new parameter of healthy aging in men?
text:
Research on healthy aging in men has increasingly focused on the changes that occur in hormone levels with age. While testosterone (T) decline has been extensively investigated, little attention has been paid to the age-related changes in other sex steroids, such as dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), estradiol (E2), and progesterone (P). Despite this, there is still a lack of an integrated hormone parameter that can accurately reflect aging processes in men.
To investigate this further, 271 healthy men between the ages of 40 and 75 provided both psychometric data and saliva samples for hormone analysis. Correlation analysis revealed negative associations between age and all four sex steroids. Principal component analysis of the salivary analytes identified a principal component that unified the variance of the four sex steroid hormones. Subsequent analysis revealed a principal component of declining steroid hormones (DSH) that was significantly moderated by psychosocial factors such as depression, chronic stress, and perceived general health.
These findings provide further evidence that sex steroids decline in aging men and that the integrated hormone parameter DSH and its rate of change can be used as biomarkers for healthy aging in men. Additionally, the negative association of age and DSH is moderated by psychosocial factors, highlighting the importance of these factors in predicting hormone changes in aging men.

title: Development of a novel helper-dependent adenovirus-Epstein-Barr virus hybrid system for the stable transformation of mammalian cells.
text: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) episomes are stably maintained in permissive proliferating cell lines due to the EBV nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA-1) protein's ability to mediate replication and segregation. Previous studies have demonstrated the capacity of EBV episomes to confer long-term transgene expression and correct genetic defects in deficient cells. To achieve quantitative delivery of EBV episomes in vitro and in vivo, we designed a binary helper-dependent adenovirus (HDA)-EBV hybrid system, consisting of one HDA vector for Cre recombinase expression and a second HDA vector containing the EBV episome sequences flanked by loxP sites. Upon coinfection of cells, Cre expressed from the first vector recombines the loxP sites on the second vector, resulting in the formation of circular EBV episomes that express a transgene and contain the EBV-derived family of repeats, an EBNA-1 expression cassette, and 19 kb of human DNA serving as a replication origin in mammalian cells. This HDA-EBV hybrid system was capable of transforming 40% of cultured cells. Transgene expression in proliferating cells was observed for over 20 weeks under conditions that selected for the expression of the transgene, with the EBV episomes being maintained at a rate of 8-10% per cell division in the absence of selection. In vivo delivery of EBV episomes was successfully demonstrated in the liver of transgenic mice expressing Cre from the albumin promoter. This novel gene transfer system has the potential to confer long-term episomal transgene expression, thereby correcting genetic defects with reduced vector-related toxicity and without insertional mutagenesis.

title: Spliceosome assembly pathways for different types of alternative splicing converge during commitment to splice site pairing in the A complex.
text: The spliceosome, a complex responsible for alternative splicing, forms mRNA isoforms through sequential rearrangements of its five core snRNPs. To determine when splice sites become functionally paired, we used kinetic trap experiments with pre-mRNAs that undergo 5' splice site selection or exon inclusion. Our findings show that splice site pairing commitment occurs in the A complex, characterized by the ATP-dependent U2 snRNP association with the branch point. Interestingly, the timing of splice site pairing is independent of the intron or exon recognition modes. Using ATPgammaS, we found that ATP hydrolysis is required for splice site pairing, independent of U2 snRNP binding to the pre-mRNA. These results identify the A complex as the spliceosomal assembly step dedicated to splice site pairing and suggest that ATP hydrolysis locks splice sites into a fixed splicing pattern after stable U2 snRNP association with the branch point.

title: Transcripts of the MHM region on the chicken Z chromosome accumulate as non-coding RNA in the nucleus of female cells adjacent to the DMRT1 locus
text: The male hypermethylated (MHM) region, located near the center of the Short Arm of the Z chromosome in chickens, comprises approximately 210 repetitions of a 2.2-kb BamHI sequence unit. In males, cytosines at the CpG dinucleotides within this region are extensively methylated, whereas in females, only a single Z chromosome is methylated. The methylation status of the MHM region is established shortly after fertilization and persists throughout embryonic development. In contrast, the MHM region is transcribed only in females, with the transcripts accumulating nearby the DMRT1 locus in the nucleus. The silencing of the MHM region in males is likely a result of CpG methylation, as treatment of male embryonic fibroblasts with 5-azacytidine leads to demethylation and active transcription of this region. Interestingly, in ZZW triploid chickens, the MHM regions are hypomethylated and transcribed on both Z chromosomes, whereas in ZZZ triploid chickens, the MHM regions are hypermethylated and transcriptionally inactive on all three Z chromosomes, suggesting a possible role of the W chromosome in regulating the state of the MHM region.

title: Macropinocytosis of protein is an amino acid supply route in Ras-transformed cells
text: Macropinocytosis is a conserved endocytic process by which cells internalize extracellular fluid and its contents through large, heterogeneous vesicles called macropinosomes. Oncogenic Ras proteins have been shown to stimulate macropinocytosis, but the functional contribution of this uptake mechanism to the transformed phenotype remains unclear. Our study reveals that Ras-transformed cells use macropinocytosis to transport extracellular protein into the cell, which undergoes proteolytic degradation and releases amino acids, including glutamine, that can enter central carbon metabolism. As Ras-transformed cells depend on free extracellular glutamine for growth, the macropinocytic uptake of protein suppresses this dependence. Consistent with macropinocytosis being an important route of nutrient uptake in tumors, pharmacological inhibition of this process compromises the growth of Ras-transformed pancreatic tumor xenografts. These findings identify macropinocytosis as a mechanism by which cancer cells support their unique metabolic needs and suggest the potential to exploit this process in the design of anticancer therapies.

title: Linking Splicing to Pol II Transcription Stabilizes Pre-mRNAs and Influences Splicing Patterns
text: RNA processing occurs close to the site of transcription, indicating a regulatory relationship between transcription and pre-mRNA splicing. Using an in vitro transcription/splicing assay, we demonstrate that an association between RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcription and pre-mRNA splicing is necessary for efficient gene expression. Pol II-synthesized RNAs containing functional splice sites are protected from nuclear degradation, likely due to the local concentration of the splicing machinery being sufficient to ensure association over interactions with nucleases. Additionally, the process of transcription influences alternative splicing of newly synthesized pre-mRNAs. Unlike other RNA polymerases, Pol II provides RNA products with protection from nucleases and altered splicing patterns, highlighting its specific link to RNA processing. We propose that the connection between Pol II transcription and pre-mRNA splicing ensures an extended half-life and proper processing of newly synthesized pre-mRNAs.

title: The emerging role of skeletal muscle extracellular matrix remodelling in obesity and exercise.
text: Renovation of skeletal muscle extracellular matrix has been proposed as a novel feature associated with obesity and metabolic disfunction. Exercise training can enhance muscle function in obesity, which may be due to the regulatory effects on muscle extracellular matrix. This review analyzed available literature on skeletal muscle extracellular matrix remodeling during obesity and the impact of exercise. A non-systematic literature review was conducted on PubMed, examining publications from 1970 to 2015. A total of 37 studies from humans and animals were retained. Findings revealed increased expression of collagen genes and proteins, growth factors, and enzymatic regulators of the skeletal muscle extracellular matrix in obesity. Only two studies investigated the effects of exercise on skeletal muscle extracellular matrix in obesity, both suggesting a regulatory effect of exercise. The mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle extracellular matrix remodeling during obesity and the impact of exercise on muscle extracellular matrix are not yet fully understood, and further research is needed to elucidate these complex processes.

title: Effect of specific exercise strategy on need for surgery in patients with subacromial impingement syndrome: randomised controlled study
text:
Objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of a specific exercise strategy targeting the rotator cuff and scapula stabilizers in improving shoulder function and reducing pain in patients with subacromial impingement syndrome compared to unspecific exercises. This exercise strategy aims to reduce the need for arthroscopic subacromial decompression.
Design: Randomized, participant and single assessor blinded, controlled study.
Setting: Department of orthopaedics in a Swedish university hospital.
Participants: 102 patients with long-standing (over six months) persistent subacromial impingement syndrome who had failed earlier conservative treatments, recruited through orthopaedic specialists.
Interventions: The specific exercise strategy included strengthening eccentric exercises for the rotator cuff and concentric/eccentric exercises for the scapula stabilizers in combination with manual mobilization. The control exercise program consisted of unspecific movement exercises for the neck and shoulder. Both groups received five to six individual guided treatment sessions over 12 weeks. In between these supervised sessions, participants performed home exercises once or twice a day for 12 weeks.
Main Outcome Measures:
* The primary outcome was the Constant-Murley shoulder assessment score, evaluating shoulder function and pain.
* Secondary outcomes included patients' global impression of change due to treatment and decision regarding surgery.

Results: Most (97%, 95%) participants completed the 12-week study. There was a significantly greater improvement in the Constant-Murley score in the specific exercise group compared to the control exercise group (24 points (95% CI 19 to 28.0) versus 9 points (5 to 13); mean difference between groups: 15 points (8.5 to 20.6)). More patients in the specific exercise group reported successful outcome (defined as large improvement or recovered) in the patients' global assessment of change due to treatment: 69% (35/51) versus 24% (11/46); odds ratio 7.6, 3.1 to 18.9; P<0.001. A significantly lower proportion of patients in the specific exercise group subsequently chose arthroscopic subacromial decomposition: 20% (10/51) versus 63% (29/46); odds ratio 7.7, 3.1 to 19.4; P<0.001.
Conclusion: A specific exercise strategy focusing on strengthening eccentric exercises for the rotator cuff and concentric/eccentric exercises for the scapula stabilizers is effective in reducing pain and improving shoulder function in patients with persistent subacromial impingement syndrome. By extension, this exercise strategy reduces the need for arthroscopic subacromial decompression within the three-month timeframe used in the study.
Trial Registration: Clinical Trials NCT01037673.

title: Nucleotide sequence of an avian sarcoma virus oncogene (src) and proposed amino acid sequence for gene product
text: satpped the gene (src) of avian sarcoma virus (ASV) and nearby regions of the viral genome using molecular cloning of viral DNA. The nucleotide sequence encompasses the entire src gene and a portion of the gene env that encodes gp37, one of two glycoproteins found in the viral envelope. Src encodes a single, hydrophobic protein with structural features that match previous descriptions of the gene product (pp60src). It appears that a single viral protein is responsible for both initiating and maintaining neoplastic transformation by ASV. In contrast to other viral oncogenes and their encoded proteins, src and its product have no obvious structural similarity. Src is flanked by a repeated nucleotide sequence that may facilitate frequent deletion of the gene from the viral genome.

title: Issues in design and interpretation of MDR-TB clinical trials: report of the first Global MDR-TB Clinical Trials Landscape Meeting
text: In recognition of the existing MDR-TB treatment regimen's inadequacies and the lack of high-quality evidence supporting it, a Global MDR-TB Clinical Trials Landscape Meeting was convened in December 2014 to strategize the coordination of research and development of novel treatment approaches for this global health burden.
