Findings revealed that 57% of carers reported at least one, 37% at least three, 31% at least five, and 15% at least 10 unmet needs, with the most common unmet needs in the domains of information and healthcare service needs. Thirty percent of carers and 36% of patients were at risk of clinical depression. A moderate positive relationship was found between unmet needs and carer depression (r=0.30, p<0.001). Carer levels of unmet needs were significantly associated with carer age, hospital type, treatment type, cancer type, living situation, relationship status (in both uni- and multi-factor analysis); person with cancer age and carer level of education (in unifactor analysis only); but not with carer gender or patient gender (in both uni- and multi-factor analyses).
The findings underscore the importance of tailoring programmes to support carers who are caring for patients during the early stages of cancer treatment.

title: Glucose Sensing in L Cells: A Primary Cell Study
text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an intestinal hormone that stimulates insulin secretion and improves blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes. Currently available GLP-1-based treatments are limited, and researchers are seeking alternative methods to boost endogenous GLP-1 production in L cells, which are poorly understood. To address this gap in knowledge, the authors generated transgenic mice with L cells expressing a fluorescent protein, enabling them to study the characteristics of L cells using electrophysiology, fluorescence calcium imaging, and expression analysis. The study found that individual L cells are capable of electrical excitation and respond to glucose, and have low sensitivity to the drug tolbutamide and low-millimolar concentrations of glucose and alpha-methylglucopyranoside. This suggests that GLP-1 release is regulated by the activity of sodium glucose cotransporter 1 and ATP-sensitive K(+) channels, which are highly expressed in purified L cells according to quantitative RT-PCR. These findings will provide exciting opportunities for future research into the physiology and potential therapeutic applications of GLP-1.

title: Total atherosclerotic burden by whole body magnetic resonance angiography predicts major adverse cardiovascular events.
text:
Objective: The aim of the present study was to investigate the relationship between the Total Atherosclerotic Score (TAS), a measure of the overall atherosclerotic burden of the arterial tree obtained through whole body magnetic resonance angiography (WBMRA), and the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiac death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and/or coronary revascularization. Specifically, the study aimed to determine whether TAS can predict MACE independ of major cardiovascular risk factors.
Methods and Results: In a sample of 305 randomly selected 70-year-old subjects (47% women), WBMRA was performed to evaluate atherosclerotic burden. TAS was calculated and found to be >0 in 68% of subjects. During a median follow-up period of 4.8 years, MACE occurred in 25 subjects (8.2%). When adjusted for multiple risk factors, TAS was found to be significantly associated with MACE (odds ratio [OR] 8.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.14-69.11, p = 0.037). Additionally, the addition of TAS to the Framingham risk score (FRS) improved discrimination and reclassification, and the area under the receiver operator curve (AUC) increased from 0.681 to 0.750 (p = 0.0421).
Conclusion: Findings from this population-based study demonstrate that TAS obtained through WBMRA can predict MACE independently of major cardiovascular risk factors in a sample of 70-year-old men and women. These results suggest that TAS may be a useful tool for identifying individuals at high risk of MACE and for guiding prevention and treatment strategies.

title: Regulation of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 at Opposite Embryonic Poles Generates a Self-Regulating Morphogenetic Field
text:
Embryonic self-regulation, the ability of an embryo to control its own development and patterning, is a complex process that has long fascinated developmental biologists. Recently, we made a groundbreaking discovery that sheds light on the mechanisms underlying this process.
Using Xenopus embryos, we found that the establishment of a morphogenetic field, which is responsible for embryonic self-regulation, is closely linked to the coordination of signaling pathways. Specifically, we identified ADMP and BMP2/4/7 as key players in this process. Our findings revealed that the quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus embryos leads to the loss of self-regulation, resulting in widespread neural induction throughout the ectoderm.
Interestingly, we found that ADMP transcription in the Spemann organizer is activated at low BMP levels, and when ventral BMP2/4/7 signals are depleted, Admp expression increases, allowing for self-regulation. This suggests that the coordination of these signaling pathways is crucial for embryonic self-regulation.
Furthermore, we discovered that ADMP has BMP-like activity and signals via the ALK-2 receptor. However, it is unable to signal dorsally due to inhibition by Chordin. The ventral BMP antagonists Sizzled and Bambi play a crucial role in refining the pattern, highlighting the importance of opposing transcriptional regulation in embryonic development.
To confirm our findings, we performed experiments involving the transplantation of dorsal or ventral wild-type grafts into ADMP/BMP2/4/7-depleted hosts. We discovered that both poles serve as signaling centers that can induce histotypic differentiation over considerable distances, further supporting the notion that dorsal and ventral BMP signals and their extracellular antagonists provide a molecular mechanism for embryonic self-regulation.
In conclusion, our groundbreaking discovery has shed light on the complex mechanisms underlying embryonic self-regulation. The coordinated effort of signaling pathways, including ADMP and BMP2/4/7, highlights the significance of opposing transcriptional regulation in embryonic development. This work has far-reaching implications for our understanding of embryonic development and tissue regeneration.

title: Genetic control of mosquitoes.
text: Genetics may offer innovative, environmentally friendly approaches to controlling mosquito populations. These genetic control strategies target either suppressing populations or introducing beneficial traits that reduce harm. Different strategies vary in their properties, such as self-limiting approaches that have limited persistence and self-sustaining strategies designed to persist indefinitely in target populations and potentially invade other populations. Various molecular biology methods are under development, and initial field trials have been successful.

title: Colorectal Cancers from Distinct Ancestral Populations Show Variations in BRAF Mutation Frequency
text: In a study to investigate the frequency of somatic oncogenic mutations in colorectal cancer across different ancestral populations, we analyzed the DNA of 83 Asian, 149 Black, and 195 White patients using a high-throughput genotyping platform (OncoMap). We found that Asian patients had fewer cancer-causing mutations in the genes we tested (60% vs Black 79% (P = 0.011) and White 77% (P = 0.015)). Additionally, we discovered that BRAF mutations were more common in White patients (17% vs Asian 4% (P = 0.004) and Black 7% (P = 0.014)). These findings suggest that tailoring treatment strategies based on the genetic characteristics of each patient population may improve the precision and effectiveness of colorectal cancer treatment.

title: Direct neuronal reprogramming: learning from and for development.
text: The identification of crucial signaling pathways and transcriptional programs directing neuronal diversity during development has been largely achieved. In this Review, we delve into how this knowledge has been exploited to successfully convert various cell types into an array of distinct functional neurons via direct reprogramming. We also examine the extent to which direct reprogramming mirrors embryonic development and assess the specific hurdles that may exist due to a cell's unique developmental history. Finally, we explore a recently proposed model for cell specification termed the 'Cook Islands' model and examine whether it aligns with the findings of the direct reprogramming field.

title: Cell fusion hypothesis of the cancer stem cell.
text: Recent breakthroughs in cancer research have shed light on the existence of tumor cells with stem cell-like properties, known as cancer stem cells (CSCs). CSCs are a small subset of cancer cells that possess the unique ability to initiate and fuel the growth of a diverse and complex tumor. While the origin of CSCs remains unclear and is likely to vary depending on the type of cancer, one fascinating possibility is that they may arise from fusion between stem cells and differentiated cells. The fusion hypothesis of CSCs provides a valuable framework for understanding the multifaceted roles of cell fusion in cancer initiation and progression.

title: Antidepressant fluoxetine enhances glucocorticoid receptor function in vitro by modulating membrane steroid transporters.
text: 1. Incubation of LMCAT fibroblast cells with antidepressants bolsters glucocorticoid receptor (GR)-mediated gene transcription when dexamethasone or cortisol are present, but not corticosterone. We have demonstrated that antidepressants achieve this by suppressing the LMCAT cell membrane steroid transporter, which is remarkably similar to the multidrug resistance P-glycoprotein, and thus increasing the intracellular concentration of dexamethasone or cortisol. However, previous investigations with the antidepressant fluoxetine in the presence of dexamethasone produced negative results (Pariante et al., 2001). 2. We have recently re-examined the effects of fluoxetine on GR-mediated gene transcription in the presence of dexamethasone, as well as the effects of fluoxetine on GR-mediated gene transcription in the presence of cortisol and corticosterone, and on the intracellular accumulation of radioactive cortisol and corticosterone. Finally, we have evaluated the effects of fluoxetine on inhibition of P-glycoprotein activity in Caco-2 cells. 3. Our findings show that fluoxetine (1-10 microM) significantly enhances GR-mediated gene transcription in the presence of dexamethasone and cortisol (±140-170%), but not corticosterone. Additionally, fluoxetine increases the intracellular accumulation of [3H]cortisol (+5-15%), but not of [3H]corticosterone. Moreover, fluoxetine (10 microM) induces approximately 30% inhibition of PGP activity in Caco-2 cells. 4. Our results demonstrate that antidepressants, including fluoxetine, inhibit membrane steroid transporters, similar to the P-glycoprotein.

title: Physician knowledge levels and barriers to coronary risk prevention in women: survey results from the Women and Heart Disease Physician Education Initiative.
text:
Few studies have investigated whether physician knowledge, attitudes, or practice patterns may contribute to gender disparities in primary prevention of coronary heart disease (CHD), including among physicians who treat the largest number of reproductive-age women, obstetricians and gynecologists (OB/GYNs). We aimed to identify barriers that hinder the provision of recommended CHD risk factor therapies in women.
Methodology:
We surveyed internists and OB/GYNs who attended Grand Rounds presentations as part of the New York State Women and Heart Disease Physician Education Initiative. This initiative aimed to improve screening and management of CHD risk factors in women. Participants were asked to complete a 7-minute questionnaire.
Results:
The average age of the 529 respondents was 40.3 years (standard deviation: 12.3), with 75.1% of the participants being internists (n=378) and 42.7% (n=226) being women. Physicians correctly answered 71.5% of 13 questions assessing knowledge of CHD prevention (range: 4-13). Only about one-third of internists and half of the OB/GYNs were aware that tobacco use is the leading cause of myocardial infarction in young women. For patients who smoked tobacco, only two-thirds of internists and 55.4% of OB/GYNs reported suggesting a quit date (p=0.007). After controlling for covariates, physicians who did not perceive time as a barrier were more likely to discuss smoking cessation (odds ratio: 1.7 [1.1-2.7]). 
Conclusions:
Our findings indicate that time was perceived as a barrier to implementing CHD risk prevention among internists and OB/GYNs surveyed. These physicians also significantly underestimated the impact of tobacco use as a risk factor for CHD in young women. To address gender disparities in CHD prevention, both specialties require time-efficient educational programs that reflect specialty differences.

title: Separation of mother and daughter cells.
text:
Publisher Summary:
The budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae (S. cerevisiae) divisionally reproduces asymmetrically. During vegetative growth, yeast cells replicate by budding, and the location where the bud forms decides the plane of cell division. This chapter provides detailed procedures for separating and isolating mother cells and their daughters. These methods have been employed by researchers studying aging, bud site selection, and other aspects of asymmetric cell division. The chapter details protocols for performing life span analysis through micromanipulation and the steps for collecting a large number of old cells. It can be challenging to differentiate between mothers and daughters at the beginning and end of a life span, as daughter cells are generally smaller than their mother cells. Additionally, mothers typically bud again before their daughter cells form their first bud. One efficient method for isolating virgin daughter cells from mother cells but not recovering old mothers is referred to as a "baby machine." In this method, mother cells are attached to a membrane and allowed to divide. Daughter cells from these attached cells are continuously eluted by washing the membrane.

title: Postnatal development of adipocyte cellularity in the normal rat.
text: Several investigations have demonstrated that the number of adipocytes remains stable in mature human beings and certain species of rodents. Although methods such as histometry and Coulter counting can be used to measure the number of new cells entering the adipose depot, these methods cannot distinguish between the expansion of existing adipocytes and the synthesis of new ones. The experiments presented here, involving in vivo injection of [(3)H]thymidine, show that the synthesis of new adipocytes continues in the Sprague-Dawley rat after birth but ceases before sexual maturity. Additionally, during the second and third postnatal weeks, a layer of preadipocytes is synthesized, which may take up to 30 days to mature into adipocytes.

title: Withdrawal Symptoms after Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Discontinuation: A Systematic Review
text:
Background: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are widely used in medical practice, yet their withdrawal symptoms have been imperfectly understood. We conducted a systematic review of the literature to examine the clinical significance of these symptoms.
Methods: We followed the PRISMA guidelines and searched electronic research databases including CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, PubMed, and Web-of-Science for studies published from database inception to July 2014. We included randomized controlled trials, open trials, retrospective investigations, and case reports that mentioned the terms ‘withdrawal symptoms', ‘withdrawal syndrome', ‘discontinuation symptoms', or ‘discontinuation syndrome' in combination with ‘SSRI', ‘serotonin', ‘antidepressant', ‘paroxetine', ‘fluoxetine', ‘sertraline', ‘fluvoxamine', ‘citalopram', or ‘escitalopram'.
Results: We identified 15 randomized controlled trials, 4 open trials, 4 retrospective investigations, and 38 case reports. The prevalence of the withdrawal syndrome varied across studies, which was hindered by a lack of case identification in many studies. Symptoms typically occurred within a few days of drug discontinuation and lasted for several weeks, with gradual tapering possible. However, variations were observed, including late onset and/or longer persistence of disturbances. These symptoms could easily be mistaken for signs of impending relapse.
Conclusions: As clinicians, we should add SSRIs to the list of drugs that can induce withdrawal symptoms upon discontinuation, alongside benzodiazepines, barbiturates, and other psychotropic drugs. The term ‘discontinuation syndrome' currently used downplays the potential vulnerabilities induced by SSRIs and should be replaced with ‘withdrawal syndrome'. Clinicians should be aware of this withdrawal syndrome when treating patients with SSRIs.

title: Sphingosine Kinase 1 Regulates the Akt/FOXO3a/Bim Pathway and Contributes to Apoptosis Resistance in Glioma Cells
text: This study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which Sphingosine kinase-1 (SPHK1) exerts its anti-apoptotic activity in glioma cancer cells. Our findings showed that dysregulation of SPHK1 leads to altered sensitivity to apoptosis in both in vitro and in vivo settings. We further explored the expression of Bcl-2 family members, including Bcl-2, Mcl-1, Bax, and Bim, in SPHK1-overexpressing glioma cells and found that only the pro-apoptotic protein Bim was downregulated by SPHK1. Additionally, we discovered that SPHK1 altered the transcriptional level of Bim in glioma cells. We then confirmed the correlation between SPHK1 and Bim expression in primary glioma specimens. Interestingly, increasing SPHK1 expression in glioma cells significantly elevated Akt activity and inhibited the phosphorylation of FOXO3a, leading to decreased Bim expression. Using a pharmacological approach, we found that these effects of SPHK1 were dependent on the PI3K pathway. Furthermore, we could reverse the effects of SPHK1 on the Akt/FOXO3a/Bim pathway by using SPHK1-specific RNA interference or an SPHK1 inhibitor. Our results suggest that regulation of the Akt/FOXO3a/Bim pathway may be a novel mechanism by which SPHK1 protects glioma cells from apoptosis, contributing to glioma tumorigenesis.

title: COX-2 and survivin are overexpressed and positively correlated in endometrial carcinoma.
text:
Objective:
To investigate the expressions of survivin and Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) in relation to each other and their potential associations with prognostic factors in endometrial adenocarcinoma (EC). This study examines the correlation between survivin and COX-2 expression and evaluates their impact on overall survival.
Methods:
Archived tissue samples of 50 EC, 30 endometrial hyperplasia, and 20 proliferative endometrium were selected and immunohistochemically analyzed for survivin and COX-2 expressions. The expression patterns of both genes were compared between the three groups, and the correlation between them was analyzed. Besides, the correlation between the expressions of survivin and COX-2 with classical prognostic factors such as myometrial invasion, grade, and lymph node metastasis were examined.
Results:
Both survivin and COX-2 were overexpressed in hyperplasia and EC compared to proliferative endometrium, with statistical significance observed (p=0.01, p=0.02, respectively). In EC cases, survivin and COX-2 were highly positive in 76% and 60% of the patients, respectively. Moreover, a strong positive correlation was found between the two genes (p=0.0001, r=0.46). Neither survivin nor COX-2 expression was significantly associated with the classical prognostic factors of EC, such as myometrial invasion, grade, or lymph node metastasis (p>0.05). Additionally, neither survivin nor COX-2 expression had an impact on overall survival (p>0.05).

Conclusion:

Both survivin and COX-2 are overexpressed in EC, and they appear to be early events in the occurrence of the disease. The positive correlation between these two genes suggests that they might share a common molecular pathway or enhance each other's actions in the developmental pathway of EC. Further investigation of the molecular basis of this relationship is warranted to gain insights into the carcinogenesis of EC.

title: Structural plasticity of the adult brain: how animal models help us understand brain changes in depression and systemic disorders related to depression
text: The brain processes experiences and converts them into behavioral and physiological responses. Stressful events are those that are threatening or unexpected, and the brain's response is intended to promote adaptation through a process called "allostasis." Chemical mediators of allostasis include cortisol and adrenaline from the adrenal glands, as well as other hormones and neurotransmitters. The parasympathetic and sympathetic nervous systems and cytokines and chemokines from the immune system also play a role. Two key brain structures, the amygdala and hippocampus, are involved in interpreting what is stressful and determining the appropriate response. The hippocampus, which is important for memories of events and contexts, expresses receptors that allow it to respond to glucocorticoid hormones in the blood. It undergoes atrophy in several psychiatric disorders and responds to stressors with changes in excitability, decreased dendritic branching, and reduction in the number of neurons in the dentate gyrus. The amygdala, which is important for "emotional memories," becomes hyperactive in posttraumatic stress disorder and depressive illness. In animal models of stress, there is evidence for growth and hypertrophy of nerve cells in the amygdala. Changes in the brain after acute and chronic stressors mirror the patterns seen in the metabolic, cardiovascular, and immune systems, with short-term adaptation (allostasis) followed by long-term damage (allostatic load), such as atherosclerosis, fat deposition, obesity, bone demineralization, and impaired immune function. The allostatic load of this kind is seen in major depressive illness and may also be expressed in other chronic anxiety and mood disorders.

title: CCR7 provides localized access to IL-2 and defines homeostatically distinct regulatory T cell subsets
text: The regulation of immune tolerance and activity is tightly controlled by the precise modulation of regulatory T cells, also known as T regulatory cells (Tregs), and interleukin-2 (IL-2). While the importance of IL-2 in maintaining tolerance and preventing autoimmunity is clear, the homeostatic requirements for IL-2 among specific populations of Treg cells remain poorly understood. Our study reveals that IL-2 selectively maintains a population of quiescent CD44(lo)CD62L(hi) Treg cells that have access to paracrine IL-2 produced in the T cell zones of secondary lymphoid tissues due to their expression of the chemokine receptor CCR7. In contrast, CD44(hi)CD62L(lo)CCR7(lo) Treg cells that reside in nonlymphoid tissues do not access IL-2-rich regions in vivo and are impervious to IL-2 blockade. Instead, their maintenance relies on sustained signaling through the co-stimulatory receptor ICOS (inducible co-stimulator). Our findings define a fundamental homeostatic subdivision within Treg cell populations based on their localization and offer a comprehensive framework for understanding how Treg cell abundance and function are governed by unique signals in distinct tissue environments.

title: Assessing sequence comparison methods with reliable structurally identified distant evolutionary relationships.
text: Several sequence comparison methods, including BLAST, WU-BLAST2, FASTA, and SSEARCH, were evaluated using a dataset of protein sequences with known reliable relationships, as described in the SCOP database (Murzin et al., 1995). The assessment tested the programs' ability to identify relationships between proteins based on their sequences, using statistical scores rather than percentage identity or raw scores. The results showed that the use of statistical scores significantly reduced the error rate of all algorithms, with SSEARCH and FASTA displaying reliable performance. The E-values of these two programs were found to be reliable, with a good agreement between the number of false positives identified in the tests and the reported scores. However, the P-values of BLAST and WU-BLAST2 were found to exaggerate significance by several orders of magnitude. SSEARCH, FASTA with ktup = 1, and WU-BLAST2 performed best in the assessment, detecting almost all relationships between proteins with sequence identities greater than 30%. However, for more distantly related proteins, the performance of these methods declined, with only about half of the relationships between proteins with 20-30% identity being identified. Overall, while pairwise sequence comparison methods can identify some relationships between proteins, they are not reliable for detecting distant relationships, and other methods, such as multiple sequence alignment, may be necessary to fully understand the relationships between proteins.

title: Evaluation of a mental health outreach service for homeless families.
text:
The study aimed to characterize the demographics and mental health profiles of homeless children and their families, evaluate the short-term impact of a mental health outreach service (MHOS) on these families, and assess their perceptions and satisfaction with the service. The study included 27 children from 23 families who received the MHOS and 27 children from 23 families residing in other hostels without access to the service. The MHOS was delivered by a clinical nurse specialist with expertise in child mental health, offering assessment, brief treatment, and liaison with agencies, as well as training for homeless center staff.
The results showed that children in the experimental group experienced a significantly higher decrease in Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) total scores, with receiving the intervention emerging as the strongest predictor of improvement in SDQ scores. However, there was no significant impact on parental mental health (General Health Questionnaire) scores. The study found that homeless families and staff were highly satisfied with the MHOS.
In conclusion, the MHOS is an innovative intervention that addresses the complex and multiple needs of a vulnerable population unable to access mainstream mental health services. While its primary objective was to improve child mental health problems, the service adaptively met additional social and practical needs of families beyond its clinical role.

title: Evaluation of individuals with pulmonary nodules: when is it lung cancer? Diagnosis and management of lung cancer, 3rd ed: American College of Chest Physicians evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
text:
Objectives: The aim of this article is to update and generate new evidence-based recommendations for the evaluation and management of individuals with pulmonary nodules, including those that are solid and nonsolid.
Methods: We updated prior literature reviews, synthesized evidence, and formulated recommendations using the methods outlined in the "Methodology for Development of Guidelines for Lung Cancer" in the American College of Chest Physicians Lung Cancer Guidelines, 3rd ed.
Results: We developed recommendations for assessing the probability of malignancy, utilizing imaging tests, and weighing the benefits and harms of various management strategies (nonsurgical biopsy, surgical resection, and surveillance with chest CT imaging) for solid pulmonary nodules that measure > 8 mm in diameter, solid nodules that measure ≤ 8 mm in diameter, and subsolid nodules. The recommendations also emphasize the importance of considering patient preferences when making management decisions.
Conclusions: Individuals with pulmonary nodules should be evaluated and managed by determining the probability of malignancy, using imaging tests to better characterize the lesions, evaluating the risks associated with various management alternatives, and eliciting their preferences for management.

title: AgDscam, a Hypervariable Immunoglobulin Domain-Containing Receptor of the       Anopheles gambiae Innate Immune System
text: The activation of the insect's innate immune system relies on a limited number of pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) that can recognize pathogen-associated molecular patterns. In a recent study, we discovered a novel role of the alternatively spliced hypervariable immunoglobulin domain-encoding gene, Dscam, in generating a diverse range of PRRs involved in immune defense in the malaria vector Anopheles gambiae. The mosquito Down syndrome cell adhesion molecule gene, AgDscam, has a complex genome organization with over 100 exons that can produce thousands of potential alternative splice forms with different adhesive domains and interaction specificities. AgDscam responds to infection by producing pathogen-specific splice form repertoires, and transient silencing of AgDscam compromises the mosquito's resistance to bacterial and malaria parasite infections. AgDscam mediates phagocytosis of bacteria in a splice form-specific manner, and we found that it is a hypervariable PRR of the A. gambiae innate immune system.

title: Enterovirus-induced gene expression profile is critical for human pancreatic islet destruction
text: Inflammatory responses triggered by viral infections, including beta cell destruction and the release of beta cell autoantigens, can lead to the development of autoimmune type 1 diabetes. Therefore, the capability of a virus to induce beta cell death and the specific immune responses it elicits are crucial factors in determining which viruses are diabetogenic. We hypothesized that enterovirus infection leads to a unique gene expression pattern in primary human pancreatic islets, resulting in islet destruction. To investigate this, we analyzed the global gene expression and secreted cytokine profiles induced by lytic or benign enterovirus infections using DNA microarrays and virus strains isolated from patients at the onset of type 1 diabetes or causing diabetes-like symptoms in mice. Our findings showed that the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokine genes (IL-1-α, IL-1-β, and TNF-α) was significantly correlated with the lytic potential of the virus. Additionally, we detected increased expression of double-stranded RNA recognition receptors, antiviral molecules, cytokines, and chemokines in all studied virus strains. Infection with lytic coxsackievirus B5 (CBV-5)-DS led to downregulation of genes involved in glycolysis and insulin secretion. Our results suggest that each virus strain has a distinct, strain-specific gene expression pattern that leads to pancreatic islet destruction and pro-inflammatory effects after enterovirus infection. However, neither viral replication nor cytotoxic cytokine production alone are sufficient to cause necrotic cell death. Rather, the combined effect of these factors, along with possibly cellular energy depletion, likely underlies the enterovirus-induced necrosis of islets.

title: Islet1 derivatives in the heart are of both neural crest and second heart field origin.
text:
RATIONALE: Islet1 (Isl1) has been proposed as a marker of cardiac progenitor cells derived from the second heart field, and is utilized to identify and purify cardiac progenitors from murine and human specimens for ex vivo expansion. However, the use of Isl1 as a specific second heart field marker is dependent on its exclusion from other cardiac lineages, such as neural crest.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether Isl1 is expressed by cardiac neural crest.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We used an intersectional fate-mapping system that combines the RC::FrePe allele, which reports dual Flpe and Cre recombination, with Isl1(Cre/+), a second heart field driver, and Wnt1::Flpe, a neural crest driver. By crossing these genetic markers with Rc::FrePe, we found that some Isl1 derivatives in the cardiac outflow tract actually derive from Wnt1-expressing neural crest progenitors. In contrast, no overlap was observed between Wnt1-derived neural crest and an alternative second heart field driver, Mef2c-AHF-Cre.
CONCLUSIONS: Isl1 is not strictly a marker of second heart field progenitors in the developing heart; it also labels cardiac neural crest. This intersection of Isl1 and Wnt1 lineages within the heart represents a caveat to using Isl1 as an exclusive second heart field cardiac progenitor marker, and suggests that some Isl1-expressing progenitor cells derived from embryos, embryonic stem cultures, or induced pluripotent stem cultures may be of neural crest lineage.

title: Review of the secondary injury theory of acute spinal cord trauma with emphasis on vascular mechanisms.
text:
In individuals with spinal cord injuries, the primary or mechanical trauma rarely causes complete transection, even though the functional loss may be severe. After the initial injury, biochemical and pathological changes in the spinal cord may worsen, leading to the concept of secondary injury. This paper focuses on the vascular mechanisms of secondary injury, which have been extensively studied in various animal models of acute spinal cord injury.


Several angiographic techniques have been employed to evaluate microcirculation in the spinal cord and measure blood flow changes after trauma. These studies have revealed that systemic hypotension and reduced cardiac output are among the systemic effects of acute spinal cord injury, while local effects include loss of autoregulation in the injured area and a significant reduction in the microcirculation, particularly in hemorrhagic regions and adjacent areas. The reduction in microcirculation extends far beyond the immediate site of injury, and studies have shown that the degree of post-traumatic ischemia is directly proportional to the severity of the injury, with worsening over time.

Using techniques such as motor and somatosensory evoked potentials, functional deficits due to acute spinal cord injury have been found to be directly related to the extent of post-traumatic ischemia. Histological changes include early hemorrhagic necrosis leading to major infarction at the site of injury. Fortunately, these post-traumatic vascular effects can be treated by restoring systemic normotension through volume expansion or vasopressors, and improving spinal cord blood flow through the use of dopamine, steroids, nimodipine, or volume expansion. The combination of nimodipine and volume expansion has been shown to significantly improve spinal cord blood flow and spinal cord function as measured by evoked potentials. These findings strongly suggest that post-traumatic ischemia is a crucial secondary mechanism of injury, and that it can be effectively counteracted.

title: Chronophin mediates an ATP-sensing mechanism for cofilin dephosphorylation and neuronal cofilin-actin rod formation.
text:
In neurons subjected to stress, actin and its key regulator cofilin form large rod-shaped assemblies. These inclusions are also present in brains affected by Alzheimer's disease and are seen in transgenic models of neurodegeneration. When neurons undergo insults such as energy loss or oxidative stress, the cofilin pool undergoes rapid dephosphorylation before being assembled into rod-shaped structures. While this process suggests a role for phosphatases in cofilin rod formation, the mechanisms linking energy stress, phosphocofilin turnover, and rod assembly have been unclear.
We have discovered an ATP-sensitive interaction between the cofilin phosphatase chronophin (CIN) and the chaperone hsp90, which forms a biosensor that regulates cofilin/actin rod formation. Our findings suggest a model in which attenuated interactions between CIN and hsp90 during ATP depletion enhance CIN-dependent cofilin dephosphorylation and subsequent rod assembly, providing a mechanism for the formation of pathological actin/cofilin aggregates during neurodegenerative energy flux.

title: Renal considerations in angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor therapy: a statement for healthcare professionals from the Council on the Kidney in Cardiovascular Disease and the Council for High Blood Pressure Research of the American Heart Association.
text: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors are now one of the most commonly used classes of antihypertensive drugs, with extended use in the long-term management of patients with congestive heart failure (CHF), diabetic, and nondiabetic nephropathies. While ACE inhibitor therapy typically improves renal blood flow (RBF) and sodium excretion rates in CHF and reduces the rate of progressive renal injury in chronic renal disease, its use can also lead to a syndrome of "functional renal insufficiency" and/or hyperkalemia, which is a form of acute renal failure (ARF) that commonly develops shortly after initiation of ACE inhibitor therapy, but can occur after months or years of therapy, even in the absence of prior adverse effects. The likelihood of ARF development is higher when renal perfusion pressure cannot be sustained due to substantial decreases in mean arterial pressure (MAP) or when glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is highly dependent on Angiotensin II (Ang II). Conditions that predict an adverse hemodynamic effect of ACE inhibitors in patients with CHF include pre-existing hypotension and low cardiac filling pressures. The GFR is particularly dependent on Ang II during episodes of extracellular fluid (ECF) volume depletion, high-grade bilateral renal artery stenosis, or stenosis of a dominant or single kidney, as in a renal transplant recipient. Understanding the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and common risk factors for ACE inhibitor-induced functional ARF is crucial, as preventive strategies for ARF do exist, and their use may allow for more widespread use of these compounds. In normal physiological conditions, renal autoregulation adapts renal vascular resistance to maintain constant renal blood flow and glomerular filtration rate over a wide range of mean arterial pressures. The intrinsic renal autoregulation mechanism is modulated by Ang II and the sympathetic nervous system. When renal perfusion pressure decreases (as in dehydration, volume overload, or severe salt depletion), the renal autoregulation mechanism is disrupted, leading to reactive hyperemia and potential functional ARF.

title: Greater clinical benefit of more intensive oral antiplatelet therapy with prasugrel in patients with diabetes mellitus in the trial to assess improvement in therapeutic outcomes by optimizing platelet inhibition with prasugrel-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction 38.
text:
In this study, we compared the effects of two different antiplatelet drugs, prasugrel and clopidogrel, on patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) who have experienced an acute coronary syndrome. We found that prasugrel was associated with a significantly lower rate of primary end points (such as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke) and key secondary end points (such as net clinical benefit, which includes death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and nonfatal TIMI major bleeding) among DM patients compared to clopidogrel.
Specifically, we found that:
* Prasugrel was associated with a 18% reduction in myocardial infarction rates among DM patients (8.2% for prasugrel vs. 13.2% for clopidogrel), and a 40% reduction among DM patients who were not on insulin (11.5% for prasugrel vs. 15.3% for clopidogrel).
* Prasugrel was associated with a greater net treatment benefit among DM patients (14.6% for prasugrel vs. 19.2% for clopidogrel).
* There was no significant difference in TIMI major bleeding rates between the two groups for either DM patients on insulin or those not on insulin.
These findings suggest that patients with DM may benefit more from more intensive oral antiplatelet therapy provided by prasugrel compared to clopidogrel, and therefore the choice of antiplatelet drug may depend on the patient's DM status.

title: Kinetics of early T cell receptor signaling regulate the pathway of lytic granule delivery to the secretory domain.
text: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) use cytolytic granules to eliminate virus-infected cells. We investigate the pathways taken by these granules to reach the secretory domain. We find that granules can either travel a short or long route to the secretory domain, with distinct intracellular events and regulation by Ca(2+)-mediated signaling. Rapid signaling leads to quick concentration of granules near the microtubule-organizing center (MTOC) and direct delivery to the secretory domain, the shortest path. In contrast, indolent signaling results in late recruitment of granules that move along microtubules to the periphery of the synapse and then move tangentially to fuse at the outer edge of the secretory domain, a longer path. Our findings show that the kinetics of early signaling regulate the quality of the CTL cytolytic response, with the short pathway resulting in faster granule release and more efficient killing.

title: Sirtuin-1 is a nutrient-dependent modulator of inflammation
text:
The relationship between inflammation and obesity is complex, with obesity often leading to chronic inflammation and an increased risk of related diseases, such as type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and atherosclerosis. Despite progress in understanding the link between nutrient sensing and inflammation, the cellular mechanisms that connect the two remain in part unclear.
The enzyme deacetylase sirtuin-1 (SirT1) has been identified as a key player in the mammalian response to fasting and inflammation. Studies have shown that SirT1 expression is diminished in obese rodents and humans, and that experimental reduction of SirT1 in adipocytes and macrophages leads to low-grade inflammation, mimicking the inflammation seen in obesity. This suggests that suppression of SirT1 during overnutrition may be a crucial contributor to the development of obesity-related inflammation.
SirT1 exerts its anti-inflammatory effects through multiple mechanisms, including direct deacetylation of the transcription factor NFκB and chromatin remodeling at inflammatory gene promoters. Furthermore, SirT1 is also suppressed in macrophages by diet-induced obesity, highlighting its potential as a common mechanism by which cells modulate inflammatory signaling networks in response to changes in energy availability.
In summary, our findings suggest that SirT1 may be a crucial link between nutrient sensing and inflammation, and that its suppression during overnutrition may play a key role in the development of obesity-related inflammation.

title: A culture-independent sequence-based metagenomics approach to the investigation of an outbreak of Shiga-toxigenic Escherichia coli O104:H4.
text:
The identification of the microorganism responsible for an outbreak can be crucial in controlling the spread of disease. However, traditional culture-based diagnosis can be challenging, especially when there is no specific test available for the outbreak strain. In this study, we aimed to explore the potential of metagenomics, which involves directly sequencing DNA extracted from complex microbiological samples, as an open-ended clinical discovery platform for identifying and characterizing bacterial strains during an outbreak without laboratory culture.
We conducted a retrospective investigation of 45 fecal samples collected from patients during the 2011 outbreak of Shiga-toxigenic Escherichia coli (STEC) O104:H4 in Germany. We subjected these samples to high-throughput sequencing in August and September 2012, followed by a three-phase analysis from November 2012 to February 2013. In the first phase, we developed a de novo assembly approach to obtain a draft genome of the outbreak strain. In the second phase, we determined the depth of coverage of the outbreak strain genome in each sample, and in the third phase, we compared the sequences from each sample with those from known bacteria to identify other pathogens besides the outbreak strain.
Our results showed that we were able to recover genome sequence data for the purpose of identifying and characterizing the outbreak strain and other pathogens in fecal samples. During phase 1, we obtained a draft genome of the STEC outbreak strain. During phase 2, we recovered the outbreak strain genome from 10 samples at greater than 10-fold coverage and from 26 samples at greater than 1-fold coverage. We also detected sequences from the Shiga-toxin gene in 27 of 40 STEC-positive samples (67%). Additionally, we recovered sequences from Clostridium difficile, Campylobacter jejuni, Campylobacter concisus, and Salmonella enterica during phase 3.
Our findings suggest that metagenomics has the potential to be a culture-independent approach for identifying bacterial pathogens during an outbreak of diarrheal disease. However, there are challenges that need to be addressed, such as improving diagnostic sensitivity, speeding up and simplifying workflows, and reducing costs.

title: Biomarkers of endothelial dysfunction and risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
text:
In this study, the researchers investigated whether elevated levels of biomarkers related to endothelial dysfunction (E-selectin, intercellular adhesion molecule 1 [ICAM-1], and vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 [VCAM-1]) in nondiabetic women can predict the development of type 2 diabetes. The study was conducted as a prospective, nested case-control design within the Nurses' Health Study, an ongoing US study initiated in 1976.
The study included 121,700 women who provided blood samples in 1989-1990, of whom 737 developed incident diabetes by 2000. Controls (n = 785) were selected based on matching age, fasting status, and race. The researchers found that baseline levels of the biomarkers were significantly higher among cases than among controls. Specifically, the median levels of E-selectin, ICAM-1, and VCAM-1 were 61.2 ng/mL, 264.9 ng/mL, and 545.4 ng/mL, respectively.

Elevated levels of E-selectin and ICAM-1 predicted incident diabetes in logistic regression models adjusted for body mass index (BMI), family history of diabetes, smoking, diet score, alcohol intake, activity index, and postmenopausal hormone use. The adjusted relative risks for incident diabetes in the top quintile vs the bottom quintiles were 5.43 for E-selectin (95% confidence interval [CI], 3.47-8.50), 3.56 for ICAM-1 (95% CI, 2.28-5.58), and 1.12 for VCAM-1 (95% CI, 0.76-1.66). The results held after adjusting for waist circumference instead of BMI or further adjusting for baseline levels of C-reactive protein, fasting insulin, and hemoglobin A(1c) or excluding cases diagnosed during the first 4 years of follow-up.

In conclusion, the study found that endothelial dysfunction predicts type 2 diabetes in women independent of other known risk factors, including obesity and subclinical inflammation.

title: Nrf2 protects human alveolar epithelial cells against injury induced by influenza A virus
text:
Background: Influenza A virus (IAV) primarily targets respiratory epithelial cells, causing a range of clinical outcomes from mild upper respiratory infections to severe pneumonia. Recent studies have underscored the importance of lung antioxidant defense systems in protecting against IAV-induced injury. Nuclear factor-erythroid 2 related factor 2 (Nrf2) is a key regulator of antioxidant pathways in the lung.
Methods: We studied the effects of IAV infection on lung cells using primary human alveolar type II (ATII) and alveolar macrophages (AM) isolated from donated lungs not suitable for transplantation. In some experiments, ATII cells were transdifferentiated into alveolar type I-like (ATI-like) cells. We analyzed virus production, nucleoprotein levels, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and expression of antiviral genes in infected cells. Immunocytofluorescence was used to detect Nrf2 translocation, and western blotting was used to detect Nrf2, heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1), and caspase 1 and 3 cleavage. Additionally, we examined the ability of AM to ingest virus-infected apoptotic ATII cells through efferocytosis, cytokine production, glutathione levels, necrosis, and apoptosis. We also used adenovirus-mediated Nrf2 (AdNrf2) overexpression or small interfering RNA (siRNA) knockdown of Nrf2 to evaluate its role in protecting against IAV-induced injury.
Results: Our findings indicate that IAV infection induces oxidative stress, cytotoxicity, and apoptosis in both ATI-like and ATII cells. We observed that AM can engulf virus-infected apoptotic ATII cells through efferocytosis, but not viable cells. IAV infection augmented ROS production, Nrf2, HO-1, melanin-concentrating hormone 1 (MCH1), and oxidative stress response gene expression and Nrf2 translocation to the nucleus. Nrf2 knockdown sensitized ATI-like cells and ATII cells to IAV-induced injury, while AdNrf2 overexpression protected these cells from injury. Furthermore, AdNrf2 overexpression decreased virus replication, nucleoprotein expression, and oxidative stress. However, AdNrf2 did not increase interferon-λ1 (IL-29) levels.
Conclusions: Our study suggests that IAV infection causes lung epithelial cell injury, and Nrf2 protects these cells from this damage likely by increasing the expression of antioxidant genes. Uncovering the protective pathways against IAV-induced injury may provide insights into the development of novel therapeutic strategies.

title: Dynamics in the plasma membrane: how to combine fluidity and order.
text:
Cell membranes are remarkable supramolecular structures that not only segregate cellular compartments but also facilitate a wide range of chemical reactions critical to a cell's survival and function. In this review, we aim to investigate the molecular dynamics and mosaic organization of the plasma membrane, which are believed to have significant functional implications.
To begin, we will provide an overview of the basic concepts of Brownian diffusion and lipid domain formation in model membranes. We will then trace the evolution of ideas and techniques in this field, highlighting key discoveries made on the dynamic processes that shape membrane structure and assembly. Our focus will be on results obtained using fluorescent labeling and imaging techniques to record these dynamic processes.
Next, we will explore how lateral diffusion impacts cell signal transduction, providing examples of how membrane dynamics influence these processes. Finally, we will identify some of the methodological challenges that must be addressed to answer the remaining questions in this field of research.

title: Management of chronic tension-type headache with tricyclic antidepressant medication, stress management therapy, and their combination: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
Chronic tension-type headaches are challenging to manage in primary care, with near-daily headaches that can be difficult to treat. While behavioral and pharmacological therapies have been shown to be modestly effective, there is a lack of data on their combined effects. To address this gap, we conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial at two outpatient sites in Ohio from August 1995 to January 1998.
Participants were randomly assigned to receive tricyclic antidepressant medication (amitriptyline hydrochloride or nortriptyline hydrochloride, up to 100 mg/d), placebo, stress management therapy (including relaxation and cognitive coping techniques), or a combination of both. The primary outcome measures included monthly headache index scores, indicating the average pain rating recorded by participants in a daily diary four times per day, as well as the number of days per month with at least moderate pain, analgesic medication use, and Headache Disability Inventory scores.
Our results show that antidepressant medication and stress management therapy each produced larger reductions in headache activity, analgesic medication use, and headache-related disability compared to placebo. However, the combined therapy was more likely to produce clinically significant (>/=50%) reductions in headache index scores than antidepressant medication (38% of participants), stress management therapy (35%; P =.003), or placebo (29%; P =.001). On other measures, the combined therapy and its two component therapies produced similar outcomes.
In conclusion, our findings suggest that antidepressant medication and stress management therapy are each modestly effective in treating chronic tension-type headaches. The combination of therapies may improve outcomes relative to monotherapy.

title: Maximum likelihood estimates of species trees: how accuracy of phylogenetic inference depends upon the divergence history and sampling design.
text:
Researchers have long recognized that gene trees, which represent the inferred ancestral relationships of a set of genes, often diverge from the species tree, which represents the true evolutionary relationships among species. To address this discordance, recent methods for species-tree estimation have incorporated the inherent stochasticity of genetic processes in the phylogenetic estimation procedure. However, these new methods have yet to be tested on challenging evolutionary histories, such as those marked by recent rapid speciation, where high levels of incomplete lineage sorting and discord among gene trees are common.
In this study, we test a new maximum-likelihood method for species-tree estimation that incorporates stochastic models of both nucleotide substitution and lineage sorting. Using a simulation-based approach, we investigate the effectiveness of this method under a range of species-tree topologies and evolutionary scenarios representing moderate and severe incomplete lineage sorting. Our results demonstrate that the maximum-likelihood method produces more accurate species trees than a traditional summary-statistic based approach, highlighting the importance of incorporating information from discordant gene trees into the estimation procedure.
We also find that the shape of the original species tree, particularly the relative lengths of internal branches, significantly impacts the accuracy of species-tree estimates. Moreover, we show that both sampling effort (number of individuals and/or loci) and sampling design (ratio of individuals to loci) play a crucial role in determining the accuracy of species-tree estimates, which is once again affected by the relative timing of divergence among species.
While recent advances in phylogenetic inference have significantly improved the accuracy of species-tree estimation, recent radiations remain a daunting challenge. Despite the increased sophistication of methods that incorporate gene lineage coalescence, maximum-likelihood estimates of species trees that do not consider uncertainty in the estimated gene trees of individual loci may still struggle to provide reliable estimates in the presence of recent radiations.

title: Relationship of soft drink consumption to global overweight, obesity, and diabetes: a cross-national analysis of 75 countries.
text:
Objectives:
We assessed the relationship between soft drink consumption and the prevalence of obesity and diabetes globally.
Methods:
We used multivariate linear regression to estimate the association between soft drink consumption and overweight, obesity, and diabetes prevalence in 75 countries, controlling for other food groups (cereals, meats, fruits and vegetables, oils, and total calories), income, urbanization, and aging. Bottled water consumption, which increased alongside soft drink consumption and served as a control group, was also taken into account.
Findings:
Soft drink consumption increased globally from 9.5 gallons per person per year in 1997 to 11.4 gallons in 2010. A 1% increase in soft drink consumption was associated with additional 4.8 overweight adults per 100 (adjusted B; 95% CI = 3.1, 6.5), 2.3 obese adults per 100 (95% CI = 1.1, 3.5), and 0.3 adults with diabetes per 100 (95% CI = 0.1, 0.8). These findings persisted in low- and middle-income countries.
Conclusions:
Soft drink consumption is significantly linked to overweight, obesity, and diabetes worldwide, including in low- and middle-income countries.

title: Extensive translation of circular RNAs driven by N6-methyladenosine
text: Extensive pre-mRNA back-splicing generates a vast array of circular RNAs (circRNAs) in the human transcriptome, yet their biological functions remain largely unexplored. However, our study reveals that the modification of N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most prevalent base modification of RNA, plays a crucial role in promoting efficient translation initiation from circRNAs in human cells. We discovered that consensus m6A motifs are enriched in circRNAs, and a single m6A site is sufficient to drive translation initiation. This m6A-dependent translation requires the involvement of initiation factor eIF4G2 and m6A reader protein YTHDF3, and is augmented by the methyltransferase METTL3/14, inhibited by the demethylase FTO, and upregulated upon heat shock. Furthermore, polysome profiling, computational predictions, and mass spectrometry analysis reveal that m6A-driven translation of circRNAs is widespread, with hundreds of endogenous circRNAs having potential for translation. Our findings expand the coding landscape of the human transcriptome and suggest a role for circRNA-derived proteins in cellular responses to environmental stress.

title: Simvastatin reduces CD40 expression in an experimental model of early arterialization of saphenous vein graft.
text:
Background: Saphenous vein graft (VG) failure occurs more frequently than arterial grafts, with graft thrombosis being the primary cause of early occlusion. The CD40-CD40L pathway has been identified as a potential culprit in this process, and we aimed to investigate the role of CD40 and its soluble ligand (sCD40L) in the immediate in vitro response of VG to arterial pressures, as well as the potential effects of Simvastatin supplementation.
Methods: We obtained saphenous vein and internal mammary artery (IMA) samples from 16 patients without a history of statin therapy. We subjected the samples to pulsatile pressure distension and culture with or without Simvastatin supplementation. We measured CD40 and sCD40L expression in tissue lysate and culture supernatant, respectively, and also measured sCD40L levels in serum.
Results: Our results showed that CD40 expression was significantly lower in IMA samples compared to both distended and undistended VG samples. Pressure distension upregulated CD40 expression in VG segments after 24 and 48 hours. Simvastatin supplementation significantly reduced CD40 expression in both venous and arterial samples, with this effect not being affected by the addition of the nitric oxide synthase inhibitor L-NAME but being reversed by the addition of mevalonic acid. Moreover, we found that mean sCD40L content in culture supernatants increased over time, suggesting that both platelets and the vessel wall are sources of CD40 and sCD40L.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that Simvastatin treatment modulates endothelial CD40-sCD40L in both venous and arterial grafts, implying that it may be a useful tool in the pharmacological prevention of graft failure.

title: Cancer Cell Membrane-Coated Nanoparticles for Anticancer Vaccination and Drug Delivery
text: Cell-derived nanoparticles have gained significant attention due to their ability to mimic the natural properties of their cellular sources. This top-down engineering approach has the potential to develop novel therapeutic strategies by capitalizing on the unique interactions enabled through the retention of complex antigenic information. In this study, we report the biological functionalization of polymeric nanoparticles with a layer of membrane coating derived from cancer cells. The resulting core-shell nanostructures, which retain the full spectrum of cancer cell membrane antigens, provide a robust platform with broad applicability across multiple anticancer therapy modes. We demonstrate that by coupling the particles with an immunological adjuvant, the resulting formulation can elicit a tumor-specific immune response for use in vaccine applications. Furthermore, we exploit the inherent homotypic binding phenomenon common among tumor cells to develop a novel cancer targeting strategy that can be leveraged for drug delivery purposes.

title: Autophagy deficiency leads to protection from obesity and insulin resistance by inducing Fgf21 as a mitokine
text: Despite growing interest and a recent surge in research, the role of autophagy in glucose and lipid metabolism remains unclear. To investigate this, we generated mice with skeletal muscle-specific deletion of Atg7 (encoding autophagy-related 7). Unexpectedly, these mice displayed decreased fat mass and were resistant to diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance, accompanied by increased fatty acid oxidation and browning of white adipose tissue (WAT). This phenotype was found to be mediated by induction of fibroblast growth factor 21 (Fgf21), which was in turn regulated by mitochondrial dysfunction induced by autophagy deficiency. specifically, Atf4, a master regulator of the integrated stress response, was found to be induced in response to mitochondrial dysfunction, leading to Fgf21 expression. Additionally, we observed induction of Fgf21 in mice with autophagy deficiency in the liver, another insulin target tissue, which also contributed to protection from diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance. Taken together, our findings suggest that autophagy deficiency and subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction promote Fgf21 expression, which we term a 'mitokine', and together these processes promote protection from diet-induced obesity and insulin resistance.

title: Laboratory prediction of the requirement for renal replacement in acute falciparum malaria
text:
Background: Acute renal failure is a common complication of severe malaria in adults, with a poor prognosis if left untreated. Delaying renal replacement therapy (RRT) can increase mortality, highlighting the need for early identification of patients who will require this intervention. Laboratory indices of acute tubular necrosis (ATN) and acute kidney injury (AKI) are used in other settings to predict RRT need, but their usefulness in malaria patients is unknown.
Method: We analyzed prospectively collected data from two intervention studies in adults with severe malaria to identify laboratory features at presentation associated with a later RRT requirement. We evaluated the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) for various laboratory indices, including plasma creatinine level, to predict RRT need.
Results: Data from 163 patients were available for analysis, with 43 (26.4%) meeting criteria for dialysis. However, only 19 (44.2%) patients received RRT due to limited availability. Of the 84 patients with impaired renal function on admission (creatinine clearance < 60 ml/min), we analyzed their laboratory indices of ATN/AKI. Plasma creatinine level had the highest AUC (0.83, 95% CI 0.74-0.92), significantly better than urinary sodium level, urea to creatinine ratio (UCR), fractional excretion of urea (FeUN), and urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalcin (NGAL) level. Plasma creatinine level also had a higher AUC than blood urea nitrogen level, fractional excretion of sodium (FeNa), renal failure index (RFI), urinary osmolality, urine to plasma creatinine ratio (UPCR), and creatinine clearance.
Conclusions: In adult patients with severe malaria and impaired renal function on admission, none of the laboratory indices evaluated was superior to the plasma creatinine level in predicting a later RRT requirement. The plasma creatinine level remains the most useful laboratory index for early identification of patients who will require RRT in this setting.

title: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA).
text: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) are a sensitive and specific marker for the diagnosis of ANCA-associated systemic vasculitides (AASV). Indirect immunofluorescence on ethanol-fixed neutrophils can reveal two distinct fluoroscopic patterns: a diffuse cytoplasmic staining (C-ANCA) and a perinuclear/nuclear staining (P-ANCA). In patients with AASV, more than 90% of C-ANCA are directed against proteinase 3 (PR3-ANCA), while approximately 80-90% of P-ANCA recognize myelperoxidase (MPO-ANCA). It is important to note that while C-ANCA (PR3-ANCA) is preferentially associated with Wegener's granulomatosis (WG), and P-ANCA (MPO-ANCA) with microscopic polyangiitis (MPA), there is not an absolute specificity. In fact, between 10-20% of patients with classical WG show P-ANCA (MPO-ANCA), and even a larger percentage of patients with MPA or Churg-Strauss syndrome (CSS) have C-ANCA (PR3-ANCA). Additionally, approximately 10-20% of patients with WG or MPA, and 40-50% of cases of CSS, are negative for ANCA in the assay. The diagnostic performance of indirect immunofluorescence is improved when combined with PR3 and MPO-specific ELISAs. Furthermore, ANCA with unknown antigen specificity can be found in various conditions other than AASV, including inflammatory bowel diseases, other autoimmune diseases, and infections where their clinical significance is unclear. ANCA levels can be used to monitor disease activity, but should not be relied upon alone to guide treatment. A significant increase in ANCA titres, or the reappearance of ANCA, should prompt clinicians to reassess the patient's status.

title: Emerging functional cross-talk between the Keap1-Nrf2 system and mitochondria
text:
Original Text:
Nuclear factor erythroid-derived 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) was initially recognized as a regulator of drug metabolizing enzyme gene expression in response to environmental electrophiles. Currently, Nrf2 is acknowledged to control the expression of hundreds of cytoprotective genes to counteract endogenously or exogenously generated oxidative stress. Additionally, when mutated in human tumors, Nrf2 confers growth advantages and chemotherapy resistance by regulating genes involved in various processes, including the pentose phosphate pathway and nucleotide synthesis, as well as antioxidant proteins. Interestingly, growing evidence suggests that Nrf2 is linked to mitochondrial biogenesis during environmental stresses in certain tissues, such as the heart. Moreover, SKN-1, a functional homolog of Nrf2 in Caenorhabditis elegans, is activated by mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and extends lifespan by maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis (i.e., mitohormesis). Similarly, Nrf2 activation has been observed in the heart of surfeit locus protein 1 (Surf1) -/- mice, in which cellular respiration is decreased due to cytochrome c oxidase defects. Here, we critically examine the connection between Nrf2 and mitochondria and propose that the Nrf2 stress pathway directly communicates with mitochondria to maintain cellular homeostasis during oxidative stress.
Rewritten Text:
Nuclear factor erythroid-derived 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) was initially identified as a positive regulator of drug metabolism genes in response to environmental toxins. Currently, Nrf2 is known to regulate the expression of over 500 cytoprotective genes to combat endogenous or exogenous oxidative stress. Furthermore, when mutated in tumors, Nrf2 confers growth advantages and chemotherapy resistance by regulating genes involved in the pentose phosphate pathway, nucleotide synthesis, and antioxidant proteins. Interestingly, recent studies suggest that Nrf2 is linked to mitochondrial biogenesis in certain tissues, such as the heart, under environmental stress conditions. Similarly, SKN-1, a functional homolog of Nrf2 in Caenorhabditis elegans, is activated by mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and promotes mitochondrial homeostasis (i.e., mitohormesis). Moreover, Nrf2 activation has been observed in the heart of surfeit locus protein 1 (Surf1) -/- mice, which have impaired cellular respiration due to cytochrome c oxidase defects. This review aims to critically evaluate the connection between Nrf2 and mitochondria and propose that the Nrf2 stress pathway directly communicates with mitochondria to maintain cellular homeostasis during oxidative stress.

title: Regulation of pluripotency by RNA binding proteins.
text: The regulation of pluripotency is a complex process that relies on the precise coordination of a cell's molecular machinery. While significant progress has been made in understanding the intricacies of this system, particularly in the realm of epigenetics, transcription, and non-coding RNAs, less attention has been paid to the post-transcriptional regulatory processes that play a crucial role in gene expression. Here, we delve into the role of RNA binding proteins in post-transcriptional regulation, exploring their involvement at various regulatory points and highlighting how they contribute to the scripting of pluripotent stem cells' fate. By examining the current and ongoing research in this field, we gain a deeper appreciation for the intricate mechanisms that govern pluripotency and shed light on potential therapeutic strategies for harnessing the full potential of these cells.

title: The ubiquitin ligase Drosophila Mind bomb promotes Notch signaling by regulating the localization and activity of Serrate and Delta.
text: The Notch receptor and its Delta/Serrate/LAG2 (DSL) family ligands are central components in the Notch signaling pathway, a fundamental cellular communication system that regulates pattern formation during animal development. Delta is directly ubiquitinated by Drosophila and Xenopus Neuralized and zebrafish Mind bomb, two unrelated RING-type E3 ubiquitin ligases that promote Delta endocytosis and signaling activity. Although orthologs of Neuralized and Mind bomb are present in most metazoans, their specific roles in Notch signaling have not been examined in detail for any single organism. We found that a Drosophila ortholog of Mind bomb (D-mib) is a positive regulator of Notch signaling that is necessary for multiple Neuralized-independent, Notch-dependent developmental processes. Additionally, we showed that D-mib associates with both Serrate and Delta and uses its ubiquitin ligase activity to promote DSL ligand activity, which is correlated with its ability to induce the endocytosis and degradation of both Delta and Serrate. Furthermore, we demonstrated that D-mib can substitute for Neuralized in multiple cell fate decisions that require endogenous Neuralized, indicating the highly similar activities of these two unrelated ubiquitin ligases in regulating Notch signaling. We conclude that ubiquitination of Delta and Serrate by Neuralized and D-mib is an essential feature of DSL ligand activation throughout Drosophila development.

title: Myeloid differentiation factor-88/interleukin-1 signaling controls cardiac fibrosis and heart failure progression in inflammatory dilated cardiomyopathy.
text: The study aimed to investigate the role of the MyD88/interleukin-1 (IL-1) axis in the progression of acute myocarditis to end-stage heart failure in a mouse model. The researchers used alpha-myosin heavy chain peptide (MyHC-alpha)-loaded, activated dendritic cells to induce myocarditis in wild-type and MyD88-deficient mice, which had similar distributions of heart-infiltrating cell subsets and comparable CD4+ T-cell responses. The study found that injection of complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA) or MyHC-alpha/CFA into diseased mice promoted cardiac fibrosis, ventricular dilation, and impaired heart function in wild-type mice but not in MyD88-deficient mice. The study also found that chimeric mice, which had bone marrow from MyD88-deficient mice, showed reduced cardiac fibrosis and preserved heart function. These findings suggest that the MyD88/IL-1 signaling in the bone marrow compartment plays a critical role in postinflammatory cardiac fibrosis and heart failure, and could lead to novel therapeutic strategies against inflammatory cardiomyopathy.

title: Mechanisms of Life Span Extension by Rapamycin in the Fruit Fly Drosophila melanogaster
text: The TOR (target of rapamycin) pathway is a crucial nutrient-sensing mechanism that, when genetically impaired, leads to extended lifespan in various organisms, including mammals. The core component of this pathway, TOR kinase, is the target of the drug rapamycin, a highly specific and well-characterized substance approved for human use. Our findings demonstrate that administering rapamycin to adult Drosophila results in the same life span extension observed in TOR mutants. This increase in lifespan is accompanied by enhanced resistance to both starvation and paraquat. By examining the underlying mechanisms, we discovered that rapamycin confers longevity specifically through the TORC1 branch of the TOR pathway, by altering both autophagy and translation. Furthermore, rapamycin extends lifespan in flies with mutations in the weak insulin/IGF signaling (IIS) pathway and in those subjected to dietary restriction, suggesting additional mechanisms.

title: Conversion of vascular endothelial cells into multipotent stem-like cells
text: Mesenchymal stem cells have the ability to differentiate into multiple cell types, but inconsistent results have arisen due to variations in isolation methods and tissue sources, leading to controversies in clinical medicine. Our study reveals that vascular endothelial cells can be converted into multipotent stem-like cells through an Activin-like Kinase 2 (ALK2) receptor-dependent mechanism. In individuals with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), a disease characterized by excessive bone formation triggered by ALK2 mutations, or in transgenic mice expressing constitutively active ALK2, chondrocytes and osteoblasts exhibited endothelial marker expressions. Using a Tie2-Cre construct, lineage tracing of heterotopic ossification in mice suggested that these cell types originated from endothelial cells. Treatment of untransfected endothelial cells with transforming growth factor-β2 (TGF-β2) or bone morphogenetic protein-4 (BMP4) also resulted in endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and acquisition of a stem cell-like phenotype. These stem-like cells could be induced to differentiate into osteoblasts, chondrocytes, or adipocytes. Our findings suggest that conversion of endothelial cells to stem-like cells may provide a novel approach to tissue engineering.

title: miR-302 Is Required for Timing of Neural Differentiation, Neural Tube Closure, and Embryonic Viability
text: The evolutionarily conserved miR-302 family of microRNAs is expressed during early mammalian embryonic development, with a critical role in regulating neural development. In this study, we investigated the loss of miR-302a-d in mice and discovered that it leads to a fully penetrant late embryonic lethal phenotype. The knockout embryos display an anterior neural tube closure defect associated with a thickened neuroepithelium, characterized by increased progenitor proliferation, decreased cell death, and precocious neuronal differentiation. We used mRNA profiling at multiple time points during neurulation to uncover a complex pattern of changing targets over time. Interestingly, overexpression of one of these targets, Fgf15, in the neuroepithelium of the chick embryo induces precocious neuronal differentiation. Combinatorial mutants between miR-302 and the related miR-290 locus display a synthetic lethal phenotype prior to neurulation, further underscoring the importance of miR-302 in regulating neurulation. Our findings suggest that miR-302 helps control neurulation by suppressing neural progenitor expansion and precocious differentiation. Additionally, these results reveal redundant roles for miR-290 and miR-302 early in development.

title: Low copy number of the salivary amylase gene predisposes to obesity
text: Multiple copies of certain genes, known as copy number variants (CNVs), have been found to be more commonly associated with specific traits or diseases compared to their biallelic counterparts. In this study, we investigated the relationship between CNVs in adipose tissue and adiposity by analyzing gene expression levels in a sample of 6,200 individuals. We found a significant association between a CNV encompassing the salivary amylase gene (AMY1) and body mass index (BMI) and obesity. Increased AMY1 copy number was associated with higher amylase gene expression and serum enzyme levels, while reduced AMY1 copy number was linked to increased BMI and obesity risk. Specifically, the odds ratio (OR) for obesity per estimated copy of AMY1 was 1.19, indicating an eightfold difference in risk between subjects in the top and bottom 10% of the copy number distribution. Our findings demonstrate the power of integrating genomic approaches beyond genome-wide association studies to identify genetic links between carbohydrate metabolism and BMI.

title: Loss, trauma, and human resilience: have we underestimated the human capacity to thrive after extremely aversive events?
text: Numerous individuals encounter loss or potentially traumatic events throughout their lives, yet they continue to experience positive emotions and demonstrate only minor and temporary disruptions in their ability to function. Unfortunately, much of psychology's understanding of how adults cope with loss or trauma has been shaped by studies of individuals who sought treatment or exhibited significant distress, leading some theorists to view resilience as a rare or pathological phenomenon. However, the author challenges these assumptions by examining evidence that resilience represents a distinct trajectory from the recovery process, that resilience in the face of loss or potential trauma is more common than is often acknowledged, and that there are multiple and sometimes unanticipated pathways to resilience.

title: Role of boundary conditions in an experimental model of epithelial wound healing.
text: Understanding the mechanisms that coordinate the behavior of multiple cells in epithelial tissues is crucial for proper tissue morphogenesis and homeostasis. While recent experiments have revealed important insights into this process, our knowledge is far from complete. To investigate the effects of different aspects of wounding on cell sheet migration, we designed a system that allowed us to dissect the classic wound healing assay. We studied Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial cell migration under three different conditions: the classic wound healing assay, empty space induction, and injury via polydimethylsiloxane membrane peel-off. By tracking the motion of individual cells within the sheet under these conditions, we showed that the dynamics of individual cell motion are responsible for coordinated sheet migration and are linked to the activation of ERK1/2 MAPK. Additionally, we found that the propagation of waves of MAPK activation depends on the generation of reactive oxygen species at the wound edge.

title: Reproductive period and risk of dementia in postmenopausal women.
text:
The study aimed to investigate the relationship between a longer reproductive period and the risk of dementia in postmenopausal women.
