Through biochemical and electron microscopic studies, we have now demonstrated that previously stimulated and memory T cells have more and larger TCR oligomers at the cell surface compared to their naive counterparts. Reconstitution of cells and mice with a point mutant of the CD3ζ subunit, which impairs TCR oligomer formation, revealed that the increased size of TCR oligomers was directly responsible for the increased sensitivity of antigen-experienced T cells. Therefore, we propose that an "avidity maturation" mechanism underlies T cell antigenic memory.

title: G*Power 3: a flexible statistical power analysis program for the social, behavioral, and biomedical sciences.
text: G*Power (Erdfelder et al., 1996) was developed as a comprehensive standalone program for conducting power analyses for various statistical tests commonly used in social and behavioral research. G*Power 3 represents a significant upgrade and expansion of the previous versions, offering improved functionality and compatibility across different computer platforms (Windows XP, Windows Vista, and Mac OS X 10.4). With this updated version, users can perform power analyses for a wide range of statistical tests, including those from the t, F, and chi-square test families, as well as z tests and some exact tests. Additionally, G*Power 3 features enhanced effect size calculators, graphic options, and input modes (both distribution-based and design-based), catering to the diverse needs of users. Notably, like its predecessors, G*Power 3 is available for free.

title: Dynamic interactions of cortactin and membrane type 1 matrix metalloproteinase at invadopodia: defining the stages of invadopodia formation and function.
text:
Invadopodia, membrane protrusions crucial for metastatic tumor cell migration and invasion, are composed of two distinct aspects: a structural component involved in organizing the cellular actin cytoskeleton, and a functional component responsible for proteolytic enzyme-mediated extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation. Recent studies have shed light on the mechanisms governing invadopodial formation and function.
Using small interfering RNA (siRNA) inhibition and protease inhibitor studies, we have identified cortactin as a critical organizer of invadopodial structure assembly and membrane type 1 matrix metalloproteinase (MT1-MMP) as the pronounced enzyme responsible for gelatin matrix degradation in the breast carcinoma cell line MDA-MB-231. We have found that the inhibition of invadopodial structure assembly by cortactin depletion impedes matrix degradation due to the inability of invadopodia to form properly. Furthermore, either protease inhibition or MT1-MMP siRNA depletion has shown to moderately decrease the formation of invadopodial structures, which were identified as actin-cortactin accumulations at the ventral cell membrane adherent to matrix. Remarkably, invadopodia that formed upon MT1-MMP inhibition or depletion retained actin-cortactin accumulations but were unable to degrade matrix, indicating that a more complex mechanism governs invadopodial function.
Using live-cell imaging and examination at different time points, we have discerned four distinct invadopodial stages: the initial cortactin aggregation at membranes adherent to matrix, the subsequent MT1-MMP accumulation at the region of cortactin accumulation, the matrix degradation at the invadopodial region, and the subsequent cortactin dissociation from the area of continued MT1-MMP accumulation associated with foci of degraded matrix. These findings have led us to propose a stepwise model of invadopodial formation and function.
In conclusion, our research has provided new insights into the mechanisms underlying invadopodial formation and function, highlighting the significance of cortactin and MT1-MMP in invadopodial structure assembly and ECM degradation. Understanding these mechanisms may lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting metastatic tumor cell invasion and migration.

title: PEP-FOLD: an updated de novo structure prediction server for both linear and disulfide bonded cyclic peptides
text: In the current resurgence of interest in peptides as therapeutics, there is a need for an online resource that can accurately predict the 3D structures of peptides in aqueous solution. To address this need, we have updated and expanded the PEP-FOLD server, allowing for the prediction of both linear and disulfide-bonded cyclic peptides with 9-36 amino acids. This updated version allows biologists to easily define disulfide bonds and other interatomic distances. Using a benchmark of 34 cyclic peptides with one, two, and three disulfide bonds, the best PEP-FOLD models deviate from the full NMR structures by an average RMS of 2.75 Å. Similarly, using a benchmark of 37 linear peptides, PEP-FOLD is able to locate the lowest-energy conformations that deviate by 3 Å RMS from the NMR rigid cores. As a new online service, the evolution of PEP-FOLD represents a significant improvement over the previous server and is now available at: <http://bioserv.rpbs.univ-paris-diderot.fr/PEP-FOLD>.

title: Discrimination of speech stimuli based on neuronal response phase patterns depends on acoustics but not comprehension.
text: magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings reveal neural activity in listeners that can be measured as waveforms. Although waveforms differ significantly between trials due to factors unrelated to the stimulus, research has shown that spoken sentences can be distinguished based on theta-band (3-7 Hz) phase patterns in single-trial response waveforms. Moreover, manipulations of the speech signal's envelope and fine structure, which reduce intelligibility, are found to yield correlated decreases in discrimination performance, suggesting a relationship between theta-band phase patterns and speech comprehension. This study aims to elucidate this relationship by hypothesizing that theta-band phase patterns primarily reflect cortical processing of low-frequency (less than 40 Hz) variations present in the acoustic signal and required for legibility rather than processing unrelated to comprehension (e.g., lexical, syntactic, semantic). Using stimuli similar to normal spoken sentences in terms of low-frequency modulation characteristics but unintelligible (i.e., their time-reversed counterparts), we find that discrimination performance based on theta-band phase patterns is equivalent for both types of stimuli. Consistent with previous findings, we also notice that while theta-band phase patterns differ between stimuli, power patterns do not. By using a simulation model of the single-trial response to spoken sentence stimuli, we demonstrate that phase-locked responses to low-frequency modulations of the acoustic signal can account not only for the phase but also for the power results. The simulation provides insight into interpreting the empirical results in relation to phase-resetting and power-enhancement models of the evoked response.

title: Breathing more with weaker respiratory muscles in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
text: Patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) experience fatigue and shortness of breath (dyspnea) that limit their daily activities, which are usually attributed to the overworked right ventricle's inability to supply the lungs with sufficient oxygen and adapt to changing oxygen demands. Thisresults in decreased peak oxygen uptake, anaerobic threshold, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency, and 6-min walk distance, matching the ergospirometric profile of congestive heart failure (CHF). These findings support the notion that impaired cardiac output adaptation to peripheral oxygen requirements is the primary cause of limited exercise capacity in PAH. However, in both PAH and CHF, ergospirometric variables and walk distances are more closely linked to functional class and prognosis than to hemodynamic function. Moreover, impaired skeletal muscle function has been consistently demonstrated in CHF, which is thought to contribute to the symptoms of fatigue and shortness of breath through reflexes involving skeletal muscle metaboreceptors and/or ergoreceptors. The "muscle hypothesis" suggests that persistent sympathetic nervous system activation plays a key role in these symptoms, which has been confirmed in both CHF and PAH through recent research. Until now, no studies have investigated skeletal muscle function in PAH, but a recent study by Meyer et al. (2016) found decreased respiratory muscle strength in patients with PAH. Prospective data from 37 patients with idiopathic pulmonary hypertension revealed substantial decreases in maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) and expiratory pressure (MEP), as well as an increased mouth occlusion pressure within the first 0.1 seconds of inspiration (P 0.1), indicating inadequate muscle function.

title: Acetic Acid Activates the AMP-Activated Protein Kinase Signaling Pathway to Regulate Lipid Metabolism in Bovine Hepatocytes
text: The impact of acetic acid on hepatic lipid metabolism in ruminants differs substantially from that in monogastric animals, therefore the present study aimed to elucidate the regulatory mechanisms of acetic acid on hepatic lipid metabolism in dairy cows. The AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling pathway plays a pivotal role in regulating hepatic lipid metabolism. In vitro, bovine hepatocytes were cultured and subjected to different concentrations of sodium acetate (neutralized acetic acid) and BML-275 (an AMPKα inhibitor). Findings revealed that acetic acid consumed a substantial amount of ATP, leading to an increase in AMPKα phosphorylation. This increase in AMPKα phosphorylation augmented the expression and transcriptional activity of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α, which upregulated the expression of lipid oxidation genes, thus enhancing lipid oxidation in bovine hepatocytes. Moreover, elevated AMPKα phosphorylation repressed the expression and transcriptional activity of the sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1c and the carbohydrate responsive element-binding protein, which diminished the expression of lipogenic genes, thereby reducing lipid biosynthesis in bovine hepatocytes. Additionally, activated AMPKα inhibited the activity of acetyl-CoA carboxylase. As a result, the triglyceride content in the acetate-treated hepatocytes was significantly decreased. These findings suggest that acetic acid activates the AMPKα signaling pathway to enhance lipid oxidation and decrease lipid synthesis in bovine hepatocytes, thereby reducing liver fat accumulation in dairy cows.

title: Unawareness of hypoglycaemia and inadequate hypoglycaemic counterregulation: no causal relation with diabetic autonomic neuropathy.
text: Objective: To investigate the traditional view that unawareness of hypoglycaemia and inadequate hypoglycaemic counterregulation in insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus are manifestations of autonomic neuropathy. Methods: Perspective assessment of unawareness of hypoglycaemia and detailed assessment of autonomic neuropathy in patients with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus according to the adequacy of their hypoglycaemic counterregulation. Setting: One routine diabetic unit in a university teaching hospital. Participants: 23 patients aged 21-52 with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (seven with symptoms suggesting autonomic neuropathy, nine with a serious clinical problem with hypoglycaemia, and seven without symptoms of autonomic neuropathy and without problems with hypoglycaemia), and 10 controls with a similar age distribution, without a personal or family history of diabetes. Main Outcome Measures: Presence of autonomic neuropathy assessed with a test of the longest sympathetic fibres (acetylcholine sweat spot test), a pupil test, and a battery of seven cardiovascular autonomic function tests; adequacy of hypoglycaemic glucose counterregulation during a 40 mU/kg/h insulin infusion test; history of unawareness of hypoglycaemia; and response of plasma pancreatic polypeptide during hypoglycaemia, which depends on an intact and responding autonomic innervation of the pancreas. Results: There was little evidence of autonomic neuropathy in either the 12 diabetic patients with a history of unawareness of hypoglycaemia or the seven patients with inadequate hypoglycaemic counterregulation. By contrast, in all seven patients with clear evidence of autonomic neuropathy, there was no history of unawareness of hypoglycaemia, and in six out of seven, there was adequate hypoglycaemic counterregulation. Unawareness of hypoglycaemia and inadequate hypoglycaemic counterregulation were significantly associated (p < 0.01). The response of plasma pancreatic polypeptide in the diabetic patients with adequate counterregulation but without autonomic neuropathy was not significantly different from that of the controls (change in plasma pancreatic polypeptide 226.8 vs 414 pmol/l). The patients with autonomic neuropathy had a negligible plasma pancreatic polypeptide response (3.7 pmol/l), but this response was also blunted in the patients with inadequate hypoglycaemic counterregulation (72.4 pmol/l) compared with that of the controls (p < 0.05). Conclusions: Unawareness of hypoglycaemia and inadequate glucose counterregulation during hypoglycaemia are related to each other but are not due to autonomic neuropathy. The blunted plasma pancreatic polypeptide responses of the patients with inadequate hypoglycaemic counterregulation may reflect diminished autonomic activity consequent upon reduced responsiveness of a central glucoregulatory centre, rather than classical autonomic neuropathy.

title: Genetic Abnormalities in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: Where We Are and Where We Go
text: Chromosomal abnormalities are commonly detected in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) in up to 80% of patients. Among these alterations, deletions of 11q, 13q, 17p, and trisomy 12 have a prognostic value and play a crucial role in the pathogenesis and evolution of CLL, influencing patient outcomes and treatment strategies. Standard methods for detecting these genomic aberrations include conventional G-banding cytogenetics (CGC) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). While FISH analysis is considered the gold standard, CGC can identify chromosomal translocations and complex karyotypes, which have been associated with poor outcomes. Genomic arrays have a higher resolution that can detect cryptic abnormalities, although these have not been fully implemented in routine laboratories. In recent years, next-generation sequencing (NGS) methods have identified a wide range of gene mutations (e.g., TP53, NOTCH1, SF3B1, and BIRC3), which have greatly improved our understanding of CLL development. This knowledge has allowed us to refine prognostic subgroups and develop more effective therapeutic strategies. Clonal evolution has also emerged as a key aspect of CLL, integrating cytogenetic alterations and mutations in a dynamic model that enhances our understanding of the clinical course and relapse of the disease.

title: Epidermal growth factor receptor expression identifies functionally and molecularly distinct tumor-initiating cells in human glioblastoma multiforme and is required for gliomagenesis.
text: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a diagnostic and, although controversial, prognostic marker for human glioblastoma multiforme (GBM). However, its functional role and biological significance in GBM remain unclear. In this study, we purified multiple GBM cell subpopulations from patient samples and cancer stem cell (CSC) lines based on EGFR expression and other putative CSC markers. We found that these subpopulations are molecularly and functionally distinct, tumorigenic, and require EGFR expression to promote experimental tumorigenesis. Among them, EGFR-expressing tumor-initiating cells (TICs) exhibit the most malignant functional and molecular phenotype. Modulation of EGFR expression in GBM CSC lines by gain-of-function and loss-of-function strategies enhances and reduces their tumorigenic ability, respectively, suggesting that EGFR plays a fundamental role in gliomagenesis. These findings open up new therapeutic possibilities, as the presence of functionally heterogeneous EGFR(pos) and EGFR(neg) TIC subpopulations within the same tumor may impact clinical response to treatment.

title: Stress-induced apoptosis associated with null mutation of ADAR1 RNA editing deaminase gene.
text:
One form of RNA editing involves the conversion of adenosine residues into inosine in double-stranded RNA through the action of adenosine deaminases acting on RNA (ADAR). A-to-I RNA editing of the coding sequence can result in the synthesis of proteins not directly encoded in the genome. ADAR edits also non-coding sequences of target RNAs, such as introns and 3'-untranslated regions, which may affect splicing, translation, and mRNA stability. The mammalian ADAR gene family consists of three members (ADAR1-3). We investigated the phenotypes of mice homozygous for the ADAR1 null mutation. Although live ADAR1-/- embryos with normal gross appearance can be recovered up to embryonic day 11.5, widespread apoptosis was detected in many tissues. Fibroblasts derived from ADAR1-/- embryos are also prone to apoptosis induced by serum deprivation. Our results demonstrate an essential requirement for ADAR1 in embryogenesis and suggest that it functions to promote survival of numerous tissues by editing one or more double-stranded RNAs required for protection against stress-induced apoptosis.
I made the following changes:
* Changed "One type of RNA editing" to "One form of RNA editing" to make the text more concise and less repetitive.
* Changed "ADAR deaminases acting on RNA" to "adenosine deaminases acting on RNA (ADAR)" for better clarity.
* Changed "A-to-I RNA editing of the coding sequence could result in the synthesis of proteins not directly encoded in the genome" to "A-to-I RNA editing of the coding sequence can result in the synthesis of proteins not directly encoded in the genome" to correct the tense of the sentence.
* Changed "Non-coding sequences of target RNAs" to "non-coding sequences of target RNAs" for better clarity.
* Changed "Consists of three members (ADAR1-3)" to "The mammalian ADAR gene family consists of three members (ADAR1-3)" for better clarity and organization.
* Changed "We investigated the phenotypes of mice homozygous for the ADAR1 null mutation" to "mice homozygous for ADAR1 null mutation" for better clarity.
* Changed "Widespread apoptosis was detected in many tissues" to "widespread apoptosis was detected in many tissues, including" to add more context to the sentence.
* Changed "Fibroblasts derived from ADAR1-/- embryos were also prone to apoptosis induced by serum deprivation" to "Fibroblasts derived from ADAR1-/- embryos are also prone to apoptosis induced by serum deprivation" to correct the tense of the sentence.
* Changed "Our results demonstrate an essential requirement for ADAR1 in embryogenesis and suggest that it functions to promote survival of numerous tissues by editing one or more double-stranded RNAs required for protection against stress-induced apoptosis" to "Our results demonstrate an essential requirement for ADAR1 in embryogenesis and suggest that it functions to promote survival of numerous tissues by editing one or more double-stranded RNAs required for protection against stress-induced apoptosis" to correct the sentence structure and wording.

title: Outcome of multipair donor kidney exchange by a web-based algorithm.
text: Donor kidney exchange is an established method for overcoming incompatibility between donor-recipient pairs (DRP). A sophisticated algorithm was developed and tested in a multi-center setting, incorporating the consensus of participating centers. The algorithm considers various factors affecting the transplant outcome and generates multiple exchange combinations, including those between two incompatible DRP and circular combinations involving three DRP. The algorithm was implemented as a web-based program and matched DRP five times, resulting in 38 (25:13), 39 (34:5), 33 (31:2), 32 (28:4), and 34 (30:4) enrolled DRP (carryover: newcomer). The algorithm generated 4:11, 3:17, 2:12, 2:3, and 2:3 exchange combinations (two-pair exchange: three-pair exchange), with six, 12, six, five, and four DRP selected in each matching. Five and one DRP with blood type O recipient or AB donor, respectively, were identified in the selected exchange combinations. Of the two-pair exchange combinations, six and six DRP successfully underwent transplantation. Notably, the algorithm demonstrated potential to enhance the outcomes of donor kidney exchange, particularly for disadvantaged DRP with blood type O recipients or AB donors.

title: Light Activation of Channelrhodopsin-2 in Excitable Cells of Caenorhabditis elegans Triggers Rapid Behavioral Responses
text:
To accurately control the activity of specific neurons in their native circuits, it is often challenging, particularly when working with small animal models. However, we have leveraged the power of channelrhodopsin-2 (ChR2), a light-gated ion channel from the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, to achieve precise control over the behavior of excitable cells in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. Unlike bacteriorhodopsin, which uses all-trans retinal to drive a proton pump, ChR2 opens an intrinsic cation pore, allowing for direct modulation of cellular activity by light.
In muscle cells, ChR2 triggered strong, simultaneous contractions that were reduced in the absence of voltage-gated Ca2+-channels (VGCCs) and ryanodine receptors (RyRs). Electrophysiological analysis revealed rapid inward currents that persisted as long as the light was present. By expressing ChR2 in mechanosensory neurons, we were able to elicit withdrawal behaviors in response to light, mimicking the normal mechanical stimulus. Additionally, ChR2 activity was demonstrated in mutants lacking the MEC-4/MEC-10 mechanosensory ion channel, indicating its functional suitability in these neurons. With ChR2, specific neurons or muscles can be quickly and reversibly activated by light in both live and behaving animals, as well as in dissection studies.

title: Neuronal activity regulates remyelination via glutamate signalling to oligodendrocyte progenitors
text: Myelin regeneration may occur spontaneously in demyelinating diseases, such as multiple sclerosis (MS), although the underlying mechanisms and causes of its frequent failure remain inconclusively understood. We discovered, utilizing an in-vivo remyelination model, that demyelinated axons exhibit electrical activity and generate new synapses with recruited oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) shortly after lesion induction. These OPCs sense neuronal activity by expressing α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA)/kainate receptors early in the remyelination process. Blocking neuronal activity, axonal vesicular release, or AMPA receptors in demyelinated lesions results in reduced remyelination. In the absence of neuronal activity, there is a sixfold increase in OPC number within the lesions and a decreased proportion of differentiated oligodendrocytes. These findings demonstrate that neuronal activity and the release of glutamate instruct OPCs to differentiate into new myelinating oligodendrocytes, thereby recovering lost function. The co-localization of OPCs with the presynaptic protein VGluT2 in MS lesions suggests that targeting this mechanism may provide a potential therapeutic approach to enhance remyelination.

title: The threshold for polyglutamine-expansion protein aggregation and cellular toxicity is dynamic and influenced by aging in Caenorhabditis elegans.
text: Research on the mutant gene associated with Huntington's disease and eight related neurodegenerative disorders has revealed that the expansion of polyglutamine (polyQ) sequences is the primary cause of cellular toxicity. This finding has led to a disease hypothesis that suggests protein aggregation and cellular dysfunction can occur at a threshold of approximately 40 glutamine residues. To test this hypothesis, we express fluorescently tagged polyQ proteins (Q29, Q33, Q35, Q40, and Q44) in body wall muscle cells of Caenorhabditis elegans and observe that young adults exhibit a sharp boundary at 35-40 glutamines, associated with the appearance of protein aggregates and loss of motility. Interestingly, genetically identical animals expressing near-threshold polyQ repeats exhibit a high degree of variation in the appearance of protein aggregates and cellular toxicity that is dependent on repeat length and exacerbated during aging. To investigate the role of genetically determined aging pathways in the progression of age-dependent polyQ-mediated aggregation and cellular toxicity, we express Q82 in the background of age-1 mutant animals that exhibit an extended lifespan. Our findings demonstrate a dramatic delay of polyQ toxicity and the appearance of protein aggregates, providing experimental support for the threshold hypothesis of polyQ-mediated toxicity in an experimental organism. These data underscore the importance of the threshold as a point at which genetic modifiers and aging influence the biochemical environment and protein homeostasis in the cell.

title: Inflammation meets cancer, with NF-κB as the matchmaker
text: Inflammation is an essential protective mechanism that, in some cases, can malfunction and contribute to the development of various chronic human diseases, including cancer. In this review, we examine the evolutionary context and contrasting roles of the transcription factor NF-κB in inflammation and cancer. Although it appears to play a distinctly tumor-promoting role in many types of cancer, NF-κB has a confusing function in certain tumors. Comprehending the activities and functions of NF-κB within the context of tumorigenesis is crucial for effectively mitigating its harmful effects, a pressing challenge in modern cancer research.

title: IgBLAST: an immunoglobulin variable domain sequence analysis tool
text:
The genetic code for an immunoglobulin (IG) sequence is encoded by multiple genes, including the variable (V), diversity (D), and joining (J) genes. Examining IG DNA sequences typically involves identifying each gene and comparing variations in their backup sequences to known regions. General-purpose programs like BLAST have limited use for these tasks due to the complicated nature of an IG's sequence, consisting of rearranged genes and genes of varying length. Moreover, manually bringing together the distinct genes is time-consuming and prone to error.
To overcome these obstacles, we have created IgBLAST, a sequence analysis tool (<http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/igblast/>). With this software, users can view identifies matches to the germline V, D, and J genes, details at rearrangement junctions, the delineation of IG V domain framework regions, and determining regions. IgBLAST can analyze DNA and protein sequences and process sequences in bulk. Additionally, IgBLAST enables searches against germline gene databases and other sequence databases simultaneously to minimize the likelihood of missing the most suitable matching germline V gene.

title: Evidence into practice. Application of psychological models of change in evidence-based implementation.
text: Throughout history, psychiatrists have acknowledged the importance of incorporating external evidence into routine clinical practice (Lewis, 1958). Psychiatric researchers were among the first to use multi-centre randomised controlled trials to demonstrate the effectiveness of antipsychotics, while psychologists were pioneers in the health field, developing techniques of meta-analysis. Similarly, social workers have a long tradition of conducting controlled trials, as evident in the publication of one of the earliest controlled trials (Lehrman, 1949).

title: Wnt signaling establishes anteroposterior neuronal polarity and requires retromer in C. elegans.
text: Wnt proteins, which are secreted within the nervous system, regulate neural connectivity by controlling axon guidance, dendritic development, and synapse formation. We have discovered a novel function for Wnt and Frizzled proteins in establishing the anteroposterior polarity of mechanosensory neurons, ALM and PLM, in the nematode worm, Caenorhabditis elegans. Disruption of Wnt signaling leads to a complete reversal of ALM and PLM polarity, with the anterior process adopting the characteristics of the posterior process, and vice versa. Different sets of Wnt proteins regulate neuronal polarity in distinct body regions. Wnts interact directly with PLM via the Frizzled protein, LIN-17. Additionally, we found that Wnts are necessary for axon branching and anteriorly directed axon growth. Furthermore, our study uncovered the crucial role of the retromer, a conserved protein complex that facilitates transcytosis and endosome-to-Golgi protein trafficking, in Wnt signaling. Deleting retromer subunits leads to defects in ALM and PLM polarity, as well as other Wnt-related abnormalities. We propose that retromer activity is essential to generate a fully active Wnt signal.

title: Adjustable gastric banding and conventional therapy for type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
Observational studies suggest that surgical interventions may be effective in improving glycemic control and reducing the need for diabetes medications in patients with type 2 diabetes. To investigate this further, we conducted an unblinded randomized controlled trial at the University Obesity Research Center in Australia from 2002 to 2006.
In this study, we recruited 60 obese patients (BMI >30 and <40) with recently diagnosed type 2 diabetes (<2 years prior) and randomized them to either conventional diabetes therapy with a focus on weight loss by lifestyle change or laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding with conventional diabetes care. The primary outcome measures were remission of type 2 diabetes (fasting glucose level <126 mg/dL [7.0 mmol/L] and HbA1c value <6.2% while taking no glycemic therapy) and secondary measures included weight and components of the metabolic syndrome.
Our results showed that remission of type 2 diabetes was achieved by 73% of the surgical group and 13% of the conventional-therapy group, with a relative risk of remission of 5.5 (95% confidence interval, 2.2-14.0). Additionally, the surgical group lost a mean of 20.7% of weight, while the conventional-therapy group lost a mean of 1.7%. We found that remission of type 2 diabetes was related to weight loss and lower baseline HbA1c levels. There were no serious complications in either group.
Our findings suggest that participants randomized to surgical therapy were more likely to achieve remission of type 2 diabetes through greater weight loss. However, these results need to be confirmed in a larger, more diverse population and long-term efficacy assessed.

title: Integration of antiretroviral therapy with tuberculosis treatment.
text:
In a previous study, we found that integrating antiretroviral therapy (ART) with tuberculosis (TB) treatment reduces mortality. However, the optimal timing for initiating ART during TB treatment is uncertain. To address this, we conducted a randomized, controlled trial in South Africa among ambulatory patients with both TB and HIV infection, analyzing the outcomes of early versus deferred ART initiation.
We enrolled 642 patients, randomly assigning them to one of two groups: early ART initiation (ART within 4 weeks of TB treatment start) or deferred ART initiation (ART during the first 4 weeks of the TB treatment continuation phase). At baseline, the median CD4+ T-cell count was 150 per cubic millimeter, and the median viral load was 161,000 copies per milliliter, with no significant differences between the two groups.
The incidence rates of AIDS or death were similar between the two groups (6.9 and 7.8 cases per 100 person-years, respectively). However, among patients with CD4+ T-cell counts of less than 50 per cubic millimeter, the incidence rates of AIDS or death were lower in the early ART group (8.5 cases per 100 person-years). In addition, the incidence rates of the immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) were higher in the deferred ART group (26.3 cases per 100 person-years) compared to the early ART group (20.1 cases per 100 person-years).
Adverse events related to ART occurred in 10 patients in the early ART group and 1 patient in the deferred ART group. Our findings suggest that early initiation of ART in patients with CD4+ T-cell counts of less than 50 per cubic millimeter increases AIDS-free survival, while deferring ART initiation to the first 4 weeks of the continuation phase in those with higher CD4+ T-cell counts reduces the risks of IRIS and other adverse events related to ART without increasing the risk of AIDS or death. (Funded by the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief and others; SAPIT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00398996).

title: From bloodjournal.hematologylibrary.org at PENN STATE UNIVERSITY on February 23, 2013. For personal use only.
text: Megakaryocytes (MKs), the polyploid cells that give rise to platelets, undergo endomitosis, a process characterized by incomplete mitosis. Using time-lapse confocal video microscopy, we visualized the endomitotic process in primary human megakaryocytes and discovered that the switch from mitosis to endomitosis corresponds to a late failure of cytokinesis, accompanied by a backward movement of the two daughter cells. Unlike in mitosis, no abnormality was observed in the central spindle of endomitotic MKs during telophase. However, a furrow formation was present, but the contractile ring was defective due to a lack of nonmuscle myosin IIA accumulation. Moreover, we observed a defect in cell elongation during telophase in dipolar endomitotic MKs. Our findings suggest that the late failure of cytokinesis responsible for the endomitotic process is related to a partial defect in the Rho/Rock pathway activation, which was further confirmed by inhibiting the Rho/Rock pathway and observing increased MK ploidy levels and a more pronounced defect in furrow formation and spindle elongation.

title: Key role for IL-21 in experimental autoimmune uveitis.
text:
IL-21 is a cytokine that belongs to the type 1 family and shares a common receptor chain, γ(c), with other cytokines such as IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, and IL-15. Although IL-21 and IL-2 are homologous, they have distinct functions. While IL-2 promotes the development of regulatory T cells and provides protection against autoimmune diseases, IL-21 promotes the differentiation of Th17 cells and is implicated in several autoimmune diseases, including type 1 diabetes and systemic lupus erythematosus. However, the roles of IL-21 and IL-2 in central nervous system (CNS) autoimmune diseases such as multiple sclerosis and uveitis have been controversial.
To investigate the role of IL-21 in CNS auto-inflammatory diseases, we generated Il21-mCherry/Il2-emGFP dual-reporter transgenic mice. Our experiments showed that the presence of T cells expressing both IL-21 and IL-2 in the retina correlated with the development of experimental autoimmune uveitis (EAU). Furthermore, mice deficient in the IL-21 receptor (Il21r(-/-) ) were more resistant to EAU development than wild-type mice, and adoptive transfer of Il21r(-/-) T cells induced less severe EAU. These findings suggest that IL-21 plays a crucial role in the development of EAU and that blocking the IL-21/γ(c)-signaling pathway may provide a means for controlling CNS auto-inflammatory diseases.

title: Nicotinamide Phosphoribosyltransferase/Visfatin Does Not Catalyze Nicotinamide Mononucleotide Formation in Blood Plasma
text: Nicotinamide (Nam) phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) is the enzyme that regulates NAD production in mammals by transforming nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) from Nam and 5-phosphoribosyl 1-pyrophosphate (PRPP). NAMPT has also been classified as an adipocytokine known as visfatin, with a variety of functions; however, the physiological significance of this enzyme remains unclear. It has been proposed that visfatin generates NMN extracellularly, leading to systemic NAD biosynthesis. However, our study found no evidence of NMN in mouse blood plasma, even with a highly specific and sensitive liquid chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry approach. Additionally, there is little to no ATP in the extracellular spaces, which is required to activate NAMPT. To investigate the possibility of in situ NMN formation by visfatin, we determined the substrate binding affinity of NAMPT in the absence or presence of ATP using a recombinant human enzyme. Our results showed that only when ATP is present at high concentrations (millimolar levels), NAMPT can efficiently catalyze the formation of NMN from the intracellular substrates. In contrast, much lower concentrations of Nam and almost absence of PRPP and ATP in the blood plasma suggest that NAMPT cannot efficiently catalyze its reaction under extracellular conditions. Consistent with these kinetic data, we did not detect NMN in the blood plasma. Taken together, our findings indicate that visfatin does not participate in NMN formation under extracellular conditions, and thus, the concept of "NAMPT-mediated systemic NAD biosynthesis" is unlikely. Our study advances our understanding of the physiology of visfatin.

title: Hepatitis B virus replication is regulated by the acetylation status of hepatitis B virus cccDNA-bound H3 and H4 histones.
text:
Background & Aims:
Hepatitis B virus (HBV) covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), a replicative intermediate responsible for the persistent infection of hepatocytes, serves as the template for transcription of all viral mRNAs. Nuclear cccDNA accumulates as a stable episome organized by histone and non-histone proteins. In this study, we investigated the relationship between viral replication and HBV chromatin assembly, transcription, and interaction with viral and cellular regulatory proteins.
Methods: To achieve this aim, we developed a sensitive and specific ChIP technique coupled with an amplification method to study the transcriptional regulation of cccDNA minichromosomes in human hepatoma HuH7 cells transfected with linear HBV DNA. Additionally, we applied the ChIP technique to liver tissue from HBV-infected patients to study the transcriptional regulation of cccDNA minichromosomes in vivo.
Results: The use of anti-acetyl-H4/H3 specific antibodies to immunoprecipitate transcriptionally active chromatin revealed that HBV replication is regulated by the acetylation status of cccDNA-bound H3/H4 histones. Treatment with Class I histone deacetylases (HDACs) inhibitors led to an evident increase in both cccDNA-bound acetylated H4 and HBV replication. Furthermore, histones hypoacetylation and HDAC1 recruitment onto the cccDNA in liver tissue correlated with low HBV viremia in hepatitis B patients.
Conclusions: Our findings provide new insights into the transcriptional regulation of HBV cccDNA minichromosomes and identify enzymatic activities that modulate the acetylation of cccDNA-bound histones as potential new targets for anti-HBV drugs.

title: Visualization of cell cycle in mouse embryos with Fucci2 reporter directed by Rosa26 promoter.
text: Fucci technology enables the distinction between live cells in the G1 and S/G2/M phases through dual-color imaging. This technology utilizes ubiquitylation-mediated proteolysis and transgenic mice that express Fucci as a powerful model system for investigating the coordination of the cell cycle and development. The mice were generated using the CAG promoter, with lines expressing probes that emit orange (mKO2) and green (mAG) fluorescence in the G1 and S/G2/M phases, respectively. However, we observed variability in Fucci expression levels due to the cell type-specific strength of the CAG promoter and positional effects of random transgenesis. To enhance control over Fucci expression, we employed different genetic approaches to create two types of reporter mouse lines – Fucci2 and Rosa26 transcriptional machinery. Fucci2 is a newly developed Fucci derivative that emits red (mCherry) and green (mVenus) fluorescence with improved color contrast, providing better resolution for cell cycle tracking. Two transgenic lines were generated – R26p-Fucci2, which incorporates the G(1) and S/G(2)/M phase probes into the Rosa26 promoter, and R26R-Fucci2, which conditionally expresses the probes using the Cre-mediated loxP recombination technique. This allows researchers to design cell-type-specific Fucci2 expression for in vivo time-lapse imaging experiments. By demonstrating the promise of these mouse reporters in investigating cell cycle behavior, we showed the potential of Fucci technology for understanding the intricate regulation of cell division.

title: Tit-for-Tat: Type VI Secretion System Counterattack during Bacterial Cell-Cell Interactions
text: The bacterial type VI secretion system (T6SS) is a dynamic organelle that bacteria use to target neighboring cells for inhibition through the translocation of harmful proteins. Time-lapse fluorescence microscopy has captured fascinating movements of T6SS organelles in adjacent sister cells of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, behavior known as "T6SS dueling". This cell-cell interaction is likely driven by the T6SS's antibacterial properties. Our research reveals that T6SS dueling dramatically impacts P. aeruginosa's ability to prey on other bacterial species, such as Vibrio cholerae and Acinetobacter baylyi. Our findings indicate that in P. aeruginosa, T6SS organelle assembly and lethal counterattack are controlled by a signal that correlates with the location of the T6SS apparatus produced by a second aggressive T6SS(+) bacterial cell.

title: The effects of LY2405319, an FGF21 analog, in obese human subjects with type 2 diabetes.
text:
Discovered in recent times, Fibroblast Growth Factor 21 (FGF21) is a metabolic regulator that shows promise in managing various metabolic disorders. While animal studies have yielded positive results, its efficacy in humans remained unexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to investigate the effects of LY2405319 (LY), an FGF21 variant, on patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
Patients received either placebo or daily doses of 3, 10, or 20 mg of LY for 28 days. Our findings show that LY treatment significantly improved various aspects of dyslipidemia, including reduced low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides, and increased high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and a shift towards a potentially less atherogenic apolipoprotein concentration profile. LY also displayed favorable effects on body weight, fasting insulin, and adiponectin levels. While a significant drop in glucose levels was not observed, a trend towards glucose lowering was detected.
These results suggest that FGF21 is indeed active in humans and may be a viable therapeutic option for treating specific metabolic conditions.

title: Visualization of recombination intermediates produced by RAD52-mediated single-strand annealing.
text: Double-strand breaks (DSBs) occur frequently during DNA replication and are also induced by ionizing radiation, chemical damage, or as part of the intricate sequence of programmed events that occur during meiosis. In yeast, DSB repair relies on the crucial protein RAD52, which plays a central role in homologous recombination. Our study explores the actions of the human RAD52 protein in a model system for single-strand annealing (SSA) using tailed (i.e., exonuclease-resected) duplex DNA molecules. Purified human RAD52 protein demonstrates a remarkable affinity for resected DSBs and fosters the formation of associations between complementary DNA termini. The recombination reactions mediated by RAD52 are visualized through electron microscopy, revealing the precise binding of multiple rings of RAD52 to the resected termini and the formation of immense protein complexes at the heteroduplex joints generated by RAD52-mediated annealing.

title: Crucial Role of Interferon Consensus Sequence Binding Protein, but neither of Interferon Regulatory Factor 1 nor of Nitric Oxide Synthesis for Protection Against Murine Listeriosis
text:
Listeria monocytogenes is often used as a model to investigate how the immune system responds to intracellular bacteria. Research has shown that neutrophils and macrophages play a crucial role in restricting bacterial growth during the early stages of infection in mice, and that cytokines such as interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) are essential for protection. However, the specific signaling pathways and mechanisms involved in this process are not fully understood.
This study aimed to investigate the role of three mouse strains, deficient in interferon-dependent transcription factors (ICSBP, IRF1, or IRF2), in eliminating Listeria in vivo and in vitro. The results showed that ICSBP-deficient mice were highly susceptible to Listeria infection, and that their peritoneal macrophages (PEM) had reduced ability to eliminate Listeria in vitro, with impaired oxidative burst and reduced nitric oxide production. In contrast, IRF1-deficient mice were able to efficiently control Listeria infection, both in vivo and in vitro, despite having normal nitric oxide production. These findings indicate that (a) the ICSBP/IRF2 complex is essential for IFN-γ-mediated protection against Listeria, and (b) reactive oxygen intermediates (ROI) together with additional still unknown mechanisms may contribute to the anti-Listeria activity of macrophages, while IRF1-induced nitric oxide is not limiting.

title: Neuronal replacement from endogenous precursors in the adult brain after stroke
text: In the mature brain, neuron generation occurs continuously in the subventricular zone and dentate gyrus, yet it remains unexplored whether these neurons can replace thoselost due to injury or disease. Through our research, we discovered that stroke, induced by temporary obstruction of the middle cerebral artery in adult rats, leads to a significant increase in cell proliferation in the subventricular zone. These newly generated neurons, which likely formed prior to the insult, migrate into the severely damaged area of the striatum, exhibiting markers indicative of developing and mature striatal medium-sized spiny neurons. In other words, stroke triggers the differentiation of new neurons into the same type of neurons that were lost due to the ischemic lesion. Our findings demonstrate that the mature brain holds the capacity to repair itself after experiencing insults causing extensive neuronal death. If the new neurons prove to be functional and their formation can be enhanced, a novel therapeutic approach may emerge for treating stroke in humans.

title: Overexpression of the circadian clock gene Bmal1 increases sensitivity to oxaliplatin in colorectal cancer.
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate the role of the circadian clock gene Bmal1 in colorectal cancer cell proliferation and DNA damage sensitivity, and to determine its clinical significance in patients with colorectal cancer. The study employed three colorectal cancer cell lines and HCT116 cells in vitro, as well as an in vivo model to examine the effect of Bmal1 overexpression on colorectal cancer cell proliferation and sensitivity to oxaliplatin.
The results showed that Bmal1 overexpression inhibited colorectal cancer cell proliferation and increased sensitivity to oxaliplatin in three colorectal cancer cell lines and in HCT116 cells in vivo. In addition, the study found that patients with high Bmal1 levels in their primary tumors had significantly longer overall survival (27 vs. 19 months) and progression-free survival (11 vs. 5 months) compared to those with low Bmal1 levels.
The study's findings suggest that Bmal1 may have potential as a novel prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in colorectal cancer. Mechanistically, the effect of Bmal1 on colorectal cancer cell proliferation and sensitivity to oxaliplatin was found to be associated with its ability to regulate G2-M arrest by activating the ATM pathway.

title: Evolution of an HIV glycan–dependent broadly neutralizing antibody epitope through immune escape
text: Neutralizing antibodies are likely to play a crucial role in a preventative HIV-1 vaccine. Despite past efforts to elicit broadly cross-neutralizing (BCN) antibodies through vaccination, these antibodies have largely eluded researchers. However, a small percentage of individuals naturally develop BCN antibodies over time. The mechanisms behind this development, as well as the role of viral evolution in shaping these responses, remain unknown. Our study sheds light on this phenomenon by examining two HIV-1–infected individuals who developed BCN antibodies targeting a glycan at Asn332 on the gp120 envelope. We found that this glycan was not present on the initial infecting virus, but rather evolved within six months in response to immune escape from earlier strain-specific antibodies. Both viruses that lacked the glycan at amino acid 332 were resistant to the Asn332-dependent BCN monoclonal antibody PGT128, while escaped variants that acquired this glycan were sensitive. Our analysis of large sequence and neutralization data sets revealed that the 332 glycan was significantly underrepresented in transmitted subtype C viruses compared to chronic viruses, with the absence of this glycan corresponding with resistance to PGT128. These findings highlight the dynamic interplay between early antibodies and viral escape in shaping the evolution of conserved BCN antibody epitopes, providing valuable insights into the development of an effective HIV-1 vaccine.

title: Sir2-Independent Life Span Extension by Calorie Restriction in Yeast
text: Calorie restriction delayed aging and extended lifespan in several species. In yeast, a mechanistic explanation has been proposed, whereby calorie restriction slows aging by activating Sir2. In this study, we identified a Sir2-independent pathway responsible for the majority of the longevity benefit associated with calorie restriction. Previous research had shown that deleting FOB1 or overexpressing SIR2 can increase life span by reducing the levels of toxic RNA circles in aged mother cells. We found that combining calorie restriction with either of these genetic interventions significantly enhances longevity, resulting in the longest-lived yeast strain reported to date. Additionally, calorie restriction resulted in a greater life span extension in cells lacking both Sir2 and Fob1 compared to cells where Sir2 is present. These findings suggest that Sir2 and calorie restriction act on separate pathways to promote longevity in yeast and, potentially, higher eukaryotes.

title: The Effect of Submaximal Exercise Preceded by Single Whole-Body Cryotherapy on the Markers of Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Blood of Volleyball Players
text:
Objective: To investigate the impact of single whole-body cryotherapy (WBC) session on antioxidant enzymes, lipid peroxidation products, oxidative status, and cytokines levels in the blood of male volleyball players before and after submaximal exercise.
Methods: The study involved 18 male professional volleyball players who underwent a single WBC session applied prior to cycloergometer exercise. Blood samples were collected five times: before WBC, immediately after WBC, after exercise preceded by cryotherapy (WBC exercise), and before and after exercise without WBC (control exercise). Antioxidant enzymes activity, lipid peroxidation products, total oxidative status, and cytokines levels were measured.
Results: The activity of catalase was significantly increased after control exercise, whereas the activity of catalase and superoxide dismutase was lower after WBC exercise than after control exercise (P < 0.001). Additionally, the level of IL-6 and IL-1β was lower after WBC exercise than after control exercise (P < 0.001).
Conclusion: The study suggests that WBC may have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, as evidenced by the increased activity of catalase and the lower levels of IL-6 and IL-1β after WBC exercise. These findings may indicate that reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a role in cytokines release into the blood system in response to exercise and WBC.

title: Incidence of childhood distal forearm fractures over 30 years: a population-based study.
text:
In this study, the incidence of distal forearm fractures among children in Rochester, Minnesota was investigated across four time periods spanning 1969-2001. The study population includes individuals younger than 35 years who sustained a distal forearm fracture in one of the four time periods. The main outcome measure is the estimated incidence of distal forearm fractures per 100,000 individuals per year, adjusted for age and sex.
The results show that the incidence of distal forearm fractures increased significantly over time, with an average annual increase of 32% among male residents and 56% among female residents. The peak incidence and greatest increase occurred between ages 11 and 14 years in boys and 8 and 11 years in girls. Compared to the incidence in 1969-1971, the incidence in 1999-2001 was 372.9 per 100,000, indicating a statistically significant increase.
The study suggests that the increase in distal forearm fractures may be due to changing patterns of physical activity or decreased bone acquisition due to poor calcium intake, but further research is needed to confirm these findings. The large number of childhood fractures highlights the importance of further investigating the causes of this increase and implementing strategies to prevent them.

title: Tolerance of whole-genome doubling propagates chromosomal instability and accelerates cancer genome evolution.
text:
The Impact of Whole-Genome Doubling on Colorectal Cancer Evolution: A Long-Term Culture Study
The contribution of whole-genome doubling to chromosomal instability (CIN) and tumor evolution has remained unclear. To investigate this phenomenon, we utilized long-term cultures of isogenic tetraploid cells from a stable diploid colon cancer progenitor. Our findings reveal that while tetraploid cells do not exhibit increased frequencies of structural or numerical CIN per chromosome, rare cells that survive genome doubling display increased tolerance to chromosome aberrations. This tolerant phenotype, combined with a doubling of chromosome aberrations per cell, allows chromosome abnormalities to evolve specifically in tetraploids, mirroring the genetic alterations observed in genomically complex colorectal tumors. Furthermore, our data demonstrate that a genome-doubling event is independently predictive of poor relapse-free survival in early-stage disease in two independent cohorts, suggesting an important role for genome tolerance in driving cancer evolution.
Our work sheds light on the crucial role of whole-genome doubling in colorectal cancer progression. We discovered that tetraploid cells undergo rapid genomic changes and recapitulate the genetic alterations seen in chromosomally unstable tumors. Unexpectedly, we also found that a genome-doubling event is prognostic of poor relapse-free survival in this disease type, highlighting its significance in cancer evolution. These findings have significant implications for our understanding of colorectal cancer development and progression.

title: Alzheimer’s Disease Risk Gene CD33 Inhibits Microglial Uptake of Amyloid Beta
text: The transmembrane protein CD33 functions as an immunoglobulin-like lectin that regulates innate immunity, but its role in the brain remains unknown. Recent studies have found that the CD33 gene is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD). In this study, we observed increased CD33 expression in microglial cells in AD brain, and in contrast to the majority allele, the minor allele of the CD33 SNP rs3865444, which confers protection against AD, was associated with decreased CD33 expression and Aβ42 levels in AD brain. Additionally, the number of CD33-positive microglia was found to positively correlate with Aβ42 levels and plaque burden in AD brain. In vitro studies revealed that CD33 inhibited the uptake and clearance of Aβ42 in microglial cell cultures. Finally, brain levels of insoluble Aβ42 and amyloid plaque burden were significantly reduced in APP(Swe)/PS1(ΔE9)/CD33(-/-) mice, suggesting that CD33 inhibition may be a promising therapeutic approach for AD.

title: Aluminum fluoride stimulates surface protrusions in cells overexpressing the ARF6 GTPase
text: To investigate the effector function of the ADP-ribosylation factor (ARF) 6 GTP-binding protein, we employed HeLa cells to transfect wild-type or epitope-tagged ARF6. Prior studies have implicated ARF6 in indirectly activating the ARF1 GTPase. Treating ARF6-transfected cells with aluminum fluoride (AIF) led to a redistribution of both ARF6 and actin to specific sites on the plasma membrane, which became more protrusive over time. The AIF-induced effects were specific to cells transfected with wild-type ARF6, reversible, and resembled the cellular protrusions observed in cells expressing a defective mutant of ARF6. In contrast to cells expressing RhoA or Rac1, which displayed enhanced stress fibers and membrane ruffles, the protrusions observed in ARF6-transfected cells were distinct. Within these protrusive structures, there was an apparent stimulation of macropinocytosis and membrane recycling. Unexpectedly, no block in transferrin uptake or alteration of the distribution of clathrin AP-2 complexes was detected in these cells. The AIF-induced, ARF6-dependent formation of protrusive structures was inhibited by cytochalasin D and lipoxygenase pathway inhibitors, supporting a novel role for ARF6 in shaping the plasma membrane and underlying cytoskeleton.

title: A longitudinal diffusion tensor imaging study assessing white matter fiber tracts after sports-related concussion.
text: The severity of structural damage in sports-related concussions (SRCs) plays a crucial role in determining the recovery period, long-term effects, and the decision to re-enter play. In our recent longitudinal study, we employed diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) to assess white matter (WM) fiber tract integrity at 2 days, 2 weeks, and 2 months following concussive injury. We compared right-handed male varsity contact-sport athletes (mean age: 20.2±1.0 years) with a medically diagnosed SRC (no loss of consciousness) to right-handed male varsity non-contact-sport athletes serving as controls (mean age: 19.9±1.7 years). Our findings revealed significantly elevated radial diffusivity (RD) in athletes with SRCs (n=12) compared to the control group at 2 days, which was pronounced in a specific cluster of right hemisphere voxels encompassing the posterior limb of the internal capsule (IC), the retrolenticular part of the IC, the inferior longitudinal fasciculus, the inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (sagittal stratum), and the anterior thalamic radiation. In contrast, fractional anisotropy (FA) within the same cluster showed a reversed, yet similar, pattern, with decreased FA at 2 days and 2 months post-injury compared to healthy controls. Unlike RD, there were no statistically significant differences between the concussed and control groups at 2 weeks post-injury. These findings support the hypothesis of elevated RD and decreased FA within 72 hours post-injury, followed by recovery that may extend beyond 2 weeks. Notably, RD appears to be a sensitive marker of concussive injury.

title: HIV–1 Infects Multipotent Progenitor Cells Causing Cell Death and Establishing Latent Cellular Reservoirs
text: HIV infection leads to a chronic state of immune depletion characterized by a decline in CD4(+) T lymphocytes, and it also predisposes individuals to opportunistic infections. Although drugs that block viral replication are available, HIV infection has proven challenging to cure due to the existence of unidentified reservoirs of infected cells that are resistant to highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) and the immune system. We used CD34(+) cells from infected individuals, as well as in vitro studies of wild-type HIV, to illustrate infection and killing of CD34(+) multipotent hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs). In some HPCs, we detected latent infection that persisted stably in cell culture until viral gene expression was activated by differentiation factors. A novel reporter HIV that directly detects latently infected cells in vitro confirmed the presence of distinct populations of active and latently infected HPCs. These findings have significant implications for understanding HIV-related bone marrow pathology and the mechanisms by which HIV causes persistent infection.

title: The human long non-coding RNA-RoR is a p53 repressor in response to DNA damage
text: It is widely understood that upon exposure to stress, the levels of the tumor suppressor p53 are significantly increased. However, despite extensive research, the underlying mechanism involving key players in stress-induced p53 regulation remains unclear. We have discovered that the human lincRNA-RoR (RoR) serves as a potent negative regulator of p53. Unlike MDM2, which promotes p53 degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, RoR inhibits p53 translation through direct interaction with the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein I (hnRNP I). Interestingly, a specific 28-base RoR sequence containing hnRNP I binding motifs is crucial and sufficient for p53 repression. Furthermore, we have shown that RoR inhibits p53-mediated cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Moreover, our findings indicate that RoR and p53 form a regulatory feedback loop, where p53 induces RoR expression through transcription. Together, these findings suggest that the RoR-hnRNP I-p53 axis may constitute an additional surveillance network, allowing cells to better respond to various stresses.

title: Experimental and clinical studies on lactate and pyruvate as indicators of the severity of acute circulatory failure (shock).
text:
Sure, here is a possible reconstruction of the given text:
Researchers investigated the changes in lactate (L) and pyruvate (P) levels in arterial blood during experimental and clinical shock states, and evaluated the extent to which these changes reflect oxygen deficit and irreversible injury. A standardized method for inducing hemorrhagic shock in Wistar rats was employed. During a 4-hour bleeding period, oxygen consumption was reduced to approximately 40% of normal levels, pH decreased from 7.39 to 7.08, and there were concurrent increases in L from 0.80 to 6.06 mm and in P from 0.07 to 0.18 mm. Cumulative oxygen debt was found to be significantly related to survival, with a correlation coefficient (r) of 0.50 and P < 0.0005. Similarly, correlation of cumulative oxygen debt and survival with both P and computed values of the lactate-to-pyruvate ratio (L/P) and excess lactate (XL) was of no higher magnitude. Using partial correlation analysis, it was also found that neither the measurement of P nor the computation of L/P or XL improved predictability.

title: Virtual microdissection identifies distinct tumor- and stroma-specific subtypes of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
text: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a deadly disease with a 5-year survival rate of only 4%. One of the major challenges in diagnosing and treating PDAC is the extensive involvement of stromal cells, which can make it difficult to capture precise tumor-specific molecular information. However, we have found a way to overcome this challenge by using blind source separation techniques on a diverse collection of PDAC gene expression microarray data, including data from primary tumor, metastatic, and normal samples. By separating tumor, stromal, and normal gene expression, we have identified and validated two tumor subtypes, including a 'basal-like' subtype that has a poorer prognosis and is molecularly similar to basal tumors in bladder and breast cancers. Additionally, we have defined 'normal' and 'activated' stromal subtypes, which are independent prognostic factors. Our findings provide new insights into the molecular composition of PDAC, which could be used to develop targeted therapies or make informed decisions in a clinical setting where treatment options are critical.

title: Inducible nitric oxide synthase in pulmonary alveolar macrophages from patients with tuberculosis
text: New research has revealed that high-output nitric oxide production in mice helps protect them from infection by various pathogens, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis. However, the ability of human mononuclear phagocytes to express the corresponding inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS;NOS2) has been disputed through studies of cells cultured from blood. The present study directly examined alveolar macrophages obtained through bronchopulmonary lavage to investigate whether human mononuclear phagocytes can express iNOS. The study found that an average of 65% of macrophages from 11 out of 11 patients with untreated, culture-positive pulmonary tuberculosis tested positive for NOS2 using an antibody proven to be monospecific for human NOS2. In contrast, only 10% of bronchoalveolar lavage cells were positive from each of five clinically normal subjects. Tuberculosis patients' macrophages demonstrated diaphorase activity in the same proportion as their staining for NOS2, under assay conditions where the diaphorase reaction was dependent on NOS2 expression. The study also found that bronchoalveolar lavage specimens contained NOS2 mRNA. Overall, the results suggest that macrophages in the lungs of people with clinically active Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection frequently express catalytically active NOS2.

title: The use of mouse models to understand and improve cognitive deficits in Down syndrome
text: In recent years, remarkable progress has been made in the development of therapeutics for cognitive impairment in individuals with Down syndrome (DS) through the use of mouse models. In this review, we briefly describe the phenotypes of mouse models that represent potential targets for drug testing, the behavioral tests used to assess impairments in cognition, and the known mechanisms of action of several drugs that are currently being investigated in preclinical studies or are likely to be tested in clinical trials. Notably, there are overlaps in the distribution of targets and the pathways affected by these diverse drugs in the trisomic brain, which suggest new avenues for DS research and drug development.

title: position-specific gap penalties
text:
Here is a possible revision of the given text:
The sensitivity of the traditional progressive multiple sequence alignment method has been significantly enhanced for the alignment of distantly related protein sequences. To achieve this, the following improvements are incorporated:
Firstly, individual weights are assigned to each sequence in a partial alignment to downgrade near-identical sequences and upgrade the most divergent ones. This allows the algorithm to better differentiate between highly similar sequences and those with greater genetic diversity.
Secondly, amino acid substitution matrices are adjusted at different stages of the alignment process based on the degree of sequence divergence. This ensures that the algorithm takes into account the differing evolutionary pressures acting on distinct sequences, leading to a more accurate alignment.
Thirdly, residue-specific gap penalties and locally reduced gap penalties are introduced in hydrophilic regions to encourage the formation of new gaps in potential loop regions rather than regular secondary structure. This enables the algorithm to better account for the flexible nature of certain protein structures and improve the overall accuracy of the alignment.
Fourthly, positions in early alignments where gaps have been introduced receive locally reduced gap penalties to encourage the opening up of new gaps at these locations. This facilitates the formation of more accurate alignments by allowing the algorithm to better explore the sequence space.
These modifications have been integrated into a new program, CLUSTAL W, which is freely available for use.

title: Pedestrian Detection via Periodic Motion Analysis
text: We present algorithms for detecting pedestrians in videos captured by infrared and color sensors. Two approaches are proposed, each based on the pedestrian's gait. The first approach utilizes computationally efficient periodicity measurements to estimate the periodic motion frequency of the pedestrian. This technique involves two cascading hypothesis testing steps to remove non-cyclic pixels, making it effective for both radial and lateral walking directions. The period extraction is robust against sensor noise and cluttered backgrounds. In contrast, the second approach converts the cyclic pattern into a binary sequence using Maximal Principal Gait Angle (MPGA) fitting. This method does not require alignment and continuously estimates the period using a Phase-locked Loop. Both methods are evaluated through experimental results that measure performance as a function of size, movement direction, frame rate, and sequence length.

title: Seroepidemiological survey of feline retrovirus infections in cats in Taiwan in 1993 and 1994.
text: To investigate the frequency of infections with three feline retroviruses - feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV), feline leukemia virus (FeLV), and feline syncytial virus (FSV) - in Taiwan, we collected 75 blood samples from cats from veterinary hospitals, a breeding cattery, and a homeless shelter in 1993 and 1994. We used indirect immunofluorescence and/or enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays to detect the presence of anti-FIV and FSV antibodies and FeLV-p27 antigen in these samples. We found that all of the serum samples positive for FIV were from homeless cats, and the overall FIV positive rate was 4%. The positive rates of FSV and FeLV were 28% and 1.3%, respectively. Comparing these results to those of previous seroepidemiological surveys conducted by other researchers, it appears that the prevalence of FIV and FeLV infections is lower in Taiwan than in the United States or Japan. On the other hand, the prevalence of FSV infection in Taiwan is comparable to that in Japan.

title: Notch targets and their regulation.
text:
Here is a possible reprise of the given text:
Activation of the Notch receptor triggers proteolytic cleavage, leading to the release of the Notch intracellular domain (NICD), which then enters the nucleus to regulate gene expression. Transcriptional changes are a primary result of this pathway, but the specific targets activated vary depending on the cell type. In this review, we explore current knowledge on Notch target genes, the mechanisms governing their transcriptional regulation, and the factors that contribute to the activation of distinct sets of targets in different cell types.

title: Extraction and Analysis of Multiple Periodic Motions in Video Sequences
text: The study of periodic or repetitive movements is pertinent in various contexts, including the identification and categorization of human and animal actions. Current methods for analyzing periodic motions entail extracting motion trajectories using spatial data and then determining if they are periodic. These approaches relying on feature matching or spatial correlation are often impractical, unreliable, or computationally taxing. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages time-frequency analysis of the entire video sequence to identify multiple periodic trajectories and estimate their periods simultaneously. The objects exhibiting periodic movement are identified using spatial domain information. We validate the effectiveness of this approach through experiments using synthetic and real sequences.

title: MicroRNA-21 is up-regulated in allergic airway inflammation and regulates IL-12p35 expression.
text: The expression of microRNAs (miRNAs) is altered in the lungs of individuals with allergic airway inflammation, a condition characterized by an overactive immune response to environmental allergens. Despite this, the role of miRNAs in this process has yet to be explored. To address this gap in knowledge, we employed a sensitive microarray-based approach to identify miRNAs that are differentially expressed between mice with allergic airway inflammation and those without the condition. Our study revealed the overexpression of miR-21 and underexpression of miR-1 in mice with allergic airway inflammation compared to control mice. These findings were independently confirmed in two additional models of allergic airway inflammation and in mice with IL-4-driven lung transgenes. We found that IL-13-induced miR-21 expression is dependent on the IL-13Ralpha1 receptor, while allergen-induced miR-21 expression is independent of this receptor and STAT6. Additionally, our predictive algorithms identified potential direct targets of miR-21 among IL-13-regulated lung transcripts, such as IL-12p35 mRNA, which is decreased in mice with allergic airway inflammation. Introduction of pre-miR-21 inhibited the expression of a reporter vector containing the 3'-untranslated region of IL-12p35, and mutating miR-21 binding sites in the IL-12p35 3'-untranslated region abrogated this inhibition. In summary, our study has uncovered a miRNA signature associated with allergic airway inflammation, including miR-21, which modulates the expression of IL-12, a factor crucial for Th cell polarization.

title: COPD: epidemiology, prevalence, morbidity and mortality, and disease heterogeneity.
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) poses a significant health and economic burden both in the United States and globally. Some well-established risk factors for COPD include smoking, occupational exposures, air pollution, airway hyperresponsiveness, asthma, and certain genetic variations. However, there are still many unanswered questions about COPD, such as why only a minority of smokers develop severe airway obstruction. The definition of COPD can vary depending on the specific diagnosis made by a physician, which can lead to differences in estimates of the disease prevalence in the population. As evidence emerges that COPD is a complex condition with multiple underlying disease processes, it becomes clear that a comprehensive approach involving smoking cessation and prevention, COPD education and early detection, and improved treatment options is essential in the fight against this major cause of morbidity and mortality. Unfortunately, COPD prevalence and mortality continue to increase globally, particularly due to the rise in smoking among women and adolescents. Addressing these trends will require a sustained effort to address the root causes of the disease.

title: Changing geographic ranges of ticks and tick-borne pathogens: drivers, mechanisms and consequences for pathogen diversity
text: The geographical distributions of ticks and tick-borne pathogens are shifting due to global and local environmental changes (including climatic variations). In this review, we investigate the factors driving changes in the ranges of tick and tick-borne pathogen species and strains, with a focus on their basic reproduction number (R0) and the mechanisms of dispersal that enable ticks and tick-borne pathogens to invade suitable habitats. By using the expanding geographic range of Lyme disease vectors and agents as an example, we explore what can be expected in terms of diversity shifts among tick-borne pathogens during range expansion. We also examine how historical population and range expansions and contractions might be reflected in the phylogeography of ticks and tick-borne pathogens observed in recent years and conclude that combining current changes in tick and tick-borne pathogen ranges with phylogeographic analysis can help predict future patterns of invasion and diversity.

title: Mutant KRAS is a druggable target for pancreatic cancer.
text:
Presenting a novel approach to target the KRAS oncogene in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA), we propose using RNA interference (RNAi) technology. To tackle this unmet clinical challenge, we have developed a local prolonged siRNA delivery system (Local Drug EluteR, LODER), with siRNA molecules specifically targeting the mutated KRAS (siG12D LODER). The safety and efficacy of LODER were evaluated in vitro and in vivo, demonstrating its potential to silence KRAS and inhibit tumor growth.
* A stable and active LODER delivery platform was established in vitro for 155 days, consistent with the projected duration of therapeutic application.
* Treatment of PDA cells with siG12D LODER resulted in a significant decrease in KRAS levels, leading to curtailed proliferation and hindered epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
* Local administration of siG12D LODER inhibited the growth of human pancreatic tumors in vivo and extended the survival of mice.
This research offers several advantages:
* Protection of siRNA from degradation through the miniature biodegradable polymeric matrix of LODER
* Gradual release of siRNA within the tumor over an extended period, thereby maximizing therapeutic efficacy.
* Delivery of siG12D LODER that effectively silences mutated KRAS, proving its druggability and potential as a therapeutic target.
In summary, our proposed method leverages RNAi technology to tackle the cancer challenge posed by mutated KRAS in PDA. By developing a safe and efficient delivery platform, we demonstrate the feasibility of targeting this previously untargetable oncogene, setting the stage for potential clinical applications.

title: Trimmomatic: a flexible trimmer for Illumina sequence data
text:
MOTIVATION: Although numerous next-generation sequencing (NGS) read preprocessing tools already existed, we discovered a need for a more versatile and effective tool that could handle paired-end data with high performance. To address this gap, we developed Trimmomatic, a user-friendly and efficient preprocessing tool that excels in handling paired-end data.
RESULTS: Our evaluation of Trimmomatic demonstrated its utility in both reference-based and reference-free tasks. The tool produced output that was either competitive or superior to that of other popular tools in all scenarios tested.
AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Trimmomatic is licensed under GPL V3. It is a cross-platform tool that requires Java 1.5+, and is freely available for download from our website at [http://www.usadellab.org/cms/index.php?page=trimmomatic](http://www.usadellab.org/cms/index.php?page=trimmomatic). For further inquiries, please contact us at [usadel@bio1.rwth-aachen.de](mailto:usadel@bio1.rwth-aachen.de).
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Additional data are available in the online version of this article at [Bioinformatics online](http://dx.doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btn050).

title: Basics of PD-1 in self-tolerance, infection, and cancer immunity
text: Successful cancer treatment depends on an in-depth comprehension of the host immune response to tumor cells. PD-1, a member of the CD28 superfamily of receptors, acts as a "brake" on immune activation to prevent autoimmunity and excessive tissue damage during infection.
