AGEs enhanced the expression of IL-1, TNF-α, and MMP-13, but decreased PPARγ expression in a time- and dose-dependent manner, which was inhibited by anti-RAGE, SB203580 (p38 MAPK specific inhibitor), and SP600125 (selective inhibitor of JNK). PPARγ agonist pioglitazone could inhibit the effects of AGEs-induced inflammatory response and PPARγ down-regulation. In human chondrocytes, AGEs induced cytosol IκBα degradation and increased the level of nuclear NF-κB p65, which was inhibited by PPARγ agonist pioglitazone.

Conclusions:
In primary human chondrocytes, AGEs down-regulated PPARγ expression and increased inflammatory mediators, which could be reversed by PPARγ agonist pioglitazone. Activation of RAGE by AGEs triggers a cascade of downstream signaling, including MAPK JNK/p38, PPARγ, and NF-κB. Therefore, PPARγ could be a potential target for pharmacologic intervention in the treatment of OA.

title: Surgical versus medical treatment with cyclooxygenase inhibitors for symptomatic patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants.
text: Background: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in preterm infants can lead to increased morbidity and mortality. Early closure of the ductus arteriosus can be achieved through pharmacological interventions using cyclooxygenase inhibitors or surgical ligation. While both treatment modalities have shown efficacy, there is no consensus on the preferred initial treatment approach for symptomatic PDA in preterm infants. Objectives: To compare the effectiveness of surgical ligation versus medical treatment with cyclooxygenase inhibitors (using indomethacin, ibuprofen, or mefenamic acid) as initial treatments for symptomatic PDA in preterm infants. Methods: A systematic search was conducted across electronic databases, including Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, CINAHL, EMBASE, and hand searches of abstracts from Pediatric Academic Societies annual meetings. Randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trials in preterm infants < 37 weeks gestational age or low-birth-weight infants (< 2500 grams) with symptomatic PDA in the neonatal period (< 28 days) were included. Results: Only one study, trial B in the report by Gersony (1983), was found eligible. The study compared the effectiveness of surgical ligation versus medical treatment with indomethacin in 154 infants. The results showed no statistically significant difference between the two groups in mortality during hospital stay, chronic lung disease, other bleeding, necrotizing enterocolitis, sepsis, creatinine level, or intraventricular hemorrhage. However, there was a statistically significant increase in the surgical group in incidence of pneumothorax (RR 2.68, 95% CI 1.45, 4.93) and retinopathy of prematurity stage III and IV (RR 3.80, 95% CI 1.12, 12.93). Conclusion: The data on the net benefit/harm of surgical ligation versus medical treatment with cyclooxygenase inhibitors as initial treatments for symptomatic PDA in preterm infants are insufficient to make a conclusion. It is noted that recent observational studies have suggested an increased risk for certain adverse outcomes associated with PDA ligation, such as chronic lung disease, retinopathy of prematurity, and neurosensory impairment. The duration of the "waiting-time" and transport to another facility with surgical capacity may also affect outcomes. Further research is needed to determine the most appropriate initial treatment approach for symptomatic PDA in preterm infants.

title: The Effect of Collinearity on Parameter Estimates in Nonlinear Mixed Effect Models
text: Purpose: To investigate the impact of correlations among predictor variables in a population pharmacokinetic model on the accuracy and precision of parameter estimates. Methods: Monte Carlo simulation was used to generate concentration-time data similar to a Phase III clinical trial, with two covariates affecting the drugs' pharmacokinetics. Five data sets with increasing correlation between the covariates were created and analyzed using NONMEM, both with and without inclusion of the covariates in the structural pharmacokinetic model. Summary measures for ill-conditioning and sensitivity analysis were employed to evaluate how correlations among predictor variables affect the accuracy and precision of parameter estimates. Results: As the correlation between covariates increased, the standard error of parameter estimates grew, and the estimated parameters became increasingly biased. For a correlation coefficient of 0.75, the standard errors were too large to declare statistical significance. Conclusions: Correlations among predictor variables exceeding 0.5 when included in the model simultaneously should serve as a warning to researchers, as both the accuracy of parameter estimates and the precision of estimates may be compromised due to ill-conditioning, resulting in biased estimates and inflated precision.

title: An analysis of age and gender influences on the relative risk for suicide and psychotropic drug self-poisoning.
text:
The study aimed to investigate the relationship between psychotropic drug prescriptions and suicide risk among different age and gender groups. Data was collected from the Australian census and studies of general practitioner prescribing, as well as patients who attempted or completed suicide through self-poisoning within a defined geographic area. The study found that:
1. Psychiatric illness is a significant risk factor for both attempted and completed suicide, and psychotropic medications account for 80% of all drug overdoses involving prescription medications.
2. The odds ratios for self-poisoning were higher for those aged less than 45 years, but this group was least likely to be prescribed psychotropic drugs.
3. Men had a much higher rate of completed suicide using more lethal methods.
4. The odds ratios for self-poisoning and suicide with psychotropic drugs, after correction for prescription rates, were 11.1 and 1.7, respectively, for those aged 15 to 24 years.
5. Those aged 25 to 44 years had ORs of 4.9 and 4.3, and, by contrast, those over 75 years had ORs of 0.03 and 0.
6. Women were slightly more likely to poison themselves with psychotropic drugs (OR 1.2), but the situation reversed after correction for prescription rates (OR 0.69).

Based on these findings, the study concluded that:

1. Greater caution should be exercised in prescribing psychotropic drugs for individuals under the age of 45, as they are at a higher risk of drug overdose.
2. The least toxic compounds should be used, especially for this age group.
3. The risk of self-poisoning among the elderly may have been overstated, so some patients may have been denied adequate treatment.

In summary, the study highlighted the importance of balancing the benefits and risks of psychotropic drug prescriptions, particularly among different age and gender groups. By correcting for prescription rates, the study established that individuals under 45 years of age are at a higher risk of suicide through psychotropic drug overdose, while the elderly may have been overstated, resulting in inadequate treatment for some patients.

title: Cell death and immune privilege.
text: The host's response to pathogens involves intricate inflammatory processes and immune reactions, which are crucial for defending against infections and restoring health. However, these responses can sometimes result in damage to surrounding tissue, which is generally reversible. Yet, there are specific areas in the body where inflammation can pose a significant risk to organ function, such as the eye, brain, and reproductive organs (testes and ovaries). In these sensitive areas, immune responses are either compromised or function differently, making them "immunologically privileged." In these areas, a properly functioning immune response can actually contribute to disease.

title: Niche-Independent Symmetrical Self-Renewal of a Mammalian Tissue Stem Cell
text: Mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells multiply symmetrically in monoculture, but in vivo, stem cells rely on specialized microenvironments and undergo predominantly asymmetric divisions. Expanding pure populations of tissue stem cells ex vivo has proven challenging, and neural progenitor cells are often propagated in combination with differentiating progeny in floating clusters called neurospheres. However, stem cells in neurospheres are difficult to observe or manipulate directly. We demonstrate that the complex neurosphere environment is dispensable for stem cell maintenance, and that the combination of fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF-2) and epidermal growth factor (EGF) is sufficient for the symmetrical division of pure cultures of neural stem (NS) cells. NS cells were derived from mouse ES cells and induced to differentiate into neural lineages. In the presence of EGF and FGF-2, resulting NS cells proliferate continuously, are diploid, and clonogenic. After prolonged expansion, they retain the ability to differentiate into neurons and astrocytes in vitro and in vivo. Colonies generated from single NS cells all produce neurons upon growth factor withdrawal, and NS cells exhibit morphological, cell biological, and molecular features of radial glia, developmental precursors of neurons and glia. Adherent NS cell lines can be established from fetal mouse brain, and similar NS cells can be generated from human ES cells and human fetal brain. The extrinsic factors EGF plus FGF-2 are sufficient to sustain pure, symmetrical self-renewing divisions of NS cells, resulting in the first known example of tissue-specific stem cells that can be propagated without accompanying differentiation. These homogeneous cultures will enable the delineation of molecular mechanisms that define a tissue-specific stem cell and allow direct comparison with pluripotent ES cells.

title: A Bivalent Chromatin Structure Marks Key Developmental Genes in Embryonic Stem Cells
text: The most highly conserved non-coding elements (HCNEs) in mammalian genomes are found in regions enriched for genes encoding transcription factors (TFs) involved in development. This suggests that these regions may harbor crucial regulatory controls that govern development. To investigate, we examined histone methylation in mouse embryonic stem cells across 56 large HCNE-rich regions. We identified a distinct modification pattern, termed "bivalent domains," characterized by large areas of H3 lysine 27 methylation with smaller regions of H3 lysine 4 methylation. Bivalent domains often overlap with TF genes expressed at low levels. We propose that bivalent domains silence developmental genes in ES cells by maintaining them in a poised state, ready for activation. Additionally, we found striking similarities between the genome sequence and histone methylation patterns in ES cells, which become less pronounced in differentiated cells. These findings highlight the importance of DNA sequence in shaping the initial epigenetic landscape and suggest a novel chromatin-based mechanism for maintaining pluripotency.

title: Ovarian Surface Epithelium in Patients with Severe Ovarian Infertility: A Potential Source of Cells Expressing Markers of Pluripotent/Multipotent Stem Cells
text: The focus of this investigation was to determine whether stem cells exist in the ovarian surface epithelium of patients experiencing premature ovarian failure and lacking mature follicles and oocytes. Upon examining the epithelial cells collected from the ovarian surface after scraping, small, unidentified cells expressing the SOX-2 marker of pluripotency were noticed among the epithelial cells. These cells were found to be an integral part of the ovarian surface epithelium. When the scraped cells were cultured in a medium supplemented with ovarian niche factors, primitive oocyte-like cells and typical round-shaped cell clusters exhibited alkaline phosphatase staining, and markers of pluripotency, such as SOX-2 and SSEA-4, were expressed early and persistently. Additionally, single oocyte-like cells displayed genes characteristic of pluripotent stem cells, including OCT4A, SOX-2, NANOG, NANOS, STELLA, CD9, LIN28, KLF4, GDF3, and MYC. The findings of this study confirm the presence of suspected stem cells in the ovarian surface epithelium of these patients and provide a foundation for establishing a stem cell line in the future.

title: Structural Homeostasis: Compensatory Adjustments of Dendritic Arbor Geometry in Response to Variations of Synaptic Input
text: As the nervous system develops, there is inherent variability in the connections formed between differentiating neurons. However, functional and remarkably robust neural circuits form despite this variability. One mechanism neurons employ to handle input variability is through homeostatic changes in electrical properties. We investigate the development of dendrites in a specific central neuron (aCC) in the late Drosophila embryo, when it first receives connections and becomes electrically active. At the same time, we track the distribution of presynaptic sites on the developing postsynaptic arbor. Genetic manipulations of presynaptic partners reveal that the postsynaptic dendritic arbor adjusts its growth to compensate for changes in synaptic activity and density. Blocking neurotransmitter synthesis or evoked release results in increased dendritic extension, while an increase in presynaptic release sites leads to a reduction in dendritic arbor size. These growth adjustments occur locally within the arbor and are mediated by the postsynaptic activity state of protein kinase A, which modifies dendritic growth in response to synaptic activity. These findings suggest that the dendritic arbor acts as a homeostatic device, adjusting its size and geometry in response to input variations to ensure appropriate input is received.

title: Nutrition and physical activity guidelines for cancer survivors.
text: Cancer survivors are frequently eager to gather knowledge on nutrition, exercise, and dietary supplements to optimize their treatment outcomes, quality of life, and overall survival. In response, the American Cancer Society (ACS) convened a team of experts in nutrition, physical activity, and cancer survivorship to evaluate the scientific evidence and clinical best practices regarding optimal nutrition and physical activity after a cancer diagnosis. This report consolidates their findings and aims to provide healthcare providers with the most comprehensive information to help cancer survivors and their families make informed decisions regarding nutrition and exercise. The report provides detailed guidelines for nutrition and physical activity during the various stages of cancer care, highlighting critical issues during treatment and for patients with advanced cancer, but primarily focusing on the unique needs of those who are disease-free or have stable disease following treatment. Additionally, the report covers key nutrition and physical activity topics such as body weight, food choices, food safety, and dietary supplements; specific issues related to various cancer sites; and frequently asked questions about diet, exercise, and cancer survivorship.

title: The role of protein clearance mechanisms in organismal ageing and age-related diseases.
text: As we age, our body's ability to maintain a functional proteome, or proteostasis, declines. This leads to the accumulation of damaged and misfolded proteins, which can disrupt cell function and tissue homeostasis. The buildup of these damaged proteins has been linked to various age-related diseases, such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and Huntington's disease. Fortunately, there are mechanisms in place to remove these damaged proteins, such as the ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy-lysosome pathways, which are crucial components of the proteostasis network. Research has shown that modulating either proteasome activity or autophagic-lysosomal potential can extend lifespan and protect against the symptoms associated with proteostasis disorders, suggesting that these protein clearance mechanisms are directly linked to aging and age-related diseases.

title: A distinctive DNA damage response in human hematopoietic stem cells reveals an apoptosis-independent role for p53 in self-renewal.
text: Highly regenerative tissues, such as blood, demand effective DNA damage responses (DDR) that balance long-term regeneration with protection from malignant transformation. Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), which are responsible for life-long blood production, have remained largely unexplored in terms of their response to DNA damage. Our investigation uncovered that human HSCs exhibit delayed DNA double-strand break rejoining, persistent gammaH2AX foci, and enhanced p53- and ASPP1-dependent apoptosis following exposure to gamma-radiation, compared to progenitors. By inhibiting p53 or overexpressing Bcl-2, we found that radiation-induced apoptosis can be reduced, yet only Bcl-2 overexpression maintained in vivo repopulating HSC function. Remarkably, despite similar resistance to irradiation-induced apoptosis, only Bcl-2-overexpressing HSCs displayed heightened self-renewal capacity, which we found to be independently associated with intact p53 function. The diminished self-renewal of HSCs with inactivated p53 was linked to an increase in spontaneous gammaH2AX foci in secondary transplants of HSCs. Our findings shed light on the multipurpose nature of p53, revealing both its role in regulating apoptosis and its crucial function in preventing the accumulation of gammaH2AX foci during HSC self-renewal.

title: Behavioral characterization of neuropeptide Y knockout mice.
text: An in-depth characterization of behavior was conducted in mice lacking the gene for neuropeptide Y (NPY). This included assessing their response to fasting for 24 and 48 hours and challenging them with small molecule antagonists of NPY receptors, which are involved in mediating the feeding effects of NPY. In addition, wildtype (WT) and NPY knockout (KO) mice were tested in various behavioral assays, including locomotor monitors, elevated plus maze, inhibitory avoidance, acoustic startle, prepulse inhibition, and hot plate assays. One key finding was that the NPY KO mice had lower food intake compared to WT controls during fasting. Additionally, the study suggests that the NPY KO mice may exhibit an anxiogenic-like phenotype and were found to be hypoalgesic in the hot plate paradigm. These findings further support the involvement of NPY in energy balance, anxiety, and possibly nociception.

title: Epigenetic-induced repression of microRNA-205 is associated with MED1 activation and a poorer prognosis in localized prostate cancer
text: Deregulation of microRNA (miRNA) expression has a crucial role in carcinogenesis, and our study on prostate cancer shows that miRNA-205 (miR-205) transcription is commonly repressed, and the MIR-205 locus is hypermethylated. The host gene LOC642587, which is located nearby the MIR-205 gene, is also inactivated. We discovered that miR-205 targets the transcription factor mediator 1 (MED1, also known as TRAP220 and PPARBP) for silencing in normal prostate cells, resulting in decreased MED1 mRNA and protein levels. Overexpression of miR-205 in prostate cancer cells leads to a decrease in cell viability, suggesting a tumor suppressor function. Our findings also show that the hypermethylation of the MIR-205 locus is strongly related to a decrease in miR-205 expression and an increase in MED1 expression in primary tumor samples (n=14), when compared to matched normal prostate tissues (n=7). An expanded patient cohort (tumor n=149, matched normal n=30) revealed significant MIR-205 DNA methylation in tumors compared to normal tissues, and MIR-205 hypermethylation was significantly associated with biochemical recurrence (hazard ratio=2.005, 95% confidence interval (1.109, 3.625), P=0.02) in patients with low preoperative prostate specific antigen. In conclusion, these results suggest that miR-205 is an epigenetically regulated tumor suppressor that targets MED1 and may serve as a potential biomarker for prostate cancer management.

title: Th2 cytokine response in Major Depressive Disorder patients before treatment
text: In Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), the interplay between the neuroendocrine and immune systems is disrupted. Our research focused on the equilibrium between pro-inflammatory Th1 cytokines and anti-inflammatory Th2 cytokines in MDD patients and non-depressed controls. Our findings revealed elevated levels of cortisol and TNF-alpha in MDD subjects, accompanied by increased proportions of CD3+CD8+ and NK cells, reduced B cell counts, and minimal variations in CD3+CD4+ lymphocyte counts. Moreover, significant increases in IL-4 and IL-13 (Th2 cytokines) and decreased levels of IL-2 and IFN-gamma (Th1 cytokines) were observed in the MDD group. In essence, we suggest that these changes may be directly linked to the elevated cortisol levels observed in MDD patients. Further investigations are necessary to delve deeper into these findings and their potential implications for future therapeutic approaches in managing MDD.

title: CDD: conserved domains and protein three-dimensional structure
text: CDD, part of NCBI's Entrez query and retrieval system, is also accessible via http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Structure/cdd/cdd.shtml. CDD provides annotation of protein sequences with information on the location of conserved domain footprints and functional sites, derived from these footprints. Annotations are available through Entrez, and interactive search services can accept single protein or nucleotide queries, as well as batch submissions of protein query sequences, using RPS-BLAST to rapidly identify potential matches. CDD utilizes various protein domain and full-length protein model collections and maintains a dedicated curation effort to provide detailed classifications for well-characterized protein domain families, supported by available 3D structure data and the scientific literature. To date, CDD has compiled the majority of protein 3D structures, which are tracked by the database, and CDD curators continue to characterize emerging novel families through protein structure determination efforts.

title: Extensive diversity of Ig-superfamily proteins in the immune system of insects.
text: The high degree of molecular diversification in immune receptors is a distinctive feature of advanced vertebrates. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether this diversity contributes to immune defense in invertebrates. Our findings indicate that immune cells in Drosophila possess the potential to generate over 18,000 variations of the Ig-superfamily receptor Down syndrome cell adhesion molecule (Dscam). We detected secreted isoforms of Dscam in the hemolymph, and a loss of Dscam in hemocytes reduced the efficiency of bacterial phagocytosis, likely due to decreased bacterial binding. Most notably, the extensive diversity of Dscam transcripts generated through a mechanism of alternative splicing is surprisingly conserved across major insect orders, suggesting an unanticipated degree of molecular complexity in the innate immune system of insects.

title: Preparing the outbreak assistance laboratory network in the Netherlands for the detection of the influenza virus A(H1N1) variant.
text:
In April 2009, as the H1N1 variant influenza virus emerged in the Northern Americas, posing a potential threat of becoming the next pandemic virus, the objective of this study was to prepare laboratories in the Netherlands for surge capacity in molecular diagnosis of patients suspected of H1N1 infection. A panel of 10 blinded specimens containing various influenza viruses, including seasonal H1N1 and H3N2, as well as the novel H1N1 virus from the Netherlands (A/Netherlands/602/2009(H1N1)v), or negative control, were distributed to outbreak assistance laboratories (OAL) along with specific primers and probes for H1N1 virus detection using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The laboratories were then asked to implement and test this protocol.
The results showed that all OAL were able to detect H1N1 virus using the CDC M-gene reagents, with similar sensitivity as in-house M-gene based assays. In contrast, real-time RT-PCRs used in routine diagnostic settings in the OAL specifically designed to detect H1, H3, or NS1 from seasonal influenza A viruses, did not or showed very low cross-reactivity with H1N1 virus. The CDC swine NP-gene and H1v-gene RT-PCRs showed somewhat reduced sensitivity compared to the CDC and in-house M-gene RT-PCRs. However, in-house developed H1N1 specific H1v-gene and N1v-gene RT-PCRs showed equal sensitivity to CDC and in-house M-gene RT-PCRs.
The study concluded that the Dutch OAL are prepared for detection and specific identification of H1N1, although some level of cross-reactivity was observed with seasonal influenza viruses. Additionally, M-gene based generic influenza A virus detection is recommended to be able to detect emerging influenza A viruses in routine settings.

title: Averting Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in India through Sugar-Sweetened Beverage Taxation: An Economic-Epidemiologic Modeling Study
text: Taxing sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs) in high-income countries has been proposed to reduce obesity and type 2 diabetes. To estimate the potential health effects of this fiscal strategy in India, a middle-income country with heterogeneous SSB consumption patterns, we used a nationally representative survey of 100,855 Indian households to analyze the impact of changed SSB prices on per capita consumption and substitution with other beverages. We incorporated sales trends, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes incidence data stratified by age, sex, income, and urban/rural residence into a validated microsimulation model that estimates caloric consumption, glycemic load, overweight/obesity prevalence, and type 2 diabetes incidence among Indian subpopulations facing a 20% SSB excise tax. We found that a 20% SSB tax would reduce overweight and obesity prevalence by 3.0% (95% CI 1.6%-5.9%) and type 2 diabetes incidence by 1.6% (95% CI 1.2%-1.9%) among various Indian subpopulations over the period 2014-2023, assuming SSB consumption continues to increase linearly in accordance with secular trends. However, if SSB consumption accelerates in line with industry marketing models, the impact of taxation could be even greater, avertising 4.2% (95% CI 2.5-10.0%) of prevalent overweight/obesity and 2.5% (95% CI 1.0-2.8%) of incident type 2 diabetes from 2014-2023. Our findings suggest that the largest relative effect of SSB taxation would be among young rural men, contradicting our initial hypothesis that urban populations would be the primary beneficiaries of SSB taxation. However, there are some limitations to our analysis, including the assumption that consumer behavior will remain constant in future years and potential underreporting of consumption in dietary recall data used to inform our calculations. In conclusion, sustained SSB taxation at a high rate could mitigate the rising obesity and type 2 diabetes epidemic in India among both urban and rural populations.

title: Acute myopericarditis after multiple vaccinations in an adolescent: case report and review of the literature.
text: We present a case of post-vaccination acute myopericarditis in an adolescent. The patient experienced sudden chest pain, along with diffuse ST-segment elevation and elevated cardiac enzyme levels. A cardiac MRI revealed acute myocarditis, and the patient recovered completely within a few days after receiving non-steroidal anti-inflammatory treatment. Furthermore, we reviewed post-vaccination cases of myopericarditis from the pediatric literature, revealing a similar clinical profile in these cases.

title: Cardiovascular protection with antihypertensive drugs in dialysis patients: systematic review and meta-analysis.
text: Epidemiological studies have shown that lower blood pressure and a gradual decrease in blood pressure over time are associated with higher mortality in individuals undergoing dialysis. However, randomized, controlled trials lack the power to establish the benefits of antihypertensive therapy in these patients. In this meta-analysis, we evaluated the effectiveness of antihypertensive drug therapy in patients on long-term dialysis, using data from five randomized, controlled trials. Our results indicate that the overall benefit of antihypertensive therapy compared to the control or placebo group had a combined hazard ratio for cardiovascular events of 0.69 (95% CI: 0.56 to 0.84) using a fixed-effects model and 0.62 (95% CI: 0.45 to 0.86) using a random-effects model. When we performed a sensitivity analysis and included normotensives in the trial, the cardiovascular protection observed in the hypertensive group was significantly reduced (pooled hazard ratio of 0.86 [95% CI: 0.67 to 1.12]). Furthermore, there was evidence of publication bias based on Egger's test and funnel plot. While randomized trials suggest a benefit of antihypertensive therapy in hemodialysis patients, adequately powered randomized trials are necessary to confirm these findings, particularly among hypertensive patients.

title: Protoplasmic astrocytes in CA1 stratum radiatum occupy separate anatomical domains.
text:
Astrocytes, which are increasingly recognized as playing a crucial role in brain function, are thought to interact extensively with neuronal elements in the central nervous system (CNS). Recent research has revealed that various forms of these cells may exist in the CNS, physiologically and possibly functionally. However, our current understanding of astrocyte morphology and distribution is based primarily on studies that use the astrocytic marker glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and metal-impregnation techniques, which have limitations for visualizing the complex interactions among these cells.
Using intracellular injection combined with immunohistochemistry for GFAP, our study found that GFAP delineates only approximately 15% of the total volume of the astrocyte, leading to incorrect conclusions about the interactions between processes of neighboring astrocytes. To investigate these interactions in detail, we injected groups of adjacent protoplasmic astrocytes in the CA1 stratum radiatum with fluorescent intracellular tracers of distinctive emissive wavelengths and analyzed them using three-dimensional (3D) confocal analysis and electron microscopy. Our findings show that protoplasmic astrocytes establish primarily exclusive territories, revealing the importance of understanding how the complex morphology of these cells affects their 3D relationships with other astrocytes, oligodendroglia, neurons, and vasculature of the brain. This knowledge is crucial for our comprehension of nervous system function.

title: Leptin-receptor-expressing mesenchymal stromal cells represent the main source of bone formed by adult bone marrow.
text: Research on the identity and function of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) has been hindered by a lack of markers that allow for both prospective identification and fate mapping in living organisms. However, we have discovered that Leptin Receptor (LepR) is a marker that selectively identifies bone marrow MSCs. Our findings show that approximately 0.3% of bone marrow cells are LepR-positive, and within this population, around 10% are colony-forming unit-fibroblastic (CFU-F) cells, accounting for 94% of bone marrow CFU-Fs. LepR-positive cells are capable of forming bone, cartilage, and adipocytes in culture and when transplanted into living organisms. These cells are also positive for other markers, including Scf-GFP, Cxcl12-DsRed, and Nestin-GFP, which highly enrich CFU-Fs. In contrast, LepR-positive cells are negative for Nestin-CreER and NG2-CreER, markers that are unlikely to be found in CFU-Fs. Fate-mapping experiments revealed that LepR-positive cells arise postnatally and give rise to the majority of bone and adipocytes formed in adult bone marrow, including bone regenerated after irradiation or fracture. Notably, LepR-positive cells are quiescent but can proliferate after injury. Overall, our findings suggest that LepR-positive cells are the main source of bone and adipocytes in adult bone marrow.

title: High-resolution sperm typing of meiotic recombination in the mouse MHC Ebeta gene.
text: By analyzing mouse pedigrrees for meiotic crossovers in the Major Histocompability Complex (MHC), we identified hotspots that we then investigated in high-resolution sperm crossover analysis of the class II E(beta) gene. Our results confirm the presence of a highly localized hotspot approximately 1.0-1.6 kilobase pairs (kbp) wide in the second intron of E(beta) and demonstrate that it is flanked by virtually completely non-recombinant DNA. Heterzygous mice for different MHC haplotypes exhibit distinct patterns of recombination across the hotspot, with the same hotspot observed in all crosses examined, regardless of the degree of genetic divergence between haplotypes. Recombination events in opposing orientations occur at similar frequencies but display different distributional patterns within the hotspot, resulting in preferential gene conversion from non-initiating haplotypes. This observed asymmetry supports the double-strand break repair model of recombination, with haplotype s serving as the predominant crossover initiator. Our findings are strikingly similar to those observed in human hotspots, highlighting the conservation of hotspot structure and function across species.

title: Long-term survival of beta thalassemia major patients treated with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation compared with survival with conventional treatment.
text: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in thalassemia remains a challenging treatment option. In a single-center case-control study of 516 children and adult patients, 258 patients (67% of the total) underwent HSCT from a sibling or unrelated donor, while 97 patients were adults (age ≥ 16 years). The median follow-up after HSCT was 11 years (range 1-30 years). The conditioning regimen consisted of busulfan (80.6%) or treosulfan-based (19.4%). A cohort of 258 age-sex matched conventionally treated (CT) patients was randomly selected. The 30-year overall survival (OS) and thalassemia-free survival (TFS) in transplanted patients were 82.6 ± 2.7% and 77.8 ± 2.9%, respectively, which were comparable to the OS of 85.3 ± 2.7% in CT patients (P = NS). The incidence of grade II-IV acute and chronic graft versus host disease (GvHD) was 23.6% and 12.9%, respectively. The probability of rejection was 6.9%. Transplant-related mortality (TRM) was similar to the probability of dying of cardiovascular events in CT patients (13.8%). A high-risk Pesaro score (class 3) was associated with lower OS (odds ratio [OR] = 1.99, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.31-3.03) and TFS (OR = 1.54, 95% CI = 1.12-2.12). In adult patients, the 23-year OS and TFS after HSCT were 70 ± 5% and 67.3 ± 5%, respectively, which were comparable to the OS of 71.2 ± 5% in CT patients (P = NS). Treosulfan was associated with a lower risk of acute GvHD (P = 0.004; OR = 0.28, 95% CI = 0.12-0.67). In conclusion, the 30-year survival rate of ex-thalassemia patients after HSCT was similar to that expected in CT thalassemia patients, with the vast majority of HSCT survivors cured from thalassemia.

title: Global analysis of ATM polymorphism reveals significant functional constraint.
text: In this study, we investigate the genetic variation in the ATM gene, which is associated with ataxia-telangiectasia, a rare genetic disorder characterized by cerebellar degeneration, abnormal blood vessel growth, and cancer. To identify sequence variations in the ATM gene, we analyzed the protein-coding exons and adjacent non-coding regions in 93 individuals from seven human populations. We also compared the ATM gene to 14 other autosomal genes in terms of nucleotide diversity. Our findings revealed that the coding regions of the ATM gene had very low diversity, especially in the last 29% of the protein sequence. Using the Hudson/Kreitman/Aguadé statistic, we found that the ATM gene was significantly constrained in its evolution compared to other genes, indicating that this region of the gene has experienced suppressed meiotic recombination. We identified seven haplotypes in the ATM gene and found that two haplotypes accounted for 82% of all chromosomes analyzed in major populations. One of these haplotypes, carrying a missense polymorphism called D126E, was found to be highly frequent in Africa (33% of chromosomes) and may be the result of either a population expansion or selective pressure. Overall, our study provides new insights into the genetic structure and evolution of the ATM gene and its implications for disease susceptibility.

title: Ablation and regeneration of tolerance-inducing medullary thymic epithelial cells after cyclosporine, cyclophosphamide, and dexamethasone treatment.
text: Immunosuppressive drugs and cytotoxic chemotherapy agents are designed to eliminate or suppress autoreactive, alloantigenic, or hyperinflammatory T cells or disseminated malignancies. However, they can also result in severe immunological side effects, such as interrupted thymopoiesis and general immunodeficiency, or even autoimmunity. Consistent with the interactions between thymocytes and stromal cells, our findings now indicate that these common therapeutic agents have significant effects on murine thymic epithelial cells (TEC), which are crucial for rebuilding immunity post-treatment. We found that the immunosuppressant cyclosporine A, which has been associated with a thymus-dependent autoimmune syndrome in some patients, causes extensive loss of autoimmune regulator (Aire(+)) tolerance-inducing MHC class II(high) medullary TEC (mTEC(high)). However, Aire expression was restored within 7 days post-cyclosporine A treatment. Complete recovery of the mTEC(high) subset occurred within 10 days, and this recovery was linked to a decrease in a relatively resistant MHC class II(low) mTEC subset (mTEC(low)). Similarly, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone caused more extensive ablation of thymocytes and stromal cells, resulting in severe depletion of tolerance-inducing mTEC(high). Overall, these data demonstrate that Aire(+) mTECs are highly sensitive to damage and that mTEC regeneration follows a conserved pattern regardless of the treatment regimen used.

title: GATA-3 regulates hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and cell-cycle entry.
text: Maintaining hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) quiescence is crucial for the lifelong production of blood cells. Approximately 75% of cells in a highly purified long-term repopulating HSC (LT-HSC) pool (Lin(-)Sca1(+)c-Kit(hi)CD150(+)CD48(-)) are quiescent, with only a small proportion of LT-HSCs in the cell cycle. Transcription factor GATA-3 is essential for the development of T cells in the thymus and Th2 cell differentiation in peripheral organs. Although GATA-3 is expressed in HSCs, its role in prethymic progenitor cells has not been definitively established. In this study, we found that Gata3-deficient mice have reduced numbers of LT-HSCs and fewer LT-HSCs in the cell cycle. Additionally, Gata3-deficient hematopoietic progenitor cells fail to enter a higher cycling state after myelosuppression induced by 5-fluorouracil. Therefore, GATA-3 is necessary to maintain normal numbers of LT-HSCs and their entry into the cell cycle.

title: CpG island methylator phenotype predicts progression of malignant melanoma.
text:
The CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP) may be linked to the development of cancer through the coordinated inactivation of tumor suppressor and tumor-related genes (TRGs) and the methylation of multiple noncoding, methylated-in-tumor (MINT) loci. These epigenetic changes create a distinct CIMP pattern that has been associated with poor prognosis in gastrointestinal cancers. Given the similarity between epigenetic alterations in gastrointestinal and cutaneous melanoma, we hypothesized that CIMP may also play a role in melanoma progression.
To investigate this, we analyzed the methylation status of TRGs and MINT loci in primary and metastatic melanoma tumors of different clinical stages (n=122). Our results show an increased frequency of hypermethylation in TRGs such as WIF1, TFPI2, RASSF1A, and SOCS1 with advancing clinical stage. Furthermore, we found a significant positive association between the methylation status of MINT17, MINT31, and TRGs. Interestingly, the methylation status of MINT31 was associated with disease outcome in stage III melanoma.
Our findings provide evidence for the significance of a CIMP pattern in the progression of malignant melanoma. Future large-scale studies may determine if CIMP-positive primary melanomas are at high risk of metastasis or recurrence. In conclusion, the present study highlights the potential of CIMP as a predictive marker for disease progression in melanoma.

title: SLC1A5 mediates glutamine transport required for lung cancer cell growth and survival.
text:
In a previous proteomic analysis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), we identified solute-linked carrier family A1 member 5 (SLC1A5) as an overexpressed protein in NSCLC tumors compared to matched controls. Based on this finding, we hypothesized that SLC1A5 overexpression is adaptive to meet the metabolic demands of lung cancer cell growth and survival. To investigate this further, we analyzed SLC1A5 protein expression in archival lung cancer tissues and cell lines using immunohistochemistry and immunoblotting (n = 98 and n = 36, respectively). We also conducted kinetic analysis of l-glutamine (Gln) uptake in lung cancer cell lines in the presence and absence of a pharmacologic inhibitor of SLC1A5, gamma-l-glutamyl-p-nitroanilide (GPNA). Finally, we examined the effect of Gln deprivation and uptake inhibition on cell growth, cell-cycle progression, and growth signaling pathways of five lung cancer cell lines.
Our results show that:
1. SLC1A5 protein is expressed in 95% of squamous cell carcinomas (SCC), 74% of adenocarcinomas (ADC), and 50% of neuroendocrine tumors.
2. SLC1A5 is localized to the cytoplasmic membrane and is significantly associated with SCC histology and male gender.
3. Approximately 68% of Gln is transported in a Na(+)-dependent manner, with 50% of this transport attributed to SLC1A5 activity.
4. Pharmacologic and genetic targeting of SLC1A5 decreased cell growth and viability in lung cancer cells, an effect mediated in part by mTOR signaling.

In conclusion, these findings suggest that SLC1A5 plays a crucial role in Gln transport, which controls lung cancer cells' metabolism, growth, and survival.

title: Eic1 links Mis18 with the CCAN/Mis6/Ctf19 complex to promote CENP-A assembly
text: Chromatin component CENP-A plays a central role in kinetochore formation. Thereplication-independent incorporation of CENP-A at centromeres depends on the chaperone HJURP (Scm3) in vertebrates and fission yeast, and Mis18 in both organisms. Cell cycle regulation is required for the recruitment of Mis18 and HJURP to centromeres. In vertebrates, Mis18 associates with Mis18BP1 (KNL2), which is crucial for the recruitment of Mis18 and HJURP. We have identified two novel fission yeast proteins, Eic1 and Eic2, that are components of the Mis18 complex. Eic1 is essential for maintaining CENP-A at centromeres and is important for kinetochore integrity, while Eic2 is non-essential. Eic1 also interacts with Fta7 (CENP-Q/Okp1), Cnl2 (Nkp2), and Mal2 (CENP-O/Mcm21), components of the constitutive CCAN/Mis6/Ctf19 complex. Since there is no Mis18BP1 Orthologue in fission yeast, it remains unclear how the key CENP-A loading factor Mis18 is recruited. Our findings suggest that Eic1 serves a function similar to that of Mis18BP1, connecting a module within the CCAN/Mis6/Ctf19 complex to temporally regulate the recruitment of the Mis18/Scm3 (HJURP) CENP-A loading factors. The novel interactions identified between CENP-A loading factors and the CCAN/Mis6/Ctf19 complex are likely to also contribute to CENP-A maintenance in other organisms.

title: INTRANASAL INSULIN IMPROVES COGNITION AND MODULATES β-AMYLOID IN EARLY AD
text:
Background: Reduced brain insulin signaling and low levels of insulin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) have been observed in individuals with Alzheimer's disease (AD). Insulin administration has been shown to improve memory, alter electroencephalography (EEG) patterns, and modulate neurotransmitters, possibly by increasing low brain levels of insulin. Intranasal insulin administration has been shown to reach the brain within 15 minutes.
Objective: We aimed to determine whether daily intranasal insulin treatment would improve cognition in patients with early AD or its prodrome, amnestic mild cognitive impairment (MCI). The primary outcome measure was the ability to retain verbal information after a delay, while secondary measures included attention, caregiver rating of functional status, and plasma levels of insulin, glucose, β-amyloid, and cortisol.
Methods: Twenty-five participants were randomly assigned to receive either placebo (n = 12) or 20 IU of intranasal insulin treatment (n = 13) using an electronic atomizer. Participants, caregivers, and all clinical evaluators were blinded to treatment assignment. Cognitive measures and blood samples were collected at baseline and after 21 days of treatment.
Results: Fasting plasma glucose and insulin levels remained unchanged with treatment. However, the insulin-treated group showed better retention of verbal information after a delay compared to the placebo-assigned group (p = 0.0374). The insulin-treated group also exhibited improved attention (p = 0.0108) and functional status (p = 0.0410). In addition, intranasal insulin treatment raised fasting plasma levels of the short form of the β-amyloid peptide (Aβ40) (p = 0.0471), without affecting the longer isoform (Aβ42), resulting in an increased Aβ40/42 ratio (p = 0.0207).
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that daily intranasal insulin treatment may be a novel approach to improving cognition in patients with Alzheimer's disease. These results support further investigation into the benefits of intranasal insulin for AD, and provide insight into the potential therapeutic mechanism of action of intranasal insulin in the brain.

title: Maternal alloantigens promote the development of tolerogenic fetal regulatory T cells in utero.
text: As the immune system matures, T cells are refined or modified to distinguish between self and foreign antigens. In mice, this process involves the elimination of self-reactive cells, but in humans, it involves an additional mechanism: the generation of regulatory T cells (Tregs) that suppress fetal immune responses. We discovered that a significant number of maternal cells cross the placenta and reside in fetal lymph nodes, inducing the development of CD4+CD25highFoxP3+ Tregs that suppress fetal antimaternal immunity and persist at least until early adulthood. These findings shed light on a unique form of antigen-specific tolerance in humans, established in utero and likely playing a role in regulating immune responses after birth.

title: β-site amyloid precursor protein-cleaving enzyme 1(BACE1) inhibitor treatment induces Aβ5-X peptides through alternative amyloid precursor protein cleavage
text:
INTRODUCTION:
The β-secretase enzyme, BACE1 (β-site amyloid precursor protein-cleaving enzyme 1), plays a crucial role in the production of β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides, a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD). BACE1 cleaves amyloid precursor protein (APP), leading to the formation of Aβ peptides. Therefore, targeting BACE1 has been proposed as a potential disease-modifying strategy for AD. In a previous study, we found that treatment with a BACE1 inhibitor resulted in decreased levels of Aβ1-34 and increased levels of Aβ5-40 in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). To further investigate these findings in humans, we conducted an investigator-blind, placebo-controlled, and randomized study in healthy subjects.
METHODS:
We randomly assigned 18 healthy subjects to receive a single dose of either 30 mg or 90 mg of LY2811376 (a BACE1 inhibitor) or placebo. We used hybrid immunoaffinity-mass spectrometry (HI-MS) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) to measure various Aβ peptides in CSF samples.
RESULTS:
Our results demonstrate dose-dependent changes in CSF Aβ1-34, Aβ5-40, and Aβ5-X after treatment with LY2811376. Specifically, Aβ5-40 and Aβ5-X increased dose-dependently, as reflected by two independent methods, while Aβ1-34 decreased dose-dependently.
CONCLUSION:
Our findings confirm that CSF Aβ1-34 may be a useful marker for monitoring target engagement in clinical trials of BACE1 inhibitors. Since it is less hydrophobic than longer Aβ species, it is less susceptible to preanalytical confounding factors and may thus be a more stable marker. Additionally, we demonstrate that BACE1 inhibition in humans is associated with APP-processing into N-terminally truncated Aβ peptides via a BACE1-independent pathway.
TRIAL REGISTRATION:


This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT00838084) on January 23, 2009, and was last updated on July 14, 2009.

title: Cardiovascular diseases in Chinese, Malays, and Indians in Singapore. I. Differences in mortality.
text:
Study Objective:
The aim of this study was to analyze differences in mortality rates from the three main cardiovascular diseases (ischaemic heart disease, hypertensive disease, and cerebrovascular disease) among Chinese, Malays, and Indians in Singapore.
Design:
The study was conducted using national death registration data in Singapore over a five-year period (1980-1984). The underlying cause of death, coded according to the International Classification of Diseases (ICD-9), was analyzed for each ethnic group.
Setting:
The study was limited to the independent island state of Singapore, with a population of 2.53 million (Chinese 76.5%, Malays 14.8%, Indians 6.4%, and Others 2.3%). Death registration was assumed to be complete.
Subjects:
All registered deaths in the age range of 30-69 years during the study period were analyzed by ethnic group.
Measurements and Main Results:
Indians had higher mortality rates from ischaemic heart disease than the other ethnic groups in both sexes, with age-standardized relative risks of Indian vs. Chinese (males: 3.8, females: 3.4), Indian vs. Malay (males: 1.9, females: 1.6), and Malay vs. Chinese (males: 2.0, females: 2.2). The excess mortality in Indians decreased with age. For hypertensive disease, Malays had the highest mortality rates, with age-standardized relative risks of Malay vs. Chinese (males: 3.4, females: 4.4), Malay vs. Indian (males: 2.0, females: 2.5), and Indian vs. Chinese (males: 1.6, females: 1.6). For cerebrovascular disease, there were only minor ethnic differences, with age-standardized relative risks of Malay vs. Chinese (males: 1.1, females: 1.9), Malay vs. Indian (males: 1.0, females: 1.1), and Indian vs. Chinese (males: 1.1, females: 1.7).
Conclusions:
There were significant differences in mortality rates from the three main cardiovascular diseases among Chinese, Malays, and Indians in Singapore.

title: Protein localization in electron micrographs using fluorescence nanoscopy
text:
A comprehensive depiction of a cell requires a detailed description of its molecular landscape, including the precise location of proteins within various organelles. While techniques such as immunocytochemical electron microscopy can provide high-resolution localization of proteins, they are limited by factors such as fixation quality, the availability of antibodies, and the inaccessibility of antigens. To overcome these limitations, we have developed a novel approach called correlative fluorescence electron microscopy, which allows for the nanoscopic localization of proteins in electron micrographs.
In this method, proteins are labeled with fluorescent proteins, such as Citrine or tdEos, and expressed in Caenorhabditis elegans. The worms are then fixed and embedded in plastic for imaging. Using stimulated emission depletion (STED) microscopy or photoactivated localization microscopy (PALM), we are able to image the tagged proteins from ultrathin sections with nanometer-scale resolution. By correlating fluorescence signals with electron micrographs from the same sections, we can accurately locate proteins within their respective organelles.
We have applied this method to study the localization of histones, a mitochondrial protein, and a presynaptic dense projection protein in electron micrographs. Our results demonstrate the power of correlative fluorescence electron microscopy for providing a complete portrait of cellular protein distribution at the nanoscale.

title: The flavonoid component isorhamnetin in vitro inhibits proliferation and induces apoptosis in Eca-109 cells.
text: The flavonoid compound isorhamnetin has been investigated for its potential anti-cancer effects against human esophageal squamous carcinoma cells (Eca-109). In vitro experiments were conducted to evaluate the effects of isorhamnetin on the proliferation and viability of Eca-109 cells. The results showed that isorhamnetin exhibited a cytostatic effect on the cells, with an IC50 value of 40±0.08 microg/ml, as determined by the MTT assay. Isorhamnetin also inhibited the proliferation of Eca-109 cells and caused cell cycle arrest in the G(0)/G(1) phase, accompanied by a significant reduction in the G(2)/M phase. Furthermore, isorhamnetin induced apoptosis in Eca-109 cells, as evidenced by morphological changes and an increase in apoptosis rate. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, the expressions of six proliferation- and death-related genes were analyzed by flow cytometry. The results showed that the expressions of bcl-2, c-myc, and H-ras were downregulated, while the expressions of Bax, c-fos, and p53 were upregulated. These findings suggest that isorhamnetin may be a potent drug against esophageal cancer, inhibiting cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis in Eca-109 cells. However, further in vivo experiments are required to confirm these results.

title: Arachidonic Acid in the Diabetic Rat Kidney
text: In an isolated and perfused rat kidney, arachidonic acid causes cyclooxygenase-dependent vasoconstriction through activating PGH2/TxA2 receptors. This effect is heightened in the kidneys of diabetic rats. The present study investigated the roles of cyclooxygenase-1 and cyclooxygenase-2 in the enhanced vasoconstrictor response of arachidonic acid in streptozotocin-diabetic rat kidneys. The release of 20-HETE was also examined, as this eicosanoid has been reported to elicit cyclooxygenase-dependent vasoconstriction. The results showed that vasoconstrictor responses to arachidonic acid were significantly higher in diabetic rat kidneys compared to control rat kidneys, with a 2-fold increase in the release of 6-ketoPGF1alpha, which serves as an index of cyclooxygenase activity. Inhibition of both cyclooxygenase isoforms with indomethacin abolished the vasoconstrictor response to arachidonic acid in both diabetic and control rat kidneys, while inhibition of cyclooxygenase-2 with nimesulide reduced perfusion pressure responses to 1 and 3 microg arachidonic acid only in the diabetic rat kidney, consistent with a 3-fold increase in the renal cortical expression of cyclooxygenase-2. Furthermore, 20-HETE release from the diabetic rat kidney was reduced almost 6-fold, and was not increased in response to arachidonic acid. These findings demonstrate that the renal vasoconstrictor effect of arachidonic acid is entirely dependent on cyclooxygenase activity, with no evidence for a contribution from 20-HETE; in the diabetic rat, cyclooxygenase-2 activity contributes to the renal vasoconstrictor effect of arachidonic acid.

title: Two sequence motifs from HIF-1alpha bind to the DNA-binding site of p53.
text: There is evidence indicating that the protein hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha) interacts with the tumor suppressor p53. To investigate this interaction, we mapped the binding of the core domain of p53 (p53c) to a collection of immobilized HIF-1alpha-derived peptides and identified two specific peptide sequences that bound to p53c with micromolar affinity in solution. One of these sequences was located near and the other coincided with the two proline residues in the oxygen-dependent degradation domain (P402 and P564) of HIF-1alpha, which play a key role in regulating HIF-1alpha's activity. Interestingly, the binding affinity was not affected by the hydroxylation state of P564. Using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, we found that these sequence motifs bind to the DNA-binding site of p53c. Since the two sequences are similar and separated by 120 residues, with one located in a largely unstructured transactivation domain, we propose that each sequence motif in HIF-1alpha binds to a different subunit of the p53 tetramer, resulting in very strong binding. The binding data support the hypothesis that p53 provides a pathway for the degradation of HIF-1alpha in hypoxic tumor cells that lack the hydroxylation of the two proline residues.

title: A functionally characterized test set of human induced pluripotent stem cells
text: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) hold great promise for studying development and creating in vitro disease models, but reported variability in their behavior has raised questions about their utility. To address this, we established a diverse bank of 16 iPSC lines from seven individuals with varying ages, genders, and health statuses. We extensively characterized each line's pluripotency and ability to differentiate into motor neurons using standardized procedures in two independent laboratories. Surprisingly, 13 of the iPSC lines produced functional motor neurons with similar efficiency to human embryonic stem cells (ESCs). Although three lines were initially resistant to neural differentiation, we were able to rescue their performance by promoting early neuralization. Encouragingly, all 16 iPSC lines demonstrated the ability to differentiate into functional motor neurons, despite variations in their karyotype and expression of early pluripotency markers and transgenes. This iPSC and ESC test set is a valuable resource for researchers interested in the basic biology of stem cells and their applications.

title: Differential regulation of MAP kinase activation by a novel splice variant of human MAP kinase phosphatase-2.
text: Membrane-associated protein kinase phosphatase-2 (MKP-2) is part of the family of dual-specificity phosphatases that regulates the ERK and JNK MAP kinase signaling pathways. In this study, we identify a new human MKP-2 variant (MKP-2-S) lacking the MAP kinase binding site but retaining the phosphatase catalytic domain. We find that endogenous MKP-2-S is expressed in PC3 prostate and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells and human prostate biopsies through transcriptional transfection of MKP-2-S led to a 33kDa nucleus protein with phosphatase activity similar to the previously described long form of MKP-2 (MKP-2-L). Due to its inability to bind to JNK or ERK, MKP-2-S did not interact with JNK or ERK, while MKP-2-L interacted with both. Protein turnover of adenoviral expressed MKP-2-S was accelerated relative to MKP-2-L, with a greater susceptibility to proteosomal-mediated degradation. MKP-2-S retained its ability to deactivate JNK in a similar manner to MKP-2-L and was an effective inhibitor of LPS-stimulated COX-2 induction. However, unlike MKP-2-L, MKP-2-S was unable to reverse serum-induced ERK activation or significantly inhibit endothelial cell proliferation. These findings reveal the occurrence of a novel splice variant of MKP-2, which may play a significant role in the dysregulation of MAP kinase activity in certain disease states, particularly in breast and prostate cancers.

title: Myeloperoxidase acts as a profibrotic mediator of atrial fibrillation
text:
Clinical and experimental studies have shown a strong association between atrial fibrillation and inflammation. However, the question of whether inflammation causes or is caused by atrial fibrillation, as well as the specific inflammatory mediators involved, remains unclear. To investigate the mechanistic role of myeloperoxidase (MPO), a heme enzyme abundant in neutrophils, in the pathophysiology of atrial fibrillation, we conducted experimental and clinical studies.
Using MPO-deficient mice pretreated with angiotensin II (AngII) to trigger leukocyte activation, we found that these mice had lower levels of the MPO product 3-chlorotyrosine in atrial tissue, reduced activity of matrix metalloproteinases, and blunted atrial fibrosis compared to wild-type mice. When these mice were subjected to right atrial electrophysiological stimulation, they were protected from atrial fibrillation, which was reversed when MPO was restored. Similarly, in humans with atrial fibrillation, we observed higher plasma levels of MPO and a larger MPO burden in right atrial tissue compared to individuals without atrial fibrillation. In the atria, MPO colocalized with increased formation of 3-chlorotyrosine, indicating that MPO is essential for the structural remodeling of the myocardium, leading to increased vulnerability to atrial fibrillation.
In summary, our data suggest that MPO plays a crucial role in the development of atrial fibrillation by promoting structural remodeling of the myocardium and increasing the vulnerability of the atria to fibrillation.

title: Knowledge and use of secondary contraception among patients requesting termination of pregnancy.
text: A survey of 769 patients attending the St. James's University Fertility Control Clinic in England found that those who saw general practitioners were less knowledgeable about contraception compared to those who attended specialist clinics. The survey revealed a need for counseling on pill and condom use and protection against sexually transmitted diseases, as well as a lack of knowledge about postcoital methods. Only 30% of patients with recognized condom failure and 12% of those who had not used any contraception had adequate knowledge of postcoital pills. Only 2% of patients knew about postcoital insertion of an intrauterine contraceptive device. The majority (718 out of 769) preferred using postcoital contraception. Contraceptive information was provided to 501 patients by a general practitioner, 102 by a community family planning clinic, and 163 had no medical advice. There was a range of knowledge of postcoital contraceptive methods among the 422 patients who had ever used the combined pill, with 19% of those seen by general practitioners and 50% of those seen at community family planning clinics providing correct answers.

title: Domestication and Divergence of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Beer Yeasts
text: Although the domestication of livestock, pets, and crops has been well-documented, the extent to which microorganisms used in food production have also undergone human selection is unclear. In this study, we aimed to investigate the origins and evolutionary history of industrial Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeasts by sequencing the genomes and analyzing the phenotypes of 157 industrial yeast strains. Our findings reveal that contemporary industrial yeasts can be divided into five sublineages that are distinct from wild strains and have descended from a limited number of ancestors through complex patterns of domestication and local divergence. Using large-scale phenotyping and genome analysis, we found strong industry-specific selection for stress tolerance, sugar utilization, and flavor production, while sexual cycle and other phenotypes related to survival in nature have deteriorated, particularly in beer yeasts. Overall, our results shed light on the origins, evolutionary history, and phenotypic diversity of industrial yeasts and provide a valuable resource for further selection of superior strains. CLIP.

title: The ascendancy of Amblyomma americanum as a vector of pathogens affecting humans in the United States.
text: Prior to the 1990s, Amblyomma americanum was viewed primarily as a nuisance species, with little significance as a vector of zoonotic pathogens affecting humans. However, recent discoveries of Ehrlichia chaffeensis, Ehrlichia ewingii, and "Borrelia lonestari" have shifted the public health importance of lone star ticks. In the next 25 years, the number of cases of human disease caused by A. americanum-associated pathogens is expected to rise. This increase will be driven by both biological and environmental factors that impact the geographic distribution and transmission of zoonotic pathogens, as well as societal and demographic changes that influence the likelihood of susceptible humans coming into contact with infected ticks. Advances in diagnostic capabilities and national surveillance efforts will also contribute to the anticipated rise in recognized cases of disease.

title: Biallelic mutations in PALB2 cause Fanconi anemia subtype FA-N and predispose to childhood cancer
text: Recently, PALB2 was found to be a nuclear partner of BRCA2. Biallelic mutations in BRCA2 lead to Fanconi anemia subtype FA-D1 and increase cancer risk in early childhood. We discovered pathogenic mutations in PALB2 (also known as FANCN) in seven families with Fanconi anemia and childhood cancers, demonstrating that biallelic PALB2 mutations cause a new subtype of Fanconi anemia, FA-N, and, similarly to biallelic BRCA2 mutations, significantly enhance the risk of childhood cancer.

title: Long tandem arrays of complex repeat units in Chironomus telomeres.
text: A DNA fragment cloned from the Chironomus pallividittatus genome using EcoRI has been localized to telomeres and connective regions between telomeres using in situ hybridization. No hybridization was observed in other regions of the chromosomes. A separate cloned EcoRI fragment, 525 bp long, was also analyzed and found to be a partial duplication of the initial 340-bp sequence. Genomic blot hybridization experiments revealed that the 340-bp sequence is a representative monomeric unit of tandemly repeated arrays, which make up approximately 1.2% of the Chironomus genome, with each telomere containing approximately 300 kb of these repeated units. The repeat unit consists of two subrepeats, each present twice per repeat unit. Northern blot hybridization experiments showed that the telomere-associated sequences are transcribed into a discrete RNA species approximately 20 kb in size. The evolution of these telomere-associated DNA sequences is discussed.

title: Localization of Na+ channel isoforms at the atrioventricular junction and atrioventricular node in the rat.
text:
THE BACKGROUND The electrical activity of the atrioventricular node (AVN) is functionally diverse, but the relationship between this diversity and the three-dimensional structure of the AVN is unknown. To address this question, we studied the expression of Na(V)1.5 and other Na+ channel isoforms in the AVN.
METHODS AND RESULTS We used Masson's trichrome staining and immunolabeling with marker proteins to identify the rat AVN. We then investigated Na+ channel expression using immunohistochemistry with isoform-specific Na+ channel antibodies. Na(V)1.1 was distributed similarly to Na(V)1.5. Na(V)1.2 was not detected, while Na(V)1.3 labeling was present in nerve fibers and cell bodies, but not myocytes, and was abundant in the penetrating atrioventricular (AV) bundle and the common bundle. Na(V)1.5 labeling was abundant in the atrial and ventricular myocardium and the left bundle branch, but was absent in the open node, penetrating AV bundle, AV ring bundle, and common bundle. Na(V)1.6 was not detected.
CONCLUSIONS Our findings provide molecular evidence of multiple electrophysiological cell types at the AV junction. Therefore, impaired AV conduction due to mutations in or loss of Na(V)1.5 must primarily affect the AVN inputs (inferior nodal extension and transitional zone) or output (bundle branches) rather than the AVN itself (open node and penetrating AV bundle).

title: Follicular B cell trafficking within the spleen actively restricts humoral immune responses.
text:
B cells within the spleen exist in two distinct subsets: Follicular (FO) and marginal zone (MZ). Though located close by, these cells have different functions and are maintained separately. Despite their proximity, the genetic basis for this separation remains poorly understood. Our research, however, has revealed that B cell migration within the spleen is regulated by lineage-specific transcription factors, most notably Klf2. Specifically, we found that altering the migratory receptors on B cells in the spleen enhances the functionality of FO B cells, allowing them to quickly respond to antigens presented in the MZ. This is remarkable, as in wild type animals, naive FO B cells are naturally removed from the MZ, limiting their ability to respond effectively to pathogens that enter the body through the bloodstream.
In summary, our study has uncovered a previously unknown mechanism that maintains the separation of B cell subsets within the spleen. By regulating the expression of migratory receptors, the transcription factor Klf2 influences the behavior of FO B cells, enabling them to more efficiently respond to infections.

title: Interleukin-2 and inflammation induce distinct transcriptional programs that promote the differentiation of effector cytolytic T cells.
text: Interleukin (IL)-2 and inflammation play a crucial role in regulating the generation of effector and memory cytolytic T-lymphocytes (CTLs) during infection. We have found that there is a complex interplay between IL-2 and inflammatory signals during CTL differentiation. Upon IL-2 stimulation, the transcription factor eomesodermin (Eomes) is upregulated, leading to increased transcription of perforin (Prf1) and repression of memory CTL markers, such as Bcl6 and IL-7Ralpha. The binding of Eomes and STAT5 to the cis-regulatory regions of Prf1 correlates with transcriptional initiation, or the recruitment of RNA polymerase II to the Prf1 promoter. Inflammation, including CpG and IL-12, enhances the expression of IL-2Ralpha and the transcription factor T-bet, but also counteracts late Eomes and perforin induction, preventing the repression of IL-7Ralpha by IL-2. In mice infected with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus, IL-2Ralpha-deficient effector CD8(+) T cells display reduced expression of Bcl6 and increased expression of granzyme B, leading to the formation of fewer KLRG-1(+) and T-bet-expressing CTLs, and impaired cytolytic activity. Our findings demonstrate that both inflammation and persistent IL-2 stimulation influence the differentiation of effector and memory CTLs, with IL-2 promoting effector differentiation at the expense of memory CTL development.

title: Neighbourhood risk factors for tuberculosis in Hong Kong.
text:
Background: Tuberculosis (TB) has historically been linked to poverty, particularly in developing countries. However, some industrialized areas, like Hong Kong, have also reported high incidences of TB despite having advanced social and economic systems. To better understand the relationship between TB and poverty in Hong Kong, this study aimed to investigate the spatial distribution of TB cases and their association with neighborhood-level risk factors.
Objective: The objective of this study was to examine the spatial distribution of TB cases and the relationship between these cases and neighborhood-level risk factors, including family, ethnicity, economic, and environmental factors, using data from 2005 to 2007.
Method: The study analyzed 17,294 TB cases at the District Council Constituency Area (DCCA) level, and used indirect age- and sex-standardization to account for differences in population demographics. The standardized TB ratio was correlated with neighborhood risk factors from different domains.
Results: The study found a spatially variable pattern of TB incidence, with significant associations between the standardized TB ratio and various neighborhood factors, including household income, place of birth, and marital status, after controlling for other risk factors on multivariate analysis.
Conclusion: These findings suggest that, despite Hong Kong's relatively low absolute poverty rates, low household income in the neighborhood is a significant predictor of TB incidence, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to address this issue. This study highlights the importance of considering the local context and the interplay between social, economic, and environmental factors in addressing TB in different regions.

title: Genomic stability and tumour suppression by the APC/C cofactor Cdh1
text: The anaphase promoting complex or cyclosome (APC/C), in collaboration with Cdc20 or Cdh1, targets and degrades cell-cycle proteins. Specifically, APC/C – Cdh1 functions in late mitosis and G1 to promote protein degradation. Mutant embryos without Cdh1 exhibit lethality caused by problems with the endoreduplication of trophoblast cells and placental malfunction. By expressing Cdh1 in the placenta, the lethality is prevented. Cdh1-deficient cells proliferate inefficiently and accumulate numeric and structural chromosomal aberrations, thereby demonstrating that Cdh1 plays a role in maintaining genomic stability. Heterozygous animals for Cdh1 show increased susceptibility to spontaneous tumors and display behavioral defects associated with increased proliferation of stem cells in the nervous system, suggesting that Cdh1 is essential for preventing unscheduled proliferation of specific progenitor cells and protecting mammalian cells from genomic instability.

title: Developing primary palliative care.
text:
Although about 65% of people with cancer want to die at home, only about 30% are able to do so.1,2 The government has emphasized the importance of providing patients with choice in end-of-life care, so primary care must play a crucial role in improving this figure.3 Developing palliative care services in primary care is essential for meeting patients' expectations and providing holistic, patient-centered care.4-6 In fact, primary care professionals have the potential and ability to provide end-of-life care to most patients, given adequate training, resources, and specialist advice when needed.7
Many cancer patients and their carers experience existential distress long before they die, and recognizing and alleviating this suffering is essential.8 However, primary care services often overlook this aspect of end-of-life care. By identifying patients who may benefit from an early palliative care approach, primary care teams can deliver both active treatment and patient-centered supportive care.9
Palliative care services must be extended to patients with non-malignant conditions who have comparable concerns and unmet needs to cancer patients.10 However, progress in this area is hindered by issues such as uncertainty about the most effective models of care, lack of non-cancer expertise, and concerns about pressure on specialist services.11
General practitioners and community nurses can lead the way in providing a palliative care approach for patients with terminal organ failure illness. The first step is to discuss and agree on the goals of care, and adjust management plans accordingly. Effective symptom control and maintaining quality of life are prioritized, and holistic, patient-centered care is provided.
Sadly, the new general medical services contract has not prioritized palliative care, and other developments are taking precedence.12 However, one important initiative is gaining momentum within primary care, and that is the Gold Standards Framework, which provides a detailed guide to providing holistic, patient-centered care in the community. Other recently initiated mechanisms for developing primary palliative care include training general practitioners with a special interest in palliative care and the new end-of-life initiative in England to improve palliative care provision by generalists.
To support these developments, it is essential that primary palliative care is supported by an adequate academic base. Although this is a challenging arena in which to undertake research, progress has been made in recent years in developing conceptual models and research architectures for studying end-of-life issues. Now we need to build on this work to ensure that the understanding and insights gleaned can be translated into effective interventions.
In conclusion, every person with a progressive illness has a right to palliative care.13 Patients desire a reassuring professional presence in the face of death, and general practitioners and community nurses are trusted by patients and are in a position to provide effective, equitable, and accessible palliative care. This will happen only if they have adequate time and resources and work in a system that encourages such care. Patients who receive holistic support in the community may be less likely to require expensive admission to hospital and often futile treatments at the end of their lives.

title: The effects of self-administering emergency contraception.
text:
BACKGROUND: Emergency postcoital contraception, also known as the "morning after" pill, can prevent pregnancy after unprotected sex. However, it is currently only available with a prescription from a doctor. Some have proposed making emergency contraception available over-the-counter or without a prescription. To investigate the potential benefits and risks of such a change, we conducted a study where some women were given a supply of emergency contraceptive pills to keep at home, while others had to visit a doctor to obtain emergency contraception.
METHODS: We randomly assigned 553 women to either a treatment group, where they received a supply of hormonal emergency contraceptive pills to take home, or a control group, where they had to visit a doctor to obtain emergency contraception. We collected data on the frequency of use of emergency contraception, the use of other contraceptives, and the incidence of unwanted pregnancies from both groups of women one year later.
RESULTS: Of the 549 women in the treatment group, 379 (69%) used emergency contraception at least once, compared to 27% of the 522 women in the control group (P<0.001). The women in the treatment group did not use emergency contraception more frequently than the control group, and their use of other contraceptives was similar. There were 18 unintended pregnancies in the treatment group and 25 in the control group (relative risk, 0.7; 95% confidence interval, 0.4 to 1.2).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that making emergency contraception more accessible may reduce the rate of unwanted pregnancies, without increasing the frequency of use or the risk of adverse effects.

title: A coactivator of pre-mRNA splicing.
text: The nuclear matrix antigen identified by the monoclonal antibody (mAb) B1C8 is a novel serine (S) and arginine (R)-rich protein linked to splicing complexes and dubbed SRm160 (SR-related matrix protein of 160 kD). SRm160 contains multiple SR repeats, but unlike proteins of the SR family of splicing factors, it lacks an RNA recognition motif.
