Infusion of the inflammatory mediator and CXCR2 ligand KC led to neutrophil mobilization from the marrow, and this effect was augmented threefold by low doses of CXCR4-blocking antibody that otherwise had no mobilizing effect. The study suggests that the CXCR4/SDF-1 axis is crucial in maintaining circulating neutrophil homeostasis and may participate in the rapid release of neutrophils from the marrow during inflammation through a novel interaction with inflammatory CXC chemokines.

title: Vitamin D and prevention of colorectal cancer.
text:
BACKGROUND: Inadequate photosynthesis or oral intake of vitamin D has been linked to a higher incidence of colorectal cancer, but the relationship between vitamin D intake and cancer risk has not been studied comprehensively.
METHODS: We analyzed observational data from studies that reported dose-response gradients for vitamin D intake and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels. We plotted these trend lines and identified the point on each line corresponding to an odds ratio of 0.50, which represented the prediagnostic vitamin D intake or serum concentration associated with a 50% lower risk of colorectal cancer compared to intake or concentration of less than 100 IU/day or 13 ng/ml, respectively. We calculated the median of these values.
RESULTS: Our analysis revealed that individuals who consumed >/=1000 IU/day oral vitamin D (p<0.0001) or >/=33 ng/ml (82 nmol/l) serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (p<0.01) had a 50% lower incidence of colorectal cancer compared to reference values.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that intake of 1000 IU/day vitamin D, which is half the safe upper intake established by the National Academy of Sciences, is associated with a 50% lower risk of colorectal cancer. Similar results were observed with serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels of 33 ng/ml, which is within the safe range. We recommend prompt public health action to increase vitamin D intake to 1000 IU/day and promote moderate sunlight exposure to raise serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels.

title: Repeat expansion in the budding yeast ribosomal DNA can occur independently of the canonical homologous recombination machinery
text: Major eukaryotic genomic regions, including ribosomal DNA (rDNA), are composed of repeated sequences with well-established copy numbers that must be maintained through regulated recombination. Although mechanisms that initiate rDNA recombination have been identified, none are directional and therefore cannot fully explain the precise control of repeat numbers. Our study reveals that yeast lacking the histone chaperone Asf1 exhibit reproducible rDNA repeat expansions, which do not require the blockage of the replication fork protein Fob1 and are therefore independent of previously identified rDNA expansion mechanisms. We propose the existence of a regulated rDNA repeat gain pathway that becomes constitutively active in asf1Δ mutants. Cells lacking ASF1 accumulate rDNA repeats with high fidelity and in a processive manner across multiple cell divisions. Notably, the mechanism of repeat gain is dependent on repetitive sequence but is unrelated to homologous recombination proteins Rad52, Rad51, and Rad59. Furthermore, mutations that reduce the processivity of DNA replication lead to progressive loss of rDNA repeats, suggesting that a novel break-induced replication mechanism occurs in repetitive DNA that is dependent on high homology but does not utilize the conventional homologous recombination machinery.

title: cDNA and genomic cloning of lacritin, a novel secretion enhancing factor from the human lacrimal gland.
text: Several extracellular factors are believed to promote the differentiation of unstimulated and/or stimulated secretory pathways in exocrine secretory cells, including the lacrimal gland. However, the specific identity of these organ-specific factors remains largely unknown. Our study aimed to investigate the role of a novel secreted glycoprotein, lacritin, in exocrine secretion in lacrimal acinar cells. mRNA and protein expression analysis revealed that lacritin is highly expressed in the human lacrimal gland, moderately in major and minor salivary glands, and slightly in the thyroid. Surprisingly, no lacritin message or protein was detected in over 50 other human tissues examined. The protein contains regions similar to glycosaminoglycan-binding areas of brain-specific neuroglycan C and fibulin-2, and its primary localization is to secretory granules and fluid in the lacrimal gland. The lacritin gene contains five exons with no alternative splicing and maps to chromosome 12q13. Recombinant lacritin enhanced unstimulated but not stimulated acinar cell secretion, promoted ductal cell proliferation, and stimulated signaling through tyrosine phosphorylation and calcium release. It also bound collagen IV, laminin-1, entactin/nidogen-1, fibronectin, and vitronectin but not collagen I, heparin, or EGF. Our findings suggest that lacritin may play a key role in the function of the lacrimal gland-corneal axis, acting as an autocrine/paracrine enhancer of the lacrimal constitutive secretory pathway, ductal cell mitogen, and stimulator of corneal epithelial cells.

title: The structure of informal care: are there differences by race?
text: In this study, the authors examined whether there are racial differences in the structure of informal caregiving networks among functionally impaired individuals aged 65 and older. Drawing on data from the 1989 National Long-Term Care Survey, the study analyzed the caregiving networks of 3,793 individuals in this age group. The investigation revealed that the size of both the total caregiver network and the unpaid network did not vary by race, but the likelihood of a non-immediate family member being an unpaid caregiver was higher among disabled older black individuals. These findings have important implications for understanding potential race differences in nursing home utilization and paid long-term care services, as observed in previous studies.

title: Proteomic and genomic approaches reveal critical functions of H3K9 methylation and Heterochromatin Protein-1γ in reprogramming to pluripotency
text:
Reprogramming somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) involves a significant reorganization of chromatin. To identify post-translational histone modifications that change in abundance during this process, we employed a quantitative mass-spectrometry-based approach. Our findings reveal that iPSCs exhibit an increase in histone modifications associated with active chromatin and a decrease in marks of transcriptional elongation and a specific repressive modification, H3K9me2/me3.
Investigating the contribution of H3K9 methylation to reprogramming, we found that the H3K9 methyltransferases Ehmt1, Ehmt2, and Setdb1 regulate global H3K9me2/me3 levels and that their depletion enhances iPSC formation from both fibroblasts and pre-iPSCs. Similarly, inhibition of the protein Heterochromatin protein-1γ (Cbx3), which recognizes H3K9 methylation, also increases reprogramming.
Using genome-wide location analysis, we discovered that Cbx3 predominantly binds to active genes in both pre-iPSCs and pluripotent cells, but with a distinct distribution. In pre-iPSCs, but not in embryonic stem cells, Cbx3 associates with transcriptional start sites, suggesting a developmentally regulated role for Cbx3 in transcriptional activation.
Our findings indicate that Cbx3 and H3K9 methylation restrict late reprogramming events, and suggest that a profound change in global chromatin character serves as an epigenetic barrier for reprogramming.

title: Tissue exit: a novel control point in the accumulation of antigen-specific CD8 T cells in the influenza a virus-infected lung.
text: Memory/effector T cells readily migrate into extralymphoid tissues and sites of infection, serving as a first line of defense against invading pathogens. Despite its potential to regulate the size, quality, and duration of a tissue infiltrate, the process of T cell egress from infected tissues is poorly understood. Utilizing a mouse model of influenza A virus infection, we discovered that CD8 effector T cells departed the infected lung in a CCR7-dependent manner. Conversely, following antigen recognition, effector CD8 T cell egress decreased, and CCR7 function was reduced in vivo and in vitro, suggesting that the exit of CD8 T cells from infected tissues is tightly regulated. Our findings imply that the regulation of T cell egress is a mechanism to retain antigen-specific effectors at the site of infection to promote viral clearance, while minimizing the presence of bystander T cells and preventing excessive inflammation.

title: The relation between dietary flavonol intake and coronary heart disease mortality: a meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies
text: Background: The association between dietary flavonol intake and the risk of coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality has been studied in several prospective cohorts. Objective: To conduct a meta-analysis of these studies to assess the relationship between dietary flavonol intake and CHD mortality. Methods: We conducted a systematic search of prospective cohort studies published before September 2001 using MEDLINE and EMBASE databases, as well as reference lists from relevant articles. We extracted data on prospective cohort size, mean age, follow-up duration, number of fatal CHD events, mean flavonol intake, main sources of flavonol intake, degree of adjustment for potential confounders, and the relation of CHD mortality to dietary flavonol intake at baseline. Results: Seven studies were included in the analysis, totaling 2087 fatal CHD events. Compared to individuals in the bottom third of dietary flavonol intake, those in the top third had a combined risk ratio of 0.80 (95% CI 0.69-0.93) after adjustment for known CHD risk factors and other dietary components. Conclusion: Our overview of prospective cohort studies suggests that high dietary intake of flavonols from a limited number of fruits, vegetables, tea, and red wine may be associated with a lower risk of CHD mortality in free-living populations. Funding: This study was funded by the Institute for International Health, University of Sydney.

title: MRI in the diagnosis of MS: a prospective study with comparison of clinical evaluation, evoked potentials, oligoclonal banding, and CT.
text:
Sure, here's a possible reconstruction of the given text:
In a prospective evaluation of 200 patients with suspected multiple sclerosis (MS), we compared the diagnostic capabilities of MRI, CT, evoked potentials (EP), and CSF oligoclonal banding analysis. MRI emerged as the best technique for demonstrating dissemination in space. An abnormal appropriate EP study in monosymptomatic patients was often supported by MRI and CSF analysis, serving as a predictive sign of MS as a clinical diagnosis. Conversely, a normal EP study was not sufficient as MRI and CSF analysis frequently failed to support a diagnosis of non-MS. When there is agreement among three of these paraclinical studies, the diagnosis of MS is likely to be unequivocal. For use in research studies, we were able to diagnose laboratory-supported definite MS (LSDMS) in 85 patients (42.5%), including 19/38 (50%) of optic neuritis patients and 24/52 (46%) of chronic progressive myelopathy patients. MRI was 100% successful in identifying patients who qualified for LSDMS in the optic neuritis and chronic progressive myelopathy groups. In a brief follow-up period (less than 1 year), 19/200 (10%) of patients went on to develop clinically definite MS (CDMS), and MRI accurately predicted this diagnosis in 18/19 cases (95%). While long-term follow-up will determine how well these studies and the category of LSDMS predict the development of CDMS, the clinical diagnosis of MS (CDMS), although only 95% accurate, remains the gold standard for diagnosis.

title: Osteoclasts promote the formation of hematopoietic stem cell niches in the bone marrow
text: The formation of the hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) niche in bone marrow (BM) is closely associated with endochondral ossification, but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To investigate the role of osteoblasts (OBLs) and osteoclasts (OCLs) in HSC niche formation, we used the oc/oc mouse, a model with impaired endochondral ossification caused by a lack of OCL activity. Our findings reveal that the absence of OCL activity leads to a defective HSC niche characterized by an increased proportion of mesenchymal progenitors and impaired HSC homing to the BM. Interestingly, restoration of OCL activity reverses the defect in HSC niche formation, suggesting that OBLs are essential for establishing HSC niches. Additionally, our data suggest that osteoblastic development is induced by OCLs, providing new insights into the complex mechanisms behind HSC niche formation. These findings have important implications for our understanding of both normal and diseased hematopoiesis.

title: A prospective study of plasma homocyst(e)ine and risk of myocardial infarction in US physicians.
text:
Objective: To assess the potential link between elevated levels of plasma homocyst(e)ine and the risk of developing coronary heart disease, including myocardial infarction (MI).
Design: Nested case-control study using prospectively collected blood samples from participants in the Physicians' Health Study.
Setting: A cohort of 14,916 male physicians aged 40 to 84 years who provided plasma samples at baseline and were followed up for 5 years.
Participants: Samples from 271 men who subsequently developed MI were compared to paired controls matched by age and smoking.
Main Outcome Measure: The risk of acute MI or death due to coronary disease.
Results: Levels of homocyst(e)ine were significantly higher in case subjects (11.1 ± 4.0 nmol/mL) compared to controls (10.5 ± 2.8 nmol/mL; P = 0.03). This difference was largely attributed to an excess of high values among men who developed MIs. The relative risk of the highest 5% of homocyst(e)ine levels compared to the bottom 90% was 3.1 (95% CI, 1.4-6.9; P = 0.005) after adjustment for diabetes, hypertension, aspirin assignment, Quetelet's Index, and total/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Furthermore, 13 controls and 31 cases (11%) had values above the 95th percentile of the controls.
Conclusions: Moderately elevated levels of plasma homocyst(e)ine are associated with an increased risk of MI independent of other coronary risk factors. Because high levels can often be easily treated with vitamin supplements, homocyst(e)ine may be a modifiable, independent risk factor for coronary heart disease.

title: Involvement of transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 receptors in protease-activated receptor-2-induced joint inflammation and nociception.
text: Activation of the Protease-Activated Receptor-2 (PAR-2) is triggered by proteolytic cleavage and localizes on various cell types, including epithelial, endothelial, and inflammatory cells, as well as on Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) receptor-expressing neurons. PAR-2 is essential in inflammatory and nociceptive processes, but there is limited information on its function in the joints. To investigate the effects of intraarticular PAR-2 activation on joint pain and inflammation, we studied secondary hyperalgesia/allodynia, spontaneous weight distribution, swelling, and inflammatory cytokine production in rats and mice. Intraarticular injection of the PAR-2 receptor agonist SLIGRL-NH(2) decreased touch sensitivity and weight bearing in both species. Secondary mechanical allodynia/hyperalgesia and impaired weight distribution were significantly reduced by the TRPV1 antagonist SB366791 in rats and by genetic deletion of this receptor in mice. In contrast, intraplantar SLIGRL-NH(2) elicited similar primary mechanical hyperalgesia and impaired weight distribution in both wild-type (WT) and TRPV1-deficient mice, but edema was smaller in the knockouts. The inactive peptide, LRGILS-NH(2), did not induce any inflammatory or nociceptive changes. Our findings demonstrate that TRPV1 receptors play a significant role in secondary mechanical hyperalgesia/allodynia and spontaneous pain induced by PAR-2 receptor activation in the knee joint. However, intraplantar PAR-2 activation-induced edema is also TRPV1 receptor-mediated, while primary mechanical hyperalgesia, impaired weight distribution, and IL-1β production are independent of this channel.

title: Relationship between reduced forced expiratory volume in one second and the risk of lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with severe lung function impairment have a higher risk of developing lung cancer. However, the relationship between milder reductions in forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) and lung cancer risk is controversial. There is limited consensus on whether men and women have equivalent risks for lung cancer with comparable declines in FEV1.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed and EMBASE from 1966 to 2005 yielded 28 abstracts examining the association between FEV1 and lung cancer. The search criteria included population-based studies with a prospective design, large sample sizes (>5000 participants), and adjustment for cigarette smoking status. Four studies that reported FEV1 in quintiles were included in the analysis.
RESULTS: The risk of lung cancer significantly increased with decreasing FEV1. Compared to the highest quintile of FEV1 (>100% of predicted), the lowest quintile (<70% of predicted) was associated with a 2.23-fold (95% CI: 1.73-2.86) increased risk for lung cancer in men and a 3.97-fold increased risk in women (95% CI: 1.93-8.25). Even small decrements in FEV1 (approximately 90% of predicted) increased the risk of lung cancer by 30% in men (95% CI: 1.05-1.62) and 2.64-fold in women (95% CI: 1.30-5.31).
CONCLUSION: Reduced FEV1 is strongly associated with an increased risk of lung cancer, particularly among women. Even a relatively mild reduction in FEV1 is a significant predictor of lung cancer.

title: Functional Architecture of RNA Polymerase I
text: The synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) by RNA polymerase (Pol) I is a crucial step in ribosome biogenesis and serves as a regulatory switch in eukaryotic cell growth. In this study, we have determined the cryo-electron microscopic structure of the complete 14-subunit yeast Pol I, as well as a homology model for the core enzyme, and the crystal structure of the subcomplex A14/43. Our results reveal that the clamp, dock domain, and subunits A14/43 contribute to a unique surface that interacts with promoter-specific initiation factors. Additionally, we found that the Pol I-specific subunits A49 and A34.5 form a heterodimer near the enzyme funnel, which acts as a built-in elongation factor and is related to the Pol II-associated factor TFIIF. In contrast to Pol II, Pol I has a strong intrinsic 3'-RNA cleavage activity, which requires the C-terminal domain of subunit A12.2 and likely enables ribosomal RNA proofreading and 3'-end trimming.

title: SWI/SNF-Brg1 regulates self-renewal and occupies core pluripotency-related genes in embryonic stem cells.
text:
The SWI/SNF-Brg1 chromatin remodeling protein plays crucial roles in cellular processes, including cell-cycle control and differentiation, by regulating gene expression. Despite its importance, little is known about Brg1's function in preimplantation embryos and embryonic stem (ES) cells. Our findings shed light on this aspect, revealing that Brg1 is essential for ES cell self-renewal and pluripotency.
Using RNA interference-mediated knockdown of Brg1 in blastocysts, we observed aberrant expression of key pluripotency-related genes, including Oct4 and Nanog. In ES cells, knockdown of Brg1 led to changes indicative of differentiation, including downregulation of self-renewal and pluripotency genes (e.g., Oct4, Sox2, Sall4, Rest) and upregulation of differentiation genes. Our genome-wide promoter analysis using chromatin immunoprecipitation revealed that Brg1 occupied the promoters of key pluripotency-related genes, including Oct4, Sox2, Nanog, Sall4, Rest, and Polycomb group (PcG) proteins. Additionally, Brg1 co-occupied a subset of Oct4, Sox2, Nanog, and PcG protein target genes. These findings demonstrate Brg1's critical role in regulating self-renewal and pluripotency in ES cells.

title: Rapid induction of Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres by depletion of the histone chaperone ASF1
text: The activation mechanism of the alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) pathway in mammalian chromosome end maintenance was previously unclear. However, we have now discovered that co-depletion of the histone chaperones ASF1a and ASF1b in human cells leads to the manifestation of all ALT characteristics, including the formation of ALT-associated PML (promyelocytic leukemia) bodies (APBs), the presence of extrachromosomal telomeric DNA species, an increased frequency of telomeric sister chromatid exchanges (t-SCE) events, and intertelomeric exchange of an integrated tag. This ALT induction results in the simultaneous suppression of telomerase, and we have found that ALT induction is positively regulated by proteins RAD17 and BLM, while negatively regulated by EXO1 and DNA2. Our finding that ALT phenotypes are induced as a result of ASF1 depletion strongly supports the hypothesis that ALT is a consequence of histone management dysfunction.

title: Targeting bromodomains: epigenetic readers of lysine acetylation
text: Lysine acetylation plays a crucial role in regulating chromatin structure, and aberrant levels of acetylation have been linked to various diseases. Acetyl-lysine modifications create binding sites for bromodomains, which are small protein modules found on different proteins. Some of these proteins have a key role in the acetylation-dependent assembly of transcriptional regulator complexes, leading to changes in transcriptional programs and subsequent phenotypic changes. Recent discoveries of potent and highly specific inhibitors for the BET (bromodomain and extra-terminal) family of bromodomains have sparked significant research activity in various therapeutic areas, particularly in oncology, where BET proteins regulate the expression of key oncogenes and anti-apoptotic proteins. Targeting BET bromodomains may also have potential applications in the treatment of inflammation and viral infection. Here, we will discuss recent advances in the development of bromodomain inhibitors and their potential uses in drug discovery.

title: Arachidonic acid cytochrome P450 epoxygenase pathway.
text: Cytochrome P450 epoxygenases convert arachidonic acid into four epoxyeicosatrienoic acid (EET) regioisomers: 5,6-, 8,9-, 11,12-, and 14,15-EET. These mediators function as autocrine and paracrine signaling molecules, promoting vascular relaxation by activating smooth muscle large-conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channels (BKCa), and also have anti-inflammatory effects on blood vessels and the kidney, promote angiogenesis, and protect against ischemic injury to the myocardium and brain. CYP epoxygenases also convert eicosapentaenoic acid into vasoactive epoxy-derivatives, and endocannabinoids containing 11,12- and 14,15-EET are formed. Many EET actions are triggered by EET binding to a membrane receptor, which activates ion channels and intracellular signal transduction pathways, but EETs also interact directly with intracellular effector systems. Soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) converts EETs to dihydroxyeicosatrienoic acids (DHETs), which reduces the functional effects of EETs. Inhibition of sEH has been proposed as a means to enhance and prolong the beneficial effects of EETs.

title: Physical activity at 36 years: patterns and childhood predictors in a longitudinal study.
text:
Objective: To investigate the differences in physical activity patterns between men and women across different age groups and to identify factors that predict high levels of participation in sports and recreational activities in adulthood.
Design: Data collected from a national prospective birth cohort study were used, with measurements taken at various points in childhood, adolescence, and at the age of 36.
Setting: The study population was resident in England, Scotland, and Wales.
Subjects: A stratified sample of approximately 3500 men and women were studied regularly from birth until the age of 43.
Measurements and Results: The study found that more men than women reported participating in sports and recreational activities, gardening, and do-it-yourself activities. In contrast, women reported higher rates of bicycling and walking. Higher levels of education were found to be associated with frequent participation in sports. Individuals were also found to be more likely to engage in one type of activity without necessarily participating in other types. Those who were most active in sports had been above average at sports in school, were more outgoing socially in adolescence, had fewer health problems in childhood, were better educated, and had more mothers with a secondary education than those who were less active.
Conclusions: The findings suggest the importance of developing skills and habits in childhood as well as encouraging healthier exercise habits in adults who may have had few opportunities or low motivation previously. Studies examining the relationship between physical activity and chronic disease should consider a broad range of pursuits rather than extrapolating from one area of physical activity, and their explanations should take account of the possible role of childhood characteristics.

title: Residual lifetime risk for developing hypertension in middle-aged women and men: The Framingham Heart Study.
text:
Lifetime Risk of Hypertension Remains High in Middle-Aged and Elderly Individuals
Background: Hypertension is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease, and monitoring its prevalence over time is crucial for developing effective prevention and treatment strategies. The lifetime risk of hypertension is best described by the lifetime risk statistic, which estimates the percentage of individuals who will develop hypertension over their lifetime. However, the current trends in this risk are unknown.
Objectives: To estimate the residual lifetime risk of hypertension in older US adults and to evaluate temporal trends in this risk.
Design, Setting, and Participants: The study was a community-based prospective cohort of 1298 participants from the Framingham Heart Study who were aged 55-65 years and free of hypertension at baseline (1976-1998).
Main Outcome Measures: Residual lifetime risk (lifetime cumulative incidence not adjusted for competing causes of mortality) of hypertension, defined as blood pressure of 140/90 mm Hg or greater or use of antihypertensive medications.
Results: The residual lifetime risk of developing hypertension and stage 1 high blood pressure or higher (greater-than-or-equal to 140/90 mm Hg regardless of treatment) was 90% in both 55- and 65-year-old participants. The lifetime probability of receiving antihypertensive medication was 60%. The risk for hypertension remained unchanged for women, but it was approximately 60% higher for men in the contemporary 1976-1998 period compared with an earlier 1952-1975 period. In contrast, the residual lifetime risk for stage 2 high blood pressure or higher (greater-than-or-equal to 160/100 mm Hg regardless of treatment) was considerably lower in both sexes in the recent period (35%-57% in 1952-1975 vs 35%-44% in 1976-1998), likely due to a marked increase in treatment of individuals with substantially elevated blood pressure.
Conclusion: The residual lifetime risk of hypertension for middle-aged and elderly individuals is 90%, indicating a huge public health burden. Although the decline in lifetime risk for stage 2 high blood pressure or higher represents a major achievement, efforts should be directed at the primary prevention of hypertension.

title: Adverse effects of excessive consumption of amino acids.
text:
CHapter 158: Phenylalanine Toxicity
Developing the 0. -Methyl Phenylalanine Model
Phenylalanine is an essential amino acid that plays a crucial role in various physiological processes, including protein synthesis, neurotransmission, and immune function. However, excessive levels of phenylalanine in the body can lead to toxicity, which can cause a range of health problems. In this chapter, we will discuss the developing of the 0. -methyl phenylalanine model, a new animal model for studying phenylalanine toxicity.
Use of the a-Methyl Phenylalanine Model in Brain Protein Synthesis
Phenylalanine is a precursor to the neurotransmitter dopamine, which is involved in various brain functions, including mood regulation and motor control. The a-methyl phenylalanine model has been developed to study the role of phenylalanine in brain protein synthesis and to investigate the mechanisms of phenylalanine toxicity.
TYROSINE TOXICITY

General Nutritional Observations
Tyrosine is another essential amino acid that is important for various physiological processes, including protein synthesis, neurotransmission, and immune function. However, excessive levels of tyrosine in the body can lead to toxicity, which can cause a range of health problems. In this section, we will discuss general nutritional observations and factors affecting tyrosine toxicity.
Factors Affecting Tyrosine Toxicity
Several factors can affect the levels of tyrosine in the body and increase the risk of toxicity. These include:
Probable Cause of Tyrosine Toxicity
The exact cause of tyrosine toxicity is not fully understood, but it is believed to involve a combination of genetic and environmental factors. Further research is needed to better understand the mechanisms of tyrosine toxicity and to develop effective treatments.
A New Animal Model for Human Tyrosinemia II
Tyrosinemia is a rare genetic disorder that affects the body's ability to break down tyrosine. In this section, we will discuss a new animal model for human tyrosinemia II, which can help researchers better understand the mechanisms of tyrosine toxicity and develop effective treatments.
TRYPTOPHAN TOXICITY

General Nutritional Observations
Tryptophan is an essential amino acid that plays a crucial role in various physiological processes, including mood regulation and immune function. However, excessive levels of tryptophan in the body can lead to toxicity, which can cause a range of health problems. In this section, we will discuss general nutritional observations and factors affecting tryptophan toxicity.
Factors Affecting Tryptophan Toxicity
Several factors can affect the levels of tryptophan in the body and increase the risk of toxicity. These include:
Tryptophan and Ruminant Interstitial Pulmonary Emphysema and Edema
Tryptophan toxicity can lead to various respiratory problems, including interstitial pulmonary emphysema and edema. This section will discuss the relationship between tryptophan toxicity and these respiratory problems.
HISTIDINE TOXICITY

General Nutritional Observations
Histidine is an essential amino acid that plays a crucial role in various physiological processes, including protein synthesis and immune function. However, excessive levels of histidine in the body can lead to toxicity, which can cause a range of health problems. In this section, we will discuss general nutritional observations and factors affecting histidine toxicity.
Metabolic Aspects
Histidine is metabolized by various enzymes in the body, including phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C (PI-PLC). This section will discuss the metabolic aspects of histidine toxicity and how they relate to its mechanisms and treatment.
ALLEVIATION OF HISTIDINE TOXICITY

In this section, we will discuss various strategies for alleviating histidine toxicity, including dietary modifications and pharmacological interventions.
METHIONINE TOXICITY

General Nutritional Observations
Methionine is an essential amino acid that plays a crucial role in various physiological processes, including protein synthesis and detoxification. However, excessive levels of methionine in the body can lead to toxicity, which can cause a range of health problems. In this section, we will discuss general nutritional observations and factors affecting methionine toxicity.
Tissue Damage
Methionine toxicity can lead to various forms of tissue damage, including liver damage and neurological disorders. This section will discuss the mechanisms of methionine toxicity and how they relate to tissue damage.
PROTECTIVE EFFECT OF GLYCINE, SERINE, OR RETINOL

In this section, we will discuss the protective effects of glycine, serine, or retinol against methionine toxicity. These compounds may help reduce the risk of methionine toxicity by inhibiting its metabolism or promoting its excretion.
CHEMICAL CHARACTERISTICS RELATED TO THE TOXICITY OF METHIONINE

This section will discuss the chemical characteristics of methionine that are related to its toxicity, including its ability to form reactive oxygen species and its interactions with various cellular components.
DAMAGING EFFECTS OF METHYLTHIONINE

Methylthionine is a metabolite of methionine that can accumulate in the body and cause toxicity. In this section, we will discuss the damaging effects of methylthionine and how they relate to methionine toxicity.
METHIONINE TOXICITY IN CHICKENS


This section will discuss the occurrence of methionine toxicity in chickens and how it affects their health and behavior.
ETHIONINE TOXICITY


In this section, we will discuss the occurrence of ethionine toxicity and the mechanisms by which it leads to various health problems. We will also discuss the potential benefits of using ethionine as a therapeutic agent.
CONCLUSION


In conclusion, this chapter has discussed the different aspects of amino acid toxicity and the mechanisms by which they lead to various health problems. We have also discussed potential therapeutic strategies for alleviating these problems and the potential benefits of using amino acids as therapeutic agents. Further research is needed to better understand the mechanisms of amino acid toxicity and to develop effective treatments for these conditions.

title: Mechanism and regulation of DNA end resection in eukaryotes.
text: The repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) through homologous recombination (HR) is triggered by the degradation of the 5' ends of the DNA strands through a process termed end resection. End resection produces 3' single-stranded DNA tails, which serve as substrates for enzymes such as Rad51, leading to homologous pairing and DNA strand exchange, and activation of the DNA damage checkpoint. The prevailing view on end resection suggests that it occurs through a two-step mechanism. The first step involves the activation of the Mre11-Rad50-Xrs2/Nbs1 (MRX/N) complex, which endonucleolytically cleaves the 5' ends of the DNA strands close to the break sites, and the second step involves the extension of the resected tracts by Exo1 and/or Dna2 nucleases, resulting in the formation of long 3' single-stranded DNA overhangs. The initiation of end resection carries significant implications, as it leads to the choice of repair pathway. In this review, I will discuss recent findings on the mechanisms of end resection and their regulation to ensure the most appropriate repair outcome.

title: Multiple-dose activated charcoal in acute self-poisoning: a randomised controlled trial
text:
The background of intentional self-poisoning in rural developing areas is significantly higher than in industrialized countries, primarily due to the use of toxic pesticides and plants. In an effort to assess the effectiveness of routine treatment with multiple-dose activated charcoal, we conducted an open-label, parallel group, randomized, controlled trial in three Sri Lankan hospitals.
We randomly assigned 4632 patients to receive no charcoal (n=1554), one dose of charcoal (n=1545), or six doses of charcoal (n=1533). Of these, 2338 (51%) had ingested pesticides, while 1647 (36%) had ingested yellow oleander seeds. The primary outcome measure was mortality, and analysis was conducted using intention to treat. The trial was registered with controlled-trials.com as ISRCTN02920054.
Our findings revealed that mortality did not differ between the groups. Specifically, 97 (6.3%) of 1531 participants in the multiple-dose group died, compared to 105 (6.8%) of 1554 in the no charcoal group (adjusted odds ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.70-1.33). We did not observe any significant differences in mortality between patients who took particular poisons, were severely ill on admission, or presented early.
In conclusion, we cannot recommend the routine use of multiple-dose activated charcoal in rural Asia Pacific. While further studies on early charcoal administration may be useful, affordable and effective treatments are urgently needed for this vulnerable population.

title: Post-prenylation-processing enzymes as new targets in oncogenesis
text: Oncogenic proteins, such as RAS, undergo a series of complex post-translational modifications starting with the addition of an isoprenoid lipid through prenylation. Following prenylation, these proteins are typically processed by the RCE1 protease and then undergo carboxyl methylation via the unique methyltransferase isoprenylcysteine carboxyl methyltransferase (ICMT). While inhibitors targeting the prenylation step are in advanced-stage clinical trials, their effectiveness appears limited. Recent findings suggest that inhibiting the post-prenylation-processing steps, particularly ICMT-catalyzed methylation, may offer a better approach to controlling cancer cell proliferation.

title: Trends in sugar-sweetened beverage consumption among youth and adults in the United States: 1999-2010.
text:
Reducing sugar-sweetened beverage (SSB) consumption is a recommended strategy for promoting optimal health. In this study, we aimed to investigate trends in SSB consumption among youth and adults in the United States using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) between 1999 and 2010.
We analyzed the energy intake from SSBs among 22,367 youth aged 2-19 years and 29,133 adults aged ≥20 years who participated in a 24-hour dietary recall. SSBs included soda, fruit drinks, sports and energy drinks, sweetened coffee and tea, and other sweetened beverages. We also examined patterns of SSB consumption, including location of consumption and meal occasion associated with consumption.
Our results showed that in 2009-2010, youth consumed an average of 155 ± 7 kcal/d from SSBs, and adults consumed an age-adjusted average of 151 ± 5 kcal/d from SSBs, which was a decrease from 1999 to 2000 of 68 kcal/d and 45 kcal/d, respectively (P-trend < 0.001 for each). In 2009-2010, SSBs contributed 8.0% ± 0.4% and 6.9% ± 0.2% of daily energy intake among youth and adults, respectively, which was a decrease compared with 1999-2000 (P-trend < 0.001 for both). Decreases in SSB consumption were observed in both the home and away from home, as well as with both meals and snacks, over the 12-year study duration (P-trend < 0.01 for each).
In conclusion, our findings suggest that there was a decrease in SSB consumption among youth and adults in the United States between 1999 and 2010.

title: Ubiquitination on nonlysine residues by a viral E3 ubiquitin ligase.
text: The regulation of cellular functions by ubiquitination is extensive. The final stage of the ubiquitination pathway is controlled by enzyme type 3 (E3) ubiquitin ligases. E3 enzymes are responsible for recognizing specific substrates and forming an isopeptide bond between a lysine residue on the substrate and ubiquitin. Two E3 ubiquitin ligases encoded by Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus, MIR1 and MIR2, were found to mediate the ubiquitination of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC I) molecules and their subsequent internalization. However, this study revealed that only MIR1 promoted the down-regulation of MHC I molecules lacking lysine residues in their intracytoplasmic domain. These molecules were ubiquitinated by MIR1, and their association with ubiquitin was sensitive to beta2-mercaptoethanol, which is different from lysine-ubiquitin bonds. This form of ubiquitination required a cysteine residue in the intracytoplasmic tail of MHC I molecules. Interestingly, an MHC I molecule containing a single cysteine residue in an artificial glycine and alanine intracytoplasmic domain was also endocytosed and degraded in the presence of MIR1, indicating that ubiquitination can occur on proteins lacking visible lysines or an accessible N terminus.

title: All dosage compensation is local: Gene-by-gene regulation of sex-biased expression on the chicken Z chromosome
text:
Recent findings have revealed that birds lack a universal mechanism for balancing the dosage of genes on their Z sex chromosome. This discovery was surprising, given that all other organisms studied with sex chromosome systems have some mechanism to compensate for the differences in gene expression between males and females. However, the Z chromosome in birds shows a unique pattern of gene expression differences between males and females, suggesting that some genes may be individually compensated, while others exhibit less than global patterns of dosage compensation, such as local or temporal variations.
To investigate this phenomenon, we performed global gene expression profiling in both male and female chickens across various tissue types and life stages. Our findings showed that the degree of sex-biased gene expression on the Z chromosome varied widely, with the smallest effects observed in embryonic brain tissue and the largest in adult gonadal tissue. While there were no distinct regions of overall dosage compensation along the Z chromosome, our data suggest that the regulation of dosage compensation in birds is gene-specific and can change over time and depending on tissue type.
This regulation may be due to the critical importance of certain genes in the body, as their expression levels are tightly regulated to avoid disrupting essential pathways and networks. Overall, our findings provide insight into the complex mechanisms of sex chromosome dosage compensation in birds and highlight the importance of studying the regulation of gene expression on a genome-wide scale.

title: Hormone replacement therapy prevents bone loss in patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
text:
Patients with inflammatory bowel disease are at a higher risk of developing osteoporosis, and they experience a higher rate of spinal bone loss compared to the general population. While hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is effective in treating and preventing osteoporosis, there is limited research on its use in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. A two-year prospective study was conducted on 47 postmenopausal women with ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, aged 44 to 67 years, to evaluate the effectiveness of HRT in preventing bone loss.
Participants underwent annual measurements of radial and spinal bone density using single photon absorptiometry and quantitative computed tomography, respectively. The mean annual rate of change in radial bone density was +1.42% (95% CI: +0.58 to +2.26; P < 0.005), and for spinal bone density, it was +2.60% (95% CI: +1.06 to +4.15; P < 0.005). There was no significant correlation between the rates of change in bone density at the two sites, or between the rates of change and the initial bone density either in the radius or spine. Twelve patients received prednisolone during the study, and their rates of change in spinal bone density were lower, but the difference was not statistically significant from those who did not receive corticosteroids. No significant differences were found in the changes in bone density between patients with ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. Additionally, there was no correlation between the change in bone density and the patients' age or number of years after menopause.
The study concluded that HRT is effective in preventing bone loss in postmenopausal women with inflammatory bowel disease.

title: Disruption of the 5S RNP–Mdm2 interaction significantly improves the erythroid defect in a mouse model for Diamond-Blackfan anemia
text:
Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a congenital erythroid hypoplasia resulting from haploinsufficiency of genes encoding ribosomal proteins (RPs). Disturbances in ribosome biogenesis in DBA have been shown to trigger a p53-mediated ribosomal stress response, but the underlying mechanisms of p53 activation and their relevance to the erythroid defect remain unclear. Earlier studies indicate that inhibition of mouse double minute 2 (Mdm2), the primary negative regulator of p53, by the 5S ribonucleoprotein particle (RNP) may trigger p53 activation. However, it is unsure whether this mechanism solely accounts for the p53-dependent aspect of DBA.
To investigate this further, we crossed our mouse model for RPS19-deficient DBA with Mdm2C305F knock-in mice, which have a disrupted 5S RNP–Mdm2 interaction. When we induced the Rps19 deficiency, Mdm2C305F reversed the p53 response and augmented the expansion of hematopoietic progenitors in vitro and improved anemia in vivo. Unsurprisingly, disrupting the 5S RNP–Mdm2 interaction also led to a selective deficit in erythropoiesis. Our findings highlight the sensitivity of erythroid progenitor cells to disturbances in p53 homeostasis mediated by the 5S RNP–Mdm2 interaction. Lastly, we provide evidence suggesting that physiological activation of the 5S RNP-Mdm2-p53 pathway may contribute to a decline in hematopoietic function in a cell-autonomous manner over time.

title: Pharmacist participation on physician rounds and adverse drug events in the intensive care unit.
text:
A study has been conducted to investigate the effectiveness of pharmacist participation on medical rounds in a medical intensive care unit (ICU) in reducing adverse drug events (ADEs) caused by ordering errors. The study compared the rate of preventable ADEs before and after the implementation of a pharmacist intervention in the ICU, with a control unit that did not receive the intervention.
The study found that the rate of preventable ADEs due to ordering errors decreased by 66% after the intervention, from 10.4 per 1000 patient-days before the intervention to 3.5 per 1000 patient-days after the intervention (P<.001). In contrast, the control unit saw a slight increase in the rate of preventable ADEs during the same time periods. The pharmacist made 366 recommendations related to drug ordering, of which 362 (99%) were accepted by physicians.
The study's findings suggest that the presence of a pharmacist on rounds as a full member of the patient care team in a medical ICU was associated with a substantially lower rate of ADEs caused by prescribing errors. The study demonstrates that pharmacist participation in medical rounds can be an effective strategy to reduce ADEs in the ICU setting.

title: Ligand-target interactions: what can we learn from NMR?
text: The conformation of a ligand in complex with a large macromolecular target can be investigated using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques in solution across a range of binding strengths. Tightly binding complexes (k(off) < 10(4) Hz) are typically accessible only for smaller complexes (<100 kDa), while weakly binding complexes (k(off) > 10(4) Hz) can be studied for larger complexes (>100 kDa) using NMR methods. In this review, I will discuss the state-of-the-art NMR techniques used for screening ligands and investigating bound ligand conformations in both tight and weak binding regimes. I will critically evaluate the advantages and limitations of each approach and highlight recent advances in NMR methodology for investigating transiently forming complexes. Particular attention will be paid to novel methods for determining bound ligand conformations, such as transferred cross-correlated relaxation, which provide new opportunities for understanding ligand-target interactions. The epothilone-tubulin complex will serve as a primary example throughout the review.

title: MotifMap: integrative genome-wide maps of regulatory motif sites for model species
text:
A key challenge in biology is to comprehensively map and understand the regulation of genes across an entire genome. So far, only a small fraction of the regulatory elements embedded in the DNA sequence of a genome have been identified, and there is a need for computational methods to systematically identify and analyze these elements. However, the sheer size of non-coding regions and the complex, Statistical variations in regulatory elements and interactions pose significant challenges to these efforts. Currently, there are no genome-wide catalogs of regulatory elements available for any model species.
The MotifMap system uses databases of transcription factor binding motifs, refined genome alignments, and a comparative genomic statistical approach to generate comprehensive maps of candidate regulatory elements in the genomes of model species. The system has been used to generate new genome-wide maps for yeast, fly, worm, mouse, and human, with the human map containing 519,108 sites for 570 matrices with a False Discovery Rate of 0.1 or less. The accuracy and coverage of the maps are assessed using high-throughput experimental ChIP-seq data and AUC statistics, providing strong evidence for their validity. The maps can be integrated with many other types of omic data and are available at http://motifmap.igb.uci.edu/.
The MotifMap system represents a significant step forward in the analysis of gene regulation on a genome-wide scale. By providing a foundation for analyzing regulatory pathways and generating hypotheses, MotifMap has the potential to significantly advance our understanding of gene regulation. As examples, the P53 apoptotic pathway and the Gli hedgehog pathways are discussed in detail, demonstrating the power of this approach.

title: Inhibition of apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter as a novel treatment for diabetes.
text: Bile acids have been shown to modulate metabolic processes, and the present study aimed to investigate the effects of a potent Asbt inhibitor (264W94) on glucose homeostasis in Zucker Diabetic Fatty (ZDF) rats. Oral administration of 264W94 for two weeks led to increased fecal bile acid concentrations and elevated non-fasting plasma total Glp-1 levels. Treatment with 264W94 significantly decreased HbA1c and glucose levels, and prevented the typical drop in insulin levels seen in ZDF rats. An oral glucose tolerance test revealed up to two-fold increases in plasma total Glp-1 and three-fold increases in insulin in 264W94-treated ZDF rats at doses that achieved glycemic control. Tissue mRNA analysis showed a decrease in farnesoid X receptor (Fxr) activation in small intestines and the liver, but co-administration of a Fxr agonist (GW4064) did not attenuate the glucose-lowering effects of 264W94. These results suggest that inhibition of Asbt increases bile acids in the distal intestine, promotes Glp-1 release, and may represent a novel therapeutic approach for type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: Early chromatin unfolding by RUNX1: a molecular explanation for differential requirements during specification versus maintenance of the hematopoietic gene expression program.
text:
At the cellular level, development progresses through distinct regulatory phases, each characterized by a unique gene expression profile. However, the molecular mechanisms controlling the initiation and maintenance of gene expression within a particular developmental pathway are still poorly understood. The hematopoietic system offers a powerful experimental model to address these questions, and our study has focused on a critical regulatory circuit involved in myelopoiesis: the transcription factor PU.1, its target gene colony-stimulating-factor 1 receptor (Csf1r), and upstream regulators such as RUNX1.
Our findings reveal that during ontogeny, the process of chromatin unfolding precedes the establishment of active histone marks and the formation of stable transcription factor complexes at the Pu.1 locus. We discovered that chromatin remodeling in this process is mediated by the transient binding of RUNX1 to specific cis-elements in the Pu.1 locus. In contrast, the chromatin reorganization of Csf1r requires the prior expression of PU.1 and the binding of RUNX1 to specific cis-elements. Once the full hematopoietic program is established, stable transcription factor complexes and active chromatin can be maintained without the presence of RUNX1.
Our experiments demonstrate how individual transcription factors function in a stage-specific manner to differentially regulate the initiation versus maintenance of a developmental program. This study highlights the complex interplay between transcription factors and chromatin structures during development and underscores the importance of understanding these mechanisms to elucidate the underlying basis of developmental disorders.

title: Whole-genome fingerprint of the DNA methylome during human B cell differentiation
text: In this study, we employed whole-genome bisulfite sequencing and high-density microarrays to investigate the DNA methylome of ten subpopulations spanning the entire B cell differentiation program. Our findings revealed that non-CpG methylation was eliminated upon B cell commitment, whereas CpG methylation exhibited extensive alterations during B cell maturation, with an accumulative pattern and affecting approximately 30% of all measured CpG sites. Enhancer demethylation was prevalent in early differentiation stages, which was accompanied by the upregulation of key B cell transcription factors and impacted multiple genes involved in B cell biology. In contrast, late differentiation stages displayed widespread demethylation of heterochromatin and methylation gain at Polycomb-repressed areas, with minimal impact on genes with apparent functional significance in B cells. This signature, which has previously been linked to aging and cancer, was particularly pronounced in mature cells with an extended lifespan. By comparing B cell neoplasms with their normal counterparts, we identified that these malignancies frequently acquire methylation alterations in regions that are already undergoing dynamic methylation during normal B cell differentiation.

title: LIN28B induces neuroblastoma and enhances MYCN levels via let-7 suppression
text: LIN28B controls the progression of development by influencing microRNAs (miRNAs) of the let-7 family. Although a role for LIN28B in cancer has been suggested, its involvement has yet to be confirmed in animal models. Our study uncovers extraordinary genomic alterations and overexpression of LIN28B in high-risk neuroblastoma relative to other tumor types and normal tissues. High levels of LIN28B expression acted as an independent predictor of unfavorable outcomes in neuroblastoma. LIN28B dampened let-7 miRNAs, which ultimately promoted elevated MYCN protein levels in neuroblastoma cells. The LIN28B–let-7–MYCN signaling pathway impeded the differentiation of both normal neuroblasts and neuroblastoma cells. These findings were precisely recapitulated in a mouse model involving LIN28B expression in the sympathetic adrenergic lineage, which resulted in the development of neuroblastomas displaying low let-7 miRNA levels and high MYCN protein expression. Targeting this pathway may offer potential therapeutic strategies.

title: Platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor expression correlates with tumour angiogenesis and prognosis in non-small-cell lung cancer.
text:
Recently, angiogenesis has been identified as a prognostic factor in non-small-cell lung cancer. Platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor (PD-ECGF), which is actually the enzyme thymidine phosphorylase (TP), promotes angiogenesis in both in vitro and in vivo settings. High levels of the enzyme within cancer cells are linked to increased sensitivity to pyrimidine antimetabolites.
To investigate PD-ECGF/TP expression in non-small-cell lung cancer, immunohistochemical analysis was conducted on surgically resected tumor samples from 107 patients. About one quarter (25%) of the cases showed high expression of PD-ECGF/TP, which was significantly associated with high vascular grade (P = 0.01). In particular, 44% of high vascular grade tumors showed positive reactivity for PD-ECGF/TP, compared to 17% of low/medium vascular grade tumors. Moreover, the expression of PD-ECGF/TP was more frequent in T2-staged cases than in T1 cases (P = 0.04).
While overall survival was not significantly impacted (P = 0.09), subgroup analysis revealed that node-negative patients with positive PD-ECGF/TP expression had a worse prognosis (P = 0.04). These findings suggest that PD-ECGF/TP may be a key player in angiogenesis in non-small-cell lung cancer, with up-regulation of the enzyme defining a more aggressive tumor phenotype in node-negative disease. Considering the vascular grade and PD-ECGF/TP expression in the design of randomized trials assessing the role of adjuvant chemotherapy in non-small-cell lung cancer may therefore be important.

title: The association between psychological distance and construal level: evidence from an implicit association test.
text: According to construal level theory (N. Liberman, Y. Trope, & E. Stephan, in press; Y. Trope & N. Liberman, 2003), people tend to adopt a more abstract, high construal level when judging, perceiving, and predicting more distant objects or targets, and they perceive more distant targets as being psychologically further away. In a series of experiments using the Implicit Association Test (IAT; A. G. Greenwald, D. E. McGhee, & J. L. K. Schwartz, 1998), the present research showed that there is a correlation between the level of construal and the perceived psychological distance of a target, with higher construal levels being associated with more distant targets. These findings not only support the theory but also demonstrate that all four dimensions of psychological distance (temporal, spatial, social, and hypothetical) are related to level of construal in a similar manner.

title: A load driver device for engineering modularity in biological networks
text: The unpredictable behavior of gene modules in sophisticated synthetic circuits can be mitigated with the use of a genetic device known as a load driver. This invention addresses the challenge of downstream elements imposing a burden on upstream modules, which can negatively impact circuit function. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the load driver in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, showing that it restores the ability of a slower transcriptional circuit to respond to time-varying input signals even in the presence of significant load. Without the load driver, we observed a 76% delay in response time and a 25% decrease in system bandwidth due to load. In contrast, the addition of a load driver almost completely restored circuit performance. The load driver serves as a fundamental building block in the construction of more complex, higher-level genetic circuits.

title: Inflammatory monocyte/macrophage modulation by liposome-entrapped spironolactone ameliorates acute lung injury in mice.
text:
Objective: To investigate the therapeutic and preventive potential of liposome-encapsulated spironolactone (Lipo-SP) in acute lung injury (ALI) and fibrosis.
Materials and Methods: Lipo-SP was prepared using the film-ultrasonic method and characterized for oral administration (10 and 20 mg/kg for SP-loaded liposome; 20 mg/kg for free SP) in a mouse model of bleomycin-induced ALI.
Results: Lipo-SP significantly enhanced the bioavailability of spironolactone and improved lung pathology. Mechanistically, spironolactone-mediated mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism contributed to inflammatory monocyte/macrophage modulation through an inhibitory effect on Ly6C(hi) monocytosis-directed M2 polarization of alveolar macrophages. Additionally, Lipo-SP exhibited more improvement in body weight gain at a lower dose (10 mg/kg).
Conclusion: These findings suggest that Lipo-SP has therapeutic and preventive potential for ALI and fibrosis, highlighting its promise as a promising approach in treating these conditions.

title: Passive Surveillance for I. scapularis Ticks: Enhanced Analysis for Early Detection of Emerging Lyme Disease Risk
text: Lyme disease (LD) is expanding in Canada due to the northward range of the tick vector, Ixodes scapularis (Say). Early detection of emerging LD areas is crucial for public health responses, but existing methods lack specificity for identifying areas with established tick populations. Passive tick surveillance has been conducted in Canada since 1990; however, this method is less effective in detecting areas where ticks are dispersed by migratory birds. Using data from 70 field sites in Quebec, we developed a logistic regression model to estimate the risk of I. scapularis population establishment based on the number of ticks submitted in passive surveillance and an environmentally derived index. We used sensitivity-specificity plots to select the optimal threshold value of the linear predictor from the model as the signal for tick population establishment. This value was used to produce an "Alert Map" identifying areas where passive surveillance data suggested ticks were establishing in Quebec. The predictions were validated by field surveillance at 76 sites, revealing a significant difference in the prevalence of established I. scapularis populations between areas predicted as high-risk (29 out of 48) and moderate-risk (4 out of 30) (P < 0.001). This study suggests that Alert Maps generated using this approach can provide a rapid and accurate tool for identifying emerging areas of LD risk at a suitable geographic scale for local disease control and prevention initiatives.

title: Reduction of transmission from malaria patients by artemisinin combination therapies: a pooled analysis of six randomized trials
text:
BACKGROUND: Artemisinin combination therapies (ACT) are increasingly being used to treat Plasmodium falciparum malaria, and they have been shown to be more effective against sexual stage parasites (gametocytes) than previous first-line antimalarials. This could potentially reduce parasite transmission. The goal of this study was to investigate the effect of ACT on the infectiousness of individual patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
METHODS: Data from six antimalarial trials conducted in The Gambia and Kenya were pooled, involving a total of 3,174 patients. Multivariable regression was used to examine the role of ACT versus non-artemisinin antimalarial treatment, treatment failure, pre-treatment gametocytes, and submicroscopic gametocytaemia on transmission to mosquitoes and the area under the curve (AUC) of gametocyte density during the 28-day follow-up period.
RESULTS: Treatment with ACT was associated with a significant reduction in the probability of being gametocytaemic on the day of transmission experiments (odds ratio [OR] 0.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.16-0.26), transmission to mosquitoes by slide-positive gametocyte carriers (OR mosquito infection 0.49, 95% CI 0.33-0.73), and the AUC of gametocyte density (ratio of means 0.35, 95% CI 0.31-0.41). Treatment failure did not account for the difference between ACT and non-artemisinin impact. The presence of slide-positive gametocytaemia prior to treatment significantly reduced the impact of ACT on gametocytaemia (p < 0.001). When submicroscopic gametocytaemia was taken into account, the estimates of ACT impact were reduced in a high transmission setting in Kenya, but not in a lower transmission setting in the Gambia.
CONCLUSION: Treatment with ACT significantly reduces the infectiousness of individual patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria compared to previous first-line treatments. Rapid treatment of cases before gametocytaemia is well developed may enhance the impact of ACT on transmission.

title: Skeletal Myogenic Progenitors Originating from Embryonic Dorsal Aorta Coexpress Endothelial and Myogenic Markers and Contribute to Postnatal Muscle Growth and Regeneration
text: In vertebrates, skeletal muscle is derived from somites, which are structures in the paraxial mesoderm. However, there have been reports of myogenic cells originating from non-somite tissues, suggesting either cell transdifferentiation or the presence of a multipotent progenitor cell population. To investigate this further, we analyzed clonal cells from various developmental stages of mouse embryos, and found that clonable skeletal myogenic cells are present in the embryonic dorsal aorta. In vitro, these cells exhibit the same morphology as satellite cells derived from adult skeletal muscle and express a range of myogenic and endothelial markers. Interestingly, adult satellite cells also express these same markers. We were able to isolate and culture myogenic cells from limbs of c-Met-/- embryos, which lack appendicular muscles but have a normal vascular system. Upon transplantation, these cells participated in postnatal muscle growth and regeneration and fused with resident satellite cells. Our findings suggest that the vascular system may have the potential to generate skeletal muscle cells, which could explain observations of nonsomite skeletal myogenesis and raise the possibility that a subset of satellite cells may originate from the vascular system.

title: Mapping of a gene for severe pediatric gastroesophageal reflux to chromosome 13q14.
text: Gastroesophageal reflux (GER), a condition previously not widely regarded as a hereditary disease, has been found to have a genetic component, particularly in its severe or chronic forms, according to a few reports. To identify a genetic locus that cosegregates with a severe pediatric GER phenotype in families with multiple affected members, a genome-wide scan using polymorphic microsatellite markers spaced at an average of 8 centimorgans (cM) was conducted on five families. The settting for the study was a general US community, with research performed in a university tertiary care hospital. The study included affected and unaffected family members from 5 families identified through a patient support group. The inheritance pattern of GER was found to be autosomal dominant with high penetrance. A gene for severe pediatric GER was mapped to a 13-cM region on chromosome 13q between microsatellite markers D13S171 and D13S263. A maximum multifamily 2-point lod score of 5.58 and a maximum multifamily multipoint lod score of 7.15 were obtained for marker D13S1253 at map position 35 cM when presumptively affected persons were modeled as unknown (a maximum multipoint score of 4.88 was obtained when presumptively affected persons were modeled as unaffected). These findings suggest that a gene for severe pediatric GER maps to chromosome 13q14.

title: Accelerating Policy Decisions to Adopt Haemophilus influenzae Type b Vaccine: A Global, Multivariable Analysis
text:
Adopting new and underutilized vaccines is crucial to reduce child mortality globally. However, policy decisions to adopt these vaccines often lag behind those in high-income countries. This study investigates the reasons for these delays by analyzing economic, epidemiological, programmatic, and policy-related factors, as well as the role of the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunisation (GAVI Alliance).
Using data from 147 countries between 1990 and 2007, we employed accelerated failure time models to identify factors associated with the time to decision to adopt Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine. Our findings reveal that the receipt of GAVI support significantly accelerated the time to decision by a factor of 0.37 (95% CI 0.18-0.76), corresponding to a 63% reduction in the time taken. Additionally, the presence of two or more neighboring country adopters of Hib vaccine accelerated decisions to adopt by a factor of 0.50 (95% CI 0.33-0.75). Conversely, a 1% increase in vaccine price was associated with a 1.02-fold (95% CI 1.00-1.04) delay in decisions to adopt. Global recommendations and local studies were not found to influence the time to decision.
Our study corroborates previous findings on the impact of vaccine price on adoption decisions and introduces new insights into the role of neighboring country adoption and GAVI eligibility. These findings suggest that supply- and demand-side factors, including GAVI eligibility and regional dynamics, should be considered in approaches to support the adoption of new vaccines.

title: Haemolysin coregulated protein is an exported receptor and chaperone of type VI secretion substrates.
text: The efficient secretion of substrates in cells requires high-fidelity mechanisms to distinguish among the vast pool of proteins in the cytoplasm. While the factors that mediate substrate recognition by the type VI secretion system (T6SS) of Gram-negative bacteria have yet to be fully understood, we have made significant progress in uncovering the underlying mechanisms. Specifically, we have found that Haemolysin coregulated protein (Hcp), a ring-shaped hexamer secreted by all characterized T6SSs, selectively binds to specific cognate effector molecules. By using electron microscopy analysis, we were able to reveal the bound effector protein on the inner surface of Hcp. Subsequent studies led us to conclude that interaction with the Hcp pore is a universal requirement for the secretion of diverse effectors, encompassing multiple enzymatic classes. While previous models depicted Hcp as a static conduit, our findings indicate that it plays a more active role as a chaperone and receptor of substrates. These discoveries highlight striking differences in the export mechanism of T6SS compared to other characterized secretory pathways.

title: Long-term effects of continuing adjuvant tamoxifen to 10 years versus stopping at 5 years after diagnosis of oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer: ATLAS, a randomised trial
text:
Here is a rewritten version of the text in a more formal and structured style:
Background: For women with oestrogen receptor (ER)-positive early breast cancer, treatment with tamoxifen for 5 years has been shown to substantially reduce breast cancer mortality rates throughout the first 15 years after diagnosis. This study aimed to assess the further effects of continuing tamoxifen treatment to 10 years instead of stopping at 5 years. Methods: In the worldwide Adjuvant Tamoxifen: Longer Against Shorter (ATLAS) trial, 12,894 women with early breast cancer who had completed 5 years of tamoxifen treatment were randomly assigned to continue treatment to 10 years or stop at 5 years (open control). The allocation was carried out by central computer using minimisation. Annual follow-up forms recorded any recurrence, second cancer, hospital admission, or death. Results: Among the 6846 women with ER-positive disease, allocation to continue tamoxifen treatment reduced the risk of breast cancer recurrence (617 recurrences in 3428 women vs 711 in 3418 controls, p=0.002), breast cancer mortality (331 deaths vs 397 deaths, p=0.01), and overall mortality (639 deaths vs 722 deaths, p=0.01). The reductions in adverse breast cancer outcomes appeared to be less extreme before than after year 10 (recurrence rate ratio [RR] 0.90 [95% CI 0.79-1.02] during years 5-9 and 0.75 [0.62-0.90] in later years; breast cancer mortality RR 0.97 [0.79-1.18] during years 5-9 and 0.71 [0.58-0.88] in later years). The cumulative risk of recurrence during years 5-14 was 21.4% for women assigned to continue versus 25.1% for controls; breast cancer mortality during years 5-14 was 12.2% for women assigned to continue versus 15.0% for controls (absolute mortality reduction 2.8%). Conclusion: For women with ER-positive disease, continuing tamoxifen treatment to 10 years can approximately halve breast cancer mortality during the second decade after diagnosis. Further investigation is needed to confirm the findings of this study.
Here are the key points of the study:
* Continuing tamoxifen treatment beyond 5 years in women with ER-positive early breast cancer reduces the risk of breast cancer recurrence, mortality, and overall mortality.
* The reduction in adverse breast cancer outcomes appears to decrease after year 10.
* The study suggests that for women with ER-positive disease, extending tamoxifen treatment to 10 years can approximately halve breast cancer mortality during the second decade after diagnosis.

Please note that the translation of the original text to a more structured and formal style may result in some loss of readability, as the rewritten text may appear more stilted and less conversational.

title: Roles for MicroRNAs in Conferring Robustness to Biological Processes
text: Biological systems employ a range of mechanisms to maintain their functional integrity in the face of environmental and genetic changes. Recent findings indicate that microRNAs (miRNAs), which typically act as post-transcriptional regulators of gene expression, play a crucial role in enhancing the robustness of biological processes by strengthening transcriptional programs and reducing excessive gene expression. In certain situations, miRNAs may also help to mitigate stochastic fluctuations in transcript copy number. These activities have significant implications for normal development, physiology, disease, and evolution. In this discussion, we will explore examples and underlying principles of how miRNAs contribute to robustness in animal systems.

title: Six-Year Follow-Up of Impact of Co-proxamol Withdrawal in England and Wales on Prescribing and Deaths: Time-Series Study
text:
BACKGROUND: The pain-relieving medication co-proxamol (a combination of paracetamol and dextropropoxyphene) has been associated with a significant number of fatal poisoning cases. Concerns about its safety and effectiveness profile led to its withdrawal from the market in the UK in 2005, with a partial withdrawal between 2005 and 2007, and full withdrawal in 2008. Our study aimed to evaluate the impact of co-proxamol withdrawal on deaths resulting from poisoning in England and Wales between 2005 and 2010, compared to the period 1998-2004.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: We analyzed prescribing data from the NHS Health and Social Care Information Centre (England) and Prescribing Services Partnership Cydwasanaethau GIG Cymru (Wales) and mortality data from the Office for National Statistics. Using an interrupted time-series analysis, we assessed changes in prescribing patterns and deaths involving single analgesics. Following the withdrawal of co-proxamol in 2005, there was a significant reduction in prescribing of this drug. In contrast, prescribing of other analgesics such as co-codamol, paracetamol, codeine, co-dydramol, tramadol, oxycodone, and morphine increased during the study period. These changes were associated with a major reduction in deaths involving co-proxamol, particularly those with suicidal verdicts (-21 deaths per quarter, approximately 500 fewer suicide deaths over 6 years). There were also reductions in accidental poisoning deaths involving co-proxamol (-25 deaths per quarter, approximately 600 fewer deaths over 6 years). However, there was no significant increase in deaths involving other analgesics. Limitations of the study included the focus on deaths involving single drugs and the inability to assess changes in deaths involving prescribed morphine.
CONCLUSIONS: Following the withdrawal of co-proxamol in the UK, there was a significant decrease in poisoning deaths involving this drug, without a corresponding increase in deaths involving other analgesics. These findings suggest that the withdrawal of co-proxamol led to a major reduction in poisoning deaths, highlighting the importance of carefully monitoring and managing the use of pain-relieving medications to minimize the risk of fatal poisoning.

title: Apolipoprotein E genotype and concussion in college athletes.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the association between genetic variations in the apolipoprotein E (APOE) gene and the history of concussions in college athletes. Specifically, we hypothesized that carrying one or more rare or minor alleles of the APOE gene would be associated with a higher likelihood of having a history of concussions.
Design: A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted at university athletic facilities.
Participants: One hundred ninety-six male football (n = 163) and female soccer (n = 33) college athletes voluntarily participated in the study.
Methods: Participants completed a written questionnaire regarding their history of concussions and provided saliva samples for genotyping.
Results: Our results showed a significant association between carrying all three rare alleles of the APOE gene and a history of previous concussions (odds ratio = 9.8, χ² = 3.82, P = 0.05). Additionally, there was a significant association between carrying the promoter minor allele and experiencing 2 or more concussions (odds ratio = 8.4, χ² = 3.96, P = 0.04).
Conclusions: Carriers of all three rare APOE alleles in this study were nearly 10 times more likely to report a previous concussion and may be at a greater risk of concussion compared to non-carriers. Additionally, promoter minor allele carriers were 8.4 times more likely to report multiple concussions and may be at a greater risk of multiple concussions compared to non-carriers. Further research involving larger samples of individuals with multiple concussions and carriers of multiple APOE rare alleles is warranted.

title: Plasma soluble corin and N-terminal pro-atrial natriuretic peptide levels in pregnancy induced hypertension.
text:
Objective: One of the theories proposed to explain the development of pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH) involves the retention of salt and water in the body. In this study, we aimed to measure the proenzyme convertase corin, which is responsible for cleaving pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) to active ANP, in the plasma of hypertensive pregnant women.
Study Design: We recruited 60 pregnant women with PIH in their second or third trimester of pregnancy and compared them to 28 healthy pregnant women of the same gestational age. Concurrent urine and plasma samples were collected for the determination of various biochemical parameters. Plasma soluble corin and N-terminal (NT) pro-ANP (1-98) levels were measured in both groups using enzyme immunoassays.
Results: Our results showed that the mean plasma soluble corin level was significantly higher in the patient group compared to the control group. Moreover, the mean plasma NT pro-ANP value was significantly higher in the group with blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg compared to the group with blood pressure <140/90 mmHg and the control group.
Conclusions: These findings suggest that hypertensive pregnant women, particularly those with blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg, may have an ANP receptor/post-receptor signaling defect, which could exacerbate their pregnancy-induced hypertensive state.

title: GATA-4 and GATA-6 modulate tissue-specific transcription of the human gene for P450c17 by direct interaction with Sp1.
text:
Cytochrome P450c17 catalyzes the activities of steroidogenic 17α-hydroxylase and 17,20 lyase. The expression of the P450c17 gene is cAMP-dependent, tissue-specific, developmentally programmed, and varies among species.
