text: Gene sequences collected at different points in time can be used to construct molecular phylogenies on a natural timescale of months or years, providing the sequences exhibit measurable evolutionary changes between sampling instances. Data sets with this characteristic are referred to as heterochronous and have become more prevalent in various fields of biology, particularly in the molecular epidemiology of rapidly evolving viruses. To visualize and analyze temporally sampled sequence data, we have developed the cross-platform software tool, TempEst (previously known as Path-O-Gen). Given a molecular phylogeny and the sampling dates of each sequence, TempEst uses an interactive regression approach to explore the association between genetic divergence over time and sampling dates. TempEst can help answer two main questions: (1) determine if there is sufficient temporal information in the data to conduct phylogenetic molecular clock analysis, and (2) identify sequences whose genetic divergence and sampling date are incongruent. Analyzing the latter can help detect data quality issues, including errors in data annotation, sample contamination, sequence recombination, or alignment errors. We recommend that users of the molecular clock models implemented in BEAST first check their data using TempEst before conducting analysis.

title: Diabetes treatments and risk of amputation, blindness, severe kidney failure, hyperglycaemia, and hypoglycaemia: open cohort study in primary care
text:
Objective: To assess the risks of amputation, blindness, severe kidney failure, hyperglycaemia, and hypoglycaemia in patients with type 2 diabetes treated with various medications, including newer agents such as gliptins and glitazones (thiazolidinediones).
Design: Open cohort study in primary care setting.
Setting: 1243 practices contributing data to the QResearch database in England.
Participants: 469,688 patients with type 2 diabetes aged 25-84 years between 1 April 2007 and 31 January 2015.
Exposures: Hypoglycaemic agents (glitazones, gliptins, metformin, sulphonylureas, insulin, and other) alone and in combination.
Main Outcome Measures: First recorded diagnoses of amputation, blindness, severe kidney failure, hyperglycaemia, and hypoglycaemia recorded on patients' primary care, mortality, or hospital records.
Cox models estimated hazard ratios for diabetes treatments adjusting for potential confounders.
Results:
* 21,308 (4.5%) and 32,533 (6.9%) patients received prescriptions for glitazones and gliptins during follow-up, respectively.
* Compared with non-use, glitazones were associated with a decreased risk of blindness (adjusted hazard ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.57 to 0.89; rate 14.4 per 10,000 person years of exposure) and an increased risk of hypoglycaemia (1.22, 1.10 to 1.37; 65.1).
* Gliptins were associated with a decreased risk of hypoglycaemia (0.86, 0.77 to 0.96; 45.8).
* Although the numbers of patients prescribed gliptin monotherapy or glitazones monotherapy were relatively low, there were significantly increased risks of severe kidney failure compared with metformin monotherapy (adjusted hazard ratio 2.55, 95% confidence interval 1.13 to 5.74).
* We found significantly lower risks of hyperglycaemia among patients prescribed dual therapy involving metformin with either gliptins (0.78, 0.62 to 0.97) or glitazones (0.60, 0.45 to 0.80) compared with metformin monotherapy.
* Patients prescribed triple therapy with metformin, sulphonylureas, and either gliptins (adjusted hazard ratio 5.07, 95% confidence interval 4.28 to 6.00) or glitazones (6.32, 5.35 to 7.45) had significantly higher risks of hypoglycaemia than those prescribed metformin monotherapy, but these risks were similar to those involving dual therapy with metformin and sulphonylureas (6.03, 5.47 to 6.63).
* Patients prescribed triple therapy with metformin, sulphonylureas, and glitazones had a significantly reduced risk of blindness compared with metformin monotherapy (0.67, 0.48 to 0.94).

Conclusions:
* Lower risks of hyperglycaemia were found among patients prescribed dual therapy involving metformin with either gliptins or glitazones compared with metformin alone.
* Compared with metformin monotherapy, triple therapy with metformin, sulphonylureas, and either gliptins or glitazones was associated with an increased risk of hypoglycaemia, which was similar to the risk for dual therapy with metformin and sulphonylureas.
* Compared with metformin monotherapy, triple therapy with metformin, sulphonylureas, and glitazones was associated with a reduced risk of blindness.
These results, while subject to residual confounding, could have implications for the prescribing of hypoglycaemic drugs.

title: Vertebrate rod photoreceptors express both BK and IK calcium-activated potassium channels, but only BK channels are involved in receptor potential regulation.
text: In salamander rods, the Ca(2+)-activated K(+) current (I(KCa)) serves as a crucial "clamp" on the dark membrane potential, maintaining it at its resting level. Through a combination of electrophysiological, pharmacological, and immunohistochemical approaches, we have shown that salamander rods express both large-conductance Ca(2+)- and voltage-dependent potassium (BK) channels, as well as intermediate-conductance Ca(2+)-dependent potassium (IK) channels, but not small-conductance Ca(2+)-dependent potassium channels (SK). Application of 100 nM iberiotoxin and 100 nM clotrimazole reduced net I(KCa) by 36% and 63%, respectively, while the current was unresponsive to 1 microM apamin. In contrast, anti-SK1, -SK2, and -SK3 antibodies failed to stain rod photoreceptors, while both anti-BK and -SK4/IK1 antibodies heavily stained the ellipsoid region of the inner segments of the rods. Interestingly, current-clamp experiments revealed that the strong clamping effect of total I(KCa) was lost when IbTx was applied to the bath, indicating that BK channels are the primary sources of this clamping effect on the photoreceptor membrane potential.

title: Ondansetron reduces nausea and vomiting after paediatric adenotonsillectomy.
text: The efficacy, safety, and resource utilization of a single intravenous dose of ondansetron (0.1 mg/kg, maximum 4 mg) were evaluated in a multinational, multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 427 children aged 1-12 years undergoing tonsillectomy with/without adenoidectomy. The study assessed the prevention of emesis (retching and/or vomiting) and nausea in the first 24 hours after surgery. Results showed that significantly more children treated with ondansetron had no episodes of emesis (60% vs 47%; P = 0.004) and experienced no postoperative nausea (64% vs 51%; P = 0.004). Ondansetron also reduced the number of emetic episodes (P < 0.001), the time to the first emetic episode (P < 0.001), and overall nausea severity (P = 0.003). Furthermore, significantly fewer ondansetron-treated children were rescued or withdrawn from the study (5% vs 10%; P = 0.042), and fewer required nursing intervention (34% vs 45%; P = 0.007). Additionally, the average intervention time was significantly shorter in the ondansetron group (4.6 vs 8.1 minutes; P = 0.001). Resource utilization was also reduced by ondansetron (43% vs 57%; P = 0.014).

title: Assessing the cost effectiveness of using prognostic biomarkers with decision models: case study in prioritising patients waiting for coronary artery surgery
text:
Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of using biomarkers to inform the prioritization process for patients with stable angina awaiting coronary artery bypass graft surgery.
Design: Decision analytical model comparing four prioritization strategies without biomarkers (no formal prioritization, two urgency scores, and a risk score) and three strategies based on a risk score using biomarkers: a routinely assessed biomarker (estimated glomerular filtration rate), a novel biomarker (C reactive protein), or both. The order in which to perform coronary artery bypass grafting in a cohort of patients was determined by each prioritization strategy, and mean lifetime costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were compared.
Data sources: Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry (9935 patients with stable angina awaiting coronary artery bypass grafting and followed up for cardiovascular events after the procedure for 3.8 years), and meta-analyses of prognostic effects (relative risks) of biomarkers.
Results: The observed risk of cardiovascular events while on the waiting list for coronary artery bypass grafting was 3 per 10,000 patients per day within the first 90 days (184 events in 9935 patients). Using a cost-effectiveness threshold of $20,000-$30,000 (euro22,000-$48,000 or $32,000-$48,000) per additional QALY, a prioritization strategy using a risk score with estimated glomerular filtration rate was the most cost-effective strategy (cost per additional QALY was < $410 compared with the Ontario urgency score). The impact on population health of implementing this strategy was 800 QALYs per 100,000 patients at an additional cost of $245,000 to the National Health Service. The prioritization strategy using a risk score with C reactive protein was associated with lower QALYs and higher costs compared with a risk score using estimated glomerular filtration rate.
Conclusion: Evaluating the cost-effectiveness of prognostic biomarkers is important even when effects at an individual level are small. Formal prioritization of patients awaiting coronary artery bypass grafting using a routinely assessed biomarker (estimated glomerular filtration rate) along with simple, routinely collected clinical information was cost-effective. Prioritization strategies based on the prognostic information conferred by C reactive protein, which is not currently measured in this context, or a combination of C reactive protein and estimated glomerular filtration rate, is unlikely to be cost-effective. The widespread practice of using only implicit or informal means of clinically ordering the waiting list may be harmful and should be replaced with formal prioritization approaches.

title: Cytokine control of memory T-cell development and survival
text: Accumulating evidence suggests that cytokines play a crucial role in the differentiation of memory T cells. We track the fate of CD8+ T cells from activation to memory cell generation, identifying key checkpoints at which cytokines determine the T cell's fate. Members of the γc-cytokine family, including interleukin-7 (IL-7) and IL-15, act at each stage of the immune response to promote proliferation and survival. By doing so, these cytokines establish a stable and protective, long-lived memory CD8+ T cell pool.

title: Histone Methylation-Dependent Mechanisms Impose Ligand Dependency for Gene Activation by Nuclear Receptors
text: Nuclear receptors change their shape when bound by a ligand, which is necessary for certain proteins to switch places and turn genes on or off. It's not clear if specific epigenetic marks (chemical modifications to DNA or histones) are required for ligands to control gene activation. Our study reveals a surprising strategy that depends on specific groups of histone methyltransferases (HMTs) to ensure that only certain genes are activated in response to stimuli. These HMTs create a "histone code" that prevents unliganded nuclear receptors and other regulatory proteins from binding to gene promoters and activating genes without proper signals. To activate genes, ligands and signals must work together with specific histone demethylases, such as LSD1, to remove epigenetic marks and allow gene expression to proceed. This mechanism links an inhibitory methylation component of the histone code to a widely used strategy that prevents harmful constitutive gene activation by physiologically regulated transcription factors.

title: Human IRGM Regulates Autophagy and Its Cell-Autonomous Immunity Functions Through Mitochondria
text:
IRGM, a protein involved in human immune function, has been shown to confer protection against intracellular pathogens through an as-yet-unidentified mechanism. Our research has unexpectedly revealed a new role for IRGM: it demonstrates a unique affinity for a specific mitochondrial lipid, cardiolipin, which is translocated to mitochondria. This interaction leads to changes in mitochondrial shape and structure, ultimately resulting in the activation of autophagy.
Interestingly, we found that overexpression of a specific IRGM splice isoform, IRGMd, leads to mitochondrial depolarization and cell death, while the other splice isoform, IRGMb, does not. This suggests that IRGMd may play a role in autophagy-independent cell death, through the activation of pro-apoptotic proteins Bax and Bak.
Our findings reveal that IRGM confers protection against intracellular pathogens, such as tuberculosis, by influencing mitochondrial function and structure. Specifically, IRGM regulates mitochondrial membrane polarization and cell death, providing a novel mechanism for its protective effects. These findings also suggest that IRGM may be a potential therapeutic target for diseases characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction, such as Crohn's disease.

title: The Developmental Transcriptome of the Mosquito Aedes aegypti, an Invasive Species and Major Arbovirus Vector
text:
Mosquitoes are crucial vectors for many devastating human and animal diseases. To develop novel strategies for controlling these vectors, a deep understanding of mosquito biology is essential. Towards this end, we employed RNA-seq to gain a comprehensive view of the mosquito's transcriptome across various stages of development and in response to blood feeding. Specifically, we analyzed the transcriptome of Aedes aegypti, the primary vector for diseases like Dengue and yellow fever.
We investigated mRNA expression at 34 distinct time points throughout Aedes development, including adult somatic and germline tissues. Using polyA+ RNA-seq, we identified a total of 14,238 novel transcribed regions, corresponding to 12,597 new loci, and numerous new isoforms of previously annotated genes. Our results increase the annotated fraction of the transcribed genome by more than twofold.
Our analysis also revealed several patterns of shared gene expression and sex-specific expression. We also determined the expression profiles of small RNAs in ovaries, early embryos, testes, and adult male and female somatic tissues, leading to the identification of 38 new Aedes-specific miRNAs and ~291,000 small RNA transcribed regions. Many of these may be endogenous small-interfering RNAs and Piwi-interacting RNAs. Additionally, we highlight genes of potential interest for transgene-based vector control strategies.
Our findings have been integrated into a user-friendly genome browser located at <https://www.aedes.caltech.edu/>, with links to Vectorbase (<https://www.vectorbase.org/>). This wealth of data provides a valuable resource for researchers seeking to develop novel vector control strategies.

title: Gut microbial diversity is associated with lower arterial stiffness in women
text:
Abstract:
The relationship between the gut microbiome and arterial stiffness in middle-aged women was investigated in this study, which included 617 women from the TwinsUK cohort. The correlation between carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV), a measure of arterial stiffness, and gut microbiome composition was examined, as well as the influence of microbiome factors on PWV after accounting for serum metabolomics data and covariates. In the adjusted analyses, PWV was found to be negatively associated with gut microbiome alpha diversity, and seven operational taxonomic units were identified as being associated with PWV. The associations between microbe abundances, microbe diversity, and PWV remained significant after accounting for levels of gut-derived metabolites. Microbiome factors were found to explain 8.3% of the variance in PWV. A formal mediation analysis revealed that only a small proportion of the total effect of the gut microbiome on PWV was mediated by insulin resistance, visceral fat, and cardiovascular risk factors. In conclusion, this study suggests that targeting the gut microbiome may be a way to treat arterial ageing, as gut microbiome diversity is inversely associated with arterial stiffness in women, and the effect of the gut microbiome on PWV is minimally mediated by MetS.

title: ALS-FUS pathology revisited: singleton FUS mutations and an unusual case with both a FUS and TARDBP mutation
text:
INTRODUCTION:
Mutations in the FUS gene have been identified as a rare cause of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS-FUS), and while extensive clinical and genetic studies have been conducted, there have been limited neuropathological investigations. Recent studies have suggested a correlation between the frequency of basophilic inclusions in neurons and the rate of clinical decline, yet other studies have shown a discrepancy between the upper motor neuron features observed clinically and the associated pathology. To further elucidate the pathological features associated with FUS mutations and to investigate their correlation with mutation and/or clinical phenotype, we conducted a neuropathological study of seven cases of ALS-FUS, including cases with newly described mutations and a case with both a known FUS mutation and a truncating TARDBP mutation.
RESULTS:
Our neuropathological examination revealed basophilic and FUS inclusions in the cord of all cases, with varying densities and types of inclusions between patients. However, we observed no clear correlation between the pathology and clinical progression. Only one case showed significant motor cortical pathology despite the presence of upper motor neuron clinical features in four patients. The case with both FUS and TARDBP mutations displayed FUS-positive inclusions but no TDP-43 pathology, and instead featured unusual p62-positive, FUS-negative neuronal and glial inclusions as well as dot-like neurites.
CONCLUSIONS:
Our study confirms that ALS-FUS is primarily a lower motor neuron disease, and the pathology does not neatly correlate with clinical features or genetics. The case with both FUS and TARDBP mutations exhibits an fascinating pathological profile, which includes an uncommon p62 staining pattern. These findings suggest that the relationship between FUS mutations and ALS pathology is complex and multifaceted, and may involve multiple pathological mechanisms.

title: Coronary heart disease in south Asians overseas: a review.
text: Coronary heart disease rates have been reported to be abnormally high in populations originating from the Indian subcontinent in various parts of the world. This phenomenon is observed across different geographical locations, religions, and languages among South Asian groups. This presents a puzzle in understanding coronary heart disease, as the high rates in South Asians cannot be attributed to elevated serum cholesterol, smoking, or hypertension alone. Instead, low plasma HDL cholesterol levels, high plasma triglyceride levels, and high prevalence of non-insulin-dependent diabetes have been consistently found in South Asians living abroad, indicating an underlying state of insulin resistance. Further research is required to determine whether this metabolic disorder can explain the high rates of coronary heart disease in South Asians and to identify potential preventive measures.

title: A systematic review of parent and clinician views and perceptions that influence prescribing decisions in relation to acute childhood infections in primary care
text: Objective: To explore the perspectives of parents, clinicians, and children regarding prescribing decisions for acute childhood infections in primary care settings. Methods: A systematic review of qualitative studies, using meta-ethnographic methods to analyze the findings. Data was drawn from the included studies in an interpretive analysis. Results: A total of 15 studies met the inclusion criteria, revealing concerns among clinicians about antibiotic over-prescription. Children's views were not reported. Clinicians prescribed antibiotics when under pressure from parents or others, when they believed there was a clear clinical indication, or when they felt uncertain about clinical or social outcomes. Parents wanted antibiotics when they expected them to improve the current illness or when under pressure from daycare providers or employers. Clinicians avoided antibiotics due to concerns about adverse reactions or drug resistance, when they were certain they were not indicated, or when there was no perceived pressure from parents. Parents also wanted to avoid adverse effects of antibiotics and did not want them when they would not relieve current symptoms. Some parents preferred to avoid medication altogether. In paediatric consultations, parents sought a medical evaluation and decision, while primary care clinicians aimed for satisfied parents and short consultations. Conclusion: Antibiotic prescriptions for childhood infections in primary care often stem from "just in case" prescribing. These findings suggest that interventions that minimize clinician uncertainty regarding social or clinical outcomes and provide strategies to meet parents' needs within a short consultation are likely to reduce antibiotic prescribing.

title: Prevalent abnormal prion protein in human appendixes after bovine spongiform encephalopathy epizootic: large scale survey
text:
Objective: To conduct a follow-up survey of archived appendix samples to assess the differences in the prevalence of subclinical infection with prions before and after the BSE epizootic, and to investigate the impact of this survey on the management of blood and blood products and surgical instruments.
Design: Anonymous and irreversibly unlinked large-scale survey of archived appendix samples from 41 UK hospitals participating in the earlier survey, as well as additional hospitals in regions with lower levels of participation.
Setting: Archived appendix samples from pathology departments of 41 UK hospitals and additional hospitals in regions with lower levels of participation in the earlier survey.
Sample: 32,441 archived appendix samples fixed in formalin and embedded in paraffin, tested for the presence of abnormal prion protein (PrP).
Results: Of the 32,441 appendix samples, 16 were positive for abnormal PrP, indicating an overall prevalence of 493 per million population (95% confidence interval 282 to 801 per million). The prevalence in those born in 1941-60 (733 per million, 269 to 1596 per million) did not significantly differ from those born between 1961 and 1985 (412 per million, 198 to 758 per million) and was similar in both sexes and across the three broad geographical areas sampled. Genetic testing of the positive specimens for the genotype at PRNP codon 129 revealed a high proportion of valine homozygous individuals compared to the normal population, and a contrasting low proportion of methionine homozygous individuals, similar to the findings in confirmed clinical cases of vCJD.
Conclusions: This study corroborates previous studies and suggests a high prevalence of infection with abnormal PrP, indicating vCJD carrier status in the population compared to the 177 vCJD cases to date. These findings have important implications for the management of blood and blood products and for the handling of surgical instruments.

title: Involvement of cortical fast-spiking parvalbumin-positive basket cells in epilepsy.
text: Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABAergic) interneurons of the parvalbumin-positive fast-spiking basket cell subtype (PV INs) play a crucial role in regulating cortical network excitability and gamma oscillations, which are involved in various cognitive processes. Dysfunction or impaired development of PV INs has been linked to epilepsy in various animal models and some genetic forms of the disorder in humans. This review aims to provide an overview of the experimental evidence highlighting the role of PV INs dysfunction in epilepsy, focusing on abnormalities in the specification, migration, maturation, synaptic function, or connectivity of these interneurons. Additionally, the review considers the potential therapeutic potential of targeting PV INs within active networks or transplanting PV INs precursors in the treatment of epilepsy and its associated disorders.

title: Dynamic Gene Regulatory Networks of Human Myeloid Differentiation.
text: The reconstruction of gene regulatory networks during cell differentiation remains a difficult task, despite the availability of high-throughput gene expression and chromatin data. Here, we developed a method to derive dynamic gene regulatory networks for human myeloid differentiation using a 5-day time series of RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data. We analyzed theexpression of key transcription factors and lineage markers in HL-60 promyelocytes differentiating into macrophages, neutrophils, monocytes, and monocyte-derived macrophages. Our findings show a rapid response in transcription factor expression followed by changes in chromatin accessibility, which occur at different times, indicating that different regulatory mechanisms are involved in the differentiation process. Interestingly, we observed differences in the transcriptional and chromatin landscapes of promyelocyte-derived macrophages and monocyte-derived macrophages, even though they are exposed to the same differentiation stimulus, highlighting the importance of the path taken by cells during differentiation in determining their end cell state. Our approach of combining neighboring time points and replicates can efficiently infer footprint-based regulatory networks from long time series data, providing valuable insights into the complex processes of cell differentiation.

title: Canonical transient receptor potential 5 channel in conjunction with Orai1 and STIM1 allows Sr2+ entry, optimal influx of Ca2+, and degranulation in a rat mast cell line.
text: The response of mast cells to agonists such as Ag or the calcium mobilizing agent, thapsigargin, is dependent on the emptying of intracellular calcium stores and the subsequent influx of external calcium, also known as store-operated calcium entry. However, it is unlikely that the calcium release-activated calcium channel is the sole mechanism for calcium entry because other divalent cations, such as strontium (Sr++), also permeate and support degranulation in stimulated mast cells. In this study, we demonstrate that the influx of calcium and Sr++ as well as degranulation are dependent on the presence of the TRPC5 channel protein, in addition to STIM1 and Orai1, using a rat mast cell (RBL-2H3) line. We found that knocking down each of these proteins with inhibitory RNAs leads to a decrease in degranulation. Overexpression of STIM1 and Orai1, which are known to be essential components of the calcium release-activated calcium channel, allows for the entry of calcium but not strontium, while overexpression of STIM1 and TRPC5 allows for the entry of both calcium and strontium. These observations suggest that the Sr++-permeable TRPC5 associates with STIM1 and Orai1 in a stoichiometric manner to enhance the entry of calcium and generate a signal for degranulation.

title: LincRNA-p21 suppresses target mRNA translation.
text: Mammalian long intergenic noncoding RNAs (lincRNAs) are primarily recognized for their ability to regulate gene expression. However, our study reveals a hitherto unknown function for lincRNA-p21 in modulating protein translation. We have found that the association of the RNA-binding protein HuR with lincRNA-p21 leads to the recruitment of let-7/Ago2 to lincRNA-p21, resulting in decreased stability of the latter. When HuR levels are reduced, lincRNA-p21 accumulates in human cervical carcinoma HeLa cells and interacts with mRNAs encoding JUNB and CTNNB1, leading to a decrease in their translation. Conversely, when HuR levels are elevated, lincRNA-p21 levels decrease, resulting in increased translation of JUNB and β-catenin, and an accompanying increase in their protein levels. Our findings indicate that HuR regulates translation of a specific subset of target mRNAs by modulating lincRNA-p21 levels, thereby uncovering a novel function for lincRNAs as posttranscriptional inhibitors of translation.

title: Large intestine-targeted nanoparticle-releasing oral vaccine to control genitorectal viral infection
text: Both rectal and vaginal mucosal surfaces can serve as routes of transmission for harmful microorganisms. Vaccination through the large intestinal mucosa, which has been proven protective for both of these mucosal sites in animal studies, can be achieved effectively through direct intracolorectal (i.c.r.) administration, but this route is impractical in a clinical setting. Oral vaccine delivery, while seemingly preferable, runs the risk of the vaccine being destroyed in the upper gastrointestinal tract. To address this challenge, we designed an oral delivery system for vaccines targeting the large intestine that utilizes pH-dependent microparticles containing vaccine nanoparticles. This approach induced colorectal immunity in mice comparable to colorectal vaccination and provided protection against rectal and vaginal viral challenge. In contrast, vaccines targeting the small intestine induced only small intestinal immunity and provided no rectal or vaginal protection, highlighting the functional compartmentalization of the gut mucosal immune system. Therefore, utilizing this oral vaccine delivery system to target the large intestine, but not the small intestine, may represent a feasible new strategy for immune protection of rectal and vaginal mucosa.

title: Timing of menarche and first full-term birth in relation to breast cancer risk.
text: In this study, the authors investigated the relationship between the timing of reproductive events and breast cancer risk among White and African-American women. The study included 4,013 breast cancer cases and 4,069 controls enrolled in a multicenter, population-based US case-control study from 1994 to 1998. Using logistic regression, the authors found that women who experienced a gap of >16 years between their age of menarche and first birth had a 1.5-fold (95% CI: 1.0, 2.2) and 1.4-fold (95% CI: 1.1, 1.8) increased risk of breast cancer compared to those with a shorter gap, among parous premenopausal and postmenopausal women, respectively. Adjusting for age at first birth altered the risk estimates slightly, with odds ratios of 1.5 (95% CI: 0.8, 2.9) and 1.0 (95% CI: 0.6, 1.5), respectively. The association was stronger for lobular and hormone-receptor-positive tumors, but was absent among premenopausal African-American women. The authors concluded that the interval between age at menarche and age at first birth is associated with the risk of hormonally sensitive types of breast cancer, particularly among White women.

title: Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance in Cardiac Amyloidosis
text:
Background: The prognosis of patients with cardiac amyloidosis, including immunoglobulin light chain (AL) and transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis, is heavily influenced by the extent of cardiac involvement. While cardiovascular magnetic resonance with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is a standard for diagnosing cardiac amyloidosis, its ability to predict risk is unknown.
Methods and Results: In this study, 250 subjects, including 122 patients with ATTR amyloid, 9 asymptomatic mutation carriers, and 119 patients with AL amyloidosis, underwent LGE cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging. Subjects were followed for a mean of 24±13 months. LGE was performed using both phase-sensitive inversion recovery (PSIR) and magnitude-only inversion recovery. The studyfound that PSIR outperformed magnitude-only inversion recovery for LGE, as it always nulled the tissue with the longest T1 (blood or myocardium). LGE was classified into three patterns: none, subendocardial, and transmural, and were associated with increasing amyloid burden as defined by extracellular volume. Transition from none to subendocardial LGE occurred at an extracellular volume of 0.40 to 0.43 in AL amyloidosis and 0.39 to 0.40 in ATTR amyloidosis, and to transmural LGE at 0.48 to 0.55 in AL amyloidosis and 0.47 to 0.59 in ATTR amyloidosis. Sixty-seven patients (27%) died during the follow-up period. Transmural LGE was found to predict death, with a hazard ratio of 5.4 (95% confidence interval, 2.1-13.7) and remained independent after adjustment for N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide, ejection fraction, stroke volume index, E/E', and left ventricular mass index (hazard ratio, 4.1; 95% confidence interval, 1.3-13.1).
Conclusions: There is a continuum of cardiac involvement in systemic AL and ATTR amyloidosis, and transmural LGE is determined reliably by PSIR and represents advanced cardiac amyloidosis. The PSIR technique provides incremental information on outcome even after adjustment for known prognostic factors.

title: Global, regional, and national comparative risk assessment of 79 behavioural, environmental and occupational, and metabolic risks or clusters of risks, 1990–2015: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2015
text:
The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2015 provides a comprehensive analysis of the burden of various risks factors on global health. The study uses a comparative risk assessment framework to estimate the attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and trends in exposure to different risk factors from 1990 to 2015. The study includes 388 risk-outcome pairs that meet the World Cancer Research Fund's criteria for convincing or probable evidence. The study found that:
* Global exposure to unsafe sanitation, household air pollution, childhood underweight, childhood stunting, and smoking decreased by more than 25% between 1990 and 2015.
* Global exposure for several occupational risks, high body-mass index (BMI), and drug use increased by more than 25% over the same period.
* All risks jointly evaluated in 2015 accounted for 57.8% (95% CI 56.6-58.8) of global deaths and 41.2% (39.8-42.8) of DALYs.
* The ten largest contributors to global DALYs among Level 3 risks were high systolic blood pressure (211.8 million [192.7 million to 231.1 million] global DALYs), smoking (148.6 million [134.2 million to 163.1 million]), high fasting plasma glucose (143.1 million [125.1 million to 163.5 million]), high BMI (120.1 million [83.8 million to 158.4 million]), childhood undernutrition (113.3 million [103.9 million to 123.4 million]), ambient particulate matter (103.1 million [90.8 million to 115.1 million]), high total cholesterol (88.7 million [74.6 million to 105.7 million]), household air pollution (85.6 million [66.7 million to 106.1 million]), alcohol use (85.0 million [77.2 million to 93.0 million]), and diets high in sodium (83.0 million [49.3 million to 127.5 million]).
* Between 1990 and 2015, attributable DALYs declined for micronutrient deficiencies, childhood undernutrition, unsafe sanitation and water, and household air pollution; reductions in risk-deleted DALY rates rather than reductions in exposure drove these declines.
* Rising exposure contributed to notable increases in attributable DALYs from high BMI, high fasting plasma glucose, occupational carcinogens, and drug use.
* Environmental risks and childhood undernutrition declined steadily with Socio-demographic Index (SDI); low physical activity, high BMI, and high fasting plasma glucose increased with SDI.
* In 119 countries, metabolic risks, such as high BMI and fasting plasma glucose, contributed the most attributable DALYs in 2015.
* Regionally, smoking still ranked among the leading five risk factors for attributable DALYs in 109 countries; childhood underweight and unsafe sex remained primary drivers of early death and disability in much of sub-Saharan Africa.

In conclusion, declines in some key environmental risk factors have contributed to declines in critical infectious diseases. Some risks appear to be invariant to Socio-demographic Index (SDI), while others are increasing globally. Public policy makers need to pay attention to the rising burden from some of these risk factors, such as high BMI, high fasting plasma glucose, and drug use, even as exposure is declining for other risks.

title: Human RecQ helicases in DNA repair, recombination, and replication.
text: RecQ helicases are an evolutionarily conserved family of genome surveillance proteins that play a crucial role in maintaining the stability and integrity of the genome across various organisms, from bacteria to humans. There are five human RecQ helicases, each with distinct functions in genome maintenance, and they are often referred to as the "guardians of the genome." Defects in specific RecQ helicases, such as BLM, WRN, and RECQL4, have been linked to inherited human disease syndromes, highlighting the importance of these proteins in maintaining cellular homeostasis. Each human RecQ helicase has a unique set of protein-interacting partners, which dictates its specialized functions in genome maintenance, including DNA repair, recombination, replication, and transcription. Additionally, human RecQ helicases interact with each other, and these interactions have a significant impact on enzyme function. Future research goals in this field include a deeper understanding of the division of labor among human RecQ helicases and the ways in which they collaborate and cooperate to enhance genome stability.

title: Metabolomics study of the therapeutic mechanism of Schisandra Chinensis lignans in diet-induced hyperlipidemia mice
text:
Schisandrin, a globally distributed plant, has been traditionally used to treat diseases such as hyperlipidemia, fatty liver, and obesity in China. In this study, we investigated the anti-hyperlipidemic effects of Schisandrin Chinensis Lignans (SCL) in hyperlipidemic mice using a rapid resolution liquid chromatography-quadruple-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (RRLC-Q-TOF-MS) metabolomics approach.
METHODS:
We induced hyperlipidemia in mice by feeding them a high-fat diet (HFD) and then administered SCL (100 mg/kg) orally once a day for 4 weeks. Serum biochemistry assays were performed to evaluate the treatment's effect on lipid levels, including triglycerides (TG), total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-c), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-c). Metabolomics analysis was carried out on serum samples, and principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) were performed to identify the treatment's effects on metabolic patterns and characteristic metabolites.
RESULTS: Our results show that oral administration of SCL significantly reduced the serum levels of TC, TG, and LDL-c and increased the serum level of HDL-c in hyperlipidemic mice compared to the control group. In contrast, there was no effect of SCL on lipid levels in the control group. Metabolomics analysis showed that serum samples from the SCL-treated mice were scattered in the PCA scores plots, indicating that SCL treatment affected metabolic patterns. Thirteen biomarkers were identified, and nine of them were recovered to normal levels after SCL treatment.
Using Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis, we found that the anti-hyperlipidemic mechanisms of SCL may involve the following metabolic pathways: tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, synthesis of ketone bodies and cholesterol, choline metabolism, and fatty acid metabolism. Additionally, SCL significantly inhibited the mRNA expression of hepatic lipogenesis genes such as sterol regulatory element-binding proteins (SREBP-1c), fatty acid synthase (FAS), acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC), and decreased the mRNA expression of liver X receptor α (LXRα). Moreover, SCL also significantly decreased the expression of SREBP-2 and 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR) in the liver of hyperlipidemic mice.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that SCL has anti-hyperlipidemic effects, which may be related to the down-regulation of LXRα/SREBP-1c/FAS/ACC and SREBP2/HMGCR signaling pathways. These results provide new insights into the mechanisms of action of Schisandrin and may lead to the development of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of hyperlipidemia and related disorders.

title: Tet1 and Tet2 regulate 5-hydroxymethylcytosine production and cell lineage specification in mouse embryonic stem cells.
text: Tet family enzymes convert 5-methylcytosine (5mC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) in DNA. Our findings show that Tet1 and Tet2 are regulated by Oct4 and work together to maintain 5hmC in mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) during the process of reprogramming fibroblasts to induced pluripotent stem cells. ESCs that are depleted of Tet1 using RNAi exhibit impaired expression of the Nodal antagonist Lefty1 and demonstrate hyperactive Nodal signaling, leading to an excessive differentiation towards the endoderm-mesoderm lineage in embryoid bodies in vitro. In the presence of Fgf4 and heparin, Tet1-depleted ESCs exhibit an unusual activation of the trophoblast stem cell lineage determinant Elf5 and are able to colonize the placenta in midgestation embryo chimeras. Consistently, Tet1-depleted ESCs form aggressive hemorrhagic teratomas with an increase in endoderm, a decrease in neuroectoderm, and an ectopic appearance of trophoblastic giant cells. These findings indicate that 5hmC is an epigenetic modification associated with pluripotency, and Tet1 regulates the lineage differentiation potential of ESCs.

title: Polycomb Associates Genome-wide with a Specific RNA Polymerase II Variant, and Regulates Metabolic Genes in ESCs
text:
Polycomb repressor complexes (PRCs) play a crucial role in regulating chromatin structure and gene expression, particularly during cellular differentiation and development. Our study aimed to investigate the relationship between PRCs and RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) in embryonic stem cells (ESCs). We conducted chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) to identify PRC repression markers and four RNAPII states in ESCs.
Our findings revealed that PRC targets are bound by different variants of RNAPII genome-wide. Specifically, developmental PRC targets are associated with unproductive RNAPII (S5p(+)S7p(-)S2p(-)) states, while a cohort of genes marked by PRC and elongating RNAPII (S5p(+)S7p(+)S2p(+)) are involved in mRNA transcription and protein production. Interestingly, these genes switch between active and PRC-repressed states within the ESC population.
Furthermore, we showed that many of these PRC targets have roles in metabolism, highlighting the importance of PRCs in regulating cellular metabolism. Our study provides new insights into the complex interplay between PRCs and RNAPII in ESCs and highlights the importance of further investigating the functional interplay between these two complexes in different cell types and contexts.

title: Chemokine-like receptor 1 (CMKLR1) and chemokine (C-C motif) receptor-like 2 (CCRL2); two multifunctional receptors with unusual properties.
text: Two 7-transmembrane receptors, Chemokine-like receptor 1 (CMKLR1) and chemokine (C-C motif) receptor-like 2 (CCRL2), were initially identified based on their similarity to G-protein-coupled receptors in the late 1990s. These receptors were once considered orphan receptors without any known biological roles, but recent investigations have revealed their functions. Chemerin, a plasma protein-derived chemoattractant, functions as a ligand for CMKLR1 and stimulates the migration of macrophages and dendritic cells (DCs) in vitro, suggesting a proinflammatory role. Nonetheless, studies using CMKLR-deficient mice have suggested an anti-inflammatory role for this receptor, possibly due to the recruitment of tolerogenic plasmacytoid DCs. Additionally, chemerin/CMKLR1 interaction promotes adipogenesis and angiogenesis. The anti-inflammatory lipid mediator, resolving E1, is another CMKLR1 ligand that inhibits leukocyte infiltration and proinflammatory gene expression. Surprisingly, chemerin, a ligand for CMKLR1, is also a ligand for CCRL2. CCRL2 binds chemerin and increases local chemerin concentration, effectively presenting it to CMKLR1 on nearby cells, forming a link between CCRL2 and CMKLR1. Although these findings suggest an anti-inflammatory role, recent studies using CCRL2-deficient mice have indicated a proinflammatory role for this receptor, thus highlighting the complexity of its function. Further research using CMKLR1- or CCRL2-deficient mice is necessary to fully characterize the role of these receptors in immune responses and other cellular processes.

title: Identification of vitronectin as an extrinsic inducer of cancer stem cell differentiation and tumor formation.
text: Mounting evidence suggests that cancer stem cells (CSCs), a rare subset of cells, play a crucial role in tumor initiation. CSCs are generally quiescent, self-renew, and form tumors at low numbers, giving rise to the diverse cell types within a tumor. Despite efforts to identify the factors responsible for CSC differentiation, this remains an elusive goal. Here, we uncover the previously unidentified role of vitronectin in driving CSC differentiation through an integrin alpha V beta 3-dependent mechanism. When CSCs are cultured on vitronectin, we observe downregulation of stem cell genes, modification of differentiation markers, and loss of beta-catenin nuclear localization. Interrupting integrin alpha V beta 3 inhibits differentiation and subsequent tumor formation. This findings highlight a previously unrecognized axis for the development of novel therapies targeting both extrinsic and intracellular mechanisms.

title: STIM1 Is a Calcium Sensor Specialized for Digital Signaling
text: Intracellular calcium signals in cells are known to take the form of repetitive and regenerative calcium discharges when activated by calcium-mobilizing agonists at low and physiological concentrations. These calcium oscillations have fascinated biologists for their potential as a mode of digital intracellular signaling. Recent studies have shed light on the role of calcium influx as an essential component of calcium oscillations, which occurs through a process termed store-operated calcium entry. This process involves calcium sensor proteins STIM1 and STIM2 in the endoplasmic reticulum, with STIM2 being activated by changes in endoplasmic reticulum calcium near the resting level, and a threshold of calcium depletion required for STIM1 activation. Contrary to previous beliefs, we have found that STIM1 is exclusively involved in calcium entry during calcium oscillations, with each oscillation producing a transient drop in endoplasmic reticulum calcium. This drop in calcium is sufficient to transiently activate STIM1, which can be observed in some cells using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. This unique arrangement enables a clearly defined and unambiguous signaling system, where a digital calcium release signal is translated into calcium influx that can signal to downstream effectors.

title: Trends in the use of complementary health approaches among adults: United States, 2002-2012.
text:
Objective: This report provides national estimates of the use of complementary health approaches among adults in the United States across three time points, with a focus on trends and demographic differences in their utilization.
Methods: Comprehensive analysis was conducted on a dataset of 88,962 adults aged 18 and over collected via the National Health Interview Survey in 2002, 2007, and 2012. The sample was weighted to produce nationally representative estimates of the civilian noninstitutionalized U.S. adult population. Significance testing was performed using two-sided tests at the 0.05 level to evaluate differences between percentages across the three time points.
Results: The analysis revealed that while individual approaches varied in popularity across the three time points, nonvitamin, nonmineral dietary supplements remained the most commonly used complementary health approach. Notably, the use of yoga, tai chi, and qi gong showed a linear increase across the three time points, with yoga accounting for approximately 80% of the prevalence. Furthermore, the use of any complementary health approach varied by selected sociodemographic characteristics, with the most notable differences observed in age and Hispanic or Latino origin and race.
In summary, this report provides detailed national estimates of complementary health approach use among adults in the United States across three time points, highlighting trends and demographic differences in their utilization.

title: Histone structure and nucleosome stability.
text: Histone proteins are crucial for the transitions between active and inactive chromatin states. Despite their high degree of conservation due to structural constraints, histone variants have evolved to take on distinct roles in gene regulation and epigenetic silencing. Variants, post-translational modifications, and interactions with chromatin remodeling complexes influence DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination. The authors examine the latest findings on chromatin structure, which corroborate earlier observations inferred from crystal structures.

title: Cerebral palsy among term and postterm births.
text:
Although preterm delivery is a well-established risk factor for cerebral palsy (CP), preterm deliveries account for only a minority of CP cases. However, there is limited information on the relationship between CP risk and gestational age in the term range, where most CP occurs. This study aimed to determine whether the timing of birth in the term and postterm period is associated with the risk of CP.
The study was a population-based follow-up study conducted in Norway using the Medical Birth Registry. The cohort consisted of 1,682,441 singleton children born between 1967 and 2001, with a gestational age of 37-44 weeks and no congenital anomalies. The cohort was followed up through 2005 by linking to other national registries. The main outcome measures were the absolute and relative risk of CP for children surviving to at least 4 years of age.
Of the term and postterm children, 1938 were registered with CP in the National Insurance Scheme. The risk of CP was lowest for children born at 40 weeks, with a prevalence of 0.99/1000 (95% CI, 0.90-1.08). The risk of CP was higher with earlier or later delivery, with a prevalence at 37 weeks of 1.91/1000 (95% CI, 1.58-2.25) and a relative risk (RR) of 1.9 (95% CI, 1.6-2.4), a prevalence at 38 weeks of 1.25/1000 (95% CI, 1.07-1.42) and an RR of 1.3 (95% CI, 1.1-1.6), a prevalence at 42 weeks of 1.36/1000 (95% CI, 1.19-1.53) and an RR of 1.4 (95% CI, 1.2-1.6), and a prevalence after 42 weeks of 1.44/1000 (95% CI, 1.15-1.72) and an RR of 1.4 (95% CI, 1.1-1.8). These associations were even stronger in a subset with gestational age based on ultrasound measurements. Specifically, at 37 weeks, the prevalence was 1.17/1000 (95% CI, 0.30-2.04) and the relative risk was 3.7 (95% CI, 1.5-9.1). At 42 weeks, the prevalence was 0.85/1000 (95% CI, 0.33-1.38) and the relative risk was 2.4 (95% CI, 1.1-5.3). Adjustment for infant sex, maternal age, and various socioeconomic measures had little effect.
In conclusion, this study found that compared to delivery at 40 weeks' gestation, delivery at 37 or 38 weeks or at 42 weeks or later was associated with an increased risk of CP. These findings suggest that the timing of birth in the term and postterm period may be an important factor in determining the risk of CP.

title: 53BP1 Inhibits Homologous Recombination in Brca1-Deficient Cells by Blocking Resection of DNA Breaks
text:
Defective DNA repair through homologous recombination (HR) is thought to be a significant factor in tumor development in individuals carrying BRCA1 mutations. Our research reveals that DNA breaks in BRCA1-deficient cells are abnormally joined into complex chromosome rearrangements through a process dependent on nonhomologous end-joining (NHEJ) factors 53BP1 and DNA ligase 4. Removal of 53BP1 alleviates the sensitivity of BRCA1 mutant cells to PARP inhibition and restores error-free repair through HR.
Our findings suggest that HR and NHEJ pathways compete to process DNA breaks generated during DNA replication, and modulating this balance can be exploited to selectively protect or kill cells harboring BRCA1 mutations. In contrast, deficiency in Lig4 does not rescue the HR defect in BRCA1 mutant cells but prevents the union of chromatid breaks into chromosome rearrangements. The results demonstrate that shifting the balance between these pathways can be used to selectively protect or kill cells carrying BRCA1 mutations.

title: The genetics of Mexico recapitulates Native American substructure and affects biomedical traits
text: Mexico boasts immense cultural and ethnic diversity, yet the minute details of human genetic variation within this region remain largely unexplored. We conducted a study on genetic variation among 1000+ individuals across 20 indigenous and 11 mestizo populations in Mexico. We found striking genetic differentiation among indigenous groups at varying levels of geographic isolation, with some groups resembling the degree of differentiation between Europeans and East Asians. Pre-Columbian genetic substructures persist in the indigenous ancestry of admixed mestizo individuals across Mexico. Moreover, two independently studied cohorts of Mexicans and Mexican Americans revealed a significant association between subcontinental ancestry and lung function. Therefore, accounting for minute ancestry patterns is crucial for medical and population genetic studies within Mexico, as well as in populations of Mexican descent globally.

title: COPI Complex Is a Regulator of Lipid Homeostasis
text: Lipid droplets are ubiquitous cellular organelles crucial for maintaining energy homeostasis and biosynthesis. Although the mechanisms of lipid droplet formation and regulation are largely uncharted territory, it is clear that the PAT protein family (comprising perilipin, adipocyte differentiation related protein, and tail interacting protein of 47 kDa) coats the droplet surface and mediates interactions with lipases that mobilize stored lipids. We employed RNA interference (RNAi) screening with an innovative optical read-out system to identify key regulatory genes in Drosophila, and found that these genes are conserved in mice. These include the vesicle-mediated COPI transport complex, which restricts lipid storage by regulating the composition of PAT proteins at the lipid droplet surface. We discovered that COPI components collaborate with adipocyte triglyceride lipase (ATGL) to facilitate lipolysis by mediating the association of ATGL with the lipid droplet surface. Interestingly, inhibition of COPI function by two compounds (Exo1 and Brefeldin A) mimics COPI knockdowns, and RNAi inhibition of ATGL combined with drug treatment supports the notion that COPI and ATGL operate in the same pathway. These findings illume the importance of the COPI complex in lipid homeostasis and underscore the interplay between different vesicle transport systems and lipid droplets.

title: Differentiation of effector CD4 T cell populations (*).
text: CD4 T cells are essential for the body's adaptive immune system, playing a crucial role in combating a range of pathogens. They are also involved in autoimmune disorders, such as asthma and allergies, as well as in the development of cancer. Upon activation of their T cell receptor (TCR) in a specific cytokine environment, naive CD4 T cells can differentiate into different lineages of T helper (Th) cells, including Th1, Th2, Th17, and iTreg, depending on the pattern of cytokine production and function. This review aims to provide an overview of the discovery, functions, and relationships among Th cells, as well as the cytokine and signaling requirements for their development, the transcription factor networks involved in their differentiation, and the epigenetic regulation of their key cytokines and transcription factors. Additionally, the review will discuss human diseases caused by defects in CD4 T cell differentiation.

title: Homocysteine and other thiols in plasma and urine: automated determination and sample stability.
text: We have developed an enhanced version of our previously described fully automated column-switching HPLC method for measuring total plasma homocysteine using single-column reverse-phase separation. This modified method allows for the simultaneous determination of homocysteine, cysteine, and cysteinylglycine in plasma, as well as their acid-precipitated and urine fractions. The automated sample processing includes derivatization and chromatography, which were optimized to achieve accurate separations within 15 minutes. The method was found to be sensitive (detection limit approximately 0.05 pmol) and had high precision (CV < 5%). The sample output rate was approximately 70 samples per 24 hours. Additional improvements to the method include the ability to analyze serum and heparin plasma samples. Hemolysis up to approximately 2.0 g/L of hemoglobin did not significantly interfere with the analytical recovery of homocysteine or cysteine. Standardization of blood-sampling procedures is essential to obtain consistent and reliable thiol results. Our modifications and standardization efforts have substantially improved the method and expanded its applications.

title: Induced pluripotent stem cells in Alzheimer’s disease: applications for disease modeling and cell-replacement therapy
text: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia in individuals aged 65 and above. While numerous genetic and risk factors have been identified, the exact mechanisms underlying AD are still unclear due to the inability to test hypotheses on non-postmortem and patient-specific models. Recent advancements in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) technology offer a promising platform for creating reliable models to better understand the etiology of AD and for efficient drug screening. Furthermore, iPSCs may provide a valuable tool for cell replacement therapy in AD. Although significant progress has been made, key challenges remain in iPSCs research, including identifying robust disease phenotypes in AD modeling and the clinical availability of iPSCs-based cell replacement therapy in humans. In this review, we will discuss recent developments in iPSCs research and the challenges of translating AD patient-derived iPSCs into disease modeling and cell replacement therapy.

title: Nitrite protects against morbidity and mortality associated with TNF- or LPS-induced shock in a soluble guanylate cyclase–dependent manner
text: Nitrite (NO2-) was previously considered an inactive metabolite and byproduct of the endogenous vasodilator nitric oxide (NO). However, recent research has revealed nitrite as a significant biological reservoir of NO in the vasculature and tissues, playing a crucial role in hypoxic signaling, vasodilation, and cytoprotection following ischemia-reperfusion injury. Enzymatic reduction of nitrite to NO can occur at low pH and oxygen levels through various enzymes, including deoxyhemoglobin, deoxymyoglobin, xanthine oxidase, mitochondrial complexes, and NO synthase (NOS). In contrast to NOS inhibition, which worsens shock, nitrite treatment significantly attenuates hypothermia, mitochondrial damage, oxidative stress, and organ dysfunction in a mouse shock model induced by a lethal tumor necrosis factor challenge. The nitrite-dependent protection mechanism is distinct from inhibition of mitochondrial complex I activity, which was previously shown to protect against ischemia-reperfusion injury. Furthermore, nitrite protection is abolished in mice lacking the soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) alpha1 subunit, a key intracellular NO receptor and signal transducer in the cardiovasculature. Additionally, nitrite provides protection against toxicity induced by Gram-negative lipopolysaccharide, although higher doses are required. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that nitrite can protect against toxicity in shock by activating sGC-dependent signaling, which may involve hypoxic vasodilation essential for maintaining microcirculation and organ function, as well as cardioprotection.

title: Mammographic density and the risk and detection of breast cancer.
text:
BACKGROUND: While extensive mammographic density is a known risk factor for breast cancer, its impact on cancer detection when using different methods is unclear.
METHODS: We conducted three nested case-control studies in screened populations, with 1112 matched case-control pairs. We evaluated the association between the percentage of density in the baseline mammogram and breast cancer risk, taking into account the method of cancer detection, time since screening initiation, and age.
RESULTS: Compared to women with density in less than 10% of their mammogram, those with density in 75% or more had a significantly higher risk of breast cancer, whether detected by screening (odds ratio [OR] 3.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.0-6.2) or within 12 months of a negative screening examination (OR 17.8, 95% CI 4.8-65.9). The increased risk persisted for at least 8 years after study entry and was more pronounced in younger women, with 26% of all breast cancers and 50% of cancers detected within 12 months of a negative screening test attributable to density in 50% or more of the mammogram among women younger than the median age of 56 years.
CONCLUSIONS: Extensive mammographic density is strongly linked to the risk of breast cancer detected through both screening and other means. A significant fraction of breast cancers can be attributed to this risk factor.

title: Pooled analysis of prospective cohort studies on height, weight, and breast cancer risk.
text: The study investigated the relationship between anthropometric measures and the risk of breast cancer using pooled data from seven prospective cohort studies, which included 337,819 women and 4,385 incident invasive breast cancer cases. In multivariate analysis adjusting for reproductive, dietary, and other risk factors, the pooled relative risk (RR) of breast cancer per height increase of 5 cm was 1.02 (95% CI: 0.96, 1.10) among premenopausal women and 1.07 (95% CI: 1.03, 1.12) among postmenopausal women. The study also found that body mass index (BMI) showed significant inverse and positive associations with breast cancer among pre- and postmenopausal women, respectively; these associations were nonlinear. Specifically, compared to premenopausal women with a BMI of less than 21 kg/m2, women with a BMI exceeding 31 kg/m2 had an RR of 0.54 (95% CI: 0.34, 0.85). However, in postmenopausal women, the RRs did not increase further when BMI exceeded 28 kg/m2, with an RR of 1.26 (95% CI: 1.09, 1.46). The authors also found little evidence for interaction with other breast cancer risk factors. The study suggests that height is an independent risk factor for postmenopausal breast cancer, while the relation is less clear among premenopausal women. Additionally, the association between BMI and breast cancer varies by menopausal status, with weight control potentially reducing the risk among postmenopausal women.

title: Cost effectiveness of ward based non-invasive ventilation for acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: economic analysis of randomised controlled trial.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of standard treatment with or without the addition of ward-based non-invasive ventilation in patients admitted to hospital with an acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
Design: Incremental cost-effectiveness analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
Setting: Medical wards in 14 hospitals across the United Kingdom.
Participants: A total of 236 patients admitted to hospital with an acute exacerbation of COPD and mild to moderate acidosis (pH 7.25-7.35) secondary to respiratory failure. The economic analysis compared the costs of treatment received by these patients after randomization.
Primary Outcome Measure: Incremental cost per in-hospital death.

Results: Of the 118 patients randomized to receive standard treatment, 24 died in hospital, while 12 of the 118 patients randomized to receive non-invasive ventilation died (P = 0.05). Allocation to the non-invasive ventilation group was associated with a reduction in costs of £49,362 (approximately $78,741 or €73,109), primarily due to reduced use of intensive care units. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was £-645 ($-$2310 or €-$386) per death avoided, indicating a dominant (more effective and less costly) strategy. Modeling of these data suggests that a typical UK hospital providing a non-invasive ventilation service would avoid six deaths and three to nine admissions to intensive care units per year, with an associated cost reduction of £12,000 to £53,000 per year.
Conclusions: Non-invasive ventilation is a highly cost-effective treatment that both reduced total costs and improved mortality in hospital, demonstrating great savings through reduced ICU use.

title: Persistent human papillomavirus infection and cervical neoplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text: The detection of persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA is used as a marker for cervical cancer risk in clinical trials. In a systematic review and meta-analysis, the authors evaluated the association between persistent HPV DNA and high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN2-3), high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL), and invasive cervical cancer (together designated CIN2-3/HSIL+) to assess the reliability of HPV persistence as a clinical marker. The meta-analysis included 41 studies with over 22,500 women, and the authors found that persistent HPV DNA detection was consistently and strongly associated with CIN2-3/HSIL+, despite variations in definitions and study methods. The magnitude of the association varied by duration of persistence and testing interval. The findings validate HPV persistence as a clinical marker and endpoint, and highlight the need for precise definitions and standardization of HPV testing, sampling procedure, and test interval for reliable clinical testing.

title: Post-transcriptional Wnt Signaling Governs Epididymal Sperm Maturation
text: The central Wnt signaling pathway plays a pivotal role in both development and disease. A current area of investigation is whether the upstream cascade of the canonical Wnt pathway has physiologically relevant functions beyond β-catenin-mediated transcription, which is challenging to study due to the ubiquitous presence of β-catenin. In this study, we uncover that Wnt signals emitted from the epididymis can regulate transcriptionally silent spermatoza, and mice lacking the Wnt regulator Cyclin Y-like 1 are male infertile due to immotile and abnormal spermatoza. Our findings indicate that post-transcriptional Wnt signaling in spermatoza involves the following mechanisms: (1) reducing global protein poly-ubiquitination to maintain protein homeostasis; (2) inhibiting septin 4 phosphorylation to establish a membrane diffusion barrier in the sperm tail; and (3) inhibiting protein phosphatase 1 to initiate sperm motility. These results highlight the crucial role of Wnt signaling in orchestrating a complex post-transcriptional program of sperm maturation and suggest reevaluating non-transcriptional Wnt signaling in somatic cells as well.

title: CD28 Costimulation: From Mechanism to Therapy.
text: The binding of the CD28 receptor on T cells provides a crucial secondary signal alongside T cell receptor (TCR) ligation for the activation of naive T cells. Here, we delve into the expression, structure, and biochemistry of CD28 and its ligands. CD28 signaling plays a pivotal role in various T cell processes, including cytoskeletal reorganization, cytokine production, survival, and differentiation. In contrast to TCR ligation alone, CD28 ligation triggers unique epigenetic, transcriptional, and post-translational changes in T cells. We discuss the function of CD28 and its ligands in both effector and regulatory T cells, highlighting their critical roles in immune homeostasis. We also highlight the importance of CD28 and its family members in human disease and provide an overview of the clinical efficacy of drugs that target CD28 ligands. Despite significant progress in understanding CD28 biology, many aspects of its function remain unclear. The translation of basic research findings into immunomodulatory therapeutics has been uneven, with both successes and failures. Factors contributing to these outcomes include complex receptor-ligand interactions among CD28 family members, species-specific differences between mouse and human CD28, and cell-type-specific roles of CD28 family members.

title: Recommended diagnostic criteria for multiple sclerosis: guidelines from the International Panel on the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis.
text: The International Panel on MS Diagnosis has revised the diagnostic criteria for multiple sclerosis (MS). The main focus remains on demonstrating the distribution of lesions in both time and space using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) in conjunction with clinical and other paraclinical diagnostic methods. The revised criteria aim to facilitate the diagnosis of MS in patients with various presentations, including "monosymptomatic" disease that may resemble MS, disease with a typical relapsing-remitting course, and disease with insidious progression without clear attacks and remissions. The use of previously employed terms such as "clinically definite" and "probable MS" is no longer recommended. Instead, the outcome of a diagnostic evaluation is categorized as either MS, "possible MS" (for individuals with a high risk of developing MS but whose diagnostic evaluation is uncertain), or "not MS."

title: Regulation of radial glial survival by signals from the meninges.
text:
Radial glial cells (RGCs) in the developing cerebral cortex serve as progenitors for both neurons and glia, and their processes act as guidance channels for migrating neurons. Initially, the question of whether RGC processes exert direct control over RGC function remained unanswered. Our study reveals that the absence of beta1 integrins in RGCs leads to a reduction in the number of RGCs and the size of the cerebral cortex. We employed TUNEL staining and time-lapse video recordings to demonstrate that beta1-deficient RGC processes detach from the meningeal basement membrane (BM) followed by apoptotic cell death of RGCs. Furthermore, we found that surgical removal of the meninges also induces apoptosis in RGCs. We additionally discovered that the attachment of RGC processes to the meninges is crucial for RGC survival and the regulation of cortical size.
In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that the connections between RGCs and the meninges play a pivotal role in the survival and proper development of RGCs, which in turn influences the size of the cerebral cortex.

title: The sterol regulatory element binding proteins are essential for the metabolic programming of effector T cells and adaptive immunity
text: Recently activated CD8(+) T cells alter their metabolism to accommodate the exorbitant biochemical needs of clonal expansion; nevertheless, the signals directing metabolic reprogramming remain inadequately characterized. We demonstrate a crucial function for sterol regulatory element-binding proteins (SREBPs) in the acquisition of effector cell metabolism. Without SREBP signaling, CD8(+) T cells are unable to proliferate, resulting in impaired clonal expansion during viral infection. Mechanistic studies reveal that SREBPs are essential for fulfilling the heightened lipid requirements of membrane synthesis during blastogenesis. In contrast, SREBPs are dispensable for homeostatic proliferation, indicating a context-specific dependency on SREBPs in effector responses. Our findings contribute to our understanding of the molecular signals driving the metabolic reprogramming of CD8(+) T cells during their transition from quiescence to activation.

title: Human contribution to the European heatwave of 2003
text: The scorching summer of 2003 was likely the hottest Europe had seen since at least 1500, with an alarming number of heat-related deaths reported in France, Germany, and Italy. While it is difficult to pinpoint the exact cause of the 2003 heatwave, it is possible to estimate the role human activities played in increasing the likelihood of such an event. Using a specific framework, we analyzed the contribution of human-induced changes in atmospheric greenhouse gas and pollutant concentrations to the risk of unusually high summer temperatures across a large swath of continental Europe. By setting a threshold for mean summer temperature that was exceeded in 2003 but never seen in any other year since 1851, we found it is highly likely (confidence level exceeding 90%) that human activities at least doubled the risk of a heatwave exceeding this threshold magnitude.

title: Do Antidepressants Cure or Create Abnormal Brain States?
text:
The term "antidepressant" refers to a drug that aims to correct specific biological abnormalities that give rise to the symptoms of depression. This adheres to the "disease-centred" model of psychotropic drug action, which is based on similar models found in general medicine, such as the use of insulin in diabetes, antibiotics in infectious diseases, and chemotherapy in cancer. This model suggests that antidepressants work by restoring normal functioning by affecting the neuropathology of depression or depressive symptoms.
However, we propose an alternative "drug-centred" model that can better explain observed drug effects in psychiatric conditions. According to this model, drugs themselves cause abnormal states that may coincidentally relieve psychiatric symptoms, rather than correcting a hypothetical biochemical imbalance underlying the symptoms. For instance, alcohol's disinhibiting effects may alleviate symptoms of social phobia, but this does not imply that alcohol corrects a chemical imbalance underlying social phobia. Similarly, sedation may reduce high arousal in acute psychiatric situations, while drugs that induce indifference, such as neuroleptics or opiates, may help reduce the distress of acute psychotic symptoms. Low-dose stimulants may improve attention and concentration in the short term.
The disease-centred model in psychiatry leads researchers to infer antidepressant effects from patients' scores on symptom rating scales that are believed to assess the manifestations of the disease. In contrast, the drug-centred model suggests that physiological and subjective effects of drugs should be examined in their own right, including various forms of sedation, stimulation, and a plethora of biopsychological states. While some drugs may produce euphoria or mood elevation, these effects are not necessarily long-term and may be diminished by being in a depressed emotional state. If antidepressants or other psychotropic drugs could be shown to have mood-elevating effects that are long-term and not diminished by being in a depressed emotional state, this could distinguish them from drugs that cause euphoria and prove uniquely useful in depressed patients. title: Cancer exosomes trigger fibroblast to myofibroblast differentiation.
text: There is a growing interest in the cell-to-cell communication roles of cancer cells through secreted vesicles called exosomes. In this study, we investigated whether exosomes produced by cancer cells could transmit information to normal stromal fibroblasts and elicit a cellular response. We discovered that some cancer-derived exosomes could induce increased α-smooth muscle actin expression and other changes consistent with fibroblast differentiation into myofibroblasts. We found that TGF-β is expressed on the surface of exosomes in association with the transmembrane proteoglycan betaglycan. Although TGF-β is typically latent, it was fully active in eliciting SMAD-dependent signaling when delivered via exosomes. Inhibiting either signaling or betaglycan expression reduced differentiation. Notably, the kinetics and overall magnitude of the response were similar to that achieved with soluble TGF-β, but we identified unique qualitative differences in the manner of TGF-β delivery through exosomes, such as a significant increase in fibroblast FGF2 production. These findings have important implications for our understanding of the mechanisms underlying cancer-recruited stroma, fibrotic diseases, and wound-healing responses.

title: A model of multiple myeloma: culture of 5T33 murine myeloma cells and evaluation of tumorigenicity in the C57BL/KaLwRij mouse.
text: The 5T33 multiple myeloma is part of a series of transplantable myelomas that spontaneously develop in C57BL/KaLwRij mice. This study investigates the establishment and characterization of the 5T33 myeloma cell line in vitro, focusing on its morphology, growth rate, paraprotein expression (specifically IgG2b), and tumorigenicity in syngeneic animals. The cell line has been continuously cultured for over 10 months and has undergone more than 34 passages. In culture, 5T33 myeloma cells grow as single cells or in small clusters of loosely adherent cells on a stromal cell layer. The maximum doubling time is around 25 hours, and over 90% of the cells express cytoplasmic IgG2b paraprotein. The cultured 5T33 myeloma cells are highly tumorigenic in C57BL/KaLwRij mice, with as few as 500 cells inducing paralysis and death as early as day 36 post-tumor inoculation. The kinetics of tumor development and IgG2b paraprotein detection are dose-dependent. Two weeks after intravenous inoculation of 5 x 105 cultured 5T33 myeloma cells, tumor cells can be identified in the bone marrow. By 3 weeks post-tumor inoculation, 5T33 myeloma cells are found in various tissues throughout the animal. Current research aims to determine the sensitivity of this cell line to various therapeutic modalities.

title: HIV Treatment as Prevention: Systematic Comparison of Mathematical Models of the Potential Impact of Antiretroviral Therapy on HIV Incidence in South Africa
text:
Background
Many mathematical models have studied the impact of expanding access to antiretroviral therapy (ART) on new HIV infections. However, comparing the results of these models has been challenging due to the different assumptions and questions addressed by each model. This study aims to determine the extent to which different mathematical models agree on the epidemiological impact of expanded ART by comparing their predictions for a set of standardized intervention scenarios in South Africa.
Methods and Findings
Twelve independent mathematical models evaluated a range of intervention scenarios in South Africa, varying the CD4 count threshold for treatment eligibility, access to treatment, and program retention. The models projected the impact of these interventions on HIV incidence over various time periods, including short-term (8 years) and long-term (38 years) reductions.
