Expression of N-cadherin in epithelial cells leads to changes in morphology that result in increased motility and invasiveness. However, in some cancers, such as osteosarcoma, N-cadherin may act as a tumor suppressor. N-cadherin can exhibit multiple functions, either promoting adhesion or inducing migration depending on the cellular context.

title: Role of fascin in filopodial protrusion
text: This study investigated the mechanisms underlying actin bundling in filopodia. By analyzing the localization of known actin cross-linking proteins in mouse melanoma B16F1 cells, it was found that fascin was specifically located along the entire length of all filopodia, while other actin cross-linkers were not. RNA interference-mediated silencing of fascin resulted in a reduction in the number of filopodia, and remaining filopodia displayed abnormal morphology with loose and wavy actin organization. It is likely that the dephosphorylation of serine 39 determines the frequency of cellular filopodia. The study found that a constitutively active mutant of fascin (S39A) increased the number and length of filopodia, while an inactive mutant (S39E) reduced filopodia frequency. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching of GFP-labeled wild-type and S39A fascin revealed that dephosphorylated fascin underwent rapid cycles of association and dissociation from actin filaments in filopodia, with a t1/2 < 10 s. The study proposes that fascin is a specific actin cross-linker that provides stiffness for filopodial bundles, and its dynamic behavior allows for efficient coordination between actin filament elongation and bundling.

title: TOR Signaling in Growth and Metabolism
text: The target of rapamycin (TOR) is a central regulator of cell growth and metabolism, conserved across species. In this review, we examine the role of TOR in mammalian cells, building on insights from studies in model organisms. TOR is composed of two distinct multiprotein complexes: TORC1, which is sensitive to rapamycin, and TORC2, which is not. Dysregulation of mammalian TORC1 has far-reaching consequences, suggesting that inhibitors of mammalian TOR may be useful in the treatment of various diseases, including cancer, cardiovascular disease, autoimmunity, and metabolic disorders.

title: Self-Organization of the Escherichia coli Chemotaxis Network Imaged with Super-Resolution Light Microscopy
text: The Escherichia coli chemotaxis network serves as a model system for biological signal processing. In E. coli, transmembrane receptors responsible for signal transmission aggregate into large clusters consisting of thousands of proteins. These sensory clusters are observed at cell poles and future division sites, despite extensive research, the mechanisms behind cluster formation, size regulation, and cellular location maintenance in growing and dividing cells remain unclear. To investigate, we employed photoactivated localization microscopy (PALM) to map the cellular locations of three key chemotaxis proteins (Tar receptor, CheY, and CheW) with unprecedented precision of 15 nanometers. Our findings reveal that cluster sizes follow an exponential distribution without a characteristic size, with approximately one-third of Tar receptors composing smaller lateral clusters distinct from the large polar clusters. By analyzing the spatial distribution of approximately 1.1 million individual proteins from 326 cells, we infer that clusters form via stochastic self-assembly. Our super-resolution PALM maps of E. coli receptors demonstrate that stochastic self-assembly can create and maintain periodic structures in biological membranes without direct cytoskeletal involvement or active transport.

title: Ciliary Extracellular Vesicles: Txt Msg Organelles
text: Cilia, specialized organelles on the surface of cells, play a crucial role in monitoring the surrounding environment and transmitting signals through the release of extracellular vesicles (EVs). This intercellular communication mechanism is conserved across all three domains of life and involves the shedding of sub-micron-sized EVs from ciliated cells. While the relationship between cilia and EVs remains poorly understood, recent studies in model organisms like Chlamydomonas and Caenorhabditis elegans have shed light on the biology of these extracellular organelles. In Chlamydomonas, EVs are shed from the tips of flagella and are bioactive, while in Caenorhabditis elegans, EVs are released in an intraflagellar transport-dependent manner by ciliated sensory neurons, and play a role in modulating animal-to-animal communication. Abnormal EV shedding or cilia-EV interactions have been linked to ciliopathies, a group of diseases characterized by defects in cilia structure and function. As research into cilia and EVs continues to advance, a new field of cell biology may emerge, with the cilium proposed as a dedicated organelle for EV biogenesis and reception. This review will explore the mechanisms by which EVs exert bioactivity, and how insights gained from model organisms may inform our understanding of human ciliopathies.

title: The NOD-like receptor NLRP12 attenuates colon inflammation and tumorigenesis.
text: NLRP12 is a member of the intracellular Nod-like receptor (NLR) family that has been proposed to downregulate the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, yet its role in regulating inflammation has not been extensively studied. To investigate its physiological function, we analyzed mice deficient in Nlrp12 and examined their susceptibility to inflammatory diseases such as colitis and colorectal tumorigenesis. Our findings revealed that Nlrp12-deficient mice are highly prone to colon inflammation and tumorigenesis, which is characterized by an increase in the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and tumorigenic factors. In contrast, normal mice with Nlrp12 expression exhibit markedly reduced colon inflammation and tumorigenesis. The underlying mechanism was found to be due to a failure of Nlrp12 to suppress NF-κB and ERK activation in macrophages, leading to uncontrolled inflammation and tumor development. These results illuminate a critical function of NLRP12 in maintaining gut homeostasis and providing protection against colorectal tumorigenesis.

title: Ionic mechanism of ouabain-induced concurrent apoptosis and necrosis in individual cultured cortical neurons
text:
Impaired function or deficiency of the Na+, K+-ATPase is a common effect of many pathological insults. However, the mechanism by which this affects cellular injury is not well understood. To investigate, we used cultured cortical neurons to examine the hypothesis that inhibiting the Na+, K+-ATPase leads to cell death through depletion of intracellular potassium and increase in intracellular calcium and sodium, accompanied by the release of cytochrome c, activation of caspases, and DNA damage.
We found that the Na+, K+-ATPase inhibitor ouabain caused concentration-dependent neuronal death. Ouabain triggered transient swelling of the cells followed by shrinkage, accompanied by an increase in intracellular calcium and sodium and a decrease in potassium, along with the release of cytochrome c, activation of caspases, and DNA laddering. Using electron microscopy, we observed the coexistence of ultrastructural features of both apoptosis and necrosis in individual cells.
We then tested the effectiveness of various drugs in preventing neuronal death caused by ouabain. Blocking caspases with the inhibitor Z-Val-Ala-Asp(OMe)-fluoromethyl ketone (Z-VAD-FMK) blocked more than half of the ouabain-induced neuronal death. Potassium channel blockers or high potassium medium, but not calcium channel blockade, prevented the release of cytochrome c, caspase activation, and DNA damage. In addition, combining the use of Z-VAD-FMK and nifedipine, which blocks calcium channels, produced near complete neuroprotection.
Our results suggest that the death of neurons caused by Na+, K+-pump failure involves a combination of apoptotic and necrotic components, mediated by the depletion of intracellular potassium and the accumulation of calcium and sodium, respectively. The hybrid death observed in ouabain-treated cells may represent a distinct form of cell death related to inadequate energy supply and disrupted ion homeostasis in the brain.

title: Potential consequences of replacing a retail alcohol monopoly with a private licence system: results from Sweden.
text:
Objective: To investigate the potential effects of replacing Sweden's alcohol retail system with a private licensing system on alcohol consumption and related harm.
Methodology: Two scenarios were analyzed: (1) replacing the current monopoly with private licensed stores specializing in alcohol sales, and (2) making all alcohol available in grocery stores. We employed a multiplicative model that projected the effects of changes in key factors such as hours of sale, retail prices, promotion, and advertising, as well as outlet density. These projections were then used to estimate the impact on a set of harm indicators. Parameter values were obtained from the scientific literature.
Main Findings: According to the projections, scenario 1 is expected to result in a 17% increase in consumption (1.4 liters/capita), leading to additional 770 deaths, 8500 assaults, 2700 drinking driving offenses, and 4.5 million sick days per year. Scenario 2 is expected to result in a 37.4% increase in consumption (3.1 liters/capita), leading to an additional annual toll of 2000 deaths, 20,000 assaults, 6600 drinking driving offenses, and 11.1 million days of sick leave.
Conclusions: The projections suggest that privatization of Sweden's alcohol retail market would significantly increase alcohol consumption and related harm, based on the findings of the study.

title: A comprehensive genomic binding map of gene and chromatin regulatory proteins in Saccharomyces.
text:
In Saccharomyces, hundreds of different proteins are involved in regulating and executing transcription. However, the relationships between these proteins have not been comprehensively studied. In this study, we determined the genome-wide binding locations of 200 transcription-related proteins under normal and acute heat-shock conditions. This allowed us to distinguish between binding at distal or proximal regions of promoters and the 3' ends of genes for nearly all mRNA and tRNA genes. Our findings reveal several key insights:
Firstly, we found that the SAGA transcription pathway exhibits greater diversity and specialization in its regulation compared to the TFIID pathway.
Secondly, we discovered new regulators enriched at tRNA genes, which highlights the importance of these genes in the regulation of transcription.
Thirdly, we identified a global co-occupancy network of over 20,000 unique regulator combinations that show a high degree of regulatory interconnections among lowly expressed genes.
Fourthly, we found that regulators of the SAGA pathway are mostly located distal to the core promoter, while regulators of the TFIID pathway are primarily located proximal to the promoter.
Finally, we observed distinct mobilization of SAGA- versus TFIID-linked regulators during acute heat shock, demonstrating the dynamic nature of transcriptional regulation.
In summary, this study highlights the complexity and interconnectedness of transcriptional regulation in Saccharomyces, with distinct pathways, regulators, and networks operating in different parts of the genome.

title: Tie2/Angiopoietin-1 Signaling Regulates Hematopoietic Stem Cell Quiescence in the Bone Marrow Niche
text: The state of dormancy, or quiescence, is essential for the proper functioning of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) in the bone marrow (BM). These cells interact with specific microenvironments, known as stem cell niches, to support adult hematopoiesis. Our research has shown that HSCs expressing the receptor tyrosine kinase Tie2 are quiescent and resistant to programmed cell death, and comprise a distinct population of HSCs known as the side-population (SP). These cells adhere to osteoblasts (OBs) in the BM niche. The interaction between Tie2 and its ligand Angiopoietin-1 (Ang-1) promotes the formation of cobblestone-like structures in HSCs in vitro and maintains their long-term repopulating activity in vivo. In addition, Ang-1 enhances the ability of HSCs to enter a quiescent state and adhere to bone, providing protection against myelosuppressive stress. These findings suggest that the Tie2/Ang-1 signaling pathway plays a critical role in maintaining HSCs in a quiescent state within the BM niche.

title: Thirty-One Novel Biomarkers as Predictors for Clinically Incident Diabetes
text:
Studies have shown that the prevalence of diabetes is increasing in industrialized countries, making it a major public health concern. However, there is a lack of understanding about the factors that contribute to the risk of developing diabetes. In this study, we evaluated the potential of 31 novel biomarkers to predict the risk of incident diabetes.
We analyzed data from the FINRISK97 cohort (n = 7,827; 417 cases of clinically incident diabetes during the follow-up) and the Health 2000 cohort (n = 4,977; 179 cases of clinically incident diabetes during the follow-up). We used Cox proportional hazards models to calculate the relative risk of diabetes after adjusting for classic risk factors, and then assessed the discriminatory ability of individual biomarkers using receiver operating characteristic curves and C-statistics, integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and net reclassification improvement (NRI).
Our findings revealed that a biomarker score consisting of adiponectin, apolipoprotein B, C-reactive protein, and ferritin almost doubled the relative risk of diabetes in the validation cohort (HR per one standard deviation increase of 1.88, p = 2.8 e-5). Additionally, the score improved discrimination of the model (IDI = 0.0149, p<0.0001) and reclassification of diabetes risk (NRI = 11.8%, p = 0.006). Gender-specific analyses showed that the best score differed between men and women. Among men, the best results were obtained with a score of four biomarkers (adiponectin, apolipoprotein B, ferritin, and interleukin-1 receptor antagonist), which gave an NRI of 25.4% (p<0.0001). Among women, the best score included adiponectin, apolipoprotein B, C-reactive protein, and insulin, which gave an NRI of 13.6% (p = 0.041).
In conclusion, our study identified novel biomarkers that were associated with the risk of clinically incident diabetes over and above classic risk factors. These findings provide new insights into the pathogenesis of diabetes and may help with targeting prevention and treatment.

title: Exploiting lymphatic transport and complement activation in nanoparticle vaccines
text:
In vaccine development, researchers have explored the use of antigen targeting and adjuvant strategies to enhance the delivery of antigens to dendritic cells and activate them. In this study, we investigate the potential of nanoparticles as a vaccine platform by targeting dendritic cells in lymph nodes through interstitial flow and in situ complement activation.
We evaluated the efficiency of ultra-small nanoparticles (25 nm) and larger nanoparticles (100 nm) in delivering antigen to lymph node-residing dendritic cells. Our results showed that the smaller nanoparticles were much more efficient, targeting half of the dendritic cells in the lymph nodes, while the larger nanoparticles were only 10% as effective.
We also found that the surface chemistry of the nanoparticles played a crucial role in activating the complement cascade, which in turn activated the dendritic cells in situ. To demonstrate this, we used nanoparticles conjugated to the model antigen ovalbumin and demonstrated the generation of both humoral and cellular immunity in mice in a size- and complement-dependent manner.
Overall, our findings suggest that nanoparticles have great potential as a vaccine platform, enabling the efficient delivery of antigens to dendritic cells in lymph nodes and promoting strong immune responses.

title: The sheddase ADAM10 is a potent modulator of prion disease
text: The prion protein (PrP(C)) is highly expressed in the nervous system and plays a critical role in prion diseases, where it misfolds into the pathogenic form PrP(Sc). Some research has suggested that PrP(C) may also act as a receptor for neurotoxicity in common neurodegenerative proteinopathies such as Alzheimer's disease. PrP(C) is shed from the plasma membrane by the enzyme ADAM10, but the impact of this shedding on prion disease is not well understood. Using conditional knockout mice, we found that reducing the amount of ADAM10 in forebrain neurons leads to an increase in PrP(C) levels. When these mice are infected with prions, we observe that the absence of ADAM10 significantly shortens the incubation time and increases the formation of the pathogenic PrP(Sc) form. However, our spatiotemporal analysis suggests that the absence of shedding actually impairs the spread of prion pathology. Our data suggest a dual role for ADAM10-mediated shedding in prion disease and highlight the importance of proteolytic processing in the progression of prion diseases.

title: High-affinity zinc inhibition of NMDA NR1-NR2A receptors
text: Research has shown that micromolar concentrations of extracellular zinc (Zn2+) can antagonize native N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors through two distinct mechanisms: a voltage-independent inhibition and a voltage-dependent inhibition. To evaluate the relative importance of these mechanisms and their subunit specificity, we studied recombinant NMDA receptors expressed in HEK 293 cells and Xenopus oocytes. Our findings revealed that the voltage-dependent inhibition is similar in both types of receptors, but the voltage-independent inhibition occurs at lower Zn2+ concentrations in NR1a-NR2A receptors (IC50 in the nanomolar range) than in NR1a-NR2B receptors (IC50 in the micromolar range). The high affinity of the effect observed with NR1a-NR2A receptors is attributable to the slow dissociation of Zn2+ from its binding site. By analyzing the effects of Zn2+ on varied combinations of NR1 (NR1a or NR1b) and NR2 (NR2A, NR2B, NR2C) subunits, we found that both the NR1 and NR2 subunits contribute to the voltage-independent Zn2+ inhibition. Interestingly, under control conditions, the addition of low concentrations of heavy metal chelators markedly potentiates the responses of NR1a-NR2A receptors, but not of NR1a-NR2B receptors. This suggests that traces of a heavy metal (probably Zn2+) contaminate standard solutions and tonically inhibit NR1a-NR2A receptors. Furthermore, chelation of a contaminant metal may account for the rapid NR2A subunit-specific potentiations produced by reducing agents like DTT or glutathione.

title: PrimPol, an Archaic Primase/Polymerase Operating in Human Cells
text: We recently discovered a second primase in human cells, known as PrimPol, which has the unique ability to initiate DNA synthesis with deoxynucleotides, unlike regular primases that only use ribonucleotides. In addition, PrimPol is an optimized DNA polymerase that specifically targets and bypasses the most common oxidative DNA damage, such as abasic sites and 8-oxoguanine, found in both nuclear and mitochondrial DNA. Our subcellular fractionation and immunodetection studies showed that PrimPol is present in both nuclear and mitochondrial DNA compartments. Interestingly, we found that PrimPol activity can be detected in mitochondrial lysates from human and mouse cells, but its presence is absent in mitochondria from PRIMPOL knockout mice. Furthermore, silencing or ablation of the PRIMPOL gene in human and mouse cells significantly impaired mitochondrial DNA replication. Based on the observed synergy between PrimPol and replicative DNA polymerases Polγ and Polε, we propose that PrimPol functions as a translesion DNA polymerase or a specific DNA primase, reinitiating DNA synthesis downstream of lesions that block replication during both nuclear and mitochondrial DNA replication.

title: Predictors of Attrition and Academic Success of Medical Students: A 30-Year Retrospective Study
text:
Objective: To determine the rate of attrition and identify predictors of academic success among medical students at the University of Split in Croatia.
Methods: We analyzed academic records of 2054 students enrolled between 1979 and 2008. We found that 26% (533/2054) of students did not graduate, with the most common reasons being "personal" factors (36.4%), transfer to another medical school (35.6%), and dismissal due to unsatisfactory academic performance (21.2%). We also observed that students with higher parental education levels had a higher grade point average (GPA) and studied for a longer duration. Only 6.4% (42/654) of students graduated in the prescribed 5-year curriculum, while 55% (240/472) of students graduated in time after the curriculum was extended to 6 years. We identified high school grades, entrance exam score, and year of enrollment as predictors of academic success. Specifically, high school grades and entrance exam score were significant predictors of graduation grades, while entrance exam score predicted the length of studying.
Conclusion: Our findings suggest that preadmission academic qualifications and year of enrollment are important predictors of academic success in medical school. Addressing the high attrition rate is crucial to improving academic outcomes.

title: Mechanical regulation of cell function with geometrically modulated elastomeric substrates
text: We have established a library of micromolded elastomeric micropost arrays that allow for independent modification of the rigidity of the post surface. By modulating the rigidity of the microposts, we demonstrated that the stiffness of the substrate can impact cell morphology, focal adhesions, cytoskeletal contractility, and stem cell differentiation. Additionally, we found that early changes in cytoskeletal contractility can predict later stem cell fate decisions in individual cells.

title: THE EMBO JOURNAL
text: "Glutamate-gated ion channels, known as ionotropic glutamate receptors (iGluRs), detect their surrounding environment through a prominent extracellular region, composed of two clamshell-shaped segments. The distal, N-terminal domain (NTD) in N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA)-type iGluRs possesses allosteric potential, a characteristic not observed in the analogous domain of α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptors (AMPARs). In this study, we present new structural data that reveal the dynamic properties of the GluA2 and GluA3 AMPAR NTDs. Unexpectedly, the GluA3 NTD adopts a zipped-open dimer interface, bearing unconstrained lower clamshell lobes, similar to metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs). This unique feature allows for interprotomer rotations, which can be transmitted to downstream receptor segments. Using normal mode analysis, we identify two primary mechanisms of AMPAR NTD motion: intraprotomer clamshell motions and interprotomer counter-rotations, as well as a switchable interconversion between AMPAR and mGluR conformations. Moreover, we detect electronic densities for a potential ligand in the GluA2 interlobe cleft, suggesting that this region may play a dynamic role in receptor function. Collectively, these findings suggest that the AMPAR NTDs may play a more dynamic role in the receptor, expanding the allosteric landscape and potentially creating new opportunities for ligand development."

title: A complex secretory program orchestrated by the inflammasome controls paracrine senescence
text: Oncogene-induced senescence (OIS) is crucial for tumor suppression. Senescent cells exhibit a complex pro-inflammatory response known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which reinforces senescence, activates immune surveillance, and paradoxically, also has pro-tumorigenic properties. Here, we present evidence that the SASP can also induce paracrine senescence in normal cells both in vitro and in vivo. By combining quantitative proteomics with small-molecule screens, we identified multiple SASP components mediating paracrine senescence, including transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) family ligands, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), club cell secretory protein 2 (CCL2), and CCL20. Among these, TGF-β ligands play a major role in regulating p15(INK4b) and p21(CIP1). The expression of the SASP is controlled by inflammasome-mediated interleukin-1 (IL-1) signaling. The inflammasome and IL-1 signaling are activated in senescent cells, and IL-1α expression can reproduce SASP activation, resulting in senescence. Our findings demonstrate that the SASP can cause paracrine senescence and impact tumor suppression and senescence in vivo.

title: Prospective Study of One Million Deaths in India: Rationale, Design, and Validation Results
text: Over 75% of India's estimated 9.5 million annual deaths occur at home, with the majority lacking a certified cause. India and other developing countries need better data on the causes of death, including physical measurements such as blood pressure and obesity, behavioral factors like smoking and HIV risk, and biological factors like blood lipids and gene polymorphisms. This report outlines the design and implementation of the world's largest prospective study to identify the causes and correlates of mortality. Nearly 14 million people in 2.4 million Indian households will be monitored through a well-validated verbal autopsy instrument to determine their vital status and, if deceased, the underlying causes of death. This study will provide comprehensive data on both the underlying causes of child and adult deaths and key risk factors, including behavioral, physical, environmental, and genetic factors. It offers a globally replicable model for estimating cause-specific mortality using verbal autopsy and strengthens India's mortality monitoring system. Although some misclassification is expected, the new cause-of-death data will be significantly better than previously available. [PLoS Medicine, February 2006]

title: Genome-wide identification of genes directly regulated by the pleiotropic transcription factor Spx in Bacillus subtilis
text: The transcriptional regulator Spx plays a crucial role in maintaining the redox balance of Bacillus subtilis cells under disulfide stress. Previous studies have shown that defects in Spx lead to abnormal expression of numerous genes, but the direct and indirect regulatory effects could not be distinguished. To investigate the direct regulation of Spx, we used chromatin immunoprecipitation to identify 283 potential binding sites of the Spx-RNA polymerase (Spx-RNAP) complex on the chromosome. We found that three-quarters of these sites were located near Sigma(A)-dependent promoters, and upon exposure to diamide, the fraction of the Spx-RNAP complex increased, along with the number and occupancy of DNA sites. Analysis of Spx-RNAP-binding sites in wild-type and Spx-deficient strains exposed or not to diamide revealed that 144 transcription units comprising 275 genes were potentially under direct Spx regulation. Notably, Spx-controlled promoters had an extended -35 box, and the nucleotide composition at positions -43/-44 strongly correlated with observed activation. In vitro transcription experiments confirmed the activation of seven newly identified promoters, including one that was also activated by reduced Spx. Our study provides a global characterization of the Spx regulatory network, revealing its role in the basal expression of some genes and its complex interplay with other stress responses.

title: Expression of interleukin-18 in human atherosclerotic plaques and relation to plaque instability.
text:
Background: Interleukin-18 (IL-18) is a proinflammatory cytokine with potential atherogenic properties, but its expression and role in atherosclerosis are still unclear.
Methods and Results: In this study, we investigated the presence and distribution of IL-18 in human carotid atherosclerotic plaques retrieved by endarterectomy using reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (PCR), Western blot, and immunohistochemical techniques. IL-18 was found to be highly expressed in atherosclerotic plaques compared to control normal arteries, primarily localized in plaque macrophages. The IL-18 receptor was also upregulated in plaque macrophages and endothelial cells, suggesting potential biological effects. To explore the role of IL-18 in atherosclerosis, we examined the relation between IL-18 mRNA expression and signs of plaque instability using real-time quantitative PCR. Interestingly, significantly higher levels of IL-18 mRNA were detected in symptomatic (unstable) plaques compared to asymptomatic (stable) plaques (P < 0.01).
Conclusions: These findings suggest a major role of IL-18 in atherosclerotic plaque destabilization leading to acute ischemic syndromes, which is a new insight into the mechanisms of atherosclerosis. This study highlights the potential of IL-18 as a therapeutic target for the prevention and treatment of atherosclerosis-related cardiovascular diseases.

title: US-SOMO HPLC-SAXS module: dealing with capillary fouling and extraction of pure component patterns from poorly resolved SEC-SAXS data
text: Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) coupled with small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), commonly performed using a flow-through capillary, can provide direct collection of monodisperse sample data. However, issues such as capillary fouling and non-baseline-resolved peaks can hinder the effectiveness of the method. The UltraScan solution modeler (US-SOMO) HPLC-SAXS module, which offers a comprehensive framework for analyzing SAXS data, has been updated with new features and improvements. These include linear baseline correction and symmetrical Gaussian decomposition tools, as well as the ability to evaluate outcomes using advanced statistical methods. A novel integral baseline-correction procedure has been developed, which takes into account the increasing impact of capillary fouling on scattering intensity as the material within the X-ray beam intensifies. Additionally, overlapping peaks can now be accurately decomposed using non-symmetrical modified Gaussian functions. As an example, the analysis of a polydisperse solution of aldolase demonstrates the ability to extract and reliably model individual SAXS profiles of tetramers, octamers, and dodecamers from heavily convoluted peaks.

title: Determination of Malaria Epidemiological Status in Iran’s Malarious Areas as Baseline Information for Implementation of Malaria Elimination Program in Iran
text:
BACKGROUND
According to the Ministry of Health's willingness and with the appropriate conditions in place, Iran's national malaria control program conducted a research study in 2007 to gather information on malaria status and provide necessary data for the elimination program. This review is based on the vision of the national malaria elimination program by 2025, which began in 2010.
METHODS
In this descriptive study, data was analyzed through various variables at the district level. All districts in the three southeastern provinces where malaria is transmitted locally were included. Malaria cases were determined and studied based on the national malaria surveillance system.
RESULTS
As vivax malaria predominates in Sistan & Baluchestan Province, the number of vivax cases is approximately equal to malaria positive cases. The maximum number of local vivax cases is found in Nikshahr, and the maximum number of falciparum cases is reported from Sarbaz district. In Hormozgan Province, no cases of autochthonous falciparum were found except in Bandar Jask and one case in Minab. Moreover, there were no cases of autochthonous falciparum in Kerman Province, except in Kahnoj and Ghale Ganj, each with one case in 2007.
CONCLUSION
The report of locally transmitted cases in Iran has increased over the past few years, before the implementation of the malaria elimination plan. With the return of Afghan refugees to their home country, the main source of reporting of imported malaria cases has reduced, allowing for a clearer demonstration of local cases.

title: Local neuroinflammation and the progression of Alzheimer’s disease
text: Postmortem immunohistochemical studies have uncovered a state of persistent inflammation confined to affected brain regions in Alzheimer's disease. Key players in this inflammatory process include activated microglia (brain macrophages), proteins from the classical complement cascade, pentraxins, cytokines, and chemokines. In contrast to the adaptive immune system, which is not involved in this inflammation, the innate immune system - which is older and more primitive - appears to be the primary underlying mechanism. This chronic inflammation can lead to damage to host tissue, and the brain may be particularly susceptible due to its postmitotic nature, making it more vulnerable to inflammation. Many inflammatory mediators have been shown to be produced locally and selectively elevated in affected areas of the Alzheimer's brain. Similar inflammatory responses have been observed in conditions like atherosclerosis and infarcted heart, suggesting their potential relevance to other degenerative disorders. While nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) have shown some promise in delaying the onset and progression of Alzheimer's disease, these drugs primarily target inflammation at the periphery. More effective results may be achieved by developing drugs that target the activation of microglia or the complement system directly in the brain, and combining multiple drugs with different targets may prove more effective than single agents.

title: BLAST+: architecture and applications
text:
Sure, here is a possible rewrite of the given text:
Background: Sequence similarity searching is a fundamental bioinformatics task, critical for identifying homologies, inferring evolutionary relationships, and understanding genetic function. While Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (BLAST) remains the gold standard for exact methods, its effectiveness is hindered by sluggish performance when dealing with extremely long queries or large databases. Current command-line applications also suffer from a lack of user-friendliness.
Results: To address these limitations, we comprehensively rewrote the BLAST software and introduced novel command-line applications. Our innovations include:
* Segmentation of long queries into more manageable chunks for processing, resulting in significantly reduced run times.
* FOR long database sequences, the ability to retrieve only the relevant parts of the sequence, thereby reducing CPU time and memory usage for short queries against databases of contigs or chromosomes.
* Integration of masking information for database sequences from BLAST databases, enhancing accuracy and efficiency.
* Design of a modular software library that can access subject sequence data from diverse data sources, providing enhanced versatility and convenience.
* Introduction of strategy files, enabling users to save and reuse their preferred set of options. These files can be uploaded to/downloaded from the NCBI BLAST web site for easy sharing and collaboration.
Conclusion: Compared to conventional BLAST tools, our newly designed command-line applications exhibit substantial speed gains for lengthy queries and chromosome-length database sequences. Moreover, we have streamlined the user interface of the command-line applications, making them more user-friendly and accessible to a broader range of users.

title: Intrauterine environments and breast cancer risk: meta-analysis and systematic review
text:
INTRODUCTION Perinatal factors, including birth weight, birth order, maternal age, gestational age, twin status, and paternal smoking, have been linked to breast cancer risk in daughters. While there is biological plausibility to these associations, epidemiological studies have yielded conflicting results. To address this, we conducted meta-analyses of breast cancer studies that provided data on these perinatal factors and breast cancer risk.
METHODS We reviewed studies published between January 1966 and February 2007 that reported data on birth weight, birth order, maternal age, gestational age, twin status, and paternal smoking. Using random effect models, we performed meta-analyses to summarize the results.
RESULTS Our findings indicate that higher birth weights are associated with increased breast cancer risk. Studies grouping birth weights into five categories found odds ratios (ORs) of 1.24 (95% CI 1.04-1.48) for birth weights of 4,000 grams or more and 1.15 (95% CI 1.04-1.26) for birth weights of 3,500-3,999 grams, compared to a birth weight of 2,500-2,599 grams. These results do not support a J-shaped relationship between birth weight and breast cancer risk. Similarly, studies based on three birth weight categories found an OR of 1.15 (95% CI 1.01-1.31) for birth weights of 4,000 grams or more compared to less than 3,000 grams, and studies based on two birth weight categories found an OR of 1.09 (95% CI 1.02-1.18) for birth weights of 3,000-3,999 grams compared to less than 3,000 grams. Women born to older mothers and twins were also found to be at some increased risk, although the results were heterogeneous across studies and publication years. Birth order, prematurity, and paternal smoking were unrelated to breast cancer risk.
CONCLUSION Our findings suggest that in utero exposures reflective of higher endogenous hormone levels may affect breast cancer risk in adulthood.

title: Epidemiologic studies on Dengue in Santiago de Cuba, 1997.
text: An insignificant outbreak of dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome (DHF/DSS) caused by the dengue virus type 2 (DEN-2) occurred in Santiago de Cuba, Cuba, starting in January 1997. There were 205 DHF/DSS cases, all affecting individuals above the age of 15. All but three patients had a previous dengue infection, with the only known opportunity being the island-wide dengue virus type 1 (DEN-1) epidemic of 1977-1979. Comprehensive clinical and laboratory surveillance was conducted on all overt cases of dengue. Between December 1997 and January 1998, a random, age-stratified serum sample was collected from 1,151 residents in 40 residential clusters in Santiago, and the sera were tested for DEN-1 and DEN-2 neutralizing antibodies. The prevalence of DEN-2 antibodies in children under the age of 15, born after the 1981 DEN-2 epidemic, was taken as the 1997 DEN-2 infection rate. This was adjusted slightly to account for observed cases, resulting in an estimated infection rate of 4.3%. The dengue fever and DHF/DSS attack rates were calculated based on estimated total primary and secondary DEN-2 infections. Only 3% of 13,116 primary infections were overt. The DHF/DSS attack rate for adults of all ages was 420 per 10,000 secondary DEN-2 infections.

title: Prognostic and Predictive Value of KRAS Mutations in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
text: Despite the known association between KRAS mutations and poor prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the clinical implications of these mutations in advanced disease remain unclear. To investigate this further, we retrospectively evaluated the prognostic and predictive value of KRAS mutations in patients with advanced NSCLC. Our analysis included 484 patients with available results for both KRAS and EGFR mutations, of whom 39 (8%) had KRAS mutations, 182 (38%) had EGFR mutations, and two patients had both mutations. Notably, the median overall survival for patients with KRAS mutations, EGFR mutations, or both wild types was significantly lower for patients with KRAS mutations compared to those with EGFR mutations (7.7, 38.0, and 15.0 months, respectively; P<0.001). In multivariate analysis, KRAS mutation status was an independent poor prognostic factor (hazard ratio = 2.6, 95% CI: 1.8-3.7). Interestingly, response rates and progression-free survival (PFS) were inferior in patients with KRAS mutations who received pemetrexed-based therapy compared to those with KRAS wild type (14% vs 28% and 2.1 vs 3.9 months, respectively). However, there was no significant difference in treatment outcomes between the two groups when gemcitabine-based chemotherapy was used. While the clinical outcomes of EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) appeared better in patients with KRAS wild type, there was no statistical difference in response rates and PFS according to KRAS mutation status when EGFR mutation status was considered. Two patients with both KRAS and EGFR mutations showed partial response to EGFR TKIs. Notably, G12D mutation was more common in never smokers, but there was no difference in clinical outcomes according to KRAS genotypes. Overall, these findings suggest that KRAS mutations have an independent prognostic value but a limited predictive role for EGFR TKIs or cytotoxic chemotherapy in advanced NSCLC.

title: A Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Covariance Matrix Estimator And A Direct Test For Heteroskedasticity
text: This paper proposes a parameter covariance matrix estimator that is consistent even when the residuals of a linear regression model exhibit heteroskedasticity. Unlike traditional estimators that rely on a specific model for the structure of the heteroskedasticity, this new estimator is model-free, providing a direct test for heteroskedasticity. By comparing the elements of the proposed estimator to those of the standard covariance estimator, one can determine whether or not the residuals exhibit heteroskedasticity, as the two estimators will generally diverge when the residuals are heteroskedastic, but will be approximately equal in the absence of heteroskedasticity. The test has a convenient least squares interpretation.

title: Two Subsets of Naive T Helper Cells with Distinct T Cell Receptor Excision Circle Content in Human Adult Peripheral Blood
text:
Here is a possible reconstruction of the given text with a more formal and technical tone:
During the aging process, thymic function declines, leading to an inability to meet the demand for peripheral T helper (Th) cell replenishment. Consequently, the maintenance of naive Th cells in the population must be at least partially reliant on peripheral expansion. Postthymic peripheral expansion of recent thymic emigrants (RTEs) that occurs during aging can lead to the loss or dilution of T cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) from a subset of naive T cells.
To investigate this phenomenon, we have identified two subsets of naive Th cells in human adult peripheral blood, differentiated by an unequal content of TRECs, indicating distinct peripheral proliferative histories. TRECs are highly enriched in peripheral naive CD45RA+ Th cells coexpressing CD31 compared to peripheral naive CD45RA+ Th cells lacking CD31 expression, where TRECs are barely detectable. We have also observed that CD31−CD45RA+ Th cells comprise an increasing proportion of the naive peripheral Th cell pool with age, yet retain the functional and phenotypic characteristics of naive Th cells.
It is hypothesized that TCR triggering is a prerequisite for homeostatically driven peripheral postthymic expansion of human naive RTEs. In line with this, we have identified peripherally expanded naive Th cells in human adult blood characterized by the loss of CD31 expression and a highly reduced TREC content.

title: A Role for the Vacuolating Cytotoxin, VacA, in Colonization and Helicobacter pylori–Induced Metaplasia in the Stomach
text: Carrying Helicobacter pylori strains with more active (s1/i1) forms of the VacA toxin is strongly linked to gastric adenocarcinoma. To our knowledge, we are the first to investigate the effects of various polymorphic forms of VacA on inflammation and metaplasia in the mouse stomach. Intriguingly, bacteria producing the less active s2/i2 form of VacA colonized mice more efficiently than mutants lacking VacA or producing more active forms of it, providing the first evidence of a beneficial role for the minimally active s2/i2 toxin. Notably, strains producing more active toxin forms induced more severe and extensive metaplasia and inflammation in the mouse stomach compared to strains producing weakly active (s2/i2) toxin. We also examined the association in humans, controlling for cagPAI status. In human gastric biopsy samples, the vacA i1 allele was strongly linked to precancerous intestinal metaplasia, with a near-absence of intestinal metaplasia in individuals infected with i2-type strains, even in a vacA s1, cagA(+) background.

title: Systematic review of role of bisphosphonates on skeletal morbidity in metastatic cancer.
text:
Objective: To systematically review the evidence for the use of bisphosphonates in reducing skeletal morbidity in cancer patients with bone metastases.
Data Sources: Electronic databases, such as MEDLINE and EMBASE, were searched, along with reference lists and consultations with experts and pharmaceutical companies. Foreign language papers were included.
Study Selection: Randomized controlled trials of patients with malignant disease and bone metastases treated with oral or intravenous bisphosphonates, compared to placebo, another bisphosphonate, or standard care, were included. All trials measured at least one outcome of skeletal morbidity.
Results: Of 95 identified articles, 30 studies fulfilled inclusion criteria. In long-term studies, bisphosphonates significantly reduced the odds ratio for fractures (vertebral, 0.69; non-vertebral, 0.65; combined, 0.65), radiotherapy (0.67), and hypercalcaemia (0.54), but not for orthopaedic surgery (0.70) or spinal cord compression (0.71). The reduction in orthopaedic surgery was significant in studies lasting over a year (0.59). Use of bisphosphonates significantly increased time to first skeletal related event, but did not affect survival. Subanalyses revealed that most evidence supports the use of intravenous aminobisphosphonates.
Conclusions: In people with metastatic bone disease, bisphosphonates significantly decrease skeletal morbidity, with the exception of spinal cord compression and increased time to first skeletal related event. Treatment should be initiated when bone metastases are diagnosed and continued until it is no longer clinically relevant.

title: Rodent Models of Depression: Neurotrophic and Neuroinflammatory Biomarkers
text: Rodent models are invaluable for studying the etiology and progression of depression. As interconnected systems of neurotrophic factors and cytokines regulate normal brain plasticity, impairments in these systems are the underlying cause of cerebral pathologies, including mental disorders. This review focuses on various experimental rodent models of depression induced by different stress factors (including exteroceptive and interoceptive stressors) during early life (including prenatal period) or adulthood, with an emphasis on changes in neurotrophic factors and neuroinflammatory indices in the brain. These parameters are closely linked to behavioral depression-like symptoms, impairments in neuronal plasticity, and are influenced by both gender and genotype. Region-specific changes in stress-related expression of neurotrophins and cytokines in the rodent brain are observed. Although experimental models are not a direct representation of clinical depression, they provide valuable insights into the involvement of neurotrophic factors and cytokines in the pathogenesis of the disease. These major regulatory systems may serve as therapeutic targets or drug development for depression treatment.

title: The docking domain of histone H2A is required for H1 binding and RSC-mediated nucleosome remodeling
text: Histone variants within the H2A family exhibit significant divergence in their C-terminal regions. This study investigates the role of these variations in the structural and functional properties of the nucleosome. Using a combination of biochemical methods and advanced imaging techniques such as Atomic Force Microscopy and Electron Cryo-Microscopy, we uncover the importance of the H2A-docking domain as a key structural feature within the nucleosome. Deletion or replacement of this domain with the incomplete docking domain from the variant H2A.Bbd leads to significant structural alterations in the nucleosome, including increased accessibility to nucleases, un-wrapping of 10 base pairs of DNA from each end of the nucleosome, and changes in the entry/exit angle of DNA ends. These structural modifications also impair the ability of the chromatin remodeler RSC to remodel and mobilize the nucleosomes, and abrogate linker histone H1 binding in nucleosomes containing the incomplete docking domain of H2A.Bbd. Our findings highlight the unique role of the H2A-docking domain in coordinating the structural and functional aspects of nucleosome properties. Moreover, our data suggest that the incorporation of a 'defective' docking domain may be a primary structural role of H2A.Bbd in chromatin.

title: Regulation of poly(A) site choice of several yeast mRNAs
text: In yeast, multiple genes produce multiple transcripts with different 3' ends. Of these, four genes are known to produce truncated transcripts that end within the coding sequence of longer transcripts: CBP1, AEP2/ATP13, RNA14, and SIR1. It has been shown that the level of the truncated CBP1 transcript increases during the transition to respiratory growth, while the level of the full-length transcript decreases. To determine whether this phenomenon is unique to CBP1, northern blot analysis was performed to investigate whether the levels of other truncated transcripts are also regulated similarly by carbon source. The levels of the shortest transcripts of AEP2/ATP13 and RNA14 increased during respiration, while the shortest SIR1 transcript remained constant. However, two longer SIR1 transcripts were regulated reciprocally by carbon source. Using sequencing of partial cDNA clones, the 3' ends of each transcript were mapped, revealing multiple 3' ends for each transcript. Examination of the sequences surrounding the 3' ends of the induced transcripts failed to identify a consensus sequence, but weak putative 3' end formation signals were identified in all of the transcripts. Similarly, no consensus sequence was found when the sequences surrounding the 3' ends of the longest transcripts were compared, but again weak putative 3' end formation signals were identified. These data suggest that carbon source regulation of alternative poly(A) site choice is present in yeast.

title: Circular RNA and miR-7 in cancer.
text: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) play a crucial role in fine-tuning gene expression and are frequently deregulated in cancer. The discovery of competing endogenous RNAs (ceRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs) as key regulators of miRNA activity highlights the growing complexity of non-coding RNA (ncRNA)-mediated regulatory networks. Of particular interest is the recently identified circRNA, ciRS-7, which acts as a designated miR-7 inhibitor/sponge, significantly altering our understanding of miRNA networks. As miR-7 regulates the expression of several oncogenes, elucidating the control of miR-7 activity may shed light on various cancer etiologies. In this review, we discuss the current knowledge on the ciRS-7/miR-7 axis in cancer-related pathways and propose possible models to explain the significance of coexpressing miR-7 alongside a circRNA inhibitor.

title: Angiotensin II Evokes Angiogenic Signals within Skeletal Muscle through Co-ordinated Effects on Skeletal Myocytes and Endothelial Cells
text: Our research has shown that when skeletal muscle is subjected to overload, it induces the production of angiogenic factors such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-2, leading to the growth of new blood vessels. We found that mice lacking the gene for VEGF (VEGF KO mice) do not exhibit this overload-induced increase in angiogenesis, highlighting the critical role of myocyte-derived VEGF in controlling this process. We also discovered that muscle overload increases the expression of angiotensinogen, a precursor of the potent vasoactive peptide angiotensin (Ang) II, and that Ang II signaling plays a key role in basal VEGF production in C2C12 cells. Furthermore, we found that matrix-bound VEGF released from myoblasts can activate endothelial cells, leading to elevated phospho-p38 levels. Interestingly, we also observed that exogenous Ang II can elevate VEGF expression and MMP-2 transcript levels in C2C12 myotubes, and that endothelial cells in response to Ang II treatment exhibit similar responses. To investigate the involvement of Ang II in muscle overload-induced angiogenesis, we blocked AT1R-dependent Ang II signaling using losartan. Surprisingly, we found that increased levels of VEGF protein were detected in overloaded muscle from losartan-treated rats, and that VEGF production is also elevated in cultured endothelial cells treated with losartan alone or in combination with Ang II. These findings demonstrate the requirement for muscle-derived VEGF in overload-induced angiogenesis and highlight a role for Ang II in basal VEGF production in skeletal muscle. However, while Ang II signaling is activated following overload and plays a role in muscle VEGF production, inhibition of this pathway is not sufficient to halt overload-induced angiogenesis, suggesting that AT1-independent signals maintain VEGF production in losartan-treated muscle.

title: A specific loop in human DNA polymerase mu allows switching between creative and DNA-instructed synthesis
text: Human DNA polymerase mu (Polμ) is a member of the X family that exhibits terminal transferase activity, despite utilizing an unorthodox method of selecting templates for catalysis. Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) is comparable to Polμ in certain aspects, including the presence of a specific loop (loop1) that grants TdT its transferase activity. Upon deletion of loop1 from Polμ, the enzyme loses its TdT activity but gains improved DNA binding and template-dependent polymerization capabilities. Conversely, when loop1 from TdT is inserted into Polμ, the resulting chimera reacquires TdT activity but exhibits a reduced capacity for template-dependent polymerization. This suggests that a unique loop structure in Polμ allows for a dual function: (i) the creation of new DNA information through template independence, in which loop1 plays an active role as a 'pseudotemplate'; and (ii) the polymerization of template-dependent strands. Recent in vivo and in vitro data suggest that this dual functionality may be advantageous in resolving microhomology-mediated end-joining reactions.

title: Dnmt1-Independent CG Methylation Contributes to Nucleosome Positioning in Diverse Eukaryotes
text: Dnmt1, an epigenetic enzyme, propagates symmetrical CG methylation across many eukaryotic genomes. However, these genomes typically lack CG dinucleotides due to imperfect repair of deaminated methylcytosines. Contrary to expectations, we uncover a novel DNA methyltransferase family, Dnmt5, that catalyzes symmetrical CG methylation in a diverse range of organisms lacking Dnmt1.remarkably, these organisms display clustered methylation, specifically in nucleosome linkers, at unprecedented densities. This clustering leads to direct disfavoritism of nucleosomes, and dense methylation is facilitated by a unique genomic sequence evolutionary regime that enriches CG dinucleotides and features exceptionally high CG frequencies. interestingly, species with linker methylation exhibit small, highly active nuclei that pushed the limits of chromatin compaction. These features constitute a previously unappreciated genome architecture, in which dense methylation exerts significant influence on nucleosome positioning, likely playing a key role in regulating nuclear processes under extreme spatial constraints.

title: The Immunogenicity and Safety of the Live-attenuated SA 14-14-2 Japanese Encephalitis Vaccine Given with a Two-dose Primary Schedule in Children
text: Ensuring both effective and tolerable vaccination is crucial to prevent Japanese encephalitis (JE) in areas where the disease is prevalent. Although the live attenuated SA 14-14-2 JE vaccine (LAJEV) has been widely used since its introduction, comprehensive data on its systemic effects in Korea was limited. Therefore, we conducted an open-label, prospective cohort study to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of this vaccine. Ninety participants were enrolled and received two doses of LAJEV, administered 12 months apart. Neutralizing antibody titers were measured before and after each vaccination, and active monitoring of adverse events was conducted. Following the first dose, 91.1% of subjects demonstrated seroprotection with a geometric mean titer (GMT) of 40.9. The seroprotection rate after the second dose was 97%, with a significant increase in GMT to 6.5-fold. Most adverse events following immunization were mild and transient, and no serious adverse events were reported within 42 days of each dose. Our findings suggest that administering two doses of LAJEV in a primary immunization schedule is both highly immunogenic and safe.

title: Centrosome-dependent asymmetric inheritance of the midbody ring in Drosophila germline stem cell division
text: Many stem cells, including Drosophila germline stem cells (GSCs), undergo asymmetric division, producing one stem cell and one differentiating daughter cell. While cytokinesis is often symmetric, with both daughter cells inheriting the midbody ring (MR) upon completion of abscission, we found that the MR is segregated asymmetrically during GSC divisions in a centrosome age-dependent manner. Specifically, male GSCs, which inherit the mother centrosome, fail to inherit the MR, while female GSCs, which we show inherit the daughter centrosome, inherit the MR. Our findings suggest that the MR does not inherently determine stem cell identity, but rather its stereotypical inheritance is controlled by stemness, and may provide a platform for the asymmetric segregation of certain factors.

title: Penile Curvature Incidence in Hypospadias: Can It Be Determined?
text: The study aimed to retrospectively determine the true incidence of congenital penile curvature in various forms of hypospadias, with the goal of guiding intraoperative assessment and correction of curvature. We analyzed 842 patients with hypospadias who underwent surgery between 2003 and 2010, categorized into two groups based on the extent of intraoperative curvature assessment. The first group underwent routine assessment for curvature, while the second group had curvature assessed primarily in severe hypospadias. The results were analyzed using Fisher's and chi-square tests. In total, 238 cases (28.3%) of associated curvature were confirmed. Curvature was found to be significantly more prevalent in the first group, specifically in regards to hypospadias in general (P < 0.01), as well as distal (P < 0.05) and midshaft forms (P < 0.01). Penile curvature is a common occurrence in hypospadias, including distal types. The study suggests that intraoperative testing for associated curvature should be considered a routine procedure in hypospadias repair.

title: Home birth and barriers to referring women with obstetric complications to hospitals: a mixed-methods study in Zahedan, southeastern Iran
text:
Background:
One factor contributing to high maternal mortality in developing countries is the delay in seeking emergency obstetric care (EmOC) facilities. This study aimed to identify the factors that hinder midwives and parturient women from using hospitals when complications occur during home births in Sistan and Baluchestan province, Iran, where 23% of deliveries take place outside of hospital settings.
Methods:
The study employed a mixed-methods approach, combining both quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis. In the quantitative phase, the research compared existing health sector data with World Health Organization (WHO) standards for EmOC availability and utilization. The qualitative phase involved interviews with 21 mothers and 23 traditional birth attendants, as well as in-depth interviews with 21 midwives. Data was analyzed based on qualitative data analysis principles.
Results:
The results indicate that three main factors lead to indecisiveness and delays in seeking EmOC among the midwives and mothers studied. Socio-cultural and familial factors compel some women to give birth at home and hesitate to seek professional emergency care for delivery complications. Midwives also report apprehension about being insulted by physicians, a need to protect their professional integrity, and an inability to convince their patients to seek hospital care. Additionally, the low quality and cost of EmOC, as well as the mothers' lack of health insurance, contribute to delays in referring patients to hospitals.
Conclusions:
Women who choose to give birth at home accept the risk of complications arising. Training midwives and persuading mothers and significant others of the importance of referring women to hospitals in the event of life-threatening complications is crucial in increasing the use of available hospitals. Hospitals must be safe, comfortable, and attractive environments for parturition, and appropriate consideration must be given to ethical and cultural concerns of the women. Addressing financial and insurance-related issues can also help midwives and mothers make rational decisions when complications arise.

title: ATPase-Dependent Control of the Mms21 SUMO Ligase during DNA Repair
text: The modification of proteins by the SUMO pathway is crucial for maintaining genome integrity, particularly during DNA replication. The Mms21 branch of the SUMO pathway counteracts recombination intermediates at damaged replication forks, allowing sister chromatid disjunction. The Mms21 SUMO ligase binds to the arm region of the Smc5 protein in the Smc5/6 complex, and together, they collaborate for recombinational DNA repair. However, the mechanisms governing the activity of the SUMO ligase remain unclear. This study reveals that the function of the SUMO ligase and chromosome disjunction of Mms21 depend on its binding to a fully intact and active Smc5/6 complex. In vivo, this complex serves as a large SUMO ligase. Despite the distance between the E3 and nucleotide-binding domains in Smc5/6, Mms21-dependent sumoylation requires the binding of ATP to Smc5, a step that is integral to the ligase mechanism and aids in Ubc9 function. The communication between the two domains is made possible by a conserved disruption in the coiled coil domain of Smc5, pointing to potential conformational changes that activate the SUMO ligase. Using scanning force microscopy, it is found that the Smc5-Mms21 heterodimer is physically remodeled in an ATP-dependent manner. Our results demonstrate that the ATP-binding activity of the Smc5/6 complex is synchronized with its SUMO ligase, through the coiled coil domain of Smc5 and the physical remodeling of the molecule, to promote sumoylation and chromosome disjunction during DNA repair.

title: Cadherins in brain morphogenesis and wiring.
text: Cadherins are calcium-dependent cell-cell adhesion molecules that are essential for animal development and function. In recent years, our understanding of the roles of these molecules in the nervous system has significantly expanded. Cadherins and related molecules play critical roles not only in the formation and maintenance of neural connections, but also in regulating cell proliferation and planar cell polarity in the brain. This review aims to summarize the current knowledge of cadherins' functions in neural development and function in the vertebrate brain.

title: Autocrine WNT signaling contributes to breast cancer cell proliferation via the canonical WNT pathway and EGFR transactivation
text: Mutations in genes that regulate the wingless and integrin site growth factor (WNT) signaling pathway, such as APC and Axin, have been associated with various types of human cancer. However, these genetic alterations are rarely observed in breast tumors. Despite this, there is evidence to suggest that WNT signaling may be dysregulated in breast cancer. Most breast tumors exhibit hypermethylation of the promoter region of secreted Frizzled-related protein 1 (sFRP1), leading to diminished expression of this protein, which in turn enhances WNT signaling and contributes to the proliferation of human breast tumor cells. Previous studies have shown that, in addition to the canonical WNT/β-catenin pathway, WNT signaling can activate the extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) pathway in mouse mammary epithelial cells via epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) transactivation. Using sFRP1 and short interfering RNA-mediated Dishevelled (DVL) knockdown, we blocked autocrine WNT signaling at the ligand-receptor level. The impact on proliferation was measured by cell counting, YOPRO, and MTT assays, and the expression of β-catenin, EGFR, ERK1/2, and poly [ADP-ribose]polymerase (PARP) was assessed by Western blotting after treatment of human breast cancer cell lines with conditioned media, purified proteins, small-molecule inhibitors, or blocking antibodies. Our findings indicate that interfering with autocrine WNT signaling in human breast cancer cell lines reduces proliferation and survival and induces apoptosis in MDA-MB-231, BT474, SkBr3, JIMT-1, and MCF-7 cells. Moreover, WNT1 rescues estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer cells from the anti-proliferative effects of 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-HT) and this activity can be blocked by an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor. Our results suggest that targeting WNT signaling at the ligand-receptor level in combination with other therapeutic approaches may improve the efficacy of breast cancer treatments.

title: Alternative Markers of Hyperglycemia and Risk of Diabetes
text: OBJECTIVE: Fructosamine, glycated albumin, and 1,5-anhydroglucitol (1,5-AG) are relevant for evaluating short-term glycemic control in diabetes patients; however, their relationships with diabetes risk are unexplored. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We employed Cox proportional hazards models to investigate the associations of fructosamine, glycated albumin, and 1,5-AG with incident diabetes in 1,299 ARIC Study participants (2005-2006) without a previous diabetes diagnosis. Diabetes incidence was self-reported during annual phone calls. RESULTS: There were 119 new diabetes cases during a median follow-up of 3.3 years. Compared to the lowest quartile, the fourth quartiles of fructosamine and glycated albumin showed significantly increased diabetes risk (hazard ratio [HR] 3.99 [95% CI 1.93-8.28] and 5.22 [2.49-10.94], respectively). In contrast, the fourth quartile of 1,5-AG was associated with a remarkable reduction in diabetes risk (0.27 [0.14-0.55]). These associations remained significant after adjusting for hemoglobin A(1c) (A1C) or fasting glucose. CONCLUSIONS: Fructosamine, glycated albumin, and 1,5-AG were found to be independently associated with the development of diabetes, beyond baseline A1C and fasting glucose levels. Our findings suggest that these alternative biomarkers might be useful in identifying individuals at high risk for diabetes.

title: ROR-γ drives androgen receptor expression and represents a therapeutic target in castration-resistant prostate cancer
text:
The androgen receptor (AR) is overexpressed and hyperactivated in human castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), a malignancy characterized by the unrelenting growth of cancer cells despite the abolition of androgen signaling. Despite the importance of AR overexpression in CRPC, the underlying mechanisms remain inadequately understood. Our research indicates that retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptor γ (ROR-γ), a transcription factor previously linked to various cancers, is overexpressed and amplified in metastatic CRPC tumors. ROR-γ binds to an AR-specific response element (RORE) and, in collaboration with nuclear receptor coactivator 1 and 3 (NCOA1 and NCOA3, also known as SRC-1 and SRC-3), stimulates the expression of the AR gene.
Our findings demonstrate that ROR-γ antagonists significantly reduce the expression of AR and its variant AR-V7 in prostate cancer (PCa) cell lines and tumors, as well as diminish the global AR binding, histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), and the expression of AR's target gene network. Moreover, treatment with ROR-γ antagonists exhibits profound suppression of tumor growth in CRPC xenograft models that express AR, while displaying minimal toxicity. Most importantly, these compounds sensitize CRPC tumors to the drug enzalutamide, without observable toxicity, in mice. Together, these results establish ROR-γ as a critical regulator of CRPC and highlight its potential as a target for advanced prostate cancer treatment.

title: affy--analysis of Affymetrix GeneChip data at the probe level.
text:
Motivation: The analysis of Affymetrix GeneChip data has been a recent priority for data analysts. In response, several alternative methods have been proposed and are now widely used.
Results: The affy package is an R package that offers a range of functions and classes for analyzing oligonucleotide arrays manufactured by Affymetrix. Currently in its second release, the package provides unparalleled flexibility in the analysis of probe intensity data, allowing users to access and manipulate data with ease. In this paper, we detail the main functions and classes in the package and demonstrate how they can be used to process data at the probe level. We also highlight the importance of probe-level analysis when utilizing the Affymetrix GeneChip platform.

title: Inducible caspase-9 suicide gene controls adverse effects from alloreplete T cells after haploidentical stem cell transplantation.
text: To assess the feasibility of a single T cell manipulation to eliminate alloreactivity while preserving antiviral and antitumor T cells, we infused 12 haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplant patients with increasingnumbers of alloreplete haploidentical T cells expressing the inducible caspase 9 suicide gene (iC9-T cells). We evaluated whether the iC9-T cells led to immune reconstruction and if any resulting graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) could be controlled by administering a chemical inducer of dimerization (CID; AP1903/Rimiducid). All patients receiving greater than 10(4) alloreplete iC9-T lymphocytes per kilogram experienced rapid reconstitution of immune responses towards five major pathogenic viruses and contemporaneous control of active infections. Four patients received a single AP1903 dose. CID infusion reduced circulating CD3(+)CD19(+) T cells by 85% to 95% within 30 minutes, with no recurrence of GVHD within 90 days. In one patient, symptoms and signs of GVHD-associated cytokine release syndrome (CRS-hyperpyrexia, high levels of proinflammatory cytokines, and rash) resolved within 2 hours of AP1903 infusion. One patient with varicella zoster virus meningitis and acute GVHD had iC9-T cells present in the cerebrospinal fluid, which were reduced by >90% after CID. Notably, virus-specific T cells recovered even after AP1903 administration and continued to protect against infection. Hence, alloreplete iC9-T cells can reconstitute immunity post-transplant and administration of CID can eliminate them from both peripheral blood and central nervous system (CNS), leading to rapid resolution of GVHD and CRS. This approach may therefore be useful for the rapid and effective treatment of toxicities associated with infusion of engineered T lymphocytes. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT01494103.

title: Clonal analysis of epiblast fate during germ layer formation in the mouse embryo.
text: An investigation into the destiny of cells in the epiblast at the prepigeonhole and early primitive streak phases has been conducted. To achieve this, single cells in situ were injected with horseradish peroxidase (HRP) into 6.7-day mouse embryos and their descendants were identified at midstreak to neural plate stages after a 24-hour culture. The study revealed that ectodermal cells were derived from epiblast progenitors located anterior to the primitive streak, while embryonic mesoderm originated from all areas of the epiblast except the distal tip and the adjacent region. Furthermore, the study showed that head process cells were derived from epiblast cells at or near the anterior end of the primitive streak, and endodermal cells were derived from a region that included but extended beyond the region producing the head process. Additionally, yolk sac and amnion mesoderm developed from posterior epiblast cells. The resulting fate map was found to be similar to those of the chick and urodele, indicating that topological fate relationships are conserved among these vertebrates. The study also showed that clonal descendants were not limited to a single germ layer or extraembryonic mesoderm, indicating that these lineages are not separated at the beginning of gastrulation. The population doubling time of labelled cells was found to be 7.5 hours, with 43% of them being in or completing a fourth cell cycle. The clonal analysis revealed that growth in the epiblast was noncoherent and anisotropic, with cells directed towards the primitive streak. Furthermore, the study showed that the midline did not act as a barrier to clonal spread in both the epiblast and the primitive streak. These findings, together with the fate map, suggest that while individual cells in the epiblast sheet behave independently, morphogenetic movement during germ layer formation is coordinated in the population as a whole.

title: Effects of a High-Intensity Functional Exercise Program on Dependence in Activities of Daily Living and Balance in Older Adults with Dementia
text:
Objective: To investigate the effects of a high-intensity functional exercise program on independence in activities of daily living (ADLs) and balance in older people with dementia, and whether exercise effects differed between dementia types.
Design: Cluster-randomized controlled trial (UMDEX study) conducted in residential care facilities in Umeå, Sweden.
Participants: A total of 186 individuals aged 65 and older with a dementia diagnosis, Mini-Mental State Examination score of 10 or greater, and dependence in ADLs were randomly allocated to either a high-intensity functional exercise program (n=93) or a seated control activity (n=93).
Measurements: Blinded assessors measured ADL independence using the Functional Independence Measure (FIM) and Barthel Index (BI) and balance using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS) at baseline and 4 (directly after intervention completion) and 7 months.
Results: Linear mixed models revealed no significant between-group effect on ADL independence at 4 (FIM=1.3, 95% CI=-1.6-4.3; BI=0.6, 95% CI=-0.2-1.4) or 7 (FIM=0.8, 95% CI=-2.2-3.8; BI=0.6, 95% CI=-0.3-1.4) months. However, a significant between-group effect on balance was observed in favor of the exercise group at 4 months (BBS=4.2, 95% CI=1.8-6.6). Interaction analyses revealed that exercise effects differed significantly between dementia types, with positive between-group exercise effects found in participants with non-Alzheimer's dementia according to the FIM at 7 months, BI, and BBS at 4 and 7 months.
Conclusion: A 4-month high-intensity functional exercise program appears to slow decline in ADL independence and improve balance, albeit only in participants with non-Alzheimer's dementia living in residential care facilities.

title: Effect of Health Literacy on Quality of Life amongst Patients with Ischaemic Heart Disease in Australian General Practice
text:
Patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) need to comprehend health information properly to manage their risk factors and enhance their quality of life. Inadequate health literacy has the potential to negatively impact patient outcomes, including HRQoL (health-related quality of life). This study aims to assess the relationship between health literacy and HRQoL in patients with ischemic heart disease (IHD). The research questions are: what is the relationship between health literacy and HRQoL in patients with IHD, and can sociodemographic and clinical factors influence this relationship?
A cross-sectional study involving 587 patients with IHD from two Australian states (Queensland and South Australia) was conducted between 2007 and 2009. The study included patients aged 72.0±8.4 years, with 76.8% being male, 84.2% retired or pensioner, and 51.4% having up to secondary educational level. Health literacy was measured using a validated questionnaire, and patients were classified as having inadequate, marginal, or adequate health literacy based on their scores. Physical and mental components of HRQoL were assessed using the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form (SF12) questionnaire. Adjustments were made for confounding variables (sociodemographic variables, clinical history of IHD, number of CVD comorbidities, and CVD risk factors) using multiple linear regression.
The findings of the study revealed that 14.3% (95%CI 11.8-17.3) of patients had inadequate health literacy, while the mean scores for the physical, mental, and overall HRQoL components were 39.6±6.7, 42.1±6.7, and 44.8±6.7 points, respectively. Compared to patients with adequate health literacy, those with inadequate health literacy had significantly lower scores on the physical and overall HRQoL components. The association persisted even after adjusting for confounding variables. Health literacy was not associated with the mental component of HRQoL. Factors that adversely affected both health literacy and HRQoL included advanced age, lower educational level, disadvantaged socioeconomic position, and a larger number of CVD comorbidities.
In conclusion, this study suggests that inadequate health literacy is a contributing factor to poor physical functioning in patients with IHD. Enhancing health literacy may improve HRQoL and reduce the impact of IHD on patients with this chronic CVD.

title: in
text: Transglutaminase 2 (TGase 2) is a calcium-dependent enzyme that catalyzes both intracellular and extracellular cross-linking reactions through transamidation of specific glutamine residues. TGase 2 plays a crucial role in membrane-mediated events necessary for glucose-stimulated insulin release from pancreatic beta cells. Our studies demonstrate that disrupting TGase 2 impairs glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. TGase 2-deficient mice exhibit glucose intolerance after intraperitoneal glucose loading and a tendency to develop hypoglycemia after exogenous insulin administration, likely due to enhanced insulin receptor substrate 2 (IRS-2) phosphorylation. The increased peripheral sensitivity to insulin in these mice partially compensates for the defective secretion. The TGase 2-deficient mouse phenotype resembles that of maturity-onset diabetes of young (MODY) patients. In our search for the human TGase 2 gene in Italian subjects with MODY-like features, we identified a missense mutation (N333S) in the active site of the enzyme, further highlighting TGase 2 as a potential candidate gene for type 2 diabetes.

title: Chromatin structure and gene expression programs of human embryonic and induced pluripotent stem cells.
