Loss of FIB function led to a range of pleiotropic abnormal phenotypes, such as small leaves with large lamina joint angles, abnormal vascular development, small panicles, unusual organ identity, and defects in root development, along with reduced internal IAA levels. Additionally, we found that auxin sensitivity and polar transport activity were altered in the fib mutant. From these findings, we propose that FIB plays a critical role in IAA biosynthesis in rice, and that auxin synthesis, transport, and sensitivity are closely interconnected.

title: Successful mouse cloning of an outbred strain by trichostatin A treatment after somatic nuclear transfer.
text: Despite its widespread use in various species for basic research and applications, the somatic cloning technique has been hindered by extremely low success rates for over a decade. In mice, the most clonable strains have been limited to F1 hybrids such as B6D2F1. We recently developed a novel cloning technique using trichostatin A (TSA), which significantly improved the success rates of cloning mouse cumulus cells from B6D2F1. To validate the effectiveness of this TSA cloning technique, we attempted to clone the ICR mouse, an outbred strain that has never been directly cloned before. Surprisingly, we achieved both male and female cloned mice from adult ICR mouse cumulus and fibroblast cells using TSA, with a success rate of 4-5%. This is comparable to the 5-7% success rate achieved with B6D2F1 cells. Our findings demonstrate that TSA treatment not only enhances the cloning efficiency of hybrid strains but also enables cloning from traditionally difficult-to-clone outbred strains, marking a significant breakthrough in the field of mouse cloning.

title: A Genome-wide CRISPR Death Screen Identifies Genes Essential for Oxidative Phosphorylation.
text:
Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) is the primary mechanism by which ATP is produced in humans. Shortcomings in OXPHOS can arise from mutations in either the mitochondrial or nuclear genome, and together they constitute the largest cluster of inherited disorders of metabolism. Currently, we lack a complete inventory of genes and pathways that are essential for OXPHOS.
To address this gap, we have developed a genome-wide CRISPR "death screen" that actively identifies cells that are unable to produce ATP through OXPHOS. This approach is inspired by the well-established observation that cells deficient in OXPHOS are unable to survive in glucose but will die in galactose. Through this screen, we have identified 191 high-confidence hits that are essential for OXPHOS, including 72 already-known OXPHOS diseases.
Our study reveals a functional module comprising NGRN, WBSCR16, RPUSD3, RPUSD4, TRUB2, and FASTKD2, which regulates the mitochondrial 16S rRNA and intra-mitochondrial translation. Our findings provide a comprehensive catalog of genes necessary for OXPHOS and illustrate the broad applicability of death screening for functional genomic analysis.

title: RecQ helicases: caretakers of the genome
text: RecQ helicases, which are highly conserved across the tree of life, from bacteria to humans, play a crucial role in maintaining genomic stability. Mutations in three of the five known family members in humans have been linked to debilitating disorders that increase the likelihood of developing cancer. One of these disorders, Bloom's syndrome, is uniquely associated with a predisposition to cancers of all types. So how do RecQ helicases protect against cancer? It appears that they act as a buffer at the interface between DNA replication and DNA repair, ensuring that genetic material is accurately copied and repaired, thus preventing the accumulation of mutations that can lead to cancer.

title: Mortality from causes amenable and non-amenable to medical care: the experience of eastern Europe.
text:
Objective:
To investigate and compare the national trends in mortality rates from conditions that can be improved through timely and appropriate medical care, and those that cannot be improved in eastern European nations versus western nations.
Design:
An analysis of the trends in direct age-standardized mortality rates from the 1950s to 1987 in four eastern European nations (Hungary, Czechoslovakia, Poland, and the German Democratic Republic) and two western European nations (the Federal Republic of Germany and England and Wales) and two North American nations (the United States and Canada).
Settings:
The study examined the total populations of the relevant countries during the period of investigation.
Population:
The study population included the entire population of the selected countries.
Outcome Measures:
The study focused on the proportional changes in age-standardized mortality rates over time. Mortality rates from amenable and non-amenable causes were also evaluated for the age group of 0-64 years.
Results:
The study found a divergent trend in the mortality rates between eastern European and western nations, with the former seeing a steady increase in mortality rates after 1970, while the latter witnessed a steady decline. Specifically, mortality rates from causes considered amenable to medical care decreased less quickly in eastern Europe than in the West, particularly after 1970. Conversely, mortality rates from non-amenable causes increased in eastern European countries from the late 1960s, compared to substantial declines in such mortality in the West.
Conclusions:
The results suggest that non-amenable causes of death are the primary, but not exclusive, reason for the lack of improvement in trends in all-cause mortality in eastern Europe after 1970. The agenda for action in eastern Europe should prioritize healthier lifestyles and environmental improvements, while also addressing quality and efficiency issues in direct health services.

title: Dynamic regulation of heterochromatin function via phosphorylation of HP1-family proteins.
text: Heterochromatin is defined by the methylation of histone H3 at lysine 9, which is specifically recognized by a group of conserved proteins called HP1-family proteins. Heterochromatin plays a crucial role in various chromosomal functions, including the silencing of transcription and the cohesion of sister chromatids. These functions are executed by distinct protein effectors that interact with HP1-family proteins, though the regulation of this interaction with the effectors remains poorly understood. Recently, our research revealed that the phosphorylation of the fission yeast HP1 homolog, Swi6, controls the association of transcriptional regulators in a differential manner and influences the transcriptional activity of heterochromatin without affecting sister chromatid cohesion. This finding, combined with another study using different systems, suggests that the phosphorylation of HP1/Swi6 serves as a dynamic pathway for the adjustable regulation of heterochromatin in response to both intra- and intercellular signals.

title: Modeling neurogenesis impairment in Down syndrome with induced pluripotent stem cells from Trisomy 21 amniotic fluid cells.
text: Down syndrome (DS), or Trisomy 21 (T21) syndrome, is one of the most common genetic abnormalities, caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21. In scientific studies of neuron development, human cell-based models are considered the most desirable and accurate for basic research. Generating diseased induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells is a crucial step in understanding the complex stages of neuronal diseases. We generated human DS iPS cell lines from second-trimester amniotic fluid (AF) cells using lentiviral delivery of Yamanaka factors and differentiated them into neuronal progenitor cells (NPCs) for further analysis. The T21 AF-iPS cells had a unique pattern of chromosomal karyotypes with three copies of chromosome 21. We found that the level of amyloid precursor protein was significantly increased in NPCs derived from T21 AF-iPS cells compared to NPCs from normal AF-iPS cells. Moreover, the expression levels of microRNAs miR-155 and miR-802 were highly elevated in the presence of low expression of MeCP2 in T21 AF-iPS-NPCs. Our results showed that T21 iPS-NPCs generated fewer neurons compared to controls and exhibited developmental defects during neurogenesis. These findings suggest that T21 AF-iPS cells can be used to elucidate the impairment of neurogenesis in Down syndrome and the onset of Alzheimer's disease.

title: Control over DNA replication in time and space.
text: DNA replication is precisely regulated throughout the cell cycle to maintain genome integrity. In eukaryotic cells, replication begins at multiple sites along the genome, known as origins of replication, and progresses in both directions. Specialized complexes called origin bound complexes control the initiation of replication at these sites. During late mitosis and G1 phase, potential replication sites are identified and become "licensed" through the assembly of pre-replicative complexes (pre-RCs) containing enzymes like MCM2-7 helicases. At the G1/S phase transition, a subset of these pre-RCs are activated, allowing for the establishment of replication forks. The location of origin selection is influenced by the structure of chromatin and the organization of the nucleus, and the regulation of these events involves the periodic fluctuations of cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) activity throughout the cell cycle.

title: MYC/MIZ1-dependent gene repression inversely coordinates the circadian clock with cell cycle and proliferation
text: The circadian clock and cell cycle are two critical cellular systems that regulate global physiology according to a temporal schedule. It is possible that these seemingly disparate programs are harmoniously coordinated. We discovered that overexpressing MYC in U2OS cells attenuates the circadian clock and enhances cell proliferation, while reducing MYC levels strengthens the clock and slows proliferation. The clock's inhibition is contingent upon the formation of repressive MYC-MIZ1 complexes, which, in turn, downregulate the core clock genes BMAL1 (ARNTL), CLOCK, and NPAS2. Furthermore, we found that BMAL1 expression levels are inverse to MYC levels in 102 human lymphomas. Our data suggest that MYC serves as a master regulator that opposingly modulates the impact of the cell cycle and circadian clock on gene expression.

title: Relevance of asystole during head-up tilt testing.
text: The prognostic value of prolonged asystole during head-up tilt testing is uncertain. In a prospective study of 209 patients with a history of syncope and positive head-up tilt tests, 19 patients had asystole lasting > 5 seconds (mean duration 15 ± 10 seconds), which was observed in 11% of the overall patients (group 1a). Compared to patients without asystole (group 1b), group 1a patients were younger (32 ± 12 years vs 47 ± 21 years, p < 0.005), but the clinical manifestations were not significantly more severe (7 ± 5 episodes of syncope vs 8 ± 6 episodes, p = NS; and 2 vs 13 patients with injury during syncope, p = NS). During follow-up (mean ± 1 year), 11% of the asystole group and 8% of the non-asystole group experienced recurrence (p = NS) despite pharmacological therapy (beta blockers, ephedrine, theophylline, or disopyramide). None of the patients in the asystole group underwent pacemaker implantation. Furthermore, in 75 normal volunteers (group 2) without a history of syncope, who underwent head-up tilt tests to evaluate the test's specificity, 3 individuals exhibited transient asystole (mean duration 10 seconds). During > 1-year follow-up, all 3 individuals remained symptom-free despite no treatment. Therefore, an asystolic response during head-up tilt testing does not indicate either a more severe outcome or a poor response to pharmacological therapy. Moreover, an asystolic response may occur in asymptomatic "normal" volunteers, which reduces the specificity of the head-up tilt test.

title: Increasing informed uptake and non-uptake of screening: evidence from a systematic review.
text:
Objective: To investigate the impact of different interventions on the informed uptake of screening tests.
Search Strategy: We conducted electronic database searches, bibliographic reviews, and consultations with experts to identify published and unpublished studies up to August 2000.
Inclusion Criteria: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-RCTs, and controlled trials that evaluated interventions aimed at enhancing informed uptake of screening tests. All participants were eligible based on the entry criteria of individual programs. Studies had to report actual uptake and meet at least three of the four criteria used to define informed uptake.
Data Extraction and Synthesis: Two reviewers independently identified relevant studies, extracted data, and assessed their validity. The outcome measures included screening uptake, knowledge, informed decision-making, and attitudes towards screening. We used a random-effects model to calculate individual relative risks and 95% confidence intervals.
Main Results: Six controlled trials (five RCTs and one quasi-RCT) that focused on antenatal and prostate-specific antigen screening were included. All of these studies reported on the risks and benefits of screening and assessed knowledge. Two of these studies also evaluated decision-making. Two of these studies reported on the risks and benefits to all randomized groups and evaluated different ways of presenting information, but neither found that interventions such as videos, information leaflets with decision trees, or touch-screen computers provided any additional benefits beyond well-designed leaflets.
Conclusions: While there is some evidence to suggest that changing the format of informed choice interventions in screening does not have a significant impact on knowledge, satisfaction, or decisions regarding screening, it is not clear whether informed choice in screening directly affects uptake. We need more well-designed RCTs and further research on the development of a valid instrument for measuring all aspects of informed choice in screening.

title: Mitochondrial RNA Granules Are Centers for Posttranscriptional RNA Processing and Ribosome Biogenesis.
text: Mitochondrial RNA granules are underappreciated for their role in mediating mRNA metabolism. By characterizing their protein complement, we discovered a diverse array of enzymes dedicated to RNA processing. We investigated four uncharacterized RNA-binding proteins and found that two helicases, DHX30 and DDX28, as well as two members of the Fas-activated serine-threonine kinase (FASTKD) family, FASTKD2 and FASTKD5, play critical roles in mitochondrial ribosome biogenesis. Using RNA-seq analysis, we found that DDX28 and FASTKD2 bind the 16S rRNA, while FASTKD5 is essential for maturing precursor mRNAs that cannot be processed by the standard mRNA maturation pathway. Silencing FASTKD5 resulted in a near-complete loss of mature COX I mRNA, significantly impairing the synthesis of complex IV. These findings demonstrate that mitochondrial RNA granules serve as hubs for post-transcriptional RNA processing and the genesis of mitochondrial ribosomes.

title: Controlling nuclear receptors: the circular logic of cofactor cycles
text: Nuclear receptors play a vital role in regulating various biological processes during development and maintenance by exhibiting a dual nature as both repressors and activators of gene transcription. The precise modulation of their transcriptional activities is essential to control highly specific and diversified gene expression programs. Recent research has shed light on the molecular mechanisms underlying the transition between repression and activation functions, the multiple cofactor complexes necessary for mediating transcriptional regulation, and the intricate process of integrating various signaling pathways at the nuclear level to achieve distinct gene expression profiles.

title: Reprogramming fibroblasts into bipotential hepatic stem cells by defined factors.
text: Recent studies have shown that fibroblasts can be directly reprogrammed into a variety of somatic cell types, but until now, stem or progenitor cells have only been reprogrammed for the blood and neuronal lineages. We previously reported generating induced hepatocyte-like (iHep) cells by introducing Gata4, Hnf1α, and Foxa3 in p19 ARF null mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs). Here, we demonstrate that Hnf1β and Foxa3, which are transcription factors involved in liver organogenesis, are sufficient to reprogram MEFs into induced hepatic stem cells (iHepSCs). iHepSCs can be expanded in vitro and have the potential to differentiate into both hepatocytic and cholangiocytic lineages. In mice with Fah deficiency, repopulating iHepSCs differentiate into hepatocyte-like cells, and they can also engraft into bile ducts of mice with DDC-induced bile ductular injury. This approach of lineage conversion into bipotential, expandable iHepSCs provides a means to efficiently derive both hepatocytes and cholangiocytes for use in disease modeling and tissue engineering.

title: Spatial genome organization: contrasting views from chromosome conformation capture and fluorescence in situ hybridization.
text: Although crucial for understanding gene regulation, most studies on genome organization rely solely on either fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) or chromosome conformation capture (3C) techniques. FISH directly visualizes the spatial relationship of sequences, but this method is typically applied to a limited number of locations at a time. In contrast, 3C methods measure the frequency at which sequences are ligated together by formaldehyde cross-linking on a genome-wide scale, with higher frequencies suggesting shorter distances. Although these methods should provide identical views of genome organization, this has not been extensively investigated. We investigated the murine HoxD locus using both 3C carbon copy (5C) and FISH in different developmental and activity states and in the presence or absence of epigenetic regulators. Our findings revealed instances where the two data sets converged, but we also identified situations where the chromatin topographies inferred from 5C or FISH data were incompatible. We propose that products captured by 3C do not always reflect spatial proximity, with ligation occurring between sequences located hundreds of nanometers apart, influenced by the nuclear environment and chromatin composition. Our results highlight the need for caution when interpreting high-resolution data obtained with either 3C methods or FISH alone. We conclude that independent validation of genome organization views is essential.

title: Development and evaluation of a self-administered computerized 24-h dietary recall method for adolescents in Europe
text:
The objective of this study was to develop a computerized 24-hour dietary recall method for adolescents in Europe and to evaluate its feasibility through self-report or interview administration. The study involved 236 adolescents (aged 14.6 years on average) from eight European cities, who completed the Young Adolescents Nutrition Assessment on Computer (YANA-C) twice - once through self-report and once through interview administration.
Results showed a small, yet statistically significant underestimation in energy and fat intake among self-reported dietary records compared to interview administration. No significant differences were found for carbohydrates, proteins, fibre, calcium, iron, and ascorbic acid intake. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients were high (ranging between 0.86 and 0.91) for all nutrients and energy. Agreement in categorizing respondents as consumers or non-consumers for 29 food groups was also high (kappa statistics ≥0.73). The average percentage of omissions was 3.7%, while the average percentage of intrusions was 2.0%. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients between both modes were also high for each food group and for the total sample (>0.76) as well as for consumers only (>0.72). When analyzing the consumer-only subset, on average, 54% of the consumed amounts were found to be exactly the same, but a significant difference was found only for one food group - 'rice and pasta'.
The study suggests that the adapted, translated, and standardized YANA-C method allows for the assessment of adolescent dietary intake in a broad international context. Overall, good agreement was found between the administration modes, and interview administration offered significant potential for large-scale surveys where data collection resources are limited.

title: JTK_CYCLE: an efficient nonparametric algorithm for detecting rhythmic components in genome-scale data sets.
text: Circadian rhythms are regular fluctuations in physiology, behavior, and metabolism that last around 24 hours. In various model organisms and humans, genes related to the circadian clock have been found to be transcription factors. To investigate the global regulation of gene expression and identify cycling variables, researchers have utilized microarrays and algorithmic approaches. This article introduces a novel algorithm, JTK_CYCLE, designed to efficiently identify and characterize cycling variables in large data sets. Compared to COSOPT and the Fisher's G test, commonly used methods for detecting cycling transcripts, JTK_CYCLE distinguishes between rhythmic and non-rhythmic transcripts more accurately and efficiently. JTK_CYCLE's resistance to outliers leads to greater sensitivity and specificity, and its ability to measure the period, phase, and amplitude of cycling transcripts enables downstream analyses. Additionally, JTK_CYCLE is several orders of magnitude faster than COSOPT, making it ideal for large-scale data sets. The algorithm was applied to legacy data sets including NIH3T3 cells, whose relatively low amplitude oscillations were identified more precisely using JTK_CYCLE. The novel cluster of RNA-interacting genes identified by JTK_CYCLE exhibits clear circadian regulation, suggesting that the algorithm is an optimal tool for identifying and characterizing oscillations in genome-scale data sets.

title: Polo-like kinase 1 regulates Nlp, a centrosome protein involved in microtubule nucleation.
text: In animal cells, most microtubules are formed at centrosomes. As mitosis begins, centrosomes undergo a structural reorganization called maturation, which enhances microtubule nucleation. This process is regulated by several kinases, including Polo-like kinase 1 (Plk1). We have identified a centrosomal protein, Nlp (ninein-like protein), that plays a crucial role in microtubule organization. Nlp interacts with two components of the gamma-tubulin ring complex and stimulates microtubule nucleation. Plk1 phosphorylates Nlp and disrupts its association with the centrosome and its interaction with gamma-tubulin. Overexpression of an Nlp mutant lacking Plk1 phosphorylation sites leads to severe disruption of mitotic spindle formation. We propose that Nlp plays an essential role in microtubule organization during interphase, and that the activation of Plk1 at the onset of mitosis triggers the displacement of Nlp from the centrosome, allowing the establishment of a mitotic scaffold with enhanced microtubule nucleation activity.

title: Consumption of isoflavone-rich soy protein does not alter homocysteine or markers of inflammation in postmenopausal women
text:
Background/Objective: To investigate the impact of soy protein, rich in isoflavones, on homocysteine (Hcy), C-reactive protein (CRP), soluble E-selectin (sE-selectin), soluble vascular adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1), and soluble intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (sICAM-1) levels.
Subject/Methods: In a randomized, crossover design, 34 postmenopausal women consumed either soy protein isolate (26±5 grams of protein containing 44±8 mg of isoflavones per day) or milk protein isolate (26±5 grams of protein per day) for 6 weeks each. Fasting blood samples were collected at the end of each diet period, and end points were analyzed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.
Results: Concentrations of Hcy, CRP, sE-selectin, sVCAM-1, and sICAM-1 were not significantly different between soy and milk diet treatments. These findings did not vary based on equol production status or baseline lipid levels. Adjusting for folate and methionine intake also did not affect the Hcy results.
Conclusions: These data suggest that reducing vascular inflammation and homocysteine concentrations are unlikely mechanisms by which soy consumption reduces coronary heart disease risk.

title: Homogeneously dispersed multimetal oxygen-evolving catalysts
text: Newly developed transition metal catalysts based on Earth-abundant elements have shown great promise for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). However, these catalysts require significantly higher potentials than what is predicted by thermodynamics. By incorporating non-3d high-valency metals like tungsten, we have discovered that it can modify 3d metal oxides, resulting in near-optimal adsorption energies for OER intermediates. We have developed a room-temperature synthesis method to produce atomically uniform metal distribution gels, specifically FeCoW oxyhydroxides, which exhibit the lowest observed overpotential of 191 millivolts at 10 milliamperes per square centimeter in alkaline electrolyte. These catalysts remain stable for over 500 hours of operation without degradation. X-ray absorption and computational studies reveal that the synergistic interaction between tungsten, iron, and cobalt creates a favorable local coordination environment and electronic structure, thereby enhancing the energetics of the OER.

title: Global strategy for the diagnosis, management, and prevention of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: GOLD executive summary.
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) poses a significant global health burden, and since 2001, the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) has issued a comprehensive strategy document for its diagnosis and management. This executive summary highlights the key updates in the second 5-year revision of the GOLD document, which incorporates the vast knowledge accumulated on COPD over the years. GOLD emphasizes the importance of spirometry in clinical diagnosis to avoid misdiagnosis and ensure accurate assessment of airflow limitation severity. The assessment of patients with COPD should include evaluations of symptoms, airflow limitation severity, history of exacerbations, and comorbidities. This categorization helps to determine the level of symptoms and risk of future exacerbations. The management of COPD is based on evidence-based nonpharmacological and pharmacological approaches, with a priority on identifying and treating comorbidities. A separate section in the document focuses on managing comorbidities and COPD in the presence of comorbidities. The revised document also includes a new section on exacerbations of COPD. The GOLD initiative will continue to raise awareness about COPD and inspire future national and local guidelines on its management.

title: Circulating tumor cells: a useful predictor of treatment efficacy in metastatic breast cancer.
text:
The text can be rewritten as follows:
The presence of five or more circulating tumor cells (CTCs) per 7.5 mL of blood in patients with metastatic breast cancer (MBC) is associated with poorer progression-free survival (PFS). In a prospective study, we found a strong correlation between CTC levels and radiographic disease progression, both at the time of imaging and in advance of imaging. Serial CTC levels were obtained in patients starting a new treatment regimen for progressive, radiographically measurable MBC. Peripheral blood was collected for CTC enumeration at baseline and at 3- to 4-week intervals. Clinical outcomes were based on radiographic studies performed in 9- to 12-week intervals. Our results showed that sixty-eight patients were evaluable for the CTC-imaging correlations, and seventy-four patients were evaluable for the PFS analysis. The median follow-up was 13.3 months. A statistically significant correlation was demonstrated between CTC levels and radiographic disease progression in patients receiving chemotherapy or endocrine therapy. This correlation applied to CTC results obtained at the time of imaging (odds ratio [OR], 6.3), 3 to 5 weeks before imaging (OR, 3.1), and 7 to 9 weeks before imaging (OR, 4.9). Stratified analyses showed that shorter PFS was observed for patients with five or more CTCs at 3 to 5 weeks and at 7 to 9 weeks after the start of treatment. Our findings provide the first evidence of a strong correlation between CTC results and radiographic disease progression in patients receiving chemotherapy or endocrine therapy for MBC. These results support the role of CTC enumeration as an adjunct to standard methods of monitoring disease status in MBC.

title: Recovery of supraspinal control of stepping via indirect propriospinal relay connections after spinal cord injury
text: Spinal cord injuries (SCIs) in humans and animals often exhibit functional recovery within the first few months post-injury, despite varying degrees of incomplete lesions. While the mechanisms underlying this recovery are unclear, it is thought to involve spared axons from the brain that bypass the injured area and descend to spare other areas. To investigate the neural basis of spontaneous recovery, we employed a combination of kinematic, physiological, and anatomical analysis to evaluate mice with different combinations of lateral hemisections and excitotoxic ablation of intrinsic spinal cord neurons. Our findings indicate that propriospinal relay connections, which bypass injured areas, can mediate functional recovery and supraspinal control of stepping, even when long descending supraspinal pathways have been essentially irreversibly interrupted. Our results suggest that pronounced functional recovery can occur after severe SCI without the need for direct projections from the brain to be maintained or regenerated, and that this recovery is mediated by the reorganization of descending and propriospinal connections. Targeting interventions to enhance the remodeling of these relay connections may provide new therapeutic strategies to bypass lesions and restore function after SCI, as well as other conditions such as stroke and multiple sclerosis.

title: "Grazing": a high-risk behavior.
text: Patients who have undergone gastric bypass surgery may be at risk of resuming unhealthy eating patterns after the procedure, according to recent research. Binge eating and "grazing" (a pattern of continuous, small amounts of food consumption) are common among obese individuals both before and after surgery, and are linked to poorer outcomes. To investigate postoperative eating patterns in this group, researchers surveyed patients before and after surgery, identifying those with high-risk eating patterns and offering them additional follow-up questionnaires. The results showed that many patients with high-risk eating patterns reported difficulty controlling their food intake and experienced weight gain following surgery. Additionally, some patients transitioned from binge eating to "grazing" patterns after surgery, which is a concern as it can lead to weight gain and poorer outcomes. The study highlights the need for interventions to help at-risk patients maintain healthy eating habits after gastric bypass surgery.

title: Molecular strategies in biological evolution of antimicrobial peptides.
text:
Gene-encoded antimicrobial peptides found in the skin of certain frogs can protect against harmful microorganisms. Unlike conventional secreted peptides, these proteins are processed from a unique family of precursor polypeptides with a distinct pattern of conserved and variable regions. Each frog species has its own set of 10-20 antimicrobial peptides, resulting in approximately 100,000 different peptide antibiotics.
The frogs' evolutionary strategy for generating this diverse array of peptides involves repeated gene duplication, hypermutation of the antimicrobial peptide domain, and positive (diversifying) selection. This process leads to the hyperdivergence of skin antimicrobial peptides, which serves as a multi-drug defense system providing maximum protection against rapidly changing microbial biota. Furthermore, the impressive variations in the expression of frog skin antimicrobial peptides can be leveraged to discover new molecules and structural motifs targeting specific microorganisms with limited therapeutic options.

title: Microbiome-driven allergic lung inflammation is ameliorated by short-chain fatty acids
text: The mammalian gastrointestinal tract houses a microbial community with metabolic activity crucial for host health, including metabolites that can modulate immune cell function. Mice administered vancomycin exhibit an altered microbiome and metabolite profile, exacerbating Th2 cell responses and susceptibility to allergic lung inflammation. In contrast, dietary supplementation with short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) alleviates enhanced asthma susceptibility by modulating T cell and dendritic cell (DC) activity. Treated dysbiotic mice exhibit fewer IL-4-producing CD4+ T cells and decreased levels of circulating immunoglobulin E (IgE). Additionally, DCs exposed to SCFAs demonstrate less robust T cell activation, reduced mobility in response to CCL19 in vitro, and impaired ability to transport inhaled allergens to lung draining nodes. Our findings indicate that gut dysbiosis exacerbates allergic lung inflammation through both T cell- and DC-dependent mechanisms, which are inhibited by SCFAs.

title: Promiscuous gene expression in medullary thymic epithelial cells mirrors the peripheral self
text: Expression of peripheral antigens in the thymus has been linked to T cell tolerance and autoimmunity. In this study, we identified medullary thymic epithelial cells as a distinct cell type that exhibits a wide range of tissue-specific antigens. We found that this promiscuous antigen expression is a inherent property of medullary epithelial cells and persists throughout the entire T cell output stage of the thymus. This phenomenon may facilitate the induction of tolerance to self-antigens that are temporally or spatially isolated from the immune system. However, the array of promiscuously expressed self-antigens appears to be random rather than selective and is not limited to secluded self-antigens.

title: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 is a transcriptional factor regulating the gene expression of SALL4.
text: Both signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) and SALL4 are essential for maintaining the pluripotent and self-renewal state of embryonic stem cells. We hypothesized that STAT3, a latent transcription factor, regulates the expression of SALL4. To test this idea, we analyzed the SALL4 gene promoter and identified four potential STAT3-binding sites. Using a SALL4-luciferase reporter gene assay, we found that modulating STAT3 activity significantly increased luciferase activity. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) analysis localized the most prominent STAT3-binding site to -366 to -163, containing only one putative binding site at -199. Site-directed mutagenesis of all four STAT3-binding sites in the SALL4 promoter significantly reduced its responsiveness to STAT3, with the most prominent effect observed at the -199 site. To investigate the functional relationship between STAT3 and SALL4, we used MDA-MB-231 cells, which constitutively express SALL4 and have active STAT3. Downregulating STAT3 activity using a dominant-negative construct resulted in a significant decrease in SALL4 expression. Our data suggest that STAT3 and SALL4 cooperate in both physiological and pathological conditions.

title: GATA3 transcription factor abrogates Smad4 transcription factor-mediated fascin overexpression, invadopodium formation, and breast cancer cell invasion.
text: Transforming growth factor beta (TGFβ) is a powerful and context-dependent regulator of tumor progression. TGFβ promotes the metastasis of basal-like (but not luminal-like) breast cancer to the lungs. Here, we demonstrate that fascin, an actin bundling protein that promotes metastasis, is a direct target of the canonical TGFβ-Smad4 signaling pathway in basal-like breast cancer cells. TGFβ and Smad4 induce fascin overexpression by directly binding to a Smad binding element on the fascin promoter. We identify GATA3, a transcription factor crucial for mammary gland morphogenesis and luminal differentiation, as a negative regulator of TGFβ- and Smad4-induced fascin overexpression. When ectopically expressed in basal-like breast cancer cells, GATA-3 abrogates TGFβ- and Smad4-mediated overexpression of fascin and other TGFβ response genes, invadopodium formation, cell migration, and invasion, suggesting suppression of the canonical TGFβ-Smad signaling axis. Mechanistically, GATA3 abolishes interactions between Smad4 and its DNA binding elements, potentially through physical interactions between the N-terminal of GATA3 and Smad3/4 proteins. Our findings provide insight into how TGFβ-mediated cell motility and invasiveness are differentially regulated in breast cancer.

title: The American Rheumatism Association 1987 revised criteria for the classification of rheumatoid arthritis.
text:
The new criteria for classifying rheumatoid arthritis (RA) were developed using a computerized analysis of 262 contemporary and consecutively studied patients with RA and 262 control subjects with other rheumatic diseases. The revised criteria are as follows:
1. Morning stiffness in and around joints lasting at least 1 hour before improvement.
2. Soft tissue swelling (arthritis) in 3 or more joint areas observed by a physician.
3. Swelling of the proximal interphalangeal, metacarpophalangeal, or wrist joints.
4. Symmetric swelling (arthritis).
5. Presence of rheumatoid nodules.
6. The presence of rheumatoid factor.
7. Radiographic erosions and/or periarticular osteopenia in the hand and/or wrist joints. These criteria must have been present for at least 6 weeks. RA is defined by the presence of 4 or more criteria, and no additional qualifications (classic, definite, or probable) or exclusions are required.
In addition, a "classification tree" schema is presented, which performs equally well as the traditional (4 of 7) format. The new criteria showed 91-94% sensitivity and 89% specificity for RA when compared to non-RA rheumatic disease control subjects.

title: A new look at the origin, function, and "stem-cell" status of muscle satellite cells.
text: Muscle satellite cells were once considered a distinct myogenic lineage solely responsible for postnatal growth, repair, and maintenance of skeletal muscle. However, recent mouse studies have shown that highly purified hematopoietic stem cells from bone marrow can participate in muscle regeneration. This finding is significant, as a population of putative stem cells isolated directly from skeletal muscle can efficiently reconstitute the hematopoietic compartment and participate in muscle regeneration upon intravenous injection in mice. The plasticity of muscle stem cells has raised important questions regarding the relationship between muscle-derived stem cells and skeletal muscle satellite cells. Moreover, the ability of hematopoietic cells to undergo myogenesis has led to new investigations into the embryonic origin of satellite cells. Recent developmental studies suggest that a population of satellite cells may be derived from progenitors in the embryonic vasculature. These findings provide the first evidence that pluripotent stem cells are present within adult skeletal muscle. Tissue-specific stem cells, including satellite cells, may share a common embryonic origin and possess the capacity to activate diverse genetic programs in response to environmental stimuli. Harnessing such tissue-specific stem cells may eventually revolutionize therapies for degenerative diseases, including muscular dystrophy.

title: Involving family members in cancer care: focus group considerations of patients and oncological providers.
text: Family members are an indispensable component of a patient's cancer care journey, commencing from the moment of diagnosis and extending through the conclusion of treatment. They bring with them a diverse array of emotional responses, interpersonal dynamics, and expectations regarding the care the patient receives. This study forms part of a multi-institutional project aimed at continuously improving the cancer care process. In this study, 19 focus groups (11 patient and 8 provider) were conducted across eight cancer centers in the United States, focusing on issues related to doctor-patient communication. The content of the conversations was analyzed, and thematic categories emerged, illuminating the various strengths and challenges associated with family involvement. The comments from the focus groups underscore the significance of holding explicit discussions between professional caregivers, patients, and their loved ones to negotiate the expectations and needs of each team member. The findings have implications for clinical practice, and strategies for working with family members are offered.

title: Improving Adherence to Antiretroviral Therapy With Triggered Real-time Text Message Reminders: The China Adherence Through Technology Study.
text:
Background: Real-time adherence monitoring is now possible through medication storage devices equipped with cellular technology. We investigated the effect of triggered cell phone reminders and counseling on antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence among Chinese HIV-infected patients, using objective adherence data to assess the outcome.
Methods: We provided ART patients in Nanning, China, with a medication device (Wisepill) that electronically monitored their ART adherence. After three months, we randomly assigned subjects within optimal (≥95%) and suboptimal (<95%) adherence strata to intervention or control arms. In months four to nine, intervention subjects received individualized reminders triggered by late dose taking (no device opening by 30 minutes past dose time) and counseling using device-generated data. Controls received no reminders or data-informed counseling. We compared post-intervention proportions achieving optimal adherence, mean adherence, and clinical outcomes.
Results: Of 120 enrolled subjects, 116 (96.7%) completed the trial. Pre-intervention optimal adherence was similar in intervention and control arms (63.5% vs. 58.9%, respectively; P = 0.60). In the last intervention month, 87.3% vs. 51.8% achieved optimal adherence (risk ratio: 1.7, 95% confidence interval: 1.3 to 2.2) and mean adherence was 96.2% vs. 89.1% (P = 0.003). Among pre-intervention suboptimal adherers, 78.3% vs. 33.3% achieved optimal adherence (risk ratio: 2.4, confidence interval: 1.2 to 4.5) and mean adherence was 93.3% vs. 84.7% (P = 0.039). Proportions were 92.5% and 62.9% among optimal adherers, respectively (risk ratio: 1.5, confidence interval: 1.1 to 1.9) and mean adherence was 97.8% vs. 91.7% (P = 0.028). Post-intervention clinical outcomes were not significant.
Conclusions: Real-time reminders significantly improved ART adherence in this population. This approach seems promising for managing HIV and other chronic diseases and warrants further investigation and adaptation in other settings.

title: Origin and T cell receptor diversity of Foxp3+CD4+CD25+ T cells.
text: Foxp3(+)CD4(+)CD25(+) regulatory T cells can differentiate from Foxp3(-)CD4(+) medullary thymocytes and Foxp3(-)CD4(+) naive T cells, but the impact of these two processes on the size and composition of the peripheral T cell repertoire is not fully understood. To address this, we tracked the fate of individual Foxp3(+)CD4(+)CD25(+) thymocytes and T cells in vivo in T cell receptor (TCR) transgenic mice with a restricted but polyclonal repertoire of TCRs. Using high-throughput single-cell analysis, we found that Foxp3(+)CD4(+) peripheral T cells were derived from thymic precursors expressing distinct TCRs compared to Foxp3(-)CD4(+) medullary thymocytes and Foxp3(-)CD4(+) T cells. Additionally, we observed higher TCR diversity on Foxp3(+)CD4(+) regulatory T cells compared to Foxp3(-)CD4(+) naive T cells, even in mice lacking expression of tissue-specific antigens. These findings suggest that the greater TCR diversity on Foxp3(+) regulatory T cells may enable these cells to match the specificities of autoreactive and naive T cells.

title: Reproducibility of the diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia: a Gynecologic Oncology Group study.
text:
BACKGROUND: Gynecologists often rely on the International Society of Gynecologic Pathologists (ISGP)/World Health Organization classification to determine endometrial hyperplasia therapy, but this system has been questioned for its reproducibility. To address this issue, the Gynecologic Oncology Group (GOG) initiated a protocol to evaluate the effectiveness of hormonal therapy for atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH).
METHODS: In this study, 306 women with a referring institution's pathologist diagnosis of AEH were assessed by a panel of 3 gynecologic pathologists using ISGP/WHO criteria. The panel determined the reproducibility of the referring institution's diagnosis and reached a consensus diagnosis for each case.
RESULTS: The panel's diagnosis of AEH was supported by the majority of the panel in only 38% of cases, and the overall kappa value for the panel diagnosis of AEH was 0.28. The majority of cases were diagnosed as adenocarcinoma (29%), cycling endometrium (7%), or nonatypical hyperplasia (18%). The panel reached unanimous agreement on any diagnosis in 40% of cases, and the kappa value for any diagnosis ranged from 0.34 to 0.43.
CONCLUSION: The reproducibility of referring institution pathologists' diagnosis of AEH was found to be poor. Both underestimation and overestimation of the severity of the lesion are common, and the level of reproducibility among subspecialist panel members for diagnosis of AEH in these specimens is also poor. Improved diagnostic criteria and sampling methods are needed to improve reproducibility of this diagnosis, particularly for clinical decision-making.

title: Replication Fork Slowing and Reversal upon DNA Damage Require PCNA Polyubiquitination and ZRANB3 DNA Translocase Activity
text: DNA damage tolerance during eukaryotic replication is regulated by PCNA ubiquitination, with different types of ubiquitination activating distinct DNA repair pathways. While monoubiquitination triggers mutagenic translesion synthesis, polyubiquitination activates an error-free pathway that is mostly absent in mammals, allowing damage to be bypassed through template switching. In vitro, multiple enzymes, including the DNA translocase ZRANB3, have been shown to interact with polyubiquitinated PCNA and drive fork reversal. However, the in vivo role of this interaction was unclear until now. Our study reveals that damage-induced fork reversal in mammalian cells requires PCNA ubiquitination, UBC13, and K63-linked polyubiquitin chains, which were previously involved in error-free damage tolerance. Fork reversal in vivo also depends on ZRANB3 translocase activity and its interaction with polyubiquitinated PCNA, identifying ZRANB3 as a crucial effector of error-free DNA damage tolerance. Furthermore, our findings suggest that fork remodeling acts as a global mechanism to slow down and protect against DNA damage, and targeting these protection systems may provide a promising strategy to enhance cancer chemotherapy.

title: Bed sharing when parents do not smoke: is there a risk of SIDS? An individual level analysis of five major case–control studies
text:
The objective of this study is to investigate the association between sleeping in bed with an infant and the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), specifically in cases where neither parent smokes and the baby is breastfed.
Methods:
The study combined data from five large SIDS case-control datasets from the UK, Europe, and Australasia. A total of 1472 SIDS cases and 4679 controls were included, with each study including all cases meeting standard criteria. Controls were randomly selected normal infants of similar age, time, and place. Results:
In the combined dataset, 22.2% of cases and 9.6% of controls were found to be bed sharing, with an adjusted odds ratio (AOR) of 2.7 (95% CI: 1.4 to 5.3). The bed sharing risk decreased with increasing infant age. When neither parent smoked, and the baby was less than 3 months old, breastfed, and had no other risk factors, the AOR for bed sharing versus room sharing was 5.1 (2.3 to 11.4), with an estimated absolute risk for these room sharing infants of very low 0.08 (0.05 to 0.14)/1000 live-births. This increased to 0.23 (0.11 to 0.43)/1000 when bed sharing, with smoking and alcohol use significantly increasing bed sharing risk.

Conclusions: The study found that bed sharing for sleep when parents do not smoke or take alcohol or drugs increases the risk of SIDS. The risk is significantly increased when combined with parental smoking, maternal alcohol consumption, and/or drug use. By avoiding bed sharing, a substantial reduction in SIDS rates could be achieved.

title: Decoupling activation and exhaustion of B cells in spontaneous controllers of HIV infection.
text:
Objective: To investigate the impact of chronic viremia and associated immune activation on B-cell exhaustion in HIV infection.
Design: Progressive HIV infection is characterized by B-cell anergy and exhaustion, as well as extreme hypergammaglobulinemia. Despite the use of CD95 and CD21 as markers of B-cell dysfunction, the specific profiles of dysfunctional B cells and the role of persistent viral replication in driving B-cell dysfunction are not well understood.
Methods: Multiparameter flow cytometry was used to define the profile of dysfunctional B cells in patients with different levels of viral replication control. The changes in CD21 and CD95 expression on B-cell subpopulations were tracked over time in both progressors and controllers of HIV infection.
Results: Although exhausted, CD21 tissue-like memory B cells developed similarly in both progressors and controllers, the frequency of CD21 activated memory B cells was lower in spontaneous controllers.
Conclusion: Our findings suggest that the loss of CD21 and the upregulation of CD95 occur as separate events during the development of B-cell dysfunction. The loss of CD21 indicates B-cell exhaustion triggered by viral replication in the absence of substantial immune activation, while the upregulation of CD95 is closely linked to persistent viral replication and associated immune activation. Therefore, these dysfunctional profiles might represent two distinct functional states within the B-cell compartment.

title: Label-free DNA imaging in vivo with stimulated Raman scattering microscopy.
text: Label-free DNA imaging is highly sought after in biology and medicine, as it enables live imaging without affecting cell function and provides instant histological tissue examination during surgical procedures. Here, we present a label-free DNA imaging method using stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy for visualizing cell nuclei in live animals and intact fresh human tissues with subcellular resolution. By exploiting the distinct Raman spectral features of carbon-hydrogen bonds in DNA, we can retrieve DNA distribution from a strong background of proteins and lipids through linear decomposition of SRS images at three optimally selected Raman shifts. Moreover, we demonstrate the ability to capture chromosome dynamics during cell division both in vitro and in vivo, as well as track mouse skin cell proliferation induced by drug treatment using in vivo counting of the mitotic rate. Additionally, we show a label-free histology method for human skin cancer diagnosis that offers comparable results to conventional tissue staining methods such as H&E, with higher sensitivity than SRS imaging of DNA in the fingerprint spectral region. Our approach is three orders of magnitude faster than spontaneous Raman imaging of DNA, allowing both chromatin dynamic studies and label-free optical histology in real time.

title: A common variant in BRCA2 is associated with both breast cancer risk and prenatal viability
text: Mutations inherited from one's parents in the BRCA2 gene are associated with an increased risk of developing breast cancer at an early age. However, these mutations account for less than 2% of all breast cancer cases in East Anglia. It is likely that low penetrance alleles, or non-pathogenic variations in genes like BRCA2, contribute to the greater part of inherited susceptibility to breast cancer. BRCA2 is believed to play a role in repairing DNA double-strand breaks. Few mice with a truncated form of Brca2 survive to birth, and most of these mice are male and smaller than their littermates. We have found that a common human polymorphism (N372H) in exon 10 of BRCA2 confers an elevated risk of breast cancer. Compared to the NN group, individuals who are homozygous for the variant (HH) have a 1.31-fold greater risk of breast cancer (95% CI: 1.07-1.61). In female controls of all ages, there is a significant deficiency of homozygotes compared to what would be expected under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, while in male controls there is an excess of homozygotes. Specifically, the HH group has an estimated fitness of 0.82 in females and 1.38 in males. Therefore, this variant of BRCA2 appears to affect fetal survival in a sex-dependent manner.

title: Pathophysiology of obstructive nephropathy in the newborn.
text: Congenital obstructive nephropathy is a developmental disorder that arises from abnormalities in the urinary tract during fetal development, resulting in renal growth failure and injury. We have investigated the renal cellular and physiological responses to unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) in neonatal rodents, including guinea pigs, rats, and mice. Interestingly, UUO has opposite effects on renal development in neonates compared to adults. While adult UUO stimulates renal cellular proliferation, UUO in neonates reduces nephrogenesis, glomerular maturation, and tubular cellular proliferation. This is accompanied by a disproportionately greater growth of the intact opposite kidney in the neonate. The impaired renal growth and tubular atrophy in neonates may be due to a combination of factors, including stimulation of renal tubular apoptosis. This may occur due to loss of epithelial cell polarity, reduction in the oncoprotein bcl-2, and increase in the expression of the fibrogenic cytokine, transforming growth factor-beta1 (TGF-beta1). Treatment with EGF (epidermal growth factor) has been shown to stimulate cellular proliferation, suppress apoptosis, and reduce tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis. TGF-beta1 is regulated by the renin-angiotensin system, which is activated by UUO in neonates. The long-term consequences of obstructive nephropathy in early development include hyperfiltration by remaining nephrons, followed by a gradual decrease in glomerular filtration rate, which may only become apparent in later life. A better understanding of the cellular mechanisms underlying congenital urinary tract obstruction may lead to the development of specific treatments, such as gene therapy or modulators of renal growth and development.

title: Lipid homeostasis, lipotoxicity and the metabolic syndrome.
text: In the 20th century, industrialized nations have experienced an unprecedented surge in obesity. In the United States, the epicenter of this epidemic, over 66% of the population is overweight, and one in every six Americans has metabolic syndrome. Although genetics play a role in susceptibility to unhealthy lifestyle habits, the primary cause of this epidemic is the excessive consumption of high-calorie, high-fat foods, combined with a significant decrease in physical activity due to technological advancements. If this trend continues, inevitable health consequences include type II diabetes and a cluster of related disorders known as metabolic syndrome, which typically manifest in middle age. The body's adaptive mechanism to store excess calories as fat in adipocyte compartments helps to buffer these consequences before middle age. Leptin, a key hormone, regulates the partitioning of surplus calories. However, multiple factors can influence the capacity of fat tissue to store lipids, leading to ectopic lipid deposition and accumulation in organs such as skeletal muscle, liver, heart, and pancreas. Abnormal levels of triglycerides in these organs can have detrimental effects, including lipoapoptosis, a gradual decline in organ function, ultimately resulting in cell death. The harmful effects of fatty acid derivatives on cell function can lead to gradual organ failure.

title: A twin-study of genetic contributions to morningness-eveningness and depression.
text: The relationship between circadian rhythms and depression has been the focus of a recent study. The study, conducted on a sample of 1237 twins from the Vietnam Era Twin Study of Aging, investigated the heritability of morningness-eveningness (ME) and its association with depression. The study found that both ME and depression are heritable, with a significant genetic correlation between the two. The genetic covariance between ME and depression accounted for 59.1% of the phenotypic correlation. The study also found that the DE sub-scale of the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression (CES-D) was significantly heritable, while the Well-Being sub-scale had a significant genetic correlation with ME. These findings suggest that there may be a shared underlying genetic factor between ME and depression, and that further study of this relationship may lead to a better understanding of the etiology of depression and potential targets for treatment.

title: The Transcription Factor T-bet Regulates Intestinal Inflammation Mediated by Interleukin-7 Receptor+ Innate Lymphoid Cells
text: Mice lacking the transcription factor T-bet in their innate immune system develop colitis, and we have found that Il-17A-producing Il-7Rα(+) innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) play a crucial role in the disease. Tnf-α produced by CD103(-)CD11b(+) dendritic cells collaborates with Il-23 to stimulate Il-17A production by ILCs, demonstrating a previously unappreciated level of cellular communication between dendritic cells and ILCs. We have discovered Helicobacter typhlonius as the key factor driving excess TNF-α production and colitis in Tbx21(-/-)Rag2(-/-) ulcerative colitis (TRUC) mice. Notably, T-bet also represses the expression of Il-7R, a crucial molecule involved in controlling intestinal ILC homeostasis. The significance of Il-7R signaling in TRUC disease is highlighted by the dramatic reduction in intestinal ILCs and alleviated colitis following Il-7R blockade. These findings elucidate the mechanism by which T-bet regulates the complex interaction between mucosal dendritic cells, ILCs, and the intestinal microbiota.

title: Chimeric Antigen Receptor-Redirected Regulatory T Cells Suppress Experimental Allergic Airway Inflammation, a Model of Asthma
text: Cellular therapy using chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-modified cytotoxic T cells has shown promising results in the treatment of blood cancers. However, we investigated the potential of regulatory T cell (Treg)-based therapy in treating allergic airway inflammation, which is similar to asthma, characterized by airway hyper-reactivity (AHR) and a chronic Th2 cell-mediated immune response to allergens. To restore balance in the lung, we redirected Tregs using a CAR towards lung epithelial cells in mice with experimentally induced allergic asthma, mimicking the clinical situation. Adoptively transferred CAR Tregs accumulated in the lung and tracheobronchial lymph nodes, reducing AHR and eosinophilic airway inflammation, as evidenced by lower cell numbers in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and decreased cell infiltrates in the lung. Furthermore, CAR Treg cells prevented excessive pulmonary mucus production, as well as increased levels of allergen-specific IgE and Th2 cytokines in exposed animals. Importantly, CAR Tregs were more effective in controlling asthma than non-modified Tregs, highlighting the crucial role of specific Treg cell activation in the affected organ. These findings suggest that targeting CAR Treg cells to the lung can ameliorate key features of experimental airway inflammation, paving the way for cell therapy in severe allergic asthma.

title: α-Catenin as a tension transducer that induces adherens junction development
text: Adherens junctions (AJs), organized by adhesion proteins and the underlying actin cytoskeleton, likely detect forces from adjacent cells and modulate opposing forces to maintain tissue integrity, but the molecular regulation remains unclear. Although the possibility of α-catenin acting as a direct linker between the membrane and actin cytoskeleton for AJ formation and function has been minimized, our study reveals that α-catenin recruits vinculin, another major actin-binding protein of AJs, through force-dependent changes in α-catenin conformation. We identified regions in the α-catenin molecule necessary for its force-dependent binding of vinculin by introducing mutant α-catenin into cells and using in vitro binding assays. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching analysis of α-catenin mobility and the existence of an antibody recognizing α-catenin in a force-dependent manner further support the notion that α-catenin functions as a tension transducer, converting mechanical stimuli into a chemical response that leads to AJ development.

title: A population-based cohort study to elucidate temporal relationship between schizophrenia and metabolic syndrome (KCIS no. PSY3).
text:
The bidirectional relationships between metabolic syndrome (MetS) and schizophrenia (SCZ) play a crucial role in the clinical treatment of both diseases, but the bidirectional causal effects have not been comprehensively elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the influence of MetS on the incidence of SCZ and vice versa, as well as their predictors for each direction using a population-based cohort sample.
Methods: The study enrolled 76,545 participants who had participated in a community-based health screening program during 1999-2004. Subjects with existing MetS or SCZ were excluded, and the study cohorts were followed over time to ascertain the incidence of SCZ and MetS. The hazard ratios for the effect of predictors on each incident outcome were estimated after controlling for confounding factors.
Results: The overall incidence rate of SCZ was 61.15 per 10(5) person-years. The incidence rate in participants with MetS was lower than those without (44.24 vs 64.20), indicating the presence of MetS did not increase the risk of developing incident SCZ. However, participants with abnormal waist circumference (WC) were twice (95% CI: 1.37 to 2.93) more likely to experience incident SCZ compared to those with normal WC. In the opposite direction, the incidence of MetS was significantly higher in patients with SCZ than those without SCZ (11.25% vs 7.94%, respectively), suggesting SCZ conferred a higher risk for incident MetS (adjusted hazard ratio=1.89, 95% CI: 1.36, 2.63).
Discussion: The study found that central obesity, one of the individual components of MetS, was an independent predictor for incident SCZ. Patients diagnosed with SCZ were at greater risk of having incident cases of MetS. The significant temporal bidirectional relationships between SCZ and central obesity suggest a reciprocal interaction exists between SCZ and central obesity.
Conclusion: The study provides evidence for the bidirectional relationships between SCZ and MetS, with central obesity as a significant predictor for both. These findings have important implications for the clinical treatment of both diseases.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A MEASURE OF EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE
text:
A series of studies aimed to develop a measure of emotional intelligence (EI) based on the model developed by Salovey and Mayer (1990). A pool of 62 items represented the different dimensions of the model. A factor analysis of the responses from 346 participants suggested the creation of a 33-item scale. Subsequent studies demonstrated good internal consistency and test-retest reliability of the 33-item measure. Validation studies also showed that scores on the 33-item measure:
1. Correlated with eight of nine theoretically related constructs, including alexithymia, attention to feelings, clarity of feelings, mood repair, optimism, and impulse control.
2. Predicted first-year college grades.
3. Were significantly higher for therapists than for therapy clients or prisoners.
4. Were significantly higher for females than males, consistent with prior findings in studies of emotional skills.
5. Were not related to cognitive ability.
6. Were associated with the openness to experience trait of the big five personality dimensions.

title: Cholesterol glucosylation promotes immune evasion by Helicobacter pylori
text: The bacterial infection Helicobacter pylori can lead to gastric pathologies such as ulcers and cancer. Since H. pylori is unable to synthesize cholesterol, we investigated its ability to assimilate this lipid in the context of infection. We found that H. pylori migrates along a cholesterol gradient and extracts cholesterol from the plasma membranes of epithelial cells, which it then glucosylates. High levels of cholesterol in the host promote the phagocytosis of H. pylori by immune cells such as macrophages and dendritic cells, and enhance antigen-specific T cell responses. Conversely, a cholesterol-rich diet during bacterial challenge can reduce the H. pylori burden in the stomach through T cell–dependent mechanisms. Intrinsic cholesterol glucosylation inhibits the phagocytosis of H. pylori and subsequent T cell activation. We identified the gene hp0421 as encoding the enzyme cholesterol-α-glucosyltransferase, which is responsible for cholesterol glucosylation. Generation of knockout mutants lacking hp0421 confirms the importance of cholesteryl glucosides for avoiding phagocytosis, T cell activation, and bacterial clearance in vivo. Therefore, we propose a mechanism regulating the host–pathogen interaction whereby glucosylation of a lipid influences immune evasion or response.

title: Regulation of in situ to invasive breast carcinoma transition.
text: The progression of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) to invasive carcinoma is a poorly understood process in breast tumor development. To investigate this process, we used a model of human DCIS and primary breast tumors, and analyzed the role of myoepithelial cells and fibroblasts in the progression of in situ carcinomas. Our findings revealed that fibroblasts promote the progression to invasion, while normal myoepithelial cells inhibit it. By analyzing the molecular profiles of isolated luminal epithelial and myoepithelial cells, we identified an intricate network of interactions involving TGFbeta, Hedgehog, cell adhesion, and p63, which are essential for myoepithelial cell differentiation and the maintenance of myoepithelial cells. Our results demonstrate that the loss of these interactions leads to the loss of myoepithelial cells and the progression to invasion.

title: Health and access to care: perspectives of homeless youth in Baltimore City, U.S.A.
text: Homeless young people are disproportionately afflicted by health issues, yet there is a scarcity of information about their views on their own health concerns. To investigate the perceived health needs of shelter-based youth in Baltimore, MD, a qualitative research approach that combined participatory rural assessment and rapid appraisal procedures was employed. According to the young people, the most common health issues they face include sexually transmitted diseases (STDs), HIV/AIDS, pregnancy, depression, drug abuse, and injuries. These findings align with more objective health status data for the same youth. The young people identified environmental danger threats, such as violence and abuse from adults, as well as racism and sexism, in their daily lives. The youth reported that trusted adult figures like grandmothers are crucial in providing health advice. Many homeless youth from unstable family backgrounds continue to seek advice from parents and other family members. Urban street youth health interventions must consider the significance of social context and the reality of violence as a persistent daily health risk.

title: Differential requirement for CARMA1 in agonist-selected T-cell development.
text:
Caspase recruitment domain-containing membrane-associated guanylate kinase protein-1 (CARMA1) plays a crucial role in the NF-κB signaling cascade triggered by T-cell receptor (TCR) engagement. While TCR signaling is essential for the activation and development of naïve T cells, it also contributes to the formation of specific T-cell subsets, including regulatory T cells (Tregs), natural killer T (NKT) cells, and CD8-alpha alpha T cells. However, the role of CARMA1 in the development of these cell types has remained largely unexplored.
Our study revealed that CARMA1-deficient mice (CARMA1(-/-)) exhibit altered populations of specific subsets of agonist-selected T cells. Specifically, CARMA1(-/-) mice show impaired development of natural and adaptive Tregs, whereas NKT cell numbers remain unchanged compared to wild-type mice. Interestingly, CD8-alpha alpha T cells, which may also develop through an extrathymic selection pathway, are enriched in the gut of CARMA1(-/-) mice, while memory-phenotype CD4(+) T cells (CD62L(low)/CD44(high)) are reduced in the periphery. These findings indicate that CARMA1 is essential for Treg development, but is not necessary for the development of other agonist-selected T-cell subsets.
Overall, our data reveal an important but differential role for CARMA1-mediated TCR signaling in T-cell development, highlighting the unique functions of this protein in regulating T-cell lineage commitment.

title: Simian immunodeficiency viruses of diverse origin can use CXCR4 as a coreceptor for entry into human cells.
text: Isolate of primary simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) from sooty mangabey (SIVsm [n = 6]), stumptail (SIVstm [n = 1]), mandrill (SIVmnd [n = 1]), and African green (SIVagm [n = 1]) primates were examined for their ability to infect human cells and their coreceptor requirements. All isolates infected human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from a CCR5(+/+) donor, and seven of eight isolates tested also infected CCR5(-/-) PBMCs. Analysis of coreceptor utilization using GHOST and U87 cell lines revealed that all of the isolates tested used CCR5 and the orphan receptors STRL33 and GPR15. Coreceptors such as CCR2b, CCR3, CCR8, and CX3CR1 were also utilized by some primary SIV isolates. More importantly, we found that CXCR4 was used as a coreceptor by the SIVstm, the SIVagm, and four of the SIVsm isolates in GHOST and U87 cells. These data suggest that primary SIV isolates from diverse primate species can utilize CXCR4 for viral entry, similar to what has been described for human immunodeficiency viruses.

title: Cloning of rat uncoupling protein-3 and uncoupling protein-2 cDNAs: their gene expression in rats fed high-fat diet.
text: To elucidate energy balance in skeletal muscle, we cloned cDNA from a homologue of uncoupling protein (UCP) in rat skeletal muscle. Additionally, we cloned UCP-2 cDNA from rat brown adipose tissue (BAT). The UCP cloned from rat skeletal muscle shared 57% and 72% identity with rat UCP-1 and UCP-2, respectively. The mRNA was primarily expressed in skeletal muscle, moderately in BAT, and marginally in white adipose tissue (WAT) with a prominent band at 2.5 kb and a minor band at 2.8 kb, while the UCP-2 gene was predominantly detected throughout the body, with notable levels in WAT and small amounts in skeletal muscle and BAT. Notably, the rat UCP shared 86% identity with recently cloned human UCP-3, which was abundantly expressed in skeletal muscle with a signal of 2.4 kb. Hence, the rat UCP was designated as rat UCP-3. In high-fat-fed rats, UCP-3 gene expression was augmented by 2-fold in skeletal muscle, while UCP-2 mRNA levels were significantly increased (1.6-fold) in epididymal WAT. Enhanced expression of UCPs may serve as a defense against high-fat-induced obesity and impaired glucose metabolism.

title: A two-step mechanism for epigenetic specification of centromere identity and function
text: The fundamental mechanism of chromosome inheritance, the centromere, is designated by an epigenetic marker in many eukaryotes. Using gene targeting in human cells and fission yeast, it has been demonstrated that chromatin enriched with the centromere-specific histone H3 variant CENP-A carries the epigenetic mark that determines, maintains, and propagates centromere function indefinitely. Initially, the centromere position is replicated and maintained through chromatin assembly with the centromere-targeting domain (CATD) of CENP-A incorporated into H3. Subsequently, the nucleation of kinetochore assembly onto CATD-containing chromatin requires either the amino- or carboxy-terminal tail of CENP-A for the recruitment of inner kinetochore proteins, such as stabilizing CENP-B binding to human centromeres or direct recruitment of CENP-C, respectively.

title: Cancer stem cell theory in gastrointestinal malignancies: recent progress and upcoming challenges
text: A growing body of research confirms the notion that malignant tumors are complex and composed of diverse subpopulations of cells with unique properties, including the ability to initiate tumors and metastasize. This phenomenon is supported by the cancer stem cell (CSC) theory, which posits that malignancies are composed of a small population of stem cells that are responsible for tumor growth and progression. Recent advances in technology have allowed for a deeper understanding and characterization of CSCs, opening up new avenues for cancer treatment. However, there are also some reservations regarding the practical application of this theory to hematopoietic malignancies and solid tumors. Efficacious therapeutic approaches targeting the CSC population are being explored to overcome treatment failure and improve patient outcomes. This review will focus on the internal and external regulation of CSCs, as well as the development of therapeutic approaches against CSCs, with a primary emphasis on gastrointestinal malignancies.

title: In vitro splicing pathways of pre-mRNAs containing multiple intervening sequences?
text:
In this study, we investigated the in vitro splicing pathways of three multi-intervening-sequence (IVS) pre-mRNAs: human beta-globin, rat alpha-lactalbumin, and murine interleukin-3. By analyzing the splicing events in detail, we found that there are distinct preferential pathways of IVS removal for each pre-mRNA.
For the rat alpha-lactalbumin pre-mRNA, we observed that the three IVSs were removed sequentially, with IVS1 being excised first, followed by IVS2 and then IVS3. In contrast, the splicing pathway of interleukin-3 pre-mRNA was more complex, with the four IVSs being excised in a non-linear and non-directional manner. Specifically, in most molecules, IVS1 and IVS4 were removed first, either simultaneously or in rapid succession, followed by IVS2 and then IVS3.
Our findings challenge existing models of splice site selection, which often assume a more linear and directional splicing process. Instead, our results suggest that the splicing pathway can be highly dynamic and depends on the specific sequence context of the IVSs. Furthermore, we did not observe any exon skipping during the splicing process, which adds further evidence to the non-linear nature of the splicing pathway.
Overall, this study provides new insights into the mechanisms of splice site selection and the complexity of the splicing pathway in mRNA processing. The findings have important implications for understanding the regulation of gene expression at the post-transcriptional level and may lead to new strategies for manipulating splicing events in various biological contexts.

title: Automated genome sequence analysis and annotation.
text:
Large-scale genome projects have led to an exponential increase in the number of protein sequences generated, but the majority of them remain biochemically uncharacterized. Bioinformatics research has contributed to the development of computational methods for the annotation of these sequences. However, the installation and application of these methods require significant experience and time.
Here, we present an automatic system for preliminary functional annotation of protein sequences, which has been applied to the analysis of sets of sequences from complete genomes to refine existing annotations and make new discoveries comparable to those made by human experts. The GeneQuiz system features a user-friendly Web-based browser that allows for the examination of the evidence leading to automatic annotations and provides additional information, views of the results, and links to relevant biological databases.
The system structure and operating principles, including the use of multiple sequence databases, underlying sequence analysis tools, and lexical analyses of database annotations, are detailed. The system performs automatic quality assessments of results based on prior experience with the underlying sequence analysis tools, resulting in estimated error rates of 2.5-5% for the most reliable annotations ('clear' cases).
We also discuss sources of over-interpretation of results and propose improvements. Furthermore, we present a conservative definition for reporting 'new findings' that takes into account the maturity of the database, along with examples of possible kinds of discoveries (e.g., new function, family, or superfamily) made by the system.
Our analysis of system performance shows that the GeneQuiz system offers inherent advantages of an integrated automatic approach using multiple databases and search methods, applied in an objective and repeatable manner. The system is publicly available for protein sequence analysis through a Web server at <http://www.sander.ebi.ac.uk/gqsrv/submit>.

title: GAPDH Mediates Nitrosylation of Nuclear Proteins
text:
Nitric oxide-mediated protein modification, known as S-nitrosylation, plays a crucial role in cellular signaling. S-nitrosylation can regulate a wide range of proteins, including prominent nuclear proteins like HDAC2 and PARP1. The reactivity of nitric oxide groups with thiol groups in proteins is high, but the selective nature of S-nitrosylation within the cell suggests the existence of targeting mechanisms. The binding of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) to target proteins, either directly or through scaffolding proteins like PSD-95 and CAPON, is one way in which specificity in nitric oxide signaling is achieved. However, the mechanisms by which nuclear proteins are selectively nitrosylated have been unclear.
One important example of S-nitrosylation involves glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH), which is nitrosylated at its Cys 150 residue.
