This review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the complex cellular processes involved in exocrine pancreas development and the underlying mechanisms that shape the pancreatic cellular landscape.

title: The history of SIVS and AIDS: epidemiology, phylogeny and biology of isolates from naturally SIV infected non-human primates (NHP) in Africa.
text: Simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) naturally infects non-human primates in Africa, with over 40 strains identified across different species. These viruses exhibit high genetic diversity, clustering into six distinct phylogenetic lineages. At least eight SIVs are considered recombinant, based on unique genomic structure in various regions. The three known types of genomes are characterized by the presence of vpr, vpx, or vpu genes. Vpx resulted from a duplication of the vpr gene and is unique to SIVs infecting the Papionini tribe of monkeys and HIV-2 in humans. Vpu is present in SIVcpz and HIV-1 and may have originated from a recombination involving SIVs from cercopitecini monkeys. SIV generally appears non-pathogenic in natural hosts despite high viral replication, likely due to virus-host adaptation, resulting in an incubation period exceeding the life span of African primate hosts. SIVs have a strong propensity for cross-species transmission, with results varying from inapparent infections to highly pathogenic, the latter observed in macaques and humans. The high genetic diversity of SIV is attributed to a combination of factors, including a low fidelity of reverse transcriptase, active viral and host cell turnover, host-dependent evolution, and recombination. Cross-species transmission is not uncommon, but preferential host switching might drive the majority of transmissions. Many SIVs are able to grow in vitro on human PBMC, leading some to suggest that SIV poses a threat to humans in Central Africa and that AIDS is a zoonosis. However, there is no conclusive evidence that AIDS is transmitted like a zoonosis, and SIV may adapt to the human host in order to emerge in the general population. Studying SIV in its natural hosts can provide valuable insights into the real threat to human populations and the mechanisms associated with long-term persistent viral infection without clinical consequences for the host.

title: The association between common physical impairments and dementia in low and middle income countries, and, among people with dementia, their association with cognitive function and disability. A 10/66 Dementia Research Group population-based study.
text:
Purpose:
Chronic physical comorbidities are common among individuals with dementia, yet there is a lack of evidence to support good practice guidelines for addressing these issues. This study aimed to investigate the extent of comorbidities and their impact on cognitive function and disability in population-based studies conducted in low- and middle-income countries, where chronic diseases and impairments are prevalent and often undertreated.
Methods:
A multicentre cross-sectional survey of all individuals aged 65 years and older residing in 11 catchment areas across China, India, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Mexico, and Peru was conducted (n = 15,022). The prevalence of pain, incontinence, hearing, and visual impairments, as well as mobility impairment and undernutrition, was estimated according to the presence and severity of dementia. The independent contribution of these impairments to cognitive function and disability was assessed among those with dementia, adjusting for age, gender, education, and dementia severity.
Results:
Consistently across regions, incontinence, hearing impairment, mobility impairment, and undernutrition were found to be linearly associated with the presence and severity of dementia. Among individuals with dementia, incontinence, hearing impairment, and mobility impairment were independently associated with disability in all regions, while the contributions of pain, visual impairment, and undernutrition were inconsistent. Hearing impairment was the only impairment that made a notable independent contribution to cognitive impairment.

Conclusion:
There is a pressing need for clinical trials to evaluate the feasibility, efficacy, and cost-effectiveness of regular physical health checks and remediation of identified pathologies, given the substantial comorbidity identified in population-based studies and the strong evidence for independent impact on functioning.

title: Serum biomarkers as predictors of lung function decline in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
text:
RECENT STUDIES HAVE SHOWN THAT PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (COPD) EXHIBIT LOW-GRADE SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION, AND THAT PLASTMA FIBRINOGEN AND HIGH NEUTROPHIL COUNTS ARE ON CORRELATED WITH FASTER DECLINES IN LUNG FUNCTION. WE EXAMINED THE CORRELATION BETWEEN SERUM BIOMARKERS AND THE DECLINE OF LUNG FUNCTION IN COPD PATIENTS.
METHODS: WE MEASURED THE SERUM LEVELS OF 9 BIOMARKERS (TIMP-1, ALPHA1-ANTITRYPSIN, MMP-9, TNF-ALPHA, TGF-BETA, IL-6, IL-8, NEUTROPHIL ELASTASE, AND CRP), FIBRINOGEN, AND WHITE BLOOD CELL COUNTS (WCC) IN 96 COPD PATIENTS AT BASELINE. LUNG FUNCTION WAS MEASURED AT THE TIME OF BLOOD SAMPLING AND EVERY 3-6 MONTHS DURING THE OBSERVATION PERIOD (MEDIAN 25.0 MONTHS).
RESULTS: 20 PATIENTS WERE Labeled as "RAPID DECLINERS" AND 53 PATIENTS WERE "NON-DECLINERS" BASED ON THE ANNUAL CHANGE OF % PREDICTED FEV(1) OVER THE OBSERVATION PERIOD. THE RAPID DECLINERS HAD HIGHER NEUTROPHIL COUNTS, SERUM CRP, and MMP-9 LEVELS THAN THE NON-DECLINERS (P<0.05). THE ANNUAL CHANGE OF % PREDICTED FEV(1) WAS INVERSELY CORRELATED WITH MMP-9 (R=-0.288; P<0.01) AND CRP (R=-0.354; P<0.005) (PARTIAL COVARIANCE COEFFICIENTS ADJUSTED FOR AGE, SEX, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, SMOKING HISTORY, AND BASELINE % PREDICTED FEV(1)). THE REMAINING BIOMARKERS WERE NOT CORRELATED WITH THE ANNUAL CHANGE OF % PREDICTED FEV(1).
CONCLUSION: OUR RESULTS SUGGEST THAT SERUM CRP AND MMP-9 LEVELS WERE RELATED TO FEV(1) DECLINE. THESE MARKERS MAY BE USEFUL AS PREDICTORS FOR RAPID DECLINE OF FEV(1) IN COPD PATIENTS. ADDITIONAL LARGE-SCALE AND LONGER-TERM STUDIES OF COPD PATIENTS COULD HELP DETERMINE THE EXACT ROLES OF THESE BIOMARKERS.

title: Phosphorylation of ATM by Cdk5 mediates DNA damage signaling and regulates neuronal death
text: The phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase-like kinase ATM (ataxia-telangiectasia mutated) plays a central role in coordinating DNA damage responses, including cell-cycle checkpoint control, DNA repair, and apoptosis. Mutations of ATM can lead to a range of defects, from neurodegeneration to cancer predisposition. Although the mechanism by which DNA damage activates ATM is not fully understood, our findings reveal a novel pathway involving the cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5). We show that Cdk5, activated by DNA damage, directly phosphorylates ATM at Ser 794 in post-mitotic neurons, which in turn precedes and requires ATM autophosphorylation at Ser 1981. This phosphorylation event activates ATM kinase activity and regulates the phosphorylation and function of ATM targets, including p53 and H2AX. Inhibition of the Cdk5-ATM pathway reduces DNA-damage-induced neuronal cell cycle re-entry and expression of the p53 targets PUMA and Bax, thereby protecting neurons from death. This study demonstrates that activation of Cdk5 by DNA damage functions as a critical signal to initiate the ATM response and regulate ATM-dependent cellular processes.

title: Nerve-induced release of nitric oxide in the rabbit gastrointestinal tract as measured by in vivo microdialysis.
text: 1. Scientists have suggested that nitric oxide (NO) may play a role as a neurotransmitter in the gastrointestinal (GI) system, mediating relaxation and the peristaltic reflex. The goal of the current study was to measure the formation of NO in the GI tract in real-time using in vivo animal models. 2. During vagal nerve stimulation in anesthetized rabbits, the formation of NO's oxidation products, nitrite and nitrate, was measured using microdialysis probes placed in the stomach and colon. These measurements were taken using capillary electrophoresis. 3. The study found that vagal nerve stimulation led to an increase in nitrite and nitrate formation in the stomach and colon, with the stomach showing the greatest increase. This increase was inhibited when the animals were given an NO synthase inhibitor, N omega-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME). 4. Furthermore, the study showed that L-NAME significantly increased gastric and colonic contractions, both in response to vagal nerve stimulation and spontaneously. In summary, this study provides evidence that NO is released in the stomach and colonic wall during vagal nerve activity at concentrations that can inhibit smooth muscle contractions in vivo.

title: Screening for concomitant diseases in peripheral vascular patients. Results of a systematic approach.
text:
Background: Patients scheduled for arterial surgery often have a high prevalence of comorbid conditions, such as cardiac, vascular, and other diseases, which can impact operative risk and survival. To address this, we developed a systematic diagnostic workup strategy for detecting these coexistent conditions in vascular surgical patients, primarily using non-invasive techniques.
Methods: We evaluated 200 consecutive patients admitted to our department of vascular surgery in an academic teaching hospital to determine the total incidence of relevant concomitant disorders, the extent to which this screening yielded new diagnostic information, and its impact on one-year survival.
Results: Our findings revealed that 46% of the patients had coronary artery disease, of which 22% had active ischemia diagnosed for the first time in 5.5% of patients. Impaired cardiac function was detected in 37% of patients, including severely impaired function in 12% and new diagnoses in 27%. Carotid artery disease was present in 32% of patients, with critical stenoses diagnosed in 9% and new diagnoses in 29.9%. Aortic aneurysms were found in 7% of patients, with 5% being newly diagnosed. Severe renal artery stenosis was present in 5% of patients, with 3.5% being newly diagnosed. Additionally, 16% of patients had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, with 3.5% being newly diagnosed, and 4.5% had unexpected disorders, all of which were new diagnoses. Overall, new diagnoses were made in 64.5% of patients, influencing therapeutic strategies in 21% of cases. The presence of coronary artery disease and cardiac failure were significantly related to one-year survival.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that a systematic diagnostic workup strategy, primarily based on non-invasive techniques, can identify coexistent diseases in vascular surgical patients. Notably, new diagnoses were made in one out of every five patients and had a significant impact on surgical management and patient prognosis.

title: Archetypal trajectories of social, psychological, and spiritual wellbeing and distress in family care givers of patients with lung cancer: secondary analysis of serial qualitative interviews
text:
Objective:
To investigate whether family caregivers of patients with lung cancer experience similar patterns of social, psychological, and spiritual wellbeing and distress as the patient, from diagnosis to death.
Design:
Secondary analysis of serial qualitative interviews conducted every three months for up to a year or until bereavement.
Setting:
South east Scotland.

Participants:
19 patients with lung cancer and their 19 family caregivers, resulting in 88 interviews (42 with patients and 46 with caregivers).

Results:
Family caregivers followed similar patterns of social, psychological, and spiritual wellbeing and distress as the patients they were caring for, with some caregivers also experiencing decline in physical health, which impacted their ability to care. Psychological and spiritual distress were particularly common and often triggered personal reflections on the meaning and purpose of life. Key time points in the illness, such as diagnosis, initial treatment, recurrence, and terminal stage, were particularly challenging for both patients and caregivers.

Conclusions:
Family caregivers share much of the illness experience of the dying patient. The multidimensional distress experienced by patients with lung cancer is reflected in the suffering of their caregivers in the social, psychological, and spiritual domains, with psychological and spiritual distress being most pronounced. Caregivers may require ongoing support throughout the illness duration, rather than just in the terminal phase and during bereavement, as currently tends to be the case.

title: HER-2/neu induces p53 ubiquitination via Akt-mediated MDM2 phosphorylation
text: Amplification or overexpression of HER-2/neu can enable cancer cells to evade apoptosis and promote their growth. p53 plays a crucial role in regulating cell growth and apoptosis, but it is often mutated or lost in many types of tumors. Our findings suggest that some oncogenic signals can suppress p53 function, even in tumors with a normal copy of the gene. In this study, we discovered that HER-2/neu-mediated resistance to DNA-damaging agents depends on the activation of Akt, which enhances MDM2-mediated p53 degradation. Akt interacts with MDM2 and phosphorylates it at specific sites, leading to increased nuclear localization and decreased interaction with p19ARF, resulting in increased p53 degradation. Our results imply that inhibiting the Akt pathway activated by HER-2/neu could enhance the cytotoxic effect of DNA-damaging drugs in tumor cells with wild-type p53.

title: T cell memory.
text: Previous infection or vaccination can induce T cell memory, providing enhanced protection against subsequent microbial infections. Recent technological advances have improved our understanding of the processes involved in generating and maintaining T cell memory. T cells develop in response to a specific set of cues, beginning with signals from antigen-loaded, activated antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and inflammatory mediators triggered by the innate immune response. As the immune response subsides towards homeostasis, additional, poorly defined signals are activated. The persistence of resting memory T cells is regulated by cytokines. This chapter explores recent findings on how memory T cells develop to confer long-term protective immunity.

title: The impact of organisational change on outcome in an intensive care unit in the United Kingdom
text:
Objective: To investigate the impact of introducing a team of resident medical staff and switching from an "open" to a "closed" organizational structure on patient outcomes in an intensive care unit (ICU).
Design: Retrospective database review of prospective data collected over a 3-year period.
Setting: ICU of a postgraduate teaching hospital.
Subjects: 1134 ICU admissions, of whom 476 (42%) underwent elective surgery.
Main Outcome Measure: Hospital mortality corrected for illness severity using the APACHE II scoring system.
Results: The crude hospital mortality rate decreased from 28% before the changes to 20% after (P=0.01). When adjusted for case-mix factors, the probability of death after the changes was reduced by almost half (OR 0.51; CI 0.32, 0.82; P=0.005).
Conclusion: The introduction of a team of resident medical staff and a "closed" organizational structure may improve patient outcomes in ICUs.

title: Monitoring effectiveness and safety of Tafamidis in transthyretin amyloidosis in Italy: a longitudinal multicenter study in a non-endemic area
text: Tafamidis is a drug that stabilizes transthyretin (TTR) molecules, preventing them from breaking down intoharmful components. While some studies have shown promising results in treating early-onset inherited transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR) caused by the Val30Met mutation, less is known about its effectiveness in later stages of the disease and with other mutations. To address this gap, we conducted an observational study of symptomatic ATTR patients treated with Tafamidis. We monitored patients for up to 3 years using a standardized protocol that included medical, cardiological, and neurological assessments at baseline and Every 6 months. A total of 61 patients (42 males) were enrolled, with only 28% carrying the common Val30Met mutation. The average age of onset was later than previously expected (59 years), and 18% were in advanced disease stages at the time of entry. Tafamidis was found to be safe and well-tolerated. Surprisingly, one-third of patients did not show significant progression over 36 months, regardless of mutation type or disease stage. Neurological function improved in 10% and remained stable in a further 33%, while it worsened in 56%. Fifteen percent of patients experienced cardiac disease progression, and 30% developed new-onset cardiomyopathy. Interestingly, a higherbaseline body mass index (mBMI) was associated with better preservation of neurological function. The study suggests that while Tafamidis does not halt the progression of neuropathy and cardiomyopathy in a significant proportion of patients, its effectiveness improves over time. Moreover, patients with more advanced neuropathy and those with non-Val30Met mutations may benefit from treatment, and body weight preservation could serve as a favorable prognostic factor.

title: The Spliceosome: Design Principles of a Dynamic RNP Machine
text: Ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) play essential roles in cellular functions such as gene expression and regulation. Unlike most RNP enzymes, which maintain a stable composition with preformed active sites, the spliceosome operates using alternative strategies. The spliceosome, which excises non-coding introns from precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs), demonstrates remarkable compositional and structural flexibility during substrate-dependent complex assembly, catalytic activation, and active site remodeling. This allows for both accurate recognition of reactive splice sites in the pre-mRNA and flexibility in choosing splice sites during alternative splicing.

title: Blimp-1 attenuates Th1 differentiation by repression of ifng, tbx21, and bcl6 gene expression.
text: Deletion of Blimp-1 in T cells leads to abnormal T cell homeostasis and function, resulting in spontaneous, fatal colitis in mice. Here, we investigate the role of Blimp-1 in Th1/Th2 differentiation. Our findings reveal that Blimp-1 is more highly expressed in Th2 cells compared to Th1 cells, and it attenuates interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) production in CD4 cells under non-stimulating conditions. Although Blimp-1-deficient T cells can differentiate normally to Th2 cytokines in vitro, Blimp-1 is essential in vivo for normal Th2 humoral responses to NP-KLH immunization. The absence of Blimp-1 in CD4 T cells leads to increased IFN-γ, T-bet, and Bcl-6 mRNA. Using chromatin immunoprecipitation, we show that Blimp-1 binds directly to the regulatory region of the ifng gene and multiple sites in the tbx21 and bcl6 genes. Our data suggest that Blimp-1 functions in Th2 cells to enhance Th2 differentiation by suppressing critical Th1 genes.

title: CX3CR1 is required for airway inflammation by promoting T helper cell survival and maintenance in inflamed lung
text: Asthma is a T helper type 2 (T(H)2)-dominated disease of the lung that is caused by an immune response to environmental allergens. In people with asthma, a subset of CD4(+) T cells express a specific receptor called CX3CR1, which is increased in airway smooth muscle, lung endothelium, and epithelium after exposure to allergens. Our research found that mice lacking the CX3CR1 receptor or treated with drugs that block it have reduced lung disease after exposure to allergens, and transfer of CD4(+) T cells from wild-type mice into CX3CR1-deficient mice restored the hallmarks of asthma. In addition, injection of B cells into CX3CR1-deficient mice that had been transduced with a gene that triggers T(H)2 cell survival restored asthma. We discovered that CX3CR1 signals promote T(H)2 cell survival in inflamed lungs, and injection of T(H)2 cells from CX3CR1-deficient mice into CX3CR1-deficient recipients restored asthma. This effect was only observed in the context of airway inflammation, but not under homeostatic conditions or after peripheral inflammation. These findings suggest that targeting CX3CR1 and the protein it binds, CX3CL1, may be a promising approach for treating asthma.

title: TRPC6 is a glomerular slit diaphragm-associated channel required for normal renal function
text: Progressive kidney failure, a genetically and clinically diverse group of disorders, involves podocyte foot processes and the interposed glomerular slit diaphragm as crucial components of the kidney's permeability barrier. Mutations in genes encoding podocyte structural proteins can result in proteinuria, leading to progressive kidney failure and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. Here, we found that the TRPC6 ion channel, a component of the glomerular slit diaphragm, is expressed in podocytes and is vital for proper podocyte structure and function. In five families with autosomal dominant focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, we identified disease-causing mutations in the TRPC6 gene on chromosome 11q. Two of these mutants exhibited increased current amplitudes, further highlighting the critical role of TRPC6 channel activity at the glomerular slit diaphragm.

title: Usefulness of high mobility group box 1 protein as a plasma biomarker in patient with peripheral artery disease.
text: Atherosclerosis is frequently linked to chronic vascular inflammation. The high-mobility group box 1 protein (HMGB1) has multiple roles, including as a transcriptional regulator in the nucleus and as an inflammatory mediator. Previous research has suggested that fibrinogen plays a significant role in the progression of atherosclerosis. To investigate the relationship between HMGB1 and atherosclerosis, we conducted a study on 24 patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) and atherosclerosis, and 10 healthy controls. Our findings revealed that the levels of plasma HMGB1 protein were significantly increased in atherosclerosis patients, and there were strong correlations between plasma HMGB1 and fibrinogen levels. These findings suggest that plasma HMGB1 may play a key role in the pathogenesis of both clinical and experimental atherosclerosis.

title: Functional specialization of Piwi proteins in Paramecium tetraurelia from post-transcriptional gene silencing to genome remodelling
text: Proteins from the Argonaute family serve as small RNA carriers, guiding regulatory complexes to their target sites. Within this family, two principal subclades exist: the Ago subclade, present in most eukaryotic lineages, and the Piwi subclade, which appears to have been lost in plant and fungal species and was primarily studied in metazoans. These proteins regulate gene expression at both the transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels by binding diverse small RNAs. While Piwi proteins were previously identified in ciliates, unicellular organisms harboring both germline micronuclei and somatic macronuclei, their functions have evolved distinctly across taxa. Here, we provide phylogenetic and functional analyses of the 15 Piwi genes from Paramecium tetraurelia. Our findings indicate that four constantly expressed proteins are involved in siRNA pathways that mediate gene silencing throughout the life cycle, while two specifically expressed proteins during meiosis are crucial for the accumulation of small RNAs during sexual reproduction and programmed genome rearrangements during the development of the somatic macronucleus. Our study suggests that Paramecium Piwi proteins have adapted to perform both vegetative and sexual functions through various mechanisms, including post-transcriptional mRNA cleavage and epigenetic regulation of genome rearrangements.

title: A parasomnia overlap disorder involving sleepwalking, sleep terrors, and REM sleep behavior disorder in 33 polysomnographically confirmed cases.
text: Over an 8-year period, a series of 33 patients with combined sleepwalking, sleep terrors, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (collectively referred to as "parasomnia overlap disorder") were studied. The average age of the patients was 34 years old, with a range of 1-66 years. Seventy percent of the patients were male, and the onset of parasomnia occurred at an average age of 15 years, with a range of 1-66 years. An idiopathic subgroup had an earlier onset of parasomnia compared to a symptomatic subgroup, whose parasomnia began with various neurological disorders such as congenital Mobius syndrome, narcolepsy, multiple sclerosis, brain tumor and treatment, brain trauma, and indeterminate disorder (exaggerated startle response/atypical cataplexy). The rate of psychiatric disorders according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual, 3rd edition, revised (DSM-III-R) was not elevated, and group scores on various psychometric tests were also not elevated. Forty-five percent of the patients had received psychological or psychiatric therapy without benefit. Treatment outcome was available for 20 patients, and 90% had substantial parasomnia control with bedtime clonazepam (n = 13), alprazolam and/or carbamazepine (n = 4), or self-hypnosis (n = 1). The findings suggest that "parasomnia overlap disorder" is a treatable condition that emerges in various clinical settings and can be comprehended within the context of current knowledge on parasomnias and motor control/dyscontrol during sleep.

title: How can health care organizations be reliably compared?: Lessons from a national survey of patient experience.
text:
ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE MEASURED THROUGH PATIENT EXPERIENCE: A NECESSARY CONSIDERATION
Patient experience is increasingly being used as a means of evaluating organizational performance, particularly in public reporting and pay-for-performance schemes. However, traditional methods that rely on 95% confidence intervals may produce unreliable comparisons between organizations.
TO THE RESCUE: ANALYSIS OF PATIENT SURVEY DATA
We analyzed data from 2.2 million patients who participated in the 2009 General Practice Patient Survey in England, which included 45 questions across six care domains (access, continuity of care, communication, anticipatory care planning, out-of-hours care, and overall care satisfaction). We calculated unadjusted and case-mix-adjusted organization-level reliability and intraclass correlation coefficients for each question.
RANGE OF RESPONSES PER ORGANIZATION:
The mean responses per organization ranged from 23 to 256 for questions assessing primary care practices, and from 1454 to 2758 for questions evaluating out-of-hours care organizations. Adjusted and unadjusted reliability values were similar, with 26 questions exhibiting excellent reliability (≥0.90). Seven nurse communication questions showed very good reliability (≥0.85), but three anticipatory care planning questions had lower reliability (<0.70).
SURPRISINGLY LOW RELIABILITY FOR CERTAIN QUESTIONS:
Reliability was typically less than 0.70 for questions with fewer than 100 mean responses per practice, indicating that these questions were only relevant to a subset of patients. Interestingly, nine questions exhibited both excellent reliability (≥0.90) and high intraclass correlation coefficients (≥0.10), suggesting both reliable measurement and substantial performance variability.
SELECTING MEASURES FOR ORGANIZATIONAL COMPARISONS:
Our findings highlight the importance of assessing reliability when selecting measures for organizational comparisons. By using measures with high reliability, we can create surveys that provide high-quality measurement while minimizing survey costs.
CONCLUSION:
In conclusion, high reliability is essential for organizational comparison measures used in patient experience assessment. By analyzing patient survey data, we can identify measures with reliable measurement and substantial performance variability, which can help create more informative and cost-effective surveys.

title: Conservation of methylation reprogramming in mammalian development: aberrant reprogramming in cloned embryos.
text: Mouse embryos undergo genome-wide demethylation reprogramming during early preimplantation development, followed by remethylation afterwards. We investigated the conservation of this process in multiple mammalian species and wondered if it also occurs in embryos cloned using highly methylated somatic donor nuclei. Our study revealed that normal zygotes from bovine, rat, and pig display a demethylated paternal genome, indicating active demethylation. In bovine embryos, methylation levels were further reduced during cleavage stages up to the eight-cell stage, followed by de novo methylation by the 16-cell stage. In contrast, cloned one-cell embryos showed a reduction in methylation that was consistent with active demethylation, but no further demethylation occurred afterwards. Instead, de novo methylation and nuclear reorganization of methylation patterns resembling those of differentiated cells occurred prematurely in many cloned embryos. Cloned morulae had highly methylated nuclei in all blastomeres that were similar to those of the fibroblast donor cells. Our findings suggest that epigenetic reprogramming occurs abnormally in most cloned embryos, and incomplete reprogramming may contribute to the low efficiency of cloning.

title: Intracellular transport of fat-soluble vitamins A and E.
text:
Vitamins are crucial compounds that promote the optimal growth, reproduction, and function of the human body. Of the 13 known vitamins, vitamins A, D, E, and K are classified as fat-soluble compounds due to their lipophilic nature. Because of their solubility in fat, these vitamins are transported and metabolized by intracellular carrier proteins.
Vitamin A and its derivatives, collectively known as retinoids, are solubilized by intracellular retinoid-binding proteins, including cellular retinol-binding protein (CRBP), cellular retinoic acid-binding protein (CRABP), and cellular retinal-binding protein (CRALBP). These proteins act as "chaperones," regulating the metabolism, signaling, and transport of retinoids. CRALBP-mediated intracellular retinoid transport is essential for vision in humans.
α-Tocopherol, the primary form of vitamin E found in the body, is transported by α-tocopherol transfer protein (α-TTP) in hepatic cells. Defects in α-TTP cause vitamin E deficiency and neurological disorders in humans. Recent research has shown that the interaction between α-TTP and phosphoinositides plays a crucial role in the intracellular transport of α-tocopherol and is associated with familial vitamin E deficiency.
In this review, we will summarize the mechanisms and biological significance of the intracellular transport of vitamins A and E, highlighting the key proteins involved in their transport and metabolism.

title: Reduced Cytokine Release in Ex Vivo Response to Cilengitide and Cetuximab Is a Marker for Improved Survival of Head and Neck Cancer Patients
text:
The text can be rewritten with a more polished and professional tone as follows:
Targeting αVβ3 and αVβ5 integrins with cilengitide may repress the growth of solid tumors, including head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Preclinical investigations suggest that combining cilengitide with other treatment modalities may have enhanced activity. The sole published trial in HNSCC, ADVANTAGE, evaluated the efficacy of cisplatin, 5-fluorouracil, and cetuximab (PFE) without or with once or twice weekly cilengitide (PFE+CIL1W or PFE+CIL2W) in recurrent/metastatic HNSCC. ADVANTAGE showed good tolerability of the cilengitide arms and numerically lower adverse events (AEs) compared to PFE, but no expected benefit in overall survival based on preclinical data. Our FLAVINO assay results revealed that only a subset of HNSCC had an enhanced inhibitory effect of cilengitide-containing combination therapies on colony formation of epithelial cells (CFec) and the release of pro-angiogenic and pro-inflammatory cytokines, while the remaining HNSCC failed to respond. The response to αVβ3 and αVβ5 integrin targeting by cilengitide can classify HNSCC based on their outcome. We present FLAVINO data advocating for further development of cilengitide plus cetuximab in the treatment of a subset of HNSCC potentially identified by the FLAVINO assay using a panel of biomarkers for response evaluation.

title: Genes required for mycobacterial growth defined by high density mutagenesis.
text: For over a century, tuberculosis has been a major infectious killer worldwide, despite extensive research. As the disease continues to manifest drug resistance, identifying genes crucial to the growth of the causative organism, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, offers new targets for developing effective antimycobacterial agents. In this study, we employ transposon site hybridization (TraSH) to comprehensively investigate the genes required for optimal growth of M. tuberculosis. We identify essential pathway genes as well as those of unknown function. Interestingly, the genes crucial for M. tuberculosis growth are conserved in the degenerate genome of the leprosy bacillus, Mycobacterium leprae, suggesting that non-essential functions have been selectively lost since their divergence. Conversely, many of these genes lack identifiable orthologues in other bacteria, indicating that the minimal gene set required for survival varies significantly between organisms with diverse evolutionary histories.

title: Production of de novo cardiomyocytes: human pluripotent stem cell differentiation and direct reprogramming.
text:
Cardiovascular disease is a significant global health concern, ranking as one of the leading causes of death worldwide. The inability of the heart tissue to regenerate naturally has prompted researchers to develop novel methods for creating new heart cells, both in vitro and in vivo. These methodological advancements have the potential to revolutionize the field of cardiovascular medicine, with applications in cell replacement therapy, drug testing, drug discovery, and disease modeling.
Recently, there have been significant breakthroughs in generating cardiomyocytes from three distinct sources: human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs), adult heart-derived cardiac progenitor cells (CPCs), and reprogrammed fibroblasts. These state-of-the-art methods offer exciting possibilities for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases, as well as providing valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms of heart disease.
In this review, we will focus on the most recent advances in generating de novo cardiomyocytes from hPSCs and reprogrammed fibroblasts, highlighting the potential applications and challenges that remain to be addressed. By understanding the complexities of cardiac cell generation, we can unlock the door to new therapeutic strategies and improve patient outcomes in the treatment of cardiovascular disease.

title: Within the hemopoietic system, LAR phosphatase is a T cell lineage-specific adhesion receptor-like protein whose phosphatase activity appears dispensable for T cell development, repertoire selection and function.
text: The expression of the receptor-type tyrosine phosphatase LAR was investigated in different cell types within the murine hemopoietic system. The gene is expressed in all cells of the T cell lineage, but not in cells of any other hemopoietic lineage. The level of expression in T cells is developmentally regulated, with low levels detected in immature (CD4(-)8(-)44(-) and CD4(+)8(+)) thymocytes and high levels found in mature (CD4(+)8(-)/CD4(-)8(+)) thymocytes and T cells. In contrast, uncommitted c-kit(+)B220(+)CD19(-) precursors in the bone marrow express low levels of LAR, while committed B cell lineage precursors (c-kit(+)B220(+)CD19(+)) do not. Interestingly, pre-B cells from PAX-5-deficient mice, which have undergone commitment to the B cell lineage, express LAR, suggesting that PAX-5-mediated commitment suppresses LAR expression. During differentiation of PAX-5-deficient pre-B cells into non-T cell lineages, expression of LAR is turned off. However, it is up-regulated during differentiation into thymocytes. These findings suggest that LAR is a T cell lineage-specific receptor-type phosphatase within the hemopoietic system. Nevertheless, surprisingly, truncation of the phosphatase domains has no obvious effect on T cell development, repertoire selection, or function.

title: Competition and the evolution of reproductive restraint in malaria parasites.
text: All living things must balance the allocation of resources between different vital processes that determine their survival and reproduction. Malaria parasites reproduce asexually inside the host but must produce sexual stages to transmit between hosts. Because different specialized stages are required for these functions, natural selection must find a solution to the problem of allocating resources between these life-history components. Despite their medical and economic significance, the reproductive strategies of these parasites are not well understood and often seem counterintuitive. Here, we tested recent theories suggesting that in-host competition shapes how parasites allocate resources between in-host replication and between-host transmission. We found, across several genotypes, that Plasmodium chabaudi parasites can detect the presence of competing genotypes and adjust their investment in sexual stages in a way predicted to maximize their competitive ability. Additionally, we found that genotypes adjust their allocation to sexual stages based on the availability of exploitable red blood cell resources. Our findings are consistent with evolutionary theory developed to explain life-history trade-offs in more traditionally studied multicellular organisms and suggest that the reason why few transmission stages are produced in natural infections is that heavy investment in reproduction may compromise in-host survival.

title: [Neutrophils and macrophages related to the pathogenesis and disease development of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease by the inflammatory reaction].
text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a chronic respiratory disorder characterized by limitations in airflow due to the narrowing of the airways, which cannot be completely reversed by treatment. It is thought that inflammation in the smaller airways (those with diameters less than 2mm), known as small airway disease, may be an early stage of COPD. Therefore, it is clear that neutrophils and macrophages play a crucial role in the development of these lesions. Bronchoalveolar lavage studies have shown an increase in neutrophil numbers and the neutrophil chemoattractant interleukin-8. More recent studies have demonstrated that neutrophils and macrophages are abundant in these lesions and contain a variety of proteolytic enzymes involved in cell infiltration and activation. Investigations using gene-engineered animals and anti-cytokine treatments will help deepen our understanding of the role of neutrophils and macrophages in COPD and pave the way for novel therapeutic strategies.

title: Piezo1 Is as a Novel Trefoil Factor Family 1 Binding Protein that Promotes Gastric Cancer Cell Mobility In Vitro
text: The Trefoil factor family 1 (TFF1) member plays a crucial part in epithelial restoration and cell movement. In the current investigation, we screened for Piezo1 as a potential TFF1 binding protein. Our findings confirm Piezo1 as a new TFF1 binding partner and examine the efficacy of this interaction in gastric cancer cell motility. Co-immunoprecipitation and localization of TFF1 and Piezo1 in GES-1 cells affirm their connection. To assess the effect of this interaction on gastric cancer cell mobility, we utilized stable RNA interference to diminish Piezo1 protein expression and re-established TFF1 in two gastric cancer cell lines, SGC-7901 and BGC-823. Cell motility was evaluated utilizing invasion and migration assays in vitro. The expression levels of integrin subunits β1, β5, α1, along with β-catenin and E-cadherin, were detected by Western blot analysis. Our results demonstrate that TFF1 exclusively binds to and co-localizes with Piezo1 in the cytoplasm in vitro. TFF1 interacts with the C-terminal region of Piezo1. Wound healing and trans-well assays showed that restoring TFF1 expression enhanced cell mobility in gastric cancer cells and this effect was attenuated by Piezo1 knockdown. Western blots revealed decreased integrin β1 expression in Piezo1-knockdown cells. Our findings indicate that Piezo1 is a novel TFF1 binding protein that plays an essential role in TFF1-mediated cell migration. In addition, our results suggest that targeting this interaction may be a viable therapeutic approach to prevent the invasion and metastasis of gastric cancer.

title: A conditionally lethal yeast mutant blocked at the first step in glycosyl phosphatidylinositol anchor synthesis.
text: Glycosyl phosphatidylinositols (GPIs) are attached to the surface of eukaryotic cells, serving as anchors for various proteins and participating in signal transduction. In order to isolate a Saccharomyces cerevisiae GPI anchoring mutant, we employed a colony screen for cells with reduced [3H]inositol incorporation into proteins. The gpi1 mutant was found to be defective in the synthesis of N-acetylglucosaminyl phosphatidylinositol, the first intermediate in GPI production, and is also temperature-sensitive for growth. It appears that the completion of the first step in GPI assembly is necessary for the growth of S. cerevisiae, a eukaryotic organism. Given the importance of GPI synthesis, targeting this process could lead to the development of novel antifungal or antiparasitic agents.

title: Beyond pattern recognition: five immune checkpoints for scaling the microbial threat
text:
The innate immune system is capable of recognizing microorganisms and assessing the level of threat they pose. However, the mechanisms by which the immune system evaluates the severity of microbial infections are not fully understood. Recent research has revealed that the immune system can detect the viability of microorganisms and respond accordingly, with responses being more robust for living microorganisms than for dead ones. In this article, we propose five immune checkpoints that collectively determine the severity of microbial encounters. These checkpoints include:
1. Assessment of microbial viability: The immune system can detect the presence of living microorganisms and respond accordingly.
2. Detection of microbial Load: The amount of microorganisms present in the body can also influence the severity of the immune response.
3. Microbial virulence: The degree of virulence of a microorganism can impact the severity of the immune response.
4. Host-microbe interactions: The interaction between the immune system and a microorganism can also influence the severity of the immune response.
5. Spatiotemporal distribution of microorganisms: The distribution of microorganisms in the body and the duration of their presence can also impact the severity of the immune response.
In conclusion, the immune system utilizes a complex network of checkpoints to evaluate the level of microbial threat and respond accordingly. Understanding these checkpoints can provide valuable insights into the mechanisms of immune response and inform strategies for modulating the immune system to mitigate disease.

title: Macrophages induce COX-2 expression in breast cancer cells: role of IL-1β autoamplification.
text: This study aimed to investigate the interdependence between tumor-associated macrophages and high levels of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) in breast cancer patients, and whether macrophages can regulate COX-2 expression in breast cancer cells. The study found that coculturing THP-1 cells (a type of immune cell) with breast cancer cells (HCC1954) led to increased COX-2 expression and elevated levels of prostaglandin E(2) in the conditioned media. Similar results were observed when other types of immune cells (THP-1 cells or human monocyte-derived macrophages) were cocultured with HCC1954 cells. The study also found that coculture triggered the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in HCC1954 cells, which in turn induced COX-2 expression through the activation of Src and mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs). The study also showed that macrophage-induced COX-2 expression was blocked when the IL-1β receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra) or anti-IL-1β IgG was used to neutralize the effects of IL-1β, suggesting that the mechanism of COX-2 induction is mediated by autocrine and paracrine effects. Overall, the study suggests that macrophage-mediated induction of COX-2 in breast cancer cells is a result of IL-1β-mediated stimulation of ROS→Src→MAPK→AP-1 signaling, providing a mechanism by which macrophages contribute to tumor progression and potentially identifying therapeutic targets in breast cancer.

title: A graphene-based platform for induced pluripotent stem cells culture and differentiation.
text: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) hold great promise as a cell source for regenerative medicine, yet their culture, maintenance of pluripotency, and induction of differentiation remain challenging. On the other hand, graphene (G) and graphene oxide (GO) have garnered significant interest in various fields of science and technology due to their unique properties. In this study, we investigate the potential of G and GO to support the culture and differentiation of mouse iPSCs. Our findings are fascinating - G and GO surfaces exhibit distinct properties that influence the proliferation and differentiation of iPSCs. Specifically, iPSCs cultured on G surfaces exhibited similar adhesion and proliferation rates as those on a glass surface, while iPSCs on GO surfaces proliferated at a faster rate. Moreover, G maintained iPSCs in an undifferentiated state, while GO expedited differentiation. Remarkably, iPSCs cultured on both G and GO surfaces spontaneously differentiated into ectodermal and mesodermal lineages without significant disparity, but G suppressed differentiation towards the endodermal lineage, while GO augmented endodermal differentiation. These findings suggest that the unique surface properties of G and GO have a profound impact on iPSC behavior, and imply the potential of graphene-based materials as a platform for iPSCs culture and diverse applications.

title: Aerobic capacity in black adolescent girls.
text: To determine the aerobic capacities (VO2max) of a group of urban black female adolescents (ages 11.4-15.8 years), we randomly selected 91 girls from a single school. Among these, 64 girls completed an incremental treadmill running test to volitional exhaustion and had their VO2max measured through expired gas measures. Additional measures included height (m), weight (kg), and skinfold measurements (for body fat percentage estimates). We also asked the girls if they had reached menarche. Our results showed that VO2max averaged 37.3 +/- 6.2 ml.kg-1 x min-1 and was significantly related to height (-.32, p < .01), body mass index (-.63, p < .001), and body fat percentage (-.65, p < .001), but not to age (-.16, p > .10). Compared to non-black U.S. female adolescents reported in the literature, our subjects' VO2max values were 14% lower on average. This difference was primarily attributable to body weight. Our findings suggest that overweight in adult black women may begin during early adolescence, and highlight the importance of aerobic fitness in reducing cardiovascular risk factors in black adolescent girls. Future longitudinal studies should investigate the effects of fitness on health outcomes in this population.

title: Acetylation controls Notch3 stability and function in T-cell leukemia
text: Enhanced knowledge of post-translational changes in Notch3 and their functional implications for T-cell leukemia is still limited. We uncovered a novel feature of Notch3: its acetylation and deacetylation at lysines 1692 and 1731 by p300 and HDAC1, respectively. This balance is impaired by HDAC inhibitors (HDACi), leading to enhanced acetylation. Using HDACi and a non-acetylatable Notch3 mutant with mutations in the intracellular domain, we demonstrate that Notch3 acetylation triggers ubiquitination and degradation of the protein. As a result, Notch3 protein expression and transcriptional activity decline both in vitro and in vivo in Notch3 transgenic mice, thus attenuating signaling downstream of target genes. Consistently, Notch3-induced T-cell proliferation is inhibited by HDACi, while it is enhanced by the non-acetylatable Notch3 mutant. Importantly, HDACi-induced Notch3 hyperacetylation abolishes in vivo growth of T-cell leukemia/lymphoma in Notch3 transgenic mice. Our findings suggest a novel level of Notch signaling regulation, where the Notch3 acetylation/deacetylation process serves as a critical regulatory switch. Therefore, targeting this process represents a potential druggable target for Notch3-driven T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia therapy.

title: Hypoglycemia: incidence and clinical predictors in a large population-based sample of children and adolescents with IDDM.
text:
Objective:
To determine the frequency of mild and severe hypoglycemia and identify clinical predictors associated with its occurrence in a large population-based sample of children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).
Research Design and Methods:
A total of 657 patients (age: 12.1 ± 4.4 years, mean ± SD) were included in the study, resulting in 1,449 patient-years of data. A prospective assessment of severe hypoglycemia (an event resulting in a seizure or coma) and moderate hypoglycemia (an event requiring assistance from another person, excluding severe episodes) was conducted over a 3-year period. Patients and caregivers documented episodes of significant hypoglycemia (moderate and severe events) and these were recorded at each 3-month clinic visit along with HbA1c. Data were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models fitted with the exchange correlation structure.
Results:
The overall incidence of severe events was 4.8/100 patient-years and of moderate events was 13.1/100 patient-years. Over 3 years, severe events occurred in 8.5% of children and moderate events occurred in 26.9%. Significant hypoglycemia was rare in the first 12 months after diagnosis. Rates of hypoglycemia were increased in children < 6 years of age versus > 6 years of age (40.9 vs. 16.6/100 patient-years, age < or = 6 years vs. age > 6 years, P < 0.001). Rates of hypoglycemia doubled when HbA1c fell below 8%, and children with HbA1c < 7% had a threefold increase in both moderate and severe hypoglycemia (e.g., severe episodes 14.9 vs. 4.1/100 patient-years, HbA1c < or = 7% vs. HbA1c > 7%, P < 0.001). Most severe events were seizures, and 75% of them occurred at night. The majority of events were related to missed meals or increased activity. However, in 38% of cases, no predisposing factor was evident.

title: Efficacy of a 6-month versus 9-month intermittent treatment regimen in HIV-infected patients with tuberculosis: a randomized clinical trial.
text:
The outcome of intermittent, thrice-weekly antituberculosis treatment of varying durations in HIV-associated tuberculosis is uncertain. This study aimed to compare the efficacy of a 6-month regimen (Reg6M) with a 9-month regimen (Reg9M) in HIV/TB patients.
HIV-infected patients with newly diagnosed pulmonary or extrapulmonary TB were randomly assigned to Reg6M (n=167) or Reg9M (n=160) and followed for 36 months. The primary outcomes were favorable responses at the end of treatment and recurrences during follow-up, with secondary outcome being death. Intention-to-treat and on-treatment analyses were performed, and all patients were antiretroviral treatment-naive during treatment.
Results showed that 70% of patients had culture-positive pulmonary TB, with a median viral load of 155,000 copies/ml and median CD4 cell count of 160 cells/mm3. By intent-to-treat analysis, favorable responses were similar between the two groups (Reg6M: 83%, Reg9M: 76%; P=NS). However, bacteriological recurrences occurred significantly less often in Reg9M than in Reg6M (15 vs. 7%; P<0.05), but overall recurrences were not significantly different (Reg6M: 19%, Reg9M: 13%). By 36 months, 36% of patients undergoing Reg6M and 35% undergoing Reg9M had died, with no significant difference between regimens. All 19 patients who failed treatment developed acquired rifamycin resistance (ARR), with baseline isoniazid resistance being the main risk factor.
In conclusion, among antiretroviral treatment-naive HIV-infected patients with TB, a 9-month regimen resulted in a similar outcome at the end of treatment but a significantly lower bacteriological recurrence rate compared to a 6-month thrice-weekly regimen. ARR was high with these intermittent regimens, and neither mortality nor ARR was altered by lengthening TB treatment.
Clinical Trials Registry Information: NCT00376012 registered at clinicaltrials.gov.

title: High prevalence of evolutionarily conserved and species-specific genomic aberrations in mouse pluripotent stem cells.
text: Pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) are the most studied pluripotent system and serve as the gold standard for comparison to human PSCs. However, while the genomic integrity of human PSCs has been a recent area of attention, the genomic stability of mouse PSCs has not been systematically evaluated. This is of significant importance, as genomic instability can impact the pluripotency, differentiation, and tumorigenicity of PSCs. To address this gap in knowledge, we performed a comprehensive analysis of the genomic integrity of 325 mouse PSC samples, including 127 induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) samples. Our findings revealed frequent genomic aberrations in mouse embryonic stem cells from various mouse strains, as well as in iPSCs from different cell origins and derivation techniques. Specifically, we identified four hotspots of chromosomal aberrations: full trisomy 11, full trisomy 8, and deletions in chromosomes 10qB and 14qC-14qE. Notably, the most recurrent aberration in mouse PSCs, gain 11qE2, was found to be fully syntenic to the common aberration 17q25 in human PSCs, while other recurrent aberrations were identified as being species-specific. In contrast, analysis of chromosomal aberrations in 74 rhesus macaque PSC samples revealed a gain in chromosome 16q, which is syntenic to the hotspot in human 17q. These findings highlight the need to carefully monitor the genomic integrity of PSCs from all species to ensure proper use in biomedical research.

title: Inhibition of cell proliferation and induction of apoptosis by ExFABP gene targeting.
text:
Here is a possible revision of the given text:
Ex-FABP, an extracellular fatty acid binding lipocalin, is expressed by differentiating chicken chondrocytes and myoblasts. Its expression is increased upon exposure to inflammatory stimuli and decreased by anti-inflammatory agents, consistent with its role as an acute phase protein. In vitro studies using chicken liver fragments show enhanced protein expression after treatment with bacterial endotoxin. To investigate the biological function of Ex-FABP, we stably transfected proliferating chondrocytes with a expression vector carrying antisense-oriented Ex-FABP cDNA. We observed a significant decline in cell viability and inhibition of cell proliferation and differentiation. The down-modulation of Ex-FABP led to an increase in apoptotic cell number. Similarly, myoblasts transfected with the same expression vector exhibited extensive cell death and impaired myotube formation. These findings suggest that Ex-FABP serves as a constitutive survival protein, and its expression and activity are essential to protect chondrocytes from cell death.

title: Profile of the Navrongo Health and Demographic Surveillance System.
text:
Based in the Kassena-Nankana districts of northern Ghana, the Navrongo Health and Demographic Surveillance System (NHDSS) was established in 1992 by the Navrongo Health Research Centre (NHRC). As one of three research centres under the Ghana Health Service, the NHRC leads the way in conducting collaborative research through the NHDSS. This system monitors the health and demographic dynamics of the two Kassena-Nankana districts, providing valuable insights into the morbidity and mortality impact of health and social interventions.
Currently, the NHDSS is responsible for monitoring the health and well-being of 152,000 individuals residing in over 32,000 households. This includes routine tracking of events such as pregnancies, births, illnesses, deaths, migration, marriages, and vaccination coverage. Fieldworkers collect data every 4 months, ensuring that the information remains up-to-date and accurate.
In addition to its core surveillance activities, the NHRC also conducts biomedical and socio-economic studies to further understand the health needs of the community. The NHDSS has a unique community key informant system, where trained volunteers provide real-time information on births, deaths, and other significant events occurring within their local area. This is complemented by the Verbal Autopsy (VA) system, which helps determine the probable causes of deaths that occur at the community level.
The NHDSS shares its data with funders, collaborators, and partners within the INDEPTH Network, and the Director of the NHDSS serves as the primary contact for potential collaboration and data use. By leveraging the wealth of data and research capabilities of the NHDSS, the Navrongo Health Research Centre is positioned to drive innovative health research and improvements in healthcare delivery throughout Ghana.

title: The impact of COPD on lung health worldwide: epidemiology and incidence.
text:
Data on the prevalence of COPD was obtained from various sources, including vital statistics, health interview surveys, hospital charge records, national publications, and the World Health Organization (WHO). These data suggest that COPD is a widespread disease with significant implications for global health. In the United States, COPD is the fourth leading cause of death, with approximately 4% of the population suffering from the disease. This is followed by heart attacks, cancer, and stroke. Internationally, there are significant variations in death rates, which may be due to factors such as smoking habits, tobacco type and processing, air pollution, climate, respiratory management, and genetic factors.
The Global Obstructive Lung Disease Initiative, launched by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute and the WHO, aims to raise awareness of the growing burden of COPD, reduce morbidity and mortality, promote further research into the disease, and implement prevention programs.

title: TLR activation triggers the rapid differentiation of monocytes into macrophages and dendritic cells
text: Investigating leprosy can provide insights into how the innate immune system contributes to defending against infection, as the disease can progress or remain limited. We discovered that activating Toll-like receptors (TLRs) on human monocytes leads to the rapid differentiation of these cells into two distinct subsets: DC-SIGN+ CD16+ macrophages and CD1b+ DC-SIGN− dendritic cells. DC-SIGN+ macrophages were found to be expanded in lesions and after TLR activation in all leprosy patients, while CD1b+ dendritic cells were not detected in lesions or after TLR activation of peripheral monocytes in individuals with the progressive lepromatous form, except during reversal reactions in which bacilli were cleared by TH1 responses. In tuberculoid lepromatous lesions, DC-SIGN+ cells were positive for macrophage markers but negative for dendritic cell markers. These findings suggest that the TLR-induced differentiation of monocytes influences the effectiveness of host defenses in human infectious diseases.

title: Mismatch repair status and clinical outcome in endometrial cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text:
BACKGROUND: The connection between the deficiency in mismatch repair (MMR) genes and prognosis in women with endometrial cancer is not well understood. To address this, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating the association between MMR status and clinical outcomes in endometrial cancer.
METHODS: We searched major literature databases (MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane) from 1980 to December 2011 to identify studies assessing the association between MMR status and clinical outcomes in endometrial cancer. The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS).
RESULTS: Twenty-three studies met our inclusion criteria. The majority of studies (74%) were retrospective case-series, and 70% used microsatellite instability (MSI) analysis to determine MMR status. However, only 22% of studies used the recommended panel of five microsatellite markers by the National Cancer Institute. Just seven studies used immunohistochemistry to evaluate MMR deficiency, with only two determining the expression of all four MMR proteins. Significant associations between MMR and outcome were observed in 32% of studies, but there was tremendous inter-study heterogeneity in estimates of OS and DFS. Pooled analysis did not reveal a significant association between MMR deficiency and worse OS (6 studies, hazard ratio [HR] 2.0, p=0.11) or DFS (4 studies, HR ratio 1.31, p=0.66).
CONCLUSION: Our findings provide no conclusive evidence of a substantial association between MMR status and detrimental survival in endometrial cancer.

title: p53 induces formation of NEAT1 lncRNA-containing paraspeckles that modulate replication stress response and chemosensitivity
text: In an effort to identify mediators of the p53 tumor suppressor pathway, which triggers diverse and often opposing cellular responses, we focused on long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) NEAT1. NEAT1 is an essential component of paraspeckle nuclear bodies, whose pathological significance remains unclear. Activation of p53, either pharmacologically or through oncogene-induced replication stress, led to the formation of paraspeckles in mouse and human cells. Silencing NEAT1 expression in mice, which prevents paraspeckle formation, enhanced sensitivity of preneoplastic cells to DNA damage-induced cell death and impaired skin tumorigenesis. Our findings provide mechanistic evidence that NEAT1 promotes ATR signaling in response to replication stress, forming a negative feedback loop that reduces oncogene-dependent p53 activation. NEAT1 targeting in established human cancer cell lines led to synthetic lethality with genotoxic chemotherapeutics, including PARP inhibitors, and nongenotoxic activation of p53. This study establishes a crucial genetic connection between NEAT1 paraspeckles, p53 biology, and tumorigenesis, making NEAT1 a promising therapeutic target to enhance cancer cell sensitivity to both chemotherapy and p53 reactivation therapy.

title: Regulation of innate immunity by NADPH oxidase.
text: NADPH oxidase plays a crucial role in both host defense and inflammation. In response to microbial threats, this enzyme is activated in phagocytes and generates reactive oxidant intermediates (ROIs), which are essential for effective antimicrobial defense. However, chronic granulomatous disease (CGD), an inherited disorder of NADPH oxidase, leads to impaired host defense and excessive inflammation, resulting in recurrent and severe bacterial and fungal infections, as well as related pathology. Research on CGD patients and mouse models has shown that NADPH oxidase not only plays a key role in modulating inflammation and injury, but also has distinct mechanisms of antimicrobial function compared to its role in inflammation regulation. Understanding the mechanisms of NADPH oxidase in both normal immune responses and disease states, such as acute lung injury and bacterial or fungal infections, has significant implications for the development of new therapeutic strategies.

title: Protection from olanzapine-induced metabolic toxicity in mice by acetaminophen and tetrahydroindenoindole
text: Objective: To investigate the potential of two compounds, acetaminophen (APAP) and tetrahydroindenoindole (THII), in preventing metabolic changes in mice treated with the antipsychotic drug olanzapine (OLZ). Methods: C57BL/6J mice were administered either a normal diet or a high-fat (HF) diet and received daily doses of OLZ (3 mg/kg body weight), alone or with APAP (30 mg/kg body weight) or THII (4.5 mg/kg body weight) for 10 weeks. Body composition and metabolic parameters, including glucose and insulin homeostasis and oxidative stress, were evaluated. Results: OLZ treatment significantly increased body weight and body fat in mice fed a HF diet, which were partially prevented by both APAP and THII. The THII protection was associated with an increase in whole body and mitochondrial respiration. OLZ also exacerbated HF diet-induced loss of glucose tolerance and insulin resistance, but both APAP and THII prevented these metabolic changes. Additionally, HF diet-induced lipid peroxidation and oxidative stress in white adipose tissue (WAT) were significantly exacerbated by OLZ, but were abolished by APAP, THII, and the NADPH oxidase inhibitor, diphenyleneiodonium chloride. Conclusion: Our findings suggest that both APAP and THII may have potential in preventing the development of obesity and metabolic complications associated with OLZ treatment.

title: Detection of prions in blood
text: Prion diseases are caused by an unconventional infectious agent known as a prion, primarily composed of misfolded prion protein (PrPSc). Identifying and quantifying this protein in blood samples is crucial for preventing the spread of prion diseases. We developed an optimized and automated protein misfolding cyclic amplification (PMCA) technology to detect PrPSc in blood samples. Our results show that 140 PMCA cycles led to a 6,600-fold increase in sensitivity compared to standard detection methods, and two consecutive rounds of PMCA cycles resulted in an impressive 10 million-fold increase in sensitivity, allowing the detection of as little as 8,000 equivalent molecules of PrPSc. Moreover, serial PMCA proved to be highly effective in detecting PrPSc in blood samples from scrapie-afflicted hamsters, with an impressive 89% sensitivity and 100% specificity. These findings represent a significant breakthrough in detecting PrPSc in blood samples, opening up new possibilities for developing a non-invasive diagnostic test for early detection of prion diseases.

title: Genetic alterations and their relationship in the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/Akt pathway in thyroid cancer.
text:
Investigating the Prevalence and Relationship of Genetic Alterations in the PI3K/Akt Pathway in Thyroid Tumors
Objective: To investigate the occurrence and interconnection of genetic alterations in the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt pathway in thyroid tumors and to explore the potential of targeting this pathway for thyroid cancer treatment.
Methodology: We examined the frequency and correlation of major genetic alterations, including PIK3CA copy number gain and mutation, Ras mutation, and PTEN mutation, in a large series of primary thyroid tumors.
Results: Genetic alterations were found in 31% of benign thyroid adenomas (BTAs), 55% of follicular thyroid cancers (FTCs), 24% of papillary thyroid cancers (PTCs), and 58% of anaplastic thyroid cancers (ATCs), with FTC and ATC showing the highest frequency. PIK3CA copy gain was associated with increased PIK3CA protein expression. There was a mutual exclusivity among these genetic alterations in BTAs, FTCs, and PTCs, suggesting an independent role of each alteration in the tumorigenesis of these differentiated thyroid tumors. However, co-occurrence of these genetic alterations was more common in the progression from differentiated tumors to undifferentiated ATC. Their co-occurrence with BRAF mutation was also frequent in PTCs and ATCs.
Conclusion: The data strongly suggest that aberrant activation of the PI3K/Akt pathway plays a significant role in thyroid tumorigenesis, particularly in FTCs and ATCs. The accumulation of genetic alterations in this pathway may facilitate the progression of BTAs to FTCs and to ATCs. The PI3K/Akt pathway may therefore be an attractive therapeutic target in thyroid cancers.

title: Vitamin D and obesity: current perspectives and future directions.
text: In recent years, new roles of vitamin D have emerged beyond its traditional function in calcium homeostasis and bone metabolism. Vitamin D deficiency (25-hydroxyvitamin D < 25-30 nmol/l) and suboptimal status (25-OHD < 50-100 nmol/l) are linked to unfavourable metabolic phenotypes, including insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease (CVD), which are also common in overweight and obese individuals. Early studies found low vitamin D levels in morbidly obese individuals, and more recent studies have observed a graded relationship between vitamin D status and body mass index (BMI) or adiposity in the general population. Several mechanisms have been proposed to explain the relationship between vitamin D and adiposity, including sequestration in adipose tissue, volumetric dilution, or negative feedback mechanisms from increased circulating 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3. Some studies have also suggested that overweight individuals may have lower vitamin D levels due to reduced sun exposure and decreased endogenous production of cholecalciferol in the skin. However, the relationship between body size and vitamin D requirements is not yet fully understood, and this review will evaluate the current evidence and discuss the implications for setting dietary requirements.

title: Transcriptional regulation by p53 through intrinsic DNA/chromatin binding and site-directed cofactor recruitment.
text: The tumor suppressor protein p53 plays a crucial role in cellular responses to stress signals by regulating genes involved in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. p53 is inactive in DNA binding unless its C-terminus is modified or structurally altered. Our findings show that unmodified p53 actively binds to two sites at -1.4 and -2.3 kb within the chromatin-assembled p21 promoter and requires the C-terminus and the histone acetyltransferase p300 for transcription. Acetylation of the C-terminus by p300 is not necessary for binding or promoter activation, instead p300 acetylates p53-bound nucleosomes in the p21 promoter with spreading to the TATA box. Therefore, p53 is an active DNA and chromatin binding protein that selectively regulates its target genes by recruiting specific cofactors to structurally distinct binding sites.

title: Pleiotropic effects of statins.
text: Statins are powerful inhibitors of cholesterol synthesis. Clinical trials have shown that statins are beneficial in both primary and secondary prevention of coronary heart disease. However, the observed benefits of statins appear to be greater than what would be expected based solely on changes in lipid levels, suggesting effects beyond cholesterol reduction. Recent studies suggest that some of these effects may be due to improvements in endothelial function, stabilization of atherosclerotic plaques, reduction of oxidative stress and inflammation, and inhibition of the thrombogenic response. Additionally, statins have been found to have beneficial effects on the immune system, central nervous system, and bone, among other extrahepatic sites. Many of these pleiotropic effects are thought to be mediated by inhibition of isoprenoids, which play a crucial role in intracellular signaling via lipid attachment. In particular, inhibition of small GTP-binding proteins, such as Rho, Ras, and Rac, whose proper membrane localization and function are dependent on isoprenylation, may play a key role in mediating the pleiotropic effects of statins.

title: Increasing the efficiency of precise genome editing with CRISPR-Cas9 by inhibition of nonhomologous end joining
text: Techniques to introduce targeted double-strand breaks (DSBs) into DNA facilitate precise genome editing by enhancing the incorporation of exogenous DNA sequences into the genome through homologous recombination. However, the efficiency of these methods is limited by nonhomologous end joining (NHEJ), another DNA repair pathway that competes with homology-directed repair (HDR). To favor HDR at the expense of NHEJ, we aimed to target DNA ligase IV, a key enzyme in the NHEJ pathway, using the inhibitor Scr7. Treatment with Scr7 increased the efficiency of HDR-mediated genome editing, using the Cas9 enzyme in mammalian cell lines and in mice for the four genes examined, up to 19-fold. This approach is likely to be applicable to other customizable endonucleases, such as zinc finger nucleases and transcription activator–like effector nucleases, as well as to nonmammalian cells with comparable NHEJ and HDR mechanisms.

title: Molecular mechanism of BST2/tetherin downregulation by K5/MIR2 of Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus.
text: Membrane-associated RING-CH (MARCH) ubiquitin ligase K3/MIR1 and K5/MIR2 of Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) direct the conjugation of ubiquitin to immunostimulatory transmembrane proteins, evading immune detection. In a proteomics screen, we found that K5 and HIV-1 immunomodulator VPU lowered the amount of bone marrow stromal cell antigen 2 (BST2; also called CD317 or tetherin), suggesting BST2 may be a novel substrate of K5 and VPU. Recent work revealed that when VPU is absent, HIV-1 virions bind to the plasma membrane in BST2-expressing HeLa cells. By targeting BST2, K5 may similarly evade an innate antiviral host defense mechanism. We show that despite its type II transmembrane topology and carboxy-terminal GPI anchor, BST2 is a bona fide target of K5 that is downregulated during primary KSHV infection and reactivation. K5 ubiquitinates lysines in the short amino-terminal domain of BST2, leading to rapid degradation. Ubiquitination is required, as BST2 lacking cytosolic lysines was K5-resistant, and ubiquitin depletion restored BST2 surface expression. BST2 is the first type II transmembrane protein targeted by K5 and the first protein to be both ubiquitinated and GPI linked. We also find that KSHV release is reduced in the absence of K5 in a BST2-dependent manner, indicating that K5 contributes to evading intracellular antiviral defense programs.

title: Regulation of beta catenin signaling and parathyroid hormone anabolic effects in bone by the matricellular protein periostin.
text: Periostin (Postn) is a protein expressed primarily by osteocytes and periosteal osteoblasts in response to mechanical stimulation and parathyroid hormone (PTH). What role this protein plays in bone anabolism, however, remains unexplored. We investigated the effects of intermittent PTH on adult mice lacking Periostin (Postn(-/-) and Postn(+/+) mice. Compared to Postn(+/+), Postn(-/-) mice had lower bone mass, cortical bone volume, and strength in response to PTH. PTH-stimulated bone-forming indices were significantly lower in Postn(-/-) mice, particularly at the periosteum. Additionally, in vivo stimulation of Wnt-β-catenin signaling by PTH was inhibited in the absence of periostin, as evaluated in TOPGAL reporter mice. PTH increased expression of periostin and inhibited MEF2C and sclerostin (Sost) expression in bone and osteoblasts in vitro. Recombinant periostin suppressed Sost expression, which was mediated through the integrin αVβ3 receptor, while periostin-blocking antibody prevented inhibition of MEF2C and Sost by PTH. Administration of a Sost-blocking antibody partially restored the PTH-mediated increase in bone mass in Postn(-/-) mice. Moreover, primary osteoblasts from Postn(-/-) mice showed lower proliferation, mineralization, and migration in both basal conditions and in response to PTH. Osteoblast gene expression levels revealed a defect in Postn(-/-) osteoblast differentiation and increased apoptosis in the absence of periostin. These findings elucidate the complex role of periostin in bone anabolism through the regulation of Sost, Wnt-β-catenin signaling, and osteoblast differentiation.

title: Lipoprotein(a) concentration and the risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and nonvascular mortality.
text: This study examined the relationship between circulating levels of lipoprotein(a) (Lp[a]) and the risk of various vascular and nonvascular outcomes. The study included over 126,000 participants from 36 prospective studies, with a mean follow-up time of over 1.3 million person-years. The study found that Lp[a] concentration was weakly correlated with several conventional vascular risk factors and was highly consistent within individuals over time. The study also found that higher Lp[a] levels were associated with an increased risk of coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke, with the risk increasing continuously across different Lp[a] levels. The adjusted risk ratio for CHD was 1.16 (95% CI, 1.11-1.22) per 3.5-fold higher usual Lp[a] concentration, and 1.13 (95% CI, 1.09-1.18) following further adjustment for lipids and other conventional risk factors. Similarly, the risk ratio for ischemic stroke was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.98-1.05), while the risk ratios for nonvascular mortality, cancer deaths, and nonvascular deaths other than cancer were 1.00 (95% CI, 0.97-1.04), 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06), and 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06), respectively. These findings suggest that Lp[a] concentration is associated with a modest increased risk of CHD and stroke, which appears to be exclusive to vascular outcomes.

title: The biphasic behavior of incoherent feed-forward loops in biomolecular regulatory networks.
text: An incoherent feed-forward loop (FFL) is a common motif observed in biomolecular regulatory networks. It was thought to be responsible for inducing a transient response with a 'fast activation and delayed inhibition'. However, we have found that the dynamics of incoherent FFLs can be classified into two types: time-dependent biphasic responses and dose-dependent biphasic responses. We wondered why structurally identical incoherent FFLs exhibit different dynamical roles. Through computational studies, we discovered that the dynamics of the two types of incoherent FFLs are mutually exclusive. Furthermore, our computational results and experimental observations suggest that incoherent FFLs have been optimally designed to achieve distinct biological functions arising from different cellular contexts. Additional supporting information can be found in the online version of the article.

title: Antipsychotic prescribing patterns in Germany: a retrospective analysis using a large outpatient prescription database.
text:
The following is a revised version of the given text:
Data on prescribing practices for antipsychotics are crucial in evaluating the quality of care. Therefore, we examined all prescriptions under the statutory health insurance claims redeemed at pharmacies in Southern Germany between July 1999 and December 2001. This database covers prescriptions for approximately 25 million people. Approximately 6% of the population were prescribed an antipsychotic at least once during the study period.
