Together, these findings demonstrate that both myristoylation and phosphorylation of the beta subunit of AMPK regulate enzyme activity and subunit cellular localization, adding to the complexity of AMPK regulation.

title: Caloric restriction delays age-related methylation drift
text: In mammals, caloric restriction consistently leads to a lengthened lifespan. Epigenetic information encoded by DNA methylation is tightly regulated, but exhibits a notable drift with age, where both gains and losses of DNA methylation occur at various sites. In this study, we investigate whether this epigenetic drift is conserved across different species and find that the rate of drift correlates with lifespan when comparing mice, rhesus monkeys, and humans. Interestingly, young rhesus monkeys exposed to caloric restriction from a mere 7-14 years of age showed attenuation of the age-related methylation drift, resulting in their blood methylation age appearing 7 years younger than their chronological age. Even more pronounced effects were observed in young mice exposed to caloric restriction starting at just 0.3 years of age. The study demonstrates that caloric restriction has a significant impact on DNA methylation, with detectable effects across different tissues and a subsequent correlation with gene expression. The authors propose that epigenetic drift is a determinant of lifespan in mammals, emphasizing the potential of caloric restriction as a means to increase lifespan.

title: Structural analysis of multiprotein complexes by cross-linking, mass spectrometry, and database searching.
text:
Generally, protein complexes are inaccessible to high-resolution structural analysis. In this study, we employed a combined approach of cross-linking, mass spectrometry, and bioinformatics to investigate two human complexes comprising large coiled-coil segments: the NDEL1 homodimer and the NDC80 heterotetramer. A significant hurdle in the cross-linking method up until now has been the identification of cross-linked peptides from fragmentation spectra. Our novel approach overcomes the data analysis bottleneck of cross-linking and mass spectrometry.
We created a custom database to match spectra with cross-linked peptides, define a score that quantifies the quality of our identification, and estimate false positive rates. Our analysis sheds light on important structural parameters, including the directionality of the homodimeric coiled coil of NDEL1, the register of the heterodimeric coiled coils of the NDC80 complex, and the organization of a tetramerization region in the NDC80 complex. Our approach is particularly useful for analyzing complexes that are challenging to study using conventional structural methods.

title: The long non-coding RNA H19-derived miR-675 modulates human gastric cancer cell proliferation by targeting tumor suppressor RUNX1.
text: The long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) H19 has been shown to be upregulated in gastric cancer and play important roles in its tumorigenesis. However, the molecular mechanisms of H19 and its mature product microRNA-675 (miR-675) in gastric cancer carcinogenesis are still unclear. In this study, we found that miR-675 was co-expressed with H19 and played a pivotal role in H19-induced gastric cancer cell proliferation. Subsequent experiments confirmed that the tumor suppressor Runt Domain Transcription Factor 1 (RUNX1) was a direct target of miR-675, and themediator of H19-induced gastric cancer cell phenotypic changes. A series of rescue assays showed that RUNX1 mediated the effects of H19/miR-675 on gastric cancer cell growth. Moreover, our study revealed an inverse relationship between the expression of RUNX1 and H19/miR-675 in gastric cancer tissues and cell lines. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that the novel pathway H19/miR-675/RUNX1 regulates gastric cancer development and may serve as a potential therapeutic target for gastric cancer treatment.

title: Methylphenidate-induced erections in a prepubertal child.
text: Methylphenidate is a commonly used medication for the management of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, in a case report, we observed an unexpected side effect in a prepubertal child who developed erections after starting a response-adjusted sustained- Release methylphenidate regimen. Although priapism is a rare adverse reaction associated with methylphenidate, it is essential for physicians and parents to be aware of this potential complication, as it can have significant long-term consequences.

title: Mechanism of NO-mediated oxidative and nitrative DNA damage in hamsters infected with Opisthorchis viverrini: a model of inflammation-mediated carcinogenesis.
text: The infection-mediated inflammation plays a crucial role in the development of cholangiocarcinoma (CHCA). Opisthorchis viverrini (OV) infection is a risk factor for CHCA, likely due to its chronic inflammatory effects. In this study, we investigated the formation of 8-nitroguanine and 8-oxo-7,8-dihydro-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-oxodG) in the liver of hamsters infected with OV, as well as the expression of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1). We also produced a specific anti-8-nitroguanine antibody without cross-reactivity. Our findings showed that 8-oxodG and 8-nitroguanine were primarily localized in the same inflammatory cells and bile duct epithelium, with the strongest immunoreactivity observed on days 21 and 30, respectively. Remarkably, these adducts persisted in bile duct epithelium even after 180 days, although alanine aminotransferase activity had returned to normal. A time-course analysis revealed that iNOS expression was associated with 8-nitroguanine formation. Furthermore, this study demonstrated that HO-1 expression and subsequent iron accumulation may contribute to the enhancement of oxidative DNA damage in small bile duct epithelium, which may play a role in CHCA carcinogenesis. In conclusion, infection-mediated inflammation through OV infection leads to the formation of nitrative and oxidative DNA damage in hamsters, which may contribute to the development of CHCA.

title: Monte Carlo tests for associations between disease and alleles at highly polymorphic loci.
text: In an analysis comparing cases and controls in regards to allele frequencies at a highly polymorphic locus, a potential issue arises when utilizing the conventional chi-squared test on large, sparse contingency tables. Fortunately, the necessity of relying on statistics with known asymptotic distributions is no longer a concern, as Monte Carlo simulations can be employed to estimate the significance level of any test statistic. We have formally evaluated the performance of four different 'chi-squared' test statistics, three of which involve the combination of alleles, using a real data set. Experimenting with combining rare alleles to avoid small expected cell counts, and evaluating each allele independently against the rest, we discovered that this approach can inadvertently reduce the power to detect a genuine association when the number of alleles is extremely large. Therefore, it is advisable to either not combine alleles at all, or to combine them in such a way that preserves the evidence for an association.

title: KLF4-dependent phenotypic modulation of smooth muscle cells has a key role in atherosclerotic plaque pathogenesis
text: Previous investigations examining the role of smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and macrophages in the development of atherosclerosis have yielded inconsistent results due to the use of unreliable methods for identifying these cell types. In an attempt to address this issue, we utilized Myh11-CreERT2 ROSA floxed STOP eYFP Apoe−/− mice to perform SMC lineage tracing. Our findings reveal that traditional methods for detecting SMCs through immunostaining for SMC markers often fail to identify over 80% of SMC-derived cells within advanced atherosclerotic lesions. These unidentified cells exhibit characteristics of other cell lineages, including macrophages and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). To further investigate the role of SMCs in atherosclerosis, we conducted conditional knockout of Krüppel-like factor 4 (Klf4) in SMCs. Our results show that this led to a decrease in the number of SMC-derived MSC- and macrophage-like cells, a significant reduction in lesion size, and increases in various indices of plaque stability, including an increase in fibrous cap thickness compared to controls. Through in vivo KLF4 chromatin immunoprecipitation–sequencing (ChIP-seq) analyses and studies of cholesterol-treated cultured SMCs, we identified >800 KLF4 target genes, many of which regulate pro-inflammatory responses in SMCs. Our findings indicate that the contribution of SMCs to atherosclerotic plaques has been significantly underestimated, and that KLF4-dependent transitions in SMC phenotype play a critical role in lesion pathogenesis.

title: Late-life depression and microstructural abnormalities in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex white matter.
text:
The aim of this study was to investigate whether abnormalities in the white matter structure of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex are linked to late-life depression.
Seventeen elderly individuals with depression and 16 non-depressed elderly controls were compared using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) to measure fractional anisotropy (FA) in the white matter of the superior and middle frontal gyri in both hemispheres and the left occipital lobe as a control region. To control for potential confounding variables, the authors analyzed the data while accounting for age, sex, and comorbid medical conditions.
The results revealed significant differences in FA values between the depressed and control groups after adjusting for these variables. Specifically, depressed patients showed lower FA values in the right superior frontal gyrus compared to non-depressed controls.
These findings suggest that microstructural changes in the white matter of the right superior frontal gyrus are associated with late-life depression. Further research is needed to elucidate how these alterations contribute to depression outcomes.

title: Pioglitazone prevents tau oligomerization.
text:
Sure, here's a possible reconstruction of the given text:
The primary causes of Alzheimer's disease (AD) are Tau aggregation and amyloid β protein (Aβ) deposition. However, recent research suggests that modulating Aβ production through Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) activation may be a potential therapeutic strategy for AD. To investigate whether PPARγ agonists, such as pioglitazone (PIO), can also prevent tau aggregation in AD, we utilized a cellular model in which wild-type tau protein (4R0N) is overexpressed (M1C cells) (Hamano et al., 2012) as well as primary neuronal cultures. Our findings reveal that PIO significantly reduced both phosphorylated and total tau levels, and inactivated glycogen synthase kinase 3β, a key tau kinase, through the activation of Akt. Additionally, PIO decreased cleaved caspase3 and C-terminal truncated tau species by caspase, indicating its potential to decrease tau aggregation. A subsequent fractionation study demonstrated that PIO reduced high molecular-weight (120 kDa), oligomeric tau species in Tris Insoluble, sarkosyl-soluble fractions. Notably, the tau-decreasing effect of PIO was reversed by adding GW9662, a PPARγ antagonist. Taken together, our current findings strongly suggest that PPARγ agonists may serve as valuable therapeutic agents for AD.

title: Prognostic impact of the mean platelet volume/platelet count ratio in terms of survival in advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
text:
Background: Mean platelet volume (MPV) is a platelet volume index that has been recognized as a hallmark of platelet activation. Recent studies have shown that MPV and MPV/platelet count (PC) ratio can predict long-term mortality in patients with ischemic cardiovascular disease. These indices have also been correlated with the pathophysiological characteristics of patients with various disorders, including malignant tumors.
Methods: In this retrospective analysis, we evaluated the contribution of platelet volume indices to survival in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). A total of 268 patients were enrolled in the study, with a median age of 68 years (range: 31-87 years). Comparisons of hematological indices were made between the NSCLC group and an age- and sex-matched comparator group.
Results: Our results demonstrated that MPV was significantly decreased in the NSCLC group compared to the comparator group, while PC was significantly increased in the NSCLC group. Consequently, the MPV/PC ratio was also decreased in the NSCLC group. ROC curve analysis revealed that the MPV/PC ratio was associated with a sensitivity of 62.3% and a specificity of 74.6% at a cutoff value of 0.408730 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.72492). Univariate analysis showed that overall survival (OS) was significantly shorter in the group with a low MPV/PC ratio than in the other group (median survival time [MST]: 10.3 months vs. 14.5 months, log-rank, P=0.0245). Multivariate analysis confirmed that a low MPV/PC ratio was an independent unfavorable predictive factor for OS (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.668, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.235-2.271, P=0.0008).
Conclusion: These findings demonstrate a close association between the MPV/PC ratio and survival in patients with advanced NSCLC. The MPV/PC ratio may be a useful predictive marker for survival outcomes in these patients.

title: Traceability of biologicals: present challenges in pharmacovigilance.
text:
Traceability is a crucial aspect of postmarketing surveillance for biologicals, as changes in the manufacturing process can result in specific risks associated with individual products or batches. With the growing biosimilar market, the ability to track and trace individual products within pharmacovigilance databases has become a concern. This article explores the current challenges in tracing biologicals during pharmacovigilance, including the processes involved in ensuring traceability.
The authors examine the existing systems for recording exposure information in clinical practice and the critical steps involved in transferring this data to various pharmacovigilance databases. They identify the limitations of these systems, including the lack of support for recording batch information and the reliance on manual data transfer in spontaneous reporting systems.
The article highlights the need for improvements in traceability, with a focus on encouraging health professionals and patients to systematically record and report detailed exposure information in the short term. Long-term solutions may involve expanding access to and increasing the electronic exchange of exposure data.
In summary, traceability is essential for ensuring the safety of biologicals, and addressing the challenges in this area requires a multifaceted approach involving both short-term and long-term solutions. By improving the systems for recording and transferring exposure data, we can enhance the traceability of biologicals during pharmacovigilance and improve patient safety.

title: Regulation of self-ligands for activating natural killer cell receptors.
text: Natural killer (NK) cells are capable of destroying infected and cancerous cells while sparing healthy cells. The recognition of diseased cells by NK cells is governed by several activating and inhibitory receptors. We will review several pathways that have been implicated in the regulation of self-ligands for activating receptors, including NKG2D, DNAM-1, LFA-1, NKp30, NKp44, NKp46, NKp65, and NKp80 found on both NK cells and some T cells. Understanding how the regulation of self- encoded ligand expression is regulated may lead to novel therapeutic approaches for infections and cancer.

title: A core Klf circuitry regulates self-renewal of embryonic stem cells
text: Embryonic stem (ES) cells exhibit exceptional self-renewal and pluripotency, which is mediated by specific transcription factors. Among these factors, Klf4 is a crucial reprogramming factor required for cellular rejuvenation, along with Oct4, Sox2, and c-Myc. However, ES cell maintenance requires only Oct4, Sox2, and c-Myc, indicating that Klf4 is dispensable. Interestingly, our findings show that Krüppel-like factors (Klfs) are essential for ES cell self-renewal. In fact, simultaneous depletion of Klf2, Klf4, and Klf5 leads to ES cell differentiation. Through chromatin immunoprecipitation coupled to microarray analysis, we discovered that Klfs and Nanog share many common targets, implying a close functional relationship between these factors. RNA interference-mediated triple knockdown of the Klfs confirmed their regulatory role in key pluripotency genes, such as Nanog. Overall, our study provides new insights into how the core Klf circuitry integrates into the Nanog transcriptional network to govern gene expression unique to ES cells.

title: A myeloid hypoxia-inducible factor 1α-Krüppel-like factor 2 pathway regulates gram-positive endotoxin-mediated sepsis.
text: Although gram-positive infections account for the majority of cases of sepsis, the molecular mechanisms underlying their effects are poorly understood. In this study, we investigated how cell wall components of gram-positive bacteria contribute to the development of sepsis. We found that gram-positive bacterial endotoxins induce the expression of hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) mRNA and protein in primary macrophages and a cell line, leading to increased cellular motility and proinflammatory gene expression. Conversely, gram-positive bacteria and their endotoxins reduced the expression of the myeloid anti-inflammatory transcription factor Krüppel-like transcription factor 2 (KLF2). Consistently, mice deficient in myeloid HIF-1α were protected from gram-positive endotoxin-induced sepsis mortality and clinical symptomatology, while myeloid KLF2-deficient mice were susceptible to gram-positive sepsis-induced mortality and clinical symptoms. Together, these findings highlight HIF-1α and KLF2 as critical regulators of gram-positive endotoxin-mediated sepsis.

title: Autophagy controls Salmonella infection in response to damage to the Salmonella-containing vacuole.
text: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (S. Typhimurium) is a facultative intracellular pathogen that infects various hosts, causing disease. S. Typhimurium invades host cells and resides within a membrane-bound compartment called the Salmonella-containing vacuole (SCV). To evade the host immune system, the bacteria use two type III secretion systems (TTSS), which damage eukaryotic cell membranes. We demonstrate that this damage results in an intracellular bacterial population targeted by the host's autophagy system during in vitro infection. Approximately 20% of intracellular S. Typhimurium colocalize with the autophagy marker GFP-LC3 at 1 hour post-infection. Autophagy of S. Typhimurium is dependent on the SPI-1 TTSS and bacterial protein synthesis. Bacteria targeted by the autophagy system are often associated with ubiquitinated proteins, indicating their exposure to the cytosol. Interestingly, these bacteria also colocalize with SCV markers. Autophagy-deficient cells (atg5-) are more permissive for intracellular growth by S. Typhimurium than normal cells, allowing increased bacterial growth in the cytosol. Our findings support a role for autophagy in the early stages of innate immunity, where it helps to retain intracellular S. Typhimurium within vacuoles to protect the cytosol from bacterial colonization. This study demonstrates the power of using Salmonella infection as a model to study the autophagy process.

title: PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-S6K1/2 axis controls Th17 differentiation by regulating Gfi1 expression and nuclear translocation of RORγ.
text: The PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 signaling axis plays a crucial role in the activation, survival, and proliferation of CD4+ T cells upon stimulation through the T cell receptor (TCR) and CD28. Our study demonstrates that disrupting this axis by deleting p85α, using PI3K/mTORC1 inhibitors, or T cell-specific deletion of raptor, an essential component of mTORC1, hinders the differentiation of Th17 cells in vitro and in vivo in a S6K1/2-dependent manner. Inhibition of the PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-S6K1 axis also impairs the reduction of Gfi1, a negative regulator of Th17 differentiation. Moreover, we found that S6K2, a nuclear counterpart of S6K1, is induced by the PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 axis, binds to RORγ, and transports RORγ into the nucleus. These findings underscore the central role of the PI3K-Akt-mTORC1-S6K1/2 axis in the differentiation of Th17 cells.

title: Disrupted-in-schizophrenia 1 and neuregulin 1 are required for the specification of oligodendrocytes and neurones in the zebrafish brain.
text: Research suggests that schizophrenia may be caused by subtle abnormalities in brain development, which can be traced back to the functions of certain candidate susceptibility genes, such as Disrupted-in-schizophrenia 1 (DISC1) and Neuregulin 1 (NRG1). To gain further insights into the role of DISC1 in brain development, we used morpholino antisense methods to study the expression of zebrafish disc1 and its role in early embryonic development. Our findings revealed a critical requirement for disc1 in the development of oligodendrocytes, as it promotes the specification of olig2-positive cells in the hindbrain and other brain regions. Interestingly, we also observed similar defects in embryos lacking nrg1 or ErbB signaling, highlighting the potential existence of overlapping pathways involving these genes in oligodendrocyte and neuron development. Given the similarity between these genes and OLIG2 and ERBB4, two promising candidate susceptibility genes for schizophrenia, our findings suggest that unrecognized connections may exist between these genes and the neurodevelopmental processes implicated in schizophrenia. To further investigate these connections, Disc1 and Nrg1 mouse models and genetically defined groups of patients may be analyzed for potential links to the pathobiology of schizophrenia. The GenBank accession number for Danio rerio disc1 is EU273350.

title: Monoclonal antibody targeting of N-cadherin inhibits prostate cancer growth, metastasis and castration resistance
text: The shift from androgen-dependent to castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is a lethal development of unknown molecular origin. By comparing gene expression in identical androgen-dependent and CRPC xenografts, we found a consistent increase in N-cadherin expression, which was also elevated in primary and metastatic tumors from individuals with CRPC. Artificially increasing N-cadherin in nonmetastatic, androgen-dependent prostate cancer models led to castration resistance, invasion, and metastasis. Antibodies targeting the ectodomain of N-cadherin reduced proliferation, adhesion, and invasion of prostate cancer cells in vitro. In vivo, these antibodies slowed the growth of established CRPC xenografts, blocked local invasion and metastasis, and at higher doses led to complete tumor regression. Treatment with N-cadherin–specific antibodies significantly delayed the emergence of castration resistance, altered tumor histology and angiogenesis, and reduced AKT serine-threonine kinase activity and serum interleukin-8 (IL-8) secretion. These findings suggest that N-cadherin is a primary contributor to both prostate cancer metastasis and castration resistance. Targeting this factor with monoclonal antibodies may have significant clinical potential.

title: PP2A regulates tau phosphorylation directly and also indirectly via activating GSK-3beta.
text:
Abnormal phosphorylation of tau proteins has been implicated in the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Previous research has suggested that a decrease in protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), the primary tau phosphatase in the human brain, contributes to excessive tau phosphorylation in AD. However, the effects of PP2A down-regulation on specific tau phosphorylation sites are not well understood.
Our study aimed to investigate the effects of PP2A down-regulation on different tau phosphorylation sites. We found that PP2A dephosphorylated tau at several sites with varying efficiencies. The most favorable sites for PP2A-mediated dephosphorylation were Thr205, Thr212, Ser214, and Ser262, while Ser199 and Ser404 were the least favored sites. Inhibition of PP2A with okadaic acid in rat brain slices led to inhibition of glycogen synthase kinase-3beta (GSK-3beta) via increased phosphorylation at Ser9. GSK-3beta, in turn, phosphorylated tau at multiple sites, with Ser199, Thr205, and Ser396 being the most favorable sites in cells.
Our findings reveal that the combined effects of reduced tau dephosphorylation due to PP2A inhibition and reduced phosphorylation by GSK-3beta due to its inhibition lead to alterations in tau phosphorylation. These changes provide new insights into the role of PP2A down-regulation in neurofibrillary degeneration in AD. Specifically, our study demonstrates that the impact of tau phosphorylation on its biological activity and neurofibrillary degeneration can vary site-specifically.

title: Human artificial chromosomes containing chromosome 17 alphoid DNA maintain an active centromere in murine cells but are not stable.
text: Human artificial chromosomes (HACs) are autonomous molecules capable of functioning and segregating like normal chromosomes in human cells. De novo HACs have successfully been used as gene expression vectors to complement genetic deficiencies in human cultured cells. HACs offer the potential for studying the regulation and expression of large genes in various cell types from different tissues and correcting gene deficiencies caused by human inherited diseases. Complementary gene expression studies in mice, particularly in mouse models of human genetic diseases, are also essential in determining if large human transgenes can be expressed appropriately from artificial chromosomes. To achieve this, we are establishing artificial chromosomes in murine cells as novel gene expression vectors. Initially, we transferred HAC vectors into murine cells, but were unable to establish de novo HACs at a reasonable frequency. We then transferred HACs pre-established in human HT1080 cells to three different murine cell types through microcell fusion, followed by positive selection. Our results indicate that the HACs in murine cells bind centromere protein C (CENP-C), a marker of active centromeres, and are detected under selection but rapidly lose their identity when selection is removed. These findings suggest that the HACs maintain at least a partially functional centromere complex in murine cells, but other factors are necessary for stability and segregation. Artificial chromosomes containing mouse centromeric sequences may be required for better stability and maintenance in murine cells.

title: How nascent phagosomes mature to become phagolysosomes.
text: Phagocytosis plays a crucial role in removing both dead cells and microbial pathogens from the body. Upon engulfing a particle, a nascent phagocytic vacuole is formed, which lacks the microbicidal and degradative capabilities of a mature phagosome. The maturation process involves the sequential fusion of the phagosomal vacuole with specialized endocytic and secretory compartments, resulting in the formation of phagolysosomes. This process is marked by the remodeling of the phagosomal membrane, resulting in inward and outward vesiculation, tubulation, and fission. The molecular machinery that governs this complex metamorphosis of phagosome maturation is summarized here.

title: Purification and structural characterization of bovine cathelicidins, precursors of antimicrobial peptides.
text: Cathelicidins are a new type of antibacterial peptide found in mammalian white blood cells. They have a consistent starting region and a variable end region that can change in sequence and length. Four cathelicidins, proBac5, proBac7, prododecapeptide, and proBMAP-28, were simultaneously extracted from cow neutrophils using quick and straightforward techniques. The cathelicidins' similarity in their cDNA-determined sequences is shown through correlation with ES-MS data from the purified proteins. The N-terminal domains of the cathelicidins have either one or two Asp-Pro bonds, which are more vulnerable to acid in proBac5 and proBac7 but stable in prododecapeptide. Prododecapeptide is displayed as dimers because of three possible combinations of its two forms. A monomeric, truncated version of this protein lacking the Antimicrobial dodecapeptide was found to be dimerized through disulfide bond-forming at the C-terminal domain. According to sequence-based predictions and CD results, cathelicidins have a 30-50% extended conformation content and less than 20% alpha-helical content, with the alpha-helix segment positioned near the amino terminus. Moreover, topology-based structure prediction and similarity searching indicate that the conserved N-terminal domain of cathelicidins is similar to cystatin-like domains, positioning this family within the cystatin superfamily. Unlike potent cystatin inhibitors, three of the four cathelicidins tested showed only a weak inhibition activity against cathepsin L (Ki = 0.6-3 micromolar).

title: Tuberculosis mortality in England and Wales during 1982-1992: its association with poverty, ethnicity and AIDS.
text: This study aims to establish the association between contemporary tuberculosis (TB) in England and Wales and various potential causative factors. Using an ecological analysis of standardized annual TB mortality rates for 403 local authority districts between 1982 and 1992, disaggregated by age and sex, the study examines the relationships between TB mortality and social, demographic, and ethnicity measures from the 1981 and 1991 censuses, as well as standardized annual AIDS-related mortality rates for young men. The study finds a strong association between TB mortality and overcrowding at the household level for both men and women. However, for women, no other factors improve the explanatory power of the models beyond overcrowding. In multiple regressions, poverty and AIDS-related mortality explain additional variation in the model for younger men. The study does not find a positive relationship between ethnicity and TB notifications, and suggests that it is the overcrowding and poverty among ethnic populations that are significant for their TB mortality. Additionally, the study finds that the relationship between AIDS and TB is limited to the group most typical of AIDS patients, indicating that AIDS has little influence on the level of TB mortality in the wider population. The study suggests that explanations for the observed relationship may include preferential certification, migration for treatment, and shortcomings in health care provision.

title: Noncognate interaction with MHC class II molecules is essential for maintenance of T cell metabolism to establish optimal memory CD4 T cell function.
text: The absence of MHC class II molecules on antigen-presenting cells (APCs) impairs the function of CD4 memory T cells, leading to changes in their gene expression profiles, differentiation, metabolic activity, and survival. By analyzing the gene expression profiles of resting memory T cells isolated from MHC class II-competent or -deficient hosts, we found that five specific transcripts related to T cell activation, metabolism, and survival were underexpressed in resting memory T cells from MHC class II-deficient hosts compared to MHC class II-competent hosts. These changes were observed even in the presence of antigen-presenting dendritic cells, indicating that the absence of MHC class II molecules compromises the accumulation of signals necessary for optimal survival and fitness of activated T cells. specifically, the absence of interactions with non-cognate MHC class II molecules may compromise the progressive accumulation of survival and metabolic signals that ensure the long-term survival and functional capacity of memory T cells. Our data suggest that signals via AKT coordinate survival and metabolic pathways and may play a crucial role in linking interaction with MHC class II molecules to the successful generation of a long-lived functional memory CD4 T cell population.

title: The kinase TAK1 integrates antigen and cytokine receptor signaling for T cell development, survival and function
text: The kinase TAK1 plays a crucial role in both innate and B cell immunity; however, its function in T cells is not well understood. To investigate, we employed T cell–specific deletion of the gene encoding TAK1. Our findings revealed that this results in a reduction in the development of thymocytes, particularly regulatory T cells expressing the transcription factor Foxp3. In mature thymocytes, TAK1 was found to be necessary for the survival that is interleukin 7–mediated and the activation of transcription factor NF-κB and the kinase Jnk upon T cell receptor stimulation. In effector T cells, TAK1 was dispensable for T cell receptor–dependent NF-κB activation and cytokine production, but was important for proliferation and activation of the kinase p38 in response to interleukins 2, 7, and 15. Our results demonstrate that TAK1 is essential for the integration of T cell receptor and cytokine signals, thereby regulating the development, survival, and function of T cells.

title: Caregiver burden in HIV-positive and HIV-negative partners of men with AIDS.
text: This research investigates the factors associated with caregiver burden in 82 HIV-positive (HIV+) and 162 HIV-negative (HIV-) partners of individuals with AIDS. We hypothesized that HIV+ caregivers would experience more burden than HIV- caregivers due to the strain of their disease on their resources. Indeed, HIV+ caregivers reported higher levels of burden and, compared to HIV- caregivers, were more religious or spiritual, had lower incomes, and relied more on positive reappraisal, cognitive escape-avoidance, and social support coping mechanisms. When compared to 61 HIV+ partners of healthy men, most of the differences between HIV+ and HIV- caregivers were due to HIV seropositivity rather than caregiving. However, of the variables associated with HIV seropositivity, only religiosity or spirituality independently contributed to burden in HIV+ caregivers, indicating a relatively weak connection between HIV seropositivity and caregiver burden. The model explained 62% of the variance in burden in HIV+ caregivers and 36% of the variance in HIV- caregivers.

title: Renal Disease and Pregnancy
text:
Pregnancy can have significant effects on a woman's kidneys and urinary tract, which must adapt to the changing status of pregnancy. This can lead to consequences for the developing fetus and the mother's health. Obstetricians must have a thorough understanding of the renal functional tests and their significance in order to accurately diagnose and manage renal diseases in pregnant women.
In modern medicine, the concept of multidisciplinary teamwork is crucial. Obstetricians should consider nephrologists as key players in the team and should refer pregnant women for routine check-ups on their renal status in the second or beginning of the third trimester, alongside usual blood and urine analysis. Nephrologists and urologists should be involved in the management of severe medical conditions such as preeclampsia, acute and chronic renal failure, and complex dialysis or transplant management.
Renal diseases encountered in pregnancy can include pre-existing conditions such as chronic glomerulonephritis, secondary glomerular nephropathies, interstitial nephropathies (chronic pyelonephritis, renal tuberculosis), diabetes nephropathy, and unique surgical kidney. Other diseases directly influenced by pregnancy include asymptomatic bacteriuria, symptomatic urinary infection, urolithiasis, and acute renal failure. The management of dialysis in pregnancy and pregnant women with renal transplant will also be discussed.
In summary, pregnancy can have a significant impact on a woman's kidneys, and obstetricians must be aware of the potential consequences for the developing fetus and the mother's health. A comprehensive understanding of renal functional tests and their significance is crucial for accurate diagnosis and management of renal diseases in pregnant women. The concept of multidisciplinary teamwork is essential in managing these conditions, and nephrologists play a key role in this process.

title: Integrin beta1-mediated matrix assembly and signaling are critical for the normal development and function of the kidney glomerulus.
text:
The kidneys of the human body filter approximately 180 liters of blood each day through a network of 2.5 million glomeruli. The glomerular filtration apparatus, consisting of fenestrated endothelium, a specialized extracellular matrix known as the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), and podocyte foot processes with modified adherens junctions called the slit diaphragm (SD), plays a crucial role in maintaining normal glomerular function. In this study, we investigated the contribution of podocyte beta1 integrin signaling to normal glomerular function. Mice lacking podocyte-specific beta1 integrin (podocin-Cre beta1-fl/fl mice) are born normal but fail to complete postnatal renal development, exhibiting detectable proteinuria from day 1 and dying within a week. The kidneys of these mice show normal glomerular endothelium but display severe GBM defects, including multilaminations and splitting, as well as podocyte foot process effacement.
ILK (integrin linked kinase), a downstream mediator of beta1 integrin activity in epithelial cells, plays a critical role in facilitating proper glomerular filtration. To further investigate the role of beta1 integrin-mediated signaling in glomerular function, we generated mice lacking ILK in podocytes (podocin-Cre ILK-fl/fl mice). These mice develop normally but exhibit proteinuria from birth and die within 15 weeks of age due to renal failure. Our findings indicate that podocyte beta1 integrin and ILK signaling are essential for postnatal development and function of the glomerular filtration apparatus.

title: The Aging Epigenome.
text: As we age, the mechanisms that maintain our health and stress resistance gradually deteriorate, leading to decrepitude, frailty, and ultimately death. While the exact timeline and causes of this decline are still unclear, research suggests that changes in transcriptional networks and chromatin state play a central role in the aging process. These epigenomic alterations not only occur during aging but also profoundly impact cellular function and stress resistance, contributing to the progression of aging. We propose that the dysregulation of transcriptional and chromatin networks is a key component of aging. Uncovering age-dependent epigenomic changes will provide crucial insights into how aging begins and progresses, and may lead to the development of new therapies that delay or even reverse aging and age-related diseases.

title: Cancer chemoprevention: Much has been done, but there is still much to do. State of the art and possible new approaches.
text:
Over the past three decades, significant progress has been made in the search for effective cancer chemoprevention strategies. The enhanced understanding of the complex transition from normal to cancer cells has led to interventions focused on lifestyle modifications, natural compounds, or drugs to impede or reverse this process. Noteworthy successes have been observed in breast and colorectal cancer, yet these strategies have yet to be widely adopted. In this article, we outline the accomplishments, shortcomings, and future steps necessary to improve the efficacy and applicability of chemoprevention strategies. Key components include:
1. Educational initiatives to equip physicians with the knowledge and cultural shifts necessary to appropriately disseminate chemoprevention.
2. Enhancing the risk-benefit ratio by striving for minimal effective doses and intermittent schedules.
3. A more personalized approach to intervention based on individual characteristics, leading to a better categorization of risk.
4. Containing costs of public and private health prevention programs through improved containment strategies.

title: Secreted Frizzled-related Protein 5 Diminishes Cardiac Inflammation and Protects the Heart from Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury.
text: Wnt signaling has diverse functions in cardiovascular development and disease processes. The secreted protein frizzled-related protein 5 (Sfrp5) has been shown to inhibit non-canonical Wnt signaling extracellularly, with high levels of expression in white adipose tissue. This study aimed to investigate the role of Sfrp5 in the heart under conditions of ischemic stress. Sfrp5 knockout (KO) and wildtype (WT) mice were subjected to ischemia/reperfusion (I/R). While Sfrp5-KO mice appeared normal at baseline, they exhibited larger infarct sizes, increased cardiac myocyte apoptosis, and decreased cardiac function following I/R. In contrast, Sfrp5-KO mice had greater infiltration of Wnt5a-positive macrophages and greater inflammatory cytokine and chemokine gene expression compared to WT mice. In bone marrow-derived macrophages, Wnt5a activated JNK and increased inflammatory gene expression, which were blocking by Sfrp5. These results suggest that Sfrp5 functions to counteract inflammatory responses after I/R in the heart, possibly through a non-canonical Wnt5a/JNK signaling pathway.

title: Asymptomatic spinal cord lesions predict disease progression in radiologically isolated syndrome.
text:
Neuroimaging advancements have led to the incidental discovery of brain and spinal cord abnormalities in individuals undergoing diagnostic tests for unrelated medical conditions. Our study aimed to investigate the potential of asymptomatic spinal cord lesions as a predictor of clinical progression in individuals with radiologically isolated syndrome (RIS).
We conducted a retrospective review of RIS cases at the University of California, San Francisco Multiple Sclerosis Center, analyzing the presence of asymptomatic cervical spinal cord MRI lesions as a potential predictor of clinical progression. We found that 25 of 71 subjects with RIS had findings within the cervical spine indicative of demyelinating disease. Of these, 21 (84%) progressed clinically to clinically isolated syndrome (n = 19) or primary progressive multiple sclerosis (n = 2) over a median time of 1.6 years from the date of RIS identification (interquartile range 0.8-3.8). The sensitivity, specificity, and positive predictive value of an asymptomatic spinal cord lesion for subsequent development of either a first demyelinating attack or primary progressive MS were 87.5%, 91.5%, and 84%, respectively. The odds ratio of clinical progression was 75.3 (95% confidence interval 16.1-350.0, p < 0.0001), which remained significant even after adjusting for potential confounders.
Our findings suggest that the presence of asymptomatic spinal cord lesions significantly increases the risk of clinical progression to either an acute or progressive event in subjects with RIS, independent of brain lesions on MRI.

title: YqhC regulates transcription of the adjacent Escherichia coli genes yqhD and dkgA that are involved in furfural tolerance
text: Previous studies have shown that the silencing of adjacent genes encoding NADPH-dependent furfural oxidoreductases (yqhD dkgA) is responsible for increased furfural tolerance in an E. coli strain EMFR9 [Miller et al., Appl Environ Microbiol 75:4315–4323, 2009]. Our recent findings reveal that this gene silencing is caused by the spontaneous insertion of an IS10 element into the coding region of yqhC, an upstream gene. YqhC shares homology with transcriptional regulators belonging to the AraC/XylS family and was shown to positively regulate the adjacent operon encoding YqhD and DkgA. We demonstrated regulation through chromosomal deletion of yqhC, firefly luciferase reporter plasmids for yqhC, and direct comparison of furfural resistance and NADPH-dependent furfural reductase activity. Related bacteria, such as E. coli LY180, contain yqhC, yqhD, and dkgA orthologs in the same arrangement as in E. coli EMFR9. Additionally, orthologs of yqhC are found in more distantly related Gram-negative bacteria. Disrupting yqhC provides a viable approach to enhance furfural tolerance in bacteria.

title: A direct role for Met endocytosis in tumorigenesis
text: The compartmentalization of signals generated by receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) endocytosis has emerged as a pivotal factor in determining various cellular processes. Using tumor-associated Met-activating mutations, we have identified a direct relationship between endocytosis and tumorigenicity. Met mutants exhibit enhanced endocytosis/recycling activity and diminished levels of degradation, resulting in accumulation on endosomes, activation of the GTPase Rac1, loss of actin stress fibers, and increased cell migration. Inhibition of endocytosis in tumor cells resulted in a decrease in anchorage-independent growth, in vivo tumorigenesis, and metastasis while maintaining their activation. Surprisingly, one mutant exhibited resistance to inhibition by a Met-specific tyrosine kinase inhibitor but remained sensitive to endocytosis inhibition, indicating that altered endocytic trafficking may be a crucial mechanism in RTK-dependent tumorigenesis. Our findings suggest that endosomal signaling may play a crucial role in regulating RTK-mediated tumorigenesis.

title: Immediate effects of droperidol
text:
The following is a rewritten version of the given text:
The subjective and behavioral responses of 20 healthy volunteers who received droperidol 5 mg as part of a cognitive challenge program were documented. All participants experienced some form of akathisia, with half feeling dysphoric. However, the intensity and nature of these effects varied widely among individuals, with sedation, dissociative experiences, alterations in sensation, and subtle changes in facial expression all being noted. The duration of these effects ranged from a few hours to over a week, and in the acute phase, participants' insight into the cause of their symptoms was variable. These findings have implications for the interpretation of cognitive challenge tests, the nature of akathisia, clinical therapeutics, and drug development. © 1998 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

title: Toxicity of Nerium oleander in the monkey (Cebus apella).
text: In this study, the toxic effects of Nerium oleander were investigated in capuchin monkeys (Cebus apella) using various doses of dried and ground oleander leaves. The monkeys were observed for clinical signs, hematological and serum chemical changes, and gross and microscopic lesions. The lethal dose of oleander was determined to be between 30 and 60 mg/kg body weight, with a cumulative dose of 60 mg/kg leading to survival in monkeys that received a dose of 3 mg/kg body weight. The clinical signs of oleander toxicity included vomiting, salivation, polyuria, bradycardia, vaginal hemorrhage, abortion, anorexia, constipation, loss of body weight, narcosis, restlessness, weakness, and shallow and rapid respirations. The study also revealed changes in blood values, including leukocytosis, neutrophilia, increased potassium, glutamic-oxalacetic transaminase, glutamic-pyruvic transaminase, blood urea nitrogen, and α-globulins; reticulo-cytopenia; and decreased calcium, glucose, total serum protein, albumin, γ-globulin levels, and hematocrit.

title: Plzf regulates limb and axial skeletal patterning
text: The Plzf protein, encoded by the Zfp145 gene, belongs to the POZ/zinc-finger family of transcription factors. We generated Zfp145-deficient mice and found that Plzf is essential for the proper patterning of the limb and axial skeleton. Inactivation of Plzf results in defects in the patterning of all skeletal structures in the limb, including transformations of anterior structures into posterior ones. We showed that Plzf acts as a growth-inhibiting and pro-apoptotic factor in the limb bud and regulates the expression of certain Hox genes and bone morphogenetic proteins in a manner independent of other patterning genes. Zfp145-deficient mice also exhibit anterior-directed homeotic transformations throughout the axial skeleton, with associated changes in Hox gene expression. Overall, Plzf plays a crucial role in both AP patterning of the axial and appendicular skeleton and the regulation of Hox gene expression.

title: Requirement for the ERI/DICER complex in endogenous RNA interference and sperm development in Caenorhabditis elegans.
text: Small regulatory RNAs, specifically endogenous small interfering RNAs (endo siRNAs), play a crucial role in regulating gene expression. In Caenorhabditis elegans, a complex of proteins known as the ERI/DICER complex mediates endo RNAi processes. To identify additional components of the endo RNAi machinery, we conducted a genetic screen. Our screen revealed two novel components: ERI-9, a DICER-interacting protein, and a missense mutation in the helicase domain of DICER (DCR-1(G492R)). ERI-9-deficient and DCR-1(G492R)-mutant animals exhibit defects in endo siRNA expression and a failure to regulate mRNAs with sequence homology to these endo siRNAs. These findings suggest that ERI-9 and the DCR-1 helicase domain function in the C. elegans endo RNAi pathway. We also identified a subset of Eri mutant animals that exhibit temperature-sensitive, sperm-specific sterility and defects in X chromosome segregation. Analyses of these mutants revealed aberrations in sperm development, starting from cytokinesis and extending through terminal differentiation. These results identify new components of the endo RNAi machinery, highlight the differential requirements for the Eri factors in the sperm-producing germline, and begin to delineate the functional requirement for the ERI/DICER complex in sperm development.

title: Drug-induced thrombocytopenia: pathogenesis, evaluation, and management.
text: Although drugs are a common trigger for acute immune-mediated thrombocytopenia in adults, the drug-induced etiology is often initially overlooked. Most cases of drug-induced thrombocytopenia (DITP) are caused by drug-dependent antibodies that specifically bind to platelets through their Fab regions, only when the drug is present. A comprehensive database of 1301 published reports detailing 317 drugs, available at <www.ouhsc.edu/platelets>, provides evidence for a causal connection to thrombocytopenia. Typically, DITP occurs 1-2 weeks after starting a new drug or suddenly after a single dose when a drug has been taken intermittently. However, severe thrombocytopenia can occur almost immediately after taking antithrombotic agents that block fibrinogen binding to platelet GP IIb-IIIa, such as abciximab, tirofiban, and eptifibatide. Recovery from DITP usually begins within 1-2 days of stopping the drug and is usually complete within a week. Drug-dependent antibodies can persist for several years, making it crucial that the drug-related etiology be established and the drug be avoided thereafter.

title: Costs and financial feasibility of malaria elimination
text: The economics of converting malaria programs from control to elimination are critical to strategic decision-making, but empirical data is limited. To address this gap, we propose a conceptual framework to evaluate the economics of elimination and analyze its central component: potential short-term to medium-term financial savings. After a review of existing literature, we calculated the net present value of elimination in five sites and compared it with effective control. Our findings show that the probability of elimination being cost-saving over 50 years ranged from 0% to 42%, with only one site achieving cost-savings in the base case. These results suggest that financial savings should not be the primary motivation for elimination, but that elimination may still be a worthwhile investment if total benefits outweigh marginal costs. Urgent research is needed to quantify these elimination benefits.

title: Expression of the angiogenic factors vascular endothelial cell growth factor, acidic and basic fibroblast growth factor, tumor growth factor beta-1, platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor, placenta growth factor, and pleiotrophin in human primary breast cancer and its relation to angiogenes
text:
Angiogenesis, or the formation of new blood vessels, is a crucial aspect of breast cancer progression. However, the molecular mechanisms that regulate angiogenesis in vivo are not yet fully understood. Multiple angiogenic proteins have been identified, and in this study, we investigated the expression of seven of these proteins in primary human breast cancers.
Using RNase protection analysis, we quantified the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1, pleiotrophin, acidic and basic fibroblast growth factor (FGF), placental growth factor, and thymidine phosphorylase (platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor) in 64 primary breast cancers. Our results showed that all tumors expressed at least six different vascular growth factors, with VEGF being the most abundant and the transcript for the 121-amino acid form predominating. Interestingly, we found that expression of thymidine phosphorylase correlated with vascular density, with a correlation coefficient of 0.3 (P = 0.03). Additionally, we observed associations between pleiotrophin and acidic FGF expression and TGF-beta with platelet-derived endothelial cell growth factor expression.
Our findings suggest that angiogenesis in breast cancer may involve a coordinated regulation of multiple vascular growth factors. High expression of VEGF was associated with poor prognosis in univariate analysis, along with ER and epidermal growth factor receptor expression. Basic FGF was also found to be more highly expressed in tumors than in normal breast tissues, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy. Therefore, broad-spectrum agents that target multiple angiogenic factors or direct endothelial cell toxicity may be effective in combination therapy.

title: Cnn1 inhibits the interactions between the KMN complexes of the yeast kinetochore
text: Kinetochores connect the replicated chromosomes to the mitotic spindle, ensuring their proper transfer to the daughter cells. The multicopy KNL1Spc105, MIS12Mtw1, and NDC80Ndc80 complexes, forming the KMN network, are responsible for mediating kinetochore–spindle binding and chromosome segregation. The activity of the KMN network is regulated by Aurora BIpl1 and MPS1Mps1 kinases. The existence of other mechanisms that support KMN activity during the cell cycle remains unclear. Through the study of budding yeast, we discovered that a kinetochore protein, Cnn1, localizes at the base of the Ndc80 complex and promotes a functionally competent configuration of the KMN network. Cnn1 regulates KMN activity in a spatiotemporal manner by inhibiting the interactions between its complexes. Cnn1 activity peaks in anaphase and is driven by the Cdc28, Mps1, and Ipl1 kinases.

title: Origin and functions of tissue macrophages.
text:
Macrophages are dispersed throughout tissues in the body and play a crucial role in both homeostasis and disease. Recent research has revealed that most adult tissue macrophages originate from embryonic development, rather than circulating monocytes. Each tissue has a unique composition of embryonically derived and adult-derived macrophages, but it is unclear whether these different types of macrophages have interchangeable functions or distinct roles at steady state. This new understanding also raises questions about the role of circulating monocytes.
Classical Ly6c(hi) monocytes patrol the extravascular space in resting organs, while Ly6c(lo) nonclassical monocytes patrol the vasculature. Upon inflammation, monocytes differentiate into macrophages, but it is unclear whether resident and newly recruited macrophages have similar functions during inflammation.
To investigate the complex origins of tissue macrophages, we employed a range of tools, including genetic tracing, fate mapping, and single-cell analysis. Our findings reveal the significance of both tissue niche and ontological origin in regulating macrophage functions during steady state and inflammation.
In conclusion, our study sheds light on the complex mechanisms that dictate the origins and functions of tissue macrophages, and highlights the importance of considering both tissue niche and ontological origin in understanding macrophage biology.

title: Treatment outcome of an unselected cohort of tuberculosis patients in relation to human immunodeficiency virus serostatus in Zomba Hospital, Malawi.
text: A study was conducted in Zomba General Hospital, Malawi, to evaluate treatment outcomes in an unselected cohort of tuberculosis (TB) patients, including those with smear-negative pulmonary TB (PTB) and extrapulmonary TB (EPTB). The study found that:

title: Statin use and risk of gallstone disease followed by cholecystectomy.
text:
INTRODUCTION
Gallstone disease is a significant health concern in developed countries, with a substantial economic burden. Statins have been found to decrease hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis, thereby reducing the risk of cholesterol gallstones by lowering the cholesterol content in bile. However, there is a lack of data on the association between statin use and gallstone risk in humans. This study aims to investigate the association between the use of statins, fibrates, or other lipid-lowering agents and the risk of incident gallstone disease followed by cholecystectomy.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
This was a case-control study conducted using the UK-based General Practice Research Database. The study population consisted of 76% women with a mean (SD) age of 53.4 (15.0) years at the index date. Incident patients between 1994 and 2008 and 4 controls per each patient were identified and matched on age, sex, general practice, calendar time, and years of history in the database.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE
The main outcome measure was the adjusted odds ratio (AOR) for developing gallstone disease followed by cholecystectomy in relation to exposure to lipid-lowering agents, stratified by exposure timing and duration. The AORs and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were adjusted for smoking, body mass index, ischemic heart disease, stroke, and estrogen use.
RESULTS
A total of 27,035 patients with cholecystectomy and 106,531 matched controls were identified, including 2396 patients and 8868 controls who had statin use. Compared with nonuse, current statin use (last prescription recorded within 90 days before the first-time diagnosis of the disease) was 1.0% for patients and 0.8% for controls (AOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.95-1.27) for 1 to 4 prescriptions; 2.6% vs 2.4% (AOR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.77-0.93) for 5 to 19 prescriptions, and 3.2% vs 3.7% (AOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.59-0.70) for 20 or more prescriptions. The AORs for current use of statins defined as 20 or more prescriptions were similar (around 0.6) across age, sex, and body mass index categories, and across the statin class.
CONCLUSION
Our findings suggest that long-term use of statins is associated with a decreased risk of gallstones followed by cholecystectomy. This association was observed across age, sex, and body mass index categories, and across different statin classes. These results provide evidence that statin therapy may have a protective effect against gallstone disease, highlighting the importance of this treatment in the prevention and management of this condition.

title: Chromatin remodeling in embryonic stem cells: regulating the balance between pluripotency and differentiation.
text: Embryonic stem cells possess an immense potential for self-renewal, yet they are also highly versatile, capable of differentiating into multiple cell types and tissues. Central to this process are key transcriptional regulators that preserve an undifferentiated state, along with epigenetic modifiers that contribute to the balance between pluripotency and differentiation by influencing chromatin structure. These mechanisms are crucial for the development and maintenance of tissue diversity in the embryo.

title: The National Advisory Group on Immunization (NAGI) of the Republic of South Africa.
text: The National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG) in South Africa, previously known as the National Advisory Group on Immunization (NAGI), was established in 1993 to provide technical advice to the National Department of Health (DoH) on issues pertaining to vaccination. Meetings are convened as needed, but at least twice a year. The scope of the group's advisory work encompasses vaccines and immunization, as well as other relevant infectious disease issues. NAGI also provides recommendations on vaccine schedules and formulations. Agendas are set by the DoH and the Chairperson of NAGI. By bringing together experts from a range of fields relevant to vaccines and immunization, NAGI has served as an invaluable resource in guiding the Expanded Program of Immunization (EPI) in South Africa.

title: Effect of n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation in pregnancy on infants’ allergies in first year of life: randomised controlled trial
text:
The objective of this study was to determine whether dietary supplementation of n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LCPUFA) in pregnant women at high risk of allergic disease can reduce immunoglobulin E (IgE)-associated allergies in their offspring at 1 year of age. This study was a follow-up of infants at high hereditary risk of developing allergic diseases in the DOMInO randomized controlled trial based in Adelaide, South Australia.
The study included 706 infants whose mothers were participating in the DOMInO trial. The intervention group (n=368) received fish oil capsules providing 900 mg of n-3 LCPUFA daily from 21 weeks' gestation until birth, while the control group (n=338) received matched vegetable oil capsules without n-3 LCPUFA. The primary outcome measure was the incidence of IgE-associated allergic disease (eczema or food allergy with sensitization) at 1 year of age.
The results showed no significant difference in the overall percentage of infants with IgE-associated allergic disease between the n-3 LCPUFA and control groups (9% vs 13%; adjusted relative risk 0.70, 0.45-1.09, p=0.12). However, the percentage of infants diagnosed with atopic eczema (i.e., eczema with associated sensitization) was lower in the n-3 LCPUFA group (7% vs 12%; unadjusted relative risk 0.61, 0.38-0.98, p=0.04; adjusted relative risk 0.64, 0.40-1.02, p=0.06). Additionally, fewer infants were sensitized to egg in the n-3 LCPUFA group (9% vs 15%; unadjusted relative risk 0.61, 0.40-0.91, p=0.02; adjusted relative risk 0.62, 0.41-0.93, p=0.02). No significant differences were seen in the incidence of IgE-associated food allergy between the two groups.
In conclusion, n-3 LCPUFA supplementation in pregnancy did not significantly reduce the overall incidence of IgE-associated allergies in infants at 1 year of age, although atopic eczema and egg sensitization were lower. Longer-term follow-up is needed to determine if supplementation has an effect on respiratory allergic diseases and aeroallergen sensitization in childhood.
The study was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12610000735055).

title: ModLoop: automated modeling of loops in protein structures.
text:
SUMMARY:
ModLoop is a web-based server for automated loop modeling in protein structures. Users can input atomic coordinates of the protein structure in Protein Data Bank (PDB) format and specify the starting and ending residues of one or more segments to be modeled, containing no more than 20 residues in total. The server uses MODELLER, a loop modeling routine that predicts loop conformations by satisfying spatial restraints, without relying on a database of known protein structures. ModLoop provides a user-friendly web interface for inputting parameters and retrieving the output, which includes the coordinates of the non-hydrogen atoms in the modeled segments. Rapid results are achieved through the use of a cluster of Linux PC computers for processing.
AVAILABILITY: ModLoop is freely accessible to academic users at <http://salilab.org/modloop>.

title: What is the best way to help caregivers in cancer and palliative care? A systematic literature review of interventions and their effectiveness.
text: Informal carers in cancer and palliative care have been found to have high levels of emotional distress and needs, yet there are limited targeted interventions available. To address this gap, a systematic review of interventions for carers of patients receiving home-based cancer and palliative care services was conducted. The review searched four major databases (Medline, CancerLit, Psycinfo, and Cinahl) using the terms "carer," "caregiver," "palliative," and "cancer." Studies were included if they reported interventions for adults providing informal care for non-institutionalized cancer and palliative care patients. Twenty-two interventions were identified, including home nursing care (4), respite services (3), social networks and activity enhancement (2), problem-solving and education (3), and group work (10). Of these, nine interventions were specifically designed for carers. Only six of these interventions had been evaluated, with two using a randomized controlled trial (RCT) design (both graded IB), three using a single-group methodology (two prospective, one retrospective), and one using facilitator feedback. The review noted several methodological challenges, including a lack of outcome evaluation designs, small sample sizes, and reliance on intervention descriptions and formative evaluations. The authors conclude that while the current evidence provides insights into the feasibility and acceptability of interventions, further development and evaluation of these interventions are necessary to determine their effectiveness. Practitioners and evaluators must prioritize the development and evaluation of intervention studies to address the emotional needs of informal carers in cancer and palliative care.

title: Brief Internet-Based Intervention Reduces Posttraumatic Stress and Prolonged Grief in Parents after the Loss of a Child during Pregnancy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
text:
Background: Losing a child during pregnancy can have a profound psychological impact on women and their partners, often leading to long-term mental health issues. internet-based interventions that incorporate exposure and cognitive restructuring techniques have shown promise in treating posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and prolonged grief. This study compared the effectiveness of an internet-based intervention for parents after prenatal loss to a waiting list control (WLC) group.
Methods: The Impact of Event Scale Revised assessed symptoms of PTSD, while the Inventory of Complicated Grief and the Brief Symptom Inventory measured depression, anxiety, and overall mental health. A total of 228 participants (92% female) were randomly assigned to either a treatment group (TG, n=115) or the WLC group (n=113). The TG received a 5-week cognitive behavioral intervention consisting of (1) self-confrontation, (2) cognitive restructuring, and (3) social sharing.
Results: The TG exhibited significantly reduced symptoms of posttraumatic stress, prolonged grief, depression, and anxiety in comparison to the WLC control group. Intention-to-treat analysis revealed treatment effects of between d=0.84 and d=1.02 for posttraumatic stress and prolonged grief from pre- to post-intervention time points. Furthermore, the TG continued to show improved symptoms of PTSD and prolonged grief at the 12-month follow-up. The attrition rate of 14% was relatively low.
Conclusions: The internet-based intervention proved to be a feasible and cost-effective treatment, reducing symptoms of posttraumatic stress, grief, depression, anxiety, and overall mental health after pregnancy loss. Given the low-threshold nature of this intervention, it is recommended that low-threshold e-health interventions be further evaluated and implemented routinely to improve psychological support after pregnancy loss.

title: Up-regulation of PPAR-gamma mRNA expression in the liver of obese patients: an additional reinforcing lipogenic mechanism to SREBP-1c induction.
text: Triglyceride accumulation in the liver is an early feature of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), which is a multifactorial syndrome associated with obesity. In obese individuals with NAFLD, the liver's peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) mRNA expression is increased, suggesting a mechanistic link between the accumulation of triglycerides in the liver and the development of NAFLD. To investigate this association, we measured PPAR-γ mRNA expression, serum total adiponectin and high molecular weight (HMW) adiponectin levels, and insulin resistance (IR) evolution in 22 obese patients with NAFLD who underwent subtotal gastrectomy with gastrojejunal anastomosis in Roux-en-Y, and in 16 nonobese subjects who underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy (controls). Our results showed that liver PPAR-γ mRNA levels were 112-188% higher in obese patients with steatosis and steatohepatitis, respectively, compared to controls, and were positively associated with serum insulin levels and homeostasis model assessment-IR. Additionally, liver PPAR-γ expression showed negative correlations with total adiponectin and HMW-adiponectin levels in serum. These findings suggest that PPAR-γ up-regulation in the liver of obese patients with NAFLD is an additional lipogenic mechanism that contributes to the development of hepatic steatosis.

title: Ribosomal protein S17 gene (RPS17) is mutated in Diamond-Blackfan anemia.
text: Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) is a congenital erythroblastopathy characterized by a normochromic macrocytic anemia with a selective deficiency in red blood cell precursors in otherwise normocellular bone marrow. In approximately 40% of DBA patients, various physical abnormalities are present. Currently, two genes have been associated with the DBA phenotype: ribosomal protein (RP) S19 in 25% of DBA patients and RPS24 in approximately 1.4% of DBA patients. Our study has now identified a mutation in an additional ribosomal protein, RPS17. The mutation affects the translation initiation start codon, changing T to G (c.2T>G), thereby disrupting the natural start of RPS17 protein biosynthesis. RNA analysis revealed that the mutated allele is expressed, and the next downstream start codon located at position +158 would produce a short peptide of only four amino acids (Met-Ser-Arg-Ile). The mutation arose spontaneously, as all healthy family members carry wild-type alleles. The identification of a mutation in the third RP of the small ribosomal subunit in DBA patients further supports the theory that impaired translation may be the primary cause of DBA pathogenesis.

title: An overview of the effective combination therapies for the treatment of breast cancer.
text:
Breast cancer (BC) is typically classified based on the receptors overexpressed on the cell nucleus, including hormone receptors such as progesterone (PR) and estrogen (ER), and HER2. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a type of cancer that lacks expression of any of these three receptor proteins (ER/PR/HER2). Tumor cells tend to exhibit drug-resistant phenotypes, reducing the effectiveness of chemotherapeutic treatments. While drug resistance often has a genetic basis, it can also arise from various mechanisms, including:
1. Efflux pumps that reduce the cellular concentration of drugs
2. Alterations in membrane lipids that reduce cellular uptake of drugs
3. Increased or altered drug targets that hinder drug activity
4. Metabolic alterations of drugs that reduce their potency
5. Inhibition of apoptosis, which permits cancer cells to survive exposure to chemotherapy
6. Repair of damaged DNA, which can lead to the development of resistant tumor cells
7. Alterations in cell cycle checkpoints that help cancer cells evade the effects of chemotherapy.
Combination therapy is widely recognized as an effective approach to treating human diseases, particularly breast cancer. In this review, we provide examples of different nanocarriers that have been used to co-deliver multiple therapeutics (chemotherapeutic agents and nucleic acids) to drug-resistant tumor cells. Finally, we offer our recommendations for future directions in co-delivery treatments.

title: Disturbed sleep in bipolar disorder is related to an elevation of IL-6 in peripheral monocytes.
text: Bipolar disorder is a severe mental illness characterized by persistent modifications in the quality, duration, and organization of sleep. Currently, there is no unifying theory explaining these changes in sleep patterns observed in individuals with bipolar disorder, and management can be challenging despite their importance. Sleep is influenced by various cytokines, including interleukin-6 (IL-6). Elevated levels of IL-6 are associated with poorer sleep quality and alterations in sleep architecture similar to those observed in bipolar disorder. Therapeutic administration of interferon can lead to increased intrathecal IL-6 concentrations, which may worsen sleep quality. Conversely, blockading IL-6 with tocilizumab in rheumatoid arthritis has been linked to improvements in sleep quality. Bipolar disorder is characterized by elevated levels of IL-6, particularly elevated levels of mRNA coding for IL-6 in peripheral monocytes. Our hypothesis suggests that the changes observed in the sleep patterns of individuals with bipolar disorder are relevant to the elevated levels of IL-6, which are associated with increased mRNA expression of IL-6 in peripheral monocytes.

title: Targeted blockade of TGF-β and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 pathways inhibits lung cancer growth promoted by bone marrow-derived myofibroblasts
text: To investigate the role of TGF-β and IL-6 in the interactions between myofibroblasts (MFs) and lung cancer cells, we stimulated lung cancer cells (Lewis and CTM-167 cell lines) with IL-6, MF-conditioned medium (MF-CM), or MFs, either alone or in combination with TGF-β signaling inhibitors (SB431542 and JSI-124). Concurrently, we stimulated MFs with TGF-β, cancer cell-conditioned medium (CCM), or cancer cells, and treated them with SB431542 and JSI-124. We measured cell proliferation, cytokine levels, mRNA expression, and protein production. To assess the therapeutic potential of targeting these signaling pathways, we treated mice bearing xenograft tumors with SB431542 or JSI-124 and monitored their tumor growth for up to 45 days. Our results showed that the TGF-β and IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathways form a positive feedback loop that mediates the interactions between MFs and lung cancer cells. Blockade of JAK2/STAT3 and TGF-β signaling significantly inhibited cell proliferation in vitro and tumor growth in vivo. These findings suggest that targeting this signaling loop could be a promising approach for lung cancer prevention and therapy.

title: Production of cloned mice and ES cells from adult somatic cells by nuclear transfer: how to improve cloning efficiency?
text: Ten years have passed since the first mammals were cloned using nuclear transfer (NT), but most cloned embryos still fail to develop beyond implantation, with a success rate below 5%. This is believed to be due to epigenetic errors, such as excessive DNA methylation, which are not yet fully understood. To overcome this challenge, we have developed a stable NT method in mice, where donor nuclei are injected directly into the oocyte using a piezo-actuated micromanipulator. While only a few laboratories can generate clones from adult somatic cells in mice, this technique has the potential to be a valuable tool for future research in basic biology. For instance, NT can be used to generate embryonic stem (NT-ES) cell lines from a patient's own somatic cells, which are equivalent to ES cells derived from fertilized embryos. Furthermore, NT-ES cells can be generated easily from a variety of mouse genotypes and cell types of both sexes, although it may be more difficult to generate clones directly. This technique is expected to be applied in regenerative medicine, but it can also be used to preserve the genetic resources of mouse strains instead of embryos, oocytes, and spermatozoa. This review aims to improve cloning efficiency and NT-ES cell establishment, as well as explore additional applications.

title: Recruitment of Tat to heterochromatin protein HP1 via interaction with CTIP2 inhibits human immunodeficiency virus type 1 replication in microglial cells.
text:
The Tat protein of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) plays a crucial role in inducing viral gene expression. Recently, we discovered that the protein chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor-interacting protein 2 (CTIP2) can potently inhibit Tat function in human microglial cells. Overexpression of CTIP2 leads to suppression of HIV-1 replication by inhibiting Tat-mediated transactivation. In contrast, the related CTIP1 was unable to affect Tat function or viral replication.
Using confocal microscopy, we found that overexpression of CTIP2, but not CTIP1, leads to disruption of Tat's subcellular localization. CTIP2 overexpression causes Tat to relocate within nuclear ball-like structures, rather than remaining in the nucleus. We also found that CTIP2 colocalizes with the protein HP1alpha, which is associated with heterochromatin. The CTIP2 protein contains two interaction domains: the 145-434 domain that interacts with the N-terminal region of Tat and the 717-813 domain that binds to HP1. These domains form a three-protein complex in which Tat is recruited.
The importance of this interaction was confirmed through analysis of CTIP2 deletion mutants. Our findings suggest that inhibition of HIV-1 expression by CTIP2 correlates with recruitment of Tat within CTIP2-induced structures and relocalization of Tat within inactive regions of the chromatin. These data reveal a novel mechanism of Tat inactivation through subnuclear relocalization, which may eventually lead to a decrease in viral pathogenesis.

title: Cryptochrome Mediates Circadian Regulation of cAMP Signaling and Hepatic Gluconeogenesis
text:
During fasting, mammals maintain normal glucose homeostasis by promoting hepatic gluconeogenesis through the activation of hepatic gluconeogenic gene expression. This process is mediated by two key transcriptional regulators, cAMP response element-binding protein (Creb) and the Creb-regulated transcription coactivator-2 (Crtc2), which are phosphorylated and dephosphorylated, respectively, in response to elevations in circulating glucagon and epinephrine. Although the underlying mechanism is unclear, hepatic gluconeogenesis is also regulated by the circadian clock, which coordinates glucose metabolism with changes in the external environment.
