Circadian control of gene expression is achieved through the action of two transcriptional activators, Clock and Bmal1, which stimulate cryptochrome (Cry1 and Cry2) and Period (Per1, Per2, and Per3) repressors that feed back on Clock-Bmal1 activity.
Here, we demonstrate that Creb activity during fasting is modulated by Cry1 and Cry2, which are rhythmically expressed in the liver. Cry1 expression is elevated during the night-day transition, when it reduces fasting gluconeogenic gene expression by blocking glucagon-mediated increases in intracellular cAMP concentrations and in the protein kinase A-mediated phosphorylation of Creb. Biochemical reconstitution studies reveal that Cry1 inhibits accumulation of cAMP in response to G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) activation but not to forskolin, a direct activator of adenyl cyclase. Cry proteins seem to modulate GPCR activity directly through interaction with G(s)α. Interestingly, hepatic overexpression of Cry1 lowers blood glucose concentrations and improves insulin sensitivity in insulin-resistant db/db mice, suggesting that compounds that enhance cryptochrome activity may provide therapeutic benefit to individuals with type 2 diabetes.

title: Toll-like receptor 4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism in myocardial infarction: a meta-analysis of 15,148 subjects.
text: A recent controversy surrounds the association between the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) gene Asp299Gly (+896 A/G) polymorphism and myocardial infarction (MI) risk. Therefore, a large-scale meta-analysis was conducted to investigate the potential association between this genetic variant and MI risk. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CBMdisc, CNKI, and Google Scholar until February 6, 2013, and included nine articles involving ten studies, covering a total of 8299 MI cases and 6849 controls. Our results failed to show a significant association between the TLR4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism and MI risk, regardless of the source of controls (G allele vs. A allele: OR=0.95, 95% CI=0.74-1.22, p=0.71; G/G vs. A/A: OR=1.03, 95% CI=0.54-1.98, p=0.93; G/G vs. A/G+A/A: OR=1.05, 95% CI=0.55-2.03, p=0.87; G/G+A/G vs. A/A: OR=0.92, 95% CI=0.75-1.13, p=0.42). In summary, our meta-analysis suggests that the TLR4 gene Asp299Gly polymorphism is not associated with MI risk.

title: Matrix metalloproteinase and proinflammatory cytokine production by chondrocytes of human osteoarthritic cartilage: associations with degenerative changes.
text: Objective: To investigate the relative distribution of six matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) (MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-3, MMP-8, MMP-9, and MMP-13) and two pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin-1beta (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα)) in osteoarthritic (OA) cartilage compared to normal, age-matched articular cartilage using immunohistochemistry. Methods: Articular cartilage samples were obtained from OA knees at arthroplasty and from normal, non-arthritic knees at autopsy. The samples were promptly fixed in Carnoy's fixative, processed, embedded in paraffin, sectioned, and examined by immunohistochemistry for MMP and cytokine production. In addition, human articular chondrocytes (HAC) were treated in vitro with either IL-1β, TNFα, or phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) to assess their production of each of the MMPs, as determined by Western blotting and gelatin zymography. Results: Immunodetection of collagenases (MMP-1, MMP-8, and MMP-13) and stromelysin-1 (MMP-3) was observed in a proportion of chondrocytes in the superficial zone of almost all OA specimens with degenerative matrix changes. Gelatinases (MMP-2 and MMP-9) were also detected, but to a lesser degree. IL-1β- and TNFα-positive chondrocytes were observed in a proportion of cells in the superficial zones of OA specimens. Very little immunostaining for MMPs and cytokines was observed in the deep zone of all OA specimens, where the cartilage matrix and chondrocyte morphology appeared normal. In contrast, virtually no immunostaining for these MMPs or cytokines was observed in full-thickness normal cartilage specimens. Confirmation that chondrocytes can produce these six MMPs was obtained from HAC cultures treated with either IL-1β, TNFα, or PMA, and conditioned medium from activated HAC contained all the MMPs detected by immunohistochemistry. Dual immunolocalization studies of OA cartilage specimens demonstrated the co-expression of IL-1β with MMP-8 by individual chondrocytes in situ. Conclusion: These results suggest that the superficial zone of OA cartilage specimens, characterized by fibrillations, chondrocyte clusters, and degenerative matrix changes, contains a variable proportion of cells that immunostain for IL-1β, TNFα, and six different MMPs. These observations support the hypothesis that cytokine-MMP associations reflect a modified chondrocyte phenotype and an intrinsic process of cartilage degradation in OA.

title: β-catenin-independent WNT signaling in basal-like breast cancer and brain metastasis.
text: A recent study has investigated the role of WNT signaling in primary breast cancers of the basal-like subtype and as a predictor of brain metastasis. Despite the known importance of WNT signaling in this context, a responsible WNT ligand has yet to be identified. To further elucidate this question, the study compared 22 human breast cancer brain metastases, as well as the highly invasive human breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 and the weakly motile MCF-7 cell line, which represent the basal-like and luminal A subtypes, respectively. The study found that WNT5A and WNT5B were overexpressed in MDA-MB-231 cells compared to MCF-7, leading to a reduction in MDA-MB-231 invasiveness upon inhibition of WNT signaling. In contrast, MCF-7 invasion was enhanced by recombinant WNT5B and abolished by inhibitors of WNT and Jun-N-terminal kinase signaling. Notably, expression and subcellular distribution of β-catenin remained unchanged. Furthermore, the study found that β-catenin was not localized in the nuclei of brain metastases, and strong nuclear c-Jun staining was observed. Consistency was observed in external gene expression datasets of different breast cancer subtypes and brain metastases, and hierarchical cluster analysis revealed a close relation between basal-like cancers and brain metastases. Gene set enrichment analyses confirmed WNT pathway enrichment in basal-like primaries and in cerebral metastases of all subtypes. In conclusion, WNT signaling appears to be highly relevant for basal-like and other subtypes of breast cancers metastasizing into the brain, with β-catenin-independent WNT signaling playing a major role in this context.

title: Retinal attenuates inflammatory arthritis by reciprocal regulation of IL-17-producing T cells and Foxp3(+) regulatory T cells and the inhibition of osteoclastogenesis.
text: The study aimed to investigate the potential of retinaldehyde, a derivatives of vitamin A, to inhibit inflammatory responses and joint destruction in mice with collagen-induced arthritis (CIA). The arthritis score and incidence of arthritis were lower in mice treated with retinal compared to those treated with cottonseed oil. Histopathological examination showed reduction in joint damage, accompanied by decreased immune cell infiltration in mice treated with retinal. Furthermore, expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress proteins, and osteoclast markers was significantly reduced in mice treated with retinal. In vitro, retinal increased Foxp3 expression and inhibited Th17 development, while the proportion of Foxp3+ T regulatory cells was increased and Th17 cells were decreased in the spleens of mice treated with retinal. In both mouse and human culture systems, tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) positive mononuclear cells and multinucleated cells were significantly reduced after treatment with retinal, and expression of osteoclast differentiation markers was dramatically decreased upon addition of retinal. These findings suggest that retinal has potent immunoregulatory functions and potential therapeutic value for the treatment of autoimmune inflammatory diseases.

title: NRAGE promotes the malignant phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma.
text:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a deadly disease due to limited effective treatments for patients with advanced or recurrent stages of the disease. To improve patient outcomes, it is crucial to identify a useful biomarker for HCC progression and a molecular target for therapy. Neurotrophin receptor-interacting melanoma antigen-encoding protein (NRAGE), a member of the type II melanoma-associated antigen family, regulates cell death through interactions with various proteins, and its role in HCC is currently unclear. The present study aimed to elucidate the function of NRAGE in HCC tumorigenesis.
We analyzed resected tumor and non-cancerous liver tissues from 151 HCC patients, alongside HCC cell lines, using polymerase chain reaction and immunohistochemical techniques to investigate NRAGE expression levels and the expression of potential interacting proteins. Our results showed that NRAGE mRNA expression levels significantly correlated with those of apoptosis-antagonizing transcription factor (AATF), and were not affected by cirrhosis in non-cancerous liver tissues compared to elevated levels in HCC tissues. Consistent expression patterns were observed among 30 representative specimen pairs. Additionally, increased NRAGE expression in HCC patients correlated significantly with a shorter disease-specific survival time and was identified as an independent prognostic factor via multivariate analysis (hazard ratio, 2.23; 95% confidence interval, 1.06-3.83; P=0.020).
Our findings indicate that increased NRAGE expression affects HCC progression through its interaction with AATF, representing a potential biomarker and molecular target for the treatment of HCC.

title: Regulation of ISW2 by concerted action of histone H4 tail and extranucleosomal DNA.
text: The stable association of ISW2 with nucleosomal DNA approximately 20 bases pairs (bp) from the dyad was proven through DNA footprinting and photoaffinity labeling using recombinant histone octamers to require the histone H4 N-terminal tail. Efficient ISW2 remodeling also required the H4 N-terminal tail, although the lack of the H4 tail can be partially compensated for by prolonging the incubation time or increasing the concentration of ISW2. Similarly, the length of extranucleosomal DNA influenced the stable interaction of ISW2 with the same internal nucleosomal site, with the optimal length ranging from 70 to 85 bp. These data suggest that the histone H4 tail, working in conjunction with an optimal length of extranucleosomal DNA, brings and aligns ISW2 correctly onto the nucleosome for effective nucleosome remodeling. This characteristic of ISW2 likely underlies its previously observed ability to alter nucleosome spacing.

title: Embryonic Stem Cells for Severe Heart Failure: Why and How?
text: The experience gained in cardiac cell therapy suggests that regeneration of severely damaged myocardial areas cannot be achieved solely through the paracrine effects of grafted cells, but rather requires the converted cells to assume the function of the lost cardiomyocytes. Human pluripotent embryonic stem cells have a strong rationale in this context, as demonstrated by encouraging results in animal models of myocardial infarction. However, before this approach can be translated to clinical applications, several critical issues must be addressed, including optimizing the cardiac differentiation of embryonic stem cells, purifying the resulting progenitor cells to ensure a pure population devoid of any residual pluripotent cells that may lead to tumorigenesis, and controlling the expected allogeneic rejection using clinically acceptable methods. Meeting these prerequisites will also rely on the ability to efficiently deliver the cells to the target tissue, keep them alive once implanted, and allow them to spatially organize in a way that enhances their contractile function in the heart.

title: A comparison of letrozole to gonadotropins for ovulation induction, in subjects who failed to conceive with clomiphene citrate.
text:
Objective: To compare pregnancy rates (PR) between letrozole and gonadotropins in individuals who failed to conceive with clomiphene citrate (CC).
Design: Retrospective cohort study.
Setting: University reproductive center.
Patients: Individuals who were treated with letrozole or gonadotropins and failed to conceive with CC.
Intervention: Controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH), transvaginal ultrasound, ovulation induction, and intrauterine insemination (IUI).
Main Outcome Measure: Pregnancy rates per cycle.
Results: Among individuals who failed to conceive with at least three cycles of CC, gonadotropins had a higher PR per cycle than letrozole. However, among individuals who failed to conceive with less than three cycles of CC and whose medications were changed due to thin uterine lining or intolerable side effects, the average PR per cycle for letrozole and gonadotropin treatments were equivalent. All patients conceived within three stimulation cycles with either gonadotropins or letrozole.
Conclusion: In patients who failed to conceive with CC, gonadotropins have higher PR for ovulation induction than letrozole. However, PR were high enough with letrozole to justify its use in this population of patients. Letrozole and gonadotropins should not be used for more than three cycles without a conception.

title: Epigenetic mechanisms in neurological disease
text: The study of brain epigenomes, which encompasses various DNA methylation and histone modification patterns, is shedding new light on the mechanisms underlying neural development, neurological disorders, and aging. Historically, chromatin abnormalities in the brain were considered fixed errors that occurred early in development, confined to rare genetic syndromes. However, it has become evident that epigenetic machinery mutations and malfunctions span a wider continuum, including adult-onset neurodegenerative diseases. This work highlights how recent advances in neuroepigenetics have enhanced our understanding of the underlying mechanisms of developmental and degenerative brain disorders, and discusses how these insights may inform the development of future therapeutic strategies.

title: Reversal of the cellular phenotype in the premature aging disease Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome
text: Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) is a rare childhood disease caused by a spontaneous mutation in the LMNA gene, which codes for lamin A, a crucial structural component of the mammalian cell nucleus. This mutation triggers abnormal splicing of lamin A pre-mRNA, resulting in the production of a truncated lamin A protein and a concurrent reduction in normal lamin A levels. In HGPS fibroblasts, we observe severe nuclear morphology defects. Interestingly, we find that the cellular disease phenotype is reversible in HGPS cells, and introducing wild-type lamin A protein does not restore the symptoms. Conversely, correcting the aberrant splicing event using a custom-made oligonucleotide targeting the activated cryptic splice site can effectively eliminate the mutant LMNA mRNA and lamin A protein. Upon splicing correction, HGPS fibroblasts display normal nuclear morphology, and the aberrant nuclear distribution and cellular levels of lamina-associated proteins are restored, along with corrections in defects in heterochromatin-specific histone modifications, and proper reexpression of misregulated genes. Our findings establish the validity of correcting the premature aging phenotype in individuals with HGPS, providing a promising therapeutic approach.

title: Agouti-related peptide–expressing neurons are mandatory for feeding
text: Several hormones involved in regulating energy homeostasis influence the expression of neuropeptide Y (NPY) and agouti-related peptide (AgRP) within the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus. Despite this, inhibiting the genes responsible for producing NPY and/or AgRP does not significantly impact food intake in mice. In contrast, we have discovered that selectively ablating AgRP-producing neurons in adult mice leads to a sudden decrease in feeding, providing strong evidence of their direct role in regulating energy homeostasis.

title: Predictors of survival after acute paraquat poisoning.
text: The study investigated the predictors of survival after acute paraquat poisoning in 602 patients. The findings revealed that young age, exposure to paraquat through the percutaneous or inhalational route, and lower levels of paraquat exposure were associated with increased chances of survival. Additionally, the study found that lower degrees of leukocytosis, acidosis, and renal, hepatic, and pancreatic failures at the time of emergency room arrival were also indicative of improved survival outcomes. The study concluded that these factors can be used as prognostic markers to identify patients who are likely to survive acute paraquat poisoning.

title: Decreased neurogenesis after cholinergic forebrain lesion in the adult rat.
text: Adult neurogenesis is regulated by various extracellular cues, including hormones, growth factors, and neurotransmitters. The cholinergic system of the basal forebrain is a key player in this process, as it is involved in learning and memory. To investigate the role of cholinergic input in adult neurogenesis, we used an immunotoxin approach to selectively lesion cholinergic neurons in the basal forebrain of adult rats. Five weeks after lesioning, we observed a significant decline in neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus and olfactory bulb, as evidenced by a decrease in the number of BrdU-labeled cells and NeuN-positive neurons. Additionally, we found an increase in apoptotic cells in the subgranular zone, the progenitor region of the dentate gyrus, and within the periglomerular layer of the olfactory bulb. These results suggest that the cholinergic system plays a vital role in promoting the survival of neuronal progenitors and immature neurons in regions of adult neurogenesis, similar to its role during brain development. We propose that neuronal loss within the cholinergic system leads not only to cognitive deficits but may also alter the functionality of the dentate gyrus, which can exacerbate cognitive deficits.

title: DNA Methylation in Major Depressive Disorder.
text: Epigenetic processes regulate gene expression, influencing protein levels and ultimately shaping an individual's phenotype over the course of their life. However, both random epigenetic variations and environmental changes to the epigenome may impact neurodevelopment and aging, which could contribute to the origins of mental illness. Investigating the role of epigenetic mechanisms is complex, as genotype, tissue, and cell type-specific epigenetic changes must be considered, while the nature of mental disorders also presents significant challenges in linking them to biological profiles. In this chapter, we review the current evidence suggesting DNA methylation as a crucial epigenetic mechanism involved in major depressive disorder.

title: Consensus structural features of purified bacterial TatABC complexes.
text:
The following is a rewritten version of the given text:
The Twin-Arginine Translocation (Tat) system facilitates the transport of folded proteins across membranes in bacteria, including the plasma membrane and chloroplast thylakoid membrane. In this study, we investigate the composition and structural organization of three purified Tat complexes from Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhimurium, and Agrobacterium tumefaciens using various biochemical techniques.
We first demonstrate the functional activity of these Tat systems in vivo by expressing the tatABC operons from S.typhimurium or A.tumefaciens in an E. coli tat null mutant strain, which resulted in efficient export of an E. coli cofactor-containing substrate, TMAO reductase, using the Tat system. The three isolated, affinity-tagged Tat complexes consisted of TatA, TatB, and TatC in each case, indicating a robust interaction between these subunits.
Using single-particle electron microscopy, we observed oval-shaped, asymmetric particles with maxima dimensions up to 13 nanometers. A common feature of these particles is the presence of stain-excluding densities surrounding a central pool of stain, suggesting the presence of protein-lined pores or cavities. The variations in particle size suggest a modular form of assembly and/or recruitment of varying numbers of TatBC/TatA units.
Despite low levels of sequence homology, the combined data indicate both structural and functional conservation in the Tat systems of these three bacterial species.

title: Advances in graft-versus-host disease biology and therapy
text: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is used to treat a range of disorders, but its effectiveness is constrained by the risk of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). The past decade has witnessed significant progress in our comprehension of the interplay between the immune systems of the donor and recipient in the development of GVHD, with important insights emerging from both basic immunology and clinical studies. New findings have led to the development of novel strategies aimed at preventing and treating GVHD, including manipulations of the immune system that are poised for clinical application. This Review highlights the recent advances in our understanding of GVHD pathogenesis and the various approaches being explored to combat this complication.

title: Ly6Chi monocytes direct alternatively activated profibrotic macrophage regulation of lung fibrosis.
text:
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a devastating disease with no effective treatments. The role of monocytes and macrophages in lung fibrogenesis and resolution is controversial and requires further investigation. To address this question, we conducted experiments using in vivo depletion strategies and adoptive transfer techniques, as well as analyzing lung tissue samples from patients with IPF.
Our findings demonstrate the crucial role of lung macrophages in pulmonary fibrosis, as depletion of these cells during fibrogenesis led to reduction in fibrosis markers, such as lung collagen, fibrosis score, and surrogate markers of fibrosis, including Col1 and a-smooth muscle actin. Furthermore, we found that the alternative macrophage activation phenotype, marked by the expression of Ym1, was downregulated in depleted macrophages. Notably, we also identified the alternative macrophage marker CD163 on lung macrophages from patients with IPF.
In contrast, depletion of circulating monocytes reduced pulmonary fibrosis and the number of Ym1-positive alternatively activated lung macrophages. However, adoptively transferred Ly6Chi cells were not observed in the lungs of recipient mice. Our results highlight the significant contribution of circulating monocytes to the progression of pulmonary fibrosis.
Additionally, we discovered that macrophages may have a resolution-promoting role during the reversible phase of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, suggesting that targeting these cells may be a potential therapeutic strategy for IPF. In conclusion, our study underscores the critical function of monocytes and macrophages in lung fibrogenesis and highlights the potential of targeting these cells for the treatment of IPF.

title: A single RNA-dependent RNA polymerase assembles with mutually exclusive nucleotidyl transferase subunits to direct different pathways of small RNA biogenesis.
text: Members of the conserved family of eukaryotic RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (Rdrs) play a critical role in the synthesis of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) intermediates in various pathways of small RNA (sRNA) biogenesis and RNA-mediated silencing. While the Rdr-dependent pathways of sRNA production are less well-understood compared to Rdr-independent processes, the Rdr enzymes themselves are also less characterized than their viral counterparts. Previous studies have shown the physical and functional coupling of the Tetrahymena thermophila Rdr, Rdr1, with the Dicer enzyme, Dcr2, in the production of approximately 24-nucleotide (nt) sRNA in vitro. In this study, we investigate the endogenous complexes that harbor Rdr1, termed RDRCs. We find that RDRCs assemble into distinct subcomplexes containing Rdr1 and subsets of the four tightly Rdr1-associated proteins. Of particular interest are the two RDRC subunits, Rdn1 and Rdn2, which possess noncanonical ribonucleotidyl transferase motifs and function as uridine-specific polymerases in separate RDRCs. Additionally, we identify two additional RDRC subunits, Rdf1 and Rdf2, which are present only in RDRCs containing Rdn1. Our findings reveal a complex structure of Rdr-dependent sRNA biogenesis in vivo, with specific disruption of each RDRC subunit leading to distinct loss-of-function consequences at the cellular level. The biochemical and biological phenotypes of RDRC subunit disruption demonstrate a previously unappreciated complexity in the Rdr-dependent pathway of sRNA biogenesis.

title: Identification of T6SS-dependent effector and immunity proteins by Tn-seq in Vibrio cholerae.
text:
The Type VI protein secretion system (T6SS) plays a crucial role in bacterial competition through direct killing of adjacent cells. T6SS transfers effectors to neighboring cells, while cognate immunity proteins offer protection against these effectors produced by sister cells. Although T6SS has been observed in over 100 gram-negative bacteria, including key human pathogens, relatively few T6SS-dependent effector and immunity proteins have been experimentally identified. Here, we employ a high-throughput approach featuring transposon mutagenesis and deep sequencing (Tn-seq) to identify T6SS immunity proteins in Vibrio cholerae.
Saturation transposon mutagenesis was performed in both wild-type and T6SS-deficient V. cholerae. Genes encoding immunity proteins were found to be essential in the wild type but non-essential in the T6SS null mutant. By comparing the relative abundance of each transposon mutant in the mutant library via deep sequencing, we identified three immunity proteins that provide protection against killing by T6SS-predatory cells. Furthermore, we identified their cognate T6SS-secreted effectors and demonstrated that these are not only essential for antibacterial and antioxidant activities but also for assembly of the T6SS apparatus. The lipase and muramidase T6SS effectors identified in this study highlight the diversity of T6SS-secreted substrates and the distinct mechanisms employed to target these substrates for secretion by the dynamic T6SS organelle.

title: Immunotherapy of metastatic kidney cancer.
text: From April 1986 to September 2000, 122 patients with Metastatic Renal Cell Cancer (MRCC) were treated with monthly intralymphatic injections of interleukin-2 (IL-2) and interferon (IFN), as well as intravenous (i.m.) administration of IL-2 and tumor necrosis factor (TF); 71 patients also received a 3-day cycle of monthly IL-2 inhalations. This treatment protocol was compared to 89 MRCC cases that were not treated with immunotherapy, serving as historical controls. The adverse clinical side effects associated with treatment were minimal. The study found that 24/122 patients (11%), including 11 patients who achieved a complete response (CR) and 13 patients who achieved a partial response (PR), experienced a reduction in tumor size. Of the 24 responding patients, 17 experienced a relapse, while 7 remained in remission for 11-69 months. The overall median survival of treated patients (28 months) was significantly higher than the median survival of historical controls (7.5 months), with a Kaplan-Meier curve showing 25% survival rate after 11 years. The addition of IL-2 by inhalation appeared to improve survival. The currently used immunotherapy protocol was found to be safe, without significant adverse side effects, and relatively inexpensive compared to other treatments. If confirmed in a multicenter trial, it could provide a basis for developing low-dose immunomodulatory treatments for MRCC patients, improving their quality of life.

title: Autoimmune T cell responses in the central nervous system
text: Autoreactive T cell responses play a significant role in central nervous system (CNS) disorders such as multiple sclerosis. Recent studies have revealed that CNS autoimmunity can be triggered by two distinct subtypes of CD4+ T cells, which are defined by their production of either interferon-γ or interleukin-17. The activity of these CD4+ T cell subsets within the CNS has a profound impact on the progression of disease. Recent animal studies have also shown that myelin-specific CD8+ T cells can also contribute to CNS autoimmunity. This review aims to summarize the latest findings in the field, including the mechanisms of pathogenesis, regulation, and interplay between these different T cell subsets in CNS autoimmune disorders.

title: Effects of FXR in foam-cell formation and atherosclerosis development.
text: The bile-acid-activated nuclear receptor Farnesoid X receptor (FXR) plays a crucial role in regulating bile acid, cholesterol, and triglyceride homeostasis. Mutations in the FXR gene have been linked to increased serum cholesterol and triglyceride levels, but the role of FXR in the formation of foam cells and the development of atherosclerosis is not fully understood. In this study, we found that peritoneal macrophages from FXR-deficient mice had reduced expression of the CD36 protein and took up less oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL-C). This result suggests that FXR may not directly modulate atherosclerosis development. To further investigate this, we generated FXR/apolipoprotein E (ApoE) double-null mice and found that they had significantly fewer atherosclerotic lesions in the aorta compared to ApoE-null mice, despite elevated serum cholesterol and triglyceride levels. Our results suggest that disrupting the FXR gene may attenuate atherosclerosis development, likely due to reduced oxLDL-C uptake by macrophages. These findings caution against relying solely on serum lipid levels as a marker of the effectiveness of FXR modulators in treating hyperlipidemia.

title: Purkinje cell compartments in the reeler mutant mouse as revealed by Zebrin II and 90-acetylated glycolipid antigen expression
text: The cerebellum is divided into distinct bands that can be visualized histologically in adult mice through the use of complementary immunostaining techniques with monoclonal antibodies. Specifically, the antibody Zebrin II (ZII) highlights Purkinje cell sets, while the antibody P-path (PP) identifies 90-acetyl glycolipids on these cells. To compare the normal staining pattern in these markers and that found in reeler mutants (rl/rl), in which Purkinje cell migration is impaired beneath the cerebellar white matter, we examined the distribution of Purkinje cells. We found that Purkinje cells in reeler mutants tended to segregate into alternating zones that are either Zebrin II-positive or P-path-positive, with transition zones of mixed labeling. However, the number of zones observed in the mutants was significantly lower than in normal adult mice, with roughly 7-9 zones per side compared to 14 major divisions in wild-type mice. These findings suggest that neurons destined to express these markers may be separated during their migration, with the final stage of migration involving further splitting or interaction between cell sets expressing the two markers.

title: Awake craniotomy with brain mapping as the routine surgical approach to treating patients with supratentorial intraaxial tumors: a prospective trial of 200 cases.
text: In a prospective clinical trial of 200 patients undergoing surgical treatment for supratentorial intraaxial tumors at a single institution, an awake craniotomy was performed as the standard surgical approach regardless of the involvement of eloquent cortex. Brain mapping was possible in 195 (97.5%) of the patients, and the overall complication rate was 16.5% with three deaths (1%). New postoperative neurological deficits occurred in 13% of patients, but were permanent in only 4.5%. The complication rate was higher in patients with gliomas, preoperative neurological deficits, or a history of prior radiation therapy or surgery. Importantly, none of the patients who entered the operating room neurologically intact experienced a permanent neurological deficit postoperatively. In the most recent 50 patients treated, three (6%) required a stay in the intensive care unit, and the median total hospital stay was 1 day. The study demonstrates that the use of awake craniotomy can significantly reduce resource utilization without compromising patient care, with a low complication rate and the ability to perform brain mapping while avoiding general anesthesia.

title: Reactive Oxygen Species Localization Programs Inflammation to Clear Microbes of Different Size
text: The manner in which the number of immune cells recruited to infected areas is determined and modified to account for differences in cellular composition between host and pathogen is unknown. Our research revealed a role for reactive oxygen species (ROS) as sensors of microbe size. When microbes vary in size, neutrophils detect this variation by sensing local ROS levels, then modulate their interleukin (IL)-1β expression through selective oxidation of NF-κB. This enables the implementation of distinct inflammatory programs. When microbes are small, they generate intracellular ROS, which inhibits IL-1β expression, limiting neutrophil recruitment since each phagocyte eliminates many pathogens. In contrast, large microbes generate extracellular ROS, amplifying IL-1β expression, attracting numerous neutrophils to form cooperative clusters. Abnormalities in ROS-mediated microbe size sensing result in excessive neutrophil infiltration and clusters in response to small microbes, contributing to inflammatory diseases. These findings highlight the significance of ROS localization in signal transduction.

title: Helicobacter pylori infection triggers aberrant expression of activation-induced cytidine deaminase in gastric epithelium
text: Infection with Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a known risk factor for the development of gastric cancer. Our study shows that infection of gastric epithelial cells with 'cag' pathogenicity island (cagPAI)-positive H. pylori leads to abnormal expression of the activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) enzyme, which belongs to the cytidine-deaminase family and acts as a DNA- and RNA-editing enzyme. This upregulation of AID is mediated by the IκB kinase–dependent nuclear factor-κB activation pathway. Our findings suggest that H. pylori infection leads to an accumulation of nucleotide alterations in the TP53 tumor suppressor gene in gastric cells in vitro, which may be a mechanism of mutation accumulation in the gastric mucosa during H. pylori-associated gastric carcinogenesis.

title: The role of the immune response during SIVagm infection of the African green monkey natural host.
text: The African green monkey (AGM) is one of numerous African species naturally infected with the simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV). Unlike other hosts, AGMs do not typically develop AIDS, and understanding the factors behind this resistance could have significant theoretical and practical implications. Initial efforts by our group to identify immune mechanisms that keep the virus under control failed to reveal any obvious candidates, as the presumption that the virus was being held in check was later shown to be false when it was found that SIVagm replicates with similar vigor in AGMs as HIV-1 does in humans. Consequently, the focus shifted to identifying any immunopathologic features that may be present in disease-susceptible hosts but absent in the AGM's natural host. The AGM's apparent tolerance of the SIVagm core protein led to the development of a hypothesis suggesting that anti-Gag antibodies play a role in trapping the virus in the lymph nodes and impairing the immune system. However, testing this idea in vivo has proven challenging and the current research focuses on the possibility that immune tolerance at the T-cell level may also contribute to the AGM's resistance to immunodeficiency virus infection.

title: The S-LANSS score for identifying pain of predominantly neuropathic origin: validation for use in clinical and postal research.
text: The present study aimed to develop and validate a self-report version of the Leeds Assessment of Neuropathic Symptoms and Signs (LANSS) pain scale, known as the S-LANSS. The S-LANSS was designed to identify pain of primarily neuropathic origin without the need for clinical examination. To validate the S-LANSS, two hundred patients with chronic pain completed the scale unaided, and a researcher then administered the S-LANSS and Neuropathic Pain Scale (NPS) in an interview format. An independent clinician determined the pain type and rated the certainty of the diagnosis. The S-LANSS was also incorporated into a chronic pain questionnaire that was sent to 160 community patients and 150 newly referred patients waiting for pain clinic assessment. The results showed that the S-LANSS correctly identified 75% of pain types when self-completed and 80% when used in an interview format. The sensitivity of the self-completed S-LANSS scores ranged from 74% to 78%, depending on the cutoff score. Significant associations were found between the NPS items and total score with the S-LANSS score. In the postal survey, 57% of patients completed the questionnaire, resulting in internally consistent and convergent valid results. The findings support the S-LANSS as a valid and reliable self-report instrument for identifying neuropathic pain, which can be used in survey research. The development of standardized measures of symptoms and signs in neuropathic pain will enable comparisons across investigational measures, leading to new insights into the relationship between the pathophysiological mechanisms and the clinical manifestations of pain.

title: Bias in meta-analysis detected by a simple, graphical test.
text: Funnel plots (diagrams depicting the relationship between effect estimates and sample size) may serve as a useful tool for identifying potential bias in meta-analyses that were later contradicted by larger trials. In this study, we examined whether a simple test of asymmetry in funnel plots can predict disagreement between meta-analysis results and those of large trials. We evaluated the prevalence of bias in published meta-analyses and analyzed funnel plots from 37 meta-analyses identified through a manual search of four leading general medicine journals from 1993 to 1996 and 38 meta-analyses from the second issue of the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 1996. Our primary outcome measure was the degree of funnel plot asymmetry, which we assessed using the intercept from regressing standard normal deviates against precision. In the eight pairs of meta-analysis and large trial that were identified (five from cardiovascular medicine, one from diabetic medicine, one from geriatric medicine, and one from perinatal medicine), there were four concordant and four discordant pairs. In all cases, discordance was attributable to meta-analyses showing larger effects. Funnel plot asymmetry was present in three of the discordant pairs, but none of the concordant pairs. In 14 (38%) of the journal meta-analyses and 5 (13%) of the Cochrane reviews, funnel plot asymmetry indicated that there was bias. Our findings suggest that a simple analysis of funnel plots can serve as a useful test for detecting potential bias in meta-analyses, but the ability to detect bias will be limited when meta-analyses are based on a small number of trials, and the results of such analyses should be treated with caution.

title: Exploring Metabolic Configurations of Single Cells within Complex Tissue Microenvironments.
text: Over the past years, significant evidence has accumulated highlighting the crucial role of metabolism in various cellular processes and its potential to drive cellular differentiation and fate. In this study, we present a novel method enabling the assessment of the metabolic profile of individual cells in their native tissue microenvironment by visualizing and quantifying multiple enzymatic activities at saturating substrate conditions, followed by cell type identification. We conducted extensive validation of the technique to demonstrate its potential and then applied it to analyze the metabolic configurations of different human immune cell populations in healthy and tumor colon tissue. Additionally, we investigated the intercellular metabolic interactions between cancer cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts in a breast cancer tissue array. This work demonstrates the potential of determining metabolic configurations in single cells as a valuable tool for researchers seeking to elucidate metabolic networks in situ.

title: Twenty-four hour and early morning blood pressure control of olmesartan vs. ramipril in elderly hypertensive patients: pooled individual data analysis of two randomized, double-blind, parallel-group studies.
text: Objective: To compare the antihypertensive efficacy of olmesartan medoxomil and ramipril on 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure (ABP) in elderly hypertensive patients. Methods: In a double-blind, randomized controlled study, 1453 elderly hypertensive patients (65-89 years) with sitting office blood pressure (DBP) of 90-109 mmHg and/or sitting office systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 140-179 mmHg were enrolled. After a 2-week placebo wash-out, patients were randomized to 12-week double-blind treatment with olmesartan medoxomil (10 mg or up-titrated to 20 or 40 mg) or ramipril (2.5 mg or up-titrated to 5 or 10 mg). ABP was recorded at baseline and end of treatment. Results: In 715 patients with valid baseline and end-of-treatment ABP recordings, baseline-adjusted ABP reductions were greater with olmesartan medoxomil than with ramipril. Olmesartan medoxomil showed larger BP reductions in the last 6 hours of the dosing interval and higher smoothness indices compared to ramipril. Olmesartan medoxomil also reduced the morning SBP rise, while ramipril did not. In patients with sustained hypertension (office and 24-hour hypertension), the largest antihypertensive effect was observed with olmesartan medoxomil. Conclusions: Olmesartan medoxomil provided more effective and sustained 24-hour BP control than ramipril in elderly hypertensive patients, particularly in the hours farthest from last intake.

title: Abi1 is essential for the formation and activation of a WAVE2 signalling complex
text: The WAVE2 protein belongs to a family of proteins that facilitate actin reorganization by transmitting signals from Rac to the Arp2/3 complex, leading to lamellipodia protrusion. WAVE2 displays actin nucleation activity when in vitro, and it does not directly bind to Rac. Instead, it forms complexes with other proteins that regulate its activity in vivo. The present study employs mass spectrometry to identify a complex containing WAVE2, Nap1 (Nck-associated protein), and PIR121, which is mediated by Abi1. Abi1 interacts directly with the WHD domain of WAVE2 and increases its actin polymerization activity, enabling the formation of a WAVE2-Abi1-Nap1-PIR121 complex. This complex is as effective as a sub-complex containing only WAVE2 and Abi1 in stimulating the Arp2/3 complex, and upon Rac activation, it is relocalized to the leading edge of ruffles in vivo. Inhibition of Abi1 by RNA interference (RNAi) impairs Rac-dependent lamellipodia protrusion, highlighting the crucial role of Abi1 in orchestrating the assembly and activation of the WAVE2 complex in vivo.

title: The dendritic cell lineage: ontogeny and function of dendritic cells and their subsets in the steady state and the inflamed setting.
text: Dendritic cells (DCs) comprise an impressive cellular network that influences the adaptive immune response according to local cues. Following decades of research, we have come to understand that DCs originate from a distinct hematopoietic lineage compared to other white blood cells, thus establishing the DC system as a separate hematopoietic branch. Recent investigations have also revealed that tissue DCs are composed of different developmentally and functionally distinct subsets, each with a unique role in modulating T lymphocyte activity. This review highlights significant advances in our understanding of the regulation of DC lineage commitment, differentiation, variety, and function in their native environment.

title: IL-15 Receptor Deletion Results in Circadian Changes of Locomotor and Metabolic Activity
text:
The cytokine interleukin-15 (IL-15) is produced in the brain and acts on specific receptors IL-15Rα, IL-2Rβ, and IL-2Rγ in neuronal cells. However, the functions of the cerebral IL-15 system are not yet fully understood. To investigate, we examined the metabolic phenotype of IL-15Rα knockout mice, which were leaner with lower fat composition. Interestingly, these mice showed a significantly higher acrophase in locomotor activity and heat dissipation throughout the day-night cycle. Specifically, during the light phase, there was a significant increase in food intake, oxygen consumption, and carbon dioxide production compared to the control mice. notably, this difference between the light and dark phases suggests that IL-15Rα plays a role in circadian rhythm regulation. Furthermore, the higher oxygen consumption in the light phase suggests adaptive thermogenesis in the knockout mice. qPCR analysis of hypothalamic homogenates revealed higher mRNA expression of orexin and transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 cation channels, supporting a direct role of IL-15Rα in the hypothalamus. Consistently, IL-15 treatment of wild-type mice induced c-Fos expression in the preoptic area, suggesting that activation of hypothalamic neurons by IL-15 contributes to thermoregulation and alters the metabolic phenotype.
In summary, the study demonstrates that the IL-15Rα pathway plays a key role in regulating metabolic activity and body temperature in mice, and provides new insights into the complex interplay between the brain and metabolism.

title: Vaginal progesterone, cerclage or cervical pessary for preventing preterm birth in asymptomatic singleton pregnant women with a history of preterm birth and a sonographic short cervix.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of different management protocols for women with singleton pregnancy, previous spontaneous preterm birth, and short cervix, using cerclage, vaginal progesterone, or cervical pessary.
Methods: This study compared the perinatal outcomes of 142 women treated with cerclage (USA), 59 with vaginal progesterone (UK), and 42 with cervical pessary (Spain) after identifying high-risk pregnancies due to a prior spontaneous preterm birth before 34 weeks and shortened cervical length detected by transvaginal ultrasound.
Results: Although there were no significant differences in perinatal losses, neonatal morbidity, and preterm births among the three groups, a higher rate of preterm birth before 34 weeks' gestation was observed in women treated with vaginal progesterone compared to those treated with cervical pessary (32% vs 12%, relative risk (RR) = 2.70, 95% CI, 1.10-6.67). When only the subgroups of women with cervical length < 25 mm, irrespective of gestational age, were compared, the difference between these two cohorts was not statistically significant (RR = 2.21; 95% CI, 0.83-5.89).
Conclusion: The study suggests that cerclage, vaginal progesterone, and pessary are similarly effective management strategies in women with singleton pregnancy, previous spontaneous preterm birth, and short cervix. Further randomized comparisons of these strategies or combinations thereof are needed to determine the optimal management approach.

title: The oxytocinase subfamily of M1 aminopeptidases.
text: The subfamily of enzymes known as the "Oxytocinase subfamily" consists of three distinct members: placental leucine aminopeptidase (P-LAP), adipocyte-derived leucine aminopeptidase (A-LAP), and leukocyte-derived aminopeptidase (L-RAP). These enzymes belong to the M1 family of aminopeptidases and share significant structural features, including HEXXH(X)18E Zn-binding and GAMEN motifs, which are essential for their enzymatic activities. What sets this subfamily apart is their intracellular localization, which is characteristic of its members. While P-LAP is transported from intracellular vesicles to the plasma membrane in a stimulus-dependent manner, A-LAP and L-RAP remain retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, with sequences that enable their specific localization within the cell. It is becoming evident that the Oxytocinase subfamily plays important roles in maintaining homeostasis, including the stability of normal pregnancy, memory retention, blood pressure regulation, and antigen presentation. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge regarding this newly identified subfamily of enzymes.

title: Myc represses primitive endoderm differentiation in pluripotent stem cells.
text: The generation of induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) offers a novel means of investigating the mechanisms that govern stem cell pluripotency and self-renewal. Previous studies have shown that Myc is crucial for maintaining murine embryonic stem cells (mESCs) and enhancing the reprogramming of fibroblasts through widespread changes in gene expression. However, the specific mechanism by which Myc regulates pluripotency remains unclear. Here, we report that deleting c- and N-MYC in iPSCs and ESCs leads to their spontaneous differentiation into primitive endoderm. We found that Myc sustains pluripotency by repressing the primitive endoderm master regulator GATA6, and also contributes to cell cycle control by regulating the mir-17-92 miRNA cluster. Our findings demonstrate the absolute necessity of c- or N-myc for pluripotency beyond proliferative and metabolic control.

title: [Vitamin D and latitude as environmental factors in multiple sclerosis].
text: Multiple sclerosis (MS) exhibits a notable increase in prevalence as one moves north or south of the equator, suggesting a multifaceted relationship with latitude. One possible factor contributing to this disparity is vitamin D, as the strength of ambient ultraviolet light, which is essential for vitamin D production, decreases with increasing latitude. It is well established that vitamin D has immunomodulatory functions and has been shown to suppress an animal model of MS. Additionally, vitamin D-related genes are believed to be critical susceptibility genes for MS. To further elucidate the connection between vitamin D and MS, an interdisciplinary approach that incorporates environmental and genetic factors is warranted.

title: Type 2 cytokines: mechanisms and therapeutic strategies
text: Type 2 immune responses are characterized by the cytokines interleukin-4 (IL-4), IL-5, IL-9, and IL-13, which can either exhibit host-protective or pathogenic activity, depending on the context. Type 2 immunity is linked to antihelminth immunity, autoimmune disease prevention, toxin neutralization, metabolic homeostasis maintenance, and wound repair and tissue regeneration regulation following infection or injury. However, when type 2 immune responses are dysregulated, they can become pivotal drivers of disease. Type 2 immunity elicits a multifaceted inflammatory response involving eosinophils, mast cells, basophils, type 2 innate lymphoid cells, IL-4- and/or IL-13-conditioned macrophages, and T helper 2 (TH2) cells, which are crucial in the pathogenesis of various allergic and fibrotic disorders. Chronic type 2 immune responses can promote disease, and the mechanisms that regulate their maintenance are believed to serve as vital disease modifiers. This Review pinpoints the intricate endogenous negative regulatory mechanisms that counteract type 2 immunity and highlights the development of therapies targeting these pathways to address type 2-mediated disease.

title: Implanted microvessels progress through distinct neovascularization phenotypes.
text:
In our previous work, we demonstrated that implanted microvessels form a new microcirculation with minimal reliance on host-derived vessel growth. Our aim was to identify the distinct vascular phenotypes that emerge during neovascularization in these implants and investigate post-angiogenesis events. Using morphological, functional, and transcriptional assessments, we identified three distinct vascular phenotypes in the implants: sprouting angiogenesis, neovascular remodeling, and network maturation.
Initially, a sprouting angiogenic phenotype appeared, characterized by high proliferation rates and low mural cell coverage. This was followed by a neovascular remodeling phenotype, marked by a perfused, disorganized neovascular network, reduced proliferation, and re-association of mural cells. The final phenotype consisted of a mature vascular network organized into a stereotypical tree structure, with vessels having normal perivascular cell associations. Additionally, proliferation was low and only occurred in the walls of larger microvessels. We observed a correlation between the transition from angiogenesis to neovascular remodeling and the establishment of blood flow in the implant neovasculature. Gene expression analysis revealed that the intermediate, neovascular remodeling phenotype is transcriptionally distinct from the other two phenotypes, indicating that it represents a distinct vascular phenotype involving unique cellular and vascular processes. Furthermore, this neovascular remodeling phase may be a normal aspect of the general neovascularization process. Given that this phenotype is potentially dysfunctional, many of the microvasculatures present within compromised or diseased tissues may not simply be failure to progress through a normally occurring neovascularization phenotype.

title: Characterization of a highly variable eutherian microRNA gene.
text: Mouse microRNAs miR-290-miR295 are encoded by a cluster of partially homologous pre-miRNA hairpin sequences and play a crucial role in embryonic stem (ES) cells and preimplantation embryos. We have found evidence that a single, spliced, capped, and polyadenylated primary transcript spans the entire Early Embryonic microRNA Cluster (EEmiRC). Processing by Drosha yields additional large nuclear RNA intermediates. A conserved promoter element containing a TATA-box directs EEmiRC transcription. Analyzing the sequence of the EEmiRC transcription unit reveals remarkable variability, and it can only be identified bioinformatically in placental (eutherian) mammals. Consistently, EEmiRC is expressed in trophoblastic stem (TS) cells. When examining the evolutionary and functional relationships between these genes, it is essential to consider the organization of the entire miRNA locus in addition to the mature miRNA sequences. This reevaluation suggests that EEmiRC is a recently evolved, rapidly changing gene that plays a crucial role in eutherian development.

title: The function of follicular helper T cells is regulated by the strength of T cell antigen receptor binding
text:
Understanding how follicular helper T cells (TFH cells) differentiate to regulate B cell immunity is crucial for effective protein vaccination. In this study, we identify and characterize three distinct subsets of TFH cells based on their transcription factor expression and functional properties.
Using a combination of in vitro and in vivo experiments, we find that TFH cells can be divided into three subsets: 'lymphoid' effector helper T cells (CD62LhiCCR7hi), 'emigrant' effector helper T cells (CXCR5lo), and 'resident' TFH cells expressing the transcriptional repressor Bcl-6 (CD62LloCCR7lo).
We observe that the subset of TFH cells with the highest specific binding of peptide-major histocompatibility complex class II and the most restricted T cell antigen receptor junctional diversity 'preferentially' develops into the antigen-specific effector TFH compartment.
Our findings demonstrate a crucial role for differences in the binding strength of the T cell antigen receptor in the antigen-specific mechanisms that 'program' specialized effector TFH function in vivo. This study highlights the importance of understanding the differentiation and function of TFH cells in the context of protein vaccination.

title: Disruption of tumor necrosis factor-alpha gene diminishes the development of atherosclerosis in ApoE-deficient mice.
text: The cytokine tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha) has been implicated in the development of atherosclerosis, but its specific role in this process is not fully understood. To investigate the effect of TNF-alpha on atherogenesis, we generated mice lacking both apolipoprotein E (apoE) and TNF-alpha (apoE-/-/TNF-alpha-/-) and compared them with apoE-/- mice. Despite similar levels of serum total cholesterol between the two groups, we observed a significant reduction in atherosclerotic plaque area in the aortic luminal surface of apoE-/-/TNF-alpha-/- mice. Additionally, the atherosclerotic lesion size in the aortic sinus of apoE-/-/TNF-alpha-/- mice was significantly smaller than that of apoE-/- mice. RT-PCR analysis revealed that the expression levels of intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) were higher in apoE-/- mice than in apoE-/-/TNF-alpha-/- mice. Furthermore, macrophages from apoE(-/-) mice showed higher levels of oxidized LDL uptake and increased expression of scavenger receptor class A (SRA) compared to those from apoE-/-/TNF-alpha-/- mice. These findings suggest that TNF-alpha plays an atherogenic role by upregulating the expression of adhesion molecules and chemoattractants in the vascular wall, and by inducing SRA expression and oxidized LDL uptake in macrophages.

title: Differential expression of bcl-2 and susceptibility to anti-Fas-mediated cell death in peripheral blood lymphocytes, monocytes, and neutrophils.
text: Newly discovered Fas antigen (Ag) is a cell surface molecule involved in apoptosis. Previous research showed that cytoplasmic product of proto-oncogene bcl-2 can prolong cell survival by inhibiting apoptosis. To understand the functional implications of both molecules' expression, we examined Fas Ag and bcl-2 expression on blood leukocyte populations and tested their sensitivity to cytotoxic effects of anti-Fas antibody. While Fas Ag was expressed in some lymphocytes, both neutrophils and monocytes expressed Fas Ag constantly. Conversely, there was a notable difference in bcl-2 expression among these leukocytes. Lymphocytes had high levels of bcl-2, while monocytes had weaker expression, and neutrophils were almost completely devoid of bcl-2. This disparity in bcl-2 expression corresponded with the differential sensitivity of these leukocytes to anti-Fas antibody. Neutrophils were more susceptible to undergoing apoptotic cell death after exposure to the antibody, while monocytes and lymphocytes exhibited much less susceptibility. These findings suggest that the cell death induced by anti-Fas antibody may be in part determined by the expression of bcl-2 in Fas+ lymphoid and hematopoietic cells.

title: Foxp2 and Foxp1 cooperatively regulate lung and esophagus development.
text: The lung's airways develop through a complex process of branching morphogenesis, generating the intricate and extensive surface area necessary for postnatal respiration. Two forkhead transcription factors, Foxp2 and Foxp1, are expressed in multiple foregut-derived tissues, including the lung and intestine. In this study, we demonstrate that loss of Foxp2 in mice impairs postnatal lung alveolarization, leading to postnatal lethality. Our findings show that T1alpha, a gene essential for lung development and function, is directly regulated by Foxp2 and Foxp1. Remarkably, loss of a single Foxp1 allele in addition to complete loss of Foxp2 results in more severe morphological defects in mutant lungs and leads to perinatal loss of all Foxp2(-/-);Foxp1(+/-) mice. Expression of N-myc and Hop, crucial regulators of lung development, is compromised in Foxp2(-/-);Foxp1(+/-) mutants. Additionally, Foxp2 and Foxp1 are also essential for the development of the esophageal muscle, as their co-expression is disrupted in Foxp2(-/-);Foxp1(+/-) embryos. These findings highlight the critical role of Foxp2 and Foxp1 in the development of anterior foregut-derived tissues, underscoring the essentiality of these transcription factors in these processes. Co-expression of Foxp1 and Foxp2 in these tissues demonstrates functional cooperativity between members of the Foxp1/2/4 family.

title: Crystal structure of the eukaryotic 60S ribosomal subunit in complex with initiation factor 6.
text: All organisms rely on ribosomes to synthesize protein. However, eukaryotic ribosomes are larger and more complexly regulated than their prokaryotic counterparts. The 60S ribosomal subunit, specifically, plays a crucial role in catalyzing peptide bond formation and houses the nascent polypeptide exit tunnel. We have crystallized the structure of the 60S ribosomal subunit from Tetrahymena thermophila in complex with eukaryotic initiation factor 6 (eIF6) and the antibiotic cycloheximide (a eukaryotic-specific inhibitor of protein synthesis) at a resolution of 3.5 angstroms. This structure reveals the intricate network of interactions between eukaryotic-specific ribosomal protein features and RNA expansion segments that comprise the eukaryotic 60S subunit. It also highlights the roles of eukaryotic ribosomal protein elements in maintaining the active site and the extent of eukaryotic-specific differences in other functional regions of the subunit. Furthermore, the structure provides insights into the molecular basis of the interaction with eIF6 and serves as a structural framework for investigating ribosome-associated diseases and the initiation of protein synthesis.

title: Hedgehog signaling regulates brain tumor-initiating cell proliferation and portends shorter survival for patients with PTEN-coexpressing glioblastomas.
text: The discovery of brain tumor stem-like cells (BTSCs) has suggested that self-renewal mechanisms play a role in the initiation and progression of brain tumors. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the tumor-forming capacity of BTSCs remain unknown. To investigate, we analyzed gene expression profiles of BTSCs and identified both Sonic Hedgehog (SHH)-dependent and -independent BTSCs, as well as their respective glioblastoma surgical specimens. We found that BTSC proliferation could be inhibited in a pathway-dependent manner in vitro and in an intracranial tumor model in athymic mice. Both SHH-dependent and -independent brain tumor growth required phosphoinositide 3-kinase-mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K-mTOR) signaling. Interestingly, we discovered that levels of SHH and patched 1 (PTCH1) were significantly higher in PTEN-expressing tumors than in PTEN-deficient tumors. Furthermore, we found that hyperactive SHH-GLI signaling in PTEN-coexpressing human GBMs was associated with reduced survival time. These findings suggest that distinct proliferation signaling dependence may underlie glioblastoma propagation by BTSCs. Understanding these mechanisms may provide a basis for individualized glioblastoma treatment.

title: Stress and host immunity amplify Mycobacterium tuberculosis phenotypic heterogeneity and induce nongrowing metabolically active forms.
text: Non-replicating and metabolically inactive bacteria are implicated in latent tuberculosis infections and relapses following "sterilizing" chemotherapy, but evidence linking bacterial dormancy and persistence in vivo is limited. Using quantitative time-lapse microscopy and a reporter of ribosomal RNA gene expression, we examine the single-cell dynamics of Mycobacterium tuberculosis replication and ribosomal activity. Our findings reveal that single cells exhibit heterogeneity under standard growth conditions, which is amplified by stressful conditions such as nutrient limitation, stationary phase, intracellular replication, and growth in mouse lungs. Moreover, the lungs of chronically infected mice harbor a subpopulation of non-growing but metabolically active bacteria, which are absent in mice lacking interferon-γ, a cytokine essential for antituberculosis immunity. These cryptic bacterial forms are prominent in mice treated with the antituberculosis drug isoniazid, suggesting a role in post-chemotherapeutic relapses. Our results imply that amplification of bacterial phenotypic heterogeneity in response to host immunity and drug pressure may contribute to tuberculosis persistence.

title: Proteomic analysis reveals Warburg effect and anomalous metabolism of glutamine in pancreatic cancer cells.
text: In this current study, we conducted a comprehensive characterization of the proteomes of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cell line PANC-1 and normal pancreatic duct cells using mass spectrometry with LTQ-Orbitrap technology. We identified over 1700 proteins from each sample using label-free quantification approach based on spectra count. The analysis revealed a large number of differentially expressed metabolic enzymes and proteins involved in various cellular processes, including cytoskeleton, cell adhesion, transport, transcription, translation, and cell proliferation. The results suggested that metabolic pathways were altered in PANC-1, consistent with the Warburg effect. Additionally, our comparative MS analysis revealed that glutamine was heavily consumed as a nitrogen donor in nucleotide and amino acid biosynthesis in PANC-1, indicating anomalous metabolism of glutamine. Overall, our findings provide a comprehensive picture of the metabolic landscape of PANC-1, which may serve as a basis for the development of new diagnostics and treatments for PDAC.

title: Prevalence of attempting weight loss and strategies for controlling weight.
text:
In the United States, overweight and obesity rates are increasing. Modifications to diet and physical activity are crucial for weight management.
Objective: To assess the prevalence of weight loss and maintenance attempts among US adults and describe weight control strategies.
Design: The Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), a random-digit telephone survey conducted by state health departments in 1996.
Participants: Adults aged 18 years and older (N = 107,804).
Main Outcome Measures: Reported current weights and goal weights, prevalence of weight loss or maintenance attempts, and strategies used to control weight (e.g., eating fewer calories, less fat, or engaging in physical activity).
Results: Attempting to lose and maintain weight was 28.8% and 35.1% among men and 43.6% and 34.4% among women, respectively. Among those attempting to lose weight, the most common strategy was reducing fat intake but not calories (34.9% of men and 40.0% of women), while only 21.5% of men and 19.4% of women used the recommended combination of reducing calorie intake and engaging in at least 150 minutes of leisure-time physical activity per week. Among men trying to lose weight, the median weight was 90.4 kg with a goal weight of 81.4 kg, while among women, the median weight was 70.3 kg with a goal weight of 59.0 kg.
Conclusions: Weight loss and weight maintenance are common concerns for US men and women. The majority of individuals trying to lose weight are not using the recommended combination of reducing calorie intake and engaging in leisure-time physical activity for 150 minutes or more per week.

title: Antibodies specific for Epstein-Barr virus nuclear antigen-1 cross-react with human heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein L.
text: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) has been associated with multiple sclerosis (MS), and elevated levels of antibodies against EBV nuclear antigen-1 (EBNA-1) are commonly observed in MS patients. Our hypothesis is that anti-EBNA-1 antibodies in MS patients may cross-react with a self-antigen. To test this hypothesis, we purified anti-EBNA-1 antibodies from human plasma and used them to immunoprecipitate antigens from human brain tissue. Using mass spectrometry, we identified the bound antigens and found that anti-EBNA-1 consistently bound to heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein L (HNRNPL). We then expressed both the long and short isoforms of HNRNPL and verified that the long isoform cross-reacts with EBNA-1 using Western blots and ELISA. Immunohistochemical analysis of cultured rat central nervous system cells revealed that anti-EBNA-1 bound to an antigen in the nucleus. Additionally, ELISA showed that both healthy controls and MS patients had antibodies to HNRNPL in their plasma, but there was no significant increase in anti-HNRNPL levels in MS patients. Our findings suggest that HNRNPL is an autoantigen that cross-reacts with EBNA-1. Further investigation is needed to determine the relevance of this autoantigen to MS and other autoimmune diseases.

title: Roles of chromatin remodellers in DNA double strand break repair.
text: With a clear understanding of the DNA double strand break (DSB) repair mechanisms and the associated damage signaling, the focus has shifted to the changes in the chromatin environment that facilitate efficient repair.Cancer mutations in chromatin remodeling complexes have been identified, underscoring the importance of assessing their impact on genomic stability. Our current knowledge of DSB repair pathways suggests that each one has unique requirements for chromatin remodeling. Moreover, restricting the extent of chromatin modifications may play a crucial role in determining which repair pathway is utilized. In this review, we will evaluate the individual DSB repair pathways in terms of their potential need for chromatin remodeling and examine the roles of ATP-driven chromatin remodelers in these pathways.

title: Epstein-Barr virus and virus human protein interaction maps.
text: A comprehensive analysis of interactions among Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) proteins and interactions between EBV proteins and human proteins can provide valuable insights into EBV's strategies for replication and persistence. Utilizing a rigorous high-throughput yeast two-hybrid system, we identified 43 interactions between EBV proteins and 173 interactions between EBV and human proteins. The resulting "interactome" maps provided a framework for generating hypotheses about protein function. For instance, we discovered that LF2, a previously uncharacterized EBV protein, interacts with the EBV immediate early R transactivator (Rta) and inhibits Rta transactivation. Examining the EBV genome from a broader perspective revealed that EBV genes can be categorized into two evolutionary classes: "core" genes, which are conserved across all herpesviruses, and "noncore" genes. Our interactome map showed that interactions among proteins in the same evolutionary class are enriched. Moreover, the human proteins targeted by EBV proteins were enriched for "hub" proteins, which are highly connected to other proteins in the human interactome network, and for proteins with relatively short paths to all other proteins. Targeting these hubs may represent an efficient mechanism for EBV to reorganize cellular processes.

title: Relation between Medicare screening reimbursement and stage at diagnosis for older patients with colon cancer.
text:
In 1998, Medicare's reimbursement policy for colonoscopies was expanded to cover screening colonoscopies for all individuals, and again in 2001, and this change was associated with an increase in the use of colonoscopy and the probability of being diagnosed with early-stage colon cancer among Medicare beneficiaries.
A study was conducted using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Medicare linked database to determine whether changes in Medicare reimbursement were associated with an increase in colonoscopy use or early-stage cancer diagnosis. The study included patients aged 67 years or older who were diagnosed with colon cancer between 1992 and 2002, as well as a control group of Medicare beneficiaries who did not have cancer.
The study found that colonoscopy use among Medicare beneficiaries without cancer increased significantly from an average rate of 285/100,000 per quarter in the no-coverage period (1992-1997) to 889 and 1919/100,000 per quarter in the limited coverage period (January 1998-June 2001) and universal coverage period (July 2001-December 2002), respectively (P<.001 for each pairwise comparison). During the study period, 44,924 eligible patients were diagnosed with colorectal cancer, and the proportion of patients diagnosed at an early stage increased from 22.5% in the no-coverage period to 25.5% in the limited coverage period and 26.3% in the universal coverage period (P<.001 for each pairwise comparison).
The study also found that the changes in Medicare coverage were strongly associated with early-stage diagnosis for patients with proximal colon lesions, but weakly associated, if at all, for patients with distal colon lesions. The selective effect of the coverage change on proximal colon lesions suggests that increased use of whole-colon screening modalities such as colonoscopy may have played a pivotal role.
In conclusion, the expansion of Medicare reimbursement to cover colon cancer screening was associated with an increased use of colonoscopy and a higher probability of being diagnosed with early-stage colon cancer among Medicare beneficiaries.

title: Direct visualization of the endomitotic cell cycle in living megakaryocytes: differential patterns in low and high ploidy cells.
text: Megakaryocyte endomitosis, a process involving repeated DNA replication without cytokinesis, is crucial for megakaryocyte development. However, the dynamics of chromosomes during this process have remained elusive in living megakaryocytes. To address this gap, we generated a new transgenic mouse model where green fluorescent protein is fused to histone H2B and expressed specifically in megakaryocytes. Using ex vivo time-lapse microscopy, we observed chromosomal condensation in mitosis of all megakaryocytes. Interestingly, in high ploidy megakaryocytes (>8N), late anaphase was marked by a ring-like arrangement of chromosomes with multiple territories separating them. In contrast, in low ploidy megakaryocytes (<8N), mitotic chromosomes segregated into two distinct groups before re-joining to form a single cluster. This study provides the first in vivo observation of chromosomal segregation patterns during endomitosis and highlights the potential for differential regulation in low and high ploidy cells.

title: Aberrant expression and altered cellular localization of desmosomal and hemidesmosomal proteins are associated with aggressive clinicopathological features of oral squamous cell carcinoma
text: Disruption of cell adhesion plays a central role in the progression of various cancers, including oral cancer. The desmosome and hemidesmosome are crucial adhesion structures that control cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions, respectively. To investigate their contributions to the biological properties of oral cancer, we examined the expression of desmoglein 1 (DSG1), DSG2, DSG3, desmocollin 2 (DSC2), integrin beta 4 (ITGB4), laminin gamma chain 2 (LAMC2), and collagen type 17 alpha 1 (COL17A1) in 51 cases of oral squamous cell carcinoma. In normal oral epithelial cells, these proteins are expressed on the plasma membrane and basement membrane, respectively. However, in cancer, their expression decreases and is internalized to the cytoplasm. In contrast, the cytoplasmic expression of DSG2, ITGB4, and LAMC2 is induced in cancer cells facing the stroma. We analyzed the immunohistochemical expression and correlated it with clinicopathological parameters, including histologic differentiation, pattern of invasion, and presence of lymph node metastasis. Our findings show that decreased expression of DSG3 and DSC2 is associated with more aggressive clinicopathological features, including less differentiated and more invasive histologic features and a higher incidence of nodal metastasis. Furthermore, lower COL17A1 expression and higher LAMC2 expression were also linked to a more aggressive phenotype. This study demonstrates that abnormal expression and altered localization of desmosomal and hemidesmosomal proteins are associated with aggressive clinicopathological features of oral cancer. This reinforces the idea that disruption of keratin-associated anchoring junctions confers aggressive properties to cancer cells.

title: Histone/protein deacetylase inhibitors increase suppressive functions of human FOXP3+ Tregs.
text: Histone/protein deacetylases (HDACs) reduce histone and protein acetylation, commonly resulting in the repression of gene transcription and modulation of various protein functions. Our investigation uncovered pronounced distinctions in HDAC expression before and after stimulation of human T regulatory (Treg) and T effector cells, suggesting the potential for focused selective targeting of Tregs with HDAC inhibitors (HDACi) in the future. We explored the effects of different HDACi small molecules on the suppressive functions of both freshly isolated and expanded human Tregs, and our findings revealed significant enhancements,ranging from 4.5-fold (average 2-fold) up to 4.5-fold (average 2-fold), in the suppressive capabilities of both freshly isolated and expanded human Tregs, which is consistent with our previous murine data. Moreover, we observed that HDACi use increased Treg expression of CTLA-4, a key negative regulator of immune responses, and we found a direct and significant correlation between CTLA-4 expression and Treg suppression. Consequently, HDACi compounds demonstrate promising potential as pharmacologic tools to enhance Treg suppressive functions, which may potentially be exploited in patients with autoimmunity or post-transplantation.

title: Enhanced pathological angiogenesis in mice lacking β3 integrin or β3 and β5 integrins
text: Inhibiting the function of αvβ3 or αvβ5 integrins has been shown to suppress tumor growth and neovascularization, suggesting that these integrins play critical roles in angiogenesis. Contrary to expectations, our study found that mice lacking β3 integrins or both β3 and β5 integrins not only support tumor formation, but also exhibit enhanced tumor growth. Furthermore, tumors in these integrin-deficient mice display increased angiogenesis, indicating that neither αvβ3 nor αvβ5 integrins are essential for neovascularization. Additionally, we observed augmented angiogenic responses to hypoxia and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) in the absence of β3 integrins. We did not observe any changes in the expression or functions of other integrins as a result of the β3 deficiency, but we did find increased levels of VEGF receptor-2 (also called Flk-1) in β3-null endothelial cells. These findings suggest that αvβ3 and αvβ5 integrins are not essential for vascular development or pathological angiogenesis, and highlight the need for further investigation into the mechanisms of action of αv-integrin antagonists in anti-angiogenic therapies.
