SRB emits strong fluorescence when excited with a laser at 488 nm and can be measured quantitatively at the single-cell level by static fluorescence cytometry.

title: A murine model of human myeloma bone disease.
text:
Research on myeloma, a cancer of the plasma cells, has led to the discovery of a unique form of osteolytic bone disease. While osteoclast activation is known to contribute to bone destruction in myeloma, the specific mechanisms by which myeloma cells enhance osteoclast activity have yet to be elucidated. To gain insights into these mechanisms, an animal model of human myeloma bone disease has been established.
Using aging C57 BL/KaLwRij mice, which spontaneously develop multiple myeloma, researchers have found that the disease exhibits the same characteristics as in humans, including characteristic bone lesions. However, the variability in the number of myeloma cells in marrow-derived preparations makes it challenging to study this model. To overcome this limitation, a myeloma cell line was established and subcloned from murine myeloma cells, which causes osteolytic bone lesions in mice similar to human myeloma bone disease. This cell line produces interleukin-6, yet grows independently of exogenous interleukin-6. Inoculation of mice with these cultured cells leads to the development of an identical disease to those injected with fresh bone-marrow-derived myeloma cells, including monoclonal gammopathy and radiologic bone lesions. Surprisingly, some of the mice became hypercalcemic, and the bone lesions were found to have increased osteoclast activity. Similar results were observed when Nu/Bg/XID mice were inoculated with cultured murine myeloma cells. Since the number of cells inoculated can be precisely controlled, it is expected that this animal model will be useful in uncovering the mechanisms by which myeloma cells stimulate osteoclast activity in this model of human myeloma bone disease.

title: Ticagrelor vs. clopidogrel in patients with acute coronary syndromes and diabetes: a substudy from the PLATelet inhibition and patient Outcomes (PLATO) trial
text:
AIMS patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) are at an elevated risk of ischaemic events and bleeding following acute coronary syndromes (ACS). In the PLATelet inhibition and patient Outcomes (PLATO) trial, ticagrelor was found to reduce the primary composite endpoint of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke, while maintaining similar rates of major bleeding compared to clopidogrel. We aimed to determine if ticagrelor is more effective than clopidogrel in patients with DM or poor glycaemic control.
METHODS AND RESULTS We analyzed 4662 patients with pre-existing DM, including 1036 patients on insulin, and compared them to 13,951 patients without DM. We also analyzed subgroups based on admission levels of hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c; n = 15,150). In patients with DM, ticagrelor showed a significant reduction in the primary composite endpoint (HR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.76-1.03), all-cause mortality (HR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.66-1.01), and stent thrombosis (HR: 0.65, 95% CI: 0.36-1.17), without an increase in major bleeding (HR: 0.95, 95% CI: 0.81-1.12). There was no significant heterogeneity between patients with or without ongoing insulin treatment. Furthermore, ticagrelor showed a reduction in the primary endpoint, all-cause mortality, and stent thrombosis in patients with HbA1c above the median (HR: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.70-0.91; HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.65-0.93; and HR: 0.62, 95% CI: 0.39-1.00, respectively), with similar bleeding rates (HR: 0.98, 95% CI: 0.86-1.12).
CONCLUSION In conclusion, our findings suggest that ticagrelor is effective in reducing ischaemic events in ACS patients regardless of diabetic status and glycaemic control, without an increase in major bleeding events. These results provide evidence for the use of ticagrelor in patients with DM or poor glycaemic control.

title: Cardiovascular risk factors and migraine: the GEM population-based study.
text:
Migraines, including those with aura, are a risk factor for early-onset ischemic stroke. The underlying mechanisms are not fully understood, but may be related to migraineurs having a higher risk profile for cardiovascular disease. To investigate this further, the authors of this study compared the cardiovascular risk profiles of adult migraineurs to those of non-migraineurs.
The study included 5,755 participants, aged 20 to 65, from the Genetic Epidemiology of Migraine (GEM) study in the Netherlands. Of these, 620 were current migraineurs, including 31% with aura (MA) and 5% unclassified. The remaining 5,135 were non-migraine controls. The researchers measured various cardiovascular risk factors, such as blood pressure (BP), serum total and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (TC, HDL), smoking, oral contraceptive use, and the Framingham risk score for myocardial infarction or coronary heart disease (CHD) death.
The results showed that migraineurs were more likely to smoke (odds ratio (OR) = 1.43, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.10-1.83), less likely to consume alcohol (OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.50-0.77), and more likely to have a parental history of early myocardial infarction. Migraineurs with aura were more likely to have an unfavorable cholesterol profile (OR = 1.43, 95% CI: 0.97-2.11), have elevated blood pressure (systolic BP > 140 mm Hg or diastolic BP > 90 mm Hg, OR = 1.76, 95% CI: 1.04-3.08), and report a history of early onset CHD or stroke (OR = 3.96, 95% CI: 1.10-14.3). Female migraineurs with aura were more likely to be using oral contraceptives (OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.05-4.08). The odds of having an elevated Framingham risk score for CHD were approximately doubled for the migraineurs with aura.
In conclusion, this study found that migraines, particularly those with aura, are associated with a higher cardiovascular risk profile than individuals without migraine.

title: Th2-mediated host protective immunity to intestinal nematode infections.
text: Despite decades of research, there is limited understanding of the mechanisms that control the expulsion of intestinal parasites, such as nematodes. Most of what is known comes from studies in rodents, which indicate that a strong Th2-mediated immune response is triggered when an infection occurs, leading to responses such as eosinophilia, intestinal mastocytosis, and elevated IgE production. These findings have provided valuable tools for dissecting the potential effector mechanisms involved, such as the use of cytokine-specific monoclonal antibodies and recombinant cytokines, as well as studying animals with genetic disruptions in key immune response genes. However, it is unclear how mast cells become activated in the absence of a T-cell compartment, and data from infections in transgenic animals suggest that the high-affinity receptor for IgE is not involved. Additionally, there is little evidence to support a protective role for eosinophilia in any system. New data also suggest that while interleukin 4 (IL-4) is generally important, it is not always sufficient to mediate protection, and other Th2 cytokines, such as IL-13, may warrant closer investigation. It is likely that the expulsion of worms is the result of a combination of multiple mechanisms, some of which may be more critical for certain species of parasites than others.

title: Wnt/β-catenin signaling defines organizing centers that orchestrate growth and differentiation of the regenerating zebrafish caudal fin.
text: Zebrafish fin regeneration is mediated by the formation of a progenitor cell population called the blastema, which relies on Wnt/β-catenin signaling for proliferation and patterning of the overlying epidermis. However, our findings reveal that β-catenin signaling remains inactive in both the epidermis and the majority of proliferative blastemal cells. Instead, tissue-specific pathway interference suggests that Wnt signaling in the nonproliferative distal blastema is necessary for cell proliferation in the proximal blastema, while signaling in cells lining the osteoblasts directs osteoblast differentiation. This indicates that Wnt signaling regulates epidermal patterning, blastemal cell proliferation, and osteoblast maturation indirectly through secondary signals. Gene expression profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and functional rescue experiments suggest that Wnt/β-catenin signaling acts through Fgf and Bmp signaling to control epidermal patterning, while retinoic acid and Hedgehog signals mediate its effects on blastemal cell proliferation. We propose that Wnt signaling orchestrates fin regeneration by defining organizing centers that instruct the behaviors of adjacent tissues.

title: The utility of cerebrospinal fluid analysis in patients with multiple sclerosis
text: A diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) requires rigorous exclusion of other possible diagnoses. To achieve this, analyzing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is typically conducted in patients experiencing their first symptoms, which could be indicative of MS. However, in the case of relapsing-remitting MS, CSF analysis is not essential for diagnosis as long as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) criteria are met. Nevertheless, caution is warranted when diagnosing MS in individuals with MRI findings or CSF analysis results that are negative, as CSF investigation can help eliminate other diseases. The detection of oligoclonal IgG bands in CSF has significant prognostic value and can inform clinical decision-making. Moreover, analyzing CSF is crucial for research into the pathogenesis of MS, as it has revealed inflammatory and neurodegenerative changes in the central nervous system (CNS). Although no validated novel CSF biomarkers have been identified for MS diagnosis and disease monitoring, ongoing technological advancements are likely to uncover more markers in the future. This review summarizes the CSF findings that aid in distinguishing MS from other potential diseases, while highlighting the potential of newly discovered biomarkers to deepen our understanding of MS pathophysiology.

title: Expression of circadian genes correlates with liver metastasis and outcomes in colorectal cancer.
text: Circadian rhythms are daily fluctuations in various biological processes, driven by the interplay of eight core circadian genes: Period1 (Per1), Period2 (Per2), Period3 (Per3), Cryptochrome1 (Cry1), Cryptochrome2 (Cry2), Clock, Bmal1, and Casein Kinase I ε (CKIε). Recent investigations have suggested that circadian genes are involved in the growth and development of various malignancies. This study aimed to investigate the correlation between circadian gene expression and clinicopathological factors, as well as patient outcomes, in patients with colorectal cancer. We analyzed surgical specimens of cancer tissue and adjacent normal mucosa from 202 patients with untreated colorectal cancer. Quantitative real-time, reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction was used to measure the relative expression levels of the circadian genes in the specimens. Our findings revealed that the expression of the Clock gene and the CKIε gene in cancer tissue were significantly higher compared to expression in adjacent normal mucosa. In contrast, the expression of the Per1 and Per3 genes in cancer tissue was significantly lower compared to expression in adjacent normal mucosa. Our analysis also showed that high expression of the Bmal1 gene and low expression of the Per1 gene were associated with liver metastasis. Additionally, high expression of the Per2 gene was found to be associated with better outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer, while reduced expression of the Per2 gene was a predictor of poorer outcomes. Overexpression of the Bmal1 gene and reduced expression of the Per1 gene may serve as useful predictors of liver metastasis, while reduced expression of the Per2 gene may be a predictor of outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer.

title: The Danish prescription registries.
text: The extensive digitization of Danish pharmacies has enabled the creation of two comprehensive prescription repositories: the Odense University Pharmacoepidemiological Database (OPED) and the Pharmacoepidemiological Prescription Database of North Jutland (PDNJ). This article discusses the content, coverage, completeness, and quality of the data in these registries, as well as the terms under which access to the data is granted. The two prescription databases serve a population ofapproximately 1 million people, which represents about 18% of the Danish population. The registries are representative of the overall population and cover all medications that are reimbursed at the individual user level. By linking prescription data to other population-based Danish registries, the unique and permanent personal identifier enables the creation of longitudinal drug histories. The completeness of the Danish prescription registries is high for reimbursed prescription drugs, and a limited number of comparison studies have shown that the register information has high validity. The Danish prescription registries represent a valuable new data source for pharmacoepidemiological studies.

title: Oridonin, a diterpenoid purified from Rabdosia rubescens, inhibits the proliferation of cells from lymphoid malignancies in association with blockade of the NF-kappa B signal pathways.
text: The study found that oridonin, a natural compound isolated from Rabdosia rubescens, inhibited the growth of various cancer cells, including multiple myeloma (U266 and RPMI8226), acute lymphoblastic T-cell leukemia (Jurkat), and adult T-cell leukemia (MT-1) cells, with an effective dose that inhibited 50% of target cells (ED50) ranging from 0.75 to 2.7 microg/mL. Oridonin caused apoptosis of MT-1 cells in a time-dependent manner, as evidenced by terminal deoxynucleotidyltransferase-mediated dUTP nick end labeling staining. The study also found that oridonin downregulated levels of Mcl-1 and BCL-x(L), but not Bcl-2 protein, in both MT-1 and RPMI8226 cells. Additionally, oridonin inhibited nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) DNA-binding activity in these cells as well as in Jurkat cells and RAW264.7 murine macrophages. Notably, oridonin decreased survival of freshly isolated T-cell leukemia cells, acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells, chronic lymphocytic leukemia cells, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma cells, and multiple myeloma cells from patients, in association with inhibition of NF-κB DNA-binding activity. However, oridonin did not affect survival of normal lymphoid cells from healthy volunteers. These findings suggest that oridonin may be useful as an adjunctive therapy for individuals with lymphoid malignancies, including the lethal disease adult T-cell leukemia.

title: Uncertainty in integrative structural modeling.
text:
Integrative structural modeling involves combining multiple types of input data and progressing through four stages:
1. Gathering Information: Uncertainty arises from data that are incomplete, noisy, ambiguous, or sourced from diverse populations.
2. Designing Model Representation and Converting Information into a Scoring Function: Uncertainty can originate from a model that is too simplistic to capture the available information or a scoring function that does not accurately reflect the data.
3. Sampling Good-Scoring Models: The main source of uncertainty in this stage is the limited number of samples, which may not accurately represent the entire population.
4. Analyzing Models and Information: In this final stage, techniques such as clustering, cross-validation, and other methods are used to estimate the accuracy and precision of the models and information.

title: Moist occlusive dressing (Aquacel(®) Ag) versus moist open dressing (MEBO(®)) in the management of partial-thickness facial burns: a comparative study in Ain Shams University.
text:
INTRODUCTION
The face is the most crucial part of our physical features, as it conveys emotions and expressions, communicates feelings, and helps establish individual identity. Facial burns are unfortunately quite common and can have devastating consequences for the affected individual, leading to numerous physical, emotional, and psychosocial sequelae. Partial thickness facial burns are particularly common, and this study compares the effectiveness of standard moist open dressing technique management and a moist closed technique for managing such burns.
PATIENTS AND METHODS:
The study included 40 patients with partial-thickness facial burns treated at Ain Shams University's burn unit in Cairo, Egypt, between April 2009 and December 2009. The patients were randomly divided into two groups: group A (n=20) received open treatment with MEBO(®), while group B (n=20) received coverage with Aquacel(®) Ag. Demographic data (age, gender, ethnicity, burn surface area, and burn location) were compared between the two groups, as well as length of hospital stay (LOS), rate of infections, time to total healing, frequency of dressing changes, pain levels, cost-effectiveness, and patient discomfort. The long-term outcome (incidence of hypertrophic scarring) was assessed in both groups up to 6 months after treatment.
RESULTS:
No significant differences were found between the two groups regarding demographics. In the group treated with Aquacel(®) Ag, the mean time for re-epithelialization was 10.5 days, which was significantly shorter than the 12.4 days observed in the MEBO(®) group (p<0.05). The frequency of dressing changes, pain levels, and patient discomfort were also significantly lower in the Aquacel(®) Ag group. Additionally, the cost of treatment was found to be similar between the two groups. However, the scar quality was found to be better in the Aquacel(®) Ag treatment group. Follow-up assessments were conducted at 3 and 6 months after treatment, and the long-term outcomes were recorded in both groups.
CONCLUSION:
The study's findings suggest that the use of a moist occlusive dressing (Aquacel(®) Ag) significantly improves the management and healing rate of partial thickness facial burns, with better long-term outcomes compared to the standard moist open dressing technique (MEBO(®)). The study demonstrates that the Aquacel(®) Ag dressing leads to faster re-epithelialization, reduced pain and discomfort, and better scar quality compared to the MEBO(®) dressing. These results suggest that the choice of dressing can have a significant impact on the management and outcomes of partial thickness facial burns.

title: Feedback upregulation of HER3 (ErbB3) expression and activity attenuates antitumor effect of PI3K inhibitors.
text: Examining the effects of PI3K inhibitor XL147 on human breast cancer cell lines with constitutively active PI3K, we found that treatment resulted in dose-dependent inhibition of cell growth and reduced levels of pAKT and pS6, key components of the PI3K/AKT/TOR signaling pathway. In HER2-overexpressing cells, inhibition of PI3K led to increased expression and phosphorylation of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases, including HER3. knockdown of FoxO1 and FoxO3a transcription factors reversed the induction of HER3, InsR, IGF1R, and FGFR2 mRNAs upon inhibition of PI3K. In HER2-positive cells, knockdown of HER3 using siRNA or cotreatment with the HER2 inhibitors trastuzumab or lapatinib further enhanced XL147-induced cell death and inhibition of pAKT and pS6. Trastuzumab and lapatinib also synergized with XL147 to inhibit pAKT and the growth of established BT474 xenografts. These findings suggest that PI3K antagonists will inhibit AKT and uncouple receptor tyrosine kinase expression and activity, limiting their sustained inhibition of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Therefore, using PI3K pathway inhibitors as single agents may have limited clinical activity. Combining these agents with HER2/HER3 antagonists in patients with HER2-overexpressing breast cancer may provide a more effective treatment approach.

title: Developmental RacGAP α2-Chimaerin Signaling Is a Determinant of the Morphological Features of Dendritic Spines in Adulthood.
text: Morphological characteristics of dendritic spines play a crucial role in cognitive ability, but the molecular mechanisms underlying their refinement during development are not fully understood. It is also unclear whether these developmental mechanisms determine the normal adult spine morphological features. To address these questions, we investigated the role of α2-isoform of Rac-specific GTPase-activating protein α-chimaerin (α2-chimaerin) in spine morphological refinement during late postnatal development. We found that disruption of α2-chimaerin leads to an increase in spine size in the hippocampus, while overexpression of α2-chimaerin in developing hippocampal neurons results in a decrease in spine size. Additionally, we showed that disruption of α2-chimaerin suppresses EphA-mediated spine morphogenesis in cultured developing hippocampal neurons. Interestingly, the disruption of α2-chimaerin beginning during the juvenile stage results in an increased size of spines in the hippocampus, while spine morphologies are unaltered when α2-chimaerin is deleted only in adulthood. Consistently, disruption of α2-chimaerin leading to an increase in contextual fear learning in adulthood, while contextual learning was recently shown to be unaffected when α2-chimaerin was deleted only in adulthood. These findings suggest that α2-chimaerin signaling in developmental stages contributes to the determination of the morphological features of adult spines and the establishment of normal cognitive ability. In summary, our results provide evidence that α2-chimaerin plays a critical role in spine morphological refinement during late postnatal development and that this developmental function is important for normal cognitive ability in adulthood.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of amitriptylinoxide in the treatment of chronic tension-type headache: a multi-centre controlled study.
text: In a double-blind, parallel-group trial of 197 patients with chronic tension-type headache, the medication amitriptyline (AO) was found to have a superior effect compared to both placebo (PL) and another dosage of amitriptyline (AM). The primary study endpoint was a reduction of at least 50% in the product of headache duration and frequency, as well as a reduction of at least 50% in headache intensity. The results showed that treatment response occurred in 30.3% of the AO group, 22.4% of the AM group, and 21.9% of the PL group. Additionally, a reduction in headache duration and frequency of at least 50% was found in 39.4% of the AO group, 25.4% of the AM group, and 26.6% of the PL group. Finally, a reduction in headache intensity of at least 50% was found in 31.8% of the AO group, 26.9% of the AM group, and 26.6% of the PL group. The results suggest that AO has a superior effect compared to PL and AM in reducing the severity of chronic tension-type headache.

title: Downregulation of Superoxide Dismutase Activity and Gene Expression in Cultured Rat Brain Astrocytes after Incubation with Vitamin C
text: The effects of ascorbic acid (vitamin C) supplementation on superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and gene expression were investigated in cultured rat brain astrocytes (RBA-1 cells). The study consisted of four groups: a control group without vitamin C and three treatment groups with vitamin C at concentrations of 40, 80, and 160 µmol/l. After short-term (2 days) and long-term (7 days) incubation, SOD activity, mRNA levels, and protein amounts were measured. The results showed that vitamin C supplementation resulted in a concentration-dependent decrease in SOD activity after 2 days, with a decrease in the activity of the Mn-SOD isoenzyme by 13.2% and the Cu/Zn-SOD isoenzyme by 16.7%. Additionally, vitamin C attenuated the mRNA levels of Mn-SOD and Cu/Zn-SOD after 2 days, with a decrease of 8.7% and 4.8%, respectively. After 7 days of incubation, a significant decrease in SOD activity was observed in all treatment groups, with a decrease of 11.8% and 8.4% in the Mn-SOD and Cu/Zn-SOD isoenzymes, respectively. Furthermore, the mRNA levels of Mn-SOD and Cu/Zn-SOD were also attenuated, with a decrease of 8.6% and 4.7%, respectively. These findings suggest that supplementation with high concentrations of vitamin C may downregulate the activity and gene expression of SOD in cultured RBA-1 cells.

title: Lateral Hypothalamic Area Glutamatergic Neurons and Their Projections to the Lateral Habenula Regulate Feeding and Reward.
text:
Unidentified factors rather than direct neural circuits regulate the consumption of high-calorie, enjoyable foods, which contributes to the global obesity epidemic. We demonstrate that neurons in the lateral hypothalamus (LHA) that release glutamate and project to the lateral habenula (LHb) negatively regulate the consumption of delightful food. We found that eliminating LHA glutamatergic neurons led to a rise in daily caloric consumption and weight gain when given access to a high-fat diet. These neurons project to the LHb, which is involved in processing unpleasant stimuli and negative predictions regarding the outcome of behavior. Using optogenetic stimulation, we discovered that LHA-LHb glutamatergic circuit functionally connected neurons in the LHb, and that the net effect of neurotransmitter release was to increase the firing of most LHb neurons. Optogenetic inhibition of LHA-LHb glutamatergic fibers created a real-time place preference, whereas optogenetic stimulation of LHA-LHb glutamatergic fibers had the opposite effect. Furthermore, optogenetic inhibition of LHA-LHb glutamatergic fibers increased the consumption of a pleasurable liquid caloric reward. Overall, these results indicate that LHA glutamatergic neurons are crucial for managing feeding behavior and possibly other behavioral states through their functional connections with the LHb and other brain regions.

The significance of this study is that it discovers the key brain circuits that regulate appetite and weight gain in response to "calorically dense, highly palatable" foods, which contribute to the worldwide obesity epidemic. To demonstrate their findings, the researchers employed genetic ablation, optogenetics, and electrophysiology to identify the neural circuits responsible for regulating food intake in mice. Overall, the article emphasizes the importance of using this information to create novel therapies for treating obesity and related conditions.

title: Glucose Metabolism Inhibits Apoptosis in Neurons and Cancer Cells by Redox Inactivation of Cytochrome c
text: Neurons and cancer cells exhibit an unusual reliance on glucose for their survival, yet the precise benefit of this adaptation remains unclear. These seemingly unrelated cell types also show an increased regulation of the apoptotic pathway, allowing them to survive over the long term. Our research reveals that both neurons and cancer cells rigorously inhibit cytochrome c-mediated apoptosis through a mechanism linked to glucose metabolism. We found that the pro-apoptotic activity of cytochrome c is influenced by its redox state, with increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) following an apoptotic insult leading to the oxidation and activation of cytochrome c. In healthy neurons and cancer cells, however, cytochrome c is reduced and inactivated by intracellular glutathione (GSH), generated as a result of glucose metabolism through the pentose phosphate pathway. These findings uncover a remarkable similarity in apoptosis regulation between neurons and cancer cells and provide insight into the adaptive advantage offered by the Warburg effect, both for cancer cells' evasion of apoptosis and for long-term neuronal survival.

title: mTORC2 Regulates Amino Acid Metabolism in Cancer by Phosphorylation of the Cystine-Glutamate Antiporter xCT.
text: Cancer cells undergo metabolic reprogramming to facilitate their uncontrolled growth, but the molecular mechanisms behind this process are not completely understood. To gain insights, we conducted an unbiased proteomic screen and discovered that the cancer-Associated protein mTORC2 plays a critical role in regulating amino acid metabolism in cancer. Specifically, mTORC2 phosphorylates the cystine-glutamate antiporter xCT at its cytosolic N-terminus, leading to decreased xCT activity. Molecular inhibition of mTORC2 or the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) kinase results in increased glutamate secretion, cystine uptake, and incorporation into glutathione, highlighting the interplay between growth factor receptor signaling and amino acid metabolism in cancer. These findings reveal a novel mechanism by which cancer cells adapt to changing environmental conditions, demonstrating the unanticipated complexity of cancer metabolism.

title: Bayesian models leveraging bioactivity and cytotoxicity information for drug discovery.
text: Recognizing distinct leads poses a substantial obstacle in drug discovery, particularly when dealing with neglected diseases like tuberculosis. To overcome this challenge, we have developed a virtual screening approach utilizing Bayesian models that integrate bioactivity and cytotoxicity information. We conducted experiments to validate this approach using a commercial library, which resulted in a significant improvement in hit rates compared to traditional high-throughput screening (HTS). This dual-event Bayesian model successfully identified compounds exhibiting antitubercular whole-cell activity and low toxicity towards mammalian cells, including one of the most potent hits displaying the desirable combination of in vitro and in vivo activity and safety. By leveraging Bayesian models, we were able to streamline the drug discovery process, yielding substantial cost and time savings.

title: A role for interleukin-1β in determining the lineage fate of embryonic rat hippocampal neural precursor cells.
text: Neurogenesis in the hippocampus of the developing and adult brain is driven by the presence of multipotent stem cells and restricted precursor cells at different stages of differentiation. The potential of these cells to be harnessed for cell transplantation approaches to treat neurodegenerative disorders and trauma has been proposed. However, an inflammatory environment during neural precursor cell (NPC) development can have deleterious effects on hippocampal neurons and hinder neurogenesis. This study investigated the impact of interleukin-1β (IL-1β) on the proliferation and differentiation of embryonic rat hippocampal NPCs in vitro. Our findings revealed that IL-1R1 is expressed on proliferating NPCs and that IL-1β treatment leads to a decrease in cell proliferation and neurosphere growth. When NPCs were differentiated in the presence of IL-1β, there was a significant reduction in the percentage of newly-born neurons and post-mitotic neurons, and an increase in the percentage of astrocytes. These effects were mitigated by IL-1 receptor antagonist. These findings demonstrate that IL-1β exerts an anti-proliferative, anti-neurogenic, and pro-gliogenic effect on embryonic hippocampal NPCs, which is mediated by IL-1R1. The results highlight the detrimental impact of an inflammatory environment during NPC development and underscore the potential need for strategies to inhibit IL-1β signaling to facilitate effective cell transplantation approaches or in conditions where endogenous hippocampal neurogenesis is impaired.

title: Bone disease in pediatric patients undergoing dialysis with CAPD or CCPD.
text:
There is limited knowledge on the histological features of renal osteodystrophy and the frequency of bone aluminum deposition in children undergoing dialysis. In this study, 44 pediatric patients receiving continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD) or cycling peritoneal dialysis (CCPD) had bone biopsies and deferoxamine (DFO) infusion tests. All patients were receiving oral calcitriol. The results showed:


* 39% of patients had osteitis fibrosa (OF), 25% had mild lesions (M), 16% had normal histology (NH), 11% had aplastic lesions (AP), and 9% had osteomalacia (OM).

* Bone surface aluminum (SA) was present in 10 out of 20 patients given aluminum-containing phosphate-binding agents and in 0 out of 24 treated with calcium carbonate.
* Serum biochemistry tests and DFO infusion tests were unable to predict bone histology, but plasma aluminum levels were markedly elevated, and bone aluminum content was highest in patients with OM.
* Bone formation rate (BFR) correlated with serum parathyroid hormone (PTH), with a correlation coefficient of 0.55 and a P value less than 0.001. BFR was also inversely related to bone aluminum content, even in patients with OF, with a correlation coefficient of -0.42 and a P value less than 0.01.
* All patients with SA greater than 30% had normal or reduced BFR compared to those with SA less than 30%, with a chi-square value of 12.2 and a P value less than 0.005.
* Based on SA greater than 30%, six patients were classified as having aluminum-related bone disease, including three patients with OM, one patient with AP, and two patients with NH.
* Two-thirds of pediatric patients undergoing CAPD/CCPD had persistent hyperparathyroidism despite treatment with calcitriol, but aluminum can adversely affect BFR when SA exceeds 30%, regardless of histologic lesion or serum PTH level.

In summary, this study found that 39% of pediatric dialysis patients had osteitis fibrosa, and 10 out of 20 patients given aluminum-containing phosphate-binding agents had bone surface aluminum. Bone formation rate correlated with serum parathyroid hormone and was inversely related to bone aluminum content, even in patients with osteomalacia. However, two-thirds of pediatric patients undergoing dialysis had persistent hyperparathyroidism despite treatment with calcitriol, highlighting the need for further research on the effects of aluminum on bone health in these patients.

title: Disruption of the immune-checkpoint VISTA gene imparts a proinflammatory phenotype with predisposition to the development of autoimmunity.
text: VISTA, a domain-containing Ig suppressor of T-cell activation, is a negative regulator that dampens immune responses. Previous studies using a VISTA-neutralizing monoclonal antibody revealed that blocking VISTA enhances T-cell activation. Our current analysis details the comprehensive characterization of mice lacking the VISTA gene. Although young mice showed normal hematopoiesis, the genetic deficiency in VISTA led to the accumulation of spontaneously activated T cells, accompanied by the production of a range of inflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Enhanced T-cell responsiveness was also observed following immunization with neoantigen. Interestingly, aged VISTA-deficient mice failed to develop systemic or organ-specific autoimmune disease, despite displaying chronic inflammation. Furthermore, interbreeding VISTA-deficient mice with 2D2 T-cell receptor transgenic mice, which are predisposed to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, significantly augmented disease incidence and severity. Correspondingly, there was a concomitant increase in the activation of encephalitogenic T cells in the periphery and infiltration into the central nervous system. Taken together, our findings suggest that VISTA functions as a negative checkpoint regulator, diminishing the threshold for T-cell activation, which in turn leads to an enhanced proinflammatory phenotype and a higher incidence and intensity of autoimmunity under susceptible conditions.

title: Molecular mechanisms that funnel RNA precursors into endogenous small-interfering RNA and microRNA biogenesis pathways in Drosophila.
text: In Drosophila, three types of endogenous small RNAs, microRNAs (miRNAs), PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs), and endogenous small-interfering RNAs (endo-siRNAs or esiRNAs), act as triggers in RNA silencing. Although piRNAs are produced independently of Dicer, the biogenesis pathways of miRNAs and esiRNAs require Dicer1 and Dicer2, respectively. Recent studies have revealed that two isoforms of the protein Loquacious (Loqs), Loqs-PB and Loqs-PD, are involved in the processing of miRNA and esiRNA precursors, respectively. However, the mechanism by which these Loqs isoforms participate in their respective small RNA biogenesis pathways remains unclear. Here, we show that Loqs-PD specifically interacts with Dicer2 through its C-terminal domain. The Dicer2-Loqs-PD complex, which also contains the known Dicer2 partner R2D2, processes both exogenous siRNAs and esiRNAs from their precursors in vitro. Interestingly, Loqs-PD, but not R2D2, enhances Dicer2 activity. The Dicer2-Loqs-PD complex processes esiRNA precursor hairpins with long stems, which leads to the production of AGO2-associated small RNAs. Notably, small RNAs derived from the terminal hairpins of esiRNA precursors are loaded onto AGO1; therefore, they are classified as a new subset of miRNAs. These findings suggest that the precursor RNA structure determines the biogenesis mechanism of esiRNAs and miRNAs, and that hairpin structures with long stems may serve as intermediates in the evolution of Drosophila miRNAs.

title: Neutralizing antibody responses in acute human immunodeficiency virus type 1 subtype C infection.
text: Examining the evolution and distinct characteristics of neutralizing antibodies during the course of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection may prove crucial in identifying potential targets for vaccine design. In this study, we investigated the autologous and heterologous neutralization responses of 14 HIV-1 subtype C-infected individuals, using envelope clones isolated within the first two months post-infection. Our findings indicate that potent yet relatively strain-specific neutralizing antibodies develop within three to 12 months of HIV-1 infection. The magnitude of this response was associated with shorter V1-to-V5 envelope lengths and fewer glycosylation sites, particularly in the V1-V2 region. Antibodies against minor determinant of envelope protein (MPER) were detected in four of 14 individuals within a year of infection, while antibodies to CD4-induced (CD4i) epitopes reached high titers in 12 participants, with most cases occurring before the development of autologous neutralizing antibodies. However, neither MPER nor CD4i antibody specificity provided broad neutralization capabilities. These results offer insights into the kinetics, potency, breadth, and epitope specificity of neutralizing antibody responses during acute HIV-1 subtype C infection.

title: The cell cycle in polyploid megakaryocytes is associated with reduced activity of cyclin B1-dependent cdc2 kinase.
text: The megakaryocyte precursor undergoes endomitosis without mitosis, resulting in the maturation to a polyploid cell through DNA replication. By analyzing the cell cycle in a megakaryocytic cell line (MegT) generated by expressing temperature-sensitive simian virus 40 large T antigen in megakaryocytes of transgenic mice, we found that endomitosis consists of a series of S/Gap phases rather than a continuous phase of DNA synthesis. Our study revealed that upon inactivation of large T antigen, the cells shift from a mitotic cell cycle to an endomitotic cell cycle, with elevated levels of G1/S cyclins, cyclin A, and G1 phase cyclins, cyclin D3, at the onset of DNA synthesis. In contrast, mitotic cyclins, such as cyclin B1, were undetectable during endomitosis. Interestingly, while levels of the mitotic kinase protein, Cdc2, were comparable during both the mitotic cell cycle and endomitosis, cyclin B1-dependent Cdc2 kinase activity was largely abolished in the polyploid cells. Importantly, we found that reduced levels of cyclin B1 are a unique feature of megakaryocytes, as fibroblasts immortalized with the same heat-labile oncogene did not display reduced levels of cyclin B1 upon shifted to high temperature nor did they become polyploid. Our findings suggest that cellular programming during endoreduplication in megakaryocytes is associated with reduced levels of cyclin B1, which likely plays a crucial role in the regulation of the cell cycle in these cells.

title: Ghrelin secretion stimulated by {beta}1-adrenergic receptors in cultured ghrelinoma cells and in fasted mice.
text: Ghrelin, an octanoylated peptide hormone produced in the stomach, experiences a dramatic increase in mouse plasma levels during chronic severe calorie deprivation, a crucial adaptation that helps maintain life. Despite its importance, the mechanism behind this increase remains unclear. To investigate, we studied the regulation of ghrelin secretion in tissue culture cells derived from mice harboring ghrelinomas, which were induced by a tissue-specific SV40 T-antigen transgene. Our findings indicate that ghrelin-producing cells exhibit high levels of mRNA encoding beta(1)-adrenergic receptors. Exposure to norepinephrine or epinephrine in the culture medium significantly enhances ghrelin secretion, a response that is blocked by the selective beta(1)-adrenergic antagonist atenolol. When mice were treated with reserpine to deplete adrenergic neurotransmitters from sympathetic neurons, the increased plasma ghrelin levels observed during fasting were prevented. Similar inhibition was observed following atenolol administration. Our results suggest that the fasting-induced surge in plasma ghrelin is primarily mediated by adrenergic agents released by sympathetic neurons, which act directly on beta(1) receptors located on ghrelin-producing cells in the stomach.

title: Dominance relationships between S-alleles in self-incompatible Brassica campestris L.
text: Dominance relationships were investigated among 249 possible pair-wise combinations of 24 S-alleles from two natural populations of Brassica campestris, derived from Turkey and Japan. Each F1 hybrid was crossed reciprocally with its parental S-homozygotes to determine the dominance relationships. The 24 S-alleles were grouped into two categories based on their stigma-side expression and three categories based on their pollen-side expression. In the stigma, codominance was observed frequently, while in the pollen, codominance was less common and a hierarchy of dominance relationships was apparent, although dominance occurred with specific S-allele combinations. Interactions among the 24 S-alleles differed between the stigma and pollen, with 20 pairs showing independent weakening of S-alleles in the pollen, which was correlated with the recessiveness of the S-alleles.

title: MicroRNA-203 inhibits cellular proliferation and invasion by targeting Bmi1 in non-small cell lung cancer.
text:
The role of microRNAs (miRNAs) in the regulation of tumor progression and invasion is of utmost significance, particularly in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the expression levels of miR-203 in NSCLC and its clinical implications remained unexplored. In this study, we investigated the association between miR-203 and B-cell-specific moloney murine leukemia virus insertion site 1 (Bmi1) and determined the tumor suppressor function of miR-203.
Our findings revealed that miR-203 expressions were downregulated in NSCLC tissues, while Bmi1 expressions were upregulated in NSCLC tissues and cell lines. Furthermore, downregulation of Bmi1 or enhancement of miR-203 expression inhibited NSCLC cell proliferation and invasion in vitro. Additionally, a dual-luciferase reporter assay identified Bmi1 as a novel target of miR-203.
In conclusion, our study demonstrated that miR-203 functions as a tumor suppressor and plays a critical role in inhibiting the proliferation of NSCLC cells by targeting Bmi1. These findings suggest that miR-203 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for NSCLC treatment.

title: Characterization of the interaction between retinoic acid receptor/retinoid X receptor (RAR/RXR) heterodimers and transcriptional coactivators through structural and fluorescence anisotropy studies.
text: Retinoid receptors (RARs and RXRs) are transcription factors that regulate gene expression by recruiting coregulator complexes to specific promoters upon ligand binding. To better understand the mechanisms involved, we crystallized the RAR beta/RXR alpha heterodimer complexed with its ligand 9-cis retinoic acid and an LXXLL-containing peptide (termed NR box 2), as well as analyzed the binding affinities of this peptide to retinoid receptors in the presence of different ligands. Our combined structural and biochemical studies revealed that heterodimerization does not significantly affect the structure of individual subunits or their ability to interact with NR box 2. Moreover, the ability of a protomer to recruit NR box 2 is unaffected by the ligand binding status of its partner receptor. In contrast, the strength of the association between the heterodimer and the full-length SRC-1 nuclear receptor interaction domain (NID) depends on both the ligand binding status of the RAR and RXR subunits and the simultaneous presence of both receptor agonists. We also identified an LXXLL-driven mechanism by which the concerted reorientation of three phenylalanine side chains generates an "aromatic clamp" that locks the RXR activation helix H12 into the transcriptionally active conformation. Additionally, we showed how variations in helix H11-ligand interactions can alter the communication pathway linking helices H11, H12, and the connecting loop L11-12 to the coactivator-binding site. Overall, our results reveal important molecular and structural features that impact the ligand-dependent interaction of the RAR/RXR heterodimer with nuclear receptor coactivators.

title: PRC2 complexes with JARID2, MTF2, and esPRC2p48 in ES cells to modulate ES cell pluripotency and somatic cell reprogramming.
text:
Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) has been implicated in the pluripotency of embryonic stem (ES) cells, but its molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. Previous studies assumed that ES cells have the same PRC2 composition as HeLa cells and Drosophila embryos. However, our study reveals that PRC2 in mouse ES cells contains additional subunits, including JARID2, MTF2, and a novel protein called esPRC2p48. These subunits are highly expressed in ES cells compared to differentiated cells.
Intriguingly, knockdown or knockout of JARID2, MTF2, or esPRC2p48 alters PRC2-mediated histone H3K27 methylation levels and leads to the expression of differentiation-associated genes in ES cells. Interestingly, co-expression of JARID2, MTF2, and esPRC2p48, but not individual knockdowns, enhances the reprogramming of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) into induced pluripotent stem cells, while knockdown or knockout of these subunits significantly hinders reprogramming.
Furthermore, we found that JARID2, MTF2, and esPRC2p48 modulate H3K27 methylation and repress lineage-associated gene expression when transduced into MEFs, and synergistically stimulate the histone methyltransferase activity of PRC2 in vitro. Therefore, our findings identify JARID2, MTF2, and esPRC2p48 as crucial regulatory subunits of PRC2 in ES cells and reveal their essential roles in modulating PRC2's activity and gene expression in both ES cells and somatic cell reprogramming.

title: General and abdominal adiposity and risk of death in Europe.
text:
The following is a rewritten version of the given text:
Background: Prior studies have primarily relied on body-mass index (BMI) to assess the association between adiposity and risk of death, but few have examined whether the distribution of body fat contributes to the prediction of death.
Methods: We assessed the association between BMI, waist circumference, and waist-to-hip ratio with the risk of death among 359,387 participants from nine countries in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC). We used a Cox regression analysis with age as the time variable, and stratified the models by study center and age at recruitment, adjusting for educational level, smoking status, alcohol consumption, physical activity, and height.
Results: During a mean follow-up of 9.7 years, 14,723 participants died. The lowest risks of death related to BMI were observed at a BMI of 25.3 for men and 24.3 for women. After adjustment for BMI, waist circumference, and waist-to-hip ratio were strongly associated with the risk of death. Among men and women in the highest quintile of waist circumference, the relative risks were 2.05 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.80 to 2.33) and 1.78 (95% CI, 1.56 to 2.04), respectively, and in the highest quintile of waist-to-hip ratio, the relative risks were 1.68 (95% CI, 1.53 to 1.84) and 1.51 (95% CI, 1.37 to 1.66), respectively. BMI remained significantly associated with the risk of death in models that included waist circumference or waist-to-hip ratio (P<0.001).
Conclusions: These data suggest that both general adiposity and abdominal adiposity are associated with the risk of death and support the use of waist circumference or waist-to-hip ratio in addition to BMI in assessing the risk of death.

title: Phosphorylation of the autophagy receptor optineurin restricts Salmonella growth.
text: Cargo-selective autophagy can be facilitated through receptor molecules that establish specific connections between cargoes and the autophagosomal membrane, where they are decorated with ubiquitin-like microtubule-associated protein light chain 3 (LC3) modifiers. Despite the identification of various autophagy receptors, little is understood regarding the in vivo mechanisms that regulate their functions. In this study, we discovered that phosphorylation of an autophagy receptor, optineurin, enhances the selective autophagy of ubiquitin-coated cytosolic Salmonella enterica through the phosphorylation of serine-177 by the protein kinase TANK binding kinase 1 (TBK1). These findings suggest that the phosphorylation of autophagy receptors may serve as a general mechanism for the regulation of cargo-selective autophagy. In support of this notion, mutations in optineurin that disrupt ubiquitin or LC3 binding, as well as the silencing of either optineurin or TBK1, resulted in impaired Salmonella autophagy and increased intracellular bacterial proliferation.

title: PKD1 Inhibits AMPKα2 through Phosphorylation of Serine 491 and Impairs Insulin Signaling in Skeletal Muscle Cells.
text:
AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is an energy-sensing enzyme whose activity is suppressed in conditions of insulin resistance. Recently, it has been shown that exposure to high levels of glucose can increase phosphorylation of AMPK at Ser(485/491) of its α1/α2 subunit, but the underlying mechanism is unknown. Diacylglycerol (DAG), which is also elevated in muscle cells exposed to high glucose, activates various signaling proteins, including protein kinase C (PKC) and protein kinase D1 (PKD1). To investigate the role of PKC and PKD1 in AMPK inhibition, we examined the effects of a PKC/D1 activator, phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA), on AMPK phosphorylation in C2C12 myotubes. Our results showed that PMA dosesly and time-dependently increased AMPK Ser(485/491) phosphorylation, which was associated with a ∼60% decrease in AMPKα2 activity. Expressing a phosphodefective AMPKα2 mutant (S491A) prevented the PMA-induced reduction in AMPK activity. Serine phosphorylation and inhibition of AMPK activity were partially inhibited by the broad PKC inhibitor Gö6983 and fully inhibited by the specific PKD1 inhibitor CRT0066101. Genetic knockdown of PKD1 also prevented Ser(485/491) phosphorylation of AMPK. In contrast, inhibition of previously identified kinases that phosphorylate AMPK at this site (Akt, S6K, and ERK) did not prevent these events. PMA treatment also impaired insulin signaling through Akt, and PKD1 inhibition prevented these effects. Furthermore, recombinant PKD1 phosphorylated AMPKα2 at Ser(491) in cell-free conditions, indicating that PKD1 is a novel upstream kinase of AMPKα2 that plays a negative role in insulin signaling in muscle cells.
In summary, our findings demonstrate that PKD1 is a key regulator of AMPK phosphorylation at Ser(485/491) in skeletal muscle cells, and its inhibition leads to impaired insulin signaling. This study identifies PKD1 as a novel player in the regulation of AMPK activity and insulin signaling, and suggests potential therapeutic strategies for the treatment of insulin resistance and associated metabolic disorders.

title: Accuracy of ICD-9-CM codes for identifying cardiovascular and stroke risk factors.
text:
Objective:
The present study aimed to determine which ICD-9-CM codes in Medicare Part A data can identify cardiovascular and stroke risk factors.

Design and Participants:
This cross-sectional study compared ICD-9-CM data to structured medical record review from 23,657 Medicare beneficiaries aged 20 to 105 years who had atrial fibrillation.
Measurements:
Quality improvement organizations used standardized abstraction instruments to determine the presence of 9 cardiovascular and stroke risk factors. The accuracy of ICD-9-CM codes was assessed to identify these risk factors using chart abstractions as the gold standard.
Main Results:
ICD-9-CM codes had high specificity (>0.95) and low sensitivity (<0.76) in identifying cardiovascular and stroke risk factors. The positive predictive values were greater than 0.95 for 5 common chronic risk factors - coronary artery disease, stroke/transient ischemic attack, heart failure, diabetes, and hypertension. The sixth common risk factor, valvular heart disease, had a positive predictive value of 0.93. For all 6 common risk factors, negative predictive values ranged from 0.52 to 0.91. The rare risk factors - arterial peripheral embolus, intracranial hemorrhage, and deep venous thrombosis - had high negative predictive value (>0.98) but moderate positive predictive values (range, 0.54-0.77) in this population.
Conclusions:
Using ICD-9-CM codes alone, heart failure, coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and stroke can be ruled in but not necessarily ruled out. Where feasible, review of additional data (e.g., physician notes or imaging studies) should be used to confirm the diagnosis of valvular disease, arterial peripheral embolus, intracranial hemorrhage, and deep venous thrombosis.

title: Modulation of cellular and viral promoters by mutant human p53 proteins found in tumor cells.
text: Recent findings have shown that wild-type p53 can repress transcription from various cellular and viral promoters. Since p53 mutations are the most common genetic alteration in human cancers, it is essential to investigate the effects of these mutations on promoter function. To study this, we analyzed the effects of wild-type and mutant human p53 on the human proliferating-cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) promoter and several viral promoters, including the herpes simplex virus type 1 UL9 promoter, the human cytomegalovirus major immediate-early promoter-enhancer, and the long terminal repeat promoters of Rous sarcoma virus and human T-cell lymphotropic virus type I. HeLa cells were cotransfected with a wild-type or mutant p53 expression vector and a plasmid containing a chloramphenicol acetyltransferase reporter gene under viral (or cellular) promoter control. Interestingly, expression of wild-type p53 inhibited promoter function, while expression of a p53 mutant resulted in a significant increase in PCNA promoter activity (2-11-fold). Similar results were observed with the viral promoters, although to a lesser extent. Additional experiments showed that activation by a mutant p53 requires a minimal promoter containing a lone TATA box, and that a more significant increase in activation (25-fold) occurs when the promoter contains a binding site for the activating transcription factor or cyclic AMP response element-binding protein. Using Saos-2 cells that do not express p53, we found that activation by a mutant p53 was a direct enhancement. These findings suggest that mutant p53s found in cancer cells may play a functional role in activating several important loci, including PCNA, which could contribute to increased cell proliferation.

title: Valvular interstitial cells suppress calcification of valvular endothelial cells.
text:
Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most prevalent heart valve disorder in Western societies. Our earlier work posited that valvular endothelial cells (VECs) restore damaged adult valve leaflets through endothelial-to-mesenchymal transformation (EndMT); however, the role of EndMT in valvular calcification was unknown. We hypothesized that aortic VECs undergo osteogenic differentiation through an EndMT process, which can be inhibited by valvular interstitial cells (VICs).
We generated VEC clones subjected them to TGF-β1-mediated EndMT, monitored by increased mRNA expression of EndMT markers (α-SMA, MMP-2, and Slug) in the treated VECs (p < 0.05). To assess the effect of VICs on VEC EndMT, clonal VIC populations were derived from the same valve leaflets, cultured in co-culture with VECs, and grown in control or TGF-β1-supplemented media. In the presence of VICs, EndMT was inhibited, as evidenced by decreased mRNA expression of α-SMA, MMP-2, and Slug (p < 0.05). When VECs were cultured in osteogenic media, they exhibited osteogenic changes, confirmed by increased mRNA expression of osteocalcin, osteopontin, and Runx2. VIC presence inhibited VEC osteogenesis, demonstrated by decreased expression of osteocalcin and osteopontin (p < 0.05). Time-course analysis revealed that EndMT precedes VEC osteogenesis, shown by an initial increase in α-SMA and MMP-2 on day 7, followed by an increase in osteopontin and osteocalcin on day 14.
Our findings indicate that EndMT may precede VEC osteogenesis. This study demonstrates that VICs inhibit VEC EndMT and osteogenesis, thereby highlighting the importance of VEC-VIC interactions in valve homeostasis.

title: The HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor simvastatin activates the protein kinase Akt and promotes angiogenesis in normocholesterolemic animals.
text: New research suggests that statins may protect the vasculature without directly affecting cholesterol levels. We found that statins rapidly activate protein kinase Akt/PKB in endothelial cells, leading to increased phosphorylation of the endogenous Akt substrate endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) and enhanced angiogenesis. Similar to the effects of VEGF treatment, both simvastatin administration and Akt activation in the endothelium promoted angiogenesis in ischemic limbs of normocholesterolemic rabbits. These findings suggest that activation of Akt represents a mechanism by which statins can promote new blood vessel growth, explaining some of their beneficial side effects.

title: Varenicline, an alpha4beta2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor partial agonist, selectively decreases ethanol consumption and seeking.
text: Alcohol dependence afflicts millions globally. While some progress has been made in treating alcohol dependence through pharmacotherapy, further innovative approaches are still required. Alcohol and nicotine are often abused together, and evidence suggests that neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) play a role in both dependencies. Varenicline, a partial agonist at the alpha4beta2 nAChRs, reduces nicotine intake and was recently approved as a smoking cessation aid. In this study, we investigated the role of varenicline in modulating ethanol consumption and seeking in three animal models of drinking. Acute administration of varenicline, in doses that reduce nicotine reward, specifically reduced ethanol but not sucrose seeking in an operant self-administration drinking paradigm. Additionally, chronic varenicline administration decreased ethanol consumption without resulting in a rebound increase in ethanol intake when the varenicline was no longer administered. These findings suggest that the alpha4beta2 nAChRs may play a role in ethanol-seeking behaviors in animals chronically exposed to ethanol. The selectivity of varenicline in decreasing ethanol consumption, combined with its reported safety profile and mild side effects in humans, suggest that varenicline may prove to be a treatment for alcohol dependence.

title: Targeting TLR4 signaling by TLR4 Toll/IL-1 receptor domain-derived decoy peptides: identification of the TLR4 Toll/IL-1 receptor domain dimerization interface.
text: Researchers have identified a key interface on the TLR4 Toll/IL-1R (TIR) domain that initiates intracellular signaling, paving the way for the rational design of therapies that block TLR4 signaling. To achieve this, a library of cell-permeating decoy peptides was created, each consisting of a non-fragmented patch of the TLR4 TIR surface. These peptides were synthesized in tandem with a cell-permeating Antennapedia homeodomain sequence and tested for their ability to inhibit early cytokine mRNA expression and MAPK activation in LPS-stimulated primary murine macrophages. Five peptides were found to be highly effective in inhibiting TLR4 signaling, while no activity was observed against TLR2 signaling. To further investigate the binding of these peptides to TLR4, Förster resonance energy transfer using time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy was employed. The findings revealed that the area between the BB loop of TLR4 and its fifth helical region mediates TLR4 TIR dimerization, and provided direct evidence for the utility of the decoy peptide approach. This approach involves probing for the ability of peptides representing various surface-exposed segments of a protein to inhibit protein function, and then identifying their specific targets by Förster resonance energy transfer to define recognition sites in signaling proteins that may be targeted therapeutically to disrupt functional transient protein interactions.

title: A paediatric case of sideroblastic anaemia. Ultrastructural studies of erythroblasts cultured from marrow BFU-E in a methylcellulose micromethod.
text: We investigated the morphological and functional characteristics of erythroblasts derived from bone marrow erythroid progenitor cells cultured in methylcellulose, which were obtained from a female child with a rare, atypical form of sideroblastic anemia (SA) that was partially responsive to pyridoxine. Our findings showed that colony formation in three successive cultures was within the normal range (median values: 82.25 CFU-E and 16.4 BFU-E derived colonies/6.6 x 10^4 cells), compared to the growth of normal cells (65-315 CFU-E and 9-40 BFU-E). We also evaluated the in vitro differentiation of these erythroid colonies by measuring the levels of a specific enzyme involved in the heme pathway, uroporphyrinogen I synthase (UROS), using biochemical microassays. The UROS levels in the erythroid colonies from SA marrow were at the lower end of the normal range (median values: 6.7 +/- 0.3 and 14.4 +/- 3.8 pmol uroporphyrinogen/h in CFU-E and BFU-E-derived colonies, respectively, versus 17.4 +/- 7.3 and 25 +/- 7.2 pmol/h in CFU-E and BFU-E colonies from normal subjects). Additionally, ultrastructural examination of non-cultured bone marrow cells or cultured BFU-E revealed the characteristic deposition of iron in mitochondria around the nucleus of most cells (ringed sideroblasts). However, the majority of cultured cells showed marked dyserythropoietic features, including bilobulated or trilobulated erythroblasts, multiple cytoplasmic vacuoles, abnormalities of the nucleus, and excessive membrane material beneath the plasma membrane, which were more pronounced than in non-cultured marrow cells.

title: Innate lymphoid cells: emerging insights in development, lineage relationships, and function.
text: Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) are a unique type of immune cell that lacks a specific antigen receptor, yet can produce a variety of effector cytokines similar to those of T helper cell subsets. ILCs play a crucial role in lymphoid organogenesis, tissue remodeling, antimicrobial immunity, and inflammation, particularly at barrier surfaces. Their rapid response to stress-causing microbes suggests that ILCs are essential in the first line of immunological defenses. This review focuses on the current understanding of ILC developmental requirements, lineage relationships, and effector functions of two main ILC subtypes: (a) Rorγt-expressing cells involved in lymphoid tissue formation, mucosal immunity, and inflammation, and (b) type 2 ILCs, which are essential for helminth immunity. Additionally, the review discusses the potential roles of ILCs in the pathogenesis of immune-mediated inflammatory and infectious diseases, including allergy.

title: No net renal extraction of homocysteine in fasting humans.
text:
BACKGROUND: Despite being a well-established disease, the pathophysiological mechanism of hyperhomocysteinemia in chronic renal failure in humans remains unclear. While it was previously hypothesized that the loss of a putative renal homocysteine extraction mechanism in chronic renal failure might contribute to elevated homocysteine levels, evidence from experimental studies in rats suggests that the normal kidney may play a role in homocysteine removal. In this study, we aimed to investigate homocysteine extraction in the normal human kidney.
METHODS: We measured plasma total (free and protein-bound) and free homocysteine (tHcy and fHcy, respectively) levels in arterial and renal venous blood samples obtained from the aorta and right-side renal vein during cardiac catheterization in 20 fasting patients with normal renal function. Renal homocysteine extraction was calculated by dividing the arteriovenous difference in homocysteine levels by the arterial levels, multiplied by 100%.
RESULTS: Our findings revealed no significant renal uptake of homocysteine in these patients, withtHcy extraction at 0.9% (standard deviation [SD] 5.8; 95% confidence interval [CI] -1.8 to +3.6) and fHcy extraction at -0.2% (SD 11.0; 95% CI -5.4 to +4.9).
CONCLUSIONS: Taken together, our results suggest that net renal uptake of homocysteine does not occur in fasting humans with normal renal function, and therefore, cannot contribute to hyperhomocysteinemia in patients with chronic renal failure. These findings have important implications for the pathophysiology of hyperhomocysteinemia in chronic renal failure and may have implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies to treat this condition.

title: Traditional Chinese acupuncture in tension-type headache: a controlled study.
text: In a study involving 30 patients with tension-type headaches, traditional Chinese acupuncture and sham acupuncture were randomly administered to assess treatment response. The study assessed symptom severity using five measures, including headache intensity, duration, and frequency, as well as headache index and analgesic consumption. These measures were evaluated at four-week intervals over a period of one year, including a four-week baseline period, plus two weeks of treatment and two weeks of follow-up. At each assessment, the Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory (MMPI) was administered to each subject before the start of the study. Using split-plot analysis of variance (ANOVA), the study found that, compared to baseline, the frequency of headache episodes, analgesic consumption, and headache index significantly decreased over time, but there was no significant difference between acupuncture and placebo treatment. Additionally, the MMPI profile of acupuncture non-responders revealed the presence of 'Conversion V'. However, no single MMPI scale predicted treatment response.

title: TCR stimulation with modified anti-CD3 mAb expands CD8+ T cell population and induces CD8+CD25+ Tregs.
text: Modified anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are being explored as a potential means of inducing immunological tolerance in various conditions, including transplantation and autoimmune diseases such as type 1 diabetes. In a trial involving a modified anti-CD3 mAb called hOKT3gamma1(Ala-Ala) in patients with type 1 diabetes, we found that treatment with the mAb led to an increase in the number of peripheral blood CD8+ T cells in response to the mAb. Our findings suggest that the anti-CD3 mAb activates CD8+ T cells in both in vitro and in vivo settings, leading to the induction of regulatory CD8+CD25+ T cells that inhibit the responses of CD4+ cells to the mAb and to antigen. These regulatory CD8+CD25+ T cells require cell-to-cell contact for their inhibitory effect, and we observed the induction of the forkhead box protein 3 (Foxp3) on CD8+ T cells in patients during mAb treatment, which may play a role in the anti-CD3 mAb's immune modulatory effects.

title: Interactions between Non-Physician Clinicians and Industry: A Systematic Review
text:
BACKGROUND: The increasing restrictions on physician-industry interactions have led to a shift in industry marketing strategies, targeting other health professionals. Recent health policy developments have underscored the importance of non-physician clinicians' decision-making in clinical practice. This systematic review aims to investigate the types and implications of non-physician clinician-industry interactions in clinical practice.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a comprehensive search of MEDLINE and Web of Science databases from January 1, 1946, to June 24, 2013, following PRISMA guidelines. We included non-physician clinicians (registered nurses, nurse prescribers, physician assistants, pharmacists, dieticians, and physical or occupational therapists) and excluded trainee samples. Fifteen studies met our inclusion criteria. Qualitative analysis of the data revealed eight outcome domains: nature and frequency of industry interactions, attitudes toward industry, perceived ethical acceptability of interactions, perceived marketing influence, perceived reliance on industry information, preparation for industry interactions, reactions to industry relations policy, and management of industry interactions. Non-physician clinicians reported regular interactions with the pharmaceutical and infant formula industries, relying on them for practice information and receiving industry-provided "information," "education," and promotional materials. Clinicians generally viewed these interactions as ethical and detected "promotion" while benefiting from industry resources. Free samples were among the most common ways clinicians interacted with industry. The studies were observational and varied in methodological rigor, so these findings may not be generalizable. However, this review is the first to our knowledge to provide a descriptive analysis of this literature.
CONCLUSIONS: Non-physician clinicians' generally positive attitudes toward industry interactions, despite recognition of issues related to bias, suggest that industry interactions are normalized in clinical practice across disciplines. To mitigate conflicts of interest and address potential impacts on patient care, industry relations policy should be implemented consistently across all disciplines.

title: Emtricitabine-tenofovir concentrations and pre-exposure prophylaxis efficacy in men who have sex with men.
text: Drug concentrations associated with protecting against HIV-1 acquisition have not been determined. In a substudy of the iPrEx trial, we evaluated drug concentrations among men who have sex with men. This randomized, placebo-controlled trial used daily oral doses of emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in men who have sex with men. We found that drug levels were lower in blood plasma and viable cryopreserved peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) in HIV-infected individuals compared to controls at the time of HIV diagnosis (8% vs 44%; P < 0.001) and in the 90 days prior (11% vs 51%; P < 0.001). An intracellular concentration of the active form of tenofovir, tenofovir-diphosphate (TFV-DP), of 16 fmol/million PBMCs was associated with a 90% reduction in HIV acquisition compared to the placebo arm. In a separate study, directly observed dosing regimens yielded TFV-DP concentrations that, when modeled after the iPrEx trial, corresponded to an HIV-1 risk reduction of 76%, 96%, and 99% for two, four, and seven doses per week, respectively. These findings suggest ways to optimize PrEP regimens for this population, as prophylactic benefits were observed across a range of doses and drug concentrations.

title: Clinical outcomes following institution of the Canadian universal leukoreduction program for red blood cell transfusions.
text:
A number of countries have implemented policies for universal leukoreduction of their blood supply, but the effectiveness of this approach in reducing postoperative mortality and infection rates is unclear. To investigate this, we conducted a retrospective cohort study in 23 hospitals across Canada, comparing clinical outcomes before and after the implementation of a national universal prestorage leukoreduction program for blood transfusions.
Our study included 14,786 patients who received red blood cell transfusions after cardiac surgery, repair of a hip fracture, or required intensive care following a surgical intervention or multiple trauma. Half of the patients (6,982) were enrolled during the control period, and the other half (7,804) were enrolled after the introduction of leukoreduction.
We found that the unadjusted in-hospital mortality rates were significantly lower after the introduction of leukoreduction compared to the control period (6.19% vs 7.03%, respectively; P = 0.04). After adjusting for potential confounding factors, we found that the adjusted odds of death were reduced with leukoreduction (odds ratio [OR], 0.87; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75-0.99), but serious nosocomial infections did not decrease (adjusted OR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.87-1.09). The frequency of posttransfusion fevers decreased significantly following leukoreduction (adjusted OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.79-0.94), as did antibiotic use (adjusted OR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.82-0.99).
Our findings suggest that a national universal leukoreduction program may be associated with decreased mortality as well as decreased fever episodes and antibiotic use after red blood cell transfusion in high-risk patients.

title: Failure of continuous venovenous hemofiltration to prevent death in paraquat poisoning.
text: Paraquat poisoning is characterized by multiorgan failure and pulmonary fibrosis with respiratory failure. Early death within 3 days of ingestion is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with circulatory collapse being a significant contributor. Recent studies have suggested that continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH) may play a role in treating multiorgan failure by promoting hemodynamic stability. To investigate this further, we conducted a study on 80 patients with paraquat poisoning who were randomly assigned to either hemoperfusion (HP) alone or HP followed by CVVH (duration, 57.4 +/- 31.3 hours; ultrafiltration volume, 40.2 +/- 4.8 L/d). Our findings indicate that prophylactic CVVH after HP significantly prolonged survival time, with a delay in time to death of 2.5 +/- 2.1 days compared to 5.0 +/- 5.0 days in the HP-alone group (P < 0.05). However, there was no significant difference in mortality rates between the two groups (66.7% versus 63.6%; P = 0.82). In the HP group, early circulatory collapse was the main cause of death, while late respiratory failure was the main cause of death in the HP-CVVH group. In conclusion, prophylactic CVVH after HP can prevent early death due to circulatory collapse but cannot prevent late death due to respiratory failure. Furthermore, there is no survival benefit in acute paraquat poisoning.

title: The antidiabetic effect of mesenchymal stem cells is unrelated to their transdifferentiation potential but to their capability to restore Th1/Th2 balance and to modify the pancreatic microenvironment.
text:
Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic metabolic disease resulting from immune-mediated destruction of insulin-producing cells. In T1DM animal models, it has been shown that systemic administration of multipotent mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) leads to regeneration of pancreatic islets. However, the underlying mechanisms are not well understood. Our study aimed to investigate whether MSCs differentiate into pancreatic β-cells and modify systemic and pancreatic pathophysiological markers of T1DM.
We found that administration of 5 × 105 syngeneic MSCs to mice with T1DM led to a significant decrease in hyperglycemia, without the presence of donor-derived insulin-producing cells. In contrast, MSCs were found to be engrafted into secondary lymphoid organs 7 and 65 days after transplantation, which was accompanied by a reduction in autoaggressive T cells and an increase in regulatory T cells. Additionally, in the pancreas of mice with T1DM treated with MSCs, we observed a shift from a proinflammatory to an anti-inflammatory cytokine profile. MSC transplantation did not reduce pancreatic cell apoptosis, but it did recover local expression and increase the circulating levels of epidermal growth factor, a pancreatic trophic factor.
Our data suggest that the antidiabetic effect of MSCs is unrelated to their potential for transdifferentiation but rather to their ability to restore the balance between Th1 and Th2 immune responses and modify the pancreatic microenvironment. These findings should be taken into account when designing clinical trials aimed at evaluating MSC transplantation in patients with T1DM, as the presence of endogenous precursors appears to be critical for restoring glycemic control.

title: Tmem27: a cleaved and shed plasma membrane protein that stimulates pancreatic beta cell proliferation.
text: The molecular mechanisms controlling the replication of terminally differentiated beta cells remain elusive. In this study, we investigate the identification and characterization of transmembrane protein 27 (Tmem27, also known as collectrin) in pancreatic beta cells. Our findings reveal that expression of Tmem27 is reduced in Tcf1(-/-) mice and increased in islets of mouse models with hypertrophy of the endocrine pancreas. Interestingly, Tmem27 forms dimers and its extracellular domain is glycosylated, cleaved, and shed from the plasma membrane of beta cells, a process that is unique to beta cells. Our results show that overexpression of full-length Tmem27 leads to increased thymidine incorporation, while silencing of Tmem27 using RNAi results in a decrease in cell replication. Moreover, mice with increased expression of Tmem27 in pancreatic beta cells exhibit increased beta cell mass. These findings uncover a novel pancreatic beta cell transmembrane protein that regulates the growth of pancreatic islets.

title: The ATM missense mutation p.Ser49Cys (c.146C>G) and the risk of breast cancer.
text: Homozygous mutations in the ATM gene are associated with ataxia telangiectasia, while heterozygous mutation carriers may be at increased risk of breast cancer. We analyzed 22 ATM variants in two large, population-based studies from the US and Poland, consisting of 2,856 breast cancer cases and 3,344 controls. Our findings suggest that a missense mutation, Ser49Cys (c.146C>G, p. S49C), which is carried by approximately 2% of individuals, is more common in breast cancer cases than controls in both study populations, with an odds ratio (OR) of 1.69 (95% CI, 1.19-2.40; P=0.004). Another missense mutation, Phe858Leu (c.2572T>C, p. F858L), was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer in the US study but not in Poland, and had a combined OR of 1.44 (95% CI, 0.98-2.11; P=0.06).
