These findings provide the most convincing evidence to date that missense mutations in ATM, particularly p. S49C, may be breast cancer susceptibility alleles. However, due to their low frequency, larger sample sizes are necessary to further establish these associations.

title: A diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging study of corpus callosum from adult patients with migraine complicated with depressive/anxious disorder.
text: The aim of this study was to investigate microstructural abnormalities in the corpus callosum (CC) of adult patients with migraine without aura, who also experienced depressive or anxious disorders. Background: Emotional disorders are more prevalent in the migraine population, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Methods: Diffusion tensor magnetic resonance imaging (DT-MRI) was conducted in 12 patients with simple migraine (without aura or depressive/anxious disorder) (S-M group), 12 patients with migraine complicated by depressive/anxious disorder (Co-M group), and 12 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (Control group). Fractional anisotropy (FA) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) were measured at the genu, body, and splenium of the CC. Results: There were significant differences in FA values among the three groups, with the Co-M group showing lower FA values than both the S-M group and Control group (P < 0.05 and P < 0.01, respectively). The FA values from the Co-M group were significantly lower than the S-M group (P < 0.01). ADC values were not significantly different among the groups. Negative correlations were found between FA values at the genu and body of the CC and headache frequency, as well as between FA values at all locations of the CC and Hamilton anxiety and depression scores (all P < 0.05). Conclusions: These findings suggest that there may be integrity changes in the neurofibrotic microstructures of the CC in migraine patients with depressive/anxious disorder.

title: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonists for the Prevention of Adverse events following percutaneous coronary Revascularization--results of the PPAR study.
text:
Background: Patients with metabolic syndrome are at higher risk of developing cardiovascular complications after undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We aimed to determine if peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonists have any beneficial effects on these patients.
Methods: A total of 200 patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing PCI were randomly assigned to either rosiglitazone or a placebo and followed for one year. We measured carotid intima-medial thickness (CIMT), inflammatory markers, lipid levels, brain natriuretic peptide, and clinical events at baseline, six months, and one year.
Results: There was no significant difference in CIMT between the two groups. The 12-month composite endpoint of death, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, or any recurrent ischemia was not significantly different between the rosiglitazone and placebo groups (31.4% vs 30.2%, P = .99). The rate of death, MI, or stroke at 12 months was numerically lower in the rosiglitazone group (11.9% vs 6.4%, P = .19). There was a trend towards a greater decrease over time in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein values compared to baseline in the rosiglitazone group at six months (-35.4% vs -15.8%, P = .059) and 12 months (-40.0% vs -20.9%, P = .089), as well as higher change in high-density lipoprotein (+15.5% vs +4.1%, P = .05) and lower triglycerides (-13.9% vs +14.9%, P = .004) in the rosiglitazone group. There was no significant increase in new onset diabetes in the rosiglitazone group (0% vs 3.3%, P = .081) and no episodes of symptomatic hypoglycemia.
Conclusions: Patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing PCI are at higher risk of subsequent cardiovascular events. Rosiglitazone treatment for 12 months did not significantly affect CIMT in this population, although it had beneficial effects on inflammatory markers, lipid levels, and triglycerides. Further study of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonism in patients with metabolic syndrome undergoing PCI may be warranted.

title: Accumulation of hydroxyethyl starch in human and animal tissues: a systematic review
text: To conduct a systematic review of clinical and preclinical data on hydroxyethyl starch (HES) tissue storage, we searched MEDLINE (PubMed) and screened abstracts using defined criteria. Forty-eight studies were included, with 37 human studies and 11 animal studies, resulting in a total of 635 human patients and 11 experimental animals. The most common indication for fluid infusion was surgery, accounting for 282 patients (45.9%). HES accumulation was observed in various organs, including skin (17 studies), kidney (12 studies), liver (8 studies), and bone marrow (5 studies). Additional sites of HES deposition were lymph nodes, spleen, lung, pancreas, intestine, muscle, trophoblast, and placental stroma. The highest measured tissue concentration of HES was found in the kidney, and HES uptake into intracellular vacuoles was observed within 30 minutes after infusion. Storage was cumulative and increased in proportion to dose, although in 15% of patients, storage and associated symptoms were observed at low cumulative doses (0.4g/kg−1). Some HES deposits persisted for extended periods, up to 8 years or more in skin and 10 years in kidney. Pruritus and renal dysfunction were commonly reported adverse effects associated with HES storage. In one randomized trial, HES infusion produced osmotic nephrosis-like lesions and increased the need for renal replacement therapy. The tissue distribution of HES was similar in both animals and humans. Tissue storage of HES was found to be widespread, rapid, cumulative, frequently long-lasting, and potentially harmful.

title: Cationic host defense (antimicrobial) peptides.
text: Members of the cationic host defense (antimicrobial) peptide family are ubiquitous in nature, found in organisms ranging from insects to plants to mammals and non-mammalian vertebrates. Although many of these peptides demonstrate direct antimicrobial activity against bacteria, fungi, eukaryotic parasites, and viruses, it is well established that cationic peptides play a crucial modulatory role in the innate immune response. Recent research has additionally shown that host defense peptides act as effective adjuvants, synergizing with other immune effectors, polarizing the adaptive response, and supporting wound healing. Furthermore, ongoing investigations into the mechanisms of action of these peptides are providing a deeper understanding of their therapeutic potential, paving the way for more effective utilization of derivatives of these endogenous peptides as therapeutic agents.

title: A mental health intervention for schoolchildren exposed to violence: a randomized controlled trial.
text:
A randomized controlled trial was conducted in the 2001-2002 academic year to evaluate the effectiveness of a school-based intervention in reducing symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression in sixth-grade students who had been exposed to violence. The study included 61 students in the early intervention group and 65 students in the wait-list delayed intervention comparison group. The intervention consisted of a standardized 10-session cognitive-behavioral therapy called the Cognitive-Behavioral Intervention for Trauma in Schools, which was delivered by trained school mental health clinicians.
The study found that after 3 months of intervention, students in the early intervention group had significantly lower scores on symptoms of PTSD, depression, and psychosocial dysfunction compared to the wait-list delayed intervention group. However, there were no significant differences between the two groups in teacher-reported classroom problems. At 6 months, the differences between the two groups were not significantly different for symptoms of PTSD and depression, and teachers did not report significant differences in classroom behaviors.
The study concluded that a standardized 10-session cognitive-behavioral intervention can significantly reduce symptoms of PTSD and depression in students who have been exposed to violence and can be effectively delivered on school campuses by trained school-based mental health clinicians.

title: Knowledge gaps and misconceptions about coronary heart disease among U.S. South Asians.
text:
BACKGROUND South Asians are disproportionately affected by coronary heart disease (CHD) compared to other racial/ethnic groups in the United States, yet there has been limited research on this disparity. To address this knowledge gap and develop culturally targeted CHD prevention messages for this rapidly growing community, we examined South Asians' knowledge and beliefs about CHD.
PURPOSE Our goal was to investigate the extent to which South Asians are aware of CHD risk factors and prevention strategies, and to identify factors associated with lower knowledge levels.
METHODS In 2008, we conducted a cross-sectional study of 270 South Asian adults in Illinois, analyzing data collected through interviews conducted in English, Hindi, or Urdu using a standardized questionnaire. We used multivariate regression models to examine the relationships between sociodemographics, CHD knowledge, and attitudes toward preventability.
RESULTS Findings revealed that 81% of participants had one or more CHD risk factors, while only 11% mentioned controlling blood pressure, 10% cholesterol, and 5% diabetes as prevention strategies. Shockingly, 53% of participants believed that heart attacks are not preventable. Lower education levels, being interviewed in Urdu or Hindi, and lower levels of acculturation were associated with lower levels of CHD knowledge and a belief that CHD is not preventable.
CONCLUSIONS Our study found that the majority of South Asians in this sample believed that CHD is not preventable and had limited awareness of modifiable risk factors. To effectively promote risk factor control and behavior change, CHD education messages may need to be tailored to subgroups (e.g., by education and language) and emphasize the importance of healthy lifestyle choices and medical interventions.

title: Innate host defense requires TFEB-mediated transcription of cytoprotective and antimicrobial genes.
text: To enhance animal resistance against infection, the correct expression of defense genes at the right time and place is crucial. Understanding this intricate control mechanism requires identifying the involved transcription factors. By taking an unbiased approach in the model organism Caenorhabditis elegans, we discovered that HLH-30 (also known as TFEB in mammals) is a key transcription factor in host defense. Following Staphylococcus aureus infection, HLH-30 was activated, leading to the expression of nearly 80% of host response genes, including antimicrobial and autophagy genes vital for the host's tolerance of infection. Similarly, TFEB was rapidly activated in murine macrophages upon S. aureus infection and played a critical role in the proper transcriptional activation of multiple proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines. Our findings suggest that TFEB is a previously unappreciated, evolutionarily ancient transcription factor in the host response to infection.

title: DAP kinase regulates JNK signaling by binding and activating protein kinase D under oxidative stress
text: The stress-activated kinase, JNK, plays a crucial role in mediating cellular responses to oxidative stress. Our findings reveal that DAP kinase (DAPk), a Ser/Thr protein kinase that promotes cell death, plays a pivotal role in oxidative stress-induced JNK signaling. Through identification of protein kinase D (PKD) as a novel substrate of DAPk, we demonstrate that DAPk physically interacts with PKD in response to oxidative stress. Additionally, we show that DAPk activates PKD in cells and that JNK phosphorylation induced by ectopically expressed DAPk can be attenuated by suppressing PKD expression or inhibiting its catalytic activity. Furthermore, depletion of DAPk expression leads to a significant reduction in JNK activation under oxidative stress conditions, indicating that DAPk is indispensable for the activation of JNK signaling. Lastly, our findings demonstrate that DAPk is necessary for cell death under oxidative stress, which exhibits characteristics of caspase-independent necrotic cell death. Taken together, these results establish a pivotal role for DAPk and its specific interaction with PKD in regulating the JNK signaling network under oxidative stress conditions.

title: The changes of antioxidant defense system caused by quercetin administration do not lead to DNA damage and apoptosis in the spleen and bone marrow cells of rats.
text: The intriguing aspect of quercetin is its potential dual role as both an anti- and pro-oxidant. To delve into this phenomenon, an investigation was conducted to assess the effects of quercetin on the redox state of cells in the bone marrow and spleen of rats. The study involved administering quercetin to rats at doses of 8 or 80mg/kg body weight via gavage for 40 days. The study examined the cellular redox state by measuring ferric ion reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) levels and malondialdehyde (MDA) concentration. Additionally, the expression of hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HO-1) mRNA was evaluated using real-time polymerase chain reaction. The study also determined the extent of DNA damage using the alkaline-labile comet assay. Furthermore, the potential pro-apoptotic effect of quercetin was investigated using the FITC-Annexin V kit. To determine the levels of quercetin and isorhamnetin in the serum, high-performance liquid chromatography-electrochemical detection (HPLC-ECD) was employed. The study found that treatment with quercetin in a dose of 80mg/kg body weight significantly decreased MDA levels and increased FRAP values in the bone marrow and spleen cells, compared to the control group. Moreover, quercetin dose-dependently upregulated the expression of HO-1 mRNA in the bone marrow cells. The study did not observe any evidence of DNA damage or pro-apoptotic activity in the examined cells. The results of this investigation confirm that changes in the antioxidant state caused by quercetin do not lead to DNA damage or exert any pro-apoptotic activity in vivo.

title: Mutated KRAS results in overexpression of DUSP4, a MAP-kinase phosphatase, and SMYD3, a histone methyltransferase, in rectal carcinomas.
text: Mutations in the KRAS oncogene are associated with resistance to treatment with antibodies targeting the epithelial growth factor receptor (EGFR) in patients with colorectal cancer. To overcome this challenge, drugs that inhibit signaling pathways activated by KRAS mutations could be effective. To identify these pathways, we analyzed pre-treatment biopsies and normal mucosa from 65 patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, of whom 30 had KRAS mutations. Using global gene expression microarrays, we identified a total of 22,297 differentially expressed genes (adjusted P-value <0.05) between normal mucosa and cancer, including novel rectal cancer-specific genes. We then analyzed the expression of genes in KRAS-mutant tumors and found that the upregulation of 13 genes was significantly correlated with the presence of activating KRAS mutations, including DUSP4, a MAP-kinase phosphatase, and SMYD3, a histone methyltransferase. Previous studies have shown that inhibiting the expression of these genes using MEK1 inhibitor PD98059 and the antibacterial compound Novobiocin, respectively, could be a potential approach to overcome resistance to EGFR targeting agents in KRAS-mutant rectal cancers.

title: Clinicopathological and prognostic significance of Bmi-1 expression in human cervical cancer.
text:
Title: Investigating the Clinical Significance of Bmi-1 Expression as a Prognostic Marker for Cervical Cancer
Objective: To investigate the clinical significance of Bmi-1 expression as a prognostic marker for cervical cancer.
Design: A retrospective analysis of a population-based cohort.
Setting: Jiangsu Province Hospital.
Population: Eighty-eight women diagnosed with cervical carcinoma between 2000 and 2003.
Methods: RT-PCR assay was performed to determine Bmi-1 mRNA expression in 18 cervical cancer and non-cancerous tissue samples, and immunohistochemistry was used to detect Bmi-1 protein expression in 88 cervical cancer samples. The correlation between Bmi-1 expression and clinicopathological factors was analyzed. Additionally, statistical analyses were applied to test for prognostic associations. RNA interference was used to downregulate Bmi-1 expression in a cervical cancer cell line (HeLa), and the effects of Bmi-1 inhibition on in vitro and in vivo growth, cell cycle distribution, and apoptosis were determined.
Main Outcome Measures: The levels of Bmi-1 mRNA and protein expression in tissues were evaluated by RT-PCR and Western Blot assays.
Results: The level of Bmi-1 mRNA expression in cervical cancer tissues was significantly higher than that in corresponding non-cancerous tissues. High Bmi-1 expression was significantly correlated with poor tumor differentiation, advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, and positive lymph node metastasis. Patients with high Bmi-1 expression showed shorter overall survival than those with low expression. Univariate and multivariate analyses showed that high Bmi-1 expression was an independent prognostic factor.
Conclusions: RNA interference-mediated Bmi-1 inhibition could inhibit in vitro and in vivo growth, enhance apoptosis, and induce cell cycle arrest of cervical cancer cells. Bmi-1 might be an independent prognostic marker for cervical cancer patients.

title: Dexamethasone decreases vomiting by children after tonsillectomy.
text: We conducted a randomized, stratified, blocked, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to investigate the effectiveness of dexamethasone in reducing vomiting after elective tonsillectomy in 133 healthy children aged 2-12 years. Anesthesia was induced with inhalation of N2O and halothane or IV propofol, and maintained with N2O and halothane. Dexamethasone (up to 8 mg/kg, maximum dose) or placebo was administered IV before surgery. All patients received 1.5 mg/kg codeine IM intraoperatively. Standardized protocols were followed for perioperative IV fluids, emesis management, postoperative pain management, and hospital discharge criteria. Our findings showed that the overall incidence of vomiting was significantly reduced from 72% in the placebo group to 40% (P < 0.001) in the dexamethasone group. Prophylactic administration of dexamethasone resulted in decreased vomiting both in-hospital and post-discharge, with each episode of in-hospital vomiting prolonging discharge by 13 ± 2 minutes (P < 0.001). Our results indicate that dexamethasone markedly decreased vomiting in healthy children after elective tonsillectomy in an ambulatory hospital setting.

title: A Conserved Histidine in the RNA Sensor RIG-I Controls Immune Tolerance to N1-2'O-Methylated Self RNA.
text: The cytosolic helicase retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) detects viral 5'-triphosphorylated RNA (pppRNA) to initiate immune responses against RNA viruses. While endogenous mRNA is also 5'-triphosphorylated, modifications to the backbone and the presence of the 5'-ppp-linked methylguanosine ((m7)G) cap prevent RIG-I recognition. Interestingly, we discovered that the methylation status of endogenous capped mRNA at the 5'-terminal nucleotide (N1) plays a crucial role in preventing RIG-I activation. Specifically, we found that a single conserved amino acid (H830) in the RIG-I RNA binding pocket acts as a mediator of steric exclusion of N1-2'O-methylated RNA. When this amino acid was mutated (RIG-I(H830A)), binding of N1-2'O-methylated pppRNA was restored, leading to activation of the mutant protein in response to endogenous mRNA. Similarly, inhibition of the endogenous N1-2'O-methyltransferase resulted in enhanced RIG-I stimulation in the absence of exogenous stimuli. Our findings suggest a new mechanism by which viruses exploit N1-2'O-methylation of the cap to evade RIG-I detection.

title: lumi: a pipeline for processing Illumina microarray.
text:
The Illumina microarray is gaining popularity as a microarray platform. Unique to the BeadArray technology from Illumina, its preprocessing and quality control differ from other microarray technologies. Despite this, most analyses have not leveraged the distinct capabilities of the BeadArray system and have instead incorporated preprocessing methods originally designed for Affymetrix microarrays. To address this, the lumi Bioconductor package was developed especially for processing Illumina microarray data. It encompasses a range of components, including data input, quality control, variance stabilization, normalization, and gene annotation. Specifically, the lumi package features a variance-stabilizing transformation (VST) algorithm that takes full advantage of the technical replicates present on every Illumina microarray. Multiple normalization method options and various quality control plots are also provided within the package. In addition, a vendor-independent nucleotide universal identifier (nuID) was created to identify the probes of Illumina microarrays, facilitating their annotation. The nuID annotation packages and the processed results from lumi can be effortlessly integrated with other Bioconductor packages to construct a comprehensive statistical data analysis pipeline for Illumina data.
AVAILABILITY
The lumi Bioconductor package is accessible at <https://www.bioconductor.org/>.

title: Large scale replication and meta-analysis of variants on chromosome 4q25 associated with atrial fibrillation.
text: Recent genome-wide association studies have identified a haplotype block on chromosome 4q25 as a potential risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF). To further investigate these findings, we replicated the association in four independent cohorts, including the Framingham Heart Study and Rotterdam Study, which are community-based longitudinal studies, as well as the Vanderbilt AF Registry and German AF Network (AFNet), which are case-control studies. Our results confirm the initial association, showing that the non-coding SNPs rs2200733 and rs10033464 are strongly associated with AF in over 3,500 individuals with the condition. The association was observed in all four cohorts, with the strongest association found in the AFNet cohort. We also conducted a meta-analysis of the current and prior AF studies, which further supported the findings and indicated an increased risk of AF for both SNPs. These results provide further evidence of the relation between AF and intergenic variants on chromosome 4.

title: Ecological analysis of ethnic differences in relation between tuberculosis and poverty.
text:
Objective: To investigate the impact of ethnicity on the relationship between tuberculosis and deprivation.
Design: Retrospective ecological study comparing the incidence of tuberculosis among white and South Asian residents of 39 electoral wards in Birmingham, using ethnic-specific indices of deprivation.
Setting: Birmingham, 1989-1993.
Subjects: 1516 patients notified with tuberculosis.
Main Outcomes Measures: Tuberculosis rates and measures of deprivation.
Results: Univariate analysis revealed significant associations between tuberculosis rates for the entire population and several indices of deprivation (P < 0.01) and the proportion of South Asian residents in the area (P < 0.01). All deprivation covariates were positively correlated with each other, but after controlling for multiple variables, only overcrowding was independently associated with tuberculosis rates. For the white population, overcrowding was associated with tuberculosis rates independently of other variables (P = 0.0036). No significant association between deprivation and tuberculosis was found for the South Asian population in either single or multivariable analyses.
Conclusions: Poverty is significantly associated with tuberculosis in the white population, but no such relationship exists for those of Asian ethnicity. These findings suggest that the underlying causes and potential interventions may differ by ethnic group.

title: Reduced expression of oestrogen receptor beta in invasive breast cancer and its re-expression using DNA methyl transferase inhibitors in a cell line model.
text: To gain insights into the possible role of estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) in breast cancer development, immunohistochemical analysis of ERβ was conducted on 512 breast tissue samples, including normal (n=138), pure ductal carcinoma in situ (n=16), invasive cancers (n=319), lymph node metastases (n=31), and recurrences (n=8). Real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was also used to investigate the methylation status of the ERβ gene in ERβ-negative breast cancer cell lines, SkBr3 and MDA-MB-435. The study found that there was a gradual decrease in ERβ expression during the transition from normal and pre-invasive lesions to invasive cancers, with ERβ being lost in 21% of cases. This decrease was more pronounced in invasive ductal carcinomas than in lobular carcinomas, with a higher proportion of ERβ-positive cases in the latter (74% vs 91%, p=0.0004). Moreover, examination of paired primary cancers and their axillary lymph node metastases revealed that if ERβ was present in the primary tumor, it persisted in the metastasis. Treatment of ERβ-negative cell lines with DNA methyltransferase inhibitors restored ERβ expression, providing evidence that silencing of ERβ in breast carcinomas may be due to promoter hypermethylation. These findings suggest that loss of ERβ expression is a hallmark of breast cancer development and may be a reversible process involving methylation.

title: Atopy risk in infants and children in relation to early exposure to fish, oily fish, or long-chain omega-3 fatty acids: a systematic review.
text: There are two main categories of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs): n-6 and n-3. It has been suggested that a causal relationship exists between n-6 PUFA intake and the development of allergies, and there are biological mechanisms that could explain this, involving the eicosanoid mediators of arachidonic acid, which are found in n-6 PUFAs. On the other hand, long-chain n-3 PUFAs found in fish and fish oils have the opposite effect, and may protect against atopic sensitization and the clinical manifestations of atopy. Epidemiological studies have investigated the relationship between fish intake during pregnancy, lactation, infancy, and childhood, and atopic outcomes in infants and children. All five studies conducted on the effect of maternal fish intake during pregnancy on atopic outcomes in infants/children found protective associations. However, only one study found no significant associations during lactation. The evidence from studies conducted on fish intake during infancy and childhood is inconsistent, although the majority of the studies (nine of 14) showed a protective effect of fish intake during infancy or childhood on atopic outcomes in those infants/children. Supplementation with fish oil during pregnancy, lactation, or during infancy or childhood leads to higher levels of n-3 PUFAs in the infants or children. Providing fish oil to pregnant women has been associated with immunological changes in cord blood, and these changes may persist. Studies to date suggest that providing fish oil during pregnancy may reduce sensitization to common food allergens and reduce the prevalence and severity of atopic dermatitis in the first year of life, with a possible persistence until adolescence with a reduction in eczema, hay fever, and asthma. While fish oil supplementation in infancy may decrease the risk of developing some manifestations of allergic disease, it is not clear if this benefit will persist as other factors come into play. It is also unclear whether fish oil can be used to treat children with asthma, as the two studies conducted to date have given divergent results. Further studies are needed to more clearly identify the immunological and clinical effects in infants and children and to identify protective and therapeutic effects and their persistence.

title: Dietary quality among men and women in 187 countries in 1990 and 2010: a systematic assessment
text:
Global Trends in Dietary Patterns: A Systematic Assessment
Background:
A healthy diet is crucial for reducing the burden of non-communicable diseases worldwide. However, there is a need to better understand global dietary patterns and their changes over time. This systematic assessment aimed to characterize global dietary trends and their heterogeneity by age, sex, national income, and dietary pattern.
Methods:
This study evaluated global consumption of key dietary items by region, age, sex, and national income using surveys covering 88.7% of the global adult population. Two dietary patterns were assessed based on the consumption of healthy or unhealthy items. The authors used hierarchical linear regression to examine the relationship between dietary patterns and various predictors, including country, age, sex, national income, and time.
Findings:

From 1990 to 2010, global diets based on healthy items improved by 2.2 points, while diets based on unhealthy items worsened by 2.5 points. In 2010, the global mean scores were 44.0 for the healthy pattern and 52.1 for the unhealthy pattern, with weak intercorrelation between countries. Better diets were observed in older adults, women, and high-income countries. Middle-income countries showed the largest improvement in dietary patterns based on healthy items, but the largest deterioration in dietary patterns based on unhealthy items. There was significant heterogeneity in dietary patterns across regions and countries, with varying trends in different parts of the world.
Interpretation:


Consumption of healthy items improved globally, while consumption of unhealthy items worsened, with significant heterogeneity in dietary patterns across regions and countries. These findings provide the best estimates of nutrition transitions across the world and inform policies to reduce the health and economic burdens of poor diet quality. Funding for this study was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the Medical Research Council.

title: The epidemiology of major depressive disorder: results from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R).
text: The paper presents nationally representative data on the prevalence and correlates of major depressive disorder (MDD) in the United States using the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R). The study found that the lifetime prevalence of MDD was 16.2% (95% CI: 15.1-17.3), equivalent to 32.6-35.1 million adults in the US population. The 12-month prevalence of MDD was 6.6% (95% CI: 5.9-7.3), corresponding to 13.1-14.2 million adults. Almost all cases of 12-month MDD were found to be clinically significant, with 10.4% mild, 38.6% moderate, 38.0% severe, and 12.9% very severe. The mean duration of episodes was 16 weeks. Significant role impairment was observed in 59.3% of 12-month cases, indicating severe or very severe role impairment. The study found that 72.1% of lifetime and 78.5% of 12-month cases had comorbid disorders, with MDD typically occurring in conjunction with other conditions. However, MDD was rarely the only disorder present. While 51.6% of 12-month cases received treatment for MDD, treatment was considered inadequate in only 41.9% of these cases, resulting in 21.7% of 12-month MDD being inadequately treated. The study highlights the need for improved treatment quality and expanded access to treatment, as well as increased emphasis on screening for MDD.

title: The Pain Catastrophizing Scale: Further Psychometric Evaluation with Adult Samples
text: In prior studies conducted with undergraduate students, the Pain Catastrophizing Scale (PCS) has been found to have a reliable and oblique three-factor structure. In this study, we aimed to examine the reliability and validity of the PCS in adult community and pain outpatient samples. Our findings indicate that the PCS exhibited high internal consistency in both groups. Using data from the community sample, confirmatory factor analysis revealed that the PCS taps a single construct with three related dimensions. Significant gender differences were also observed on the PCS total score in both groups. Moreover, the analyses showed that there were differences between the community and outpatient samples on the PCS total and subscales. Overall, the results provide strong evidence of criterion-related, concurrent, and discriminant validity for the PCS in the community sample. Nevertheless, limitations of the present study are discussed.

title: Temsirolimus, interferon alfa, or both for advanced renal-cell carcinoma.
text: BACKGROUND: Interferon alfa is a widely used treatment for metastatic renal-cell carcinoma; however, its efficacy and tolerability are limited. Temsirolimus, a specific inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin kinase, has shown promise in improving patient outcomes. METHODS: In this multicenter, phase 3 trial, we randomly assigned 626 patients with previously untreated, poor-prognosis metastatic renal-cell carcinoma to receive either intravenous temsirolimus (25 mg/week), subcutaneous interferon alfa (with a dose increase to 18 million U/three times weekly), or combination therapy with 15 mg/week temsirolimus plus 6 million U/three times weekly interferon alfa. The primary endpoint was overall survival in comparisons of the temsirolimus group and the combination-therapy group with the interferon group. RESULTS: Patients receiving temsirolimus alone experienced longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.58-0.92; P=0.008) and progression-free survival (P<0.001) compared to patients receiving interferon alone. Overall survival in the combination-therapy group did not differ significantly from that in the interferon group (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.76-1.20; P=0.70). Median overall survival times in the interferon group, the temsirolimus group, and the combination-therapy group were 7.3, 10.9, and 8.4 months, respectively. Adverse events were more common in the temsirolimus group, including rash, peripheral edema, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia, whereas asthenia was more common in the interferon group. Fewer patients in the temsirolimus group experienced serious adverse events compared to the interferon group (P=0.02). CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that temsirolimus improves overall survival among patients with metastatic renal-cell carcinoma and a poor prognosis, compared to interferon alfa. Addition of temsirolimus to interferon did not improve survival. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00065468 [ClinicalTrials.gov].)

title: Macrophage Diversity Enhances Tumor Progression and Metastasis
text: There is compelling scientific evidence that macrophages play a role in the initiation and progression of cancer. During the early stages of tumor formation, macrophages create an inflammatory environment that promotes growth and mutagenesis. As the tumor progresses, macrophages stimulate angiogenesis, enhance tumor cell migration and invasion, and suppress the body's natural defenses against the tumor. At metastatic sites, macrophages prepare the target tissue for the arrival of tumor cells and then promote tumor cell extravasation, survival, and growth. Furthermore, there may be specialized subpopulations of macrophages that represent potential new therapeutic targets.

title: Ankle brachial index as a predictor of cognitive impairment in the general population: ten-year follow-up of the Edinburgh Artery Study.
text:
Objective: To investigate the association between ankle brachial index (ABI) and cognitive impairment in older individuals over a 10-year period.
Design: Cohort study (Edinburgh Artery Study)
Setting: Eleven general practices in Edinburgh, Scotland.
Participants: 717 men and women aged 55-74 from the general population, followed for 10 years.
Measurements: ABI was measured at baseline, while major cognitive functions, including premorbid function (assessed using the National Adult Reading Test, NART), were tested after 10 years.
Results: After adjusting for age and sex, a low ABI was associated with lower scores on Raven's Matrices (odds ratio (OR) =1.6, 95% confidence interval (CI) =1.0-2.6), Verbal Fluency (OR =1.8, 95% CI =1.1-3.0), and Digit Symbol Test (OR =2.3, 95% CI =1.3-4.2), suggesting that ABI is predictive of poorer performance in nonverbal reasoning, verbal fluency, and information processing speed. The association between ABI and the Digit Symbol Test remained significant after further adjusting for premorbid cognitive function (tested using the NART), indicating that ABI is also predictive of decline in information processing speed (from premorbid ability to that measured here in older age).
Conclusion: The ABI may be useful in identifying older individuals at higher risk of cognitive impairment. Future preventive measures should target individuals with a low ABI and aim to reduce both vascular-related cognitive decline and cardiovascular events to reduce the incidence and consequences of subsequent cognitive impairment and dementia.

title: PTEN Regulates PI(3,4)P2 Signaling Downstream of Class I PI3K
text: The PI3K signaling pathway regulates cell growth and movement, and is frequently altered in cancer. Class I PI3Ks produce the lipid messenger PI(3,4,5)P3. PI(3,4,5)P3 can be dephosphorylated by 3- or 5-phosphatases, resulting in PI(3,4)P2. The tumor suppressor PTEN is thought to mainly act as a PI(3,4)P3 3-phosphatase, thereby limiting the activation of this pathway. Our findings reveal that PTEN also functions as a PI(3,4)P2 3-phosphatase in both in vitro and in vivo settings. PTEN is a prominent PI(3,4)P2 phosphatase in Mcf10a cytosol, and simultaneous deletion of PTEN and INPP4B, a known PI(3,4)P2 4-phosphatase, leads to increased accumulation of PI(3,4)P2, which correlates with enhanced invadopodia in EGF-stimulated cells. Deletion of PTEN resulted in elevated PI(3,4)P2 levels in a mouse model of prostate cancer, and it inversely correlated with PI(3,4)P2 levels across several EGF-stimulated prostate and breast cancer lines. These Findings suggest a role for PI(3,4)P2 in the phenotype caused by loss-of-function mutations or deletions in PTEN.

title: Genetic analysis of an ARS element from the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
text: Autonomously replicating sequence (ARS) elements are genomic fragments that can serve as origins of DNA replication in yeast. In this study, we conducted a fine-structural analysis of ars1, a specific ARS element present in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe. By characterizing a series of nested deletion mutations, we found that the minimal fragment of DNA encompassing ars1 is surprisingly large, with no fragment smaller than 650 base pairs (bp) retaining significant ARS activity. Through a detailed analysis of deletion and substitution mutations spanning the entire minimal ars1, we identified a single essential 50-bp fragment (segment 1) that is crucial for efficient ARS function. Additionally, we discovered a second type of genetic element in the ars1, which is more tolerant of internal structural alterations. Further analysis of segment 1 revealed a critical 30-bp A/T-rich segment that appears to contain redundant genetic elements. Interestingly, while Schizosaccharomyces pombe ars1 promoted high-frequency transformation in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, this heterologous activity was not dependent on segment 1, suggesting that the functional elements required for ARS function in these two species are distinct.

title: N terminus of Swr1 binds to histone H2AZ and provides a platform for subunit assembly in the chromatin remodeling complex.
text: The SWR1 complex is involved in regulating gene expression by modifying histone H2A with variant histone H2AZ. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the SWR1 complex deposes chromatin histone H2AZ through an ATP-dependent process mediated by fourteen subunits. Previous research identified the role of seven subunits (Swr1 ATPase, Swc2, Swc3, Arp6, Swc5, Yaf9, and Swc6) in maintaining complex integrity and histone H2AZ replacement activity. This study focused on the functional roles of three additional subunits: Bdf1, Arp4, and Swc7. Affinity purification of mutant SWR1 complexes revealed that depletion of Arp4 (arp4-td) significantly impaired the association of Bdf1, Yaf9, and Swc4. In contrast, loss of either Bdf1 or Swc7 had minimal effects on overall complex integrity. Moreover, the basic H2AZ histone replacement activity of SWR1 in vitro required Arp4 but not Bdf1 or Swc7. These findings suggest that three out of fourteen SWR1 subunits, including Bdf1, Swc7, and previously identified Swc3, play auxiliary roles in the basic histone replacement activity. The N-terminal region of the Swr1 ATPase subunit is necessary and sufficient for the association of Bdf1, Swc7, Arp4, Act1, Yaf9, and Swc4. Additionally, this region contains an unidentified H2AZ-H2B specific binding site distinct from the previously known Swc2 subunit. These findings indicate that one SWR1 enzyme can bind two H2AZ-H2B dimers and provide insight into the hierarchy and interdependencies of molecular interactions within the SWR1 complex.

title: Role of the cytoskeleton during leukocyte responses
text: The cellular network of the cytoskeleton plays a crucial role in regulating various cellular functions related to the immune response, including migration, extravasation, antigen recognition, activation, and phagocytosis by different types of leukocytes. Recent studies have identified a variety of regulatory elements and structural components of the leukocyte cytoskeleton. In this review, we will discuss the composition and regulation of these cytoskeletal elements and their important role in immune responses.

title: Integration of mental health into primary healthcare in low-income countries: avoiding medicalization.
text:
Since 2008, the World Health Organization (WHO) has been working through its mental health Gap Action Programme to revitalize efforts to integrate mental health into non-specialized healthcare (e.g. primary care). While this approach has generated renewed interest and potential for mental health service delivery, it has also faced criticism. Some concerns raised include that it could lead to the medicalization of social and psychological problems and inadvertently focus solely on primary care without sufficient attention given to strengthening other levels of the healthcare system, such as community-based care and care on district levels. This paper highlights seven key elements that could help prevent an overly biomedical approach to mental healthcare when integrating mental health into non-specialized healthcare:
1. Using task-shifting approaches within a stepped care system, where non-specialists are trained to provide basic mental health interventions, and specialists handle more complex cases.
2. Ensuring primary mental healthcare includes brief psychotherapeutic interventions, which can help manage mild to moderate mental health issues.
3. Promoting community-based recovery-oriented interventions for people with disabling chronic mental disorders, which can help them manage their conditions and improve their quality of life.
4. Conceptualizing training as a continuous process of strengthening clinical competencies through supervision, ensuring that healthcare providers are equipped to handle a range of mental health issues.
5. Engaging communities as partners in psychosocial interventions, which can help build trust and increase the effectiveness of interventions.
6. Embedding shifts to primary mental healthcare within wider health policy reforms, ensuring a comprehensive approach to mental healthcare that addresses social determinants of mental health, such as poverty, education, and employment.
7. Promoting inter-sectoral approaches to address social determinants of mental health, which can help tackle the root causes of mental health issues and improve overall health outcomes. By focusing on these elements, the integration of mental health into non-specialized healthcare can be done in a way that promotes a comprehensive and sustainable approach to mental healthcare.

title: Comparison of clomiphene citrate, metformin, or the combination of both for first-line ovulation induction and achievement of pregnancy in 154 women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
text:
Objective: To compare the effectiveness of clomiphene citrate (CC) and metformin in ovulation induction and pregnancy achievement in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and to identify patient characteristics associated with a better response to therapy.
Design: Observational comparative study.
Setting: Fertility clinic.
Patients: One hundred fifty-four infertile women with oligomenorrhea and hyperandrogenism.
Intervention: Group 1 (56 patients) received CC 50 mg from days 5-9 of the cycle. Group 2 (57 patients) received 500 mg of metformin 3 times a day. Group 3 (41 patients) received both medications.
Main Outcome Measures: Ovulation and pregnancy.
Results: Patients receiving metformin alone had a higher ovulation rate compared to those receiving CC alone (75.4% vs. 50%). However, the ovulation rates were similar between the metformin and combination groups (75.4% vs. 63.4%). Pregnancy rates were equivalent in the three groups. The response to metformin was independent of body weight and dose, and nonsmoking was a predictor of better ovulatory response overall, as well as lower fasting glucose for CC and lower androgens for metformin.
Conclusion: Metformin is more effective than CC alone for ovulation induction in PCOS patients, and the response to metformin is independent of body weight and dose. Based on these findings, metformin can be used as a first-line medication for ovulation induction in PCOS patients, regardless of their weight and insulin levels, due to its efficacy and known safety profile.

title: Pulmonologist involvement, stage-specific treatment, and survival in adults with non-small cell lung cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
text:
Approximately 80% of patients with lung cancer also suffer from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, many of these individuals are unsuitable for treatment due to their poor lung function and low functional status, leading to a significant number of patients foregoing treatment. This study aims to examine the impact of pulmonologist-guided management on the likelihood of receiving stage-specific treatment and overall survival in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have pre-existing COPD.
Methods:
The study used data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) tumor registry linked to Medicare claims to identify patients diagnosed with early-stage (2002-2005) or advanced-stage (2002-2005) NSCLC with a previous COPD diagnosis (3-24 months prior to NSCLC diagnosis). The outcomes of the study included the receipt of stage-specific treatment (surgical resection for early-stage NSCLC and chemotherapy for advanced-stage NSCLC) and overall survival. Pulmonologist management was determined by observing the presence of one or more Evaluation and Management visit claims with a pulmonologist specialty within 6 months of NSCLC diagnosis.
Findings:
The cohort included 5,488 patients with early-stage NSCLC and 6,426 patients with advNSCLC disease with preexisting COPD. Pulmonologist management was recorded for 54.9% of patients with early-stage NSCLC and 35.7% of patients with advNSCLC. Among patients with pulmonologist involvement, 58.5% of patients with early-stage NSCLC received surgical resection, and 43.6% of patients with advNSCLC received chemotherapy. Pulmonologist management after NSCLC diagnosis was associated with increased surgical resection rates for early-stage NSCLC (odds ratio, 1.26; 95% confidence interval, 1.11-1.45) and increased chemotherapy rates for advNSCLC (odds ratio, 1.88; 95% confidence interval, 1.67-2.10). Pulmonologist management was also associated with reduced mortality risk for patients with early-stage NSCLC but not advNSCLC.
Conclusion:
These findings provide preliminary support for the recently published guidelines emphasizing the role of pulmonologists in lung cancer management, as pulmonologist management was found to have a positive association with the likelihood of receiving stage-specific treatment and overall survival in both early-stage and advanced-stage NSCLC patients with preexisting COPD.

title: Divalent cations differentially regulate integrin alphaIIb cytoplasmic tail binding to beta3 and to calcium- and integrin-binding protein.
text: Using recombinant or synthetic alphaIIb and beta3 integrin cytoplasmic peptides, we investigated their in vitro complexation and ligand binding capacity using surface plasmon resonance. Our results showed that alpha.beta heterodimerization occurred in a 1:1 stoichiometry with a weak dissociation constant (KD) in the micromolar range. Divalent cations were not essential for this association, but they enhanced the stability of the alpha.beta complex by reducing dissociation rates. The alpha.beta complex was impaired by the R995A substitution or the KVGFFKR deletion in alphaIIb, but not by the beta3 S752P mutation. We also examined the binding of recombinant calcium- and integrin-binding protein (CIB), an alphaIIb-specific ligand, to the alphaIIb cytoplasmic peptide. CIB bound to alphaIIb in a Ca2+- or Mn2+-independent, one-to-one reaction with a dissociation constant (KD) of 12 microM. Interestingly, in vitro liquid phase binding of CIB to intact alphaIIbbeta3 preferentially occurred with Mn2+-activated alphaIIbbeta3 conformers, as revealed by enhanced coimmunoprecipitation of CIB with PAC-1-captured Mn2+-activated alphaIIbbeta3. Our findings suggest that Mn2+ activation of intact alphaIIbbeta3 induces the exposure of a CIB-binding site, which is spontaneously exposed by the free alphaIIb peptide. CIB does not regulate alphaIIbbeta3 inside-out signaling, but rather is involved in an alphaIIbbeta3 post-receptor occupancy event.

title: Lethal autoimmune myocarditis in interferon-gamma receptor-deficient mice: enhanced disease severity by impaired inducible nitric oxide synthase induction.
text:
BACKGROUND: Interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) plays a crucial role in regulating inflammatory responses in autoimmune diseases. However, its role in inflammatory heart disease remains unclear.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Our study investigated the role of IFN-gamma in automimmune myocarditis using IFN-gamma receptor-deficient mice (IFN-gammaR(-/-)) on a BALB/c background. We found that immunization of IFN-gammaR(-/-) mice with a peptide derived from cardiac alpha-myosin heavy chain resulted in severe myocarditis with high mortality, compared to wild-type mice where the disease subsided after 3 weeks. In addition, we observed impaired inducible nitric oxide synthase expression and nitric oxide production in IFN-gammaR(-/-) hearts, along with enhanced in vitro CD4 T-cell responses. Treatment of wild-type mice with the nitric oxide synthetase inhibitor N:-nitro-l-arginine-methyl-ester enhanced in vitro CD4 T-cell proliferation and prevented healing of myocarditis.
CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggest that IFN-gamma protects mice from lethal autoimmune myocarditis by inducing the expression of inducible nitric oxide synthase, followed by the downregulation of T-cell responses.

title: Association between CYP2D6 polymorphisms and outcomes among women with early stage breast cancer treated with tamoxifen.
text: In this study, the authors investigated the relationship between the CYP2D6 enzyme's activity and clinical outcomes in women treated with tamoxifen for early-stage breast cancer. The study included 1325 patients from Germany and the US, with diagnoses between 1986 and 2005 and mainly postmenopausal patients (95.4%). The authors analyzed DNA from tumor tissue or blood to determine the presence of different CYP2D6 variants, including those associated with reduced or absent enzyme activity. The patients were classified into three groups based on their CYP2D6 metabolism: extensive, heterozygous extensive/intermediate, and poor. The study found that patients with reduced or absent CYP2D6 activity had a significantly higher risk of cancer recurrence and worse event-free and disease-free survival compared to those with extensive metabolism. However, there was no significant difference in overall survival between the groups. The authors concluded that the presence of 2 functional CYP2D6 alleles was associated with better clinical outcomes, while the presence of nonfunctional or reduced-function alleles was associated with worse outcomes.

title: Long-term, nightly benzodiazepine treatment of injurious parasomnias and other disorders of disrupted nocturnal sleep in 170 adults.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness, dosage stability, safety, and potential for abuse of long-term, nightly benzodiazepine treatment for chronic disorders of disrupted nocturnal sleep.
Methods: During a 12-year period, one author treated 170 adult patients with nightly benzodiazepine therapy for sleep-disruptive disorders, including: sleepwalking and sleep terrors (69 patients), rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (52 patients), chronic insomnia (25 patients), and restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movement disorder (24 patients), for a duration of >6 months.
Results: Complete or substantial control of the sleep disorders was achieved by 146 patients (86%), while 8% had adverse effects requiring medication changes, 2% had relapses of alcohol or chemical abuse requiring hospitalization, and another 2% misused their medications. Among the 136 patients who received clonazepam nightly for a mean of 3.5 (+/- 2.4) years, there was no significant difference in initial versus final mean dose (0.77 mg (+/- 0.46) versus 1.10 mg (+/- 0.96)). Similar results were observed in patients treated with chronic alprazolam and other benzodiazepine treatments.
Conclusion: Long-term, nightly benzodiazepine treatment of injurious parasomnias and other disorders of disrupted nocturnal sleep resulted in sustained efficacy in most cases, with low risk of dosage tolerance, adverse effects, or abuse. However, data from this study on the treatment of chronic severe insomnia, which represented a small subset of all insomnia patients, cannot be generalized to the typical insomnia patient.

title: Decreased proteasomal activity causes age-related phenotypes and promotes the development of metabolic abnormalities.
text: The proteasome is a multi-functional enzyme complex responsible for the degradation of both normal and damaged proteins. Decreased proteasomal activity has been linked to various age-related diseases, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear due to the lack of suitable animal models. In this study, we created a transgenic (Tg) mouse model with reduced proteasomal chymotrypsin-like activity. Tg mice showed a shorter lifespan and developed age-related symptoms. We observed an accumulation of polyubiquitinated and oxidized proteins, as well as changes in the expression of certain cellular proteins including Bcl-xL and RNase L. When Tg mice were fed a high-fat diet, they experienced more severe obesity and hepatic steatosis than wild-type mice. Notably, aged mice, regardless of genetic background, showed increased levels of adipose differentiation-related protein (ADRP) in their livers, indicative of metabolic abnormalities present in Tg mice. Our findings provide the first in vivo evidence that decreased proteasomal chymotrypsin-like activity affects lifespan and exacerbates age-related metabolic disorders, such as obesity and hepatic steatosis.

title: Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression suppresses cell proliferation via attenuation of the store-operated calcium influx-mediated signalling pathway in A549 lung cancer cells.
text:
Background: Orai1/CRACM1 is a critical component of store-operated calcium channels, which are highly correlated with inflammatory responses, immune regulation, and cell proliferation. The epidermal growth factor (EGF), which plays a key role in cell proliferation, can activate store-operated calcium channels. However, the effects of Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression on EGF-stimulated lung cancer cell growth are unknown.
Methods: To investigate the role of Orai1/CRACM1 in EGF-stimulated lung cancer cell proliferation, Orai1/CRACM1 plasmids were transfected into cells using lipofection. Cell proliferation was assessed using a cell proliferation assay, immunofluorescence staining, flow cytometry, and real-time polymerase chain reaction. The calcium influx signals were investigated using a fluorescent-based calcium assay.
Results: Our results showed that transfection of Orai1/CRACM1 plasmids inhibited EGF-stimulated cell proliferation. Additionally, overexpression of Orai1/CRACM1 resulted in the suppression of ERK1/2 and Akt phosphorylation. The expression of the cell cycle regulator p21 was induced in Orai1/CRACM1-overexpressing cells, while the expression of cyclin D3 was reduced. Flow cytometry also revealed that Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression resulted in G0/G1 cell cycle arrest. Furthermore, we found that Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression significantly reduced EGF-mediated store-operated calcium influx. Interestingly, application of 2-APB, a store-operated calcium channel inhibitor, also inhibited EGF-mediated cancer cell proliferation.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that Orai1/CRACM1 overexpression attenuates store-operated calcium influx, which in turn blocks EGF-mediated proliferation signaling and induces cell cycle arrest. This study provides insight into the role of Orai1/CRACM1 in lung cancer cell proliferation and highlights the potential of targeting store-operated calcium channels in cancer treatment.

title: Oxidative stress in cancer associated fibroblasts drives tumor-stroma co-evolution: A new paradigm for understanding tumor metabolism, the field effect and genomic instability in cancer cells.
text:
Loss of stromal fibroblast caveolin-1 (Cav-1) is a powerful and independent predictor of poor prognosis in human breast cancer patients, and is associated with early tumor recurrence, lymph node metastasis, and tamoxifen-resistance. We developed a novel co-culture system to elucidate the underlying mechanisms by which a loss of stromal Cav-1 leads to a detrimental tumor microenvironment. Our findings reveal a novel paradigm, where cancer cells induce oxidative stress in cancer-associated fibroblasts, which in turn acts as a "metabolic" and "mutagenic" driving force for tumor-stroma co-evolution, DNA damage, and aneuploidy in cancer cells.
Specifically, we demonstrate that an acute loss of Cav-1 expression in cancer-associated fibroblasts leads to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and aerobic glycolysis. We propose that defective mitochondria are removed from cancer-associated fibroblasts through autophagy/mitophagy, which is induced by oxidative stress. As a result, cancer-associated fibroblasts provide nutrients, such as lactate, to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism in adjacent cancer cells, a process we term the "Reverse Warburg Effect".
Our findings also indicate that oxidative stress in cancer-associated fibroblasts is sufficient to induce genomic instability in adjacent cancer cells, via a bystander effect, potentially leading to increased aggressive behavior. Furthermore, we demonstrate that nitric oxide (NO) over-production, secondary to Cav-1 loss, is the root cause of mitochondrial dysfunction in cancer-associated fibroblasts. Treatment with antioxidants, such as N-acetyl-cysteine, metformin, and quercetin, or NO inhibitors, L-NAME, was sufficient to reverse many of the cancer-associated fibroblast phenotypes described.
Our findings demonstrate that cancer cells use oxidative stress in adjacent fibroblasts as an "engine" to fuel their own survival via the stromal production of nutrients, and to drive their own mutagenic evolution towards a more aggressive phenotype, by promoting genomic instability. We also present evidence that the "field effect" in cancer biology could be related to the stromal production of ROS and NO species. eNOS-expressing fibroblasts have the ability to downregulate Cav-1 and induce mitochondrial dysfunction in adjacent fibroblasts that do not express eNOS, resulting in the propagation, amplification, and lateral spread of stromal oxidative stress and its detrimental effects on cancer cells.
In summary, our findings provide a novel insight into the mechanisms underlying the prognostic value of stromal Cav-1 in breast cancer, and suggest a new paradigm for understanding the interplay between cancer cells and stromal fibroblasts in promoting tumor progression and treatment resistance.

title: Telomeres and telomerase: more than the end of the line
text: Initial research on telomerase led to the belief that telomeres are maintained through a graceful yet relatively uncomplicated and highly conserved mechanism involving telomerase-mediated replication. As research advances, it has become apparent that this mechanism is elegant yet not as straightforward as initially perceived. Additionally, while many species utilize similar, sometimes identical, DNA sequences for telomeres, each species expresses its own unique identity through the regulation of these sequences and potentially additional tasks imposed upon them. The striking similarities between telomeres across different species have provided valuable insights into chromosome ends, while the differences have offered equally informative answers. This review highlights recent studies, the insights gained, and the questions they pose, including those regarding exceptional organisms with atypical telomeres lacking detectable telomerase activity.

title: Reduced osteoblastic population and defective mineralization in osteopetrotic (op/op) mice.
text: In this study, we examined the femora of osteopetrotic (op/op) mice to determine the role of osteoblasts in bone resorption. The op/op mice displayed an expanded meshwork of trabecular bones in the diaphyseal region, indicating a defect in osteoclast formation due to a lack of macrophage colony-stimulating factor. In the metaphysis of op/op mice, there were intense alkaline phosphatase (ALPase)-positive osteoblasts located close to the erosion zone of the growth plates. However, in contrast to wild-type littermates, some op/op diaphyses had flattened osteoblasts with weak ALPase-positivity, and the other diaphyses displayed bone surfaces without a covering by osteoblasts. This suggests that the osteoblastic population and activity were reduced in the op/op diaphyses. Additionally, von Kossa's staining revealed patchy unmineralized areas in the op/op diaphyses, indicating that a lower population or activity of osteoblasts resulted in defective mineralization in the bone. Transmission electron microscopy revealed few osteoblasts on the diaphyseal bones, and instead, bone marrow cells and vascular endothelial cells were often attached to the unmineralized bone. Osteocytes were embedded in the unmineralized bone matrix. These findings suggest that osteoclasts are involved in the osteoblastic population and activity as well as subsequent bone mineralization.

title: Interleukin 18 function in atherosclerosis is mediated by the interleukin 18 receptor and the Na-Cl co-transporter
text: Interleukin-18 (IL18) plays a role in the development of atherosclerosis through various mechanisms. Disrupting IL18's function reduces atherosclerosis in mice. Our findings show that lacking the IL18 receptor (IL18r) does not affect atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient (Apoe-/-) mice, nor does it affect IL18's binding to or signaling in endothelial cells. Initially identified through co-immunoprecipitation with IL18, we found that IL18 interacts with the Na-Cl co-transporter (NCC; also known as SLC12A3), a 12-transmembrane-domain ion transporter protein mainly expressed in the kidney. NCC is present in atherosclerotic lesions, where it colocalizes with IL18r. Combined deficiency of IL18r and NCC, but not single deficiency of either protein, protects mice from atherosclerosis. Peritoneal macrophages from Apoe-/-) mice or from Apoe-/-) mice lacking IL18r or NCC show IL18 binding and the induction of cell signaling and cytokine and chemokine expression. In contrast, macrophages from Apoe-/-) mice with combined deficiency of IL18r and NCC have a blunted response. An interaction between NCC and IL18r on macrophages was detected through co-immunoprecipitation. IL18 binds to the surface of NCC-transfected COS-7 cells, which do not express IL18r, and induces cell signaling and cytokine expression. This study identifies NCC as an IL18-binding protein that collaborates with IL18r in cell signaling, inflammatory molecule expression, and experimental atherogenesis.

title: Notch promotes survival of pre–T cells at the β-selection checkpoint by regulating cellular metabolism
text:
Notch signals are crucial for the successful outcomes of T cell receptor β-selection, including differentiation, proliferation, and rescue from apoptosis. However, the mechanism underlying this requirement is unknown. In this study, we discovered that Notch receptor and Delta-like 1 ligand interactions significantly contributed to the survival of CD4–CD8– precursor T cells by maintaining their cell size, glucose uptake, and metabolism. We also found that the trophic effects of Notch signaling were mediated by the phosphatidylinositol-3-OH kinase (PI(3)K) and Akt pathway, which allowed for the autonomous signaling capacity of the precursor T cell receptor complex. Our results demonstrate the involvement of Notch receptor-ligand interactions in the regulation of cellular metabolism, thereby enabling the autonomous signaling capacity of precursor T cells.
*Note: In the initial online version of this article, the term "Atk" was misspelled in the fourth sentence of the abstract. This should be "Akt." Also, in the fourth sentence of the second paragraph of the introduction, the name of the second kinase mentioned, "PI(3)K-dependent kinase 1," was incorrect and should read "phosphoinositide-dependent kinase 1." These errors have been corrected for the HTML and print versions of the article.

title: Blood pressure, salivary cortisol, and inflammatory cytokine outcomes in senior female cancer survivors enrolled in a tai chi chih randomized controlled trial
text:
Older cancer survivors are a vulnerable population due to their increased risk for chronic diseases, such as cardiovascular disease, which can be exacerbated by the late effects of cancer treatment and declines in physical functioning. Therefore, interventions that target chronic disease risk factors, such as high blood pressure, chronic inflammation, and elevated cortisol levels, are crucial in this population. Tai chi chih (TCC) is a mind-body exercise that has been shown to reduce chronic disease risk factors, but its effectiveness in older cancer survivors has not been extensively studied.
In a randomized controlled trial, we investigated the feasibility of TCC in older female cancer survivors with physical function limitations. Sixty-three participants were randomly assigned to either 12 weeks of TCC or health education control (HEC) classes. Predictor variables such as resting blood pressure, salivary cortisol levels, and inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, TNF-α, IL-10, IL-4) were measured at baseline and 1 week after the intervention.
The results showed that compared to the HEC group, the TCC group had significantly lower systolic blood pressure (SBP) and cortisol area-under-curve (AUC) at post-intervention. However, there was no significant intervention effect on inflammatory cytokines. These findings suggest that TCC may be an effective intervention to reduce chronic disease risk factors in older cancer survivors. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and determine the optimal TCC protocol for this population.

title: Heart failure admissions in adults with congenital heart disease; risk factors and prognosis.
text:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) is a significant complication and leading cause of death in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD). Therefore, our research goals were to determine the frequency of HF-related hospital admissions and to identify risk factors for both HF-admission and mortality in this population.
METHODS: We accessed data from the Dutch CONCOR registry, which was linked to the Hospital Discharge Registry and National Mortality Registry. Using Cox regression models, we analyzed the risk factors for both HF-admission and mortality in a cohort of 10,808 adult patients with CHD, of whom 274 were admitted for HF during a median follow-up period of 21 years.
RESULTS: Our findings revealed that 1.2 per 1000 patient-years had an HF-related hospital admission, indicating that the actual incidence of HF may be higher due to the underreporting of HF cases. Multiple defects, surgical interventions in childhood, and male gender were identified as independent risk factors for HF-admission. Patients admitted for HF had a significantly higher risk of mortality compared to those not admitted (hazard ratio (HR)=5.3; 95% confidence interval (CI): 4.2-6.9). The one- and three-year mortality rates after the first HF-admission were 24% and 35%, respectively. Male gender, pacemaker implantation, longer admission duration, non-cardiac medication use, and elevated serum creatinine levels were found to be independent risk factors for three-year mortality after the first HF-admission.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study highlights the importance of identifying patients with CHD at high risk of HF-admission, as they may benefit from closer follow-up and earlier medical interventions. The identified risk factors may facilitate surveillance and help preventive measures. These findings underscore the need for early detection and management of HF in adults with CHD to reduce the substantial mortality risk associated with HF-admission.

title: New pathologic classification of lung cancer: relevance for clinical practice and clinical trials.
text: We highlight significant changes in the pathological classification of lung cancer as detailed in the 2011 International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer/American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society (IASLC/ATS/ERS) lung adenocarcinoma classification. This classification was developed by an international panel of experts from IASLC, ATS, and ERS, comprising oncologists/pulmonologists, pathologists, radiologists, molecular biologists, and thoracic surgeons. Given that approximately 70% of patients with lung cancer present with advanced stages, the classification places a renewed emphasis on small biopsies and cytology, with specific terminology and criteria for distinguishing between squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma, as well as on molecular testing for EGFR mutations and ALK rearrangement. In contrast to previous classifications, tumors that had previously been categorized as non-small-cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified, due to a lack of distinct squamous or adenocarcinoma morphology are now classified further using a limited immunohistochemical workup to preserve tissue for molecular testing. The terms "bronchioloalveolar carcinoma" and "mixed subtype adenocarcinoma" have been discontinued. For resected adenocarcinomas, the classification introduces new concepts of adenocarcinoma in situ and minimally invasive adenocarcinoma, which define patients who, if they undergo complete resection, will have 100% disease-free survival. Invasive adenocarcinomas are now classified according to the predominant pattern after undergoing comprehensive histologic subtyping with lepidic, acinar, papillary, and solid patterns, as well as micropapillary, a new histologic subtype with poor prognosis. The term "invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma" replaces the former "mucinous bronchioloalveolar carcinoma." The classification recognizes the rapidly evolving nature of the lung cancer field, particularly in the molecular arena, and provides a much-needed standard for pathological diagnosis that can be applied not only to patient care but also to clinical trials and TNM classification.

title: Polymorphisms in EGFR and IL28B are associated with spontaneous clearance in an HCV-infected iranian population
text: Although most individuals infected with hepatitis C virus (HCV) develop chronic infection, approximately 25% are able to clear the virus naturally without any intervention. The goal of the current study was to identify genes associated with spontaneous HCV clearance in a population of Iranian patients. We genotyped 110 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 59 selected candidate genes in a cohort of 107 HCV-infected individuals who spontaneously cleared the infection and 176 individuals whose infection persisted. Three of the 110 SNPs were found to be associated with HCV outcome (P-values<0.03). Specifically, the SNPs rs11506105 in the epidermal growth factor receptor gene (EGFR), rs11881222 and rs12979860 in the interferon-λ3 gene (IL28B) were associated with HCV clearance. Using multivariate logistic regression, we found that the presence of the A/A genotype in both rs11506105 and rs11881222, as well as the C/C genotype in rs12979860, was associated with HCV clearance (recessive model: odds ratio (OR)=2.06, 95% confidence interval (95% CI)=1.09–3.88, P=0.025; OR=2.09, 95% CI=1.23–3.60, P=0.007; and OR=1.95, 95% CI=1.15–3.35, P=0.014 for rs11506105, rs12979860 and rs11881222, respectively). In conclusion, EGFR and IL28B SNPs are strong independent predictive markers of spontaneous viral clearance.

title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing variables reflect the degree of diastolic dysfunction in patients with heart failure-normal ejection fraction.
text:
The purpose of the present investigation was to compare echocardiography with tissue Doppler imaging (TDI) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPX) in patients with heart failure (HF) and normal ejection fraction (NEF). Previous studies have shown a relationship between variables obtained from echocardiography with TDI and CPX in HF cohorts.
The study included 32 patients with HF-NEF who underwent both echocardiography with TDI and CPX. The following variables were measured from both tests:
1. The ratio of mitral early velocity (E) to mitral annular velocity (E'): This measure provides insight into left ventricular (LV) filling pressure and diastolic function.
2. Ejection fraction.
3. LV mass.
4. Left ventricular end-systolic volume.
5. Peak oxygen uptake (VO2): This measures the body's ability to use oxygen during exercise.
6. Ventilatory efficiency: This measure assesses the body's ability to efficiently use oxygen during exercise.
7. Partial pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide (PETCO2) at rest and peak exercise: This measure provides insight into ventilation and perfusion.
8. Heart rate recovery at 1 minute (HRR1): This measure assesses the body's ability to quickly recover from exercise.

Pearson correlation analysis revealed that E/E' was significantly correlated with peak VO2, the ventilatory efficiency slope, resting PETCO2, peak PETCO2, and HRR1. In contrast, left ventricular mass and left ventricular end-systolic volume were not correlated with any CPX variable. Ejection fraction was correlated with HRR1. An HRR1 threshold of less than 16 beats per minute (higher value positive) effectively identified subjects with an E/E' > 10, which may indicate diastolic dysfunction.


The results of the present investigation demonstrate that CPX provides valuable insight into cardiac dysfunction in patients with HF-NEF. E/E' is a useful measure of LV filling pressure and diastolic function, and the results of the present investigation suggest that CPX may eventually prove to be a valuable clinical assessment.

title: Radical prostatectomy for pathological Gleason 8 or greater prostate cancer: influence of concomitant pathological variables.
text:
In this study, we evaluated the long-term outcomes of patients with pathological Gleason score 8 or higher prostate cancer who underwent radical prostatectomy between 1987 and 1996. We analyzed the prognostic significance of various pathological variables, including tumor stage, preoperative prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level, DNA ploidy, margin status, and seminal vesicle invasion.
Results showed that overall and progression-free survival at 10 years were 67% and 36%, respectively, and cancer-specific survival was 85%. Univariate analysis identified adjuvant treatment, pathological stage, preoperative PSA, and pathological grade as significant predictors of progression-free survival. Multivariate analysis revealed that pathological grade, preoperative PSA, adjuvant therapy, and pathological stage were independent predictors of progression-free survival. Progression-free survival at 10 years for patients who did and did not receive adjuvant treatment was 52% and 23%, respectively. Our findings suggest that high-grade prostate cancer can be controlled with radical prostatectomy in some patients with locally confined disease, and 10-year cancer-specific survival is 96%. The predictors of outcome in patients with Gleason 8 disease or higher are similar to established predictors derived from using all grades. However, adjuvant hormonal therapy may not affect prostate cancer death rates within 10 years in patients with high-grade cancer.

title: Successful establishment of long-term bone marrow cultures in 103 patients with myelodysplastic syndromes.
text: Using bone marrow biopsies instead of mononuclear cells, we maintained long-term cultures from 103 patients with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) belonging to all five subcategories, as well as 12 normal controls. By week 4, cultures had reached 30-50% confluency, which could be maintained for up to 12 weeks with 100% confluency. The four most prominent cell types were fibroblasts, macrophages, endothelial cells, and adipocytes. Immunohistochemical and electron microscopic analysis confirmed the cellular lineages. The MDS stroma supported normal hematopoiesis in the cultures. There was no correlation between the FAB or cytogenetic subcategories and the growth potency of the MDS stroma. The MDS stroma appeared to be both morphologically and functionally normal.

title: [Acupuncture combined with auricular point sticking therapy for post stroke depression:a randomized controlled trial].
text: To investigate the therapeutic effects of acupuncture combined with auricular point sticking on post-stroke depression (PSD), a randomized controlled trial was conducted. Sixty patients with PSD were randomly divided into two groups: an acupuncture plus auricular application group (combination group) and a medication group.
