The medication group received oral paroxetine hydrochloride (20 mg/day) for 8 weeks, while the combination group received 30 minutes of acupuncture once a day and auricular point sticking three times a week for 8 weeks at specific points, including Baihui (GV 20), Sishencong (EX-HN 1), Shenting (GV 24), Yintang (GV 29), Shenmen (HT 7), Neiguan (PC 6), Taichong (LR 3), Hegu (LI 4), Zusanli (ST 36), Sanyinjiao (SP 6), and Fenglong (ST 40). The Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD) was used to evaluate the total score and each factor scores before and after treatment, as well as the Asberg's Antidepressant Side-Effect Rating Scale (SERS) and clinical effect. The results showed that both groups exhibited improved symptoms after treatment, but the combination group had better outcomes in terms of total HAMD scores, anxiety/somatization factor, sleep disturbance factor, and hopelessness factor. The total effective rate of the combination group was higher than that of the medication group (86.7% vs 66.7%, respectively). Furthermore, the SERS score of the combination group was lower than that of the medication group. The study concluded that acupuncture combined with auricular point sticking is an effective and safe treatment for PSD.

title: Selective enhancement of endothelial BMPR-II with BMP9 reverses pulmonary arterial hypertension
text: Genetic data suggests that the loss of bone morphogenetic protein type II receptor (BMPR-II) signaling in the endothelium is a primary factor in the development of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Yet, targeting this signaling pathway selectively using BMP ligands has not been investigated as a therapeutic approach. In this study, we identify BMP9 as the most effective ligand for preventing cell death and enhancing monolayer integrity in both pulmonary arterial endothelial cells and blood outgrowth endothelial cells from PAH patients who carry BMPR-II mutations. To create an animal model of PAH caused by BMPR-II deficiency, we generated mice with a heterozygous knock-in allele of a human BMPR2 mutation, R899X. These mice spontaneously developed PAH. Treatment with BMP9 reversed established PAH in these mice, as well as in two other experimental PAH models that develop in response to either monocrotaline or VEGF receptor inhibition combined with chronic hypoxia. These results suggest that enhancement of endothelial BMP signaling has therapeutic promise for PAH.

title: Coordinated actions of SLX1-SLX4 and MUS81-EME1 for Holliday junction resolution in human cells.
text: Holliday junctions (HJs) are four-way DNA intermediates that arise during homologous recombination, and their proper resolution is crucial for maintaining proper chromosome segregation. Our study reveals that three structure-selective endonucleases, specifically SLX1-SLX4, MUS81-EME1, and GEN1, collaborate to resolve HJs in human cells, defining two distinct pathways. One pathway is mediated by GEN1, while the other, referred to as SLX-MUS, involves the coordinated action of SLX1-SLX4 and MUS81-EME1. Depletion of proteins involved in the SLX-MUS pathway leads to severe defects in chromosome segregation and reduced cell survival. Interestingly, these enzymes can associate with each other in response to CDK-mediated phosphorylation during the G2/M transition, forming a stable SLX-MUS holoenzyme that can be reconstituted in vitro. Our biochemical studies demonstrate that SLX-MUS is a HJ resolvase that coinhibits the active sites of two distinct endonucleases during HJ resolution, resulting in a more efficient and finely tuned process than that mediated by SLX1-SLX4 alone, which exhibits a promiscuous nickase activity that affects DNA secondary structures.

title: Prevalence of frequent headache in a population sample.
text:
In this study, we aimed to investigate the prevalence and characteristics of frequent headaches in the general population. We conducted a telephone interview survey among 13,343 individuals aged 18 to 65 in Baltimore County, Maryland, and classified subjects reporting 180 or more headaches per year as having frequent headaches. We identified three subtypes of frequent headaches: migrainous, tension-type, and unclassified.
Our findings show that the overall prevalence of frequent headaches was 4.1%, with a higher prevalence in Caucasians (4.4%) compared to African Americans (3.3%). The prevalence of frequent headaches was highest in the lowest educational category in both males and females. Among frequent headache sufferers, more than half met criteria for chronic tension-type headache, while almost one-third met criteria for frequent headache with migrainous features, and the remainder were unclassified. Notably, 30% of female and 25% of male frequent headache sufferers met International Headache Society (IHS) criteria for migraine (with or without aura).
Our results indicate that frequent headache is a common condition in the general population, with a slightly higher prevalence in Caucasians and those with lower educational levels. Chronic tension-type headache is the most common subtype, followed by frequent headache with migrainous features, and the remainder are unclassified. Despite the higher prevalence of migraine in the IHS criteria subgroup, the female preponderance of frequent headache is less pronounced than in migraine. The sex ratio varies by frequent headache subtype.
In conclusion, this study provides valuable insights into the prevalence and characteristics of frequent headaches in the general population. Our findings highlight the need for further research into the underlying mechanisms and potential treatments for this common and disruptive condition.

title: HTLV-I/II associated disease in England and Wales, 1993-7: retrospective review of serology requests.
text: Beyond HIV, two endogenous retroviruses (human T cell leukaemia viruses type I (HTLV-I) and type II (HTLV-II)) infect humans. HTLV-I infection is prevalent in Japan, the Caribbean, Africa, and Melanesia and affects immigrants from these regions in Europe. HTLV-I infection is associated with a 1-5% lifetime risk of adult T cell leukaemia/lymphoma, a 0.25% lifetime risk of HTLV-I associated myelopathy, and other inflammatory conditions (uveitis, alveolitis, and arthritis). HTLV-II infection is prevalent in some indigenous American and African populations and among individuals who use injection drugs, and has been linked to neurological disorders. Between 1986 and 1992, 100 cases of HTLV-I associated myelopathy and 44 cases of adult T cell leukaemia/lymphoma were diagnosed in the United Kingdom. Adult T cell leukaemia/lymphoma was first described in 1977, and patients with this condition have a mean life expectancy of only six months, so most of the 44 cases were likely incident cases.

title: Lentiviral vector design and imaging approaches to visualize the early stages of cellular reprogramming.
text: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) can be generated from somatic cells through gene transfer of reprogramming transcription factors. The efficiency of iPSC formation is influenced by the expression levels of these factors, but additional stochastic cellular factors have been proposed to play a role. To better understand these early reprogramming events, we developed engineered lentiviral vectors that co-express reprogramming factors with a strong retroviral promoter, and implanted them into fibroblasts. Using fluorescence microscopy and live-cell imaging, we were able to track the emergence and composition of early iPSC clusters. Our findings demonstrate that vector silencing usually occurs before or simultaneously with the induction of the Oct4-EGFP pluripotency marker. After 7 days, a subfraction of cells in clonal colonies expressed Oct4-EGFP and rapidly expanded. By tracking individual cell-derived iPSC colonies over time, we found that stochastic epigenetic changes are necessary for reprogramming. Additionally, we discovered that iPSC colonies may arise from a genetic mosaic consisting of different clusters. Improved vector design and continuous cell tracking have created a powerful system to investigate the subtle dynamics of early reprogramming events.

title: EIF2AK3, encoding translation initiation factor 2-α kinase 3, is mutated in patients with Wolcott-Rallison syndrome
text: Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (WRS) is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder characterized by insulin-dependent diabetes that occurs in infancy or early childhood, accompanied by epiphyseal dysplasia, osteoporosis, and growth retardation. Additional manifestations include hepatic and renal dysfunction, mental retardation, and cardiovascular abnormalities. By analyzing two consanguineous families, we mapped the WRS locus to a region of less than 3 cM on chromosome 2p12, with maximum evidence of linkage and homozygosity at four microsatellite markers within an interval of approximately 1 cM. The gene encoding the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2-α kinase 3 (EIF2AK3) resides in this interval, and we identified distinct mutations of EIF2AK3 that segregated with the disorder in each of the families. The first mutation leads to a truncated protein lacking the entire catalytic domain, while the other mutation affects a highly conserved amino acid in the catalytic domain of the protein. Our findings offer insight into the etiology of WRS and may provide clues for understanding the more common forms of diabetes and other associated manifestations.

title: Beta oscillations in a large-scale sensorimotor cortical network: directional influences revealed by Granger causality.
text: Prior studies have shown that synchronized beta frequency (14-30 Hz) oscillations in the primary motor cortex are involved in maintaining steady contractions of contralateral arm and hand muscles. Nonetheless, the function of postcentral cortical areas in motor maintenance and their patterns of interaction with motor cortex remain largely unexplored. To investigate these questions, we examined the functional connections of beta-synchronized neuronal assemblies in pre- and postcentral areas of two monkeys as they performed a visual discrimination task involving hand lever pressing. By employing power and coherence spectral analysis, we identified a synchronized network linking pre- and postcentral areas. Subsequently, we used Granger causality spectra to assess the directional influences among recording sites. In both monkeys, strong Granger causal influences were observed from primary somatosensory cortex to both motor cortex and inferior posterior parietal cortex, with the latter area also exerting Granger causal influences on motor cortex. Conversely, Granger causal influences from motor cortex to postcentral sites were found to be weak in one monkey and absent in the other. These findings represent the first evidence, to our knowledge, of synchronized beta oscillations integrating multiple sensorimotor areas into a large-scale network during motor maintenance behaviors, and carrying Granger causal influences from primary somatosensory and inferior posterior parietal cortices to motor cortex in awake monkeys.

title: Aging, frailty and age-related diseases
text: The concept of frailty as a distinct medical syndrome has evolved based on the clinical expertise of geriatricians and is recognizable in medical practice. Frailty refers to a state of vulnerability that manifests as multisystem physiological changes, often without reaching the threshold for a specific life-threatening illness. Current understanding emphasizes the interplay of physical, psychological, cognitive, and social factors in the development and progression of frailty, which is characterized by a reduced functional reserve and diminished adaptability to stressors. This syndrome is an important risk factor for accelerated physical and cognitive decline, disability, and mortality in elderly individuals. The features of frailty are equally applicable to the aging process in general, and there is limited consensus regarding the underlying physiological/biological pathways. However, it is widely accepted that heightened chronic systemic inflammation plays a significant role in the development and maintenance of frailty. This review aims to explore the relationship between aging, frailty, and age-related diseases, and to identify potential interventions to mitigate the occurrence and impact of frailty in elderly individuals.

title: A case of paraquat intoxication caused by intravenous injection.
text:
Paraquat intoxication is a life-threatening condition that can occur through various means, including oral administration. However, we report a rare case of fatal paraquat intoxication following intravenous injection. There is limited clinical data available on parenteral paraquat exposure, and we document this rare occurrence and its rapid progression to severe organ dysfunction and death.
The patient developed toxic symptoms and profound organ function impairment shortly after injection. Attempts at treatment with repeated activated charcoal hemoperfusion, pulse steroids, cyclophosphamide, and antioxidants were undertaken, but the patient succumbed to multiple organ failure three days after intoxication. This case underscores the extremely poor prognosis associated with paraquat intoxication via intravenous injection, even at very low doses.

title: Genome-wide association study identifies variants at CLU and CR1 associated with Alzheimer's disease
text: The gene encoding apolipoprotein E (APOE) on chromosome 19 is the sole confirmed susceptibility locus for late-onset Alzheimer's disease. To identify additional risk loci, we conducted a large genome-wide association study of 2,032 individuals from France with Alzheimer's disease (cases) and 5,328 controls. Markers outside APOE with suggestive evidence of association (P < 10−5) were further examined in collections from Belgium, Finland, Italy, and Spain, comprising 3,978 Alzheimer's disease cases and 3,297 controls. Two loci showed replicated evidence of association: one located within CLU (also known as APOJ), encoding clusterin or apolipoprotein J, on chromosome 8 (rs11136000, OR = 0.86, 95% CI 0.81–0.90, P = 7.5 × 10−9 for combined data), and the other within CR1, encoding the complement component (3b/4b) receptor 1, on chromosome 1 (rs6656401, OR = 1.21, 95% CI 1.14–1.29, P = 3.7 × 10−9 for combined data). Previous studies have demonstrated roles for CLU and CR1 in the clearance of β amyloid (Aβ) peptide, the primary component of amyloid plaques, which are a hallmark of the brains of individuals with Alzheimer's disease.

title: Identification and characterization of subpopulations in undifferentiated ES cell culture.
text: Embryonic stem (ES) cells are pluripotent cells derived from the inner cell mass (ICM) and the epiblast, and have been suggested to be a heterogeneous population with characteristics intermediate between them. These cells express the Oct3/4 and Rex1 genes, which are used as markers to indicate the undifferentiated state of ES cells. In contrast to Oct3/4, which is expressed in totipotent and pluripotent cells throughout the mouse development cycle, Rex1 expression is confined to the ICM and is downregulated in pluripotent cell populations in later stages, including the epiblast and primitive ectoderm (PrE). To investigate whether ES cells comprise a homogeneous population or a heterogeneous population of cells corresponding to different stages of differentiation, we generated knock-in ES cell lines expressing fluorescent proteins in the Rex1 and Oct3/4 gene loci, allowing us to visualize the expression of these genes. Our findings revealed the presence of at least two distinct populations within undifferentiated ES cells: Rex1(+)/Oct3/4(+) cells and Rex1(-)/Oct3/4(+) cells. Strikingly, these populations could exchange their characteristics in the presence of LIF, supporting the notion that they represent distinct stages of differentiation. Interestingly, Rex1(+)/Oct3/4(+) cells predominantly differentiated into primitive ectoderm and contributed to chimera formation, whereas Rex1(-)/Oct3/4(+) cells differentiated more efficiently into somatic cell types and showed poor ability to contribute to chimera formation. Taken together, these data confirm that undifferentiated ES cell culture contains subpopulations corresponding to ICM, epiblast, and PrE.

title: Isolation of intact nuclei of high purity from mouse liver.
text:
Current methods of nuclear isolation from the liver involve disrupting the plasma membrane via homogenization and separating the nuclei using high centrifugal force (HCF) through gradients of sucrose or other substances for up to 80 minutes. However, this prolonged exposure to HCF can lead to nuclear damage and degradation due to endogenous proteases. To address this limitation, we compared four alternative methods of nuclear isolation:
1. Mouse liver was gently crushed through a fine mesh without in vivo perfusion with collagenase. The cell suspension was then centrifuged at 600 g to remove gross debris and further centrifuged at moderate centrifugal force (MCF, 16,000 g) or high centrifugal force (HCF, 70,000 g) through sucrose gradients for 30 minutes.
2. Mouse liver was gently crushed through a fine mesh with in vivo perfusion with collagenase. The cell suspension was then centrifuged at 600 g to remove gross debris and further centrifuged at MCF (16,000 g) or HCF (70,000 g) through sucrose gradients for 30 minutes.
3. Mouse liver was gently crushed through a fine mesh without in vivo perfusion with collagenase, and the cell suspension was centrifuged at 600 g to remove gross debris and further centrifuged at MCF (16,000 g) or HCF (70,000 g) through sucrose gradients for 30 minutes.
4. Mouse liver was gently crushed through a fine mesh with in vivo perfusion with collagenase, and the cell suspension was centrifuged at 600 g to remove gross debris and further centrifuged at MCF (16,000 g) or HCF (70,000 g) through sucrose gradients for 30 minutes.
We evaluated the purity of the isolated nuclei using biological and morphological analyses of representative marker proteins for nuclei and cytoplasm. Our results show that MCF and no collagenase provided the highest nuclear integrity and purity, while MCF with collagenase is a viable option if priority is given to yield. This method is particularly useful for small sample sizes, making it an ideal choice for studies involving human liver biopsies and livers from mice, the most commonly used species for gene targeting.

title: Two structurally independent domains of E. coli NusG create regulatory plasticity via distinct interactions with RNA polymerase and regulators.
text: NusG is a conserved regulator that modulates transcription through various mechanisms by interacting with elongation complexes (ECs) of RNA polymerase, DNA, and RNA. In Escherichia coli, NusG alleviates pausing and enhances elongation speed, promotes termination by E. coli rho and phage HK022 Nun protein, and supports antitermination by lambdaN in ribosomal RNA operons. Our nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) studies reveal that E. coli NusG is composed of two largely independent structural domains: N-terminal domain (NTD) and C-terminal domain (CTD). Hydrodynamic analysis indicates that NTD is sufficient to suppress pausing and enhance transcript elongation in vitro. However, neither domain alone can support rho-dependent termination or antitermination, suggesting that interactions of both domains with ECs are necessary for these processes. We propose that NTD interacts with RNA polymerase, while CTD interacts with rho and other regulators, allowing NusG to achieve distinct regulatory outcomes through diverse interactions.

title: Cytochemistry and C-values: the less-well-known world of nuclear DNA amounts.
text:
In the plant sciences, two primary technologies are used to measure nuclear DNA content: Feulgen absorbance cytophotometry and flow cytometry (FCM). While FCM has gained popularity among plant scientists, absorbance-cytophotometric techniques are gradually losing ground. This reduction in methodological diversity is undesirable and hinders the advancement of plant genome research. Both approaches have their advantages, but static cytophotometry faces instrumental and material-based challenges that can lead to less reliable data compared to FCM.
For over two decades, it has been known that plant polyphenols can interfere with Feulgen DNA cytophotometry, causing unreliable results. However, there is limited information on the specific plant metabolites that can interfere with DNA staining and the mechanisms behind these inhibitions. Additionally, plant slimes can pose challenges in these measurements.
Recently, research into the effects of secondary metabolites on FCM results has begun. In particular, analyzing intraspecific genome size variation requires a stringent methodology that accounts for inhibitors. FCM tests for inhibitory effects of endogenous metabolites should become obligatory. Using dry seeds for harvesting embryo and endosperm nuclei can sometimes overcome staining inhibitors. Proper internal standardization is crucial, and this highlights the importance of understanding phytochemical/cytochemical interactions in plant DNA photometry to improve plant genome size measurements.

title: Integrins and cell proliferation: regulation of cyclin-dependent kinases via cytoplasmic signaling pathways.
text: Mammalian cell cycle progression is tightly regulated by both cell-cell adhesion mediated by integrins and the binding of growth factors to their receptors. This regulation is mediated by G1 phase cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs), which are downstream of signaling pathways that are under the coordinated control of both integrins and growth factor receptors. Recent discoveries have revealed a remarkable diversity of integrin-dependent signaling pathways that navigate cell cycle progression through the G1 phase. The regulation of cyclin D1 by the ERK pathway may serve as a model for illuminating how cell adhesion influences cell cycle progression.

title: Interplay between microtubule bundling and sorting factors ensures acentriolar spindle stability during C. elegans oocyte meiosis
text: In various species, meiosis in oocytes takes place without the presence of centrioles. As a result, cell division mechanisms are altered, leading to unique and specialized processes. Here, we provide insights into the underlying principles of this phenomenon through the study of two related proteins, KLP-15 and KLP-16, which localize to the acentriolar oocyte spindle in the nematode worm Caenorhabditis elegans. These proteins promote microtubule bundling during spindle assembly, but following depletion of KLP-15/16, microtubules form a disorganized array. Surprisingly, despite this defect, microtubules are able to reorganize during anaphase and form a bundled array that facilitates chromosome segregation. This phenomenon allows us to identify factors that promote microtubule organization during anaphase, whose contributions are normally undetectable in wild-type worms. We found that SPD-1 (PRC1) bundles microtubules and KLP-18 (kinesin-12) sorts those bundles into a functional orientation capable of mediating chromosome segregation. Our studies reveal an interplay between distinct mechanisms that together promote spindle formation and chromosome segregation in the absence of structural cues such as centrioles.

title: Development of a questionnaire to measure heart disease risk knowledge in people with diabetes: the Heart Disease Fact Questionnaire.
text: This study investigates the Heart Disease Fact Questionnaire (HDFQ), a paper and pencil questionnaire designed to assess heart disease risk knowledge in individuals with diabetes. The 25-item questionnaire was developed to evaluate respondents' knowledge of major risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD). Approximately half of the questions focus on diabetes-related CHD risk factors. Initial piloting data was analyzed from 524 individuals with diabetes to evaluate the psychometric properties of the HDFQ. The questionnaire is accessible to an average 13-year-old and places a minimal burden on respondents. It shows good content and face validity, and demonstrates adequate internal consistency with a Kuder-Richardson-20 formula of 0.77 and good item-total correlations. Item analysis revealed a desirable range of P-values, and discriminant function analyses showed that HDFQ scores differentiated respondents based on their knowledge of their own cardiovascular health, use of lipid-lowering medications, health insurance status, and educational attainment, indicating good criterion-related validity. Overall, the HDFQ is a brief, easily understandable, and manageable measure of heart disease risk knowledge that can be used in both research and clinical settings. Future studies should establish norms for the questionnaire and investigate its test-retest reliability and predictive validity.

title: Prevalence of Multiple Sclerosis in Isfahan, Iran
text:
The prevalence of multiple sclerosis (MS) varies widely across the world, with Iran reported to have a low prevalence. However, a recent study conducted in the central part of Iran, Isfahan, aimed to estimate the period prevalence and risk factors of MS in the region.
The study was a cross-sectional case register conducted between 2004 and 2005, involving 1,391 patients with definite MS from the Isfahan MS Association. The patients were identified through a neurologist and radiologist evaluation using clinical information and MRI findings. Demographic and case-related information was collected, and population data were obtained from the 1999 Iran Census.
The study found that the period prevalence of MS was 35.5 per 100,000 (95% CI: 33.6-37.3) in a population of 3,923,255, with a higher rate in women than men. The female/male ratio was 3.6 (95% CI: 3.2-4.1). The direct age-adjusted period prevalence was 59.5 per 100,000 (95% CI: 44.8-75.2) for women and 17.0 per 100,000 (95% CI: 8.9-25.1) for men. The most common initial presentations were sensory and visual disturbances, with a prevalence of 51.1% (95% CI: 48.4-53.7) and 47.0% (95% CI: 44.4-49.7), respectively.
The study concluded that Isfahan could be considered an area with a medium to high risk of MS, which contrasts with the gradient hypothesis. The findings suggest that factors other than latitude may influence the distribution of MS, and further research is needed to identify these risk factors.

title: A kinetochore-independent mechanism drives anaphase chromosome separation during acentrosomal meiosis
text:
Although the assembly of acentrosomal meiotic spindles has been extensively studied, little is known about the separation of chromosomes on these spindles. This study focuses on Caenorhabditis elegans oocytes and shows that the kinetochore protein, KNL-1, directs the assembly of meiotic kinetochores that orient chromosomes. However, in contrast to mitosis, chromosome separation during meiotic anaphase is kinetochore-independent.
Prior to anaphase, meiotic kinetochores and spindle poles disassemble along with the microtubules on the poleward side of chromosomes. During anaphase, microtubules then form between the separating chromosomes. Functional analysis implicated a set of proteins that localize to a ring-shaped domain between kinetochores during pre-anaphase spindle assembly and anaphase separation. These proteins are localized by the chromosomal passenger complex, which regulates the loss of meiotic chromosome cohesion. Therefore, meiotic segregation in C. elegans is a two-stage process, where kinetochores orient chromosomes, but are then dispensable for their separation. It is suggested that separation is controlled by a meiosis-specific chromosomal domain to coordinate cohesin removal and chromosome segregation.

title: Association between the Medicare Modernization Act of 2003 and patient wait times and travel distance for chemotherapy.
text: In 2003, the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act (MMA) altered reimbursements for outpatient chemotherapy drugs and drug administration services. Some anecdotal evidence suggests that these changes may have reduced access to chemotherapy for Medicare beneficiaries. To investigate, we analyzed data from a nationally representative sample of Medicare claims from 2003 to 2006. We found that the proportion of patients receiving chemotherapy in inpatient settings decreased from 10.2% to 8.8% between 2003 and 2006, while the proportion in institutional outpatient settings increased from 21.1% to 22.5%. The proportion of patients treated in physician offices remained relatively unchanged at 68.7%. The median time from diagnosis to initial chemotherapy visit did not significantly change between 2003 and 2006. However, there was a small but significant increase in travel distance for chemotherapy between 2003 and 2004, followed by a slight decrease in the subsequent years. Overall, our findings suggest that there have not been major changes in patient wait times and travel distances for chemotherapy in the Medicare population since the MMA-related changes in reimbursement.

title: 20-year outcomes following conservative management of clinically localized prostate cancer.
text:
The appropriate treatment for men with clinically localized prostate cancer is uncertain, according to a recent study that detected an increasing prostate cancer mortality rate for men who are still alive more than 15 years after diagnosis. To estimate 20-year survival rates based on a competing risk analysis, the study analyzed data from 767 men aged 55 to 74 who were diagnosed with clinically localized prostate cancer between 1971 and 1984 and treated with observation or androgen withdrawal therapy alone, stratified by age at diagnosis and histological findings.
During the first 15 years of follow-up, the prostate cancer mortality rate was 33 per 1000 person-years (95% confidence interval [CI], 28-38), then dropped to 18 per 1000 person-years after 15 years of follow-up (95% CI, 10-29). There was no significant difference in the mortality rates for these two follow-up periods after adjusting for differences in tumor histology (rate ratio, 1.1; 95% CI, 0.6-1.9). Men with low-grade prostate cancers had a minimal risk of dying from prostate cancer within 20 years of diagnosis (Gleason score of 2-4, 6 deaths per 1000 person-years; 95% CI, 2-11). In contrast, men with high-grade prostate cancers had a high probability of dying from prostate cancer within 10 years of diagnosis (Gleason score of 8-10, 121 deaths per 1000 person-years; 95% CI, 90-156). Finally, men with Gleason score of 5 or 6 tumors had an intermediate risk of prostate cancer death.
The study's findings indicate that the annual mortality rate from prostate cancer does not change significantly after 15 years from diagnosis, which suggests that aggressive treatment for localized low-grade prostate cancer may not be necessary.

title: Role of beta adrenergic receptor polymorphisms in heart failure: systematic review and meta-analysis.
text:
Heart Failure (HF) is a common condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality. The beta adrenergic receptor (betaAR) pathway plays a crucial role in regulating cardiac function. Chronic activation of beta(1)ARs has been implicated in the development and progression of HF, and betaAR blockade can improve survival in individuals with left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Variations in the beta adrenergic receptor gene (ADRB) have been linked to HF phenotypes and interactions with beta blockers. However, these associations have not been consistently replicated.
A review of the evidence on the involvement of ADRB variants in the pathogenesis, progression, and response to beta blockers in HF is provided. A meta-analysis of three studies examining the effect of the ADRB1 Arg389Gly polymorphism on left ventricular remodeling with beta blockers shows a 5% improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction in homozygous Arg389 individuals. Recent studies suggest that there may be a different functional response to beta blockers associated with this polymorphism, which could lead to genotypic associations that enable patients to be identified as having a greater risk of developing HF, rapidly progressing HF, or a lack of response to beta blockers. This could lead to targeted and aggressive therapy for these patients.

title: New development of the yolk sac theory in diabetic embryopathy: molecular mechanism and link to structural birth defects.
text: Maternal diabetes mellitus poses a considerable risk factor for structural birth defects, including congenital heart defects and neural tube defects, given the escalating prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity among women of reproductive age. The increasing magnitude of this public health concern underscores the imperative for continued research into the molecular mechanisms linking diabetes mellitus to birth defects. In vitro and in vivo studies have demonstrated that high glucose concentrations lead to cellular and organellar damage in the yolk sac, which is the first system to develop during embryogenesis. This damage can result in impaired nutrient transportation due to vascular dysfunction. While the relationship between yolk sac vasculopathy and structural birth defects remains to be definitively established, recent research has uncovered key molecular intermediates involved in diabetic yolk sac vasculopathy, including hypoxia-inducible factor-1α, apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1, and its inhibitor thioredoxin-1, c-Jun-N-terminal kinases, nitric oxide, and nitric oxide synthase. Moreover, abnormalities in arachidonic acid and myo-inositol have been linked to yolk sac vasculopathy. Dietary supplementation with lipids has been shown to reduce diabetes mellitus-induced malformations, highlighting the potential therapeutic potential of this approach. While the role of the human yolk sac in embryogenesis is less pronounced than in rodents, human embryonic vasculogenesis is nonetheless affected negatively by maternal diabetes mellitus. Investigations into the underlying mechanisms have identified potential therapeutic targets for intervention against yolk sac vasculopathy, birth defects, and other complications associated with diabetic pregnancies.

title: Hepatitis B and C in HIV-infected patients. Prevalence and prognostic value.
text:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: There is limited information on the frequency and impact of co-infection with hepatitis B or C on the clinical course of patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
METHODS: We followed 232 HIV-infected patients (age 37±8 years, CD4 count 167±167 microl; 46% had AIDS) and investigated their samples for markers of HBV and HCV infection (HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV-DNA, Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, anti-HCV, HCV-RNA).
RESULTS: Of the 232 patients, 60 (23%) were anti-HCV positive, and 78% of these sera were positive for HCV-RNA. Twenty-two patients (9%) had chronic HBV infection (HBsAg positive), and 82% of these sera had detectable HBeAg and 86% had HBV-DNA. The presence of HCV-RNA, HBeAg, and HBV-DNA levels were associated with the degree of immunodeficiency. In contrast to the control group without HBV or HCV infection, patients infected with HIV and either HBV or HCV showed a direct correlation between a decrease in CD4 counts and decreased cholinesterase activity. In patients with AIDS, coinfection with HBV or HCV was associated with a reduced survival rate compared to controls (HBV: 212 days, 95% CI, 106-317; HCV: 267 days, 95% CI, 112-396; controls: 439 days, 95% CI, 364-513).
CONCLUSIONS: Co-infection with HIV and HBV or HCV is common. Our results suggest that as HIV-infected patients survive longer, co-infection with either HBV or HCV is associated with a lower survival rate.

title: Requirement of endogenous stem cell factor and granulocyte-colony-stimulating factor for IL-17-mediated granulopoiesis.
text: IL-17 is a new cytokine that only affects certain types of immune cells in the body. In lab tests, we found that IL-17 helps make more immature white blood cells called granulocytes in the bone marrow. We also discovered that IL-17 needs two other proteins, G-CSF and SCF, to work properly. G-CSF helps create more immature granulocytes, while SCF helps them mature into fully-functional cells. However, IL-17 also helps protect mice from losing their granulocytes when we block the action of G-CSF. When we blocked G-CSF in mice, IL-17 helped preserve the number of mature granulocytes in the blood. Interestingly, IL-17 also has a different effect on granulopoiesis (the process of making granulocytes) in the spleen, which is not affected by G-CSF. Overall, our findings suggest that IL-17 has the potential to be developed into a new treatment for some immune-related diseases.

title: The expression of immediate early gene X-1 (IEX-1) is differentially induced by retinoic acids in NB4 and KG1 cells: possible implication in the distinct phenotype of retinoic acid-responsive and -resistant leukemic cells
text: In a cell-type and stimulus-specific manner, the immediate early gene X-1 (IEX-1) is involved in growth regulation and modulation of apoptosis. Our current study reveals that in two acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) cell lines, NB4 and KG1, showing distinct responses to retinoic acid (RA), IEX-1 expression is rapidly induced (within 30-60 minutes) by all-trans or cis-RA, and independent of other signal transduction mediators, such as TNFα, NF-κB, or MAP kinases, in NB4 cells (expressing PML-RARα), the increased IEX-1 expression is transient and completely reversible, along with a cell cycle arrest, ongoing differentiation, and reduced sensitivity to anti-cancer drug-induced apoptosis. In contrast, in KG1 cells (expressing PLZF-RARα), the RA-induced IEX-1 expression persists over days, along with continued cell cycle progression, and increased apoptotic sensitivity. Furthermore, two functional RA response elements in the IEX-1 promoter were identified through gel shift and luciferase reporter gene assays. It appears that IEX-1 may be a unique transcriptional target of the two X-RARα fusion receptors, which exhibit distinct responsiveness to RAs. Following a distinct time course of direct transcriptional induction by PML-RARα and PLZF-RARα in NB4 and KG1 cells, respectively, IEX-1 expression may play a role in the varied actions of these receptors and the distinct phenotypes of APL cells.

title: Comorbidity between ADHD and obesity: exploring shared mechanisms and clinical implications.
text: Recent studies suggest a possible link between Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and obesity. This review aims to systematically examine and critically evaluate the available evidence on the prevalence of ADHD in obese individuals and the weight status of those with ADHD. Relevant articles were searched in three major scientific databases (PubMed, PsychInfo, and ISI Web of Science) between January 1980 and June 2010. Our findings indicate a high prevalence of ADHD in clinical samples of individuals seeking treatment for obesity, as well as higher-than-average body mass index z scores and a significantly higher prevalence of obesity among individuals with ADHD compared to those without. Proposed mechanisms underlying this association include the possibility that obesity-related factors (such as sleep-disordered breathing) can manifest as ADHD-like symptoms, shared common biological dysfunctions between ADHD and obesity, and ADHD's potential contribution to obesity. Based on our findings, it is important to screen for ADHD in patients with obesity and to explore abnormal eating behaviors as a potential contributing factor of obesity in individuals with ADHD. Additionally, preliminary evidence suggests that treating ADHD may improve the weight status of individuals with both obesity and ADHD.

title: Rapamycin treatment augments motor neuron degeneration in SOD1(G93A) mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
text:
Aberrant protein misfolding may contribute to the development of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. In a previous study, we discovered that autophagy is altered in the mouse model of ALS. To investigate the correlation between autophagic alterations and motor neuron (MN) degeneration in ALS mice, we conducted a comprehensive analysis in the present study.
We found that the autophagic protein marker LC3-II is significantly increased in the spinal cord MNs of ALS mice, and electron microscopy and immunochemistry studies revealed significant accumulation of autophagic vacuoles in dystrophic axons of spinal cord MNs. These changes in ALS mice become evident at 90 days of age, when mice display mild clinical symptoms, and become more pronounced at 120 days. The clinical symptoms correlate with the progression of MNs degeneration. Moreover, we observed that p62/SQSTM1 accumulates progressively in the spinal cord, suggesting impaired autophagic flux in ALS mice.
Surprisingly, we found that treatment with autophagy enhancer rapamycin accelerates MNs degeneration, shortens the life span of ALS mice, and has no significant effects on the accumulation of SOD1 aggregates. We also observed that rapamycin treatment in ALS mice leads to more severe mitochondrial impairment, higher Bax levels, and greater caspase-3 activation, suggesting that selective degeneration of MNs is associated with impairment of the autophagy pathway, and that rapamycin treatment may exacerbate this process through apoptosis and other mechanisms in ALS mice.

title: Improvements in survival and clinical benefit with gemcitabine as first-line therapy for patients with advanced pancreas cancer: a randomized trial.
text:
"The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of gemcitabine in managing symptoms and improving survival outcomes in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer. Prior studies had shown promise in the use of gemcitabine for this indication, and this study aimed to confirm these findings through a larger, more definitive trial.
Patients with symptomatic, advanced pancreatic cancer were randomized to receive either gemcitabine or the standard of care treatment, fluorouracil (5-FU). The primary outcome measure was clinical benefit response, which was defined as a sustained improvement in pain intensity, analgesic consumption, Karnofsky performance status, or weight over a minimum of 4 weeks. Secondary outcomes included response rate, time to progressive disease, and overall survival.
Compared to patients treated with 5-FU, those receiving gemcitabine experienced a significantly higher rate of clinical benefit response (23.8% vs. 4.8%, P = 0.0022). The median survival duration was also longer in the gemcitabine group (5.65 months vs. 4.41 months, P = 0.0025). At 12 months, the survival rate was 18% in the gemcitabine group and 2% in the 5-FU group. Treatment was well tolerated in both groups.
Overall, these findings suggest that gemcitabine is more effective than 5-FU in alleviating symptoms and improving survival outcomes in patients with advanced, symptomatic pancreatic cancer."

title: Endothelial-myofibroblast transition contributes to the early development of diabetic renal interstitial fibrosis in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice.
text:
Diabetic nephropathy is the leading cause of chronic kidney disease. Myofibroblasts play a crucial role in the synthesis and secretion of extracellular matrix in diabetic kidney fibrosis. Emerging evidence suggests that endothelial cells may transition to myofibroblasts under both normal and abnormal conditions. Therefore, this study investigated whether endothelial-myofibroblast transition occurs and contributes to the development of diabetic kidney interstitial fibrosis.
To induce diabetes, we used a mouse model called Tie2-Cre;LoxP-EGFP, which has endothelial cells genetically marked with the green fluorescent protein (EGFP). The mice were given a drug called streptozotocin to induce diabetes, and we examined the kidneys of these mice at 1 and 6 months after induction. Confocal microscopy showed that 10.4 +/- 4.2 and 23.5 +/- 7.4% of renal interstitial myofibroblasts (alpha-smooth muscle actin positive, alpha-SMA+) were of endothelial origin (EGFP+/alpha-SMA+) in diabetic kidneys compared to only 0.2 +/- 0.1% in vehicle-treated Tie2-Cre;LoxP-EGFP mice (P < 0.01).
We also studied the effect of transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-beta1) on endothelial cells. We found that TGF-beta1 induced de novo expression of alpha-SMA and loss of expression of vascular endothelial cadherin (VE-cadherin) and CD31 in mouse pancreatic microvascular endothelial cells (MMECs) and primary cultures of renal endothelial cells in a time- and dose-dependent manner. These findings suggest that the endothelial-myofibroblast transition may be a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of diabetic renal interstitial fibrosis.

title: Effect of phosducin silencing on the photokinetic motile response of Blepharisma japonicum.
text: The colored ciliate Blepharisma japonicum exhibits alterations in swimming velocity (positive photokinesis) and elongation of its body in response to prolonged illumination. We have previously proposed that modifications in the phosphorylation status of the ciliate phosducin (Pdc) may play a crucial role in light-induced cell elongation, which in turn affects the interaction between G-protein βγ subunits (Gβγ) and β-tubulin, ultimately leading to cytoskeletal remodeling. The cellular mechanism underlying the photokinetic effect in this ciliate remains unclear. To further elucidate this mechanism, we employed real-time PCR to investigate the expression levels of Pdc mRNA in cells exposed to Pdc-RNAi treatment. Our findings revealed a significant decrease in Pdc mRNA levels in Pdc-RNAi-treated cells compared to control cells. Corroborating these results, we observed a lower expression level of the Pdc protein in these cells using western immunoblotting. Moreover, our assay revealed that in ciliates treated with Pdc-RNAi and exposed to light, the cytosolic levels of Gβ (approximately 36 kDa) were reduced, while the membrane-bound level of Gβ (approximately 32 kDa) was elevated compared to control cells. In addition, behavioral analysis of the cells revealed a substantial reduction in photokinesis. These findings provide deeper insight into the functional properties of the Pdc protein in the photokinetic phenomenon of the ciliate protist Blepharisma and suggest a probable role for this phosphoprotein in mediating the light-dependent changes observed in these organisms.

title: Alzheimer’s disease and NGF signaling
text: Age-related degeneration of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons (BFCNs) commences early and significantly contributes to cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Proper function and morphology of BFCNs rely on the supply of nerve growth factor (NGF) from the cortex and hippocampus. A large number of experiments have demonstrated that decreased NGF supply at the BFCN cell body level leads to loss of neuronal markers and shrinkage, similar to those observed in AD. The delivery of sufficient NGF to BFCN cell bodies depends on various factors, including adequate synthesis and release of NGF, expression of NGF receptors by BFCNs, normal signaling and retrograde transport of NGF-receptor complex, and effective gene induction by NGF. Recent studies have shown that decreased NGF levels in BFCN cell bodies are primarily due to impaired retrograde transport rather than decreased synthesis, binding, or expression of NGF receptors in BFCN terminals. We will discuss in vivo evidence supporting impaired retrograde transport of NGF in a mouse model of BFCN degeneration and compare these findings with our postmortem human AD brain studies. We will speculate on the possible mechanisms of failed NGF retrograde transport and its relationship to AD pathology.

title: Echocardiographic assessment of left ventricular hypertrophy: comparison to necropsy findings.
text: In this study, the accuracy of echocardiographic measurements of left ventricular (LV) dimension and mass was evaluated to determine their reliability in detecting and quantifying LV hypertrophy. The study included 55 patients who underwent echocardiography before death, and LV mass was measured at necropsy using the Penn and American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) methods. The results showed that the Penn-cube LV mass correlated closely with necropsy LV mass (r = 0.92, p < 0.001) and overestimated it by only 6%. The ASE-cube LV mass also correlated with necropsy LV mass (r = 0.90, p < 0.001), but systematically overestimated it by a mean of 25%. However, this overestimation could be corrected using an equation: LV mass = 0.80 (ASE-cube LV mass) + 0.6 g. The use of ASE measurements in the volume correction formula systematically underestimated necropsy LV mass by a mean of 30%. In a subset of 9 patients, 2-dimensional echocardiographic (echo) LV mass measurements using two methods were significantly related to necropsy LV mass (r = 0.68, p < 0.05 and r = 0.82, p < 0.01). Additionally, measurement of myocardial cross-sectional area was found to be acceptably accurate for quantitation of LV mass (r = 0.80, p < 0.001) or diagnosis of LV hypertrophy (sensitivity = 72%, specificity = 94%). Overall, the study suggests that while echocardiographic measurements of LV dimension and mass can be accurate, there are some limitations in their use for diagnosis and quantification of LV hypertrophy, particularly when using the ASE method.

title: R93W mutation in Orai1 causes impaired calcium influx in platelets.
text: The cytosolic calcium concentration of many non-excitable cells is regulated by calcium store release and store-operated calcium entry (SOCE). In platelets, STIM1, a calcium sensor expressed in the endoplasmic reticulum, was recently identified as the main calcium sensor. To investigate the role of the SOCE channel moiety, Orai1, in platelet SOCE, we generated mice expressing a mutated, inactive form of Orai1 (Orai1(R93W)) in blood cells only. Platelets expressing Orai1(R93W) exhibited significantly reduced SOCE and impaired agonist-induced increases in intracellular calcium levels (Ca(2+)). These platelets also showed reduced integrin activation and impaired degranulation when stimulated with low agonist concentrations under static conditions. However, the ability of Orai1(R93W) platelets to aggregate or adhere to collagen under arterial flow conditions ex vivo was not significantly affected. In contrast, these adherent Orai1(R93W) platelets were defective in surface phosphatidylserine exposure, indicating that Orai1 is crucial for the platelets' procoagulant response rather than other calcium-dependent cellular responses.

title: [Efficacy on post-stroke depression treated with acupuncture at the acupoints based on ziwuliuzhu and prozac].
text:
Objective: To investigate the effects of combining acupuncture at specific points (acupoints) based on the midnight-noon ebb-flow theory (ziwuliuzhu) with oral administration of fluoxetine hydrochloride (Prozac) on post-stroke depression.
Methods: Ninety-three patients were randomly divided into three groups: a comprehensive group that combined acupuncture and oral Prozac, a ziwuliuzhu group that received acupuncture based on the midnight-noon ebb-flow theory, and a prozac group that received oral Prozac. The treatment consisted of 6 sessions over a period of 24 weeks, with each session lasting 4 weeks. The clinical efficacy and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) scores were compared among the groups.
Results: The total effective rate was highest in the comprehensive group (96.8%, 30/31 patients), followed by the ziwuliuzhu group (83.9%, 26/31), and the prozac group (80.6%, 25/31). HAMD scores decreased significantly in all groups after treatment, with the lowest scores observed in the comprehensive group at each time point. The ziwuliuzhu group and the prozac group were not significantly different in terms of HAMD scores at 4 and 12 weeks, but the comprehensive group had a lower score at 24 weeks. Moreover, the comprehensive group had fewer adverse reactions (2 cases) compared to the prozac group (6 cases).
Conclusion: The combination of acupuncture at specific points based on the midnight-noon ebb-flow theory and oral administration of Prozac is more effective and safer than either simple Prozac administration or ziwuliuzhu acupuncture alone in treating post-stroke depression. The comprehensive therapy exhibited superior clinical efficacy and longer-term improvements in depressive state compared to the other two groups.

title: Linkage with methadone treatment upon release from incarceration: a promising opportunity.
text: Opiate addicts who inject drugs (IDUs) are disproportionately represented on the incarcerated population in the US, with over a quarter of inmates struggling with this addiction. Fortunately, methadone maintenance treatment has been proven to be highly effective in reducing drug use, criminal activity related to drug use, and the risk of HIV transmission. Inmates who are released from prison are particularly vulnerable to overdose and disease transmission, making immediate access to methadone treatment upon release a crucial opportunity to combat these issues and facilitate a smooth reintegration into society. By connecting individuals to methadone treatment immediately after release, we can significantly reduce the risk of disease transmission, support successful reentry, and minimize the chances of recidivism.

title: The Diabetes Prevention Program: baseline characteristics of the randomized cohort. The Diabetes Prevention Program Research Group.
text: The Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) is a 27-center randomized clinical trial aimed at evaluating the safety and efficacy of interventions designed to delay or prevent the development of type 2 diabetes in individuals at high risk. The trial enrolled 3,234 participants aged 25 years or older, with a body mass index (BMI) of 24 kg/m2 or greater (or 22 kg/m2 for Asian Americans), and impaired glucose tolerance plus a fasting plasma glucose of 5.3-6.9 mmol/l (or < 6.9 mmol for American Indians). Participants were randomly assigned to one of three treatment groups: intensive lifestyle modification, standard care plus metformin, or standard care plus placebo. Baseline data for the three groups are presented, including the demographic characteristics of the participants, such as age, gender, race, and smoking status. The average age of the participants was 51 years, with 67.7% being women and 55% being Caucasian. The study also found that 16% of participants were younger than 40 years and 20% were older than 60 years, and that 48% of women were postmenopausal. There were similar frequencies of history of hypercholesterolemia or hypertension among men and women. The study also found that 66% of men and 71% of women had a first-degree relative with diabetes, and that overall BMI averaged 34 kg/m2 with 57% of men and 73% of women having a BMI greater than or equal to 30 kg/m2. Fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c levels were comparable between men and women, with an average value of 6.0 mmol/l and 5.9% respectively. The DPP aims to determine the effects of these interventions on the development of type 2 diabetes.

title: Chronic Helicobacter pylori infections induce gastric mutations in mice.
text:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Helicobacter pylori infection has been identified as a crucial risk factor for the development of gastric cancer. This study aimed to assess the role of H. pylori infections in inducing genetic alterations in gastric epithelial cells, as well as investigating the potential contribution of a high-salt diet as a genotoxic risk factor.
METHODS: Big Blue transgenic male mice (C57Bl/6) were inoculated with H. pylori (strain SS1 or Helicobacter felis (strain CS1) for 6 and 12 months. The frequency and spectrum of mutations at the stomach level were assessed using techniques such as polymerase chain reaction and immunohistochemistry analysis. Inflammatory host response and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) expression were also evaluated using similar methods.
RESULTS: After 6 months, the gastric mutant frequency was found to be 4-fold and 1.7-fold higher in mice infected with H. pylori and H. felis, respectively, compared to uninfected mice. This increase in mutations was attributed to the creation of transversions (AT --> CG and GC --> TA), which are known to result from oxidative DNA damage. H. pylori-infected mice exhibited severe gastritis and an elevated level of iNOS messenger RNA expression. Hyperplasia developed 12 months after inoculation, and both the mutagenic effects and iNOS expression decreased in H. pylori- and H. felis-infected mice. No synergistic effects of a high-salt diet and Helicobacter infection were observed regarding the frequency of gastric mutation.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides evidence for a direct gastric mutagenic effect of H. pylori infection in the Big Blue transgenic mouse model, which is attributable to oxidative DNA damage and the inflammatory host response.

title: A minimal Tat system from a gram-positive organism: a bifunctional TatA subunit participates in discrete TatAC and TatA complexes.
text: The Tat protein transport system shuttles folded proteins across bacterial and thylakoid membranes. In Gram-negative organisms, a TatABC substrate-binding complex and separate TatA complex are believed to cooperate to form an active translocon, with all three subunits necessary for translocation. Most Gram-positive organisms lack the tatB gene, indicating considerable differences in organization and potential differences in mode of action. We have investigated Tat complexes encoded by the tatAdCd genes of Bacillus subtilis. Expressing tatAdCd in a Tat-deficient Escherichia coli mutant enables efficient export of a large, cofactor-containing E. coli Tat substrate, TorA. Our findings suggest a bifunctional role for the tatAd subunit in B. subtilis.

title: A systemic granulomatous response to Schistosoma mansoni eggs alters responsiveness of bone-marrow-derived macrophages to Toll-like receptor agonists.
text:
In this study, we investigated the impact of systemic Th2-type cytokine polarization on macrophage differentiation and activation in response to Schistosoma mansoni infection. To address this question, we analyzed bone marrow-derived macrophages from mice with S. mansoni egg-induced pulmonary granulomas and unchallenged (or naïve) mice to determine their activation state and response to specific TLR agonists, including S. mansoni egg antigens.
Our findings revealed that macrophages from Th2-polarized mice constitutively expressed higher levels of "found in inflammatory zone-1" (FIZZ1) and ST2 (M2 markers) compared to naïve macrophages, along with lower levels of NO synthase 2, CCL3, MIP-2, TNF-alpha, and IL-12 (M1 markers). Additionally, Th2-polarized macrophages exhibited enhanced responses to the presence of specific TLR agonists, which induced significantly higher levels of gene and protein expression for M2 and M1 markers in these cells.
These data suggest that signals received by bone marrow precursors during S. mansoni egg-induced granuloma responses dynamically alter the development of macrophages and enhance the TLR responsiveness of these cells, which may have a significant impact on the pulmonary granulomatous response. In conclusion, our findings provide new insights into the complex interplay between macrophages and Th2-type cytokines in the context of schistosome infection.

title: Orai1 and STIM reconstitute store-operated calcium channel function.
text: The two membrane proteins, STIM1 and Orai1, are crucial for the activation of store-operated channels (SOCs). However, the interplay between these proteins is not fully understood. To address this, we investigated the effect of coexpressing STIM1 and Orai1 on SOC function. Surprisingly, we found that when these proteins are expressed together, they greatly enhance Ca2+ entry through SOCs. In contrast, expression of Orai1 alone significantly reduces Ca2+ entry through SOCs in human embryonic kidney 293 cells and rat basophilic leukemia cells. Interestingly, when STIM1 is coexpressed with Orai1, it causes a massive increase in Ca2+ entry through SOCs, which is entirely dependent on the store. This entry is completely blocked by the SOC blocker, 2-aminoethoxydiphenylborate. Additionally, coexpression of Orai1 and STIM1 also leads to a significant gain in the function of the CRAC channel in rat basophilic leukemia cells. Notably, the close STIM1 homologue, STIM2, inhibits SOCE when expressed alone, but coexpression with Orai1 leads to substantial constitutive (store-independent) Ca2+ entry. STIM proteins are known to mediate Ca2+ store-sensing and endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane coupling without any intrinsic channel properties. Our findings reveal a powerful gain in SOC function when both Orai1 and STIM1 are present, suggesting that Orai1 contributes the PM channel component responsible for Ca2+ entry. The suppression of SOC function by Orai1 overexpression likely reflects a required stoichiometry between STIM1 and Orai1.

title: Tet and TDG mediate DNA demethylation essential for mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition in somatic cell reprogramming.
text: Tet-mediated DNA oxidation is a recently identified epigenetic modification in mammals, and its function in cell-fate transitions remains incompletely understood. To investigate its role in cell reprogramming, we derived mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) lacking all three Tet genes and assessed their ability to reprogram into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). We discovered that Tet-deficient MEFs are unable to undergo reprogramming due to a block in the mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET) step. Similarly, reprogramming of MEFs lacking the TDG gene is also impaired. The block in reprogramming is attributed to defective activation of key miRNAs, which depends on oxidative demethylation promoted by Tet and TDG. Restoring either the affected miRNAs or catalytically active Tet and TDG in the knockout MEFs revives reprogramming to pluripotency. These findings provide insight into the role of epigenetic barriers in cell-lineage conversion during reprogramming.

title: The last and the next hundred years of malariology.
text: The forefront figures in malariology demonstrated impressive scientific creativity, perseverance in their research, unwavering determination, breadth of interest, and social concern. A century later, despite substantial progress in malaria research, the world continues to grapple with a formidable burden of the disease. To tackle this challenge in the next century, research necessitates both greater specialization and a wider scope of inquiry, calling for multidisciplinary teamwork. Climate change and interventions have yielded a dynamic and evolving malaria landscape, as opposed to the static one of the past. Through detailed analysis of the parasite's life cycle at various scales, including electron microscopy, biochemistry, and genetics, researchers have gained valuable insights into the biomedical aspects of malariology. Recent advancements have centered on stage-specific antigens, disease cycles, population genetics of parasites, vectors, and humans, as well as genetic variations within these components. This comprehensive understanding provides a framework for the new century, enabling the development of effective strategies to combat drug resistance, vaccine creation, insecticidal and net control, and socio-economic support for malaria control efforts. Furthermore, recent work on large-scale changes in malaria incidence across space and time has enabled researchers to predict epidemics with greater accuracy. The next generation of malariology will require a concerted effort to integrate these various scales of understanding and link them to the different levels of the health system. Most importantly, addressing the grim situation in impoverished holoendemic countries necessitates practical support, akin to that provided by the founders of malariology. A combined understanding of the biomedical and socio-economic aspects of malaria must feed into the ongoing control efforts, from Roll Back Malaria and beyond, to create a more sustainable future for generations to come.

title: Activation of AMP-activated protein kinase suppresses oxidized low-density lipoprotein-induced macrophage proliferation.
text:
Macrophage-derived foam cells play a crucial role in the development and progression of atherosclerosis, a disease characterized by the accumulation of lipids and inflammatory cells in the arterial wall. In a previous study, we showed that the expression of granulocyte/macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) is essential for oxidized low density lipoprotein (Ox-LDL)-induced macrophage proliferation. Here, we investigated whether activating the AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) pathway could inhibit macrophage proliferation.
We found that the AMPK activator, 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside (AICAR), significantly inhibited Ox-LDL-induced macrophage proliferation in mouse peritoneal macrophages. This inhibition was mediated by AMPK activation, as dominant-negative AMPKα1 restored macrophage proliferation. AICAR only partially suppressed Ox-LDL-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation and GM-CSF expression, suggesting that there are additional mechanisms involved in the AICAR-mediated suppression of macrophage proliferation.
Interestingly, AICAR also suppressed GM-CSF-induced macrophage proliferation without affecting p38 MAPK/Akt signaling. GM-CSF, in turn, suppressed p53 phosphorylation and expression and induced Rb phosphorylation. Overexpression of p53 or p27(kip) suppressed GM-CSF-induced macrophage proliferation. AICAR induced cell cycle arrest, increased p53 phosphorylation and expression, and suppressed GM-CSF-induced Rb phosphorylation through AMPK activation. Moreover, AICAR induced p21(cip) and p27(kip) expression via AMPK activation, and small interfering RNA (siRNA) of p21(cip) and p27(kip) restored AICAR-mediated suppression of macrophage proliferation.
In conclusion, our findings suggest that AMPK activation can suppress macrophage proliferation by suppressing GM-CSF expression and inducing cell cycle arrest, which may be a promising therapeutic strategy for atherosclerosis.

title: Evaluation of cortical bone by peripheral quantitative computed tomography in renal transplant recipients.
text:
BACKGROUND:
Renal transplant patients have an approximately threefold higher risk of fractures compared to healthy controls. Most of these fractures are located in the periphery, indicating a more severe deterioration of cortical bone. Peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) is a noninvasive imaging method that allows for detailed evaluations of both cortical and trabecular bone. We conducted a study to investigate cortical bone parameters in 12 renal transplant patients using pQCT, in comparison to a group of 27 healthy controls.
METHODS:
We performed pQCT scans on the distal radius of the nondominant forearm (15% of the length of the ulna, proximal to the radius end plate) in 12 renal transplant patients (7 men and 5 women) and 27 healthy controls. We measured total and cortical bone mineral density (TBMD, cBMD), total (cross-sectional) and cortical area (TA, cA), cortical thickness (cThk), endosteal and periosteal circumferences, and the buckling ratio (r/cThK).
RESULTS:
Our results revealed significant increases in total area (TA), endosteal circumference, and the buckling ratio in renal transplant patients compared to controls. Female patients showed a pronounced decrease in cortical area (cA) and cortical thickness (cThk), while male patients exhibited a decrease in cortical thickness and an increase in endosteal perimeter. Total time on dialysis before transplantation correlated negatively with cortical thickness.
CONCLUSIONS:
Our findings suggest that a pronounced thinning of cortical bone may underlie the increased incidence of peripheral fractures in renal transplant patients.

title: Ataxia, dementia, and hypogonadotropism caused by disordered ubiquitination.
text: A century ago, the combination of ataxia and hypogonadism was first described, but the genetic basis of this syndrome has remained elusive until now. In this study, we used whole-exome sequencing and targeted sequencing of candidate genes to identify the genetic cause of ataxia and hypogonadism in a consanguineous family. We found that digenic homozygous mutations in RNF216 and OTUD4, which encode a ubiquitin E3 ligase and a deubiquitinase, respectively, were present in three affected siblings. Additional screening identified compound heterozygous truncating mutations in RNF216 in an unrelated patient and single heterozygous deleterious mutations in four other patients. We also found that knockdown of RNF216 or OTUD4 in zebrafish embryos resulted in defects in the eye, optic tectum, and cerebellum, and that combinatorial suppression of both genes exacerbated these phenotypes. Importantly, we detected neuronal loss in cerebellar pathways and the hippocampus, and ubiquitin-immunoreactive intranuclear inclusions in surviving hippocampal neurons. Additionally, we detected defects at the hypothalamic and pituitary levels of the reproductive endocrine axis. Our findings demonstrate that inactivating mutations in RNF216 or the combination of mutations in RNF216 and OTUD4 can cause the syndrome of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, ataxia, and dementia. These findings highlight the importance of disordered ubiquitination in neurodegeneration and reproductive dysfunction, and illustrate the power of whole-exome sequencing and functional studies for uncovering genetic interactions that cause disease. (Funded by the National Institutes of Health and others)

title: Combination cancer immunotherapies tailored to the tumour microenvironment
text: Emerging evidence suggests that cancer immunotherapy will play a significant role in the combination treatment plans of many patients with various cancer types in the near future. There are multiple immune processes involving different antitumor and tumor-promoting white blood cells, and cancer cells employ various strategies to evade the immune response. The tumor microenvironment can help determine which immune suppressive pathways become activated to restrain antitumor immunity. This includes immune checkpoint receptors on effector T cells and myeloid cells and the release of inhibitory cytokines and metabolites. Therapeutic approaches that target these pathways, particularly immune-checkpoint receptors, can induce durable antitumor responses in patients with advanced-stage cancers, including melanoma. However, many patients do not respond well to monotherapy approaches, and alternative strategies are required to achieve optimal therapeutic benefits. These strategies include eliminating the bulk of tumor cells to stimulate tumor-antigen release and APC function, using adjuvants to enhance APC function, and using agents that enhance effector-cell activity. In this review, we discuss the categorization of the tumor microenvironment based on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and PD-L1 expression in the tumor and how this categorization enables the design of personalized combination cancer therapies tailored to target different tumor microenvironments.

title: Cyclic AMP-dependent phosphorylation of thromboxane A(2) receptor-associated Galpha(13).
text: Newly discovered evidence suggests that cAMP selectively inhibits platelet activation triggered by all agonists by targeting the thromboxane A(2) signal transduction pathway. Previous studies have shown that cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA) regulates the phosphorylation of the thromboxane A(2) receptor-G-protein complex. To investigate this further, we analyzed the effects of cAMP on PKA-dependent protein phosphorylation in the region of Gα subunits. Our results showed that cAMP triggers PKA-dependent [γ-(32)P]ATP labeling of solubilized membrane proteins in the Gα subunit region, with a visible labeling density of 38-45 kDa. Furthermore, thromboxane A(2) receptor-G-protein complexes isolated from these membranes exhibited co-purification with 38-45 kDa phosphoproteins. Using immunoprecipitation, we found that the affinity chromatography-purified complexes exhibited increased phosphorylation of thromboxane A(2) receptor-associated Gα(13) upon treatment with 8-Br-cAMP, with an increase of 87 ± 27%. In addition, immunopurification of Gα(13) on microtiter wells coated with a different Gα(13) antibody revealed that 8-Br-cAMP increased Gα(13) phosphorylation by 53 ± 19%. Lastly, treatment of [32]P-labeled whole platelets with prostacyclin led to a 90 ± 14% increase in phosphorylated Gα(13), which was abolished by the adenylate cyclase inhibitor MDL-12. These findings provide the first evidence that PKA mediates phosphorylation of Gα(13) both in vitro and in vivo, and demonstrate a basis for the selective inhibition of thromboxane A(2)-mediated signaling in platelets by cAMP.

title: Tet proteins can convert 5-methylcytosine to 5-formylcytosine and 5-carboxylcytosine.
text: In DNA, 5-methylcytosine (5mC) plays a crucial role in gene expression, genomic imprinting, and the suppression of transposable elements. This methylation can be converted to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) by the Tet (ten eleven translocation) proteins. We have discovered that, in addition to 5hmC, the Tet proteins can generate two further cytosine derivatives, 5-formylcytosine (5fC) and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC), through an enzymatic activity-dependent process. These cytosine derivatives are present in genomic DNA from mouse embryonic stem cells and mouse organs. By manipulating the levels of Tet proteins, we have found that the genomic content of 5hmC, 5fC, and 5caC can be increased or reduced. Our findings suggest that DNA demethylation may occur through a mechanism involving the oxidation of 5mC followed by decarboxylation.

title: Long-term use of aspirin and age-related macular degeneration.
text:
Aspirin is commonly used to relieve pain and exhibit cardioprotective effects, but its usage poses concerns for ophthalmologists, particularly when ocular surgery is being considered or in the presence of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The Beaver Dam Eye Study, a population-based, longitudinal study conducted in Wisconsin over 20 years, aimed to investigate the association between regular aspirin use and the incidence of AMD.
The study examined 4926 participants aged 43 to 86 years at the baseline examination, with the mean duration of follow-up being 14.8 years. Participants were asked if they had regularly used aspirin at least twice a week for more than 3 months during subsequent examinations. Incident cases of early AMD, late AMD, and subtypes of late AMD (neovascular AMD and pure geographic atrophy) were identified in retinal photographs based on the Wisconsin Age-Related Maculopathy Grading System.
The study found that regular aspirin use 10 years prior to retinal examination was associated with a small but statistically significant increase in the risk of incident late and neovascular AMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.63, 95% CI 1.01-2.63, P = .05). The estimated incidence of late AMD in regular users was 1.76%, and 1.03% in nonusers. However, aspirin use 5 years or 10 years prior to retinal examination was not associated with incident early AMD.
In conclusion, the study found that regular aspirin use 10 years prior to observed incidence was associated with a small but statistically significant increase in the risk of incident late and neovascular AMD. These findings suggest that aspirin use may have a protective role in the development of late and neovascular AMD.

title: Growth control and ribosomopathies.
text: Two of the most energy-intensive processes in a growing cell are ribosome biogenesis and protein synthesis. Defects in these molecular components can significantly alter the pattern of gene expression, making it understandable why cells have evolved a surveillance system to monitor the status of the translational machinery. In recent years, researchers have identified specific genetic mutations and deletions linked to ribosome biogenesis, leading to the classification of these conditions as ribosomopathies. The study of ribosomopathies has provided valuable insights into the relationship between growth regulation and ribosome biogenesis over the past decade. New findings on the extra-ribosomal functions of certain ribosome proteins and their influence on p53 levels have shed light on the connection between ribosome impairment and cell cycle regulation. Nevertheless, evidence suggests that p53 and Hdm2-independent pathways may also be involved. In this review, we will summarize the latest discoveries regarding the mechanisms underlying ribosomopathies and explore the connection between ribosome production and tumorigenesis.

title: Tunable signal processing through modular control of transcription factor translocation.
text: Signaling pathways can lead to diverse transcription factor (TF) activation dynamics. To investigate how TFs process signals to produce varying responses, we studied the general stress-responsive TF Msn2 in budding yeast. Msn2 acts as a versatile signal processor, capable of adapting its processing of input signals in an input-dependent manner. This tunable signal processing is mediated by dual regulation of nuclear import and export through phosphorylation, with sustained functionality of only one signal-processing function in mutants lacking regulation of one form. The versatility of Msn2's signal processing is crucial for generating distinct dynamic responses to various environmental stresses. Our findings provide insights into how complex signal-processing functions can be integrated into a single molecule, offering a framework for designing TFs with "programmable" signal-processing capabilities.

title: Killing by bactericidal antibiotics does not depend on reactive oxygen species.
text: Traditionally, it was believed that bactericidal antibiotics kill by modulating their respective targets. However, recent studies have challenged this view by proposing an alternative mechanism of killing, whereby toxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) are produced in the presence of antibiotics. Contrary to expectations, we found no correlation between an individual bacterial cell's probability of survival in the presence of antibiotics and its level of ROS. Surprisingly, the use of an ROS quencher, thiourea, protected bacterial cells from the toxic effects of antibiotics, even under anaerobic conditions. Notably, there was no significant difference in the survival of bacteria treated with various antibiotics under either aerobic or anaerobic conditions, suggesting that ROS do not play a role in killing bacterial pathogens by antibiotics.

title: A naturally occurring mouse model of X-linked congenital stationary night blindness.
text:
The purpose of this study is to describe a naturally occurring X-linked recessive mutation in mice, known as nob, which affects the transmission of visual information between photoreceptors and second-order neurons in the retina.
