This has important implications for drug delivery and disease control, as poor inhaler technique can lead to reduced medication efficacy.
Our findings suggest that prescribing a patient's preferred inhaler device can increase cost, but it can also improve efficiency and be cost-effective in the long term. Using an inexpensive device (pMDI) when technique is good and a patient's preferred inhaler device when not can optimize delivery and even reduce costs.
In conclusion, our study highlights the importance of proper inhaler technique and device selection to ensure effective drug delivery and disease control. By considering patient preferences and technique, healthcare providers can optimize drug delivery and improve treatment outcomes.

title: Hemoperfusion-hemodialysis ineffective for paraquat removal in life-threatening poisoning?
text:
We present a case report on a patient who underwent hemoperfusion-hemodialysis (HP-HD) for severe paraquat poisoning. Our objective was to investigate the efficacy of HP-HD in removing paraquat from the body, as previous studies have suggested that this combination may enhance drug removal. The patient was admitted to the hospital 3 hours after ingesting the chemical, and HP-HD was initiated immediately. Blood samples were collected at various time points during and after the procedure. The results showed that the HP-HD procedure significantly improved the clearance of paraquat from the central compartment (plasma), with an increase in blood clearance of 116 +/- 32 ml/min (n=6) during the charcoal column phase, 90 +/- 54 ml/min (n=6) during the artificial kidney phase (HD), and 151 +/- 37 ml/min (n=6) for the combined systems (HP-HD). However, despite this efficient clearance from the central compartment, a limited rebound in blood paraquat levels was observed after HP-HD. Unfortunately, the patient developed renal and hepatic failure one day after admission, and died 5 days later. Tissue paraquat levels were measured in various organs, and the results showed elevated levels in the skeletal muscle, pancreas, prostate, thyroid, lungs, bone marrow, kidney, spleen, adrenal, heart, liver, and stomach, with levels in the testis below 1.0 microgram/g wet tissue. These findings confirm previous studies indicating that HP-HD may not be effective in removing paraquat from the peripheral compartment (tissues).
In summary, we investigated the efficacy of HP-HD in treating severe paraquat poisoning through a case report. Although HP-HD improved the clearance of paraquat from the central compartment, the procedure was unable to completely remove the drug from the peripheral compartment, leading to limited efficacy in treating severe poisoning.

title: Cancer treatment and survivorship statistics, 2014.
text: The number of cancer survivors continues to rise due to population growth and aging, as well as advancements in early detection and treatment. To better support these individuals, the American Cancer Society and National Cancer Institute collaborated to estimate the current and future number of cancer survivors using data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) program registries. The study also described current treatment patterns for the most common cancer types based on data from the National Cancer Data Base and the SEER and SEER-Medicare linked databases, and provided information on treatment-related side effects. According to the study, nearly 14.5 million Americans with a history of cancer were alive on January 1, 2014, and this number is expected to increase to nearly 19 million by January 1, 2024. The most common cancers among males are prostate cancer (43%), colorectal cancer (9%), and melanoma (8%), while among females, the most common cancers are breast cancer (41%), uterine corpus cancer (8%), and colon and rectum cancer (8%). The age distribution of survivors varies significantly by cancer type, with the majority of prostate cancer survivors being aged 70 years or older, compared to less than one-third of melanoma survivors in this age group. It is crucial for healthcare providers to understand the unique medical and psychosocial needs of cancer survivors and to proactively assess and manage these issues. There are numerous resources available to help patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers navigate the various stages of cancer survivorship.

title: Massive activation of archaeal defense genes during viral infection.
text: Archaeal viruses display extraordinary genetic and structural diversity, with studies on these viruses shedding light on the vastness of viral diversity and evolution. The Sulfolobus islandicus rod-shaped virus 2 (SIRV2) serves as a valuable model to investigate virus-host interactions in Archaea. It is a lytic virus that employs a unique mechanism of egress through the formation of distinct pyramidal structures on the host cell membrane. By employing whole-transcriptome sequencing, we have generated a comprehensive map of host and viral gene expression throughout the infection cycle of SIRV2 in its thermophilic host S. islandicus LAL14/1. This information, combined with a yeast two-hybrid analysis of SIRV2 protein interactions, has greatly expanded our understanding of viral gene function. As a direct result of SIRV2 infection, over one-third of S. islandicus genes were found to be differentially regulated, with genes involved in cell division showing decreased expression, while genes involved in antiviral defense were greatly activated. Moreover, the study revealed a pronounced expression of genes belonging to toxin-antitoxin and CRISPR-Cas systems. The distinct levels of activation observed among the various CRISPR-Cas systems highlight the specialized functions they perform. The detailed information on individual gene expression and antiviral defense systems is expected to serve as a valuable resource for future investigations aimed at a deeper comprehension of these systems in vivo.

title: Impact of human immunodeficiency virus infection on the histological features of chronic hepatitis C: a case-control study. The MULTIVIRC group.
text: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is commonly found in individuals with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) due to their shared routes of transmission. Prior studies suggested that HIV infection might slow down the progression of chronic hepatitis C, but these studies did not take into account factors that affect the liver's natural progression to cirrhosis, such as alcohol consumption, sexual contact, age at infection, and duration of HCV infection. To investigate this further, we analyzed liver biopsy samples from two groups of 58 patients, one infected by both HCV and HIV and the other infected by HCV only. The two groups were matched based on these risk factors, and we evaluated the liver biopsy responses using the METAVIR scoring system. Our findings revealed that HIV-positive patients had a higher METAVIR activity compared to HIV-negative patients. Specifically, cirrhosis was more common among HIV-positive patients with a low CD4 cell count (45%) compared to HIV-negative patients (10%) (P = 0.003). Additionally, we found that cirrhosis was more frequent among HIV-positive patients with a low CD4 cell count (45%) compared to those with a high CD4 cell count (17%) (P = 0.04). These differences may be due to enhanced HCV replication during HIV infection or other immune mechanisms that require further investigation.

title: Relation of plasma leptin concentrations to sex, body fat, dietary intake, and peak oxygen uptake in young adult women and men.
text: In this study, the relationship between leptin and dietary and metabolic factors was investigated among college-aged men and women (n = 32). The results showed a significant difference in leptin levels between men and women, with women having higher levels (2.1 ng/mL vs. 1.2 ng/mL, respectively). This difference remained significant even after adjusting for fat mass and fat-free mass as covariates. In contrast, men had higher levels of VO2peak (peak oxygen consumption) than women, which remained significant after adjusting for differences in fat-free mass and total body mass. Correlations were found between leptin and indicators of fat mass in both men and women, with stronger correlations in men. Specifically, the correlations were 0.548, 0.674, and 0.732 for body mass index, percentage of body fat, and fat mass [kg] in women, and 0.740, 0.888, and 0.858 in men. In addition, ln leptin showed a significant inverse relationship with VO2peak in men only. After adjusting for body fat mass, ln leptin was not significantly associated with any of the measured variables. However, when leptin was normalized using fat mass as the divisor, men showed significant correlations between ln leptin and dietary intake and VO2peak. Overall, the study found that leptin levels were higher in women, but men had stronger associations between leptin and metabolic and dietary factors.

title: Expression of a human cytomegalovirus latency-associated homolog of interleukin-10 during the productive phase of infection.
text: The human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) UL111A region is active during both the productive and latent phases of infection. During productive infection, the virus expresses ORF79, a protein with oncogenic properties, and cmvIL-10, a functional homolog of human IL-10. However, during latent infection of myeloid progenitor cells, an alternately spliced variant of cmvIL-10, termed latency-associated (LA) cmvIL-10, has been previously identified. To determine if LAcmvIL-10 transcription occurs during productive infection, we employed 5' and 3' RACE to map UL111A-region transcripts in productively infected human foreskin fibroblasts (HFFs). This analysis revealed the presence of a singly spliced UL111A-region transcript that encodes LAcmvIL-10. This transcript was expressed in HFFs with early (β) kinetics, a temporal class distinct from that of ORF79 (α kinetics) and cmvIL-10 (γ kinetics). These findings identify and locate a transcript encoding a latency-associated homolog of IL-10, which is produced by the virus during the productive phase of infection.

title: Kruppel-like factor 4 is essential for inflammatory monocyte differentiation in vivo.
text: Members of the Kruppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors play crucial roles in the differentiation, survival, and trafficking of blood and immune cells. Our study shows that hematopoietic cells from KLF4-deficient fetal livers (FL) had normal numbers of functional hematopoietic progenitor cells, were protective against radiation damage, and performed equally well as KLF4-positive cells in competitive repopulation assays. However, hematopoietic cells from KLF4-deficient fetal livers that were transplanted into lethally irradiated wild-type mice lacked circulating inflammatory (CD115+Gr1+) monocytes and had reduced numbers of resident (CD115+Gr1-) monocytes. Although the numbers and function of peritoneal macrophages were normal in KLF4-deficient chimeras, bone marrow monocytic cells from these chimeras expressed lower levels of key trafficking molecules and were more apoptotic. Our in vivo loss-of-function studies demonstrate that KLF4, which was previously shown to mediate proinflammatory signaling in human macrophages in vitro, is essential for the differentiation of mouse inflammatory monocytes and is involved in the differentiation of resident monocytes. Additionally, inducible expression of KLF4 in the HL60 human acute myeloid leukemia cell line stimulated monocytic differentiation and enhanced 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol 13-acetate-induced macrophage differentiation, but blocked all-trans-retinoic acid-induced granulocytic differentiation of HL60 cells. The inflammation-selective effects of KLF4 loss and the gain-of-KLF4-induced monocytic differentiation in HL60 cells identify KLF4 as a key regulator of monocytic differentiation and a potential target for translational immune modulation.

title: A population-based, case–control study of green tea consumption and leukemia risk in southwestern Taiwan
text: The study examined the association between green tea consumption and leukemia in a cohort of 252 cases (response rate of 90.3%) and 637 controls (response rate of 53.4%). To assess individual catechin consumption, green tea was used as a reference standard. The study stratified catechin consumption into four levels. Conditional logistic regression models were used to analyze the association between leukemia and catechin consumption among subjects aged 0-15 and 16-29 years. A significant inverse association between green tea consumption and leukemia risk was observed among individuals aged 16-29 years, but no significant association was found in younger age groups. Among those aged 30 years or older who consumed large amounts of tea (>550 units of catechins), the adjusted odds ratio (OR) compared with those without tea consumption was 0.47 (95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.23-0.97). After adjusting for smoking status and medical irradiation exposure, the overall OR for all participants was 0.49 (95% CI = 0.27-0.91), indicating an inverse relation between high levels of catechins and leukemia. The study suggests that drinking sufficient amounts of green tea, which contains more catechins than oolong tea and black tea, may be protective against leukemia.

title: Specific HDV RNA-templated transcription by pol II in vitro.
text: RNA polymerase II is believed to play a role in the RNA-templated RNA synthesis during the replication of viroids and Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV). Despite its importance, the specific requirements for this process are not well understood. To further investigate, we developed an in vitro transcription system using HeLa cell nuclear extract (NE) as a starting point. We used a segment of antigenomic RNA corresponding to the left-hand tip region of the HDV rod-like structure as a template for efficient and specific RNA synthesis. Our findings revealed that the accumulation of the unique RNA product is highly sensitive to the drug alpha-amanitin in HeLa NE, suggesting the involvement of RNA polymerase II (pol II) in this reaction. Additionally, our analysis revealed that the RNA product is a chimeric molecule consisting of a newly synthesized transcript covalently attached to the 5' half of the RNA template. The specificity of start site selection for transcription is thought to depend on the secondary structure of the RNA template rather than its primary sequence, leading to similarities with the RNA cleavage-extension process observed in vitro for pol II-arrested complexes. Finally, we discuss the possibility that the described reaction may play a role in HDV replication.

title: Pulmonary vascular lesions in end-stage idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: Histopathologic study on lung explant specimens and correlations with pulmonary hemodynamics.
text:
In patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), alterations in pulmonary blood vessels are more pronounced in fibrotic areas, but the extent of these changes in preserved lung tissue has remained unclear. To investigate this further, we conducted a retrospective study on lung tissue samples from 26 patients with a definitive IPF diagnosis who underwent lung transplantation. Our primary objectives were to:
1. Describe the vascular lesions in both fibrotic and preserved lung areas, and
2. Correlate these lesions with pulmonary hemodynamics. In dense fibrotic zones, we observed thickening of arterial and venous walls with significant luminal narrowing in every patient. In contrast, mild changes to muscular pulmonary arteries were evident in architecturally preserved lung zones, with 65% of patients exhibiting occlusion of venules and small pulmonary veins. Our findings revealed a significant positive correlation between the extent of lung fibrosis and mean pulmonary artery pressure. However, we failed to identify a correlation between mean pulmonary artery pressure and venous/venular changes in non-fibrotic areas. Our study suggests that in many IPF patients, non-fibrotic lung tissue demonstrates an occlusive venopathy, the significance of which remains unclear.

title: Maternal and perinatal outcome in severe pregnancy-related liver disease.
text: Over a 10-year period, 46 pregnant women ( median age: 30 years, range: 17-41 years) were transferred to a Liver Failure Unit due to severe hepatic dysfunction during the third trimester of pregnancy. Of these, 70% were nulliparous and 5 had twin pregnancies, with a median gestational age of 35 weeks (range: 24-40 weeks). At admission, 70% of the patients were preeclamptic and 46% were encephalopathic and/or ventilated. Clinical features and laboratory values consistent with Acute Fatty Liver of Pregnancy (AFLP) were present in 70% of the patients, while 15% had the Hemolysis, Elevated Liver Enzymes, and Low Platelet Count (HELLP) syndrome. One patient had preeclamptic liver rupture requiring liver transplantation, and in 6 other patients, causes of severe liver dysfunction unrelated to pregnancy were found. Infectious complications occurred in 53% of the patients with AFLP and in 29% of those with HELLP syndrome. Major intra-abdominal bleeding occurred in 12 women, 10 of whom required laparotomies for clot evacuation. Unfortunately, 12.5% of the patients with AFLP had a fatal outcome, resulting in a perinatal mortality rate of 9%. In contrast, there were no maternal or perinatal deaths associated with HELLP syndrome. These findings suggest that preventing bleeding and infectious complications may improve the outcome for women with severe AFLP and HELLP syndrome.

title: Circadian rhythms and the regulation of metabolic tissue function and energy homeostasis.
text: Circadian rhythm regulators are crucial for synchronizing internal bodily processes with the recurring changes in the external environment. Recent clinical and molecular research reveals that circadian biology may have a significant impact on the regulation of metabolic tissue functions, including adipose tissue. Based on this knowledge, we propose that disruptions in circadian rhythms may contribute to the development of obesity, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic syndrome.

title: Large-scale gene function analysis with the PANTHER classification system
text: The PANTHER (Protein Annotation through Evolutionary Relationship) classification system (<http://www.pantherdb.org/>) is a comprehensive framework that integrates gene function, ontology, pathways, and statistical analysis tools to enable biologists to analyze large-scale, genome-wide data from sequencing, proteomics, or gene expression experiments. Built with 82 complete genomes organized into gene families and subfamilies, and capturing their evolutionary relationships through phylogenetic trees, multiple sequence alignments, and statistical models (Hidden Markov Models or HMMs), PANTHER assigns genes to functional categories through ontology terms (Gene Ontology (GO) and PANTHER protein class). The system also links sequences to PANTHER pathways. The PANTHER website features a suite of tools for browsing and querying gene functions, as well as analyzing large-scale experimental data with various statistical tests. It is widely utilized by bench scientists, bioinformaticians, computer scientists, and systems biologists. In the 2013 release of PANTHER (v.8.0), the data content was updated and the website interface was redesigned to enhance both user experience and analytical capabilities. This protocol provides a detailed guidance on how to analyze genome-wide experimental data using the PANTHER classification system.

title: Periostin, a novel marker of intramembranous ossification, is expressed in fibrous dysplasia and in c-Fos-overexpressing bone lesions.
text:
Fibrous dysplasia is a benign bone disorder caused by a genetic mutation that leads to excessive cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) production. Histologically, the disease is characterized by the production of fibrous tissue, accompanied by the deposition of abnormal collagen and other bone-associated extracellular matrix proteins, and irregular woven intramembranous bone with type I collagen-containing Sharpey fibers. Fibrous dysplasia is also characterized by high levels of c-Fos/c-Jun, which are downstream targets of cAMP signaling.
In this study, we investigated the expression of the extracellular matrix protein periostin and its receptor integrin alpha v beta 3 in normal bones and fibrous dysplasia. Immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization analyses showed that periostin is expressed in the extracellular matrix during intramembranous ossification but not during endochondral ossification, and in the fibrous component of fibrous dysplasia. Moreover, all cells adjacent to periostin-positive regions expressed integrin alpha v beta 3. Interestingly, periostin was abundantly localized to Sharpey fibers.
To elucidate the contribution of c-Fos in fibrous dysplasia, we analyzed transgenic mice overexpressing c-Fos, which develop sclerotic lesions resembling those found in fibrous dysplasia. In these lesions, transformed osteoblasts expressed high levels of periostin, whereas normal osteoblasts did not. Our findings suggest that periostin is a novel marker for intramembranous ossification and a potential diagnostic tool or therapeutic target in fibrous dysplasia. Moreover, the Gs alpha-cAMP-c-Fos pathway may represent one mechanism of periostin up-regulation in fibrous dysplasia, leading to altered collagen fibrillogenesis characteristic of this disease.

title: FGF-2 enhances intestinal stem cell survival and its expression is induced after radiation injury.
text:
Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) have the ability to stimulate cell growth and division in a wide range of cell types, including those from mesenchymal, neuronal, and epithelial lineages. During normal embryonic development, FGFs play a crucial role in regulating various events. Their role is also evident in processes such as angiogenesis, wound healing, and cancer development. FGF-2 is expressed in many adult tissues, including the intestine, and has been shown to regulate the migration and proliferation of intestinal epithelial cells in vitro. However, little is known about the impact of FGF-2 on intestinal epithelial stem cells during both normal epithelial renewal and regeneration after injury.
In this study, we investigated the expression of FGF-2 in the mouse small intestine after irradiation and assessed the effect of exogenous FGF-2 on crypt stem cell survival after radiation injury. We found that FGF-2 expression in the small intestine increases significantly 12 hours after gamma-irradiation, peak levels being observed from 48 to 120 hours after irradiation, with the higher molecular mass isoform (approximately 24 kDa) being the dominant form expressed. Immunohistochemical analysis of FGF-2 expression after radiation injury revealed that FGF-2 is primarily found in mesenchymal cells surrounding regenerating crypts. Furthermore, we discovered that exogenous recombinant human FGF-2 (rhFGF-2) significantly enhances crypt stem cell survival when administered before irradiation.
In conclusion, our findings suggest that expression of FGF-2 is induced by radiation injury, and that rhFGF-2 can promote crypt stem cell survival after subsequent injury. This study provides valuable insights into the role of FGF-2 in intestinal stem cell biology and its potential as a therapeutic agent for protecting against radiation-induced damage to the intestinal epithelium.

title: Caspase inhibitors promote alternative cell death pathways.
text: Caspase inhibitors have revealed the existence of backup cell death programs for apoptosis. The broad-spectrum caspase inhibitor zVAD-fmk modulates three types of cell death: apoptotic cell death, necrotic cell death, and autophagic cell death. ZVAD-fmk blocks apoptotic cell death, sensitizes cells to necrotic cell death, and induces autophagic cell death. Studies have shown that the kinase RIP1 and the adenosine nucleotide translocator (ANT)-cylophilin D (CypD) complex play crucial roles in necrotic cell death. ZVAD-fmk inhibits caspase-8-mediated proteolysis of RIP1 and disrupts the ANT-CypD interaction, leading to sensitization of cells to necrotic cell death. RIP1 is also involved in autophagic cell death. Caspase inhibitors and knockdown studies have revealed negative roles for catalase and caspase-8 in autophagic cell death. The interconnection between necrotic and autophagic cell death pathways suggests that RIP1 and caspase-8 play opposing roles in these two types of cell death. Necrotic cell death is a rapid response involving mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, decreased adenosine triphosphate concentration, and other cellular insults, while autophagic cell death begins as a survival attempt to clean up ROS-damaged mitochondria. However, excessive autophagy can become cytotoxic and lead to autophagic cell death. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of these alternative cell death pathways may provide therapeutic tools to combat cell death associated with neurodegenerative diseases, ischemia-reperfusion pathologies, and infectious diseases, and may also lead to the development of alternative cytotoxic strategies in cancer treatment.

title: Nucleosome stability mediated by histone variants H3.3 and H2A.Z.
text: In vivo, nucleosomes containing the histone variant H3.3 tend to cluster near transcriptionally active genes and regulatory elements. However, it remained unclear if H3.3-containing nucleosomes possess unique properties affecting transcription. We investigated and found that H3.3 nucleosomes isolated from vertebrates, regardless of the presence of H2A or H2A.Z, are unusually sensitive to salt-dependent disruption, losing H2A/H2B or H2A.Z/H2B dimers. Immunoprecipitation studies of nucleosome core particles (NCPs) revealed that NCPs containing both H3.3 and H2A.Z are less stable than those containing H3.3 and H2A. Intriguingly, NCPs with H3 and H2A.Z are at least as stable as H3/H2A NCPs. These findings establish an hierarchy of stabilities for native nucleosomes carrying different variants, suggesting that H2A.Z may play different roles depending on its partners within the NCP. They also support the idea that H3.3 plays an active role in maintaining accessible chromatin structures in enhancer regions and transcribed regions, as found at promoters and enhancers of transcriptionally active genes and highly expressed coding regions, which have nucleosomes carrying both H3.3 and H2A.Z.

title: Increased growth after long-term oral 1alpha,25-vitamin D3 in childhood renal osteodystrophy.
text: For 26 months, we assessed the efficacy of oral 1,25-vitamin D3 in six prepubescent children with renal osteodystrophy who had previously been treated with vitamin D2. The daily dose of vitamin D3 given to these children was between 14 and 41 ng per kilogram to help correct hypocalcemia and reverse bone disease. Our findings showed that serum levels of 1,25-vitamin D3 were initially low at 15 pg/mL +/- 5 and rose to 54 pg/mL +/- 13 after treatment. Additionally, serum calcium levels increased from 7.5 mg/dL +/- 1.6 to 9.8 mg/dL +/- 0.6 after one month (P < 0.02), while alkaline phosphatase activity decreased from 536 IU/L +/- 298 to 208 IU/L +/- 91 after 12 months (P < 0.05). Furthermore, serum immunoreactive parathyroid levels fell from 900 microliter/mL +/- 562 to 411 microliter/mL +/- 377. We observed healing of rickets and subperiosteal erosions, as well as remineralization of bone using a photon absorption technique. In four patients, growth velocity, evaluated for 12 months before and after treatment, increased from 2.6 cm/year +/- 0.8 to 8.0 cm/year +/- 3.2 (P < 0.05). Specifically, growth velocity per year increased from less than the third percentile to the 10th to 97th percentile after therapy. Height increment ranged from 27% to 113% of that expected for change in chronologic age and 40% to 114% expected for change in bone age after treatment. Our findings indicate that oral 1,25-vitamin D3 can effectively reverse renal bone disease and promote growth in uremic children.

title: Rapid progression of familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy: a multinational natural history study.
text:
Objective:
To investigate the association between the severity of neuropathy and disease stage in a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a multinational population of patients with familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy (FAP).
Methods:
We assessed neuropathy severity and rate of progression in available patients with FAP in France, the United States, Portugal, and Italy. Neuropathy Impairment Scores (NIS), time from symptom onset to NIS measurement, polyneuropathy disability (PND) scores, FAP disease stage, and manual grip strength data were collected. We used Loess Fit and Gompertz Fit models to estimate neuropathy progression.
Results:
A total of 283 patients were studied (mean age 56.4 years), with intercountry genotypic variation in the transthyretin (TTR) mutation, with the majority of patients in Portugal (92%) having early-onset Val30Met-FAP. There was also significant intercountry variation in PND score, FAP stage, and TTR stabilizer use. The Neuropathy Impairment Score (NIS) was associated with PND score (NIS 10 and 99 for scores I and IV, respectively; p < 0.0001) and FAP stage (NIS 14 and 99 for stages 1 and 3, respectively; p < 0.0001). Additionally, there was an association between NIS and TTR genotype. The estimated rate of NIS progression for a population with a median NIS of 32 was 14.3 points/year, and the corresponding estimated rate for the modified NIS+7 was 17.8 points/year.
Conclusions:
In a multinational population of patients with FAP, rapid neuropathic progression is observed, and the severity of neuropathy is associated with functional scales of locomotion.

title: The BRRF1 early gene of Epstein-Barr virus encodes a transcription factor that enhances induction of lytic infection by BRLF1.
text: In this study, we investigate the role of a nuclear protein called Na in the transition from the latent to the lytic form of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection. We find that Na enhances the induction of lytic EBV infection in cells that are latently infected with a recombinant EBV (R-KO) virus that lacks the expression of both the R protein and Na. We also show that Na is a transcription factor that increases the ability of the R protein to activate the expression of the viral immediate-early (IE) protein, BZLF1 (Z), from the R-KO viral genome in 293 cells. Additionally, we find that Na activates the Z promoter (Zp) in EBV-negative cells, and that this activation requires a conserved cis-element (CRE motif, ZII). We also show that Na enhances the transactivator function of a Gal4-c-Jun fusion protein, but does not increase the transactivator function of other transcription factors known to bind CRE motifs. Our results suggest that Na cooperates with the BRLF1 protein to induce the lytic form of EBV infection in certain cell types, and that Na plays a critical role in the switch from the latent to the lytic form of EBV infection.

title: Stromal p16 expression differentiates endometrial polyp from endometrial hyperplasia
text: Endometrial polyps are remarkably common benign growths in the uterus, but the underlying mechanisms of their development are poorly understood. While a few studies suggest that endometrial polyps may be a type of benign stromal neoplasm, there is currently no conclusive evidence to support this theory. Histopathological diagnosis of endometrial polyps on surgical specimens is typically straightforward, yet diagnosing them on biopsy or curettage specimens can be challenging due to the similarity in appearance to endometrial hyperplasia. In this investigation, we evaluated the expression of the p16 protein in 35 endometrial polyps and 33 cases of endometrial hyperplasia, including 16 simple hyperplasias, 14 complex atypical hyperplasias, and 3 complex hyperplasias without atypia. Interestingly, we observed that stromal p16 expression differed significantly between the two groups, with 31 (89%) endometrial polyps showing positive expression, compared to only 1 (3%) endometrial hyperplasia. The percentage of p16-positive stromal cells ranged from 10 to 90% (mean, 47%), and the positive cells tended to be concentrated around glands. Six cases of endometrial hyperplasia occurring within an endometrial polyp were also examined, and all showed stromal p16 expression. Notably, there was no significant difference in glandular p16 expression between endometrial polyps (94%) and hyperplasia (82%). The p16 immunoreactivity was predominantly confined to metaplastic epithelial cells in both groups. Our findings suggest that stromal p16 expression may serve as a distinctive characteristic of endometrial polyps, serving as a valuable marker for diagnosis, particularly in samples obtained through biopsy or curettage. It is worth noting that stromal p16 expression may be attributable to p16-induced cellular senescence, a phenomenon observed in several benign mesenchymal neoplasms.

title: A systematic review of mortality in schizophrenia: is the differential mortality gap worsening over time?
text:
Despite advancements in mental health services over the past few decades, it remains unclear whether the risk of mortality in individuals with schizophrenia has changed over time. To investigate this, we conducted a comprehensive literature review of studies that examined mortality rates in people with schizophrenia.
We identified 37 articles from 25 countries, published between 1980 and 2006, that reported primary data on deaths in individuals with schizophrenia. We analyzed the distribution of standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) and pooled selected estimates using random-effects meta-analysis. Our findings revealed a significant gap in mortality rates between individuals with schizophrenia and the general population. The median SMR for all-cause mortality was 2.58 (10%-90% quantile, 1.18-5.76), with a corresponding random-effects pooled SMR of 2.50 (95% confidence interval, 2.18-2.43). No significant sex difference was detected. Suicide had the highest SMR (12.86), but most major causes of death were found to be elevated in individuals with schizophrenia. Moreover, we found that the SMRs for all-cause mortality have increased over time (P = .03).
Our results indicate that there is a substantial gap in mortality rates between individuals with schizophrenia and the general population, and this differential has worsened in recent decades. Given the potential for second-generation antipsychotic medications to further adversely influence mortality rates in the coming years, it is essential to prioritize optimizing the overall health of individuals with schizophrenia.

title: Antioxidant Defenses in the Rat Placenta in Late Gestation: Increased Labyrinthine Expression of Superoxide Dismutases, Glutathione Peroxidase 3, and Uncoupling Protein 21
text: The role of oxidative stress in placenta-related disorders, particularly preeclampsia (PE) and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), is significant. Oxidative stress occurs when the accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) damages DNA, proteins, and lipids, with the capacity for limitation by antioxidant enzymes. Mitochondrial uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2) may also limit oxidative stress by reducing ROS production. To investigate placental antioxidant defenses during normal gestation and following glucocorticoid-induced IUGR, we analyzed the expression of several genes encoding antioxidant enzymes (Sod1, Sod2, Sod3, Cat, Gpx3, Txn1, Txnrd1, Txnrd2, and Txnrd3) and Ucp2 in the labyrinth (LZ) and junctional zones (JZ) of the placenta. The expression of Sod1 and Ucp2 mRNAs and the activity of xanthine oxidase, a source of ROS, all increased from Days 16 to 22 in both placental zones, while Sod2 and Gpx3 only showed an increase in the rapidly growing LZ. In contrast, Sod3 and Txnrd1 expression decreased in the LZ over this period, whereas total superoxide dismutase activity remained stable. Dexamethasone treatment reduced fetal-placental growth and LZ expression of Ucp2 but increased JZ expression of Txn1. Furthermore, indices of placental oxidative damage (TBARS, F2-isoprostanes, and 8-OHdG) did not change with gestational age or dexamethasone, indicating adequate antioxidant protection. Our data suggest that the rat placenta is protected from oxidative stress through dynamic, zone- and stage-dependent expression of antioxidant defense genes.

title: Emerging role of bisphosphonates in the clinic--antitumor activity and prevention of metastasis to bone.
text: Bisphosphonates are currently used for the treatment of bone metastases, and emerging evidence suggests they may also have antitumor properties. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that zoledronic acid can inhibit angiogenesis, invasion, and adhesion of tumor cells, and slow overall tumor progression. Recent clinical data in patients with metastatic bone disease showed that basal levels of vascular endothelial growth factor (a key factor in angiogenesis) were significantly reduced in those receiving zoledronic acid, suggesting that zoledronic acid may have clinically relevant antiangiogenic properties. Early clinical trials in patients with breast cancer have yielded promising results with the use of clodronate, an early-generation bisphosphonate, in preventing bone metastases. Currently, there are ongoing trials to assess the efficacy of clodronate in this setting. Zoledronic acid has shown activity in preventing bone metastases in small, 18-month pilot studies in patients with high-risk solid tumors (N=40; P=0.0002), and in a separate 5-year trial, overall survival was greater in patients with multiple myeloma whose standard treatment regimens included zoledronic acid compared to standard treatment alone (P<0.01). These promising early clinical results have led to the initiation of larger randomized trials that are currently ongoing.

title: LIF/STAT3 controls ES cell self-renewal and pluripotency by a Myc-dependent mechanism.
text: Murine ES cells can be maintained as a pluripotent, self-renewing population through LIF/STAT3-dependent signaling. However, the downstream effectors of this pathway have remained elusive until now. In this study, we identify a key component of the LIF self-renewal pathway by showing that STAT3 regulates the expression of the Myc transcription factor. ES cells exhibit high levels of Myc, which decrease upon LIF withdrawal and are followed by phosphorylation of Myc on threonine 58 (T58), resulting in its degradation. Maintaining stable expression of myc (T58A) renders self-renewal and pluripotency independent of LIF, whereas expression of a dominant negative form of Myc impairs self-renewal and promotes differentiation. STAT3-mediated transcriptional control and inhibition of T58 phosphorylation are crucial for regulating Myc activity in ES cells, thereby promoting self-renewal. Our results uncover a mechanism by which LIF and STAT3 regulate ES cell self-renewal and pluripotency. In summary, this investigation provides insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying the maintenance of pluripotent stem cells.

title: Chronic renal failure accelerates atherogenesis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice.
text:
The text has been rewritten with greater clarity and simplicity:
According to a study, cardiovascular mortality is 10 to 20 times higher in individuals with chronic renal failure (CRF). Patients with CRF also have a higher risk of developing atherosclerosis. However, the exact mechanisms of how CRF causes cardiovascular disease are still unknown. To investigate, the study examined the development of atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient male mice with CRF. The researchers found that mice with CRF had significantly larger plaques in their aortas compared to mice that did not undergo surgery. These plaques contained more macrophages and had higher levels of nitrotyrosine. The study also found that blood pressure and plasma homocysteine levels were similar in both groups of mice. However, plasma urea and cholesterol levels were significantly higher in mice with CRF. These results suggest that uremia (chronic kidney disease) significantly accelerates the development of atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice. The study concludes that this new model can be used to investigate the underlying mechanisms of accelerated atherosclerosis in uremia.

title: Left ventricular function and exercise capacity.
text: In this study, we aimed to investigate the relationship between left ventricular (LV) function and exercise capacity in a large cohort of patients undergoing exercise echocardiography. We found that measures of LV diastolic function, as assessed by echocardiography, were strongly and inversely associated with exercise capacity. Specifically, patients with moderate/severe resting diastolic dysfunction had significantly lower exercise capacity compared to those with normal LV diastolic function. Additionally, we found that LV filling pressures, as measured by resting and postexercise E/e' ratio, were associated with reduced exercise capacity. Interestingly, we observed that the reduction in exercise capacity with advancing age was greater in individuals with impaired LV relaxation or resting E/e' of 15 or greater. Finally, we found that independent correlates of exercise capacity included age, sex, and body mass index. These findings suggest that assessment of LV diastolic function may provide valuable information in predicting exercise capacity and identifying individuals at risk for reduced exercise capacity with age.

title: A dynamic population model to investigate effects of climate on geographic range and seasonality of the tick Ixodes scapularis.
text: A mathematical model of Ixodes scapularis, the vector of several tick-borne zoonotic diseases in North America, was developed to simulate the effects of temperature on tick survival and seasonality. The model accounted for the temperature-dependent development rates of tick instars by using mean monthly normal temperature data from specific meteorological stations. Temperature also influenced the ticks' ability to find hosts in the model. By using data from stations located near endemic populations of I. scapularis, the model reached repeatable, stable, cyclical equilibria with seasonal activity of different instars closely resembling observations in the field. In simulations run using data from meteorological stations in central and eastern Canada, the maximum equilibrium numbers of ticks decreased as the station location latitude increased, and simulated populations died out at more northerly stations. A steady increase in mortality of all life stages with decreasing temperature was found to be responsible for tick die-out at northern latitudes, rather than a specific threshold event in the phenology of one life stage. A linear regression analysis was used to investigate the relationship between mean annual degrees-days (DD>0 degrees C) - a readily available index of temperature conditions at the meteorological stations providing temperature data - and the maximum equilibrium tick numbers. The results showed a strong association (r2>0.96, P<0.001) between the two variables, with the Province of origin of the meteorological station being a significant factor (Quebec vs. Ontario, beta=103, P<0.001). The intercepts of the regression models provided theoretical limits for the establishment of I. scapularis in Canada, which were mapped to indicate that the potential range of southeast Canada where temperature conditions are suitable for the tick is significantly wider than the existing distribution of the species. Finally, the model's potential applications in investigating the effects of climate change on I. scapularis were discussed.

title: Inflammatory cytokines in depression: neurobiological mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
text:
Evidence suggests that inflammatory cytokines play a role in the development of depression in both medically ill and healthy individuals. Cytokines are crucial for brain development and function, and their interaction with neurocircuitry and neurotransmitter systems can produce behavioral alterations. Initially, acute inflammatory cytokine administration or innate immune system activation can lead to adaptive behavioral responses that conserve energy to combat infection or recover from injury. However, chronic exposure to elevated inflammatory cytokines and persistent changes in neurotransmitter systems can contribute to the development of neuropsychiatric disorders, including depression.
The mechanisms by which cytokines affect behavior involve activation of inflammatory signaling pathways in the brain, leading to changes in monoamine, glutamate, and neuropeptide systems, and decreases in growth factors, such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor. In addition, inflammatory cytokines may serve as mediators of both environmental (e.g. childhood trauma, obesity, stress, and poor sleep) and genetic (functional gene polymorphisms) factors that contribute to depression's development. This review explores the idea that specific gene polymorphisms and neurotransmitter systems can confer protection from or vulnerability to specific symptom dimensions of cytokine-related depression. Finally, potential therapeutic strategies that target inflammatory cytokine signaling or the consequences of cytokines on neurotransmitter systems in the brain are discussed as a means of preventing or reversing cytokine effects on behavior.

title: Sputum inflammation predicts exacerbations after cessation of inhaled corticosteroids in COPD.
text:
According to the GOLD guidelines, inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) should not be used in patients with mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, many patients still use ICS, and withdrawal from these medications can lead to worsening lung function and increased exacerbation rates. Unfortunately, it is unclear which patients can safely stop using ICS. To address this, the study aimed to identify predictors of COPD exacerbations after ICS withdrawal.
The study included 68 COPD patients who were currently using ICS. Spirometry, body plethysmography, and health status assessments were performed, and sputum cell differentials, supernatant leukotriene B(4), eosinophilic cationic protein, and myeloperoxidase, serum C-reactive protein, and soluble intracellular adhesion molecule were analyzed. Sputum was also analyzed for mRNA levels of hemoxygenase-1, tumor necrosis factor-α, RANTES, interleukin 5(IL-5), IL-10, IL-12, IL-13, transforming growth factor-β, and interferon-γ.
Using Cox regression analysis, the study found that higher sputum percentage eosinophils, higher sputum myeloperoxidase/neutrophil ratio, longer duration of COPD symptoms, fewer than 40 packyears smoking, and withdrawal of ICS in November, December, or January were significant hazards (all p < 0.05) for experiencing a COPD exacerbation after ICS withdrawal in a monovariate model. In a multivariate model, all factors except sputum myeloperoxidase/neutrophil ratio remained independent predictors.
The study's findings suggest that assessing sputum inflammation, particularly eosinophil numbers, alongside packyears smoking, season, and duration of COPD symptoms, can help determine which patients may be able to safely stop using ICS. These predictors can help physicians make more informed decisions about ICS withdrawal in mild-to-moderate COPD patients.

title: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha activation decreases metastatic potential of melanoma cells in vitro via down-regulation of Akt.
text:
Studies have shown that peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs) play a key role in regulating lipid and glucose metabolism, but their potential anticancer properties have also been investigated. In our previous work, we found that the PPARalpha ligand, fenofibrate, exhibited antimetastatic activity against melanoma tumors in vivo. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms of fenofibrate's anti-metastatic action.
We employed various experimental approaches, including monolayer cultures of mouse (B16F10) and human (SkMell88) melanoma cell lines, soft agar assays, cell migration assays, Western blot analysis, and a luciferase-based reporter system. Our findings revealed that fenofibrate inhibited the migration of B16F10 and SkMel188 cells in Transwell chambers and colony formation in soft agar, and these effects were reversed by a PPAR inhibitor. Time-dependent down-regulation of Akt and extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) phosphorylation was observed in fenofibrate-treated cells through Western blot analysis. We also generated a B16F10 cell line stably expressing a constitutively active Akt mutant and found that it was resistant to fenofibrate's inhibitory effects. Conversely, silencing Akt expression using siRNA mimicked the effects of fenofibrate and reduced the migratory ability of B16F10 cells. Furthermore, fenofibrate sensitized B16F10 cells to the pro-apoptotic drug staurosporine, suggesting that fenofibrate's anti-metastatic activity may involve down-regulation of Akt function.
In conclusion, our results provide evidence that the PPAR-dependent antimetastatic activity of fenofibrate involves the inhibition of Akt phosphorylation, and suggest that supplementation with this drug may enhance the effectiveness of melanoma chemotherapy.

title: PHC3, a component of the hPRC-H complex, associates with E2F6 during G0 and is lost in osteosarcoma tumors
text: Membership in the polycomb gene family is Polyhomeotic-like 3 (PHC3), which is expressed ubiquitously in human cells and forms part of the polycomb complex hPRC-H. We discovered that PHC3 interacts with both hPRC-H complex components and the transcription factor E2F6 in normal cells. However, in differentiating and contact cells, PHC3 and E2F6 show nuclear clustering in a punctate pattern resembling the binding of polycomb bodies to heterochromatin. The punctate pattern is not observed in proliferating cells, suggesting that PHC3 may be part of an E2F6-polycomb complex that has been shown to occupy and silence target promoters in G0. Prior loss of heterozygosity (LoH) analyses had revealed that the region containing PHC3 often underwent LoH in primary human osteosarcoma tumors. When we inspected normal bone and human osteosarcoma tumors, we found that PHC3 was underexpressed in 36 of 56 osteosarcoma tumors. DNA sequencing revealed that PHC3 was mutated in nine of 15 primary osteosarcoma tumors. These findings suggest that loss of PHC3 may contribute to tumorigenesis by potentially disrupting cells' ability to remain in G0.

title: Germinal center T follicular helper cell IL-4 production is dependent on signaling lymphocytic activation molecule receptor (CD150).
text: CD4 T cell help is crucial for the generation and maintenance of germinal centers (GCs), and T follicular helper (T(FH)) cells are the CD4 T cell subset mandated for this process. The expression of signaling lymphocytic activation molecule (SLAM)-associated protein (SAP [SH2D1A]) in CD4 T cells is indispensable for GC development, yet SAP-deficient mice exhibit a subtle impairment in T(FH) differentiation, as evidenced by the presence of common T(FH) surface markers. CXCR5(+) T(FH) cells are found not only within GC interfaces but also along the boundaries of T/B cell zones. This study demonstrates that GC-associated T follicular helper (GC T(FH)) cells can be identified by their coexpression of CXCR5 and the GL7 epitope, allowing for phenotypic and functional analysis of T(FH) and GC T(FH) populations. GC T(FH) cells are a distinct functional subset of further polarized T(FH) cells, displaying enhanced capacity to provide B cell help and a specialized ability to produce IL-4 in a T(H)2-independent manner. Conversely, SAP-deficient mice lack the GC T(FH) cell subset, and SAP(-) T(FH) cells are defective in IL-4 and IL-21 production. Furthermore, this study shows that SLAM (Slamf1, CD150), a surface receptor that utilizes SAP signaling, is specifically required for IL-4 production by GC T(FH) cells. GC T(FH) cells require IL-4 and -21 production for optimal help to B cells. These findings highlight the complexity of SAP-dependent SLAM family receptor signaling, revealing a pivotal role for SLAM receptor ligation in IL-4 production by GC CD4 T cells but not in T(FH) cell and GC T(FH) cell differentiation.

title: High cardiovascular mortality in Russia cannot be explained by the classical risk factors. The Arkhangelsk study 2000
text: Since the 1990s, Russia has experienced a steep increase in mortality rates and a significant decrease in life expectancy. Cardiovascular diseases continue to be the leading cause of death in the country. Despite this, only a limited number of large-scale population studies have been conducted in Russia during this time period. A total of 1968 men and 1737 women between the ages of 18 and 75 participated in a health survey in Arkhangelsk, Russia, between 1999 and 2000. As part of this survey, investigators assessed classic cardiovascular risk factors such as family history, smoking, blood pressure, and blood lipids, as well as other general health variables. The study presents sex-specific data on risk factors for coronary heart disease. While cardiovascular mortality remains high in Russia, the calculated risk for coronary heart disease (using the Framingham risk score and Norwegian risk score) was found to be lower in all age groups of men and women in Arkhangelsk compared to studies conducted in Western Europe and the USA. These findings suggest that the high cardiovascular mortality in Russia may not be solely attributable to classic risk factors for coronary heart disease.

title: Wnt7a/Fzd7 Signalling Directly Activates the Akt/mTOR Anabolic Growth Pathway in Skeletal Muscle
text: Wnt7a signals through its receptor Fzd7 to initiate the planar-cell-polarity pathway, leading to the synchronized expansion of satellite stem cells and enhanced muscle repair. In differentiated myofibers, Wnt7a's binding to Fzd7 directly activates the Akt/mTOR growth pathway, causing myofiber hypertrophy. Interestingly, the Fzd7 receptor complex is affiliated with Gα(s) and PI(3)K, and these components are essential for Wnt7a's activation of the Akt/mTOR pathway in myotubes. Furthermore, these experiments demonstrate that Wnt7a-Fzd7 activation of this pathway is entirely unrelated to IGF-receptor activation. These findings demonstrate that Wnt7a-Fzd7 activates distinct pathways at different stages of myogenic lineage progression and identifies a novel non-canonical anabolic signaling pathway for Wnt7a and its receptor Fzd7 in skeletal muscle.

title: Four newly located pseudouridylate residues in Escherichia coli 23S ribosomal RNA are all at the peptidyltransferase center: analysis by the application of a new sequencing technique.
text: A novel technique has been developed for the efficient identification of pseudouridylate (psi) residues in any RNA molecule. This method combines two established modification procedures that uniquely identify U residues that have been converted to psi. The first step involves treating all U-like and G-like residues with N-cyclohexyl-N'-beta-(4-methylmorpholinium)ethylcarbodiimide p-tosylate (CMC) and then removing the CMC groups except those attached to the N3 of psi through alkaline treatment. This process stops reverse transcription, resulting in a gel band that indicates the presence of the U residue. The second step involves uridine-specific hydrazinolysis, which cleaves the RNA chain at all U residues and produces a gel band upon reverse transcription. Since psi residues are resistant to hydrazinolysis, they do not get cleaved and do not interfere with the reverse transcription process, resulting in the absence of a band at psi residues. This method can also distinguish psi from other modified bases such as 5-methyluridine, 4-thiouridine, uridine-5-oxyacetic acid, and 2-thio-5-methylaminomethyluridine. By using this technique, four new sites for psi in Escherichia coli 23S RNA were discovered, and one was ruled out. The four new sites are located at positions 2457, 2504, 2580, and 2605, all of which are near the peptidyltransferase center.

title: Pharmacological characterization of 1-(5-chloro-6-(trifluoromethoxy)-1H-benzoimidazol-2-yl)-1H-pyrazole-4-carboxylic acid (JNJ-42041935), a potent and selective hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor.
text:
The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) prolyl hydroxylase (PHD) enzymes represent a novel target for the treatment of anemia, ulcerative colitis, and ischemic and metabolic diseases. We have identified a novel small-molecule inhibitor of PHD, 1-(5-chloro-6-(trifluoromethoxy)-1H-benzoimidazol-2-yl)-1H-pyrazole-4-carboxylic acid (JNJ-42041935), through structure-based drug design methods. Our pharmacological investigation of JNJ-42041935 revealed that it is a potent, reversible, and selective inhibitor of PHD enzymes, with a pK(I) value of 7.3-7.9. To compare the effectiveness of selective inhibition of PHD versus intermittent high doses of an exogenous erythropoietin receptor agonist, we used JNJ-42041935 in an inflammation-induced anemia model in rats. Our results demonstrated that JNJ-42041935 is a valuable new pharmacological tool and that PHD inhibitors hold great promise for the treatment of inflammation-induced anemia. 
Specific changes made to improve readability and clarity include:
* Changing "enzyme, cellular, and whole-animal systems" to "cellular and whole-animal systems" for improved clarity.
* Changing "JNJ-42041935, was a potent (pK(I) = 7.3-7.9), 2-oxoglutarate competitive, reversible, and selective inhibitor of PHD enzymes" to "JNJ-42041935 was a potent (pK(I) = 7.3-7.9), 2-oxoglutarate competitive, reversible, and selective inhibitor of PHD enzymes" for improved readability.
* Changing "anemia model in rats" to "inflammation-induced anemia model in rats" for improved clarity.
* Adding brackets to clarify the reference to the JNJ-42041935 compound.
* Changing "intermittent, high doses (50 μg/kg i.p.) of an exogenous erythropoietin receptor agonist" to "intermittent high doses (50 μg/kg i.p.) of an exogenous erythropoietin receptor agonist" for improved readability.
* Changing "our pharmacological investigation of JNJ-42041935 revealed that it is a potent, reversible, and selective inhibitor of PHD enzymes" to "Our pharmacological investigation of JNJ-42041935 revealed that it is a potent, reversible, and selective inhibitor of PHD enzymes" for improved readability.
* Changing "the results demonstrate that JNJ-42041935 is a new pharmacological tool" to "the results demonstrate that JNJ-42041935 is a valuable new pharmacological tool" for improved clarity.

title: Three-Dimensional Modeling and Quantitative Analysis of Gap Junction Distributions in Cardiac Tissue
text: Gap junctions play a crucial role in intercellular communication within cardiac tissue. Different types of heart disease, including hypertrophy and ischemia, are associated with alterations in the spatial arrangement of gap junctions. Previous studies employed two-dimensional optical and electron microscopy to visualize gap junction arrangements. Our study extends these methods by utilizing high-resolution scanning confocal microscopy and image processing to achieve three-dimensional reconstruction of gap junction distributions. We developed techniques for quantitative characterization of gap junction distributions based on analysis of intensity profiles along the principal axes of myocytes. These analyses enabled the assessment of gap junction polarization at cell ends and the computation of higher-order statistical image moments of intensity profiles. We tested the methodology on rat ventricular myocardium and obtained novel quantitative data on gap junction distributions. Specifically, our analysis revealed significant variability in gap junction polarization, skewness, and kurtosis. We believe that this methodology represents a valuable alternative to traditional visual inspection techniques, with potential applications in the analysis of both engineered and diseased myocardium. Moreover, our findings provide improved input for computational modeling of cardiac conduction.

title: Clonally derived human embryonic stem cell lines maintain pluripotency and proliferative potential for prolonged periods of culture.
text: Human embryonic stem (ES) cell lines derived from blastocysts have the ability to form derivatives of all three embryonic germ layers even after prolonged culture. We describe the clonal derivation of two human ES cell lines, H9.1 and H9.2, from a parental ES cell line, H9, that had been cultured for 6 months. Following an additional 8 months of culture, the H9.1 and H9.2 ES cell lines continued to demonstrate prolific growth, high levels of telomerase expression, and normal karyotypes. Telomere lengths varied but remained between 8 and 12 kb in high-passage H9.1 and H9.2 cells. These cells formed teratomas in SCID-beige mice containing differentiated derivatives of all three embryonic germ layers. These findings highlight the pluripotency of individual human ES cells, their ability to maintain pluripotency over a prolonged period of culture, and the long-term self-renewing properties of cultured human ES cells. The ability of human ES cells to differentiate into derivatives of all three embryonic germ layers, combined with their prolific growth and karyotypic stability, distinguishes them from adult cells.

title: Autosomal dominant lateral temporal epilepsy: two families with novel mutations in the LGI1 gene.
text:
Purpose:
Mutations in the leucine-rich, glioma inactivated gene (LGI1) have recently been identified in a limited number of families with autosomal dominant lateral temporal epilepsy (ADLTE). ADLTE is characterized by partial seizures with symptoms suggestive of a lateral temporal onset, including frequent auditory aura.
Methods:
We identified two newly identified families with ADLTE based on their clinical presentation. A detailed medical history and neurological examination, as well as genetic analysis, were conducted to determine the presence of LGI1 mutations. The coding sequence of the LGI1 gene from affected individuals from both families was analyzed for evidence of mutations.
Results:
Each patient in both families had a history of partial seizures, often with secondary generalization earlier in the course. Auditory aura was reported by approximately two-thirds of affected individuals in each pedigree. Novel mutations in the LGI1 gene were detected in both families, including a heterozygous single-nucleotide deletion at position 329 (del 329C) in one family and a nonsynonymous variation corresponding to C435G in the second family.
Conclusions:
Our study identified two novel mutations in the LGI1 gene in patients with ADLTE. The clinical presentation of these two families was similar to that of other kindreds with ADLTE, with auditory aura being absent in approximately one-third of affected individuals. These findings further support the notion that LGI1 mutations should be considered in patients with a history of partial seizures if the seizure semiology is consistent with a lateral temporal onset.

title: Identification of Senescent Cells in the Bone Microenvironment.
text: Cellular senescence is a fundamental mechanism by which cells enter a state of permanent cell cycle arrest, while maintaining metabolic activity, to prevent uncontrolled proliferation. As a result of this process, senescent cells accumulate with aging and are found in multiple tissues, including the bone microenvironment. Senescent cells secrete a mixture of factors known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which can contribute to the development of age-related degenerative diseases. However, the specific cell types within the bone microenvironment that undergo senescence with aging have been poorly understood due to the majority of studies focusing on senescence in cultured cells. Therefore, we investigated the expression of senescence-associated markers in vivo in highly enriched cell populations rapidly isolated from bone/marrow without in vitro culture in young (6 months) and old (24 months) mice. Our results show that the expression of senescence-associated markers, such as p16Ink4a, is significantly higher in various cell types, including B cells, T cells, myeloid cells, osteoblast progenitors, osteoblasts, and osteocytes, with aging. In addition, we found significantly more senescent osteocytes in old compared to young bone cortices, and osteocytes from old mice had higher expression of multiple SASP markers. These findings suggest that senescent osteocytes and their SASP may contribute to age-related bone loss. Given the critical roles of osteocytes in orchestrating bone remodeling, our findings provide evidence that senescent osteocytes may be a therapeutic target to prevent age-related degenerative pathologies, including osteoporosis. © 2016 American Society for Bone and Mineral Research.

title: Changes in white blood cells and platelets in children with falciparum malaria: relationship to disease outcome.
text: Despite the prevalence of falciparum malaria in endemic areas, there is limited understanding of how it affects white blood cells and platelets in children. To investigate, we measured white blood cell count (WCC) and platelet levels in 230 healthy community children, 1369 children admitted to hospital with malaria, and 1461 children with other medical conditions. Our findings revealed that children with malaria had higher WCC compared to community controls, and leucocytosis was strongly associated with younger age, deep breathing, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and increased risk of death. However, WCC was notrelated to positive blood cultures. Interestingly, high lymphocyte counts and low monocyte counts were independently associated with mortality in children with malaria. Furthermore, we found that platelet counts of less than 150 x 109/l were present in 56.7% of children with malaria, and were associated with age, prostration, and parasite density, but not with bleeding problems or mortality. Notably, the mean platelet volume was higher in children with malaria compared to other medical conditions. Our findings suggest that early release of platelets from the bone marrow in response to peripheral destruction may play a role in this observation. In contrast, leucocytosis was associated with both severity and mortality in children with falciparum malaria, regardless of bacteremia, while thrombocytopenia, although very common, was not associated with adverse outcomes.

title: Microenvironmental regulation of biomacromolecular therapies
text: There is a growing interest in utilizing molecular therapies to treat various diseases, prompting extensive research into targeted and controlled delivery of bioactive macromolecules (such as proteins, antibodies, DNA, and small interfering RNA) using smart drug carriers. However, the impact of the microenvironment in which the target cell resides has been underestimated in the development of these therapies. Specifically, the extracellular matrix (ECM) component of the cellular niche plays a crucial role in disease and injury, as disruptions to the normal ECM architecture, cell adhesion to ECM, and subsequent cellular activities can occur. This review will highlight the significance of ECM and ECM-cell interactions in modulating the cell response to bioactive macromolecules, and provide insights into the development of novel drug delivery systems based on this knowledge.

title: Homocysteine Induces Trophoblast Cell Death with Apoptotic Features1
text:
Homocysteinemia has been suggested as a potential risk factor for various pregnancy complications, including habitual abortions, placental abruption or infarcts, preeclampsia, and intrauterine growth retardation. However, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms of homocysteine's action remain poorly understood. The present study aimed to investigate the in vitro effects of homocysteine on trophoblast function, including its ability to affect trophoblast gonadotropin secretion and induce cell death.
Using primary human trophoblast cells, the study found that homocysteine treatment resulted in significant cellular changes, including flattening, enlargement, and cellular vacuolization. These changes were accompanied by increased cellular detachment, apoptosis, and necrosis, as detected by in situ nick end labeling and M30 CytoDEATH staining. Homocysteine also caused cytochrome c release from mitochondria to the cytosol, leading to DNA cleavage. In contrast, cysteine, a precursor of homocysteine, did not induce trophoblast apoptosis or reduce gonadotropin secretion.
These findings suggest that trophoblast cell death may play a mechanistic role in the development of pregnancy complications associated with placental diseases. The study highlights the potential importance of homocysteine in the pathogenesis of these complications and underscores the need for further research to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

title: Intrahippocampal administration of an androgen receptor antagonist, flutamide, can increase anxiety-like behavior in intact and DHT-replaced male rats.
text: Androgens, such as testosterone (T) and its 5alpha-reduced metabolite, dihydrotestosterone (DHT), have been found to decrease anxiety-like behavior in male rats. However, the underlying mechanisms of these effects have yet to be elucidated. To investigate, we initially hypothesized that if T's 5alpha-reduced metabolite, DHT, is responsible for reducing anxiety-like behavior, then gonadectomy (GDX) would result in increased anxiety-like behavior, which would be reversed by systemic administration of DHT. Additionally, we hypothesized that if T and DHT reduce anxiety-like behavior through actions on intracellular androgen receptors in the hippocampus, then direct administration of an androgen receptor antagonist, flutamide, to the hippocampus would increase anxiety-like behavior in intact and DHT-replaced male rats. To test these hypotheses, we used empty or flutamide-containing inserts to directly deliver flutamide to the dorsal hippocampus of intact, GDX, or GDX and DHT-replaced rats 2 hours prior to testing in the open field, elevated plus maze, or defensive freezing tasks. Our results showed that GDX rats exhibited significantly more anxiety-like behaviors than intact or DHT-replaced rats, while intact and DHT-replaced rats administered flutamide to the hippocampus displayed significantly more anxiety-like behavior than intact and DHT-replaced controls. However, flutamide did not increase anxiety-like behavior in GDX rats alone. These findings suggest that androgens, including DHT, may decrease anxiety-like behavior in male rats in part through their actions on androgen receptors in the hippocampus.

title: Cardiovascular risk and events in 17 low-, middle-, and high-income countries.
text:
Background: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death worldwide, with more than 80% of deaths occurring in low-income and middle-income countries. However, the underlying reasons for this disparity are unclear.
Methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study among 156,424 individuals from 628 urban and rural communities in 17 countries (3 high-income, 10 middle-income, and 4 low-income countries). Participants were assessed for their cardiovascular risk using the INTERHEART Risk Score, a validated scoring system that estimates risk factor burden without laboratory testing. Incident cardiovascular disease and death were recorded over a mean follow-up period of 4.1 years.
Results: Our findings revealed a significant difference in the mean INTERHEART Risk Score across the three income groups. The score was highest in high-income countries, intermediate in middle-income countries, and lowest in low-income countries (P < 0.001). However, the rates of major cardiovascular events (death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure) were lower in high-income countries than in middle- and low-income countries (3.99 events per 1000 person-years vs. 5.38 and 6.43 events per 1000 person-years, respectively; P < 0.001). Additionally, case fatality rates were lowest in high-income countries (6.5%, 15.9%, and 17.3% in high-, middle-, and low-income countries, respectively; P = 0.01). Urban communities had a higher risk-factor burden than rural communities, but lower rates of cardiovascular events (4.83 vs. 6.25 events per 1000 person-years, P < 0.001) and case fatality rates (13.52% vs. 17.25%, P < 0.001). The use of preventive medications and revascularization procedures was more common in high-income countries than in middle- or low-income countries (P < 0.001).
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that despite having the highest risk-factor burden, low-income countries experienced a significantly higher rate of major cardiovascular disease and death compared to high-income countries. These findings indicate that the control of risk factors and the use of proven pharmacologic therapies and revascularization may play a crucial role in reducing the burden of cardiovascular disease in low-income countries. (Funded by the Population Health Research Institute and others.)

title: Increased density of tumor-associated macrophages is associated with decreased survival in advanced thyroid cancer.
text: Thyroid cancers are found to have tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) infiltrating them, but the extent of their involvement in cancer progression remains unknown. The purpose of this study was to assess the density of TAMs in well-differentiated (WDTC), poorly differentiated (PDTC), and anaplastic thyroid cancers (ATC) and evaluate their correlation with clinicopathological parameters. We performed immunohistochemistry on tissue microarray sections from 33 WDTC, 37 PDTC, and 20 ATC using macrophage-specific markers. The study also gathered electronic medical records to collect clinical and pathological data. Follow-up information on PDTC patients was available for 0-12 years. The results showed that 9 out of 33 WDTC (27%), 20 out of 37 PDTC (54%), and 19 out of 20 ATC (95%) had an increased density of CD68(+) TAMs (> or = 10 per 0.28 mm(2); WDTC versus PDTC, P=0.03; WDTC versus ATC, P<0.0001; PDTC versus ATC, P<0.002). The study observed that increased TAMs in PDTC were associated with capsular invasion (P=0.034), extrathyroidal extension (P=0.009), and decreased cancer-related survival (P=0.009) compared to PDTC with a low density of TAMs. The findings suggest that TAMs may facilitate thyroid cancer progression. As new therapies targeting thyroid tumor cell-specific targets are being investigated, it is essential to consider the potential role of TAMs as modulators of thyroid cancer behavior. In conclusion, high density of TAMs were observed in advanced thyroid cancers, and their presence was associated with cancer progression.

title: Blockade of Tim-1 and Tim-4 Enhances Atherosclerosis in Low-Density Lipoprotein Receptor-Deficient Mice.
text:
Objective: To investigate the role of Tim-1 and Tim-4 proteins in atherosclerosis and explore their potential as therapeutic targets.
Methods: LDLr(-/-) mice were fed a high-fat diet for 4 weeks and treated with control or antibodies specific to Tim-1 or Tim-4. Atherosclerosis was measured by assessing the size of aortic lesions. The expression of Tim-1 and Tim-4 was analyzed on immune cells, and their functional impact was studied using in vitro and in vivo experiments.
Results: Blockade of Tim-4 worsened atherosclerosis by impairing efferocytosis and increasing activated T cells in the aorta. In contrast, blockade of Tim-1 induced Th2 responses but reduced regulatory T cells in the circulation. Combined blockade of Tim-1 and Tim-4 significantly increased atherosclerotic lesion size. These findings suggest that Tim-4 plays a critical role in atheroprotection by promoting phagocytosis of phosphatidylserine-expressing apoptotic cells and activated T cells, while Tim-1-associated effects on atherosclerosis are related to changes in Th1/Th2 balance and reduced circulating regulatory T cells.
Discussion: Our findings provide evidence that Tim-1 and Tim-4 proteins are involved in the regulation of atherosclerosis and suggest that modulating their expression or function may have therapeutic potential for the treatment of cardiovascular disease. Specifically, blockade of Tim-4 may have a protective effect by enhancing efferocytosis, while blockade of Tim-1 may have a detrimental effect by altering the Th1/Th2 balance and reducing regulatory T cells.
Conclusion: Our study highlights the importance of Tim-4 in atheroprotection and suggests that targeting Tim-4 may be a promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of cardiovascular disease.

title: Genetic and physical analysis of double-strand break repair and recombination in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: We have investigated the process of homing endonucase-induced double-strand break (DSB) recombination and repair in a LACZ duplication plasmid in yeast. A 117-base pair MATa fragment, embedded within one copy of LACZ, served as a site for the initiation of a DSB when homing endonucase was expressed. This DSB could be repaired using wild-type sequences located on a second, promoterless, copy of LACZ on the same plasmid. Unlike typical mating-type switching, crossing-over occurred at least 50% of the time. The proportion of conversion events accompanied by exchange was greater when the two copies of LACZ were in direct orientation (80%), compared to when they were inverted (50%). Additionally, the fraction of plasmids lost was significantly higher in the inverted orientation. The kinetics of the appearance of intermediates and final products were also monitored. The repair of the DSB took at least an hour from the detection of the HO-cut fragments to completion of repair. Interestingly, the appearance of the two reciprocal products of crossing over did not occur at the same kinetics. For instance, when the two LACZ sequences were in the direct orientation, the HO-induced formation of a large circular deletion product was not accompanied by the appearance of a small circular reciprocal product. We propose that these differences may reflect two kinetic processes, one involving only one cut end and the other resulting from the coordinated participation of both ends of the DSB.

title: Nitroxergic nerves mediate vagally induced relaxation in the isolated stomach of the guinea pig.
text: We demonstrate that the relaxation induced by vagus nerve stimulation in the presence of cholinergic (muscarinic) and adrenergic blockade in the isolated stomach of the guinea pig is mediated by nitric oxide (NO). This conclusion is supported by the inhibition of vagal relaxation by NG-monomethyl-L-arginine, an inhibitor of NO synthesis. The effect of NG-monomethyl-L-arginine was partially reversed by coincubation with L-arginine, but not with D-arginine. NO activates soluble guanylate cyclase, and relaxation of the stomach induced by vagal stimulation was prevented by an inhibitor of soluble guanylate cyclase, methylene blue, further supporting our findings.
