This result is consistent with histological findings of significant axonal degeneration with no detectable demyelination at 3 days after ischemia. The elevation of lambdaperpendicular observed 5 days after ischemia is consistent with histological findings of myelin degeneration at this time. These results support the hypothesis that lambdaparallel and lambdaperpendicular hold promise as specific markers of axonal and myelin injury, respectively, and, further, that the coexistence of axonal and myelin degeneration does not confound this utility.

title: Direct isolation and identification of promoters in the human genome.
text: Transcriptional regulatory elements, vital for gene expression during animal development and cellular responses to environmental cues, have limited knowledge in the human genome despite the availability of the complete genome sequence. Promoters, the starting point of every transcript, are a crucial regulatory class. A complex protein structure known as the pre-initiation complex (PIC) is assembled on active promoters, distinguishing them from other genome sequences. By isolating promoters via protein-DNA complexes and identifying the resulting DNA sequences using genomic tiling microarrays, we examined promoters directly from human cells in four cell lines. Our investigation found 252 PIC-binding sites within 44 semirandomly chosen human genomic regions, comprising 1% of the human genome. Nearly 72% of the identified fragments overlap or are situated near 5' ends of known cDNA sequences, while the rest is found in other regions that are likely to host as-yet-unannotated promoters. In fact, molecular analysis of RNA from one cell line discovered transcripts initiated from nearly half of the putative promoter fragments, and transient transfection assays demonstrated promoter activity for a substantial portion of the fragments when linked to a luciferase reporter gene. These findings demonstrate the specificity of a genome-wide analysis method for mapping transcriptional regulatory elements, as well as the discovery that a considerable number of human genes remain undiscovered.

title: Attempted suicide in Europe: rates, trends and sociodemographic characteristics of suicide attempters during the period 1989-1992. Results of the WHO/EURO Multicentre Study on Parasuicide.
text: The World Health Organization/EURO Multicentre Project on Parasuicide is part of the WHO's "Health for All by the Year 2000" program for the European region. The project involves 16 centers in 13 European countries in monitoring trends in suicide attempt rates. The study found significant differences in suicide attempt rates among countries, with Finland having the highest rate (314/100,000) and Spain having the lowest (45/100,000), a sevenfold difference. The study also found that females had higher suicide attempt rates than males, and that rates were higher among younger age groups. The study additionally found that more than half of suicide attempters made multiple attempts, and that 20% of these second attempts occurred within 12 months of the first attempt. Suicide attempters were also found to be more likely to belong to social categories associated with poverty and social destabilization compared to the general population.

title: Recurrent outbreaks of Salmonella Enteritidis infections in a Texas restaurant: phage type 4 arrives in the United States.
text: In recent years, infections caused by Salmonella Enteritidis (SE) phage type 4 have emerged in Europe, but have been rare in the United States. The first identified outbreak of this strain in the USA occurred in a Chinese restaurant in El Paso, Texas, in April 1993, with no determined source. In September 1993, a second outbreak associated with the same restaurant occurred. To investigate the cause of the second outbreak, we analyzed the food exposures of the 19 ill patients compared to two control groups. Egg rolls were the only item significantly linked to illness in both analyses (first control group: odds ratio [OR] 8.2, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.3-31.6; second control group: OR 13.1, 95% CI 2.1-97.0). A retrospective analysis of the April outbreak also implicated egg rolls (OR 32.4, 95% CI 9.1-126.6). The egg roll batter was made from pooled shell eggs left at room temperature throughout the day. These two outbreaks of SE phage type 4 could have been prevented by using pasteurized eggs and safe food preparation practices.

title: Strand-specific mismatch correction in nuclear extracts of human and Drosophila melanogaster cell lines.
text: Nuclear extracts derived from both HeLa and Drosophila melanogaster KC cell lines have been found to rectify single base pair mutations within open circular DNA heteroduplexes, with a specific incision located 808 base pairs from the mismatch. The correction process is strand specific and biased towards the incised DNA strand in both extract systems. Different mispairs within a homologous set of heteroduplexes were processed with varying efficiencies (G.T > G.G ≈ A.C > C.C), and correction was accompanied by mismatch-dependent DNA synthesis localized to the region spanning the mispair and the strand break, indicating that recognition of mismatches is an integral part of the repair reaction. Correction of these heteroduplexes was rendered ineffective by aphidicolin, but was relatively insensitive to high concentrations of ddTTP, suggesting the involvement of alpha and/or delta class DNA polymerase(s). These findings imply that higher eukaryotic cells possess a general, strand-specific mismatch repair system analogous to the Escherichia coli mutHLS and the Streptococcus pneumoniae hexAB pathways, which contribute significantly to the genetic stability of these bacterial species.

title: Renal outcomes with telmisartan, ramipril, or both, in people at high vascular risk (the ONTARGET study): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, controlled trial.
text:
Background Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) and angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors have been shown to reduce proteinuria in patients with established atherosclerotic vascular disease or diabetes with end-organ damage. However, there is limited long-term data on the comparative effects of these drugs on renal function. We aimed to investigate the renal effects of ramipril (an ACE inhibitor), telmisartan (an ARB), and their combination in patients aged 55 years or older with these conditions.
Methods We conducted a randomized controlled trial from 2001 to 2007, in which 25,620 patients were randomly assigned to receive ramipril (10 mg/day), telmisartan (80 mg/day), or a combination of both drugs. Renal function and proteinuria were measured at the end of the 56-month follow-up period. The primary renal outcome was a composite of dialysis, doubling of serum creatinine, and death.
Findings A total of 784 patients discontinued randomized therapy during the trial due to hypotensive symptoms, with 406 patients on combination therapy, 149 on ramipril, and 229 on telmisartan. The number of events for the composite primary outcome was similar among telmisartan (1147 events [13.4%]) and ramipril (1150 events [13.5%]; hazard ratio [HR] 1.00, 95% CI 0.92-1.09), but higher with combination therapy (1233 events [14.5%]; HR 1.09, 1.01-1.18, p=0.037). The secondary renal outcome, dialysis or doubling of serum creatinine, was similar among telmisartan (189 events [2.21%]) and ramipril (174 events [2.03%]; HR 1.09, 0.89-1.34) and more frequent with combination therapy (212 events [2.49%]: HR 1.24, 1.01-1.51, p=0.038). Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) declined less with ramipril compared with telmisartan (-2.82 mL/min/1.73 m(2)) or combination therapy (-6.11 mL/min/1.73 m(2)) than with telmisartan (-4.12 mL/min/1.73 m(2)) or combination therapy (-7.74 mL/min/1.73 m(2)); p<0.0001. Additionally, the increase in urinary albumin excretion was less with telmisartan or combination therapy than with ramipril (p=0.004 or p=0.001, respectively).
Interpretation Our findings suggest that in patients at high vascular risk, the effects of telmisartan on major renal outcomes are similar to those of ramipril. However, combination therapy with both drugs resulted in greater proteinuria but worsened major renal outcomes compared with monotherapy with either drug. These findings highlight the importance of carefully selecting and monitoring patients receiving combination therapy for cardiovascular disease.

title: Hypothermic preservation up-regulates calpain expression and increases ubiquitination in cultured vascular endothelial cells: influence of dopamine pretreatment.
text: EXTENDED HYPOTHERMIA DURING SOLID ORGAN TRANSPLANTATION CAN NEGATIVELY IMPACT TRANSPLANTATION OUTCOME. PROTEOLYSIS, OR THE BREAKDOWN OF PROTEINS, IS ONE OF THE ADVERSE EVENTS ASSOCIATED WITH PRESERVATION INJURY AND ORGAN ALLOGRAFT QUALITY DEGRADATION. THIS CAN RESULT IN IMMEDIATE ORGAN DYSFUNCTION FOLLOWING TRANSPLANTATION. TO EXAMINE THE INFLUENCE OF DOPAMINE (DA) PRETREATMENT ON HYPOTHERMIA-INDUCED PROTEOLYSIS IN ENDOTHELIAL CELLS SUBJECTED TO PROLONGED COLD STORAGE, THE CURRENT STUDY WAS CONDUCTED. METHODOLOGY LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE (LDH) ASSAY, TWO-DIMENSIONAL ELECTROPHORESIS, UBIQUITINATION ANALYSIS, INTracellular CALCIUM MEASUREMENT, AND WESTERN BLOT ANALYSIS WERE PERFORMED ON HUMAN UMBILICAL VEIN ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (HUVEC) EXPOSED TO HYPOTHERMIACH OR NOT. RESULTS SHOWED THAT HUVEC WERE SUSCEPTIBLE TO COLD STORAGE, WITH OBSERVED MORPHOLOGICAL CHANGES, LOSS OF VIABILITY, AND SIGNIFICANT CHANGES IN THE CELLULAR PROTEOME. DA PRETREATMENT PREVENTED CELL DEATH DURING COLD STORAGE. WESTERN BLOT ANALYSIS REVEALED A TIME-DEPENDENT UP-REGULATION OF CALPAIN 1 AND 2 DURING COLD STORAGE, WHICH COULD BE PREVENTED BY ADDITION OF EDTA. DA PRETREATMENT ABSOLVED AUTOPROTEOLYSIS OF CALPAIN 1. UBIQUITINATION ANALYSIS REVEALED A SIGNIFICANT INCREASE IN UBIQUITINATED CONJUGATES AFTER COLD STORAGE, WHICH WAS NOT PREVENTED BY DA PRETREATMENT. NEITHER PROTEASOME NOR CALPAIN INHIBITORS PREVENTED CELL DEATH DURING COLD STORAGE. CONCLUSIONINDICATES THAT ACTIVATION OF THE CALPAIN PATHWAY AND THE UBIQUITIN PROTEASOME SYSTEM OCCUR IN ENDOTHELIAL CELLS SUBJECTED TO COLD PRESERVATION. THOUGH DA PRETREATMENT INHIBITS THE FORMER, CALPAIN INHIBITION DID NOT PROTECT ENDOTHELIAL CELLS DURING COLD STORAGE. DA PRETREATMENT MAY ALTER THE PROTEOLYSIS PROCESS, BUT PROTEOLYSIS IS NOT THE PRINCIPAL CAUSE OF ENDOTHELIAL CELL DEATH.

title: The three 'C' s of chromosome conformation capture: controls, controls, controls
text: Transcriptional regulation in higher eukaryotes is directed by regulatory elements such as enhancers, which are recognized by transcription factors. In many instances, these regulatory elements can be located far away from the target genes, up to several megabases distant. Recent studies have shown that long-range control of gene expression can be achieved through direct physical interactions between genes and these regulatory elements. This phenomenon, known as looping, can be detected using the chromosome conformation capture (3C) methodology. Although 3C is relatively straightforward to perform, it is crucial to carefully design and execute 3C experiments to obtain meaningful results. The guidelines provided here can aid in experimental design and help minimize misinterpretation of 3C findings.

title: Effects of exercise training of 8 weeks and detraining on plasma levels of endothelium-derived factors, endothelin-1 and nitric oxide, in healthy young humans.
text:
Exercise training has been shown to manipulate the function of vascular endothelial cells in animals, so we explored whether this applies to humans as well. We hypothesized that exercise training would affect the production of nitric oxide (NO) and endothelin-1 (ET-1) in humans.
To test this hypothesis, we recruited eight healthy young adults (20.3 ± 0.5 years old) and subjected them to 8 weeks of cycling exercise on a leg ergometer at 70% of their maximum oxygen uptake (VO2max) three to four times a week. Before and after the exercise training, we measured the concentrations of NO and ET-1 in their venous plasma.
Our results showed that after the exercise training, the plasma concentration of NO significantly increased (30.69 ± 3.20 vs. 48.64 ± 8.16 micromol/L, p < 0.05), while the plasma concentration of ET-1 significantly decreased (1.65 ± 0.14 vs. 1.23 ± 0.12 pg/mL, p < 0.05). The increase in NO levels and the decrease in ET-1 levels persisted until the fourth week after cessation of exercise training, after which the levels returned to baseline (the levels before the exercise training) in the eighth week.
Furthermore, we found a significant negative correlation between plasma NO concentration and plasma ET-1 concentration.
Our findings suggest that chronic exercise leads to an increase in production of NO and a decrease in production of ET-1 in humans, which may have beneficial implications for the cardiovascular system. Specifically, the increased production of NO may contribute to vasodilation and anti-atherosclerosis effects, while the decreased production of ET-1 may slow down the progression of atherosclerosis.

title: Neuron-specific expression of CuZnSOD prevents the loss of muscle mass and function that occurs in homozygous CuZnSOD-knockout mice.
text: Deletion of copper-zinc superoxide dismutase (CuZnSOD) in Sod1(-/-) mice leads to accelerated loss of muscle mass and force during aging, but the losses do not occur in mice with muscle-specific deletion of CuZnSOD. To investigate the role of motor neurons in the muscle decline, we generated transgenic Sod1(-/-) mice in which CuZnSOD was expressed under the control of the synapsin 1 promoter (SynTgSod1(-/-) mice). This resulted in CuZnSOD expression in brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerve, but not in other tissues. Notably, sciatic nerve CuZnSOD content in SynTgSod1(-/-) mice was approximately 20% lower than in control mice, yet there was no reduction in muscle mass or isometric force observed in SynTgSod1(-/-) mice compared to control animals. In contrast, muscles of age-matched Sod1(-/-) mice displayed 30-40% reductions in mass and force. Additionally, we observed increased oxidative damage and adaptations in stress responses in muscles of Sod1(-/-) mice, which were absent in SynTgSod1(-/-) mice. Furthermore, degeneration of neuromuscular junction (NMJ) structure and function occurred in Sod1(-/-) mice but not in SynTgSod1(-/-) mice. Our findings demonstrate that specific CuZnSOD expression in neurons is sufficient to preserve NMJ and skeletal muscle structure and function in Sod1(-/-) mice, highlighting the key role of redox homeostasis in motor neurons in initiating sarcopenia during aging.

title: A developmental transition in definitive erythropoiesis: erythropoietin expression is sequentially regulated by retinoic acid receptors and HNF4.
text: The cytokine erythropoietin (Epo) plays a crucial role in promoting the proliferation and differentiation of erythropoietic progenitor cells. Our studies have shown that the Epo gene is directly regulated by retinoic acid signaling during early erythropoiesis in the fetal liver, prior to embryonic day E12.5. Mice lacking the retinoic acid receptor gene RXR alpha have a similar morphological and histological phenotype as embryos with mutated Epo genes, and flow cytometric analysis reveals that RXR alpha-deficient embryos are deficient in erythroid differentiation. We found that Epo mRNA levels are significantly reduced in the fetal livers of RXR alpha-deficient embryos at embryonic days E10.25 and E11.25, and genetic analysis showed that the RXR alpha and Epo genes are linked in the same signaling pathway. Our results also indicate that the Epo gene is inducible by retinoic acid in embryos and contains a specific sequence that binds retinoic acid receptors. Interestingly, unlike Epo-deficient embryos that die from anemia, the erythropoietic deficiency in RXR alpha-deficient embryos is transient, and Epo mRNA is expressed at normal levels by E12.5, and erythropoiesis and liver morphology are normal by E14.5. Our study shows that the transcription factor HNF4, a member of the nuclear receptor family, is abundantly expressed in fetal liver hepatocytes and competes with retinoic acid receptors for occupancy of the Epo gene enhancer DR2 element. Based on our findings, we propose that Epo expression is regulated during the E9.5-E11.5 phase of fetal liver erythropoiesis by RXR alpha and retinoic acid, and that expression then becomes dominated by HNF4 activity from E11.5 onward. This transition may explain why Epo expression is regulated by hypoxic control throughout the remainder of life.

title: Tetraspanin 7 (TSPAN7) expression is upregulated in multiple myeloma patients and inhibits myeloma tumour development in vivo.
text:
BACKGROUND: Increased expression of the tetraspanin protein TSPAN7 has been identified in various cancers, including multiple myeloma (MM). However, the role of TSPAN7 in cancer progression is currently unclear.
METHODS: In this study, we investigated the expression of TSPAN7 in MM and examined its impact on the adhesion, migration, and growth of MM plasma cells (PCs) in vitro and in bone marrow (BM) homing and tumor growth in vivo. Additionally, we characterized the association of TSPAN7 with cell surface partner molecules in vitro.
RESULTS: Our results revealed that TSPAN7 was highly expressed at the RNA and protein level in approximately 50% of MM patient samples. Overexpression of TSPAN7 in the murine myeloma cell line 5TGM1 significantly reduced tumor burden in 5TGM1/KaLwRij mice 4 weeks after intravenous administration of 5TGM1 cells. While TSPAN7 overexpression did not affect cell proliferation in vitro, it increased 5TGM1 cell adhesion to BM stromal cells and transendothelial migration. Moreover, TSPAN7 was found to interact with the cell surface molecule calnexin.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that elevated TSPAN7 levels may be associated with better outcomes for up to 50% of MM patients.

title: Association of body mass index with outcomes in patients with CKD.
text: Obesity is linked to lower mortality rates among the general population, but this relationship is reverse in patients undergoing dialysis. The exact nature of the relationship between obesity and adverse clinical outcomes in non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients and the potential interaction between the severity of the disease and this association are unclear. We analyzed data from a nationally representative cohort of 453,946 United States veterans with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of less than 60 ml/min per 1.73 m(2). The associations between different body mass index (BMI) categories and all-cause mortality and disease progression (measured using multiple definitions, including the incidence of end-stage renal disease, doubling of serum creatinine levels, and slopes of eGFR) were examined in Cox proportional hazards models and logistic regression models. Multivariate adjustments were made for age, race, comorbidities, and medications, as well as baseline eGFR. The BMI was found to have a relatively consistent U-shaped association with clinical outcomes, with the best outcomes observed in overweight and mildly obese patients. BMI levels of less than 25 kg/m(2) were associated with poorer outcomes in all patients, regardless of the severity of CKD, while BMI levels of 35 kg/m(2) or greater were associated with poorer outcomes in patients with earlier stages of CKD, but this association was attenuated in those with an eGFR of less than 30 ml/min per 1.73 m(2). Therefore, until clinical trials establish the ideal BMI, a cautious approach to weight management is warranted in this patient population.

title: WRN, the protein deficient in Werner syndrome, plays a critical structural role in optimizing DNA repair.
text: Werner syndrome (WS), a rare genetic disorder, predisposes individuals to cancer and premature aging due to WRN mutations. WRN is a RECQ-like helicase that plays a crucial role in DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair through non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) or homologous recombination (HR). Previous studies have shown that WS cells exhibit extensive deletions during DSB repair, which are complemented by wild-type (wt) WRN. WRN exhibits both 3' --> 5' exonuclease and 3' --> 5' helicase activities. To investigate the relative contributions of these enzymatic activities to DSB repair, we examined NHEJ and HR in WS cells complemented with wtWRN, exonuclease-defective WRN (E-), helicase-defective WRN (H-), or exonuclease/helicase-defective WRN (E-H-). Our results suggest that balanced exonuclease and helicase activities of WRN are essential for optimal HR. Moreover, WRN appears to play a structural role in DSB repair, independent of its enzymatic activities. Another human RECQ helicase, BLM, suppressed HR but had little or no effect on NHEJ, highlighting the distinct functions of mammalian RECQ helicases.

title: In vitro generated antibodies specific for telomeric guanine-quadruplex DNA react with Stylonychia lemnae macronuclei.
text:
The majority of eukaryotic telomeres contain a repetitive sequence with stretches of guanine bases that form a 3' overhang beyond the telomeric duplex region. The telomeric repeat of hypotrichous ciliates, d(T(4)G(4)), forms a 16-nucleotide 3' overhang. These sequences can adopt parallel-stranded or antiparallel-stranded quadruplex conformations in vitro. Although it has been proposed that guanine-quadruplex structures may play important cellular roles, including telomere function, recombination, and transcription, evidence for their existence in vivo has been elusive until now.
We generated high-affinity single-chain antibody fragment (scFv) probes for the guanine-quadruplex formed by the Stylonychia telomeric repeat through ribosome display from the Human Combinatorial Antibody Library. Among the scFvs selected, one (Sty3) showed an affinity of K(d) = 125 pM for the parallel-stranded guanine-quadruplex and could discriminate with at least 1000-fold specificity between parallel or antiparallel quadruplex conformations formed by the same sequence motif. A second scFv (Sty49) bound both the parallel and antiparallel quadruplexes with similar (K(d) = 3-5 nM) affinity. Indirect immunofluorescence studies showed that Sty49 reacted specifically with the macronucleus but not the micronucleus of Stylonychia lemnae. The replication band, where replication and telomere elongation occur, was also not stained, suggesting that the guanine-quadruplex is resolved during replication. Our results provide experimental evidence that the telomeres of Stylonychia macronuclei adopt in vivo a guanine-quadruplex structure, indicating that this structure may play an important role in telomere functioning.

title: Incidence of skin cancer after renal transplantation in The Netherlands.
text: The analysis of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and basal cell carcinoma (BCC) in 764 patients who received a renal allograft at Leiden University Hospital between 1966 and 1988 revealed that 176 skin cancers were diagnosed in 47 patients during a mean follow-up period of 8.7 years (range of 1-21 years). The risk of developing a first tumor increased from 10% after 10 years to 40% after 20 years of graft survival. Comparatively, the incidence of SCC was 250 times higher and that of BCC was 10 times higher among the patients than in the general Dutch population. Notably, the locations of SCCs and BCCs differed significantly. While solar radiation is believed to be a major risk factor for skin cancer, the occurrence of skin cancer in long-term graft survivors poses a significant problem in countries with a higher latitude, such as the Netherlands.

title: Myogenic and morphogenetic defects in the heart tubes of murine embryos lacking the homeo box gene Nkx2-5.
text: The mouse homeobox gene Nkx2-5 is expressed in precardiac mesoderm and the myocardium of embryonic and fetal hearts. Disrupting Nkx2-5 leads to abnormal heart morphogenesis, growth retardation, and embryonic lethality around 9-10 days post-coitum (p.c.). Although heart tube formation occurs normally in mutant embryos, looping morphogenesis, a crucial step in heart development, is not initiated at the linear heart tube stage (8.25-8.5 days p.c.). Myofilament gene expression and myofibrillogenesis are not compromised, but the myosin light-chain 2V (MLC2V) gene is not expressed in mutant hearts or in mutant ES cell-derived cardiocytes. MLC2V expression typically occurs only in ventricular cells and is the earliest known molecular marker of ventricular differentiation. The regional expression of two other ventricular markers, myosin heavy chain beta and cyclin D2, in mutant hearts indicates that not all ventricle-specific gene expression depends on Nkx2-5. The data demonstrate that Nkx2-5 is essential for normal heart morphogenesis, myogenesis, and function, and that it is a component of a genetic pathway required for myogenic specialization of the ventricles.

title: Hygiene hypothesis in inflammatory bowel disease: a critical review of the literature.
text: The hygiene hypothesis is believed to play a significant role in the increasing prevalence of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) worldwide. However, the specific factors involved in this association are not yet fully understood. To investigate, we conducted a systematic review of the literature on the relationship between hygiene-related factors and the development of IBD. Our search yielded publications from 1966 to 2007, including studies on H pylori exposure, helminths, cold chain hypothesis, measles infection and vaccination, antibiotic use, breastfeeding, family size, sibling relationship, urban upbringing, day care attendance, and domestic hygiene. While the literature suggests that the hygiene hypothesis and reduced microbial exposure in childhood likely contribute to the development of IBD, the quality of supporting data varies widely. The most promising factors associated with IBD development are H pylori exposure, helminths, breastfeeding, and sibling relationship. However, the majority of studies in this area are plagued by methodological limitations, including reliance on retrospective recall of information, which makes it difficult to accurately establish the importance of the hygiene hypothesis in IBD. Further research in this area may provide valuable insights into the etiology of IBD.

title: Are dual eligibles admitted to poorer quality skilled nursing facilities?
text:
Medicare beneficiaries who are also eligible for Medicaid, known as dual eligibles, often receive lower quality care compared to other Medicare beneficiaries. To investigate whether dual eligibles are discharged to lower quality post-acute skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) than Medicare-only beneficiaries, we conducted a study using the random utility maximization model.
We analyzed a dataset of 692,875 Medicare fee-for-service patients (22% of whom were dual eligibles) who were discharged from hospitals and received Medicare-paid SNF care between July 2004 and June 2005. We used Medicare enrollment and Medicaid Analytic Extract files to determine dual eligibility, and we measured the proportion of Medicaid patients and nursing staff characteristics at SNFs as indicators of quality.
Our results showed that dual eligibles were more likely to be discharged to SNFs with a higher proportion of Medicaid patients and fewer nurses compared to Medicare-only beneficiaries. These findings were robust after using alternative subsample of patients based on primary diagnoses, propensity of being dual eligible, and likelihood of remaining in the nursing home.
Our study found that dual eligibles face disparities in access to quality SNF care. To address these disparities, we recommend improving discharge planning processes to redirect patients to higher quality providers, regardless of their Medicaid eligibility.

title: Quantitative phosphoproteomic analysis of acquired cancer drug resistance to pazopanib and dasatinib
text:
Drug resistance is a significant challenge in modern cancer treatment, particularly for patients treated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). Our study aimed to understand the signalling mechanisms underlying resistance to two FDA-approved TKIs, pazopanib and dasatinib, in the A204 rhabdoid tumour cell line. Using mass spectrometry, we comprehensively characterized the global phosphoproteomic changes that occur upon resistance acquisition. Our results showed that only a minor fraction (6% for pazopanib and 9.7% for dasatinib) of the quantified phosphoproteome was altered upon resistance acquisition. Interestingly, we observed distinct signalling pathways involved in drug resistance for each drug. Pazopanib-resistant cells displayed increased phosphorylation in cytoskeletal regulatory pathways, while dasatinib-resistant cells showed enhanced activation of the insulin receptor/IGF-1R signaling pathway. Additionally, we identified new vulnerabilities associated with drug resistance and discovered a promising approach to overcome resistance by inhibiting HSP90 function using a second-generation inhibitor, NVP-AUY-922. Overall, our study provides valuable insights into the candidate signalling determinants of TKI resistance and highlights HSP90 inhibition as a potential salvage therapy.
Key points:

1. Drug resistance is a major challenge in cancer treatment, particularly for patients treated with TKIs.
2. Our study used mass spectrometry to comprehensively characterize phosphoproteomic changes in drug-resistant A204 rhabdoid tumour cells.
3. Only a minor fraction (6% for pazopanib and 9.7% for dasatinib) of the quantified phosphoproteome was altered upon resistance acquisition.
4. Distinct signalling pathways were involved in drug resistance for each drug.
5. Pazopanib-resistant cells showed increased phosphorylation in cytoskeletal regulatory pathways, while dasatinib-resistant cells displayed enhanced activation of the insulin receptor/IGF-1R signaling pathway.
6. We identified new vulnerabilities associated with drug resistance and discovered a potential salvage therapy by inhibiting HSP90 function.

In summary, our study provides valuable insights into the signalling mechanisms underlying TKI resistance and identifies potential therapeutic strategies to overcome this resistance.

title: Pandemic H1N12009 influenza and HIV: a review of natural history, management and vaccine immunogenicity.
text:
PURPOSE:
The 2009 H1N1 (HIN1) pandemic strain caused more severe illness and increased mortality risk, particularly for immune-compromised individuals such as HIV patients. To address this concern, a focused effort was made to assess the disease burden and vaccine efficacy in these populations.
RECENT FINDINGS:
Unlike other immune-compromised individuals, most HIV-infected individuals recovered from the 2009 H1N1 flu without significant complications. While HIV infection was believed to be a risk factor for more severe disease and death, the available literature does not support this assumption. Neuraminidase inhibitors were well tolerated in this population, and there was no evidence of significant drug interactions with antiretroviral therapy. The H1N12009 vaccine showed improved immunogenicity compared to historical results with non-pandemic vaccines, and booster dosing was found to be beneficial. The H1N12009 vaccine was generally well tolerated and did not have any detrimental effect on HIV status.
SUMMARY:
The worst-case scenario did not materialize for H1N12009 in the general population or in those with HIV. Immunization with adjuvants represents a crucial measure to protect these populations from H1N12009 and future novel influenza strains.

title: Population genomics of the honey bee reveals strong signatures of positive selection on worker traits.
text: Most theories proposing the development of eusociality rely on two fundamental assumptions: mutations affecting the physical traits of sterile workers evolve through positive selection if they benefit the fertile relatives, and worker traits are primarily responsible for allowing social insects to adapt to their environment. Despite the prevalent belief that positive selection drives the evolution of worker traits, the actual prevalence of positive selection acting on the genomes of eusocial insects remains largely unknown. To address this knowledge gap, we analyzed the genomes of 40 individual Apis mellifera, identifying thousands of genes and regulatory sequences with signs of adaptive evolution across multiple evolutionary time scales. Our findings reveal Apoidea- and Apis-specific genes to be enriched with signatures of positive selection, suggesting that newly emerged genes play a disproportionately large role in the adaptive evolution of eusocial insects. Worker-biased proteins show a higher density of adaptive evolution compared to queen-biased proteins, underscoring the crucial role of worker traits in adaptation. Furthermore, genes related to worker division of labor were found to be enriched with signs of positive selection. Additionally, genes involved in worker behavior based on brain gene expression analysis were highly enriched for adaptive protein and cis-regulatory evolution. Our study underscores the significant contribution of worker phenotypes to adaptive evolution in social insects and provides an abundance of information on the loci that influence fitness in honey bees.

title: An acetylation switch in p53 mediates holo-TFIID recruitment.
text: Posttranslational modifications play a crucial role in regulating biological processes by modulating the activity of transcription factors. For example, the acetylation of the p53 transcription factor enhances its ability to activate target genes, such as p21. In this study, we demonstrate that the acetylation of two lysine residues in p53 (K373 and K382) leads to the recruitment of the TFIID subunit TAF1 to the p21 promoter through its bromodomains. Upon UV irradiation, p53 becomes diacetylated at these lysine residues, which in turn recruits TAF1 to a distant p53-binding site on the p21 promoter prior to looping to the core promoter. Inhibition of the acetyl-p53/bromodomain interaction prevents TAF1 recruitment to both the distal p53-binding site and the core promoter. Additionally, we found that TFIID subunits TAF4, TAF5, and TBP are detected on the core promoter prior to TAF1, suggesting that different subunits of TFIID may be recruited to the p21 promoter in a sequential manner, and that the transcriptional activation depends on the posttranslational modification of the p53 transcription factor.

title: Dasatinib inhibits both osteoclast activation and prostate cancer PC-3-cell-induced osteoclast formation.
text:
New research aims to uncover potential treatments for prostate cancer bone metastases by targeting the interaction between cancer cells, bone marrow cells, and the bone matrix. One key player in this process is osteoclasts, which play a crucial role in the development of bone tumors caused by prostate cancer. Since Src kinase has been shown to be essential for osteoclast function, researchers hypothesized that inhibiting this kinase could reduce osteoclast activity and prostate cancer cell-induced osteoclast formation.
Experiments were conducted in vitro using dasatinib, a Src family kinase inhibitor, to target osteoclast activation. Dasatinib was found to inhibit osteoclast differentiation of mouse primary bone marrow-derived monocytes and PC-3 cell-induced osteoclast differentiation by 29% and 58%, respectively. Additionally, dasatinib inhibited osteoclast degradation activity by 58%. These findings suggest that targeting osteoclast differentiation and activity may be a promising targeted therapy for patients with prostate cancer bone metastases.
In summary, the research focuses on developing new treatments that target the interaction between cancer cells, bone marrow cells, and the bone matrix in prostate cancer bone metastases. By inhibiting Src kinase, dasatinib reduces osteoclast activity and prostate cancer cell-induced osteoclast formation, suggesting that targeting osteoclast differentiation and activity may be an effective treatment approach for patients with prostate cancer bone metastases.

title: BMP receptor ALK3 controls collecting system development.
text: The molecular cues that regulate the growth and branching of the ureteric bud during the formation of the renal collecting system are still poorly understood. Members of the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) family communicate through the type I BMP receptor ALK3 to inhibit the morphogenesis of ureteric bud and collecting duct cells in vitro. To investigate the function of the BMP signaling pathway in vivo, we generated a mouse model (Alk3(UB-/-) mice) in which the ALK3 gene is deficient in the ureteric bud lineage only. At the onset of branching morphogenesis, Alk3(UB-/-) kidneys display an abnormal primary ureteric bud branch pattern and an increased number of ureteric bud branches. However, during later stages of renal development, Alk3(UB-/-) kidneys have fewer ureteric bud branches and collecting ducts compared to wild-type kidneys. Postnatal Alk3(UB-/-) mice exhibit a renal dysplasia characterized by hypoplasia of the renal medulla, a decreased number of medullary collecting ducts, and abnormal expression of beta-catenin and c-MYC in medullary tubules. In essence, proper kidney development necessitates the functional ALK3-dependent BMP signaling pathway, which regulates ureteric bud branching.

title: Increased release of ferritin and iron by iron-loaded alveolar macrophages in cigarette smokers.
text: Cigarette smokers' lower respiratory tract contains higher levels of iron, primarily sequestered in alveolar macrophages (AM), compared to non-smokers. However, some of this extracellular iron could potentially be released by reductants in cigarette smoke, leading to the formation of highly reactive hydroxyl radicals and oxidant injury. To investigate AM's contribution to alveolar extracellular iron and ferritin, we analyzed the release of iron and ferritin from AM recovered through bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) in 27 healthy individuals, including nine nonsmokers, nine light smokers, and nine heavy smokers. Our results showed that iron release in vitro over 20 hours was significantly higher in AM from light and heavy smokers compared to nonsmokers (p < 0.001). Similarly, ferritin release was increased in AM from light and heavy smokers (p < 0.001). Furthermore, AM from 12 smokers (8 heavy, 4 light) contained more than 10 nanomoles of iron per 10 million cells, and these iron-loaded AM released a greater percentage of cell ferritin stores in vitro over 4 hours compared to AM from nonsmokers (p < 0.01). Moreover, the release of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was significantly lower than ferritin release over 4 hours (p < 0.001). These findings suggest that AM play a significant role in the increased iron content in the lower respiratory tract of cigarette smokers, and may contribute to oxidant injury through the release of iron-bound metals.

title: The spectrum of retinopathy in adults with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
text: In the study, a detailed observational analysis of malarial retinopathy was conducted among Bangladeshi adults using high-definition portable retinal photography. The findings revealed that retinopathy was present in 63% of adults with severe malaria and 70% of those with cerebral malaria, with moderate or severe retinopathy more frequent in cerebral malaria (55% vs 20% in uncomplicated malaria and 0% in healthy controls). Although the spectrum of malarial retinopathy was similar to that in African children, vessel discoloration was not observed in adults. Retinal whitening severity corresponded with admission venous plasma lactate levels, suggesting that retinal ischemia represents systemic ischemia. The study concluded that retinal changes related to microvascular obstruction are common in adults with severe falciparum malaria and correlated with disease severity and coma, implying that a compromised microcirculation has important pathophysiological significance in severe and cerebral malaria. Portable retinal photography exhibited potential as a valuable tool for investigating malaria-related retinopathy.

title: Prospective randomized open blinded end-point (PROBE) study. A novel design for intervention trials. Prospective Randomized Open Blinded End-Point.
text: A novel research design for intervention studies, known as the PROBE study (Prospective Randomized Open Blinded Endpoint), is presented. This design is compared to the traditional double-blind design. One of the key benefits of the PROBE design is its lower cost, which is because it more closely mimics standard clinical practice. Additionally, the blinded end-point committee evaluates end-points, ensuring that there is no difference between the two types of trials in this regard.

title: PSGL-1 function in immunity and steady state homeostasis.
text:
The crucial role of P-selectin glycoprotein ligand 1 (PSGL-1) in leukocyte migration has become increasingly evident beyond its initial characterization as a selectin ligand. PSGL-1, initially thought to be a simple molecule with an extracellular mucin domain, has been found to play a dynamic role in leukocyte trafficking, influenced by the addition of branched O-glycans on specific amino acid residues. These glycans are expressed differently in various cell types, such as neutrophils, which constitutively express the glycosyltransferases involved in O-glycan formation, and T cells, which only express these enzymes after appropriate activation. This highlights the diverse functions of PSGL-1 in supporting leukocyte recruitment in both the innate and adaptive immune responses.
The selectin-PSGL-1 interaction is mediated by a complex array of amino acids within the selectins that engage multiple sugar residues of the branched O-glycans on PSGL-1, leading to velcro-like catch bonds that facilitate leukocyte rolling. Moreover, binding of PSGL-1 can also trigger signaling events that influence cell phenotype and function. Recent studies have uncovered additional functions of PSGL-1, including its ability to bind homeostatic chemokines CCL19 and CCL21 and support the chemotactic response to these chemokines. However, interestingly, the O-glycan modifications of PSGL-1 that support rolling mediated by selectins in inflammatory conditions can interfere with PSGL-1 binding to homeostatic chemokines, thereby limiting T-cell responsiveness to steady-state chemotactic cues.
The multifaceted influence of PSGL-1 on cell traffic in both inflammatory and steady-state settings is determinaed by the coordinated addition of O-glycans, indicating the importance of this process. However, in vivo regulation of PSGL-1 glycosylation in T cells remains poorly understood, and this aspect of PSGL-1 function warrants further investigation. In summary, this review aims to update our understanding of PSGL-1 glycosylation and its functional scope, highlighting the complex interplay between cellular processes and the ensuing implications for leukocyte trafficking and immune function.

title: Ligand binding determines whether CD46 is internalized by clathrin-coated pits or macropinocytosis.
text:
CD46 is a ubiquitous cell surface receptor found on human cells that plays a crucial role in the immune system. It interacts with complement components C3b and C4b, as well as various pathogens such as measles virus and human herpes virus 6. The binding of ligands to CD46 affects several processes within immune cells, including protection from complement attack, regulation of immune cell function, antigen presentation, and down-regulation of cell surface CD46. Recent research has shown that CD46 signaling can integrate both innate and acquired immune functions.
The internalization of CD46 has been found to occur through two distinct pathways, depending on the strength of cross-linking of CD46. In non-lymphoid cells, CD46 is constitutively internalized through clathrin-coated pits, traffics to multivesicular bodies, and is then recycled to the cell surface. However, upon cross-linking of CD46 at the cell surface, either through multivalent antibody or measles virus, CD46 undergoes pseudopodial extension, leading to the engulfment of the ligand and the degradation of cell surface CD46. This process is similar to macropinocytosis.
The study of CD46 internalization has important implications for CD46 signaling, antigen presentation, CD46 down-regulation, and the engulfment of pathogens. Understanding the mechanisms of CD46 internalization can provide insight into the regulation of immune responses and the integration of innate and acquired immune functions.

title: A three-dimensional cell biology model of human hepatocellular carcinoma in vitro
text: We developed an in vitro three-dimensional (3D) model of metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) by culturing MHCC97H cells within a rotating wall vessel bioreactor. Our analysis revealed that the 3D HCC model exhibited many clinical pathological features of HCC in vivo, including cancer cell morphology, tissue ultrastructure, protein production and secretion, glucose metabolism, tissue-specific gene expression, and apoptosis. When we transplanted these spheroids into the livers of nude mice, they resulted in tumorigenesis and metastasis. This 3D HCC spheroid model shows promise as a tool for studying HCC tumor biology, testing anticancer drugs, and creating animal models of HCC.

title: Patterns of age-specific mortality in children in endemic areas of sub-Saharan Africa.
text: Understanding the age- and season-dependent nature of malaria mortality is crucial for developing effective epidemiological models of malaria immunity. However, most studies have aggregated their results into broad age groups and across seasons, making it difficult to predict the impact of targeted interventions on specific age groups of children. To address this limitation, we gathered age-specific mortality rates for children under 15 years old in 7 demographic surveillance sites in sub-Saharan Africa with stable Plasmodium falciparum malaria transmission. We used verbal autopsies (VAs) to estimate the proportion of deaths attributed to malaria and calculated age-specific mortality rates for each site, age group, and month of the year. Our findings revealed that a significant proportion of deaths (ranging from 20.1% in Mozambique to 46.2% in Burkina Faso) were due to malaria in all sites. Age patterns in malaria mortality were similar across sites, with the majority of deaths occurring in children over 1 year old. Deaths in the youngest age groups (< 3 months) were rarely attributed to malaria, while mortality rates in older children were more strongly age-dependent. Interestingly, all-cause mortality rates peaked during the rainy season in most sites, but there was little seasonality in the proportion of deaths attributed to malaria, except in the 2 Burkina Faso sites. Improving the specificity of VA analysis would enhance the interpretation of age and season patterns in malaria mortality data.

title: Obesity due to melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) deficiency is associated with increased linear growth and final height, fasting hyperinsulinemia, and incompletely suppressed growth hormone secretion.
text: The study investigated the somatotroph axis in obese individuals with a deficiency in melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R) and compared them to equally obese controls. Anthropometric measurements, insulin concentrations, and hormone levels were measured in a subset of the subjects. The results showed that children with MC4R deficiency had a higher height standard deviation score (SDS) compared to controls, which persisted throughout childhood. Adults with MC4R deficiency had a greater final height compared to controls, despite having similar fasting insulin levels. Pulsatile growth hormone (GH) secretion was maintained in MC4R deficiency, consistent with animal studies, suggesting a role for MC4R in regulating hypothalamic somatostatinergic tone. However, GH levels were suppressed in obese controls, suggesting a mismatch between GH secretion and insulin resistance. Both factors may contribute to the accelerated growth phenotype characteristic of MC4R deficiency.

title: The selectivity of beta-adrenoceptor antagonists on isoprenaline-induced changes in heart rate, blood pressure, soleus muscle contractility and airways function in anaesthetized cats.
text:
In this study, the activity of four beta-adrenoceptor antagonists (propranolol, metoprolol, atenolol, and butoxamine) was compared in anaesthetized cats, using the synthetic phenylethanolamine derivatives as a measure of beta-adrenoceptor activity. The effects of the beta-adrenoceptor antagonists on four parameters in the anaesthetized cat - heart rate, blood pressure, soleus muscle contractility, and airway reactance - were measured, and the modification of the isoprenaline dose-response relation by each of the antagonist drugs was assessed.
The results showed that parallel shifts in log dose-response curves for isoprenaline were caused by propranolol for all parameters, by metoprolol and atenolol for each parameter except blood pressure, and butoxamine for each except soleus muscle and heart rate. Propranolol was the most potent antagonist and showed slight selectivity of action on soleus muscle compared to heart. Atenolol and metoprolol were approximately equipotent and were cardioselective at low doses only. Butoxamine was the least potent antagonist and possessed non-beta-adrenoceptor effects on the parameters measured.
The new compounds, 4'-bromo-2'-methoxy-N-isopropyl phenylethanolamine, the 4'-chloro- and 4'-methyl analogues, and 4'-methoxy-N-t-butyl phenylethanolamine, were found to be potent antagonists but did not exhibit any selectivity of action. These results suggest that there is no clear separation of beta-adrenoceptors into beta 1- and beta 2-subclasses in organs of the cat, and no apparent separation of beta-adrenoceptor-mediated effects on skeletal muscle and airways.
In summary, the study demonstrates that propranolol, metoprolol, atenolol, and butoxamine are beta-adrenoceptor antagonists that can affect various physiological processes in the anaesthetized cat, including heart rate, blood pressure, soleus muscle contractility, and airway reactance. The results suggest that these drugs do not exhibit clear separation of beta-adrenoceptor subtypes in different organs of the cat, and there is no obvious separation of beta-adrenoceptor-mediated effects on skeletal muscle and airways.

title: Breast cancer and obesity: an update.
text: The relationship between obesity and breast cancer is complex and varies depending on the stage of life. In postmenopausal women, particularly the elderly, various measures of obesity are positively associated with an increased risk of breast cancer. Conversely, before menopause, increased body weight is inversely related to breast cancer risk. The mechanisms by which body weight and obesity affect breast cancer risk are related to estrogenic activity, with obesity also being associated with poorer prognosis in both premenopausal and postmenopausal breast cancer. Notably, breast cancer in African-American women exhibits some differences in its relationship to obesity compared to white women, despite the high prevalence of obesity among African-American women contributing to a relatively poorer prognosis. While estrogens are often highlighted as the key factor in the effects of obesity on breast cancer, other factors, such as insulin, insulin-like growth factor-I, and leptin, may play an equal or more important role in determining the aggressive tumor phenotype. This review aims to emphasize the importance of these factors and their relationship to angiogenesis and transcriptional factors.

title: Dietary saturated and unsaturated fats as determinants of blood pressure and vascular function.
text: For many years, the amount and type of dietary fat have been linked to the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Arterial stiffness and endothelial dysfunction are significant risk factors in the development of heart disease (CHD). Various methods are used in nutritional science to assess vascular function, including clinic and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, pulse wave analysis, pulse wave velocity, flow-mediated dilatation, and venous occlusion plethysmography. The present review examines the impact of dietary fat quantity and type on blood pressure, arterial compliance, and endothelial function. With regards to fat quantity, habitual dietary fat intake has little effect on vascular function beyond fatty acid composition, although single high-fat meals postprandially impair endothelial function compared to low-fat meals, possibly due to increased circulating lipoproteins and NEFA which may induce pro-inflammatory pathways and increase oxidative stress. In contrast, cross-sectional data suggest that saturated fat has adverse effects on vascular function, while polyunsaturated fat (mainly linoleic acid (18 : 2n-6) and n-3 PUFA) are beneficial. EPA (20 : 5n-3) and DHA (22 : 6n-3) can lower blood pressure, improve arterial compliance in type 2 diabetics and dyslipidaemics, and enhance endothelium-dependent vasodilation. Future research should focus on uncovering the underlying mechanisms and identifying the specific physiological effects induced by EPA and DHA. Since high-quality observational or interventional data on dietary fatty acid composition and vascular function are scarce, no additional recommendations can be made at this time beyond current guidelines.

title: Very small embryonic-like stem cells with maximum regenerative potential get discarded during cord blood banking and bone marrow processing for autologous stem cell therapy.
text: The text discusses the possible loss of very small embryonic-like stem cells (VSELs) during cord blood banking and bone marrow (BM) processing for autologous stem cell therapy. The study compared VSELs in human umbilical cord blood (UCB) and discarded red blood cells (RBC) fraction obtained after separation of mononuclear cells from human BM, and found that VSELs settle along with RBCs during Ficoll-Hypaque density separation. VSELs are small in size (3-5 μm), have a high nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio, and expression of pluripotent markers such as Oct-4, Nanog, Sox-2, Rex-1, and Tert. Interestingly, a distinct population of slightly larger, round hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) with cytoplasmic Oct-4 were detected in the "buffy" coat. Immunohistochemical studies on umbilical cord tissue (UCT) sections showed the presence of nuclear Oct-4-positive VSELs and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) with cytoplasmic Oct-4. The study suggests that the true stem cells in adult body tissues are VSELs, while HSCs and MSCs are progenitor stem cells that arise by asymmetric cell division of VSELs. The results may explain the low efficacy reported during adult autologous stem cell trials, where unknowingly progenitor stem cells are injected rather than the pluripotent stem cells with maximum regenerative potential.

title: CNS repair requires both effector and regulatory T cells with distinct temporal and spatial profiles.
text:
Monocyte-derived macrophages (mo-MΦs) and T cells play a crucial role in spinal cord repair, but their contribution can be influenced by the presence of inflammation-resolving immune cells. Recent studies have identified the remote brain choroid plexus epithelium (CP) as a portal for monocyte recruitment, and its activation is dependent on interferon-gamma (IFN-γ). However, the mechanisms by which effector T cells and inflammation-resolving immune cells contribute to the repair process remain unclear.
Using an acute spinal cord injury model in mice, we found that the choroid plexus was not activated in the absence of IFN-γ-producing T cells, leading to limited recruitment of inflammation-resolving mo-MΦ to the spinal cord parenchyma. Additionally, we demonstrated that mo-MΦ locally regulated the recruitment of thymic-derived Foxp3(+) regulatory T (Treg) cells to the injured spinal cord parenchyma at the subacute/chronic phase. Interestingly, an ablation protocol that resulted in reduced Tregs at this stage interfered with tissue remodeling, while transient ablation of Tregs before the injury favored repair. Our findings suggest that reduced systemic immunosuppression at the time of injury can enhance central nervous system (CNS) repair, highlighting the importance of a dynamic immune cell network that acts in discrete compartments and stages, involving both effector and regulatory T cells. Any dysregulation in the level or activity of these populations can hinder the repair process, underscoring the need for temporally and spatially controlled therapeutic interventions.

title: Sperm function tests and fertility.
text: Historically, the diagnosis of male infertility relied on a subjective evaluation of human semen, focusing on the number of sperm, their motility, and morphology. The core principle behind this approach is that male fertility can be defined by a threshold number of motile, normal sperm that must be surpassed for conception. However, numerous studies have shown that this approach is flawed, as it is not necessarily the absolute number of sperm that determines fertility, but rather their functional competence. To address this limitation, various in vitro tests have been developed to evaluate sperm function, including their ability to move, penetrate cervical mucus, capacitate, recognize the zona pellucida, undergo the acrosome reaction, and fuse with oocytes. These functional assays have been found to accurately predict the fertilizing capacity of human spermatozoa both in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, recent advances in the field have led to the development of tests to assess oxidative stress and DNA integrity in sperm, providing valuable information not only on fertilizing capacity but also embryonic development.

title: Isolation and characterization of the cDNA encoding BKLF/TEF-2, a major CACCC-box-binding protein in erythroid cells and selected other cells.
text: CACCC boxes are found in abundance in the regulatory elements of genes expressed in erythroid cells, as well as in other select cell types. Previous research has shown that an erythroid cell-specific CACCC-box-binding protein, EKLF, is crucial for proper expression of the adult beta-globin gene in vivo. However, this protein is dispensable for the regulation of several other globin and non-globin genes expressed in erythroid cells. In this study, we investigated whether additional CACCC-box transcription factors exist in murine erythroid cells. Through gel shift assays, we identified a significant activity (termed BKLF) found in yolk sac and fetal liver erythroid cells that differed from EKLF. Utilizing relaxed-stringency hybridization, we obtained the cDNA encoding BKLF, a novel zinc finger protein that shares similarities with EKLF and other Krüppel-like proteins in its DNA-binding domain but exhibits distinct differences elsewhere in its structure. BKLF, which is expressed at high levels in the midbrain region of embryonic mice, is likely to correspond to the gel shift activity TEF-2, a transcriptional activator implicated in the regulation of the simian virus 40 enhancer and other CACCC-box-containing regulatory elements. Given that BKLF binds with high affinity and selectivity towards many CACCC sequences present in genes expressed in erythroid cells, it is likely to play a crucial role in the control of a wide range of genes whose expression appears to be independent of EKLF.

title: Effect of osteoporosis treatments on risk of non-vertebral fractures: review and meta-analysis of intention-to-treat studies
text: Most osteoporosis treatments have demonstrated efficacy in reducing the risk of vertebral fractures, although there is less consensus on their ability to prevent non-vertebral fractures. It is important to base conclusions about a treatment's efficacy on a thorough analysis of the intention-to-treat (ITT) population, rather than on post-hoc subgroup analyses. However, non-vertebral anti-fracture efficacy has been primarily derived from post-hoc subgroup analyses. To assess the non-vertebral anti-fracture efficacy of several osteoporosis therapies, including a more rigorous evaluation of the ITT populations, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized, placebo-controlled, phase III clinical trials with at least 3-year follow-up. The trials included in the analysis had to provide data on non-vertebral anti-fracture efficacy, a defined endpoint confirmed by radiographs. Eleven clinical trials met the inclusion criteria, and three of them showed statistically significant (P ≤0.05) non-vertebral anti-fracture efficacy in the ITT population: two trials with risedronate and one trial with strontium. A meta-analysis of the data showed significant reductions in the relative risk of non-vertebral fracture for both alendronate (RR=0.86; 95% CI: 0.76–0.97, P =0.012) and risedronate (RR=0.81; 95% CI: 0.71–0.92, P =0.001). Risedronate and strontium ranelate were the only treatments to demonstrate non-vertebral anti-fracture efficacy in this comprehensive assessment of anti-fracture efficacy of osteoporosis therapy using ITT populations in trials of 3 years or more in duration. Risedronate was the only agent shown to demonstrate efficacy in more than one trial. The meta-analysis found that both alendronate and risedronate provide non-vertebral anti-fracture efficacy.

title: Islet1 deletion causes kidney agenesis and hydroureter resembling CAKUT.
text: Isl1 (Islet1) is a transcription factor that is transiently expressed in a distinct subset of heart and limb progenitors during embryonic development. In studies focused on limb development, conditional deletion of Isl1 unexpectedly brought to light kidney abnormalities. To investigate the role of Isl1 in kidney development, we conducted in situ hybridization analysis in mice and found Isl1 expression in mesenchymal cells surrounding the base of the ureteric bud. Conditional deletion of Isl1 resulted in kidney agenesis or hypoplasia, as well as hydroureter, a phenotype resembling congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) found in humans. The absence of Isl1 led to ectopic branching of the ureteric bud, potentially resulting in obstruction of the ureter-bladder junction and subsequent hydroureter. Our findings suggest that Isl1 plays a critical role in regulating the proper development of the kidney and ureter by restricting the aberrant formation of the ureteric bud. Moreover, we found that the lack of Isl1 diminished the expression of Bmp4, a gene linked to the CAKUT-like phenotype, in the metanephric region prior to ureteric budding. In conclusion, our study demonstrates the essential role of Isl1 in the proper formation of the kidney and ureter, and highlights the possibility that Isl1 may be a causative gene for CAKUT in humans, warranting further investigations in this regard.

title: Tissue transglutaminase (TG2)--a wound response enzyme.
text: The repair of tissue following injury is a complex process that involves a series of coordinated but overlapping events, including inflammation, re-epithelialization, neovascularization, and the synthesis and stabilization of a fibrous extracellular matrix (ECM) that is remodeled over time to resemble normal tissue. Members of the transglutaminase (TG) family play a crucial role in this process, as they crosslink proteins via epsilon(gamma-glutamyl) lysine bridges, stabilizing proteins and regulating cell behavior. In this article, we focus on the function of tissue transglutaminase (TG2), the most widely expressed member of the TG family, in wound repair. Using both early and recent evidence from the literature, we demonstrate how TG2 affects the stability of the ECM, cell-ECM interactions, and cell behavior during the different phases of wound healing, and highlight potential therapeutic applications of this enzyme.

title: Crystal structures of the glutamate receptor ion channel GluK3 and GluK5 amino-terminal domains.
text: Ionotropic glutamate receptors (iGluRs) are in charge of the majority of fast excitatory synaptic transmission in the central nervous system. The specific assembly of iGluRs into AMPA, kainate, and N-methyl-d-aspartic acid (NMDA) receptor subtypes is controlled by their extracellular amino-terminal domains (ATDs). Kainate receptors are further divided into low-affinity receptor families (GluK1-GluK3) and high-affinity receptor families (GluK4-GluK5) based on their affinity for the neurotoxin kainic acid. These two families have a 42% sequence identity for the intact receptor but only a 27% sequence identity at the ATD level. We have determined the high-resolution crystal structures of GluK3 and GluK5 ATDs, which crystallize as dimers but have a strikingly different dimer assembly at the R1 interface. In contrast, both GluK3 and GluK5 dimer assembly at the R2 domain is similar to that reported previously for other non-NMDA iGluRs. This observation is consistent with the reports that GluK4-GluK5 cannot form functional homomeric ion channels and require obligate coassembly with GluK1-GluK3. Our analysis also reveals that the relative orientation of domains R1 and R2 in individual non-NMDA receptor ATDs varies by up to 10°, whereas the 50° difference reported for the NMDA receptor GluN2B subunit is observed. This restricted domain movement in non-NMDA receptor ATDs seems to result both from extensive intramolecular contacts between domain R1 and domain R2 and from their assembly as dimers, which interact at both R1 and R2 domains. Our results provide the first insights into the structure and function of GluK4-GluK5, the least understood family of iGluRs.

title: Effectiveness of screening older people for impaired vision in community setting: systematic review of evidence from randomised controlled trials.
text:
AIM To evaluate whether population-based screening for impaired vision among older individuals in the community leads to improvements in vision.
DESIGN Systematic review of randomized controlled trials of community-based screening that assessed visual function or impairment with at least 6-month follow-up.
SUBJECTS Adults aged 65 and older.
PRIMARY OUTCOME MEASURE Proportion of individuals with visual impairment in intervention and control groups, as measured by various methods.
RESULTS Only five trials were identified that included visual assessments, with a total of 3494 participants. All trials used self-reported measures of visual impairment, both as screening tools and outcomes. Despite including a visual screening component in the assessment, no significant improvement in self-reported visual problems was observed (pooled odds ratio 1.04, 95% confidence interval 0.89-1.22). A small reduction (11%) in the number of older people with self-reported visual problems cannot be excluded.
CONCLUSION The findings suggest that community-based screening for impaired vision in older individuals is not justified based on the present evidence. Treatment of visual impairment in this age group can typically improve vision. It is unclear why no benefit was observed in the screened population. Further research is needed to determine the most effective interventions for older individuals with unreported vision impairment.

title: Protein interaction network of the mammalian Hippo pathway reveals mechanisms of kinase-phosphatase interactions.
text:
The Hippo signaling pathway regulates organ size and tissue homeostasis in response to multiple stimuli, including changes in cell density and mechanotransduction. Pharmacological inhibition of phosphatases can also activate Hippo signaling in cell culture. To understand the protein-protein interactions within the Hippo pathway, we created a comprehensive interaction network using both phosphorylation-dependent and -independent interactions. We identified 749 interactions, including 599 previously unknown interactions, and demonstrated that several interactions with serine and threonine phosphatases are dependent on phosphorylation.
We found that MST2 (mammalian STE20-like protein kinase 2), a key component of the Hippo pathway, requires autophosphorylation to interact with the STRIPAK complex. Deletion of the amino-terminal forkhead-associated domain of SLMAP (sarcolemmal membrane-associated protein), another component of the STRIPAK complex, prevented MST1 and MST2 from associating. Phosphatase inhibition led to changes in protein interactions in MOB1A and MOB1B (Mps one binder kinase activator-like 1A and 1B) and promoted interactions with upstream Hippo pathway proteins, including MST1 and MST2, as well as with the trimeric protein phosphatase 6 complex (PP6).
We also found that mutating specific amino acids in MOB1B that are involved in phosphorylation-dependent interactions prevented its interaction with MST1 and PP6 in cells treated with okadaic acid. Our results suggest that changes in phosphorylation levels orchestrate the interactions between kinases and phosphatases in the Hippo pathway, providing a potential mechanism for its regulation.

title: Differential Effects of N-Acetylcysteine, Theophylline or Bicarbonate on Contrast-Induced Rat Renal Vasoconstriction
text:
Background: Vasoconstriction and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation following contrast media (CM) injection are the primary factors responsible for CM-induced nephropathy. In this study, we investigated the effects of N-acetylcysteine (NAC), theophylline, and sodium bicarbonate on intrarenal vasoconstriction and ROS generation in a rat model of CM-induced nephropathy.
Methods: After a 3-day dehydration, Sprague-Dawley rats received CM (Telebrix) or sham 'CM' injection of 0.9% saline. Some of the rats received NAC, theophylline, or bicarbonate prior to CM injection. Medullary renal blood flow was estimated using laser Doppler. The animals were sacrificed 1, 15, or 30 minutes after the respective treatments, and their kidneys were collected for the assessment of intrarenal STAT-8 isoprostane, prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), and nitric oxide (NO) levels.
Results: NAC was found to significantly attenuate vasoconstriction, while theophylline only showed mild effects at 15 minutes and was ineffective after 30 minutes. In contrast, NAC significantly increased intrarenal PGE2 levels, while theophylline and bicarbonate had no such effect. Moreover, NAC, but not theophylline or bicarbonate, gradually increased intrarenal NO levels. Interestingly, CM-induced ROS accumulation, as measured by STAT-8 isoprostane estimation, progressed unimpeded by any of the pharmacological interventions.
Conclusions: (1) Intrarenal vasoconstriction triggered by CM injection could be effectively prohibited by NAC but not bicarbonate or theophylline; (2) the vasodilatory effect of NAC was mediated by increased PGE2 synthesis; and (3) ROS accumulation was a primary renal response to CM-induced injury, and was not affected by any of the pharmacological interventions.

title: Induction of AMPK activity corrects early pathophysiological alterations in the subtotal nephrectomy model of chronic kidney disease.
text: The rat kidney ablation and infarction (A/I) model of subtotal or 5/6th nephrectomy is the most commonly studied model of non-diabetic chronic kidney disease (CKD). At one week post-A/I, the kidney exhibits decreased function and metabolic efficiency, as determined by glomerular filtration rate and oxygen consumption per sodium transport (QO2/TNa), respectively. This leads to reduced AMPK activity, a renoprotective enzyme that is affected by metabolic changes and cellular stress. To investigate further, we evaluated AMPK activity in this model system and found that it decreases paradoxically early on, followed by progressive worsening of kidney parameters, including extensive structural, functional, metabolic, and fibrotic changes, at four weeks after A/I. Interestingly, inducing AMPK activity through the use of metformin or 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide (AICAR) was found to increase AMPK activity in this model, improve kidney function, and ameliorate kidney fibrosis and structural alterations. Our findings suggest that AMPK activity is reduced in the subtotal nephrectomy model of non-diabetic CKD, and that altered regulation of AMPK is coincident with the progression of disease parameters. Additionally, restoration of AMPK activity may prove to be an effective therapeutic target for the treatment of non-diabetic CKD.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging for volume estimation of large multinodular goitres: a comparison with scintigraphy.
text: In recent years, there has been growing interest in non-surgical treatments for reducing the size of large multinodular goitres. In a study of 20 patients with goitres larger than 100 ml, the use of magnetic resonance (MR) imaging for volume estimation was evaluated. MR measurements were compared to scintigraphic (SC) volume estimations, and the results showed that MR imaging can be used for in vivo thyroid volume estimation in large multinodular goitres. The high precision of MR measurements makes this technique potentially useful for evaluating thyroid growth and non-surgical treatment for reducing goitre size. However, the correlation between MR and SC measurements was not strong, and the resulting coefficient of variation (CV) was 17.3 +/- 14.2%. It was also found that MR imaging can provide detailed anatomical information on mechanical complications of large goitres, which is an additional advantage of this technique.

title: Differential role of CbpA and PspA in modulation of in vitro CXC chemokine responses of respiratory epithelial cells to infection with Streptococcus pneumoniae.
text: Respiratory epithelial cells play a crucial role in the body's response to respiratory pathogens like Streptococcus pneumoniae by releasing chemokines that attract neutrophils. To investigate the specific virulence factors of S. pneumoniae that trigger these chemokine responses, researchers infected human lung cells (A549) and nasal cells (Detroit-562) with wild-type S. pneumoniae or mutants lacking certain proteins. The results showed that both cell types responded to wild-type S. pneumoniae by producing more chemokine mRNA and protein, but the response was stronger in A549 cells. Deleting the N-terminal domains of a protein called choline-binding protein A (CbpA) inhibited the chemokine response, while deleting a protein called pneumococcal surface protein A (PspA) had the opposite effect. Deleting the first N-terminal alpha-helical domain of PspA reduced its ability to stimulate chemokine production, but deleting the entire region did not have an effect. Overall, these findings suggest that the N-terminal regions of CbpA and PspA have different effects on chemokine induction in epithelial cells infected with S. pneumoniae.

title: HIV-1 therapy with monoclonal antibody 3BNC117 elicits host immune responses against HIV-1
text: 3BNC117 is a powerful and broadly neutralizing antibody against HIV-1 that targets the CD4 binding site on the viral envelope spike. When administered passively, this antibody can protect animals from HIV-1 infection and reduce viral load in infected individuals. In this study, we investigated the impact of HIV-1 immunotherapy with a single injection of 3BNC117 on host antibody responses in viremic individuals. Unlike untreated controls, who showed little change in their neutralizing activity over a 6-month period, 3BNC117 infusion significantly improved neutralizing responses to heterologous tier 2 viruses in nearly all study participants. Our findings suggest that 3BNC117-mediated immunotherapy enhances host humoral immunity to HIV-1.

title: Safety and efficacy of RNAi therapy for transthyretin amyloidosis.
text:
Transthyretin amyloidosis is caused by the accumulation of abnormal proteins in nerves and the heart, leading to various health problems. A potential therapeutic approach to treat this disease is by using RNA interference (RNAi), which can reduce the production of the disease-causing protein. In this study, we developed two formulations of lipids (ALN-TTR01 and ALN-TTR02) that were tested in clinical trials to evaluate their safety and efficacy in reducing transthyretin levels.
We conducted two separate phase 1 clinical trials, one with patients suffering from transthyretin amyloidosis and the other with healthy volunteers. The results showed that both formulations led to rapid and sustained reductions in transthyretin levels, with a significant decrease of up to 87% at the highest dose. Moreover, the reduction in transthyretin levels was found to be RNAi-mediated, indicating the effectiveness of the approach. While some participants experienced mild to moderate infusion-related reactions, these were relatively common across both formulations.
Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of RNAi therapy targeting transthyretin amyloidosis, providing hope for effective treatment options for this debilitating disease. (Funded by Alnylam Pharmaceuticals; ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT01148953 and NCT01559077.)

title: The mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 is inhibited by the peptide GsMTx4.
text: Cells can respond to mechanical stress by opening mechanosensitive ion channels (MSCs), which are selectively activated by external stimuli. The isolation of Piezo1, a eukaryotic cation-selective MSC, has given researchers a new avenue for studying mechanical transduction at the cellular level. Piezo1 shares electrophysiological properties with naturally occurring cationic MSCs, which are inhibited by the peptide GsMTx4. In this study, we tested whether GsMTx4 targets Piezo1 activity. Exposure to micromolar concentrations of GsMTx4 reversibly inhibited approximately 80% of the mechanically induced current from transfected HEK293 cells. The inhibition was voltage-insensitive, and the mirror image of GsMTx4 inhibited currents in a similar manner, consistent with the idea that GsMTx4 acts as a gating modifier. The rate constants for binding and unbinding were found to be 7.0 x 10(5) M(-1) s(-1) and 0.11 s(-1), respectively, with a K(D) of approximately 155 nM, which is similar to previous reports for endogenous MSCs. The ability of GsMTx4 to target the mechanosensitivity of Piezo1 supports its use in high-throughput screens for pharmacological agents and diagnostic assays. Furthermore, whole-cell Piezo1 currents were also found to be reversibly inhibited by GsMTx4, with differences observed for the on and off rates. These findings demonstrate that GsMTx4 can selectively target Piezo1 activity and provide valuable insights into the mechanisms of mechanical transduction in cells.

title: Thiazolidinediones improve beta-cell function in type 2 diabetic patients.
text: Thiazolidinediones (TZDs) enhance glucose metabolism and insulin sensitivity in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Intestinal and in vitro studies suggest that TZDs may improve pancreatic beta-cell function, but this study aimed to investigate whether TZD-induced glycemic improvements are related to improved beta-cell function.
