We evaluated 11 healthy glucose-tolerant individuals and 53 T2DM patients [age 53 ± 2 years; body mass index (BMI) 29.4 ± 0.8 kg/m2; fasting plasma glucose (FPG) 10.3 ± 0.4 mM; HbA1c 8.2 ± 0.3%]. Patients were randomized to receive placebo or TZD for 4 months. Subjects underwent 2-h oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTTs) and two-step euglycemic insulin clamps with [3-(3)H]glucose. T2DM patients were subsequently randomized to receive 4 months of pioglitazone (45 mg/day), rosiglitazone (8 mg/day), or placebo. Pioglitazone and rosiglitazone improved FPG, mean plasma glucose during OGTT, Hb A1c, and insulin-mediated total body glucose disposal (Rd) and decreased mean plasma free fatty acid (FFA) during OGTT (all P < 0.01, ANOVA). Comparatively, the insulin secretion/insulin resistance (disposition) index [DeltaISR(AUC)/Deltaglucose(AUC)/IR] was significantly increased in all TZD-treated groups: +1.8 ± 0.7 (PIO + drug-naive diabetics), +0.7 ± 0.3 (PIO + sulfonylurea-treated diabetics), and +0.7 ± 0.2 (ROSI + sulfonylurea-withdrawn diabetics) versus -0.2 ± 0.3 in the two placebo groups (P < 0.01, ANOVA). Improved insulin secretion positively correlated with increased body weight, fat mass, and Rd and negatively correlated with decreased plasma glucose and FFA during the OGTT. In T2DM patients, TZD treatment leads to enhanced beta-cell function, which strongly correlates with improved glycemic control.

title: A novel Ku70 function in colorectal homeostasis separate from nonhomologous end joining
text: Ku70, a nonhomologous end-joining (NHEJ) factor, has been shown to play a role in tumor suppression, although the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Our earlier work demonstrated that mice lacking DNA ligase IV (Lig4), another key NHEJ factor, developed aggressive lymphoma in the absence of tumor suppressor p53. However, introducing a mutant p53R172P, which impaired p53-induced apoptosis but not cell cycle arrest, abrogated the tumor phenotype. Interestingly, breeding Ku70-deficient mice with p53R172P resulted in mice that were free of diabetes, despite 80% of the mutant mice exhibiting enlarged colons with pronounced inflammation. Surprisingly, most of these mutant mice progressed to dysplasia, adenoma, and adenocarcinoma, indicating an NHEJ-independent function of Ku70. In-depth analysis of colonic epithelial cells from these mice revealed nuclear stabilization of β-catenin, along with increased expression of cyclin D1 and c-Myc, in the affected colon sections. This phenomenon was found to be independent of the p53 mutation, as Ku70-deficient mice also exhibited the same phenotype. Our findings not only uncover a novel function of Ku70 in maintaining colon homeostasis, but also establish an excellent in vivo model to study the mechanisms underlying chronic inflammation and abnormal cellular proliferation that contribute to tumorigenesis and tumor progression in the colon.

title: Association of Sickle Cell Trait With Hemoglobin A1c in African Americans
text:
In this study, the authors analyzed data from 7938 participants in two community-based cohorts (the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study and the Jackson Heart Study) to investigate the relationship between sickle cell trait (SCT) and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels. They found that participants with SCT had lower HbA1c levels than those without SCT, even when their fasting or 2-hour glucose levels were similar. This suggests that HbA1c may underestimate past glycemia (blood sugar levels) in black patients with SCT.
The study included 4620 participants (mean age 52.3 years, 61.3% women, and 367 participants with SCT) with a total of 9062 concurrent measures of fasting glucose and HbA1c levels. The authors found that for a given fasting glucose level, HbA1c levels were statistically significantly lower in participants with SCT (5.72%) compared to those without SCT (6.01%). The difference in HbA1c levels between the two groups was greater at higher fasting and 2-hour glucose concentrations.
The prevalence of prediabetes and diabetes was lower among participants with SCT when defined using HbA1c values. This suggests that HbA1c may underestimate the risk of prediabetes and diabetes in black patients with SCT.
In conclusion, this study found that participants with SCT had lower HbA1c levels than those without SCT, even at similar fasting or 2-hour glucose levels. These findings suggest that HbA1c may underestimate past glycemia in black patients with SCT and may require further evaluation.

title: PGAP2 mutations, affecting the GPI-anchor-synthesis pathway, cause hyperphosphatasia with mental retardation syndrome.
text:
A recent study has identified mutations in genes involved in the biosynthesis of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor in a new subclass of congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDGs) with distinct clinical features. The study found mutations in six genes (PIGA, PIGL, PIGM, PIGN, PIGO, and PIGV) encoding proteins in the GPI-anchor-synthesis pathway in individuals with severe neurological features, including seizures, muscular hypotonia, and intellectual disability. To investigate further, a diagnostic gene panel was developed to target all known genes encoding proteins in the GPI-anchor-synthesis pathway, and three missense mutations (c.46C>T, c.380T>C, and c.479C>T) were identified in two unrelated individuals with hyperphosphatasia with mental retardation syndrome (HPMRS). The mutations were found to cosegregate in the investigated families.
PGAP2 is involved in fatty-acid GPI-anchor remodeling, which occurs in the Golgi apparatus and is essential for stable association between GPI-anchored proteins and the cell-surface membrane rafts. To explore the effect of these mutations on GPI-anchor remodeling, altered protein constructs were transfected into PGAP2-null cells. The study found that only partial restoration of GPI-anchored marker proteins, CD55 and CD59, on the cell surface was observed. These findings suggest that an impairment of GPI-anchor remodeling can cause HPMRS, highlighting the diagnostic potential of targeted sequencing of genes encoding proteins in the GPI-anchor-synthesis pathway for this subclass of CDGs.

title: Screening for Lung Cancer: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement
text: The US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) recommends annual lung cancer screening for adults aged 55-80 who have a 30 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years. The USPSTF bases its recommendation on the evidence of both the benefits and harms of screening, as well as the balance between the two. The task force does not consider the cost of providing screening in its assessment. The recommendation is for screening to be discontinued once a person has not smoked for 15 years or develops a health problem that significantly limits life expectancy or the ability or willingness to have curative lung surgery. The USPSTF recognizes that clinical decisions involve more considerations than evidence alone and that policy and coverage decisions involve considerations beyond the evidence of clinical benefits and harms. The task force notes that smoking cessation remains essential, and that screening cannot prevent most lung cancer-related deaths. The benefits of screening depend on the person's risk for lung cancer, and those who are at highest risk are most likely to benefit. The USPSTF found insufficient evidence on the harms associated with incidental findings, and overdiagnosis of lung cancer occurs, but its precise magnitude is uncertain. The task force used modeling studies to predict the benefits and harms of screening programs that use different screening intervals, age ranges, smoking histories, and times since quitting. A program that annually screens adults aged 55-80 who have a 30 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years is projected to have a reasonable balance of benefits and harms. The task force notes that screening may not be appropriate for patients with substantial comorbid conditions, particularly those at the upper end of the screening age range. The baseline characteristics of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) showed a relatively healthy sample, and fewer than 10% of enrolled participants were older than 70 years. Persons with serious comorbid conditions may experience net harm, no net benefit, or at least substantially less net benefit. The NLST excluded persons who were unlikely to complete curative lung cancer surgery and those with medical conditions that posed a substantial risk for death during the 8-year trial. The task force used a validated multivariate model to show that persons in the highest 60% of risk accounted for 88% of all deaths preventable by screening. Lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) has shown high sensitivity and acceptable specificity for detecting lung cancer in high-risk persons. Chest radiography and sputum cytologic evaluation have not shown adequate sensitivity or specificity as screening tests, and therefore, LDCT is currently the only recommended screening test for lung cancer. Surgical resection is the current standard of care for localized non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This type of cancer is treated with surgical resection when possible, and also with radiation and chemotherapy. Annual LDCT screening may not be useful for patients with life-limiting comorbid conditions or poor functional status who may not be candidates for surgery. Smoking cessation is the most important intervention to prevent NSCLC, and advising smokers to stop smoking and preventing nonsmokers from being exposed to tobacco smoke are the most effective ways to decrease the morbidity and mortality associated with lung cancer. Current smokers should be informed of their continuing risk for lung cancer and offered cessation treatments. Screening with LDCT should be viewed as an adjunct to tobacco cessation interventions. Clinicians have many resources to help patients stop smoking, including the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's website with information on tobacco quit lines, available in several languages.

title: Dual role of interleukin-10 in the regulation of respiratory syncitial virus (RSV)-induced lung inflammation.
text:
Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) are a common cause of hospitalization in children, and can lead to acute respiratory failure, as well as sequelae such as secondary bacterial infections and reactive airway disease. One host response observed in severe RSV-induced LRTI and/or subsequent development of asthma is increased expression of interleukin (IL)-10. However, conflicting results have been reported regarding the role of IL-10 in regulating the host response to RSV LRTI, with some studies suggesting that IL-10 inhibits asthmatic responses, while others suggest that it intensifies the disease. To reconcile these discordant observations, we used a lung-specific, inducible IL-10 over-expression (OE) transgenic mouse model to investigate the role of IL-10 in regulating the host response to RSV LRTI.
Our results showed that the presence of IL-10 at the time of RSV infection not only attenuated acute inflammatory processes (i.e., 24 hours post-infection), but also late inflammatory changes characterized by Th2 cytokine and chemokine expression. However, when IL-10 OE was delayed until the late immune response to RSV infection, additive effects rather than inhibitory effects were observed. Interestingly, in non-infected IL-10 OE mice, IL-10 OE alone induced up-regulation of Th2 cytokine and Th2-related chemokine expression. We identified a subset of CD11b(+)CD11c(+)CD49b(+)F4/80(-)Gr-1(-) myeloid cells as the principal source of IL-10-induced IL-13 production. Therefore, the augmented pathological responses observed in our 'delayed' IL-10 over-expression model could be attributed to IL-10 OE alone.
Taken together, our study revealed dual roles of IL-10 on RSV-induced lung inflammation, which appear to depend on the timing of when elevated IL-10 is expressed in the lung.

title: Latent membrane protein 1 of Epstein–Barr virus coordinately regulates proliferation with control of apoptosis
text: Latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1), an oncogenic protein encoded by Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), functions as a constitutively active transmembrane receptor. LMP1 is crucial for specific aspects of EBV infection and proliferation of infected B cells. It mimics the signaling of the CD40 receptor and has been implicated in regulating B cell proliferation, survival, or both. To identify the immediate-early cellular target genes regulated by LMP1, we generated a conditional LMP1 allele within the context of the full EBV genome. Our findings revealed that LMP1 specifically induces mitogenic B cell activation through c-Myc and Jun/AP1 family members, confirming its direct role in upregulating expression of multiple genes involved in cell survival. LMP1's signals are essential for the G1/S transition in human B cells, and cells lacking these signals are cell cycle arrested and survive quiescently. Contrary to previous assumptions, LMP1's activities are not required to maintain survival in non-proliferating cells. Instead, LMP1 induces both pro- and anti-apoptotic genes whose balance allows survival during LMP1-mediated proliferation.

title: Crizotinib in ROS1-rearranged non-small-cell lung cancer.
text:
BACKGROUND: Chromosomal rearrangements of the ROS1 gene, which encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase, have been identified in a subset of non-small-cell lung cancers (NSCLCs). These rearrangements may render these cancers vulnerable to treatment with ROS1 kinase inhibitors. Crizotinib is a small-molecule inhibitor of multiple tyrosine kinases, including ROS1, and has shown promising antitumor activity in patients with ROS1-rearranged NSCLC.
METHODS: In this study, we enrolled 50 patients with advanced NSCLC who tested positive for ROS1 rearrangement in an expansion cohort of a phase 1 study of crizotinib. Patients received crizotinib at a standard oral dose of 250 mg twice daily and were assessed for safety, pharmacokinetics, and response to therapy. ROS1 fusion partners were identified using next-generation sequencing or reverse-transcriptase-polymerase-chain-reaction assays.
RESULTS: The objective response rate was 72% (95% confidence interval [CI], 58-84), with 3 complete responses and 33 partial responses. The median duration of response was 17.6 months (95% CI, 14.5-not reached), and median progression-free survival was 19.2 months (95% CI, 14.4-not reached), with 25 patients (50%) still in follow-up for progression. Seven ROS1 fusion partners were identified in 30 tumors tested: 5 known partners and 2 novel partners. No correlation was observed between the type of ROS1 rearrangement and the clinical response to crizotinib. The safety profile of crizotinib was similar to that seen in patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, crizotinib showed significant antitumor activity in patients with advanced ROS1-rearranged NSCLC. ROS1 rearrangement defines a second molecular subgroup of NSCLC for which crizotinib is highly active. (Funded by Pfizer and others; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00585195.)

title: The S. cerevisiae Rrm3p DNA helicase moves with the replication fork and affects replication of all yeast chromosomes.
text:
The Saccharomyces cerevisiae DNA helicase Rrm3p plays a crucial role in the progression of DNA replication forks through the genome. Our findings indicate that Rrm3p is required for normal fork progression through over 1,000 discrete sites scattered throughout the genome. Surprisingly, delayed replication was observed even in regions without any predicted Rrm3p-dependent sites, suggesting that Rrm3p has a global role in DNA replication.
Our results show that the rate of fork movement in Rrm3p-deficient cells is similar to that of wild-type cells except at known Rrm3p-dependent sites. These findings suggest that while Rrm3p has a significant impact on DNA replication, its activity is primarily or exclusively required at specific, challenging-to-replicate sites.
Using chromatin immunoprecipitation, we found that Rrm3p is associated with both Rrm3p-dependent and -independent sites and moves along with the replication fork through both. In addition, we detected interactions between Rrm3p and Pol2p, the catalytic subunit of DNA polymerase epsilon, in vivo. Together, these findings indicate that Rrm3p is not simply recruited to its sites of action when replication forks stall at these sites, but rather is an integral part of the replication fork apparatus.

title: The pathophysiology of protein-overload proteinuria.
text:
In a study on protein-overload nephrosis in rats induced by intraperitoneal administration of bovine serum albumin (BSA), changes in glomerular function and structure were investigated using fractional clearance (C/GFR) studies with inulin and tracer proteins of different molecular size and charge. The results showed:
1. Unchanged glomerular filtration rate and renal plasma flow in proteinuric rats.
2. A 34-fold increase in the fractional clearance of rat serum albumin, reaching values similar to BSA.
3. A 2-fold increase in the fractional clearance of anionic horse radish peroxidase (HRP), but normal values for neutral and cationic HRP.
4. An 11- and 3-fold increase in the fractional clearance of heterologous IgG and IgM, respectively.
Glomerular epithelial cells showed degenerative changes in proteinuric rats, but the distribution of anionic sites in the glomerular basement membrane was found to be unaltered, as determined by polyethyleneimine binding studies. In summary, an elevation of serum albumin concentration led to an increased transcapillary albumin transport, which resulted in degenerative changes in glomerular epithelial cells, including the development of large pore defects. These changes were completely reversible.

title: Effects of aging on central and peripheral mammalian clocks.
text: The impact of aging on the circadian organization is not fully understood, and it is unclear whether age-related changes are due to alterations in central pacemakers, peripheral oscillators, or coupling mechanisms. To investigate, we used transgenic rats with a luciferase reporter to examine the effects of aging on the expression of the Period 1 (Per1) gene in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) and peripheral tissues. Young (2 months) and aged (24-26 months) Per1-luc transgenic rats, entrained to light-dark cycles, were sacrificed, and tissues were cultured. Per1-luc expression was measured in 10 tissues. In the SCN, the central mammalian pacemaker, Per1-luc expression showed robust rhythmicity for over 7 weeks in culture, with only a small age-related shortening of the free-running period. However, circadian rhythmicity in some peripheral tissues was unaffected by aging, while in others it was either advanced relative to the light cycle or absent. Interestingly, these arrhythmic tissues could be induced to oscillate with the application of forskolin, suggesting that they retained the capacity to oscillate but were not being driven appropriately in vivo. Overall, our findings provide new insights into the effects of aging on the mammalian circadian system, suggesting that aging affects some but not all tissues, and may act primarily by modulating interactions among circadian oscillators, potentially reducing the SCN's ability to drive oscillators in the periphery.

title: CtBP3/BARS drives membrane fission in dynamin-independent transport pathways
text: Membrane fission is a crucial process in membrane transport, and while dynamin has been the only fission protein machinery discovered to date, it is possible that other fission mechanisms exist. Here, we investigate the role of carboxy-terminal binding protein 3 (CtBP3)/brefeldin A-ribosylated substrate (BARS) in controlling membrane fission during basolateral transport from the Golgi to the plasma membrane and in fluid-phase endocytosis. Our findings reveal that CtBP3/BARS controls fission in these steps, whereas dynamin is not involved. Interestingly, CtBP3/BARS is inactive in apical transport to the plasma membrane and in receptor-mediated endocytosis, both of which are controlled by dynamin. This suggests that CtBP3/BARS regulates membrane fission in endocytic and exocytic transport pathways that are distinct from those that rely on dynamin.

title: Influenza A myocarditis developing in an adult liver transplant recipient despite vaccination: a case report and review of the literature.
text: Individuals who undergo solid organ transplants and receive chronic immunosuppressive drugs are more susceptible to acquiring the influenza virus, even after receiving vaccination. Myocarditis, a rare but known complication of influenza infection, can occur in these individuals. We report the first adult liver transplant recipient who received prophylactic vaccination but still developed influenza A myocarditis. This highlights the potential vulnerability of solid organ transplant recipients to infections, which may be due to their reduced response to protein-based vaccines. Further research is needed to determine whether antiviral chemoprophylaxis during the influenza season would be an effective preventive measure against influenza in this high-risk population.

title: Extrapulmonary effects of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on physical activity: a cross-sectional study.
text: RATIONALE: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) often experience reduced physical activity due to the systemic effects of the disease and its comorbidities. OBJECTIVES: To investigate the relationship between extrapulmonary effects of COPD and its comorbidities, and reduced physical activity in patients with COPD. METHODS: In a cross-sectional study, 170 outpatients with COPD (GOLD stages I-IV; BODE score 0-10) underwent a series of tests to assess physical activity over 5-6 consecutive days using a multisensor accelerometer armband. Cardiovascular status was evaluated by echocardiography, vascular Doppler sonography, and levels of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide. Mental and metabolic/muscular status, systemic inflammation, and anemia were assessed using the Beck Depression Inventory, bioelectrical impedance analysis, handgrip strength, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein/fibrinogen, and hemoglobin measurements, respectively. RESULTS: In a multivariate linear regression analysis, independent of GOLD stages or BODE score, higher values of systemic inflammation and left cardiac dysfunction, as measured by N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels and echocardiographically measured left ventricular diastolic function, respectively, were associated with reduced physical activity in patients with COPD. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that higher levels of systemic inflammation and left cardiac dysfunction are associated with reduced physical activity in patients with COPD.

title: Cleavage efficient 2A peptides for high level monoclonal antibody expression in CHO cells.
text: Linking the heavy chain (HC) and light chain (LC) genes for monoclonal antibody (mAb) production using a single cassette with 2A peptides allows for control of the LC/HC ratio and reduction of non-expressing cells. Four different 2A peptides, derived from foot-and-mouth disease virus (F2A), equine rhinitis A virus (E2A), porcine teschovirus-1 (P2A), and Thosea asigna virus (T2A), were compared for their expression of three biosimilar IgG1 mAbs in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell lines. HC and LC were linked with different 2A peptides in both the absence and presence of GSG linkers. Insertion of a furin recognition site upstream of 2A enabled the removal of 2A residues that would otherwise be attached to the HC. Different 2A peptides demonstrated varying cleavage efficiencies that correlated with the mAb expression level. The relative cleavage efficiency of each 2A peptide remained similar for the expression of different IgG1 mAbs in different CHO cells. While complete cleavage was not observed for any of the 2A peptides, GSG linkers enhanced the cleavage efficiency and thus the mAb expression level. T2A with a GSG linker (GT2A) exhibited the highest cleavage efficiency and mAb expression level. Stably amplified CHO DG44 pools generated using GT2A had titers of 357, 416, and 600 mg/L for the three mAbs in shake flask batch cultures. Incomplete cleavage likely resulted in incorrect processing of mAb species and aggregates, which were removed through a chromatin-directed clarification method and protein A purification. The vector and methods presented provide a convenient process beneficial for both mAb development and manufacturing.

title: The complexity of human ribosome biogenesis revealed by systematic nucleolar screening of Pre-rRNA processing factors.
text: Mature ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs) are synthesized from more complex precursors through a process of maturation. Previous studies have thoroughly characterized the processing of these precursors in yeast, leading to the assumption that a similar process occurs in humans. However, our functional analysis of 625 nucleolar proteins in HeLa cells revealed 286 proteins required for pre-rRNA processing, including 74 without a direct yeast homolog. We found that defects in pre-rRNA processing are conserved across different cell types, including primary cells, and are not caused by activation of a p53-dependent nucleolar tumor surveillance pathway. Furthermore, these defects occur prior to cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. In addition, we investigated the role of the exosome in processing internal transcribed spacers (ITSs) and found that 3' end maturation of 18S rRNA involves EXOSC10/Rrp6, a yeast ITS2 processing factor. These findings suggest that human cells employ unique strategies and recruit distinct trans-acting factors to execute critical processing steps, with significant implications for understanding ribosomopathies at the molecular level and developing effective therapeutic agents.

title: Maximal aerobic capacity in African-American and Caucasian prepubertal children.
text: The purpose of this study was to investigate differences in resting, submaximal, and maximal oxygen consumption (VO2) between African-American (n = 44) and Caucasian (n = 31) prepubertal children aged 5-10 years old. Resting VO2 was measured using indirect calorimetry in the fasted state. Submaximal VO2 and VO2max were determined during an all-out, progressive treadmill exercise test tailored for children. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry was used to determine total fat mass (FM), soft lean tissue mass (LTM), and leg soft LTM. Doubly labeled water was used to determine total energy expenditure (TEE) and activity energy expenditure (AEE). The study found a significant effect of ethnicity (P < 0.01) on VO2max, with African-American children having an absolute VO2max approximately 15% lower than Caucasian children (1.21 ± 0.032 vs. 1.43 ± 0.031 l/min, respectively). Even after adjusting for soft LTM, FM, leg LTM, TEE, and AEE, the lower VO2max persisted in African-American children. These findings suggest that while African-American and Caucasian children have similar rates of VO2 at rest and during submaximal exercise, VO2max is approximately 15% lower in African-American children, independently of various factors.

title: Penaeus monodon Dscam (PmDscam) has a highly diverse cytoplasmic tail and is the first membrane-bound shrimp Dscam to be reported.
text: The Down syndrome cell adhesion molecule (Dscam) appears poised to play a central role in the "alternative adaptive immunity" observed in invertebrates. Dscam is composed of a cytoplasmic tail involved in signal transduction and a highly variable extracellular region that could potentially employ a pathogen recognition mechanism similar to that employed by vertebrate antibodies. In our previous study, we isolated a unique tail-less form of Dscam from Litopenaeus vannamei. This investigation presents the first membrane-bound form of shrimp Dscam, PmDscam, which was isolated from Penaeus monodon and exists in both membrane-bound and tail-less forms. Phylogenetic analysis reveals that crustacean Dscams from shrimp and water fleas do not share a single subclade, but are distinct from invertebrate Dscam-like molecules and insect Dscams. The variable regions of PmDscam are localized in the N-terminal Ig2, N-terminal Ig3, and entire Ig7 domain in the extracellular region. PmDscam extracellular and transmembrane domain variants are generated by mutually exclusive alternative splicing events, while cytoplasmic tail variants are produced by exon inclusion/exclusion. Based on the genomic organization of Daphnia Dscam's cytoplasmic tail, we propose a model for how the shrimp Dscam genomic locus might employ Type III polyadenylation to generate both tail-less and membrane-bound forms.

title: The different biological effects of telomestatin and TMPyP4 can be attributed to their selectivity for interaction with intramolecular or intermolecular G-quadruplex structures.
text:
The existence of G-quadruplex structures in telomeres of Stylonychia macronuclei and the promoter of c-myc in human cells has been validated as potential drug targets. However, the next crucial issue is the selectivity of G-quadruplex-interactive agents towards different types of G-quadruplex structures. In this study, we have taken an important step towards understanding the specific biological effects of these drugs by analyzing their interaction with either intramolecular or intermolecular G-quadruplex structures formed in telomeres.
Telomestatin, a natural product isolated from Streptomyces anulatus 3533-SV4, has been shown to be a potent inhibitor of telomerase through its G-quadruplex interaction. Our findings demonstrate that telomestatin prefers to interact with intramolecular G-quadruplex structures and displays a remarkable selectivity of 70-fold towards intramolecular G-quadruplex structures over duplex DNA. Interestingly, telomestatin is able to stabilize G-quadruplex structures formed from either duplex human telomeric DNA or single-stranded DNA. What's more, it can do so in the absence of monovalent cations, a unique characteristic among G-quadruplex-interactive compounds. At non-cytotoxic concentrations, telomestatin suppresses the proliferation of telomerase-positive cells within several weeks.
In contrast, TMPyP4, a compound that preferentially promotes the formation of intermolecular G-quadruplex structures, leads to the suppression of proliferation in both ALT-positive cells and telomerase-positive cells. Importantly, TMPyP4 induces anaphase bridges in sea urchin embryos, whereas telomestatin does not have this effect. These findings suggest that the selectivity of telomestatin for intramolecular G-quadruplex structures and TMPyP4 for intermolecular G-quadruplex structures is crucial in determining their biological effects. Stabilization of intramolecular G-quadruplex structures leads to telomerase inhibition and accelerated telomere shortening, whereas facilitation of the formation of intermolecular G-quadruplex structures induces the formation of anaphase bridges.

title: Targeting oxidative stress to treat endometriosis.
text:
INTRODUCTION
Endometriosis affects approximately 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. This condition is characterized by the presence of implanted, growing endometrial tissue outside the uterine cavity. Despite its prevalence, the exact pathophysiology of endometriosis remains unclear. However, various theories have been proposed to explain its development. Given its significant impact on fertility and quality of life, there is a pressing need for a novel treatment approach.
Recent studies have shed light on the pathological characteristics of endometriosis, revealing a vicious cycle in which oxidative stress (OS) is generated, which in turn facilitates the implantation of ectopic endometrium. This cycle is further fueled by the generation of high amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS), leading to a state of OS.
AREAS COVERED
In this review, we examined the available evidence associating OS with endometriosis. We then searched for antioxidant agents that have been investigated specifically in endometriosis patients, including vitamins C and E, melatonin, resveratrol, xanthohumol, and epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG). Our review found significant effects of these antioxidants on endometriosis.
EXPERT OPINION
While aiming to reduce OS is a promising approach for endometriosis treatment, most studies to date are either in vitro or animal-based. As such, further research in human subjects is required to fully understand the impact of OS reduction on patients with endometriosis. Nevertheless, this review highlights the potential of antioxidants as a novel treatment strategy for this debilitating condition.

title: Interferon alpha for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C in patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus. Hepatitis-HIV Spanish Study Group.
text:
Liver disease caused by hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection is becoming a major cause of morbidity and mortality among individuals who have been infected with HIV through parenteral transmission, such as injection drug users, hemophiliacs, and transfused patients. To investigate the effectiveness of interferon (IFN) alpha therapy in these patients and identify predictors of response, we conducted a multicenter, prospective, open, non-randomized observational study.
A total of 119 patients with chronic hepatitis C (90 of whom were HIV-infected and 29 of whom were not) were enrolled in the study. IFN-alpha was given subcutaneously at a dosage of 5 million units three times a week for 3 months, followed by a maintenance dose of 3 million units given subcutaneously three times a week for an additional 9 months. One hundred seven patients completed the study.
The study found that 26 (32.5%) of 80 HIV-infected patients and 10 (37.0%) of 27 non-HIV-infected patients achieved a complete response (normalization of aminotransferases and undetectable HCV RNA in the blood) after completing the treatment. Two variables were found to be independently associated with a response in HIV-infected patients: a CD4+ T lymphocyte count of > 500 x 10(6)/L and a baseline HCV viremia level of < 10(7) copies/mL. Relapses occurred in 30.8% of HIV-infected patients and 12.5% of non-HIV-infected patients in the 12 months following treatment.
In conclusion, our study suggests that IFN-alpha therapy can be effective in treating liver disease caused by HCV infection in HIV-infected patients, particularly those with higher CD4+ T lymphocyte counts and lower baseline HCV viremia levels. However, the study also showed that relapse rates remain high despite treatment, emphasizing the need for further research into more effective therapies for this patient population.

title: Vanishing cerebellar infarcts in a migraine patient.
text: Recent studies have suggested that migraine may be a risk factor for the development of infarct-like lesions in the posterior circulation. These lesions are thought to be true vascular infarcts based on their size, location, and MRI characteristics. However, due to the lack of postmortem studies on the pathology of these MRI findings, the true cause of these lesions remains unknown. A case of a patient with migraine who developed MRI-identified cerebellar infarcts is presented, which vanished on repeat imaging 16 days later, casting doubt on their vascular ischemic origin.

title: A novel viral transcript with homology to human interleukin-10 is expressed during latent human cytomegalovirus infection.
text: Human cytomegalovirus (CMV) establishes latent infections in hematopoietic cells, such as granulocyte-macrophage progenitors (GM-Ps). During latency, the virus is sequestered in a non-replicating state, although limited transcriptional activity has been observed in previous studies. In this study, we aimed to further investigate viral gene expression during the latent phase of infection. We used an experimental model of latency and extracted RNA from primary human GM-Ps that were latently infected with CMV strains Toledo, AD169, and Towne. Using reverse transcription-PCR, we detected transcription from the UL111.5A region of the viral genome. Interestingly, we found that this transcription was independent of the CMV strain and was also detected in healthy donors with natural latent infections. Further mapping experiments revealed the expression of a novel UL111.5A region transcript with a unique splicing pattern compared to that observed during productive infection in permissive cells. This UL111.5A region transcript encoded a 139-amino-acid protein with homology to the immunosuppressive cytokine interleukin-10 (IL-10) and the viral IL-10 homolog expressed during productive CMV infection. The expression of latency-associated cmvIL-10 may enable the virus to evade immune recognition and clearance during the latent phase of infection.

title: Treatments for somnambulism in adults: assessing the evidence.
text:
Sleepwalking, also known as somnambulism, is a type of parasomnia that occurs during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. During sleepwalking episodes, individuals display behaviors typically reserved for wakefulness, such as walking, crawling, or eating. If sleepwalking is causing distress or poses a danger to the individual despite safety measures, medical or psychological treatment may be necessary.
To assess treatment options, clinicians consulted various databases, including MEDLINE, EMBASE, PsycINFO, and the Ovid Evidence-Based Medicine Reviews (EBM) multifile databases. However, no high-quality, rigorously controlled trials were found for treating sleepwalking in adults. Of the seven reports identified, six were small trials with some kind of control arm or retrospective case series, involving 30 or more patients. Given the lack of strong evidence supporting specific treatments for sleepwalking, a thorough discussion with the patient is recommended.
Given the absence of rigorously controlled trials, clinicians must rely on less rigorous studies to inform treatment decisions. However, these studies have limitations, and further research is needed to provide high-quality evidence to guide treatment recommendations. Adequately powered, well-designed clinical trials are now required to obtain the sample sizes necessary to draw meaningful conclusions. Collaboration among multiple centers may be necessary to obtain the required sample sizes.

title: Premature chromosome condensation: evidence for in vivo cell fusion in human malignant tumours.
text: Studies on premature chromosome condensation (PCC) were conducted in tissue preparations from patients with various haematological diseases and carcinomas. Using the GTG technique, PCC was observed in 6 out of 166 malignancies (128 haematological cases and 35 carcinomas) examined. Chromosome analysis revealed that PCC occurred in S-phase and G1-phase in each case, with frequencies ranging from 1% to 8.6% of metaphases examined. These findings suggest that PCC chromosomes, which are thought to represent cell fusion in vivo, are not uncommon in naturally-occurring human malignancies. In combination with other factors, PCC may contribute to the heterogeneity of tumor cell populations.

title: Blockade of the angiotensin system improves mental health domain of quality of life: A meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
text:
The goal of this investigation was to assess the impact of inhibiting the angiotensin system on mental health. Specifically, we aimed to determine the effects of angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) blockers on various domains of quality of life (QoL) in adults without any major physical symptoms.
To achieve this objective, we conducted a meta-analysis of published studies that compared these medications to placebo or other antihypertensive drugs. We searched PubMed and clinicaltrials.gov databases and included randomized controlled trials that evaluated the QoL of adults taking ACE inhibitors or AT1R blockers versus those taking placebo or other medications. We followed PRISMA and Cochrane Collaboration guidelines for meta-analysis reporting.
Our analysis included 11 studies with a total of 17,426 participants. We found that ACE inhibitors and AT1R blockers were associated with improved overall QoL (difference = 0.11, 95% CI = 0.08, 0.14, p < 0.0001), positive wellbeing (difference = 0.11, 95% CI = 0.05, 0.17, p < 0.0001), mental health (difference = 0.15, 95% CI = 0.06, 0.25, p < 0.0001), and anxiety domains (difference = 0.08, 95% CI = 0.01, 0.16, p < 0.0001) of QoL compared to placebo or other medications. However, we found no significant difference in the depression domain (difference = 0.05, 95% CI = 0.02, 0.12, p = 0.15).
Our findings suggest that using ACE inhibitors and AT1R blockers to treat hypertension in otherwise healthy adults leads to improved mental health domains of QoL. Given the secondary nature of these studies, further research is necessary to more fully evaluate the utility of these medications as a novel psychiatric target.

title: The role of epigenetics in aging and autoimmunity.
text: As we age, our immune system declines, leading to an increase in the incidence of autoimmune diseases. This phenomenon, known as immunosenescence, is characterized by a decline in the function of both T cells and B cells, as well as the presence of low-grade chronic inflammation. Recent research has also shown that epigenetic changes, which refer to inherited changes in gene expression that are not encoded in the DNA sequence itself, occur with aging. Intriguingly, emerging evidence suggests that epigenetics play a significant role in human pathologies, including inflammatory and neoplastic disorders. In this review, we will explore the possible mechanisms that contribute to the rise in autoimmune responses in aging. Specifically, we will discuss how epigenetic alterations, such as DNA methylation and histone acetylation, accumulate with age and how these events increase the risk of autoimmunity.

title: A framework for understanding and targeting residual disease in oncogene-driven solid cancers
text: Molecular targeted therapy has the potential to significantly enhance survival rates in cancer patients. However, complete and sustainable responses to targeted therapy are uncommon in patients with advanced solid tumors. Even the most effective targeted therapies seldom induce a full tumor response, resulting in lingering disease and tumor progression that compromises patient survival. We pinpoint the growing need to comprehend the underlying molecular mechanisms that contribute to residual disease. This knowledge will lay the groundwork for designing therapeutic strategies to eradicate or restrict residual disease, permitting us to transition from temporary control of disease to long-term, or even total, remission for patients with advanced solid cancers. Ultimately, we advocate for a shift from the current reactive approach of monitoring and overcoming drug resistance to a proactive approach that focuses on identifying and neutralizing the mechanisms that instigate residual disease, thereby minimizing or eliminating this disease reservoir.

title: Long-term inhibition of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 in Alzheimer's prone mice.
text: In this study, we investigated the impact of long-term inhibition of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) with sitagliptin on the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD) in a transgenic mouse model. We found that daily doses of sitagliptin (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg) administered for 12 weeks significantly improved memory function in the contextual fear conditioning test. Additionally, treatment with sitagliptin increased the levels of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) in the brain, which is known to have neuroprotective effects. Furthermore, we observed significant reductions in nitrosative stress and inflammation within the brain, as well as a reduction in the number and area of beta-amyloid peptide (Abeta) deposits. The most notable effects were observed with the highest dose of 20 mg/kg sitagliptin. Our results suggest that long-term inhibition of DPP-4 with sitagliptin can significantly delay the progression of AD pathology, including Abeta deposition, when administered early in the disease course of transgenic mice.

title: Structural and mechanistic insights into phospholipid transfer by Ups1–Mdm35 in mitochondria
text: Eukaryotic cells are divided into specialized organelles, each with their own unique membranes, which are maintained through the efficient transportation of lipids. In this study, we specifically examined the Ups1-Mdm35 system, which plays a crucial role in the transfer of phosphatidic acid (PA) between the outer and inner mitochondrial membranes. Using X-ray crystallography, we determined the structures of Mdm35 and Ups1-Mdm35 with and without PA. The Ups1-Mdm35 complex forms a single domain with a distinct pocket and flexible lid. Through structure-based mutational analysis, we found that basic residues at the bottom of the pocket and the lid are essential for PA extraction from the membrane upon Ups1 binding. In addition, we discovered that the dissociation of Mdm35 enhances Ups1 binding to the membrane. Furthermore, we found that basic residues near the pocket entrance are critical for Ups1 binding and PA extraction from the membrane. These findings provide a structural basis for understanding the mechanisms of PA transfer between mitochondrial membranes.

title: Redox regulation of cell migration and adhesion.
text: Reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly hydrogen peroxide, and the enzymes that regulate them play a crucial role in the movement and bonding of cells. When cell surface receptors are stimulated by growth factors and chemoattractants, ROS are generated, which transmit signals from the cell surface to vital signaling proteins inside the cell. ROS inside the cell work to promote movement and also affect the behavior of migrating cells in nonmigrating cells. Hydrogen peroxide has additionally been proposed to act as a chemoattractant in its own right, drawing immune cells to injuries. We examine the latest advances in understanding how organisms utilize ROS and to what extent they depend on them during the processes of cell migration and adhesion.

title: Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome, Quick Sequential Organ Function Assessment, and Organ Dysfunction: Insights From a Prospective Database of ED Patients With Infection
text: Background: A recent revision to sepsis definitions has abandoned the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) and instead focuses on quick sequential organ failure assessment (qSOFA) as a bedside indicator of organ dysfunction. We aimed to (1) evaluate the prognostic impact of SIRS, (2) compare the diagnostic accuracy of SIRS and qSOFA for detecting organ dysfunction, and (3) compare the clinical utility of standard (Sepsis-2) and revised (Sepsis-3) definitions for organ dysfunction in emergency department (ED) patients with infections. Methods: We conducted a prospective study over three years, enrolling consecutive ED patients with suspected infection. Sufficient data were collected to calculate SIRS, qSOFA, sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA), comorbidity, and mortality. Results: We included 8,871 patients, of whom 4,176 (47.1%) had SIRS. SIRS was associated with an increased risk of organ dysfunction (relative risk 3.5) and mortality (odds ratio 3.2) in patients without organ dysfunction. SIRS and qSOFA showed similar ability to discriminate between patients with and without organ dysfunction (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.72 vs 0.73). qSOFA was specific but poorly sensitive for identifying organ dysfunction (96.1% and 29.7%, respectively). Mortality rates for patients with organ dysfunction were similar for Sepsis-2 and Sepsis-3 (12.5% vs 11.4%, respectively), although 29% of patients with Sepsis-3 organ dysfunction did not meet Sepsis-2 criteria. Increasing numbers of Sepsis-2 organ system dysfunctions were associated with greater mortality. Conclusions: While abandoning the concept of SIRS may be premature, qSOFA showed high specificity but poor sensitivity as a bedside screening method. Although mortality rates for organ dysfunction were similar for Sepsis-2 and Sepsis-3, more clinical and prognostic information is provided by Sepsis-2 regarding the number and type of organ dysfunctions. The SOFA score may require recalibration.

title: Requirement of NAD and SIR2 for life-span extension by calorie restriction in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: Caloric restriction promotes longer life span across a range of organisms, despite theories suggesting it may work by reducing oxygen species levels produced during respiration. The mechanism by which this regimen slows aging remains unclear. To investigate, we experimented with yeast using either physiological or genetic means to mimic caloric restriction, resulting in a significant extension of life span. Conversely, strains devoid of the SIR2 (which encodes the silencing protein Sir2p) or NPT1 (a gene involved in NAD oxidation) pathways did not exhibit this extended lifespan. These findings suggest that the increased longevity observed with caloric restriction requires the activation of Sir2p through NAD.

title: Pathways disrupted in human ALS motor neurons identified through genetic correction of mutant SOD1.
text: Although various genetic mutations have been identified as the root cause of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), researchers are still grappling to comprehend the intricacies of how these mutations specifically impact motor neuron biology. Specifically, it remains unclear whether these mutations converge onto a set of common pathways, leading to neuronal degeneration. To address this question, scientists have combined cutting-edge techniques such as reprogramming, stem cell differentiation, genome engineering, and RNA sequencing. By conducting these experiments, the group was able to uncover the transcriptional and functional changes that occur in human motor neurons as a result of mutant SOD1 protein. The study found that mutant SOD1 triggers a transcriptional signature indicative of enhanced oxidative stress, impaired mitochondrial function, disrupted subcellular transport, and activation of the ER stress and unfolded protein response pathways. Additionally, functional experiments revealed that these pathways are impacted in a manner that varies depending on the specific SOD1 mutation. Furthermore, the study found that similar changes are observed in motor neurons derived from ALS patients harboring a repeat expansion in C9orf72, suggesting that some of these changes may be more broadly conserved in ALS.

title: Effect of enalapril on 12-year survival and life expectancy in patients with left ventricular systolic dysfunction: a follow-up study.
text:
In the SOLVD (Studies of Left Ventricular Dysfunction) trials, enalapril reduced mortality in patients with symptomatic but not asymptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction during the original trial. To determine if this mortality reduction was sustained and if a subsequent reduction in mortality would emerge among those with asymptomatic ventricular dysfunction, we conducted a 12-year follow-up of the original SOLVD patients.
Of the 6797 patients enrolled in the SOLVD prevention and treatment trials, we identified the subsequent vital status of 5165 individuals who were alive when the trials ended. We conducted follow-up through direct contacts in Belgium and linkages with national death registries and federal beneficiary or historic tax summary files in the USA and Canada.
Our findings showed that follow-up was complete for 99.8% of the patients (6784/6797). In the prevention trial, 50.9% (1074/2111) of the enalapril group had died compared to 56.4% (1195/2117) of the placebo group (p=0.001). In the treatment trial, 79.8% (1025/1285) of the enalapril group had died compared to 80.8% (1038/1284) of the placebo group (p=0.01). The reductions in cardiac deaths were significant and similar in both trials. When data from the prevention and treatment trials were combined, the hazard ratio for death was 0.90 for the enalapril group compared to the placebo group (95% CI 0.84-0.95, p=0.0003). Enalapril extended median survival by 9.4 months in the combined trials (95% CI 2.8-16.5, p=0.004).
Our interpretation is that treatment with enalapril for 3-4 years led to a sustained improvement in survival beyond the original trial period in patients with left ventricular systolic dysfunction, resulting in a significant increase in life expectancy.

title: TGFbeta/activin/nodal signaling is necessary for the maintenance of pluripotency in human embryonic stem cells.
text: Human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) have the ability to self-renew indefinitely and give rise to cells from all three primary germ layers, yet the signaling mechanisms that sustain their pluripotency are poorly understood. To investigate, we focused on the transforming growth factor beta (TGFβ) superfamily of signaling pathways, as these play a crucial role in early cell fate decisions during embryonic development. Our findings reveal that hESCs exhibit distinct patterns of TGFβ signaling, with the TGFβ/activin/nodal branch being activated in undifferentiated cells and the BMP/GDF branch being only active in isolated mitotic cells. Upon early differentiation, TGFβ/activin/nodal signaling is decreased while BMP/GDF signaling is activated. We demonstrate that TGFβ/activin/nodal signaling is essential for maintaining the undifferentiated state of hESCs, and that this requirement is upstream of WNT signaling, which we have previously shown to be sufficient to maintain the undifferentiated state. Strikingly, we find that TGFβ signaling is also crucial in ex vivo mouse blastocyst cultures, where it maintains the inner cell mass (from which stem cells are derived). These findings reveal a critical role for TGFβ signaling in early cell fate determination and highlight an interconnectedness between TGFβ and WNT signaling in these contexts.

title: The structure and expression of a novel gene activated in early mouse embryogenesis.
text: We have investigated the cloning and determination of the mouse H19 gene sequence. This gene is controlled by two trans-acting loci in mice, referred to as raf and Rif, which determine the basal and inducible levels of H19 mRNA, respectively, as well as the mRNA for alpha-fetoprotein. By analyzing the sequence and structure of the H19 gene, we found that it is genetically distinct from the alpha-fetoprotein gene, indicating that the regulation of the H19 gene by raf and Rif occurred independently. Furthermore, the H19 gene has a unique structure, composed of five exons ranging in size from 1307 to 560 base pairs, along with four tiny introns totaling 270 bases. The largest open reading frame within the gene, which encodes a protein approximately 14 kDa, is entirely contained within the first large exon, located 680 base pairs downstream of the mRNA cap site. Prior to the translation initiation codon, there are four consecutive ATG codons followed by translation termination codons. The remaining gene, spanning all five exons, is assumed to be non-coding, although the long 5' untranslated region may play a role in regulating mRNA translation through in vitro translation studies. In vitro cell culture studies of mesodermal lineage cell lines suggest that the gene is activated early in muscle cell differentiation.

title: Diminished linear growth during intermittent calcitriol therapy in children undergoing CCPD.
text:
Medical Research Study: Intermittent Calcitriol Therapy and Linear Growth in Children with Renal Bone Disease
Background:
* Daily calcitriol therapy has been shown to improve linear growth in children with renal bone disease.
* 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D is a key regulator of chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation.
* Although large intermittent doses of calcitriol can lower serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels and reverse skeletal changes of secondary hyperparathyroidism, the impact of intermittent calcitriol therapy on linear growth in children is unknown.
* We conducted a 12-month prospective clinical trial of intermittent calcitriol therapy in 16 pre-pubertal patients with bone biopsy-proven secondary hyperparathyroidism.
* Biochemical results and growth data obtained during intermittent calcitriol therapy were compared to values determined during the preceding 12 months of daily calcitriol therapy in each study subject.
* Changes in bone histology were assessed after one year of intermittent calcitriol therapy.

Results:
* Z-scores for height did not change during 12 months of daily calcitriol therapy.
* Although skeletal lesions of secondary hyperparathyroidism improved in most patients, Z-scores for height decreased from -1.8 ± 0.32 to -2.0 ± 0.33, P < 0.01, during intermittent calcitriol therapy. The largest reductions were seen in patients who developed adynamic bone lesions after 12 months of treatment.
* Delta Z-scores for height correlated with serum PTH, r = 0.71, P < 0.01, and alkaline phosphatase levels, r = 0.67, P < 0.01, during intermittent calcitriol therapy but not during daily calcitriol therapy.

Conclusion:

* The data suggest that high-dose intermittent calcitriol therapy adversely affects linear growth, particularly in patients with the adynamic lesion.
* The higher doses of calcitriol or the intermittent schedule of calcitriol administration may directly inhibit chondrocyte activity within growth plate cartilage of children with end-stage renal disease.

Note: Z-scores are a standardized measure of growth, where a Z-score of 0 represents the median value for a given age and sex group. Positive Z-scores indicate growth above the median, while negative Z-scores indicate growth below the median.

title: Comparison of pain syndromes associated with nervous or somatic lesions and development of a new neuropathic pain diagnostic questionnaire (DN4)
text: Numerous studies have yet to directly compare the clinical features of neuropathic and non-neuropathic pains. To fill this knowledge gap, the French Neuropathic Pain Group developed a comprehensive questionnaire, the DN4, consisting of sensory descriptors and signs related to bedside sensory examination. This questionnaire was administered to 160 patients with pain associated with a neurlogical or somatic lesion in a prospective study. The most common underlying neurological disorders (n=89) included traumatic nerve injury, post herpetic neuralgia, and post-stroke pain, while osteoarthritis, inflammatory arthropathies, and mechanical low back pain were the non-neurological disorders (n=71). Two expert clinicians independently assessed each patient to confirm the diagnosis of neuropathic or non-neuropathic pain. The questionnaire's psychometric properties, including face validity, inter-rater reliability, factor analysis, and logistic regression, were also examined to determine the Discriminant properties of individual items or combinations of items for the diagnosis of neuropathic pain. Our findings indicate that a relatively small number of questions are sufficient to distinguish neuropathic pain. The 10-item DN4 questionnaire developed in this study can serve as a valuable diagnostic instrument in both clinical research and everyday practice.

title: Changing the density of alcohol outlets to reduce alcohol-related problems.
text: As legal and political debates surrounding the issuance of new liquor licenses continue to evolve, a growing focus has emerged on the potential impact of alcohol outlet density on alcohol consumption and related harm. However, a thorough examination of the evidence on this topic has yet to be conducted. In this Harm Reduction Digest, Livingston, Chikritzhs, and Room systematically review the research literature on the effects of alcohol sales outlet density on alcohol consumption and related problems, propose a novel framework for understanding these relationships, and discuss the implications for reducing alcohol-related harm.

title: [Pharmacokinetics and biotransformation of the antimycotic drug ciclopiroxolamine in animals and man after topical and systemic administration].
text:
1. Following the topical application of carbon-14 labelled broad-spectrum antimicrobial ciclopiroxolamine (Hoe 296, Batrafen) in the form of a 1% aqueous cream to healthy human skin (penetration time: 6 hours; occlusive dressing for 5 hours), the drug was found to account for approximately 1.3% of the applied dose through percutaneous absorption. Excretion occurred primarily through the kidneys, with biological half-lives of 1.7 hours. Interestingly, even after 5 hours of occclusion, the highest concentrations of ciclopiroxolamine were detected in the stratum corneum, with values ranging from 2300 to 4500 micrograms per cubic centimeter. The levels determined in the corium remained above the minimum inhibitory concentrations throughout the 6-hour penetration period. Using histoautoradiography, it was found that ciclopiroxolamine can penetrate the skin through both the epidermis and hair follicles. When applied to fingernails, the radioactive-labelled compound penetrated right through the nail. In comparison to humans, dogs exhibited higher percutaneous absorption, with approximately 5-15% of the dose being absorbed.
2. After vaginal application (1 mg/kg) of ciclopiroxolamine in the form of a 1% aqueous cream to bitches, between 42 and 97% of the dose was recovered in the urine and faeces, with the remainder having penetrated into the tampon used to close the vagina.
3. Ciclopiroxolamine is primarily excreted in the urine of dogs and humans as a glucuronide, with minor amounts as other conjugated, non-polar metabolites. The metabolite patterns after oral and dermal application were found to be similar. The binding of ciclopiroxolamine to serum proteins in humans was found to be approximately 96 ± 2% in a concentration range of 0.01-11.0 micrograms per milliliter.
4. Placental transfer of ciclopiroxolamine was found to be low in rats, with good absorption by the mother animal but low levels of radioactivity in the foetal tissues relative to maternal blood.

title: Maximizing the diagnostic utility of endoscopic biopsy in dogs and cats with gastrointestinal disease.
text: Flexible endoscopy has become a crucial tool for diagnostic purposes in small animal gastrointestinal (GI) diseases, but its effectiveness depends on careful technique and attention to detail. This review assesses the current diagnostic utility of flexible endoscopy, including practical and technical considerations for endoscopic biopsy, optimal instrumentation for mucosal specimen collection, correlations with clinical activity and histopathologic findings, and recent developments in endoscopic diagnosis of GI disease. Recent studies have established guidelines for endoscopic biopsy, including the optimal number and quality of diagnostic specimens from different regions of the gut. These studies have also demonstrated the value of ileal biopsy in the diagnosis of canine and feline chronic enteropathies and the utility of endoscopic biopsy specimens beyond routine histopathological analysis, including their use in immunohistochemical, microbiological, and molecular studies.

title: Age-structured red blood cell susceptibility and the dynamics of malaria infections.
text: The relationship between malaria parasites and the immune responses of an infected individual is a complex and dynamic interaction that is not well understood. While the dynamics of parasite populations are relatively unexplored, they offer unique insights into the processes that control most malaria infections. Our focus on the observation that three out of four malaria-parasite species are restricted to particular age classes of red blood cells (RBCs) allows us to explicitly incorporate this observation into models of infection dynamics, distinguishing common from species-specific pressures on host immune responses. We find that age structuring has profound effects on the course of infection, with catastrophic anemia occurring even with the two species that attack only the youngest RBCs, although only a small fraction of cells are parasitized at any point. Furthermore, with these two species, compensatory erythropoetic responses in the host accelerate parasite population growth, leading to differences in outcomes that we characterize as a "basic reproduction rate."

title: Helicobacter pylori AlpA and AlpB bind host laminin and influence gastric inflammation in gerbils.
text: The bacteria Helicobacter pylori persistently colonizes the human stomach, leading to gastritis, ulcers, and gastric cancer. Exploration has revealed that adherence to the stomach lining is enhanced through inflammation, although few H. pylori adhesins have been connected to host tissue targets. The alpAB region is known to hold adhesins involved in adherence to human gastric tissue. Our findings demonstrate that abrogating H. pylori AlpA and AlpB reduces the bacteria's ability to bind to laminin, a crucial component of the stomach lining. Conversely, introducing plasmids bearing alpA or alpB renders Escherichia coli capable of binding to laminin. The absence of AlpB, but not AlpA, in an H. pylori strain results in a loss of laminin binding. Therefore, we have determined that both AlpA and AlpB contribute to H. pylori's capacity to bind to laminin. Surprisingly, the H. pylori SS1 mutant lacking AlpA and AlpB leads to more pronounced inflammation than the isogenic wild-type strain in gerbils. By identifying laminin as the target of AlpA and AlpB, future studies will be better equipped to investigate host-pathogen interactions that occur during H. pylori infection.

title: A quantitative analysis of kinase inhibitor selectivity
text: Kinase inhibitors are a promising new class of drugs that have the potential to target multiple proteins within the body. However, the full scope of their biological effects is not yet fully understood, particularly with regards to their interaction with the vast array of kinases present in the human body. To address this knowledge gap, we have generated a comprehensive map of how 38 kinase inhibitors interact with a panel of 317 kinases, representing over 50% of the predicted human protein kinome. This data provides the most detailed examination of kinase inhibitor selectivity to date and reveals a diverse range of interaction patterns. To facilitate a global analysis of the results, we have developed a novel tool - the selectivity score - which allows us to quantify and differentiate the various interaction patterns observed. By investigating the impact of panel size on our findings, we have also discovered that smaller assay panels are not a reliable measure of selectivity.

title: Ribosomal protein S9 is a novel B23/NPM-binding protein required for normal cell proliferation.
text: B23 (NPM/nucleophosmin) is a versatile protein that plays a crucial role in embryonic development, genomic stability, and anti-apoptotic signaling. As a member of the nucleoplasmin superfamily of acidic histone chaperones, B23 is also involved in ribosome biogenesis. While its molecular function is not fully understood, B23 has been shown to interact with a complex consisting of ribosomal proteins and RNA helicases. Our study investigated the interaction between B23 and ribosomal protein S9 (RPS9) and found that S9 binding requires an intact B23 oligomerization domain. Depletion of S9 by small interfering RNA (siRNA) resulted in decreased protein synthesis and G(1) cell cycle arrest, accompanied by induction of p53 target genes. We also discovered that S9 is a short-lived protein in the absence of ribosome biogenesis, and proteasomal inhibition significantly increased S9 protein levels. Overexpression of B23 facilitated nucleolar storage of S9, while knockdown of B23 led to decreased levels of nucleolar S9. Our findings suggest that B23 selectively stores and protects S9 in nucleoli, which could potentially facilitate ribosome biogenesis.

title: Vasculature-associated cells expressing nestin in developing bones encompass early cells in the osteoblast and endothelial lineage.
text: In adult bone marrow, Nestin-positive (Nes(+)) cells play a crucial role in supporting hematopoiesis. However, little is known about their origin during endochondral bone development. By using mice expressing GFP under the direction of nestin promoter/enhancer (Nes-GFP), studies have revealed two distinct populations of Nes(+) cells in the embryonic perichondrium: endothelial and non-endothelial cells. The latter are early osteoblast lineage cells that descend from their progenitors upon Indian hedgehog signaling and Runx2 expression. During vascular invasion and ossification center formation, these Nes(+) cells are closely associated with each other and increase in number progressively. Interestingly, when tamoxifen-inducible cre recombinase was driven by the nestin enhancer (Nes-creER) in developing bone marrow, the majority of cells targeted were endothelial cells. Additionally, Nes(+) cells in postnatal bones are composed of a heterogeneous population, including cells in the osteoblast and endothelial lineages. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized complexity in stromal cell populations, highlighting the role of Nes(+) cells as early vasculature-associated cells in the osteoblast and endothelial lineages.

title: Public health, academic medicine, and the alcohol industry's corporate social responsibility activities.
text: Our investigation into the evolving dynamics between the alcohol industry, academic medicine, and the public health sector revealed a complex web of relationships within the context of public health theory focusing on corporate social responsibility. Specifically, we analyzed the sponsorship of scientific research, attempts to shape public perceptions of research findings, dissemination of scientific information, and industry-backed policy initiatives. As the scientific evidence clearly supports reducing alcohol consumption through regulatory and legal measures, the academic community has increasingly clashed with the alcohol industry's views. Our analysis indicates that the alcohol industry has stepped up its scientific and policy-related activities under the guise of corporate social responsibility initiatives, with most of these efforts serving the industry's economic interests.

title: RET, ROS1 and ALK fusions in lung cancer
text: Through an integrated molecular- and histopathology-based screening system, we conducted a screening for fusions of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) and c-ros oncogene 1, receptor tyrosine kinase (ROS1) in 1,529 lung cancers and identified 44 ALK-fusion–positive and 13 ROS1-fusion–positive adenocarcinomas, including unidentified fusion partners for ROS1 in some cases. Additionally, we discovered previously unidentified kinase fusions that could be potential targets for molecular-targeted therapy, such as kinesin family member 5B (KIF5B)-ret proto-oncogene (RET) and coiled-coil domain containing 6 (CCDC6)-RET in 14 adenocarcinomas. A multivariate analysis of 1,116 adenocarcinomas, including 71 kinase-fusion–positive adenocarcinomas, revealed four independent factors that are prognostic indicators: age ≥50 years, male sex, high pathological stage, and negative kinase-fusion status.

title: Genetic and biochemical interactions among Yar1, Ltv1 and Rps3 define novel links between environmental stress and ribosome biogenesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: In the yeast species Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the assembly of ribosomes is influenced by environmental conditions through the coordinated transcriptional regulation of genes involved in ribosome biogenesis. This study demonstrates that two nonessential stress-responsive genes, YAR1 and LTV1, play a role in the production of 40S subunits. Genetic and biochemical evidence shows that Yar1, a small ankyrin-repeat protein, physically interacts with RpS3, a component of the 40S subunit, and with Ltv1, a protein recently identified as a substoichiometric component of a 43S preribosomal particle. The findings suggest that cells lacking YAR1 or LTV1 are sensitive to certain protein synthesis inhibitors and exhibit abnormal polysome profiles, with a reduced number of 40S subunits and an excess of free 60S subunits. Surprisingly, both mutants are also sensitive to a variety of environmental stress conditions. Overexpression of RPS3 suppresses both the stress sensitivity and the ribosome biogenesis defect of Deltayar1 mutants, but does not suppress either defect in Deltaltv1 mutants. The study reveals that YAR1 and LTV1 play distinct, nonessential roles in 40S subunit production, and the stress-sensitive phenotypes of strains lacking these genes uncover a previously unknown link between ribosome biogenesis factors and environmental stress sensitivity.

title: Rational design of acridine-based ligands with selectivity for human telomeric quadruplexes.
text: Structure-based modeling techniques have been employed to design a series of disubstituted triazole-linked acridine compounds with selectivity for human telomeric quadruplex DNA. A focused library of these compounds was prepared using click chemistry, and the selectivity concept was validated against two promoter quadruplexes from the c-kit gene with known molecular structures, as well as with duplex DNA using a FRET-based melting method. Lead compounds were found to exhibit reduced effects on the thermal stability of the c-kit quadruplexes and duplex DNA structures. These effects were further explored with a series of competition experiments, which confirmed that binding to duplex DNA is negligible even at high duplex:telomeric quadruplex ratios. Selectivity towards the c-kit quadruplexes is more complex, with some evidence of their stabilization at increasing excess over human telomeric quadruplex DNA. The unique dimensions of the triazole-acridine compounds, particularly the separation of the two alkyl-amino terminal groups, contribute to their selectivity. Moreover, both lead compounds have shown selective inhibitory effects on the proliferation of cancer cell lines compared to a normal cell line, and one has been demonstrated to inhibit the activity of the telomerase enzyme, which is selectively expressed in tumor cells where it plays a role in maintaining telomere integrity and cellular immortalization.

title: Hospital volume and the outcomes of mechanical ventilation.
text: An analysis of data from 37 acute care hospitals in the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation (APACHE) clinical information system found that a higher volume of patients admitted to a hospital is associated with improved survival outcomes among patients receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU) and within the hospital. Specifically, admission to a hospital in the highest quartile according to volume (i.e., >400 patients receiving mechanical ventilation per year) was associated with a 37% reduction in the adjusted odds of death in the ICU compared to admission to hospitals in the lowest quartile (< or =150 patients receiving mechanical ventilation per year, P<0.001). Similarly, in-hospital mortality was reduced (adjusted odds ratio, 0.66; 95% confidence interval, 0.52 to 0.83; P<0.001). Compared to a typical patient in a hospital in a low-volume quartile, a patient in a hospital in a high-volume quartile had a significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality of 25.5% compared to 34.2%. Among survivors, there were no significant trends in the length of stay in the ICU or the hospital. The study suggests that the relationship between hospital volume and outcome among patients with a critical illness is real and warrants further investigation to determine the underlying mechanism.

title: A meta-analysis of depression during pregnancy and the risk of preterm birth, low birth weight, and intrauterine growth restriction.
text:
This article examines the association between antenatal depression and adverse birth outcomes, including preterm birth (PTB), low birth weight (LBW), and intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR). The study included 29 prospective studies from the United States and non-US countries, published between 1980 and 2009. The findings showed that women with antenatal depression are at increased risk for these adverse birth outcomes, with significant differences observed across different study populations.
The analysis found that women who experienced antenatal depression had a significantly higher risk of PTB (1.39-1.61), LBW (1.25-1.77), and IUGR (1.05-2.02) compared to those without depression. However, the magnitude of the effect varied depending on the measurement of depression, country location, and socioeconomic status. Specifically, the risk of LBW was found to be significantly higher in developing countries (2.05) compared to the United States (1.10) or European social democracies (1.16). Additionally, categorically defined antenatal depression was associated with an increased risk of PTB among women of lower socioeconomic status in the United States.
The study's findings suggest that antenatal depression should be identified through universal screening and treated to reduce the risk of adverse birth outcomes. The study highlights the importance of early detection and intervention for women with antenatal depression to optimize birth outcomes.

title: ES cell pluripotency and germ-layer formation require the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling component BAF250a.
text: ATP-driven chromatin remodeling complexes are a notable class of epigenetic modulators that harness the energy from ATP hydrolysis to alter the structure of chromatin, thus impacting the accessibility of nuclear factors. BAF250a (ARID1a) is a distinct subunit of the BAF chromatin remodeling complex, with the potential to facilitate crucial chromosomal rearrangements during development. Our studies have shown that ablatating BAF250a in early mouse embryos leads to developmental arrest at around embryonic day 6.5 and the absence of the mesodermal layer, highlighting its essential role in early germ layer formation. Moreover, BAF250a deficiency impairs embryonic stem (ES) cell pluripotency, strongly reduces self-renewal, and promotes differentiation into primitive endoderm-like cells under normal feeder-free culture conditions. Interestingly, this phenotype can be partially rescued by the presence of embryonic fibroblast cells. DNA microarray, immunostaining, and RNA analyses have revealed that BAF250a-mediated chromatin remodeling contributes to the proper expression of numerous genes involved in ES cell self-renewal, including Sox2, Utf1, and Oct4. Furthermore, the pluripotency defects in BAF250a-mutant ES cells appear to be lineage-specific, with BAF250a-ablated stem cells displaying a defect in differentiating into fully functional mesoderm-derived cardiomyocytes and adipocytes but being capable of differentiating into ectoderm-derived neurons.
