Our findings revealed that cord blood-graft recipients approximated the TCR diversity of healthy individuals after six months, while recipients of T cell-depleted peripheral-blood stem cell grafts exhibited significant deficits in CD4+ and CD8+ T cell diversity, with a 28-fold and 14-fold reduction, respectively, compared to healthy individuals. Notably, the deficits in CD8+ T cell diversity persisted beyond 12 months. This novel approach provides unprecedented insights into T cell repertoire recovery after allo-HSCT and may enable the identification of high-risk patients for infection or relapse.

title: Silver sulfadiazine for the treatment of partial-thickness burns and venous stasis ulcers.
text:
Background: Silver-containing antibiotics, such as silver sulfadiazine (SSD), have been used as a standard topical treatment for decades to improve burn and ulcer healing. However, there is limited evidence to support its effectiveness in ambulatory patients with partial-thickness burns or venous stasis ulcers. This review aims to address the following research question: Does the use of topical SSD in ambulatory patients with partial-thickness burns or stasis dermatitis ulcers improve mortality, wound healing, re-epithelialization, or infection rates compared to non-antibiotic dressings?
Methods: We conducted a systematic review of the literature using databases such as MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library. We included studies that enrolled patients with partial-thickness burns or venous stasis ulcers and randomized them to either topical SSD or placebo, saline-soaked gauze, paraffin gauze, sterile dry dressing, or non-antibiotic moist dressing. Outcome measures included mortality, wound healing, speed of re-epithelialization, and infection rates.
Results: Our search revealed 400 potential articles for burns and 50 articles for stasis dermatitis ulcers. However, after reviewing 20 abstracts, only one article met the inclusion criteria. This study found no significant improvement in the rate of complete healing in the SSD group compared to the placebo group at 4 weeks (relative risk 6.2, 95% confidence interval 0.8-48) or 1 year (relative risk 5.2, 95% confidence interval 0.6-41.6) of follow-up.
Conclusion: The evidence is insufficient to support the routine use of SSD for ambulatory patients with either partial-thickness burns or stasis dermatitis ulcers. Further research is needed to determine its effectiveness in these patient populations.

title: Putting p53 in Context
text: TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancer, and its dysfunction is a hallmark of malignant transformation. When activated by a variety of stressors, p53 coordinates a complex network of transcriptional responses that regulate multiple biological processes. Despite significant progress in understanding the intricate mechanisms of the p53 network, the full scope of its tumor-suppressive activities and how they are modulated by cell type, mutation profile, and epigenetic cell state remain poorly characterized. Unraveling the complex interplay between p53 and these factors is crucial to deciphering the consequences of p53 dysfunction in cancer, and ultimately, to developing effective strategies for restoring its tumor-suppressive functions in cancer treatment.

title: Modeling the evolution of culture-adapted human embryonic stem cells.
text: Long-term cultures of human embryonic stem (ES) cells are inherently prone to evolutionary changes, as any mutant with an growth advantage will be selectively amplified. However, the influence of evolutionary factors such as population size, mutation rate, and selection pressure on the growth and spread of mutant ES cells is often overlooked. To address this gap in knowledge, we developed a Monte Carlo simulation model to predict how variations in these factors affect the emergence and spread of mutant ES cells. We verified the accuracy of our model by comparing it with in vitro data. Our simulation highlights the significance of population size in reducing the likelihood of abnormal cultures developing, providing an estimate of the expected rate of generation of culture-adapted ES cells under different assumptions regarding key parameters. In essence, our findings emphasize the importance of considering evolutionary factors when working with long-term cultures of ES cells.

title: CD28 delivers a unique signal leading to the selective recruitment of RelA and p52 NF-kappaB subunits on IL-8 and Bcl-xL gene promoters.
text: CD28 is a crucial costimulatory receptor required for full T cell activation. CD28 enhances T cell antigen receptor (TCR) signals and sends independent signals, as shown by its ability to generate TCR-independent signals that lead to IκB kinase and NF-κB activation. In this study, we found that the TCR-independent CD28 signal leads to the selective transcription of survival (Bcl-xL) and inflammatory (IL-8 and B cell activation factor, but not proliferative (IL-2), genes in a NF-κB-dependent manner. CD28-stimulated T cells actively secrete IL-8, and Bcl-xL up-regulation protects T cells from radiation-induced apoptosis. The transcription of CD28-induced genes is mediated by the specific recruitment of RelA and p52 NF-κB subunits to target promoters. In contrast, p50 and c-Rel, which preferentially bind NF-κB sites on the IL-2 gene promoter after anti-CD3 stimulation, are not involved. Therefore, we have identified CD28 as a key regulator of genes important for both survival and inflammation.

title: Netting neutrophils are major inducers of type I IFN production in pediatric systemic lupus erythematosus.
text: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by a breakdown of tolerance to nuclear antigens and the formation of immune complexes. Recent genomic studies have shown that SLE white blood cells exhibit homogeneous expression of type I interferon (IFN)-induced and neutrophil-related transcripts. Elevated production and/or availability of IFN-α have been linked to SLE pathogenesis, and alterations in dendritic cell (DC) homeostasis may also play a role. Neutrophils, which have historically been associated with SLE, have remained obscure in terms of their role in disease pathogenesis. However, our study suggests that mature SLE neutrophils are primed in vivo by type I IFN and undergo programmed cell death upon exposure to anti-ribonucleoprotein antibodies, releasing neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). NETs contain significant amounts of DNA and LL37 and HMGB1, neutrophil proteins that facilitate the uptake and recognition of mammalian DNA by plasmacytoid DCs (pDCs). Furthermore, NETs have been shown to activate pDCs to produce high levels of IFN-α in a DNA- and TLR9 (Toll-like receptor 9)-dependent manner. Our findings uncover a novel role for neutrophils in SLE pathogenesis and highlight a previously unknown connection between nucleic acid-recognizing antibodies and type I IFN production in this disease.

title: Assessment for selection for the health care professions and specialty training: consensus statement and recommendations from the Ottawa 2010 Conference.
text: The evaluation of candidates for medicine and health professions should follow the same quality assurance processes as in-course assessment. The literature on selection is limited and lacks theoretical or conceptual rigor. For written assessments, there is evidence that the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) has predictive validity for medical school and licensing examination performance. Additionally, there is evidence that grade point average, particularly in combination with MCAT, has predictive validity for graduate entry. However, there is limited evidence on the predictive validity of school leaver scores. Interviews have not been shown to be effective selection tools. Studies of multiple mini-interviews have revealed good predictive validity and reliability. The use of personality testing in selection is an area that warrants further research. With the growing priority of widening access to medical and health professional programs, there is a need to address the social accountability mandate of medical and health professional schools. While traditional selection measures may discriminate against certain population groups, there is limited evidence on the effectiveness of non-traditional measures in widening access. Preparation and outreach programs show the most promise. In summary, there are only a few areas of consensus in assessment for selection, and recommendations for future action focus on the adoption of good assessment practices, the use of multi-method programmatic approaches, the development of interdisciplinary frameworks, and the utilization of sophisticated measurement models. The social accountability mandate of medical and health professional schools requires that social inclusion, workforce issues, and widening of access be embedded in the principles of good assessment for selection.

title: THE GLYOXAL BIS(2-HYDROXYANIL) METHOD MODIFIED FOR LOCALIZING INSOLUBLE CALCIUM SALTS.
text:
To facilitate staining of insoluble calcium salts with glyoxal bis(2-hydroxyanil) (GBHA), the original solution containing 2 ml of 0.4% GBHA in absolute ethanol and 0.3 ml of aqueous 5% NaOH was modified as follows:
1. Modification I: 1 ml of 0.4% GBHA in 0.6 ml of 10% aqueous NaOH was added to 2 ml of absolute ethanol. This mixture was evaporated gradually to dryness on the section to concentrate the GBHA and NaOH on the insoluble calcium salts.
2. Modification II: 0.1 gm GBHA was dissolved in 2 ml of 3.4% NaOH in 75% ethanol. The solution was applied to the section and allowed to stain for 5 minutes. The stained sections were then rinsed and counterstained in 95% ethanol containing 0.1% each of fast green and fast red to enhance the visibility of the calcium deposits.
To ensure specificity of the stain, the stained slides were immersed in a solution of 90% ethanol saturated with potassium cyanide (KCN) and sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) for 15 minutes. The slides were then rinsed and observed under a microscope for the presence of calcium deposits.

title: Detecting selective sweeps: a new approach based on hidden markov models.
text: Recent advancements in detecting and locating selective sweeps using SNP data have garnered significant interest. Here, we introduce the use of hidden Markov models (HMMs) for identifying selective sweeps in DNA sequences. In contrast to traditional methods, our HMMs explicitly model the correlation structure between adjacent sites, providing improved detection capabilities. Our techniques possess similar detection power and accuracy as other methods when applied to constant-sized populations, but outperform them in the context of population bottlenecks, with fewer false positives.

title: A Balance between Secreted Inhibitors and Edge Sensing Controls Gastruloid Self-Organization.
text:
The earliest stages of human embryonic development remain shrouded in mystery. To model these events, we utilized colonies of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) grown on microscopically patterned surfaces and differentiated with BMP4. These structures, termed gastruloids, recapitulate the arrangement of the mammalian germ layers and provide a platform to investigate the mechanisms governing structure and signaling during human embryonic development.
Structurally, the hESCs in gastruloids display novel patterns of receptor localization. At their lateral sides, these cells locate their receptors in close proximity to the transforming growth factor β, while maintaining apical receptor expression at the colony's edges. This redistribution of receptors shields cells in the center of the colony from apical ligands while maintaining responsiveness to basal signals. Additionally, BMP4 directs the expression of its own inhibitor, NOGGIN, resulting in a reaction-diffusion mechanism that underlies patterning.
To better understand these mechanisms and predict human fate positioning in gastruloids and the human embryo, we developed a quantitative model integrating edge sensing and inhibitors. This model provides a framework for analyzing the complex interplay between these factors and their role in shaping human development.

title: Tenectin is a novel alphaPS2betaPS integrin ligand required for wing morphogenesis and male genital looping in Drosophila.
text: The morphogenesis of adult structures in holometabolous insects, such as flies, is regulated by two key hormones: ecdysteroids and juvenile hormones. Cell-cell interactions play a crucial role in this process, and integrin receptors on the cell surface are mediators of these interactions. However, the characterization of adhesion molecules and their regulation by hormones is not well understood. To address this knowledge gap, we investigated the gene structure of a newly discovered extracellular matrix (ECM) molecule called tenectin. We found that tenectin is a hormonally regulated ECM protein essential for proper adult wing and male genitalia morphogenesis. Our experiments also reveal that tenectin functions as a novel ligand of the PS2 integrins, which are expressed on the surface of cells. The interaction between tenectin and PS2 integrins is dependent on specific motifs, such as RGD and RGD-like sequences. Our findings suggest that PS integrins play a role in the execution of left-right asymmetry during development of the male genitalia.

title: Schedule-dependent interaction between anticancer treatments
text:
The oncogene MDMX is overexpressed in many cancer cells, which leads to the suppression of the tumor suppressor protein p53. Inhibiting MDMX could potentially reactivate p53 and enhance the effectiveness of drugs that damage DNA. However, we currently lack a comprehensive understanding of how MDMX inhibition affects the p53 signaling pathway and cellular sensitivity to DNA damage.
Using live cell imaging, we discovered that when MDMX is depleted in single cells, two distinct phases of p53 accumulation occur: an initial postmitotic pulse followed by low-amplitude oscillations. These phases have different effects on the response to DNA damage: in the first phase, MDMX depletion enhances the damage caused by DNA by increasing cell death, while in the second phase, depletion of MDMX actually reduces cell death.
Therefore, gaining a detailed understanding of the signaling dynamics and cellular states is crucial for designing the most effective schedule for administering dual drugs that target MDMX and DNA damage.

title: Potent, Selective, and Orally Bioavailable Inhibitors of VPS34 Provide Chemical Tools to Modulate Autophagy in Vivo.
text: Autophagy is a complex process that controls the degradation of cellular components through lysosomal mechanisms. until recently, the study of autophagy has been hindered by the lack of effective drug targets. However, recent advances have led to the development of selective inhibitors of VPS34, a key player in the PI 3-kinase signaling pathway required for autophagy. In this study, we report the discovery of highly potent and selective VPS34 inhibitors, their pharmacokinetic properties, and their ability to inhibit autophagy in cell and animal models.

title: The role of neutrophils in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus.
text:
Recent findings have implicated neutrophils as critical regulators of the innate and adaptive immune systems, as well as in the development of organ damage in systemic autoimmune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Emerging evidence suggests that various putative SLE biomarkers, such as neutrophil-derived proteins and histones undergoing post-translational modifications during neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, may play a significant role in the pathogenesis of this disease. Furthermore, the bone marrow environment, where lupus neutrophils are observations, may contribute to the development of B and T cell abnormalities, at least in part, through the enhanced production of cytokines, including type-I interferons, tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNFα), and B-cell activating factors (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) by lupus neutrophils. Additionally, lupus neutrophils and, in particular, lupus low-density granulocytes (a distinct pathogenic subset) exhibit epigenetic modifications and genomic alterations that may be relevant to their deleterious roles in SLE. Notably, proteins and enzymes externalized by NETs can affect vascular health by inducing endothelial apoptosis and oxidizing lipoproteins, creating a favorable environment for atherosclerosis. Inhibiting NET formation through peptidylarginine deiminase inhibitors has been shown to abrogate the lupus phenotype and atherosclerosis in murine studies, suggesting the potential of targeting these immunostimulatory pathways in this disease.
In conclusion, recent discoveries support the notion that neutrophils, low-density granulocytes, and abnormal NET formation and clearance play significant roles in the pathogenesis of SLE. Future investigations should focus on developing strategies to selectively target these immunostimulatory pathways, with the goal of developing more effective and safer treatments for this disease.

title: Enhancement of proteasome function by PA28α overexpression protects against oxidative stress.
text: The principal function of the proteasome is the targeted degradation of intracellular proteins, and dysfunction of the proteasome has been implicated in various cardiovascular diseases, including experimental cardiomyopathies and human congestive heart failure. Currently, there are no measures to enhance the proteolytic function of the proteasome, but such interventions could have significant therapeutic potential. The association of the proteasome activator 28 (PA28) with the 20S proteasome may also play a role in antigen processing. However, it is unclear whether PA28 plays any important role outside of antigen presentation. Our study shows that overexpressing PA28α (PA28αOE) in cultured neonatal rat cardiomyocytes leads to increased levels of 11S proteasomes and enhanced degradation of a validated proteasome surrogate substrate (GFPu). PA28αOE also attenuates increases in protein carbonyls and suppresses apoptosis in cultured cardiomyocytes under basal conditions or upon exposure to oxidative stress. Our findings suggest that PA28αOE can up-regulate 11S proteasomes, enhance proteasome-mediated protein degradation, and protect against oxidative stress in cardiomyocytes, providing a promising means to increase the removal of abnormal cellular proteins.

title: A unified concept of species and its consequences for the future of taxonomy
text: Species concepts are diverse today, yet they all share a fundamental idea: species are segments of lineages at the population level of biological organization. However, they differ in secondary properties, such as reproductive isolation, monophyly, and diagnosability, which are treated as necessary for considering lineages to be species. A unified species concept exists by interpreting the common fundamental idea of being a separately evolving lineage segment as the only necessary property of species and viewing the various secondary properties as lines of evidence relevant to assessing lineage separation or as properties that define different subcategories of the species category, such as reproductively isolated species, monophyletic species, and diagnosable species. This unified concept has significant implications for taxonomy, including the recognition of undifferentiated and undiagnosable lineages as species, the ability of species to fuse, the nesting of species within other species, the non-ranking nature of the species category, and the need for novel taxonomic practices and conventions to accommodate these conclusions. Although accepting a unified species concept has radical implications for taxonomy, it reflects a long-standing shift in the general conceptualization of the species category, from viewing it as one member of a taxonomic hierarchy to viewing it as a natural kind whose members are the fundamental units of biology. This shift is part of a broader shift in the scope of systematics (including taxonomy) from classifying organisms to testing hypotheses about lineage boundaries and phylogenetic relationships. The unified species concept represents the fuller acceptance of the idea that species are a fundamental level of biology, and is, therefore, central to the future of taxonomy.

title: Regulation of the small GTP-binding protein Rho by cell adhesion and the cytoskeleton.
text: Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) present in serum is thought to activate the small GTP-binding protein Rho through its ability to induce actin stress fibers and focal adhesions in a Rho-dependent manner. However, the role of cell adhesion to extracellular matrices (ECM) in Rho activation has been a topic of debate due to the challenge of distinguishing changes in Rho activity from the structural contributions of ECM to the formation of focal adhesions. To address these questions, we developed an assay to measure GTP-bound cellular Rho. When Swiss 3T3 cells were plated on fibronectin-coated dishes, a transient inhibition of Rho was followed by a phase of Rho activation. This activation was enhanced by serum, indicating the involvement of soluble factors. In addition, we found that adherent cells showed a transient Rho activation in response to LPA, while suspended cells exhibited sustained Rho activation. Furthermore, suspended cells had higher Rho activity than adherent cells in the presence of serum, suggesting the existence of an adhesion-dependent negative-feedback loop. Interestingly, we also observed that both cytochalasin D and colchicine, which have opposite effects on stress fibers and focal adhesions, could activate Rho. Our findings suggest that ECM, cytoskeletal structures, and soluble factors all contribute to the regulation of Rho activity.

title: Core binding factors are necessary for natural killer cell development and cooperate with Notch signaling during T-cell specification.
text: CBFβ is the non-DNA-binding subunit of the core binding factors (CBFs). Mutant mice with reduced CBFβ levels display profound, early flaws in T-cell but not B-cell development. This work demonstrates that CBFβ is also crucial at very early stages of natural killer (NK)-cell development. Additionally, we show that T-cell development abruptly halts during the specification phase, as the expression of Gata3 and Tcf7, which encode key regulators of T lineage specification, is substantially diminished, as are functional thymic progenitors. Constitutive activity of Notch or IL-7 signaling cannot revive T-cell expansion or differentiation of CBFβ-insufficient cells, nor can overexpression of Runx1 or CBFβ overcome a deficiency in Notch signaling. Therefore, the prethymic cell's ability to respond appropriately to Notch is dependent on CBFβ, and both signals converge to activate the T-cell developmental program.

title: VEGF and podocytes in diabetic nephropathy.
text: Vascular endothelial growth factor-A (VEGF-A) is produced by podocytes and plays a crucial role in the survival of endothelial cells, podocytes, and mesangial cells. VEGF-A regulates slit-diaphragm signaling and podocyte shape by interacting with VEGF receptors 2, nephrin, nck, and actin. Elevated podocyte VEGF-A levels and decreased endothelial nitric oxide production in response to chronic hyperglycemia contribute to the development and progression of diabetic nephropathy. The dysregulated crosstalk between VEGF-A and nitric oxide signaling pathways is exacerbated by the diabetic environment, leading to increased oxidative stress. Latest research on these harmful molecular mechanisms offers new potential therapeutic targets for diabetic kidney disease.

title: Detection and distribution patterns of telomerase activity in insects.
text: Most insects possess telomeres consisting of pentanucleotide (TTAGG)n repeats, with the exception of certain species, including Diptera, where telomere maintenance occurs without the presence of telomerase. To expand our understanding of the diverse and unusual telomere formation among insects, we examined a previously unreported insect telomerase. Using a modified telomeric repeat amplification protocol (TRAP), we first detected telomerase activity in crickets, cockroaches, and two Lepidopteran insects. Unlike other telomerases, the enzyme from crickets and cockroaches requires dATP, dGTP, and dTTP as substrates, and sequence analysis of TRAP products revealed that (TTAGG)n repeats are synthesized by telomerase. We found that the cockroach telomerase is expressed in both somatic (fat body, muscle, and neural tissues) and germline (testis) cells, indicating that its expression is not tissue-specific at the adult stage. In contrast, high levels of telomerase activity were detected in crickets and cockroaches, but not in all tissues and cell cultures of the silkworm, Bombyx mori, and three Drosophila and one Sarcophaga cell lines, supporting the theory that Dipteran insects maintain their telomeres without the presence of telomerase.

title: Conversion of the lac repressor into an allosterically regulated transcriptional activator for mammalian cells.
text: A novel mammalian transcriptional regulatory system was developed by modifying the Escherichia coli lac repressor. The lac repressor was converted into a mammalian transcriptional activator by introducing a nuclear localization signal from the simian virus 40 (SV40) large tumor antigen and the transcription activation domain from the herpes simplex virus type 1 virion protein 16 into the lac repressor coding region. The resulting lac activator protein (LAP) fusions were potent activators of various promoters containing lac operator sequences placed either upstream or downstream of the transcription unit. A single lac operator was sufficient for transactivation, while multiple operators acted synergistically when separated by a small distance. Promoters containing 14 or 21 operator sequences were induced at least 1,000-fold in response to LAP, with levels of activity 20 to 30 times higher than that of the SV40 early promoter in HeLa cells. Activation was inhibited by isopropyl-beta-D-thiogalactoside (IPTG), indicating that LAP retained the necessary functions for allosteric regulation. LAP was also found to be bifunctional, acting as a repressor of expression of an SV40 promoter containing an operator immediately downstream of the TATA box. To facilitate the generation of LAP-expressing cell lines, genetic selection schemes were developed that allow for high-frequency generation of LAP-expressing cells from either established or primary cells in culture.

title: Antigen availability determines CD8⁺ T cell-dendritic cell interaction kinetics and memory fate decisions.
text: T cells are activated by antigen-bearing dendritic cells (DCs) in lymph nodes through three distinct phases. The duration of the initial phase of temporary, serial DC-T cell interactions is inversely correlated with the dose of antigen. The second phase, marked by stable DC-T cell contacts, was previously believed to be essential for full T cell activation. However, our findings show that this is not the case. CD8+ T cells interacting with DCs presenting low-dose, short-lived antigen did not transition to the second phase, whereas higher antigen doses led to a transition. Both types of antigen presentation promoted T cell proliferation and effector differentiation, but yielded distinct transcriptome signatures at 12 and 24 hours. T cells that experienced the second phase developed long-lasting memory, while conditions without stable DC-T cell contacts resulted in immunological amnesia. Therefore, T cells make fate decisions within a few hours after antigen exposure, leading to long-term memory or abortive effector responses, which are closely linked to the kinetics of T cell-DC interactions.

title: BAX/BAK-independent mitoptosis during cell death induced by proteasome inhibition?
text: Proteasome inhibitors initiate rapid cell death in cancer cells. We demonstrate that in epithelial cancer cells, this death is associated with a dramatic and simultaneous boost in several BH3-only proteins, including BIK, BIM, MCL-1S, NOXA, and PUMA, as well as p53. Elevated levels of these proteins appear to be the result of direct inhibition of their degradation by the proteasome, induction of transcription, and active translation. Following this, cell death becomes independent of BAX and BAK, and occurs through the intrinsic mitochondrial apoptosis pathway. We identify the sequence of molecular events that occur upon treatment with a prototypical proteasome inhibitor, MG132, starting with the rapid accumulation of BH3-only proteins in the mitochondria, followed by mitochondrial membrane permeabilization and subsequent loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, leading to irreversible changes in mitochondrial ultrastructure, degradation of the mitochondrial network, and impairment of crucial mitochondrial functions. Our findings also provide a basis for broadening the use of proteasome inhibitors to eliminate apoptosis-resistant tumor cells that lack functional BAX/BAK proteins.

title: Site of action of a ribosomal RNA methylase responsible for resistance to erythromycin and other antibiotics.
text: The enzyme responsible for conferring resistance to erythromycin in the producing organism Streptomyces erythraeus modifies a single adenine residue in the 23S rRNA of Bacillus stearothermophilus. This adenine residue corresponds to residue Ade 2058 in Escherichia coli 23S rRNA. Moreover, the same enzyme responsible for resistance to macrolides, lincomycin, and streptogramin B-related antibiotics in Staphylococcus aureus also acts at this same site.

title: 53BP1 nuclear bodies form around DNA lesions generated by mitotic transmission of chromosomes under replication stress
text: The completion of genome duplication is hampered by structural and topological barriers that hinder the progression of replication forks, posing a threat to genome integrity. Despite this challenge, the fate of DNA with unresolved replication intermediates remains unclear. Our study uncovers that mild replication stress leads to an increased frequency of chromosomal lesions that are passed on to daughter cells. During G1 phase, these lesions are segregated into nuclear compartments marked by p53-binding protein 1 (53BP1) and other chromatin-associated genome caretakers. We discovered that the number of 53BP1 nuclear bodies increases after genetic ablation of BLM, a DNA helicase involved in resolving tangled DNA. Conversely, 53BP1 nuclear bodies are partially diminished when we knock down SMC2, a condensin subunit essential for the mechanical stability of mitotic chromosomes. Our findings suggest that the preservation of DNA or chromatin integrity at sites susceptible to replication issues requires transmission to the next cell generation through mitosis.

title: Targeted inhibition of tumor-specific glutaminase diminishes cell-autonomous tumorigenesis.
text: Glutaminase (GLS), which converts glutamine to glutamate, plays a crucial role in cancer cell metabolism, growth, and proliferation. GLS is being explored as a potential cancer therapeutic target, but its impact on cancer cell-autonomous growth and the host microenvironment is unclear. Recent studies have shown that loss of one copy of the Gls gene blunts tumor progression in an immune-competent mouse model of hepatocellular carcinoma. Moreover, administration of a GLS-specific inhibitor, bis-2-(5-phenylacetamido-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-yl)ethyl sulfide (BPTES), prolonged survival and inhibited growth of a MYC-dependent human B cell lymphoma cell line (P493) in mice. However, P493 xenografts expressing a BPTES-resistant GLS mutant or overexpressing GLS were not affected by BPTES treatment. A customized Vivo-Morpholino that targets human GLS mRNA also inhibited P493 xenograft growth without affecting mouse Gls expression. In contrast, a Vivo-Morpholino directed at mouse Gls had no antitumor activity in vivo. Together, these findings suggest that GLS is essential for tumorigenesis and support small molecule and genetic inhibition of GLS as potential strategies for targeting the tumor cell-autonomous dependence on GLS for cancer therapy.

title: Dominant optic atrophy, deafness, ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, dystaxia, and myopathy. A new syndrome.
text: A study was conducted on 96 members of a family, of which 23 showed signs of an autosomal dominant disorder that had not been previously described. This disorder resulted in progressive optic atrophy, abnormal electroretinography without retinal pigment changes, and progressive sensorineural hearing loss, typically appearing during the first or second decade of life. As the individuals aged, they also experienced midlife symptoms such as ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, dystaxia, and a nonspecific myopathy.

title: Dynein is required for polarized dendritic transport and uniform microtubule orientation in axons
text: Axons and dendrites exhibit distinct differences in microtubule organization and the organelles and proteins they contain. Our findings indicate that the microtubule motor dynein plays a crucial role in polarized transport and in regulating the orientation of axonal microtubules in Drosophila melanogaster dendritic arborization (da) neurons. Changes in organelle distribution within the dendritic arbors of dynein mutant neurons correlate with a proximal shift in dendritic branch position. Additionally, dynein is essential for the dendrite-specific localization of Golgi outposts and the ion channel Pickpocket. In contrast, axonal microtubules typically exhibit uniform plus-end-distal orientation; however, in the absence of dynein, axons exhibit both plus- and minus-end-distal microtubules. These findings suggest that dynein is necessary for the unique properties of axons and dendrites, as dendritic organelles and proteins enter the axon, and axonal microtubules cease to be uniform in polarity without dynein.

title: Small molecule screening in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived terminal cell types.
text: There is a growing need for improved clinical outcomes, which has increased interest in the use of biologically relevant human cells in the drug discovery process. Patient-specific human induced pluripotent stem cells may provide a valuable, reliable, and cost-effective model of human disease physiology. High-throughput screening of small molecules in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cells is becoming more common in the drug discovery process, with the aim of identifying potential new therapeutic compounds. However, developing and optimizing high-throughput screening assays for these cells poses significant challenges. Nevertheless, this technology has the potential to revolutionize the way drugs are discovered.

title: Gene expression during gonadogenesis in the chicken embryo.
text: Researchers investigated genes involved in vertebrate sex determination and differentiation in embryonic chicken gonads using reverse transcription and polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). Expression profiles were acquired during gonadal sex differentiation for AMH, SOX9, SOX3, the Wilms Tumour gene, WT1, and the orphan nuclear receptor genes, SF1 and DAX1. Some of these genes displayed sexually dimorphic expression profiles during gonadal development, while others were expressed at similar levels in both sexes. The gene encoding Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) was expressed in both sexes before and during sexual differentiation of the gonads, with levels of expression consistently higher in males than in females. SOX9 expression was uniquely male-specific, and was up-regulated after the detection of AMH transcripts. SOX3 expression was observed prior to clear SOX9 expression and was up-regulated in both sexes at the onset of gonadal sex differentiation (but declined later in development). The WT1 gene was highly expressed in both sexes, whereas SF1 expression was significantly higher in developing ovaries compared to testes. DAX1 transcripts were observed in both sexes at all stages examined, but expression appeared slightly higher in developing ovaries. These expression profiles were evaluated in light of current theories of vertebrate sex determination.

title: Organ-resident, nonlymphoid cells suppress proliferation of autoimmune T-helper lymphocytes.
text: The presentation of autoantigens by resident cells in an organ is implicated in organ-specific autoimmunity. An experimental model of autoimmune uveoretinitis in rats, induced by immunization with retinal soluble antigen, is used to study organ-specific autoimmunity. In vitro, uveitogenic rat T-helper cells specific to the retinal soluble antigen or control T-helper cells reactive to tuberculin were cocultured with Ia-expressing syngeneic retinal glial cells (Müller cells) in the presence of specific antigen. Antigen presentation was not apparent under standard culture conditions, and the Müller cells significantly suppressed the proliferative response of primed T-helper cells to antigen presented on conventional antigen-presenting cells, as well as their subsequent IL-2-dependent expansion. suppression of proliferation was accompanied by inhibition of IL-2 production in response to antigen, as well as by reduction in high-affinity IL-2 receptor expression, and proceeded via a contact-dependent mechanism. The results suggest a role for locally acting suppression mechanisms in immune regulation and maintenance of tissue homeostasis.

title: Drug induced refractory headache--clinical features and management.
text:
In this study, 200 patients who were reliant on daily or near-daily symptomatic or immediate relief medications for their headaches were analyzed. Of these patients, 116 (58%) were also taking concomitant prophylactic medications that proved to be ineffective. The patients were then instructed to follow a low-tyramine, low-caffeine diet and undergo biofeedback training. The impact of continuing symptomatic medications, discontinuing symptomatic medications, and altering or modifying prophylactic medications was evaluated in various treatment groups.
The findings of the study indicate the following:
1. Patients who relied on daily or near-daily symptomatic or immediate relief medications for their headaches were more likely to experience chronic daily headaches.
2. Discontinuing the use of daily symptomatic medications resulted in an improvement in headache symptoms.
3. The concomitant use of symptomatic medications neutralized the beneficial effects of prophylactic medications.
4. Discontinuing daily symptomatic medications enhanced the effectiveness of prophylactic medications.

In conclusion, the study suggests that the continuous use of symptomatic or immediate relief medications can lead to chronic daily headaches, and that discontinuing these medications can result in improvement. Additionally, the study found that the concomitant use of symptomatic medications can negate the effectiveness of prophylactic medications, and that discontinuing daily symptomatic medications can enhance the beneficial effects of prophylactic medications.

title: Neuromodulation of neurons and synapses.
text: Neuromodulation is essential for the flexibility of neural circuits and behavior, as individual neuromodulators can have different effects on the same neuron by targeting multiple physiological mechanisms. Conversely, multiple neuromodulators may have similar effects on different targets, leading to either synergistic or antagonistic interactions. Unlike the straightforward modification of neural excitability or synaptic strength, neuromodulation operates through a complex balancing act of nonlinear membrane and synaptic properties, targeting ion channel and synaptic dynamics. Additionally, neuromodulators can act on different timescales, influencing short-term neuron and synapse function as well as long-term regulation. This brief review highlights some key aspects of the diverse effects of neuromodulators on ion channel and synaptic properties.

title: Mutation frequency and specificity with age in liver, bladder and brain of lacI transgenic mice.
text: The frequency and specificity of mutations were examined in nuclear DNA from liver, bladder, and brain of Big Blue lacI transgenic mice at different ages (1.5-25 months). Mutations increased with age in liver and bladder, but a small initial increase in mutation frequency was observed in young animals in the brain, followed by no further increase in adult mice. To determine the origin of these mutations, the mutational spectra were analyzed for each tissue and age group. DNA sequence analysis of mutant lacI transgenes revealed no significant changes in mutational specificity across different tissues and ages, suggesting that the mutations originated from a common set of DNA lesions that occur during DNA replication. The data also indicated that there were no significant age-related changes in mutational frequencies due to oxidative damage or errors arising from changes in DNA polymerase fidelity or DNA repair efficiency. Therefore, no evidence was found to support the notion that oxidative damage or accumulation of errors in nuclear DNA contributes significantly to the aging process in these three somatic tissues.

title: Breaching the basement membrane: who, when and how?
text: The basement membrane (BM), a specialized network of extracellular matrix macromolecules, surrounds various cell types, including epithelial, endothelial, muscle, fat, and nerve cells. During development, immune surveillance, and disease states such as cancer and fibrosis, host cells penetrate the BM by activating distinct programs, whose identity remains largely unexplored. Contrary to the commonly held belief that all cells employ similar mechanisms to cross BM barriers, recent evidence suggests that cells may selectively deploy protease-dependent or -independent invasion programs. Emerging data reveal that protease-dependent transmigration is largely reliant on a group of membrane-anchored metalloenzymes, termed membrane-type matrix metalloproteinases, which irreversibly alter the BM matrix. In contrast, the mechanisms that enable protease-independent transmigration remain unclear and may involve the reversible disassembly of the BM network. Further elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying BM transmigration has the potential to shed light on pathophysiological tissue remodeling processes and lead to the development of new therapeutic strategies.

title: Soluble MD-2 is an acute-phase protein and an opsonin for Gram-negative bacteria.
text:
Myeloid differentiation factor-2 (MD-2) is a protein that plays a crucial role in the host innate immune response to Gram-negative infections. It acts as a binding protein for lipopolysaccharide (LPS), which is a component of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, and enhances the responsiveness of immune cells to LPS. MD-2 is primarily expressed on the surface of immune cells, but it can also be found in a soluble form (sMD-2) in plasma and other inflamed tissues.
Interestingly, our studies have shown that sMD-2 is a type II acute-phase protein, which means that its production is up-regulated in response to inflammation. In fact, sMD-2 levels are markedly elevated in plasma from patients with severe infections, and in other fluids from inflamed tissues. We have also found that sMD-2 is secreted by human hepatocytic cells and up-regulated by interleukin-6, a cytokine that plays a key role in the innate immune response.
Moreover, sMD-2 plays a critical role in enhancing the phagocytosis of Gram-negative bacteria by immune cells, particularly polymorphonuclear neutrophils. Our findings suggest that sMD-2 functions as an opsonin for Gram-negative bacteria, marking them for recognition and engulfment by immune cells. Overall, our results highlight the important role of sMD-2 in the host innate immune response to Gram-negative infections, and suggest that it may be a promising target for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of sepsis and other bacterial infections.

title: Division-coupled astrocytic differentiation and age-related depletion of neural stem cells in the adult hippocampus.
text:
The production of new neurons in the adult hippocampus declines with age, a phenomenon that may contribute to age-related cognitive impairment. Our findings suggest that the continuous depletion of neural stem cells, as a result of their division, may be a major factor in this decline. It appears that adult hippocampal stem cells, upon exiting their quiescent state, rapidly undergo a series of asymmetric divisions to produce dividing progeny destined to become neurons, which subsequently convert into mature astrocytes. Therefore, the decrease in the number of neural stem cells is an intrinsic process that is directly related to their production of new neurons.
To gain a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying neurogenesis in the adult hippocampus, we have developed a comprehensive scheme of the neurogenesis cascade. This scheme includes a novel "disposable stem cell" model, which accounts for the disappearance of hippocampal neural stem cells, the appearance of new astrocytes, and the age-related decline in the production of new neurons.
In summary, our findings suggest that the production of new neurons in the adult hippocampus is a complex process that is directly related to the depletion of neural stem cells. The disposable stem cell model provides a framework for understanding the mechanisms underlying age-related cognitive impairment, and may have important implications for the development of novel therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving cognitive function in the elderly.

title: P19 embryonal carcinoma cells.
text: P19 cells are a type of pluripotent embryonal carcinoma cell line that can be cultured continuously in media supplemented with serum. The differentiation of these cells can be controlled using non-toxic drugs, such as retinoic acid, which can induce the development of specific cell types, including neurons, astroglia, and microglia, which are normally derived from the neuroectoderm. Exposure to dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) can also induce the differentiation of P19 cells into endodermal and mesodermal derivatives, such as cardiac and skeletal muscle. P19 cells can be easily transfected with recombinant DNA and stable lines expressing these genes can be isolated, making them a useful tool for investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying the decision-making process during cell differentiation.

title: Iguanas and Salmonella marina infection in children: a reflection of the increasing incidence of reptile-associated salmonellosis in the United States.
text:
Study Objective:
To investigate the clinical aspects and risk factors associated with Salmonella serotype Marina infections in the United States.
Methodology:
We analyzed all reported isolates of Salmonella Marina in 1994 to the National Salmonella Surveillance System. We interviewed patients regarding their demographic information, clinical course, diet, travel history, and contact with reptiles before illness.
Results:
Twenty-six (81%) of the 32 patients were infants (<1 year of age) and 24 (75%) were male. This is in contrast to other Salmonella isolates reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in 1994, where 14% were from infants and 49% were from male patients. Eleven patients (34%) were hospitalized for a median of 3.5 days (range: 2 to 21 days), and one died. Of the 28 patients (88%) with reported iguana exposure, only 4 (14%) touched the reptile, and only 12 respondents (43%) realized that it might have been the source of infection. Seven (32%) of 22 families who owned an iguana at the time of illness continued to own an iguana when contacted a median of 28 weeks later. Persons who thought that the iguana was the source of infection were more likely to have given away or sold the pet than those who did not. Four isolates (13%) were from blood. Bacteremia was associated with taking antibiotics during the 30 days before S Marina infection (odds ratio: 24; 95% confidence interval: 1.2-1309).
Conclusion:
Salmonella serotype Marina infection is a potentially serious illness associated with iguana exposure. The larger problem of reptile-associated salmonellosis highlights the need for pediatricians, veterinarians, and pet store owners to inform their patients and customers of the potential risks of owning reptiles and provide appropriate preventive education.

title: Siblings with opposite chromosome constitutions, dup(2q)/del(7q) and del(2q)/dup(7q).
text: Chromosome 7q36 microdeletion syndrome is a rare genetic disorder characterized by brain underdevelopment, microcephaly, sexual organ abnormalities, and language difficulties. Key features of this condition include developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorders, BDMR syndrome, and distinctive facial structures. Using high-resolution chromosomal analysis and subtelomeric multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification, we found subtelomeric rearrangements on the same sites of 2q37.2 and 7q35 in two brothers with global developmental delay. These rearrangements included reversed deletions and duplications. Both brothers showed severe disabilities in physical and intellectual development, as well as abnormal genitalia with distinct differences in their phenotypes. The family did not have any abnormal genetic phenotypes. Based on the segregation of the gene mutation from their mother, we suggest that adjacent-1 mechanism may be the cause of their gene mutation. By comparing the phenotypes of our patients with previous reports on similar patients, we attempted to identify related genes and their chromosomal locations.

title: Methods for quantifying follicular numbers within the mouse ovary.
text: Accurate assessment of the number of ovarian follicles at various stages of development is crucial for understanding the process of folliculogenesis and the endocrine signals and paracrine/autocrine mechanisms that regulate oocyte growth and maturation. Previous studies have reported large differences in follicular numbers per ovary, making it challenging to interpret ovarian function in both control and experimental conditions. This study introduces unbiased, assumption-free stereological methods for counting early and growing follicular numbers in the mouse ovary. The fractionator approach was used to sample a defined fraction of histological sections from adult wild-type ovaries, and primordial and primary follicles were counted using the optical and physical disector methods. The results revealed an estimated 1930 +/- 286 and 2227 +/- 101 primordial follicles, and 137 +/- 25 and 265 +/- 32 primary follicles per ovary at 70 and 100 days of age, respectively. Additionally, secondary and later follicular numbers at 100 days of age were estimated to be 135 per ovary. The methodology described in this study will greatly enhance our understanding of follicular dynamics and the factors that govern their growth and maturation, allowing for more accurate comparisons between studies. Moreover, the application of these quantitative methods will provide a comprehensive understanding of the ovarian follicular hierarchy, including the number of remnants of zona pellucidae (a marker of previous follicular atresia), which were estimated to be approximately 500 per ovary.

title: Identification of functional cooperative mutations of SETD2 in human acute leukemia
text: Acute leukemia characterized by chromosomal rearrangements often requires additional genetic alterations to progress to full-blown malignancy, but the mechanisms underlying this cooperation remain unclear. By analyzing the whole genomes of monozygotic twin brothers with MLL (also known as KMT2A) gene-rearranged leukemia, we discovered a transforming MLL-NRIP3 fusion gene and biallelic mutations in SETD2 (a histone H3K36 methyltransferase). Furthermore, we found that loss-of-function point mutations in SETD2 were present in 6.2% of 241 patients with acute leukemia and were associated with multiple chromosomal abnormalities. Interestingly, we observed a global loss of H3K36 trimethylation (H3K36me3) in leukemic cells with mutations in SETD2. Our findings suggest that downregulation of SETD2 contributes to both initiation and progression of leukemia development by enhancing the self-renewal potential of leukemia stem cells. Therefore, our study provides strong evidence for SETD2 as a tumor suppressor gene. Disruption of the SETD2-H3K36me3 pathway represents a distinct epigenetic mechanism underlying leukemia development.

title: Evidence regarding human papillomavirus testing in secondary prevention of cervical cancer.
text:
Clinicians need regular updates on the latest research and reviews regarding innovative cervical cancer prevention methods, given the increasing amount of new information. Recent meta-analyses and systematic reviews have summarized the following 3 possible clinical applications of HPV testing:
* Triage of women with equivocal or low-grade cytologic abnormalities: HPV-triage with the Hybrid Capture(®) 2 assay (Qiagen Gaithersburg, Inc., MD, USA) is more accurate than repeat cytology.
* Prediction of the therapeutic outcome after treatment of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) lesions: HPV testing can predict the likelihood of treatment success.
* Primary screening for cervical cancer and pre-cancer: HPV testing can detect high-grade CIN and cancer more effectively than cytology, especially in women aged 30 years or older.
consistent evidence indicates that HPV-triage with the Hybrid Capture(®) 2 assay is more accurate than repeat cytology. Other tests, such as mRNA testing with the APTIMA(®) (Gen-Probe Inc., San Diego, CA, USA) test, are similar in accuracy but have different characteristics. In triage of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions, HC2 is more sensitive but has lower specificity compared to repeat cytology, while the APTIMA(®) test is more specific. HPV testing can identify DNA or RNA of HPV types 16 and/or 18, allowing selection of women at highest risk for CIN3+. However, the sensitivity and negative predictive value of these markers are lower than full-range high-risk HPV (hrHPV) testing. After conservative treatment of cervical pre-cancer, HPV testing picks up more quickly and with higher sensitivity and specificity than follow-up cytology. Primary screening for hrHPV generally detects more CIN2, CIN3 or cancer compared to cytology at a cut-off of atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US) or LSIL, but is less specific. Combined HPV and cytology screening provides a small gain in sensitivity but at the expense of a considerable loss in specificity if positive by either test is referred to colposcopy. Randomized trials and follow-up of cohort studies consistently demonstrate a significantly lower cumulative incidence of CIN3+ and even of cancer in women aged 30 years or older who were at enrollment HPV DNA negative compared to those who were cytologically negative. The difference in cumulative risk of CIN3+ or cancer for double-negative (cytology & HPV) versus only HPV-negative women is small. HC2, GP5+/6+ PCR, cobas(®) 4800 PCR, and Real Time PCR can be considered clinically validated for use in primary screening. The loss in specificity associated with primary HPV-based screening can be compensated by appropriate algorithms involving reflex cytology and/or HPV genotyping for HPV16 or 18. There is a substantial evidence base to support that HPV testing is advantageous in triage of women with equivocal abnormal cytology, in surveillance after treatment of CIN lesions, and in primary screening of women aged 30 years or older. However, a well-organized program with good compliance is necessary to maintain the advantages offered by HPV-based screening.

title: International standards for fetal growth based on serial ultrasound measurements: the Fetal Growth Longitudinal Study of the INTERGROWTH-21st Project.
text:
In 2006, the World Health Organization (WHO) developed international growth standards for infants and children up to the age of 5 years based on expert committee recommendations. Building on this work, the Fetal Growth Longitudinal Study (FGLS), part of the INTERGROWTH-21(st) Project, aimed to create international growth and size standards for fetuses using a similar methodological approach.
The FGLS was a multicenter, population-based study that assessed fetal growth in geographically defined urban populations in eight countries where mothers had adequate health and nutritional needs and adequate antenatal care. Using ultrasound, the study took fetal anthropometric measurements prospectively from 14 weeks and 0 days of gestation until birth in a cohort of women at low risk of intrauterine growth restriction. The five primary ultrasound measures of fetal growth--head circumference, biparietal diameter, occipitofrontal diameter, abdominal circumference, and femur length--were obtained every 5 weeks (within 1 week either side) from 14 weeks to 42 weeks of gestation. The best-fitting curves for these measures were selected using second-degree fractional polynomials and further modeled in a multilevel framework to account for the longitudinal design of the study.
The study screened 13,108 women starting antenatal care at less than 14 weeks and 0 days of gestation, of whom 4607 (35%) were eligible. Of these, 4321 (94%) had pregnancies without major complications and delivered live singletons without congenital malformations, making up the analysis population. The study found very low maternal and perinatal mortality and morbidity, confirming that the participants were at low risk of adverse outcomes. For each of the five fetal growth measures, the mean differences between the observed and smoothed centiles for the 3rd, 50th, and 97th centiles, respectively, were small: 2·25 mm (SD 3·0), 0·02 mm (3·0), and -2·69 mm (3·2) for head circumference; 0·83 mm (0·9), -0·05 mm (0·8), and -0·84 mm (1·0) for biparietal diameter; 0·63 mm (1·2), 0·04 mm (1·1), and -1·05 mm (1·3) for occipitofrontal diameter; 2·99 mm (3·1), 0·25 mm (3·2), and -4·22 mm (3·7) for abdominal circumference; and 0·62 mm (0·8), 0·03 mm (0·8), and -0·65 mm (0·8) for femur length. The study calculated the 3rd, 5th, 10th, 50th, 90th, 95th, and 97th centile curves according to gestational age for these ultrasound measures, providing the international standards for fetal growth interpretation.
The FGLS recommends these international fetal growth standards for clinical interpretation of routinely taken ultrasound measurements and for comparisons across populations. Funding for the study was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

title: Role of NF-kappa B in cell survival and transcription of latent membrane protein 1-expressing or Epstein-Barr virus latency III-infected cells.
text: The Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) latency III infection transforms B lymphocytes into lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCLs) by expressing EBV nuclear and membrane proteins, EBNAs, and latent membrane proteins (LMPs), which regulate transcription through Notch and tumor necrosis factor receptor pathways. The study investigated the role of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) in LMP1 and overall EBV latency III transcriptional effects using the inhibitor BAY11-7082. BAY11 rapidly and irreversibly inhibited NF-κB, leading to decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, apoptosis, and altered LCL gene expression. The study found that BAY11 effects were similar to those of an NF-κB inhibitor, Delta N-I kappa B alpha, in reducing JNK1 expression and in microarray analyses. More than 80% of array elements that decreased with Delta N-I kappa B alpha expression also decreased with BAY11 treatment. Newly identified NF-κB-induced, LMP1-induced, and EBV-induced genes included pleckstrin, Jun-B, c-FLIP, CIP4, and I kappa B epsilon. EBV latency III-regulated gene products mediate cell migration, antigen presentation, mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway, and interferon signaling. The study compared EBV latency III LCL gene expression to immunoglobulin M (IgM)-stimulated B cells, germinal-center B cells, and germinal-center-derived lymphomas and found that LCLs clustered with IgM-stimulated B cells separately from germinal-center cells or germinal-center lymphoma cells. Expression of IRF-2, AIM1, ASK1, SNF2L2, and components of IFN signaling pathways further distinguished EBV latency III-infected B cells from IgM-stimulated or germinal-center B cells.

title: Endotoxin tolerance: new mechanisms, molecules and clinical significance.
text: Previous exposure to small amounts of endotoxin can make immune cells such as monocytes/macrophages less responsive to subsequent endotoxin challenge, a phenomenon known as "endotoxin tolerance". In sepsis patients, this state is linked to impaired immune function and mortality. While the underlying mechanisms of endotoxin tolerance are still unclear, recent research has shed light on the role of inflammation as a self-regulating process, the importance of MyD88 versus TRIF signaling pathways, the plasticity of NF-κB function, and the roles of chromatin modification and microRNAs in endotoxin-induced gene reprogramming. This review aims to integrate these new findings into a comprehensive understanding of endotoxin tolerance, its molecular basis, and clinical implications in various diseases.

title: Pancreatic tumor cells with mutant K-ras suppress ERK activity by MEK-dependent induction of MAP kinase phosphatase-2.
text: In human pancreatic carcinomas, mutations occur frequently within the K-ras gene. Previous studies found that oncogenic, activated K-ras did not lead to constant activation of extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERK1 and ERK2) in pancreatic carcinoma cell lines. To further investigate the ERK signaling pathway in these tumors, we analyzed pancreatic tumor cell lines to determine if the pathway is subject to compensatory downregulation. Our findings revealed that the attenuation of serum-induced ERK activation was not due to a delay in ERK phosphorylation kinetics. Treatment with the tyrosine phosphatase inhibitor orthovanadate increased ERK phosphorylation, indicating the presence of a vanadate-sensitive tyrosine phosphatase in negative ERK regulation. Additionally, we found that expression of the dual specificity phosphatase mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase phosphatase-2 (MKP-2) was elevated in most pancreatic tumor cell lines and correlated with the presence of active MAP kinase kinase (MEK). These results suggest that pancreatic tumor cells expressing oncogenic K-ras may compensate, in part, by upregulating MKP-2 expression to repress the ERK signaling pathway.

title: E2F3 is a mediator of DNA damage-induced apoptosis.
text: E2F transcription factors have emerged as key regulators of programmed cell death. In this study, we investigate the pathways involved in the induction of E2F3a, a member of the E2F family, upon DNA damage. We show that both transcriptional and posttranslational mechanisms are involved in the induction of E2F3a, and that the latter is dependent on checkpoint kinases. We also demonstrate that E2F3a is a substrate for these kinases and that mutating the phosphorylation site attenuates its ability to respond to DNA damage. Furthermore, we demonstrate that E2F1 and E2F2 are transcriptionally induced by DNA damage in an E2f3-dependent manner. Finally, using both in vitro and in vivo approaches, we demonstrate that E2f3 is essential for DNA damage-induced apoptosis, highlighting its central role as a master regulator of the DNA damage response.

title: miR-294/miR-302 promotes proliferation, suppresses G1-S restriction point, and inhibits ESC differentiation through separable mechanisms.
text: The miR-294 and miR-302 microRNAs promote an abbreviated G1 phase of the embryonic stem cell (ESC) cell cycle and suppress differentiation induced by let-7, and we investigated the role of the retinoblastoma (Rb) family proteins in these processes. Under normal growth conditions, miR-294 accelerates the rapid G1-S transition independently of the Rb family. On the other hand, miR-294 inhibits the further accumulation of cells in G1 in response to nutrient deprivation and cell-cell contact in an Rb-dependent manner. We discovered five additional microRNAs (miR-26a, miR-99b, miR-193, miR-199a-5p, and miR-218) that silence ESC self-renewal when other microRNAs are absent, all of which are counteracted by miR-294 and miR-302. Four of the six differentiation-inducing microRNAs induce an Rb-dependent G1 accumulation. However, all six still silence self-renewal in the absence of the Rb proteins. These results demonstrate that the miR-294/miR-302 family acts through Rb-dependent and -independent pathways to regulate the G1 restriction point and the silencing of self-renewal, respectively.

title: Bacteriophage latent-period evolution as a response to resource availability.
text: Bacteriophages (phages) alter microbial communities by lysing hosts, transferring genetic material, and inducing lysogenic conversion. To develop accurate predictions of how natural communities are affected, it is crucial to create models that account for variations in parameters such as eclipse period, latent period, adsorption constant, burst size, and modeling strategy. Here, we compare two existing models of phage growth, which differ in their approaches to modeling the kinetics of phage adsorption: one is a computer simulation, and the other is an explicit calculation. At higher host densities (approximately 10(8) cells/ml), both models accurately predict phage population growth rates experimentally observed. However, at lower host densities (10(7) cells/ml), the computer simulation continues to accurately predict phage growth rates, while the explicit model fails to do so. Next, we focus on predicting latent-period optima, which is the latent period that maximizes the population growth of a specific phage when growing in a specific quantity and quality of host cells. Both models predict similar latent-period optima at higher host densities (e.g., 17 minutes at 10(8) cells/ml). However, at lower host densities (e.g., 10(5) cells/ml), the computer simulation predicts significantly shorter latent-period optima than explicit calculations (e.g., 90 versus 1,250 minutes). Finally, we examine the impact of host quality on phage latent-period evolution. By differentiating between latent-period phenotypic plasticity and latent-period evolution, we argue that the impact of host quality on phage latent-period evolution may be relatively small.

title: Neutrophil elastase-mediated lung disease.
text: Elastases from both neutrophils and macrophages have been implicated in the initiation and progression of lung disease. Although it is unlikely that these proteases were specifically designed to damage lung tissue, the elastin-rich connective tissue framework of the lungs appears to be particularly susceptible to their action. Given that neutrophil elastase likely plays a role in neutrophil migration and protein degradation, the inhibition of this protease could protect normal tissues from its harmful effects. In alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, a genetic disruption of the protease-anti-protease balance can lead to an increased risk of destructive lung disease, serving as an experimental model of the role of elastases in lung disease.

title: Role of TRPML and two-pore channels in endolysosomal cation homeostasis.
text: The transient receptor potential (TRP) channels TRPML1, TRPML2, and TRPML3 (also known as mucolipins 1-3 or MCOLN1-3) are nonselective cation channels. Mutations in the Trpml1 gene result in mucolipidosis type IV in humans, characterized by psychomotor retardation, corneal clouding, and retinal degeneration. Conversely, mutations in the Trpml3 gene cause deafness, circling behavior, and coat color dilution in mice. No disease-causing mutations have been reported for the Trpml2 gene. Like TRPML channels, which are expressed in the endolysosomal pathway, two-pore channels (TPCs), including TPC1, TPC2, and TPC3, are found in intracellular organelles, such as endosomes and lysosomes. Both TRPML channels and TPCs may function as calcium/cation release channels in endosomes, lysosomes, and lysosome-related organelles, with TRPMLs being activated by phosphatidylinositol 3,5-bisphosphate and regulated by pH, and TPCs being activated by nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate in a calcium- and pH-dependent manner. They may also be involved in endolysosomal transport and fusion processes, such as intracellular calcium sources. However, the exact physiological roles of TRPML channels and TPCs remain unclear, and it is unknown whether TRPML channels are solely endolysosmal ion channels or if they may also be functional at the plasma membrane in vivo.

title: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma in London: clinical experience of 21 cases.
text: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) is a rare disease in the United Kingdom, predominantly affecting individuals of Afro-Caribbean descent. A retrospective analysis of 21 cases presented to two inner London teaching hospitals between 1981 and 1995 revealed that 17% of the population share this ancestry. The clinical presentation of ATLL in this setting was found to be similar to that observed in HTLV-I-endemic areas. A combination of chemotherapy regimens resulted in major responses (CR + PR) in 10/16 assessable patients (63%), with a median survival of 5.5 months. However, disease progression and opportunistic infections were the primary causes of treatment failure and mortality. Moreover, three patients (14%) relapsed in the central nervous system (CNS). These findings underscore the severely compromised immune system in ATLL, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic approaches such as zidovudine and alpha-interferon, which should include prophylaxis against CNS disease and opportunistic infections.

title: Regeneration, tissue injury and the immune response.
text: The connection between the immune system and tissue regeneration after injury has garnered significant interest. While some believe that immune factors may hinder regeneration, there is also evidence to suggest that immune components play a more positive role. The immunoprivileged nature of the vertebrate eye offers a unique opportunity to study the interplay between the immune system and regeneration. In various newt species, ocular tissues like the lens can regenerate following injury, and recent research has shown that the immune system plays a crucial role in this process. When the lens is injured, antigen-presenting cells are activated and migrate to the spleen, where they return to the damaged lens and initiate regeneration by engulfing and displacing the damaged tissue. The activation of thrombin in the dorsal iris is another key factor in the regenerative process. The relationship between the immune response and regeneration is not limited to the eye, but rather a phylogenetically conserved mechanism that has evolved across different species.

title: Poverty, Hunger, Education, and Residential Status Impact Survival in HIV
text:
Despite combinations of antiretroviral therapy (ART), individuals living with HIV continue to experience higher mortality rates compared to those without the virus. Socioeconomic status (SES) has been shown to predict higher mortality rates in various chronic illnesses, but data on its impact in people with HIV is limited. We analyzed 878 HIV-infected individuals followed from 1995 to 2005. Using Cox proportional hazards models, we examined the association between SES measures and mortality risk. Mixed effects analyses also explored how SES impacts factors predicting death. Of the 200 individuals who died, they were generally older, had lower CD4 counts, and higher viral loads (VL) compared to those who survived. In univariate analyses, age, transmission category, education, albumin, CD4 counts, VL, hunger, and poverty were all associated with increased mortality risk. After controlling for these factors in a multivariable model, only age, CD4 counts, albumin, VL, and poverty remained significantly associated with mortality. Using mixed models, we found direct and indirect associations between SES measures and mortality, highlighting the importance of targeting health policies at this population.


In summary, despite the benefits of combination antiretroviral therapy (ART), individuals living with HIV continue to experience higher mortality rates than the non-infected population. Socioeconomic status (SES) plays a significant role in predicting mortality in people with HIV, both directly and indirectly. By examining the relationships between SES measures and mortality risk factors, this study highlights the need to target health policies at this population to improve outcomes.

title: The INO80 ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complex is a nucleosome spacing factor.
text: The ATP-dependent remodeler INO80 mobilizes nucleosomes in a distinct manner compared to another remodeler (SWI/SNF) involved in gene activation. Unlike SWI/SNF, INO80 cannot disassemble nucleosomes when working with short nucleosomal arrays. Instead, INO80 resembles, yet with notable differences, the nucleosome spacing activity of ISW2 and ISW1a, which are typically involved in transcription repression. INO80 required 33-43 base pairs (bp) of extranucleosomal DNA for mobilizing nucleosomes, with optimal performance at 70 bp. INO80 preferentially moves mononucleosomes to the center of DNA, similar to ISW2 and ISW1a, but with higher precision. In contrast to ISW2/1a, INO80 does not require the H4 tail for nucleosome mobilization; instead, the H2A histone tail negatively regulates nucleosome movement by INO80. INO80 moves arrays of two or three nucleosomes with 50 or 79 bp of linker DNA closer together, resulting in a final length of approximately 30 bp of linker DNA or a repeat length of approximately 177 bp. A minimum length of >30 bp of linker DNA was necessary for nucleosome movement and spacing by INO80 in arrays.

title: Concentrations of tenofovir and emtricitabine in saliva: implications for preexposure prophylaxis of oral HIV acquisition.
text: To prevent HIV transmission through oral sex, medications known as preexposure prophylaxis (Prep) must reach sufficient concentrations in saliva to be effective. In a study of 41 HIV-infected patients on stable antiretroviral therapy, we measured the concentrations of tenofovir (TFV) and emtricitabine (FTC) in both plasma and saliva. The mean ratio of saliva to plasma concentration was 3% (±4%) for TFV and 86.9% (±124%) for FTC. These findings suggest that TDF, a combination of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) and FTC, may be an effective strategy for preventing oral transmission of HIV.

title: Increased lean body mass as an early indicator of olanzapine-induced weight gain in healthy men.
text: One of the primary limitations of many psychiatric medications is weight gain, which remains poorly understood. To investigate the possible mechanisms of weight gain, we conducted a 2-week double-blind placebo-controlled study on weight gain with olanzapine, a medication commonly associated with this side effect. Healthy male volunteers were randomly assigned to olanzapine (5 mg/day for 7 days, then 10 mg/day for 7 days) or a matching placebo. Of the 24 participants, 19 completed the study (olanzapine, n=13; placebo, n=6). We measured body weight, glucose, triglyceride, total cholesterol, lipid, leptin, insulin, and aldosterone levels, resting metabolic rate, body composition, physical activity, and 24-hour dietary intake. We found significant weight gain, along with increased triglyceride, insulin, and leptin levels, in the olanzapine group as a whole. In participants who actually gained weight (n=8), lean body mass increased, while fat mass remained stable, and insulin, glucose, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein, and non-high-density lipoprotein levels increased. Conversely, aldosterone levels decreased. There were no significant metabolic or endocrine changes in participants receiving placebo or in those receiving olanzapine who did not gain weight. These findings suggest that early metabolic changes may be independent of fat accumulation.

title: QTc interval length and QT dispersion as predictors of mortality in patients with non-insulin-dependent diabetes.
text: Individuals with non-insulin-dependent diabetes (NIDDM) are at a heightened risk of cardiovascular death, although the underlying reason for this is only partially understood. In order to investigate the impact of corrected QT interval length (QTc) and QT dispersion (QT-disp) on mortality in a cohort of 324 Caucasian NIDDM patients, a resting 12-lead ECG was conducted at baseline. The findings revealed that prolonged QTc interval (PQTc), defined as QTc-max > 440 ms(1/2), was present in 67% of the patients, while prolonged QT-disp (PQT-disp), defined as QT-disp > 50 ms, was seen in 51%. During the 9-year follow-up period, 100 patients died, with 37% of those with PQTc dying compared to 17% of those with normal QTc interval (p < 0.001). The Cox proportional hazard model, taking into account potential risk factors at baseline, revealed the following independent predictors of all-cause mortality: QTc-max (p < 0.05), age (p < 0.0001), albuminuria (p < 0.01), retinopathy (p < 0.01), HbA1c (p < 0.05), insulin treatment (p < 0.01), total cholesterol (p < 0.01), serum creatinine (p < 0.05), and presence of cardiac heart disease based on Minnesota coded ECG (p < 0.001). On the other hand, QT-disp was not a predictor, but QTc-max interval was an independent predictor of cardiovascular mortality. The study showed a high prevalence of QTc and QT-disp abnormalities and indicated that QTc-max, but not QT-disp, is an independent predictor of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in NIDDM patients.

title: Repriming of DNA synthesis at stalled replication forks by human PrimPol
text: When DNA replication forks fail during genome duplication, they can result in double-strand breaks, posing a threat to genome stability. This risk is higher when replication inhibitors or UV radiation is present, which introduces unique modifications to DNA. In these situations, DNA polymerases called TLS (translesion synthesis) can help fork progression by bypassing damage. Alternatively, the replisome may skip the damaged DNA, leaving an unreplicated gap that must be repaired after replication. This process requires a primer created downstream of the damage. Here, we demonstrate that PrimPol, a human primase and TLS polymerase, can mediate continuous fork progression after UV exposure and restart DNA synthesis after dNTP depletion. As an enzyme that helps tolerate DNA damage, PrimPol may become a target for cancer treatment.

title: Recombinant human tumor necrosis factor administered as a five-day continuous infusion in cancer patients: phase I toxicity and effects on lipid metabolism.
text: Recombinant human tumor necrosis factor (rH-TNF) is a cytotoxic cytokine with multiple effects.
