These findings provide new insights into the potential role of soluble corin in the pathogenesis of HDP and highlight the importance of further investigations into the mechanisms underlying this association.
Conclusion: Our study demonstrates that increased serum soluble corin levels in mid-pregnancy are associated with an increased risk of HDP. These findings provide new insights into the potential role of soluble corin in the pathogenesis of HDP and highlight the importance of further investigations into the mechanisms underlying this association.

title: The in vitro effect of dandelions antioxidants on microsomal lipid peroxidation.
text: Dandelions have been used for centuries in herbal medicine due to their versatile therapeutic properties. These properties include choleretic, diuretic, anti-inflammatory, appetite-stimulating, and laxative effects. Additionally, it is believed that an antioxidant property underlies the therapeutic effects of dandelions. To investigate the mechanism of the drug's action, the effects of natural extracts on a microsomal fraction of rat liver were examined. The extracts showed a concentration-dependent decrement in enzyme-induced lipid peroxidation and reduced cytochrome c levels, both without and with NADPH.

title: Local Ca2+ influx through Ca2+ release-activated Ca2+ (CRAC) channels stimulates production of an intracellular messenger and an intercellular pro-inflammatory signal.
text: The entry of Ca2+ through store-operated Ca2+ channels in mast cells induces the production of the pro-inflammatory molecule leukotriene C4 (LTC4) through a Ca2+-dependent protein kinase C, mitogen-activated protein kinases ERK1/2, phospholipase A2, and 5-lipoxygenase signaling pathway. Here, we investigate the role of local Ca2+ influx through plasma membrane CRAC channels in stimulating this pathway. By manipulating the amplitude and spatial extent of Ca2+ entry, we find that protein kinase C and ERK activation, arachidonic acid generation, and LTC4 secretion are all affected. However, despite similar bulk cytoplasmic Ca2+ concentrations, protein kinase C activation and LTC4 secretion are larger in high Ca2+ and La3+ conditions than in low Ca2+ conditions, suggesting that a subplasmalemmal Ca2+ rise is central to these processes. The nonreceptor tyrosine kinase Syk is found to couple CRAC channel opening to protein kinase C and ERK activation, and recombinant TRPC3 channels also activate protein kinase C, implying that subplasmalemmal Ca2+ rather than a microdomain exclusive to CRAC channels is the trigger. Overall, this study reveals the versatility of subplasmalemmal Ca2+ increases in mast cells, which can trigger both cytoplasmic responses and long-distance changes through increased secretion of paracrine signals.

title: Cytokine production patterns and lymphoproliferative responses in volunteers orally immunized with attenuated vaccine strains of Salmonella typhi.
text: New recombinant strains of attenuated Salmonella typhi, used as live oral vaccines, elicit potent immune responses. This study investigated the patterns of cytokine production and proliferation in response to specific S. typhi antigens in individuals immunized orally with attenuated S. typhi vaccines CVD 906, CVD 908, and CVD 908 expressing the circumsporozoite protein of Plasmodium falciparum. Following immunization, lymphocytes were found in the blood with significantly enhanced proliferative responses and interferon-gamma production compared to pre-immunization levels. Negative correlations were observed between interleukin-4 production and both interferon-gamma production and proliferation to S. typhi flagella. These findings demonstrate that oral immunization with attenuated S. typhi strains or those carrying a foreign gene triggers a strong systemic cell-mediated immune response to purified S. typhi antigens, including the production of cytokines characteristic of T1-type responses.

title: Molecular interplay of the noncoding RNA ANRIL and methylated histone H3 lysine 27 by polycomb CBX7 in transcriptional silencing of INK4a.
text:
The expression of the INK4b/ARF/INK4a tumor suppressor locus in normal and malignant cell growth is governed by the methylation of histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me), a process directed by the Polycomb group (PcG) proteins. The antisense noncoding RNA ANRIL, located within the INK4b/ARF/INK4a locus, also plays a crucial role in the expression of the protein-coding genes in cis, although its underlying mechanism has remained elusive. Our study uncovers the mechanism by which ANRIL interacts with chromobox 7 (CBX7), a component of the polycomb repressive complex 1. Notably, both ANRIL and CBX7 exhibit elevated levels in prostate cancer tissues. By binding to RNA and working in conjunction with H3K27me recognition, the interplay between noncoding RNA and H3K27me is crucial for the epigenetic transcriptional repression of the INK4b/ARF/INK4a locus. Our findings provide insight into the mechanism by which noncoding RNA contributes directly to epigenetic transcriptional repression.
Key points:
* The expression of the INK4b/ARF/INK4a tumor suppressor locus is controlled by histone methylation (H3K27me) directed by the Polycomb group (PcG) proteins.
* The antisense noncoding RNA ANRIL interacts with chromobox 7 (CBX7) in a way that is relevant to the expression of the INK4b/ARF/INK4a locus.
* Both ANRIL and CBX7 are found at higher levels in prostate cancer tissues.
* The interplay between noncoding RNA and H3K27me is essential for the epigenetic transcriptional repression of the INK4b/ARF/INK4a locus.
* The mechanism by which noncoding RNA contributes directly to epigenetic transcriptional repression is uncovered in our study.

title: Tumor necrosis factor alpha mediates apoptosis of brown adipocytes and defective brown adipocyte function in obesity.
text: Obesity frequently exhibits severe and comprehensive defects in both quantitative and qualitative brown adipocyte function. To explore whether aberrant TNF-alpha expression in obesity contributes to the atrophy of functional brown fat, we investigated genetically obese (ob/ob) mice with targeted null mutations in the genes encoding the two TNF receptors. Our findings revealed that the absence of both TNF receptors or the p55 receptor alone led to a significant decrease in brown adipocyte apoptosis and an increase in beta(3)-adrenoreceptor and uncoupling protein-1 expression in obese mice. Additionally, increased numbers of multi-locular functionally active brown adipocytes and improved thermoregulation were observed in obese animals lacking TNF-alpha function. These results suggest that TNF-alpha plays a crucial role in various aspects of brown adipose tissue biology and mediates the abnormalities that occur in this tissue during obesity.

title: Engineered FGF19 eliminates bile acid toxicity and lipotoxicity leading to resolution of steatohepatitis and fibrosis in mice
text:
Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a growing chronic liver condition with no approved therapies. Despite significant research efforts, the underlying mechanisms of NAFLD remain poorly understood. However, emerging evidence implicates dysregulated bile acid metabolism as a novel mechanism contributing to NAFLD pathogenesis. In particular, NAFLD patients often exhibit low levels of fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19), a hormone in the gut-liver axis that regulates bile acid synthesis, lipogenesis, and energy homeostasis.
Using a mouse model that mimics the clinical progression of human NAFLD, including the development of simple steatosis, nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), and advanced NASH with hepatocellular carcinoma, we investigated the therapeutic potential of FGF19 and its engineered nontumorigenic analogue, M70. Our results demonstrated that both FGF19 and M70 ameliorate bile acid toxicity and lipotoxicity, restoring liver health. Lipidomics analysis of liver tissues from treated mice revealed significant reductions in toxic lipid species (e.g., diacylglycerols, ceramides, and free cholesterol) and an increase in levels of unoxidized cardiolipins, an important component of the inner mitochondrial membrane. Treatment with FGF19 or M70 also rapidly improved liver enzymes, resolved NASH histological features, and enhanced insulin sensitivity, energy homeostasis, and lipid metabolism. In contrast, FGF19 induced hepatocellular carcinoma formation in mice exposed to this hormone for prolonged periods, but animals expressing M70 showed no evidence of liver tumorigenesis in this model. Our findings suggest that engineered FGF19 has the potential to be a promising therapeutic for patients with NASH by regulating multiple pathways to deliver antisteatotic, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic activities. (Hepatology Communications, 2017;1:1024-1042).

title: Leptin deficiency contributes to the pathogenesis of alcoholic fatty liver disease in mice.
text: The study investigated the effects of alcohol on adipokines and the underlying mechanisms that contribute to alcoholic fatty liver disease. Mice were fed alcohol for various periods of time to analyze changes in adipokines over time. The results showed that alcohol exposure reduced white adipose tissue (WAT) mass and body weight, accompanied by an accumulation of lipids in the liver. The plasma concentration of adiponectin was elevated at an early stage of alcohol exposure, but declined thereafter. However, alcohol exposure suppressed leptin gene expression in WAT and reduced the plasma leptin concentration. There was a highly positive correlation between plasma leptin concentration and WAT mass or body weight. To determine whether leptin deficiency contributes to the development of alcoholic fatty liver disease, mice were fed alcohol for an additional 2 weeks with or without leptin administration. Leptin administration normalized the plasma leptin concentration and reversed the alcohol-induced fatty liver. The study also found that leptin administration attenuated genes involved in fatty acid β-oxidation, very low-density lipoprotein secretion, and transcriptional regulation, which are perturbed by alcohol. Moreover, leptin normalized alcohol-reduced phosphorylation levels of signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (Stat3) and adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK). These findings demonstrate for the first time that leptin deficiency in association with WAT mass reduction plays a key role in the development of alcoholic fatty liver disease.

title: Three-dimensional chemical imaging of skin using stimulated Raman scattering microscopy
text:
Abstract:
Using Stimulated Raman Scattering (SRS) microscopy, we have obtained detailed, three-dimensional images of the structure and chemical composition of native skin. By collecting image depth stacks at different wavelengths corresponding to various vibrational modes of proteins, lipids, and water in the skin, we were able to visualize the microanatomical features of skin and the penetration of topically applied substances. Our results show that corneocytes in the stratum corneum are clustered together, ranging in size from 100 to 250 μm in diameter, and separated by thin, 10- to 25-μm-wide microanatomical skin-folds called canyons. These canyons occasionally extend down to depths comparable to that of the dermal-epidermal junction below the flat surface regions in both porcine and human skin. Using SRS imaging, we were able to detect the distribution of chemical species within these cell clusters and canyons. Water is predominantly located within the cell clusters, with its concentration increasing significantly at the boundary between the stratum corneum and viable epidermis. Conversely, canyons are rich in lipids and do not contain detectable levels of water. When oleic acid-d34 was applied to the skin surface, it lined the canyons down to a depth of 50 μm below the skin surface. This observation may have important implications for the evaluation of penetration profiles of bioactive materials using traditional methods, such as tape-stripping.

title: Familial amyloidosis: a study of 52 North American-born patients examined during a 30-year period.
text: Between 1961 and 1990, 52 patients with biopsy-proven familial amyloidosis residing in North America were evaluated at the Mayo Clinic. At the time of diagnosis, 83% of patients had peripheral neuropathy, 33% had autonomic neuropathy, and 27% had cardiomyopathy. Renal disease was rare, and liver involvement was extremely rare. The median age at diagnosis was 64 years. The sensitivity of various diagnostic biopsies was similar to that of primary amyloidosis, with deposits of amyloid found in 77-78% of subcutaneous fat aspirate or rectal biopsy specimens and 41% of bone marrow specimens. The median survival time for patients with inherited amyloidosis was 5.8 years, which was superior to that of patients with primary amyloidosis. When patients were stratified by organ involvement, the survival of patients with familial amyloidosis remained superior. The presence of cardiomyopathy and an interaction variable of age and the presence of autonomic neuropathy were powerful predictors of survival. Of the 52 patients, 22 died, with 12 (55%) dying of cardiac failure or cardiac arrhythmia, and nine (41%) dying of inanition in conjunction with progressive peripheral or autonomic neuropathy. Transthyretin was identified by immunohistochemical studies in 31 of 34 tissue specimens tested, and a transthyretin mutation was identified in 24 of these specimens. Additionally, a transthyretin mutation was found in five additional patients for whom tissue was unavailable for immunostaining.

title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and the environment within the phagosome.
text: Macrophages act as the primary immune defenders as soon as they cross the epithelial barrier. Most microorganisms meet their demise in the acidic, enzyme-rich environment of the phagolysosome. Although we have a good understanding of how phagosome maturation is regulated, we are just starting to uncover the specifics of the phagolysosome's inner environment. Through real-time functional assays that measure pH changes, phagosome/lysosome fusion, protein degradation, lipolysis, and beta-galactosidase activity, we are gaining insights into the intricacies of this process. It is particularly essential to comprehend how pathogens like Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which can manipulate the maturation process of the phagosome and maintain a pH-tolerant vacuole at around pH 6.4, are handled by the host cell. We are investigating the transcriptional response of the bacteria to the changing environment inside the macrophage phagosome. We are discovering that by manipulating these environmental signals, such as by preventing the pH drop to pH 6.4 with concanamycin A, we can greatly reduce the bacteria's transcriptional response, demonstrating that pH is the primary signal that the bacteria recognize and respond to. These approaches represent our ongoing attempts to understand the intricate dialogue between the pathogen and its host cell.

title: High density DNA methylation array with single CpG site resolution.
text: We have developed a cutting-edge genome-wide DNA methylation microarray, allowing for the comprehensive analysis of DNA methylation patterns across the human genome. Our new high-density BeadChip can interrogate over 480,000 CpG sites in parallel and detect methylation levels in twelve samples simultaneously. This innovative technology boasts an impressive coverage of 99% of RefSeq genes, with multiple probes per gene, as well as 96% of CpG islands from the UCSC database, including CpG island shores and additional content selected from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing data and expert input. We utilize the well-established Infinium® Assay for analysis of CpG methylation using bisulfite-treated genomic DNA. By applying this technology to analyze DNA methylation in normal and tumor DNA samples, we were able to generate highly comparable methylation profiles using both the microarray and sequencing methods (with an average R2 of 0.95). The ability to map genome-wide methylation patterns will expedite methylation research and provide valuable insights into the role of DNA methylation in human disease.

title: Acentrosomal Microtubule Assembly in Mitosis: The Where, When, and How.
text: During mitosis, the cell constructs a bipolar spindle, a microtubule (MT)-based structure that separates the duplicated chromosomes and divides them into two daughter cells. Most animal cells initiate mitosis with duplicated centrosomes that generate a continuous supply of dynamic MTs. However, recent research has revealed that spindle assembly actually relies on the spontaneous nucleation of acentrosomal MTs near the chromosomes after the nuclear envelope breaks down, rather than the centrosomes providing the entire MT supply. The exact mechanisms of how chromosome-dependent MT nucleation occurs, when MT amplification takes place, and how these two pathways interact are still sources of controversy. By combining the available data, we have developed a comprehensive model that explains how the cell assembles the spindle in the dividing cell.

title: Molecular mechanisms of mammalian DNA repair and the DNA damage checkpoints.
text:
DNA damage is a common occurrence in the life cycle of a cell, which can lead to mutations, cancer, and ultimately, cellular or organismic death. When DNA is damaged, the cell responds with various mechanisms to either eliminate or cope with the damage, or to initiate a programmed cell death process to eliminate cells with potentially harmful mutations. These responses include:
1. Removing DNA damage and restoring the continuity of the DNA duplex.
2. Activating a DNA damage checkpoint, which halts cell cycle progression to allow for repair and prevent the transmission of damaged or incompletely replicated chromosomes.
3. Changes in the transcription profile that may be beneficial to the cell.
4. Eliminating heavily damaged or seriously deregulated cells through apoptosis.

Different DNA repair mechanisms include direct repair, base excision repair, nucleotide excision repair, double-strand break repair, and cross-link repair. These repair processes involve various protein sensors, including ATM, ATR, Rad17-RFC, and 9-1-1 complex, to detect DNA damage and initiate signal transduction cascades that ultimately inhibit cell cycle progression from G1 to S (the G1/S checkpoint), DNA replication (the intra-S checkpoint), or G2 to mitosis (the G2/M checkpoint).

In this review, we will discuss the molecular mechanisms of DNA repair and the DNA damage checkpoints in mammalian cells, highlighting the key players involved in these processes.

title: Characterization of serotonin 5-HT2C receptor signaling to extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1 and 2.
text: Serotonin 5-HT2C receptors (5-HT2Crs) are primarily expressed in the central nervous system (CNS), and have been implicated in various disorders such as obesity, depression, and schizophrenia. We investigated the mechanisms by which 5-HT2Crs couple to extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERKs) 1/2 in CHO cells stably expressing the receptor at levels similar to those found in the brain. Using the non-RNA-edited isoform of the 5-HT2Cr, we observed constitutive ERK1/2 phosphorylation and found that this was modulated by full, partial, and inverse agonists. Interestingly, we also observed agonist-directed trafficking of the receptor stimulus, which affected the phosphoinositide accumulation and intracellular Ca2+ elevation pathways differently from the ERK1/2 pathway. Our subsequent molecular characterization revealed that 5-HT-stimulated ERK1/2 phosphorylation in this cellular background requires phospholipase D, protein kinase C, and activation of the Raf/MEK/ERK module, but is independent of both receptor- and non-receptor tyrosine kinases, phospholipase C, phosphoinositide 3-kinase, and endocytosis. Our findings highlight the potential for manipulating pathway-selective receptor states to modulate signaling pathways involved in normal and abnormal neuronal signaling.

title: Short-term medical service trips: a systematic review of the evidence.
text:
Short-term medical service trips (MSTs) aim to address unmet health care needs in low- and middle-income countries by providing much-needed medical care and support. However, a significant concern is the lack of empirical evidence regarding the activities and outcomes of these trips. To address this issue, I have conducted a systematic research review of empirical studies on MSTs to develop evidence-based recommendations for health care delivery.
My search in May 2013 yielded a total of 67 studies published since 1993, of which only 6% were found to have empirical results. Nearly 80% of these studies reported on surgical trips, highlighting the prevalence of surgical MSTs in the field. While the MST field is indeed growing, the medical literature lagging behind in providing sufficient data and analysis to support their efforts.
To addressed this issue, I propose that future MSTs prioritize data collection and analysis. By incorporating data collection into service trips, groups can validate their practices and provide valuable insights into areas that require improvement. This will not only enhance the effectiveness of MSTs but also provide a solid foundation for future research and evaluations.

title: Comparison of Beck Depression Inventories -IA and -II in psychiatric outpatients.
text: The revised Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-IA; Beck & Steer, 1993b) and the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II; Beck, Steer, & Brown, 1996) were administered to 140 psychiatric outpatients with various psychiatric disorders. The coefficient alphas of the BDI-IA and the BDI-II were, respectively, .89 and .91. Notably, the mean rating for Sadness on the BDI-IA was higher than it was on the BDI-II, but the mean ratings for Past Failure, Self-Dislike, Change in Sleeping Pattern, and Change in Appetite were higher on the BDI-II than they were on the BDI-IA. Additionally, the mean BDI-II total score was approximately 2 points higher than it was for the BDI-IA, and the outpatients also endorsed approximately one more symptom on the BDI-II than they did on the BDI-IA. Correlational analyses revealed that the BDI-IA and BDI-II total scores were similarly correlated with variables such as sex, ethnicity, age, the diagnosis of a mood disorder, and the Beck Anxiety Inventory (Beck & Steer, 1993a).

title: Tumor engraftment in nude mice and enrichment in stroma- related gene pathways predict poor survival and resistance to gemcitabine in patients with pancreatic cancer.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the engraftment rate, factors influencing engraftment, and predictability of clinical outcome of low-passage xenografts from patients with resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA) and establish a bank of PDA xenografts.
Methods: Patients with resectable PDA undergoing surgery at Johns Hopkins Hospital were enrolled in the study. Representative tumor pieces were implanted in nude mice, and the status of the SMAD4 gene and content of tumor-generating cells were determined by immunohistochemistry. Gene expression was analyzed using a U133 Plus 2.0 array. Progression-free survival and overall survival were monitored, and treatment with gemcitabine was administered to patients with metastatic disease.
Results: A total of 94 patients with PDA were resected, and 69 tumors were implanted in nude mice. Among these, 42 (61%) engrafted. Engrafted carcinomas were more frequently SMAD4 mutant and had a metastatic gene expression signature and poorer prognosis. Tumors from patients resistant to gemcitabine were enriched in stroma-related gene pathways, while tumors sensitive to gemcitabine were enriched in cell cycle and pyrimidine gene pathways. The time to progression for patients who received treatment with gemcitabine for metastatic disease was double in patients with xenografts sensitive to gemcitabine.
Conclusion: A successful xenograft was generated in 61% of patients attempted, resulting in a pool of 42 PDA xenografts with significant biological information and annotated clinical data. Patients with PDA and SMAD4 inactivation had a better engraftment rate. Engraftment was a poor prognosis factor, and engrafted tumors had a metastatic gene expression signature. Tumors from gemcitabine-resistant patients were enriched in stromal pathways.

title: The MCM8-MCM9 complex promotes RAD51 recruitment at DNA damage sites to facilitate homologous recombination.
text: Prior research has suggested that the minichromosome maintenance proteins MCM8 and MCM9 play roles in DNA replication and prereplication complex (pre-RC) formation, respectively. We have found that these proteins interact with one another and that MCM8 is essential for maintaining the stability of MCM9 in mammalian cells. When MCM8 or MCM9 is depleted or mutated in human cancer cells or mouse embryonic fibroblasts, cells become more sensitive to the DNA cross-linking agent cisplatin. Consistently, decreasing the amount of MCM8 or MCM9 impairs the ability of cells to repair DNA damage through homologous recombination (HR). Using chromatin immunoprecipitation analysis with human DR-GFP cells or Xenopus egg extract, we have observed that MCM8 and MCM9 rapidly accrue at sites of DNA damage and facilitate the recruitment of the key HR protein RAD51. These findings suggest that these two metazoan-specific MCM homologs are novel components of HR and may represent viable targets for cancer treatment in combination with DNA cross-linking agents.

title: The 5TMM series: a useful in vivo mouse model of human multiple myeloma.
text:
The present invention offers a novel combination of a sink and dishwashing apparatus, featuring a shared side wall between a cabinet and the sink. The cabinet houses a wire basket for washing multiple dishes within the closed space defined by the cabinet. The common side wall, located along one side of the sink, can be opened to allow the wire basket to slide in and out of the sink for loading and unloading dishes.
Inside the cabinet, the invention introduces a motor-powered pump that sprays water through a rotating spray arm to clean the dishes in a manner similar to traditional dishwashing machines. Additionally, the invention may include a garbage disposal powered by the same motor.
Alternatively, the invention can consist of two adjacent cabinets on opposite sides of the sink, each serving the same purpose as the single cabinet described above.

title: Ionic protein-lipid interaction at the plasma membrane: what can the charge do?
text: Phospholipids are the primary structural components of cell membranes, yet they exert functional roles beyond their role in creating lipid bilayers. Specifically, acidic phospholipids form specialized microdomains in the plasma membrane, where they can ionically interact with proteins through polybasic sequences, leading to significant consequences for the protein's function. The list of proteins affected by these ionic interactions has expanded dramatically, encompassing both membrane proteins and soluble cytoplasmic proteins, as well as viral proteins. We will herein examine how acidic phospholipids in the plasma membrane regulate protein structure and function through ionic interactions, as well as the mechanisms by which calcium (Ca2+) influences these interactions via both direct and indirect means.

title: A20 is overexpressed in glioma cells and may serve as a potential therapeutic target.
text:
Objective A20 is a tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-inducible primary response gene that has been found to have antiapoptotic functions in various cancer cells. This study investigated A20 expression in human glioma tissues and four glioma cell lines, and its impact on tumorigenesis of glioma cells and a mouse tumor model.
Methods:
Human glioma tissue samples and cells were subjected to reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Glioma cells were tested using flow cytometry. A xenograft tumor model in mice was used to assess the knock-down effect of specific A20 small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) on tumorigenesis.
Results:
A20 was overexpressed in 63.9% of clinical glioma tissue samples and correlated with clinical staging. All four human glioma cell lines expressed A20, with U87 displaying the strongest expression signals. Inhibiting A20 expression using siRNAs in vitro reduced the growth rates of glioma cells and resulted in G1/S arrest and increased apoptosis. Local administration of siRNA in a mouse tumor model significantly suppressed solid tumor growth.

Conclusions:
A20 was overexpressed in both human glioma tissues and cell lines, and inhibiting A20 expression significantly slowed tumor cell growth in culture and in mice. These findings suggest that A20 is involved in tumorigenesis of human glioma and may serve as a future therapeutic target.

title: Prevalence and size of directly detected patent foramen ovale in migraine with aura.
text:
Migraine patients with aura have a higher prevalence of right-to-left shunts compared to healthy controls, according to a new study. Using transesophageal contrast echocardiography, the authors investigated the anatomy and size of these shunts in 93 migraine patients with aura and 93 healthy controls.
Findings revealed that 47% of migraine patients had a patent foramen ovale, a small shunt, or a moderate-sized or large shunt. In contrast, only 17% of controls had a patent foramen ovale and similar sized shunts. The presence of more than a small shunt increased the odds of having migraine with aura by 7.78-fold.
Interestingly, the study found no significant echocardiographic differences between the two groups beyond patent foramen ovale prevalence and shunt size. Moreover, headache and baseline characteristics were similar in migraine patients with and without a patent foramen ovale.
In conclusion, the study highlights that nearly half of migraine patients with aura have a right-to-left shunt due to a patent foramen ovale, with larger shunts observed in migraineurs compared to controls. The findings suggest that patent foramen ovale may be a key factor in the development of migraine with aura, underscoring the need for further research into this promising area.

title: A Live Attenuated Chimeric West Nile Virus Vaccine, rWN/DEN4&Dgr;30, Is Well Tolerated and Immunogenic in Flavivirus-Naive Older Adult Volunteers
text: West Nile virus (WNV) poses a significant threat to public health in the United States, causing a range of illnesses from mild fever to severe neurological infections. Adults aged 60 and older are particularly vulnerable to the latter, with a high mortality rate or prolonged neurological sequelae. In a promising development, a chimeric live attenuated WNV vaccine, rWN/DEN4&Dgr;30, has been shown to be safe and immunogenic in healthy adults aged 18-50. This study aimed to evaluate the vaccine in flavivirus-naive adults aged 50-65, and found it to be safe and immunogenic. With unpredictable outbreaks of WNV infection occurring frequently, a reliable and effective vaccine will be a valuable tool in controlling the spread of the virus.

title: Localization and requirement for Myosin II at the dorsal-ventral compartment boundary of the Drosophila wing.
text: As organisms evolve, cell populations within tissues can become segregated into distinct groups through the formation of barriers. Despite being observed in various tissues, the molecular mechanisms responsible for these barriers are poorly understood in many cases. For instance, in the Drosophila wing, a Notch activation strip maintains the dorsal-ventral compartment boundary, which depends on the actin cytoskeleton. We discovered that the dorsal-ventral boundary exhibits a distinct accumulation of Myosin II, and this accumulation is regulated downstream of Notch signaling. Conversely, the dorsal-ventral boundary is depleted for the Par-3 homologue Bazooka. Our findings further reveal that mutations in the Myosin heavy chain subunit encoded by zipper can impair dorsal-ventral compartmentalization without affecting anterior-posterior compartmentalization. These observations highlight a distinct requirement and accumulation of Myosin activity in dorsal-ventral compartmentalization, suggesting that contractile tension along an F-actin cable at the compartment boundary plays a novel role in compartmentalization.

title: The cause of hepatic accumulation of fructose 1-phosphate on fructose loading.
text: 1. The metabolic changes in livers of fed rats subjected to perfusion with 10 mmol/L fructose were investigated, focusing on the effects of fructose on metabolite content. 2. Fructose exposure resulted in the accumulation of fructose 1-phosphate (up to 8.7 μmol/g liver within 10 min), a decrease in total adenine nucleotides (up to 35% after 40 min) and a corresponding decrease in ATP content to 23% within 10 min, as well as a sevenfold increase in IMP and an eightfold increase in alpha-glycerophosphate. 3. A transient decrease in Pi from 4.2 to 1.7 μmol/g was observed, followed by a recovery to normal values within 40 min, likely due to uptake of Pi from the perfusion medium. 4. The degradation of adenine nucleotides beyond the stage of AMP can be attributed to the decrease in ATP and Pi, as ATP inhibits 5-nucleotidase and Pi inhibits AMP deaminase, allowing for the dephosphorylation or deamination of AMP in the tissue. 5. The liver concentration of lactate increased to 4.3 μmol/g at 80 min, while pyruvate also increased, resulting in a [lactate]/[pyruvate] ratio within physiological limits. 6. The amount of free fructose within the liver remained significantly lower than the concentration in the perfusion medium, indicating that the rate of fructose uptake into the tissue was lower than its metabolism. 7. The inhibition of fructose 1-phosphate fission by liver aldolase is competitive with a Ki of 0.1 mm, and the accumulation of fructose 1-phosphate on fructose loading is attributed to the inhibition of fructose 1-phosphate fission by the IMP arising from the degradation of adenine nucleotides. 8. The maximum rates of enzymes synthesizing and splitting fructose 1-phosphate are roughly equal, and the accumulation of fructose 1-phosphate on fructose loading is due to the inhibition of the fission of fructose 1-phosphate by the IMP arising from the degradation of adenine nucleotides.

title: Reported side effects to chloroquine, chloroquine plus proguanil, and mefloquine as chemoprophylaxis against malaria in Danish travelers.
text:
Background:
The study aimed to compare the relative frequency of reported symptoms among travelers who used chloroquine, chloroquine plus proguanil, or mefloquine as malaria prophylaxis.
Method:
The study was an open, non-randomized study that recorded self-reported events in travelers recruited consecutively from two travel clinics in Copenhagen, Denmark. The main outcome measures were the relative proportion of travelers reporting particular symptoms in the three prophylaxis groups, compliance, hospitalization, and premature termination of the travel.
Results:
From May 1996 to April 1998, a total of 5,446 travelers were included, and 4,158 questionnaires (76.3%) were returned. Compliance was significantly better in mefloquine users (83.3% in short-term travelers) compared to chloroquine plus proguanil users (76.3%). Additionally, 84.8%, 59.3%, and 69.5% of travelers using chloroquine, chloroquine plus proguanil, and mefloquine, respectively, reported no symptoms, while 0.6%, 1.1%, and 2.8% reported "unacceptable" symptoms. Compared to chloroquine, mefloquine users had a significantly higher risk of reporting depression (RR 5.06, 95% CI 2.71-9.45), "strange thoughts" (RR 6.36, 95% CI 2.52-16.05), and altered spatial perception (RR 3.00, 95% CI 1.41-6.41).
Conclusion:
Overall, mefloquine was found to be at least as well tolerated as chloroquine plus proguanil, with better compliance. However, travelers using mefloquine reported more symptoms related to the central nervous system, which were perceived as more severe.

title: Ubiquitinylation of the cytosolic domain of a type I membrane protein is not required to initiate its dislocation from the endoplasmic reticulum.
text: Human cytomegalovirus US2 and US11 proteins target newly synthesized class I major histocompatibility complex (MHC) heavy chains for rapid degradation through a process called dislocation. Unlike US11, US2 induces the formation of class I MHC heavy chain conjugates of increased molecular weight, which are recognized by a specific monoclonal antibody called W6/32. These conjugates are properly glycosylated and folded heavy chains modified with one, two, or three ubiquitin molecules. In contrast to US11, US2 targets class I MHC heavy chains in a distinct manner, and the two proteins have different requirements for the heavy chain molecule's conformation. Although ubiquitin conjugation may occur on the cytosolic tail of the class I MHC molecule, replacing lysines in the tail with arginine does not prevent degradation by US2. In an in vitro system mimicking US2-mediated dislocation, heavy chains lacking these lysines still occur in an ubiquitin-modified form, but in the soluble (cytoplasmic) fraction. Ubiquitin conjugation on the class I MHC lumenal domain likely occurs after discharge from the endoplasmic reticulum, and is not required during the initial step of US2-mediated dislocation. Therefore, we conclude that ubiquitinylation of class I MHC heavy chains is not essential during the initial step of US2-mediated dislocation.

title: The adaptor protein Tks5/Fish is required for podosome formation and function, and for the protease-driven invasion of cancer cells.
text:
Here is a possible reconstruction of the given text:
Tks5/Fish is a protein that functions as a scaffolding molecule, consisting of five SH3 domains and one PX domain. In cells transformed by the Src protein, Tks5/Fish localizes to structures called podosomes, which are protrusions on the ventral surface of the cell membrane. When we reduced the levels of Tks5/Fish in Src-transformed cells, they were no longer able to form podosomes, degrade the extracellular matrix protein gelatin, or invade surrounding tissue. We observed Tks5/Fish expression in podosomes in invasive cancer cells and in human breast cancer and melanoma samples. Furthermore, Tks5/Fish expression was necessary for protease-driven invasion of matrigel in human cancer cells. Finally, when we co-expressed Tks5/Fish and Src in epithelial cells, podosomes began to form. Therefore, it appears that Tks5/Fish plays a crucial role in podosome formation, extracellular matrix degradation, and invasion of certain cancer cells.

title: Corticosteroid injections for shoulder pain.
text:
Background: While various treatments, including corticosteroid injections in and around the shoulder, are commonly advocated for shoulder pain relief, there is limited evidence proving their efficacy. This review aims to determine the effectiveness and safety of corticosteroid injections in the treatment of shoulder pain in adults.
Objectives: To assess the efficacy and safety of corticosteroid injections in the treatment of shoulder pain in adults by conducting a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
Search Strategy: MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and the Science Citation Index were searched up to and including June 2002 for RCTs of corticosteroid injections compared to placebo or another intervention in adults with shoulder pain.
Selection Criteria: Randomized and pseudo-randomized trials that involved corticosteroid injections in adults with shoulder pain were included, with specific exclusions such as durations of shoulder pain less than three weeks, rheumatoid arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, and fracture.
Data Collection and Analysis: Two independent reviewers assessed the inclusion and methodological quality of the trials according to predetermined criteria. The results were presented separately for rotator cuff disease, adhesive capsulitis, full-thickness rotator cuff tear, and mixed diagnoses, and a meta-analysis was performed where possible.
Main Results: Twenty-six RCTs met the inclusion criteria, with varying numbers, sites, and dosages of injections. The number of participants per trial ranged from 20 to 114 (median 52 participants), and the methodological quality was variable. For rotator cuff disease, subacromial steroid injection showed a small benefit over placebo in some trials, but no benefit of subacromial steroid injection over nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) was demonstrated based on the pooled results of three trials. For adhesive capsulitis, two trials suggested a possible early benefit of intra-articular steroid injection over placebo, but there was insufficient data for pooling of any of the trials. One trial suggested a short-term benefit of intra-articular corticosteroid injection over physiotherapy in the short term (success at seven weeks: relative risk of 1.66, 1.21 to 2.28).
Reviewers' Conclusions: Despite numerous RCTs of corticosteroid injections for shoulder pain, their small sample sizes, variable methodological quality, and heterogeneity mean that there is little overall evidence to guide treatment. Subacromial corticosteroid injection for rotator cuff disease may be beneficial, although its effect may be small and not well-maintained. More research is needed to investigate the efficacy of corticosteroid injections for shoulder pain, including clarifying whether the accuracy of needle placement, anatomical site, frequency, dose, and type of corticosteroid influences efficacy.

title: IL-2 receptor signaling is essential for the development of Klrg1+ terminally differentiated T regulatory cells.
text: Thymic-derived natural T regulatory cells (Tregs) exhibit functional and phenotypic heterogeneity. Recent studies have shown that a small proportion of peripheral Tregs express the protein Klrg1, but it is unclear how much Klrg1 definition defines a unique Treg subset. This investigation aims to determine whether Klrg1(+) Tregs represent a distinct terminal differentiation subset derived from Klrg1(-) Tregs. Our findings indicate that Klrg1(+) Tregs are a recent Ag-responsive, highly activated short-lived Treg population residing predominantly in mucosal tissues. This subset exhibits elevated levels of Treg suppressive molecules and requires extensive IL-2R signaling for its development. These properties are reminiscent of terminally differentiated short-lived CD8(+) T effector cells, suggesting an important pathway for Ag-activated conventional T lymphocytes to also operate in Tregs. This work highlights the diverse nature of Tregs and uncovers a novel function for IL-2 in Treg differentiation.

title: The aurora B kinase promotes inner and outer kinetochore interactions in budding yeast.
text: The kinetochore, a macromolecular protein complex, plays a central role in chromosome segregation. The Dsn1 component is particularly important for kinetochore assembly and is phosphorylated by the Aurora B kinase. Our findings reveal that Aurora B phosphorylation of Dsn1 enhances the interaction between outer and inner kinetochore proteins in budding yeast.

title: AMP-activated/SNF1 protein kinases: conserved guardians of cellular energy
text: The SNF1/AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) family plays a crucial role in maintaining the delicate balance between ATP production and consumption in all eukaryotic cells. These kinases are composed of a catalytic subunit and regulatory subunits that sense cellular energy levels, allowing them to activate catabolic pathways and inhibit protein, carbohydrate, and lipid biosynthesis, as well as cell growth and proliferation, when energy status is compromised. However, recent studies have shed light on the system's broader functions, revealing that AMPK also plays a key role in maintaining cell polarity in epithelial cells.

title: Mammographic density, plasma vitamin D levels and risk of breast cancer in postmenopausal women.
text: The relationship between mammographic density and breast cancer risk is well established, but the underlying biology remains unclear. Some studies suggest that vitamin D may play a protective role in reducing breast cancer risk, and dietary vitamin D intake has been associated with reduced breast density. To investigate the potential mechanisms underlying this association, we conducted a case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study cohort. We included 463 postmenopausal cases and 497 controls and measured mammographic density, as well as plasma levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D [1,25(OH)(2)D]. We found that women in the highest tertile of mammographic density had a fourfold increased risk of breast cancer compared to those in the lowest tertile of plasma 25(OH)D levels. However, there was no significant cross-sectional association between circulating levels of 25(OH)D or 1,25(OH)(2)D and mammographic density. Our results suggest that the association between mammographic density and breast cancer is independent of plasma vitamin D metabolites in postmenopausal women. Further research is warranted to explore the potential role of vitamin D in reducing breast cancer risk.

title: Finding the right niche: B-cell migration in the early phases of T-dependent antibody responses.
text: The migration of B cells during humoral immune responses is a complex and highly regulated process. B cells encounters antigen, interacts with helper T cells, proliferates, and differentiates into low-affinity plasma cells or, after organizing into a germinal center (GC), high-affinity plasma cells and memory B cells. Each stage of this process is associated with specific stromal cells in different subcompartments of the lymphoid tissue. B cells must migrate rapidly and efficiently between these niches to successfully mount an immune response. The chemokine CXCL13 plays a central role in guiding B cells to follicles, while T-zone chemokines direct activated B cells to the T zone. Additionally, sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) promotes cell egress from the tissue and marginal-zone B-cell positioning in the spleen. Recent studies have also highlighted the role of the orphan receptor, EBV-induced molecule 2 (EBI2; GPR183), in guiding activated B cells to inter and outer follicular niches, and down-regulation of this receptor is essential for organizing cells into GCs. This review summarizes current understanding of the roles played by chemokines, S1P, and EBI2 in the migration events that underlie humoral immune responses.

title: Arginine Starvation Impairs Mitochondrial Respiratory Function in ASS1-Deficient Breast Cancer Cells
text:
Autophagy is the primary catabolic response to nutrient deprivation and is essential for removing damaged or dysfunctional organelles. However, excessive autophagy can be toxic or cytostatic and can lead to cell death. Depending on the availability of enzymes involved in molecule biosynthesis, cells may be dependent on exogenous nutrient uptake to obtain these molecules. Argininosuccinate synthetase 1 (ASS1) is a crucial enzyme in arginine biosynthesis, and its abundance is often reduced in various types of solid tumors, making these cells sensitive to external arginine depletion.
We demonstrated that prolonged arginine starvation by exposure to ADI-PEG20 (pegylated arginine deiminase) resulted in autophagy-dependent death in ASS1-deficient breast cancer cells. These cells are arginine auxotrophs, requiring external arginine for their survival. Additionally, exposure to ADI-PEG20 or culturing breast cancer cells in the absence of arginine led to their death in vitro and in vivo. Arginine starvation caused mitochondrial oxidative stress, impairing mitochondrial bioenergetics and integrity. Furthermore, only autophagy-competent breast cancer cells were vulnerable to arginine starvation-induced death.
Interestingly, ASS1 is low or absent in over 60% of 149 random breast cancer biosamples, suggesting that patients with such tumors may be potential candidates for arginine starvation therapy. In conclusion, a key mechanism underlying the lethality induced by prolonged arginine starvation is the cytotoxic autophagy that occurs in response to mitochondrial damage.

title: A prospective natural-history study of coronary atherosclerosis.
text: In a study of 697 patients who experienced an acute coronary syndrome and underwent percutaneous coronary intervention, the researchers found that major adverse cardiovascular events occurring during follow-up were equally attributed to recurrence at the site of the initial (culprit) lesions and to nonculprit lesions. Although nonculprit lesions responsible for unanticipated events were often angiographically mild, they were more likely to be characterized by a large plaque burden, a small luminal area, or some combination of these features, as determined by gray-scale and radiofrequency intravascular ultrasonography. The study suggests that thin-cap fibroatheromas, which are typically identified by intravascular ultrasonography, may play a role in the development of unanticipated events. The findings suggest that it is important to consider the potential risks of nonculprit lesions in patients who have experienced an acute coronary syndrome, even if they appear mild on angiography. (Funded by Abbott Vascular and Volcano; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00180466.)

title: What do medical schools teach about women's health and gender differences?
text:
Objective: To investigate the inclusion of women's health and gender-specific content in medical school curricula and identify institutional factors associated with its presence.
Methodology: The authors conducted a curriculum search of medical schools using data from the Association of American Medical Colleges' Curriculum Management and Information Tool (CurrMIT) from November 2003 to February 2004. They identified schools that entered interdisciplinary women's health or gender-specific courses/clerkships and analyzed a subset of schools that provided comprehensive information in CurrMIT for a list of specified women's health topics and gender-specific content on any topic. Statistical analyses were performed to assess the relationship between the frequency of topics and school characteristics.
Findings: Of the 95 schools identified, ten met the criteria for an interdisciplinary women's health course/clerkship, and in the subset of 60 schools with comprehensive CurrMIT information, 18 specified women's health topics and 24 topics on gender-specific content were identified, for a total of 42 topics. The number of topics taught ranged from zero to 26, with more than 50% of schools teaching 11 of the 18 specified topics and fewer than 30% including gender-specific topics. In a regression model, a women's health program and having a female dean were positively associated with the inclusion of gender-specific content in the curriculum.
Conclusion: Few medical schools offer interdisciplinary women's health courses and include gender-specific content in their curricula. A designated women's health program may increase the inclusion of this content in medical school curricula.

title: A molecular framework for plant regeneration.
text: Plants and some animals have the remarkable ability to regenerate organs from adult tissues. While the molecular mechanisms behind this process have been largely unexplored, our research focuses on a local regeneration response in Arabidopsis roots. Using laser-induced wounding, we disrupt the flow of auxin, a cell-fate-instructive plant hormone, in root tips. We find that the resulting cell-fate changes require the collaboration of three transcription factors: PLETHORA, SHORTROOT, and SCARECROW. These transcription factors regulate the expression and polar position of PIN auxin efflux-facilitating membrane proteins to reestablish auxin transport in renewed root tips. In essence, a regeneration mechanism that utilizes embryonic root stem-cell patterning factors first responds to and then stabilizes a new hormone distribution.

title: Cocoa flavonols and procyanidins promote transforming growth factor-beta1 homeostasis in peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
text: Research suggests that certain flavan-3-ols and procyanidins (FP) may have a positive impact on cardiovascular health. Previous studies have shown that FP isolated from cocoa can affect the production of signaling molecules linked to immune function and inflammation, including cytokines and eicosanoids. In this study, we investigated whether FP fractions, ranging from monomers to decamers, could modulate the release of the cytokine transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta(1) from resting human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC). A total of 13 healthy individuals were involved in the study, and their baseline TGF-beta(1) production was grouped into low and high levels. Stimulation of cells from low TGF-beta(1) individuals with individual FP fractions (25 microg/ml) resulted in enhanced TGF-beta(1) release, ranging from 15% to 66% over baseline (P < 0.05; monomer, dimer, and tetramer). The low-molecular-weight FP fractions (<or=pentamer) were more effective at augmenting TGF-beta(1) secretion than larger counterparts (>or=hexamer), with the monomer and dimer inducing the greatest increases (66% and 68%, respectively). In contrast, TGF-beta(1) secretion from high TGF-beta(1) baseline subjects was inhibited by individual FP fractions (P < 0.05; trimer through decamer). Inhibition was most pronounced with trimeric through decameric fractions (28%-42%), and monomers and dimers moderately inhibited TGF-beta(1) release (17% and 23%, respectively). The mechanisms by which FP-rich foods may benefit cardiovascular health through the modulation of TGF-beta(1) production offer an additional benefit to their vascular actions.

title: BMP receptor IA is required in mammalian neural crest cells for development of the cardiac outflow tract and ventricular myocardium.
text: The neural crest, a multipotent and migratory cell population derived from the boundary between the neural and surface ectoderm, undergoes continuous developmental migration in mice, commencing at the five-somite stage. The BMPs, particularly BMP2 and BMP4, have been implicated as regulators of neural crest cell induction, maintenance, migration, differentiation, and survival. Mouse models have identified three type I BMP receptors, Bmpr1a, which is expressed sufficiently early in the neural tube to be involved in neural crest development from the onset, though earlier roles in other anatomical domains approximation its requirement in the neural crest. To investigate the necessity of BMPRIA in the neural crest, we conducted ablation studies beginning at the five-somite stage. Our findings suggest that most aspects of neural crest development occur normally, indicating that BMPRIA is dispensable for many aspects of early neural crest biology. However, mutant embryos display a narrowed outflow tract with imperfect septation, a process that necessitates neural crest cells and is fundamental for fetal viability. Surprisingly, these embryos perish prematurely from acute heart failure due to reduced proliferation of ventricular myocardium. This myocardial defect may be attributable to diminished BMP signaling in a minor, novel population of neural crest derivatives located in the epicardium, which serves as a prominent source of ventricular myocardial proliferation signals. These results underscore the importance of BMP2/4 signaling in mammalian neural crest derivatives for outflow tract development and highlight the possibility that this signaling pathway regulates a crucial proliferation cue for the ventricular myocardium.

title: Early intermittent noninvasive ventilation for acute chest syndrome in adults with sickle cell disease: a pilot study
text:
Introduction: Alveolar hypoxia and hypoxic vasoconstriction can cause sickle cells to become trapped in the pulmonary vasculature, leading to poor oxygenation and acute chest syndrome (ACS). Improving alveolar ventilation and oxygenation may improve the outcome of ACS. A randomized, single-center, open-label study was conducted from November 1998 to February 2002 to evaluate whether noninvasive ventilation (NIV) was more effective than oxygen therapy in improving oxygenation in adults with ACS.
Methods: Consecutive ACS episodes in 67 patients were randomly allocated to either oxygen therapy (n=36) or NIV (n=35) for 3 days in a medical step-down unit. Baseline respiratory rate and pain score were higher in the NIV group. NIV quickly lowered respiratory rate, increased PaO2, and decreased the alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient (A-aO2). However, PaCO2 worsened significantly only in the oxygen group. On day 3, the groups did not differ in the proportion of episodes with normal PaO2 (35% with NIV and 25% with oxygen; P=0.5) or the alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient (A-aO2). Patient satisfaction and compliance were lower with NIV. No differences were noted in pain relief, transfusions, or length of stay. In the subgroup of patients with severe hypoxemia (PaO2 ≤ 65 mmHg), physiological variables improved faster with NIV, with slightly more pronounced differences. Respiratory rate and gas exchange improved faster with NIV, but NIV failed to significantly reduce the number of patients remaining hypoxemic at day 3 and was associated with greater patient discomfort.
Conclusion: The study found that NIV was not more effective than oxygen therapy in improving oxygenation in adults with acute chest syndrome (ACS). While NIV improved respiratory rate and gas exchange, it failed to significantly reduce the number of patients remaining hypoxemic at day 3 and was associated with greater patient discomfort. Oxygen therapy was more effective in reducing the alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient and improving PaCO2 levels. Further research is needed to determine the optimal treatment strategy for ACS.

title: Serum Exosome MicroRNA as a Minimally-Invasive Early Biomarker of AML
text: Relapse remains the major contributor to mortality in patients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). Enhanced tracking of minimal residual disease (MRD) offers the potential for timely treatment adjustments to prevent relapse. Current surveillance methods detect circulating blasts that coincide with advanced disease and poorly reflect MRD during early relapse. In this investigation, we explore the use of exosomes as a non-invasive platform for a microRNA (miRNA) biomarker. We identify a specific set of miRNAs enriched in AML exosomes and assess the levels of circulating exosome miRNA in leukemic xenografts, non-engrafted controls, and human CD34+ cells. We develop statistical models that reveal the presence of circulating exosomal miRNA at low marrow tumor burden and before detectable circulating blasts. Notably, both leukemic blasts and marrow stroma contribute to serum exosome miRNA. We propose the development of serum exosome miRNA as a novel, sensitive compartment biomarker for prospective tracking and early detection of AML recurrence.

title: Human cytomegalovirus encodes an MHC class I-like molecule (UL142) that functions to inhibit NK cell lysis.
text: Clinical and low passage strains of human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) encode an extra MHC class I-related molecule named UL142, in addition to the previously described UL18. The UL142 open reading frame is located within the ULb' region, which is absent from many common high passage laboratory strains. We used transfected cells and fibroblasts infected with a recombinant adenovirus for UL142 expression to evaluate the impact on natural killer (NK) cell killing. We examined 100 NK cell clones derived from five donors and discovered 23 clones that were inhibited by fibroblasts expressing UL142 alone. We also found that by using small interfering RNA (siRNA) to reduce UL142 mRNA expression, HCMV-infected cells became more susceptible to lysis. Based on these results, we conclude that UL142 is a novel HCMV-encoded MHC class I-related molecule that inhibits NK cell killing in a clonally dependent manner.

title: Identification of the conserved serine/threonine residues important for gibberellin-sensitivity of Arabidopsis RGL2 protein.
text: The DELLA proteins GAI, RGA, RGL1, and RGL2 in Arabidopsis serve as negative regulators of plant growth, hindering various developmental processes. Research has shown that gibberellin (GA) can weaken the repressive role of DELLA proteins by inducing their degradation through the proteasome pathway. Nonetheless, it remains unclear if GA-mediated protein degradation is the sole means of regulating the biological activity of DELLA proteins. To address this uncertainty, we employed the tobacco BY2 cell system to investigate GA signaling. We discovered that RGL2 exists in a phosphorylated form in BY2 cells and undergoes GA-induced degradation, which can be obstructed by proteasome inhibitors and serine/threonine phosphatase inhibitors, yet serine/threonine kinase inhibitors have no detectable effect, suggesting that dephosphorylation of serine/threonine is necessary for RGL2 degradation via the proteasome pathway. Further investigation revealed that mutating all 17 conserved serine and threonine residues in RGL2 resulted in six mutants (RGL2(S441D), RGL2(S542D), RGL2(T271E), RGL2(T319E), RGL2(T411E), and RGL2(T535E)) that mimicked the constitutive phosphorylation status and were resistant to GA-induced degradation. These findings implicate these sites as potential phosphorylation sites. A functional experiment based on GA 20-oxidase expression revealed that RGL2(T271E) is likely a null mutant, while RGL2(S441D), RGL2(S542D), RGL2(T319E), RGL2(T411E), and RGL2(T535E) retained varying levels of activity, with RGL2(T535E) retaining approximately 66% of the wild-type RGL2's activity. However, expression of GA 20-oxidase in cells expressing these mutant proteins remained responsive to GA, suggesting that enhancing RGL2 protein stability is not the sole means of regulating its bioactivity.

title: A chart review of cyproheptadine for stimulant-induced weight loss.
text: Children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often experience weight loss when taking stimulants, which can complicate optimal dosing and adherence. However, studies have shown that the antihistamine cyproheptadine can promote weight gain in these individuals. In this study, we retrospectively analyzed medical records of 28 pediatric psychiatry outpatients who were prescribed cyproheptadine for weight loss or insomnia while taking stimulants. We found that 4 patients did not consistently take cyproheptadine, and 3 discontinued it within the first week due to intolerable side effects. Of the remaining 21 patients, 17 had lost weight on stimulants alone, but all of them gained weight when taking cyproheptadine (mean gain of 2.2 kg, p < 0.0001). In addition, 11 of the 17 patients who initially experienced insomnia on stimulants alone saw significant improvements in sleep after adding cyproheptadine. Our findings suggest that cyproheptadine may be a useful adjunct in treating weight loss associated with stimulants in children with ADHD, pending further randomized controlled trials.

title: Life course breast cancer risk factors and adult breast density (United Kingdom)
text:
Objective: To investigate whether risk factors in childhood and early adulthood are associated with breast density on mammograms later in life.
Methods: We analyzed data from 628 women who underwent a medical examination at the University of Glasgow Student Health Service between 1948 and 1968, completed a questionnaire in 2001, and had a screening mammogram in Scotland between 1989 and 2002. Mammograms were classified into six categories based on breast density percentages. Logistic regression was used to identify associations between risk factors and having a high-risk mammogram (≥25 dense).
Results: In multivariate analyses, high-risk mammograms were associated with parity (odds ratio (OR) per child: 0.77, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.61–0.99), age at first birth (OR per year: 1.05, 0.99–1.11), smoking at university (OR smokers versus non-smokers: 0.58, 0.36–0.92), and body mass index (BMI) while at university (OR per 1kg/m2: 0.75, 0.69–0.82). No significant associations were found for age at menarche, birth weight, oral contraceptive (OC) use, height, leg length, or exercise at age 20.
Conclusions: We confirm previous findings that breast density is influenced by reproductive events and some anthropometric measures, but most of the risk factors we examined that occur throughout the life course had little to no impact on adult breast density.

title: Osteoclast nuclei of myeloma patients show chromosome translocations specific for the myeloma cell clone: a new type of cancer-host partnership?
text:
The text can be rewritten as follows:
A hallmark of bone cancers is the destruction of bone tissue, which is generally believed to be caused by osteoclasts, specialized cells of monocytic origin that are the only cells capable of degrading bone. Recent research has revealed additional insights into this process, showing that bone-resorbing osteoclasts from myeloma patients contain nuclei with translocated chromosomes bearing the genetic material of the myeloma B-cell clone, in addition to nuclei without these translocations. Through a combination of fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and immunohistochemistry on bone sections, these malignant nuclei were found to be transcriptionally active and fully integrated into the normal osteoclast population. The contribution of malignant nuclei to the osteoclast population analyzed in this study was greater than 30%, and osteoclast-myeloma clone hybrids were found to contain more nuclei than normal osteoclasts, with their occurrence correlating with the proximity of myeloma cells. Furthermore, myeloma cells were able to fuse with osteoclasts in co-culture experiments, leading to the generation of hybrid cells bearing malignant nuclei. These findings suggest that malignant cells play a significant role in the formation of bone-resorbing osteoclasts in multiple myeloma, and that the mechanisms of bone destruction in cancer may be more complex and dynamic than previously thought. The ability of malignant cells to corrupt host cells through the transfer of malignant DNA may have been underestimated in cancer research thus far.

title: Frequency modulation entrains slow neural oscillations and optimizes human listening behavior.
text: The ability of humans to continuously track dynamic environmental stimuli, particularly speech, is believed to be enhanced through the process of "entrainment" of endogenous neural oscillations, which involves the reorganization of phase patterns to coincide with anticipated critical events. Previous studies have focused on either how broadly entrainment occurs to environmental rhythms (i.e., can neural oscillations be entrained by gentle, continuous rhythmic stimuli without abrupt onsets?) or whether entrainment improves perceptual processing (i.e., does reorganization of neural phase patterns enhance cognitive performance?). To further address these questions, the current experiment employed a human electroencephalography (EEG) study in which listeners detected brief gaps in a 3-Hz frequency-modulated stimulus distributed uniformly across the phase angle. However, instead of being randomly distributed throughout time, the listeners' ability to detect gaps clustered in specific phases of the modulation, indicating that neural entrainment plays a role in perceptual processing. Furthermore, the optimal stimulus phase was found to be individually determined by the neural delta oscillation, which was itself entrained by the stimulus. Notably, delta phase was a better predictor of behavior than stimulus phase or the subsequent event-related potential (ERP), suggesting that phase realignment in response to frequency-modified auditory stimuli can have a significant impact on perceptual processing. Overall, this study suggests that fluctuations in frequency in natural environmental stimuli function as a guiding signal for endogenous neural oscillations, thereby influencing cognitive processing.

title: Interventions by pharmacists in out-patient pharmaceutical care.
text: Pharmacist interventions have long been regarded as a valuable input to the patient care process by reducing medication errors, rationalizing therapy, and decreasing treatment costs. This study aimed to determine the frequency and types of medication errors intervened by dispensing pharmacists at the OPD pharmacy of Khoula Hospital during 2009 through a retrospective analysis of interventions filed by pharmacists and assistant pharmacists in the OPD pharmacy. The study found that 72.3% of interventions were minor, with 40.5% related to changes in medication orders. Prescriptions for female patients were more frequently intervened than those for male patients. Notably, 98.2% of interventions were accepted by prescribers, indicating the doctors' awareness of the importance of pharmacy practice. A total of 688 interventions were due to prescribing errors, with 40.5% related to changing or clarifying medication orders. Administrative issues accounted for 14.9% of interventions, while selection of medications and errors due to ignorance of patient history accounted for 8.7% each. Interventions to address overdoses accounted for 8.2% of the total. Moderately significant interventions were observed in 19.4% of cases, with 7.5% having a significant impact on major medication errors. Pharmacists intervened in 20.8% of prescriptions to prevent complications, 25.1% to rationalize treatment, and 7.9% to improve compliance. Based on the findings, we conclude that the role of pharmacists in improving the healthcare system is crucial. We recommend conducting more research-based studies to raise awareness among healthcare professionals, provide solutions to prescription and dispensing problems, improve documentation, emphasize the importance of pharmacy practice, reduce prescribing errors, and update the knowledge of pharmacists and other healthcare professionals.

title: Biochemical studies on Mycobacterium tuberculosis UreG and comparative modeling reveal structural and functional conservation among the bacterial UreG family.
text:
Living organisms have developed efficient systems to utilize and maintain homeostasis of nickel, a micronutrient essential for cellular life, despite its toxicity in soluble form at non-physiological concentrations. One such mechanism is the incorporation of nickel into the active site of urease, a multistep process requiring the cooperation of various accessory proteins. Understanding this activation mechanism may lead to medical applications against ureolytic bacteria, including the deadly pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This study focuses on UreG, an essential chaperone involved in the in vivo activation of urease upon nickel insertion into the active site.
The protein was investigated using both experimental and computational methods. The soluble M. tuberculosis UreG (MtUreG) was overexpressed in Escherichia coli, purified to homogeneity, and its identity was confirmed by mass spectrometry. Size-exclusion chromatography and light scattering revealed that MtUreG exists as a dimer in solution, and the presence of a disulfide bond was confirmed. The free thiol concentration showed that MtUreG has low GTPase activity under native conditions, with a kcat of 0.01 min-1. Circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the presence of a well-defined secondary structure (8% alpha-helices, 29% beta-strands) in MtUreG, while NMR spectroscopy indicated that this protein does not have a rigid three-dimensional fold and can be classified as an intrinsically unstructured polypeptide.
Using fold recognition algorithms, a molecular model of MtUreG in its fully folded and functional form was built. An extensive similarity search was conducted to identify conserved patterns in known bacterial UreG sequences. A multiple-sequence alignment and phylogenetic tree were created, revealing key residues and motifs crucial for protein function. A structural database containing homology-built models of the most representative UreG proteins was constructed, illustrating the structural similarities among the UreG family. A flexible region, likely important for protein function, was identified. The conservation of structure among this class of GTPases was discussed in light of their role in the urease assembly process.

title: (99m)Tc-HisoDGR as a Potential SPECT Probe for Orthotopic Glioma Detection via Targeting of Integrin α5β1.
text: Intracellular proteins known as integrins play a significant part in glioma cell proliferation and invasion. Certain integrin receptors, such as alpha-v beta-3, alpha-v beta-5, and alpha-5 beta-1, have received attention for glioma diagnosis and antitumor therapy. In particular, integrin alpha-5 beta-1 has been highlighted as a prognostic and diagnostic marker in glioma, and its expression is linked to a less advantageous prognosis in high-grade gliomas. Yet, unlike integrins alpha-v beta-3 and alpha-v beta-5, which have been extensively examined, few integrin alpha-5 beta-1-specific radiotracers have been reported. Developing alpha-5 beta-1-specific radiotracers may offer alternative diagnosis and prognosis options alongside extensively researched alpha-v beta-3/alpha-v beta-5-specific tracers, and they might add new insights to understanding tumor progression. Here, we fabricated a novel integrin alpha-5 beta-1-specific probe (99m)Tc-HisoDGR for single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) imaging of glioma. To determine its selective targeting of integrin alpha-5 beta-1 in vivo, we performed SPECT/CT scans, biodistribution experiments, and blocking studies in alpha-5 beta-1-positive U87MG human glioma mouse models. Small-animal SPECT/CT imaging experiments demonstrated that tumors were clearly visualized in both subcutaneous and orthotopic glioma tumor models with a clear background at 0.5, 1, and 2 hours post-injection (p.i.). The tumor accumulation of (99m)Tc-HisoDGR was significantly reduced when excess cold isoDGR peptide was coinjected, indicating that the tumor uptake was specifically mediated. Our findings revealed that (99m)Tc-HisoDGR represents a potent molecular probe for integrin alpha-5 beta-1-positive cancer imaging, and it may serve as a promising tool for evaluating malignancy, predicting prognosis, identifying patients sensitive to integrin alpha-5 beta-1-targeted drugs, and monitoring the response to integrin alpha-5 beta-1-targeted drugs in clinical trials.

title: Effect of cyclic AMP-dependent protein phosphorylating conditions on the pH-dependent activity of tyrosine hydroxylase from beef and rat striata.
text: Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH, EC 1.14.16.2) from beef brain striata was purified 23-fold from an acetone powder extract using a series of purification steps. When this enzyme preparation is treated with a cyclic AMP[-dependent protein phosphorylation system], there is a change in the pH dependence of the enzyme activity. Specifically, the pH optimum at saturating tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) concentration shifts from below pH 6 to approximately pH 6.7. At pH 7, activation is mainly observed as an increase in the maximum velocity (Vmax), while at pH 6, activation is mainly observed as a decrease in the Michaelis constant (Km) for the pterin cofactor. Additionally, even with the control enzyme, the Km for pterin cofactor decreases precipitously as the pH is increased from 6 towards neutrality. Similar results were obtained using G-25 Sephadex-treated rat striatal TH. In situ activation of TH by phosphoryling conditions is primarily expressed as an increase in the maximum rate of dopamine synthesis. These findings indicate that changes in TH activity caused by cyclic AMP-dependent protein phosphorylation will depend significantly on the TH environment's pH.

title: Interaction of TNF with TNF receptor type 2 promotes expansion and function of mouse CD4+CD25+ T regulatory cells.
text: Although TNF is known to be a key pro-inflammatory cytokine, recent evidence suggests that it also has immunosuppressive effects. In this study, we found that mouse peripheral T regulatory cells (Tregs) express significantly higher levels of TNFR2 compared to T effector cells (Teffs) in both resting and activated states. In cocultures of Tregs and Teffs, TNF initially abrogated the suppression of Teffs by Tregs, but longer exposure to TNF restored the suppressive effects. Moreover, TNF expanded the Treg population, up-regulated the expression of CD25 and FoxP3, and enhanced the suppressive activity of Tregs. In contrast, IL-1beta and IL-6 did not up-regulate FoxP3-expressing Tregs. Interestingly, the number of Tregs increased in wild-type mice following sublethal cecal ligation and puncture, but not in TNFR2-deficient mice. Depletion of Tregs significantly decreased mortality following cecal ligation and puncture, highlighting the critical role of Tregs in immunosuppression. Our findings suggest that the stimulatory effect of TNF on Tregs is more pronounced due to the higher expression of TNFR2, and that the slower response of Tregs to TNF results in delayed immunosuppressive feedback effects.

title: The basics of epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
text: The origins of the mesenchymal cells involved in tissue repair and pathological processes, such as fibrosis, tumor invasiveness, and metastasis, are not well understood. However, recent research suggests that epithelial-mesenchymal transitions (EMTs) may play a crucial role in the development of these cells. As this article will explain, processes similar to those seen during embryonic implantation, embryonic development, and organ formation are being repurposed and subverted by chronically inflamed tissues and neoplasias. The identification of the signaling pathways that lead to the activation of EMT programs during these disease processes is revealing new insights into the plasticity of cellular phenotypes and potential therapeutic interventions.

title: Child maltreatment, other trauma exposure, and posttraumatic symptomatology among children with oppositional defiant and attention deficit hyperactivity disorders.
text: Repeated child psychiatric outpatient admissions with disruptive behavior or adjustment disorders were evaluated using validated instruments to assess exposure to trauma and symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The study identified four reliably diagnosed groups: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD), comorbid ADHD-ODD, and adjustment disorder controls. The findings revealed that ODD and, to a lesser extent, ADHD were associated with a history of physical or sexual maltreatment. The severity of PTSD symptoms was most pronounced when ADHD and maltreatment co-occurred or when ODD and accident/illness trauma co-occurred. While controlling for overlapping symptoms, the association between ODD and PTSD Criterion D (hyperarousal/hypervigilance) symptoms remained, but the association between ADHD and PTSD symptoms was primarily due to an overlapping symptom.
