This mutation had a complex outcome, with the major product resulting from the skipping of exons 5 and 6, as well as smaller amounts of products in which only exon 5 was skipped or in which cryptic acceptor sites within exon 5 were used. All products were in frame and produced pro-alpha1(V) chains with abnormal N-propeptides that were incorporated into the extracellular matrix.
Our findings suggest that the order of intron removal plays a crucial role in the outcome of splice-site mutations. In particular, we observed that the two-exon skip occurred in transcripts in which intron 5 was removed rapidly relative to introns 4 and 6, resulting in a large (270 nt) composite exon that can be skipped in its entirety. Transcripts in which only exon 5 was skipped were derived from those in which intron 6 was removed prior to intron 5. Finally, the use of cryptic acceptor sites in exon 5 occurred in transcripts in which intron 4 was removed subsequent to introns 5 and 6.
Our findings provide a model that explains why multiple products can arise from a mutation at a single splice site and highlight the importance of considering the order of intron removal when analyzing splice-site mutations.

title: Kruppel-like factor KLF10 targets transforming growth factor-beta1 to regulate CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells and T regulatory cells.
text:
Research has shown that Kruppel-like factor 10 (KLF10/TIEG1) plays a crucial role in the suppression of CD4(+)CD25(-) T cell activation and the maintenance of self-tolerance. In this study, we investigate the mechanisms by which KLF10 regulates T regulatory cell (T reg) function and CD4(+)CD25(-) T cell activation.
We find that KLF10 overexpressing CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells induce the expression of transforming growth factor (TGF)-beta1 and forkhead box protein 3 (Foxp3), which are important in suppressing CD4(+)CD25(-) T cell activation. Conversely, KLF10(-/-) CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells have enhanced differentiation along both Th1 and Th2 pathways and elaborate higher levels of Th1 and Th2 cytokines. Moreover, KLF10(-/-) CD4(+)CD25(-) T cell effectors cannot be appropriately suppressed by wild-type T regs.
Surprisingly, KLF10(-/-) T reg cells have reduced suppressor function, independent of Foxp3 expression, with decreased expression and elaboration of TGF-beta1. Mechanistic studies demonstrate that in response to TGF-beta1, KLF10 can transactivate both TGF-beta1 and Foxp3 promoters, implicating KLF10 in a positive feedback loop that may promote cell-intrinsic control of T cell activation. Finally, KLF10(-/-) CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells promote atherosclerosis in ApoE(-/-)/scid/scid mice by approximately 2-fold, with increased leukocyte accumulation and peripheral pro-inflammatory cytokines.
These findings suggest that KLF10 is a critical regulator in the transcriptional network controlling TGF-beta1 in both CD4(+)CD25(-) T cells and T regs, and plays an important role in regulating atherosclerotic lesion formation in mice. Overall, this study highlights the important role of KLF10 in the maintenance of self-tolerance and immune homeostasis.

title: Synchrotron radiation solution X-ray scattering study of the pH dependence of the quaternary structure of yeast pyruvate decarboxylase.
text: The pH-dependent structure of pyruvate decarboxylase from yeast was investigated over a range of pH values (6.2 < pH < 8.4). The enzyme exhibits an equilibrium between tetramers and dimers, with the midpoint of this equilibrium located around pH 7.5. The catalytic activity of the enzyme is dependent on the volume fraction of tetramers. This equilibrium may serve as an additional regulatory mechanism, as the accumulation of pyruvate would lead to a decrease in pH and an increase in the concentration of the catalytically active tetramer. Radiation damage during X-ray scattering experiments resulted in a shift of this equilibrium and the formation of octamers. To circumvent these effects and analyze the data, specialized experimental and data processing methods were employed, which can be easily applied to other radiation-sensitive systems. The low-resolution shapes of the dimers and tetramers were determined from the scattering curves using spherical harmonics. The results indicate that a conformational change occurs in the dimers upon formation of the tetramers, consistent with earlier circular dichroism measurements.

title: Enhancement of anxiety-like responsiveness to the cannabinoid CB(1) receptor agonist HU-210 following chronic stress.
text: The impact of chronic unpredictable stress on the anxiety-like response triggered by the cannabinoid receptor agonist HU-210, specifically 3-(1,1-dimethylheptyl)-(-)-11-hydroxy-delta 8-tetrahydrocannabinol, was investigated in male Long-Evans rats. The study tested the effect of unpredictable chronic stress on the anxiety response elicited by HU-210 in the elevated plus maze. The rats were either unstressed or underwent a 21-day chronic stress regimen and were then divided into three testing groups (vehicle, 10, and 50 microg/kg of HU-210). The results showed that in unstressed animals, a low dose of HU-210 produced an anxiolytic response, while a high dose induced an anxiogenic response. In contrast, both low and high doses of HU-210 induced anxiogenic responses in stressed animals. These findings suggest that chronic stress enhances the responsiveness of cannabinoid receptors or interacting systems involved in emotional states.

title: Cardiac glycosides inhibit TNF-α/NF-κB signaling by blocking recruitment of TNF receptor-associated death domain to the TNF receptor
text: Digitoxin and closely related cardiac glycoside drugs have been found to strongly inhibit the TNF-α/NF-κB signaling pathway. In an effort to uncover the underlying mechanism, we conducted a systematic search for selective inhibition throughout the entire pathway. Our findings reveal that these drugs block TNF-α-dependent binding of TNF receptor 1 to TNF receptor-associated death domain, which can be observed in both native cells (e.g., HeLa) and reconstituted systems in HEK293 cells. Furthermore, all of the anti-inflammatory effects of digitoxin on NF-κB and c-Jun N-terminal kinase pathways are believed to result from this initial, upstream signaling event.

title: Zinc supplementation during lactation: effects on maternal status and milk zinc concentrations.
text: In this study, the impact of zinc supplementation on maternal zinc status and milk zinc concentrations during lactation was investigated. Seventy-one lactating women were randomly assigned to either a zinc supplement (ZS, n = 40) or a placebo (NZS, n = 31) starting at 2 weeks postpartum. The overall mean zinc intake was significantly higher in the ZS group (13.0 +/- 3.4 mg/d) compared to the NZS group (3.4 +/- 3.9 mg/d, including supplement). Plasma zinc concentrations were significantly higher in the ZS group compared to the NZS group (P = 0.05). However, milk zinc concentrations did not differ between the two groups over the course of the study. The mean dietary zinc intake observed in the nonsupplemented group was adequate to maintain normal maternal zinc status and milk zinc concentrations through at least 7 months of lactation. Further controlled intervention trials in less well-nourished populations are needed to assess the impact of lower zinc intakes on milk zinc concentrations.

title: DMSO as a vehicle for central injections: tests with feeding elicited by norepinephrine injected into the paraventricular nucleus.
text: Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is gaining popularity as a vehicle for central injections, particularly for solubilizing substances that are insoluble in water. The purpose of our study was to investigate whether the vehicle used for solubilization, specifically 75% DMSO and 25% artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF), affects the well-established stimulatory response to norepinephrine (NE) administered into the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) over a short period. To evaluate its suitability, we compared the effects of repeated unilateral injections of NE dissolved in two different vehicles: 100% aCSF or 75% DMSO, 25% aCSF. Each injection was administered every 48 hours over a 30-day period. Notably, NE (40 nmol) significantly increased food intake by approximately sevenfold compared to either vehicle control, and the stimulatory effect was similar when aCSF or 75% DMSO was used as a vehicle. Moreover, the NE-induced feeding response remained consistent across multiple tests (n=13). These findings suggest that 75% DMSO is a suitable vehicle for delivering NE (and likely other hydrophobic substances) in small volumes (0.3 microl) directly into specific brain regions.

title: Dodecameric structure and ATPase activity of the human TIP48/TIP49 complex.
text: TIP48 and TIP49 are two closely related and highly conserved eukaryotic proteins with an essential biological function and a critical role in major pathways linked to cancer. Both proteins are found together in several highly conserved chromatin-modifying complexes. Although they share some sequence similarities with the bacterial RuvB protein, the nature and mechanism of their biochemical function remain unknown. To investigate their activity, recombinant human TIP48 and TIP49 were assembled into an equimolar complex and tested for ATPase activity in vitro. Surprisingly, the formation of the TIP48/TIP49 complex resulted in a synergistic increase in ATPase activity, yet ATP hydrolysis was not stimulated in the presence of single-stranded, double-stranded, or four-way junction DNA, and no DNA helicase or branch migration activity could be detected. The absence of ATPase activity in complexes with catalytic defects in either TIP48 or TIP49 demonstrated that both proteins within the TIP48/TIP49 complex are necessary for ATP hydrolysis. The three-dimensional structure of the TIP48/TIP49 complex was resolved using negative stain electron microscopy, revealing a unique arrangement of two stacked hexameric rings with C6 symmetry. Remarkably, TIP48 formed oligomers in the presence of adenine nucleotides, while TIP49 did not. These findings suggest that the biochemical differences between TIP48 and TIP49 may be responsible for the distinct structural features of the two hexameric rings and may play a crucial role in their specialised functions.

title: Associations between work-related factors and specific disorders of the shoulder--a systematic review of the literature.
text:
Objective:
To conduct a systematic review of the literature and assess the quantitative relationship between work-related physical and psychosocial factors and the occurrence of specific shoulder disorders in occupational populations.
Methods:
A systematic review of the literature was conducted to identify studies that investigated the associations between work factors and the occurrence of tendinitis of the biceps tendon, rotator cuff tears, subacromial impingement syndrome (SIS), and suprascapular nerve compression. The odds ratio (OR) or relative risk (RR) was used to quantify the association between work factors and shoulder disorders.
Results:
The findings of the review revealed that SIS was associated with the following work-related factors:
* Force requirements exceeding 10% of maximum voluntary contraction (MVC)
* Lifting heavy loads (>20 kg) more than 10 times a day
* High levels of hand force (>1 hour/day)

* Repetitive movements of the shoulder, hand, and wrist (>2 hours/day)
* Hand-arm vibration
* Working with the hand above shoulder level

* Upper-arm flexion exceeding 45 degrees for 15% of the time or duty cycle of forceful pinch >0% of time

* High psychosocial job demands

The fish processing industry had the highest risk of both tendinitis of the biceps tendon and SIS. Jobs in slaughterhouses and as betel pepper leaf culters were also associated with SIS. None of the studies described the association between job title/risk factors and the occurrence of rotator cuff tears or suprascapular nerve compression.


Conclusion:

Repetitive work, forceful exertion, awkward work posture, and high psychosocial job demands are associated with the occurrence of SIS. There is a need for further research to determine the specific risk factors for rotator cuff tears and suprascapular nerve compression.

title: Altered TCR signaling from geometrically repatterned immunological synapses.
text: The immunological synapse, a specialized cell-cell junction characterized by large-scale patterns of receptors and signaling molecules, has remained largely shrouded in mystery regarding its formation and function. To shine light on this enigmatic process, we employed supported bilayer membranes and nanometer-scale structures fabricated on the substrate to impose geometric constraints on immunological synapse formation. Analyzing the resulting alternately patterned synapses, we uncovered a direct correlation between the radial position of T cell receptors (TCRs) and signaling activity, with prolonged signaling emanating from TCR microclusters that had been mechanically trapped in the peripheral regions of the synapse. These findings support a model in which the spatial translocation of TCRs represents a primary mechanism of signal regulation within the synapse.

title: Molecular regulation of histone H3 trimethylation by COMPASS and the regulation of gene expression.
text: The COMPASS complex, a yeast homolog of the human MLL complex, is essential for the mono-, di-, and trimethylation of lysine 4 on histone H3. To further elucidate the COMPASS complex's role in histone trimethylation, we performed a comprehensive global proteomic assay. Our results reveal that both Cps60 and Cps40 components of COMPASS are crucial for proper histone H3 trimethylation, but not for regulating telomere-associated gene silencing. Surprisingly, purified COMPASS lacking Cps60 can only mono- and dimethylate histone H3(K4), but is incapable of completing the trimethylation process. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays indicate that the missing subunits of COMPASS essential for histone trimethylation do not affect the localization of the Set1 enzyme to chromatin for the genes tested. Our findings suggest that multiple components of COMPASS are required for proper histone H3 trimethylation and gene expression, highlighting the diverse roles of different forms of histone methylation in COMPASS.

title: Mitosis-specific anchoring of gamma tubulin complexes by pericentrin controls spindle organization and mitotic entry.
text: The study investigates the role of pericentrin in centrosomal microtubule nucleation and spindle organization during mitosis. Centrosomal microtubule nucleation is primarily mediated by gamma tubulin ring complexes (gamma TuRCs), but the molecular mechanisms that anchor these complexes to the centrosome are not well understood. The authors show that pericentrin, a centrosomal coiled-coil protein, plays a critical role in anchoring gamma TuRCs to the centrosome at spindle poles. Silencing of pericentrin in somatic cells disrupts gamma tubulin localization and spindle organization during mitosis, while overexpression of a GCP2/3 binding domain of pericentrin perturbs astral microtubules and spindle bipolarity. The study also demonstrates that pericentrin is required for proper spindle organization and that its loss of function elicits a checkpoint response that prevents mitotic entry and triggers apoptotic cell death. The results provide insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying centrosomal microtubule nucleation and spindle organization during mitosis, and highlight the importance of pericentrin in maintaining proper cell division.

title: High levels of viral replication contrast with only transient changes in CD4(+) and CD8(+) cell numbers during the early phase of experimental infection with simian immunodeficiency virus SIVmnd-1 in Mandrillus sphinx.
text: Early stages of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infections are believed to reflect the host's ability to control the infection. We studied early virus and host parameters during the early phase of nonpathogenic simian immunodeficiency virus (SIVMnd-1) infection in its natural host, Mandrillus sphinx. Four mandrills were experimentally infected with a primary SIVMnd-1 strain derived from a naturally infected mandrill, while two non-infected control animals were monitored in parallel. Blood and lymph node samples were collected at three time points before infection, twice a week during the first month, and at days 60, 180, and 360 post-infection (p.i.). Antibodies against SIVMnd-1 were detected starting from days 28 to 32 p.i. Neither elevated temperature nor increased lymph node size was observed. The viral load in plasma peaked between days 7 to 10 p.i. (2 x 10(6) to 2 x 10(8) RNA equivalents/ml), followed by a 10- to 1,000-fold decrease, reaching the viral set point between days 30 to 60 p.i. The levels during the chronic phase of infection were similar to those in the naturally infected donor mandrill (2 x 10(5) RNA equivalents/ml). CD4(+) cell numbers and percentages in blood and lymph nodes decreased slightly (<10%) during primary infection, while CD8(+) cell numbers increased transiently. All values returned to pre-infection levels by day 30 p.i. However, CD8(+) cell numbers or percentages in peripheral blood and lymph nodes did not increase during the one-year follow-up period. In conclusion, SIVMnd-1 has the capacity for rapid and extensive replication in mandrills, despite stabilized CD4(+) and CD8(+) cell numbers in the post-acute phase of infection. These findings raise questions regarding the susceptibility of mandrill T cells to activation and/or cell death in response to SIVMnd-1 infection in vivo.

title: Vascular endothelial growth factor stimulates bone repair by promoting angiogenesis and bone turnover.
text: Several growth factors are expressed in distinct temporal and spatial patterns during fracture repair. Of these, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is particularly interesting due to its ability to induce neovascularization (angiogenesis). To investigate whether VEGF is essential for bone repair, we inhibited its activity during secondary bone healing in a novel mouse model. Treatment with a soluble, neutralizing VEGF receptor reduced angiogenesis, bone formation, and callus mineralization in femoral fractures. Inhibition of VEGF also significantly hindered healing of a tibial cortical bone defect, which we found to have a direct, autocrine role in osteoblast differentiation. In separate experiments, exogenous VEGF enhanced blood vessel formation, ossification, and new bone (callus) maturation in mouse femur fractures and promoted bony bridging of a rabbit radius segmental gap defect. Our results highlight the distinction between endochondral and intramembranous ossification, as well as skeletal development and bone repair. The responses to exogenous VEGF observed in two distinct model systems and species suggest that a local, slow-release formulation of VEGF may prove to be a valuable therapy for promoting human bone repair.

title: Psychiatric comorbidity in chronic daily headache.
text: Research indicates that there is a strong link between chronic daily headaches (CDH) and psychiatric disorders. Previous studies have primarily focused on migraines, but our study expands on this research by examining a larger population of 88 patients (18 males and 70 females) affected by CDH (mean duration of 7.4 +/- 8.7 years). Our findings show that nearly 90% of this population exhibited a psychiatric disorder, with anxiety and mood disorders being the most common comorbidity. The co-occurrence of psychiatric disorders and headaches has significant implications for treatment approaches.

title: An Expanded Oct4 Interaction Network: Implications for Stem Cell Biology, Development, and Disease
text: The transcription factor Oct4 plays a crucial role in maintaining the stem cell state and reprogramming. Exploring its partners can help elucidate the mechanisms underlying pluripotency and development. Here, we uncover a significantly expanded list of Oct4-binding proteins in mouse embryonic stem cells. Our findings show that Oct4 associates with a diverse set of proteins, including gene expression regulators and modulators of Oct4 function. Half of these partners are transcriptionally regulated by Oct4 or other stem cell transcription factors, while one-third exhibit altered expression during cell differentiation. Most of the proteins interacting with Oct4 have been studied to date have an early lethal phenotype when mutated. A subset of human orthologs are linked to inherited developmental disorders or cause cancer. The Oct4 interactome provides a valuable resource for dissecting Oct4 function, shedding light on the basis of pluripotency and development, and identifying potential additional reprogramming factors.

title: Reproductive and lifestyle determinants of anti-Müllerian hormone in a large population-based study.
text:
The study aimed to investigate the influence of reproductive and lifestyle factors on anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) levels in a large population-based cohort of premenopausal women. AMH is increasingly used as a prognostic and diagnostic tool in clinical practice, but large-scale studies addressing the determinants of AMH levels are scarce. The study included 2,320 premenopausal women from the general community who were assessed for the effect of female reproductive and lifestyle factors on shifts in age-specific AMH percentiles.
The results showed that women who used oral contraceptives (OCs), had irregular menstrual cycles, or were pregnant had significantly lower age-specific AMH percentiles compared to women with a regular menstrual cycle. Age at menarche and age at first childbirth were not associated with AMH levels, while higher parity was associated with a 2 percentile increase in AMH. The study also found that current smoking was associated with 4 percentiles lower age-specific AMH percentiles, regardless of smoking dose. Body mass index, waist circumference, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, and socioeconomic status were not significantly associated with AMH levels.
The study's findings suggest that several reproductive and lifestyle factors are associated with AMH levels, and these factors may affect the interpretation of AMH in a clinical setting. The lower AMH levels associated with OC use and smoking seem reversible, as the effects were confined to current use of these factors. Therefore, it is important to consider the effect of these determinants when interpreting AMH levels to base patient management on AMH.

title: Primary care and health insurance among women released from New York City jails.
text: In a study conducted from 1997 to 2001, the utilization of primary care and health insurance coverage among 511 women released from jail in New York City was examined. One year after their release, approximately half of the sample (47%) reported utilizing primary care, while about 56% had health insurance coverage. The study found that neither having diabetes, asthma, or depression increased the likelihood of primary care utilization or health insurance coverage. Instead, primary care utilization was more likely among those who reported receiving public benefits, having health insurance coverage, moderate social support, avoiding illegal activities, and being HIV seropositive. Health insurance coverage was associated with receiving public benefits, hospitalization, primary care, and avoiding re-arrest. The study suggests that a majority of women leaving jail, including those with chronic diseases, often lack primary care. These findings highlight the need for continuity of care from corrections to the community and suggest that providing health benefits and social support can facilitate this continuity.

title: The effects of prion protein proteolysis and disaggregation on the strain properties of hamster scrapie.
text: Native mammalian prions display self-propagating strains characterized by distinctive clinical, pathological, and biochemical features. Despite the association between prion strain diversity and PrP(Sc) conformation, the exact physical properties of the PrP(Sc) molecule that encode mammalian prion strain phenotypes remain unknown. In this study, we examined the effects of proteinase K digestion or sonication on prion-infected brain homogenates from three hamster scrapie strains, and inoculated the modified samples into normal hamsters. Our findings show that the strain-specific clinical features and neuropathological profiles of inoculated animals were not affected by either treatment. Similarly, the strain-dependent biochemical properties of the PrP(Sc) molecules, including their electrophoretic mobility, glycoform composition, conformational stability, and susceptibility to protease digestion, remained unchanged by either proteolysis or sonication of the original inocula. These results suggest that the infectious strain properties of native prions are not altered by disaggregation of the PrP(Sc) molecules, and that maintenance of these properties does not require the N-domain (residues 23-90) of the protease-resistant PrP(Sc) molecules or protease-sensitive PrP(Sc) molecules.

title: Methylation of histone H3 lysine-79 by Dot1p plays multiple roles in the response to UV damage in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
text: The study investigated the function of histone H3 lysine-79 methylation in the repair of UV-damaged DNA in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The results showed that various proteins play roles in both repair processes, including those involved in lysine-79 histone methylation by Dot1p. The study found that a dot1 mutation and a histone H3 lysine-79 point mutation increased sensitivity to UV radiation, suggesting that lysine-79 methylation plays a crucial role in efficient repair. Epistasis analysis with UV repair genes revealed that lysine-79 methylation functions in various repair pathways, including nucleotide excision, post-replication, and recombination repair, as well as RAD9-mediated checkpoint function. In contrast, epistasis analysis with a lysine-79 point mutation revealed that this allele disrupts a subset of lysine-79 methylation functions specifically in nucleotide excision and post-replication repair pathways. The findings suggest that histone H3 lysine-79 methylation has distinct and separable roles in the response to UV damage, potentially coordinating various repair processes.

title: Unmet need for personal assistance with activities of daily living among older adults.
text: In this study, we investigated the prevalence, correlates, and negative consequences of unmet needs for personal assistance with activities of daily living (ADLs) among older adults. To achieve this, we analyzed cross-sectional data from the 1994 National Health Interview Survey's Supplement on Aging. Our findings revealed that 20.7% of individuals who needed help to perform one or more ADLs reported inadequate assistance, with the prevalence of unmet need varying across different ADLs (e.g., 10.2% for eating, 20.1% for transferring). Our results also showed that lower household income, multiple ADL difficulties, and living alone increased the likelihood of having unmet needs. Moreover, nearly half of those with unmet needs reported experiencing negative consequences, such as being unable to eat when hungry, as a result of their unmet need. Based on our findings, we recommend that greater, targeted efforts are needed to reduce the prevalence and consequences of unmet need for ADL assistance in elderly individuals.

title: Multi-stage chemical carcinogenesis in mouse skin: Fundamentals and applications
text: For over 60 years, researchers have used the chemical induction of tumors in mouse skin to study the mechanisms of epithelial carcinogenesis and evaluate modifying factors. In the traditional two-stage skin carcinogenesis model, the initiation phase involves applying a sub-carcinogenic dose of a carcinogen to the skin, followed by repeated treatments with a tumor-promoting agent to induce tumor development. This process typically takes 1-3 hours, depending on the number of mice used. The promotion phase requires twice-weekly treatments (1-2 hours) and weekly tumor palpation (1-2 hours) for the duration of the study. Using this protocol, a highly reproducible papilloma burden is expected within 10-20 weeks, with a portion of the tumors progressing to squamous cell carcinomas within 20-50 weeks. Unlike complete skin carcinogenesis, the two-stage model allows for a greater yield of premalignant lesions, as well as a separation of the initiation and promotion phases.

title: Preventing deaths by drowning in children in the United Kingdom: have we made progress in 10 years? Population based incidence study.
text: Detailed information on drowning incidents in children is typically not collected by national statistics offices. Very few studies have been conducted in the United Kingdom, and none have been carried out on British children living abroad. In 1988-9, two authors (AMK and JRS) compiled data from national statistics offices, police forces (Royal Life Saving Society), and a press cutting service (Royal Society for Prevention of Accidents) to conduct a comprehensive analysis of drowning deaths among children. This analysis revealed that 149 children had drowned in the United Kingdom during 1998-9. The study also identified a safety agenda, which focused on young children in garden ponds and pools, as well as older children who swim without proper supervision. Over the past decade, there have been various initiatives aimed at improving children's safety in water, particularly through swimming programs. The authors obtained similar data for 1998-9 to assess any changes that may have occurred.

title: Hypoxic heterogeneity in human tumors: EF5 binding, vasculature, necrosis, and proliferation.
text: In this study, we investigated the levels and distribution of hypoxia in 31 human tumors using fluorescent immunohistochemical detection of binding by the 2-nitroimidazole, EF5. Hypoxia was found to be a heterogeneous property of human tumors, with areas of high binding often adjacent to areas of necrosis. However, hypoxia can occur without necrosis. The most common relationship between blood vessels (PECAM/CD31) and EF5 staining in the tumors studied was consistent with diffusion-limited hypoxia, with acute hypoxia occurring infrequently. Within a given patient's tumor, there was an inverse correlation between regions of high proliferation (Ki-67) and regions of hypoxia. However, the absence of proliferation did not predict the presence of hypoxia in a given patient. The relationships between hypoxia and other biological endpoints are complex, and within a given tumor's spatial relationships, they are in accord with known physiological principles. Our data emphasize that the relationships between hypoxia and other biological parameters vary between patients. Necrosis, proliferation, and blood vessel distribution cannot predict the level or presence of hypoxia in an individual patient's tumor.

title: The Sp1-like protein BTEB3 inhibits transcription via the basic transcription element box by interacting with mSin3A and HDAC-1 co-repressors and competing with Sp1.
text: Sp1-like proteins are distinguished by three conserved C-terminal zinc finger motifs that recognize GC-rich regions in promoter sequences of numerous essential genes in mammalian cell homeostasis. These proteins function as either transcriptional activators or repressors. Although significant information has been reported on the molecular mechanisms underlying the function of Sp1-like activators, relatively little is known about the mechanisms of repressor proteins. In this study, we investigate the functional characterization of BTEB3, a ubiquitously expressed Sp1-like transcriptional repressor. GAL4 assays reveal that the N-terminal region of BTEB3 harbors repressor sites. Immunoprecipitation assays demonstrate that BTEB3 interacts with the co-repressor mSin3A and the histone deacetylase protein HDAC-1. Gel shift assays demonstrate that BTEB3 binds the BTE site, a well-characterized GC-rich DNA element, with an affinity similar to that of Sp1. Reporter and gel shift assays in Chinese hamster ovary cells show that BTEB3 can also repress transcription by competing with Sp1 for BTE binding. This study expands the repertoire of BTEB-like members of the Sp1 family involved in transcriptional repression. Furthermore, our results suggest a mechanism of repression for BTEB3, involving direct repression by the N-terminal region through interaction with mSin3A and HDAC-1 and competition with Sp1 via the DNA-binding domain.

title: Perceptual limits in a simulated "Cocktail party".
text: Researchers investigated how people perceive the number of speakers in simultaneous dialogues. Listeners were asked to report the number of talkers they heard, with the number varying from 1 to 13 in four experiments. The researchers manipulated various factors, including the listeners' location in relation to the speakers, the length of time each speaker's voice was heard, and the gender mix of the speakers. They found that the proportion of correct numerosity judgments decreased as the number of talkers increased, but the perceptual limits (the number of talkers that resulted in a correct judgment score of 0.5) varied between 3 and 5 talkers, depending on the listening conditions. The results suggest that listeners first group talkers into distinct voices before attempting to count them, and that the auditory world for simultaneous voices may consist of no more than 3-5 talkers in different situations. The study's findings have implications for understanding how listeners perceive and process simultaneous speech in everyday life.

title: The MOS social support survey.
text: This paper describes the development and evaluation of a brief, multidimensional, self-administered social support survey designed for patients in the Medical Outcomes Study (MOS), a two-year study of patients with chronic conditions. The survey aimed to be comprehensive in its conceptualization of the various dimensions of social support, while also being distinct from other related measures. We present an overview of the major conceptual issues considered when selecting items for the social support battery, describe the items themselves, and provide findings based on data from 2987 patients aged 18 and older. Multitrait scaling analyses supported the dimensionality of four functional support scales: emotional/informational, tangible, affectionate, and positive social interaction. These support measures are distinct from structural measures of social support and related health measures, and demonstrate reliable (all Alphas greater than 0.91) and relatively stable over time results. Selected construct validity hypotheses were also supported.

title: Can hematological parameters discriminate malaria from nonmalarious acute febrile illness in the tropics?
text: Background: Malaria is often considered the primary differential diagnosis for acute fever in tropical regions, and altered hematological parameters have been observed in patients with malaria. Objective: To determine whether specific hematological abnormalities increase the likelihood of malaria in patients with acute fever. Methods: This hospital-based, prospective cohort study included all patients with fever of less than 7 days duration. Patients with a known localizing cause for their fever were excluded. Hematological parameters, including hemoglobin, red blood cell distribution width (RDW), leukocyte count, and platelet count, were measured using an automated counter, and a peripheral smear examination was used as the gold standard for malaria diagnosis. Statistical analysis was performed to determine the diagnostic accuracy of these parameters. Results: A total of 184 patients were included in the study, and 70 (38%) had a positive peripheral smear for malarial parasites. Thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 150,000/mm3) was found to be a significant predictor of malaria (sensitivity 60%, specificity 88%, LR+ 5.04), and when combined with anemia (Hb < 10 g/dl), it was the next most predictive parameter (sensitivity 69%, specificity 74%, LR+ 2.77). RDW and leukocyte count were not found to be predictive. Conclusion: The presence of thrombocytopenia in a patient with acute fever increases the likelihood of malarial infection.

title: 14q deletions are associated with trisomy 12, NOTCH1 mutations and unmutated IGHV genes in chronic lymphocytic leukemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma.
text: Rare and recurrent deletions of the long arm of chromosome 14 (del(14q)) are more commonly observed in mature B-cell neoplasms, particularly in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). To further investigate this abnormality, we analyzed 81 cases with del(14q), including 54 CLL and 27 small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) cases, the largest reported series to date. Our findings revealed that the most frequently observed additional abnormality was trisomy 12 (tri12), present in 35% of cases, followed by del13q14 (15%), delTP53 (14%), delATM (6%), and del6q21 (4%). The IGHV genes were unmutated in 77% of patients, with a high frequency of IGHV1-69 (40%). The NOTCH1 gene was mutated in 31% of patients. There was no significant difference in cytogenetic and molecular abnormalities between CLL and SLL. Using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) array analysis, we found that the deletions were heterogeneous in size. However, a specific group with a deletion of 14q24.1q32.33 was identified in 48% of cases, which showed a higher frequency of tri12 and NOTCH1 mutations compared to the other patients. In CLL patients with del(14q), the median treatment-free survival (TFS) was 27 months. In conclusion, del(14q) is associated with unfavorable prognostic factors, including tri12 and unmutated IGHV genes, NOTCH1 mutations, and short TFS.

title: Rapid DNA methylation changes after exposure to traffic particles.
text:
Introduction: Exposure to particulate air pollution has been linked to increased hospitalizations and deaths, particularly from cardiovascular diseases. Recent studies have also revealed that long-term exposure to particulate pollution can lead to lower levels of DNA methylation in certain genes. Our study aims to investigate whether exposure to particulate pollution can alter DNA methylation in heavily methylated regions of the genome.
Methods: We conducted a cohort study involving 1,097 elderly participants in the Boston area Normative Aging Study. We measured DNA methylation levels of long interspersed nucleotide element (LINE)-1 and Alu repetitive elements using quantitative polymerase chain reaction-pyrosequencing. We used mixed models accounting for within-subject correlation to analyze the effect of ambient particulate pollutants (black carbon, PM2.5, or sulfate) on DNA methylation levels.
Results: Our findings reveal that DNA methylation levels vary in association with time-related variables, such as day of the week and season. Specifically, we found that LINE-1 methylation decreased after recent exposure to higher levels of black carbon, and this association remained significant after adjusting for other pollutants. In contrast, we found no significant association between Alu methylation and particulate pollution exposure.
Discussion: Our study suggests that exposure to traffic-related particulate pollution may decrease DNA methylation levels in certain genes. While the exact mechanisms remain unclear, our findings imply that decreased DNA methylation may play a role in the adverse health effects of particulate pollution. Further research is needed to determine whether these changes in DNA methylation are a causal link between exposure to particulate pollution and the development of cardiovascular diseases.

title: Incidence of adverse drug events and potential adverse drug events. Implications for prevention. ADE Prevention Study Group.
text:
Objective: To determine the incidence and preventability of adverse drug events (ADEs) and potential ADEs among hospitalized patients.
Design: Prospective cohort study.
Participants: All 4031 adult admissions to a stratified random sample of 11 medical and surgical units in two tertiary care hospitals over a 6-month period.
Outcome Measures: Adverse drug events and potential ADEs.
Methods: Incidents were detected through stimulated self-report by nurses and pharmacists and daily review of all charts by nurse investigators. Incidents were then classified by two independent reviewers as to whether they represented ADEs or potential ADEs, as well as their severity and preventability.
Results: Over a 6-month period, 247 ADEs and 194 potential ADEs were identified. Extrapolated event rates were approximately 1900 ADEs and 1600 potential ADEs per year, per hospital. Of all ADEs, 1% were fatal and 12% life-threatening, 30% were serious, and 57% were significant. Twenty-eight percent of ADEs were judged preventable. Of life-threatening and serious ADEs, 42% were preventable, compared to 18% of significant ADEs. Errors resulting in preventable ADEs occurred most often at the stages of ordering (56%) and administration (34%), while transcription (6%) and dispensing errors (4%) were less common. Errors were more likely to be intercepted if they occurred earlier in the process, with 48% of errors occurring at the ordering stage and 0% at the administration stage.
Conclusion: Adverse drug events were common and often preventable. Most ADEs resulted from errors at the ordering stage, but many also occurred at the administration stage. Prevention strategies should focus on both stages of the drug delivery process.

title: Induction of galactokinase in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: kinetics of induction and glucose effects.
text: The study investigated the induced synthesis of galactokinase and the repressive effects of glucose on this synthesis in whole yeast cells that were made permeable using dimethyl sulfoxide. It was discovered that the induction response of uninduced cells to galactose was dependent on the type of carbon source used to grow the cells before exposure to galactose. Glucose-grown cells showed a prolonged lag before induction, while lactate-grown cells exhibited induced synthesis within 8 minutes. An optimal concentration of 0.5% galactose was found to induce synthesis. The addition of glucose to yeast cultures grown on galactose led to a transient repression of synthesis, followed by a resumed rate of synthesis typical of weaker permanent catabolite repression. Neither 2-deoxygalactose nor fucose acted as uninduced inducers of the pathway, nor did they serve as substrates for galactokinase.

title: Gene--nutrition interactions in coronary artery disease: correlation between the MTHFR C677T polymorphism and folate and homocysteine status in a Korean population.
text:
Elevated plasma total homocysteine levels are a significant risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). Methyltetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) is a key enzyme involved in homocysteine metabolism, and a common C677T mutation in the MTHFR gene can lead to reduced enzyme activity and increased homocysteine levels. We investigated the frequency of the C677T mutation in a Korean population, determined the genotype-specific threshold levels of folate or vitamin B12 required to maintain normal homocysteine levels, and examined the relationship between the TT genotype and the risk of CAD.
Our study included 163 CAD patients and 50 healthy controls, and we used real-time PCR with melting point analysis to identify the MTHFR C677T polymorphism. We also measured plasma homocysteine, folate, and vitamin B12 levels. We found that the frequency of the TT genotype was higher in CAD patients than in controls (18% vs 26%, respectively), and individuals with the TT genotype had significantly elevated homocysteine levels compared to those with the CC or CT genotypes. We also found that the genotype-specific folate threshold level was significantly higher in TT individuals than in the CC or CT genotypes. Additionally, we observed that individuals with low folate status and the TT genotype had a significantly higher relative risk of CAD compared to those with high folate status and the TT genotype.
Our findings suggest the presence of a gene-nutrient interaction that may contribute to an increased risk of CAD based on specific threshold folate levels required by different MTHFR C677T genotypes in the Korean population. These findings have important implications for the prevention and treatment of CAD in this population.

title: Human bone marrow adipocytes block granulopoiesis through neuropilin-1-induced granulocyte colony-stimulating factor inhibition.
text:
Here is a possible reconstruction of the given text with a more formal and academic tone:
Adipocytes, being part of the hematopoietic microenvironment, have remained a subject of debate regarding their role in hematopoiesis. We previously demonstrated that the accumulation of adipocytes in the femoral bone marrow (BM) is associated with increased expression of neuropilin-1 (NP-1). In contrast, NP-1 expression is scarce in hematopoietic iliac crest BM. From this observation, we hypothesized that adipocytes might exert a negative impact on hematopoiesis through NP-1. To test this hypothesis, we established a BM adipocyte model differentiated into fibroblast-like fat cells (FLFCs), which exhibit characteristics similar to those of primitive unilocular fat cells. As expected, FLFCs constitutively produce macrophage colony-stimulating factor and induce CD34(+) cell differentiation into macrophages independently of cell-to-cell contact. However, granulopoiesis was impaired by cell-to-cell contact, but this inhibition could be overcome in transwell culture conditions or when FLFCs were treated with an antibody neutralizing NP-1. The latter proved to be essential for contact inhibition. Inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin-1β or dexamethasone, can modulate FLFC properties to restore granulopoiesis. Our findings provide the first evidence that primary adipocytes exert regulatory functions during hematopoiesis that may be relevant to certain pathological processes. Disclosure of potential conflicts of interest can be found at the end of this article.

title: The transcriptome profile of human embryonic stem cells as defined by SAGE.
text: Human embryonic stem (ES) cell lines possessing the capacity for self-renewal and differentiation into specific cell types have been developed. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these processes are not well understood. To address this knowledge gap, we analyzed the transcriptome profiles of two proprietary human ES cell lines (HES3 and HES4) from ES Cell International, and compared them with murine ES cells and other human tissues. Surprisingly, despite sharing some similarities, there are notable differences between human and mouse ES cells, including an inactive leukemia inhibitory factor pathway and a preponderance of specific genes like POU5F1 and SOX2 in human ES cells. We have compiled a list of genes consisting of both known ES-specific genes and new candidates that can serve as markers for human ES cells and may also contribute to their 'stemness' phenotype. Of particular interest was the downregulation of DNMT3B and LIN28 mRNAs during ES cell differentiation. The convergence of similarities and differences in gene expression profiles between human and mouse ES cells provides a solid foundation for a detailed and coordinated analysis of the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing their pluripotency, directed differentiation into specific cell types, and extended ability for self-renewal.

title: Small-molecule antagonists of p53-MDM2 binding: research tools and potential therapeutics.
text: p53 plays a vital role in protecting normal tissues from tumor development by regulating a key pathway. Under normal conditions, p53's growth-suppressive and pro-apoptotic activity is inhibited by MDM2, which binds to p53 and negates its activity and stability. However, the latest research has found that using MDM2 antagonists to activate p53 may offer a promising new approach to cancer treatment. Recently, our team identified potent and selective low-molecular-weight inhibitors of MDM2-p53 binding, known as Nutlins. These molecules activate the p53 pathway and suppress tumor growth in vitro and in vivo. They represent valuable new tools for studying the p53 pathway and its defects in cancer. Interestingly, Nutlins induce p53-dependent apoptosis in human cancer cells, but remain relatively inert against proliferating normal cells. Their impressive activity against osteosarcoma xenografts suggests that MDM2 antagonists may have potential clinical utility in the treatment of tumors with wild-type p53.

title: Slipped (CTG)•(CAG) repeats can be correctly repaired, escape repair or undergo error-prone repair
text: The expansion of (CTG)•(CAG) repeats, associated with 14 or more diseases, is believed to arise from the improper repair of slipped DNA. Using human cell extracts and DNA samples with slip-outs of (CAG)20 or (CTG)20, we evaluated the fidelity of slipped-DNA repair through three different outcomes: correct repair, escaped repair, and error-prone repair. The choice of repair path depended on the location of the nick and the composition of the slip-out (CAG or CTG). We discovered a new form of error-prone repair in which excess repeats were incompletely excised, generating expansions but not deletions. Neuron-like cell extracts exhibited each of the three repair outcomes, suggesting a role for these processes in the instability of (CTG)•(CAG) repeats in patient post-mitotic brain cells. We found that MMR and NER proteins hMSH2, hMSH3, hMLH1, XPF, XPG, or polymerase β were not required for the observed instability, indicating that their role in instability may occur before the processing of slipped repeats. These findings may explain the differences in mutation patterns between various disease loci or tissues.

title: High Dub3 expression in mouse ESCs couples the G1/S checkpoint to pluripotency.
text: The molecular mechanism underlying the G1/S checkpoint bypass in mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) is still unknown. DNA damage hinders entry into S phase by inhibiting the CDK2 kinase through the breakdown of its activator, the Cdc25A phosphatase. Interestingly, we discovered that Cdc25A levels remain high in G1 despite DNA damage in mouse ESCs. Furthermore, we found elevated expression of Dub3, a deubiquitylase responsible for regulating Cdc25A protein levels. Our results also revealed that the Dub3 gene is directly targeted by Esrrb, a crucial transcription factor in the self-renewal machinery. We discovered that Dub3 expression is significantly diminished during neural conversion and precedes Cdc25A instability, while forceful Dub3 expression in ESCs leads to fatal consequences upon differentiation. Notably, knockdown of either Dub3 or Cdc25A triggers spontaneous differentiation of ESCs. These findings collectively demonstrate the integration of the self-renewal machinery and cell-cycle regulation through the deubiquitylase pathway in ESCs.

title: Paracrine effects of direct intramyocardial implantation of bone marrow derived cells to enhance neovascularization in chronic ischaemic myocardium.
text:
Objective: To determine the optimal bone marrow (BM) cell types and their potential mechanisms of action for promoting neovascularization in chronic ischemic myocardium.
Methods: This study used a swine model of chronic ischemic myocardium to compare the functional effects, angiogenic potential, and cytokine expression of direct intramyocardial implantation of autologous BM CD31-positive endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) and mononuclear cells (MNCs) versus saline. The BM cells were harvested and catheter-based electromechanical mapping-guided direct intramyocardial injection was performed to target the ischemic myocardium. The outcomes were assessed after 12 weeks.
Results: The injection of BM-MNC resulted in significant improvements in left ventricular dP/dt, left ventricular pressure, and regional microsphere myocardial perfusion over ischaemic endocardium and epicardium compared to the saline group. In contrast, no significant effects were observed following injection of BM-EPC. The capillary density and expression of mRNA of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and angiopoietin-2 in the ischaemic myocardium were significantly greater in the BM-MNC group than the saline group. A positive correlation was found between capillary density and VEGF expression in the ischaemic myocardium.
Conclusion: The study found that catheter-based direct intramyocardial injection of BM-MNC enhanced angiogenesis more effectively than BM-EPC or saline, possibly via a paracrine effect, with increased expression of VEGF that subsequently improved cardiac performance of ischaemic myocardium.

title: Endogenous miRNA sponge lincRNA-RoR regulates Oct4, Nanog, and Sox2 in human embryonic stem cell self-renewal.
text:
The regulatory network of embryonic stem cell (ESC) transcription and epigenetics is intricately structured with multiple layers of control, including core transcription factors (TFs), post-transcriptional modifier microRNAs (miRNAs), and other regulators. However, the role of large intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) in this network and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our study aims to fill this knowledge gap by investigating the function of a specific lincRNA, linc-RoR, in the regulatory circuitry.
We demonstrate that linc-RoR functions as a key competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA), linking the network of miRNAs and core TFs, such as Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog. Surprisingly, linc-RoR shares miRNA-response elements with these core TFs, suggesting a competitive relationship between these molecules. We find that linc-RoR inhibits the suppression of these core TFs by miRNAs in self-renewing human ESCs, establishing a feedback loop between lincRNA, TFs, and miRNAs.
Our findings provide new insights into the complex interactions between components of genetic networks during development, and may lead to the discovery of new therapeutic approaches for various diseases. By shedding light on the mechanisms of ESC maintenance and differentiation, we pave the way for the development of novel therapies for regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, and beyond.

title: Foxp3(+) T cells regulate immunoglobulin a selection and facilitate diversification of bacterial species responsible for immune homeostasis.
text: Foxp3(+) T cells play a crucial role in maintaining immune tolerance. Our findings in mice reveal that these cells contribute to the diversification of the gut microbiota, particularly among species of the Firmicutes phylum. The control of indigenous bacteria by Foxp3(+) T cells involves both regulatory functions outside and inside germinal centers (GCs), including the suppression of inflammation and regulation of immunoglobulin A (IgA) selection in Peyer's patches. The diversified and selected IgAs contribute to maintaining a diverse and balanced microbiota, which in turn enables the expansion of Foxp3(+) T cells, the induction of GCs, and IgA responses in the gut through a regulatory loop. In essence, the adaptive immune system, through its cellular and molecular components required for immune tolerance, mediates the host-microbial symbiosis by controlling the richness and balance of bacterial communities necessary for homeostasis.

title: The isolation and characterization of a cDNA encoding phospholipid-specific inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase.
text: We have successfully reported the cloning and characterization of a novel human inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase (5-phosphatase), which exhibits distinct substrate specificity relative to previously described members of this large gene family. Previous studies have established that these enzymes hydrolyze water-soluble inositol phosphates, whereas our novel enzyme specifically targets lipid substrates, including phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate. Our cDNA isolation and sequence analysis have revealed a protein product of 644 amino acids and an estimated molecular mass (M(r)) of 70,023. We designate this 5-phosphatase as type IV, due to its highly basic nature (pI = 8.8) and pronounced affinity for phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate, with a comparatively low K(m) value of 0.65 micrometer, approximately 1/10 that of the previously characterized SHIP enzyme (K(m) = 5.95 micrometer). Our enzymatic assays have demonstrated that the activity of 5-phosphatase type IV is sensitive to the presence of detergents in the in vitro assay, consistent with the enzyme's preference for lipid substrates. Notably, SHIP, a previously characterized 5-phosphatase, also showed remarkable substrate versatility, efficiently hydrolyzing phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate in the presence of n-octyl beta-glucopyranoside or Triton X-100, but not cetyltriethylammonium bromide, which has been commonly used in other studies of hydrolysis of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate. Using antibodies raised against a peptide predicted by the cDNA, we were able to identify the 5-phosphatase type IV enzyme in various human tissues, with particularly high expression levels observed in the brain, as revealed by Western blotting. Additionally, we detected high levels of expression in the brain, testes, and heart, as well as lower levels of expression in other tissues, using Western blotting in mouse tissues. Furthermore, mRNA was found to be expressed in many tissues and cell lines, as revealed by Northern blotting.

title: Lack of Absent in Melanoma 2 (AIM2) expression in tumor cells is closely associated with poor survival in colorectal cancer patients.
text: Functional studies on colorectal cancer cells have shown that the interferon-inducible DNA sensor Absent in Melanoma 2 (AIM2) plays a protective role in cancer progression. Previous studies found that a high mutation rate and lack of AIM2 expression were present in a subset of colorectal cancers. To investigate the association between AIM2 expression and patient prognosis, we performed a tissue microarray analysis of 476 matched tissue pairs (colorectal tumor and adjacent normal colon epithelium) from 414 patients. We observed that 279 (67.4%) of the tumor samples had reduced AIM2 expression compared to their normal counterparts, while 38 (9.18%) had completely lost AIM2 expression in tumor cells. After adjusting for various clinical and pathological factors, we found that complete lack of AIM2 expression was associated with a significantly increased risk of overall mortality (HR=2.40; 95% CI=1.44-3.99) and disease-specific mortality (HR=3.14; 95% CI=1.75-5.65) compared to AIM2-positive tumor samples. Our findings strongly suggest that lack of AIM2 expression is a poor prognostic marker in colorectal cancer, and may be useful as a biomarker for identifying patients with poor prognosis. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to determine the underlying mechanisms by which AIM2 regulates colorectal cancer progression.

title: VSL#3 probiotic upregulates intestinal mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase and reduces inflammation.
text:
The present study aimed to investigate the effect of VSL#3 probiotic therapy on mucosal levels of alkaline sphingomyelinase in a mouse model of colitis and in patients with ulcerative colitis. Alkaline sphingomyelinase is an enzyme found exclusively in the bile and the intestinal brush border, which hydrolyzes sphingomyelin into ceramide, sphingosine, and sphingosine-1-phosphate, leading to epithelial apoptosis. Reduced levels of alkaline sphingomyelinase have been observed in premalignant and malignant intestinal epithelial cells as well as in ulcerative colitis tissue. Probiotic bacteria, such as VSL#3, may be a source of sphingomyelinase.
The study was conducted in two parts: in the first part, interleukin-10 gene-deficient (IL10KO) mice were treated with VSL#3 (10(9) colony-forming units per day) for three weeks, and alkaline sphingomyelinase activity was measured in ileal and colonic tissue. In the second part, 15 patients with ulcerative colitis were treated with VSL#3 (900 billion bacteria two times per day for five weeks), and alkaline sphingomyelinase activity was measured through biopsies. The study results showed that mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity was lower in the colon and ileum of IL10KO mice compared to controls, and VSL#3 treatment led to upregulation of mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity in both the colon and the ileum. Similarly, VSL#3 treatment of human patients with ulcerative colitis resulted in increased mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity and decreased ulcerative colitis disease activity index scores.
In conclusion, this study suggests that mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity is reduced in the intestine of mice with colitis and in humans with ulcerative colitis. Probiotic therapy with VSL#3 can upregulate mucosal alkaline sphingomyelinase activity, which may contribute to the therapeutic effects of probiotics in the management of inflammatory bowel diseases.

title: Nodal/Activin signaling predicts human pluripotent stem cell lines prone to differentiate toward the hematopoietic lineage.
text: Knowing which human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC) lines have the highest differentiation potential for a specific lineage is crucial, as it can greatly impact their use in various applications. To compare the hematopoietic differentiation potential of 14 hESC/iPSC lines, we analyzed their emergence of hemogenic progenitors, primitive and mature blood cells, and colony-forming unit (CFU) potential at different time points. Our findings revealed significant differences in the propensity to differentiate towards blood among hPSCs, with some showing good blood differentiation potential, while others exhibited limited capacity. Interestingly, we found that the CFU potential robustly correlated with hemogenic progenitors and primitive blood cells, but not with mature blood cells. Moreover, microarray analysis revealed distinct gene expression profiles between hPSCs with good and poor hematopoietic potential. Surprisingly, downregulation of neuroectoderm-associated genes and upregulation of Nodal/Activin signaling genes were observed in hPSCs with good hematopoietic differentiation potential. Using loss- and gain-of-function functional assays, we confirmed that Nodal/Activin signaling predicts hPSC lines with good blood-differentiation potential. Our findings underscore the importance of prospective comparative studies to determine the lineage-specific differentiation potential among different hPSCs and highlight the potential of Nodal/Activin signaling as a predictive marker for hematopoietic differentiation.

title: Addition of a Gastrointestinal Microbiome Modulator to Metformin Improves Metformin Tolerance and Fasting Glucose Levels.
text:
Once upon a time, there was a problem faced by many people with type 2 diabetes (T2D): the inability to tolerate metformin, a common medication used to treat the disease. The main reason for this intolerance was related to adverse effects in the gastrointestinal (GI) system. To address this challenge, researchers decided to test whether a GI microbiome modulator (GIMM) could be used in combination with metformin to alleviate the GI symptoms and improve the medication's tolerability.
In this study, 10 T2D patients who experienced metformin GI intolerance were enrolled in a 2-period crossover design. During the first week, the participants took 500 mg metformin with either GIMM or placebo, and in the second week, they took 500 mg metformin three times a day (t.i.d.) with the same treatment. The results showed that the combination of metformin and GIMM resulted in a significantly better tolerance score compared to the placebo combination. Moreover, the mean fasting glucose levels were significantly lower with the metformin-GIMM combination than with metformin-placebo.
In conclusion, the study suggests that combining a GI microbiome modulator with metformin may provide an effective solution to improve the tolerability of this medication in T2D patients, thereby expanding its potential use in treating the disease.

title: Diverse tumorigenic pathways in ovarian serous carcinoma.
text: The purpose of this study was to investigate genetic changes in 108 cases of sporadic serous ovarian neoplasms to gain insights into the development of ovarian serous carcinomas. Our findings show that approximately 50% of serous borderline tumors (SBTs), non-invasive micropapillary serous carcinomas (MPSCs), and invasive micropapillary serous carcinomas exhibit K-ras mutations, which indicate a progression of tumor types along a morphological continuum. In contrast, high-grade (conventional serous carcinoma) tumors had no K-ras mutations and displayed high levels of allelic imbalance even in early stages of the disease. Based on these observations, we propose a dualistic model for ovarian serous carcinogenesis, which involves either a stepwise progression from SBT to non-invasive and invasive MPSC or a rapid progression from the ovarian surface epithelium or inclusion cysts to a conventional (high-grade) serous carcinoma.

title: Tissue-inherent fate of GPI revealed by GPI-anchored GFP transgenesis.
text: To delve into the destiny of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) in mammals, we created GPI-anchored enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP-GPI) and transgenic mice lugging this fusion construct. When introduced into cultured cells, the EGFP-GPI protein was properly sorted to plasma membranes and microsomes based on GPI biosynthesis. Transgenic mice carrying EGFP-GPI displayed a wide range of transgene expression. Histologically, a striking polarized localization of EGFP-GPI protein was observed in various epithelia, the nervous system, and liver, as well as secretion from some exocrine glands, along with non-polarized presence in non-epithelial tissues, illustrating a tissue-inherent mechanism of GPI sorting.

title: Essential role for the SANT domain in the functioning of multiple chromatin remodeling enzymes.
text: The SANT domain, a novel motif identified in eukaryotic transcriptional regulatory proteins, has been found to play a crucial role in the in vivo functions of yeast proteins Swi3p, Ada2p, and Rsc8p, which are involved in chromatin remodeling complexes. Our studies show that the SANT domain of Ada2p is essential for its histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity, as well as for an Ada2p-dependent enhancement of histone tail binding and enzymatic catalysis by Gcn5p, another protein involved in the HAT complex. These findings suggest that SANT domains may play a general role in functional interactions with histone N-terminal tails.

title: Mechanisms of pancreatic beta-cell death in type 1 and type 2 diabetes: many differences, few similarities.
text: Type 1 and type 2 diabetes are characterized by progressive beta-cell failure, primarily due to apoptosis. While the mechanisms of beta-cell death in these two forms of the disease share some similarities, they also have distinct differences. In type 1 diabetes, invading immune cells produce cytokines such as IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, and IFN-gamma, which induce beta-cell apoptosis through the activation of beta-cell gene networks under the control of transcription factors NF-κB and STAT-1. NF-κB activation leads to the production of nitric oxide (NO) and chemokines, as well as depletion of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) calcium, ultimately resulting in the execution of beta-cell death through mitogen-activated protein kinases, ER stress, and the release of mitochondrial death signals. In contrast, chronic exposure to elevated levels of glucose and free fatty acids (FFAs) in type 2 diabetes causes beta-cell dysfunction and may induce beta-cell apoptosis through different mechanisms. While high glucose initially triggers "glucose hypersensitization," it can later induce apoptosis via mechanisms that are distinct from those in type 1 diabetes. High glucose does not induce or activate IL-1β, NF-κB, or inducible nitric oxide synthase in rat or human beta-cells in vitro or in vivo. In contrast, FFAs may cause beta-cell apoptosis through ER stress, which is NF-κB and NO independent. These findings suggest that cytokines and nutrients trigger beta-cell death through fundamentally different mechanisms, and different approaches may be needed to prevent beta-cell death in type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

title: Health-related quality of life among children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
text:
Study Objective:
The aim of this study was to assess the health-related quality of life (HRQL) of children treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and identify specific areas that require intervention.
Study Design:
This study included two groups: ALL patients aged 5 and older participating in a multi-center clinical trial and a general population control group. HRQL was evaluated during all four phases of active treatment and approximately 2 years after treatment using the Health Utilities Index Mark 2 (HUI2) and Mark 3 (HUI3). Quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were calculated based on HRQL scores, and excess disability rates were identified to inform remediation efforts.
 Haupt Ergebnisse:
HRQL assessments were conducted on 749 patients during the five treatment phases. HRQL scores improved significantly from induction to the post-treatment phase (P < 0.001). There were no significant differences in HRQL based on demographic or treatment characteristics, except for the type of asparaginase during continuation therapy (P = 0.005 for HUI2 and P = 0.007 for HUI3). Compared to controls, patients lost approximately 0.2 QALYs during active treatment. Disability was observed in mobility/ambulation, emotion, self-care, and pain, with a decline over time.
Conclusion:
Patients with ALL experienced significant but declining deficits in HRQL during active treatment phases, equivalent to losing approximately 2 months of life in perfect health. HRQL in the 2-year post-treatment phase was similar to controls. To address this policy challenge, new treatment protocols are needed that minimize disabilities in mobility/ambulation, emotion, self-care, and pain without compromising survival.

title: JUVENILE MORTALITY INCREASES WITH CLUTCH SIZE IN A NEOTROPICAL BIRD
text: The relationship between avian clutch size and latitude is a well-known example of geographic variation in a vertebrate life-history trait. Previous studies have proposed several hypotheses to explain this pattern, including nest predation, limited food Availability for nestlings, and post-fledging juvenile mortality, which act as selection pressures leading to small clutch size in tropical birds. To test these hypotheses, we empirically manipulated the clutch size of Spotted Antbirds (Hylophylax naevioides) in central Panama. Our findings revealed that parental activity at nests had no effect on nest predation rates, and parents could successfully feed nestlings in larger broods. However, larger broods produced the most fledged juveniles, but these individuals had a lower survival probability until dispersal compared to juveniles from smaller broods. Consequently, clutch size did not affect nest productivity. We also found that post-fledging mortality was not related to nestling mass two to three days prior to fledging. Instead, differences in parental investment allocation among differently sized broods influenced juvenile survival probability. These results suggest that post-fledging parental care may play a crucial role in shaping the evolution of small clutch size in tropical birds.

title: Diagnosis of rotator cuff tears.
text: Rotator cuff tears account for nearly 50% of severe shoulder injuries, but diagnosis can be challenging. To improve diagnostic accuracy, we conducted a prospective study comparing the results of 23 clinical tests on 400 patients with and without rotator cuff tears. We found that three basic tests were highly predictive of rotator cuff tears: weakness in the supraspinatus muscle, weakness in external rotation, and impingement. When all three of these tests were present, or when two tests were present and the patient was aged 60 or older, the likelihood of a rotator cuff tear was 98%. Conversely, the absence of these features excluded the diagnosis of a rotator cuff tear.

title: Increased susceptibility to UV-induced skin carcinogenesis in polymerase eta-deficient mice.
text: Individuals with Xeroderma pigmentosum variant (XPV) harboring mutations in the DNA polymerase eta (Pol eta) gene are particularly sensitive to sunlight and have a heightened risk of developing skin cancer. Pol eta's ability to bypass UV light-induced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers contributes to its protective function, as XPV cells lacking Pol eta have reduced capacity to repair UV-damaged DNA and are more susceptible to UV light-induced killing and mutagenesis. To delve deeper into the mechanisms of Pol eta, we generated Pol eta-deficient mice. Notably, these mice are viable and fertile, with no apparent spontaneous defects during the first year of life. However, fibroblasts derived from Pol eta-deficient mice are sensitive to UV light-induced killing, and all Pol eta-deficient mice develop skin tumors upon exposure to UV light, in contrast to wild-type littermate controls that do not develop such tumors. These findings, together with biochemical studies of mouse Pol eta, demonstrate that Pol eta-dependent bypass of cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers shields mice from UV light-induced skin cancer. Furthermore, 37.5% of Pol eta heterozygous mice also developed skin cancer following a 5-month exposure to UV light, suggesting that individuals who are heterozygous for mutations in Pol eta may also be at an increased risk of skin cancer.

title: Hydrogen sulfide interacts with nitric oxide in the heart: possible involvement of nitroxyl.
text: The present study aimed to investigate the interaction between nitric oxide (NO) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S), two important gaseous mediators, in rat hearts. The study used isolated cardiomyocytes and measured intracellular calcium levels with a spectrofluorometric method and myocyte contractility with a video edge system. The results showed that sodium hydrosulfide (NaHS) did not significantly affect the resting calcium levels or myocyte contractility, but unexpectedly reversed the negative inotropic and lusitropic effects of increasing NO production with l-arginine or exogenous NO donors, such as sodium nitroprusside (SNP) and 2-(N,N-diethylamino)-diazenolate-2-oxide. Additionally, the combination of SNP and NaHS increased, while SNP alone decreased, the resting calcium levels and the amplitudes of electrically induced calcium transients. The study also found that three thiols (N-acetyl-cysteine, l-cysteine, and glutathione) abolished the effects of the nitroxyl anion (HNO) donor, which mimicked the effect of SNP + NaHS on calcium handling and myocyte contractility. The study suggest that H2S may interact with NO to form a thiol-sensitive molecule (probably HNO) that produces positive inotropic and lusitropic effects, providing new insights into the interaction of NO and H2S and potentially shedding light on the development of new treatments for cardiovascular diseases.

title: A novel mechanism of rapid nuclear neutrophil extracellular trap formation in response to Staphylococcus aureus.
text: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are complex structures comprised of DNA and antimicrobial molecules that play a novel role in innate immune defense. Prior studies suggested that NETs form within 3-4 hours after neutrophil death through an oxidant-dependent process. However, in this study, we uncovered a unique mechanism of NET formation in which neutrophils respond to Staphylococcus aureus without undergoing lysis or membrane breach. Instead, the multilobular nucleus rapidly condenses, leading to the separation of inner and outer nuclear membranes and the budding of vesicles filled with nuclear DNA. These vesicles are extruded into the extracellular space and rupture, releasing chromatin into the surrounding environment. This process occurs rapidly (within 5-60 minutes) and does not rely on oxidants. While mitochondrial DNA is present in NETs, it plays a limited role in this process. Active proteolytic enzymes are also present in supernatants from NET-inducing cells, which contribute to the killing of S. aureus. Interestingly, Panton-Valentine leukocidin, autolysin, and a lipase were identified as NET-inducing factors, with Panton-Valentine leukocidin being the most prominent. Our findings highlight a new, rapid mechanism of NET release that plays a critical role in trapping and eliminating S. aureus.

title: 131-I radioiodine therapy for hyperthyroidism in patients with Graves' disease, uninodular goitre and multinodular goitre.
text: We analyzed 201 patients who received a standardized dose of radioiodine for the treatment of hyperthyroidism between 1981 and 1986.Of these patients, 170 had Graves' disease and were treated with a mean (SE) dose of 369 (10) MBq of 131-I, resulting in a remission rate of 94% at 6 months and a cumulative relapse rate of 12% at 1 year and 21% at 5 years. The incidence of hypothyroidism was 26% at 3 months, 55% at 6 months, 61% at 1 year, and 66% at 5 years.Only 10 patients had a uninodular goiter, who were treated with a mean (SE) dose of 438 (85) MBq of 131-I, resulting in a 100% remission rate at 6 months without relapse at 1 year but relapsing in 17% at 5 years. The incidence of hypothyroidism was 26% at 3 months, 30% at 6 months, 40% at 1 year, and 40% at 5 years.Twenty-one patients had a multinodular goiter, who were treated with a mean (SE) dose of 613 (77) MBq of 131-I, resulting in a 79% remission rate at 6 months and a cumulative relapse rate of 26% at 1 year and 39% at 5 years. The incidence of hypothyroidism was 5% at 3 months, 14% at 6 months, 24% at 1 year, and 24% at 5 years.

title: Enteral nutrition in the critically ill patient.
text: The timing and route of nutrition provision to critically ill patients can have a significant impact on their outcome. Early enteral nutrition has been shown to reduce specifically infectious morbidity in critically ill patients. However, there is a subset of patients who are malnourished upon admission to the intensive care unit, and in these cases, parenteral nutrition may be beneficial.

title: Genomewide analysis of nucleosome density histone acetylation and HDAC function in fission yeast.
text: We have conducted a comprehensive analysis of the enzymatic specificity, expression profiles, and binding locations of four histone deacetylases (HDACs) in fission yeast (Schizosaccharomyces pombe). By comparing the acetylation patterns of histones and nucleosome density, as well as the binding of HDACs to different regions of the genome, we found that Sir2 (class III) and Hos2 (class I) play a role in maintaining histone stability, while Clr6 (class I) is primarily responsible for repressing gene expression at promoters.
