The final prevalence was adjusted for loss to follow-up and logistic regression was used to identify risk factors.
Results:
BP distribution at the initial screen was 81.1% normal, 9.5% pre-hypertension, and 9.4% hypertension (8.4% Stage 1 and 1% Stage 2). After 3 screenings, the prevalence was 81.1% normal, 15.7% pre-hypertension, and 3.2% hypertension (2.6% Stage 1 and 0.6% Stage 2). Hypertension and pre-hypertension increased with increasing body mass index. Sex, race, and classification as either at-risk for overweight or overweight were independently associated with pre-hypertension, while only classification as overweight was associated with hypertension.

title: Increased short- and long-term risk of inflammatory bowel disease after salmonella or campylobacter gastroenteritis.
text:
In this study, we aimed to investigate the association between commensal enteric bacteria and the development of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD). We compared the risk of IBD between individuals who had experienced Salmonella or Campylobacter gastroenteritis and an age- and gender-matched control group from the same population in Denmark.
We identified 13,324 patients with Salmonella/Campylobacter gastroenteritis from laboratory registries in North Jutland and Aarhus counties, Denmark, between 1991 and 2003, and 26,648 unexposed controls from the same counties. Of these, 176 exposed patients with IBD before the infection, their 352 unexposed controls, and 80 unexposed individuals with IBD before the Salmonella/Campylobacter infection were excluded. The final study cohort consisted of 13,148 exposed individuals and 26,216 unexposed individuals, who were followed for up to 15 years (mean, 7.5 years).
Our results showed that a first-time diagnosis of IBD was more common in exposed individuals (1.2%) than in unexposed individuals (0.5%). Adjusting for age, gender, and comorbidities by using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis, the hazard ratio (95% confidence interval) for IBD was 2.9 (2.2-3.9) for the whole period and 1.9 (1.4-2.6) if the first year after the Salmonella/Campylobacter infection was excluded. The increased risk of IBD was observed throughout the 15-year observation period and was similar for Salmonella and Campylobacter infections, as well as for first-time diagnoses of Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
In conclusion, our population-based cohort study found that individuals who experienced an episode of Salmonella/Campylobacter gastroenteritis had an increased risk of developing IBD.

title: Establishment of a cell line (NPC/HK1) from a differentiated squamous carcinoma of the nasopharynx.
text: An extended cell culture of epithelial cells was established from a squamous carcinoma of the nasopharynx in a Chinese male who had received radiation therapy 17 years and 6 months prior. The cell line, named NPC/HK1, has been passaged 72 times over the course of one year. Through light and electron microscopy, the cells were identified as squamous epithelial in nature. When these cells were implanted subcutaneously into the backs of athymic nude BALB/c (nu/nu) mice, tumors developed at the injection sites, which upon histological analysis were found to be well-differentiated squamous carcinomas resembling the original human tumor from which they were derived. Karyotypic analysis of the cells from the cell line revealed an aneuploid human karyotype with a modal chromosome number of 74, featuring both numerical and structural chromosomal aberrations. Essentially, no viral particles or Epstein-Barr viral nuclear antigen (EBNA) was found in the cells from the primary culture or several subsequent subcultures. Although the presence of EBNA was inconclusive in touch smears taken from the biopsy tissue, attempts to infect subcultured cells with EBV from P3HR1 and B95-8 cells were unsuccessful.

title: Effect of lipid restriction on mitochondrial free radical production and oxidative DNA damage.
text: Numerous studies have shown that a 40% reduction in caloric intake (ribo) diminishes mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in rodents. Recently, we discovered that 7 weeks of 40% protein restriction without significant caloric restriction also lowered ROS levels in rat liver. This is intriguing since it has been reported that protein restriction can extend the lifespan of rodents. In the current study, we investigated the potential link between dietary lipids and the effects of caloric restriction on mitochondrial oxidative stress. Employing semipurified diets, we decreased lipid intake by 40% in male Wistar rats compared to controls, while maintaining the other dietary components at the same level as in ad libitum-fed animals. Following 7 weeks of treatment, liver mitochondria from lipid-restricted rats exhibited elevated oxygen consumption with complex I-linked substrates (pyruvate/malate and glutamate/malate). Additionally, we did not observe modifications in mitochondrial hydrogen peroxide (H(2)O(2)) production or oxidative damage to mitochondrial or nuclear DNA in lipid-restricted animals. Notably, mitochondrial DNA damage was about 10 times higher than nuclear DNA damage in both dietary groups. These findings refute a role for lipids and reinforce the possibility that dietary proteins play a significant role in the decrease in mitochondrial ROS production and DNA damage attributed to caloric restriction.

title: Kruppel-like factor 2 is a transcriptional regulator of chronic and acute inflammation.
text: Myeloid cell activation is crucial for a optimal innate immune response, but uncontrolled activation can lead to collateral damage to host tissues. Kruppel-like factor 2 (KLF2) is a potent regulator of myeloid cell proinflammatory activation, and studies have shown that reduced KLF2 levels are associated with acute or chronic inflammatory disorders in humans. To investigate the biological response to inflammation in KLF2-deficient mice, we subjected them to acute (sepsis) and subacute (skin) inflammatory challenges. Our findings showed that partial deficiency of KLF2 modulates the in vivo response to inflammation. Mechanistically, we found that KLF2 inhibits NF-κB transcriptional activity, which is a key regulator of inflammatory responses. These observations provide valuable insights into the KLF2-mediated modulation of inflammatory processes, which could potentially be leveraged for therapeutic gain.

title: Simian immunodeficiency viruses replication dynamics in African non-human primate hosts: common patterns and species-specific differences.
text: To identify potential common features of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infections in different naturally infected host species, we compared the replication dynamics of SIV in 31 African green monkeys (10 sabeus, 15 vervets, and seven Caribbean AGMs), 14 mandrills, and three sooty mangabeys (SMs) that were experimentally infected with their respective viruses. RESULTS showed that SIV replicated rapidly, reaching viral loads (VLs) of 105-109 copies/ml of plasma between days 9-14 post-infection (p.i.). A set point viremia was established between days 42-60 p.i., with levels of approximately 105-106 copies/ml in SM and mandrills, and lower levels (103-105 copies/ml) in AGMs. VL during the chronic phase did not correlate with viral genome structure, as SIVmnd-2 (a vpx-containing virus) and SIVmnd-1 (which does not contain vpu or vpx) replicated to similar levels in mandrills. VL was dependent on virus strain, as vervets infected with three different viral strains showed different patterns of viral replication. The pattern of viral replication of SIVagm.sab, which uses both CCR5 and CXCR4 co-receptors, was similar to those of the other viruses. CONCLUSIONS reveal a common pattern of SIV replication in naturally and experimentally infected hosts, similar to that observed in pathogenic SIV infection of macaques. This finding suggests that differences in clinical outcome between pathogenic and non-pathogenic infections rely on host responses rather than the characteristics of the virus itself.

title: The role of the transcription factor KLF2 in vascular development and disease.
text: The zinc-finger transcription factor KLF2 serves as a crucial mediator between the physical forces of blood flow and the molecular signals responsible for a wide range of biological responses. Initially identified as a flow-responsive endothelial transcription factor, KLF2 has since been found to be expressed in a variety of cell types and play a role in numerous processes during both development and disease, including endothelial homeostasis, vasoregulation, vascular growth and remodeling, and inflammation. This review will provide an overview of the current understanding of KLF2's functions in vascular biology.

title: Implementation of contemporary oral antiplatelet treatment guidelines in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a report from the GReek AntiPlatelet rEgistry (GRAPE).
text:
The implementation of contemporary oral antiplatelet treatment guidelines in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains understudied. The Greek AntiPlatelet registry (GRAPE), initiated in January 2012, is a prospective, observational, multicenter cohort study that aims to investigate the use of P2Y12 inhibitors in contemporary practice. GRAPE evaluated the appropriateness of P2Y12 selection in 1434 patients using an eligibility-assessing algorithm based on contraindications/specific warnings and precautions.
Initially, appropriate, less preferable, and inappropriate P2Y12 inhibitor selections were made in 45.8%, 47.2%, and 6.6% of patients, respectively. The selection of clopidogrel was the most commonly made less preferable, both initially (69.7%) and at discharge (75.6%). The use of newer agents such as prasugrel or ticagrelor was largely appropriate initially (79.2-82.8%), with a further increase at discharge (89.4-89.8%). Inappropriate selection of the newer agents was 17.2-20.8% initially, decreasing to 10.2-10.6% at discharge.
Conditions and co-medications related to increased bleeding risk, presentation with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, and the absence of reperfusion within the first 24 hours were the most powerful predictors of appropriate P2Y12 selection initially. However, at discharge, age ≥75 years, conditions and co-medications related to increased bleeding risk, and regional trends were the most significant factors affecting appropriate P2Y12 selection.
The study findings indicate that adherence to the recently released guidelines on oral antiplatelet therapy was satisfactory. Clopidogrel was the most commonly used less preferable selection, while prasugrel or ticagrelor selection was mostly appropriate. Certain factors may predict initial and at discharge guideline implementation.
Clinical Trial Registration: NCT01774955 (http://clinicaltrials.gov/)

title: Comorbidity of depressive and anxiety disorders in chronic daily headache and its subtypes.
text:
Investigating the Prevalence of Depressive and Anxiety Disorders in Patients with Chronic Daily Headache
Objective: To investigate the frequency of depressive and anxiety disorders in patients with chronic daily headache (CDH).
Background: There is a lack of data in the literature on the extent of psychiatric comorbidity in patients with different subtypes of CDH.
Methods: Consecutive patients with CDH seen in a headache clinic from November 1998 to December 1999 were recruited. The subtypes of CDH were classified according to the criteria proposed by Silberstein et al. A psychiatrist evaluated the patients using the structured Mini-International Neuropsychiatric Interview to assess the comorbidity of depressive and anxiety disorders.
Results: Two hundred sixty-one patients with CDH were recruited, with a mean age of 46 years and 80% being women. Transformed migraine was diagnosed in 152 patients (58%), and chronic tension-type headache in 92 patients (35%). Seventy-eight percent of patients with transformed migraine had psychiatric comorbidity, including major depression (57%), dysthymia (11%), panic disorder (30%), and generalized anxiety disorder (8%). Sixty-four percent of patients with chronic tension-type headache had psychiatric diagnoses, including major depression (51%), dysthymia (8%), panic disorder (22%), and generalized anxiety disorder (1%). The frequency of anxiety disorders was significantly higher in patients with transformed migraine after controlling for age and sex (P =.02). Both depressive and anxiety disorders were significantly more frequent in women.
Conclusion: This study demonstrates that psychiatric comorbidity, especially major depression and panic disorders, is highly prevalent in patients with chronic daily headache seen in a headache clinic. Women and patients with transformed migraine are at higher risk of psychiatric comorbidity. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating patients with CDH for psychiatric disorders and provide further support for the need for multidisciplinary approaches to manage headache and psychiatric disorders.

title: The precursor form of IL-1alpha is an intracrine proinflammatory activator of transcription.
text: Although most cytokines are typically studied for their biological effects after binding to their specific cell surface receptors, recent evidence suggests that some cytokines, such as IL-1alpha, can also function within the nucleus. In the current study, we overexpressed the precursor form of IL-1alpha in various cells and measured its activity in the presence of saturating concentrations of IL-1 receptor antagonist to prevent receptor signaling. Interestingly, we found that IL-1alpha precursor translocated to the nucleus after activation by endotoxin, a Toll-like receptor ligand. The precursor form of IL-1alpha, but not the mature form, activated the transcriptional machinery in the GAL4 system by 90-fold, with a 50-fold increase observed using only the IL-1alpha propiece. This suggests that the transcriptional activation is localized to the N terminus, where the nuclear localization sequence resides. Under conditions of IL-1 receptor blockade, intracellular overexpression of the precursor and propiece forms of IL-1alpha were sufficient to activate NF-κB and AP-1. Stable transfectants overproducing precursor IL-1alpha released the cytokines IL-8 and IL-6 and had a lower threshold of activation to subpicomolar concentrations of tumor necrosis factor alpha or IFN-gamma. Therefore, intracellular functions of IL-1alpha may play an unforeseen role in the genesis of inflammation. During disease-driven events, the cytosolic precursor moves to the nucleus, where it enhances transcription of proinflammatory genes. Because this mechanism of action is not affected by extracellular inhibitors, reducing intracellular functions of IL-1alpha may prove beneficial in some inflammatory conditions.

title: Three-dimensional structure of the AAH26994.1 protein from Mus musculus, a putative eukaryotic Urm1.
text: Using NMR spectroscopy, we have determined the solution structure of protein AAH26994.1 from Mus musculus and proposed that it represents the first three-dimensional structure of a ubiquitin-related modifier 1 (Urm1) protein. Amino acid sequence comparisons suggest that AAH26994.1 belongs to the Urm1 family of ubiquitin-like modifier proteins, which are known to be involved in nutrient sensing, invasive growth, and budding in yeast. While AAH26994.1 shares little sequence identity with ubiquitin, its structure bears a closer resemblance to MoaD subunits of molybdopterin synthases, which are known structures of three bacterial MoaD proteins with 14%-26% sequence identity to AAH26994.1. The structures of AAH26994.1 and MoaD proteins both contain the signature ubiquitin secondary structure fold, but they differ significantly from ubiquitin in regions outside of this fold. This structural similarity supports the hypothesis that ubiquitin and ubiquitin-related proteins evolved from a protein-based sulfide donor system of the molybdopterin synthase type.

title: Concurrent endometrial carcinoma in women with a biopsy diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia: a Gynecologic Oncology Group study.
text: The article discusses the prevalence of concurrent endometrial carcinoma in women with a biopsy diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH). The study included 306 women who underwent hysterectomy within 12 weeks of being diagnosed with AEH. The study pathologists reviewed the biopsy specimens and found that 25.6% were diagnosed as less than AEH, 39.8% as AEH, and 29.1% as endometrial carcinoma. In 5.5% of the specimens, there was no consensus on the biopsy diagnosis. The rate of concurrent endometrial carcinoma was found to be 42.6%. Of these, 30.9% were myoinvasive and 10.6% involved the outer 50% of the myometrium. The study concluded that the prevalence of endometrial carcinoma in patients with a biopsy diagnosis of AEH is high, and clinicians and patients should take this into account when considering management strategies.

title: The prevalence and clustering of four major lifestyle risk factors in an English adult population.
text:
Objective: To investigate the clustering of four major lifestyle risk factors (smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, poor fruit and vegetable consumption, and physical inactivity) among the English adult population and to examine variations in clustering across different socio-demographic groups.
Methods: The study population consisted of 11,492 individuals from the 2003 Health Survey for England. Clustering was assessed by comparing observed and expected combinations of the four risk factors. A multinomial multilevel regression model was used to examine socio-demographic variations in clustering.
Results: The study found that a majority of the English population had multiple lifestyle risk factors concurrently, as per British health recommendations. Clustering was more pronounced among women than men, and higher in lower social class households, singles, and inactive individuals. Conversely, home ownership and older age groups had lower prevalence of multiple risk factors.
Conclusion: The findings support the implementation of multiple-behavior interventions rather than single-behavior interventions, given the clustering of risk factors among the English population.

title: Cutting edge: interleukin 17 signals through a heteromeric receptor complex.
text: IL-17 is a cytokine that plays a crucial role in the development of various autoimmune diseases. Its primary producers are a distinct lineage of CD4 T cells. The IL-17RA receptor is ubiquitously expressed and essential for the biological activity of IL-17. However, the activity of IL-17 is most notably defined by its ability to induce the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and other mediators in stromal cells. Interestingly, mouse stromal cells lacking IL-17RA are poorly complemented by human IL-17RA, suggesting the presence of an essential ancillary component whose activity is species-specific. This component is IL-17RC, a distinct member of the IL-17R family. Therefore, the biological activity of IL-17 is contingent upon a complex consisting of IL-17RA and IL-17RC, which throws light on a new paradigm for understanding the interactions between the expanding family of IL-17 ligands and their receptors.

title: Long non-coding RNAs with low expression levels in cells are enriched in secreted exosomes.
text: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play a crucial role in regulating chromatin modifications, gene transcription, mRNA translation, and protein function. Recently, we found substantial differences in the basal expression levels of a panel of lncRNAs in HeLa and MCF-7 cells, as well as their differential response to DNA damage induction. Here, we hypothesized that lncRNAs with varying cellular expression may exhibit distinct abundance in secreted exosomes, with their exosome levels reflecting the cellular response to DNA damage. We characterized MALAT1, HOTAIR, lincRNA-p21, GAS5, TUG1, and CCND1-ncRNA in exosomes secreted from cultured cells and observed a distinct expression pattern of lncRNAs in exosomes compared to cells. Specifically, RNAs with low cellular expression (lincRNA-p21, HOTAIR, and ncRNA-CCND1) were highly enriched in exosomes, while TUG1 and GAS5 levels were moderately elevated, and MALAT1, which was the most abundant molecule in cells, was present at levels comparable to its cellular levels. LincRNA-p21 and ncRNA-CCND1 were the predominant molecules, and their exosome levels best reflected the change in their cellular levels upon exposure of the cells to bleomycin-induced DNA damage. We conclude that lncRNAs exhibit a selective loading in exosomes, indicating a differential abundance.

title: Olanzapine depot exposure in male rats: Dose-dependent lipogenic effects without concomitant weight gain.
text: Treatment with second-generation antipsychotic agents, such as olanzapine, is frequently associated with metabolic adverse effects, including hyperphagia, weight gain, and dyslipidemia, in both male and female patients. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood, and studies in rodents are crucial in exploring these mechanisms. Nevertheless, the validity of the rodent model is limited by the fact that antipsychotics cause weight gain in female rats but not male rats. Previous studies have shown that a single intramuscular injection of a long-acting olanzapine formulation resulted in clinically relevant plasma concentrations and dysmetabolic features in female rats. In the current study, we investigated the effect of depot injections of olanzapine on plasma concentrations and metabolic effects in male rats. Our results showed that depot injections of 100-250 mg/kg olanzapine resulted in clinically relevant plasma concentrations of olanzapine in male rats, despite transient hyperphagia. However, olanzapine did not lead to weight gain in male rats, but instead resulted in weight loss. The reduction in weight gain was accompanied by a slight elevation of thermogenesis markers in brown adipose tissue for the highest olanzapine dose. Furthermore, olanzapine doses of 200 mg/kg or above induced significantly elevated plasma cholesterol levels and pronounced activation of lipogenic gene expression in the liver, indicating that olanzapine stimulates lipogenic effects independently of weight gain. These findings suggest that endocrine factors may play a role in the gender-specific metabolic effects of antipsychotics in the rat.

title: Glutamate mediates the function of melanocortin receptor 4 on Sim1 neurons in body weight regulation.
text: The melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R) plays a crucial role in maintaining body weight homeostasis, but the neurotransmitters that interact with MC4Rs are still largely unknown. As a result, the second-order neurons of the MC4R neural pathway remains poorly understood. Single-minded 1 (Sim1)-expressing brain regions, such as the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVH), are key brain sites involved in melanocortin action. In this study, we conditionally restored MC4R expression in Sim1 neurons in MC4R-null mice. This restoration significantly reduced obesity in these mice. However, the anti-obesity effect was completely reversed when we selectively disrupted glutamate release from the same Sim1 neurons. This led to a decrease in energy expenditure and an increase in hyperphagia, resulting in rapid obesity development. Consistent with these findings, selective disruption of glutamate release from adult PVH neurons also resulted in rapid obesity development due to reduced energy expenditure and hyperphagia. This study has therefore identified glutamate as the primary neurotransmitter that mediates MC4R function in body weight regulation.

title: Intracellular sterol dynamics.
text: We dive into the cellular mechanisms involved in cholesterol transport and distribution. Recent research has shed light on the distribution of sterols within cells, including an analysis of their transbilayer distribution. The cholesterol-lipid interaction and participation in various trafficking processes determine its optimal concentration in a particular membrane, thus resulting in an uneven distribution among intracellular organelles. Cholesterol content is crucial, as it plays a vital role in regulating membrane physicochemical properties and facilitating key cellular events such as signal transduction and protein transport. Cholesterol movement between organelles is highly dynamic, with both vesicular and non-vesicular processes involved. Various studies have investigated the proteins that play a significant role in these processes, providing new insights into the relative importance of these two trafficking pathways in cholesterol transport. Although still poorly characterized in many cases, several potential sterol transport proteins have been identified in detail, thus beginning to appreciably understand the molecular mechanisms underlying cholesterol transport across membranes.

title: A plasma membrane component able to bind and alter virions of poliovirus type 1: studies on cell-free alteration using a simplified assay.
text: HeLa cells can bind and convert poliovirus type 1 virions into altered particles through incubation at 37°C. Altered particles have a slower sedimentation rate, lack VP-4, and can be disrupted by sodium dodecyl sulfate treatment. However, their RNA remains intact and resistant to ribonuclease digestion. Using a simple assay protocol, the binding and alteration processes can be quantitatively measured, and the activity can be localized to plasma membranes. Pure membranes can also be shown to carry out the alteration process, which is abolished by proteases and nonionic detergents. In contrast, only altered particles are formed through membrane-bound activity, and the release of RNA is not caused by membranes but rather by intact cells. Importantly, binding and alteration are closely associated processes, and it is possible that alteration is a consequence of binding by multiple receptors in a fluid membrane.

title: Resequencing studies of nonmodel organisms using closely related reference genomes: optimal experimental designs and bioinformatics approaches for population genomics.
text: Advances in next-generation sequencing (NGS) technology have made it possible to study a wide range of genomic questions in nonmodel organisms, despite the lack of genomic resources. However, designing and analyzing NGS data from less well-known species can be challenging due to the absence of a species-specific reference genome. In this study, we investigate the performance of alternative bioinformatics approaches in estimating variability and neutrality tests based on the site-frequency-spectrum (SFS) from individual resequencing data. We specifically address the challenges faced in studying nonmodel organisms, including the absence of a reference genome, and compare the performance of three alternative approaches: genotype calling, genotype–haplotype calling, and direct estimation without calling genotypes. Our results show that relying on genotype calls provides biased estimates of population genetic statistics at low to moderate read depth, while genotype–haplotype calling returns more accurate estimates, but only at moderate depth. Direct estimation without calling genotypes returns the most accurate estimates, including at low read depth. We conclude that studies without a species-specific reference genome should aim for low read depth and avoid genotype calling whenever possible, while studies with moderate to high read depth can use genotype–haplotype calling.

title: Thalassemia and malaria: new insights into an old problem.
text:
Here is a reprise of the given text with some slight modifications for improved readability and clarity:
Hemoglobinopathies are the most common genetic diseases worldwide, with an estimated 5% of the population carrying one or more of the alpha-thalassemia, beta-thalassemia, or structural hemoglobin variants such as S, C, and E. These conditions provide protection against malaria, which is thought to have driven their prevalence in malarial regions through natural selection, an idea first proposed 50 years ago by J.B.S. Haldane. Epidemiological studies in Africa in the 1950s supported the "malaria hypothesis," but it has been challenging to verify this until recent advances in molecular methods. Now, population and molecular genetic analysis of thalassemia variants, as well as microepidemiological studies of the relationship between alpha-thalassemia and malaria in the southwest Pacific, have provided conclusive evidence for protection. Interestingly, some of this protection appears to originate from the increased susceptibility of very young thalassemic children to both Plasmodium falciparum and, especially, P. vivax, with early exposure providing the basis for better protection in later life.

title: Endocrine control of spermatogenesis: Role of FSH and LH/ testosterone.
text: Evaluating testicular function, including sperm production and androgen levels, is a crucial aspect of preclinical safety assessments, and testicular toxicity is significantly more common than ovarian toxicity. This chapter focuses on the histological consequences of disrupted reproductive endocrinology in rats, dogs, and nonhuman primates, as well as a review of our current understanding of the roles of gonadotropins and androgens. The rodent testis exhibits different responses to endocrine disturbances compared to dogs and primates, with distinct germ cell types and spermatogenic stages affected at different stages, and end-stage spermatogenic involution more pronounced in dogs and primates. Luteinizing hormone (LH)/testosterone and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) are the primary endocrine regulators of testicular function. While the relative importance of these hormones varies between rodents and primates, both LH/testosterone and FSH are essential for quantitatively normal spermatogenesis in non-seasonal species.

title: Extravasation injuries on regional neonatal units.
text: A survey of regional neonatal intensive care units revealed a prevalence of 38 per 1000 neonates who sustained an extravasation injury resulting in skin necrosis. Most injuries occurred in infants who were 26 weeks gestation or younger, and were caused by parenteral nutrition administered through intravenous cannulae. Treatment options included exposing wounds to air, infiltrating them with hyaluronidase and saline, and applying occlusive dressings.

title: Nonstructural protein 3-4A: the Swiss army knife of hepatitis C virus.
text: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) nonstructural protein 3-4A (NS3-4A) is a complex composed of NS3 and its cofactor NS4A, which harbors both serine protease and NTPase/RNA helicase activities. This complex plays a crucial role in viral polyprotein processing, RNA replication, and virion formation. Recent studies have shown that specific inhibitors of the NS3-4A protease can significantly improve sustained virological response rates in patients with chronic hepatitis C when combined with pegylated interferon-α and ribavirin. Moreover, NS3-4A has been found to target selected cellular proteins, thereby blocking innate immune pathways and modulating growth factor signaling, contributing to the persistence and pathogenesis of HCV. This review provides an updated overview of the biochemical and structural aspects of NS3-4A, its role in the pathogenesis of chronic hepatitis C, and the clinical development of NS3-4A protease inhibitors.

title: Phase 2 safety trial targeting amyloid beta production with a gamma-secretase inhibitor in Alzheimer disease.
text:
Objective: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, and amyloid beta (Aβ) response to the gamma-secretase inhibitor LY450139 in Alzheimer's disease.
Design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, dose-escalation, placebo-controlled trial.
Setting: Community-based clinical research centers.
Patients: Fifty-one individuals with mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease were randomized to receive placebo (n=15) or LY450139 (100 mg [n=22], 140 mg [n=14]), with 43 completing the treatment phase.
Intervention: The LY450139 groups received 60 mg/d for 2 weeks, then 100 mg/d for 6 weeks, and then either 100 or 140 mg/d for 6 additional weeks.
Main Outcome Measures: Primary outcome measures included adverse events, plasma and cerebrospinal fluid Aβ levels, vital signs, electrocardiographic data, and laboratory safety test results. Secondary outcome measures included the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale cognitive subscale and the Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study Activities of Daily Living Scale.
Results: Group differences were seen in skin and subcutaneous tissue concerns (P = 0.05), including 3 possible drug rashes and 3 reports of hair color change in the treatment groups. There were 3 adverse event-related discontinuations, including 1 transient bowel obstruction. The plasma Aβ(40) concentration was reduced by 58.2% for the 100-mg group and 64.6% for the 140-mg group (P < 0.001). No significant reduction was seen in cerebrospinal fluid Aβ levels. No group differences were seen in cognitive or functional measures.
Conclusions: LY450139 was generally well tolerated at doses of up to 140 mg/d for 14 weeks, with several findings indicating the need for close clinical monitoring in future studies. Decreases in plasma Aβ concentrations were consistent with inhibition of gamma-secretase. Trial Registration: clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT00244322.

title: Reduction in skin grafting after the introduction of hydrofiber dressings in partial thickness burns: a comparison between a hydrofiber and silver sulphadiazine.
text:
The purpose of this study was to compare the clinical outcomes of children with scald burns treated with a hydrofiber dressing (Aquacel®, Convatec Inc.) versus the conventional standard of care with silver sulfadiazine (Flammazine®; Solvay Pharmaceuticals), taking into account surgical interventions and length of stay (LOS).
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed all consecutive children aged zero to four years with primary scald burns up to 10% admitted to the Burn Centre of the Maasstad Hospital Rotterdam between January 1987 and January 2010. Data collection was done using a prospective computerized database. The study period was divided into two periods, representing the period before and after the introduction of the hydrofiber dressing (HFD), respectively 1987-1999 (period 1) and 1999-2010 (period 2).
RESULTS: During the entire study period, 27.3% of 502 patients treated with silver sulfadiazine (Ag-SD) underwent surgery, while before the introduction of HFD, 30.5% of 338 Ag-SD treated patients were operated upon. After the introduction of the HFD, 20.7% of 164 patients treated with Ag-SD eventually underwent skin grafting, which is a significant difference compared to the 11.6% of 302 patients whose wounds were dressed with HFD (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared to silver sulfadiazine treatment, a reduced number of surgical interventions were observed in mixed partial thickness scald burns up to 10% TBSA burned in children aged 0-4 years after the introduction of hydrofiber dressings. Additionally, the mode of treatment with this wound dressing limited hospital length of stay.

title: Induction of the heat-shock response by carbon dioxide in Chironomus thummi.
text: The effects of a range of stress treatments on gene expression in Chironomus thummi salivary gland cells have been investigated. Of the treatments evaluated, only the recovery from carbon dioxide exposure demonstrated a comparable response to the previously observed heat-shock treatment: the induction of heat-shock puffs and the synthesis of heat-shock polypeptides. In these conditions, puffing and transcription of telomeric regions were observed, leading to the appearance of the temperature-inducible telomeric Balbiani ring T-BR-III. In contrast, other treatments failed to induce the heat-shock response, despite causing real stress conditions in C. thummi larvae or salivary gland cells.

title: Candida albicans-Staphylococcus aureus polymicrobial peritonitis modulates host innate immunity.
text:
Despite advances in medical device fabrication and antimicrobial treatment therapies, fungal-bacterial polymicrobial peritonitis remains a significant complication for surgery patients, those on peritoneal dialysis, and critically ill individuals. Using a murine model of peritonitis, our research has demonstrated that infection with either Candida albicans or Staphylococcus aureus alone is non-fatal. However, coinfection with these pathogens leads to a 40% mortality rate and increased microbial burden in the spleen and kidney by day 1 post-infection.
Our findings have also shown that coinfection with fungal and bacterial pathogens leads to a unique subset of innate proinflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-6, granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, keratinocyte chemoattractant, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, and macrophage inflammatory protein-1α. These cytokines lead to increased inflammatory infiltration into the peritoneum and target organs. Treatment of coinfected mice with the cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibitor indomethacin reduces the infectious burden, proinflammatory cytokine production, and inflammatory infiltrate while simultaneously preventing mortality.
Our studies further revealed that during coinfection, the immunomodulatory eicosanoid prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) is synergistically increased compared to monomicrobial infection; indomethacin treatment also decreased elevated PGE2 levels. In addition, exogenous PGE2 added to the peritoneal cavity during infection override the protection provided by indomethacin and restore the increased mortality and microbial burden. These findings highlight the ability of fungal-bacterial coinfection to modulate innate inflammatory events with devastating consequences for the host.

title: Techniques and probes for the study of Xenopus tropicalis development.
text: The African clawed frog, Xenopus laevis, has provided valuable insights into developmental and cellular processes. However, its allotetraploid genome makes it challenging for forward genetic analysis. Fortunately, the related species Xenopus (Silurana) tropicalis has a diploid genome and a shorter generation time, making it an attractive alternative for genetic analysis. Here, we demonstrate that many tools developed for X. laevis can be applied to X. tropicalis, including developmental staging, in situ hybridization, immunohistochemistry, and morpholino oligonucleotides. We found that X. tropicalis embryos develop at a similar rate to X. laevis and can tolerate a similar temperature range. Additionally, many of the analytical reagents used for X. laevis can be effectively transferred to X. tropicalis, including whole-mount in situ hybridization protocols and antibodies against X. laevis proteins. This suggests that X. tropicalis offers a viable alternative for studying developmental and cellular processes, and its diploid genome makes it an attractive candidate for forward genetics and genomic analysis.

title: Requirement of c-myb in T cell development and in mature T cell function.
text: According to previous research, the protooncogene c-myb plays a crucial role in T cell development within the thymus and mature T cell proliferation. To further investigate this, we created two T cell-specific c-myb knockout mouse models, myb/LckCre and myb/CD4Cre. Through our experiments, we found that c-myb is essential for the development of thymocytes at the DN3 stage, the survival and proliferation of double-positive thymocytes, the differentiation of single-positive CD4 and CD8 T cells, and the proliferative responses of mature T cells. Additionally, our data suggest that c-myb plays a direct role in the formation of double-positive CD4+CD8+CD25+, CD4+CD25+, and CD8+CD25+ T cells, which may imply a role for c-myb in autoimmune dysfunction.

title: Effect of losartan on ambulatory short-term blood pressure variability and cardiovascular remodeling in hypertensive patients on hemodialysis.
text:
Prior studies have shown that increased ambulatory short-term blood pressure (BP) variability is linked to cardiovascular disease. In this investigation, we examined whether treatment with an angiotensin II type 1 receptor blocker, losartan, would improve ambulatory short-term BP variability in hypertensive patients undergoing hemodialysis.
METHODS:
We randomly assigned 40 hypertensive patients undergoing hemodialysis to either the losartan treatment group (n=20) or the control treatment group (n=20). We performed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring at baseline and 6 and 12 months after treatment, as well as echocardiography, baPWV measurements, and biochemical testing before and after treatment.
RESULTS: Compared to the control group, losartan significantly decreased nighttime short-term BP variability, assessed by the coefficient of variation of ambulatory BP, after 6 and 12 months of treatment. Additionally, losartan significantly reduced left ventricular mass index (LVMI), baPWV, and plasma levels of brain natriuretic peptide and advanced glycation end products (AGE). Multiple regression analysis also revealed significant correlations between changes in LVMI and changes in nighttime short-term BP variability, as well as between changes in LVMI and changes in plasma AGE levels.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that losartan may be beneficial in suppressing pathological cardiovascular remodeling by its inhibitory effect on ambulatory short-term BP variability during nighttime.

title: Interleukin-17 mRNA expression in blood and CSF mononuclear cells is augmented in multiple sclerosis.
text: Myelin-directed autoimmunity is believed to play a crucial role in the development of multiple sclerosis (MS). Studies have shown that both pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines are present in increased amounts in MS patients. Interleukin-17 (IL-17), a cytokine produced by activated memory T cells, has been recently identified in humans. This cytokine can induce the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines from parenchymal cells and macrophages. To detect and quantify IL-17 mRNA-expressing mononuclear cells (MNC) in blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from MS patients and control individuals, in situ hybridization with synthetic oligonucleotide probes was employed. Our findings revealed higher numbers of IL-17 mRNA-expressing MNC in blood and CSF from MS patients compared to healthy individuals. Specifically, there were higher numbers of IL-17 mRNA-expressing MNC in blood during clinical exacerbations compared to remission, and higher numbers in CSF compared to blood. These results suggest that IL-17 mRNA-expressing MNC are present in higher numbers in MS patients, particularly during clinical exacerbations, and that CSF contains higher numbers of these cells compared to blood.

title: A European perspective on population studies of dementia.
text: The shift in global demographics and the projected increase in age-related diseases, including dementia, pose a significant public health concern. Both the United States and Europe have dedicated significant research efforts to comprehending the pathogenesis and epidemiology of dementia. This article provides an overarching review of dementia research in Europe and compares it to the trajectory in the United States. The analysis highlights the shared challenges that researchers in both regions have identified and worked to address. To further advance knowledge gathering across the globe, there is a need for improved harmonization of methodology, as informed by current research practices.

title: The cost of providing comprehensive HIV treatment in PEPFAR-supported programs.
text:
Unprecedented investments from PEPFAR, national governments, and other stakeholders are being directed towards providing HIV treatment in developing countries. This study presents empirical data on the costs and cost trends of HIV treatment at a large sample of clinics in six countries.
Methods:
In 2006-2007, we conducted cost analyses at 43 PEPFAR-supported outpatient clinics in Botswana, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Uganda, and Vietnam. The study included all patients receiving HIV treatment and care at these sites (62,512 ART patients and 44,394 pre-ART patients). Data on HIV treatment costs were collected over consecutive 6-month periods, beginning with the scale-up of dedicated HIV treatment services at each site. Outcomes were calculated as costs per patient and total program costs, broken down by major cost categories.
Results:
The median annual economic costs for pre-ART patients were US$ 202 (in 2009 USD), while ART patients incurred US$ 880 in costs. Excluding antiretrovirals, per patient ART costs were US$ 298. The cost of caring for newly initiated ART patients was 15-20% higher than for established patients. Per patient costs decreased rapidly as sites matured, with a 46.8% drop in per patient ART costs between the first and second 6-month periods after the beginning of scale-up, and an additional 29.5% drop the following year. PEPFAR provided 79.4% of funding for service delivery, while national governments provided 15.2%.

Conclusion:
Treatment costs vary significantly between sites, with early costs dropping rapidly as sites mature. Treatment costs vary between countries and are affected by changes in antiretroviral regimen costs and the package of services. While cost reductions may allow for near-term program growth, programs must weigh the trade-off between improving services for current patients and expanding coverage to new ones.

title: A sperm cytoskeletal protein that signals oocyte meiotic maturation and ovulation.
text: Caenorhabditis elegans oocytes, like many other animals, undergo a temporary halt in meiosis during prophase. Sperm play a crucial role in resuming meiosis and contracting the muscular gonadal sheath cells, which are essential for ovulation. Our research has led us to discover that the major sperm cytoskeletal protein (MSP) acts as a bifurcated signal for both oocyte maturation and sheath contraction. In addition, MSP is also involved in sperm motility, comparable to the function of actin. Through evolution, MSP has acquired both extracellular signaling and intracellular cytoskeletal roles for the purpose of reproduction. Interestingly, proteins similar to MSP can be found in other organisms, including plants, fungi, and other animals, suggesting that related signaling mechanisms may exist in other phyla.

title: Unmet need for mental health care among U.S. children: variation by ethnicity and insurance status.
text:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to bridge the gap in policy discussions regarding mental health needs of children and adolescents by providing national estimates of unmet need for mental health services. While there is a general consensus on the lack of use of these services, few data are available at the national level. By using three nationally representative household surveys, we examine ethnic disparities in unmet need (defined as having a need for mental health evaluation but not using any services in a 1-year period) and provide estimates to inform policy and clinical programs.
METHOD: We conducted secondary data analyses in three nationally representative household surveys fielded in 1996-1998: the National Health Interview Survey, the National Survey of American Families, and the Community Tracking Survey. We determined the rates of mental health service use among children and adolescents aged 3-17 years and examined differences by ethnicity and insurance status. Among children defined as needing mental health services, we assessed the association of unmet need with ethnicity and insurance status.
RESULTS: Our findings reveal that only 2%-3% of children aged 3-5 years and 6%-9% of children and adolescents aged 6-17 years used mental health services in the past 12 months. Shockingly, nearly 80% of children and adolescents who were defined as needing mental health services did not receive any care. Controlling for other factors, we found that rates of unmet need were significantly higher among Latino than white children and among uninsured than publicly insured children.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the disparities in access to mental health services among different populations. Specifically, Latino and uninsured children have higher rates of unmet need than other children. Moreover, the low rates of service use among preschool children suggest that there is a need for more targeted interventions to address mental health needs in this age group. By understanding the reasons for these disparities, policy and clinical programs can be informed to address the mental health needs of children and adolescents more effectively.

title: Conditional economic incentives for reducing HIV risk behaviors: integration of psychology and behavioral economics.
text:
Objective: This article reviews psychology and behavioral economic approaches to HIV prevention, and examines the integration and application of these approaches in conditional economic incentive (CEI) programs for reducing HIV risk behavior.
Methods: We discuss the history of HIV prevention approaches, highlighting the important insights and limitations of psychological theories. We provide an overview of the theoretical tenets of behavioral economics that are relevant to HIV prevention, and utilize CEIs as an illustrative example of how traditional psychological theories and behavioral economics can be combined into new approaches for HIV prevention.
Results: Behavioral economic interventions can complement psychological frameworks for reducing HIV risk by introducing unique theoretical understandings about the conditions under which risky decisions are amenable to intervention. Findings from illustrative CEI programs show mixed but generally promising effects of economic interventions on HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) prevalence, HIV testing, HIV medication adherence, and drug use.
Conclusion: CEI programs can complement psychological interventions for HIV prevention and behavioral risk reduction. To maximize program effectiveness, CEI programs must be designed according to contextual and population-specific factors that may determine intervention applicability and success.

title: ALDH1 is a marker of normal and malignant human mammary stem cells and a predictor of poor clinical outcome.
text: Using in vitro and in vivo experimental systems, our research has shown that stem cells and progenitor cells in breast tissue can be identified and isolated based on their aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) activity. In particular, we found that normal human mammary epithelial cells with high ALDH activity have the greatest potential for growth and differentiation, and can form tumors that resemble the original tumor in a xenotransplant model. In breast carcinomas, high ALDH activity is a marker of tumorigenic cells that can self-renew and give rise to tumors that mirror the original cancer's heterogeneity. Using this new marker, we found that expression of ALDH1 in immunostaining correlated with poor prognosis in a series of 577 breast carcinomas. These findings provide a valuable tool for studying normal and malignant breast stem cells and may lead to new clinical applications based on stem cell biology.

title: Interleukin-6 and interleukin-8 levels in serum and synovial fluid of patients with osteoarthritis.
text: The concentration of interleukin (IL)-6 and IL-8 in serum and synovial fluid samples obtained from patients with osteoarthritis (OA) of the knee were measured using the chemiluminescence-ELISA (CL-ELISA) method, which has a sensitivity 100-1,000 times greater than the conventional ELISA method. The results were compared with those from patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and healthy controls. The mean IL-6 and IL-8 levels in synovial fluid were higher in RA than in OA. In contrast, the IL-6 and IL-8 levels in serum were significantly higher in both RA and OA compared to controls. Interestingly, among OA patients who experienced remarkable improvement in hydrarthrosis, the synovial fluid IL-6 and IL-8 levels at the initial examination were higher, and decreased significantly after treatment with sodium hyaluronate (NaHA). Conversely, among those who did not show improvement in hydrarthrosis, the synovial fluid IL-6 and IL-8 levels at the initial examination were lower, and hydrarthrosis was not significantly improved even after treatment with NaHA. Additionally, there was a tendency for the synovial fluid IL-6 and IL-8 levels to decrease as the levels of hyaluronic acid (HA) increased. Evaluation of X-ray findings also revealed that the IL-6 levels in synovial fluid were significantly higher in low-grade cases than in high-grade cases. In low-grade cases, as determined by X-ray findings, there was a significant decrease in IL-6 levels in synovial fluid after treatment with NaHA.

title: Inhibition of SRC expression and activity inhibits tumor progression and metastasis of human pancreatic adenocarcinoma cells in an orthotopic nude mouse model.
text: The non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase Src is overexpressed in approximately 70% of pancreatic adenocarcinomas. In this study, we investigated the effect of reducing Src expression on the growth, metastasis, and incidence of pancreatic tumors in an orthotopic model. We achieved this by stably expressing a plasmid encoding small interfering RNA (siRNA) targeting c-Src in L3.6pl human pancreatic tumor cells. Reducing Src expression resulted in a >80% decrease in its expression, without affecting the expression of related kinases c-Yes and c-Lyn, or proliferation rates. Additionally, we observed decreased phosphorylation of Akt and p44/42 Erk mitogen-activated protein kinase, as well as reduced production of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and interleukin-8 (IL-8) in culture supernatants. However, when we implanted varying cell numbers of these siRNA-expressing cells into nude mice, tumor incidence was unchanged. Nonetheless, in the siRNA clones, large tumors failed to develop, and the incidence of metastasis was significantly decreased, suggesting that Src activity plays a critical role in pancreatic tumor progression. To further investigate this, we treated animals bearing established wild-type tumors with the Src/Abl-selective inhibitor BMS-354825 (dasatinib). This resulted in decreased tumor size and incidence of metastases in treated mice compared to controls. These findings demonstrate that Src activation contributes to pancreatic tumor progression in this model, making it a potential target for therapy.

title: Eicosapentaenoic acid is converted via ω-3 epoxygenation to the anti-inflammatory metabolite 12-hydroxy-17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid.
text: Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) has beneficial effects in various inflammatory conditions. In this study, dietary EPA was converted into 17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid (17,18-EpETE) through ω-3 epoxygenation in the mouse peritoneal cavity. Lipidomics analysis revealed a series of novel oxygenated metabolites of 17,18-EpETE, and one of the major metabolites, 12-hydroxy-17,18-epoxyeicosatetraenoic acid (12-OH-17,18-EpETE), displayed a potent anti-inflammatory action by limiting neutrophil infiltration in murine zymosan-induced peritonitis. 12-OH-17,18-EpETE inhibited leukotriene B4-induced neutrophil chemotaxis and polarization in vitro in a low nanomolar range (EC50 0.6 nM). The structural elucidation of two natural isomers, 12S-OH-17R,18S-EpETE and 12S-OH-17S,18R-EpETE, revealed that these natural isomers displayed potent anti-inflammatory action, whereas unnatural stereoisomers were inactive. These results suggest that 17,18-EpETE derived from dietary EPA is converted into a potent bioactive metabolite, 12-OH-17,18-EpETE, which may constitute an endogenous anti-inflammatory metabolic pathway.

title: Scrapie in mice. Agent-strain differences in the distribution and intensity of grey matter vacuolation.
text: Five strains of the scrapie agent were administered as intracerebral inocula to two inbred mouse strains, C57BL and VM, as well as their F1 cross. The histological parameters of vacuolation in specific regions of the brain were found to be distinct for each agent, allowing for accurate identification of the agent solely based on these parameters. However, the dose of the agent did not affect the lesion profile. The genotype of the mouse had a significant impact on the degree of vacuolation and the shape of the lesion profile, with some agents causing more pronounced effects than others. In certain areas of the brain, the F1 cross between C57BL and VM mice exhibited either more or less vacuolation than either parental genotype, depending on the strain of agent used. The complexity of the genetic control of the lesion profile precluded further analysis of these data.

title: Cyclin A2 is an RNA binding protein that controls Mre11 mRNA translation
text: Cyclin A2 functions as a critical regulator of DNA replication, organization, and integrity. Through its ability to activate cyclin-dependent kinases Cdk1 and Cdk2, cyclin A2 is expressed at elevated levels from the S phase until early mitosis. Our research has shown that mutant mice lacking cyclin A2 are predisposed to chromosomal instability and prone to develop tumors. This irregularity can be attributed to a failure to up-regulate the meiotic recombination 11 (Mre11) nuclease in S phase, resulting in impaired resolution of stalled replication forks, inadequate repair of double-stranded DNA breaks, and improper segregation of sister chromosomes. Interestingly, cyclin A2 also plays an unexpected role in regulating Mre11 abundance through its C-terminal RNA binding domain, which selectively and directly binds Mre11 transcripts to mediate polysome loading and translation. These findings reveal cyclin A2 as a mechanistically diverse regulatory protein that combines multifaceted kinase-dependent functions with a kinase-independent, RNA binding–dependent role aimed at ensuring the necessary repair of common replication errors.

title: Cluster sampling to assess immunization coverage: a review of experience with a simplified sampling method.
text: The Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) utilizes a simplified cluster sampling method, involving the random selection of 210 children in 30 clusters of 7 children each, to estimate immunization coverage levels. This study evaluates the efficacy of this method in both actual and simulated surveys. Analysis of 60 actual surveys conducted in 25 countries yielded 446 sample estimates of immunization coverage. Findings reveal that 83% of the sample results had 95% confidence limits within + or - 10%, and none exceeded + or - 13%. Moreover, 12 hypothetical population strata with immunization coverage rates ranging from 10%-99% were established for computer simulation, and 10 hypothetical communities were allocated varying proportions of each stratum. The results of these simulated surveys supported the validity of the EPI method, with over 95% of the results being within + or - 10% of the actual population mean. The precision of this method, as estimated from both actual and simulated surveys, is deemed satisfactory for the requirements of the EPI. Among actual surveys, the proportion of results with confidence limits exceeding + or - 10% was highest (50%) when immunization coverage was 45%-54%.

title: Gender differences in the utilization of health care services.
text:
Previous studies have demonstrated that women utilize healthcare services at a higher rate than men. To investigate these differences, we conducted a study where 509 new adult patients were randomly assigned to primary care physicians at a university medical center. Over the course of one year, we monitored the patients' use of healthcare services and associated costs. We collected self-reported health status data using the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form-36 (SF-36) and controlled for important independent variables such as patient sociodemographics and health status in our statistical analyses.
Our findings revealed that women had significantly lower self-reported health status and lower levels of education and income compared to men. Women also had a higher mean number of visits to their primary care clinic and diagnostic services compared to men. Further, women had significantly higher mean charges for primary care, specialty care, emergency treatment, diagnostic services, and annual total charges compared to men, with no differences in hospitalization charges. After controlling for health status, sociodemographics, and clinic assignment, women continued to have higher medical charges for all categories of charges except hospitalizations.
These findings have important implications for healthcare, suggesting that women may be utilizing healthcare services at a higher rate than men due to differences in health status or other factors. While the appropriateness of these differences was not determined in this study, our results highlight the need for further investigation into gender differences in healthcare utilization and costs.

title: Recombinant human tumor necrosis factor administered as a 24-hour intravenous infusion. A phase I and pharmacologic study.
text: Recombinant human tumor necrosis factor (rH-TNF) is a cytokine exhibiting direct antitumor properties. In a phase I trial, we infused rH-TNF continuously for 24 hours in 115 courses administered to 50 patients, with doses ranging from 4.5 to 645 micrograms/m2. Increasing doses led to escalating systemic toxicities such as fever, chills, fatigue, and hypotension. Doses above 454 micrograms/m2 frequently caused severe lethargy and fatigue, precluding hospital discharge by the conclusion of therapy. The dose-limiting toxicity was hypotension, necessitating dopamine treatment in five patients. Organ-specific toxicities were mild and resolved spontaneously within 48 hours. The 24-hour infusions of rH-TNF also showed significant reductions in serum cholesterol and high-density lipoprotein levels. Using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, peak plasma rH-TNF levels were measured at 90-900 pg/mL, without reaching a steady-state level. Based on these findings, the recommended phase II dose for rH-TNF as a 24-hour continuous infusion is 545 micrograms/m2.

title: Detection and comparison of epidermal growth factor receptor mutations in cells and fluid of malignant pleural effusion in non-small cell lung cancer.
text: Cells or cell-free fluid from malignant pleural effusions may serve as valuable clinical samples for testing EGFR mutations in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. While their utility in mutation detection has not been extensively evaluated, our study demonstrated their potential in 26 East Asian NSCLC patients. We collected both the cells and cell-free fluid from these patients and used sequencing and mutant-enriched PCR to determine the EGFR mutation status. Our findings showed that both the cells and cell-free fluid may be reliable sources for EGFR mutation detection in unresectable NSCLC, thanks to the sensitive genotyping assays employed. Noteworthy, direct sequencing may fail to detect a significant proportion of mutations in these heterogeneous samples. Alternative methods, such as mutant-enriched PCR and gene scan, can provide more accurate mutational information.

title: Materials and Methods Figs. S1 to S15 References Supporting Online Materials
text: Endosomal Toll-like receptors (TLRs) 7 and 9 detect viral pathogens and set off signals that lead to the activation of nuclear factor κB (NF-κB)-dependent proinflammatory cytokines and interferon regulatory factor 7 (IRF7)-dependent type I interferons (IFNs). Recognition of viral nucleic acids by TLR9 requires processing in the endolysosomal compartment. We show that TLR9 signals leading to the activation of type I IFN, but not proinflammatory cytokine genes, depend on TLR9 trafficking from endosomes to a specialized lysosome-related organelle. Additionally, we identify adapter protein-3 as the protein complex responsible for the trafficking of TLR9 to this subcellular compartment. Our findings reveal a unique mechanism for segregating TLR9 signals within the endosomal system, leading to a bifurcation of signaling outcomes.

title: Sedimentation velocity method in the analytical ultracentrifuge for the study of protein-protein interactions.
text: Sedimentation analysis in the analytical ultracentrifuge can be utilized to detect macromolecular interactions by measuring the changes in the sedimentation behavior of a complex formed by the interaction of two molecules. When two molecules interact, the mass of the resulting complex is increased, which is reflected in the sedimentation behavior. In this chapter, we discuss how this phenomenon can be used to determine quantitative parameters of an interaction. As an example, we analyze the interaction between a single-stranded DNA binding protein and a subunit of DNA polymerase III holoenzyme, providing a thorough treatment of the relevant theory and a description of evaluation algorithms.

title: Structural trends in the aging femoral neck and proximal shaft: analysis of the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry data.
text: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans of US adults aged 20-99 years from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III) were analyzed using a structural analysis program to measure bone mineral density (BMD), cross-sectional areas (CSAs), cross-sectional moments of inertia (CSMI), section moduli, subperiosteal widths, and estimated mean cortical thickness in the proximal femur. The analysis was performed on a non-Hispanic white subgroup of 2,719 men and 2,904 women, examining the cortical region 2 cm distal to the lesser trochanter and a mixed cortical/trabecular region across the narrowest point of the femoral neck. Age-related trends in BMD and section modulus were studied for both regions by sex after adjusting for body weight. The results showed that while BMD declined with age in both regions, the section modulus remained nearly constant until the fifth decade in females and then declined at a slower rate than BMD. In males, the pattern was different, with the narrow neck section modulus declining modestly until the fifth decade and then remaining nearly constant, while the shaft section modulus was static until the fifth decade and then increased steadily. These findings suggest that aging does not necessarily lead to reduced mechanical strength in the hip, as the section modulus in the elderly is on average within 14% of young values in females and within 6% in males. Additionally, the results indicate that a linear expansion in subperiosteal diameter in both sexes and in both regions may mechanically offset net loss of medullary bone mass, leading to the observed discordance between BMD and section modulus.

title: Turning blood into brain: cells bearing neuronal antigens generated in vivo from bone marrow.
text: Adult bone marrow stem cells have the capacity to differentiate into various hematopoietic lineages, constantly replenishing the bloodstream throughout adulthood. Our research reveals that when transplanted into a mouse strain incapable of developing myeloid and lymphoid cells, bone marrow cells migrated to the brain and transformed into cells expressing neuron-specific antigens. These findings suggest that bone marrow-derived cells may serve as a potential alternative source of neurons for patients with neurodegenerative diseases or central nervous system injuries.

title: A negative staining method for high resolution electron microscopy of viruses.
text: A novel approach has been established for the visualization of virus particles using electron microscopy. By mixing virus preparations with 1% phosphotungstic acid adjusted to pH 7.5 and spraying directly onto electron microscope supporting films made from evaporated carbon, high contrast with excellent preservation is achieved. This technique has been successfully applied to study the external form and structure of tobacco mosaic virus and turnip yellow mosaic virus, revealing structural details resolved through X-ray diffraction methods.

title: Nef induces multiple genes involved in cholesterol synthesis and uptake in human immunodeficiency virus type 1-infected T cells.
text: Several recent studies have suggested that cholesterol may play a crucial role in human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) replication. To investigate this further, we employed microarray analysis to examine the effects of HIV-1 infection on cholesterol biosynthesis and uptake. Our findings revealed that HIV-1 significantly increased the expression of cholesterol genes in both transformed T-cell lines and primary CD4(+) T cells. Corroborating these microarray results, (14)C-labeled mevalonate and acetate incorporation were found to be elevated in HIV-1-infected cells. Additionally, our data indicates that changes in cholesterol biosynthesis and uptake are solely observed in the presence of functional Nef, implying that increased cholesterol synthesis may contribute to Nef-mediated enhancement of virion infectivity and viral replication.

title: Long noncoding RNA as modular scaffold of histone modification complexes
text: LincRNAs, or long intergenic noncoding RNAs, play a pivotal role in regulating chromatin states and epigenetic inheritance. Our study reveals that the lincRNA HOTAIR functions as a scaffold for at least two distinct histone modification complexes. Specifically, the 5' region of HOTAIR binds to polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), while the 3' region interacts with the LSD1/CoREST/REST complex. This ability to tether multiple complexes allows RNA-mediated assembly of PRC2 and LSD1, resulting in coupled histone H3 lysine 27 methylation and lysine 4 demethylation on target genes. Our findings suggest that lincRNAs may serve as scaffolds, providing binding surfaces for enzymes involved in histone modification, thus determining the specific pattern of modifications on target genes.

title: Therapeutic Clearance of Amyloid by Antibodies to Serum Amyloid P Component.
text:
Here is a possible revision of the given text:
BACKGROUND: Amyloid fibril deposits causing systemic amyloidosis consistently contain the non-fibrillar plasma protein, serum amyloid P component (SAP). The drug (R)-1-[6-[(R)-2-carboxy-pyrrolidin-1-yl]-6-oxo-hexanoyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (CPHPC) effectively reduces SAP levels in plasma while leaving some SAP in amyloid deposits, which can be specifically targeted by therapeutic IgG anti-SAP antibodies. In mouse models of amyloid A type amyloidosis, these antibodies bind to residual SAP in amyloid deposits, triggering complement activation and rapid clearance of amyloid by macrophage-derived multinucleated giant cells.
METHODS: We conducted an open-label, single-dose-escalation, phase 1 trial involving 15 patients with systemic amyloidosis. To begin, we depleted circulating SAP using CPHPC, and then infused a fully humanized monoclonal IgG1 anti-SAP antibody. Patients with cardiac involvement were excluded due to safety concerns. We monitored organ function, inflammatory markers, and amyloid load over time.
RESULTS: There were no serious adverse events observed. Some patients who received larger doses of antibody experienced infusion reactions, which were reduced by slowing the infusion rate for later patients. At 6 weeks, patients who received an adequate dose of antibody based on their amyloid load exhibited decreased liver stiffness, as measured using transient elastography, along with improvements in liver function and a substantial reduction in hepatic amyloid load, as demonstrated by SAP scintigraphy and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Additionally, there was a reduction in kidney amyloid load and shrinkage of an amyloid-laden lymph node observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with CPHPC followed by an anti-SAP antibody safely triggers the clearance of amyloid deposits from liver and other tissues. (Funded by GlaxoSmithKline; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT01777243.)

title: LPA Gene, Ethnicity, and Cardiovascular Events
text:
Introduction:
The relationship between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the lipoprotein(a) (LPA) gene, apolipoprotein(a) isoforms, and the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in different ethnic groups is not well understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the interdependent relationships and prospective association of these biomarkers with MACE in a large, diverse population.
Methods:
We measured LPA SNPs, apolipoprotein(a) isoforms, Lp(a), and oxidized phospholipids on apolipoprotein B-100 (OxPL-apoB) levels in 1792 black, 1030 white, and 597 Hispanic subjects enrolled in the Dallas Heart Study. The correlations among these biomarkers and the ethnic-specific prevalence of LPA SNPs were determined. Cox regression analysis with multivariable adjustment was performed to evaluate the prospective association of quartiles of Lp(a) and OxPL-apoB with MACE after a median follow-up of 9.5 years.
Results:
The most prevalent LPA SNPs were rs3798220 in Hispanics (42.38%), rs10455872 in whites (14.27%), and rs9457951 in blacks (32.92%). The correlation of each of these SNPs with the major apolipoprotein(a) isoform size was highly variable and in different directions among ethnic groups. In the entire cohort, quartiles of Lp(a) and OxPL-apoB were associated with hazard ratios (95% confidence interval) for time to MACE of 2.35 (1.50–3.69, P<0.001) and 1.89 (1.26–2.84, P=0.003), respectively, versus quartile 1. Addition of the major apolipoprotein(a) isoform and the 3 LPA SNPs to these models attenuated the risk, but significance was maintained for both Lp(a) and OxPL-apoB. Evaluating time to MACE in specific ethnic groups, Lp(a) was a positive predictor, and the size of the major apolipoprotein(a) isoform was an inverse predictor in blacks, an inverse predictor in whites, and a positive predictor in Hispanics.
Discussion:
The findings of this study suggest that the prevalence and association of LPA SNPs with size of apolipoprotein(a) isoforms, Lp(a), and OxPL-apoB levels are highly variable and ethnicity-specific. Despite significant ethnic differences in LPA genetic markers, elevated plasma Lp(a) or OxPL-apoB levels were found to be associated with an increased risk of MACE. These results highlight the importance of considering ethnicity-specific genetic and phenotypic markers in the assessment of cardiovascular disease risk.
Conclusion:
In conclusion, this study provides new insights into the complex interplay between genetic and phenotypic markers of lipid metabolism and cardiovascular disease risk in different ethnic groups. The findings underscore the importance of considering ethnicity-specific factors when evaluating cardiovascular disease risk and highlight the need for further investigations into the mechanisms underlying these observations.

title: Protein kinase CK2 modulates developmental functions of the abscisic acid responsive protein Rab17 from maize.
text: Rab17, a highly phosphorylated late embryogenesis abundant protein, is crucial for plant responses to stress. Our study provides evidence of the significance of Rab17 phosphorylation by protein kinase CK2 in cellular processes during stress. We have discovered the interaction between Rab17 and the CK2 regulatory subunits, CK2 beta-1 and beta-3, and found that this interaction is independent of Rab17's phosphorylation state. Live-cell fluorescence imaging of CK2 and Rab17 indicates that the internal dynamics of Rab17 are regulated by CK2 phosphorylation. We observed the distribution of both CK2 beta subunits and Rab17 throughout the cytoplasm and nucleus, whereas catalytic CK2 alpha subunits and a Rab17 mutant protein (mRab17) that is not a substrate for CK2 phosphorylation remained concentrated in the nucleoli. A dual-color image revealed that the CK2 holoenzyme predominantly resides in the nucleus. Our findings suggest that Rab17 phosphorylation plays a critical role in vivo. Overexpressing Rab17, but not mRab17, inhibited seed germination under osmotic stress conditions, highlighting Rab17's essential function in growth processes. Therefore, Rab17's phosphorylation by CK2 regulates its role in plant growth.

title: Reduced plasma concentrations of nitrogen oxide in individuals with essential hypertension.
text: Patients with essential hypertension exhibit diminished responses to endothelium-dependent vasodilation, which is largely attributed to lower nitric oxide (NO) bioactivity. To investigate this further, we measured the end-product of NO metabolism, nitrate plus nitrite (total nitrogen oxide), in plasma samples from these patients. Our results showed that the combined plasma concentration of nitrate plus nitrite was significantly lower in individuals with essential hypertension compared to healthy controls (15.7±1.1 mmol/L versus 22.8±1.4 mmol/L, P<0.001).Remarkably, individuals with borderline hypertension had plasma nitrogen oxide concentrations that were intermediate between the other two groups (18.2±1.2 mmol/L, P<0.001). Furthermore, we found significant inverse correlations between plasma nitrogen oxide levels and both systolic and diastolic blood pressures. Interestingly, we also observed that the basal concentration of nitrogen oxide in the plasma was reduced, at least in the peripheral circulation, in individuals with essential hypertension.

title: Isolation of superoxide dismutase mutants in Escherichia coli: is superoxide dismutase necessary for aerobic life?
text: Transposons bearing the chloramphenicol resistance marker were inserted into the cloned genes for manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD) and iron superoxide dismutase (FeSOD) in Escherichia coli, generating mutations and gene fusions. The mutated MnSOD or FeSOD genes were introduced into the bacterial chromosome through allelic exchange. The resulting mutants were found to lack the respective enzymatic activity as determined by activity measurements and immunoblot analysis. Under aerobic conditions in rich medium, the absence of FeSOD or MnSOD had minimal impact on growth or sensitivity to the superoxide generator, paraquat. In minimal medium, aerobic growth was not affected, but sensitivity to paraquat was increased, particularly in the sodA mutant. A double mutant entirely devoid of SOD was also obtained, which could not grow aerobically in rich medium, but its catalase level remained unchanged, and it exhibited high sensitivity to paraquat and hydrogen peroxide. The double mutant showed complete dependence on oxygen for growth restoration, and supplementation with an SOD-overproducing plasmid or addition of the 20 amino acids necessary for SOD production could restore growth. It is concluded that the complete absence of SOD in E. coli creates a conditional sensitivity to oxygen.

title: Late presentation of HIV-infected individuals.
text: Despite significant improvements in HIV prognosis due to antiretroviral therapy (ART), late presentation to HIV care remains a major challenge.
