title: Levels of selection in evolution
text: Since the groundbreaking work of George Williams, W. D. Hamilton, and Richard Dawkins, evolutionary biologists have recognized that natural selection typically operates at the level of individual organisms, cells, or genes, rather than for the benefit of the larger group. This presents a significant challenge in understanding why cooperation exists among different levels of biological organization. To address this question, twelve leading scientists from various disciplines within evolutionary biology have contributed to this volume, providing a comprehensive overview of the current state of theoretical and empirical research. Recent studies have revealed that various mechanisms have evolved to prevent conflicts between different levels of selection, such as mechanisms that promote cooperation at the individual level or between cells. The aim of editor Laurent Keller is to bring together experts from different fields to explore these mechanisms and how they are resolved, in order to gain a deeper understanding of the evolution of life. The book's multi-author approach provides a unique synergy, as each chapter is guided by a rigorous theoretical framework. The contributors, including the editor and notable figures such as H. Charles J. Godfray, Edward Allen Herre, and John Maynard Smith, offer a breadth of perspectives and insights that bridge the gap between molecular and organismal biology.

title: A psychometric evaluation of the Beck Depression Inventory–II.
text: The present study investigates the psychometric properties of the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II; A.T. Beck, R.A. Steer, & G.K. Brown, 1996) across various aspects, including internal consistency, factorial validity, and gender differences. Both versions of the inventory demonstrated high internal reliability within the overall student sample. However, there were significant differences in the mean BDI and BDI-II scores, leading to the establishment of new cutoffs for analogous research on the BDI-II. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis revealed that a 2-factor solution best represented the data for both inventories, accounting for approximately 41% and 46% of the common variance in BDI and BDI-II responses, respectively. These factor solutions were consistently validated across gender, with the BDI-II emerging as a stronger instrument in terms of its factor structure.

title: Why people feel crowded: An examination of objective and subjective crowding
text: Previous research has found only a moderate association between objective and subjective crowding, contradicting common sense notions of why people perceive they are crowded. To investigate this phenomenon, we leveraged data from a representative sample of Bangkok, Thailand, where household crowding is four times higher than in Western societies. We explored several possible explanations for this discrepancy by analyzing seven different indicators of objective crowding. Our findings revealed that the modest relationship between objective and subjective crowding is not a measurement artifact. In contrast to prior studies, our results suggest that the objective-subjective crowding relationship is nonlinear, with a ceiling effect muffling the impact of increased objective crowding. Moreover, we found that part of the subjective feeling of crowding can be attributed to household circumstances, such as the degree of control an individual has over household space.

title: Self-Report and Tests of Memory Aging
text: Despite a lack of correlation between memory complaints and traditional memory tests, self-report questions that assess everyday memory processes were found to be strongly correlated with objective measures of memory performance. In a study of 60 volunteers aged 21-84 years, the participants' ratings of their own memory competence were categorized into four memory processes and compared to scores from six tests of verbal, face, story, and nonverbal auditory, visual, and tactile memory. The results showed that both sets of measurements were highly correlated (r = 0.67), and both declined with age in parallel. Interestingly, the older participants tended to be more accurate in their ratings than the younger ones, but this difference was not observed across all tests. Additionally, the study found that expectations of poor performance can influence some test results, suggesting that self-report measures may be influenced by psychological factors.

title: Code of the Street: Decency, Violence, and the Moral Life of the Inner City
text:
Inner-city black America is commonly characterized by senseless street violence, yet this violence is not entirely random. Instead, it is governed by an informal code of the street that is widely understood and strictly adhered to. The code is a coping mechanism developed in response to the lack of well-paying jobs, racial stigma, drug abuse, feelings of alienation, and hopelessness.
Young people are particularly vulnerable to the consequences of not adhering to the code, which can have life-or-death repercussions. The code is maintained through a combination of physical and psychological control, as well as an implied threat of violence. It dictates how one dresses, speaks, makes eye contact, and understands the social hierarchy.
The lack of police control and the primacy of public opinion further reinforce the code, making it challenging for individuals to escape its grip. In this environment, the safety and self-worth of individuals are determined by their ability to command respect in public. Decent families are the strongest counterforce to the code, but the culture of the street often prevails, ensnaring those with better aspirations in its web of morally corrosive behaviors.
Overall, the code of the street is a complex and self-perpetuating cycle that hinders the potential of inner-city black America. It is crucial to comprehend the intricacies of this code to develop effective strategies for breaking its hold and fostering positive change.

title: A generic measure of relationship satisfaction.
text: The need for concise and reliable measures of relationship satisfaction in today's diverse society has prompted the development of the Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS). This article details the creation and validation of this measure. Study I involved 125 individuals who identified themselves as "in love" and showed unifactorial structure, substantial item loadings, and moderate intercorrelations. The RAS correlated with measurements of love, sexual attitudes, self-disclosure, commitment, and investment in a relationship. In Study II, the RAS was administered to 57 couples in committed relationships, yielding a single factor, high alpha reliability (0.86), and significant correlations with relevant relationship variables. The RAS demonstrated strong correlations (0.80) with a longer criterion measure, the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (Spanier, 1976), and effectively distinguished between couples who remained together and those who broke up (with a subsample). The RAS is a brief, psychometrically sound, and generic measure of relationship satisfaction.

title: ECONOMIC RESTRUCTURING AND SUBURBANIZATION IN CHINA
text: In other countries, suburbanization has typically followed a period of sustained industrial and population growth in cities. This study focuses on suburbanization in Beijing, Shanghai, Shenyang, and Dalian. Due to economic restructuring, the urban core experienced net population loss from 1982 to 1990 as a result of decentralization, while the inner suburbs gained population. Marketization of urban land, shift of industrial land to tertiary use, improved transportation, availability of foreign and domestic capital, housing rehabilitation in the city, and new housing construction in the suburbs were among the factors driving suburbanization in China. While there are some similarities between suburbanization in China and the United States, there are also notable differences. Unlike the current metropolitan landscape in the United States, where suburban growth has given rise to a polycentric spatial structure, suburbanization in China is still in its early stages of development, with suburbs dominated by centralized commercial and industrial areas.

title: The Assumption of Caregiving: Grandmothers Raising the Children of the Crack Cocaine Epidemic:
text: In this study, the experiences of 71 African American women who have taken on the role of sole caregiver for their grandchildren or great-grandchildren due to their parents' involvement in crack cocaine use were explored. Through in-depth interviews and participant observation, three patterns of caregiving emerged: sudden assumption, negotiated assumption, and inevitable assumption of the permanent caregiver role. Each pattern was characterized by six dimensions: forewarning, initiation, the trigger event, the caregiver's goals, their assumed trajectory of caregiving, and their perceived influence on their own destiny. These findings offer critical insights for professionals working with women, children, and families, as well as a deeper understanding of the far-reaching consequences of the crack cocaine epidemic.

title: The effect of information related to fat content and taste on consumer responses to a reduced-fat frankfurter and a reduced-fat chocolate bar
text: In a study examining the impact of product information on consumer responses to frankfurters and chocolate bars, researchers compared sensory and hedonic ratings in two conditions: blind tasting and tasting with information present. They also investigated the effect of information alone by asking subjects to rate the expected sensory and hedonic intensities of the products based on packages with different claims. Three groups of subjects were tested, each provided with different information: a basic group with no added claims (n = 31), a reduced-fat group with products claimed to have reduced-fat content (n = 29), and a flavorful group with products claimed to have full meat/chocolate flavor (n = 31). The results showed that product information significantly increased the rated pleasantness of the frankfurter in all three information groups compared to blind ratings. However, the effect of information was not observed for chocolate bars. Additionally, the reduced-fat group rated the expected attribute intensities of the frankfurters and chocolates lower than the other groups. The study found that product information had a greater impact on ratings of sensory attributes than on pleasantness ratings.

title: Transnationalism and identity
text: The concepts of transnationalism and identity are inherently intertwined, as many individuals' transnational networks of connection and engagement are rooted in a shared perception of common identity. Conversely, the identities of numerous individuals and groups are shaped within social contexts that span multiple locations. In this initial article, we explore the transnational perspective on migration studies, followed by critiques and unresolved queries. Finally, we summarize the main arguments presented by the contributing authors of this themed issue of JEMS, particularly with regard to the diverse ways in which transnational settings and dynamics shape the construction, negotiation, and reproduction of identities.

title: Social Isolation and Social Support: An Applied Perspective
text: Numerous empirical studies have demonstrated the crucial role of social networks and support in maintaining the health and well-being of older adults. However, more research is needed to develop effective interventions that can positively impact an individual's social network. In this article, the authors examine social support and isolation from an applied perspective, drawing on presentations originally given at a National Institute on Aging-sponsored symposium on applied gerontology in 1992. They offer general observations on the field of applied social relations in later life, discuss the mental health implications of these relations, outline fundamental principles and existing technologies in this field, describe the use of a screening instrument for social isolation developed by one of the authors (Lubben), and explore various domains of knowledge related to elder social relations. Finally, the authors highlight areas where more research is needed to improve interventions aimed at enhancing social connections and overall well-being among older adults.

title: Wine and health: faraway concepts?
text:
The following is a rewritten version of the given text:
Objective: This study aims to investigate the relationship between consumers' perceptions and beliefs regarding the health benefits of wine and their consumption patterns.
Methods: To gather data, we conducted in-store face-to-face surveys among 402 wine consumers. Using two-step cluster analysis, we identified four groups based on their responses. ANOVA was used to confirm the differences among the groups. Additionally, we conducted a multivariate binary logistic regression to assess the influence of wine consumption on healthiness perceptions.
Results: Our findings reveal that consumers can be categorized into four groups: two health-oriented groups - optimistic and medical - and two non-health-oriented groups - unintentional drinker and unconvinced. Notably, these groups do not differ significantly in terms of socio-economic factors. Wine consumption behavior has a significant impact on health orientation, with monthly and wine drinkers showing a stronger preference for health-enhancing wine compared to weekly and other alcohol drinkers. Health-oriented consumers are more likely to welcome and pay more for wine with perceived health benefits. Furthermore, consumers believe that wine can positively impact their health, with 70% of the sample reporting that they believe wine has health benefits.
In summary, this study demonstrates that consumer perceptions and beliefs regarding the health benefits of wine have a significant impact on their consumption patterns, with health-oriented consumers more likely to prioritize wine with perceived health benefits.

title: The Changing Problem of Overcrowded Housing
text: Overcrowding in the United States has experienced a significant increase after decades of decline, with some areas and ethnic groups being affected more severely than others. The nature and definition of the problem for policy purposes are evolving, and ethnicity, age, immigration, and poverty play a crucial role in the resurgence of crowding. However, housing market conditions appear to be less important. The planning standards used to measure overcrowding are relative and have changed over time, and social norms vary among ethnic groups. The issue of overcrowding highlights the challenges of implementing uniform standards in a diverse, multiethnic society. Providing more "place diversity" in the setting of standards could help target the worst-case housing needs more effectively in highly impacted areas.

title: Best response dynamics and socially stable strategies
text:
An evolutionarily stable strategy (ESS), as first introduced by Maynard Smith and Price in Nature (London) in 1973 (Volume 246, Pages 15-18), is a strategy that is resilient to a small invasion of mutants. In other words, an ESS is a strategy that can withstand a limited introduction of new strategies without being displaced. This concept has been further developed by Gilboa and Matsui in Econometrica in 1991 (Volume 59, Pages 859-867), who proposed a stability concept based on the dynamics of best response. Specifically, they showed that the equilibrium frequencies of strategies in a dynamic system will converge to an ESS if the system is allowed to evolve over time.
In this paper, we explore the equivalence between two different stability concepts: a static concept and a dynamic one. Our results show that these two concepts are equivalent, and their set-valued versions always exist. To illustrate the practical application of these concepts, we provide examples of how they can be used to analyze forward induction and preplay communication.

title: From youth to adult homelessness
text: Governments have shown an interest in implementing early intervention strategies to prevent youth homelessness, but some critics argue that these programs lack clear outcomes. This study aims to investigate the consequences of not providing early intervention programs by examining what happens when young people progress to adult homelessness. The study tests the "social adaptation" hypothesis, which suggests that the longer a person is homeless, the more they will adapt to the lifestyle. Using data from 1,677 individuals who became homeless before the age of 18, the study finds that the longer a person is homeless, the more difficult it becomes for them to escape homelessness. However, the study also reveals that the social adaptation hypothesis overstates the extent to which people embrace homelessness as a way of life. With long-term support, people can transition back into conventional accommodation. The study concludes with three policy recommendations.

title: Urban spatial development in the land policy reform era: evidence from Beijing
text: This study investigates the characteristics of urban spatial development in Beijing and assesses the extent to which these characteristics can be attributed to the emerging land market in Beijing, as well as the impact of land policy reforms. By analyzing land use rights granted between 1993 and the first half of 2000 in the built-up area of Beijing, the study provides empirical evidence that both land prices and land development density decrease with distance from the city core. Additionally, it shows that the slope of the land rent curve varies depending on land use types. These findings suggest that the land market plays a significant role in shaping land development decisions and urban form. Furthermore, the study reveals that the slope of the land rent curve and the elasticity of land-capital substitution changes over time. Specifically, the former declines, likely due to Beijing's substantial investments in transportation, which have reduced transportation costs and shifted the land rent curve. Conversely, the latter rises, indicating that price effects play a more significant role in shaping land development density. These changes in the land rent function and the elasticity of land-capital substitution suggest that the Beijing land market is maturing. It is important to note, however, that there are significant land developments occurring outside of the formal land market (land development on administratively allocated land), which can distort urban land use patterns and impact the findings of this study.

title: The Mismatch Argument: The Construction of a Housing Orthodoxy in Australia
text:
Australia's housing policy discourse is rife with dominant narratives, or orthodoxies, that hold significant symbolic authority. One such orthodoxy is the notion of a 'mismatch' in the housing system, where the available stock and the size of households fail to match, resulting in significant underutilization and underoccupancy of housing. This mismatch argument is so influential that it is often assumed in housing policy discussions without question. Critics of this orthodoxy can take various approaches, including empirical, conceptual, and discursive analyses.
The discursive critique, in particular, focuses on the statements made about the relationship between households and dwellings, rather than the empirical relationship itself. Through this analysis, this paper sheds light on how the mismatch orthodoxy emerged in Australia in the early 1970s and gained widespread acceptance in national and state housing policy research by the early 1990s. The paper also examines how the structures of the discourse contribute to the entrenchment of this orthodoxy, despite criticisms from various quarters.
Of particular note is the impact that the mismatch orthodoxy has on individuals believed to be underutilizing their dwellings, as well as its influence on policy interpretations, such as occupancy standards. By examining the ways in which this orthodoxy shapes the housing discourse, this paper aims to provide a more nuanced understanding of the complex relationships between households, dwellings, and public policy.

title: Citizen Participation and Citizen Evaluation in Disaster Recovery
text: In April 1997, the twin cities of Grand Forks, North Dakota, and East Grand Forks, Minnesota, endured a devastating flood. Both cities have been recognized as exemplary cases of success by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), thanks to their updated infrastructure, largely funded by the federal government. Their downtown areas are witnessing a revitalization with new constructions and businesses. However, the cities have taken different paths in the aftermath of the disaster, with East Grand Forks embracing extensive citizen participation initiatives and Grand Forks relying more on bureaucratic guidance. This study aims to investigate the impact of citizens' perceptions of participation on their evaluation of the recovery effort.

title: Population growth, urban sprawl and landscape integrity of Beijing City
text: The detailed landscape analysis of the urban area within the 6th ring road in Beijing City was conducted using airborne remote sensing data acquired between 1997 and 2002. Landscape indices were calculated using Fragstats 3.3, and changes in land use/cover types in Beijing over this period were examined. The findings revealed significant changes within the 6th ring road, with urban built area (UBA) and farmland undergoing significant transformations. Farmland was replaced by UBA, resulting in a 106.6% increase in the number of patches and a 51.6% decrease in mean patch area. The splitting index increased by 94.3%, and the landscape diversity index rose by 17.8%, indicating a more fragmented and diverse landscape. The main drivers of these changes were the growing demand for land due to a rapidly increasing population, unplanned urban growth, and improved housing standards. The transformation of the landscape in Beijing as a result of rapid urbanization has had a negative impact on the city's...

title: Drink Choice: Factors Influencing the Intention to Drink Wine
text: This study investigates the factors that influence consumers' preference for wine over other alcoholic beverages, with a specific focus on the beliefs and attitudes held by consumers regarding wine drinking. Our findings suggest that while both attitudes and social norms play arole in determining wine consumption, attitudes are more strongly linked to intentions to drink wine. However, the study also highlights that neither attitudes nor norms alone can fully explain wine consumption. although the health benefits of wine were a prominent theme in the initial qualitative phase of the research, the subsequent quantitative findings revealed that drinking wine for its purported health benefits was not a significant motivator for consumers. On the other hand, the variety of tastes and flavors associated with wine, as well as its ability to complement food, emerged as more significant factors. These results suggest that efforts to promote the health benefits of wine drinking may be limited in their effectiveness.

title: Application of growth technologies in enhancing food security and sustainability
text:
Anabolic steroids have been widely utilized in the beef cattle industry for over 50 years as safe and effective growth-promoting agents. According to the National Animal Health Monitoring System (NAHMS) of the USDA (2000), more than 90% of feedlot cattle in the US receive some type of steroidal implant during their lifetime. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved a list of growth promotants, including steroidal implants, which have been shown to increase growth rate by 8-28%, improve feed efficiency by 5-20%, and enhance lean tissue mass of the carcass by 3-10% (Duckett and Owens, 1997). These production improvements have several benefits, including reducing production costs by decreasing the amount of feed required per unit of gain (Avery and Avery, 2007), reducing the amount of land needed to produce equivalent amounts of food for consumers (Avery and Avery, 2007), limiting the production of greenhouse gases by reducing the number of animals required to produce equivalent amounts of beef (Avery and Avery, 2007), and providing a year-round, affordable supply of beef at reduced prices (Lawrence and Ibarburu, 2006).
In addition to steroidal implants, a newer class of orally active growth promotants, known as beta-adrenergic agonists (BAA), have been approved for use in finishing beef cattle in the last decade. These products provide similar production benefits as steroidal implants, but differ in application and mode of action. Beta-adrenergic agonists are fed during the last 20-42 days of the cattle finishing period, depending on the specific product. The purpose of this paper is to explain the mechanisms of action and benefits of anabolic implants and BAA for beef cattle production.

title: Metabolic modifiers as performance-enhancing technologies for livestock production
text: With the projected surge in global population and rising consumer demand for food, the competition for land, water, and energy will intensify, posing a significant challenge to food production. To make matters worse, there is an urgent need to reduce the environmental impact of food production. Globalization has fueled trade in livestock inputs and products, leading to rapid industry growth, but this has also created a challenge for livestock producers, who must meet growing demand with dwindling resources. The only solution is to improve efficiency. As incomes rise in developing economies, the demand for high-quality animal proteins like meat, milk, and eggs is expected to increase by 70% by 2050, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. New technologies hold great promise for the animal industries, but widespread adoption requires additional emphasis on acceptance and development. Meat packers have benefited from improved processing efficiencies, while consumers have seen leaner and cheaper meat. However, some concerns have been raised about the quality of meat produced through increased production efficiency and lean meat yield. Despite the need for these technologies, market differentiation and trade barriers, as well as consumer resistance, pose significant challenges to their adoption. To meet the increased global demand for animal protein, we must continue to develop and adopt technologies to improve livestock efficiency, but we must be aware of the potential barriers to acceptance.

title: Assessment of hemodynamic efficacy and safety of 6% hydroxyethylstarch 130/0.4 vs. 0.9% NaCl fluid replacement in patients with severe sepsis: The CRYSTMAS study
text: Severe sepsis patients who do not receive appropriate initial treatment and delayed hemodynamic stabilization (HDS) are at increased risk of death. To investigate the efficacy and safety of 6% HES 130/0.4 and NaCl 0.9% in achieving HDS in severe sepsis patients, we conducted a prospective, multicenter, active-controlled, double-blind, randomized study in intensive care units. Of the 196 patients enrolled, 174 achieved HDS (88 and 86 patients for HES and NaCl, respectively). We found that significantly less HES was required to achieve HDS in the HES group compared to the NaCl group (mean difference = -331± 1,033, 95% CI -640 to -21, P = 0.0185). The time to reach HDS was also shorter in the HES group (11.8 ±10.1 hours vs. 14.3 ±11.1 hours). Furthermore, the total amount of study drug infused over four consecutive days, ICU and hospital length of stay, and area under the curve of Serum Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score were comparable between the two groups. However, acute renal failure occurred in more patients in the HES group (24.5%) than in the NaCl group (20%). There were no significant differences in mortality, coagulation, or pruritus between the two groups up to 90 days after treatment initiation or between the two groups using different criteria for acute kidney injury (AKIN and RIFLE). However, significantly less volume was required to achieve HDS for HES vs. NaCl in the initial phase of fluid resuscitation in severe sepsis patients without any difference in adverse events between the two groups (NCT00464204).

title: Comparisons between different polychemotherapy regimens for early breast cancer: meta-analyses of long-term outcome among 100,000 women in 123 randomised trials.
text:
The article discusses the results of an individual-patient-data meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluating the efficacy of different chemotherapy regimens for breast cancer. The analysis included 44,000 patients and found that:
* Adding four cycles of a taxane to a fixed anthracycline-based regimen reduced breast cancer mortality by 16% compared to the control group.
* In trials with four extra cycles of a taxane, there was no significant difference in breast cancer mortality compared to trials with more non-taxane chemotherapy.
* Anthracycline-based regimens with higher cumulative dosage than standard were superior to standard CMF in terms of breast cancer mortality.
* CAF was more effective than standard 4AC and standard CMF in reducing breast cancer mortality.

The analysis also found that the reductions in breast cancer mortality were not significantly affected by age, nodal status, tumor diameter or differentiation, oestrogen receptor status, or tamoxifen use. The authors conclude that some taxane-plus-anthracycline-based or higher-cumulative-dosage anthracycline-based regimens (not requiring stem cells) reduced breast cancer mortality by about one-third, on average, and that 10-year overall mortality differences paralleled breast cancer mortality differences.

title: Invariant NKT cells modulate the suppressive activity of IL-10-secreting neutrophils differentiated with serum amyloid A.
text: Neutrophils are the primary immune cells involved in inflammation; however, they can also inhibit excessive inflammatory responses by secreting anti-inflammatory cytokines. The mechanisms that regulate their adaptability, or plasticity, are not fully understood. Our research reveals that systemic serum amyloid A 1 (SAA-1) controls the plasticity of neutrophil differentiation. SAA-1 not only induces anti-inflammatory interleukin 10 (IL-10)-secreting neutrophils but also facilitates the interaction between invariant natural killer T cells (iNKT cells) and these neutrophils, resulting in a reduction in the suppression of immune responses. Because SAA-1-producing melanomas enhance the differentiation of IL-10-secreting neutrophils, harnessing iNKT cells may be therapeutically beneficial by decreasing the frequency of immunosuppressive neutrophils and restoring tumor-specific immune responses.

title: Body-mass index and cause-specific mortality in 900 000 adults: collaborative analyses of 57 prospective studies.
text:
Background: Assessing the relationship between body-mass index (BMI) and mortality requires long-term prospective follow-up of large numbers of people. The Prospective Studies Collaboration aimed to investigate these associations by analyzing data from numerous studies.
Methods: Collaborative analyses were conducted to investigate the association between BMI and mortality in 57 prospective studies with 894,576 participants, mostly from western Europe and North America. Participants' mean age was 46 years (standard deviation [SD] 11 years), and the median recruitment year was 1979 (interquartile range [IQR] 1975-1985). The analysis was adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, and study. To limit reverse causality, the first five years of follow-up were excluded, leaving 66,552 deaths of known cause during a mean of eight (SD six) further years of follow-up (mean age at death 67 years [SD 10 years]).
Findings: In both sexes, mortality was lowest at around 22.5-25 kg/m(2). Above this range, positive associations were recorded for several specific causes, and inverse associations were recorded for none. The absolute excess risks for higher BMI and smoking were roughly additive, and each five kg/m(2) higher BMI was on average associated with about 30% higher overall mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 1.29 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.27-1.32]). In particular, BMI was associated with vascular mortality (HR 1.41 [1.37-1.45]), diabetic, renal, and hepatic mortality (HRs 2.16 [1.89-2.46], 1.59 [1.27-1.99], and 1.82 [1.59-2.09], respectively), neoplastic mortality (HR 1.10 [1.06-1.15]), and respiratory and all other mortality (HRs 1.20 [1.07-1.34] and 1.20 [1.16-1.25], respectively). Below the range 22.5-25 kg/m(2), BMI was associated inversely with overall mortality, mainly due to strong inverse associations with respiratory disease and lung cancer. These inverse associations were much stronger for smokers than for non-smokers, despite cigarette consumption per smoker varying little with BMI.
Interpretation: Although other anthropometric measures (such as waist circumference and waist-to-hip ratio) could add extra information to BMI, BMI is a strong predictor of overall mortality both above and below the apparent optimum of around 22.5-25 kg/m(2). The progressive excess mortality above this range is due mainly to vascular disease and is likely to be causal. At 30-35 kg/m(2), median survival is reduced by 2-4 years; at 40-45 kg/m(2), it is reduced by 8-10 years (which is comparable with the effects of smoking). The definite excess mortality below 22.5 kg/m(2) is due mainly to smoking-related diseases and is not fully explained.

title: Targeting metabolic remodeling in glioblastoma multiforme.
text: A significant biological difference between cancer cells and normal differentiated cells is altered metabolism, where cancer cells acquire genetic and epigenetic changes to sustain proliferation, survival in unfavorable environments, and invasion of surrounding tissues. A typical biochemical adaptation is the shift towards aerobic glycolysis, independent of oxygen availability, a phenomenon known as the "Warburg Effect". This metabolic change is characterized by high glucose uptake, low oxygen consumption, and elevated production of lactate, which provides a survival advantage and generates necessary substrates such as fatty acids, amino acids, and nucleotides in rapidly proliferating cells. This review focuses on the role of key metabolic enzymes involved in modulating the "Warburg Effect" in Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM), an aggressive, highly glycolytic, and deadly brain tumor. Targeting these enzymes may offer a novel therapeutic approach, either alone or in combination with existing treatments, in managing GBMs.

title: Signaling architectures that transmit unidirectional information despite retroactivity
text:
A signaling pathway conveys information from an upstream system to downstream systems, ideally in a unidirectional manner. However, the phenomenon of retroactivity, where additional flux is generated in a system due to interactions with downstream systems, can hinder unidirectional transmission. This raises the question of whether signaling pathways have evolved specialized architectures to overcome retroactivity and transmit signals in a one-way manner.
To address this question, we propose a general mathematical framework for analyzing signaling pathways and their ability to transmit unidirectional signals. By tuning key biological parameters, we analyze the performance of various signaling architectures, including single-stage phosphorylation and phosphotransfer systems, cascades of these architectures, and phosphotransfer systems with single and double phosphorylation cycles.
Our results show that single-stage phosphorylation systems face a design trade-off that limits their ability to overcome retroactivity, while cascades of these architectures are more effective in achieving unidirectional transmission. Phosphotransfer systems and double phosphorylation cycles, on the other hand, are unable to mitigate retroactivity effects, even when organized into cascades.
These findings have important implications for understanding how signaling pathways evolved to transmit information in a unidirectional manner. By identifying the design principles that enable unidirectional transmission, we can decompose natural signal transduction networks into modules that can be reused in synthetic biology applications. These modular approaches can facilitate the design of novel signaling circuits with desired behaviors, enabling the creation of more sophisticated and efficient biological systems.

title: Association between pre-diabetes, type 2 diabetes and trabecular bone score: The Vietnam Osteoporosis Study.
text: The present study aimed to investigate the association between type 2 diabetes (T2D) and trabecular bone score (TBS) in adult Vietnamese men and women. The study was part of the Vietnam Osteoporosis Study, which recruited 2702 women and 1398 men aged ≥30 years from the general community in Ho Chi Minh City. HbA1c levels were measured using the ADAMS™ A1c HA-8160 (Arkray, Kyoto, Japan) and categorized into three groups: normal (HbA1c <5.7%), pre-diabetes (5.7-6.4%), and diabetes (>6.4%). TBS was evaluated using iNsight Software, version 2.1 (Medimaps, Merignac, France) on lumbar spine bone mineral density (BMD) scans (Hologic Horizon). The results showed that the prevalence of pre-diabetes and diabetes in men and women was 30.2% and 8.3%, respectively. In women, TBS was significantly lower in pre-diabetes (-0.02; P<0.001) and diabetes (-0.02; P<0.001) compared to normal individuals. In contrast, there was no statistically significant difference in TBS between diabetic status in men. Additionally, TBS was inversely correlated with HbA1c levels in women (P = 0.01), but not in men (P = 0.89). These findings suggest that diabetes and pre-diabetes are associated with a deterioration of bone microarchitecture, with a greater impact on women than men.

title: Adhesion molecules and chemokines: relation to anthropometric, body composition, biochemical and dietary variables
text:
Introduction:
In the complex pathogenesis of obesity, various inflammatory mediators play a significant role. Among these, the cell adhesion molecules Pselectin, E-selectin, VCAM-1, ICAM-1, and the chemokine MCP-1 are of particular interest. These molecules are crucial in cell adhesion to endothelial surfaces, vascular wall integrity, and can be modulated by body composition and dietary patterns.
Objectives:
The aim of this study is to investigate the correlation between these cell adhesion molecules and chemokines and anthropometric, body composition, dietary, and biochemical markers in obesity.
Methods:
We conducted a systematic search of scientific databases using specific keywords and no time restrictions.
Results:
Our findings indicate that all of these molecules are positively associated with anthropometric markers, but controversial results were found for ICAM-1 and VCAM-1. Furthermore, visceral fat is more strongly correlated with E-selectin and MCP-1 levels. Weight loss is shown to reduce levels of these molecules, except for VCAM-1. A Western dietary pattern, excessive consumption of saturated and trans fats, and a low intake of w-3 fatty acids are associated with increased levels of these molecules. Conversely, a healthy dietary pattern, high calcium intake, and high dairy consumption are associated with decreased levels. These molecules also show inverse relations with HDLC and positive relations to total cholesterol, triglycerides, blood glucose, fasting insulin, and insulin resistance.
Conclusion:
Our study reveals that normal anthropometric indicators, body composition, biochemical parameters, and eating patterns positively modulate the subclinical inflammation that results from obesity by reducing these cell adhesion molecules and chemokines.
